EDCS-03300964.summary: This is a very brief funerary inscription recording the name Florentina and the phrase 'in pace', suggesting a Christian burial.

EDCS-03300965.summary: This is a very brief funerary inscription recording the name Septimina and the phrase 'in peace', suggesting a Christian burial.

EDCS-03300967.translation: Celia Domitia Gabinilla lived and reigned for 38 years.
EDCS-03300967.summary: This inscription records the lifespan of Celia Domitia Gabinilla, unusually using the term 'reigned' for a woman, possibly in a symbolic or honorific sense.

EDCS-03300968.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespan of Monnika, described as 'fidelis' (faithful), possibly indicating a Christian context.

EDCS-03300969.summary: This epitaph records the lifespan of Secundiana, who lived 73 years.

EDCS-03300970.translation: Iulianus lived 15 days in peace, and Iana lived 70 years, 1 month, and 10 days in peace.
EDCS-03300970.summary: This epitaph records the lifespans of Iulianus (15 days) and Iana (70 years, 1 month, 10 days), both of whom lived in peace.

EDCS-03300971.translation: Hilarianus the faithful lived 46 years, 2 months, and 11 days in peace.
EDCS-03300971.summary: This epitaph records the lifespan of Hilarianus the faithful, who lived 46 years, 2 months, and 11 days.

EDCS-03300972.translation: A son made this monument for his most modest mother Fadiliana, faithful in peace.
EDCS-03300972.summary: This epitaph records a son dedicating a monument to his mother Fadiliana, describing her as most modest and faithful in peace.

EDCS-03300973.translation: For Fadiliana the innocent, most sweet, her uncle (places this) in peace.
EDCS-03300973.summary: This epitaph is dedicated to Fadiliana the innocent and most sweet by her uncle.

EDCS-03300974.translation: Lucia Iulia Candida lived 11 months. Sacred to the departed spirits.
EDCS-03300974.summary: This epitaph records the lifespan of Lucia Iulia Candida, who lived 11 months, and is dedicated to the departed spirits.

EDCS-03300975.translation: Concordia made (this) for Octavia Data in peace.
EDCS-03300975.summary: This epitaph records Concordia dedicating a monument to Octavia Data.

EDCS-03300976.summary: This epitaph records Achilles resting in peace.

EDCS-03300977.summary: This epitaph records Victoria resting in peace.

EDCS-03300978.translation: Gloriosus, her devoted husband, made (this) for Aemilia Honorata, most holy and most faithful woman, who sleeps here in peace, lived 2 months.
EDCS-03300978.summary: This epitaph records Gloriosus dedicating a monument to his wife Aemilia Honorata, who lived 2 months and is described as most holy and faithful.

EDCS-03300979.translation: Baleria lived in peace for 37 years.
EDCS-03300979.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Baleria.

EDCS-03300980.translation: Mariniana lived in peace for 60 years.
EDCS-03300980.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Mariniana.

EDCS-03300981.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Donatus.

EDCS-03300982.summary: This is a funerary epitaph stating Modestus was faithful and lived in peace.

EDCS-03300983.translation: Terentina, a faithful girl, lived for 17 years and 3 months.
EDCS-03300983.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Terentina.

EDCS-03300984.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Aemilius Plotinus lived for 40 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-03300984.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan and burial of Lucius Aemilius Plotinus.

EDCS-03300985.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Inventa lived for [---] years.
EDCS-03300985.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Inventa, with the duration lost.

EDCS-03300986.translation: Clodia lived for [---] years; she is buried here.
EDCS-03300986.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Clodia, with the duration lost.

EDCS-03300987.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Aruntia Saturnina lived for 83 years; she is buried here. She made this monument herself during her lifetime.
EDCS-03300987.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Aruntia Saturnina and stating she erected her own tomb while alive.

EDCS-03300988.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulia Saturnina lived for 40 years. Her son made this for his most dutiful mother.
EDCS-03300988.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Iulia Saturnina and stating it was erected by her son.

EDCS-03300989.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Pomponia Marcia lived 10 years. Her sons made this for their mother. She is buried here.
EDCS-03300989.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Pomponia Marcia at age 10, set up by her sons.

EDCS-03300990.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Aurelia Ingenua lived 25 years. Felix Pallida made this for her dearest wife.
EDCS-03300990.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Aurelia Ingenua at age 25, set up by her wife.

EDCS-03300991.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Gaius Julius Victor.
EDCS-03300991.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the name of Gaius Julius Victor.

EDCS-03300992.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Caecilia Gemellina lived 31 years. She is buried here. Mascunius made this.
EDCS-03300992.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Caecilia Gemellina at age 31, set up by Mascunius.

EDCS-03300994.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Aelia Felicula lived 45 years. Salvius made this for his most dutiful mother.
EDCS-03300994.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Aelia Felicula at age 45, set up by her son Salvius.

EDCS-03300995.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Iulia Felicia lived 20 years and 6 months. Fortunatus made this for his dearest wife.
EDCS-03300995.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Iulia Felicia at age 20 years and 6 months, set up by her husband Fortunatus.

EDCS-03300996.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Attia Libosa lived 16 years. Her brothers made this.
EDCS-03300996.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Attia Libosa at age 16, set up by her brothers.

EDCS-03300997.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Publius Celius Felix lived 3 years. His most dutiful father Pontianus made this. He is buried here.
EDCS-03300997.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Publius Celius Felix at age 3, set up by his father Pontianus.

EDCS-03300999.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Urbinius Micssi lived 80 years and Suchia Rogata lived 30 years. Codu is the heir.
EDCS-03300999.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the deaths of Urbinius Micssi (age 80) and Suchia Rogata (age 30), with Codu named as heir.

EDCS-03700781.translation: Benenatus, servant of God, lived in peace for 70 years, departed on the 8th day before the Kalends of August. Margarita, servant of God, lived in peace for 72 years, departed on the 3rd day before the Kalends of June.
EDCS-03700781.summary: A Christian funerary epitaph recording the lives and death dates of two individuals, Benenatus and Margarita, who were servants of God.

EDCS-03700782.translation: Elpison and Afrodisias made this for their most beloved son Quiricus, who lived 15 months, well-deserving, in peace.
EDCS-03700782.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by parents for their son, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-03700788.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Pascasius, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-03700789.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Cobulus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-03700792.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Victor, son of Masculus, priest of Minerva, lived 78 years.
EDCS-03700792.summary: A funerary epitaph dedicated to the Divine Spirits, recording the life of Victor, priest of Minerva, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-03700793.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Masculus, son of Masculus, lived 75 years. To the Divine Spirits. Secunda Tita lived 65 years.
EDCS-03700793.summary: A funerary epitaph dedicated to the Divine Spirits, recording the lives of two individuals, Masculus and Secunda Tita, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-03700795.translation: Iulia Ansara, who was also called Honoratiana, a chaste and faithful girl, lived 17 years, 6 months, and 3 hours in peace.
EDCS-03700795.summary: A funerary epitaph for Iulia Ansara (also known as Honoratiana), a young woman, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-03700796.translation: Acepius lived 2 years, 17 days, and 9 hours in peace.
EDCS-03700796.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the short lifespan of Acepius, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-03700797.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Ispendeus, faithful, lived in peace for years, months, days, and hours.
EDCS-03700797.summary: A funerary epitaph dedicated to the Divine Spirits for Ispendeus, with incomplete details of his lifespan, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-03700798.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Iulius Nabor lived 40 years, a month, and 17 days and 7 hours in peace.
EDCS-03700798.summary: A funerary epitaph dedicated to the Divine Spirits for Iulius Nabor, recording his lifespan, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-03700799.text_edition: \n Feliciter Faustus votum libens animo solvit\n
EDCS-03700799.translation: Successfully, Faustus gladly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-03700799.summary: A short votive inscription recording the fulfillment of a vow by Faustus, likely from the Imperial Roman period.

EDCS-03700800.summary: A funerary epitaph consisting only of a name, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-03700804.translation: Felix Fidelis lived 25 years in peace, buried on the fifth day before the Kalends of June.
EDCS-03700804.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan and burial date of Felix Fidelis, likely from the late Roman period.

EDCS-03700809.summary: This is a very short inscription, possibly a dedication or ownership marker, for Titus Aelius Sabinus.

EDCS-03700817.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Dead. Valeria Secundula lived 35 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-03700817.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Valeria Secundula, who is buried at this location.

EDCS-04000001.translation: To the divine will of Augustus, Emperor Caesar Trajan Hadrian Augustus. Callistus, freedman and record-keeper, under the procurator of Augustus, Gaius Sestius Panthera, [erected] a small marble shrine with columns.
EDCS-04000001.summary: This is a dedication of a marble shrine with columns to the divine will of Emperor Hadrian, erected by a freedman and record-keeper under a procurator. It is likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04000002.translation: To Titus Flavius Macro, son of Titus, of the voting tribe Quirina, twice a chief magistrate, perpetual priest, prefect of the Musulamian people, curator of grain procurement for the city's supply, appointed by the deified Nerva Trajan Augustus, procurator of Augustus for the estates of the Hipponian and Thevestine hunting grounds, procurator of the province of Sicily, [this was erected by] the college of the Lares of our Caesar and the freedmen and household staff, and also the tenants residing in the Hipponian region.
EDCS-04000002.summary: This is a complex dedication by various officials and groups, including a procurator of Sicily and administrators of imperial estates, to Titus Flavius Macro, a prominent local magistrate and official, likely from the late 1st or early 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04000003.translation: Here lies in the tomb, glory, a distinguished man, he brought calm to harshness, despising shameful things; here among the nobles, he was an example.
EDCS-04000003.summary: This is a funerary epitaph praising the deceased for his distinguished character, leadership, and virtuous example, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04000004.translation: In honor of the god Mercury, for the safety of the Emperor and the entire divine household, Decimus Caecilius Successus, priest, erected this altar by order.
EDCS-04000004.summary: This is a dedication of an altar to the god Mercury for the safety of the Emperor and his family, erected by a priest, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04000006.summary: This is a short inscription, possibly a dedication or an indication of ownership, related to Licentius and the Gilventii.

EDCS-04000007.summary: This is a short inscription, possibly a dedication or an indication of ownership, related to Procopeius and the Gilventii.

EDCS-04000008.summary: This is a short inscription, possibly a dedication or an indication of relationship, related to Safargius and Mercurialis.

EDCS-04000014.translation: Severus, a veteran of the third Praetorian cohort, lived 59 years; pious to his own, he is buried here.
EDCS-04000014.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Severus, a veteran of the Praetorian guard, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04000015.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Cnaeus Domitius Primullus lived 80 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-04000015.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Cnaeus Domitius Primullus, a Roman citizen, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04000016.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus Fabius Fabianus lived 21 years and 1 month; he is buried here.
EDCS-04000016.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Quintus Fabius Fabianus, a Roman citizen, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04000017.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulia Felicitas lived 38 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-04000017.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Iulia Felicitas, a Roman woman, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04000018.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulia Stratonice lived 51 years, 2 months, and 25 days; she is buried here.
EDCS-04000018.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Iulia Stratonice, a Roman woman, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04000019.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Iunius Adventus lived 40 years, 6 months, and 8 days; he is buried here.
EDCS-04000019.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Iunius Adventus, a Roman citizen, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04000021.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Sempronius Manilius lived 17 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-04000021.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Sempronius Manilius, a Roman citizen, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04000024.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Praeliae Sabinae, wife most dutiful, to her husband, Malchio, freedman of the procurator of Augustus, is buried here.
EDCS-04000024.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated by a wife to her husband, Malchio, a freedman of an imperial procurator, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04000025.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Helvia Secunda lived.
EDCS-04000025.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary epitaph for Helvia Secunda, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04000026.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Martialis lived 41 years and 1 month.
EDCS-04000026.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary epitaph for Martialis, who served the emperor, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04000027.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Flavia Tyche lived 85 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-04000027.summary: A funerary epitaph for Flavia Tyche, recording her age at death and burial, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04000028.translation: For the Municipium Augustum of the Hipponenses Regiores, a colony of veterans, of the Julian tribe of the Thabracenses.
EDCS-04000028.summary: An inscription identifying the administrative and tribal affiliations of a Roman colony, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-04000029.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Martis lived 85 years.
EDCS-04000029.summary: A funerary epitaph for Martis, recording his age at death, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04000030.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Seduce, daughter of Ni et Gad, lived [---].
EDCS-04000030.summary: A funerary epitaph for Seduce, daughter of Ni et Gad, recording her lifespan, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04000031.translation: Successus, a builder and slave, made [this] for the safety of the forests, successfully.
EDCS-04000031.summary: An inscription recording a dedication by Successus, a slave builder, for the well-being of forests, possibly related to agricultural or environmental concerns.

EDCS-04000032.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Cornelius Elmasa lived 55 years, 5 months, and 15 hours.
EDCS-04000032.summary: A funerary epitaph for Cornelius Elmasa, detailing his precise age at death, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04000033.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Iulia Festa, daughter of Gallus, lived 25 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-04000033.summary: A funerary epitaph for Iulia Festa, recording her age at death and burial, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04000034.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Lucius Postumius Crescens lived 60 years.
EDCS-04000034.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lucius Postumius Crescens, recording his age at death, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04000042.translation: Marcus Basilius Macer willingly paid his vow.
EDCS-04000042.summary: A dedication recording Marcus Basilius Macer fulfilling a vow, likely a votive inscription from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04000047.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Quintus Auficius Senecio lived 20 years.
EDCS-04000047.summary: A funerary epitaph for Quintus Auficius Senecio, recording his age at death, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04000048.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Marcia Prima lived 56 years, 8 months, and 1 day; she is buried here.
EDCS-04000048.summary: A funerary epitaph for Marcia Prima, recording her lifespan and burial.

EDCS-04000049.translation: Sacred to Saturn Augustus. Donatus dedicated this.
EDCS-04000049.summary: A dedication to Saturn Augustus by Donatus.

EDCS-04000050.translation: Sacred to the god Saturn Augustus. Lucius Victor brought this.
EDCS-04000050.summary: A dedication to Saturn Augustus by Lucius Victor.

EDCS-04000051.translation: Sacred to Saturn Augustus. L. Publius Simplicius [dedicated this].
EDCS-04000051.summary: A dedication to Saturn Augustus by L. Publius Simplicius.

EDCS-04000052.translation: Amotalat fulfilled a vow to Saturn.
EDCS-04000052.summary: A record of Amotalat fulfilling a vow to Saturn.

EDCS-04000054.summary: A record of Agrippinus willingly fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-04000055.translation: Auficius Sabinus willingly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-04000055.summary: A record of Auficius Sabinus willingly fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-04000056.translation: Basilius S. willingly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-04000056.summary: A record of Basilius S. willingly fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-04000057.translation: Didius Dexter willingly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-04000057.summary: A record of Didius Dexter willingly fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-04000058.translation: Gaius Fabricius willingly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-04000058.summary: A record of Gaius Fabricius willingly fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-04000059.summary: A private dedication by Matrona, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-04000060.translation: Octavia Fundana willingly fulfilled her vow.
EDCS-04000060.summary: A private dedication by Octavia Fundana, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-04000061.translation: Caius Pomponius Capito willingly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-04000061.summary: A private dedication by Caius Pomponius Capito, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-04000062.translation: Rutilius Felix willingly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-04000062.summary: A private dedication by Rutilius Felix, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-04000063.translation: Scantius Fundanus willingly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-04000063.summary: A private dedication by Scantius Fundanus, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-04000064.translation: Lucius Vecius Tiburtinus Cerialis, his son, willingly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-04000064.summary: A private dedication by Lucius Vecius Tiburtinus Cerialis, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-04000069.summary: An inscription likely naming a person, possibly Tironius Gaetulus.

EDCS-04000071.translation: To the Emperor Caesar, son of the deified Nerva, Nerva Trajan Optimus Augustus.
EDCS-04000071.summary: An honorific inscription dedicated to Emperor Trajan.

EDCS-04000076.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Annius Martialis lived for 67 years.
EDCS-04000076.summary: A funerary epitaph for Annius Martialis, who lived 67 years.

EDCS-04000078.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Marcus Dextrius Rufus, dutiful, made this for himself and his wife while alive. He lived for 75 years. Iulia Clementilla, dutiful, lived for [---] years.
EDCS-04000078.summary: A funerary epitaph for Marcus Dextrius Rufus and his wife Iulia Clementilla, specifying their ages at death.

EDCS-04000079.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Euprope lived 23 years.
EDCS-04000079.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Euprope, who died at the age of 23.

EDCS-04000081.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Quintus Furius Bassianus, dutiful.
EDCS-04000081.summary: This is a funerary epitaph, likely for Quintus Furius Bassianus, identified as dutiful.

EDCS-04000082.translation: Lived 55 years. Ianuarius placed [this] for his well-deserving wife.
EDCS-04000082.summary: This epitaph records the lifespan of a woman and its dedication by her husband, Ianuarius.

EDCS-04000083.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Quintus Magnius Rufinus, dutiful, lived 40 years.
EDCS-04000083.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Quintus Magnius Rufinus, who died at the age of 40.

EDCS-04000084.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Nicia Maxima, dutiful, lived 60 years. Cominia Maia, dutiful, lived 30 years. Sacred to the Divine Manes. Quintus Memmius Quietus, dutiful, lived 50 years.
EDCS-04000084.summary: This inscription is a collection of funerary epitaphs for Nicia Maxima, Cominia Maia, and Quintus Memmius Quietus, recording their lifespans.

EDCS-04000085.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Sittia Rosaria, dutiful, lived 40 years. Iulius Maior, her husband, placed [this] for her, who deserved well of him.
EDCS-04000085.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan of Sittia Rosaria and was dedicated by her husband, Iulius Maior.

EDCS-04000086.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Marcus Safidius Felicianus, dutiful, lived 45 years. Sacred to the Divine Manes. Magnia Honorata, dutiful, lived 40 years.
EDCS-04000086.summary: This inscription contains two funerary epitaphs for Marcus Safidius Felicianus and Magnia Honorata, recording their lifespans.

EDCS-04000087.translation: Silicia Rustica, daughter of Publius, lived 60 years, is buried here.
EDCS-04000087.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Silicia Rustica, daughter of Publius, who died at the age of 60.

EDCS-04000088.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Caius Sittius Saturninus, dutiful, lived 30 years and 5 months.
EDCS-04000088.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Caius Sittius Saturninus, who died at the age of 30 years and 5 months.

EDCS-04000089.translation: Marcus Stertinius Rogatus, son of Marcus, of the Arnensi tribe, dutiful, lived 75 years, is buried here.
EDCS-04000089.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan and tribal affiliation of Marcus Stertinius Rogatus.

EDCS-04000094.translation: Under this sacred veil of the altar are the memories of the saints Massa Candida, Saint Hesidorus, the Three Holy Youths, Saint Martin, and Saint Romanus.
EDCS-04000094.summary: This inscription lists various saints whose memories are housed under the altar's veil, likely from a church or shrine.

EDCS-04000096.translation: [Name] and their children, out of longing in their hearts, decorated this.
EDCS-04000096.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by a person and their children, likely for a funerary or religious monument.

EDCS-04000098.summary: This inscription is a short epitaph for Alexis, identified as an innocent cleric.

EDCS-04000099.translation: Amantius lived for 1 year and 6 months and rested on the 4th day of March in the 6th indiction.
EDCS-04000099.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan and death date of Amantius, with a specific indiction year suggesting a post-Roman date.

EDCS-04000100.translation: Donatus lived for 17 years and rested in peace.
EDCS-04000100.summary: This is a simple funerary epitaph for Donatus, stating his age at death and his resting in peace.

EDCS-04000102.translation: Rogatus, son of Arinis, lived for 53 years and is buried here.
EDCS-04000102.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the name, parentage, age at death, and burial location of Rogatus.

EDCS-04000105.translation: Dedicated to the spirits of the underworld. Vibia Felicitas, the dutiful, lived for 56 years. Successus and [---]
EDCS-04000105.summary: This funerary inscription begins with a dedication to the Manes and records the lifespan of Vibia Felicitas, with space for another individual.

EDCS-04000106.translation: Pitia, daughter of Laio, [father's name], lived 43 years.
EDCS-04000106.summary: This inscription appears to be a funerary epitaph, recording the name, parentage, and lifespan of Pitia, though parts are highly abbreviated or damaged.

EDCS-04000108.translation: Dedicated to the spirits of the underworld. Manilia Spesina lived for 31 years. Dedicated to the spirits of the underworld. Caius Sittius Rogatus, veteran.
EDCS-04000108.summary: This inscription contains two distinct funerary dedications, one for Manilia Spesina and another for Caius Sittius Rogatus, a veteran.

EDCS-04000109.translation: Dedicated to the spirits of the underworld. Monnica, the empresses' slave girl, lived for 35 years. Optatus placed this for his wife. Dedicated to the spirits of the underworld. Lucius Optatus lived for 100 years and is buried here.
EDCS-04000109.summary: This inscription contains two funerary dedications: one for Monnica, a slave, placed by Optatus for his wife, and another for Lucius Optatus, who lived to 100.

EDCS-04000110.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Spesina, slave of the emperors, lived 20 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-04000110.summary: A tombstone recording the death of Spesina, a freedwoman of the emperors, who died at the age of 20.

EDCS-04000111.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Apronius Quintasius lived 42 years; he is buried here. Iulia Urbana lived 31 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-04000111.summary: A tombstone recording the deaths of Apronius Quintasius (42) and Iulia Urbana (31).

EDCS-04000112.translation: Quintus Aufidius, son of Cirrenia, Afrodisia.
EDCS-04000112.summary: A fragmentary inscription possibly naming Quintus Aufidius and his mother Cirrenia, with a possible cognomen Afrodisia.

EDCS-04000113.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Fundanus Secundini lived 55 years; his grandson made this. Sacred to the departed spirits. Saturninia Secunda lived 20 years; she is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Hospitalis lived 13 years. Sacred to the departed spirits. Bassus lived 30 years.
EDCS-04000113.summary: A tombstone recording the deaths of Fundanus Secundini (55), Saturninia Secunda (20), Hospitalis (13), and Bassus (30), with the grandson of Fundanus mentioned as the maker.

EDCS-04000114.translation: Iulius Maternus from Seratis lived 25 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-04000114.summary: A tombstone recording the death of Iulius Maternus from Seratis at the age of 25.

EDCS-04000115.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Magnius lis pius lived 45 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-04000115.summary: A tombstone recording the death of Magnius lis pius at the age of 45.

EDCS-04000117.translation: To Numidia, wife of SEN, the legate.
EDCS-04000117.summary: A dedication to Numidia, wife of a legate named SEN.

EDCS-04000119.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Faonius Maximus lived 80 years. Sacred to the departed spirits. To Domitia Catulla, his wife, lived 70 years. Sacred to the departed spirits. Sacred to the departed spirits.
EDCS-04000119.summary: A tombstone recording the deaths of Faonius Maximus (80) and his wife Domitia Catulla (70).

EDCS-04000120.summary: A tombstone recording the death of Rufianus at the age of 30.

EDCS-04000122.translation: Victor, son of Rufilla, from Atunucadus, lived 33 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-04000122.summary: A tombstone recording the death of Victor, son of Rufilla, from Atunucadus, at the age of 33.

EDCS-04000123.translation: Gaius Maesius Bassilius lived 23 years. Gaius Maesius made [this] for his most devoted son. He is buried here.
EDCS-04000123.summary: This is a tombstone for Gaius Maesius Bassilius, set up by his father, also named Gaius Maesius.

EDCS-04000124.translation: Here lie the remains of blessed Peter the apostle and of the saints Felix and Vincent, martyrs.
EDCS-04000124.summary: This inscription marks the burial place of the martyrs Peter, Felix, and Vincent.

EDCS-04000126.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Gaius Aquilius Telesinus lived 103 years, during which time he held the priesthood of the Genius of his homeland for 48 years. He is buried here. Casta Satura, wife of the aforesaid, lived 70 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-04000126.summary: This is a tombstone for Gaius Aquilius Telesinus and his wife Casta Satura, noting their ages and his priestly service.

EDCS-04000127.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus Asmunius Quintianus the pious lived 32 years, 6 months, and [some] days and hours. He is buried here.
EDCS-04000127.summary: This is a tombstone for Quintus Asmunius Quintianus, recording his age and pious character.

EDCS-04000129.translation: Cornelia Maxima lived 25 years. She is buried here. [Her son?] Cornel N lived [age not specified] years. He is buried here.
EDCS-04000129.summary: This is a tombstone for Cornelia Maxima and an unidentified male relative.

EDCS-04000131.translation: Honorata, daughter of Clementis, lived 28 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-04000131.summary: This is a tombstone for Honorata, daughter of Clementis.

EDCS-04000132.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulia Sa...
EDCS-04000132.summary: This is a tombstone fragment for Iulia Sa...

EDCS-04000133.translation: Marcus Licinius Quintianus lived 50 years. He is buried here. Licinia Quinta lived 35 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-04000133.summary: This is a tombstone for Marcus Licinius Quintianus and Licinia Quinta.

EDCS-04000136.translation: He erected these small altars during his lifetime and dedicated them. He lived 75 years and 8 months. He is buried here.
EDCS-04000136.summary: This inscription records the erection and dedication of altars by an individual who lived 75 years and 8 months.

EDCS-04000140.translation: Cornelia Honorata, wife of Lucanus. Lived [age not specified] years. Marcus Licinius Lucanus, veteran of the Second Legion Adiutrix.
EDCS-04000140.summary: This is a tombstone commemorating Cornelia Honorata, wife of Marcus Licinius Lucanus, a veteran of the Second Adiutrix Legion.

EDCS-04000141.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Basilia Laenilla, dutiful daughter of Publius, lived 37 years and is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Basilius Honoratus, son of Lucius, having held public offices, dutiful, lived 81 years and is buried here.
EDCS-04000141.summary: This is a joint funerary epitaph for Basilia Laenilla and Lucius Basilius Honoratus, likely husband and wife, who died at advanced ages.

EDCS-04000142.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulia Urbana, wife of Bassilius Hospitalis, lived [years]. Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcus Basilius Hospitalis, having held all public offices, lived 75 years. Sacred to the departed spirits. Proculeia Sextulla, dutiful wife of Basilius Hospitalis, lived 35 years and is buried here.
EDCS-04000142.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcus Basilius Hospitalis and his wife Proculeia Sextulla, and also mentions Iulia Urbana, likely a former wife of Hospitalis.

EDCS-04000143.translation: [dia] Matrona, dutiful, lived 31 years. Sacred to the departed spirits. Publius Basilius Iunianus, having held public offices, dutiful, lived 79 years.
EDCS-04000143.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Publius Basilius Iunianus and possibly a woman named Matrona, recording their ages at death.

EDCS-04000144.translation: Marcus Aemilius Iustus, son of Medocenus, lived 51 years and is buried here.
EDCS-04000144.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcus Aemilius Iustus, recording his name, parentage, age at death, and burial.

EDCS-04000145.translation: Saturnina, wife of Nereus, lived 61 years. [Belonging to] Lucius Aemilius Nereus.
EDCS-04000145.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Saturnina, wife of Nereus, noting her age at death and associating her with Lucius Aemilius Nereus.

EDCS-04000146.translation: Antonia Fortunata, wife of Lucius Antonius, lived 70 years and is buried here.
EDCS-04000146.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Antonia Fortunata, recording her name, marital status, age at death, and burial.

EDCS-04000147.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Arellia Casta, daughter of Fuscus, wife of Iulius Andericius, dutiful, lived 33 years and is buried here.
EDCS-04000147.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Arellia Casta, recording her parentage, marital status, age at death, and burial.

EDCS-04000148.translation: Baebia Paula Vitosa, daughter of Lucius, wife, lived 45 years and is buried here.
EDCS-04000148.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Baebia Paula Vitosa, recording her parentage, marital status, age at death, and burial.

EDCS-04000149.translation: Crescentius, son of Baliaton, lived [years]. Victoria Fortunata, wife of Baliaton.
EDCS-04000149.summary: This inscription appears to be a fragmented funerary epitaph, mentioning Crescentius and Victoria Fortunata, possibly related.

EDCS-04000150.translation: Son of Baliathon, lived 80 years and is buried here.
EDCS-04000150.summary: This is a funerary epitaph fragment for a son of Baliathon, recording his age at death and burial.

EDCS-04000151.translation: Bennia Matrona, daughter of Germanus, lived 35 years, is laid here.
EDCS-04000151.summary: This is a tombstone forennia Matrona, daughter of Germanus, who died at the age of 35.

EDCS-04000152.translation: Caecilius Latro, dutiful, lived 85 years, is laid here.
EDCS-04000152.summary: This is a tombstone for Caecilius Latro, who died at the age of 85.

EDCS-04000153.translation: Lucius Caecilius Numa, son of Regilla, dutiful, lived 35 years, is laid here.
EDCS-04000153.summary: This is a tombstone for Lucius Caecilius Numa, son of Regilla, who died at the age of 35.

EDCS-04000154.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Tiberius Claudius Felix lived 60 years, is laid here.
EDCS-04000154.summary: This is a tombstone for Tiberius Claudius Felix, who died at the age of 60.

EDCS-04000155.translation: Dexter, son of Iustus, lived 21 years, is laid here.
EDCS-04000155.summary: This is a tombstone for Dexter, son of Iustus, who died at the age of 21.

EDCS-04000156.translation: Fabricius Rogatus lived 51 years, is laid here.
EDCS-04000156.summary: This is a tombstone for Fabricius Rogatus, who died at the age of 51.

EDCS-04000157.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Lucius Fadius Victor Romatianus lived 21 years, is laid here. Lucius Fadius Romatius Felix, son of Fadius Fronto, lived 70 years, is laid here.
EDCS-04000157.summary: This is a double tombstone recording the deaths of Lucius Fadius Victor Romatianus at 21 and Lucius Fadius Romatius Felix at 70.

EDCS-04000160.summary: This tombstone records the life of Gabinia Saturnina, who died at the age of 23.

EDCS-04000161.translation: Here is laid X. Gudeia, daughter of Nepos, dutiful, lived 25 years, is laid here.
EDCS-04000161.summary: This is a tombstone for Gudeia, daughter of Nepos, who died at the age of 25.

EDCS-04000162.summary: This tombstone records the life of Honorata, who died at the age of 90.

EDCS-04000163.translation: Iulius Balcilecis, a dutiful son, lived 71 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-04000163.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan and burial of Iulius Balcilecis, dating likely to the Imperial period.

EDCS-04000164.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Quintus Iulius Fortunatus Romanianus, son of Quintus Iulius Romanus, a dutiful man, lived 20 years and 3 months; he is buried here.
EDCS-04000164.summary: A funerary epitaph for Quintus Iulius Fortunatus Romanianus, detailing his parentage, lifespan, and burial, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-04000165.translation: Caius Iulius Victor Rufinus, a dutiful man, lived; he is buried here.
EDCS-04000165.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the burial of Caius Iulius Victor Rufinus, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-04000166.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Iulia Donata lived 50 years. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Iulius Ra lived 95 years.
EDCS-04000166.summary: Two separate funerary epitaphs, one for Iulia Donata and one for Iulius Ra, recording their lifespans, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-04000167.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Iulia Monica, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-04000168.translation: Iulianus, son of Maximi, lived 45 years; he is buried here. Saturnina, daughter of Severi.
EDCS-04000168.summary: A funerary epitaph for Iulianus, also mentioning Saturnina, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-04000169.translation: Licinius Sextianus lived 15 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-04000169.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan and burial of Licinius Sextianus, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-04000170.summary: An epitaph identifying Lubria Urbana as the wife of Victor, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-04000171.translation: Lucretia Trifera lived 45 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-04000171.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan and burial of Lucretia Trifera, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-04000172.translation: Lucius Lutatius Martialis lived 70 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-04000172.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan and burial of Lucius Lutatius Martialis, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-04000173.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Iulia Fortunata, wife of Zabullus, (and) Mactorius Zabullus, pious, lived 60 years, is buried here.
EDCS-04000173.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Iulia Fortunata and Mactorius Zabullus, recording their ages and burial.

EDCS-04000174.translation: Marcella Vitalis, wife, lived 55 years, is buried here.
EDCS-04000174.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcella Vitalis, recording her age and burial.

EDCS-04000175.translation: At the age of 21 years, Maximus Africanus lived 60 years.
EDCS-04000175.summary: This funerary epitaph records the age at death (21 years) and lifespan (60 years) of Maximus Africanus.

EDCS-04000176.translation: Gaius Octavius Marcus lived 60 years, is buried here. Zibbo, son of Baliatonis, lived 50 years, is buried here.
EDCS-04000176.summary: This is a funerary epitaph commemorating two individuals, Gaius Octavius Marcus and Zibbo, son of Baliatonis, with their ages and burial locations.

EDCS-04000177.translation: Son of Optatus, pious, lived 85 years, is buried here. Optatus, (son) of Victoris, (lived) here.
EDCS-04000177.summary: This funerary epitaph records the age of a son of Optatus and mentions Optatus, son of Victoris, who is also buried here.

EDCS-04000178.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Rufina, wife of Pisonis, lived 8 years, is buried here. His wife INA Maxima lived 35 years, is buried here. Pisso lived 80 years. Marchella lived 70 years. Marcus lived 30 years, is buried here.
EDCS-04000178.summary: This is a collective funerary epitaph for Rufina, INA Maxima, Pisso, Marchella, and Marcus, recording their ages and burial.

EDCS-04000179.translation: Quintus, son of Rogatus, lived 21 years.
EDCS-04000179.summary: This funerary epitaph records the age of Quintus, son of Rogatus, at the time of his death.

EDCS-04000180.translation: Regilla, daughter of Fortunatus Rufus, pious, lived 55 years, is buried here.
EDCS-04000180.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Regilla, daughter of Fortunatus Rufus, recording her age and burial.

EDCS-04000182.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Rogatus, son of Saturninus, pious, lived 70 years, is buried here.
EDCS-04000182.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Rogatus, son of Saturninus, recording his age and burial.

EDCS-04000184.translation: Romanus, son of Martialis, pious, lived 15 years, is buried here.
EDCS-04000184.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Romanus, son of Martialis, recording his age and burial.

EDCS-04000185.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Rufus, son of Baribgalis, lived 40 years. Fortunata lived [---]
EDCS-04000185.summary: A funerary inscription for Rufus and Fortunata, likely from the Roman era, recording their lifespans.

EDCS-04000186.translation: Biric, daughter of Quintillus, lived 61 years, is buried here. Sallustius Felix, dutiful, lived 35 years, is buried here. Caius Sallustius Fortunatus lived 81 years, is buried here.
EDCS-04000186.summary: A funerary inscription for Biric, Sallustius Felix, and Caius Sallustius Fortunatus, dating from the Roman Imperial period, recording their ages and burial.

EDCS-04000187.summary: A funerary epitaph for Sallustia Aemiliana, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04000188.translation: To Silvana, daughter of Baribal. Lived 35 years, is buried here.
EDCS-04000188.summary: A funerary inscription for Silvana, daughter of Baribal, likely from the Roman era, noting her age and burial.

EDCS-04000189.translation: Spana, daughter of Autrgais, lived 91 years, is buried here.
EDCS-04000189.summary: A funerary epitaph for Spana, daughter of Autrgais, from the Roman Imperial period, recording her age and burial.

EDCS-04000190.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Spana the dutiful lived 35 years, is buried here.
EDCS-04000190.summary: A funerary inscription for Spana, likely from the Roman era, noting her age and burial.

EDCS-04000191.translation: Urbana, wife of Victor, lived 30 years, is buried here. Victor, the dutiful son, lived 60 years, is buried here.
EDCS-04000191.summary: A funerary inscription for Urbana and her son Victor, likely from the Roman era, recording their ages and burial.

EDCS-04000192.translation: N., son of Victor, lived 65 years, is buried here.
EDCS-04000192.summary: A funerary inscription for N., son of Victor, likely from the Roman era, recording his age and burial.

EDCS-04000193.translation: Urbanus, son of Flaccus, lived 40 years, is buried here.
EDCS-04000193.summary: A funerary inscription for Urbanus, son of Flaccus, likely from the Roman era, recording his age and burial.

EDCS-04000194.translation: Urbana, wife of Rufinus, the dutiful, lived 51 years, is buried here.
EDCS-04000194.summary: A funerary inscription for Urbana, wife of Rufinus, likely from the Roman era, recording her age and burial.

EDCS-04000195.translation: Urbana, daughter of Fortunatus, wife, lived here for 21 years.
EDCS-04000195.summary: This epitaph records the life of Urbana, who died at the age of 21.

EDCS-04000199.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Fortunata lived 90 years. Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintasius lived 65 years.
EDCS-04000199.summary: This tombstone commemorates two individuals, Fortunata and Quintasius, with their ages at death.

EDCS-04000232.translation: For the memory of Hammonia, daughter of Beregbalus, priestess of Ceres. Marcus Nonius Victor made this.
EDCS-04000232.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Marcus Nonius Victor in memory of Hammonia, a priestess of Ceres.

EDCS-04000233.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Titus Flavius Euthyces, dutiful, lived 75 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-04000233.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Titus Flavius Euthyces, who died at the age of 75.

EDCS-04000234.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Publius Modius Rufinus, dutiful, lived 60 years. He is laid here.
EDCS-04000234.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Publius Modius Rufinus, who died at the age of 60.

EDCS-04000236.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Netiani EM Silva lived 87 years.
EDCS-04000236.summary: This tombstone records the lifespan of Netiani EM Silva, who died at the age of 87.

EDCS-04000237.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits and to Piety. Firmus, son of Victoris, lived 8 years.
EDCS-04000237.summary: This epitaph records the death of Firmus, son of Victoris, at the age of 8.

EDCS-04000238.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Aufidia Nabra lived 57 years. She is laid here. Felix lived 75 years. He is laid here.
EDCS-04000238.summary: This tombstone commemorates two individuals, Aufidia Nabra and Felix, with their ages at death.

EDCS-04000239.translation: Lucius Grasidius Nigrinus, dutiful, lived 75 years. May you rest well here.
EDCS-04000239.summary: This epitaph records the life of Lucius Grasidius Nigrinus, who died at the age of 75.

EDCS-04000240.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Papiria Quinta made this for her deserving husband, Spurinna Munatianus, while she was alive. He lived and is laid here.
EDCS-04000240.summary: This funerary inscription was made by Papiria Quinta for her husband, Spurinna Munatianus, indicating it was a pre-arranged burial site.

EDCS-04000242.translation: Sabonis, daughter of ITME, lived 85 years.
EDCS-04000242.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the age of the deceased, Sabonis.

EDCS-04000243.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Dead. Sisa, daughter of Titi Barici, a dutiful woman, lived 45 years.
EDCS-04000243.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Sisa, stating her age and filial relationship.

EDCS-04000244.translation: Lived 35 years, is buried here. Likewise Victoria lived 40 years, is buried here.
EDCS-04000244.summary: This funerary inscription records the ages and burial places of two individuals, one identified as Victoria.

EDCS-04000247.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Dead. Primus, son of SCEIVLI.
EDCS-04000247.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicating the burial to Primus, son of SCEIVLI.

EDCS-04000248.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Dead. Thader, daughter of Baliathon, a dutiful woman, lived 80 years, is buried here.
EDCS-04000248.summary: This funerary inscription records the age and burial of Thader, daughter of Baliathon.

EDCS-04000249.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Dead. Augustalis lived 40 years.
EDCS-04000249.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the age of the deceased, Augustalis.

EDCS-04000250.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Dead. Publius Lollius Iulianus, son of Faustus, lived 100 years, is buried here.
EDCS-04000250.summary: This funerary inscription records the age and burial of Publius Lollius Iulianus.

EDCS-04000251.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Dead. Maris, son of VARX, lived 85 years, is buried here. Sacred to the Spirits of the Dead. Catta, daughter of Adiutoris S., lived 83 years.
EDCS-04000251.summary: This funerary inscription records the ages and burials of two individuals, Maris and Catta.

EDCS-04000252.translation: Lived 95 years. Dutiful sons made this. SE Honoratus lived 71 years, is buried here.
EDCS-04000252.summary: This funerary inscription records the ages of two individuals and states that the monument was erected by dutiful sons.

EDCS-04000253.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Dead. Sextia Aureola, a dutiful woman, lived 28 years, is buried here.
EDCS-04000253.summary: This funerary inscription records the age and burial of Sextia Aureola.

EDCS-04000254.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Statorius Adiutor, pious, lived 70 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-04000254.summary: This is a tombstone commemorating Statorius Adiutor, who lived 70 years and is buried here.

EDCS-04000255.translation: SI AAE LXL V lived 103 years, NIA ARIA lived 75 years.
EDCS-04000255.summary: This inscription records the ages of two individuals, SI AAE LXL V (103 years) and NIA ARIA (75 years).

EDCS-04000258.summary: This inscription likely refers to a person who held or was designated for the office of praetor.

EDCS-04000259.translation: To the perpetual priestess SR, and also HEI, and a statue to Annia Paulina.
EDCS-04000259.summary: This inscription dedicates a statue and possibly honors Annia Paulina, who held the perpetual priesthood.

EDCS-04000260.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Caius Aemilius Felix, pious veteran, lived [---] years. Claudius Aemilius Tus lived 165 days. Arrania Sura, his wife, made and dedicated this according to the provisions of his will.
EDCS-04000260.summary: This is a tombstone set up by Arrania Sura for her husband Caius Aemilius Felix, a veteran, also mentioning the lifespan of Claudius Aemilius Tus.

EDCS-04000261.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Aelius Martialis, perpetual priest, pious, lived 75 years. Aelius Rogatianus, honored with all offices, pious, lived 73 years. Priest of Jupiter, Aelius Martialis, the grandfather and father.
EDCS-04000261.summary: This inscription commemorates Aelius Martialis, a perpetual priest and veteran, and Aelius Rogatianus, both of whom lived to advanced ages, possibly erected by a descendant.

EDCS-04000262.summary: This is an incomplete inscription referring to a pious veteran who lived for an unstated duration.

EDCS-04000263.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. To Adaucta, his most pious wife. Victoricus made this. She lived 50 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-04000263.summary: This is a tombstone erected by Victoricus for his wife Adaucta, who lived 50 years and is buried there.

EDCS-04000264.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that appears to be a name, possibly of a person or a dedication.

EDCS-04000265.translation: Cornelia Victoria. Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Caecilius Victorinus lived 60 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-04000265.summary: This is a tombstone for Caecilius Victorinus, who lived 60 years and is buried here, possibly associated with Cornelia Victoria.

EDCS-04000266.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Caecilia Fortunata, daughter of Quintus, dutiful, lived 35 years. She is buried here. Quintus Caerellius Rusticus placed [this] for his dutiful wife.
EDCS-04000266.summary: A funerary epitaph for Caecilia Fortunata, set up by her husband Quintus Caerellius Rusticus, likely dating to the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-04000267.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Callistus, also called Ardalio, dutiful, lived 10 years. His dutiful father Athenio made [this].
EDCS-04000267.summary: A funerary epitaph for Callistus (Ardalio), set up by his father Athenio, likely dating to the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-04000268.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcus Kassius Lollianus, dutiful, lived 91 years. He is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Columba, daughter of Datus Africanus, dutiful, lived 70 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-04000268.summary: A double funerary epitaph for Marcus Kassius Lollianus and Columba, daughter of Datus Africanus, likely dating to the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-04000269.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Domitius Victor lived 75 years.
EDCS-04000269.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lucius Domitius Victor, likely dating to the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-04000270.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Flavia Victoria, dutiful, lived 22 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-04000270.summary: A funerary epitaph for Flavia Victoria, likely dating to the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-04000271.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Octavia Ingenua, dutiful, lived 35 years. Publius Perellius Gallus, also called Nasseus, [placed this] for his wife.
EDCS-04000271.summary: A funerary epitaph for Octavia Ingenua, set up by her husband Publius Perellius Gallus (Nasseus), likely dating to the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-04000272.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Pontilius Fortunatus.
EDCS-04000272.summary: A funerary epitaph for Pontilius Fortunatus, likely dating to the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-04000273.summary: A funerary epitaph for Romana, likely dating to the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-04000274.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Victor, son of Rogatus, dutiful, lived 80 years. Nabera, daughter of M., lived 75 years. Aelius Rogatus, son [of Victor], made [this].
EDCS-04000274.summary: A funerary epitaph for Victor and Nabera, possibly his wife, set up by their son Aelius Rogatus, likely dating to the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-04000276.translation: Iulius Nictentius, dutiful, innocent, lived 10 years.
EDCS-04000276.summary: A funerary epitaph for Iulius Nictentius, likely dating to the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-04000277.translation: In the name of God, Flavianilla lived 65 years. Iucundus, faithful, lived in peace for [some duration].
EDCS-04000277.summary: This inscription commemorates the life of Flavianilla and Iucundus, likely a Christian epitaph indicating their faithful lives.

EDCS-04000278.summary: This is a Christian epitaph recording the lifespan of Iulia Florianae, described as faithful.

EDCS-04000279.translation: Iulia Vitrubia, happy, lived 65 years in peace.
EDCS-04000279.summary: This inscription is likely a Christian epitaph for Iulia Vitrubia, noting her happy life and peaceful repose.

EDCS-04000280.translation: Seiasius, faithful, lived 6 years, 11 months, and 28 days in peace.
EDCS-04000280.summary: This Christian epitaph records the short life of Seiasius, who lived faithfully and in peace.

EDCS-04000281.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Vitrubia Fortunata, dutiful and faithful, lived 25 years in peace. She is buried here.
EDCS-04000281.summary: This epitaph is dedicated to the memory of Vitrubia Fortunata, a dutiful and faithful woman who died at 25.

EDCS-04000284.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Flavia Festa, dutiful, lived 51 years, 1 month, and 7 days. For the memory of her most beloved wife, Flavius Fortunatus, husband and perpetual priest of [the cult of the emperor/a god], [did this]. What remains for you, departed, from your faithful husband, and what he can lighten, our sorrow, and for you preserve your name for long ages, receive, my dear dutiful wife, these annual gifts of death, vows, solemn processions in order. She is buried here. May your bones rest well.
EDCS-04000284.summary: This epitaph, erected by Flavius Fortunatus for his deceased wife Flavia Festa, describes her life and his enduring love and remembrance.

EDCS-04000285.translation: For the safety of the Emperor Antoninus Augustus Pius and his children, Datus, son of Africanus, priest of Saturn, made and dedicated this gate.
EDCS-04000285.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a gate by Datus, son of Africanus, a priest of Saturn, for the well-being of Emperor Antoninus Pius and his family.

EDCS-04000286.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. A. Honorata, dutiful, lived 42 years and 7 months.
EDCS-04000286.summary: This epitaph is dedicated to A. Honorata, a dutiful woman who died at the age of 42 years and 7 months.

EDCS-04000287.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulius I.
EDCS-04000287.summary: This is a very brief epitaph dedicated to the departed spirit of Iulius I.

EDCS-04000288.summary: This epitaph records the lifespan of Iulia, who lived for 61 years, with part of her name or a descriptor being illegible.

EDCS-04000289.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Nabor lived piously for 80 years.
EDCS-04000289.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the name and age of the deceased, Nabor.

EDCS-04000290.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Erim lived for 70 years.
EDCS-04000290.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the name and age of the deceased, Erim.

EDCS-04000291.translation: Vivas! This monument is for you. The bones of A. S. I. V. M. A., who lived 51 years, and of H. E. I. I. I. A. C. V., who lived 61 years, may they rest well for you.
EDCS-04000291.summary: This funerary epitaph records the names (partially abbreviated) and ages of two individuals whose remains are interred together, with a wish for their peaceful rest.

EDCS-04000292.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the name of Natalis and his father, Saturninus.

EDCS-04000293.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the name of Zaba and her father, Balsamon.

EDCS-04000294.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the name of Africanus and his father, Muthunis.

EDCS-04000295.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Antilia Casta lived piously for 75 years, 9 months, and 18 days. Publius Antilius Crescens for his most pious mother.
EDCS-04000295.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated by Publius Antilius Crescens to his mother, Antilia Casta, recording her name, piety, and lifespan.

EDCS-04000312.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits, for Crementius, son of Ulpius Hilarius.
EDCS-04000312.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated to Crementius, son of Ulpius Hilarius.

EDCS-04000313.summary: This inscription records a sacred dedication to the deity Aesculapius Augustus.

EDCS-04000314.translation: To Felicitas Augusta, by decree of the decurions, with public money.
EDCS-04000314.summary: This inscription records a public dedication to Felicitas Augusta, funded by the town council.

EDCS-04000315.summary: A dedication to the deified empress Fortuna, likely from the imperial period.

EDCS-04000318.translation: Sacred to the Genius of the Numidian People.
EDCS-04000318.summary: A religious dedication to the Genius of the Numidians, probably from Roman North Africa.

EDCS-04000319.translation: Sacred to Hercules Augustus. By the hundred Numidians of the city of Vazalitanorum.
EDCS-04000319.summary: A dedication to Hercules Augustus by a group of 100 Numidians from the city of Vazalitanorum, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-04000320.translation: For the unconquered Hercules. The council and people decreed that this should be set up in this place for the well-being of Diocletian and Maximian Augusti, under the supervision of Gaius Umbrius Tertullus, an outstanding man and curator of the republic.
EDCS-04000320.summary: A decree by the local council and populace to erect a monument to Hercules Invictus for the health of Emperors Diocletian and Maximian, during the curatorship of C. Umbrius Tertullus, likely in the late 3rd or early 4th century CE.

EDCS-04000321.translation: Sacred to the honor and valor of the Augusti. For the prosperity of the times. A statue of another colossal figure, having fallen, was restored, with ornaments previously buried in the ruins placed around it. Flavius Atilius Theodotus, a most distinguished man and his legate, took care for its preservation during the proconsulship of Claudius Hermogenianus, a most excellent and renowned man.
EDCS-04000321.summary: A dedication honouring the emperors' virtue and ensuring prosperity, recording the restoration of a fallen colossal statue, commissioned by a legate during the proconsulship of Claudius Hermogenianus, likely in the 4th century CE.

EDCS-04000325.translation: With Quintus Pomponius Marcellus, son, legate.
EDCS-04000325.summary: An inscription possibly referring to a monument set up in conjunction with Q. Pomponius Marcellus, serving as a legate.

EDCS-04000327.translation: Metha Innibalis' son set up this sacred offering to Juno Regina, gladly and deservedly.
EDCS-04000327.summary: A personal votive offering to Juno Regina by Metha, son of Innibalis, who dedicated it willingly and appropriately.

EDCS-04000328.summary: A brief religious dedication to the deified emperor Augustus.

EDCS-04000329.translation: Quintus Vetidius Iuvenalis, son of Papiria and Quintus Vetidius Felix, having promised a statue for the honour of his aedileship, beyond the highest honorary sum, placed it within a year of his office, having spent 5,000 sesterces. He dedicated the flame-offering of 6,000 sesterces from his own funds for the office of flamen, 4,000 sesterces for the decurionate, and 4,000 sesterces for the aedileship.
EDCS-04000329.summary: A detailed record of public expenditures by Quintus Vetidius Iuvenalis for his offices of flamen, decurion, and aedile, including the dedication of a statue and various monetary contributions, likely in the late Roman Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-04000332.translation: The city of Thubursicitana gladly paid its vow to Saturn.
EDCS-04000332.summary: The city of Thubursicitana fulfilling a votive offering to the god Saturn with willing heart, likely from Roman North Africa.

EDCS-04000333.translation: To the Municipality of Ulpius Traianus Augustus, Saturnus gladly paid his vow with a willing spirit.
EDCS-04000333.summary: A vow paid to the municipality of Ulpius Traianus Augustus, likely from the Roman era, honoring the god Saturn.

EDCS-04000334.translation: Sacred to the August Virtues. For the safety of our lords Emperors Diocletian and Maximian, the priests Castinianus the father and Festucius and Purpurius his sons established and dedicated a temple from the ground up with its sanctuary, which is at the rear; to this dedication, the deities from neighbouring cities and all the villages, along with their worshippers, gathered.
EDCS-04000334.summary: A temple dedicated to the August Virtues by priests for the safety of Emperors Diocletian and Maximian, likely in the late 3rd or early 4th century CE, detailing a large gathering for its dedication.

EDCS-04000335.translation: To Emperor Caesar Nerva Trajan Augustus Germanicus, son of the deified Nerva, father of the fatherland, chief priest, with tribunician power for the 3rd time, consul for the 2nd time, designated consul for the 3rd time.
EDCS-04000335.summary: An inscription honoring Emperor Trajan, likely a dedication or honorary titulature, dating to his third tribunician power and second consulship, circa 99-100 CE.

EDCS-04000338.translation: For the prosperous times, Atilius Theodotus, a most distinguished man, his legate, transferred a statue of Trajan from the ruins to the new forum, having removed it from the ruins, during the proconsulship of Claudius Hermogenianus, a most distinguished and most illustrious man.
EDCS-04000338.summary: An inscription recording the relocation of a statue of Emperor Trajan to a new forum during the proconsulship of Claudius Hermogenianus, likely in the late 4th century CE, commissioned by his legate Atilius Theodotus.

EDCS-04000349.translation: Of the greatest Parthicus, chief priest, with tribunician power, and of Julia Augusta, mother of the Augusti.
EDCS-04000349.summary: An fragmentary inscription referencing the titles of Emperor Trajan (Parthicus) and Empress Julia Domna, likely a dedication or honorary inscription from the early 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04000357.translation: To the deified Gordian, grandfather of our Augustus, Lucius Aelius [---]
EDCS-04000357.summary: A dedication to the deified Emperor Gordian, grandfather of the current emperor, by Lucius Aelius, likely from the mid-3rd century CE.

EDCS-04000359.translation: To Emperor Caesar Valerius Diocletianus Pius Felix Augustus.
EDCS-04000359.summary: An inscription honoring Emperor Diocletian, likely a dedication or honorary titulature, dating to his reign (284-305 CE).

EDCS-04000360.translation: To the eternal and most noble Caesar, Gaius Valerius Constantius the Invincible, the state of the colony of Thurbursicum Numidarum.
EDCS-04000360.summary: A dedication to Emperor Constantius I by the city council of Thurbursicum in Numidia, likely from the late 3rd or early 4th century CE.

EDCS-04000361.translation: In the most blessed times, Flavius Atilius Theodotus, a most distinguished man, his legate, provided a suitable site for the new forum founded by him, with the statue and inscriptions transferred from the ruins, during the proconsulship of Flavius Valerius Constantinus Maximus, during the veneration of him.
EDCS-04000361.summary: An inscription detailing the establishment of a new forum and the transfer of a statue and inscriptions during the proconsulship of Flavius Valerius Constantinus Maximus, likely in the 4th century CE, commissioned by his legate Flavius Atilius Theodotus.

EDCS-04000363.translation: In the most fortunate age of our lord Iulianus the victorious and triumphant Augustus, Atilius Theodotus, a most distinguished man, his legate, completed and dedicated the new forum which he had established, adorning it with columns and statues, during the proconsulship of Hermogenianus, a most illustrious man.
EDCS-04000363.summary: An inscription recording the completion and dedication of a new forum by Atilius Theodotus, legate to Emperor Julian the Apostate, during the proconsulship of Hermogenianus, likely in the 360s CE.

EDCS-04000364.summary: A very fragmentary inscription beginning with the imperial titulature of an emperor, its exact purpose and date are unknown.

EDCS-04000370.translation: Iulius Coelius Sparsus, consul, proconsul, pontifex, and Flavial sodalis, dedicated this with his wife Bassilla and his son Quintus Pomponius Rufus Marcellus, legate pro praetore.
EDCS-04000370.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a monument by a high-ranking official and his family.

EDCS-04000371.translation: To Septimius Severus, consul, proconsul of the province of Africa, legate of the Augusti pro praetore of Lower Germany, legate of the Augusti pro praetore of Lycia and Pamphylia, XV vir sacris faciundis, sodalis Hadrianalis, legate of the 16th Flavia Firma legion, curator of the road, praetor, tribune of the plebs, quaestor, commissioner of roads, the state of the municipium of Thubursicensium Numidarum, his most excellent patron, by decree of the decurions, with public funds.
EDCS-04000371.summary: This is a dedicatory inscription honoring Septimius Severus for his various important offices and his patronage of Thubursicensium Numidarum.

EDCS-04000373.translation: Mixing hardships with success, Clodius Hermogena, during his salubrious proconsulship, dedicates this citadel by the care of his legate Theodoti; I, Ianuarius, have taken care to compose these verses.
EDCS-04000373.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a citadel by Clodius Hermogena, a proconsul, with verses composed by Ianuarius.

EDCS-04000374.translation: For love of the foundation of the new forum, the council and people of Thubursicensium, adding distinction to the work and honoring its author with their own expenditure, retain Flavius Atilius Theodorus, most illustrious man, prefect of the treasury of the Roman people, legate of the province of Numidia, this most beloved monument with the most abundant generosity of Furius Reginus, perpetual priest.
EDCS-04000374.summary: This inscription records the people of Thubursicensium's appreciation for Flavius Atilius Theodorus, who was instrumental in building the new forum, with contributions from Furius Reginus.

EDCS-04000376.translation: To his predecessor, proconsul of the province of Africa, also judge of sacred cases...
EDCS-04000376.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription honoring a former proconsul of Africa and judge.

EDCS-04000377.translation: [... E]ali Emnitius, consular, for VI [... REMOT]
EDCS-04000377.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription mentioning a consular official named Emnitius.

EDCS-04000381.translation: The most sacred and flourishing council and people of Thubursicensium Numidarum, in their united affection, have bestowed upon Egnatuleius Navigius Egnatuleius, the perpetual priest, a good citizen, both for his universal faithful and diligent services to his country and citizens, and out of love for all past and present services, the honor of a statue, in perpetual gratitude, as he had long since secured this position for himself after the presentation of the tablet, and has happily proceeded to erect this statue.
EDCS-04000381.summary: This inscription records the erection of a statue to Egnatuleius Navigius Egnatuleius by the people of Thubursicensium Numidarum in recognition of his services as a perpetual priest.

EDCS-04000382.translation: To Larcia Laeta, wife of Aulus Larcius Macrinus, prince of the Numidian people and perpetual priest, to whom the council had decreed that a statue be publicly erected, but she, content with the honor, placed it with her own money and dedicated it.
EDCS-04000382.summary: This inscription records the erection of a statue to Larcia Laeta by herself, despite the council's decree, honoring her husband and her status.

EDCS-04000383.translation: To Sallustia, the noble perpetual priestess, the curiales, because of her merits...
EDCS-04000383.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription honoring Sallustia, a noble perpetual priestess, by the curiales.

EDCS-04000384.translation: Gaius Vasidius Pacatus, perpetual priest, a most accomplished man, curator of the state, erected this at his own expense.
EDCS-04000384.summary: This inscription records the erection of a monument by Gaius Vasidius Pacatus, a perpetual priest and curator, at his own expense.

EDCS-04000398.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Quintus Pescennius, likely a tombstone or memorial.

EDCS-04000413.translation: The place is occupied by the hot rooms of Anicivaga.
EDCS-04000413.summary: This inscription records a boundary or property notice, indicating that the hot rooms (caldarii) of Anicivaga are located here.

EDCS-04000417.translation: Herennius Martialis, a retired veteran of Legio XIII Gemina, made this mausoleum for himself.
EDCS-04000417.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording that Herennius Martialis, a veteran, built his own mausoleum.

EDCS-04000418.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Caius Salvidenius Victor, a pious soldier of the Praetorian Guard, lived 40 years and is buried here.
EDCS-04000418.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Caius Salvidenius Victor, a Praetorian Guard soldier, dating to his lifetime.

EDCS-04000419.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Marcus Iulius Gallicus, son of Ingenuus, former decurion and former duovir, a pious man, lived 65 years and is buried here.
EDCS-04000419.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Marcus Iulius Gallicus, detailing his public career as a former decurion and duovir, dating to his lifetime.

EDCS-04000420.translation: Lucius Iunius Papiria Florus, a pious duovir, lived 41 years and is buried here.
EDCS-04000420.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Iunius Papiria Florus, detailing his tenure as duovir, dating to his lifetime.

EDCS-04000421.translation: Marcus Laberius Largus, son of Lucius, of the Quirina tribe, a duovir, lived 48 years and is buried here.
EDCS-04000421.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Marcus Laberius Largus, detailing his tenure as duovir, dating to his lifetime.

EDCS-04000422.translation: Lucius Laberius Prudens, son of Marcus, of the Quirina tribe, aedile and duovir of the colony Iulia Sicca, lived 55 years and is buried here.
EDCS-04000422.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Laberius Prudens, detailing his magistracies as aedile and duovir in Colonia Iulia Sicca, dating to his lifetime.

EDCS-04000423.translation: Lucius Laberius Vibullus, son of Lucius, of the Quirina tribe, former aedile of the colony Iulia Cirta Nova, lived 34 years and is buried here.
EDCS-04000423.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Laberius Vibullus, detailing his former position as aedile in Colonia Iulia Cirta Nova, dating to his lifetime.

EDCS-04000424.translation: Lucius Seius Iuvenalis, son of Lucius, of the Quirina tribe, aedile and duovir of the municipium of Thubursicensis and duovir of the colony of Sicca, a pious man, lived 55 years and is buried here.
EDCS-04000424.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Seius Iuvenalis, detailing his civic career holding multiple duoviral and aedilician offices in Thubursicensis and Sicca, dating to his lifetime.

EDCS-04000425.translation: Petronia Frontilla, daughter of Candidus, wife of Mustiolus, dutiful, lived 29 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-04000425.summary: A funerary inscription recording the death of Petronia Frontilla, who died at age 29.

EDCS-04000426.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus Vetidius Felix, son of Mustius, dutiful, lived 62 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-04000426.summary: A funerary inscription recording the death of Quintus Vetidius Felix, who died at age 62.

EDCS-04000427.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulia Procula, wife of Marcus Vetidius Vetidianus, dutiful, lived 26 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-04000427.summary: A funerary inscription recording the death of Iulia Procula, who died at age 26.

EDCS-04000428.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Vetidius Honoratus, son of Quintus, dutiful, lived 26 years.
EDCS-04000428.summary: A funerary inscription recording the death of Lucius Vetidius Honoratus, who died at age 26.

EDCS-04000429.translation: Lucius Vetidius Iuvenalis, dutiful, lived 25 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-04000429.summary: A funerary inscription recording the death of Lucius Vetidius Iuvenalis, who died at age 25.

EDCS-04000430.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits of Iuventus. Gellia Honorata, daughter of Gellius Honoratus, established this small altar for herself and her husband who died from the beginning of their marriage, out of duty. Dutiful, she lived 78 years, 8 months, 29 days. She is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus Vetidius Iuvenalis, son of Quintus, having held all offices, father of three Roman knights, skilled in law in the forum, a good farmer, a father, lived 87 years, 8 months, 27 days. He is buried here.
EDCS-04000430.summary: A double funerary inscription for Gellia Honorata, who died at age 78, and her husband Quintus Vetidius Iuvenalis, who died at age 87 and was a Roman knight and respected citizen.

EDCS-04000431.text_edition: \n Heracli Dis Manibus sacrum Lucius Vetidius Maternus Vetidianus eques Romanus Quinti Vetidi Iuvenalis quinquennalici filius utraque lingua eruditus pius vixit annos XVIII menses IIII dies XXVIII permissu praesidis a Karthagine de studio relatis reliquiis hic situs est\n
EDCS-04000431.translation: Dedicated to the spirits of the departed. Lucius Vetidius Maternus Vetidianus, a Roman knight and son of Quintus Vetidius Iuvenalis, quinquennalis, educated in both languages, devoted and pious, lived 18 years, 4 months, and 28 days. With permission of the governor from Carthage, from the study with the brought-back relics, he is buried here.
EDCS-04000431.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lucius Vetidius Maternus Vetidianus, a Roman knight, detailing his age and education, and noting his burial with relics and permission from a governor, likely from Roman North Africa.

EDCS-04000432.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits of Iuventus. Quintus Vetidius Honoratianus, Roman knight, son of Quintus Vetidius Iuvenalis, who held the quinquennial office, learned in both languages, dutiful, lived 21 years, 7 months. He is buried here.
EDCS-04000432.summary: A funerary inscription recording the death of Quintus Vetidius Honoratianus, a Roman knight, who died at age 21.

EDCS-04000433.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus Gellius Honoratus, son of Gellius Massus, erected this for himself during his lifetime, dutiful, lived 59 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-04000433.summary: A funerary inscription recording the death of Quintus Gellius Honoratus, who died at age 59 and erected his own tomb.

EDCS-04000434.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Vetidia Mustacia, daughter of Mustiolus, wife of Gellius Honoratus, dutiful, lived 31 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-04000434.summary: A funerary inscription recording the death of Vetidia Mustacia, who died at age 31.

EDCS-04000436.translation: Laeta, daughter of Rufus, priestess of the temple of Liber Pater, dutiful, lived 61 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-04000436.summary: A funerary inscription recording the death of Laeta, priestess of Liber Pater, who died at age 61.

EDCS-04000437.translation: Matrona, daughter of Pulcher, priestess of the Earth, lived piously for 83 years.
EDCS-04000437.summary: A tombstone recording the life of Matrona, a priestess of Tellus, who lived to the age of 83.

EDCS-04000438.translation: Rufina, daughter of Rufinus Crassus, priestess of the Earth, is placed here; she lived piously for 85 years.
EDCS-04000438.summary: A tombstone commemorating Rufina, priestess of Tellus and daughter of Rufinus Crassus, who lived to 85.

EDCS-04000439.translation: Publius Tullius Prudens, son of Publius, of the Quirina tribe, priest of Pluto, lived piously for 67 years; he is placed here.
EDCS-04000439.summary: A tombstone for Publius Tullius Prudens, a priest of Pluto, who lived to 67.

EDCS-04000440.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Avianius Marcellus, son of Lucius, of the Quirina tribe, a citizen of Hipponium, lived piously for 83 years; he is placed here.
EDCS-04000440.summary: A tombstone dedicated to the spirits of the departed for Lucius Avianius Marcellus, a citizen of Hipponium, who lived to 83.

EDCS-04000441.translation: Iulia Arbuscula, daughter of Caius, a Syrian woman, lived piously for 80 years; she is placed here.
EDCS-04000441.summary: A tombstone for Iulia Arbuscula, daughter of Caius, who lived to 80.

EDCS-04000442.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Adiutor, son of Tiberius, lived piously for 32 years. CATVI
EDCS-04000442.summary: A tombstone dedicated to the departed spirits for Adiutor, son of Tiberius, who lived to 32.

EDCS-04000443.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus Aedinius Festus, of the Papiria tribe, lived piously for 65 years; he is placed here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Iunia Bona placed this for herself while alive and for her husband.
EDCS-04000443.summary: A tombstone for Quintus Aedinius Festus, who lived to 65, and a separate dedication by Iunia Bona for herself and her husband.

EDCS-04000444.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Aemilius Baricis, son of Baricis, lived for 100 years; he is placed here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Iunia Lucceia lived for 80 years.
EDCS-04000444.summary: Two tombstone fragments, one for Aemilius Baricis who lived to 100, and another for Iunia Lucceia who lived to 80.

EDCS-04000445.translation: Gellia Saturnina, daughter of Quintus, wife of Caius Aemilius Proculus, lived piously for 55 years; she is placed here.
EDCS-04000445.summary: A tombstone for Gellia Saturnina, daughter of Quintus and wife of Caius Aemilius Proculus, who lived to 55.

EDCS-04000446.translation: Aemilia Saturnina, daughter of Marcus Aemilius Rufus, lived piously for 14 years; she is placed here.
