EDCS-04000446.summary: A tombstone for Aemilia Saturnina, daughter of Marcus Aemilius Rufus, who lived to 14.

EDCS-04000447.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Gaius Aemilius, son of Caius.
EDCS-04000447.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the departed by Gaius Aemilius.

EDCS-04000448.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Publius Aemilius.
EDCS-04000448.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the departed by Publius Aemilius.

EDCS-04000449.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Quintus Ancharius Numidicus, dutiful, lived 60 years, is buried here. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Apronia Novella, dutiful, lived 45 years, is buried here.
EDCS-04000449.summary: This is a double funerary inscription recording the burials of Quintus Ancharius Numidicus and Apronia Novella, noting their ages.

EDCS-04000450.translation: Gaius Antonius Felix, dutiful, lived 80 years, is buried here.
EDCS-04000450.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the burial of Gaius Antonius Felix and his age.

EDCS-04000451.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Antonia Honorata, wife of Petronicus Datus, dutiful, lived 32 years, is buried here.
EDCS-04000451.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Antonia Honorata, wife of Petronicus Datus, noting her age.

EDCS-04000453.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Titus Aprosius Datus, dutiful, lived...
EDCS-04000453.summary: This is an incomplete funerary inscription for Titus Aprosius Datus, recording his name and that he was dutiful.

EDCS-04000454.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Marcus Aquilius Valens, father of Aquilia Gemina.
EDCS-04000454.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicating a monument to the departed, by Marcus Aquilius Valens for his daughter Aquilia Gemina.

EDCS-04000455.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Marcus Arellius Rufinus, dutiful, lived 60 years, is buried here.
EDCS-04000455.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the burial of Marcus Arellius Rufinus and his age.

EDCS-04000456.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Arrius Felix, son of Ianuarius, set this up for himself during his lifetime, and for his wife. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Namgidde, daughter of Sallucus.
EDCS-04000456.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Arrius Felix for himself and his wife, and also mentions Namgidde, daughter of Sallucus.

EDCS-04000458.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Gaius Avianius Marcellinus, dutiful, lived 19 years.
EDCS-04000458.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Gaius Avianius Marcellinus, noting his age and dutiful character.

EDCS-04000459.translation: Lucius Avillius Celer, [curator of public works?].
EDCS-04000459.summary: This is an incomplete inscription, possibly a tombstone, naming Lucius Avillius Celer.

EDCS-04000460.translation: Vibia Quieta, devoted daughter of Lucius, wife of Lucius Avillius Celer, lived 65 years, is buried here. May your bones rest well, may the earth lie lightly upon you.
EDCS-04000460.summary: This funerary epitaph records the death of Vibia Quieta, wife of Lucius Avillius Celer, and includes standard wishes for the deceased.

EDCS-04000461.translation: Gaius Avillius Musulanus, devoted son of Lucius, lived 15 years, is buried here. May your bones rest well, may the earth lie lightly upon you.
EDCS-04000461.summary: This funerary epitaph records the death of Gaius Avillius Musulanus, son of Lucius Avillius Celer, and includes standard wishes for the deceased.

EDCS-04000462.translation: Avillia Lucustina, devoted daughter of Lucius Avillius Celer, lived 30 years, is buried here.
EDCS-04000462.summary: This funerary epitaph records the death of Avillia Lucustina, daughter of Lucius Avillius Celer.

EDCS-04000463.translation: Gaius Aurelius Paetus, devoted, lived 85 years.
EDCS-04000463.summary: This is a brief funerary inscription recording the age of Gaius Aurelius Paetus.

EDCS-04000464.translation: Lucius Aurelius, son of Lucius, of the tribe Quirina.
EDCS-04000464.summary: This is an incomplete inscription, possibly naming Lucius Aurelius, son of Lucius, and indicating his tribal affiliation.

EDCS-04000465.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Aurelia Victoria, devoted, lived 30 years, is buried here.
EDCS-04000465.summary: This funerary epitaph is dedicated to the underworld spirits and records the death of Aurelia Victoria.

EDCS-04000466.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Barisal, son of Ianuarius, lived 80 years.
EDCS-04000466.summary: This funerary epitaph is dedicated to the underworld spirits and records the death of Barisal.

EDCS-04000467.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Basabulus, lived 81 years. Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Aemilia Natalis, lived 91 years.
EDCS-04000467.summary: This funerary epitaph is dedicated to the underworld spirits and records the deaths of Basabulus and Aemilia Natalis.

EDCS-04000468.translation: Berecbal, daughter of Secundus, wife of Gallus, set this up herself while alive, aged 85 years.
EDCS-04000468.summary: This funerary inscription records that Berecbal, wife of Gallus, set up her own tombstone while alive.

EDCS-04000469.translation: Devoted Bodin, slave of Caius Vesidius Paetus, lived 30 years; he lies here.
EDCS-04000469.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a slave named Bodin, who lived 30 years.

EDCS-04000470.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Bullatia Hilara, devoted daughter of Bullatius Felix, lived 90 years.
EDCS-04000470.summary: This funerary inscription honors Bullatia Hilara, daughter of Bullatius Felix, who lived 90 years.

EDCS-04000471.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. C. Palma lived 80 years; he lies here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Valeria Mutthunim lived 45 years.
EDCS-04000471.summary: This inscription contains two funerary notices, one for C. Palma (80 years) and another for Valeria Mutthunim (45 years).

EDCS-04000472.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus C. B. Sacred to the departed spirits. Caius Numidica.
EDCS-04000472.summary: This inscription consists of two incomplete funerary dedications to the departed spirits.

EDCS-04000473.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Eucharia the devoted lived 32 years. Sacred to the departed spirits. C. Victor the devoted lived 45 years. Sacred to the departed spirits. C. Optatus the devoted lived 70 years.
EDCS-04000473.summary: This inscription records the lives of three individuals: Eucharia (32 years), C. Victor (45 years), and C. Optatus (70 years), all dedicated to the departed spirits.

EDCS-04000475.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulia Antonilla, daughter of Marcus Iulius Quirina. Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Caecilius Barbarus erected this monument for himself and his wife, Quirina, during his lifetime; he was devoted, lived 65 years; he lies here.
EDCS-04000475.summary: This inscription contains two funerary dedications; the second is for Lucius Caecilius Barbarus, who set up a monument for himself and his wife Quirina and lived 65 years.

EDCS-04000476.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Caecilius Martinus the devoted lived 61 years; he lies here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcus A. M. the devoted lived 75 years.
EDCS-04000476.summary: This inscription has two funerary notices for Caecilius Martinus (61 years) and Marcus A. M. (75 years), both honored as devoted.

EDCS-04000477.translation: Caius Caecilius Saturninus, devoted freedman of Caius Caecilius Fidelis, lived 41 years; he lies here.
EDCS-04000477.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Caius Caecilius Saturninus, freedman of Caius Caecilius Fidelis, who lived 41 years.

EDCS-04000695.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Priscianus, dutiful, lived 18 years; he rests here.
EDCS-04000695.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the death of Priscianus at the age of 18.

EDCS-04000696.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Proculeia Honorata, daughter of Caius Proculeius Honoratus, dutiful wife of Quintus Pescennius Avitus, lived 53 years; she rests here.
EDCS-04000696.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the death of Proculeia Honorata, daughter of Caius Proculeius Honoratus and wife of Quintus Pescennius Avitus.

EDCS-04000697.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Pusinnica, daughter of Iuvenalis, dutiful, lived 90 years; she rests here.
EDCS-04000697.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the death of Pusinnica, daughter of Iuvenalis, at the age of 90.

EDCS-04000698.translation: Q. Beregbal, dutiful, lived 61 years; she rests here.
EDCS-04000698.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the death of Q. Beregbal at the age of 61.

EDCS-04000699.translation: Quartilla, wife of Opacus, dutiful, lived...
EDCS-04000699.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the death of Quartilla, wife of Opacus, with her age incomplete.

EDCS-04000700.translation: Rogatus, dutiful, lived 71 years; he rests here.
EDCS-04000700.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the death of Rogatus at the age of 71.

EDCS-04000701.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Rogatus, son of Baricbalis, dutiful, lived 30 years; he rests here.
EDCS-04000701.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the death of Rogatus, son of Baricbalis, at the age of 30.

EDCS-04000702.translation: Rogata, daughter of Fuscus, dutiful, lived 23 years; she rests here.
EDCS-04000702.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the death of Rogata, daughter of Fuscus, at the age of 23.

EDCS-04000703.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Rogatina, dutiful, lived 1 year.
EDCS-04000703.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the death of Rogatina at the age of 1.

EDCS-04000704.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. SONLSSA Romana, lived 55 years. Sacred to the Divine Spirits.
EDCS-04000704.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the death of SONLSSA Romana at the age of 55.

EDCS-04000705.summary: A funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Rubellia Blanda.

EDCS-04000707.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Pious Rufilla, daughter of Rogatus, lived 75 years.
EDCS-04000707.summary: A funerary inscription to the departed spirits, recording the lifespan of Rufilla.

EDCS-04000708.translation: Rufilla, daughter of Pudentis, lived 50 years and is buried here.
EDCS-04000708.summary: A funerary inscription recording the lifespan and burial place of Rufilla.

EDCS-04000709.translation: Pious Salus, son of Lukanius, lived 35 years and is placed here.
EDCS-04000709.summary: A funerary inscription recording the lifespan and burial place of Salus.

EDCS-04000710.translation: Pious Saturius, son of Nugacius, lived 110 years and is placed here.
EDCS-04000710.summary: A funerary inscription recording the lifespan and burial place of Saturius.

EDCS-04000711.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Pious Saturninus, son of Fronto, lived 25 years.
EDCS-04000711.summary: A funerary inscription to the departed spirits, recording the lifespan of Saturninus.

EDCS-04000713.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Pious Secunda, daughter of Rogatus, lived 41 years and is placed here.
EDCS-04000713.summary: A funerary inscription to the departed spirits, recording the lifespan and burial place of Secunda.

EDCS-04000714.translation: Pious Seia Pulchra, daughter of Lucius, lived 63 years and is placed here.
EDCS-04000714.summary: A funerary inscription recording the lifespan and burial place of Seia Pulchra.

EDCS-04000715.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Pious Servilius Fortunatus lived 30 years and is placed here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Pious Servilius Crementius lived 22 years.
EDCS-04000715.summary: A funerary inscription recording the lifespans and burial of Servilius Fortunatus and Servilius Crementius.

EDCS-04000716.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Pious Servilia Hospita lived 81 years. Pious Memmius Rurentius lived 21 years. Sacred to the departed spirits. Pious Memmius Dunamius lived 21 years and is placed here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Pious Aelia Donata lived 35 years and is placed here.
EDCS-04000716.summary: A funerary inscription recording the lifespans and burial of Servilia Hospita, Memmius Rurentius, Memmius Dunamius, and Aelia Donata.

EDCS-04000717.translation: Sacred to the departed gods. Sextilia Chelido, dutiful, lived 35 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-04000717.summary: A funerary inscription recording the life and burial of Sextilia Chelido.

EDCS-04000718.translation: Sacred to the departed gods. Sidina, dutiful wife of Aevarius, lived 35 years.
EDCS-04000718.summary: A funerary inscription recording the life of Sidina, wife of Aevarius.

EDCS-04000719.translation: Publius Silius Peregrinus, dutiful, lived 65 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-04000719.summary: A funerary inscription recording the life and burial of Publius Silius Peregrinus.

EDCS-04000720.translation: Sacred to the departed gods. Caius Silius Saturninus, son of Silius Saturninus, dutiful, lived 30 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-04000720.summary: A funerary inscription recording the life and burial of Caius Silius Saturninus, son of Silius Saturninus.

EDCS-04000721.translation: Spica, son of Barecbalus, dutiful, lived 80 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-04000721.summary: A funerary inscription recording the life and burial of Spica, son of Barecbalus.

EDCS-04000722.translation: Of Marcus Tadius Priscus, dutiful, lived 65 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-04000722.summary: A funerary inscription recording the life and burial of Marcus Tadius Priscus.

EDCS-04000723.translation: ....ia, daughter of Lucius, wife of CAL TERTIUS, dutiful, lived 21 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-04000723.summary: A funerary inscription recording the life and burial of a woman identified as daughter of Lucius and wife of CAL TERTIUS.

EDCS-04000724.translation: Sacred to the departed gods. Aulus TETR Honoratus, son of Aulus Honoratus, dutiful, lived 20 years.
EDCS-04000724.summary: A funerary inscription recording the life of Aulus TETR Honoratus, son of Aulus Honoratus.

EDCS-04000725.translation: Therefnat, daughter of Mitatis, wife of Quirinus Thililis, dutiful, lived 81 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-04000725.summary: A funerary inscription recording the life and burial of Therefnat, daughter of Mitatis and wife of Quirinus Thililis.

EDCS-04000727.translation: Publius Valerius Clemens, dutiful, lived 60 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-04000727.summary: A funerary inscription recording the life and burial of Publius Valerius Clemens.

EDCS-04000728.translation: Publius Valerius Fructus placed this in his own lifetime, pious, lived 97 years.
EDCS-04000728.summary: A tombstone erected by Publius Valerius Fructus for himself.

EDCS-04000729.translation: Valeria Helena, wife of Iulius Flaminalis, pious, lived 35 years, is buried here.
EDCS-04000729.summary: A tombstone for Valeria Helena, wife of Iulius Flaminalis.

EDCS-04000730.translation: Varilla, daughter of Vari, wife of Methatis, lived 45 years.
EDCS-04000730.summary: A tombstone for Varilla, daughter of Vari and wife of Methatis.

EDCS-04000731.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Veneria, wife of Silenus, pious, lived 31 years.
EDCS-04000731.summary: A tombstone dedicated to the departed spirits for Veneria, wife of Silenus.

EDCS-04000733.translation: Laetina, daughter of Veturius Bellicus, wife of Bellicus Rufus, pious, lived 24 years, is buried here.
EDCS-04000733.summary: A tombstone for Laetina, daughter of Veturius Bellicus and wife of Bellicus Rufus.

EDCS-04000734.translation: Lived 80 years and 5 months, is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Vibia, pious, lived 22 years.
EDCS-04000734.summary: A tombstone for Vibia, stating her lifespan and burial, dedicated to the departed spirits.

EDCS-04000735.translation: Vibia Secunda, daughter of Lucius Vibius, lived 30 years, is buried here.
EDCS-04000735.summary: A tombstone for Vibia Secunda, daughter of Lucius Vibius.

EDCS-04000736.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. The wife of Victor, pious, lived 81 years, is buried here.
EDCS-04000736.summary: A tombstone for the wife of Victor, dedicated to the departed spirits.

EDCS-04000737.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Vincentia, pious, wife of Felix, good, lived 30 years, is buried here.
EDCS-04000737.summary: A tombstone for Vincentia, wife of Felix, dedicated to the departed spirits.

EDCS-04000738.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Vinicius Saturninus, son of Lucius, of the Papiria tribe, pious, lived 66 years, is buried here. The Lord feeds me, happily.
EDCS-04000738.summary: A tombstone for Lucius Vinicius Saturninus, son of Lucius, of the Papiria tribe, which includes a Christian invocation.

EDCS-04000739.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Salvia, devout, lived 45 years. Marcus Ulpius Eufrosynus the younger made this for his most exceptional wife, who rests here. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Ulpia Eufrosyna, devout, lived 12 years and 5 months. Marcus Ulpius Eufrosynus made this for his sweetest daughter, who rests here.
EDCS-04000739.summary: This inscription records the funerary epitaphs for a wife and daughter, made by Marcus Ulpius Eufrosynus, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04000741.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Aulus Marpius lived 90 years. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Urbana, devout, lived 71 years.
EDCS-04000741.summary: This inscription provides the ages at death for two individuals, Aulus Marpius and Urbana, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04000742.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Urbana, daughter of Victor, devout, lived 25 years, who rests here.
EDCS-04000742.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Urbana, daughter of Victor, who died at the age of 25.

EDCS-04000743.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Zabullim, devout, lived 50 years. Hordionias. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Nampame, devout, lived 30 years. Dativa lived...
EDCS-04000743.summary: This inscription lists the ages at death for several individuals, Zabullim, Nampame, and Dativa, likely representing funerary markers.

EDCS-04000744.translation: He lived 95 years, who rests here.
EDCS-04000744.summary: This is a brief funerary epitaph stating that an individual lived for 95 years and is buried here.

EDCS-04000745.translation: He rests here, 90 years, he rests here.
EDCS-04000745.summary: This is a very brief funerary marker indicating that someone who lived 90 years is buried here.

EDCS-04000746.translation: Wife, devout, lived 45 years, who rests here. 80 years, he rests here.
EDCS-04000746.summary: This inscription appears to be a composite funerary marker, recording a wife who lived 45 years and another individual who lived 80 years.

EDCS-04000747.translation: Sns, devout, lived 70 years, who rests here.
EDCS-04000747.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the life of an individual named Sns who lived 70 years.

EDCS-04000748.translation: ...us lived 65 years, who rests here. May the earth lie lightly upon you.
EDCS-04000748.summary: This funerary inscription records an individual identified by the name fragment '...us' who lived 65 years and includes a common epitaph wishing peace.

EDCS-04000750.translation: To the spirits of the departed. A IV V NOV lived 50 years, who rests here. May your bones rest well.
EDCS-04000750.summary: This funerary inscription records an individual named A IV V NOV who lived 50 years and includes a wish for their bones to rest well.

EDCS-04000751.translation: He lived 45 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-04000751.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the age and burial place of an individual, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04000752.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording an exceptionally long lifespan, likely an exaggeration or error in the inscription, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04000754.translation: Ella Sagsa, a devoted wife, lived 30 years.
EDCS-04000754.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the name, marital status, devotion, and lifespan of Ella Sagsa, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04000755.translation: Opisca Chie, devoted, lived 30 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-04000755.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the name, devotion, lifespan, and burial place of Opisca Chie, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04000759.translation: Why do you tear at those whom you see growing? You yourself are your own tormentor; you carry your own wounds.
EDCS-04000759.summary: This is a moralizing distich, possibly inscribed on a tomb, offering philosophical reflection on envy and self-inflicted suffering, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04000760.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the departed. Calpurnia Sedata Asprenatiana, granddaughter of Calpurnius Geminius, daughter of the priest Calpurnius Sedatus and Vasidia Rufilla, devout, lived 32 years and 3 months. Caius Annius L., her husband, made this monument for his most cherished and faithful wife. She is buried here.
EDCS-04000760.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Calpurnia Sedata Asprenatiana, detailing her lineage, devotion, lifespan, and the monument erected by her husband, Caius Annius L., likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04000761.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the departed. Mustiolus, son of Zabullus, devoted, lived 61 years. Sacred to the Spirits of the departed. Iulia Privata, wife of Mustiolus, devoted, lived 71 years.
EDCS-04000761.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lives of two individuals, Mustiolus and his wife Iulia Privata, including their parentage, devotion, and lifespans, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04000762.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the departed. Onesimus, freedman, devoted, lived 55 years.
EDCS-04000762.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Onesimus, a freedman, recording his devotion and lifespan, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04000763.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the departed. Gaius Postumius Rufinus Honoratianus, devoted, lived...
EDCS-04000763.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Gaius Postumius Rufinus Honoratianus, mentioning his devotion and the beginning of his lifespan, but the inscription is incomplete, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04000764.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the departed. Victor Vctor. Sacred to the Spirits of the departed. Faustina, devoted, lived.
EDCS-04000764.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary epitaph possibly mentioning two individuals, Victor and Faustina, noting Faustina's devotion and the beginning of her lifespan, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04000765.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Art lived 60 years. Satu, 101.
EDCS-04000765.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the ages of two individuals, Art and Satu, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04000766.translation: To the son of Antoninus Hadrianus Caesar Augustus Pius, father of the fatherland, Iulius Urbanus, perpetual priest, placed and dedicated this, with added funds, for that same honor.
EDCS-04000766.summary: This is a dedication to Emperor Antoninus Pius by Iulius Urbanus, who held the office of perpetual priest, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04000767.translation: ilius Mar, priest of Jupiter, lived 60 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-04000767.summary: This is a funerary inscription for ilius Mar, a priest of Jupiter, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04000769.translation: Fortunata Publia, dutiful, lived 75 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-04000769.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Fortunata Publia, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04000770.translation: Fronto, son of Mutthunis, dutiful, lived 85 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-04000770.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Fronto, son of Mutthunis, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04000771.translation: Ianuarius, son of Nota, dutiful, lived 73 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-04000771.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Ianuarius, son of Nota, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04000772.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Marcus Iulius Felix Aemilianus, son of Marcus Iulius Marci, dutiful, lived 39 years, 8 months, and 19 days. He is buried here.
EDCS-04000772.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Marcus Iulius Felix Aemilianus, providing his full name, parentage, and precise age at death, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04000773.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Iulia Victoria, dutiful.
EDCS-04000773.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Iulia Victoria, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04000774.translation: Lucius Iunius, dutiful, lived 5 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-04000774.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Iunius, likely a child, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04000775.translation: Marcus, son of Zabonis, dutiful, lived 15 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-04000775.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Marcus, son of Zabonis, likely a youth, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04000776.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Marisa T.
EDCS-04000776.summary: A funerary dedication to the Manes by Marisa T.

EDCS-04000777.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. E. Maximillae the dutiful, who lived 20 years, is buried here. Marius Honoratus [dedicated this].
EDCS-04000777.summary: A funerary dedication by Marius Honoratus to E. Maximillae, who lived 20 years.

EDCS-04000778.translation: Marcus Munatius, son of Lucius, of the Quirina tribe, Rufinus, who lived 30 years, is buried here.
EDCS-04000778.summary: A funerary epitaph for Marcus Munatius Rufinus, who lived 30 years.

EDCS-04000780.translation: Valerius Fortunatus the dutiful, who lived 107 years, is buried here.
EDCS-04000780.summary: A funerary epitaph for Valerius Fortunatus, who lived 107 years.

EDCS-04000781.translation: [Someone] the dutiful, who lived 65 years, is buried here. Fortunatus the dutiful, who lived 21 years, is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Luria Fortunata the dutiful, who lived 65 years, is buried here.
EDCS-04000781.summary: A funerary inscription likely from a family tomb, recording the burials and ages of at least three individuals, including Luria Fortunata.

EDCS-04000782.translation: Sacred to Mercury and Vesta. Flavi Honorius and Veneria [dedicated this].
EDCS-04000782.summary: A religious dedication to Mercury and Vesta by Flavi Honorius and Veneria.

EDCS-04000783.translation: Sacred to Neptune Augustus. Titus Flavius Rogatianus fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-04000783.summary: A votive inscription to Neptune Augustus by Titus Flavius Rogatianus.

EDCS-04000786.translation: CAI Messallina, wife of Claudius, [aged] C [? years].
EDCS-04000786.summary: A fragmentary funerary inscription mentioning CAI Messallina, possibly the wife of a Claudius.

EDCS-04000792.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Caius Iulius Dius the dutiful, who lived 11 years, is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Caius Iulius Sabinus the younger, the dutiful, who lived 16 years, is buried here.
EDCS-04000792.summary: A funerary inscription recording the burials of two young boys, Caius Iulius Dius and Caius Iulius Sabinus iunior.

EDCS-04000793.summary: A fragmentary funerary epitaph for Modia Secunda, who lived 10 years.

EDCS-04000794.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Scribonia Celsa, pious daughter of Marcus, lived 75 years; she lies here.
EDCS-04000794.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death and burial of Scribonia Celsa.

EDCS-04000798.translation: Iulia Victoria, a basket-maker, made and dedicated a statue of the goddess Carea Maurusia Augusta at her own expense.
EDCS-04000798.summary: A dedication of a statue to the goddess Carea Maurusia by Iulia Victoria, a basket-maker.

EDCS-04000799.translation: Sacred to Augusta Chalimaca. Virtius Florentius, together with his family, willingly fulfilled his vow and dedicated it.
EDCS-04000799.summary: A votive dedication to Augusta Chalimaca by Virtius Florentius and his family.

EDCS-04000801.translation: Sacred to Damio Augustus. Caius Iulius Victor, a basket-maker from Thugga, made it with his own money and dedicated it.
EDCS-04000801.summary: A dedication of a monument to Damio Augustus by Caius Iulius Victor, a basket-maker from Thugga.

EDCS-04000803.translation: To Fortune of the Augusti, by decree of the decurions, with public funds.
EDCS-04000803.summary: A dedication to Fortune of the Augusti, funded by public money and decreed by local councillors.

EDCS-04000805.summary: A simple dedication to Fortune Augusta.

EDCS-04000806.translation: To the Fruit-Bearing Augustus, for the safety of the Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus Arabicus Adiabenicus, pontifex maximus, holder of tribunician power, consul II, emperor, father of the fatherland.
EDCS-04000806.summary: A dedication to the 'Fruit-Bearing Augustus' (likely an imperial cult title) for the safety of Emperor Septimius Severus.

EDCS-04000811.translation: Sacred to Hercules Augustus, for the safety of the Emperors Caesar Publius Licinius Valerianus Pius Felix Augustus and Publius Licinius Gallienus Augustus and Publius Licinius Cornelius Valerianus Nobilissimus Caesar Augustus and Cornelia Salonina Augusta and the entire divine family. Festus made it sacred with his own money and dedicated it.
EDCS-04000811.summary: A dedication to Hercules Augustus for the safety of the imperial family, made by Festus.

EDCS-04000812.translation: To the most blessed age of our lords Diocletian and Maximian Augusti, the temple of the god Hercules with its porticoes, which had fallen into ruin from excessive age and had been abandoned for many years, was dedicated by the order of Titus Claudius Aurelius Aristobulus, proconsul, through the insistence of Caius Macrinius Sossianus, vir consularis, legate of Numidia, who was also the proconsul, together with the same legate.
EDCS-04000812.summary: The rededication of a dilapidated temple of Hercules and its porticoes during the reign of Diocletian and Maximian, ordered by the proconsul Aristobulus and carried out by the legate Sossianus.

EDCS-04000813.translation: Sacred to Hercules Augustus. Marcus Antonius Martialis Valerianus, perpetual flamen.
EDCS-04000813.summary: A dedication to Hercules Augustus by Marcus Antonius Martialis Valerianus, a perpetual flamen.

EDCS-04000814.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the goddess Hygieia Augusta.

EDCS-04000816.translation: Sacred to the god Liber. Quintus Calpurnius Donatus, aedile and twice duovir, son of the former priest Laetus, made the market building from its foundation and the paving at his own expense, and dedicated it with his wife Laeta and Calpurnia Laeta Matrona and I.
EDCS-04000816.summary: This inscription records the construction and dedication of a market building by Quintus Calpurnius Donatus, who held several local magistracies, likely in the late 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04000817.translation: Sacred to the god Liber Pater Augustus. Marcus Flavius M nus [---] his descendant.
EDCS-04000817.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Liber Pater Augustus by Marcus Flavius M nus, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-04000820.translation: Sacred to Mars Augustus. Marcus Antonius Martialis Valerinus, quaestor, aedile, perpetual priest, and his wife Viria Pomponilla, with their children, joyfully dedicated the entrance hall with all its furnishings, and also the wall, which had fallen into disrepair through age, after restoring it.
EDCS-04000820.summary: This inscription records the restoration of an entrance hall and a wall by Marcus Antonius Martialis Valerinus, a prominent local official, and his wife Viria Pomponilla, likely in the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-04000824.translation: Sacred to Mercury Augustus. For the safety of the Emperors Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus, father of the fatherland, father of victories, Arabicus, Adiabenicus, Maximus, Pontifex Maximus, Consul for the third time, and Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus Pius, Pontifex, Prince of Youth. T. Vitruvius Victor paid his vow willingly.
EDCS-04000824.summary: This inscription records a vow paid by T. Vitruvius Victor to Mercury Augustus for the safety of Emperors Septimius Severus and Caracalla, likely around 198-202 CE.

EDCS-04000825.translation: Sacred to Mercury Augustus. Titus Flavius Martialis paid his vow and also dedicated it willingly.
EDCS-04000825.summary: This inscription is a dedication and vow payment to Mercury Augustus by Titus Flavius Martialis, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-04000826.translation: To Mercury Augustus. Lucius Pescennius Castus paid his vow.
EDCS-04000826.summary: This is a record of a vow paid to Mercury Augustus by Lucius Pescennius Castus, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-04000827.translation: Sacred to Mercury Augustus. Claudius Possidentius and his sonrius, priests of Virtue and also of Mercury, made this at their own expense. With good fortune.
EDCS-04000827.summary: This inscription records the joint construction by two priests of Mercury (and Virtue) of something dedicated to Mercury Augustus, likely in the Imperial period.

EDCS-04000828.translation: Sacred to Mercury Augustus. Gaius Gessius Felix.
EDCS-04000828.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Mercury Augustus by Gaius Gessius Felix, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-04000829.translation: Under Emperor Nerva Caesar Augustus [and] [M. XXX?] Augustus. Sacred. [Lucius Gra]nius Honoratus, son of [Lucius], [from the tribe] Quirina, [XXX]anus, twice duumvir, [XXX]em [XXX]MVT had it made.
EDCS-04000829.summary: A sacred dedication under Emperors Nerva and a second Augustus, recording the name of Lucius Granius Honoratus who served as a duumvir, likely from the late 1st century CE.

EDCS-04000830.translation: Sacred to Pluto Augustus. Aemilius Victorianus, priest.
EDCS-04000830.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Pluto Augustus by the priest Aemilius Victorianus, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-04000831.translation: To the August Pluto, Gaius Julius Felix Probianus, priest.
EDCS-04000831.summary: This inscription records a dedication to the god Pluto by the priest Gaius Julius Felix Probianus.

EDCS-04000832.summary: This inscription records a dedication to the goddess Venus.

EDCS-04000834.translation: Sacred to the Holy Goddess Venus Erucina Augusta. Lucius Velleius Castus and Gaius Julius Surus, priests, built and dedicated the cella at their own expense, from a vision.
EDCS-04000834.summary: This inscription records the construction and dedication of a temple cella to Venus Erucina by the priests Lucius Velleius Castus and Gaius Julius Surus.

EDCS-04000835.translation: Names of the cistophori (bearers of the sacred basket) of the goddess Virtus: two, right and left, and the steps, they made from their own resources. Victor, perpetual flamen, priest; S. Madaurius, priest; Primianus, priest; Ius Sabinus, priest; Vibius Servilius, priest; Quintus Domitius Numidius; Quintus Cluvius Crementius; Terentia Bonifatia, basket-bearer; Titus Flavius Natalis; Caius Valerius Sabinus; Lucius Avianus Felix; Caius Flavius Domitius; Titus Flavius Maximus; Quintus Agrius Vitalis. Names of the basket-bearers: Antonia Matrona; Manilia Honorata; Iulia Lucilla.
EDCS-04000835.summary: This inscription lists the names of officials, including priests and basket-bearers, associated with the cult of the goddess Virtus.

EDCS-04000836.translation: Sacred to the August [Jupiter?]. S. Festus.
EDCS-04000836.summary: This inscription records a dedication to an August deity, possibly Jupiter, by S. Festus.

EDCS-04000838.summary: This inscription records a dedication to an August deity named Campanus, with an unclear initial P.

EDCS-04000840.translation: To the August god Saturn. Aemilius Venerius paid a vow and gave this gift.
EDCS-04000840.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to the god Saturn by Aemilius Venerius.

EDCS-04000841.summary: This inscription records a vow made by Titus Evasius.

EDCS-04000843.summary: This inscription records the voluntary restoration of something by Marcus Vettius Innocens.

EDCS-04000845.summary: This inscription records the name of Emperor Nerva, likely indicating an imperial dedication or connection.

EDCS-04000846.summary: This inscription records the name of Emperor Nerva, likely part of a larger inscription or dedication.

EDCS-04000853.translation: For the safety of the Emperors, Caesars Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus, father of the fatherland, Arabicus Adiabenicus Parthicus Maximus, Pontifex Maximus, and Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus Pius Felix, Pontifex Maximus, Prince of Youth, and Publius Septimius Geta Nobilissimus Caesar Augustus, Prince of Youth, and Julia Augusta, mother of the Augusti, mother of the camps, and Fulvia Plautilla Augusta. Quintus Calpurnius Festus erected and dedicated the statue which he had promised above the legal requirement for the honor of his aedileship.
EDCS-04000853.summary: This inscription is a dedication of a statue by Quintus Calpurnius Festus for the safety of Emperor Severus, his sons Caracalla and Geta, and their mother Julia Augusta, as well as Fulvia Plautilla, likely to commemorate his aedileship.

EDCS-04000855.translation: For the safety of the Emperors, Caesars Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus, father of the fatherland, and Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus, and Publius Septimius Geta Augustus, and Julia Augusta, mother of the Augusti, mother of the camps. Quintus Mattius Rusticus Flavianus made and dedicated the statue, which he had promised above the legal requirement for the honor of his aedileship, having previously brought forth the honorary offering, and gave it to the gymnasium.
EDCS-04000855.summary: This inscription records Quintus Mattius Rusticus Flavianus dedicating a statue for the safety of Emperor Severus, his sons Caracalla and Geta, and Julia Augusta, as part of his aedileship honors and also endowed a gymnasium.

EDCS-04000856.summary: This inscription appears to be a fragment mentioning Severus, likely Emperor Septimius Severus, with possibly incomplete titles or names.

EDCS-04000857.translation: To Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus Pius Felix, consul-designate, Prince of Youth, son of Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus, father of the fatherland, Arabicus Adiabenicus Parthicus Maximus, Pontifex Maximus, by decree of the decurions, at public expense.
EDCS-04000857.summary: This inscription records a monument erected at public expense by decree of the local council, dedicated to Emperor Caracalla, son of Septimius Severus.

EDCS-04000858.translation: For the safety of Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Severus Antoninus Augustus Pius Felix, Pontifex Maximus, Britannicus Maximus, Parthicus Maximus, Germanicus Maximus, and Julia Domna Augusta, mother of the Augustus, and of the Senate, and of the fatherland, and of the entire divine family. Publius Cestius Martialis erected and dedicated the statue at his own expense above the legal requirement for the honor of his aedileship.
EDCS-04000858.summary: This inscription records Publius Cestius Martialis dedicating a statue for the safety of Emperor Caracalla and Empress Julia Domna, in fulfillment of his aedileship obligations.

EDCS-04000860.summary: This inscription is a fragment possibly referring to the deified Emperor Augustus, perhaps as part of a dedication or title.

EDCS-04000861.translation: For the safety of Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Severus Alexander Pius Felix Augustus. Lucius Lucceius Faustus, a veteran discharged with honor, [erected] the statue which, for the honor of his aedileship, Lucius Lucceius Faust...
EDCS-04000861.summary: This inscription records Lucius Lucceius Faustus, a veteran, dedicating a statue for the safety of Emperor Severus Alexander, in relation to his aedileship.

EDCS-04000862.translation: To Emperor Caesar Gaius Vibius Afinius Gallus Veldumnianus Volusianus
EDCS-04000862.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Emperor Gallus, likely part of a larger monument.

EDCS-04000863.translation: For the safety of the Emperor Caesar and of the entire divine family, he made [this] at his own expense.
EDCS-04000863.summary: This inscription records a private dedication made at personal expense for the safety of the Emperor and his family, likely from the Severan or later period.

EDCS-04000865.translation: Of our lords Augustus and Caesar.
EDCS-04000865.summary: A fragment mentioning the emperors Augustus and Caesar, likely part of a larger dedication or honorific inscription.

EDCS-04000867.translation: For the great security of the times of our lords Valentinian and Valens, the perpetual Augusti, the summer baths, once most splendid for the colony, were ruined by years of decay and their walls and all ceilings were so corrupted that they were suffering grave damage; now they have been constructed with every suitability and decorated with splendid adornment, and also the basins, made most firm with increased weight of bronze, were completed by Pontilius Paulinus, perpetual priest and patron of the colony, curator of public affairs, at public expense, during the proconsulship of Publius Ampelius, a most distinguished man, and Octavius Privatianus, a most distinguished man, legate of Numidia, the portico entering from the atrium and also the pronaos adjoining it, for those passing by the road, with beams, timbers, and other things in due order.
EDCS-04000867.summary: This inscription records the restoration of summer baths and related structures in a colony, funded by the curator of public affairs and completed by the perpetual priest, during the proconsulship of Publius Ampelius and the legateship of Octavius Privatianus, likely in the late 4th century CE.

EDCS-04000868.translation: For the great good fortune of the times of our most invincible princes, the perpetual lords Augusti Valentinian and Valens, this fishpond and cellar, so defiled by dense leaks that they showed the lowest parts of the pavement and thus prevented the retention of heat, were restored with exquisite marbles of diverse colors and foreign artisans, and tessellated with splendid and entirely new work, during the proconsulship of Julius Festus, a most distinguished man, and Fabio Fabiano, a most distinguished man and illustrious legate of Numidia, by the curator of public affairs, among other things, which he had long since restored and dedicated with noble order and the entire populace, happily.
EDCS-04000868.summary: This inscription details the restoration of a fishpond and cellar, decorated with imported marble and mosaics, by the curator of public affairs during the proconsulship of Julius Festus and legateship of Fabio Fabiano, likely in the late 4th century CE.

EDCS-04000869.translation: For the good fortune of the times of our most blessed lords Flavius Gratian, Valentinian, and Theodosius, the invincible princes and ever Augusti, the temple of Fortune, where various goods are frequently sold, newly restored from the ground.
EDCS-04000869.summary: This inscription commemorates the restoration of the temple of Fortune, a market area, for the emperors Gratian, Valentinian, and Theodosius, likely in the late 4th century CE.

EDCS-04000871.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Flavius Gratian, pious, fortunate, victor, and triumphant, always Augustus, the ordo of the colony of Madaura, devoted to his divinity and majesty.
EDCS-04000871.summary: This is a dedication by the town council of Madaura to Emperor Gratian, expressing their devotion, likely dating to his reign in the late 4th century CE.

EDCS-04000873.translation: Under the flourishing glory of our lords Arcadius and Honorius, the most invincible princes and victorious throughout the whole world, during the proconsulship of the lord Apollodorus, a most distinguished man, and the legateship of the most distinguished man, the forum with all its buildings, which were defiled by ruin, was reformed into a new appearance with the reinforcement of beams, the construction of roofs, and the stage of the theatre, and fortified with lesser walls, repaired and roofed; the perpetual priest, curator of public affairs, dedicated it at his own expense for artisans and with the joy of all citizens.
EDCS-04000873.summary: This inscription records the renovation of the forum, including its buildings, theatre, and walls, by the perpetual priest and curator of public affairs, during the proconsulship of Apollodorus and legateship of an unnamed distinguished man, honoring the emperors Arcadius and Honorius in the early 5th century CE.

EDCS-04000874.translation: Under the excellent glory of our lords Arcadius, Honorius, and Theodosius, the most invincible princes and always Augusti, while Pompeius Proculus, a most distinguished man, proconsul of the province of Africa, administered, and Quintus Thersius Crispinus Megestius, a most distinguished man, legate of Numidia, Claudius Sisenna Germanianus, curator of public affairs, dedicated at his own expense the bathhouse cella, desolate from a long series of ruin and denied for the uses of bathing, and the vault with its suspended structures, constructed with splendid decrees and titles from the noble council.
EDCS-04000874.summary: This inscription details the reconstruction of a bathhouse and its vault by Claudius Sisenna Germanianus, curator of public affairs, at his own expense, during the proconsulship of Pompeius Proculus and legateship of Quintus Thersius Crispinus Megestius, honoring the emperors Arcadius, Honorius, and Theodosius in the early 5th century CE.

EDCS-04000877.summary: A very brief inscription, likely a personal dedication or a mark of allegiance to the emperor.

EDCS-04000881.translation: The citizens of Madaura, at their own expense, by decree of the decurions, to Apuleius the Platonic philosopher, as their ornament, to our lord, son of the divine Constantine the Great.
EDCS-04000881.summary: This inscription is a public dedication by the citizens of Madaura to the philosopher Apuleius, honoring him as an ornament to their city and acknowledging the emperor Constantine the Great, likely dating to the 4th century CE.

EDCS-04000884.translation: To Julius Sabinus Victorinus, Roman knight, perpetual priest, centenarian, a man of glorious innocence and proven fidelity, Quintus Calpurnius Honoratus, perpetual priest, Flavius Victor, Flavius Janus, perpetual priest, Julius Nustus, Cornelius Salvius, from loving parents.
EDCS-04000884.summary: This is an epitaph honoring Julius Sabinus Victorianus, a Roman knight and priest, listing several dedicators, including other priests, and mentioning his virtues, likely dating to the late Roman period.

EDCS-04000887.summary: This is a dedication to Gaius Gabinius Fortunatus, described as a grandfather, likely on a tombstone.

EDCS-04000888.summary: This is a dedication to Marcus Gabinius Sabinus, described as a father, likely on a tombstone.

EDCS-04000889.summary: This is a dedication to Secundia Victoria, described as a mother, likely on a tombstone.

EDCS-04000890.translation: To Marcus Cornelius Frontonus Gabinianus, son of an aunt.
EDCS-04000890.summary: This is a dedication to Marcus Cornelius Frontonus Gabinianus, identified as the son of an aunt, likely on a tombstone.

EDCS-04000891.translation: To Cornelia Gabinilla, daughter of an aunt.
EDCS-04000891.summary: This is a dedication to Cornelia Gabinilla, identified as the daughter of an aunt, likely on a tombstone.

EDCS-04000892.translation: To Marcus Flavius Fortunatus Gabinianus, nephew of an aunt.
EDCS-04000892.summary: This is a dedication to Marcus Flavius Fortunatus Gabinianus, identified as the nephew of an aunt, likely on a tombstone.

EDCS-04000893.translation: Quintus Obstorius Honoratus, son of Quintus, of the Palatine tribe, a veteran of the First Urban Cohort, honorably discharged, perpetual flamen, and twice duovir, because the town council of the colony of Madaura offered him the position of decurion while he was serving, and because they conferred upon him the honor of perpetual flaminates, he constructed an arch and a statue at his own expense with all the highest public honors granted to the state, costing 40,000 sesterces, and on account of the dedication he gave gifts to the decurions and a banquet to the curiae and a gymnasium to the people.
EDCS-04000893.summary: This is a dedication by Quintus Obstorius Honoratus, a veteran and local official in Madaura, who funded public works including an arch, statue, banquet, and gymnasium to commemorate his civic honors.

EDCS-04000894.translation: Tiberius Clodius Loquella, who held the offices of aedilicius, duoviricius, perpetual flamen, and priest of Liber, built the temple of the sanctuary at his own expense; after his death, at the request of his sons Clodius Florentinus and Dio, the council of priests permitted inscriptions to be set up in his memory.
EDCS-04000894.summary: This inscription records the construction of a sanctuary by Tiberius Clodius Loquella and the subsequent permission granted to his sons to erect commemorative inscriptions after his death.

EDCS-04000895.translation: Lucius Flavius Venusianus Faustus and Fa constructed and dedicated the temple from its foundations, along with the rest of their property, according to instructions.
EDCS-04000895.summary: This is a dedication by Lucius Flavius Venusianus Faustus and Fa for the construction and dedication of a temple, funded with their own resources as instructed.

EDCS-04000897.translation: Dedicated the atrium of the temple, made of square stone, at his own expense as priest of LR, along with the small shrine, and with his daughter named... QVI I N.
EDCS-04000897.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a temple atrium and a small shrine, funded by a priest identified as LR and his daughter.

EDCS-04000898.translation: The names of the council members who [built?] the old basilica. POMP VS
EDCS-04000898.summary: This inscription lists names of council members related to the old basilica, likely from a municipal building record.

EDCS-04000899.translation: Quintus Servilius Honoratus and Marcus Scribonius Honoratus Bennianus, chief of the litter-bearers, built the column from its foundation with its ornaments with their own money and dedicated it.
EDCS-04000899.summary: This inscription records the construction and dedication of a column by the chiefs of the litter-bearers, likely a public works project.

EDCS-04000904.translation: For Gaius Avidius Speratianus Vettonianus, the pontiff. Gaius Avidius Optatus and Livia Ianuaria, his parents, made [this].
EDCS-04000904.summary: This inscription is a dedication made by parents for their son, Gaius Avidius Speratianus Vettonianus, who held the religious office of pontiff.

EDCS-04000905.summary: This inscription likely records the name and perpetual priestly office of an individual named Aurelius Filus.

EDCS-04000906.translation: For Lucius Caesonio Honorato Caesoniano, perpetual flamen, an excellent man. EM MV
EDCS-04000906.summary: This inscription honors Lucius Caesonio Honorato Caesoniano, a distinguished man who held the office of perpetual flamen.

EDCS-04000907.text_edition: \n Marco Cornelio Frontoni Quirina Gabiniano equiti Romano ex inquisitione allecto flamini perpetuo IIvirali honestae memoriae viro Marci Corneli Victorini flaminis perpetui bis IIviralis filio splendissimus ordo et populus coloniae Madaurensium ob insignem in se amorem et frumenti copiam tempore inopiae sibi largiter praestitam honorem bigae et statuae decreverunt pecunia publica quam Corneliae Romanilla Postumiana et Victorina Claudiana et Eulogia Romanilla filiae et heredes eius sua pecunia posuerunt sportulis decurionibus et curialibus datis\n
EDCS-04000907.translation: To Marcus Cornelius Frontonus Quirinus Gabinianus, Roman knight, promoted by inquiry, perpetual flamen, twice duumvir, a man of honorable memory, son of Marcus Cornelius Victorinus, perpetual flamen and twice duumvir. The most distinguished order and people of the colony of Madaura decreed the honor of a chariot and a statue to him, because of his exceptional love for them and for generously providing grain during a time of scarcity. His daughters Cornelia Romanilla Postumiana and Victorina Claudiana, and Eulogia Romanilla, and their heirs, erected it with public funds, giving handouts to the decurions and curial councillors.
EDCS-04000907.summary: A dedication by the city of Madaura to Marcus Cornelius Frontonus, a distinguished local official, honoring him with a chariot and statue for his public service and generosity, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04000908.translation: Flamen, aedile, duovir, and Filicinia Secura, priestess of the Capitol. A plot of land was granted to their son, the pontiff, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-04000908.summary: This inscription records the allocation of land by a town council to the son of local magistrates and a priestess.

EDCS-04000910.translation: For Lucius Iulius Victori Faustinianus, pontiff. Lucius Iulius Pudens, flamen and aedilician official.
EDCS-04000910.summary: This inscription records the civic and religious offices held by Lucius Iulius Pudens, likely in honor of Lucius Iulius Victori Faustinianus.

EDCS-04000911.translation: MA VS IIVLANFIOSATI I SVLAN set up and dedicated the statue, which he promised for the honor of his aedileship, within his year.
EDCS-04000911.summary: This inscription records the fulfillment of a promise to erect a statue by an official within his term, likely related to his aedileship.

EDCS-04000914.translation: …us, an excellent man, curator of the public affairs.
EDCS-04000914.summary: This inscription describes a man of notable character who served as a public official responsible for civic matters.

EDCS-04000917.translation: [...]enses brothers, called by mutual agreement, for the honor of a communal [office/gift].
EDCS-04000917.summary: This inscription refers to brothers who were mutually recognized or appointed for a shared honor or office.

EDCS-04000924.translation: The client order of Madaurensians decreed that a marble statue be erected to Ceionius Julianus, a most distinguished man, patron of the colony, good and outstanding, and an ornament of senatorial dignity, under whose proconsulship the community and the state received very many benefits, and with honorable obedience, although unequal to his benefits, they erected it; and Aurelius Saturninus Crescentianus, perpetual priest and patron of the colony, and Nicander, perpetual priest and patron of the colony, brothers, also erected it and brought it here at their own expense.
EDCS-04000924.summary: This is a dedication of a marble statue to the proconsul Ceionius Julianus by the order of Madaurensians, and erected by two brothers who were perpetual priests and patrons of the colony.

EDCS-04000925.translation: Julius Maximianus made this at his own expense.
EDCS-04000925.summary: This is a private dedication by Julius Maximianus, likely for a building or artwork.

EDCS-04000927.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription mentioning a person named 'ularis' and his son.

EDCS-04000931.translation: Caius Julius V, Marcus Antonius, Quintus Antonius, VS CASVS.
EDCS-04000931.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription listing the names of Caius Julius V, Marcus Antonius, and Quintus Antonius.

EDCS-04000938.summary: This is a simple inscription bearing the name Lucius Occius Martialis.

EDCS-04000939.translation: DI AE of the Augusti Pancratio, life.
EDCS-04000939.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription mentioning 'Augusti' and possibly a name or concept related to life.

EDCS-04000944.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that likely refers to a quantity, possibly of years or a measure.

EDCS-04000946.translation: GET us and OCTONIS C SIT from A.
EDCS-04000946.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription containing names or place names and prepositional phrases.

EDCS-04000948.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription containing abbreviations that likely relate to titles or familial relationships.

EDCS-04000952.summary: This is a short, common Latin wish for good fortune or prosperity, often found on objects.

EDCS-04000954.summary: This inscription has no legible content.

EDCS-04000956.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Tiberius Claudius Hispanus, son of Tiberius, of the Quirina tribe, a military tribune of the III Augusta legion, quaestorian scribe, prefect of engineers, and perpetual priest, dutiful, lived 33 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-04000956.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Tiberius Claudius Hispanus, detailing his career and lifespan, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04000957.translation: Perhaps you ask why you are delayed? You will learn quickly: here lies Laelius Timminus, patient in hardship, thrifty, watchful, sober, who prepared a substantial estate and a modest home, and rose to the equestrian rank. Joined with him is his wife Calpurnia Victoria, endowed with sanctity of character and modesty. Together they rest. Their children erected this monument, sorrowful, sacred to the departed spirits.
EDCS-04000957.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Laelius Timminus and his wife Calpurnia Victoria, celebrating his career advancement and their character, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04000958.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Caesonius Honoratus, son of Lucius, of the Quirina tribe, Roman knight, dutiful, an example of modesty and gravity, lived 65 years; he is buried in this tomb.
EDCS-04000958.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Caesonius Honoratus, highlighting his status as a Roman knight and his virtuous character, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04000959.translation: Tiberius Claudius Crescens, a Roman knight of the ala Gallorum, served for 36 years, lived 75 years; he is buried here, dutiful, innocent.
EDCS-04000959.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Tiberius Claudius Crescens, detailing his military service in a cavalry unit and his lifespan, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04000961.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Fannius Paetus, a veteran, dutiful, lived 65 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-04000961.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Fannius Paetus, identifying him as a veteran, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04000962.translation: Pia lived 75 years; she is buried here. Quintus Flavius Saturninus, a centurion of the IIII cohorts, made and dedicated this for his mother, a veteran, dutiful, lived 67 years. Galla made it at her own expense; she is buried here.
EDCS-04000962.summary: This funerary inscription records the deaths of Galla and her mother, with her father Quintus Flavius Saturninus also being a veteran centurion, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04000964.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Cassia Secunda, dutiful, lived 43 years; she is buried here. Caius Iulius Victor, son of Caius Iulius, of the Quirina tribe, dutiful, lived 47 years. Caius Iulius Saturninus, a soldier of the III Augusta legion, made this for his parents.
EDCS-04000964.summary: This funerary inscription records the deaths of Cassia Secunda and Caius Iulius Victor, with their parent Caius Iulius Saturninus being a soldier in the III Augusta legion, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04000965.translation: Saturninus, of the Quirina tribe, centurion of the army of the province of Britannia Superior, chief of the presidential staff, a beneficiarius consularis, optio of the praetorium, made a tomb for himself for burial at the expense of 30,000 sesterces and dedicated it while alive, and died at the age of 85 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-04000965.summary: This is a self-funded funerary monument for Saturninus, a centurion and staff officer in Roman Britain, who died at the age of 85, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-04000966.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus Sextilius Felix, a veteran, dutiful, lived [XX] years. Tertulla, sober and dutiful, lived 75 years; she is buried here. Caecilia Maxima, dutiful, lived 40 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-04000966.summary: This funerary inscription records the deaths of Tertulla and Caecilia Maxima, with Quintus Sextilius Felix identified as a veteran, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-04000967.translation: To the spirits of the departed. M. Nvs, a veteran of the Quirina tribe, priest of the Goddess Bona, and priestess of Liber Pater.
EDCS-04000967.summary: This is a funerary inscription honoring M. Nvs, a veteran and priest, and the priestess of Liber Pater.

EDCS-04000968.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Tiberius Claudius Lucinus, son of Tiberius, of the Quirina tribe, twice chief magistrate and perpetual flamen, lived 62 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-04000968.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Tiberius Claudius Lucinus, a prominent local official, who lived 62 years.

EDCS-04000969.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Marius, by his deeds and name once beloved of his fatherland, teaching with affection, completed seven years of life; moreover, he lived long ago, a lover of his country's virtue, whom his lineage, strong in honours, produced, renowned in fame, in which the greatest offspring rejoices; he is buried here.
EDCS-04000969.summary: This funerary inscription commemorates Marius, who died at the age of seven, highlighting his love for his country and virtue.

EDCS-04000970.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Lucius Aemilius Victor, a pious priest, lived 55 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-04000970.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Lucius Aemilius Victor, a pious priest, who lived 55 years.

EDCS-04000971.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Lucius Antonius Maximus, priest of Mercury, lived 55 years. Flavia Tertulla lived 41 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-04000971.summary: This funerary inscription records the deaths of Lucius Antonius Maximus, a priest of Mercury, and Flavia Tertulla.

EDCS-04000972.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Bass Primossa Marisa, priestess of Tellus, lived 70 years.
EDCS-04000972.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Bass Primossa Marisa, a priestess of Tellus, who lived 70 years.

EDCS-04000973.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Caelia Sperata, daughter of Caelius Felix, a pious priestess of Tellus, lived 75 years; she is buried here. Lollius Victor, pious, lived 15 years; Publius Lollius, pious, lived 3 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-04000973.summary: This funerary inscription records the deaths of Caelia Sperata, a priestess of Tellus, her son Lollius Victor, and another Publius Lollius.

EDCS-04000974.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Calpurnius Datus, a pious priest of Saturn, lived 95 years; he is buried here. [He/She] lived 65 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-04000974.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Calpurnius Datus, a priest of Saturn, who lived 95 years, and another individual who lived 65 years.

EDCS-04000975.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Lucius Castricius Messor, a pious priest of Jupiter, lived 50 years. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Lucius Castricius Severus, pious, lived 10 years.
EDCS-04000975.summary: This funerary inscription records the deaths of Lucius Castricius Messor, a priest of Jupiter, and Lucius Castricius Severus.

EDCS-04000976.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Claudia Paula, a pious high priestess, lived 90 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-04000976.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Claudia Paula, a pious high priestess, who lived 90 years.

EDCS-04000977.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Datia Fortunata, priestess of Ceres, pious, lived 85 years, is buried here.
EDCS-04000977.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Datia Fortunata, a priestess of Ceres, who died at the age of 85.

EDCS-04000978.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Titus Flavius Matutinus Tranquillianus, priest of Pluto, pious, lived 81 years. [Buried here with] Iulia Frontilla, his most dear and obedient wife, pious, lived [---] years.
EDCS-04000978.summary: This tombstone inscription records the death of Titus Flavius Matutinus Tranquillianus, a priest of Pluto, and his wife Iulia Frontilla.

EDCS-04000979.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. You rest securely, renowned devotee of sacred rites. Young man whom Earth holds, whom Tartarus himself seeks, may you find a pious resting place, for here lie buried. Flavius Natalis Veturianus, lived 50 years, is buried here.
EDCS-04000979.summary: This tombstone inscription records the death of Flavius Natalis Veturianus, who is described as a devotee of sacred rites.

EDCS-04000980.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Titus Flavius Primus, priest of Saturn, pious, lived 75 years, is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Tiberia Claudia Zaba, pious, lived 90 years, is buried here.
EDCS-04000980.summary: This tombstone inscription records the deaths of Titus Flavius Primus, a priest of Saturn, and Tiberia Claudia Zaba.

EDCS-04000982.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Bennia Saturnina, sober, pious, lived 55 years. Caius Iulius Quinti Iuli Quirina Felix Kaellianus, priest of Pluto, pious, lived 50 years.
EDCS-04000982.summary: This tombstone inscription records the deaths of Bennia Saturnina and Caius Iulius Quinti Iuli Quirina Felix Kaellianus, a priest of Pluto.

EDCS-04000983.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Caius Iulius Namphamo, priest, lived 101 years, is buried here.
EDCS-04000983.summary: This tombstone inscription records the death of Caius Iulius Namphamo, a priest, who died at the age of 101.

EDCS-04000984.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulia Katullina, priestess of the Earth, pious, lived 90 years, is buried here. Quintus Calpurnius Festus, pious, lived 75 years, is buried here.
EDCS-04000984.summary: This tombstone inscription records the deaths of Iulia Katullina, a priestess of the Earth, and Quintus Calpurnius Festus.

EDCS-04000985.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. To Quintus Pompeius Pompeianus, son of Lucius, of the Quirina tribe, priest of the god Liber Pater, pious, lived 80 years, one month, and 23 days, is buried here.
EDCS-04000985.summary: This tombstone inscription records the death of Quintus Pompeius Pompeianus, a priest of Liber Pater, who died at the age of 80 years, 1 month, and 23 days.

EDCS-04000986.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Publius Quintianus, priest.
EDCS-04000986.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the name and priesthood of Publius Quintianus.

EDCS-04000987.translation: Priestess [---], pious, lived 65 years, is buried here. May her bones rest well. Titus Flavius Marinus made [this] for his excellent mother.
EDCS-04000987.summary: This tombstone inscription records the death of an unnamed priestess who lived 65 years, and was made by her son Titus Flavius Marinus.

EDCS-04000988.translation: Sacred to the departed gods. Marcus Iulius Festus of the Quirina tribe, dutiful, lived 85 years. Because of his generous spirit and the love with which he uniquely regarded his fellow members, he left in his will 12 modii to his fellow members and their descendants. The same fellow members and their descendants erected this monument to him and his wife IOI, and jointly dedicated it in restored condition.
EDCS-04000988.summary: This funerary inscription records the erection of a monument by a sodality (a collegium or association) to Marcus Iulius Festus and his wife, in recognition of his bequest to them.

EDCS-04000989.translation: Sacred to the departed gods. Titus Flavius Ammonianus rests in this tomb, who [was skilled in] the discipline of arithmetic.
EDCS-04000989.summary: This fragmentary inscription is a funerary epitaph for Titus Flavius Ammonianus, a man skilled in arithmetic.

EDCS-04000990.translation: Sacred to the departed gods. Lucius Baebius Crescens, dutiful, of Italian origin, lived 72 years; he is buried here. Aelia Fortunata, dutiful, lived 62 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-04000990.summary: This is a joint funerary epitaph for Lucius Baebius Crescens and Aelia Fortunata, who lived and died in the same place.

EDCS-04000991.translation: Sacred to the departed gods. Berecth V Victor, citizen of Theveste, lived [---] years.
EDCS-04000991.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription for Berecth V Victor, a citizen of Theveste.

EDCS-04000992.translation: Sacred to the departed gods. Souls united in concord, who once while alive were equal in outstanding character and marital love, rest joined in these seats for long ages. For alas, the good Marcus Aemilius Primus Flavianus, renowned by his lineage and distinguished by his name, when he had completed his thirteenth year, an unjust year brought him to his end. After his death, his chaste wife, bereft of her sweet husband, overcoming her grief through her own efforts, Julia Setina, an example to all women in her morals, born of noble stock and glorious family, rests here, but she deserved to reach the seats of the pious, celebrating Elysium, joined to her dear husband. He had completed his sixteenth decade of years. Their sons Aemilius Aquilinus and Barbarus erected these monuments in their time through the duty of piety and now frequently attend the funeral rites there with customary solemnity. They are buried here.
EDCS-04000992.summary: This is a complex funerary epitaph for Marcus Aemilius Primus Flavianus and his wife Julia Setina, detailing their lives, their ages at death, and the monument erected by their sons.

EDCS-04000993.translation: Sacred to the departed gods. Marcus Aemilius Setinus, son of Marcus, of the Quirina tribe, dutiful, lived 24 years, 5 months, and 2 days. His mother Iulia Setina, and his brothers Aemilius Aquilinus and Barbarus, are buried here.
EDCS-04000993.summary: This funerary epitaph records the death of Marcus Aemilius Setinus, specifying his age at death, and identifies his mother and brothers who are also buried there.

EDCS-04000994.translation: To Aurelia Mammosa. Do not inquire too much, stranger, whose monument Mammosa, Florus erected for his wife, whom he loved not without reason with great love, as a genial guardian, since she had provided provisions and upkeep for the small household gods, and while she led a frugal life with talent, and had filled her home with children through fruitful childbirth, a chaste wife of triple wedlock. This woman, snatched away in pitiable death here, after flourishing for thirty-two years of life, was buried by her husband with no small grief and expense. If by chance, traveler, you wish to know curiously who this person was when alive, he was Iulius Florus, keeping his name, who, when he was a young man of fifty years, and had entered his fifty-first year by lot, departed with an easy death. To him, indeed, his dear wife Mammosa, the triple offspring of children, and likewise chaste, is now joined, and as you reread this, the associated tomb preserves the honor of both, now that the former has died.
EDCS-04000994.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Aurelia Mammosa and her husband Iulius Florus, detailing their ages at death and the monument erected by Florus.

EDCS-04000995.translation: CVNIC Iulius MERIDIA MAXI ETAGAN NS EEVO AVISV INCI S ATAVP AFR INV IM lived 5 years, worthy, patient in labor, industrious, generous, and fortunate in seeking ADOI N, sanctified by his wife NO AII adorned you all RE dear wife, your tomb and holy ashes serv
EDCS-04000995.summary: This is a very fragmented funerary inscription for Iulius, who lived 5 years and was described with positive attributes; his wife likely erected the monument.

EDCS-04000997.translation: MAIIVS after his lamentable twentieth year of age was snatched away, the Fates gave you, uncle, to rest, hanging in the lamentable arms of infants, reaching the end of life, pitiable boy, you fulfilled the decrees of fate while life remained. Madaurius was his name.
EDCS-04000997.summary: This inscription is a lament for a deceased boy named Madaurius, who died in his twentieth year and is described as pitiable.

EDCS-04000998.translation: A prudent, patient, frugal, sober, dutiful woman lived 29 years, 11 months, and 10 days. Pet Iustus dedicated [this monument]. She is buried here.
EDCS-04000998.summary: This funerary epitaph records the death of a woman described with virtuous qualities, who died at age 29, and was commemorated by Pet Iustus.

EDCS-04000999.translation: To the Manes. With sober eye, a pious mother, a harmonious daughter, tested in discipline, who lived prudently and patiently for thirty-seven years, and for seven months. For her, in her prosperity, she attained the honours of her mother.
EDCS-04000999.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a virtuous woman, likely from the late antique period, praising her character and longevity.

EDCS-04001001.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Dead. Whoever you are, you will soon learn whose name this is. He was of excellent birth, and he who guarded this place was raised this young man by his father with no expense, and skilled in every art. Joined in body to her husband, for the sixth time the tenth year had completed its span for her. Guard these monuments.
EDCS-04001001.summary: A funerary inscription for a young man of noble birth, emphasizing his upbringing and connection to his wife, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04001002.translation: Here lies... loved with excessive love. Fate was cruel to me; I left my parents. I offered these titles to the sacred Manes according to custom. He lived 12 years and 10 months.
EDCS-04001002.summary: A funerary epitaph for an individual who died young, expressing grief and devotion to the Manes, probably from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04001003.translation: To preserve glory and achieve renown for himself. The father, Sexsus, and his twin sons, whose names are lost, lived for about fifty years beyond the Alps. He saw the pears he cultivated. This monument was erected by the freedman of his patron, whom he served. May his name and honor remain forever.
EDCS-04001003.summary: A funerary monument erected by a freedman for his patron, celebrating their lives and the patron's cultivation of pears, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04001004.summary: A fragmentary inscription recording the lifespan of someone named CIRONE, likely a tombstone inscription from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04001005.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Dead. Adiutor lived 90 years.
EDCS-04001005.summary: A simple funerary epitaph recording the name and age of the deceased, Adiutor, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04001006.summary: A tombstone inscription recording the name and lifespan of Aebutia Sala, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04001007.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Dead. Caius Aemilius Kapito lived 100 years. Caius Aemilius [---] lived [---] years. Caius Aemilius Fortunatus lived 45 years. They are buried here.
EDCS-04001007.summary: A funerary inscription listing three individuals, Caius Aemilius Kapito, another Caius Aemilius, and Caius Aemilius Fortunatus, with their ages, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04001008.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Dead. Caius Aemilius Clodianus Quirina, pious, lived 60 years. Aemilius Aemilianus, pious, lived [---] years.
EDCS-04001008.summary: A funerary inscription for Caius Aemilius Clodianus Quirina and Aemilius Aemilianus, noting their piety and lifespans, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04001009.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Dead. S. Victor, grandson of Ingenui, lived 11 years. Aemilia Ingenua lived 62 years. Flavius Ianuarius, grandson of Ingenui, lived 25 years. Flavius Rogatus, grandson of Ingenui, lived 21 years. Flavia Sterceia, pious, lived 12 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-04001009.summary: A family tombstone inscription dedicated to the Manes, listing five individuals, including grandchildren of Ingenui, with their ages, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04001010.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Publius Afinius Ternus, dutiful, lived for 7 years and 8 months; he is buried here.
EDCS-04001010.summary: A funerary epitaph for Publius Afinius Ternus, recording his age at death and burial location, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04001012.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Memmia Rogata lived for 85 years; she is buried here. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Decimus Alfenius Victor lived for 92 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-04001012.summary: A funerary epitaph containing two individuals, Memmia Rogata and Decimus Alfenius Victor, recording their ages and burial, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04001013.translation: Caius Antonius Crispus lived for 90 years. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Vitalis lived for 50 years; he is buried here. Victor, dutiful, lived for 35 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-04001013.summary: A funerary epitaph listing three individuals, Caius Antonius Crispus, Vitalis, and Victor, with their ages and burial information, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04001014.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Caius Antonius Felix, dutiful, lived for 63 years.
EDCS-04001014.summary: A funerary epitaph for Caius Antonius Felix, stating his age at death and likely burial, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04001015.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Marcus Antonius Valerianus, son of Caius, dutiful, lived for 20 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-04001015.summary: A funerary epitaph for Marcus Antonius Valerianus, son of Caius, detailing his age and burial, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04001018.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Antonia Quirina Valeria, daughter of Caius, dutiful, lived for 70 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-04001018.summary: A funerary epitaph for Antonia Quirina Valeria, daughter of Caius, recording her age and burial, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04001019.translation: lived for 57 years Antonia Victoria MONI, dutiful, lived for 10 years Marcus Antonius
EDCS-04001019.summary: A fragmented funerary inscription mentioning Antonia Victoria MONI and Marcus Antonius, with ages given for Antonia Victoria, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04001020.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Licceia Quirina Fausta, daughter of Lucius, lived for 40 years; she is buried here. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Lucius Appius Quirinus Saturninus lived for 65 years; he is buried here.
