EDCS-04001498.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Flavius AMRILIVS, veteran of the III Augusta legion, lived for 100 years; his heir made this.
EDCS-04001498.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Flavius AMRILIVS, a veteran of the III Augusta legion, recording his lifespan and mentioning his heir, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04001499.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Catta lived for 75 years.
EDCS-04001499.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Catta, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04001500.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Felix lived for 70 years. Tsedden lived for 73 years. V. Cirrenius made this testimony at his own expense.
EDCS-04001500.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespans of Felix and Tsedden and mentions V. Cirrenius as the maker of the testimony, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04001501.translation: Mensa Pontiorum. Lucius Pontius Martis, also called Pattiso, lived for 80 years. His date of burial was the 15th day before the Kalends of October. His date of burial was the Kalends of June. He lived for 61 years. Silicia.
EDCS-04001501.summary: This complex funerary inscription records the lifespans of Lucius Pontius Martis (Pattiso) and possibly Silicia, along with conflicting burial dates, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04001515.translation: Sacred to Caelestis Augusta. By command of the divine power of our Augustus, Coronatus, assistant to the record-keepers, established the doors and the arch from the foundations, and adorned and enlarged the temple, with a willing heart.
EDCS-04001515.summary: This is a dedication by Coronatus, an assistant to the record-keepers, to Caelestis Augusta, detailing his construction and embellishment of a temple and associated structures, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04001516.text_edition: \n Dibus sic Mauris Iulius Donatianus sacerdos deae Caelestis Augustae ex viso suo cum suis omnibus votum solvit\n
EDCS-04001516.translation: To the gods, thus to the Moors. Iulius Donatianus, priest of the August goddess Caelestis, fulfilled his vow according to his vision, with all his household.
EDCS-04001516.summary: A votive inscription by Iulius Donatianus, a priest of the goddess Caelestis, fulfilling a vow after a vision, likely from Roman North Africa.

EDCS-04001517.translation: Dedicated to Mercury Augustus. Quintus Longeius Faustinus, son of Quintus of the Papiria tribe, aedile and prefect with the power of judicial decision, in honor of his aedileship, dedicated the statue of Mercury with its ornaments, which he had promised for 5,000 sesterces. He spent 4,000 sesterces in lawful payments to the state and more on the statue's cost, spending 2,000 sesterces. The place was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-04001517.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a statue of Mercury by Quintus Longeius Faustinus, who served as aedile and prefect, to commemorate his office. The monument was erected in an unspecified location granted by the decurions, likely in the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-04001518.translation: The priests whom he appointed on the Nones of June, he himself advanced: Caius Porcius Felix, his freedman, Happiest Exceptus Vernulus, Augurinus, son of Atellius Martialis, and Silvanus Iulianus, and Pullaenianus Victorinus, Donatus Saturninus, Maius, Rufinus, and Rufinus, Martialis, Iucundus and his son Iucundus, and Nivasus Fortunatus Priscus, his freedmen and sons, Antonius and Ciripitta, son, under the consulship of Aurelius Lollianus on the 15th day before the Kalends of June.
EDCS-04001518.summary: This inscription lists the names of priests appointed and advanced by an unnamed individual, likely a high-ranking official, during the consulship of Aurelius Lollianus in the late Roman Empire.

EDCS-04001528.translation: To Fortuna Redux. Curis XI, Curis XI. Marcellus I, XII.
EDCS-04001528.summary: This is a dedication to Fortuna Redux, possibly related to a journey or safe return, with numerical notations that are unclear in their specific meaning, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04001530.summary: This inscription identifies the origin or association of an object with the Third Augustan Legion, a prominent Roman legion, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04001531.summary: This inscription identifies the origin or association of an object with the Third Augustan Legion, a prominent Roman legion, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04001574.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Quintus Babullius Felix, a veteran, lived 80 years and is buried here. Soetonia Procula, his wife, and Babullius Thevestinus, his son, made this for their dutiful father.
EDCS-04001574.summary: A funerary epitaph for Quintus Babullius Felix, erected by his wife and son, dating likely to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04001575.translation: She lived 27 years, served 8 years. Her husband, Calpurnius Galla, placed this here.
EDCS-04001575.summary: This tombstone records the life and military service of an individual, with his wife Calpurnia Galla as the dedicator, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04001576.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Flavius Flavinus, optio principalis, the name SAT[...]
EDCS-04001576.summary: An incomplete funerary inscription for Flavius Flavinus, an optio principalis, likely Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04001577.text_edition: \n Titus Sergius Satur miles legionis III Augustae centuria Valeri Marcelli militavit annis XIX vixit annis XXXX hic situs est Lucius Flavius Ferox milex sic legionis III Augustae centuria Augustalis exs sic testamento arbitratu Fulviae Saturninae factum est\n
EDCS-04001577.translation: Titus Sergius Satur served as a soldier in the III Augusta legion, in the centuria of Valerius Marcellus, for 19 years, and lived 40 years. He is buried here. Lucius Flavius Ferox, a soldier of the III Augusta legion, in the centuria Augustalis, was buried here by will and at the arbitration of Fulvia Saturnina.
EDCS-04001577.summary: A funerary epitaph for Titus Sergius Satur, a soldier of the III Augusta legion, and Lucius Flavius Ferox, also of the same legion, indicating military service and burial arrangements.

EDCS-04001578.translation: Region of Mauri, Legate, lived 25 years, served 25 years, lived 37 years. Fate and what was left by Lysa.
EDCS-04001578.summary: This fragmentary inscription commemorates an individual who served as a legate and lived to be 37 years old, with unclear references to 'fate' and 'Lysa', likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04001579.summary: This is a very fragmented inscription, only providing the beginning of a phrase related to birth or origin, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04001580.translation: From the II viri, placed [this]. He lived [X] years. He is buried here.
EDCS-04001580.summary: This inscription marks a burial place and indicates that the deceased was a 'II viri' (a type of local magistrate) and lived an unspecified number of years, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04001581.translation: Of Polius... to the god, lived 10 years.
EDCS-04001581.summary: This inscription records the lifespan of a young individual, dedicated to a god, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04001582.translation: Ab Camia, daughter of Musulamus, of the tribe Gubul, wife of Daris, made this monument at her own expense for her husband.
EDCS-04001582.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by a wife for her husband, likely dating from the Roman Imperial period given the tribal name and naming conventions.

EDCS-04001583.translation: The servants of Italy and those following, who, while we were entering the guard post where fate was leading, made vows and went out long ago; there one of them stayed behind...
EDCS-04001583.summary: This inscription appears to be part of a narrative, possibly commemorating soldiers or travellers, and its context is lost due to damage.

EDCS-04001584.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Publius Aelius Marcianus the Younger lived 2 years, 5 months, and 7 days and is buried here. Victorinus made this for his son.
EDCS-04001584.summary: A funerary epitaph for Publius Aelius Marcianus the Younger, a very young child, erected by his father Victorinus, likely Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04001587.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Quintus Baebius Balbus lived 3 years and is buried here. Quintus Baebius Bassinus, his father, saw to it that this was made.
EDCS-04001587.summary: A funerary epitaph for Quintus Baebius Balbus, a young child, erected by his father Quintus Baebius Bassinus, likely Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04001588.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Publius Bo[---] Ser[---] lived 5 years, 4 months, and 10 days. Sextus B[---]us Felix made this for his most dutiful son. He is buried here.
EDCS-04001588.summary: A funerary epitaph for an unidentified child, erected by his father Sextus [---]us Felix, likely Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04001589.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Caecilius Felicianus lived 2 years. Felicior made this for his dutiful son.
EDCS-04001589.summary: A funerary epitaph for Caecilius Felicianus, a young child, erected by Felicior, likely Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04001590.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Caecilia Saturnina lived 30 years. Felicior made this for his dutiful wife.
EDCS-04001590.summary: A funerary epitaph for Caecilia Saturnina, erected by her husband Felicior, likely Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04001592.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Caelia Ingenua lived for 10 years. Her husband placed this.
EDCS-04001592.summary: A funerary epitaph for a young girl, Caelia Ingenua, erected by her husband, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04001594.summary: This fragmentary text likely continues the previous inscription, specifying the lifespan of Cornelia Fortunata.

EDCS-04001595.translation: 17 days. Here lies Crepereia VA A, wife.
EDCS-04001595.summary: This funerary epitaph records the very short lifespan of 17 days for a person named Crepereia, likely a child, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04001596.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Titus Decimius Speratus lived 55 years [...]. SORO[---] [---]RAI[---]. He is buried here.
EDCS-04001596.summary: An incomplete funerary epitaph for Titus Decimius Speratus, likely Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04001597.translation: To Domitia Maxima the innocent, Gaius Julius Maximus made this for his daughter.
EDCS-04001597.summary: A funerary monument dedicated to an innocent daughter, Domitia Maxima, by her father, Gaius Julius Maximus, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04001598.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. For his daughter Euodia, who lived 5 years and 4 months.
EDCS-04001598.summary: A funerary epitaph for Euodia, erected by her father, likely Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04001600.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Flavia Ingenua lived 45 years. Insteius Monitus, her husband, erected this tomb for his most sacred and most dutiful wife.
EDCS-04001600.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Flavia Ingenua, erected by her husband, Insteius Monitus.

EDCS-04001601.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Publius Folius Urbanus lived [unknown age]. Martialis erected this for his dutiful son.
EDCS-04001601.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Martialis's son, Publius Folius Urbanus.

EDCS-04001602.translation: Gaius Julius Valens, son of Gaius, of the tribe Papiria, lived for 60 years. Here lies Iulia Venusta.
EDCS-04001602.summary: A funerary epitaph for Gaius Julius Valens, recording his lifespan and tribe, with Iulia Venusta also mentioned, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04001603.translation: [Name missing] lived 51 years. Curtia(?) erected this for her most dear husband.
EDCS-04001603.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a husband, erected by his wife Curtia(?).

EDCS-04001605.translation: Lived for 21 years. Manilius Natalis made this for his devoted brother.
EDCS-04001605.summary: A funerary epitaph for Manilius Natalis, recording his age and indicating it was made by his brother, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04001607.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Caius Marius Musicus lived for 21 years. Marius Tevestinus made this for his devoted son.
EDCS-04001607.summary: A funerary epitaph for Caius Marius Musicus, recording his age and the dedicant as his father, Marius Tevestinus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04001608.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Caius Memmius Victor lived 50 years. His sons erected this.
EDCS-04001608.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Caius Memmius Victor, erected by his sons.

EDCS-04001609.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Milesia Silvana lived 45 years. Her husband erected this for his dutiful wife.
EDCS-04001609.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Milesia Silvana, erected by her husband.

EDCS-04001610.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Optatula, deceased at 16 years of age. Cincius Rogatus made this for his daughter.
EDCS-04001610.summary: A funerary epitaph for Optatula, who died at 16, erected by her father Cincius Rogatus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04001611.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Lucius Petronius Ianuarius lived 40 years. His wife, Flavina, erected this for him who deserved well. He is buried here.
EDCS-04001611.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Petronius Ianuarius, erected by his wife Flavina.

EDCS-04001612.translation: Secura, having been dedicated by DDORO, was restored.
EDCS-04001612.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely recording a restoration, but the context and original dedication are unclear due to significant damage.

EDCS-04001613.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Suetonius Fidus.
EDCS-04001613.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicating a burial place to Suetonius Fidus, likely a freedman or slave given the common name.

EDCS-04001614.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Caius Suetonius Rogatus lived 80 years, he is buried here. His sons made this for their dearest father.
EDCS-04001614.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Caius Suetonius Rogatus, set up by his sons, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-04001615.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Valeria Celsa, dutiful daughter of Caius, lived 24 years, 4 months, and 27 days. She is buried here.
EDCS-04001615.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Valeria Celsa, likely erected by her family.

EDCS-04001621.summary: This is a very short funerary inscription, possibly for a Christian or someone adopting peaceful imagery, with a non-Latin name.

EDCS-04001622.translation: Colonica lived 5 years and 3 months. Maxsima lived 2 years and [some months].
EDCS-04001622.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the short lives of two children, likely sisters, from the Imperial period.

EDCS-04001623.translation: Passivus lived 20 years, eight months, and sixteen days in peace.
EDCS-04001623.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Passivus, likely a freedman or slave, indicating a peaceful death and burial.

EDCS-04001624.summary: This is a very short funerary inscription with a non-Latin name, likely from the Late Roman period.

EDCS-04001633.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Cornelius Donatus [ inscription incomplete ]
EDCS-04001633.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Cornelius Donatus, with the inscription incomplete.

EDCS-04001634.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Iulius Saturninus lived 31 years.
EDCS-04001634.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Iulius Saturninus, recording his age at death.

EDCS-04001635.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Pulaenius Salvius lived 91 years, he is buried here.
EDCS-04001635.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Pulaenius Salvius, likely a Roman citizen, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-04001639.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Lucius Valerius, son of Quintus, of the Quirina tribe, [ inscription incomplete ]
EDCS-04001639.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Valerius, son of Quintus, with the inscription incomplete.

EDCS-04001640.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Caesia Aucta lived 52 years. Marcus Ulpius Datus made this for his devoted mother.
EDCS-04001640.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Caesia Aucta, set up by her son Marcus Ulpius Datus, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-04001641.translation: Sapunum lived 75 years, he is buried here. His devoted heir placed this.
EDCS-04001641.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Sapunum, likely a freedman or slave, whose heir erected the monument.

EDCS-04001643.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Aufidius Messor lived 63 years; he is buried here. Aufidius Messor, his son, made this for his most beloved father.
EDCS-04001643.summary: A funerary epitaph for Aufidius Messor, erected by his son of the same name, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-04001644.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Amabilis lived 35 years. Her devoted sisters made this for her.
EDCS-04001644.summary: A funerary epitaph for Amabilis, erected by her sisters, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-04001645.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Gabinia Secunda.

EDCS-04001646.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. The sons made this for their most beloved mother, Sabinia(?) Felicula, who lived about 76 years, and for their father, Marcus Julius Cupitus, dutiful, who lived 70 years.
EDCS-04001646.summary: A funerary epitaph for Sabinia(?) Felicula and Marcus Julius Cupitus, erected by their sons, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-04001647.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Laelia(?) Tertulla lived sixty years.
EDCS-04001647.summary: A funerary epitaph for Laelia(?) Tertulla, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-04001723.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Caecilius Felix made this for his exceedingly rare wife, Valeria Fortunata, who lived 45 years.
EDCS-04001723.summary: A funerary monument dedicated by Caecilius Felix to his wife, Valeria Fortunata, noting her lifespan.

EDCS-04001724.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Vedia Felicula lived 85 years.
EDCS-04001724.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Vedia Felicula.

EDCS-04001726.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus Helvius F, a veteran, lived 80 years. Maria Quieta [dedicated this].
EDCS-04001726.summary: A funerary monument dedicated by Maria Quieta for Quintus Helvius F, a veteran, noting his lifespan.

EDCS-04001727.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. For Caecilia Marchellina, a devoted wife, who lived 19 years.
EDCS-04001727.summary: A funerary epitaph dedicated to Caecilia Marchellina, noting her age and devotion to her husband.

EDCS-04001728.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Domitia Flava lived 20 years. Valerius made this for his deserving wife.
EDCS-04001728.summary: A funerary monument dedicated by Valerius to his wife, Domitia Flava, noting her lifespan.

EDCS-04001729.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Clodius Felix, dutiful, lived [X] years and 4 months; he lies here.
EDCS-04001729.summary: A funerary epitaph for Clodius Felix, noting his lifespan and burial location.

EDCS-04001730.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. For the deserving Flavius Fortunatus the Numidian, who lived 28 years, his mother made this.
EDCS-04001730.summary: A funerary monument dedicated by the mother of Flavius Fortunatus, a Numidian, noting his lifespan.

EDCS-04001731.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Flavius Saturninus lived 30 years. His father Flavius FII made this for his dutiful son.
EDCS-04001731.summary: A funerary monument dedicated by the father of Flavius Saturninus, noting his lifespan.

EDCS-04001734.translation: Flavius Silvanus made this without the usual plasterwork.
EDCS-04001734.summary: An inscription by Flavius Silvanus concerning the construction method of a monument.

EDCS-04001736.translation: Let the good places be for the good to Aulialicus.
EDCS-04001736.summary: This is a funerary epitaph or boundary marker with a Latin inscription, likely from the Roman era.

EDCS-04001737.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Publius Pontilius Saturninus lived here; he is buried here.
EDCS-04001737.summary: This is a Roman funerary epitaph dedicating the burial place to the deceased Publius Pontilius Saturninus.

EDCS-04001738.translation: On the third Ides of June, the birthday of Saint Varagus and his companions.
EDCS-04001738.summary: This inscription records the feast day of a saint and his companions, likely from the Late Roman or early Christian period.

EDCS-04001743.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Marcus Antonius Gordianus Pius Felix Augustus, pontifex maximus, holding tribunician power for the third time, consul, father of the fatherland, the state of the colony of Hipponium.
EDCS-04001743.summary: This inscription is a dedication by the state of the colony of Hipponium to Emperor Gordian III, dating to his third consulship and tribunician power.

EDCS-04001745.translation: To the Pious, Fortunate, Unconquered Augustus, pontifex maximus, holding tribunician power for the second time, consul, father of the fatherland, proconsul. (LXII)
EDCS-04001745.summary: This inscription is a dedication to an emperor, likely Gordian III, referencing his titles and proconsular year LXV.

EDCS-04001746.translation: To our most noble Caesars, our Flavius Valerius Constantius and Galerius Valerius Maximianus, divine...
EDCS-04001746.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the Roman emperors Constantius I and Maximian, likely from the Tetrarchic period.

EDCS-04001747.translation: To our lords forever Emperors Flavius Theodosius and Flavius Arcadius and Flavius Honorius, Emperors, always August, most unconquered, felicitously.
EDCS-04001747.summary: This is a dedication to the Eastern Roman Emperors Theodosius I, Arcadius, and Honorius, dating to their joint rule in the late 4th or early 5th century.

EDCS-04001748.translation: To our Augustus, the state of the colony of Thubursicensium. (LXII)
EDCS-04001748.summary: This inscription is a dedication by the state of the colony of Thubursicensium to an emperor, possibly Gordian III, referencing proconsular year LXV.

EDCS-04001756.translation: To our lord Flavius Valerius Constantius, most noble Caesar, prince of youth.
EDCS-04001756.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Flavius Valerius Constantius (Constantius I), referred to as Caesar and prince of youth, likely from the Tetrarchic period.

EDCS-04001757.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Emperor Constantine I, likely from the early 4th century.

EDCS-04001758.translation: To our lord Flavius Claudius Constantinus Pius Felix Augustus, our lord Magnvs Decentivs, most noble Caesar, twice. To our lords Flavius Valentinianus and Valens Augusti, twice. To our lord Flavius Gratianus, ever Augustus.
EDCS-04001758.summary: A dedication to multiple Roman emperors and a Caesar, likely from the 4th century CE, mentioning Constantinus (Constantine I or II), Magnvs Decentivs, Valentinianus, Valens, and Gratianus.

EDCS-04001761.translation: To our Emperor Caesar, the unconquered, our lord, Lucius Domitius Alexander, unconquered, pious, fortunate, Augustus.
EDCS-04001761.summary: This is a dedication to the emperor Lucius Domitius Alexander, likely from the period of his reign (308-311 CE).

EDCS-04001762.translation: To our lords, the Perpetual Augusti Valentinianus and Valens, for the 21st time.
EDCS-04001762.summary: This inscription records the counting of years of rule for the emperors Valentinian I and Valens, likely from the period 364-375 CE.

EDCS-04001766.translation: To the Emperor Caesar, Diocletian, unconquered, pious, fortunate, Augustus, chief priest, holding tribunician power for the 4th time, consul, father of the fatherland, proconsul, and to the Emperor Caesar, Marcus Aurelius Valerius Maximian, unconquered, pious, fortunate, Augustus, chief priest, holding tribunician power for the 3rd time, consul, father of the fatherland, proconsul.
EDCS-04001766.summary: This is a joint dedication to Emperors Diocletian and Maximian, likely from their co-reign, possibly around 297-299 CE.

EDCS-04001767.translation: To our Emperor, Galerius Valerius Maximian, unconquered, pious, fortunate, Augustus, for the 187th time.
EDCS-04001767.summary: This inscription records a count related to the emperor Galerius Valerius Maximian, likely from the period 305-311 CE.

EDCS-04001768.translation: To the Emperor Caesar, Marcus Aurelius Valerius Maxentius, unconquered, pious, fortunate, Augustus, and to Flavius Valerius Constantinus, the most noble Caesar.
EDCS-04001768.summary: This inscription honors Emperors Maxentius and Constantine I, likely from the period 307-311 CE.

EDCS-04001770.translation: To our lord, Magnvs Decentivs, the most noble Caesar, for the 9th time.
EDCS-04001770.summary: This inscription records a count related to Caesar Magnvs Decentivs, likely from the period 350-353 CE.

EDCS-04001773.translation: To our lords, Flavius Valerius Constantinus, Germanicus, Sarmaticus, Persicus, and Galerius Maximinu, Sarmaticus, Germanicus, Persicus, and Galerius Valerius, unconquered, pious, fortunate, Augustus, for the 11th time.
EDCS-04001773.summary: This inscription honors multiple emperors including Constantine I, Maximian II (Galerius Maximianus), and Valerius Maximianus, likely from the period 309-311 CE.

EDCS-04001780.translation: To our lords, Constantius Augustus, and Constantius, the most noble Caesar.
EDCS-04001780.summary: This inscription honors Emperor Constantius II and Caesar Constantius Gallus, likely from the period 351-354 CE.

EDCS-04001781.translation: To our Emperor, Constantine the Great, Victor, always Augustus, born for the good of the republic, for the 18th time.
EDCS-04001781.summary: This inscription records a count related to Emperor Constantine I, likely from the period 325-337 CE.

EDCS-04001782.translation: To our lord, Flavius Claudius Julianus, victor and triumphant, always Augustus.
EDCS-04001782.summary: This inscription honors Emperor Julian, likely from the period 361-363 CE.

EDCS-04001794.translation: To the Emperor, our lord, Constantine Maximus Victor, ever Augustus.
EDCS-04001794.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Emperor Constantine, likely on a public monument.

EDCS-04001799.translation: To the Emperor, our lord, Constantine Maximus, ever Augustus, born for the good of the republic.
EDCS-04001799.summary: This inscription honors Emperor Constantine, emphasizing his birth for the public good, probably on a monument.

EDCS-04001801.translation: and to our lords, our lords Flavius Valens Pius Felix Augustus.
EDCS-04001801.summary: This inscription likely records a dedication or acclamation for Emperors Valens and Valentinian, possibly from the late 4th century.

EDCS-04001802.translation: Our lord, Flavius Gratianus, ever Augustus.
EDCS-04001802.summary: This inscription is a title for Emperor Gratian, likely part of a larger dedication or acclamation from the late 4th century.

EDCS-04001806.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Octavia Celsa, dutiful, lived 85 years. She is placed here. Her husband erected [this]. Sacred to the departed spirits. L. Lucutionis, while alive, H.V.C., lived [X?] years.
EDCS-04001806.summary: This funerary inscription records the death and burial of Octavia Celsa and L. Lucutionis, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04001807.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Aurelia Biri, dutiful, lived 30 years.
EDCS-04001807.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Aurelia Biri, probably from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04001808.summary: This is a very brief inscription, likely funerary, recording the existence of Saturninus.

EDCS-04901008.summary: This inscription records a vow made by Istefanus, possibly related to a religious or commemorative act.

EDCS-04901012.text_edition: \n Marcus Aedius Marci filius Teretina Allifis vixit annis LVI militavit annis XXVII centuria Cosconi ossa de Risucade vecta hic situs est\n
EDCS-04901012.translation: Marcus Aedius, son of Marcus, of the Teretina tribe, from Allifae, lived 56 years, served in the army 27 years in the century of Cosconius. His bones were brought from Risucade. He is buried here.
EDCS-04901012.summary: A funerary epitaph for Marcus Aedius, a soldier from Allifae, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-04901013.text_edition: \n Marti Augusto sacrum Publius Caelius Victor sacerdos et Furnia Donatula uxor votum solverunt libentes animo faciendos curaverunt gradus numero IIII\n
EDCS-04901013.translation: Sacred to Mars Augustus. Publius Caelius Victor, priest, and Furnia Donatula, his wife, fulfilled their vow, and gladly took care to have four steps made.
EDCS-04901013.summary: A dedication to Mars Augustus by a priest and his wife, likely from the Imperial period, recording the construction of four steps.

EDCS-04901014.text_edition: \n Marti Augusto sacrum pro salute Impperatorum Caessarum Luci Septimi Severi Pii Pertinacis Augusti et Marci Aureli Antonini Getae Caesaris et Iuliae Augustae matris castrorum Caius Rusticelius Proculus sacerdos pro salute mea et coniugis meae Faoniae Doniatulae et filiorum meorum votum solvi libens animo\n
EDCS-04901014.translation: For the safety of the Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus and Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Geta Caesar and Julia Augusta, mother of the camps. Caius Rusticelius Proculus, priest, paid his vow gladly for the safety of myself and my wife Faonia Doniatula and my sons.
EDCS-04901014.summary: A dedication to Emperor Septimius Severus, his son Geta, and Julia Domna, by a priest for himself, his family, and the emperors, dating to the Severan period (early 3rd century CE).

EDCS-04901015.text_edition: \n Pro salute Imperatoris Septimi Severi Pertinacis Augusti eiusque domus divinae Augustae Iani custodibus domino Saturno Augusto sacrum Asidonius Pilatus Saracinus sacerdos pro salute mea et coniugis meae Cassiae Vinniolae et filiorum meorum in anniversali meo votum solvi libens animo\n
EDCS-04901015.translation: Sacred to Saturn, guardian of Janus, for the safety of the Emperor Septimius Severus Pertinax Augustus and his divine household Augustan. Asidonius Pilatus Saracinus, priest, paid his vow gladly for the safety of myself and my wife Cassia Vinniola and my sons on my anniversary.
EDCS-04901015.summary: A dedication to Saturn by a priest for himself and his family, likely during the reign of Septimius Severus (late 2nd/early 3rd century CE), mentioning a vow made on his anniversary.

EDCS-04901016.translation: The memory of Saint Milichus, bishop. He served God faithfully in the presbyterate for 9 years and in the episcopate for 17 years and 25 days. He rested in peace on the 5th day before the Ides of July.
EDCS-04901016.summary: This inscription is a memorial epitaph for Saint Milichus, a bishop, detailing his service and date of death in the 6th century AD.

EDCS-04901017.translation: Rogatus the faithful lived in peace for 4 years and 2 months. He was laid to rest on the day before the Kalends of April, in the 7th indiction.
EDCS-04901017.summary: This inscription is a funerary epitaph for Rogatus, recording his lifespan and date of burial, likely from the late Roman or early Byzantine period.

EDCS-04901018.translation: Emperor Caesar Augustus, Legion III Augusta.
EDCS-04901018.summary: This inscription identifies Emperor Caesar Augustus and Legion III Augusta, likely marking a building or standard associated with the legion. It is likely from the early imperial period.

EDCS-04901020.text_edition: \n Votum sacro Saturno Rufinus cum suis solvit\n
EDCS-04901020.translation: Rufinus and his household paid their vow to sacred Saturn.
EDCS-04901020.summary: A votive offering to Saturn by Rufinus and his family, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-04901021.text_edition: \n Ennius Felix Marianus solum templo Telluris cum arboribus duabus copressi sic sacratis concessit\n
EDCS-04901021.translation: Ennius Felix Marianus granted the temple of Tellus with its two cypress trees, so consecrated, in its entirety.
EDCS-04901021.summary: This inscription records a private grant of land, including a temple and trees, to the goddess Tellus by Ennius Felix Marianus.

EDCS-04901023.translation: Sacred to Ceres Augusta, Publius Caecilius Faustus Aelianus Baliatho, son of Cai, master of the porticus, arranged for its construction from the ground up at public expense by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-04901023.summary: This is a dedication to Ceres Augusta by Publius Caecilius Faustus Aelianus Baliatho, who funded the construction of a porticus from the ground up, as decreed by the local council. The mention of decurions suggests a date in the imperial period, possibly late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-04901024.translation: Fidelis lived in peace for 70 years. Fidelis lived in peace for 60 years.
EDCS-04901024.summary: This epitaph records the peaceful lives of two individuals named Fidelis, one living to 70 and the other to 60 years of age, likely from the late Roman or early Christian period.

EDCS-04901025.translation: Stefanus lived in peace for 56 years.
EDCS-04901025.summary: This epitaph records that Stefanus lived peacefully for 56 years, likely dating to the late Roman or early Christian period.

EDCS-04901026.translation: In this place rested Menas the innocent, who lived in peace for more or less 7 years.
EDCS-04901026.summary: This epitaph records that Menas, described as innocent, rested here after living for approximately 7 years, likely from the early Christian period.

EDCS-04901027.translation: In this place rested Bictoricus in peace for eighty years.
EDCS-04901027.summary: This epitaph records that Bictoricus rested here in peace, having lived for eighty years, likely from the late Roman or early Christian period.

EDCS-04901028.translation: Cresconius lived in peace for more or less 38 years.
EDCS-04901028.summary: This epitaph records that Cresconius lived peacefully for approximately 38 years, likely dating to the late Roman or early Christian period.

EDCS-04901029.translation: Basilius the presbyter lived in peace for 80 years; he was buried on the Kalends of December, in the second indiction.
EDCS-04901029.summary: This epitaph records that Basilius, a presbyter, lived for 80 years and was buried on December 1st in the second indiction, indicating an early Christian context and a date within a specific imperial reign.

EDCS-04901030.translation: Tribunus the presbyter, by the grace of God, lived in peace for 52 years, in the thirteenth indiction, on the Kalends of August.
EDCS-04901030.summary: This epitaph records that Tribunus, a presbyter, lived for 52 years and died on August 1st in the thirteenth indiction, placing it in the early Christian period and within a specific imperial calendar.

EDCS-04901031.translation: Pascasius the presbyter lived in peace for 60 years. Ianuarius the presbyter lived in peace for 85 years.
EDCS-04901031.summary: This epitaph records the peaceful lives of two presbyters, Pascasius who lived 60 years and Ianuarius who lived 85 years, likely from the early Christian period.

EDCS-04901032.translation: Peregrinus fulfilled his vow to God.
EDCS-04901032.summary: This is a votive inscription by Peregrinus fulfilling a vow to God.

EDCS-04901033.translation: Anastasia, with her community, fulfilled her vow to God.
EDCS-04901033.summary: This is a votive inscription by Anastasia and her community fulfilling a vow to God.

EDCS-04901034.translation: Purpurius fulfilled his vow to God. Purfurius fulfilled his vow to God.
EDCS-04901034.summary: This is a votive inscription, possibly with a duplication, by Purpurius and Purfurius fulfilling vows to God.

EDCS-04901036.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum itemque Quintus Sentius Saturninus equestri dignitate exornatus hoc opus instituit et post vitam eius perpetuo pe\n
EDCS-04901036.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Quintus Sentius Saturninus, honored with equestrian rank, established this work and after his life, perpetually...
EDCS-04901036.summary: This funerary inscription records the establishment of a monument by Quintus Sentius Saturninus, a man of equestrian rank, dedicated to the Divine Shades.

EDCS-04901037.text_edition: \n Marco Aelio Aurelio Caesari consuli II designato III Imperatoris Caesaris Titi Aeli Hadriani Antonini Augusti Pii pontificis maximi tribunicia potestate XXIII imperatoris II consulis IIII patris patriae filio Lucius Sempronius Paetus Nivis ob honorem flamonii perpetui ci filii sui HS III milia legitimae summae item \n
EDCS-04901037.translation: To Marcus Aelius Aurelius Caesar, twice consul and designated consul, son of Imperator Caesar Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Augustus Pius, Pontifex Maximus, in his 23rd year of tribunician power, Imperator II, consul IIII, Father of the Fatherland. Lucius Sempronius Paetus Nivis, for the honor of perpetual flaminate, [donated] 3,000 legitimate sesterces and...
EDCS-04901037.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Marcus Aelius Aurelius Caesar (later Marcus Aurelius) by Lucius Sempronius Paetus Nivis upon receiving the honor of perpetual flaminate, likely dating to the mid-2nd century CE.

EDCS-04901038.text_edition: \n Marti Augusto sacrum pro salute Imperatoris Caesaris divi Marci Antonini Pii Germanici Sarmatici filii divi Commodi fratris divi Pii nepotis divi Hadriani pronepotis divi Traiani Parthici abnepotis divi Nervae adnepotis Luci Septimi Severi Pii Pertinacis Augusti Arabici Adiabenici Parthici maximi et Imperatoris Caesaris Marci Aureli Antonini Augusti et Publi Septimi Getae nobilissimi Caesaris et Iuliae Domnae Augustae matris castrorum Selicius Saturninus Selici Felicis filius ob honorem XIprimatus quem ordo civitatis suae in loco patris eius suffragio detulit ex HS III milibus nummum legitimae summae honorariae adiectis a se HS |(mille) nummum item adiectis a se HS |(mille) D qui fiunt partis suae dimidium de HS III milibus XIprimatus summa honoraria Felicis patris sui defuncti insuper hoc amplius adiecta a se tertia eius summae id est HS D nummum statuae Martis dei quae est ultima pars taxationis HS VI |(milium) nummum sua pecunia fecit idemque dedicavit d(ecreto)? d(ecurionum)\n
EDCS-04901038.translation: Sacred to Mars Augustus. For the safety of Imperator Caesar Lucius Septimius Pius Pertinax Augustus Arabicus Adiabenicus Parthicus Maximus and Imperator Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus and the most noble Caesar Publius Septimius Geta and Julia Domna Augusta, Mother of the Camps. Selicius Saturninus, son of Selicius Felix, for the honor of XIprimatus, which the town council bestowed upon him in his father's place by vote, [paid] 3,000 legitimate sesterces of the honorarium sum, with an additional 1,000 sesterces added by himself, and an additional 1,500 sesterces added by himself, which makes half of the 3,000 sesterces for the honorarium XIprimatus of his deceased father Felix. Furthermore, he additionally contributed a third of this sum, that is, 500 sesterces, for the statue of the god Mars, which is the final part of the valuation of 6,000 sesterces, and he made it with his own money and dedicated it, [by decree] of the decurions.
EDCS-04901038.summary: This inscription records a substantial dedication by Selicius Saturninus to the god Mars and for public honors, made on behalf of the imperial family and for his own magistracy, likely dating to the early 3rd century CE.

EDCS-04901039.translation: To Gnaeus Apertio Gaetulicus, son of Lucius, twice duovir, cereal official of the most splendid colony of Carthage, of singular goodness and innocence, most humane to individuals and the fatherland, who, in addition to what he contributed to the public aqueduct project, further joined another discovered water source by constructing his own work with his own money, and also built a bridge over the river with finely cut stone, a very costly project, to carry the public water; and in addition to all these things, he also made a reservoir for the use of both water supplies and for the adornment of the city from his own funds, and decorated it with marble and mosaic work. For all these generous gifts and munificence, the council decreed that a statue be made from their own contributions to repay his merits, which he himself chose the location for in the forum and erected it with its base, the site having been granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-04901039.summary: This inscription honors Gnaeus Apertio Gaetulicus for his extensive public works, including an aqueduct, bridge, and reservoir, in the colony of Carthage, for which the town council erected a statue in his honor.

EDCS-04901040.translation: Cyprianus the priest lived in peace for 60 years and departed on the 16th day before the Kalends of June.
EDCS-04901040.summary: This funerary inscription records the life and death date of Cyprianus, a priest.

EDCS-04901041.translation: A sinner fulfilled his devotion to God.
EDCS-04901041.summary: This is a votive inscription recording the fulfillment of devotion to God by a sinner.

EDCS-04901042.text_edition: \n Lucio Aelio Aurelio Commodo consuli Imperatoris Caesaris Titi Aeli Hadriani Antonini Augusti Pii patris patriae filio Lucius Manilius Felix ob magistratum ampliata legitima sufetatus summa ex HS milibus nummum posuit decreto decurionum\n
EDCS-04901042.translation: To Lucius Aelius Aurelius Commodus, consul of Imperator Caesar Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Augustus Pius, Father of the Fatherland. Lucius Manilius Felix, for the magistracy, having expanded the legitimate suphate sum, erected [this monument] with 10,000 sesterces, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-04901042.summary: This inscription records the erection of a monument by Lucius Manilius Felix to Lucius Aelius Aurelius Commodus (later Commodus) upon completing a magistracy, likely dating to the reign of Marcus Aurelius.

EDCS-04901043.translation: Felix the deacon lived in peace for 65 years and rested on the 10th day before the Kalends of August.
EDCS-04901043.summary: This funerary inscription records the life and death date of Felix, a deacon.

EDCS-04901044.text_edition: \n Saturno Augusto sacrum civitas Chul sufetatus Caius Lepthini et Mani Senti anni LXXXXI\n
EDCS-04901044.translation: Sacred to Saturn Augustus. The community of Chul, under the suphates Caius Lepthini and Mani Senti, [in the year] 91.
EDCS-04901044.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Saturn Augustus by the community of Chul, mentioning two suphates and a regnal year, likely from North Africa.

EDCS-04901045.text_edition: \n Saturno Augusto sacrum Civitas Chul sufetatus Titi Trebelli Saturnini et Marci Corneli Honorati Iuliani anni LXXXXVIIII\n
EDCS-04901045.translation: Sacred to Saturn Augustus. The community of Chul, under the suphates Titi Trebelli Saturnini and Marci Corneli Honorati Iuliani, [in the year] 99.
EDCS-04901045.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Saturn Augustus by the community of Chul, mentioning two suphates and a regnal year, likely from North Africa and similar to EDCS-04901044.

EDCS-04901046.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Lucius Arulenus Fundanus, a soldier of the First Urban Cohort, in the century of Ti. [---], lived for 55 years and served for [---] years. Annius Flaccus, the heir, made this; he is buried here.
EDCS-04901046.summary: This funerary inscription records the death and military service of Lucius Arulenus Fundanus, a soldier of the First Urban Cohort, with his tomb erected by Annius Flaccus.

EDCS-04901047.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Titus Aelius Eutyches, freedman of Augustus, an official from the records office, originally from Carthage, lived for 54 years, 9 months, and 7 days. Ulpia Elpis made this for her most holy husband; he is buried here.
EDCS-04901047.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Titus Aelius Eutyches, a freedman official from Carthage, with his tomb erected by his wife Ulpia Elpis.

EDCS-04901048.translation: Sacred to Liber Pater Augustus. Marcus Cassius Felix, priest of Liber Pater, restored the idol upon receiving a decree and made the statue of Liber Pater, and placed the altar in the year of the II viri quinquennales Marcus Orfius Clarus and Quintus Terentius Felix. He fulfilled his vow willingly.
EDCS-04901048.summary: This dedication records Marcus Cassius Felix, priest of Liber Pater, restoring a statue and altar, likely in the early 2nd century AD based on the dating by II viri.

EDCS-04901049.text_edition: \n Diti et Saturno Augustis sacrum pro salute Imperatoris Caesaris divi Vespasiani filii Domitiani Augusti Germanici pontificis maximi tribunicia potestate XIII imperatoris XXII consulis XVI censoris perpetui patris patriae civitas Thignicensis templum et basilicam et porticus et cisternam et custodiam sua pecunia facienda curavit\n
EDCS-04901049.translation: Sacred to Dis and Saturn Augustus. For the safety of Imperator Caesar Domitian Augustus Germanicus, son of the deified Vespasian, Pontifex Maximus, in his 13th year of tribunician power, Imperator XXII, Consul XVI, Censor for life, Father of the Fatherland. The community of Thignica took care of the construction of the temple, basilica, porticoes, cistern, and guardhouse with their own funds.
EDCS-04901049.summary: This inscription records the construction of several public buildings by the community of Thignica for the worship of Dis and Saturn, and for the safety of Emperor Domitian, likely dating to the late 1st century CE.

EDCS-04901050.text_edition: \n Publio Septimio Getae Caesari Lucius Clodius Quirina Rufinus statuam quam dum adviveret ex HS IImilibus promiserat adiectis ex testamento eius HS IImilibus nummum Lucius Caecilius Quietus Rufinianus Quintus Caecilius Victor Quintianus Blandius flamines perpetui municipii heredes ampliata pecunia posuerunt idemque dedicaverunt\n
EDCS-04901050.translation: To Publius Septimius Geta Caesar. Lucius Clodius Quirinus Rufinus, who had promised this statue in his lifetime for 2,000 sesterces, with an additional 2,000 sesterces from his will. Lucius Caecilius Quietus Rufinianus, Quintus Caecilius Victor Quintianus Blandius, perpetual flamines of the municipality, as heirs, with the increased funds, erected it and also dedicated it.
EDCS-04901050.summary: This inscription records the erection and dedication of a statue to Publius Septimius Geta Caesar by his heirs, who fulfilled a promised donation that was augmented by his will.

EDCS-04901051.text_edition: \n Deo Silvano Augusto Genio civitatis pro salute Imperatoris Caesaris divi Marci Antonini Pii Germanici fili divi Pii nepotis divi Hadriani pronepotis divi Traiani Parthici abnepotis divi Nervae adnepotis Luci Septimi Severi Pii Pertinacis Augusti Arabici Adiabenici patris patriae pontificis maximi tribunicia potestate III imperatoris VII consulis II procons(ulis) Castricius Rogatianus Silvani SCI filius ornandae patriae causa fecit et in testamento suo HS II(milia) DV suis legavit ut ob dedicationem universis decurionibus sportulas praestarent\n
EDCS-04901051.translation: To the god Silvanus Augustus, and the Genius of the state, for the health of the Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus, son of the deified Marcus Antoninus Pius Germanicus, grandson of the deified Pius, great-grandson of the deified Hadrian, great-great-grandson of the deified Trajan Parthicus, great-great-great-grandson of the deified Nerva, father of the country, Pontifex Maximus, holding tribunician power for the 3rd time, Imperator for the 7th time, Consul for the 2nd time, Proconsul. Castricius Rogatianus, son of Silvanus, made this for the adornment of his fatherland and bequeathed 2,500 sesterces in his will to his freedmen, so that for the dedication they might receive gifts. The date is inferable from Severus' titulature.
EDCS-04901051.summary: This inscription records a public works dedication to the god Silvanus and the Genius of the state, funded by Castricius Rogatianus, and includes a bequest for future celebrations, likely dating to the reign of Septimius Severus.

EDCS-04901052.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Lucius Venidius Repostus miles legionis III Augustae centuria Antoni Clementis vixit annis XXXXV hic situs est\n
EDCS-04901052.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Lucius Venidius Repostus, a soldier of the III Augusta legion, in the century of Antonius Clemens, lived 45 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-04901052.summary: This is a tombstone for Lucius Venidius Repostus, a soldier in the III Augusta legion, who died at age 45.

EDCS-04901053.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Cassius Iscoesius Valens miles cohortis II Flaviae equitatae pius vixit nnos XXXII Anicius Celer Andronicus commilito et contibernalis sic libens fecit hic situs est\n
EDCS-04901053.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Cassius Iscoesius Valens, a soldier of the II Flavia equitata cohort, a dutiful man, lived 32 years. Anicius Celer Andronicus, a fellow soldier and tent-mate, willingly made this. He is buried here.
EDCS-04901053.summary: This tombstone records the death of Cassius Iscoesius Valens, a soldier in the II Flavia equitata cohort, who died at age 32, and was erected by his comrade and tent-mate.

EDCS-04901054.translation: To Antoninus Augustus, prefect of the II Flavia Equitata Cohort.
EDCS-04901054.summary: This is a dedication to Antoninus Augustus, who served as prefect of the II Flavia Equitata Cohort.

EDCS-04901056.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription referring to the will of a prefect.

EDCS-04901057.text_edition: \n Lucius Obulcius miles legionis III Augustae centuria Sallusti vixit nnos \n
EDCS-04901057.translation: Lucius Obulcius, a soldier of the III Augusta legion, in the century of Sallustius, lived [lacuna] years.
EDCS-04901057.summary: This is a fragmentary tombstone for Lucius Obulcius, a soldier in the III Augusta legion, recording his name and unit but not his lifespan.

EDCS-04901058.translation: Lucius Iulius Niger, son of Devilius, a horseman from Vienna, is buried here.
EDCS-04901058.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Iulius Niger, identified as an equestrian from Vienna, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04901059.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Lucius Volaseina Honoratus miles legionis III Augustae centuria Cressi pius vixit annos XXI hic situs est\n
EDCS-04901059.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Lucius Volaseina Honoratus, a soldier of the III Augusta legion, in the century of Cressus, a dutiful man, lived 21 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-04901059.summary: This tombstone records the death of Lucius Volaseina Honoratus, a soldier in the III Augusta legion, who died at the age of 21.

EDCS-05000782.text_edition: \n Vanammoni Augusto sacrum Aurelius Varixen ordinarius qui ex fortia et suffragio vexillationi profecit ex voto a solo extruxit libens animo\n
EDCS-05000782.translation: Sacred to Vanammon Augustus. Aurelius Varixen, an ordinary official, who advanced with strength and by selection to the detachment, erected this from the ground according to his vow, with a willing heart.
EDCS-05000782.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated by Aurelius Varixen, an official, to the god Vanammon Augustus, likely related to his military service or promotion.

EDCS-05000783.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Silvanus, (?) a freedman.
EDCS-05000783.summary: This is a funerary dedication to the Manes, mentioning Silvanus, possibly a freedman, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05000785.translation: In the estate of Flavius Faustinus.
EDCS-05000785.summary: This inscription possibly marks property belonging to Flavius Faustinus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05000787.translation: Deacon Lucilianus was accepted on the fourteenth day before the Kalends of October in the seventh year of our lord King Gunthamund.
EDCS-05000787.summary: This inscription records the reception of a deacon named Lucilianus on a specific date in the 7th regnal year of King Gunthamund, likely indicating a Vandalic period inscription in North Africa.

EDCS-05000794.translation: To Avidius Vitalis, daughter of Caius, perpetual priestess of the colony of Concordia Julia Karthago, Gnaeus Salvius Saturninus, perpetual priest, [erected this] for her merits.
EDCS-05000794.summary: This is a dedication honoring Avidius Vitalis, a perpetual priestess of Carthage, by Gnaeus Salvius Saturninus, a perpetual priest, for her merits, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05000795.translation: Prompted by the happy times of our lords Valens, Gratian, and Valentinian, ever invincible Augusti, I, Publicius Felix Hortensius, priest and curator of the republic, restored and dedicated the Rostra to adorn the fatherland, bringing them into a better state.
EDCS-05000795.summary: This inscription records the restoration and dedication of the Rostra by Publicius Felix Hortensius, a priest and curator, during the reigns of Emperors Valens, Gratian, and Valentinian, likely in the late 4th century CE.

EDCS-05000796.translation: Prompted by the happy times of our lords Valens, Gratian, and Valentinian, I, Publicius Felix Hortensius, perpetual priest and curator of the republic, restored and dedicated the Rostra to adorn the fatherland, bringing them into a better state.
EDCS-05000796.summary: This inscription records the restoration and dedication of the Rostra by Publicius Felix Hortensius, a perpetual priest and curator, during the reigns of Emperors Valens, Gratian, and Valentinian, likely in the late 4th century CE.

EDCS-05000797.translation: Prompted by the happy times of our lords Valens, Gratian, and Valentinian, ever invincible Augusti, I, Publicius Felix Hortensius, perpetual priest and curator of the republic, restored and dedicated the Rostra to adorn the fatherland, bringing them into a better state.
EDCS-05000797.summary: This inscription records the restoration and dedication of the Rostra by Publicius Felix Hortensius, a perpetual priest and curator, during the reigns of Emperors Valens, Gratian, and Valentinian, likely in the late 4th century CE.

EDCS-05000798.translation: Prompted by the happy times of our lords Valens, Gratian, and Valentinian, ever invincible Augusti, I, Publicius Felix Hortensius, perpetual priest and curator of the republic, erected the eternal city of Rome's Rostra.
EDCS-05000798.summary: This inscription records the erection of the Rostra of Rome by Publicius Felix Hortensius, a perpetual priest and curator, during the reigns of Emperors Valens, Gratian, and Valentinian, likely in the late 4th century CE.

EDCS-05000800.translation: Faithful Miccina lived in peace for 11 years and rested on the 18th day before the Kalends of February.
EDCS-05000800.summary: This inscription records the lifespan and death date of a woman named Miccina, who lived for 11 years.

EDCS-05000801.translation: Fortuna the innocent lived in peace for [an unspecified number of] years.
EDCS-05000801.summary: This inscription records the lifespan of a person named Fortuna, who lived in peace.

EDCS-05000802.translation: Stercul the innocent lived in peace for 15 months and died on the 16th day before the Kalends of February.
EDCS-05000802.summary: This inscription records the lifespan and death date of a person named Stercul, who lived for 15 months.

EDCS-05000803.summary: This inscription is a simple dedication or epitaph for a person named Victoria.

EDCS-05000804.translation: Italica lived in peace for 35 years and departed on the ninth day before the Kalends of May.
EDCS-05000804.summary: This inscription records the lifespan and death date of a woman named Italica, who lived for 35 years.

EDCS-05000805.translation: Caesaria lived in peace for 56 years and departed on the sixth day before the Kalends of November.
EDCS-05000805.summary: This inscription records the lifespan and death date of a woman named Caesaria, who lived for 56 years.

EDCS-05000806.translation: Faithful Ancilla lived in peace for 73 years and rested on the ninth day before the Kalends of April.
EDCS-05000806.summary: This inscription records the lifespan and death date of a woman named Ancilla, who lived for 73 years.

EDCS-05000807.translation: Exsitiosa lived in peace for 70 years and rested on the third day before the Kalends of September.
EDCS-05000807.summary: This inscription records the lifespan and death date of a woman named Exsitiosa, who lived for 70 years.

EDCS-05000810.translation: Donatus was received [into the community/family?], lived for 62 years, and died on the 16th day before the Kalends.
EDCS-05000810.summary: This inscription records the lifespan and death date of a person named Donatus, who lived for 62 years.

EDCS-05000811.translation: Miccina lived in peace for 60 years and rested on the fifth day before the Kalends of August.
EDCS-05000811.summary: This inscription records the lifespan and death date of a woman named Miccina, who lived for 60 years.

EDCS-05000812.translation: Buccellicus the deacon lived in peace for 50 years and rested on the third day before the Kalends of December.
EDCS-05000812.summary: This epitaph records the life and repose of Buccellius, a deacon, who died in the peace of the church.

EDCS-05000814.translation: Bennius Paternus, his heir, made this for the well-deserving. He is buried here. He lived for about 50 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-05000814.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Bennius Paternus, erected by his heir, and notes his lifespan of approximately 50 years.

EDCS-05000815.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Delius Felicissimus avunculus dulcissimus vixit annis LVI mense I diebus XVI\n
EDCS-05000815.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Delius Felicissimus, a most beloved uncle, lived 56 years, 1 month, and 16 days.
EDCS-05000815.summary: This tombstone records the death of Delius Felicissimus, an uncle, who died at the age of 56 years, 1 month, and 16 days.

EDCS-05000816.translation: Licinius Bassus, son of Publius, pious, lived for 43 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-05000816.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Licinius Bassus, son of Publius, who lived for 43 years.

EDCS-05000818.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Lucius Amicaius, son of Amatus, pious, lived for 90 years. He set up and made this tomb for himself.
EDCS-05000818.summary: This tomb inscription records Lucius Amicaius, son of Amatus, who lived for 90 years and dedicated the tomb for himself.

EDCS-05000821.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Marcus Sextilius Peregrinus, pious, lived for 3 years and 6 months, for his most beloved son.
EDCS-05000821.summary: This inscription, dedicated to the underworld spirits, records the early death of Marcus Sextilius Peregrinus, who lived for 3 years and 6 months.

EDCS-05000823.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Alexandria pia vixit plus minus annos XXVIII quod fuit scriptum debitum communem reddidit cui Galata Augusti nostri verna dispensator marmorum Numidicorum alumnae merenti fecit\n
EDCS-05000823.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Alexandria the dutiful lived approximately 28 years. She paid the common debt owed. Galata, a slave of our Emperor and a freedman steward of Numidian marble, made this for his deserving foster-child.
EDCS-05000823.summary: This tombstone commemorates Alexandria, who died at about 28 years old, and was erected by her foster-father, a steward in the imperial administration.

EDCS-05200641.translation: lius Iannus lived for 10 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-05200641.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Iannus (with a partial name prefix) who lived for 10 years.

EDCS-05200642.translation: To the goddess Juno Caelestis, Respectus [dedicated this?].
EDCS-05200642.summary: This is a dedication to the goddess Juno Caelestis, likely by a person named Respectus.

EDCS-05200643.translation: Fabbatia Ianuaria, pious, lived for 62 years and 2 months. May your bones rest well, and may the earth be light upon you.
EDCS-05200643.summary: This epitaph for Fabbatia Ianuaria, who lived 62 years and 2 months, includes a wish for her peaceful repose.

EDCS-05200644.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Co di lived for [---] years, months, days.
EDCS-05200644.summary: This incomplete epitaph is dedicated to the underworld spirits and records the lifespan of 'Co di' in years, months, and days.

EDCS-05200645.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Lurius Casius lived for 67 years, 8 months, and 8 days.
EDCS-05200645.summary: This inscription, dedicated to the underworld spirits, records the lifespan of Lurius Casius as 67 years, 8 months, and 8 days.

EDCS-05200646.translation: Innocens Teofanius lived in peace for 5 years, buried on the 6th day of May, indiction VIII. Reader, pray with the sign of the cross.
EDCS-05200646.summary: This is a Christian funerary inscription recording the lifespan and burial date of Innocens Teofanius.

EDCS-06000003.summary: This is a dedication to the personification of Concord, possibly a shrine or honorific inscription.

EDCS-06000004.translation: To the fruitful Genius of Augustus, Iunius Crescens [dedicated this].
EDCS-06000004.summary: This is a dedication by Iunius Crescens to the Genius of Augustus, likely from the imperial period.

EDCS-06000009.translation: To Jupiter Optimus Maximus, Quintus Aemilius Aristides, legal official for Alexandria.
EDCS-06000009.summary: This is a dedication to Jupiter by Quintus Aemilius Aristides, who held a legal office in Alexandria, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-06000010.summary: This is a dedication to the deity Sol Invictus, popular in the Roman Empire, particularly the 3rd century.

EDCS-06000011.translation: Aemilius Sa fulfilled his vow to Lord Silvanus.
EDCS-06000011.summary: This is a votive inscription by Aemilius Sa dedicated to the god Silvanus.

EDCS-06000012.translation: Flavius Bon, scribe, fulfilled his vow to his masters.
EDCS-06000012.summary: This is a votive inscription by Flavius Bon, an official (exceptor), dedicating to his superiors or patron deities.

EDCS-06000016.translation: To the deified Trajan, the father [of the fatherland].
EDCS-06000016.summary: This is an inscription honoring the deified Emperor Trajan, likely from a public monument.

EDCS-06000019.text_edition: \n Divae Faustinae Imperatoris Caesaris Titi Aeli Hadriani Antonini Augusti Pii\n
EDCS-06000019.translation: To the deified Faustina, wife of the Emperor Caesar Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Augustus Pius.
EDCS-06000019.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription dedicated to the deified Empress Faustina, wife of Emperor Antoninus Pius.

EDCS-06000021.translation: To the Emperor Caesar, son of the deified Antoninus, brother of the deified Verus, conqueror of the Parthians, grandson of the deified Hadrian, great-grandson of the deified Trajan Parthicus, descendant of the deified Nerva, Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus, pontifex maximus, with tribunician power for the 24th time, imperator for the 5th time, consul for the 3rd time, father of the fatherland, two statues which Anicia Pudentilla ordered to be erected in her will for 30,000 sesterces, [paid for by] Manlia Macrina, mother and heir, adding 8,000 sesterces, with Gaius Manilius Manilianus, her son-in-law, overseeing the work.
EDCS-06000021.summary: This is a complex inscription from the reign of Marcus Aurelius, detailing imperial titles and the funding and erection of two statues by Anicia Pudentilla and Manlia Macrina, overseen by Manilius Manilianus.

EDCS-06000024.text_edition: \n Marco Annio Vero Augusti filio Lucio Aurelio Commodo Augusti filio Lucillae Augustae\n
EDCS-06000024.translation: To Marcus Annius Verus, son of Augustus, to Lucius Aurelius Commodus, son of Augustus, [and] to Lucilla Augusta.
EDCS-06000024.summary: This inscription records dedications to Marcus Aurelius (as Caesar), Commodus (as Caesar), and Lucilla, likely from the mid-to-late 2nd century CE.

EDCS-06000027.text_edition: \n Fadillae Augusti filiae Cornificiae Augusti filiae Faustinae Augusti filiae\n
EDCS-06000027.translation: To Faustina, daughter of Augustus, daughter of Cornificia, daughter of Augustus, daughter of Faustina, daughter of Augustus.
EDCS-06000027.summary: This inscription is a dedication likely to an imperial woman, possibly Faustina the Younger, given the triple filiation.

EDCS-06000035.translation: To Germanicus Caesar, for the 8th time consul.
EDCS-06000035.summary: This is an inscription honoring Germanicus Caesar, likely an honorific dedication or part of a building, noting his eighth consulship.

EDCS-06000037.summary: This is a fragmented inscription likely referring to the deified emperor Septimius Severus.

EDCS-06000038.translation: To the Emperor Caesar, son of Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pius
EDCS-06000038.summary: This is a fragmented inscription likely part of a dedication to Emperor Septimius Severus.

EDCS-06000040.translation: To Julia Domna Augusta, mother of the Augusti and of the camps, by the people of the colony of Sabratha, on behalf of Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus.
EDCS-06000040.summary: This inscription is a public dedication by the people of Sabratha to Julia Domna, mother of emperors, likely during the reign of Septimius Severus.

EDCS-06000046.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Severus Alexander Pius Felix Augustus, pontifex maximus, holder of tribunician power for the 10th time, consul for the 3rd time, father of the country, proconsul. Tonius Aemilianus erected this in recognition of the honor of the augurship, beyond 10,000 sesterces for the highest honorary sum, and the stipends given to the decurions for the dedication.
EDCS-06000046.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Tonius Aemilianus to Emperor Alexander Severus, commemorating the honor of the augurship and related expenses, likely in the 230s CE.

EDCS-06000051.text_edition: \n Marco Iulio Philippo nobilissimo Caesari Pio Felici Augusto principi iuventutis domino nostro Imperatoris Caesaris Marci Iuli Philippi Pii Felicis Augusti domini nostri filio Sabrathenses publice\n
EDCS-06000051.translation: To Marcus Julius Philippus, most noble Caesar, Pious, Fortunate, Augustus, prince of youth, our lord, son of the Emperor Caesar Marcus Julius Philippus, Pious, Fortunate, Augustus, our lord. The people of Sabratha publicly [dedicated this].
EDCS-06000051.summary: This is a public dedication from the people of Sabratha to Emperor Philip the Arab and his son.

EDCS-06000052.text_edition: \n Quinto Herennio Etrusco Messio Decio filio Augusti domini nostri tribunicia [potestate ------\n
EDCS-06000052.translation: To Quintus Herennius Etruscus Messius Decius, son of Augustus, our lord, [holding] tribunician power for the [number]th time. [...]
EDCS-06000052.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Quintus Herennius Etruscus Messius Decius, a co-emperor with Decius.

EDCS-06000053.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari Publio Licinio Gallieno Pii Felici Augusto domino nostro pontifici maximo tribunicia potestate XIIII consuli VI designato VII patri patriae proconsuli et Corneliae Saloninae Augustae coniugi Gallieni Augusti Sabrathenses publice\n
EDCS-06000053.translation: To Emperor Caesar Publius Licinius Gallienus, Pious, Fortunate, Augustus, our lord, chief priest, holding tribunician power for the 14th time, consul for the 6th time, designated consul for the 7th time, father of the country, proconsul, and to Cornelia Salonina Augusta, wife of Gallienus Augustus. The people of Sabratha publicly [dedicated this].
EDCS-06000053.summary: This is a public dedication from the people of Sabratha to Emperor Gallienus and his wife Cornelia Salonina.

EDCS-06000058.text_edition: \n Aedem Liberi Patris quam antiqua ruina cum labe PIVS instaurationem EARISO ddominorum nnostrorum Flavi Iuli Constantii maximi et Flavi Iuli Constantis maximi triumphatorum semper Augustorum amrimum praesidicium viri perfectissimi Flavi Victoris Calpurni servavit hanc Lucius Aemilius Caelestinus duovir quinquennalis flamen perpetuus amori patriae studiose respondita viro perfectissimo patrono provinciae dedicanteR fecit ex decreto ordinis\n
EDCS-06000058.translation: Lucius Aemilius Caelestinus, duovir quinquennalis, perpetual priest, dedicated this temple of Liber Pater, which the ancient ruin with its collapse had destroyed, and which the most excellent Flavius Victor Calpurnius, a guard of our lords Flavius Julius Constantius, greatest triumphant Augustus, and Flavius Julius Constans, greatest triumphant Augustus, had preserved with affection and the greatest protection, out of love for his country, responding eagerly to the most excellent Flavius Victor Calpurnius, patron of the province, by decree of the council.
EDCS-06000058.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a restored temple of Liber Pater by Lucius Aemilius Caelestinus, a local magistrate, likely during the reign of Constantius II and Constantius Gallus.

EDCS-06000060.translation: To our lord Valentinian, most victorious, Augustus of the whole world, perpetual founder of celestial justice and piety and Roman happiness, Antonius Dracontius, most distinguished man, acting on behalf of the prefects of the praetorium for the African provinces, has always dedicated himself to his divine will and majesty.
EDCS-06000060.summary: This inscription is a dedication by Antonius Dracontius to Emperor Valentinian I, praising his virtues and expressing his own devotion, likely in the late 4th century CE.

EDCS-06000061.translation: To our lord Valens, most victorious, Augustus of the whole world, perpetual founder of celestial justice and piety and Roman happiness, Antonius Dracontius, most distinguished man, acting on behalf of the prefects of the praetorium for the African provinces, has always dedicated himself to his divine will and majesty.
EDCS-06000061.summary: This inscription is a dedication by Antonius Dracontius to Emperor Valens, praising his virtues and expressing his own devotion, likely in the late 4th century CE.

EDCS-06000066.translation: To the grandson, holder of tribunician power
EDCS-06000066.summary: This is a fragmented inscription likely part of a larger dedication, referring to an emperor's grandson who held tribunician power.

EDCS-06000073.summary: This is a fragmented inscription, a dedication to an emperor addressed as 'Pius Felix', likely from the Severan period or later.

EDCS-06000079.text_edition: \n invicti Augusti pontificis maximi Germanici maximi tribunicia potestate \n
EDCS-06000079.translation: [holding] tribunician power. [...] of the unconquered Augustus, chief priest, greatest Germanicus.
EDCS-06000079.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription that refers to an emperor's titles, likely from the 3rd century AD.

EDCS-06000081.summary: This is a very short inscription dedicating something to an emperor named Aurelius Augustus.

EDCS-06000090.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription mentioning honorific titles of an emperor.

EDCS-06000101.text_edition: \n Caio Anicio Quirina Frontoni equo publico ornato Anici Bassiani filio quaestori aedili IIviro IIviro quinquennali designato amatori patriae cives ob merita curante Quinto Flavio Hiceta\n
EDCS-06000101.translation: To Gaius Anicius Fronton, son of Anicius Bassianus, of the voting tribe Quirina, honored with the public equestrian rank, quaestor, aedile, duovir, designated duovir quinquennalis, lover of his country. Erected by the citizens because of his merits, under the supervision of Quintus Flavius Hicetas.
EDCS-06000101.summary: This inscription honors Gaius Anicius Fronton, a prominent local official, and records his career and posthumous recognition by the citizens.

EDCS-06000102.text_edition: \n Avitio Quinti filio Quirina (tribu) Rufo tribuno militum legionis VII geminae felicis praefecto cohortis I Augustae Thracum proximo tertiae militiae IIviro decreto ordinis ob merita eius erga rem publicam eximia Quintus Avitius Lucanus pater titulo et honore contentus sua pecunia posuit\n
EDCS-06000102.translation: Quintus Avitius Lucanus, the father, content with the title and honor, placed this at his own expense to Avitius Rufus, son of Quintus, of the voting tribe Quirina, tribune of the soldiers of the seventh legion Gemina Felix, prefect of the first cohort of Thracians Augusta, recently holding the third military command, duovir, by decree of the council, because of his outstanding merits towards the state.
EDCS-06000102.summary: This inscription records the erection of a monument by a father for his son, Quintus Avitius Rufus, a military officer and local magistrate, honoring his military service and civic career.

EDCS-06000106.text_edition: \n DEM statuam co curante Calpurnio viro perfectissimo praeside provinciae Tripolitanae\n
EDCS-06000106.translation: A statue, erected under the supervision of Calpurnius, most excellent man, governor of the province of Tripolitana.
EDCS-06000106.summary: This inscription records the erection of a statue, dedicated to Calpurnius, the governor of Tripolitana, by an unknown individual or group.

EDCS-06000109.text_edition: \n Flavi Vivi Benedicti viri perfectissimi totius integritatis moderationis iustitiae provisionis fidei benignitatis fortitudinis ac beneficentiae viro Flavio Vivio Benedicto viro perfectissimo praesidi provinciae Tripolitanae inter cetera beneficia sua quibus omnem provinciam conpendiis sic remediis et virtutibus fovit sublevabit erexit etiam ob ea quae sibi specialiter conlata sunt civitas Sabrathensis exsultans quod post ruinam et abnegatum thermarum populo exercitium citra ullius dispendium ornamentis patriae revocavit ordo populusque concinentibus omnibus votis statuam patrono praestantissimo gratanti studio conlocavit Dedicata consulum dominorum nostrorum Valentis VI et Valent<in>iani II Augustorum die V Kalendas Augustas\n
EDCS-06000109.translation: To Flavia Vivi Benedicta, a man of utmost integrity, moderation, justice, foresight, loyalty, kindness, strength, and beneficence, and to Flavia Vivi Benedicto, a man of utmost excellence, governor of the province of Tripolitana. In addition to his other benefits, with which he fostered and supported the entire province through efficiencies, remedies, and virtues, the city of Sabratha also rejoiced, elevating him because of these special honors bestowed upon him. As after the ruin and denial of exercise in the baths to the people, he restored the ornaments of the fatherland without any loss, the council and the people, with all their wishes in unison, placed a statue for their most outstanding patron with jubilant zeal. Dedicated under the consulship of our lords Valens VI and Valentinian II Augusti, on the fifth day before the Kalends of August.
EDCS-06000109.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a statue to the governor Flavia Vivi Benedicto by the city of Sabratha, celebrating his restoration of public bath facilities and general good governance, dating to the consulship of Valens VI and Valentinian II.

EDCS-06000110.translation: The council and people of the colony of Sabratha publicly set up this monument to [---]tius, a most perfect man of integrity, [---] for the order and people of the colony of Sabratha, under the care of Gaius Aurelius Felicissimus Damasius, perpetual flamen and priest of the god Hercules, quinquennial curator of the state, successfully.
EDCS-06000110.summary: This inscription records the erection of a monument by the council and people of Sabratha to a distinguished official named [---]tius, likely during the 3rd or 4th century CE, highlighting his integrity and service.

EDCS-06000111.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription, likely recording the title or honorific of a 'vir perfectissimus' and mentioning his parentage or origin.

EDCS-06000114.text_edition: \n Dis manibus sacrum Varigata Lucius Munatius Dexter veteranus pius vixit annis LV ossa tibi bene quiescant terra tibi levis sit hic situs est\n
EDCS-06000114.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Varigata, Lucius Munatius Dexter, a pious veteran, lived 55 years. May your bones rest well; may the earth lie lightly on you. Here he is buried.
EDCS-06000114.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Munatius Dexter, a veteran, recording his name, status, age at death, and a wish for his peaceful rest.

EDCS-06000115.text_edition: \n Ulpiano V sagittario natione nus nnos plus minus directo anni curante Flavio P\n
EDCS-06000115.translation: To Ulpianus, a sagittary (archer) by nation, with... more or less [X] years, under the supervision of Flavius P...
EDCS-06000115.summary: This fragment likely records the dedication of a monument or honors to Ulpianus, an archer, specifying his nationality and age, and naming Flavius P as supervisor.

EDCS-06000117.translation: The council and people of the splendid colony of Sabratha, according to the decrees of the whole province, dedicated this to Lucius Aemilius Quintus, perpetual flamen, for the continuous labor he sustained for the needs of his province and for bringing common miseries to the sacred ears and deserving a remedy, under the care of Flavius Venantius.
EDCS-06000117.summary: This inscription records a dedication by the people of Sabratha to Lucius Aemilius Quintus, a perpetual flamen, for his significant efforts in addressing provincial needs and reporting problems, likely in the late 2nd or early 3rd century CE.

EDCS-06000119.text_edition: \n Publio o Publi filio Galeria (tribu) Maximo Numerio Avito V G C V rarissimo Sabrathenses publice patrono \n
EDCS-06000119.translation: To Publius o Publi son, of the Galeria tribe, Maximus Numerius Avitus, most excellent man, most rare, from the people of Sabratha, publicly, as patron.
EDCS-06000119.summary: This inscription honors Publius o Publi filio Galeria Maximo Numerio Avito as a patron of the people of Sabratha, describing him as a 'most excellent' and 'most rare' man.

EDCS-06000120.text_edition: \n Aurelius Flacianus P sacerdotalis scola felix et cum uiveret moreretur fuit fil vixit annis L\n
EDCS-06000120.translation: Aurelius Flacianus P, priest of the college, happy, both when alive and when dying, his son lived 50 years.
EDCS-06000120.summary: This inscription records the life and death of Aurelius Flacianus P, a priest, mentioning his son's age at death and implying a posthumous dedication.

EDCS-06000121.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription mentioning a son of Cornelius and the office of aediles.
