EDCS-06000447.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Publius Licinius Gallienus Germanicus Pius Felix Augustus, chief priest, Germanicus Maximus, with tribunician power for the 13th time, Imperator for the 12th time, Consul for the 6th time, Father of the Fatherland, Proconsul, and to Cornelia Salonina, our most sacred Augusta, wife of Gallienus Augustus, from the people of Lepcis Septimiani Saloniniani.
EDCS-06000447.summary: This inscription dedicates honors to Emperor Gallienus and Empress Salonina from the people of Lepcis, dating to approximately 265-268 AD based on titles.

EDCS-06000451.text_edition: \n Publio Cornelio Licinio Valeriano nobilissimo Caesari Lepcitani Septimiani publice\n
EDCS-06000451.translation: To Publius Cornelius Licinius Valerianus, most noble Caesar, from the people of Lepcis Septimiani.
EDCS-06000451.summary: This inscription dedicates honors to Caesar Valerianus II (likely Gallienus' son) from the citizens of Lepcis.

EDCS-06000452.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that likely honored a Publius Cornelius, with the rest of the text missing.

EDCS-06000453.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari Marco Aurelio Caro Pio Felici invicto Augusto pontifici maximo tribunicia potestate II consuli II patri patriae proconsuli Lucius Iulius Paulinus vir clarissimus proconsul \n
EDCS-06000453.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Carus Pius Felix unconquered Augustus, chief priest, with tribunician power for the 2nd time, Consul for the 2nd time, Father of the Fatherland, Proconsul, from Lucius Julius Paulinus, most distinguished man, proconsul.
EDCS-06000453.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Emperor Carus by Lucius Julius Paulinus, the proconsul, likely in 282-283 AD.

EDCS-06000454.text_edition: \n Fortissimis et invictissimis imperatoribus ddominis nnostris Marco Flavio Valerio Constantio Pio Felici invicto Augusto et Caio Galerio Valerio Maximiano Pio Felici invicto Augusto Lepcitani devoti numini maiestatique eorum publice\n
EDCS-06000454.translation: To our most brave and unconquered Lords Emperors Marcus Flavius Valerius Constantius Pius Felix unconquered Augustus and Gaius Galerius Valerius Maximianus Pius Felix unconquered Augustus, from the people of Lepcis, devoted to their divine majesty.
EDCS-06000454.summary: This inscription honors Emperors Constantius I and Maximian, dedicated by the citizens of Lepcis, likely dating to the Tetrarchy period (late 3rd to early 4th century AD).

EDCS-06000455.translation: To our lord, the unconquered and most noble Caesar Flavius Valerius Severus, the people of Lepcis Minor devoted to his divine power and majesty, publicly [dedicated this].
EDCS-06000455.summary: A public dedication by the people of Lepcis Minor to Caesar Flavius Valerius Severus.

EDCS-06000456.text_edition: \n Indulgentissimo ac libertatis restitutori victoriosissimoque imperatori domino nostro Maxentio Pio Felici invicto Augusto Valerius Alexander vir perfectissimus agens vices praefecti praetorio numini maiestatique eius dicatissimus\n
EDCS-06000456.translation: To our most indulgent and restorer of liberty, most victorious Emperor, our Lord Maxentius Pius Felix unconquered Augustus, from Valerius Alexander, most perfect man, acting in place of the praetorian prefect, devoted to his divine majesty.
EDCS-06000456.summary: This inscription dedicates honors to Emperor Maxentius by Valerius Alexander, acting praetorian prefect, likely from the early 4th century AD.

EDCS-06000457.text_edition: \n Indulgentissimo ac libertatis restitutori victorioriosissimoque Imperatori domino nostro Maxentio Pio Felici Invicto Augusto Volusius Donatianus vir perfectissimus praeses provinciae Tripolitanae numini maiestatique eius dicatissimus\n
EDCS-06000457.translation: To our most indulgent and restorer of liberty, most victorious Emperor, our Lord Maxentius Pius Felix Unconquered Augustus, from Volusius Donatianus, most perfect man, governor of the province of Tripolitana, devoted to his divine majesty.
EDCS-06000457.summary: This inscription dedicates honors to Emperor Maxentius by Volusius Donatianus, governor of Tripolitana, likely from the early 4th century AD.

EDCS-06000459.text_edition: \n Cum basilica vetus ex maxima parte ruina esset deformata conlabsu sic ac spatio sui breviasset aream forensem divino icta conflagrarat incendio adque is locus saeculo fortunatissimo meliora deposceret tantae stragis labe sublata tripertita porticus magnitudine sui ac Troadensium columnarum adornata operis provincialium ac sumptu publico disponente Laenatio Romulo viro perfectissimo rectore provinciae intra anni spatium perfecta ac dedicata est adque ad sempiternam memoriam statuam marmoream suo numine radiantem domino nostro Constantino maximo victori semper Augusto idem vir perfectissimus dicata mente constituit curante Claudio Aurelio Generoso viro egregio curatore rei publicae et splendidissimo ordine coloniae Lepcimagnensium\n
EDCS-06000459.translation: Since the old basilica was in ruins for the most part and had become deformed, and its space had been diminished by the fire that had struck it with divine force and the forum area, and since that place demanded better things in the most fortunate age, with such a ruin removed, a portico with three aisles, adorned with its size and the workmanship of Phrygian columns and provincial work, was completed and dedicated within the space of a year at public expense, under the administration of Laenatius Romanus, most perfect man, governor of the province; and for eternal memory, the same most perfect man erected a marble statue radiant with his divine power to our lord Constantine the Great Victorious Always Augustus, under the supervision of Claudius Aurelius Generosus, most excellent man, curator of the republic, and the most splendid order of the colonus of Lepcimagnesium.
EDCS-06000459.summary: This long inscription details the reconstruction of a basilica and the dedication of a statue to Constantine the Great by governor Laenatius Romanus and others in Lepcimagnesium, completed within a year, likely in the early 4th century AD.

EDCS-06000463.translation: Marcus Nicentius, an outstanding man, prefect of the province of Tripolitana, devoted to his divine power and majesty, dedicated this with his great piety, as the most just governor of all laws, to our lord Flavius Julius Constantius, ever victorious Augustus, together with the people of Lepcis Minor.
EDCS-06000463.summary: A dedication by Marcus Nicentius, prefect of Tripolitana, to Emperor Constantius II.

EDCS-06000464.translation: Antonius Dracontius, a most distinguished man, acting in place of the praetorian prefect throughout the African provinces, always most devoted to their divine power and majesty, dedicated this to our lords Valentinian and Valens, the most victorious princes and Augusti of the whole world, [who are] founders of justice and piety, and of eternal Roman happiness.
EDCS-06000464.summary: A dedication by Antonius Dracontius, acting prefect of the praetorian guard, to Emperors Valentinian I and Valens.

EDCS-06000465.translation: Antonius Dracontius, a most distinguished man, acting in place of the praetorian prefect throughout the African provinces, always most devoted to their divine power and majesty, dedicated this to our lords Valentinian and Valens, the most victorious princes and Augusti of the whole world, [who are] founders of justice and piety, and of eternal Roman happiness.
EDCS-06000465.summary: A dedication by Antonius Dracontius, acting prefect of the praetorian guard, to Emperors Valentinian I and Valens.

EDCS-06000467.translation: With the glory of the Roman name flourishing and under the fortune of our lords, princes, and forever Augusti, Valens, Gratian, and Valentinian, and wherever they conquer, the faithful and innocent council of Lepcimagnensis, with its most outstanding people, dedicated this with all their vows to Flavius Nicomachus, a most distinguished man, acting at that time in place of the praetorian prefect through the African provinces, the most esteemed patron of the flourishing age of the Flavians.
EDCS-06000467.summary: A dedication by the council and people of Lepcimagnensis to Flavius Nicomachus, acting prefect, honoring the emperors Valens, Gratian, and Valentinian.

EDCS-06000468.translation: The council of Lepcis Minor, devoted to his divine power and majesty, set this up for our lord Flavius Theodosius, the pious, fortunate, ever victorious Augustus, the propagator of the Roman world and conservator of the public order.
EDCS-06000468.summary: A monument set up by the council of Lepcis Minor for Emperor Theodosius I, honoring his role as propagator of the Roman world.

EDCS-06000469.translation: To our lord Flavius Arcadius, pious, fortunate, ever victorious and triumphant Augustus, consul for the whole world in peace, the people of Lepcis Minor, devoted to his divine power and majesty.
EDCS-06000469.summary: A dedication by the people of Lepcis Minor to Emperor Arcadius, who is honored as consul for the peaceful world.

EDCS-06000470.translation: To our lord Flavius Honorius, pious, fortunate, ever victorious and triumphant Augustus, consul for the whole world in peace, the people of Lepcis Minor, devoted to his divine power and majesty.
EDCS-06000470.summary: A dedication by the people of Lepcis Minor to Emperor Honorius, who is honored as consul for the peaceful world.

EDCS-06000471.translation: In the most flourishing ages of our lords Honorius and Theodosius, ever perpetual Augusti, the most distinguished and noble council and the most outstanding people of Lepcimagnensis publicly [dedicated this] to Flavius Ortygius, a most distinguished and notable man, count and duke of the province of Tripolitana, for his distinguished merits and the labor and faithfulness shown in the suppression of the revolt of the Austurians.
EDCS-06000471.summary: A public dedication by the council and people of Lepcimagnensis to Flavius Ortygius, count and duke of Tripolitana, for his military achievements during the reigns of Honorius and Theodosius.

EDCS-06000474.translation: To Caesar VDIALISQV, son of Lucius Poli.
EDCS-06000474.summary: An inscription recording a dedication to Caesar VDIALISQV, son of Lucius Poli.

EDCS-06000485.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription mentioning Emperor Marcus Aurelius.

EDCS-06000486.summary: This inscription likely records the name of Emperor Antoninus, possibly in a dedicatory or honorific context, dating to the Antonine period (2nd century AD).

EDCS-06000490.summary: This inscription fragment mentions the deified Emperor Marcus Aurelius, suggesting a monument or dedication related to him, likely from the late 2nd century AD.

EDCS-06000494.summary: This inscription fragment likely refers to the deified Emperor Nerva, possibly as part of a dedication or title, dating from the period after his reign (from 98 AD onwards).

EDCS-06000499.translation: The people of Lepcis, most devoted to his divine will...
EDCS-06000499.summary: This inscription records a public dedication by the people of Lepcis to the divine will of an emperor, likely from the imperial period.

EDCS-06000502.summary: This inscription fragment mentions 'Augustus', referring to an emperor, possibly in a context of 'our emperor', dating to the imperial period.

EDCS-06000503.summary: This inscription fragment includes the epithet 'Pius Felix' (Devout and Fortunate), commonly associated with Roman emperors, likely referring to one from the 2nd or 3rd century AD.

EDCS-06000504.summary: This inscription fragment contains the beginning of the imperial epithet 'Pius Felix', suggesting a reference to an emperor, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century AD.

EDCS-06000505.summary: This inscription fragment mentions someone as the 'son of Augustus', possibly referring to a deified emperor or a descendant, dating to the imperial period.

EDCS-06000506.summary: This inscription fragment refers to 'our lord Pius Felix', a common imperial titulature, likely dating to the 3rd century AD.

EDCS-06000507.text_edition: \n VS Liberatori orbis ac RLepcitani devoti numini maiestatique eius\n
EDCS-06000507.translation: ...Liberator of the world and the people of Lepcis, devoted to his divine will and majesty...
EDCS-06000507.summary: This inscription records a dedication by the people of Lepcis to an emperor, hailed as the 'Liberator of the world', emphasizing their devotion to his divine authority, likely from the imperial period.

EDCS-06000509.text_edition: \n Marcus Annius Messalla adlectus in senatum a divo a divo Vespasiano legatus Africae\n
EDCS-06000509.translation: Marcus Annius Messalla, appointed to the Senate by the deified Vespasian, governor of Africa.
EDCS-06000509.summary: This inscription records the career of Marcus Annius Messalla, who served as governor of Africa after being appointed to the Senate by Emperor Vespasian.

EDCS-06000510.text_edition: \n Marcus Annius Messalla adlectus in senatum a divo a divo Vespasiano legatus Africae\n
EDCS-06000510.translation: Marcus Annius Messalla, appointed to the Senate by the deified Vespasian, governor of Africa.
EDCS-06000510.summary: This inscription records the career of Marcus Annius Messalla, who served as governor of Africa after being appointed to the Senate by Emperor Vespasian.

EDCS-06000511.text_edition: \n Marco Atilio Metilio Braduae Caucidio Tertullo Claudio Attico Vibullio Pollioni Gavidio Latiari Atrio Basso proconsuli Decimus Iunius Crescens Decimus Iunius Galba Quintus Calpurnius Capito Lucius Plautius Octavianus patrono\n
EDCS-06000511.translation: To Marcus Atilius Metilius Bradua Cauccidius Tertullus Claudius Atticus Vibullius Pollio Gavidius Latiaris Atrius Bassus, proconsul, by Decimus Iunius Crescens, Decimus Iunius Galba, Quintus Calpurnius Capito, Lucius Plautius Octavianus, his patron.
EDCS-06000511.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Marcus Atilius Metilius Bradua Cauccidius Tertullus, a proconsul, likely honoring his service, by several individuals including his patron.

EDCS-06000513.text_edition: \n Elpidii Omnium virtutum praedicabili viro et supra documenta bonitatis insigni adque magnifico Caecilio Severo viro clarissimo agenti vices praeffectorum praetorio ob multiformem iudiciorum eius in se moderationem ex decreto et sufragio M Lepcitani publice\n
EDCS-06000513.translation: To Caecilius Severus, a man of the highest distinction, acting on behalf of the prefects of the Praetorian Guard, for his multifaceted moderation in his judgments concerning him, publicly by the decree and vote of Lepcis, a man of all virtues, praiseworthy, and outstanding and magnificent beyond measure for his goodness.
EDCS-06000513.summary: This inscription honors Caecilius Severus, who acted in place of the Praetorian prefect, for his judicial moderation, with a public dedication from Lepcis.

EDCS-06000514.text_edition: \n Cnaeus Calpurnius Cnaei filius Piso consul pontufex sic proconsul\n
EDCS-06000514.translation: Gnaeus Calpurnius Piso, son of Gnaeus, consul, pontiff, proconsul.
EDCS-06000514.summary: This inscription lists the high offices held by Gnaeus Calpurnius Piso, including consul, pontiff, and proconsul.

EDCS-06000515.text_edition: \n Lucius Caninius Luci filius Gallus XVvir sacris faciundis consul proconsul patronus dedicavit\n
EDCS-06000515.translation: Lucius Caninius Gallus, son of Lucius, appointed to the XVviri sacris faciundis, consul, proconsul, patron, dedicated this.
EDCS-06000515.summary: This inscription records Lucius Caninius Gallus, who held multiple prestigious religious and political offices, as the dedicator of a monument.

EDCS-06000516.text_edition: \n Claudio A proconsuli provinciae Africae omnium virtutum viro innocentis integritatis vicoratae lenitatis sublimis moderationis laudavilis sic iustitiae Lepcimagnenses ex decreto ordinis patrono perpetuo\n
EDCS-06000516.translation: To Claudius, proconsul of the province of Africa, a man of all virtues, of innocent integrity, victorious gentleness, sublime moderation, praiseworthy justice, by Lepcimagnenses, by decree of the council, his perpetual patron.
EDCS-06000516.summary: This inscription honors Claudius, proconsul of Africa, for his virtues and justice, with a dedication from the people of Lepcimagnenses who acclaimed him their perpetual patron.

EDCS-06000517.translation: Gaius Cornelius Rarus Sextius Na, consul, quindecimvir for sacred rites, proconsul of the province of Africa.
EDCS-06000517.summary: This inscription lists the offices held by Gaius Cornelius Rarus Sextius Na, including consul and proconsul of Africa, likely for a monument honoring him.

EDCS-06000518.text_edition: \n Caio Fulvio Plautiano praefecto praet[orio] Marcus Cornelius Bassus Servianus egregiae memoriae vir fieri iussit Cornelia Servianilla clarissima femina filia et heres posuit\n
EDCS-06000518.translation: To Gaius Fulvius Plautianus, prefect of the Praetorian Guard, Marcus Cornelius Bassus Servianus, a man of exceptional memory, ordered it to be made; Cornelia Servianilla, a woman of the highest distinction, his daughter and heir, placed it.
EDCS-06000518.summary: This monument was ordered by Marcus Cornelius Bassus Servianus and erected by his daughter and heir, Cornelia Servianilla, in honor of Gaius Fulvius Plautianus, the Praetorian prefect.

EDCS-06000519.translation: Crispus, a most distinguished young man, by his most distinguished uncle, erected this from the will of his mother, Sextilla, by decree of the most splendid order.
EDCS-06000519.summary: This inscription records the erection of a monument by Crispus in honor of his uncle, motivated by his mother's will and an order of the local council.

EDCS-06000520.translation: The client order, together with the people, eternally established for Decimus Hesperius, a most distinguished man, former proconsul of the province of Africa, judge of sacred cases, a descendant honored for his dignity and growing glory through steps and merits, in honor of the justice which he displayed in the delicate cause of the Tripolitani by sacred judgment, a most excellent patron, the order and people of Lepcis Magna erected this.
EDCS-06000520.summary: This inscription records the erection of a monument by the order and people of Lepcis Magna to honor Decimus Hesperius, a former proconsul and judge, for his distinguished service and justice, particularly in the case of the Tripolitani.

EDCS-06000523.translation: The splendid order and the entire people of Lepcis Magna decreed and established for Flavius Macidonius Patricius, a most distinguished man, with outstanding virtue, admirable equity, and moderate temperance, defender of justice, vindicator of the innocent, a count and duke of the province of Tripolitana, a worthy patron.
EDCS-06000523.summary: This inscription records the decree by the people of Lepcis Magna to honor Flavius Macidonius Patricius, a count and duke, as their worthy patron for his virtues and service.

EDCS-06000524.text_edition: \n Dimittendus in splendidissimam coloniam Leptim Magnam iussu Fulvi Plautiani clarissimi viri praefecti praetorio ac necessari dominorum nostrorum\n
EDCS-06000524.translation: He is to be dismissed into the most splendid colony of Leptis Magna by order of Fulvius Plautianus, a man of the highest distinction, prefect of the Praetorian Guard and confidant of our lords.
EDCS-06000524.summary: This inscription records an order by Fulvius Plautianus, a Praetorian prefect, regarding the dismissal of someone to the colony of Leptis Magna.

EDCS-06000526.text_edition: \n Gaio Gavio Macro legato pro praetore III Lepcitani publice\n
EDCS-06000526.translation: To Gaius Gavius Macro, legate with the power of a proconsul, publicly by the Lepcitani.
EDCS-06000526.summary: This inscription is a public dedication by the people of Lepcis to Gaius Gavius Macro, who served as a legate with proconsular authority.

EDCS-06000527.translation: To Quintus Granius Caelestinus, most distinguished man, quaestor, most splendid senator, and Quintus Granius Nummius Gaetulicus and Tuticius M, by permission of the order.
EDCS-06000527.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Quintus Granius Caelestinus and others, likely by a local order, possibly for their senatorial or quaestorian roles.

EDCS-06000529.text_edition: \n Proscaenium columnis et marmoribus ex HS CCducentibus milibus a Marcio Vitale itemque ex HS CCCtrecentibus milibus a Iunio Galba in eam rem datis item tetrastylis lacunarum pecunia publica exornatum dedicatum est Lucio Hedio Rufo Lolliano Avito proconsule Caio Vibio Gallione Claudio Severo legato\n
EDCS-06000529.translation: The stage building, adorned with columns and marble and a money grant of 200,000 sesterces from Marcius Vitalis, and likewise with 300,000 sesterces from Junius Galba, with its coffered ceilings decorated by the state treasury, was dedicated under the proconsul Lucius Hedius Rufus Lollianus Avitus and the legate Gaius Vibius Gallio Claudius Severus.
EDCS-06000529.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a theater's stage building, funded by private donations and public money, under the proconsul and legate.

EDCS-06000530.summary: This fragmentary inscription likely records a dedication or action performed by Lucius Hedius Rufus Lollianus Avitus.

EDCS-06000532.text_edition: \n Proculus legatus pro praetore dedicavit Caius Maecius Cnaei filius Falerna Flaccus sua pecunia fecit\n
EDCS-06000532.translation: Proculus, legate with praetorian power, dedicated [this monument], which Gaius Maecius Flaccus, son of Cnaeus, from the Falernian tribe, made at his own expense.
EDCS-06000532.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a monument built at private expense by Gaius Maecius Flaccus, commissioned by Proculus, a legate with praetorian power.

EDCS-06000534.text_edition: \n Caius Rubellius Blandus proconsul Marcus Etrilius Lupercus legatus pro praetore \n
EDCS-06000534.translation: Gaius Rubellius Blandus, proconsul, and Marcus Etrilius Lupercus, legate with praetorian power.
EDCS-06000534.summary: This inscription simply lists the names and titles of two officials, likely a proconsul and a legate.

EDCS-06000535.translation: To Publius Septimius Geta, most distinguished man, member of the board of fifteen for judging lawsuits, broad-striped tribune of the II Augusta legion, quaestor of the province of Crete and Cyrene, aedile of the grain supply, curator of the public affairs of Ancona, praetor with the hastarium and tutelary magistracy, fetial priest, legate of the I Italica legion, proconsul of Sicily, legate of the Augusti with proconsular authority of the province of Lusitania, consul, legate of the Augusti with proconsular authority of the province of Lower Moesia, legate of the Augusti with proconsular authority of the provinces of Dacia. The Dacian curia erected this in fulfillment of a vow.
EDCS-06000535.summary: This inscription details the extensive career of Publius Septimius Geta, listing numerous high-ranking military and administrative positions, and records its erection by the Dacian curia in fulfillment of a vow.

EDCS-06000536.translation: To Lucius Silis Amicus Haterianus, most distinguished man, curator and patron, by the Oeenses publicly.
EDCS-06000536.summary: This inscription records a public dedication by the people of Oeum to Lucius Silis Amicus Haterianus, honoring him as curator and patron.

EDCS-06000537.text_edition: \n Curni Lucio Volusio Basso Caereali clarissimo viro et consulari curatori rei publicae suae quae sic inter cetera opera quae industria et labore maximo renovavit Ulpiam basilicam cum ORVS in meliorem faciem publico sumptu restituit gratiam afferentes Lepcitani publice \xce\x9b\xe1\xbd\xb3\xcf\x80\xce\xba\xce\xb9\xcf\x82 \xe1\xbc\xa1 \xce\x9c\xce\xb5\xce\xb3\xe1\xbd\xb1\xce\xbb\xce\xb7 \xcf\x86\xce\xb9\xce\xbb(\xce\xb5)\xe1\xbf\x96 \xcf\x83\xce\xb5 \xe1\xbf\xac\xe1\xbd\xbd\xce\xbc\xce\xb7 Genio coloniae Lepcis Magnae Crescentina fecit\n
EDCS-06000537.translation: The people of Lepcis Magna, bringing gratitude, dedicated to Lucius Volusius Bassus Cerealis, a most distinguished man and consular, the curator of their republic, who, among other works, renewed the Ulpian Basilica with great industry and effort, restoring it to a better appearance at public expense, [and to the] Genius of the colony of Lepcis Magna, Crescentina made [this].
EDCS-06000537.summary: This inscription records the restoration of the Ulpian Basilica and a dedication to Lucius Volusius Bassus Cerealis and the Genius of Lepcis Magna, executed by Crescentina at public expense.

EDCS-06000538.text_edition: \n Lucio Volusio Basso Cereali clarissimo viro legato totius innocentiae et aequitatis et consimilis moderationis viro Lepcimagnenses ex decreto ordinis municipi et patrono perpetuo\n
EDCS-06000538.translation: To Lucius Volusius Bassus Cerealis, a most distinguished man, legate, a man of all innocence, equity, and similar moderation, the people of Lepcis Magna, by decree of the town council and as perpetual patron.
EDCS-06000538.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Lucius Volusius Bassus Cerealis, honoring him as a legate and patron of Lepcis Magna for his moderation and justice.

EDCS-06000543.summary: This fragmentary inscription likely refers to an individual who held the offices of consul and proconsul.

EDCS-06000549.translation: ...of the province of Africa, candidate of the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus, Parthicus Maximus, Germanicus, Sarmaticus.
EDCS-06000549.summary: This fragmentary inscription identifies an individual as a candidate of Emperor Marcus Aurelius Antoninus for a position in the province of Africa.

EDCS-06000551.translation: S. who is most illustrious, and V. most illustrious.
EDCS-06000551.summary: A very brief inscription, possibly a dedication or a greeting between two highly ranked individuals.

EDCS-06000552.translation: To the most distinguished man, acting in place of the praetorian prefects for the African provinces, the council and people of Lepcis Magna decreed that a marble statue be erected to him, in addition to the guest-token, so that the memory of his incomparable benefits might be passed down to posterity, and because of his preservation of justice and moderation through many trials.
EDCS-06000552.summary: This inscription records the decision by the council and people of Lepcis Magna to erect a marble statue to an official acting as governor for the African provinces, honoring his benefits and just rule.

EDCS-06000553.text_edition: \n Dulciti Aurelio Sempronio Sereno equiti Romano principali Alexandriae ob insigne et admirabile studiorum ingenium praeter deccurionatuum honorem et statuam apud se conlocatam etiam apud Lepcimag[nenses ------ clarissimo viro agenti vices praefectorum praetorio per Africanas provincias Lepcimagnensis ordo et populus ut incomparabilium beneficiorum eius memoria etiam ad posteros mitteretur praeter <h=K>ospitalem tesseram etiam statuam marmoream constituendam esse duxerunt ut servati moderatione iudiciorum eius ac multis tempestatibus to \n
EDCS-06000553.translation: To Dulcitius Aurelius Sempronius Serenus, a Roman knight, a principal official in Alexandria, for his remarkable and admirable intellectual talent, in addition to the honor of a decurionate and a statue erected there, also to [the most distinguished man] acting in place of the praetorian prefects for the African provinces, the council and people of Lepcis Magna decreed that a marble statue be erected to him, in addition to the guest-token, so that the memory of his incomparable benefits might be passed down to posterity, and because of his preservation of justice and moderation through many trials.
EDCS-06000553.summary: This inscription records the erection of a marble statue to Dulcitius Aurelius Sempronius Serenus for his talents and to an official acting as governor of the African provinces for his benefits and justice.

EDCS-06000555.text_edition: \n Consentii Lucio Domitio Iusto Aemiliano equiti Romano viro perfectissimo curatori rei publicae ob eximium amorem in patriam et cives ex decreto ordinis et suffragiis populi civi karissimo Lepcitani publice Quintii flaminis perpetui sacerdotalis Ob meritum laboris et legationis perfectae Lucio Aemilio Quinto flamini perpetuo sacerdotali ordo splendidissimus civitatis Lepcimagnensium dedit\n
EDCS-06000555.translation: To Lucius Domitius Iustus Aemilianus, a Roman knight, a most accomplished man, curator of the republic, the people of Lepcis, publicly, as their dearest citizen, for his exceptional love for his homeland and citizens, by decree of the council and by vote of the people. To Quintus, perpetual flamen and priest, for his merit of labor and perfect legation, the most distinguished council of the city of Lepcis Magna gave [this].
EDCS-06000555.summary: This inscription honors Lucius Domitius Iustus Aemilianus, a curator, and Quintus, a perpetual flamen and priest, for their service and love for the city of Lepcis.

EDCS-06000556.translation: To Flavius Archontius Nilus, most perfect man, count and president of the province of Tripolitana, our best patron, for his outstanding vigilance and counsel at home and abroad, his exceptional integrity, his particular justice and moderation in judgments, his most provident role as restorer of public works and protector of the safety of all citizens, his most friendly guardianship of truth, honor, and loyalty, the people of Lepcis Magna, grateful for his infinite benefits by which they were supported and revived, either individually or with the entire province, have unanimously decreed a second statue for him and, on account of his exceptional merit and singular excellence, have had it erected in the Severian Forum for the eternal memory of posterity.
EDCS-06000556.summary: A statue erected by the people of Lepcis Magna to Flavius Archontius Nilus, president of Tripolitana, for his excellent administration and benefits to the city, likely dating to the 3rd or 4th century CE.

EDCS-06000558.text_edition: \n Heraclii Benignissimo viro principali prudentissimo et integ<e=I>rrimo Tito Flavio Frontino Heraclio viro perfectissimo auguri sacerdoti Laurentium Labinatium sic IIviro ob diversarum voluptatum exhibitiones adque admirabilem ludorum editionem amoremque incomparabilem in patriam et cives suos sufragio quietissimi populi et decreto splendidissimi ordinis \n
EDCS-06000558.translation: To Heraclius, a most benignant man, a principal official, most prudent and most upright, and to Titus Flavius Frontinus Heraclius, a most accomplished man, augur, priest of the Laurentes Labinati, and IIvir of Laurentum, because of his provision of various pleasures and his admirable staging of games and incomparable love for his homeland and citizens, by vote of the most peaceful people and decree of the most distinguished council.
EDCS-06000558.summary: This inscription is a dedication by the people and council to Heraclius and Titus Flavius Frontinus Heraclius, honoring them for public entertainment, games, and their love for the city.

EDCS-06000559.inscription_type: inscriptiones christianae, tituli honorarii, tituli operum
EDCS-06000559.text_edition: \n Nepotianii Flavio Nepotiano viro perfectissimo comiti et praesidi provinciae Tripolitanae iustitia et integritati sic praecipuo moderatione ac benignitate praestantissimo abstinentiae et honestatis officiorumque omnium cultori rei etiam militaris peritissimo armis consiliisque inconparabili sic quod idem ordines universosque provinciales iuridicendo fide benivolentia multis beneficiis cumulaverit quod barbarorum insolentiam exercitio scientiae militaris adtriberit quod limitis defensionem tuitionemque perpetuam futuris etiam temporibus munitam securamque ab omni hostile incursione praestiterit quod civitatum moenia operum instauratione vel novitate decoraverit ordo civitatis Lepcimagnensis cum populo statuam marmoream ob haec merita decretis et sufragiis concin<n>entibus conlocavit\n
EDCS-06000559.translation: The council of the city of Lepcis Magna, with the people, erected a marble statue to Flavius Nepotianus, a most accomplished man, count and governor of the province of Tripolitana, outstanding in justice and integrity, distinguished in moderation and kindness, a cultivator of abstinence and all duties, very skilled also in military matters, incomparable in arms and counsel, who has overwhelmed the orders and all provincials with his juridical skill, benevolence, and many benefits; who has attributed the insolence of barbarians to the exercise of his military knowledge; who has provided for the defense and perpetual protection of the border, secured and safe from any hostile incursion for future times; who has adorned the city walls with the restoration or novelty of works, because of these merits, by unanimous decrees and votes.
EDCS-06000559.summary: This inscription records the erection of a marble statue by the council and people of Lepcis Magna to Flavius Nepotianus, governor of Tripolitana, honoring his justice, military skill, and contributions to city defenses and infrastructure.

EDCS-06000560.text_edition: \n Petasii Eximiae integritatis et inconparabilis prudentiae ac totius bonitatis viro Flavio Petasio viro perfectissimo ex praesidibus provinciae Tripolitanae ordo splendidissimae civitatis Lepcimagnensis decreto suo et populi sufragiis memor meritorum in se ab eius praestantia conlatorum statuam in foro novo Severiano ad perpetuitatis memoriam patrono dignissimo posuit\n
EDCS-06000560.translation: The council and people of the most illustrious city of Lepcimagna erected this statue in the new Severian Forum to Flavis Petasius, a man of exceptional integrity, incomparable prudence, and all goodness, a most accomplished man and former governor of the province of Tripolitana, as a memorial to his merits bestowed upon them by his excellence, to their most worthy patron.
EDCS-06000560.summary: This is a civic honorific statue erected by the city of Lepcimagna to a former governor, Flavis Petasius, for his merits.

EDCS-06000561.text_edition: \n Heraclii Uno eodemque anno duumviro Lepcimagnensium et sacerdoti provinciae Tripolitanae innocentissimo viro principali integerrimo amatori patriae ac civium suorum Tito Flavio Vibiano viro perfectissimo flamini perpetuo et pontifici curatori rei publicae Lepcimagnensium sacerdoti Laurentium Labinatium sic et sacerdoti Matris Deum praefecto omnium sacrorum ob diversarum voluptatum exhibitionem et Libycarum ferarum X ex populi sufragio et ordin(is) decreto\n
EDCS-06000561.translation: Titus Flavius Vibianus, a most innocent man, most upright principal, lover of his country and citizens, a most accomplished man, perpetual flamen and pontiff, curator of the public affairs of Lepcimagna, priest of the Laurentes Labinates, and priest of the Mother of the Gods, prefect of all sacred rites, who in one and the same year served as chief magistrate of Lepcimagna and priest of the province of Tripolitana, [this monument is erected] by popular vote and decree of the council in recognition of his exhibition of various pleasures and ten beasts from Libya.
EDCS-06000561.summary: This inscription honors Titus Flavius Vibianus, a prominent local official and priest, for his service and entertainment provided to the community, likely with a statue or similar monument.

EDCS-06000562.translation: To Heraclius, for his numerous merits and exceptional love for his country and its citizens, [erected by] Titus Flavius Vibianus, most perfect man, pontiff, perpetual flamen, priest of the Mother of the Gods of Laurentum Lavinatium, prefect of all sacred rites, duovir, and priest of the province of Tripolitana, also here by the vote of the people and the decree of the most splendid order.
EDCS-06000562.summary: An inscription honoring Heraclius and Titus Flavius Vibianus, likely a dedication from the 3rd or 4th century CE, highlighting their religious and civic roles in Tripolitana.

EDCS-06000563.translation: To Flavius Victorianus, count throughout Africa, for his praiseworthy integrity and benevolent vigor, his singular justice, because, on account of his tempering of judgments with moderation, he restored the territory, exhausted by the excessive incursions of barbarians and by the watchfulness of... [restored text, likely regarding military service]..., also for the people of Lepcis Magna.
EDCS-06000563.summary: A dedication to Flavius Victorianus, count of Africa, commending his justice and administrative actions in restoring territory damaged by barbarian incursions, likely from the 3rd or 4th century CE.

EDCS-06000564.translation: Dedicated by Benedictus, a most perfect man, on the 6th day before the Ides of June, during the consulship of our lords Valens VI and Valentinian II Augustus. To Flavius Vivius Benedictus, most perfect man, president of the province of Tripolitana, steadfast interpreter of justice, supporter of the innocent, avenger of liberty, punisher of all wrongdoers, the most splendid order of the city of Lepcis Magna [erected this statue] as a worthy patron and patron.
EDCS-06000564.summary: A dedication from the Lepcis Magna city council to their patron Flavius Vivius Benedictus, president of Tripolitana, for his justice and defense of the innocent, dating to the consulship of Valens and Valentinian II (likely 365 CE).

EDCS-06000565.text_edition: \n [[]] [[]] [[]] [[]] [[]] praefecto vehiculorum procuratori XX hereditatium fratri pio Fulvia Nepotilla soror cum Quinto Fulvio Didabibuliano marito et Quinto Fulvio Didabibuliano et Quinto Fulvio Severo Iuniore sacerdotio Caeninense ornato liberis posuit\n
EDCS-06000565.translation: Fulvia Nepotilla, his sister, with her husband Quintus Fulvius Didabibulianus, and her sons Quintus Fulvius Didabibulianus and Quintus Fulvius Severus the Younger, adorned with the priesthood of Caenina, erected [this monument] to [---], prefect of transport, procurator of twenty estates, her pious brother.
EDCS-06000565.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by a woman and her sons for her brother, a prefect of transport and procurator, honoring his public roles and family relationship.

EDCS-06000566.translation: Julius Ho, most perfect man, from Cirta.
EDCS-06000566.summary: A very brief inscription identifying Julius Ho, a highly ranked individual from Cirta, possibly a tombstone or a dedication.

EDCS-06000567.text_edition: \n Romulii ob tantam moderationem iudiciorum provisionesque saluberrimas adque felicitatem adventus eius Laenatio Romulo viro perfectissimo praesidi provinciae Tripolitanae sufragio quietissimi populi et decreto splendidissimi ordinis sumptibus suis posuit\n
EDCS-06000567.translation: Laenatius Romulus, a most accomplished man and governor of the province of Tripolitana, erected [this monument] at his own expense, by the vote of the most peaceful people and the decree of the most illustrious council, because of his great moderation in judgments, his most beneficial foresight, and the felicity of his arrival.
EDCS-06000567.summary: This inscription records the erection of a monument by the citizens of an unnamed city to Laenatius Romulus, their governor, in recognition of his good governance and beneficial presence.

EDCS-06000568.text_edition: \n Flavianii Omnium virtutum experientissimo viro ingenitae mansuetudinis et benignitate patientiae pollenti iudiciorum aequissimo moderatori antistiti innocentiae Magnio Aspero Flaviano viro perfectissimo praesidi provinciae Tripolitanae Lepcimagnenses ob eius amorem in se conlatum et integritatem perpensae sic sibi cognitam patrono dignissimo famae et gloriae perpetuum testimonium posuerunt\n
EDCS-06000568.translation: The people of Lepcimagna erected this everlasting testimony of fame and glory to their most worthy patron, Magnius Asper Flavianus, a most accomplished man and governor of the province of Tripolitana, most experienced in all virtues, abounding in innate gentleness and kindness of patience, fairest moderator of judgments, prelate of innocence, for his bestowed love and integrity recognized by them.
EDCS-06000568.summary: The citizens of Lepcimagna erected a monument to Magnius Asper Flavianus, their governor, to honor his virtues and his love and integrity towards the city.

EDCS-06000569.text_edition: \n Inachii Omnium virtutum viro Publicio Valeriano viro perfectissimo ex praesidibus singularis integritatis et moderationis Lepcimagnenses patrono praestantissimo posuerunt\n
EDCS-06000569.translation: The people of Lepcimagna erected [this monument] to their most outstanding patron, Publicius Valerianus, a man of all virtues, a most accomplished man and former governor of singular integrity and moderation.
EDCS-06000569.summary: The people of Lepcimagna erected a monument to their patron, Publicius Valerianus, a former governor esteemed for his virtues, integrity, and moderation.

EDCS-06000570.text_edition: \n Obsequii Caio Valerio Vibiano viro perfectissimo praesidi provinciae Tripolitanae singularis aequitatis et beniboli sic vicoris sic M omnium virtutum viro ob tunc incipientem deinceps iugem erga se eius dignationem ordo splendidissimus Lepcimagnensium et populus patrono ex decreto splendidissimi ordinis posuerunt\n
EDCS-06000570.translation: The most illustrious council and people of Lepcimagna erected [this monument] to their patron, Gaius Valerius Vibianus, a most accomplished man and governor of the province of Tripolitana, a man of singular fairness and kindness, a victor in contests, a man of all virtues, by decree of the most illustrious council, because of his then-beginning and thereafter continuous favor towards them.
EDCS-06000570.summary: The city of Lepcimagna and its council erected a monument to their patron, Governor Gaius Valerius Vibianus, in gratitude for his ongoing favor and esteemed virtues.

EDCS-06000571.text_edition: \n Amelii Multiplici laborum merito varioque voluptatum genere stimulantibus paternis avitiis etiam documentis ab ineunte aetate patriam civesque suos promerenti Marco Vibio Anniano Gemino viro perfectissimo flamini perpetuo pontifici sacerdotali provinciae Tripolitanae bis IIviro ex sufragio quietissimi populi et decreto splendidissimi ordinis\n
EDCS-06000571.translation: Marcus Vibius Annianus Geminus, a most accomplished man, perpetual flamen, pontiff, priest of the province of Tripolitana, twice chief magistrate, [this monument is erected] by the vote of the most peaceful people and the decree of the most illustrious council, for his many merits in labors and his diverse kind of pleasures, urged on by ancestral examples and for his service to his country and citizens from his early age.
EDCS-06000571.summary: This inscription records the erection of a monument by the people and council to Marcus Vibius Annianus Geminus, a prominent local official and priest, honoring his public service, honors, and dedication from a young age.

EDCS-06000572.text_edition: \n Aemiliae Lychnidi Clementillae Aemili Arriani Caeciliani duoviralici pontificis filiae Lucius Volusius Gallus eques Romanus pontifex duoviralis flamen perpetuus ob insignem adfectionis castitatem matri Volusiorum Appianillae Bassi et Cerealis filliorum suorum permissu splendidissimi ordinis posuit\n
EDCS-06000572.translation: Lucius Volusius Gallus, a Roman knight, pontiff, chief magistrate, perpetual flamen, erected [this monument] with the permission of the most illustrious council to his mother, Aemilia Lychnis Clementilla, daughter of Aemilius Arrianus Caecilianus, a duovir and pontiff, and to his mother Volusia Appianilla Bassus and Cerealis, his sons, for her outstanding affection and chastity.
EDCS-06000572.summary: Lucius Volusius Gallus erected a monument to his mother, Aemilia Lychnis Clementilla, honoring her affection and chastity, and also including his sons in the dedication.

EDCS-06000577.translation: To the departed spirits. Marcus Cornelius Saturninus, soldier of the Third Augustan Legion, lived for 35 years.
EDCS-06000577.summary: A tombstone inscription for Marcus Cornelius Saturninus, a soldier of the Legio III Augusta, who died at the age of 35.

EDCS-06000580.text_edition: \n Caio Aelio Rufino flamini Aquilia Blaesilla mater filio piissimo\n
EDCS-06000580.translation: Aquilia Blaesilla, mother, to her most dutiful son, Gaius Aelius Rufus, perpetual flamen.
EDCS-06000580.summary: A mother dedicates a monument to her dutiful son, Gaius Aelius Rufus, who held the religious office of perpetual flamen.

EDCS-06000581.translation: To Lucius Aemilius Quintus, perpetual priest and flamen, for his merit in labor and perfect legation, the most distinguished council of the citizens of Lepcimagna decreed this.
EDCS-06000581.summary: This inscription records a dedication by the council of Lepcimagna to Lucius Aemilius Quintus for his service as a priest and legation.

EDCS-06000583.text_edition: \n Tiberius Claudius Amicus Marcus Heliodorius Apollonides aediles mensas pecunia sua dono dederunt\n
EDCS-06000583.translation: Tiberius Claudius Amicus and Marcus Heliodorius Apollonides, as aediles, presented tables at their own expense.
EDCS-06000583.summary: This inscription records a donation of tables by two aediles, Tiberius Claudius Amicus and Marcus Heliodorius Apollonides.

EDCS-06000588.translation: To Clementis, a distinguished man, son of the militia, patron of the city, the most splendid order of Lepcis Magna [erected this monument].
EDCS-06000588.summary: A monument erected by the city council of Lepcis Magna to Clementis, a distinguished man and patron of the city, likely from the 3rd or 4th century CE.

EDCS-06000589.translation: Cornelius Geta erected this for his brother Cornelius Amicus, flamen and pontiff, with the permission of the most splendid order.
EDCS-06000589.summary: A tomb inscription by Cornelius Geta for his brother Cornelius Amicus, a religious official, erected with the council's permission, likely from the 3rd or 4th century CE.

EDCS-06000590.translation: Tiberius and Quintus Plautii Lupus and Haterianus Rufini, brothers, took care to have this erected in accordance with the will of Marcus Cornelius Papirius Capitolinus, flamen, and his son-in-law, Rufinus.
EDCS-06000590.summary: An inscription indicating the erection of a monument according to the will of Marcus Cornelius Papirius Capitolinus, a flamen, by his relatives Tiberius, Quintus Plautii Lupus, and Haterianus Rufini, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-06000591.translation: Marcus Cornelius Amicus erected this for his most devoted son, Quintus Cornelius Va, the curator of the munus.
EDCS-06000591.summary: This funerary inscription records a son erecting a monument for his father, who held the office of curator muneris, likely in Republican or early Imperial times.

EDCS-06000592.translation: Marcus Fulvius Saturninus, the flamen of Tiberius Caesar Augustus, gave this offering.
EDCS-06000592.summary: This inscription records a donation made by Marcus Fulvius Saturninus, who served as a flamen for Emperor Tiberius, likely dating to the 1st century CE.

EDCS-06000594.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription mentioning an aedile named Geta, possibly indicating public works or a distribution, dating to the Roman Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-06000595.translation: The entire council of the colony of Lepcis Magna decreed a statue to Tiberius Iulius Papiria Frontinus, flamen of the deified Augustus, as he deserved it; Tiberius Iulius Fronto, his son, content with the honor bestowed upon his most indulgent father, erected it at his own expense.
EDCS-06000595.summary: This inscription records the decree of a statue by the city council of Lepcis Magna for the flamen Tiberius Iulius Frontinus, with his son erecting it, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-06000596.translation: Iuttaph Domitius, suffes, had this made from the funds; the aediles gave it as a gift from their own money.
EDCS-06000596.summary: This inscription records a public work funded by the suffes Iuttaph Domitius and completed by the aediles at their own expense, likely from North Africa during the Roman period.

EDCS-06000597.translation: Gaius Marcius Dento, the Augustalis flamen, permanent flamen and suffes, made with his own money the statue decreed to himself publicly for his merits.
EDCS-06000597.summary: This inscription records a priest, Gaius Marcius Dento, who funded the erection of a statue publicly decreed to him for his merits, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-06000598.translation: To the flamen and pontifex, the entire council, because of his munificence, ... from his will... among other things, the council decided that a chariot should be placed at public expense for Plautius Lupus, a most excellent man of our council, and when asked what he wished to be done about it, the decurions decreed as follows: Since Plautius Lupus, a most excellent man of our council, willingly accepted the office of flamen entrusted to him with the consent of all, and held games of extraordinary magnificence and showed singular and most splendid generosity, and also in the office of II vir he conducted all affairs according to the splendor of his birth and the dignity of our colony, and with most abundant affection held most splendid games again, and not content with these generosities, he adorned the cella of the baths with Numidian marbles and mosaic work, and on every occasion showed himself singular, and most recently when he was chosen curator to carry out the public duty from the will of Iunius Afra of most famous memory, he spared no solicitude or labor and, observing the will of the most ample senate, he saw to it that the duty was carried out most splendidly, and such affections ought to be rewarded so that others might also be stimulated to the same enjoyment; it is decreed that a chariot be placed for Plautius Lupus, a most excellent man of our council, at public expense, wherever he wishes. Afterwards, Plautius Lupus said he would place it at his own expense. Because of the request of all the decurions that a chariot be placed for Plautius Lupus, the II vir of the past year, at public expense because of his singular integrity and modesty as well as his recent munificence, Acilius Pompeianus, the II vir, made a statement as to what he wished to be done about it. When Plautius Lupus spoke according to his modesty, so as not to burden the city whose youth adored the commitment of the decurions, and contented with their authority, he said he would place it at his own expense if they permitted. And so, following the opinion of Marcus Rufus, the permanent flamen, as to what should be done about it, the decurions decreed that Plautius Lupus should place a chariot for himself wherever he wished at his own expense.
EDCS-06000598.summary: This lengthy inscription details the honors and public services of Plautius Lupus, a prominent citizen who served as flamen, pontifex, and II vir, and who was recognized for his generosity and public spirit, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-06000601.translation: The most splendid council decreed [this] to Lucius Pompeius Cerealis Salvianus, flamen; his wife Silia, daughter of Lucius, his heir, made it at her own expense for her most excellent husband.
EDCS-06000601.summary: This inscription records a statue erected by a wife for her husband, Lucius Pompeius Cerealis Salvianus, who held the office of flamen, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-06000602.text_edition: \n Amatori patriae et civium suorum quod ex indulgentia sacra civibus suis feras dentatas quattuor vivas donavit ex decreto splendidissimi ordinis bigam decreverunt Porfyri Porfyri\n
EDCS-06000602.translation: To a lover of his country and his citizens, because by his generosity he donated four live wild beasts with teeth to his citizens, the most distinguished council decreed a two-horse chariot to Porphyrius.
EDCS-06000602.summary: This inscription records a decree by the council honoring Porphyrius for donating four live wild beasts to the citizens.

EDCS-06000604.translation: Augustus Sentius Proximus, II vir and augur, erected this with his own money after the temple was repaired and adorned.
EDCS-06000604.summary: This inscription records the repair and adornment of a temple by Augustus Sentius Proximus, who held the offices of II vir and augur, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-06000605.translation: Publius Albucius Apollonius of Mediolanum, from Italy, a friend of rare example, with the permission of the most splendid council, erected this for Marcus Septimius Aurelius Agrippa, freedman of Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus, the foremost pantomime of his time in Rome, a fellow student of the young performers, advanced to the spectacles of Italy by our lord Augustus, honored with decurional ornaments in Verona and Vicetia, accepted among the young men in Mediolanum, appointed in Africa by our lord Augustus at Lepcis Magna.
EDCS-06000605.summary: This inscription records the erection of a monument by Publius Albucius Apollonius for Marcus Septimius Aurelius Agrippa, a distinguished freedman, pantomime, and public official honored in various cities across the Roman Empire, likely dating to the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-06000606.translation: To Septimia Polla, daughter of Lucius Septimius Severus, twice-conferred priest, Publius Septimius Geta, heir, to his most holy sister, set up this monument, from 144 pounds of silver and 10.5 ounces, by decree of the most distinguished council, from her will; he added to this gift a twentieth and 4 pounds and 10.5 ounces of silver, more than was bequeathed.
EDCS-06000606.summary: This inscription records a funerary monument erected by Publius Septimius Geta for his sister Septimia Polla, endowed with a significant amount of silver according to her will and his own addition.

EDCS-06000609.translation: To P. R. O., a most perfect man, governor of the province of Tripolitana, a man of all virtues, innocent, incorruptible, vigorous, mild, sublime, moderate, just, praiseworthy, and of complete fairness, the people of Lepcimagna, by decree of the most distinguished council, [dedicate this] to their benevolent patron.
EDCS-06000609.summary: This is a dedicatory inscription by the people of Lepcimagna to their governor, honoring his virtues and benevolence.

EDCS-06000612.translation: The council decreed and, content with the honor, remitted the money.
EDCS-06000612.summary: This brief inscription records a decision by a council to forego financial compensation in favor of an honor.

EDCS-06000614.translation: The Senate and People of Lepcis, for Gaius, son of Macris, grandson of Caius Annonius, have decreed honors to Phelyssa for the columns, the pavement, and the forum floor. Balitho, son of Macris, (erected this).
EDCS-06000614.summary: This inscription records a decree by the Senate and People of Lepcis to honor Phelyssa for public works, with Balitho listed as the erector.

EDCS-06000616.translation: The people of Lepcis [honor] Titus Caesernius.
EDCS-06000616.summary: This is a very brief inscription indicating that the people of Lepcis honored Titus Caesernius.

EDCS-06000620.summary: This inscription likely records a public dedication or action by a group identified as the Septimiani of Lepcis.

EDCS-06000621.summary: This inscription simply identifies the Septimiani of Lepcis, possibly as donors or the subject of a dedication.

EDCS-06000624.translation: To Frontonus, priest of the colony, [---] gave with a broad stripe [---] of the deified Trajan Parthicus.
EDCS-06000624.summary: This inscription dedicates something to Frontonus, a priest of the colony, possibly related to an imperial honor or a gift, mentioning Trajan Parthicus.

EDCS-06000625.text_edition: \n ------ C]nae-- Calpurni ex pecunia publica O\n
EDCS-06000625.summary: This is a fragmented inscription likely recording a public expense associated with someone named Calpurnius.

EDCS-06000631.translation: Quintus Ulpius Boccius erected this at his own expense, with the permission of the most distinguished council, to Marcus Antistius Arrianus, son of Antistius Cerialis, his most devoted patron and foster-son.
EDCS-06000631.summary: This inscription records the erection of a monument by Quintus Ulpius Boccius for his patron and foster-son, Marcus Antistius Arrianus, funded by Boccius and approved by the council.

EDCS-06000632.translation: Quintus Plautius Haterianus erected this by his will, by permission of the most distinguished council, to Aquilia Blaesilla, his brother Tiberius Plautius Lupus's mother.
EDCS-06000632.summary: This inscription records the erection of a monument by Quintus Plautius Haterianus to his brother's mother, Aquilia Blaesilla, in accordance with a will and with council approval.

EDCS-06000633.translation: The council decreed a chariot for Lucius Avillius Marsus, son of Caius Avillius Castus, of the Quirina tribe, at the request of all; his father, content with such honor for his most dutiful son, provided it at his own expense.
EDCS-06000633.summary: This inscription records a chariot decreed by the council for Lucius Avillius Marsus, with his father funding its construction.

EDCS-06000635.translation: Haterianus Gavilianus Proximus, friend of Caecilius Proculus, Lucius Silius Plautius Haterianus Blaesilianus, and his heirs through succession, set up this monument by permission of the most distinguished council, according to the will of Sentia Caeciliana.
EDCS-06000635.summary: This inscription records a monument set up by heirs in accordance with a will and with permission from the council.

EDCS-06000636.translation: Quinto Caecilio Severo Anniano, his heirs Clodius Agrippa and Rufinus, by will of their father and permission of the most distinguished council.
EDCS-06000636.summary: This inscription records heirs setting up a monument in accordance with their father's will and council permission.

EDCS-06000637.translation: To Marcus Clodius Clodianus, son of Clodius Clodianus, by decree of the council from his most dutiful father Clodius Clodianus.
EDCS-06000637.summary: This inscription records a monument dedicated by a father to his dutiful son, by decree of the council.

EDCS-06000638.translation: Flavius Crescens Saloninus erected this for Publius Cornelius Philocalus, father of the Cornelii Cotta and Cornelianus, by permission of the venerable council, according to the will of the Cornelii Cotta and Cornelianus.
EDCS-06000638.summary: This inscription records Flavius Crescens Saloninus erecting a monument for Publius Cornelius Philocalus, funded by will and approved by the council.

EDCS-06000639.translation: The sons, I, Cosconia Regina, mother, by permission of the council.
EDCS-06000639.summary: This inscription records Cosconia Regina, mother, acting with council permission, likely setting up a monument for her sons.

EDCS-06000641.translation: Flavia Procla erected this for her most dutiful sister Flavia Pia, by permission of the council.
EDCS-06000641.summary: This inscription records Flavia Procla setting up a monument for her sister Flavia Pia with council permission.

EDCS-06000642.translation: Lucius Granius Sollers Paulianus, by permission of the council, for his most dutiful daughter Grania Iovina.
EDCS-06000642.summary: This inscription records Lucius Granius Sollers Paulianus dedicating a monument to his daughter Grania Iovina with council permission.

EDCS-06000643.translation: Caius Hostilius Flaccus erected this for his most dutiful son Caius Hostilius Barea, by decree of the council, at his own expense.
EDCS-06000643.summary: This inscription records a father, Caius Hostilius Flaccus, funding a monument for his son Caius Hostilius Barea by council decree.

EDCS-06000644.translation: Caecilia Regina, mother, erected this for her most dutiful son Marcus Junius Caecilianus, by decree of the council.
EDCS-06000644.summary: This inscription records a mother, Caecilia Regina, dedicating a monument to her son Marcus Junius Caecilianus by council decree.

EDCS-06000645.translation: Decimus Iunius Proculus erected this for his most obedient wife, Iunia Perpetua, with the permission of the council.
EDCS-06000645.summary: A funerary monument dedicated by a husband to his wife, likely from the Roman imperial period, with council approval.

EDCS-06000646.translation: Claudius Claudianus, the heir, erected this for Marcus Licinius Flaccus the younger in accordance with his will, with the permission of the most distinguished council.
EDCS-06000646.summary: A funerary inscription by an heir for Marcus Licinius Flaccus the younger, executed according to the deceased's will and approved by the council.

EDCS-06000647.translation: Quintus Marcius Pudens erected this for his most excellent father, Quintus Marcius Pudens, a legal expert, by decree of the council.
EDCS-06000647.summary: A funerary dedication by a son to his father, a jurist, commissioned by a council decree.

EDCS-06000648.translation: Marcus Pompeius Geta Chirit and Marcia Rerycth, parents, erected this for their most devoted son, Marcus Pompeius Gaetulicus, in memory, by decree of the council.
EDCS-06000648.summary: A memorial inscription by parents for their devoted son, Marcus Pompeius Gaetulicus, approved by a council decree.

EDCS-06000649.translation: Iulius Kamerinus erected this for his most beloved wife, Vitulasia Procla, by decree of the most distinguished council.
EDCS-06000649.summary: A funerary monument for Vitulasia Procla, erected by her husband, with the approval of a distinguished council.

EDCS-06000653.translation: Aquilia Hedone erected this for her husband, Narcissus, freedman of Augustus and architect.
EDCS-06000653.summary: A tombstone set up by a wife for her husband, Narcissus, who was an architect and a freedman of Emperor Augustus.

EDCS-06000654.translation: Philippus, a scribe, notary, accountant, and bookkeeper, consumed by all these, lived for 27 years without a single blemish; his father erected this for his most devoted son.
EDCS-06000654.summary: A funerary epitaph for Philippus, a man of various financial and administrative roles, who died at 27; his father erected the monument.

EDCS-06000655.translation: Publius Cornelius Balbus, the heir, erected this for Gaius Aelius Crescent, in accordance with the will of Aelia Myris.
EDCS-06000655.summary: An inscription recording the erection of a monument by an heir for Gaius Aelius Crescent, as stipulated in the will of Aelia Myris.

EDCS-06000658.translation: To Ammicarus, for his brother Rucus.
EDCS-06000658.summary: A simple dedication, likely funerary, from a brother to his sibling, Ammicarus to Rucus.

EDCS-06000660.summary: An inscription identifying Publius Antistius and his origin from Ron, possibly a boundary marker or dedication.

EDCS-06000662.translation: Marcus Aquilius Veteri, son of Aquilianus.
EDCS-06000662.summary: This is a personal funerary inscription identifying Marcus Aquilius Aquilianus Veteri.

EDCS-06000663.summary: This is a dedication made by Aristius Antiochus.

EDCS-06000664.summary: This is a dedication made by Aristius Antiochus.

EDCS-06000665.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Atilia Marith lived for 30 years, 3 months, and 25 days. Atilius Corinthus Aurellianus made this for his most sacred and faithful wife.
EDCS-06000665.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Atilia Marith, erected by her husband Atilius Corinthus Aurellianus.

EDCS-06000666.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Aurelius Eros erected this for his most sacred father.
EDCS-06000666.summary: This is a funerary dedication for a father, erected by his son Aurelius Eros.

EDCS-06000668.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Ianuarius erected this for Lucius Caecilius Barichionis, his brother, who lived for 30 years.
EDCS-06000668.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Caecilius Barichionis, erected by his brother Ianuarius.

EDCS-06000669.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Quintus Caecilius Caecilianus made this for his most dutiful brother, Quintus Caecilius Cerialis Phischon.
EDCS-06000669.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Quintus Caecilius Cerialis Phischon, erected by his brother Quintus Caecilius Caecilianus.

EDCS-06000670.translation: Ginus also made and erected this with the dearest spirit for his son Africanus, and for his father Caecilius Ginus.
EDCS-06000670.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Ginus for his son Africanus and his father Caecilius Ginus.

EDCS-06000671.translation: Caius Caecina Artemas and Caecinia Pusinna, daughter of Artemas, and Caecinia Glyce Pusinna, her daughter, the heirs, saw to the construction of this for their best and most indulgent patron, Caius Caecina Apollinaris, son of Papiria.
EDCS-06000671.summary: This is a dedication for a patron, Caius Caecina Apollinaris, funded by his heirs.

EDCS-06000672.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Zena and Aristos, the brothers of Calpurnius Dosides, erected this monument and tomb for their dearest brothers.
EDCS-06000672.summary: This is a funerary monument and tomb erected by Zena and Aristos for their brothers.

EDCS-06000673.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription that appears to record the name of S. Cerialis Calpurnius, likely a dedication or epitaph.

EDCS-06000674.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Calvisiana set this up for her husband, Quintus Calvisius Amicus, of unique devotion.
EDCS-06000674.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by a wife for her devoted husband, Quintus Calvisius Amicus.

EDCS-06000675.summary: This is a very fragmentary epitaph, possibly dedicating something or someone named Amaras Corellius.

EDCS-06000676.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that seems to record the name and possibly some abbreviations for Cornelius.

EDCS-06000678.summary: This is a short inscription likely recording a dedication or memorial to Calliepius by Publius Cornelius Saecularis.

EDCS-06000679.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Caius Cosconius Marsus.
EDCS-06000679.summary: This is a funerary epitaph that records the name of Caius Cosconius Marsus.

EDCS-06000680.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Marcus Clutorius Baliahon, O. L. I. [---]
EDCS-06000680.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcus Clutorius Baliahon, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-06000682.translation: Quintus Domitius Camillus, son of Criton, Nysim, lived 20 years and 50 days. Marcus Domitius Crito, father, made this for his quiet son.
EDCS-06000682.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by a father for his son, Quintus Domitius Camillus Nysim, who died at the age of 20 years and 50 days, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-06000683.text_edition: \n [] P[] thi Presbyti Geronti Euphrasi Patricii viri clarissimi Virtute praestanti aequitate miravili sic temperantia moderato sic defensori iustitiae innocentium vindici Flavio Macedonio Patricio viro clarissimo comiti et duci provinciae Tripolitanae ordo splendidus et populus universus Lepcis Magnae civitatis digno patrono decrevit adque constituit\n
EDCS-06000683.translation: To Flavius Macedonius, a most distinguished man, count and duke of the province of Tripolitana, defender of justice and protector of the innocent, for his outstanding virtue, wonderful equity, and moderate temperance, the distinguished council and the entire populace of the city of Lepcis Magna decreed and established him as a worthy patron.
EDCS-06000683.summary: This inscription records the honoring of Flavius Macedonius as a patron of Lepcis Magna by its council and people for his virtues and service as a provincial duke.

EDCS-06000684.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Elia Victoria Masquiitana lived 21 years. Elius Datus made this.
EDCS-06000684.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Elia Victoria Masquiitana, made by Elius Datus, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-06000687.translation: ornator, at the same time mortal, Felyssa to his most obedient wife.
EDCS-06000687.summary: This is a fragmentary dedication, possibly a funerary epitaph, mentioning an 'ornator' (decorator or preparer) and his very obedient wife, Felyssa.

EDCS-06000688.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Flaminia Agaue lived 66 years and 9 months.
EDCS-06000688.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the name and age at death of Flaminia Agaue, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-06000689.translation: And Flavius Capito's heirs placed four statues, for 8 denarii, adding more than 1005 denarii from his own funds.
EDCS-06000689.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the posthumous dedication of statues by heirs, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-06000694.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Fulviae Crescentillae uxoris sanctissimae Quintus Marcius Candidus Rusonianus maritus fecit\n
EDCS-06000694.translation: To the divine shades of Fulvia Crescentilla, his most devoted wife, Quintus Marcius Candidus Rusonianus, her husband, made this.
EDCS-06000694.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Quintus Marcius Candidus Rusonianus for his wife, Fulvia Crescentilla.

EDCS-06000695.text_edition: \n Quinto Furio Cereali socero Carmini Saturnini qui statuas XVI HS testa[mento ------\n
EDCS-06000695.translation: To Quintus Furius Cerealis, father-in-law of Carminus Saturninus, who by his will [bequeathed] sixteen statues for [---].
EDCS-06000695.summary: This inscription records a bequest of sixteen statues by Quintus Furius Cerealis, father-in-law of Carminus Saturninus.

EDCS-06000697.translation: Lucius Granius Sollers Paulianus, son of Quintus, made this.
EDCS-06000697.summary: This is a funerary inscription by Lucius Granius Sollers Paulianus, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-06000700.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Imaia Iunia Victoria lived 14 years.
EDCS-06000700.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Imaia Iunia Victoria, who died at age 14, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-06000702.translation: Lucius Caecilius Pusio Caecilianus, their common son, gladly and deservedly placed this for Iulia Capitolina, according to the will of her former husband, Caecilius Amicus Caecilianus.
EDCS-06000702.summary: This is a funerary inscription placed by a son for his mother Iulia Capitolina, following the will of her deceased husband, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-06000703.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcus Aemilius Athictus consecrated this for his wife Iulia Clymenis.
EDCS-06000703.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by Marcus Aemilius Athictus to his wife Iulia Clymenis, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-06000704.translation: Gaius Iulius Silvanus, having removed ma...
EDCS-06000704.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription mentioning Gaius Iulius Silvanus, its exact purpose is unclear, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-06000705.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription naming Lucius Iunius Afer, its context is unknown, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-06000706.translation: Iunius Silanus to his best brother, Marcus Iunius Cossus, son of Marcus.
EDCS-06000706.summary: This is a funerary inscription from a brother to his deceased brother, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-06000707.translation: [...]sius Las and Irene, freedwoman, and Commodus E[...]
EDCS-06000707.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription mentioning several individuals, likely part of a funerary or commemorative context, from the Imperial period.

EDCS-06000712.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcia Eutychia lived 47 years. Cornelius Marsus made this for his wife.
EDCS-06000712.summary: This is a funerary inscription commemorating Marcia Eutychia, who died at age 47, dedicated by her husband Cornelius Marsus, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-06000714.translation: Caius Marius Pudens Boccius Zurgem and Velia Longina Bibai made this for their sons and grandson, Caius Marius Iovinus, Caius Marius, and Maria Victorina, and her son Marso.
EDCS-06000714.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by parents for their children and grandchild, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-06000715.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription possibly recording the decoration of something by Merula A, date and context uncertain.

EDCS-06000716.translation: Caius Nerianus Severus and Caius Rustius Pudens M Sep [dedicated this] to Augusta.
EDCS-06000716.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Augusta by Caius Nerianus Severus and Caius Rustius Pudens, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-06000717.translation: To the departed spirits of Nyftha.
EDCS-06000717.summary: This is a short funerary dedication to the departed spirit of Nyftha, likely Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-06000718.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription mentioning Tiberius Plautius alsille, likely a name on a monument, date uncertain.

EDCS-06000719.summary: This is a very brief inscription, likely a name (Pompeii Damarus) on a monument, date uncertain.

EDCS-06000721.summary: This inscription records a dedication by someone named Scipione, likely Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-06000722.summary: This inscription records a dedication by S Segullianus and T Nicebi, date and context uncertain.

EDCS-06000723.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Septimia Cariota rests here.
EDCS-06000723.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording that Septimia Cariota rests here, likely Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-06000724.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. SIZ Aureli Faustini Cunni [rests here or dedicated this].
EDCS-06000724.summary: This is a funerary inscription, likely from the Roman Imperial period, to the departed spirits and possibly naming SIZ Aureli Faustini Cunni.

EDCS-06000726.translation: Arinis son of Tapafius, Diodorus Nizaz made this for himself and his family.
EDCS-06000726.summary: A private dedication made by Diodorus Nizaz for himself and his family.

EDCS-06000727.translation: Tetia Prima, freedwoman of Lucius, [made this] for herself, and for Lucius Meianthos, freedman of Lucius, her husband, and for her family.
EDCS-06000727.summary: A private dedication by Tetia Prima for herself, her husband, and family.

EDCS-06000728.translation: He gave [this] for his wife VAE [from] a hundred thousand sesterces from his own money. Tiberinus.
EDCS-06000728.summary: A bequest from Tiberinus to his wife VAE, funded by a substantial sum of money.

EDCS-06000729.translation: To the divine spirits. Venusia the pious lived for seventy years.
EDCS-06000729.summary: A funerary epitaph for Venusia, commemorating her piety and lifespan.

EDCS-06000730.translation: To the divine spirits of Victorina.
EDCS-06000730.summary: A funerary dedication to the divine spirits of Victorina.

EDCS-06000731.translation: The heirs of Gnaeus Vitulasius Africanus.
EDCS-06000731.summary: An inscription recording the heirs of Gnaeus Vitulasius Africanus.

EDCS-06000732.translation: Marcus Ulpius Balsilus Cerialis, a man of good memory.
EDCS-06000732.summary: A funerary epitaph for Marcus Ulpius Balsilus Cerialis, noting his good reputation.

EDCS-06000737.summary: An ownership or dedication inscription related to Aquilius Aquilianus and Tyra.

EDCS-06000752.summary: An inscription identifying someone as the son of Salviana.

EDCS-06000753.summary: A simple inscription bearing the name Septimia Marcilla, likely a tombstone or dedication.

EDCS-06000760.summary: This is a very fragmented inscription, likely a funerary marker, with the name Marcus.

EDCS-06000798.text_edition: \n Celso II et Marcello II consulibus\n
EDCS-06000798.translation: In the consulship of Celsus and Marcellus (second time).
EDCS-06000798.summary: This is a dating formula indicating the year based on the consulship of Celsus and Marcellus.

EDCS-06000801.translation: Under the care and supervision of Hesperius, freedman of the procurator.
EDCS-06000801.summary: This inscription records a funerary monument or dedication supervised by Hesperius, a freedman of a procurator.

EDCS-06000810.summary: This is a very fragmented inscription that likely mentions a person named Calist.

EDCS-06000821.text_edition: \n EPONI flamin perpetu--) cura rum se s vir- perfectissim--\n
EDCS-06000821.translation: EPONI, perpetual priest, through his perfect achievement...
EDCS-06000821.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription likely recording the name and title of a priest named Eponi, possibly related to a public work or honor.

EDCS-06000822.text_edition: \n FRV fecerunt de c MK VALCI ETAT coll\n
EDCS-06000822.translation: FRV made from the bronze of VALCI ETAT and coll[egues]...
EDCS-06000822.summary: This inscription indicates that someone named FRV created something from bronze contributed by VALCI ETAT and others.

EDCS-06000825.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription, only containing a few letters that offer little contextual information.

EDCS-06000826.text_edition: \n ano anos umi L uti M\n
EDCS-06000826.translation: ano anos umi L uti M...
EDCS-06000826.summary: This is a highly fragmented inscription with no clear recoverable meaning.

EDCS-06000837.translation: Siden, daughter of Luia. Via Ocles, daughter of Oces. 20.
EDCS-06000837.summary: This inscription likely records the names of two individuals, Siden and Ocles, possibly related to a boundary or property marker indicated by 'XX'.

EDCS-06000838.translation: To Mythics, my friend. The house of Ysa, daughter of Mylthe.
EDCS-06000838.summary: This inscription seems to be a dedication or statement about property, possibly funerary, mentioning Mythics and Ysa.

EDCS-06000839.translation: To my son Baricbal, son of Typafius. To Uiystila, daughter of Lilystimus. And to Byrysoth, daughter of Uybivius. To Mystyth, son of Baiaemus. To Bithem.
EDCS-06000839.summary: This inscription appears to be a funerary dedication listing several individuals, possibly family members, with patronymic and other relationships indicated.

EDCS-06000844.translation: Here lies Alexandrus, son of Bagai, who lived eighty-six years and was buried in the third indiction in the month of September. He was a man wise and skillful in his knowledge.
EDCS-06000844.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Alexandrus, son of Bagai, who lived 86 years, with specific burial details including the indiction and month, dating it to late Roman or Byzantine period.

EDCS-06000845.translation: Of good memory, Anna, innocent daughter of Stefani, keeper of the place. She lived in peace for one year, 9 months, and 9 and a half days. She died on the 5th day of the month of June in the 12th indiction.
EDCS-06000845.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Anna, daughter of Stefani, recording her death at just over one year old, with precise dating by day, month, and indiction, placing it in the Byzantine era.

EDCS-06000846.translation: Of good memory, Demetria, daughter of Stefani, keeper of the place. She lived in peace for 3 years, 6 months, and 14 days. She died on the day of Mars in the month of March in the 8th indiction.
EDCS-06000846.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Demetria, daughter of Stefani, recording her death at age 3 years, 6 months, and 14 days, with specific dating by day, month, and indiction, placing it in the Byzantine era.

EDCS-06000847.translation: Of good memory, Dominica. She lived approximately A [years].
EDCS-06000847.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary epitaph for Dominica, indicating her approximate age at death, but the specific number of years is lost.
