EDCS-06000848.translation: Of good memory, Eufemia, sister of Austheodorus. She lived 5 years.
EDCS-06000848.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Eufemia, sister of Austheodorus, recording her death at the age of 5.

EDCS-06000849.translation: To the good memory of Iaennia, who lived about seven years.
EDCS-06000849.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Iaennia, recording her age at death.

EDCS-06000850.translation: To the good memory of Iuliana, daughter of Stefani, keeper of the place, who lived in peace for one year and three months, having died on the Lord's Day in the month of March, in the 8th indiction.
EDCS-06000850.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Iuliana, daughter of Stefani, recording her age, date of death, and the indiction.

EDCS-06000851.translation: Here rests the son of Stefani, keeper of the place, innocent, named Longinus, who lived seven days in the month of September, in the 11th indiction.
EDCS-06000851.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Longinus, son of Stefani, recording his age and date of death.

EDCS-06000854.translation: To the good memory of Sambas, son of Stefani, keeper of the place, who lived in peace for 8 years, two months, and two days, having died on Monday in the month of March, in the eighth indiction.
EDCS-06000854.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Sambas, son of Stefani, recording his age and date of death.

EDCS-06000855.translation: To the good memory of Sergi and Maria, who lived about seventy years and 9 months.
EDCS-06000855.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Sergi and Maria, recording their approximate lifespan.

EDCS-06000856.translation: To the good memory of Aystheodorus, son of Sifila, who lived in peace for 8 years, having died in the month of March in the eighth indiction.
EDCS-06000856.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Aystheodorus, son of Sifila, recording his age and date of death.

EDCS-06000858.translation: To God the Lord, YANIL ATIY, at your command.
EDCS-06000858.summary: This inscription appears to be a votive or devotional text with names of uncertain origin.

EDCS-06000860.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Quintus Aemilius Fronto, son of Massenagana.
EDCS-06000860.summary: This is a funerary dedication to the departed spirits for Quintus Aemilius Fronto.

EDCS-06000861.translation: Lucius Canuleius Verna, a teacher in the gladiatorial school, made this for his dearest wife, Ulpia Rogatilla, daughter of Arisuth.
EDCS-06000861.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by a gladiator school master for his wife.

EDCS-06000862.translation: Masof, lived 57 years a good life.
EDCS-06000862.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Masof, recording his lifespan.

EDCS-06000863.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus Licinius Rufus, son of Quintus Licinius Pison, made this for his dearest father, by his vow, at his own expense.
EDCS-06000863.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Quintus Licinius Pison, erected by his son Quintus Licinius Rufus.

EDCS-06000864.text_edition: \n orum Geta et Roae et Cea Domitius C et Casana quae et gyddus es filis suis simis\n
EDCS-06000864.translation: ...orum Geta and Roae and Cea, Domitius C and Casana, who is also called Gyddus, to their most similar sons...
EDCS-06000864.summary: This inscription appears to be a dedication made by parents, possibly including Domitius C and Casana (also known as Gyddus), to their sons, including Geta, Roae, and Cea.

EDCS-06000865.text_edition: \n Ex auctoritate Imperatoris divi Vespasiani filii Domitiani Augusti Germanici pontificis maximi tribunicia potestate VI imperatoris XIIII consulis XIII censoris perpetui patris patriae iussu Suelli Flacci legati Augusti pro praetore terminus positi sic inter nationem sic Muduciuviorum et Zamuciorum ex conventione utrarumque nationum\n
EDCS-06000865.translation: By the authority of the Emperor, son of the divine Vespasian, Domitian Augustus Germanicus, chief priest, in his sixth year of tribunician power, hailed as Emperor for the 14th time, consul for the 13th time, perpetual censor, father of the country, by order of Suellius Flaccus, imperial legate with praetorian powers, this boundary was set, thus between the nation of the Muduciuvii and the Zamucii, according to the agreement of both nations.
EDCS-06000865.summary: This inscription, dated to the reign of Domitian (late 1st century AD), records the establishment of a boundary marker between two tribal groups, the Muduciuvii and the Zamucii, under the authority of the emperor and his legate.

EDCS-06000869.translation: Marcus Ulpius Chinitius made this for himself and his family. Septim
EDCS-06000869.summary: This is a private funerary or commemorative inscription made by Marcus Ulpius Chinitius for himself and his family.

EDCS-06000870.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Flabi sic Mysun vixit annos XL\n
EDCS-06000870.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Flabia Mysun lived 40 years.
EDCS-06000870.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the name and age of a deceased woman named Flabia Mysun.

EDCS-06000871.translation: With the god's favor, here rests Turrentius the presbyter, of good memory, who lived in peace for forty-seven years more or less. He rested in peace.
EDCS-06000871.summary: This is a Christian funerary inscription for Turrentius the presbyter, recording his age at death.

EDCS-06000895.translation: Of good memory. Macrina lived seventy-five years more or less. She departed on the 1st day of March, in the 3rd indiction.
EDCS-06000895.summary: This is a Christian funerary inscription for Macrina, recording her age at death and the date of her departure.

EDCS-06000896.summary: This entry indicates that the inscription was not transcribed and refers the user to an image for details.

EDCS-06000897.translation: To the departed spirits. Calpurnia lived about fifty-five years.
EDCS-06000897.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Calpurnia, recording her approximate age at death.

EDCS-06000898.translation: Drink this because you deserve it, with your sons Semp and Eisrelia. AI
EDCS-06000898.summary: This inscription appears to be a dedication for a public fountain or drinking place, possibly with a Christian reference.

EDCS-06000899.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Dolicheno pro salute et victoria dominorum nostrorum Imperatorum Luci Septimi Severi Pii Pertinacis Augusti et Marci Aureli Antonini Augusti Augusti nostri filii et [Publi] [Septimi Getae] Augusti Augusti nostri filii Augusti nostri fratris et Iuliae Augustae matris castrorum Marcus Caninius Adiutor Faustinianus praefectus cohortis II Hamiorum praepositus vexillatione legionis III Augustae piae vindicis aram posuit et dedicavit\n
EDCS-06000899.translation: To Jupiter Optimus Maximus Dolichenus, for the safety and victory of our lords the Emperors Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus, and Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus, our Emperor's son, and [Publius] [Septimius Geta] Augustus, our Emperor's brother, and Julia Augusta, mother of the camp, Marcus Caninius Adiutor Faustinianus, prefect of the II Cohort of Hamians, in command of a detachment of the III Augustan Pia Vindex legion, erected and dedicated this altar.
EDCS-06000899.summary: This inscription, dating to the early 3rd century AD, records the dedication of an altar to Jupiter Dolichenus by Marcus Caninius Adiutor Faustinianus for the well-being of the emperors Septimius Severus, Caracalla, Geta, and their mother Julia Domna.

EDCS-06000900.translation: Marcus Coelius Ninus arranged for the bath, corrupted by age, to be restored. He also built the adjacent room from the ground up and established the changing room, under the supervision of Iunius Successus, the chief centurion.
EDCS-06000900.summary: This inscription records the restoration of a bathhouse and the construction of an adjacent room and changing room, funded by Marcus Coelius Ninus.

EDCS-06000903.translation: Caius Clodius Paulus, son of Caius, of the Collina tribe, a veteran honored with appropriate distinctions, made this for himself.
EDCS-06000903.summary: This is a private funerary or commemorative inscription made by the veteran Caius Clodius Paulus for himself.

EDCS-06000904.summary: This entry indicates that the inscription was not transcribed and refers the user to images for details.

EDCS-06000907.text_edition: \n Flavii Sebentius centen(arius) et Stiddin eius coniunx hunc locum didicarunt sic O bonum initium natisqui filiis concilium salvis libiris sic cum filicitati sic triumfanti Binaitir possissu sic\n
EDCS-06000907.translation: Flavius Sebentius, a centenarian, and his wife Stiddin dedicated this place. May it be a good beginning for their children and their sons, with their children and their family in happiness and triumph.
EDCS-06000907.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a place by a centenarian and his wife, likely for the benefit of their descendants, probably from the Roman period.

EDCS-06000908.translation: Flavius Gaudentius, proceed in your goodness, and in the name of Christ may all of the Seberi family drink. Farewell. This tower was built, barley and 30 sacks.
EDCS-06000908.summary: This inscription seems to be a dedication for a tower, possibly related to a water supply or storage, with a Christian invocation.

EDCS-06000910.summary: This entry indicates that the inscription text was not transcribed and is only available in image form.

EDCS-06000912.translation: Bodschichun Chalia, a priest of the gods, son of Avus, in good health.
EDCS-06000912.summary: This is a short dedication in an unknown language with Latin elements, possibly a personal memorial or dedication, from an ancient period.

EDCS-06000913.text_edition: \n Imperator Caesar Marcus Iulius Philippus Invictus Augustus et Marcus Iulius Philippus Caesar noster regionem limitis Tentheitani partitam et eius viam incursibus barbarorum constituto novo centenario -AS praecluserunt Cominio Cassiano legato Augustorum pro praetore Gallicano viro egregio praeposito limitis cura Numisii Maximi domo sia tibuni\n
EDCS-06000913.translation: Emperors Caesar Marcus Julius Philippus Augustus Invictus and Marcus Julius Philippus Caesar, our Caesar, closed off the region of the Tentheitan frontier and its road from the incursions of barbarians by establishing a new fort, under the command of Cominius Cassianus, legate of the Augusti, proconsul of Gaul, an excellent man, and overseer of the frontier, with the care of Numisius Maximus.
EDCS-06000913.summary: This inscription records the fortification of a frontier region in Gallia by Emperors Philip the Elder and Philip the Younger, dated to their joint reign (c. 244-249 AD).

EDCS-06000915.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Aelia Donata vixit annis tribus\n
EDCS-06000915.translation: Sacred to the departed gods. Aelia Donata lived for three years.
EDCS-06000915.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a young child named Aelia Donata, who died at the age of three.

EDCS-06000916.translation: Julius Severus, son of Masinthanis, renovated the fortifications. Gaudentius, with the consent of his parents and sons, to the gods below, may they live well. The devoted sons of Severus Masinthanis.
EDCS-06000916.summary: This inscription records the renovation of fortifications by Julius Severus and his sons, likely as a dedication to the gods.

EDCS-06000917.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Barbagnarus militiae praenuntiu insolito casu GIINTE MAT OI VI ICROEAT karus pater us vixit annos\n
EDCS-06000917.translation: Sacred to the departed gods. Barbagnarus, a military scout, by an unusual accident [text illegible]. His dear father lived for [number] years.
EDCS-06000917.summary: This funerary inscription honors Barbagnarus, a military scout who died in an accident, and also records the lifespan of his father.

EDCS-06000919.translation: Julius Masthalul, by his father Chyrdid, son of Sir..., son of Blam, son of Saba, [rest illegible].
EDCS-06000919.summary: This inscription appears to be a patronymic, listing the ancestry of Julius Masthalul, likely a local notable, in an unknown language with some Latin elements.

EDCS-06000921.translation: Macama, by his father Isachu, tribune.
EDCS-06000921.summary: This inscription identifies Macama as a tribune, and notes his father Isachu, likely from a Romanized local population.

EDCS-06000922.text_edition: \n Iulius Ibituathif Misirkar ben Amrr ben Chyrdidry bymysiyrir aban bal sm sabare masadyth sic le Misaieruchan dni msatyrth vy mysorthim sic ys sy barrecilim tim useb sylo Machrus ben Rogate\n
EDCS-06000922.translation: Julius Ibituathif, son of Misirkar, son of Amrr, son of Chyrdidry, by his wife Irir, father of Balasm, son of Sabare, and his wife Masadyth, and their children Misaieruchan,dni, Msatyrth, and their son Ys, and his wife Barrecilim, and their son Usleb, son of Machrus, son of Rogate.
EDCS-06000922.summary: This is a complex genealogical inscription and dedication, listing multiple generations of a family, possibly related to local leadership or land ownership.

EDCS-06000923.translation: Julius Nasif, tribune, son of Siraban, son of Iyσihan, son of Rirachan, [rest illegible]. He made this for himself, the son of Rasm, son of Mycne, son of Isaufath, son of Aabsmun, son of Eos.
EDCS-06000923.summary: This inscription records Julius Nasif, a tribune, and lists his paternal lineage, possibly indicating his status and local importance.

EDCS-06000924.translation: Ainmus, son of Nimira, from Iarnvhan.
EDCS-06000924.summary: This inscription appears to be a funerary marker for Ainmus, son of Nimira, with his tribal affiliation, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-06000926.translation: Flabius Isiguarus, a military tribune from Iarnvhan.
EDCS-06000926.summary: This inscription records Flabius Isiguarus, identified as a military tribune with his tribal affiliation, likely dating to the Roman military presence.

EDCS-06000927.translation: To Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus.
EDCS-06000927.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the Emperor Lucius Septimius Severus, likely from the Severan period (late 2nd to early 3rd century CE).

EDCS-06000931.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Naborsurnia avo sanu numero LXXX SATH MILIME DVO S NY FO\n
EDCS-06000931.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Naborsurnia, aged eighty years.
EDCS-06000931.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the spirits of the departed for Naborsurnia, who lived to be eighty years old, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-06000932.translation: Lauratianus founded the foundations, and with his sons and grandsons, fortune increases him, God permitting.
EDCS-06000932.summary: This inscription records the founding of some structures by Lauratianus and his family, likely in the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-06000936.translation: Thanubda, son of Nasif, son of Muynsif, son of Masauchan, son of Iylul, bought for one thousand thousand denarii, and he bought for him [her?] the wealth of Annobal Chylvvybylndsyana.
EDCS-06000936.summary: This inscription appears to be a record of a land purchase by Thanubda, a Libyan or Berber name, possibly from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-06000939.translation: To the Divine Spirits, I, Rosauaruarage, a good woman, made this memorial monument for myself; I lived 40 years, 1 month, and 5 days.
EDCS-06000939.summary: This is a self-provided funerary monument for a woman named Rosauaruarage, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-06000940.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari Lucio Septimio Severo Pio Pertinaci Augusto Arabico Adiabenico Parthico pontifici maximo tribunicia potestate X imperatori XI consuli III patri patriae et Imperatori Caesari Marco Aurelio Antonino Augusto tribunicia potestate III consuli et Lucio Septimio GetaeCaesari Augusto per vexillationem legionis III Augustae\n
EDCS-06000940.translation: For the Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus, Arabicus, Adiabenicus, Parthicus, pontifex maximus, with tribunician power for the 10th time, imperator for the 11th time, consul for the 3rd time, father of the fatherland; and for the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus, with tribunician power for the 3rd time, consul; and for Lucius Septimius Geta Caesar Augustus, by the detachment of the Legio III Augusta.
EDCS-06000940.summary: This is a dedicatory inscription honoring emperors Septimius Severus, Caracalla, and Geta, mentioning the Legio III Augusta and likely dating to the Severan period.

EDCS-06000941.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari Lucio Septimio Severo Pio Pertinaci Augusto tribunicia potestate IX imperatori XI consuli II patri patriae et Imperatori Caesari Marco Aurelio Antonino Augusto tribunicia potestate [IIII et Lucio] Septimio Getae Caesari Augusto Quinto Anicio Fausto legato Augustorum consulari legionis III Augustae piae vindicis\n
EDCS-06000941.translation: For the Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus, with tribunician power for the 9th time, imperator for the 11th time, consul for the 2nd time, father of the fatherland; and for the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus, with tribunician power for the 4th time; and for Lucius Septimius Geta Caesar Augustus, by Quintus Annius Faustus, consular legate of the emperors and the Legio III Augusta, the pious and victorious.
EDCS-06000941.summary: This dedicatory inscription honors emperors Septimius Severus, Caracalla, and Geta, naming the legate Quintus Annius Faustus and the Legio III Augusta, dating to the Severan period.

EDCS-06000942.translation: Sacred to Sol Invictus. Peticius Pastor willingly paid his vow with a willing heart.
EDCS-06000942.summary: This is a votive inscription to the god Sol Invictus, dedicated by Peticius Pastor, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-06000943.text_edition: \n Quaesii multum quot sic memoriae tradere agens prae cunctos in hac castra milites votum communem sic proque reditu exercitus inter priores et futuros reddere dum quaero mecum digna divom nomina inveni tandem nomen et numen deae votis perennem sic quem sic dicare in hoc loco salutis igitur quandium sic cultores sient qua potui sanxi nomen et cunctis dedi veras salutis lymphas tantis ignibus in istis semper harenacis sic collibus nutantis austeri solis flammas fervidas tranquille ut nando delenirent corpora ita tu qui sentis magnam facti gratiam aestuantis animae fucilari sic spiritum noli pigere laudem voce reddere veram qui voluit esse te sanum tibi set sic protestare vel salutis gratia\n
EDCS-06000943.translation: Quest for much, to hand down to memory as it is, acting before all the soldiers in this camp, a common vow, to be repaid for the return of the army, both past and future, as I searched within myself for worthy names of the gods, I finally found the name and divine power of the goddess, an everlasting vow to be dedicated in this place of salvation. Therefore, as long as there are worshippers, by whatever means I could, I sanctioned the name and gave to all the true waters of salvation, so that those who sent flames in such fires on these sandy hills, gently assuaged their bodies in the burning sun, thus you who feel great gratitude for the deed, do not hesitate to render true praise with your voice, for who wanted you to be healthy, but to testify for salvation.
EDCS-06000943.summary: This is a lengthy votive inscription dedicated to a goddess for salvation and the safe return of the army, likely erected at a sanctuary or military site.

EDCS-06000945.text_edition: \n Iovi Hammoni reduci Augusti sacrum Tullius Romulus centurio ex maioriario praepositus vexillationi\n
EDCS-06000945.translation: Sacred to Jupiter Hammon the Returned, by Tullius Romulus, centurion from the larger unit, in command of a detachment.
EDCS-06000945.summary: This is a dedication to Jupiter Hammon the Returned by Tullius Romulus, a centurion in charge of a military detachment, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-06000946.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Lucius Domitius Crescens lived 20 years. Octavius Ro and Hostilia Maxima, his heirs, set this up deservedly.
EDCS-06000946.summary: This funerary inscription records the life and death of Lucius Domitius Crescens, with the monument erected by his heirs, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-06000947.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Euasius qui et Calvana vixit annum I menses IIII hic situs\n
EDCS-06000947.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Euasius, also called Calvana, lived 1 year and 4 months. Buried here.
EDCS-06000947.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Euasius (Calvana), who died in infancy, dating to the Roman period.

EDCS-06000949.text_edition: \n Imperator Caesar Caius Iulius Verus Maximinus Pius Felix Augustus Germanicus maximus Sarmaticus maximus Dacicus maximus tribuniciae potestatis tertium imperator V pontifex maximus et Caius Iulius Verus Maximus nobilissimus Caesar princeps iuventutis Germanicus maximus Sarmaticus maximus Dacicus maximus pontes vetustate delapsos et iter longa iniuria corruptum restituerunt sua infaticabili sic providentia pervium commeantibus reddiderunt I\n
EDCS-06000949.translation: Emperor Caesar Gaius Julius Verus Maximinus Pius Felix Augustus, Germanicus Maximus, Sarmaticus Maximus, Dacicus Maximus, with tribunician power for the third time, imperator for the fifth time, pontifex maximus, and Gaius Julius Verus Maximus, most noble Caesar, prince of youth, Germanicus Maximus, Sarmaticus Maximus, Dacicus Maximus, restored the bridges that had collapsed from age and the road corrupted by long neglect, and made it passable for travelers again with their tireless foresight.
EDCS-06000949.summary: This inscription records the restoration of bridges and a road by Emperors Maximinus Thrax and his son Caesar Maximinus, dating to their joint rule in the 230s AD.

EDCS-06000951.text_edition: \n Imperator Caesar Marcus Claudius Tacitus Pius Felix Augustus pontifex maximus tribuniciae potestatae sic II consul milia V\n
EDCS-06000951.translation: Emperor Caesar Marcus Claudius Tacitus Pius Felix Augustus, pontifex maximus, with tribunician power for the second time, consul.
EDCS-06000951.summary: This inscription honors Emperor Tacitus, recording his titles and consular status, likely dating to his brief reign (275-276 AD).

EDCS-06000955.text_edition: \n Imperatoris Tiberi Caesaris Augusti iussu Lucius Aelius Lamia proconsul ab oppido in mediterraneum direxsit sic milia passuum XLIV\n
EDCS-06000955.translation: By order of Emperor Tiberius Caesar Augustus, the proconsul Lucius Aelius Lamia directed this road from the town inland for 44 miles.
EDCS-06000955.summary: This is a milestone inscription recording a road construction project initiated by Emperor Tiberius and carried out by the proconsul Lucius Aelius Lamia, dating to Tiberius' reign (14-37 AD).

EDCS-06000965.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari Publio Licinio GENA Galenio sic Pio invicto PIP Augusto Pio ANMOX Parthico maximo IVGRIE ONSAI milia passuum LIII\n
EDCS-06000965.translation: To Emperor Caesar Publius Licinius Gena Gallienus Pius, unconquered, Augustus, Pius, of the Parthians, the greatest, etc., 53 miles.
EDCS-06000965.summary: This is a milestone inscription dedicated to Emperor Gallienus, listing his titles and indicating a distance of 53 miles, likely dating to his reign (253-268 AD).

EDCS-06000966.text_edition: \n Imperator Caesar Marcus Antonius Gordianus Pius Felix Augustus pontifex maximus tribuniciae potestatis his pater patriae consul milia passuum numero LVII\n
EDCS-06000966.translation: Emperor Caesar Marcus Antonius Gordianus Pius Felix Augustus, chief priest, holding tribunician power, father of the fatherland, consul, 57 miles.
EDCS-06000966.summary: This milestone inscription records Emperor Gordian III, listing his titles and indicating a distance of 57 miles, dating to his reign (238-244 AD).

EDCS-06000968.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari divi Septimi Severi Pii Arabici Adiabenici Parthici maximi Britanici maximi filio divi Antonini Pii Germanici Sarmatici nepoti divi Antonini Pii pronepoti divi Hadriani ab nepoti divi Traiani Parthici et divi Nervae adnepoti Marco Aurellio sic Antonino Pio Felici Augusto Parthico maximo Britanico maximo Germanico maximo pontifici maximo tribunicia potestate XVIIII imperatori III consuli IIII patri patriae pro consuli miliarium numero LXXXII\n
EDCS-06000968.translation: To Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurellius Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus Parthicus Maximus, Britannicus Maximus, Germanicus Maximus, chief priest, holding tribunician power for the 19th time, emperor for the 3rd time, consul for the 4th time, father of the fatherland, proconsul, 82 miles, grandson of the deified Antoninus Pius Germanicus Sarmaticus, great-grandson of the deified Antoninus Pius, grand-nephew of the deified Hadrian, great-great-nephew of the deified Trajan Parthicus and the deified Nerva.
EDCS-06000968.summary: This extensive milestone inscription honors Emperor Marcus Aurelius Antoninus (likely Caracalla), listing his numerous titles and achievements, and marking a distance of 82 miles, dating to his reign (198-217 AD).

EDCS-06000969.text_edition: \n Imperator Caisar Marcus Antonius Gordianus Pius Felix Augustus miliarium numero LXXXII\n
EDCS-06000969.translation: Emperor Caesar Marcus Antonius Gordianus Pius Felix Augustus, 82 miles.
EDCS-06000969.summary: This milestone inscription records Emperor Gordian III, listing his titles and indicating a distance of 82 miles, dating to his reign (238-244 AD).

EDCS-06000970.text_edition: \n Perpetuo mperatori invicto mperatori fortissimo imperatori Lucio Domitio Aurelliano sic Pio Felici Augusto Germanico maximo Carpico maximo consuli ter patri patriae proconsule sic miliarium numero LXXXII\n
EDCS-06000970.translation: To the perpetual, unconquered, most powerful Emperor Lucius Domitius Aurelianus Pius Felix Augustus Germanicus Maximus, Carpicus Maximus, consul for the third time, father of the fatherland, proconsul, 82 miles.
EDCS-06000970.summary: This milestone inscription honors Emperor Aurelian, listing his titles and indicating a distance of 82 miles, dating to his reign (270-275 AD).

EDCS-06000980.text_edition: \n Imperator Caesar Lucius Domitius Aurelianus invictus Pius Felix Augustus pontifex maximus tribunicia potestate II miliarium C \n
EDCS-06000980.translation: Emperor Caesar Lucius Domitius Aurelianus, unconquered, Pius, Felix Augustus, chief priest, holding tribunician power for the 2nd time, 100 miles.
EDCS-06000980.summary: This milestone inscription records Emperor Aurelian, listing his titles and indicating a distance of 100 miles, dating to his reign (270-275 AD).

EDCS-06000983.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari Publio Licinio Egnatio Gallienio sic invicto Pio Felici Augusto pontifici maximo Parthico maximo Germanico tribunicia potestate X consuli V patri patriae proconsuli miliarium\n
EDCS-06000983.translation: To Emperor Caesar Publius Licinius Egnatius Gallienus, unconquered, Pius, Felix Augustus, chief priest, Parthicus Maximus, Germanicus, holding tribunician power for the 10th time, consul for the 5th time, father of the fatherland, proconsul.
EDCS-06000983.summary: This milestone inscription is dedicated to Emperor Gallienus, listing his titles and achievements, and likely marks a distance, dating to his reign (253-268 AD).

EDCS-06100521.text_edition: \n II io sacerdoti Antestus sic Burucus libertus et heres ec sic testamento eius ex decreto ordinis posuit\n
EDCS-06100521.translation: To the priest Antestus Burucus, his freedman and heir, erected this by decree of the council.
EDCS-06100521.summary: This is a funerary or honorary inscription for a priest named Antestus Burucus, set up by his freedman and heir, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-06100522.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription, likely a tombstone or dedication, recording a person named Crescentis, possibly indicating his parentage or a dedication to himself.

EDCS-06100523.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the Divine Spirits by Caecilius, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-06100526.translation: I love wine and so does the medium.
EDCS-06100526.summary: This very brief inscription expresses a liking for wine, possibly graffiti from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-06100527.translation: Painted in peace, he lived 20 years, 5 months, and 8 days.
EDCS-06100527.summary: This funerary inscription records the life and death of an individual referred to as 'painted', likely a tomb inscription from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-06100528.translation: Umbrianus lived in peace 6 years and 6 months.
EDCS-06100528.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Umbrianus, recording his lifespan, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-06100529.translation: Quintilianus, faithful in peace, lived 65 years and two days and 8 hours.
EDCS-06100529.summary: This funerary inscription for Quintilianus records his lifespan and faithfulness, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-06100533.translation: He made and dedicated this for his fellow citizens, as flamen of Augustus in his homeland, and for his people, and for the order.
EDCS-06100533.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by a flamen of Augustus for his homeland and people, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-06100534.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Iulia Migginia lived 41 years, 8 months, 3 days.
EDCS-06100534.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Iulia Migginia, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-06100538.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely part of a larger text mentioning the Licinii family, whose context is unclear.

EDCS-06100541.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Publius Aelius Sabinianus lived 95 years.
EDCS-06100541.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Publius Aelius Sabinianus, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-06100542.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Caius Aemilius Crescentianus Fortunatianus lived 44 years, 2 months, 16 days. His daughter Palmula made this.
EDCS-06100542.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan of Caius Aemilius Crescentianus Fortunatianus and was made by his daughter, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-06100543.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Aemilia, pious, modest, temperate, charming, lived 41 years, 9 months, 7 days.
EDCS-06100543.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan and virtues of Aemilia, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-06100544.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Gaia Aemilia Victorina lived 35 years, 10 months, 6 hours.
EDCS-06100544.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan of Gaia Aemilia Victorina, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-06100545.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Claudius Ilarianus lived 47 years.
EDCS-06100545.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Claudius Ilarianus, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-06100546.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Cocceia Quarta, daughter of Gallus Saturus, lived 35 years, 3 months. Saturninus made this.
EDCS-06100546.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan of Cocceia Quarta, daughter of Gallus Saturus, and was made by Saturninus, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-06100547.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Quintus Fabius Donatulus lived 70 years, pius and true.
EDCS-06100547.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan and virtues of Quintus Fabius Donatulus, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-06100548.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Flavia Successa lived 25 years, 3 months, and 5 days, and Aelia Serotina lived 16 years, 2 months, and 3 days. Aelius Soropot made this for his dearest wife and sister, buried here.
EDCS-06100548.summary: This is a funerary epitaph commemorating Flavia Successa and Aelia Serotina, dedicated by Aelius Soropot, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-06100549.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Sextus Iulius Martialis lived 81 years, 6 months, 3 days, and 9 hours.
EDCS-06100549.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan of Sextus Iulius Martialis, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-06100550.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Iulia Fortunata the dutiful lived 6 years and 4 days; she is buried here.
EDCS-06100550.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for the young Iulia Fortunata, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-06100551.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. [---]nius Saturninus.
EDCS-06100551.summary: This incomplete funerary epitaph is dedicated to [---]nius Saturninus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-06100552.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Lucius Marius Donatulus lived 19 years. Marius V made this for his most dutiful son; he is buried here.
EDCS-06100552.summary: This funerary epitaph commemorates Lucius Marius Donatulus, dedicated by his father Marius V, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-06100553.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Lucius Mucius Saturninus lived 29 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-06100553.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan of Lucius Mucius Saturninus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-06100554.summary: This is a very brief funerary inscription recording the burial of Mucia Casta, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-06100555.translation: To Titus Ofasius. His daughter lived 70 years; she made the vow dutifully.
EDCS-06100555.summary: This funerary epitaph records the death of Titus Ofasius' daughter, who lived 70 years and fulfilled a vow, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-06100556.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Sextus Seppius Rogatus lived 70 years. It is well.
EDCS-06100556.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan of Sextus Seppius Rogatus and includes a common closing phrase, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-06100557.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Marcus Tullius Montanus, called Luxuriosus.
EDCS-06100557.summary: This funerary epitaph records the name Marcus Tullius Montanus, identified by a cognomen, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-06100558.translation: Us Sinus lived for 3 years, 5 months, and 6 days.
EDCS-06100558.summary: This is a tombstone recording the lifespan of a person named Us Sinus.

EDCS-06100559.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Dardanus lived for 27 years, 7 months, 12 days, and 11 hours.
EDCS-06100559.summary: This is a tombstone recording the lifespan of Dardanus, dedicated to the departed spirits.

EDCS-06100560.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Donatus lived for 50 years.
EDCS-06100560.summary: This is a tombstone recording the lifespan of Donatus, dedicated to the departed spirits.

EDCS-06100561.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Generosa is here.
EDCS-06100561.summary: This is a tombstone recording the presence of Generosa, dedicated to the departed spirits.

EDCS-06100562.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Rufinus made this for his wife Nereis, who lived for 25 years, 6 months, and 5 days.
EDCS-06100562.summary: This is a tombstone erected by Rufinus for his wife Nereis, recording her lifespan.

EDCS-06100563.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. P. Secunda lived for 75 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-06100563.summary: This is a tombstone recording the lifespan of P. Secunda and her burial place.

EDCS-06100564.translation: Secundianus was laid to rest. PFS R T.
EDCS-06100564.summary: This inscription records the burial of Secundianus, with an accompanying abbreviation.

EDCS-06100565.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Sorex lived for 70 years and 9 months.
EDCS-06100565.summary: This is a tombstone recording the lifespan of Sorex, dedicated to the departed spirits.

EDCS-06100567.translation: To the Emperor, our lord, Flavius Valerius Constantinus, Pious, Fortunate, Augustus. (Fifth)...
EDCS-06100567.summary: This is a dedication to Emperor Constantine, likely part of a larger inscription praising him.

EDCS-07000893.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari divi Septimi Severi Adiabenici Parthici maximi Brittannici maximi filio divi Antonini Pii Germanici Sarmatici nepoti divi Antonini Pii pronepoti divi Hadriani abnepoti divi Traiani Parthici et divi Nervae adnepoti Marco Aurelio Antonino Pio Felici Augusto Parthico maximo Brittanico maximo Germanico maximo pontifici maximo tribuniciae potestatis XVIII imperatori III consuli IIII I\n
EDCS-07000893.translation: To the Emperor Caesar, son of the deified Septimius Severus Adiabenicus Parthicus Maximus Britannicus Maximus, grandson of the deified Antoninus Pius Germanicus Sarmaticus, great-grandson of the deified Antoninus Pius, descendant of the deified Hadrian, later descendant of the deified Trajan Parthicus and the deified Nerva, Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus, Parthicus Maximus, Britannicus Maximus, Germanicus Maximus, chief priest, with tribunician power for the 18th year, Imperator for the 3rd time, Consul for the 4th time. [---]
EDCS-07000893.summary: This is a long imperial titulature for Caracalla, listing his extensive honors and titles, probably from a public monument erected during his reign (circa 212-217 AD).

EDCS-07000894.summary: This inscription records the name Codbuldeus and states he is at peace, likely from a tomb.

EDCS-07000896.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Marturia and Mulio.

EDCS-07000897.translation: Sacred to Sol Invictus Augustus, for the safety of our emperor, lord, Julian, victorious and triumphant, always Augustus, devoted to their divine majesty.
EDCS-07000897.summary: This is a religious inscription dedicated to Sol Invictus Augustus for the emperor's well-being, likely from the reign of Julian.

EDCS-07000898.text_edition: \n Publio Fabio Luci filio Q(uirina) Firmano legato consuli patrono civitatis senatus decreto pecunia publica\n
EDCS-07000898.translation: To Publius Fabio Firmano, son of Lucius, of the voting tribe Quirina, former consul, patron of the city, erected by public funds by decree of the Senate.
EDCS-07000898.summary: This inscription records the erection of a monument or public work in honor of Publius Fabio Firmano, a former consul and patron of the city, funded by the state and decreed by the Senate, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-07000899.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Dead. Lucius Minius Honoratus, son of Lucius, of the Arnensis tribe, pious, lived 39 years and 5 months, is buried here.
EDCS-07000899.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Minius Honoratus, providing his age and tribal affiliation.

EDCS-07000900.translation: For Gaius Sallustius Felix, son of Caius, of the Quirina tribe, aedile, because he was the first in his colony to improve the amphitheater at his own expense, and because he increased the pleasures of his fatherland with a distinguished display of games, adding also singular and generous freedom towards all citizens, the curiales, gratefully acknowledging his service, erected this monument at their own expense so that they might reward him and so that the glory of his deed might endure even to posterity, under the supervision of Marcus Petronius Felix, and dedicated it by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-07000900.summary: This is a dedication by the curiales of a colony to Gaius Sallustius Felix, an aedile, honoring him for funding improvements to the amphitheater and for his generosity.

EDCS-07000901.translation: To Mercury, for the safety of the Emperor Caesar. Nasidius Firmus, officer of the VI Legion, and Amianus, a most distinguished man, prefect of the province, [dedicated this] willingly and with joy.
EDCS-07000901.summary: This is a religious inscription dedicated to Mercury for the safety of the emperor, mentioning military officials.

EDCS-07000908.translation: From the workshop of Quodvultdei. Crescens made the pugillum.
EDCS-07000908.summary: This is a maker's mark or inscription indicating that Crescens, from Quodvultdei's workshop, produced a pugillum (likely a type of vase or container).

EDCS-07400705.summary: This short inscription indicates that Filoserapis is the author or creator of the object it is attached to, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-07400706.text_edition: \n Aulo Caecina Severo proconsule legio III Augusta IIII\n
EDCS-07400706.translation: To Aulus Caecina Severus, proconsul. Legio III Augusta [erected this].
EDCS-07400706.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Aulus Caecina Severus, a proconsul, by the III Augusta legion, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-07400709.translation: Sacred to the Mother of the Gods, Magna, and to Attis, the Augusti.
EDCS-07400709.summary: This is a religious inscription dedicated to the Phrygian deities Magna Mater (Cybele) and Attis.

EDCS-07400712.translation: To our lord Flavius Valerius Constantinus.
EDCS-07400712.summary: This is an inscription honoring Emperor Constantine I, addressing him as 'Dominus Noster' (Our Lord), dating to his reign (306-337 AD).

EDCS-07400715.text_edition: \n Domino nostro Flavio Iulio Constantio nobillissimo sic Caesari\n
EDCS-07400715.translation: To our lord Flavius Julius Constantius, most noble Caesar.
EDCS-07400715.summary: This inscription honors the Caesar Flavius Julius Constantius (likely Constantius II), addressing him as 'Dominus Noster' (Our Lord), dating to the Constantinian dynasty (mid-4th century AD).

EDCS-07400716.text_edition: \n Germanic tribunicia potestate Vconsul- II proconsul-) contstitui XXXXV\n
EDCS-07400716.translation: [erected by] Germanus, with tribunician power for the 5th year, consul for the 2nd, proconsul. [---] XXXXV
EDCS-07400716.summary: This inscription likely records a public work or dedication made by someone named Germanus, who held significant consular and tribunician titles, possibly dating to the late Roman Empire.

EDCS-07400717.translation: Born for the good of the state, 45 miles from Carthage.
EDCS-07400717.summary: This is a milestone inscription indicating a distance of 45 miles from Carthage, likely marking a road built for the benefit of the state.

EDCS-07400718.text_edition: \n Ddominis nnostris Flavio Constantio nobilissimo Caesari\n
EDCS-07400718.translation: To our lords Flavius Constantinus, most noble Caesar.
EDCS-07400718.summary: This inscription honors Emperor Constantine I or one of his sons (likely Constantine II or Constantius II in their role as Caesar), addressing him as 'Dominus Noster' (Our Lord), dating to the Constantinian dynasty (early to mid-4th century AD).

EDCS-07400721.translation: Sacred to Neptune Augustus. Lucius Apronius Processus, the master, erected this by his own command and money.
EDCS-07400721.summary: This is a religious inscription dedicated to Neptune Augustus by Lucius Apronius Processus, who served as magister and funded the dedication.

EDCS-07400723.translation: Titus Helvacius Papia, freedman of Titus, lived 82 years, is buried here. Gaius Helvacius, son of Titus, of the Ars tribe, lived 13 years, is buried here. Marcus Helvacius Defensor, freedman of Titus, of the Arnensis tribe, lived 17 years, is buried here. May they rest well.
EDCS-07400723.summary: This is a funerary inscription for multiple members of the Helvacius family, detailing their ages, relationships, and tribal affiliations.

EDCS-07400724.text_edition: \n Domino nostro Flavio Connstante sic Pio Felici Augusto miliarum LX\n
EDCS-07400724.translation: To our lord Flavius Constans, pious, happy Augustus. Sixty miles.
EDCS-07400724.summary: This inscription honors Emperor Constans, referring to a distance of sixty miles, likely marking a road or milestone, dating to his reign (337-350 AD).

EDCS-07400725.text_edition: \n ------ tribunicia] potestate pater patriae consul proconsul a civitate Sucubucensis XIIII\n
EDCS-07400725.translation: holding the tribunician power, father of the fatherland, consul, proconsul, from the town of Sucubucensis, the fourteenth [year].
EDCS-07400725.summary: This inscription lists imperial titles and a year, likely for an emperor, and mentions the town of Sucubucensis.

EDCS-07400727.translation: The state with the money of Live [paid for this].
EDCS-07400727.summary: This inscription records a public work funded by an individual named Live.

EDCS-07400730.translation: The state of Girba, devoted to the ever-victorious, triumphant Emperor Augustus, [and] to his divine majesty.
EDCS-07400730.summary: This inscription is a dedication by the community of Girba to Emperor Augustus, likely from the late Roman period.

EDCS-07400750.translation: To our lord Flavius Claudius Constantius, most noble Caesar.
EDCS-07400750.summary: This is a dedication to Caesar Flavius Claudius Constantius, likely dating to the 4th century CE.

EDCS-07400751.translation: To the Unconquered, Pious, Fortunate Emperor, 191.
EDCS-07400751.summary: This inscription honors an emperor, possibly Caracalla, with the date 191 (likely referring to a regnal year or a count of victories).

EDCS-07600464.translation: Gaius Julius Secundus, dutiful, lived 76 years.
EDCS-07600464.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the name and age of Gaius Julius Secundus.

EDCS-07600465.text_edition: \n Geminia Lucana Geminaes sic filia Tertullaes sic vixit annos LXXXVI hic sita est ossa tua bene quiescant tibi terra levis sit\n
EDCS-07600465.translation: Gaius Julius Impetratus, dutiful. He lived 81 years.
EDCS-07600465.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Gaius Julius Impetratus, recording his name, a character attribute, and his age at death.

EDCS-07600466.text_edition: \n Caius Iulius Impetratus pius vixit annis LXXXI\n
EDCS-07600466.translation: Gaius Julius Impetratus, dutiful, lived 81 years.
EDCS-07600466.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the name, piety, and age at death of Gaius Julius Impetratus, likely dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-07600467.text_edition: \n Sextus Tullius Fuscus pius vixit annis LXX ex eius ffiliis duobus\n
EDCS-07600467.translation: Sextus Tullius Fuscus, dutiful. He lived 70 years; from his two sons.
EDCS-07600467.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Sextus Tullius Fuscus, recording his name, a character attribute, his age at death, and his surviving sons.

EDCS-08000806.text_edition: \n [Lucillae Augustae] Imperatoris Antonini Augusti patris patriae filiae Imperatoris Luci Aureli Veri coniugi pagus Uchitanorum Maiorum decreto decurionum pecunia publica fecit Caio Mario Faustino Lucio Propertio Rogato magistris pagi\n
EDCS-08000806.translation: For Lucilla Augusta, daughter of Emperor Antoninus Augustus, father of the fatherland, wife of Emperor Lucius Aurelius Verus. The community of the Uchitani Maiorum, by decree of the decurions and at public expense, erected this monument, with Gaius Marius Faustinus and Lucius Properius Rogatus as magistrates of the community.
EDCS-08000806.summary: This is a dedication for Lucilla Augusta, wife of Marcus Aurelius Verus and daughter of Antoninus Pius, erected by the pagus Uchitanorum Maiorum.

EDCS-08000809.summary: This inscription likely records the name of Emperor Marcus Aurelius Severus Alexander, possibly as a dedication or ownership marker.

EDCS-08000814.translation: Sacred to the Dis Manes. Marcus Allius Victorianus lived 11 years.
EDCS-08000814.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for a child, Marcus Allius Victorianus, who died at the age of 11.

EDCS-08000815.translation: Sacred to the Dis Manes. Ambia Fortunata, dutiful, lived [some number] years.
EDCS-08000815.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Ambia Fortunata, whose age at death is incomplete.

EDCS-08000817.translation: Sacred to the Dis Manes. Aselia [---]ia, dutiful, lived [some number] years.
EDCS-08000817.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Aselia [---]ia, whose full name and age at death are incomplete.

EDCS-08000818.translation: Sacred to the Dis Manes. Cominia sto[---].
EDCS-08000818.summary: This is an incomplete tombstone inscription, likely for someone named Cominia.

EDCS-08000819.translation: Sacred to the Dis Manes. Gaius Durvius Citinus, son of Caius, dutiful, lived 35 years, is buried here.
EDCS-08000819.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the name, parentage, age at death, and burial place of Gaius Durvius Citinus.

EDCS-08000820.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Caius Durvius Felix, dutiful, lived 37 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-08000820.summary: A funerary epitaph for Caius Durvius Felix, who lived 37 years, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08000821.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Quintus Durvius Fortunatus, dutiful, lived 12 years.
EDCS-08000821.summary: A funerary epitaph for Quintus Durvius Fortunatus, who lived 12 years, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08000827.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Quintus Ranilius Secundus.
EDCS-08000827.summary: A funerary epitaph for Quintus Ranilius Secundus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08000830.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Caius Apronius P.
EDCS-08000830.summary: A fragmentary funerary epitaph for Caius Apronius P., likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08000831.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Caius Apustius Felix, dutiful, lived ... years.
EDCS-08000831.summary: A fragmentary funerary epitaph for Caius Apustius Felix, indicating his lifespan, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08000832.translation: ...nius, dutiful, lived 45 years more or less. He is buried here.
EDCS-08000832.summary: A fragmentary funerary epitaph indicating a lifespan of approximately 45 years and burial, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08000833.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Arminius Privatianus, dutiful, lived 53 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-08000833.summary: A funerary epitaph for Arminius Privatianus, who lived 53 years, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08000834.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Caius Aurelius Victor, son of Quintus, of the Arnensis tribe, dutiful, lived 21 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-08000834.summary: A funerary epitaph for Caius Aurelius Victor, son of Quintus, who lived 21 years, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08000835.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. ...lia Extri, dutiful, lived 25 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-08000835.summary: A funerary epitaph for ...lia Extri, who lived 25 years, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08000836.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Marcus Furius Fortunatus lived 11 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-08000836.summary: A funerary epitaph for Marcus Furius Fortunatus, who lived 11 years, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08000839.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Sextus Marius Silvanus, dutiful, lived for 37 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-08000839.summary: A funerary epitaph for Sextus Marius Silvanus, recording his age at death, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08000840.translation: Lucius, son of Quintus, of the Arnensian tribe. [---]
EDCS-08000840.summary: An incomplete inscription mentioning Lucius, son of Quintus, and his tribal affiliation, likely part of a funerary or commemorative text.

EDCS-08000843.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Pomponia Onorata, dutiful, lived for 85 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-08000843.summary: A funerary epitaph for Pomponia Onorata, recording her age at death, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08000845.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Lucius Sallustius Primus [---]
EDCS-08000845.summary: An incomplete funerary epitaph for Lucius Sallustius Primus, beginning with a dedication to the Divine Shades.

EDCS-08000846.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Quintus Statius Felix Cim[---] lived [---]
EDCS-08000846.summary: An incomplete funerary epitaph for Quintus Statius Felix, starting with a dedication to the Divine Shades and mentioning his lifespan.

EDCS-08000848.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Caius Statius Honoratus, dutiful, lived for 20 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-08000848.summary: A funerary epitaph for Caius Statius Honoratus, recording his age at death, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08000849.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Valeria Africana lived for 63 years, dutiful [---]
EDCS-08000849.summary: An incomplete funerary epitaph for Valeria Africana, recording her age at death and her dutiful nature.

EDCS-08000850.translation: Valerius Saturninus, dutiful, lived for 41 years.
EDCS-08000850.summary: A funerary epitaph for Valerius Saturninus, recording his age at death, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08000851.translation: To Augustus, Felix, son of Caius, and Mucia, in addition to the dignity of the decurionate, with money added by themselves.
EDCS-08000851.summary: A dedication likely related to a public building or honor, mentioning Felix, son of Caius, and Mucia, who contributed money and held decurional status, possibly from a municipal context.

EDCS-08100140.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Primasius lived for 35 years and 10 months. For Castrensis, his wife, who deserved well.
EDCS-08100140.summary: A funerary epitaph for Primasius, recording his lifespan, and dedicated by his deserving wife Castrensis, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08201695.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus, son of Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus Arabicus Adiabenicus, grandson of Marcus Antoninus Pius, great-grandson of divine Antoninus Pius, great-great-grandson of divine Hadrian, great-great-great-grandson of divine Trajan Parthicus and divine Nerva, the people of Gigthis, publicly.
EDCS-08201695.summary: A public dedication by the people of Gigthis to Emperor Marcus Aurelius Antoninus (Caracalla), dating to his reign (198-217 CE).

EDCS-08201696.translation: His heirs, for his merit, made and set up [this monument] for Messius Crescens, his son, devotedly.
EDCS-08201696.summary: A funerary monument erected by heirs for a deserving individual, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08201697.translation: Lucius Domitius Tellus and Miha Vasar.
EDCS-08201697.summary: The names of two individuals, Lucius Domitius Tellus and Miha Vasar, likely appearing on a shared tombstone or dedicatory base, Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08201698.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Lucius Domitius Aumura lived 83 years and his wife Aurelia Tammassa lived 82 years. Made by his heirs for 250 denarii.
EDCS-08201698.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lucius Domitius Aumura and his wife Aurelia Tammassa, recording their ages and the cost of their burial, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08201700.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Lucius Domitius Masculus lived 42 years and his wife Mallia.
EDCS-08201700.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lucius Domitius Masculus and his wife Mallia, recording the husband's age, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08201701.translation: For the safety of our lords Emperors Augustus, Lucius Septimius Severus and Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Britannicus Parthicus Germanicus, and Julia Augusta, mother of the camp. The detachment of the Third Augustan Legion, the dutiful, the victorious, which is stationed at Vezere and advances against the enemy, and Titus Genius Ianuarius, optio, immunis, principalis, from the century of Carus Publilius, centurion of Errius Saturninus, Julius Julius Porcius Silvanus, Granius Felix, Aufidius Victorianus, Varius Saturninus, from the century of Aulus Surus Iustus, Mundius Co, from the century of Valerius Proculus, nnus Silvanus, Silicius Urbanus, Corn Rogatus, Marius Marcellus, Julius Victor, Sedius Felix, Julius Faustus, Helvius Silvanus, Valerius Rogatus, Aurelius Severianus, Julius Primus, principalis, Aelius Saturn, principalis, Aelius Saturn, sequtor, from Mussius Fuscinus, Annius Quintus, Flavius Victor, Lurius Beatus, Pomponius Silvanus, Marcus Acilius Fortunatus, Papirius Sallustianus, Aelius Crescens, Flavius Vibianus, Aelius Vitalis, Pontius Donatus, Antistius Felix, Safidius Ammon, Cattius Ingenuus, Julius Primus, sequtor, from Papius Fortun, Pinarius Martialis, Julius Donatus, Quintus Sulpicius Saturninus, Scribonius Priscus, Florius Rogatus, from the century of Flavius Victor, Pompeius Liberalis, Euped, from Catullinus, Flavius Victor, from the century of Maximus, Annius Saturus, Gaius Aufidius Niger, from the century of Quintus Gellius Iuvenalis, Aelius Iucundus, attius Fortunatus, from the cohort III, from the century of Julius Donatus, Julius Aemilius Victor, Vitellius Ianuarius, Flavius Proculus, from the century of Domitius Maximus, Lucilius Iulianus, Quintus Flavius Ianuarius, Eppius Donatus, Julius Donatus, Veturius Proculus, Hostilius Salutaris, Sulpicius Successus, Clodius Antoninus, Publius Clementi[---], C. Stertinius Iuvenalis, Flavius Verecundus, Agrius Felix, Arrunt Maximus, Gaius Pompeius Donatus, Silicius Quartus, Cornelius Saturninus, Geminius Rufus, Flavius Saturninus, Julius Honoratus, Fannius Catullinius, Pomponius Novatianus, Junius Verissimus, Gemini Fortunatus, Petronius Felix, Marcus Aemilius Felix, Gaius Pompeius Felix, from the century of Aurelius Auctus, Domitius Amo, Dentilius Adiutor, nnus Felix, Aemilius Sa, Geminius C, Aurelius Julius, Julius Julius, Julius Statilius D [[]] [[]] DEM.
EDCS-08201701.summary: This inscription is a dedication by a detachment of the Third Augustan Legion and various soldiers for the well-being of the Emperors Septimius Severus, Caracalla, and Geta (implied), and Julia Domna, dating to their co-reign.

EDCS-08201706.summary: A statement of renewal or restoration of a monument or building by Celsinus and his family, Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08201709.translation: Quodbuldeus the bishop lived 58 years and rested in peace on the Nones of January.
EDCS-08201709.summary: An epitaph for Bishop Quodbuldeus, recording his age and date of death, likely from the Late Antique or Early Christian period.

EDCS-08201711.summary: A short inscription with personal names and geographical locations, the meaning of which is obscure but could relate to identity or origin, Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08201712.translation: Marcus Aurelius, for Gaius Fabricius Felix Salvianus, most distinguished man, former praetor, quaestor of the plebs, and aedile, an incomparable man, from his own land granted to him by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-08201712.summary: A dedication by Marcus Aurelius for Gaius Fabricius Felix Salvianus, honoring his distinguished public career, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08201714.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Aemilia Exorata lived 18 years.
EDCS-08201714.summary: A funerary epitaph for Aemilia Exorata, recording her age, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08201715.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Quintus Aemilius Graecinus lived 70 years.
EDCS-08201715.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Quintus Aemilius Graecinus, who lived 70 years.

EDCS-08201716.translation: Of Marcus Venidius Fides, son of Rusticus.
EDCS-08201716.summary: This inscription records the name of Marcus Venidius Fides, son of Rusticus.

EDCS-08201717.translation: Quintilla Donatianilla, an honorable woman, lived in peace for 25 years. She departed.
EDCS-08201717.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Quintilla Donatianilla, who lived 25 years.

EDCS-08201718.translation: Aurelius Cuccas lived in peace for 20 years, 10 months, and 12 days.
EDCS-08201718.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Aurelius Cuccas, who lived 20 years, 10 months, and 12 days.

EDCS-08201719.translation: Caelia Rogata lived in peace for more or less 30 years.
EDCS-08201719.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Caelia Rogata, who lived approximately 30 years.

EDCS-08201720.translation: Here lies Zionysius. He lived in peace for 65 years and nine months.
EDCS-08201720.summary: This funerary inscription records that Zionysius lived 65 years and nine months.

EDCS-08201721.translation: Saturnina the faithful lived in peace for 43 years, 7 months, and 15 days.
EDCS-08201721.summary: This funerary inscription records the life span of Saturnina, who lived 43 years, 7 months, and 15 days.

EDCS-08201722.translation: Verrius Petronius Candidus lived in peace for 42 years, nine months, 15 days, and 5 hours.
EDCS-08201722.summary: This funerary inscription records the life span of Verrius Petronius Candidus, who lived 42 years, nine months, 15 days, and 5 hours.

EDCS-08201726.translation: To good memory. Quiriacus lived for 3 years and 2 days. He rests in peace on the 3rd day before the Kalends of July.
EDCS-08201726.summary: This funerary inscription commemorates Quiriacus, who died at age 3 and 2 days, with his burial date recorded.

EDCS-08201727.translation: Laeda lived in peace for 34 years, 8 months, and 15 days and one hour.
EDCS-08201727.summary: This funerary inscription records that Laeda lived 34 years, 8 months, 15 days, and one hour.

EDCS-08201728.translation: Sacred to Mercury Silvanus Augustus. Caius Sextilius Maximus, son of Faustus Italicus, flamen of Neptune, fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-08201728.summary: This is a dedication to Mercury Silvanus Augustus made by Caius Sextilius Maximus, flamen of Neptune, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-08201729.translation: Potitus set this up as a vow to Minerva at his own expense.
EDCS-08201729.summary: This is a votive offering to Minerva by Potitus.

EDCS-08201730.translation: Marcus Iunius Caius, Iunius Marcus, Marcus Iunius, Marcus Iunius, Decimus Iunius, for themselves.
EDCS-08201730.summary: This inscription records the names of six individuals, Marcus Iunius Caius, Iunius Marcus, Marcus Iunius, Marcus Iunius, and Decimus Iunius, likely dedicating something for themselves.

EDCS-08201736.translation: Fidelis Paulus lived in peace for more or less 19 years, a disciple. May SDVID be with us in peace.
EDCS-08201736.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Fidelis Paulus, who lived about 19 years and was a disciple.

EDCS-08201738.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Urbanus, scribe of the colony, a patron, is buried here.
EDCS-08201738.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Urbanus, a scribe and patron of the colony, dedicated to the Divine Spirits.

EDCS-08201739.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Quintus Aelius Felix, son of Tusca, lived for 1 year and 3 months. May it happen for you that you have this goddess favorable, so that you do not violate this sacred offering.
EDCS-08201739.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Quintus Aelius Felix, son of Tusca, who lived 1 year and 3 months, with a warning against violating his sacred offering.

EDCS-08201740.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Calventia Maiorina lived for 8 years, having been initiated. May it happen for you that you have this temple favorable and what you desire, so that you do not violate my bones.
EDCS-08201740.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Calventia Maiorina, who lived 8 years and was initiated, with a warning against violating her sacred offering and temple.

EDCS-08201741.translation: May what you desire happen for you, so that you do not violate this sacred offering. Nonia Vitalis, daughter of Marcus, lived for 4 years, 10 months, and 7 days.
EDCS-08201741.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Nonia Vitalis, daughter of Marcus, who lived 4 years, 10 months, and 7 days, with a warning against violating her sacred offering.

EDCS-08201743.translation: May what you desire happen for you, so that you do not violate this sacred offering. Suillius Genialis, son of Rufus, lived for 1 year, 7 months, and 12 days.
EDCS-08201743.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Suillius Genialis, son of Rufus, who lived 1 year, 7 months, and 12 days, with a warning against violating his sacred offering.

EDCS-08201744.translation: For Quintus Valerius Maximus, son of Valerius. May it happen for you as you wish, so that you do not violate this sacred offering.
EDCS-08201744.summary: This inscription is for Quintus Valerius Maximus, son of Valerius, with a conditional curse against violating his sacred offering.

EDCS-08201745.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Caelia Celsina Cyrilla lived 10 months; she will rest here.
EDCS-08201745.summary: A funerary inscription for Caelia Celsina Cyrilla, who died in infancy, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08201747.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Caecilia Eutychia lived 27 years. Caecilius Amimetus made this for his well-deserving wife.
EDCS-08201747.summary: A funerary epitaph for Caecilia Eutychia, erected by her husband, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08201748.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. For Martial, son of Quintus Cari Kallistus.
EDCS-08201748.summary: A funerary inscription for Martial, son of Quintus Cari Kallistus, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08201751.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Lucius Pomponius Titi Cossus lived 9 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-08201751.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lucius Pomponius Titi Cossus, who died in childhood, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08201753.translation: A sailor from Thaena lived 17 years, more or less.
EDCS-08201753.summary: A funerary epitaph for an unnamed sailor from Thaena, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08201755.translation: Gregoria, faithful daughter in Christ, of good memory, rested in this place; she lived 39 years in peace; she was buried on the 14th day before the Kalends of December, in the fifth indiction.
EDCS-08201755.summary: A funerary inscription for Gregoria, a Christian woman, recording her death and burial date, likely from the Late Roman or early Byzantine period.

EDCS-08201756.translation: Iulius Maximianus, an official (exceptor), lived 40 years, more or less.
EDCS-08201756.summary: A funerary epitaph for Iulius Maximianus, who held a specific administrative role, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08201757.summary: A very brief inscription, likely a funerary epitaph, for Cilius Vonifatius, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08201758.translation: For Marcus Petronius Mamertinus, prefect of the praetorian guard, by decree of the decurions, with public money.
EDCS-08201758.summary: An inscription recording a public honor, possibly a statue or monument, dedicated to Marcus Petronius Mamertinus, a high-ranking official, by local town councillors.

EDCS-08201759.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. For Anthia Metra, freedwoman of Augusti procurator; she lived 32 years; she is buried here. Onesimus, freedman of Augusti procurator, made this for his most devoted wife.
EDCS-08201759.summary: A funerary epitaph for Anthia Metra, a freedwoman, erected by her husband Onesimus, also a freedman, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08201760.translation: A soldier of the 1st Urban Cohort, Vesinius' century, lived 25 years. To his most devoted son.
EDCS-08201760.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for a soldier who died at age 25, with a dedication to his son.

EDCS-08201764.translation: Namgiddo, son of Camillus, from Namgiddo, for the honor of perpetual priesthood, made at his own expense a temple to the Augusti and a silver image of him, and dedicated it himself.
EDCS-08201764.summary: This is a dedication by Namgiddo, a citizen, to the Augusti, for the honor of his perpetual priesthood, likely dating to the reign of Trajan (based on the imperial titles).

EDCS-08201765.translation: Istrikatus, a shipowner, son of Bion, lived 35 years and 3 months.
EDCS-08201765.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Istrikatus, a shipowner, who died at the age of 35 years and 3 months.

EDCS-08201768.summary: This is a very brief inscription, likely a name on a monument or tomb, possibly for Claudia and her son Victorianus.

EDCS-08201769.translation: On the 5th day before the Kalends of May, Ioanna the virgin rests in the Lord.
EDCS-08201769.summary: This is a Christian tombstone inscription for a virgin named Ioanna, who died on April 27th.

EDCS-08201770.translation: Florentia iuniora, a girl of Campanian descent, lived six years, devoted and faithful in spirit, joined with God; she died on the 3rd day before the Kalends of February, and was buried on the Ides of March.
EDCS-08201770.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for a young girl named Florentia, of Campanian origin, who died in February and was buried in March.

EDCS-08201771.translation: To Theodotus, servant of God, from Sextina and Macarius, for their dearest son, for the sake of remembrance.
EDCS-08201771.summary: This is a memorial inscription for Theodotus, a servant of God, set up by Sextina and Macarius for their son.

EDCS-08201772.translation: Eusebia, brothers, a most rare and chaste wife, was here. She deserved to live a married life with me, as the times show. She lived sixteen years, eight months, and twenty days. God himself approved of her life, as I confess. An innocent wife, an example of the rarest sex. I, Successus, the archivist and her husband, implore you, brothers, to remember her always with your prayers.
EDCS-08201772.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Eusebia, written by her husband Successus, praising her virtues, recording her age at death, and asking for remembrance and prayers.

EDCS-08201773.translation: Ianuaria, a cloth merchant, in peace.
EDCS-08201773.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Ianuaria, identified as a cloth merchant, with a common epitaph indicating peace.

EDCS-08201774.translation: Severus Severus Severus. On the 6th day before the Nones of March, in the consulship of Lupo.
EDCS-08201774.summary: This inscription repeats the name Severus three times and records a date, likely a tombstone or memorial.

EDCS-08201775.translation: Arisus, in peace. Born at the sixth hour. Lived 9 scruples.
EDCS-08201775.summary: This is a very brief funerary epitaph for Arisus, indicating his name, status ('in peace'), time of birth, and a very short lifespan measured in scruples.

EDCS-08201776.translation: Diogas made this for his sweetest wives and sisters. The 5th day before the Kalends of February. Lord, Besse(?), Diogas.
EDCS-08201776.summary: This is a dedication by Diogas to his wives and sisters, with a date (January 28th) and a possible invocation or mention of a deity.

EDCS-08201777.translation: Vincincius lived in this world 12 years and 11 months.
EDCS-08201777.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Vincincius, who died at the age of 12 years and 11 months.

EDCS-08201778.translation: Vincincius lived in this world for 9 years and 8 months, these two brothers on the 12th day of the Lord's resurrection.
EDCS-08201778.summary: This inscription records the lifespan of Vincincius and possibly two brothers, likely from a funerary context.

EDCS-08201790.summary: This inscription simply records the name Amitellanus Fabius, possibly as a tombstone or memorial.

EDCS-08201800.summary: This inscription indicates Aurelius Robustius is 'in peace', a common phrase on Christian funerary monuments.

EDCS-0820182.translation: Fastidius lived 15 years, 7 months, and 15 days in peace.
EDCS-0820182.summary: A tombstone recording the lifespan of Fastidius, who died at the age of 15 years, 7 months, and 15 days.

EDCS-08201839.summary: This inscription records the name Autronia Rufina, likely from a funerary context.

EDCS-08201842.translation: Hermes to his dearest wife and son.
EDCS-08201842.summary: An epitaph for Hermes, dedicated to his wife and son.

EDCS-08201843.summary: This inscription records the name Hilarianus Iunior, likely indicating a younger person of that name in a funerary context.

EDCS-08201845.summary: This inscription records the name Onoria Primitiva, likely from a funerary context.

EDCS-08201847.summary: This inscription records the name Ianuaria Felicissima, likely from a funerary context.

EDCS-08201884.summary: This inscription records the name Pompeia Augustina, likely from a funerary context.

EDCS-08201921.summary: This inscription records the lifespan of Bigulantius, likely from a funerary context.

EDCS-08201933.translation: Gravis to his son Donatus, by a gift/contribution, lived 50 years.
EDCS-08201933.summary: This inscription records the lifespan of Donatus, dedicated by his father Gravis, likely from a funerary context.

EDCS-08201934.translation: Publius Caecilius Felix, priest of Saturn Augustus, willingly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-08201934.summary: A private religious dedication by Publius Caecilius Felix, priest of Saturn Augustus, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-08201935.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Lucius Numitorius Donatus Ianuarius, dutiful, lived for [---] years.
EDCS-08201935.summary: A funerary inscription for Lucius Numitorius Donatus Ianuarius, recording his name, piety, and lifespan.

EDCS-08201936.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Sedatus, servant of Augustus, lived for 10 years and 3 months; he is buried here, [along with?] Quintus and Optata, [his] most dutiful son.
EDCS-08201936.summary: A funerary inscription for Sedatus, a servant of Augustus, detailing his age at death and mentioning his parents, Quintus and Optata.

EDCS-08201937.translation: The dutiful man Dion lived in peace for eighty years and planted four thousand trees.
EDCS-08201937.summary: An epitaph for Dion, who lived to eighty and was known for planting four thousand trees.

EDCS-08201939.text_edition: \n Neptuno Augusto sacrum pro salute Imperatoris Caesaris Antonini Augusti Pii patris patriae liberorumque eius Marcus Barigbalius Ghuddis filius Pheraditanus maius statuam cum ostiis ex HS V milibus nummum sua pecunia fecit idemque dedicavit\n
EDCS-08201939.translation: Marcus Barigbalius Ghuddis, son of Pheraditanus the elder, dedicated at his own expense a statue with doors to Neptune Augustus for the health of the Emperor Caesar Antoninus Augustus Pius, father of the country, and his children, and dedicated it.
EDCS-08201939.summary: A dedication of a statue to Neptune Augustus by Marcus Barigbalius Ghuddis for the health of Emperor Antoninus Pius and his family, likely dating to his reign (138-161 AD).

EDCS-08201940.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Flavius Valerius Constantinus Pius Felix Invictus Augustus, pontifex maximus, holding tribunician power for the Xth time, consul for the Xth time, proconsul.
EDCS-08201940.summary: A dedication to Emperor Constantius, listing his imperial titles and dignities, likely dating to the 4th century AD.

EDCS-08201941.translation: To our Lord Flavius Claudius Constantinus, the Victorious, ever Augustus, born for the good of the state.
EDCS-08201941.summary: A dedication or acclamation honoring the emperor Flavius Claudius Constantinus.

EDCS-08201942.translation: To our Lord Valentinus, the Pious, Fortunate, Victorious and Triumphant, ever Augustus.
EDCS-08201942.summary: A dedication or acclamation honoring the emperor Valentinus.

EDCS-08201944.text_edition: \n Didi Preiecti flamen perpetuus probatissimo adque sic integerrimo viro cuius multa praeclara venefactorum sic praemia retinentur quem adornat integritas quem fides vera conmendat sic a cuius cunabulis titulis obsequemtem sic probabimus sic liberalitatem et ita sumptu proprio indulgentem ut et fastigia moenibus dederit et colomina sic repararit quibus rebus Didio Preiecto flamini perpetuo amplissimo proceri nostrae curiae quem et laus familiae et eloqui conmendat sic instructio ordo splendissimae coloniaeDAM PRO DE\n
EDCS-08201944.translation: To Didius Praeiectus, perpetual priest, the most approved and most upright man, whose many outstanding rewards are retained by sorcerers [or: whose many outstanding deeds are remembered by wise men], who is adorned by integrity, who is commended by true faith, from whose cradle we shall test his obedience, his generosity, and his indulgence with his own expense to such an extent that he has both granted battlements to the walls and repaired the columns, by which deeds to Didius Praeiectus, perpetual priest, the most eminent, whom the praise of his family and eloquence adorn, the most splendid order of the colony recommends [him] from the family of DAM PRO DE.
EDCS-08201944.summary: A lengthy honorary inscription praising Didius Praeiectus, a perpetual priest, for his integrity, generosity, and public works, likely from a Roman colony in the 2nd or 3rd century AD.

EDCS-08201945.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Publius Mulleius Proculus of Ariminum lived for 27 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-08201945.summary: A funerary inscription for Publius Mulleius Proculus, recording his name, origin, lifespan, and burial.

EDCS-08201946.translation: To Jupiter the Repulser, Marcus Fabius Mettianus, son of Marcus, of the Papirian tribe, perpetual priest and prefect of the III Cohort of Bracaraugustani, tribune of the XXX Ulpia Victrix Legion, prefect of the I Flavian Wing of Spaniards, Roman citizens, dedicated by vow with his wife Lartidia and daughter Optata.
EDCS-08201946.summary: A complex military and religious dedication by Marcus Fabius Mettianus, listing his career and honoring Jupiter, made with his family.

EDCS-08201947.translation: Sacred to Saturn, from the property of Pompeius Primus.
EDCS-08201947.summary: A private religious dedication to Saturn by Pompeius Primus, stating it was made from his own funds.

EDCS-08201948.translation: Fabius Philippianus to his most sweet daughter Fabia Maxima Faustianilla. The place was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-08201948.summary: A funerary dedication by Fabius Philippianus to his daughter Fabia Maxima Faustianilla, noting the burial plot was granted by local officials.

EDCS-08201949.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Iulius Dasimus, the barber.
EDCS-08201949.summary: A funerary dedication to the spirits of the departed for Iulius Dasimus, identified by his profession.

EDCS-08201951.translation: If you have money, it is yours. If you do not, you will not have it with you when you die. When I lived well, I obtained this; whoever lives well has this. To Furios Donatus, my incomparable husband, with kind affection and good will, Ceniyra.
EDCS-08201951.summary: A funerary epitaph by Ceniyra for her husband, Furios Donatus, emphasizing his virtuous life and the ephemeral nature of wealth.

EDCS-08201954.translation: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen. In this tomb rests the body of Sisinnius, servant of Christ, son of Firmus the reader. May he have eternal rest. He lived in the faith of Christ for 65 years and departed from this world on the 21st day before the Kalends of June in the year of Our Lord 1040, indiction 1. May he hear the voice of the Lord and rise again to eternal life. Amen.
EDCS-08201954.summary: A Christian funerary inscription recording the burial of Sisinnius, a servant of Christ and reader, who died in 1040 AD.

EDCS-08201955.translation: Matrona Tunnu. She lived for [some number of] months in peace.
