EDCS-08201955.summary: A funerary epitaph for Matrona Tunnu, recording her death after living a certain number of months in peace.

EDCS-08201957.translation: Sacred to the spirits. Maxima lived 77 years. Domnus G CCA lived 85 years. LB made this.
EDCS-08201957.summary: A funerary inscription dedicated to the spirits of the departed, recording the lifespans of Maxima and Domnus G CCA, with LB as the maker.

EDCS-08201958.translation: Of the relics of the blessed martyr Quiriacus.
EDCS-08201958.summary: An inscription indicating the presence of the relics of the martyr Quiriacus, likely from a church or tomb.

EDCS-08201964.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Lucius Hostilius Tertius Pius lived for one year, eight months, and twenty-six days, and one hour. Hostilius Tertius and Aufidia Concessa, parents, made this for their dearest son. Byzacio.
EDCS-08201964.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lucius Hostilius Tertius Pius, made by his parents, recording his very short life.

EDCS-08201965.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. He lived for 60 years and three months. His father Rimita made this.
EDCS-08201965.summary: A funerary epitaph dedicated to the spirits of the departed, stating the deceased lived 60 years and 3 months, made by his father Rimita.

EDCS-08201972.translation: Iulia Equitia Iuliana, an honorable woman, lived 84 years.
EDCS-08201972.summary: An epitaph for Iulia Equitia Iuliana, recording her age at death.

EDCS-08201974.translation: To Mallia Donatilla, in peace, who died on the day before the Nones of December. Rogatus Agapitus and his daughter set this up.
EDCS-08201974.summary: A funerary epitaph for Mallia Donatilla, who died on December 4th, set up by her husband and daughter.

EDCS-08201977.translation: Volussius Victor Tullianus, dearest son of Cornelius. Good, obedient, modest, respectful, dutiful, innocent, content, timid, patient. He lived for 10 years and 4 days. Lucius Volussius Tertullus and Iulia Attica, parents, took care of him.
EDCS-08201977.summary: A funerary epitaph for Volussius Victor Tullianus, detailing his virtues and lifespan, erected by his parents.

EDCS-08201980.summary: This inscription records the name of Tiberius Claudius Saturninus Ovinus, likely on a tombstone.

EDCS-08201981.summary: This inscription records the name of Titus Flavius Longinus Mamaius, likely on a tombstone.

EDCS-08201984.translation: Rornarius Iuzgagis, freedman, lived for [X] years.
EDCS-08201984.summary: This inscription records the lifespan of Rornarius Iuzgagis, a freedman, likely on a tombstone.

EDCS-08201985.translation: With Constantinus the presbyter in charge, we paid contributions from ARCOMANOAR.
EDCS-08201985.summary: This inscription records a payment or contribution made by individuals, overseen by the presbyter Constantinus, possibly for a church building.

EDCS-08201986.translation: From the workshop of Lucillus, in Christ. From the workshop of Lucillus.
EDCS-08201986.summary: This inscription mentions the workshop of Lucillus and references Christianity, possibly indicating a Christian artisan or a product from a Christian-run business.

EDCS-08201989.translation: Stephanus the faithful lived in peace for 14 years, laid to rest on the third day before the Nones of June, in the seventh indiction, and served in the military for 3 years.
EDCS-08201989.summary: This inscription records the lifespan and military service of Stephanus, a faithful Christian, and specifies his burial date.

EDCS-08201995.translation: Vitalis and Cardela fulfilled their vow.
EDCS-08201995.summary: This inscription records Vitalis and Cardela fulfilling a votive offering.

EDCS-08201996.translation: Bellator the bishop lived in peace.
EDCS-08201996.summary: This inscription records the name and peaceful life of Bellator, a bishop.

EDCS-08201997.translation: The burial of Saint Iucundus the bishop was found here through the investigation of Amacius the bishop.
EDCS-08201997.summary: This inscription records the discovery of the burial place of Saint Iucundus the bishop, initiated by Amacius the bishop.

EDCS-08201998.translation: Cresconius the presbyter lived in peace for [X] years, 5 months, 15 days, laid to rest [illegible] in the [X] indiction.
EDCS-08201998.summary: This inscription records the lifespan and burial details of Cresconius the presbyter.

EDCS-08201999.translation: Rusticus the presbyter lived in peace for 52 years, he left the presbyterate after 16 years, 4 months, and 10 days, buried on the 16th day before the Kalends of September in the 13th indiction.
EDCS-08201999.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Rusticus, a presbyter, recording his lifespan and length of service.

EDCS-08202000.translation: Presbyter Servus of blessed memory lived in peace for 68 years, buried on the 5th day before the Ides of October.
EDCS-08202000.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Presbyter Servus, recording his lifespan and date of burial.

EDCS-08202002.translation: Pe the faithful lived in peace for 9 years, 11 months, buried on the 5th day before the Ides of May in the seventh indiction, lived in military service for 3 years.
EDCS-08202002.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Pe, a faithful individual, recording their lifespan, military service, and burial date.

EDCS-08202004.translation: Here Honorata the innocent lived in peace for 3 periods, buried on holy Pentecost.
EDCS-08202004.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Honorata, recording her lifespan and burial on Pentecost.

EDCS-08202009.translation: Constantius the faithful lived in peace for nine years.
EDCS-08202009.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Constantius, a faithful individual, recording their lifespan.

EDCS-08202011.translation: Crescentina the faithful lived in peace for 7 years and 2 months, buried on the 15th day before the Kalends of June in the eighth indiction.
EDCS-08202011.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Crescentina, a faithful individual, recording her lifespan and burial date.

EDCS-08202013.translation: Iohannes the faithful lived in peace for 2 years and 7 months, buried on the 6th day before the Kalends of April in the 14th indiction.
EDCS-08202013.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Iohannes, a faithful individual, recording his lifespan and burial date.

EDCS-08202015.translation: Nonia the faithful lived in peace for 61 years, buried on the 17th day before the Nones.
EDCS-08202015.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Nonia, a faithful individual, recording her lifespan and burial date.

EDCS-08202016.translation: Teodorus lived in peace for 3 months.
EDCS-08202016.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Teodorus, recording a short lifespan.

EDCS-08202018.translation: Saint Honorius the bishop lived in peace for 80 years and 5 months, buried on the Ides of October.
EDCS-08202018.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Saint Honorius, a bishop, recording his lifespan and date of burial.

EDCS-08202019.translation: Gaius Memius Maxutius, son of Marcus Memius, [and] Gaius Memius Donatus.
EDCS-08202019.summary: This inscription appears to be a simple list of names, possibly related to a family or a funerary context, with no further explicit information.

EDCS-08202021.translation: Quintus Aelius Saturninus built a mausoleum at no small expense.
EDCS-08202021.summary: This inscription records the construction of a mausoleum by Quintus Aelius Saturninus, indicating a significant expenditure.

EDCS-08202022.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Publius Aelius Donatianus, son of Donatus, lived 52 years.
EDCS-08202022.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Publius Aelius Donatianus, dedicated to the departed spirits.

EDCS-08202023.translation: Gorgonia, aged 21. Palladius, [her] son, arranged for her burial.
EDCS-08202023.summary: This funerary inscription records the age of Gorgonia and credits her son, Palladius, with arranging her burial.

EDCS-08202025.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Memmia lived [---]. Martialis. Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcus Fannius Martialis the Younger.
EDCS-08202025.summary: This inscription appears to be a fragmented funerary text mentioning at least two individuals, Memmia and Marcus Fannius Martialis the Younger, and dedicating the space to the departed spirits.

EDCS-08202026.summary: This is a very brief inscription consisting solely of a name, Quintus Ocea Papiria, likely a tombstone or dedication.

EDCS-08202027.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Soludmia, daughter of Ecoinius, lived 62 years, 4 months, and 12 days.
EDCS-08202027.summary: This funerary inscription records the detailed lifespan of Soludmia, daughter of Ecoinius, dedicated to the departed spirits.

EDCS-08202028.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Cucristus, who lived 149 years, his sons set this up.
EDCS-08202028.summary: This funerary inscription records the exceptionally long lifespan of Cucristus and states that it was erected by his sons.

EDCS-08202029.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Gaius Julius Saturninus, who lived 75 years, erected this for his pious father; he lies here.
EDCS-08202029.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespan of Gaius Julius Saturninus, who erected the monument for his pious father, and indicates the father is buried there.

EDCS-08202030.translation: Gaius Aurelius Commodus lived 3 years [---]. I placed this for my most dutiful son. He lies here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Aurelius Commodus lived 3 years [---]. I placed this for my most dutiful son. He lies here.
EDCS-08202030.summary: This inscription, repeated likely due to a stone-cutting error or a deliberate emphasis, records the short life of Aurelius Commodus (aged 3) and was set up by his parent.

EDCS-08202031.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Ulpia Secunda, dutiful, lived 85 years.
EDCS-08202031.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Ulpia Secunda, recording her age at death.

EDCS-08202032.translation: Iatuvatus willingly paid his vow to Pluto Augustus.
EDCS-08202032.summary: A votive offering to Pluto Augustus by Iatuvatus, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08300554.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Titus Flavius ninus Achul Vuzale filius Masthan nepos vixit annis XXIX monimentum fecerunt athobbab et Imensis inpensis Thaneci filiae Sanmilc Lepcitanae item matris eorum |(denariis) CCL (ducentis miliis quinquaginta)\n
EDCS-08300554.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Titus Flavius Ninus Achul, son of Vuzale, grandson of Masthan, lived 29 years. A monument was made by Athobbab and Imensis at the expense of Thanec, daughter of Sanmilc Lepcitana, and their mother, for 250 denarii.
EDCS-08300554.summary: A tombstone for Titus Flavius Ninus Achul, who died at 29, with details of the monument's cost and builders, likely from the Roman provinces in the Imperial period.

EDCS-08300555.translation: Agatho lived 60 years, 5 months, 2 days, in peace. Laid to rest on the 5th day before the Ides of July, on a Thursday.
EDCS-08300555.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan and burial date of Agatho.

EDCS-08300556.text_edition: \n Iohannes fidelis in pace vixit annos LXXX depositus XIII Kalendas Octobres\n
EDCS-08300556.translation: Johannes the faithful lived 80 years in peace, buried on the 13th day before the Kalends of October.
EDCS-08300556.summary: An epitaph for Johannes, recording his lifespan and burial date, likely from a Christian context in the late Roman or early Byzantine period.

EDCS-08300558.translation: laid to rest on the ninth day before the Kalends of January.
EDCS-08300558.summary: This inscription fragment records the burial date of an individual.

EDCS-08300562.translation: Fatius the faithful lived 40 years, in peace. Laid to rest on the fourth day of the indictional cycle.
EDCS-08300562.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan of Fatius and his burial date within an indictional cycle.

EDCS-08300565.summary: This epitaph commemorates Speranda, indicating she lived in peace.

EDCS-08300567.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Victoria, which is incomplete but records her name.

EDCS-08300568.text_edition: \n Epifanius sic fidelis in pace vixit annis LX depositus IIII Nonas Sebtenbres sic\n
EDCS-08300568.translation: Epifanius the faithful lived 60 years in peace, buried on the 4th day before the Nones of September.
EDCS-08300568.summary: An epitaph for Epifanius, recording his lifespan and burial date, likely from a Christian context in the late Roman or early Byzantine period.

EDCS-08300569.text_edition: \n Maria fidelis in pacae! fidelis in pacae sic vixit annis XXX \n
EDCS-08300569.translation: Maria, faithful in peace! She lived faithfully in peace for 30 years.
EDCS-08300569.summary: A funerary inscription recording the death of Maria, who died at the age of 30.

EDCS-08300570.summary: This epitaph identifies Bernacla as faithful and having lived in peace.

EDCS-08300668.inscription_type: reges, termini, tituli honorarii, tituli sacri
EDCS-08300668.text_edition: \n Imperator Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus Arabicus Adiabenicus Parthicus maximus pontifex maximus pater patriae et Imperator Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Augustus Arabicus Adiabenicus Parthicus maximus pater patriae et Publius Septimius Geta [] castellanis Thudedensibus fines et immunitatem a rege Iuba per confirmatione divi Augusti concessos post multis maximisque saeculis felicissimis temporibus suis divino iudicio restituerunt Thudedenses determinatione saeculi terminos posuerunt et dedicaverunt feliciter\n
EDCS-08300668.translation: Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus Arabicus Adiabenicus Parthicus maximus pontifex maximus pater patriae and Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Augustus Arabicus Adiabenicus Parthicus maximus pater patriae and Publius Septimius Geta restored for the Thudedensian castellan community the boundaries and immunities granted by King Juba through the confirmation of the divine Augustus, after many and greatest centuries, during their most happy times by divine judgment; the Thudedenses erected boundary stones and dedicated them successfully.
EDCS-08300668.summary: An official inscription from the reign of Septimius Severus and Caracalla, confirming land rights and boundaries for the Thudedenses, a community of castellan farmers, likely dating to the early 3rd century CE.

EDCS-08400553.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Caius Sextilius Donatus miles cohortis I urbanae militavit annos VI vixit annos XXV hic situs est\n
EDCS-08400553.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Gaius Sextilius Donatus, a soldier of the I Urbana cohort, served for 6 years, lived for 25 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-08400553.summary: A funerary inscription for Gaius Sextilius Donatus, a soldier who died at the age of 25 after 6 years of service.

EDCS-08400554.text_edition: \n TI perp IIII publica Africae Dis Manibus sacrum Caius Sextilius Donatus pius vixit annis LXXXX hic situs est\n
EDCS-08400554.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Gaius Sextilius Donatus, dutiful, lived for 90 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-08400554.summary: A funerary inscription for Gaius Sextilius Donatus, who lived to the age of 90.

EDCS-08400556.text_edition: \n Sexto Furnio Fausto Sulpiciano clarissimo puero\n
EDCS-08400556.translation: To Sextus Furnius Faustus Sulpicianus, a most distinguished boy.
EDCS-08400556.summary: A funerary dedication to a young boy named Sextus Furnius Faustus Sulpicianus.

EDCS-08400557.translation: Of Victor, freedman of the emperor.
EDCS-08400557.summary: A partial inscription likely referring to a freedman of the emperor named Victor.

EDCS-08400558.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Calpurnia Quartilla vixit annis LXXXVI mensibus IIII hic sita est Dis Manibus sacrum Selnius Optatus vixit annis LXXXVII mensibus VII hic situs est\n
EDCS-08400558.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Calpurnia Quartilla lived for 86 years and 4 months; she is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Selnius Optatus lived for 87 years and 7 months; he is buried here.
EDCS-08400558.summary: A double funerary inscription recording the deaths of Calpurnia Quartilla and Selnius Optatus.

EDCS-08400562.text_edition: \n Honeratus sic et Lucia qum sic filis suis votum quot sic fecerunt libentes animo solverunt\n
EDCS-08400562.translation: Honeratus and Lucia, together with their children, made this vow as they had vowed, and freely paid it with willing hearts.
EDCS-08400562.summary: A votive inscription recording the fulfillment of a vow by Honeratus and Lucia for themselves and their children.

EDCS-08500625.text_edition: \n Pro salute Imperatoris Caesaris Traiani Hadriani Augusti Taphrurenses templum Saturno impensa publica fecerunt curantibus \n
EDCS-08500625.translation: For the safety of the Emperor Caesar Trajan Hadrian Augustus, the people of Taphrura built this temple to Saturn at public expense, under the care of...
EDCS-08500625.summary: A public dedication of a temple to Saturn by the people of Taphrura, likely during the reign of Hadrian.

EDCS-08500628.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Aufidia dia pia mater vixit annis LX\n
EDCS-08500628.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Aufidia, pious mother, lived for 60 years.
EDCS-08500628.summary: A funerary inscription for Aufidia, a mother who died at the age of 60.

EDCS-08500629.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed.
EDCS-08500629.summary: This is a short funerary dedication to the Manes.

EDCS-08500631.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Quintus Lappius Saturninus pius vixit annis XXXVII Lappia Felicitas vixit annis XVI\n
EDCS-08500631.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Quintus Lappius Saturninus, dutiful, lived for 37 years. Lappia Felicitas lived for 16 years.
EDCS-08500631.summary: A funerary inscription recording the lives of Quintus Lappius Saturninus and Lappia Felicitas, likely a family memorial.

EDCS-08500632.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Cezzonia sic Lucaniane havete Zasgia sic Victoria Cezzonia sic bene merens femina pia vixit nnos XXXV menses VIII dies XVI Lucius Turius Fabius Lucanianus filius eius pius vixit nnos IIII menses IIII dies XVIIII hic siti sunt titulo usi bene quiescant\n
EDCS-08500632.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Cezzonia, called Lucaniane, greetings! Zasgia, greetings! Victoria Cezzonia, greetings! A well-deserving, dutiful woman, lived 35 years, 8 months, and 16 days. Lucius Turius Fabius Lucanianus, her son, dutiful, lived 4 years, 4 months, and 19 days. They are buried here, having used this tombstone; may they rest well.
EDCS-08500632.summary: A detailed funerary inscription for Cezzonia and her son Lucius Turius Fabius Lucanianus, providing their ages and emphasizing their virtues.

EDCS-08500633.text_edition: \n Calpurnia Quinti filia Gemina pia vixit annos LX Lucius Calpurnius S\n
EDCS-08500633.translation: Calpurnia Gemina, daughter of Quintus, dutiful, lived 60 years. Lucius Calpurnius S...
EDCS-08500633.summary: An incomplete funerary inscription recording the life of Calpurnia Gemina, daughter of Quintus.

EDCS-08500634.text_edition: \n Sextus Terentius Saturninus Donnicianus et Bommia Saturnina Terentilla titulos sibi fecerunt et dedicaverunt\n
EDCS-08500634.translation: Sextus Terentius Saturninus Donnicianus and Bommia Saturnina Terentilla made and dedicated this monument for themselves.
EDCS-08500634.summary: A self-funded funerary inscription indicating that Sextus Terentius Saturninus Donnicianus and Bommia Saturnina Terentilla prepared their own tomb.

EDCS-08500635.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Sentius Namphamonis pius vixit annis LXI Fortunata filia pia vixit annis XV Dis Manibus sacrum Sentius Namfamo sic Tires pius vixsit sic annis XXII\n
EDCS-08500635.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Sentius Namphamonis, dutiful, lived 61 years. Fortunata, daughter, dutiful, lived 15 years. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Sentius Namfamo Tires, dutiful, lived 22 years.
EDCS-08500635.summary: A funerary inscription honoring three individuals: Sentius Namphamonis, his daughter Fortunata, and Sentius Namfamo Tires, likely part of the same family.

EDCS-08500637.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Saturnina M Zandulis filia vixit nnos LXXV hic sita est Dis Manibus sacrum Rufus Senlisi filius pius vixit nnos LXXXV hic situs est\n
EDCS-08500637.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Saturnina, daughter of M. Zandulis, lived 75 years; she is buried here. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Rufus, son of Senlis, dutiful, lived 85 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-08500637.summary: A funerary inscription recording the burial and ages of Saturnina and Rufus, possibly related individuals.

EDCS-08500638.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Nasidia Concessa pia vixit annis LXI hic sita est\n
EDCS-08500638.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Nasidia Concessa, dutiful, lived 61 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-08500638.summary: A funerary inscription stating that Nasidia Concessa, a dutiful woman, lived for 61 years and is buried at this location.

EDCS-08500639.translation: Caius Sempronius Ianuarius and Petronia Proba.
EDCS-08500639.summary: This is a very brief inscription likely indicating the burial or memorial of Caius Sempronius Ianuarius and Petronia Proba.

EDCS-08500641.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Bommia Luci filia Saturnina pia vixit annos hic sita est\n
EDCS-08500641.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Bommia Saturnina, daughter of Lucius, dutiful, lived... is buried here.
EDCS-08500641.summary: An incomplete funerary inscription for Bommia Saturnina, daughter of Lucius.

EDCS-08500642.text_edition: \n Titus Volusenus Potitus Rufiani filius pius vixit annos LXVII hic situs est Geminia Secunda inpensis suis fecit\n
EDCS-08500642.translation: Titus Volusenus Potitus, son of Rufianus, lived 67 years. He is buried here. Geminia Secunda had this made at her own expense.
EDCS-08500642.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the life span of Titus Volusenus Potitus and noting his burial by Geminia Secunda.

EDCS-08500643.text_edition: \n Perellia Fortunata Luci Perelli Luperci contubernalis Lucius Cornelius Saturninus A \n
EDCS-08500643.translation: Perellia Fortunata, consort of Lucius Perellius Lupercus, [and] Lucius Cornelius Saturninus.
EDCS-08500643.summary: An incomplete inscription that appears to be a funerary epitaph or a dedication by Perellia Fortunata and Lucius Cornelius Saturninus.

EDCS-08500644.text_edition: \n Apollini Patrio Augusto Sextus Iulius Possessor praefectus cohortis Gallorum curator numeri Syrorum sagittariorum item alae primae Hispanorum tribunus militum legionis XII fulminatae adlectus in decurias ab optimis maximisque Impperatoribus Antonino et Vero Auggustis adiutor praefecti annonae ad horrea Ostiensia et Portuensia procurator Augusti ad ripam Baetis procurator Augusti Ostis ad annonam procurator Augusti Alexandriae ad Mercurium statuam aheneam transmare advectam dono dedit\n
EDCS-08500644.translation: To Apollo the Father, Augustus, Sextus Julius Possessor, prefect of the Gallic cohort, curator of the unit of Syrian archers, also tribune of soldiers in the first Spanish ala and the twelfth Fulminata legion, appointed to the decuries by the best and greatest Emperors Antoninus and Verus Augusti, assistant prefect of the grain supply at the Ostian and Portian granaries, procurator Augusti on the bank of the Baetis, procurator Augusti at Ostia for the grain supply, procurator Augusti in Alexandria, dedicated a bronze statue of Mercury brought across the sea.
EDCS-08500644.summary: A dedication by Sextus Julius Possessor, a high-ranking official with extensive military and administrative experience, to Apollo and Mercury, detailing his career and the dedication of a statue.

EDCS-08600644.translation: The place of the seven holy brothers, here in memory of the Maccabees.
EDCS-08600644.summary: This inscription identifies a location as a memorial site for the Seven Holy Maccabean brothers.

EDCS-08600645.translation: To Gaius Annaeus Nonianus Arnensis Quartianus, decurion of the districts, principal man, who fulfilled all offices in his city and in his homeland with generosity...
EDCS-08600645.summary: This is a dedication honoring Gaius Annaeus Nonianus Arnensis Quartianus for his public service and generosity, likely on a public building or monument.

EDCS-08600646.text_edition: \n Imperatori Tito Aelio Antonino Caesari Augusto templum Minervae Augustae sacravit Apisa minus ex arca publlica fecerunt sufetes Macer et Baliato\n
EDCS-08600646.translation: To Emperor Titus Aelius Antoninus Caesar Augustus, they dedicated a temple to Minerva Augusta. Apisa minus had this made from the public treasury; the sufetes Macer and Baliato.
EDCS-08600646.summary: A dedication of a temple to Minerva Augusta, funded by Apisa minus and executed by the sufetes Macer and Baliato, to Emperor Antoninus Pius.

EDCS-08600647.text_edition: \n Plutoni Augusto sacrum pro salute Imperatoris Caesaris Marci Aureli Commodus! Antonini Pii Felicis Augusti Sarmatici Germanici maximi patris patriae civitas AbbiritanaLICVIERIII AFCTA ampliavit VSILERIIA per Natalem llisii et Namphamonem Gudis sufetes pecunia publica fecerunt\n
EDCS-08600647.translation: Sacred to Pluto Augustus. For the health of the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Commodus Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus Sarmaticus Germanicus Maximus, father of the fatherland, the Abbiritan civic community enlarged [the temple/building] for the sixth time. The sufetes Natalis and Namphamon, sons of Gudis, made this with public money.
EDCS-08600647.summary: A dedication to Pluto Augustus by the Abbiritan community for the health of Marcus Aurelius Commodus, noting public funding and the sufetes Natalis and Namphamon.

EDCS-08600648.text_edition: \n Caius Iulius Paris Igilgili vixit annos XXXV hic est situs\n
EDCS-08600648.translation: Caius Iulius Paris Igilgili lived 35 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-08600648.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the life span and burial of Caius Iulius Paris Igilgili.

EDCS-08600649.text_edition: \n Lucius Iulius Mustus vixit annos LXXXV hic situs est\n
EDCS-08600649.translation: Lucius Iulius Mustus lived 85 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-08600649.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the life span and burial of Lucius Iulius Mustus.

EDCS-08600650.text_edition: \n Publius Iulius Ianuarius vixit annis XXXV hic situs est\n
EDCS-08600650.translation: Publius Iulius Ianuarius lived 35 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-08600650.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the life span and burial of Publius Iulius Ianuarius.

EDCS-08600651.translation: To the most blessed era of our lords Valentinian and Valens, most invincible and most merciful princes, at the height and renowned marketplace and of the long series of ..., by neglect and division no longer of the republic, by the proconsul Nusta.
EDCS-08600651.summary: This inscription, likely from the reign of Valentinian and Valens (late 4th century), discusses the marketplace and its neglect, mentioning a proconsul.

EDCS-08600652.text_edition: \n Numini Augusti et Veneri Augustae sacrum Augusti libertus procurator telonei maritumi de sua pecunia fecit\n
EDCS-08600652.translation: Sacred to the Divine Augustus and Augusta Venus. An imperial freedman, procurator of maritime tolls, made this from his own money.
EDCS-08600652.summary: A religious dedication by an imperial freedman serving as a procurator of maritime tolls, made at his own expense.

EDCS-08600653.text_edition: \n Saturno Domitius Saturninus soliarius palmis argenteis ex libris IIII votum solvit\n
EDCS-08600653.translation: To Saturn, Domitius Saturninus the sandal-maker fulfilled his vow with silver palms weighing 4 pounds.
EDCS-08600653.summary: A votive offering to Saturn by Domitius Saturninus, a sandal-maker, for silver palms weighing 4 pounds.

EDCS-08600655.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Quintus Fabius Antistianus pius vixit annis XVIIII ossa tibi bene quiescant\n
EDCS-08600655.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Quintus Fabius Antistianus, dutiful, lived 19 years. May your bones rest well.
EDCS-08600655.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Quintus Fabius Antistianus, who lived 19 years.

EDCS-08600656.text_edition: \n IV sacrum Marcus Salluvius Hamillus de sua pecunia\n
EDCS-08600656.translation: Sacred. Marcus Salluvius Hamillus, from his own funds.
EDCS-08600656.summary: A dedication made by Marcus Salluvius Hamillus at his own expense.

EDCS-08600658.translation: Under the authority of the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Claudius Invictus Pius Felix Augustus, chief priest, holder of tribunician power, father of the country, consul for the second time, proconsul, the municipium of Thibilitani erected this with public funds.
EDCS-08600658.summary: This inscription records a public building or monument funded by the municipality of Thibilis under Emperor Claudius Gothicus, likely in the 270s AD.

EDCS-08600663.text_edition: \n Imperator Caesar Marcus Claudius Tacitus Pius Felix Augustus fecerunt coloni loci Legum Maiorum et dono dederunt\n
EDCS-08600663.translation: Emperor Caesar Marcus Claudius Tacitus, Pious, Fortunate, Augustus, made and dedicated this with the colonists of the place called Leges Maiorum.
EDCS-08600663.summary: An inscription recording a dedication by Emperor Tacitus and the colonists of Leges Maiorum.

EDCS-08600664.translation: For the prosperity of the blessed times, Quintus Cassius Taurus, perpetual and legal flamen, in honor of his paternal flaminate, with the consent of the most splendid council, restored the seating and the curia at his own expense.
EDCS-08600664.summary: This inscription details the restoration of civic buildings by Quintus Cassius Taurus, a perpetual flamen, likely in the 2nd or 3rd century AD.

EDCS-08600666.text_edition: \n Marco Asellio Rogato patri piissimo Marcus Asellius Mummius\n
EDCS-08600666.translation: To Marcus Asellius Rogatus, most dutiful father, Marcus Asellius Mummius [dedicated this].
EDCS-08600666.summary: A dedication by Marcus Asellius Mummius to his most dutiful father, Marcus Asellius Rogatus.

EDCS-08600668.text_edition: \n Quinto Calpurnio Honorato Quintus Calpurnius Ianuarius filio piissimo\n
EDCS-08600668.translation: To Quintus Calpurnius Honoratus, [dedicated by] Quintus Calpurnius Ianuarius, his most dutiful son.
EDCS-08600668.summary: A dedication by Quintus Calpurnius Ianuarius to his most dutiful son, Quintus Calpurnius Honoratus.

EDCS-08600671.text_edition: \n Pinariae Publi filiae Extricatae Sextus Valerius Fuscinus augur Thevestini filius matri piissimae item Publio Valerio Fuscino filio\n
EDCS-08600671.translation: To Pinaria Extricata, daughter of Publius, from Sextus Valerius Fuscinus, augur of Theveste, son, to his most dutiful mother; also to Publius Valerius Fuscinus, son.
EDCS-08600671.summary: A dedication by Sextus Valerius Fuscinus to his mother Pinaria Extricata and his brother Publius Valerius Fuscinus.

EDCS-08600672.text_edition: \n Lucio Marcio Luci filio Quirina Feroci flamini Augggustorum marito Iuliana eius\n
EDCS-08600672.translation: To Lucius Marcius Ferox, son of Lucius, of the Quirina tribe, flamen of the Augusti, and to her husband, [this was dedicated by] Iuliana.
EDCS-08600672.summary: A dedication by Iuliana to her husband Lucius Marcius Ferox, flamen of the Augusti.

EDCS-08600674.translation: He made [this] to Felicis, dearest son.
EDCS-08600674.summary: A dedication made to a beloved son named Felicis.

EDCS-08600675.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Aponi A Mai Helvia \n
EDCS-08600675.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. From Helvia [dedicated to] Aponius.
EDCS-08600675.summary: A funerary dedication made by Helvia to Aponius.

EDCS-08600676.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Tiberius Claudius Exupius bonus vir vixit annos XXVII menses VII dies \n
EDCS-08600676.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Tiberius Claudius Exupius, a good man, lived 27 years, 7 months, [and X] days.
EDCS-08600676.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Tiberius Claudius Exupius, who lived 27 years, 7 months, and an incomplete number of days.

EDCS-08600678.text_edition: \n Lucius Munatius Pastor vixit annos XXXV Talincia uxor marito fecit\n
EDCS-08600678.translation: Lucius Munatius Pastor lived 35 years. His wife Talincia made this for her husband.
EDCS-08600678.summary: A tombstone recording the life of Lucius Munatius Pastor, erected by his wife.

EDCS-08600679.text_edition: \n Alto labsa sic loco casu defuncta nefando primis rapta annis istic Fidentia dormit cui pater hunc tumulum sibi haec solacia fecit Fidentius filiae\n
EDCS-08600679.translation: Fidentia, snatched away in her earliest years by a terrible accident in this place, sleeps here. Fidentius the father made this tomb for his daughter as a solace.
EDCS-08600679.summary: A tombstone recording the premature death of Fidentia, dedicated by her father Fidentius.

EDCS-08600805.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. The owner set up this tombstone for his good slave girl; she lived for six months.
EDCS-08600805.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a young slave girl, dated by the style and content to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08600806.text_edition: \n Iulius Burdigala ritus miles legionis III Augustae quui sic vixit annos militavit annos centuria Marcelli\n
EDCS-08600806.translation: Iulius Burdigala, a soldier of the Third Augustan Legion, lived 32 years and served 14 years in the century of Marcellus.
EDCS-08600806.summary: A tombstone for Iulius Burdigala, a soldier of the Third Augustan Legion, indicating his age and service length.

EDCS-08600809.translation: Aca Simo made this for Marcus Arranicus Venustus Bassilianus, a most distinguished boy, son of Marcus Arranicus Venustus.
EDCS-08600809.summary: This inscription is a dedication, likely funerary, for a young boy named Marcus Arranicus Venustus Bassilianus, probably from the 2nd or 3rd century AD.

EDCS-08600810.translation: Quintus Fabius Victor, a veteran of the Third Augustan Legion, lived 71 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-08600810.summary: A tombstone for Quintus Fabius Victor, a veteran of the Third Augustan Legion, stating his age and burial place.

EDCS-08600811.text_edition: \n Quinto Faianio Clementi militi legionis III Augustae centuria Atrocis vixit annis XLIIII militavit annis XXIIII Marcus Cornelius centuria Sextili heres fecit hic situs est\n
EDCS-08600811.translation: Quinto Faianio Clementi, a soldier of the Third Augustan Legion in the century of Atrocius, lived 44 years and served 24 years. Marcus Cornelius, of the century of Sextilius, made this as heir. He is buried here.
EDCS-08600811.summary: A tombstone for Quinto Faianio Clementi, a soldier of the Third Augustan Legion, erected by his heir Marcus Cornelius.

EDCS-08600812.text_edition: \n Gallico militi legionis III Augustae centuria Volusi militavit nnis XXVIIII vixit annis LVIIII hic situs est Marcus Cornelius Martialis commilito et amicus centuria Cluenti de sua pecunia fecit pro meritis Gallici amici\n
EDCS-08600812.translation: Gallicus, a soldier of the Third Augustan Legion in the century of Volusius, served 29 years and lived 59 years. He is buried here. Marcus Cornelius Martialis, a fellow soldier and friend from the century of Cluentius, made this from his own money for the merits of his friend Gallicus.
EDCS-08600812.summary: A tombstone for Gallicus, a soldier of the Third Augustan Legion, erected by a fellow soldier and friend who funded it out of appreciation.

EDCS-08600813.text_edition: \n Quintus Geminius Quinti filius Polianus Thunusida eques centuria Catonis vixit annis XXXVI militavit annis IIX hic situs est\n
EDCS-08600813.translation: Quintus Geminius Polianus, son of Quintus, of the Thunusid tribe, an equestrian, in the century of Caton, lived 36 years and served 8 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-08600813.summary: A tombstone for Quintus Geminius Polianus, an equestrian, detailing his age, service length, and tribal affiliation.

EDCS-08600814.text_edition: \n Marcus Sempronius Marci filius Galeria Lugudunensi miles legionis III Augustae centuria Ex vixit annos XXV militavit annos V hic situs est Titus Baronius centuria Sallusti heres posuit\n
EDCS-08600814.translation: Marcus Sempronius Galerus, son of Marcus, of the tribe Galeria, from Lugudunum, a soldier of the Third Augustan Legion in the century of Ex, lived 25 years and served 5 years. He is buried here. Titus Baronius, of the century of Sallustius, placed this as heir.
EDCS-08600814.summary: A tombstone for Marcus Sempronius Galerus, a soldier of the Third Augustan Legion, erected by his heir Titus Baronius.

EDCS-08600815.text_edition: \n Lucius Tadius Cnaei filius Arnensi domo Carthagine miles legionis III Augustae vixit nnos XLVI militavit nnos XXV hic situs est curam egit Cassius Carus amicus post mortem\n
EDCS-08600815.translation: Lucius Tadius, son of Cnaeus, from Arna, originally from Carthage, a soldier of the Third Augustan Legion, lived 46 years and served 25 years. He is buried here. His friend Cassius Carus took care of this after his death.
EDCS-08600815.summary: A tombstone for Lucius Tadius, a soldier of the Third Augustan Legion from Carthage, erected by his friend Cassius Carus after his death.

EDCS-08600816.translation: Quintus Gavius Repentinus, son of Quintus, of the Arnensis tribe, pious, lived 85 years; he is buried here. Quintus Gavius Sterceius, his son, placed this for his father.
EDCS-08600816.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Quintus Gavius Repentinus, erected by his son, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century AD.

EDCS-08600817.translation: Percennius lived 92 years. Marcus Percennius Firmus, his son, lived 22 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-08600817.summary: This funerary inscription records the lives of two individuals, likely father and son, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08600818.translation: Marcus Valerius Fortunatus, his son, placed this; he is buried here.
EDCS-08600818.summary: This is a funerary inscription for an individual named Marcus Valerius Fortunatus, erected by his son, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08600819.translation: By the gifts of God and his saints, Candidus and Adeudata made this.
EDCS-08600819.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by Candidus and Adeudata, likely in a Christian context from the later Roman Empire.

EDCS-08600821.translation: To the most glorious and most blessed martyrs who suffered under the divine laws during the persecution of Diocletian and Maximian, whose bodies remain here eternally with the Lord, for whom Marcellus the illustrious, divinely inspired, has enclosed their venerable names and bodies within lapis anaclitis with herms and a table, Marcellus gives thanks for the merits of the martyrs and the fulfillment of his cherished vows; may he always live happily; and happier still shall be whoever believes with all faith in Almighty God through His Christ.
EDCS-08600821.summary: This inscription is a dedication by Marcellus to martyrs of the Diocletianic persecution, dating it to the early 4th century AD or later, in a Christian context.

EDCS-08600822.translation: To Ianuarie, son of Dovitiana, and Apronius, Maximinius, Victor, Secundianus, Successus, Comes, Purpurius, Pulens, Pomponius; to the gods. Sacred. To the spirits of the underworld. To Primabius, Primose, Valens, Ianuarie, Vincentius, of Julia Felicitas, Probus, Libos, Licinius, Saturninus, Fortunatus.
EDCS-08600822.summary: This inscription appears to be a complex funerary dedication listing multiple individuals and possibly patrons or family members, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08600823.translation: Here lie the remains of the blessed martyr and bishop Cyprian, deposited by the blessed bishop Melleus in the fourth year of the reign of Lord Justin the Emperor.
EDCS-08600823.summary: This inscription records the deposition of the relics of Saint Cyprian by Bishop Melleus during the reign of Emperor Justin.

EDCS-08600825.translation: Xlimarcus lived 65 years and 9 months; he is buried here.
EDCS-08600825.summary: This inscription records the lifespan and burial of Xlimarcus.

EDCS-08600827.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Quinta Aberrinia Procula lived 75 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-08600827.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespan and burial of Quinta Aberrinia Procula.

EDCS-08600828.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Agria Namgedde lived 45 years.
EDCS-08600828.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespan of Agria Namgedde.

EDCS-08600829.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Agria Soluta lived [---] years; she is buried here.
EDCS-08600829.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Agria Soluta, with her age partially lost.

EDCS-08600830.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Gemienus Fuscus lived 85 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-08600830.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespan and burial of Gemienus Fuscus.

EDCS-08600831.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Arspia lived 70 years.
EDCS-08600831.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespan of Arspia.

EDCS-08600832.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Babullia Concordia lived 40 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-08600832.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespan and burial of Babullia Concordia.

EDCS-08600833.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Caius C S lived 25 years.
EDCS-08600833.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespan of Caius C S.

EDCS-08600834.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Caeria lived 31 years.
EDCS-08600834.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespan of Caeria.

EDCS-08600835.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Considius C lived for 27 years.
EDCS-08600835.summary: A funerary inscription recording the age at death of Considius C.

EDCS-08600836.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Copia Victoria lived for 75 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-08600836.summary: A funerary inscription recording the age at death and burial place of Copia Victoria.

EDCS-08600837.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Domitia lived for 80 years.
EDCS-08600837.summary: A funerary inscription recording the age at death of Domitia.

EDCS-08600838.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Du Rogat lived for 30 years.
EDCS-08600838.summary: A funerary inscription recording the age at death of Du Rogat.

EDCS-08600839.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Decimus Caetrius Felix lived for 53 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-08600839.summary: A funerary inscription recording the age at death and burial place of Decimus Caetrius Felix.

EDCS-08600840.translation: Ilia Fortunata, a dutiful woman, lived for 40 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-08600840.summary: A funerary inscription recording the age at death and burial place of Ilia Fortunata.

EDCS-08600841.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Marcus Lucretius lived for 52 years.
EDCS-08600841.summary: A funerary inscription recording the age at death of Marcus Lucretius.

EDCS-08600842.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Marcus Lucretius Silanus lived for 51 years.
EDCS-08600842.summary: A funerary inscription recording the age at death of Marcus Lucretius Silanus.

EDCS-08600843.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Petronia Felicula lived for [unknown] years.
EDCS-08600843.summary: A funerary inscription recording the name of Petronia Felicula, with an incomplete age at death.

EDCS-08600845.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Quintus lived for 75 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-08600845.summary: A funerary inscription recording the age at death and burial place of Quintus.

EDCS-08600846.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Rup Ianuarius lived 65 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-08600846.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Rup Ianuarius, who lived 65 years.

EDCS-08600847.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Salustia Ospita lived 75 years.
EDCS-08600847.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Salustia Ospita, who lived 75 years.

EDCS-08600848.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Saluvius Felix, dutiful, lived 43 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-08600848.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Saluvius Felix, who lived 43 years.

EDCS-08600849.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Sata ra Meridanus lived 75 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-08600849.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Sata ra Meridanus, who lived 75 years.

EDCS-08600850.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Pius Saturninus [lived] 65 years.
EDCS-08600850.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Pius Saturninus, whose age is given as 65.

EDCS-08600851.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Secunda Trebelia. Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Postumus Saturninus lived 70 years.
EDCS-08600851.summary: This inscription records two individuals, Secunda Trebelia and Postumus Saturninus, with the latter having lived 70 years.

EDCS-08600852.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Tannonia Felicia lived 35 years. She is buried here. Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Elius Felix.
EDCS-08600852.summary: This inscription honors Tannonia Felicia, who lived 35 years, and also mentions Elius Felix.

EDCS-08600853.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Tannonia Fortunata lived [X] years. Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Marcus Duresius Barachianus lived 91 years.
EDCS-08600853.summary: This inscription records the lifespans of Tannonia Fortunata (partially illegible) and Marcus Duresius Barachianus, who lived 91 years.

EDCS-08600854.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Tanonia Getula lived 30 years. She is buried here. Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Lucius Tanonius Ini lived 55 years.
EDCS-08600854.summary: This inscription honors Tanonia Getula, who lived 30 years, and Lucius Tanonius Ini, who lived 55 years.

EDCS-08600855.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Lucius Tanonius Flavi lived 91 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-08600855.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Tanonius Flavi, who lived 91 years.

EDCS-08600856.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Tanonius Namphamo lived 75 years; he is buried here. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Postumia Matrona lived 85 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-08600856.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Tanonius Namphamo and Postumia Matrona, with their ages at death.

EDCS-08600857.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Pious Tertulla lived 21 years.
EDCS-08600857.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Tertulla, with her age at death.

EDCS-08600858.summary: This is a fragmentary epitaph for Trebellius Primus, recording his age at death, with the age incomplete.

EDCS-08600859.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Caius Vettius Firmus lived 81 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-08600859.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Caius Vettius Firmus, with his age at death.

EDCS-08600860.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Nunius Rosi lived 77 years.
EDCS-08600860.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Nunius Rosi, with his age at death.

EDCS-08600861.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Victor lived 30 years.
EDCS-08600861.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Victor, with his age at death.

EDCS-08600862.translation: Barigbal, son of Homullus, lived 53 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-08600862.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Barigbal, son of Homullus, with his age at death.

EDCS-08600863.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Flavia Victoria. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Quintus Octavius Victor lived 4 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-08600863.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Flavia Victoria and Quintus Octavius Victor, with the latter's age at death.

EDCS-08600864.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Publius Cacius Maximus lived 65 years.
EDCS-08600864.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Publius Cacius Maximus, with his age at death.

EDCS-08600865.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Papinia Maxima lived 87 years. Ceianius Rogatus [dedicated this] for her merits.
EDCS-08600865.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Papinia Maxima, with her age at death, and mentions Ceianius Rogatus as the dedicator.

EDCS-08600866.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Saturninus lived 35 years.
EDCS-08600866.summary: A funerary epitaph for Saturninus, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08600869.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Publius Aerius Danaius, dutiful, lived 60 years and is buried here. Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Pora Forinata, dutiful, lived 40 years and is buried here.
EDCS-08600869.summary: A double funerary epitaph for Publius Aerius Danaius and Pora Forinata, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08600870.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lucilla, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08600871.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Geminia Severa, dutiful, lived 80 years and is buried here.
EDCS-08600871.summary: A funerary epitaph for Geminia Severa, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08600872.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Pompeia Crispina lived [---] years.
EDCS-08600872.summary: A funerary epitaph for Pompeia Crispina, with a missing lifespan, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08600873.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Gaius Titurnius Felix, son of Gaius, lived 62 years and is buried here. Titurnius erected this for his father out of duty.
EDCS-08600873.summary: A funerary epitaph for Gaius Titurnius Felix, erected by his son Titurnius, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08600875.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Lucius Cassius Ianuarius Severianus, dutiful, lived 40 years and is buried here.
EDCS-08600875.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lucius Cassius Ianuarius Severianus, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08600876.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Lucius Geminius Ianuarius Minnus lived 8 years, 6 months, and 10 days.
EDCS-08600876.summary: A funerary epitaph for the child Lucius Geminius Ianuarius Minnus, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08600877.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Lucius Geminius Mustulus lived 37 years, 8 months, and 17 days.
EDCS-08600877.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lucius Geminius Mustulus, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08600878.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Lucius Mal Victor the younger lived 25 years and four months.
EDCS-08600878.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lucius Mal Victor the younger, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08600879.translation: Publius Terentius Otodorus the pious lived 80 years.
EDCS-08600879.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Publius Terentius Otodorus.

EDCS-08600881.translation: Sacred to Liber Pater Augustus, dedicated by Caelianus, an outstanding man, perpetual priest of Augustus of the colony of Zama Regia, and priest of the god Magnes.
EDCS-08600881.summary: This is a religious dedication to the god Liber Pater by Caelianus, who held several prominent priesthoods in the colony of Zama Regia.

EDCS-08600882.translation: The vow was fulfilled to Saturn on a good day by Regilla.
EDCS-08600882.summary: This is a votive inscription recording the fulfillment of a vow to the god Saturn by Regilla.

EDCS-08600883.translation: Marcus Aranius Prulus, a citizen of exceptional kindness and unmatched in promoting public and private interests, made this at his own expense for Titus Julius Pansae Crispinianus, an outstanding man, curator of the public affairs of the most splendid colony of Zama Regia.
EDCS-08600883.summary: This is a dedication by Marcus Aranius Prulus to Titus Julius Pansae Crispinianus, a former official of the colony of Zama Regia, likely a posthumous honor or a memorial erected by a friend.

EDCS-08600884.translation: Marenius Iulius Maracitanus and his family made this at their own expense for Titus Julius Pansae Crispinianus, an outstanding man, curator of the public affairs of the most splendid colony of Zama Regia, a man of singular kindness and unmatched in promoting public and private interests.
EDCS-08600884.summary: This is a dedication by Marenius Iulius Maracitanus and his family to Titus Julius Pansae Crispinianus, a former official of the colony of Zama Regia, likely a posthumous honor or a memorial erected by friends.

EDCS-08600885.translation: For Lucius Julius Victor Modianus, son of Lucius, of the Papiria tribe, an outstanding man, procurator of our lords Augusti of the province of Numidia for grain supply, because of his exceptional benevolence and integrity towards them.
EDCS-08600885.summary: This is a dedication honoring Lucius Julius Victor Modianus, a procurator responsible for grain supply in Numidia, for his service to the emperors.

EDCS-08600886.translation: The singer sings, the defeated shouts, the traveler rejoices.
EDCS-08600886.summary: This inscription is a short, possibly proverbial or playful, statement about contrasting reactions to an event.

EDCS-08600887.summary: This is a very brief inscription, likely a name, possibly marking ownership or a personal dedication.

EDCS-08600888.summary: This inscription consists solely of a name, likely a funerary epitaph or a personal marker.

EDCS-08600889.summary: This inscription is a patronymic name, possibly a funerary epitaph or a personal marker.

EDCS-08600890.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Novius Exoratus Arruntianus.

EDCS-08600891.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Phazania Saturnina.

EDCS-08600894.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcus Varius Rogatus.

EDCS-08600897.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Titus Ancharius Ianuarius lived for 15 years; he is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Anchari D. Sacred to the departed spirits. Saeia Quintula lived for 28 years; Ancharia Quarta lived for 2 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-08600897.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the deaths of Titus Ancharius Ianuarius, Saeia Quintula, and Ancharia Quarta.

EDCS-08600899.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Ancharia Quarta.

EDCS-08600901.translation: to the most powerful and invincible C. I. of the greatest father of the fatherland, the pontifex maximus, and Julia Domna Augusta, the city of Chusira, a temple collapsed by age.
EDCS-08600901.summary: This inscription records the city of Chusira dedicating a temple, possibly to Emperor Caracalla and Julia Domna, which had collapsed due to age.

EDCS-08600902.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Atia Crescentia, dutiful, lived for 85 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-08600902.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Atia Crescentia.

EDCS-08600906.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Aulonia Rufina lived for 80 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-08600906.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Aulonia Rufina.

EDCS-08600907.translation: Sacred to Mercury Augustus. Publius Attius Arnensi Felix, because of the honor of the augurship, placed the promised statue and temple with his own money by decree of the decurions, and he himself dedicated it.
EDCS-08600907.summary: This inscription records Publius Attius Arnensi Felix dedicating a statue and temple to Mercury Augustus, fulfilling a vow by decree of the local council.

EDCS-08600910.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus, prince of the youth, son of the Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus Arabicus Adiabenicus Parthicus Maximus, pontifex maximus, with tribunician power for the 7th time, consul for the 2nd time, father of the fatherland, grandson of the deified Marcus Antoninus Germanicus Sarmaticus, great-grandson of the deified Antoninus Pius, great-great-grandson of the deified Hadrian, great-great-great-grandson of the deified Trajan, great-great-great-great-grandson of the deified Nerva, son of Dino Egge Marullus, a man of consular rank, son of D. Cossonius Scipio Orfitus, a most distinguished man, his legate, the city of Maraguitana Sara, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-08600910.summary: This inscription is a dedication by the city of Maraguitana Sara to Emperor Caracalla, listing his extensive titles and ancestry, likely commissioned during his consulship or early reign.

EDCS-08600911.translation: Marcus Iulius Pacatus, son of Vindex, pious, lived 17 months, is buried here.
EDCS-08600911.summary: A tombstone recording the short life and burial of Marcus Iulius Pacatus.

EDCS-08600913.summary: An inscription noting the establishment of something by Bishop Symeon.

EDCS-08600915.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Iulia Rogata, pious, lived 12 years, 12 months, 10 days.
EDCS-08600915.summary: A funerary inscription for Iulia Rogata, recording her age at death.

EDCS-08600916.translation: Caius Iulius Felix lived 80 years, piously, is buried here.
EDCS-08600916.summary: A tombstone recording the life and burial of Caius Iulius Felix.

EDCS-08600918.translation: By the authority of the Emperor Vespasian Caesar Augustus, father of the country, the boundaries of the new and old province were rectified where the Royal Canal was, under the consulship of Rutilius Gallicus, priest, and the propraetorian legates of the Emperor, Sentius Caecilianus.
EDCS-08600918.summary: An official decree from the Flavian period, likely the 1st century CE, defining provincial boundaries under the authority of Emperor Vespasian and executed by imperial legates.

EDCS-08600919.text_edition: \n Ex auctoritate Imperatoris Vespasiani Caesaris Augusti patris patriae fines provinciae novae et veteris derecti qua fossa regia fuit per Rutilium Gallicum consulem pontificem et Sentium Caecilianum praetorem legatos Augusti pro praetore\n
EDCS-08600919.translation: By the authority of Emperor Vespasian Caesar Augustus, father of the country, the boundaries of the new and old provinces were demarcated, where the royal ditch was, under Rutilius Gallicus, consul and pontifex, and Sentius Caecilianus, praetor, legates of the emperor.
EDCS-08600919.summary: An official inscription recording the demarcation of provincial boundaries under Emperors Vespasian, Rutilius Gallicus, and Sentius Caecilianus, likely from the Flavian period.

EDCS-08600921.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Sacconius. Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed.
EDCS-08600921.summary: A funerary inscription, possibly a dedication to the underworld deities by Sacconius.

EDCS-08600922.translation: Sacred to Caelestis Augusta. Publius Geminius Cossus willingly paid his vow, as deserved.
EDCS-08600922.summary: A votive inscription from Publius Geminius Cossus dedicating something to the goddess Caelestis Augusta.

EDCS-08600923.translation: Sacred to Mercury Augustus. The owners of the Tappus estate, in the year of the magistracies of Lucius Geminius Rogatus and Julius Geminianus, under the supervision of Tannus Felix Primianus and S.
EDCS-08600923.summary: A dedication to Mercury Augustus made by landowners of the Tappus estate during a specific year of local magistracies.

EDCS-08600924.translation: For the safety of the Emperors Augusti Severus and Antoninus and Geta Caesar and Iulia Augusta and Fulvia Plautilla. Caius Aufidius Utilis Mancianus, a worshipper, willingly paid his vow with a willing heart.
EDCS-08600924.summary: A votive inscription from the reign of Septimius Severus (early 3rd century CE), expressing loyalty and good wishes to the imperial family.

EDCS-08600926.summary: A fragmentary inscription suggesting a dedication or recognition inspired by someone's leniency or kindness.

EDCS-08600927.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcus Antonius Victor Extricatianus lived 20 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-08600927.summary: A funerary inscription recording the death and burial of Marcus Antonius Victor Extricatianus.

EDCS-08600931.translation: Quintus Sabidius Victor made this monument for himself while alive. He lived 30 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-08600931.summary: A funerary inscription recording the self-funded monument of Quintus Sabidius Victor.

EDCS-08600933.translation: The martyrdom of Saint Stephen, the first, on the twelfth day before the Kalends of November.
EDCS-08600933.summary: A funerary or commemorative inscription marking the date of Saint Stephen's martyrdom.

EDCS-08600934.translation: Felix, son of Felicianus, lived in peace for 80 years.
EDCS-08600934.summary: A funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Felix, son of Felicianus.

EDCS-08600935.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Aufidia Rogata, daughter of Rogatus, pious, lived 31 years. She is buried here. May the earth rest lightly upon you.
EDCS-08600935.summary: A funerary inscription for Aufidia Rogata, daughter of Rogatus, including a common wish for the deceased.

EDCS-08600940.translation: Cata Stisicis, daughter of Baliathon, wife of Vibus Mento, pious, lived 50 years. She is buried here. May the earth rest lightly upon you.
EDCS-08600940.summary: A funerary inscription for Cata Stisicis, daughter of Baliathon and wife of Vibus Mento.

EDCS-08600941.translation: For Germanicus. Caius Aufidius Macer took care to have this made at his own expense for the Roman citizens who reside in Suo.
EDCS-08600941.summary: An inscription indicating Caius Aufidius Macer funded a project for the Roman citizens living in Suo.

EDCS-08600942.translation: Marcus Tuccius Felicio, freedman of Marcus Tuccius the veteran, made this at his own expense.
EDCS-08600942.summary: An inscription recording the self-funded monument of Marcus Tuccius Felicio, a freedman.

EDCS-08600943.summary: A very brief inscription, likely a tombstone, naming Gaius Sempronius Ianuarius and Petronia Proba.

EDCS-08600946.translation: Sacred to Mars Augustus. Primus, son of Germanus Diopanthus, priest of Saturn, gladly paid his vow to Mars Augustus and Saturn, a silver palm worth 10 denarii.
EDCS-08600946.summary: A votive inscription by Primus, priest of Saturn, dedicating a silver palm to Mars Augustus and Saturn.

EDCS-08600947.translation: Of Saturn, Sol, Luna, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus.
EDCS-08600947.summary: This inscription is a list of deities, likely dedicating a shrine or a series of altars.

EDCS-08600948.translation: Aninia Laeta, daughter of Marcus, fulfilled her vow.
EDCS-08600948.summary: This inscription records a woman, Aninia Laeta, fulfilling a votive offering.

EDCS-08600950.summary: This is a simple funerary epitaph for Petronia Saturnina.

EDCS-08600951.translation: Marcus Bullatius Victor erected a bronze statue, which he was to dedicate in honor of his quinquennial magistracy, in addition to the legally required 3,000 sesterces for 2,000,000 sesterces, and...
EDCS-08600951.summary: This is a dedication by Marcus Bullatius Victor of a bronze statue, likely for a public office, possibly dating to the reign of Marcus Aurelius or Commodus.

EDCS-08600953.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the emperor Septimius Severus.

EDCS-08600956.translation: The colonia Iulia Aurelia Commoda Thuburbo Maius, devoted to their divine majesty and authority, [dedicates this] to the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Carus Pius Felix Augustus Invictus, Pontifex Maximus, holder of tribunician power, Consul, Father of the Fatherland, Proconsul, and to Marcus Aurelius Carinus Nobilissimus Caesar Augustus, pacifiers of the world and all nations.
EDCS-08600956.summary: This inscription is a dedication by the colonia of Thuburbo Maius to Emperors Carus and Carinus, likely from the late 3rd century CE.

EDCS-08600957.translation: Marcus Vettius Myrinus, freedman, to his most excellent patron, by decree of the decurions, using public funds: to Marcus Vettius, son of Caius, of the Quirina tribe, Latro, flamen of the deified Augustus, priest of Ceres, aged 137 years, holder of the public horse, admitted into the five decuries, prefect of the I Alpine Cohort, mounted, honored with military gifts by the Emperor Caesar Nerva Trajan Augustus Germanicus Dacicus with a pure spear, a wall crown, a silver vexillum, tribune of the II Adiutrix Pia Fidelis legion, prefect of the Silian ala of Roman citizens, awarded the torque and armilla, procurator of the grain supply of Ostia and Portus, procurator of the province of Sicily, procurator of the Cottian Alps, procurator of Mauretania Caesariensis.
EDCS-08600957.summary: This inscription honors Marcus Vettius Latro, a prominent figure with extensive military and administrative career, likely erected in the 2nd century CE by his freedman.

EDCS-08600958.translation: Marcus Vettius, son of Caius, of the Quirina tribe, Latro, flamen of the deified Augustus, priest of Ceres, aged 137 years, holder of the public horse, admitted into the five decuries, prefect of the fabrum, prefect of the I Alpine Cohort, mounted, honored by the Emperor Nerva Trajan Caesar Augustus Germanicus Dacicus with military gifts, a pure spear, a vexillum, and a wall crown, tribune of the II Adiutrix Pia Fidelis legion, prefect of the Silian ala of Roman citizens, awarded the torque and armilla.
EDCS-08600958.summary: This inscription details the honors and career of Marcus Vettius Latro, likely a posthumous dedication or a record of his achievements during the reign of Trajan.

EDCS-08600959.translation: Lucius Apollodorus Paterno, to his most distinguished patrons, by decree of the decurions, with public money.
EDCS-08600959.summary: This inscription records a dedication to patrons by Lucius Apollodorus Paterno, funded by the local community.

EDCS-08600960.text_edition: \n Publio Attio Anniano Iuliano Publi filio Arnensi flamini divi Titi coloniae Iuliae Karthaginis sacerdoti Aesculapi bis equo publico adlecto ab Impperatoribus Caessaribus Marco Aurelio Antonino et Marco Aurelio Commodo Antonino Auggustis Sarmaticis Germanicis ob pietatis flamin--- mque N locus datus decreto decurionum\n
EDCS-08600960.translation: To Publius Attius Annianus Iulianus, son of Publius, of the Arnensian tribe, priest of the deified Titus of the colony Julia Karthago, priest of Aesculapius, twice enrolled by the equites by the Emperors Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus and Marcus Aurelius Commodus Antoninus Augusti Sarmaticus Germanicus for his piety and priesthood, a place was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-08600960.summary: This inscription records the granting of a public space to Publius Attius Annianus Iulianus, a prominent local official in Karthago, likely dating to the co-reign of Marcus Aurelius and Commodus.

EDCS-08600961.translation: To Gaius Caesennius Auctus, son of Publius, for his generosity by his brother Caesennius Secundus, by decree of the decurions, with public money.
EDCS-08600961.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Gaius Caesennius Auctus for his generosity, funded by his brother and the community.

EDCS-08600962.translation: Lucius Caesennius Auctus Aurelianus, son of Lucius Caesennius Secundio, honoured by the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus with the public equestrian rank, gave this gift from the will of his father.
EDCS-08600962.summary: This inscription records a gift made by Lucius Caesennius Auctus Aurelianus, who received a prestigious honour from the emperor, funded by his father's will.

EDCS-08600963.translation: To Lucius Caesennius Auctus Aurelianus, from the will of his father Secundio.
EDCS-08600963.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Lucius Caesennius Auctus Aurelianus, funded by his father's will.

EDCS-08600965.translation: The curiales of all eleven curiae, at the decree of the decurions, erected this at their own expense for Quintus Geminius Felix Baebianus Caesennianus, annual flamen.
EDCS-08600965.summary: This inscription records the erection of a monument by the curiales of eleven districts for Quintus Geminius Felix Baebianus Caesennianus, an annual flamen, funded by their own money and approved by the decurions.

EDCS-08600966.translation: To Quintus Geminius Saturninus Caesennianus, twice consul for five years, perpetual flamen, quaestor, prefect with judicial authority.
EDCS-08600966.summary: This inscription lists the distinguished public offices held by Quintus Geminius Saturninus Caesennianus.

EDCS-08600967.translation: To Lucius Julius Secundus Botrianus, prefect with judicial authority of the colony of Concordia Iulia Karthago. Gnaeus Cornelius Felix Aeeta, quaestor. And Lucius Julius Cnaei filius Secundus Botrianus.
EDCS-08600967.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Lucius Julius Secundus Botrianus, prefect with judicial authority of Karthago, and mentions Gnaeus Cornelius Felix Aeeta and Lucius Julius Cnaei filius Secundus Botrianus.

EDCS-08600969.translation: Bosthar son of Bardas, son of Asdrubal, son of Echo, son of Iddibal, son of Mian, son of Thaddac, son of Bosthar, son of Sider, son of Muthumbal, son of Audasso, son of Asdrubal, son of Mindig, son of Acho, son of Chubur. The cella was built and completed with plastered decoration. It was executed under the supervision of Mastlivus Sucan, collector, and Miana, who later came to Sapotes Ruces. The work was commissioned by the contractors listed above.
EDCS-08600969.summary: This inscription details the construction and decoration of a cella, listing numerous patrons and contractors, likely in a Punic context, with a complex familial lineage and oversight by tax collectors.

EDCS-08600973.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus Memmius lived X years; he is buried here.
EDCS-08600973.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Quintus Memmius, stating his lifespan and burial place.

EDCS-08600974.summary: This is a simple funerary inscription naming Terentia Satura.

EDCS-08600976.translation: Fortuna the faithful, laid to rest in peace on the sixth day before the Kalends of February.
EDCS-08600976.summary: This inscription records the burial of 'Fortuna the faithful' on a specific date.

EDCS-08600977.translation: Boraides the faithful, lived 85 years, buried in April, during the indiction.
EDCS-08600977.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespan and burial date of Boraides the faithful.

EDCS-08600978.translation: Let men enter and let dogs be kept out; I, Esizosus, built and completed it. Whoever seeks me will find the work easy.
EDCS-08600978.summary: This is an owner's inscription on a building, likely a shop or workshop, stating the builder's name and a proud claim about the quality of his work.

EDCS-08600979.translation: To our lords and Augusti, Marcus Catillius Felicianus [erected this].
EDCS-08600979.summary: This is a dedication to the reigning emperors, likely by Marcus Catillius Felicianus, possibly on a public building or monument.

EDCS-08600981.translation: To our lord Flavius Valentinianus Pius Felix Augustus, the town council of Giufi, together with the curator of the state, devoted to his divine will and majesty.
EDCS-08600981.summary: This inscription records the devotion of the town council and curator of Giufi to the emperor Valentinian, likely on a public monument dedicated to him.

EDCS-08600984.translation: Quintus Bellenus Nicephorus dedicated this to Vereia Lucida, his most chaste and most holy wife and most dutiful mother.
EDCS-08600984.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated by a husband to his deceased wife, highlighting her virtues as a spouse and mother.

EDCS-08600985.translation: Sacred to Saturn Augustus. Lucius Elvius Caius gladly paid his vow.
EDCS-08600985.summary: This is a votive inscription to the god Saturn, indicating Lucius Elvius Caius fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-08600989.translation: Sacred to Saturn Magnus. Octavius Proculus gladly paid his vow.
EDCS-08600989.summary: This is a votive inscription to the god Saturn Magnus, indicating Octavius Proculus fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-08600990.translation: Sacred to Saturn Magnus. Marcus Salvius gladly paid his vow.
EDCS-08600990.summary: This is a votive inscription to the god Saturn Magnus, indicating Marcus Salvius fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-08600991.translation: Sacred to Saturn Magnus. Publius Suficius Celsianus gladly paid his vow.
EDCS-08600991.summary: This is a votive inscription to the god Saturn Magnus, indicating Publius Suficius Celsianus fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-08600992.translation: Sacred to Saturn Magnus. Ivolus Saturus gladly paid his vow.
EDCS-08600992.summary: This is a votive inscription to the god Saturn Magnus, indicating Ivolus Saturus fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-08600999.translation: To Quintus Appaeus Felicis son of Felicis, a citizen of the entire community of Gorita, a citizen and patron, by decree of the decurions, at public expense.
EDCS-08600999.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a public monument or building by the city council of Gorita to Quintus Appaeus Felicis, honoring him as a citizen and patron.

EDCS-08601000.translation: To Uranius Gaius Marius Caelestinus, decurion of the community of Goritana, his mother Maria and his father Marius erected this statue to their most dutiful son, promising for its dedication one thousand denarii from its revenue, as long as there was a pugilist and a feast for the decurions, and afterwards... given from this place by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-08601000.summary: A statue was erected by parents for their son, a decurion, with funds promised for its dedication and upkeep.

EDCS-08601003.translation: To Quintus Geminius Sabinus, son of Quintus, of the Arnensis tribe, centurion of the 7th Gemina legion, centurion of the 6th Ferrata legion, centurion of the 14th Martia Gemina Victrix legion, centurion of the 10th Gemina Pia Fidelis legion, centurion of the 3rd Augusta legion, chief centurion of the 7th Gemina legion, primus pilus and princeps peregrinorum, honored with gifts by the Emperor Caesar Trajanus Augustus Germanicus with a vallaris crown, torques, armillae, and phalerae, Prefect of the 10th Fretensis legion in the German war; the villagers of the Annaei district, for whom the same Geminius Sabinus ordered this to be made by his will, erected and dedicated it in the magistracy year of Decimus Annaeus Advena of the Arnensis tribe.
EDCS-08601003.summary: A monument dedicated by villagers to Quintus Geminius Sabinus, a highly decorated military officer, as stipulated in his will.

EDCS-08601004.translation: To Quintus Geminius Sabinus, son of Quintus, of the Arnensis tribe, centurion of the 7th Gemina legion, centurion of the 6th Ferrata legion, centurion of the 14th Martia Gemina Victrix legion, centurion of the 10th Gemina Pia Fidelis legion, centurion of the 3rd Augusta legion, chief centurion of the 7th Gemina legion, primus pilus and princeps peregrinorum, honored with gifts by the Emperor Caesar Trajanus Augustus Germanicus with a vallaris crown, torques, armillae, and phalerae, Prefect of the 10th Fretensis legion in the German war; the villagers of the Annaei district, for whom the same Geminius Sabinus ordered this to be made by his will, erected and dedicated it by decree of the decurions with public funds.
EDCS-08601004.summary: A monument dedicated by villagers to Quintus Geminius Sabinus, a highly decorated military officer, as stipulated in his will, funded by the state.

EDCS-08601006.translation: Minucius, son of Caius, of the Iulia tribe, Felicis.
EDCS-08601006.summary: A simple funerary dedication for Minucius.

EDCS-08601007.translation: Glory to God in the highest. Pia Iulia Fauti, martyr. In peace.
EDCS-08601007.summary: A Christian epitaph commemorating Pia Iulia Fauti, a martyr, dated between the 4th and 6th centuries CE.

EDCS-08601012.summary: A short epitaph for Faustinianus, a martyr.

EDCS-08601017.translation: Floriana, sweet one, living always in God. Rendered on the 17th day before the Kalends of August in the year M [likely 1000 or 1000 AD].
EDCS-08601017.summary: A Christian epitaph for Floriana, dated to the 17th day before the Kalends of August in the year 1000.

EDCS-08601019.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Antonia Donata established this place for herself and her most dutiful husband.
EDCS-08601019.summary: A funerary inscription set up by Antonia Donata for herself and her husband.

EDCS-08601020.translation: To Saturn, he fulfilled his vow willingly.
EDCS-08601020.summary: A votive inscription dedicated to the god Saturn.

EDCS-08601021.translation: He fulfilled his vow willingly, devoted to his divine power.
EDCS-08601021.summary: A votive inscription expressing devotion and fulfillment of a vow to a deity.

EDCS-08601022.translation: With tribunician power, father of the fatherland, proconsul.
EDCS-08601022.summary: This inscription fragment records titles held by a Roman official, likely an emperor, indicating his political and military authority.

EDCS-08601023.translation: To Flavius Constantinus Pius Felix, our lord and restorer of public liberty.
EDCS-08601023.summary: This dedicatory inscription honors Emperor Flavius Constantinus (Constantine the Great) as the restorer of public liberty.

EDCS-08601024.translation: By virtue, clemency, and memorable piety, surpassing all, to our lord Flavius Claudius Constantinus Iunior Augustus, Lucius Papinius Pacatianus, Flavius Ablabius, Caius Annius Tiberianus, Nestorius, Timonianus, most illustrious men and praetorian prefects.
EDCS-08601024.summary: This inscription honors Emperor Flavius Claudius Constantinus Iunior (Constantine the Younger) and lists high-ranking officials, likely praetorian prefects, who dedicated it.

EDCS-08601025.summary: This inscription records the name and priestly office of Atreius Ianuarius.

EDCS-08601028.translation: To the envious virgin, live and see more.
EDCS-08601028.summary: This is an unusual, perhaps personal or humorous, inscription addressed to a virgin, wishing her to live long and witness more.

EDCS-08601029.translation: Margarita, faithful, lived in peace for 83 years, laid to rest on the 5th day before the Kalends of December in the 33rd year.
EDCS-08601029.summary: This funerary inscription records the name, lifespan, and burial date of Margarita, indicating a Christian context with 'in pace' and a regnal year.

EDCS-08601031.summary: This short inscription likely refers to a deceased individual named Maurus, in a Christian context indicated by 'in pace'.

EDCS-08601034.summary: This inscription seems to commemorate Dativa and her grandchildren, possibly on a tomb or monument.

EDCS-08601037.summary: This inscription simply records the name Sextus Bullatius Saramanna, possibly as an owner or dedicator.

EDCS-08601038.translation: Victor, priest, paid his vow to Lord Saturn of Siga.
EDCS-08601038.summary: This inscription records a vow paid by a priest named Victor to the deity Saturn of Siga.

EDCS-08601039.translation: Sacred to Saturn Augustus. Quintus Fullonius Felix, priest, gladly fulfilled his vow.
