EDCS-08601039.summary: A religious dedication to Saturn Augustus by a priest named Quintus Fullonius Felix.

EDCS-08601040.summary: A very brief inscription, possibly naming individuals or a place.

EDCS-08601049.translation: Sacred to Juno Caelestis. [Belonging to] Ae. Claudia Theophila, freedwoman of the Augusti, procurator.
EDCS-08601049.summary: A religious dedication to Juno Caelestis by Ae. Claudia Theophila, a freedwoman and procurator.

EDCS-08601050.translation: Tertulla, a young maiden, lived 30 years and departed on the 14th day before the Kalends of February.
EDCS-08601050.summary: A funerary epitaph for Tertulla, recording her age at death and the date of her passing.

EDCS-08601051.translation: Gaudentius departed in peace at age 14. Felicitas departed in peace at age 12.
EDCS-08601051.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the peaceful passing of two young individuals, Gaudentius and Felicitas.

EDCS-08601052.translation: Vitrix in the Lord's peace departed on the 3rd day before the Ides of April. Victoria departed.
EDCS-08601052.summary: A funerary epitaph for Vitrix and Victoria, mentioning their passing 'in pace domini' (in the Lord's peace), suggesting a Christian context.

EDCS-08601053.translation: Sweet Dalmatia lived 30 years in peace and departed on the 15th day before the Kalends of January.
EDCS-08601053.summary: A funerary epitaph for Dalmatia, recording her age at death and the date of her passing, with an expression of endearment.

EDCS-08601054.translation: Donata lived 55 years in peace and departed on the 7th day before the Kalends of May.
EDCS-08601054.summary: A funerary epitaph for Donata, recording her age at death and the date of her passing, indicating she died 'in pace' (in peace).

EDCS-08601056.translation: Munatia Christiana lived 70 years and departed on the 9th day before the Ides of February.
EDCS-08601056.summary: A funerary epitaph for Munatia Christiana, recording her age at death and the date of her passing.

EDCS-08601057.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Sweet Piculus lived more or less 72 years in peace.
EDCS-08601057.summary: A funerary epitaph to the Manes for Piculus, recording his approximate age at death and noting he lived 'in pace' (in peace).

EDCS-08601058.translation: Popla lived 18 years, 1 month, and 27 days; she is here in peace.
EDCS-08601058.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Popla, recording her age at death.

EDCS-08601060.translation: Felicitas, faithful, lived 30 years; buried on the 8th day before the Ides of January.
EDCS-08601060.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Felicitas, recording her age and date of burial.

EDCS-08601062.translation: Sacred to Aesculapius Augustus. Zmaragdus, a servant of Augustus from Augustana, on behalf of himself and his companion Flavia Euphrosyne, enlarged a small shrine worn out by age at his own expense, and placed two Numidian columns and a marble pediment, and gilded it himself, and gave a vow with a purple-bordered garment to Aesculapius and to the Divine Pantheon. Caeler, servant and custos of the granaries of our Caesar, renewed it and clothed it with a vow and placed a silver palm at his own expense.
EDCS-08601062.summary: This is a dedication recording the restoration and embellishment of a shrine to Aesculapius and the Divine Pantheon by Zmaragdus and Caeler, officials serving the emperor.

EDCS-08601069.translation: Sacred to Nemesis Augusta. Honoratus Lucius Gressius and Caius Cererius Rogatianus.
EDCS-08601069.summary: This is a dedication to the goddess Nemesis Augusta, made by Honoratus Lucius Gressius and Caius Cererius Rogatianus.

EDCS-08601072.summary: This is a brief dedication to the god Saturn Augustus.

EDCS-08601073.translation: Erucius willingly fulfilled his vow to the Lord.
EDCS-08601073.summary: This is a votive inscription by Erucius, fulfilling a vow to a deity referred to as "Domino".

EDCS-08601074.translation: Gaius Valerius Faustinus willingly fulfilled his vow on behalf of his daughter.
EDCS-08601074.summary: This is a votive inscription by Gaius Valerius Faustinus, who fulfilled a vow for his daughter.

EDCS-08601075.summary: This is a brief votive inscription by Ius Athoius.

EDCS-08601077.text_edition: \n Publius Valerius Alexa Publi libertus pius vixit nnos LXX sacerdos Cererum hic situs est nni CV Luci filia Valeria Secunda pia fuit in suis vixit nnos LXX hic sita est\n
EDCS-08601077.translation: Publius Valerius Alexa, freedman of Publius, pious, lived 70 years, priest of Ceres. Here lies Lucius, son of Anna, Valeria Secunda, pious, was his. She lived 70 years, here she lies.
EDCS-08601077.summary: This funerary inscription records the lives and burial of Publius Valerius Alexa, a priest of Ceres, and Valeria Secunda, with their ages and familial connections, in the Roman colony of Karthago.

EDCS-08601078.translation: To the divine Nerva Augustus Germanicus.
EDCS-08601078.summary: This is a dedication to the deified emperor Nerva Augustus Germanicus.

EDCS-08601079.translation: To Anto, tribune of the soldiers of the legion, of the province of Pannonia.
EDCS-08601079.summary: This is a dedication to Anto, a military tribune in Pannonia.

EDCS-08601081.translation: To Aurelius, a man of consular rank.
EDCS-08601081.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Aurelius, a man of consular rank.

EDCS-08601082.translation: To Diana, his wife, from Maritius, procurator of the Augusti.
EDCS-08601082.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Diana, wife of Maritius, who was a procurator of the emperors.

EDCS-08601084.translation: To Diana, his wife, from T. Aarius, procurator of the Augusti.
EDCS-08601084.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Diana, wife of T. Aarius, who was a procurator of the emperors.

EDCS-08601089.summary: This inscription lists the names of three individuals: Rusticus, Thallus, and Fortunatus.

EDCS-08601092.translation: To the departed spirits. Marcius Callinicus, father and physician of the II Adiutrix Legion, and Tettedia Hygia, mother, erected this for their well-deserving son who lived for one year and five months.
EDCS-08601092.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by parents for their young son, who served as a physician in the II Adiutrix Legion.

EDCS-08601093.translation: Gaius Julius, son of Caius, of the Quirina tribe, a soldier of the III Augusta Legion, from Chirtis, served for 3 years, lived 28 years. Pious, he rests here. Caius Fadius, a fellow citizen, took care of this.
EDCS-08601093.summary: This is a funerary monument for Gaius Julius, a soldier of the III Augusta Legion, erected by Caius Fadius.

EDCS-08601095.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the emperors.

EDCS-08601096.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Paconius, a priest.

EDCS-08601098.summary: This inscription likely refers to a quinquennalis, an official holding office for five years, with the initials R.R.

EDCS-08601100.translation: Architect, pious, lived 10 years. He rests here.
EDCS-08601100.summary: This is a funerary monument for a young architect who died at the age of ten.

EDCS-08601103.translation: To the Alma Mater of Carthage
EDCS-08601103.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the Alma Mater of Carthage, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-08601106.translation: Deborosi X and others made this wall from Tuaddanis for a thousand paces.
EDCS-08601106.summary: This inscription records the construction of a wall by a group of individuals, possibly from Tuaddanis, dated to the Roman period.

EDCS-08601107.summary: This inscription simply records the name and title of Lulullus, a secretary, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-08601108.translation: Dardanius, the proconsul, for the Baths.
EDCS-08601108.summary: This inscription indicates a dedication by Dardanius, a proconsul, likely for the benefit of public baths, dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-08601110.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Siraton, son of Horatius, probable from the Roman period.

EDCS-08601121.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Laeta lived for 2 years and 2 days, born at Ostia, she is buried here.
EDCS-08601121.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a young girl named Laeta who died at the age of 2, born in Ostia, dated to the Roman period.

EDCS-08601122.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Publius Annaeus Mussius, a child, obedient to discipline, never disrespectful, a loving son to his parents, acting well and doing good.
EDCS-08601122.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a young boy, Publius Annaeus Mussius, highlighting his virtuous character and obedience, dated to the Roman period.

EDCS-08601123.translation: To the departed spirits. Caius Caeletharithus Faustinianus lived 18 and a half years. He lies here.
EDCS-08601123.summary: This is a short funerary epitaph for Caius Caeletharithus Faustinianus, who died at the age of 18, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08601124.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Lucius Elius Onoratus lived for 35 years, he is buried here.
EDCS-08601124.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Elius Onoratus, who died at the age of 35, dated to the Roman period.

EDCS-08601126.translation: Marcus Aemilius Ephagatus, dutiful, lived for 44 years.
EDCS-08601126.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcus Aemilius Ephagatus, who died at the age of 44, emphasizing his piety, dated to the Roman period.

EDCS-08601127.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Lucius Aemilius Secundulus, dutiful, lived for 25 years, he is buried here.
EDCS-08601127.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Aemilius Secundulus, who died at the age of 25, emphasizing his piety, dated to the Roman period.

EDCS-08601128.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Afrania Orbulania, dutiful, lived 41 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-08601128.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Afrania Orbulania, recording her age at death and burial.

EDCS-08601129.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Ampedius [died...].
EDCS-08601129.summary: This is a funerary epitaph, incomplete, beginning with a dedication to the departed spirits and naming Ampedius.

EDCS-08601131.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Publius Annaeus Romanus lived 2 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-08601131.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Publius Annaeus Romanus, recording his age at death and burial.

EDCS-08601133.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Auctus, who lived 5 years, 5 months, and 5 days, is buried here, having lived here.
EDCS-08601133.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Auctus, recording his age at death and burial.

EDCS-08601134.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Augenda, dutiful, lived 15 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-08601134.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Augenda, recording her age at death and burial.

EDCS-08601136.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Baebia Phiiurlia, dutiful, lived 46 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-08601136.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Baebia Phiiurlia, recording her age at death and burial.

EDCS-08601139.translation: Caecilia Felicia, dutiful, lived 22 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-08601139.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Caecilia Felicia, recording her age at death and burial.

EDCS-08601140.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus Caelus Hospes lived 2 years, 3 months, and 29 days.
EDCS-08601140.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Quintus Caelus Hospes, recording his age at death.

EDCS-08601141.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Caesia ta, dutiful, lived about 26 years.
EDCS-08601141.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Caesia ta, recording her approximate age at death.

EDCS-08601142.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Cesulema ve...
EDCS-08601142.summary: This is a funerary epitaph, incomplete, beginning with a dedication to the departed spirits and naming Cesulema.

EDCS-08601143.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Chrysis, the devoted, lived 30 years; here she is laid to rest.
EDCS-08601143.summary: A funerary epitaph for Chrysis, recording her devotion and age at death.

EDCS-08601145.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Cirtesia, the devoted, lived more or less 30 years; here she is laid to rest.
EDCS-08601145.summary: A funerary epitaph for Cirtesia, noting her devotion and approximate age at death.

EDCS-08601146.translation: Cluentia Fausta, daughter of Caius, lived 42 years; here she is laid to rest.
EDCS-08601146.summary: A funerary epitaph for Cluentia Fausta, stating her age at death.

EDCS-08601147.translation: Publius Cordius Probus, freedman of Publius, (and) Cordia Prima, freedwoman of Publius, (and) Frutila, freedwoman of Publius, (and) Caius Cordius Fortis, son of Publius, from the Arnensis tribe.
EDCS-08601147.summary: A funerary inscription for several individuals, likely a family group, listing their names, patronymic or freedman status, and tribal affiliation.

EDCS-08601148.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Cornelia, the devoted, lived [unknown age] years and 7 months.
EDCS-08601148.summary: A funerary epitaph for Cornelia, mentioning her devotion and completed months of life.

EDCS-08601149.summary: A simple funerary epitaph consisting only of a name.

EDCS-08601150.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Lucius Cornelius Iucundus, the devoted, lived 89 years and 1 month; here he is laid to rest.
EDCS-08601150.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lucius Cornelius Iucundus, recording his devotion and age at death.

EDCS-08601152.translation: Datus, son of Arius, aged 25, after the public works (service?) of Turr[a?], Evidius, aedile, dedicated (this).
EDCS-08601152.summary: An inscription recording Datus, son of Arius, aged 25, and mentioning a public works service and an aedile named Evidius, likely related to a funerary monument or public dedication.

EDCS-08601154.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Egnatia Dativa, the devoted, lived 10 years and 55 days; here she is laid to rest.
EDCS-08601154.summary: A funerary epitaph for Egnatia Dativa, noting her devotion and age at death.

EDCS-08601155.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Publius Egrilius Renatus, lived 30 years and 2 months; here he is laid to rest.
EDCS-08601155.summary: A funerary epitaph for Publius Egrilius Renatus, recording his age at death.

EDCS-08601156.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Sacred. Fabia Felicia, dutiful, lived 17 years and 3 months. She is laid here.
EDCS-08601156.summary: This funerary epitaph records the death of Fabia Felicia, who lived to be 17 years and 3 months old.

EDCS-08601158.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Sacred. Felicia, dutiful, lived 21 years. She is laid here.
EDCS-08601158.summary: This funerary epitaph records the death of Felicia, who lived to be 21 years old.

EDCS-08601160.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Sacred. Flavia Nice, dutiful, lived 52 years. She is laid here.
EDCS-08601160.summary: This funerary epitaph records the death of Flavia Nice, who lived to be 52 years old.

EDCS-08601161.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Sacred. Quintus Flavius.
EDCS-08601161.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription for Quintus Flavius.

EDCS-08601162.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Sacred. Fortunatus, dutiful, lived 3 years and 4 months. He is laid here.
EDCS-08601162.summary: This funerary epitaph records the death of Fortunatus, who lived to be 3 years and 4 months old.

EDCS-08601163.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Sacred. Lucius Fundanius Victor, most dutiful, lived 50 years and two months. His heir made [this tomb]. He is laid here.
EDCS-08601163.summary: This funerary epitaph records the death of Lucius Fundanius Victor, who lived to be 50 years and 2 months old, and states it was made by his heir.

EDCS-08601164.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely a funerary marker, for Gabinia Fortunata.

EDCS-08601165.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Sacred. Gargilia Ampliata, dutiful father, erected [this monument]. Lived 21 years. She is laid here.
EDCS-08601165.summary: This funerary epitaph records the death of Gargilia Ampliata, who lived to be 21 years old and was erected by her dutiful father.

EDCS-08601168.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Sacred. Iulius Fortunatus lived 30 years.
EDCS-08601168.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription for Iulius Fortunatus, who lived to be 30 years old.

EDCS-08601169.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Sacred. Caius Iulius Liberalis of Arnums, dutiful, lived 62 years. He is laid here.
EDCS-08601169.summary: This funerary epitaph records the death of Caius Iulius Liberalis of Arnums, who lived to be 62 years old.

EDCS-08601170.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Gaius Iunius Diphantus, dutiful, lived 40 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-08601170.summary: A funerary epitaph for Gaius Iunius Diphantus, recording his age and burial.

EDCS-08601171.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Licinia Maiorica, dutiful daughter of Lucius, lived 18 years.
EDCS-08601171.summary: A funerary epitaph for Licinia Maiorica, recording her age.

EDCS-08601172.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. His wife and sons made (this) for Gaius Licinius Felix, who was also called Duodecere, who lived 90 years.
EDCS-08601172.summary: A funerary epitaph for Gaius Licinius Felix, commissioned by his wife and sons, and recording his age.

EDCS-08601173.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Magnius Saturninus lived 2 years, 5 months, and 3 days. He is buried here.
EDCS-08601173.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lucius Magnius Saturninus, recording his age at death and burial.

EDCS-08601174.summary: A very brief inscription, likely a tombstone or dedication for Gaius Manlius Mercurius.

EDCS-08601175.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Manneia Victoria, dutiful, lived 70 years and 3 months. She is buried here.
EDCS-08601175.summary: A funerary epitaph for Manneia Victoria, recording her age and burial.

EDCS-08601176.translation: Marcia Caecilia, sacred to the departed spirits and to Mars, dutiful, lived [some number] years.
EDCS-08601176.summary: A funerary epitaph for Marcia Caecilia, sacred to both the departed spirits and Mars, with an incomplete recording of her age.

EDCS-08601177.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Memmia Veneria lived 53 years.
EDCS-08601177.summary: A funerary epitaph for Memmia Veneria, recording her age.

EDCS-08601179.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcus Messalinus Aliquas lived 30 years and 6 months and 5 days. His most dutiful sisters made (this).
EDCS-08601179.summary: A funerary epitaph for Marcus Messalinus Aliquas, commissioned by his sisters and recording his age at death.

EDCS-08601180.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus Mucius Donatianus, dutiful, lived 20 years and 6 months.
EDCS-08601180.summary: A funerary epitaph for Quintus Mucius Donatianus, recording his age at death.

EDCS-08601181.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Nata, dutiful, lived 21 years, 6 months, 10 days. She is buried here.
EDCS-08601181.summary: A tombstone recording the life span of Nata, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08601182.translation: Nicomachus lived 52 years, 7 months, 25 days. He is buried here.
EDCS-08601182.summary: A tombstone recording the life span of Nicomachus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08601183.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Niger existed for [number unclear] years.
EDCS-08601183.summary: A tombstone fragment recording the life span of Niger, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08601184.summary: A tombstone fragment with the name Nigillius Paternus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08601185.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Optata, dutiful, lived 24 years, 3 months, 13 days, made by her freedman husband ARV IA I D.
EDCS-08601185.summary: A tombstone recording the life span of Optata and mentioning her husband, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08601186.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Ortisia Victoria lived 100 years, 10 months, 7 days, 4 hours.
EDCS-08601186.summary: A tombstone recording the exceptionally long life span of Ortisia Victoria, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08601189.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Primitivos, dutiful, lived 3 years. Felicitas, dutiful, lived 8 years, 8 months. She is buried here.
EDCS-08601189.summary: A tombstone recording the short life spans of Primitivos and Felicitas, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08601191.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Prisca, dutiful, lived 13 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-08601191.summary: A tombstone recording the life span of Prisca, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08601194.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Quintus Rutilius Sapidus, dutiful, lived 21 years.
EDCS-08601194.summary: A tombstone recording the life span of Quintus Rutilius Sapidus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08601196.translation: Marcus Servilius Nicephorus, freedman of Marcus Servilius. Servilia Gymnasia, freedwoman of Marcus Servilius.
EDCS-08601196.summary: An epitaph possibly recording the manumission of two freedpersons, Marcus Servilius Nicephorus and Servilia Gymnasia, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08601197.translation: To the Divine Shades. Quintus Servilius Plebianus, dutiful, lived 25 years and 10 months. Flavius Bachyllus made this for his deserving son.
EDCS-08601197.summary: This is a tombstone recording the life and death of Quintus Servilius Plebianus, set up by Flavius Bachyllus.

EDCS-08601198.translation: To the Divine Shades. Caius Sulpicius Felix, dutiful, lived 40 years and some months.
EDCS-08601198.summary: This is a tombstone recording the life and death of Caius Sulpicius Felix.

EDCS-08601199.translation: Tadia Profutura, freedwoman of Caius, of the Publician family.
EDCS-08601199.summary: This is a tombstone for Tadia Profutura, a freedwoman.

EDCS-08601200.translation: To the Divine Shades. Spurius Tadius Securus, dutiful, lived 51 years, 3 months, and 12 days.
EDCS-08601200.summary: This is a tombstone recording the life and death of Spurius Tadius Securus.

EDCS-08601202.translation: To the Divine Shades. Todote, dutiful, lived 30 years, she is buried here.
EDCS-08601202.summary: This is a tombstone recording the life and death of Todote, who is buried here.

EDCS-08601204.translation: To the Divine Shades. Decimus Valerius Felix lived 85 years and 3 months, he is buried here.
EDCS-08601204.summary: This is a tombstone recording the life and death of Decimus Valerius Felix, who is buried here.

EDCS-08601205.translation: Publius Veibius Philocrates, freedman of Gaius, of the Palatina tribe, is buried here in a plot of 16 feet in all directions, for himself and his family: Publius Veibius Felix, son of Publius, of the Pacilia family, and Euphrosyne.
EDCS-08601205.summary: This is a tombstone recording the burial plot of Publius Veibius Philocrates and his family, purchased by Philocrates for himself and his descendants.

EDCS-08601206.translation: To the Divine Shades. Caius Ventidius Atventus lived 51 years, more or less, but he lived.
EDCS-08601206.summary: This is a tombstone recording the life and death of Caius Ventidius Atventus, with a slightly unusual phrasing about his lifespan.

EDCS-08601208.summary: This is a tombstone for Victorius Primitivus.

EDCS-08601209.translation: To the Divine Shades. Quintus Vinnicius Festus, dutiful, lived 26 years, he is buried here.
EDCS-08601209.summary: This is a tombstone recording the life and death of Quintus Vinnicius Festus, who is buried here.

EDCS-08601210.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Vipsania Repentina, dutiful, lived 33 years; she is laid here.
EDCS-08601210.summary: A funerary epitaph for Vipsania Repentina, recording her age at death.

EDCS-08601211.translation: Marcus Veolumnius Faustus, son of Marcus, of the Arnensis tribe.
EDCS-08601211.summary: A fragmentary inscription recording the name and tribal affiliation of Marcus Veolumnius Faustus.

EDCS-08601213.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Ioicus, dutiful.
EDCS-08601213.summary: A fragmentary funerary inscription, likely for Ioicus.

EDCS-08601214.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Pius Nasus lived 7 years and 6 months; he is laid here.
EDCS-08601214.summary: A funerary epitaph for Pius Nasus, recording his age at death.

EDCS-08601236.translation: In peace. X [days/years?] lived. Laid to rest on the fifth day before the Kalends of September. Cobul, consecrated virgin, in peace.
EDCS-08601236.summary: A funerary inscription for Cobul, a consecrated virgin, noting her date of repose.

EDCS-08601240.translation: Eutitia will rest here in a blessed, faithful death, adorning the church, which appears with such a sacred name, since she gave herself to God.
EDCS-08601240.summary: A funerary inscription for Eutitia, likely from a Christian context, expressing her blessed afterlife and dedication to God.

EDCS-08601242.translation: Paulus the goldsmith, faithful in peace. Felicissima, faithful in peace, lived years. February, indiction 14. Paulus the innocent, in peace.
EDCS-08601242.summary: A Christian funerary inscription mentioning Paulus the goldsmith and Felicissima, with a reference to the 14th indiction, likely in the 4th or 5th century.

EDCS-08601253.translation: Sabinianus, deacon and abbot, in peace. The seventh day before the Kalends of [Month], indiction 13.
EDCS-08601253.summary: A funerary inscription for Sabinianus, a deacon and abbot, noting his rank and date of repose with reference to the 13th indiction, likely dating to the 4th-6th centuries.

EDCS-08601254.summary: A fragmentary inscription recording the name of Pontia Pescennia Octaviana.

EDCS-08601258.translation: Ag[---] Ga[---], faithful in peace, lived 40 years and 2 months.
EDCS-08601258.summary: A fragmentary Christian funerary inscription recording the lifespan of an individual.

EDCS-08601259.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Caledia Prima, daughter of Lucius, dutiful, lived 67 years and 4 months. She lies here.
EDCS-08601259.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Caledia Prima, dated by its formula to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-08601261.summary: A dedication or inscription related to a quinquennial (five-yearly) event, likely public or religious.

EDCS-08601262.translation: May you be in peace, Bazuzice, and may prayers be offered for the new ones.
EDCS-08601262.summary: A short epitaph with a peaceful wish for the deceased, Bazuzice, and a request for prayers for newcomers, likely from a Christian context.

EDCS-08601263.translation: Caprasius lived 24 years, 2 months, and 1 day.
EDCS-08601263.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Caprasius.

EDCS-08601264.summary: A brief epitaph for Leontulus and Cassia, indicating a peaceful repose, likely from a Christian context.

EDCS-08601270.translation: Quindecem, deacon of Justiniana of Carthage, second region, was laid to rest on the eighteenth day before the Kalends of December.
EDCS-08601270.summary: A funerary inscription recording the burial date of Quintus, a deacon from Justiniana in the province of Africa.

EDCS-08601271.translation: Worshippers, the relics of the holy martyr apostle and [---]
EDCS-08601271.summary: A fragmentary inscription related to the veneration of relics of a holy martyr apostle.

EDCS-08601272.translation: Fortuna lived 106 years. Placed to rest on the 1st day before the Kalends of September.
EDCS-08601272.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the remarkable age of Fortuna and her burial date, likely from a Christian context.

EDCS-08601274.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Iulius Servandus, son of Samsala, lived 4 years.
EDCS-08601274.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the short life of Iulius Servandus, dated by formula to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-08601276.translation: Here are held the relics of the holy martyr Isidore, placed on the 16th day before the Kalends of November, in the 19th indiction.
EDCS-08601276.summary: An inscription indicating the location of the relics of Saint Isidore, with a specific date and indiction, likely from a Byzantine or early medieval Christian context.

EDCS-08601277.translation: To the divine Carus, father of our lords the Emperors Caesar Marcus Aurelius Carinus Pius Felix Augustus and Marcus Aurelius Numerianus Pius Felix Augustus, the municipium of Antonium Gordianum Rucuma dedicated this to their divine will.
EDCS-08601277.summary: This inscription records a dedication by the municipium of Antonium Gordianum Rucuma to the divine emperors Carinus and Numerian, likely from the late 3rd century CE.

EDCS-08601278.translation: Theodoricus the tribune lived in peace for 6 years; he was buried on the fourth day before the Kalends of May in the fifth indiction.
EDCS-08601278.summary: This epitaph records the life and burial of Theodoricus, a tribune, dated by an indiction cycle, likely from the late Roman or early Byzantine period.

EDCS-08601279.translation: Quintus Rupilius, son of Besan, dedicated this sacred offering to Saturn.
EDCS-08601279.summary: This inscription records a dedication to the god Saturn by Quintus Rupilius.

EDCS-08601281.translation: He made this for the priest of Ceres and prefect of the IV Scythica legion.
EDCS-08601281.summary: This fragmentary inscription records a dedication made for an official who held the positions of priest of Ceres and prefect of a Roman legion.

EDCS-08601285.summary: This is a simple inscription identifying Sextus Caecilius Salvius as a freedman.

EDCS-08601286.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Us Felix, pious, lived 14 years and 2 months; Issa, his freedwoman, dedicated this.
EDCS-08601286.summary: This tombstone records the death of a young boy, Us Felix, and indicates his freedwoman, Issa, erected the monument.

EDCS-08601287.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Lollia Redducta, pious, lived 80 years and 5 months; she is buried here.
EDCS-08601287.summary: This epitaph records the death and burial of Lollia Redducta, noting her piety and age.

EDCS-08601289.translation: Flavius Pompeianus lived in peace for not less than seventy years.
EDCS-08601289.summary: This epitaph records that Flavius Pompeianus lived a peaceful life for at least seventy years.

EDCS-08601290.translation: Sacred to Saturn, Lord. Caius Bommius Felix willingly paid his vow.
EDCS-08601290.summary: This inscription records Caius Bommius Felix fulfilling a vow made to the god Saturn.

EDCS-08601291.translation: Aurea Fidelis lived in peace for 8 years and 8 months, buried on the eighth day before the Kalends of July, died in hope.
EDCS-08601291.summary: This epitaph records the death of a young girl, Aurea Fidelis, who died in hope, and provides her age and burial date.

EDCS-08601292.translation: Titurnia Fausta, fortunate, and you, lived 30 years.
EDCS-08601292.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Titurnia Fausta, recording her lifespan.

EDCS-08601293.translation: Clodius Iulius Ma, pious, lived here. Furia Iulia lived 100 years, lies here. She was pious and lived 100 years, lies here. May your bones rest well. Caius Caesius Firmus, pious, lived 80 years. Clodia, pious, lived 75 years, lies here. May your bones rest well.
EDCS-08601293.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for multiple individuals, including Clodius Iulius Ma, Furia Iulia, and Clodia, recording their lifespans and expressing a wish for their repose.

EDCS-08601295.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Julius Honoratus, pious, lived 21 years.
EDCS-08601295.summary: This tombstone inscription is dedicated to the gods of the underworld and records the life of Julius Honoratus.

EDCS-08601296.translation: Marcus Agrius Optatus, son of Marcus, of the Quirina tribe, from Utica, a soldier of the Third Augustan Legion, served and lived 29 years, lies here.
EDCS-08601296.summary: This tombstone inscription commemorates Marcus Agrius Optatus, a soldier of the Third Augustan Legion, detailing his service and lifespan.

EDCS-08601297.translation: To Marcus Rossius Vitulus, son of Marcus, of the Pupinia tribe, an excellent man, imperial procurator of the public revenues of the province of Africa, imperial procurator of the district of Carthage, procurator of the XX inheritances, procurator of the Annona for the expedition, procurator of the XX inheritances across the Po in Liguria, Emilia, and Venetia, procurator of the expeditionary fund, prefect of the II Cohort of Spaniards, tribune of the XXX Ulpian Legion, tribune of the II Adiutrix Legion, commander of the Onsori tribe, decorated with military honors for the most successful campaign against the Quadi and Marcomanni, prefect of the Praetorian Wing of Roman citizens, commander of the Annona for the most successful urban expedition, decurion, perpetual flamen, and for his sons Iustus Proculianus and Vitulus Iulianus. All the decurions of the colony of Bullenses Regii, as patron and benefactor, for the benefits which he constantly confers upon all their fellow townsmen from his own means, have erected this monument.
EDCS-08601297.summary: This extensive dedication honors Marcus Rossius Vitulus, a high-ranking imperial official, by the decurions of Bullenses Regii for his numerous services and benefactions.

EDCS-08601298.summary: This is a simple name inscription, likely a tombstone or a dedication.

EDCS-08601300.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Titus Sextius Philurtius, pious, lived 43 years, lies here.
EDCS-08601300.summary: This tombstone inscription is dedicated to the gods of the underworld and records the life of Titus Sextius Philurtius.

EDCS-08601302.summary: This inscription simply names two individuals, Sabbatolus and Iubentinus, likely found on a tomb or monument.

EDCS-08601303.text_edition: \n Papiae Quinti filiae Novellae Cai Iuli Commodi Orfitiani legati Augusti pro praetore patroni coloniae decreto decurionum pecunia publica\n
EDCS-08601303.translation: To Papias, daughter of Quintus Novella, of Caius Iulius Commodus Orfitianus, legate of the emperor, governor of the colony, by decree of the decurions, with public money.
EDCS-08601303.summary: This inscription honors Papias Novella, daughter of Quintus, for whom public funds were used to erect a monument, likely a tomb, in recognition of her association with the governor Caius Iulius Commodus Orfitianus in the colony of Karthago.

EDCS-08601304.summary: This is a simple name inscription, likely a tombstone or a dedication.

EDCS-08601305.summary: This is a simple name inscription, likely a tombstone or a dedication.

EDCS-08601306.translation: To our lord Galerius Valerius Maximianus, most noble Caesar, the city of Rencum.
EDCS-08601306.summary: An honorary inscription from the city of Rencum to the emperor Galerius Valerius Maximianus.

EDCS-08601309.translation: Virinus, a decurion, for the safety of our lord the Emperor Augustus, on the days of Corona, in addition to those, established and dedicated a statue at his own expense for fifty thousand sesterces and its base, and on account of this dedication gave sportulas to his fellow decurions and hosted a banquet in his own curia; the site was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-08601309.summary: A dedication by a decurion named Virinus of a statue and base, funded by himself, for the emperor's safety, and records associated public festivities and the granting of land by decree.

EDCS-08601311.translation: Adeodatus, a deacon, faithful in peace, lived for years.
EDCS-08601311.summary: A funerary inscription recording the name, title (deacon), and lifespan of Adeodatus.

EDCS-08601312.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Marco Praecilio Secundo Cai filio vixit annis LXX Praecili Rogatus et Saturninus patri karissimo fecerunt\n
EDCS-08601312.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcus Praecilius Secundus, son of Caius, lived 70 years. Praecilius Rogatus and Saturninus made this for their dearest father.
EDCS-08601312.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Marcus Praecilius Secundus at age 70 and is dedicated by his sons, Rogatus and Saturninus, in the colony of Karthago.

EDCS-08601313.translation: Marcus Aninius Rogatianus, Caius Aninius Felix, Marcus Aninius Rogatus.
EDCS-08601313.summary: A list of three names, likely indicating a family or associated individuals, possibly on a monument.

EDCS-08601314.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcus Volussenius Victor, dutiful, lived 94 years; he is buried here. May your bones rest well, may the earth be light upon you.
EDCS-08601314.summary: A funerary epitaph for Marcus Volussenius Victor, recording his name, piety, age at death, burial location, and wishes for his afterlife.

EDCS-08601316.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Fortunata, dutiful, lived 6 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-08601316.summary: A funerary epitaph for Fortunata, recording her name, piety, and age at death.

EDCS-08601319.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Arvilia Sextila, dutiful, lived 50 years; she is buried here. May your bones rest well, may the earth be light upon you.
EDCS-08601319.summary: A funerary epitaph for Arvilia Sextila, recording her name, piety, age at death, burial location, and wishes for her afterlife.

EDCS-08601321.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Vibulena Sahorina, dutiful, lived 13 years.
EDCS-08601321.summary: A funerary epitaph for Vibulena Sahorina, recording her name, piety, and age at death.

EDCS-08601322.translation: Quintus Caecilius Latro, son of Quintus, of the voting tribe Quirina, was granted citizenship with his children; he lived 80 years; he is buried here. May your bones rest well, may the earth be light upon you.
EDCS-08601322.summary: A funerary epitaph for Quintus Caecilius Latro, detailing his citizenship grant, lifespan, burial location, and wishes for his afterlife.

EDCS-08601323.translation: For 23 years; she is buried here. Felicianus made this for Maxuti, his daughter, who died as an infant.
EDCS-08601323.summary: A funerary epitaph indicating the burial location and age of a child, and recording that it was made by her father, Felicianus.

EDCS-08601324.translation: Sacred to the Augusti. Speratus and Octavia, on their own behalf and that of the Minerviani, the most ancient [tribe] CI PI and the marble P NOVVI.
EDCS-08601324.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the Augusti by Speratus and Octavia, likely officials or members of the Minerviani community.

EDCS-08601325.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Nonius Felix, dutiful, lived 75 years.
EDCS-08601325.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the death of Lucius Nonius Felix and his age at death.

EDCS-08601326.translation: For the safety of the Emperor Caesar Augustus, Paccius Thibe, public priest, fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-08601326.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by Paccius Thibe, a public priest, for the well-being of the Emperor Augustus.

EDCS-08601327.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Aelia Gaetula, dutiful daughter of Publius, lived 70 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-08601327.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the death of Aelia Gaetula, her age, and her burial place.

EDCS-08601328.translation: Privatianus, deacon, lived 70 years, more or less, in peace.
EDCS-08601328.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespan of Privatianus, a deacon who died 'in peace'.

EDCS-08601329.translation: Religiosa Tertulla, wife, born for a short time, who lived 27 years in peace.
EDCS-08601329.summary: This funerary inscription records the short life of Religiosa Tertulla, a wife, who died 'in peace'.

EDCS-08601330.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Caninius Ianuarius Flavianus, decurion of Carthage, Roman knight with military honors, master of the district, dutiful, lived [X] years.
EDCS-08601330.summary: This funerary inscription records the life and distinctions of Lucius Caninius Ianuarius Flavianus, a man of high status in Carthage.

EDCS-08601331.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Aternia Zaba, dutiful, lived 81 years.
EDCS-08601331.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the death of Aternia Zaba and her age at death.

EDCS-08601332.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulia Zabullica, dutiful, lived 80 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-08601332.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Iulia Zabullica, her age, and her burial place.

EDCS-08601333.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Octavia Victoria lived 43 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-08601333.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Octavia Victoria, her age, and her burial place.

EDCS-08601336.translation: Sitius paid his vow to Saturn.
EDCS-08601336.summary: This is a votive inscription by Sitius to the god Saturn.

EDCS-08601339.translation: Modia Victoriana willingly paid her vow.
EDCS-08601339.summary: This is a votive inscription by Modia Victoriana.

EDCS-08601340.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Marcus Germanicus.
EDCS-08601340.summary: This is a dedication to Emperor Marcus Germanicus.

EDCS-08601345.text_edition: \n Aulo Gabinio Auli filio Arnensi Dato patrono pagi et civitatis Thuggensium flamini divi Titi aedili auguri coloniae Concordiae Iuliae Karthaginis equo publico in quinque decuriis ab Imperatore Caesare Traiano Hadriano Augusto adlecto\n
EDCS-08601345.translation: To Aulus Gabinius, son of Aulus, of the Arnensian tribe, Dato, patron of the district and of the citizenship of the Thuggenses, priest of the deified Titus, aedile and augur of the colony Concordia Iulia Karthago, enrolled by the emperor Caesar Trajan Hadrianus Augustus among the equites in the group of the five decuries.
EDCS-08601345.summary: This inscription honors Aulus Gabinius Dato, a significant local official and priest in Karthago who was also recognized by Emperor Hadrian, likely dating to the Hadrianic period.

EDCS-08601427.translation: Sacred to the Infernal Spirits. Julius Bari lived 95 years and 3 months. Sacred to the Infernal Spirits. Iulia Iambaria lived 85 years.
EDCS-08601427.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the ages at death of Julius Bari and Iulia Iambaria, dedicated to the Manes.

EDCS-08601429.summary: This is a dedication to Augusta, likely the empress.

EDCS-08601430.translation: In the most blessed times of our lords Flavius Julius Constantius and Magnentius, victorious perpetual Augusti, and Decentius, most noble Caesar, the forum of passage, which was not previously provided for, was begun and completed by the most distinguished and most excellent proconsuls, with Egnatuleius Crescens, most distinguished legate of Numidia, assisting, and under the supervision of the curator of the Republic of the Mustitani.
EDCS-08601430.summary: This is a building inscription from the period of Constantius II, Magnentius, and Decentius, recording the construction of a forum by proconsuls and a legate in Mustitana.

EDCS-08601431.translation: Carassius, sacred to the Infernal Spirits. Caius Orfius, son of Cai, and Cornelia Quietus, pious, lived 50 years and 5 months; here he is laid to rest.
EDCS-08601431.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Caius Orfius and Cornelia Quietus, dedicated to the Manes.

EDCS-08601432.translation: Aquilla pia lived 22 years; here she is laid to rest.
EDCS-08601432.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Aquilla, recording her age at death.

EDCS-08601433.translation: Sacred to the Infernal Spirits. Attia Saturnina pia lived 90 years; here she is laid to rest. Sacred to the Infernal Spirits. Quintus Papius Privatus pia lived 120 years; here he is laid to rest.
EDCS-08601433.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Attia Saturnina and Quintus Papius Privatus, recording their ages at death and dedication to the Manes.

EDCS-08601434.translation: ntana pia lived 72 years; here she is laid to rest. Cornelius Felix Potitianus pius lived 81 years; here he is laid to rest.
EDCS-08601434.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for an unnamed woman and Cornelius Felix Potitianus, recording their ages at death.

EDCS-08601435.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Quintus Octavius.
EDCS-08601435.summary: A funerary dedication to the Manes by Quintus Octavius.

EDCS-08601436.translation: Rufus, dutiful and pious, lived 81 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-08601436.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan and burial of Rufus.

EDCS-08601437.translation: Caius Sextius Primitianus, dutiful and pious, lived 42 years. He is buried here. Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Caius Sextius Felix, dutiful and pious, lived 30 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-08601437.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespans of Caius Sextius Primitianus and Caius Sextius Felix, with dedications to the Manes.

EDCS-08601439.translation: Caius Iulius Annius Maximus Catapalianus, a man of remarkable memory, lived 36 years, 4 months, 11 days, and 7 hours. Appaenia Salviana, his wife, lived 24 years and 2 months. She is buried here.
EDCS-08601439.summary: A funerary epitaph for Caius Iulius Annius Maximus Catapalianus and his wife Appaenia Salviana, detailing their lifespans and burial.

EDCS-08601440.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Iulia Rufina, wife of Rufinus, Rufina the priestess, is interred in this tomb and covered by this earth, holy, modest, most chaste of matrons. She lived 57 years.
EDCS-08601440.summary: A funerary inscription for Iulia Rufina, wife of Rufinus and a priestess, praising her virtues and stating her age at death.

EDCS-08601441.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Quintus Antonius, son of Quintus, Cornelia Reductianus, dutiful and pious, lived 83 years. He is buried here. I was a family servant for a long time, strong while alive...
EDCS-08601441.summary: A funerary epitaph for Quintus Antonius, son of Quintus, detailing his lifespan and burial, with a fragment of a personal statement.

EDCS-08601443.translation: Tadia Secunda, pious, lived 85 years. She is buried here. Bonifatia, pious, lived 91 years. She is buried here. Vittelia Bonifatia, pious, lived 57 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-08601443.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespans and burials of Tadia Secunda, Bonifatia, and Vittelia Bonifatia.

EDCS-08601445.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Rusticanus, dutiful and pious, lived 85 years. Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Aemilia Rustica, pious, lived 85 years.
EDCS-08601445.summary: Two funerary dedications to the Manes, one for Rusticanus and one for Aemilia Rustica, both stating their age at death.

EDCS-08601446.summary: A fragmentary inscription naming Olus Marceius Faustus, likely a funerary dedication or identification.

EDCS-08601447.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Papius Fortunatus, dutiful and pious.
EDCS-08601447.summary: A funerary dedication to the Manes by Papius Fortunatus.

EDCS-08601448.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Cholobonius Victoricus lived 14 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-08601448.summary: This funerary inscription records the life and burial of Cholobonius Victoricus, who died at the age of 14.

EDCS-08601450.translation: Saturus lived 81 years; he is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Ateria Secunda lived 68 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-08601450.summary: This funerary inscription records the lives and burials of two individuals, Saturus and Ateria Secunda.

EDCS-08601453.translation: Adiutor, son of De, lived 80 years.
EDCS-08601453.summary: This inscription records the age of Adiutor, son of De.

EDCS-08601454.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Aemilia.
EDCS-08601454.summary: This is a simple funerary dedication to the departed spirits for Aemilia.

EDCS-08601456.translation: His father consecrated this to Pilarius himself, whom death's cruel injury snatched away in the flower of his age, with parents groaning and weeping together with twin griefs.
EDCS-08601456.summary: This dedication by a father honors his son Pilarius, who died young, lamenting his untimely death.

EDCS-08601457.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Titus Aelius Martius.
EDCS-08601457.summary: This is a funerary dedication to the departed spirits for Titus Aelius Martius.

EDCS-08601458.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Aelius Pudens lived 70 years; he is pious and buried here.
EDCS-08601458.summary: This funerary inscription records the life and burial of Aelius Pudens, who died at the age of 70.

EDCS-08601459.translation: Aemilia Lade lived 48 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-08601459.summary: This funerary inscription records the life and burial of Aemilia Lade, who died at the age of 48.

EDCS-08601460.summary: This inscription records the age of Aemilia Secunda, who died at 15.

EDCS-08601461.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Aemilia ria lived 15 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-08601461.summary: This funerary inscription records the life and burial of Aemilia ria, who died at the age of 15.

EDCS-08601462.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Gaius Aemilius Arrator.

EDCS-08601463.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Alfius Rogatus.

EDCS-08601464.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits: Marcus Antonius Frontinianus lived 57 years. Sacred to the departed spirits: Larcia Lallosa lived 46 years.
EDCS-08601464.summary: This is a double funerary epitaph recording the lifespans of Marcus Antonius Frontinianus and Larcia Lallosa, dedicated to the departed spirits.

EDCS-08601465.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits: Lucius Antonius Luculus lived 85 years, here buried.
EDCS-08601465.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan and burial place of Lucius Antonius Luculus, dedicated to the departed spirits.

EDCS-08601466.translation: Lucius Antonius Saturninus, son of Publius, of the Quirina tribe, lived 23 years.
EDCS-08601466.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Lucius Antonius Saturninus.

EDCS-08601467.translation: Caecilia Venuta lived 80 years, here laid to rest.
EDCS-08601467.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan and burial place of Caecilia Venuta.

EDCS-08601468.translation: Calpurnia Saturnina lived 29 years, here laid to rest.
EDCS-08601468.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan and burial place of Calpurnia Saturnina.

EDCS-08601469.summary: This is a funerary epitaph possibly recording the name of Lucius Carmeius Roggatus.

EDCS-08601470.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits: Chelidon.
EDCS-08601470.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the name of Chelidon, dedicated to the departed spirits.

EDCS-08601473.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Clodia Xospita.

EDCS-08601474.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Clodius Calatianus lived for 45 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-08601474.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Clodius Calatianus, recording his lifespan and burial location.

EDCS-08601475.translation: Lucius Clodius Melior, son of Lucius, lived for 37 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-08601475.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Clodius Melior, recording his lifespan and burial location.

EDCS-08601477.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Cornelia Fortunata the pious lived for 70 years; she is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Caius Lucceius Ianuarius lived for 60 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-08601477.summary: This inscription contains two funerary epitaphs, one for Cornelia Fortunata and one for Caius Lucceius Ianuarius, recording their lifespans and burial locations.

EDCS-08601478.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Domitia Casta, daughter of Lucius, lived for 50 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-08601478.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Domitia Casta, recording her lifespan and burial location.

EDCS-08601479.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Donatus lived for 40 years.
EDCS-08601479.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Donatus, recording his lifespan.

EDCS-08601480.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Electra lived for 60 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-08601480.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Electra, recording her lifespan and burial location.

EDCS-08601481.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus Fabius Fortunatus lived for 51 years.
EDCS-08601481.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Quintus Fabius Fortunatus, recording his lifespan.

EDCS-08601482.translation: Furia Anthusa, daughter of Lucius, lived for 75 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-08601482.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Furia Anthusa, recording her lifespan and burial location.

EDCS-08601483.translation: Gargilia Salva lived for 31 years; she is buried.
EDCS-08601483.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Gargilia Salva, recording her lifespan and burial location.

EDCS-08601485.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Herennia Afrodisia lived for 33 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-08601485.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Herennia Afrodisia, recording her lifespan and burial location.

EDCS-08601486.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Hesia Victoria lived 31 years. Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Clodius Clodinus lived 35 years.
EDCS-08601486.summary: This inscription is a funerary monument recording the lives of Hesia Victoria and Lucius Clodius Clodinus.

EDCS-08601487.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulia Saturnina, dutiful, lived 75 years, is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulius Lupercus, dutiful, lived 97 years, is buried here.
EDCS-08601487.summary: This inscription is a funerary monument recording the lives and burial of Iulia Saturnina and Iulius Lupercus.

EDCS-08601488.translation: Caius Iulius Farbigil lived 35 years, is buried here.
EDCS-08601488.summary: This inscription is a funerary monument recording the life and burial of Caius Iulius Farbigil.

EDCS-08601489.translation: Lucius Iulius Saturninus lived 55 years, is buried here.
EDCS-08601489.summary: This inscription is a funerary monument recording the life and burial of Lucius Iulius Saturninus.

EDCS-08601490.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Caius Iulius Venustianus lived 28 years.
EDCS-08601490.summary: This inscription is a funerary monument recording the life of Caius Iulius Venustianus.

EDCS-08601491.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Licinia Satura lived 80 years.
EDCS-08601491.summary: This inscription is a funerary monument recording the life of Licinia Satura.

EDCS-08601492.summary: This inscription is a funerary monument recording the life of Lucilia Maxima.

EDCS-08601493.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Memmius Saturus lived 55 years.
EDCS-08601493.summary: This inscription is a funerary monument recording the life of Memmius Saturus.

EDCS-08601494.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Caius Minucius Macer, son of Caius, of the tribe Quirina, lived 23 years, is buried here.
EDCS-08601494.summary: This inscription is a funerary monument recording the life and burial of Caius Minucius Macer.

EDCS-08601495.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Modia Iovina lived 86 years. Munatius Rufus lived 57 years.
EDCS-08601495.summary: This inscription is a funerary monument recording the lives of Modia Iovina and Munatius Rufus.

EDCS-08601496.translation: Musta lived for 35 years; she is laid here.
EDCS-08601496.summary: A tombstone recording the lifespan and burial of Musta.

EDCS-08601497.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Quintus Octavius Fortunatus, son of Quintus, of the Quirina tribe, lived for 77 years.
EDCS-08601497.summary: A tombstone dedicated to the Divine Spirits, recording the name, parentage, tribe, and lifespan of Quintus Octavius Fortunatus.

EDCS-08601498.translation: Pacilia Estricata, pious, lived for 91 years; she is laid here.
EDCS-08601498.summary: A tombstone recording the lifespan and burial of the pious Pacilia Estricata.

EDCS-08601499.translation: Petreia Faustina, daughter of Caius, pious, lived for 39 years; she is laid here.
EDCS-08601499.summary: A tombstone recording the lifespan and burial of the pious Petreia Faustina.

EDCS-08601500.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Rosula.
EDCS-08601500.summary: A dedication to the Divine Spirits for Rosula.

EDCS-08601501.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Rufus, pious, lived for [X] years.
EDCS-08601501.summary: A tombstone dedicated to the Divine Spirits, recording the name and piety of Rufus, with an incomplete lifespan.

EDCS-08601502.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Secunda lived for 15 years.
EDCS-08601502.summary: A tombstone dedicated to the Divine Spirits, recording the lifespan of Secunda.

EDCS-08601503.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Vibius Fassota.
EDCS-08601503.summary: A dedication to the Divine Spirits for Vibius Fassota.

EDCS-08601504.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Marcus Vitruvius Optatus, pious, lived for 15 years; he is laid here.
EDCS-08601504.summary: A tombstone recording the lifespan and burial of the pious Marcus Vitruvius Optatus.

EDCS-08601506.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Lucius Zabbius Marullus.
EDCS-08601506.summary: A dedication to the Divine Spirits for Lucius Zabbius Marullus.

EDCS-08601507.translation: Iulius Victoricus lived for 31 years. Sacred to the departed gods.
EDCS-08601507.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Iulius Victoricus at the age of 31.

EDCS-08601508.translation: Sacred to the departed gods. Lucius Licinius Silvanus, son of Aulus, of the Quirina tribe, lived for 41 years. He is buried here in memory of Crispin.
EDCS-08601508.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Lucius Licinius Silvanus at the age of 41 and commemorates Crispin.

EDCS-08601509.translation: Sacred to the departed gods. Arranius Lavecus lived for 67 years. He is buried here. Sacred to the departed gods. Arrania Basila lived for 38 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-08601509.summary: This funerary inscription records the deaths of Arranius Lavecus (aged 67) and Arrania Basila (aged 38), likely a couple.

EDCS-08601510.translation: Sacred to the departed gods. Gargilia Fausta lived for...
EDCS-08601510.summary: This is a fragment of a funerary inscription recording the name of Gargilia Fausta, with her age missing.

EDCS-08601511.translation: Sacred to the departed gods. Artorius Papiria Celer Munatianus, pious, lived for 22 years. Sacred to the departed gods. Caius Artorius Celer, son of Caius, of the Papiria tribe, Epicurean philosopher, pious, lived for 32 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-08601511.summary: This funerary inscription records the deaths of two individuals, Artorius Papiria Celer Munatianus (aged 22) and Caius Artorius Celer (aged 32), likely father and son, the latter identified as a philosopher.

EDCS-08601512.translation: Caius Calicius Abascantus, pious, lived for 80 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-08601512.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Caius Calicius Abascantus, who lived to be 80 years old.

EDCS-08601513.summary: This inscription records the name Caius Lucornius Mustus, likely a dedication or a funerary marker with missing details.

EDCS-08601514.translation: Sacred to the departed gods. Ochius Barih, pious, lived for 1 year.
EDCS-08601514.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Ochius Barih at the age of 1 year.

EDCS-08601517.translation: Publia Ogulnia made this eternal home for Gaius Attius Felix Postumus, her husband; for they lived long together, equal in fortune, flourishing together in many years.
EDCS-08601517.summary: This funerary inscription records Publia Ogulnia dedicating an eternal home for her husband, Gaius Attius Felix Postumus, emphasizing their long and harmonious marriage.

EDCS-08601518.translation: Sacred to the departed gods. Sertoria Saturnina, wife of Licinius Fortunatus, daughter of Maria Plancina, a respected matron of honorable memory, lived for 75 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-08601518.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Sertoria Saturnina, wife of Licinius Fortunatus, at the age of 75, described as a respected matron.

EDCS-08601519.summary: This inscription records the name Marcus Livius Optatus, likely a dedication or a funerary marker with missing details.

EDCS-08601520.translation: Lucius Publicius Maximus lived 81 years; he lies here.
EDCS-08601520.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the lifespan and burial place of Lucius Publicius Maximus.

EDCS-08601521.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Publius Valerius Tevestinus, son of Quintus Valerius Victor, pious, lived 41 years; he lies here.
EDCS-08601521.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the lifespan and burial place of Publius Valerius Tevestinus, identifying his father and stating his piety.

EDCS-08601522.summary: This inscription appears to be an incomplete tombstone or dedicatory text, recording the name Gaius Vibius Masot.

EDCS-08601523.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcus Umbrius Iuvenalis, son of Marcus, of the Quirina tribe, lived 47 years.
EDCS-08601523.summary: This tombstone inscription records the lifespan and tribal affiliation of Marcus Umbrius Iuvenalis.

EDCS-08601524.summary: This is a milestone inscription indicating the distance between two locations.

EDCS-08601525.translation: Decimus Baribgal lived 55 years; he lies here. Aurelia Rogata lived 105 years; she lies here.
EDCS-08601525.summary: This tombstone inscription records the lifespans and burial places of Decimus Baribgal and Aurelia Rogata.

EDCS-08601526.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Octavius Peculiaris lived 50 years; he lies here.
EDCS-08601526.summary: This tombstone inscription records the lifespan and burial place of Octavius Peculiaris.

EDCS-08601528.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. D. Successa, pious, lived 11 years.
EDCS-08601528.summary: This tombstone inscription records the short lifespan of D. Successa and notes her piety.

EDCS-08601529.summary: This inscription appears to be a name and patronymic, likely part of a tombstone or dedication.

EDCS-08601530.translation: By the authority of the Emperor Nerva Trajan Caesar Augustus Germanicus Dacicus, pontifex maximus, with tribunician power for the 9th time, imperator for the 4th time, consul for the 5th time, father of the country. Lucius Minicius Natalis, imperial legate with praetorian authority, between the Musulami and Valeria Atticilla, 190 paces to the nearest [road marker], 121,400 paces.
EDCS-08601530.summary: This is a boundary or milestone inscription, issued under Emperor Trajan, detailing distances and referencing imperial officials and tribal territories.

EDCS-08601531.translation: Annius Ephemer Rufinus lived for X years, X months, and X days.
EDCS-08601531.summary: This epitaph records the lifespan of Annius Ephemer Rufinus.

EDCS-08601532.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Fulcinia Victoria.
EDCS-08601532.summary: This funerary dedication is for Fulcinia Victoria.

EDCS-08601533.translation: Gaius Aemilius Victor, son of Publius, of the Quirina tribe, lived for 90 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-08601533.summary: This epitaph records the lifespan and burial of Gaius Aemilius Victor.

EDCS-08601536.translation: Vibius Satrius Pontianus lived for 65 years in peace.
EDCS-08601536.summary: This epitaph records the lifespan of Vibius Satrius Pontianus.

EDCS-08601537.translation: To Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus Armeniacus.
EDCS-08601537.summary: This is a dedication to Emperor Marcus Aurelius Antoninus.

EDCS-08601538.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Aemilia Marcia, pious wife of Flavius Clementianus, lived for 29 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-08601538.summary: This funerary dedication records the lifespan and burial of Aemilia Marcia.

EDCS-08601539.translation: Abundantius, father. FI CI ER 20 FIER TRESSI.
EDCS-08601539.summary: This inscription, possibly a funerary or commemorative one, mentions Abundantius and some numerical notations that are difficult to interpret.

EDCS-08601540.translation: Gaius Furius Speratus, son of Gaius.
EDCS-08601540.summary: This is a personal name inscription, likely identifying an individual.

EDCS-08601541.summary: This inscription mentions 'Ecclesia mater' (Mother Church) and indicates a state of peace, likely within a Christian context.

EDCS-08601543.translation: Privata, with Victoria, rejoicing, triumphant, consecrated by victorious virginity and confession, bearing angelic vestments, in peace. Worthy of the worthy, crowned for conquering.
EDCS-08601543.summary: This inscription, likely Christian, celebrates the triumph and virtues of Privata and Victoria, possibly martyrs, in a state of peace.

EDCS-08601544.translation: Portuensis, innocent in peace in the name of the martyrs.
EDCS-08601544.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Portuensis, who is described as innocent and buried in peace in the name of the martyrs.

EDCS-08601546.translation: Civica, minister of God, in peace, Secunde, lover of the poor, in peace.
EDCS-08601546.summary: This epitaph records two individuals, Civica, a minister of God, and Secunde, a lover of the poor, both buried in peace.

EDCS-08601547.translation: Privatus, priest, guardian of discipline, master of piety, on the 12th day before the Kalends of June.
EDCS-08601547.summary: This epitaph records Privatus, a priest and master of piety, with a date that likely marks his death or burial on May 21st.

EDCS-08601548.translation: Naucelius, lover of the poor, worshipper of God, in peace. Dulcis, faithful, lived for 43 years. Nepotianus, in peace.
EDCS-08601548.summary: This epitaph records the deceased Naucelius, described as a lover of the poor and worshipper of God, and Nepotianus, who lived for 43 years, both in peace.

EDCS-08601549.translation: Pompeia Maxima, servant of God, in peace.
EDCS-08601549.summary: This epitaph records Pompeia Maxima, identified as a servant of God, buried in peace.

EDCS-08601550.translation: Victoria, mother, servant of God, in peace. Glyceria.
EDCS-08601550.summary: This epitaph records Victoria, a mother and servant of God, buried in peace, with another name, Glyceria, possibly associated.

EDCS-08601551.translation: Victorina, servant of God, in peace.
EDCS-08601551.summary: This epitaph records Victorina, identified as a servant of God, buried in peace.

EDCS-08601553.translation: Dedicated by Victoria, a girl, she made it in peace.
EDCS-08601553.summary: This epitaph records a dedication by a girl named Victoria, indicating she made the monument in peace.

EDCS-08601555.translation: Quoddeus the elder, in peace, though late, yet with the Lord.
EDCS-08601555.summary: This epitaph records Quoddeus the elder, who is described as being in peace, even if he came to faith late.

EDCS-08601556.translation: They gave back the father on the 17th day before the Kalends of November, the mother on the 15th day before the Kalends of May; they received this crown of perpetuity, because Stercorius and Crescentia, created by God, lived in peace for 188 years.
EDCS-08601556.summary: This epitaph records the death dates of parents, Stercorius and Crescentia, who lived an exceptionally long life of 188 years, and their reception of a crown of perpetuity, likely a Christian epitaph commemorating their long lives and salvation.

EDCS-08601557.translation: Victorina, a testament to widowhood and modesty, an example of chastity and devotion.
EDCS-08601557.summary: This epitaph commemorates Victorina, highlighting her virtues.

EDCS-08601558.translation: Felix, a ship-owner from the East, lived happily in peace for 75 years.
EDCS-08601558.summary: This epitaph records the lifespan and profession of Felix, a ship-owner from the East.

EDCS-08601559.translation: The innocent child, named Vitalis, lived for six years in peace and refreshment.
EDCS-08601559.summary: This epitaph commemorates the young child Vitalis, noting his short life and peaceful rest.

EDCS-08601560.translation: Secundinus, sweet in peace and rest.
EDCS-08601560.summary: This epitaph is a simple dedication to Secundinus, emphasizing his peaceful repose.

EDCS-08601561.translation: Canpesis Domitius, sweet soul, lived for fifty years in peace.
EDCS-08601561.summary: This epitaph records the lifespan and peaceful end of Canpesis Domitius.

EDCS-08601562.translation: M. A. I. V. R., sweet soul, Felix, in peace.
EDCS-08601562.summary: This epitaph appears to commemorate individuals named Felix and M. A. I. V. R., highlighting their peaceful state.

EDCS-08601565.summary: This epitaph is a short dedication to Abundantius, indicating his peaceful rest.

EDCS-08601571.translation: Amator, sweet, lived for 70 years in peace.
EDCS-08601571.summary: This epitaph records the lifespan and peaceful passing of Amator.

EDCS-08601577.summary: This is a simple naming inscription, likely for Aurelius Honoratus.

EDCS-08601578.summary: This epitaph is a brief memorial for Bonifatia, emphasizing her peaceful repose.

EDCS-08601579.translation: Bonitas lived innocently in peace for six years, sweet.
EDCS-08601579.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the short life of Bonitas.

EDCS-08601581.summary: This is a tombstone inscription, possibly a dedication to Calendio Fortunata.

EDCS-08601582.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Calistus.

EDCS-08601588.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Donatus.

EDCS-08601589.translation: Aegyptia, sweet, lived in peace for more or less twenty-five years.
EDCS-08601589.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the life of Aegyptia.

EDCS-08601591.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Faustina.

EDCS-08601595.summary: This inscription likely records Flavius Nardus, possibly a soldier, and A. Cottorus.

EDCS-08601596.translation: Flavius, a soldier, sweet, lived in peace for forty-four years.
EDCS-08601596.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the life of Flavius, identified as a soldier.

EDCS-08601598.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Fortunatus Paliaricus.

EDCS-08601613.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Manilia Restuta.

EDCS-08601620.translation: Pascassa lived about 17 years in peace.
EDCS-08601620.summary: This epitaph records the life span of Pascassa, who died at approximately 17 years of age.

EDCS-08601623.summary: This brief epitaph likely marks the resting place of Primula.

EDCS-08601624.translation: Primulus to the greatest priest Parthicus in peace.
EDCS-08601624.summary: This inscription is a dedication, possibly funerary, from Primulus to a figure identified as "pontifici maximo Parthico".

EDCS-08601631.summary: This epitaph is a simple dedication to Restuta, described as "sweet".

EDCS-08601636.summary: This inscription likely identifies an individual named Sterculus, referred to as "the old man".

EDCS-08601638.summary: This inscription records the name Susanna and her alternative name, Lolliana.

EDCS-08601640.summary: This brief epitaph likely marks the resting place of Veneria.

EDCS-08601647.translation: Sacred to Aesculapius Augustus. Lucius Demetrius Damon willingly paid his vow.
EDCS-08601647.summary: This is a votive inscription by Lucius Demetrius Damon to the divinity Aesculapius Augustus.

EDCS-08601648.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Vergilius Africanus lived for [X] years, a soldier of the I Urban Cohort. He is buried here.
EDCS-08601648.summary: This funerary inscription records the death and burial of Vergilius Africanus, a soldier of the I Urban Cohort.

EDCS-08601649.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Lucius Cerficius Victor lived for 65 years. He lived well while he lived. He is buried here.
EDCS-08601649.summary: This funerary inscription records the death and burial of Lucius Cerficius Victor, who lived for 65 years and is noted to have lived well.

EDCS-08601650.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Marcus Cilicius Felix, dutiful, lived X years, and Saturnina, his dutiful wife, lived Y years. They built this temple of security for themselves and their descendants while alive. Marcus Cilicius Felicianus, dutiful, lived 31 years. Marcus Cilicius Silvanus, dutiful, lived 23 years.
EDCS-08601650.summary: This funerary inscription records the construction of a temple of security by Marcus Cilicius Felix and his wife Saturnina, and lists the ages of other family members.

EDCS-08601651.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. To Hygieia, most devoted wife, and for himself, freedmen, and freedwomen. Arpocra Gavianus [dedicated this] on the 3rd of December.
EDCS-08601651.summary: This funerary dedication by Arpocra Gavianus is for his wife Hygieia, and also for himself and his freed dependents, dated to December 3rd.

EDCS-08601652.summary: This is a simple funerary epitaph identifying the deceased as Lucius Aelius Macer.

EDCS-08601653.summary: This is a simple funerary epitaph identifying the deceased as Quintus Cornelius Zabo.

EDCS-08601654.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Lollius Donatus lived 55 years.
EDCS-08601654.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Lollius Donatus, who lived 55 years.

EDCS-08601655.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Octavia Donatula lived X years. Felix and [possibly more names or details follow].
EDCS-08601655.summary: This fragmentary funerary inscription records the death of Octavia Donatula and likely another person named Felix.

EDCS-08900647.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Titus Gargilius Arnensi Laetus, son of Gargilius Valentis, dutiful, lived 30 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-08900647.summary: This funerary inscription identifies Titus Gargilius Arnensi Laetus, son of Gargilius Valentis, as having lived 30 years and being buried here.

EDCS-08900648.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Quintus Florius Publi filius Arnensi Tertullus, dutiful, lived 77 years; he is buried here. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Valeria Luci filia Saturnina, dutiful, lived 71 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-08900648.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of two individuals, Quintus Florius Tertullus and Valeria Saturnina, with their ages and familial connections.

EDCS-08900649.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Iulia Rogata, dutiful, lived 10 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-08900649.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Iulia Rogata, who died at the age of 10.

EDCS-08900650.text_edition: \n Caio Selio Rufo Quinto Ostorio Scapula consulibus Marcus Papius Rogatus \n
EDCS-08900650.translation: In the consulship of Gaius Silius Rufus and Quintus Ostorius Scapula, Marcus Papius Rogatus [erected this].
EDCS-08900650.summary: This is a dating reference within an inscription, noting the year by the consuls Gaius Silius Rufus and Quintus Ostorius Scapula, and mentioning Marcus Papius Rogatus.

EDCS-08900651.translation: In the consulship of Volasenna [erected this].
EDCS-08900651.summary: This inscription is a dating fragment, referencing the year by the consul Volasenna.

EDCS-08900652.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Titus Flavius Lucianus, veteran, lived 45 years, 6 months, and 20 days; he is buried here.
EDCS-08900652.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Titus Flavius Lucianus, a veteran, with his age at death.

EDCS-08900653.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Gaius Julius Ianuarius lived 58 years; he is buried here, a veteran.
EDCS-08900653.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Gaius Julius Ianuarius, a veteran, who lived to be 58 years old.

EDCS-08900654.summary: This is a simple funerary inscription naming Romulus, son of Accavo.

EDCS-08900655.translation: Gaius Julius Ianuarius, grandson, is buried here.
EDCS-08900655.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Gaius Julius Ianuarius, identified as a grandson.

EDCS-08900656.text_edition: \n Caius Iulius Felix Nargudianus pius vixit annis LXX hic situs est ossa tibi bene quiescant terra tibi levis sit\n
EDCS-08900656.translation: Gaius Iulius Felix Nargudianus, pious, lived 70 years. He lies here. May your bones rest well, may the earth be light upon you.
EDCS-08900656.summary: This is a standard funerary epitaph for Gaius Iulius Felix Nargudianus, who lived 70 years, including common wishes for the deceased's peace.

EDCS-08900657.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Gaius Julius Rogatianus, son of Ftus.
EDCS-08900657.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to Gaius Julius Rogatianus, son of Ftus.

EDCS-08900658.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulia Maria the pious lived 28 years and 11 months.
EDCS-08900658.summary: This funerary inscription records the life and death of Iulia Maria, who lived 28 years and 11 months.

EDCS-08900659.translation: The owner of the estate established the temple of Caelestis.
EDCS-08900659.summary: A landowner erected a temple dedicated to the goddess Caelestis.

EDCS-08900660.translation: May it be good, auspicious, and fortunate for the city of Tapphuzabensis: they made a small shrine to Fortune under the supervision of Saturninus Naboris, son of Iddibalis Moconi, the sufes.
EDCS-08900660.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a small shrine to Fortune by the citizens of Tapphuzabensis, supervised by Saturninus Naboris and Iddibalis Moconi, who held the office of sufes.

EDCS-08900661.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Peculiaris servus actor \n
EDCS-08900661.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Peculiaris, the steward.
EDCS-08900661.summary: A funerary inscription for Peculiaris, a freedman serving as a steward.

EDCS-08900663.translation: Pomponia Saturnina, daughter of Cupitus, is buried here.
EDCS-08900663.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Pomponia Saturnina, daughter of Cupitus.

EDCS-08900664.translation: Maximia Saturnina, daughter of Caius, the pious, lived 10 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-08900664.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Maximia Saturnina, daughter of Caius, who died at the age of 10.

EDCS-08900665.translation: Phrigna, daughter of Saturnus, lived 3 years.
EDCS-08900665.summary: This funerary inscription records that Phrigna, daughter of Saturnus, lived for 3 years.

EDCS-08900668.summary: This is a simple funerary inscription naming Titus Caelius Maximus.

EDCS-08900669.translation: Gaius Pomponius, son of Lucius, lived piously for 25 years; he is buried here. RA
EDCS-08900669.summary: A tombstone recording the lifespan and burial of Gaius Pomponius, a man who lived 25 years.

EDCS-08900670.translation: Quintus Cassius Primigenius lived for 61 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-08900670.summary: A tombstone recording the lifespan and burial of Quintus Cassius Primigenius, a man who lived 61 years.

EDCS-08900671.translation: Astinamus, son of Bassus, lived for 30 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-08900671.summary: A tombstone recording the lifespan and burial of Astinamus, son of Bassus, a man who lived 30 years.
