EDCS-08900672.translation: Faustilla, wife of Vibullius Impratatus, lived piously for... years.
EDCS-08900672.summary: A tombstone fragment recording the lifespan of Faustilla, wife of Vibullius Impratatus.

EDCS-08900673.translation: Lucius Volussius Primus, son of Lucius, of the Arnensis tribe, lived piously for 75 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-08900673.summary: A tombstone recording the lifespan and burial of Lucius Volussius Primus, a man who lived 75 years.

EDCS-08900674.translation: Marcus Selicius Bassus, pious, lived for 70 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-08900674.summary: A tombstone recording the lifespan and burial of Marcus Selicius Bassus, a man who lived 70 years.

EDCS-08900675.translation: Lucius Egnatius Felix lived for... years. Matrona lived for 55 years.
EDCS-08900675.summary: A tombstone recording the lifespans of Lucius Egnatius Felix and Matrona, who lived 55 years.

EDCS-08900676.translation: Iulius Victor, son of Lucius, of the Horatia tribe, pious, lived for 2 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-08900676.summary: A tombstone recording the lifespan and burial of Iulius Victor, a child who lived 2 years.

EDCS-08900677.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulius Saturninus, the pearl merchant, lived for 65 years. Sacred to the departed spirits. Magnia Saturnina lived for 85 years. They are buried here.
EDCS-08900677.summary: A tombstone for two individuals, Iulius Saturninus (a pearl merchant) and Magnia Saturnina, recording their lifespans and burial.

EDCS-08900678.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Aurelia Macula, pious, lived for 56 years, a midwife.
EDCS-08900678.summary: A tombstone for Aurelia Macula, a pious midwife, recording her lifespan.

EDCS-08900679.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Victor the pious lived 58 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-08900679.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Victor, who lived 58 years, from an unknown date.

EDCS-08900680.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Helvius Victorinus lived 1 year, 3 months, and 9 days.
EDCS-08900680.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Helvius Victorinus, who died in infancy, from an unknown date.

EDCS-08900681.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Passinia Secunda the pious lived 81 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-08900681.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Passinia Secunda, who lived 81 years, from an unknown date.

EDCS-08900682.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus Gabinius Victor lived 80 years. Valeria Secundula lived [an unspecified number of] years.
EDCS-08900682.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the ages at death of Quintus Gabinius Victor and Valeria Secundula, from an unknown date.

EDCS-08900683.translation: Sentia Namfame lived 102 years. Lucius Sentius Bassus lived 85 years. Sacred to the departed spirits.
EDCS-08900683.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the ages at death of Sentia Namfame and Lucius Sentius Bassus, from an unknown date.

EDCS-08900684.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus Aridius Porus lived 22 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-08900684.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Quintus Aridius Porus, who lived 22 years, from an unknown date.

EDCS-08900685.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Magullius Victoricus lived 19 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-08900685.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Magullius Victoricus, who lived 19 years, from an unknown date.

EDCS-08900686.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus Aurelius Candidus, friend of his country, observer of his friends, lived 58 years and 4 months.
EDCS-08900686.summary: A funerary epitaph honoring Quintus Aurelius Candidus, who lived 58 years and 4 months, from an unknown date.

EDCS-08900687.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Caecilius lived 75 years; he is buried here. Tertulla daughter of Asmunis lived [an unspecified number of] years.
EDCS-08900687.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the ages at death of Caecilius and Tertulla, from an unknown date.

EDCS-08900688.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Caius Julius Rogatianus, son of the people, benefactor, son of a priest.
EDCS-08900688.summary: A funerary epitaph honoring Caius Julius Rogatianus with several honorific titles, from an unknown date.

EDCS-08900691.translation: Sacred to Augustus. Junius Primus Sidin fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-08900691.summary: This is a votive inscription by Junius Primus Sidin dedicated to Augustus, likely from the imperial period.

EDCS-08900694.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Gaius Julius Verus Maximinus Pius Felix Augustus, twice conqueror of the Germans, twice conqueror of the Sarmatians, twice conqueror of the Dacians, pontifex, with the tribunician power for the third time, emperor V, and to Gaius Julius Verus Maximus, most noble Caesar, prince of the youth, twice conqueror of the Germans, twice conqueror of the Sarmatians, twice conqueror of the Dacians, [who restored] the interrupted bridges.
EDCS-08900694.summary: This is a titulus honoring Emperors Maximinus Thrax and his son Maximus Caesar, likely dating to their co-reign around 236-238 AD, possibly related to military campaigns or infrastructure projects.

EDCS-08901175.text_edition: \n salutem a Geminio Crescente unum asinum cuis sic nobis attulisti Barlas decimum Calendas emit asinum valias sic opto te bene valere\n
EDCS-08901175.translation: Greetings from Geminius Crescens. You brought us one donkey, for which Barlas paid ten, bought the donkey. I wish you well.
EDCS-08901175.summary: A personal letter, likely on a wax tablet, concerning the purchase of a donkey and general well-being.

EDCS-08901176.text_edition: \n VIIII Kalendas Ianuarias numerus LVII in his librarius I optio I proculcator I equites VIII quintanari XXII de speculis I ad portam I ad praepositum I structor I aegri III Sulpicius Donatus Titus Buzuris Aurelius Rufus ad virgas I religui sic repungent XVII furnus XV balneus II\n
EDCS-08901176.translation: On the ninth day before the Kalends of January, a contingent of 57 men, including one scribe, one optio, one proculcator, eight equites, twenty-two quintanarii, one from the watch posts, one at the gate, one engineer, three sick, Sulpicius Donatus, Titus Buzuris, Aurelius Rufus, reporting for duty; the rest, 17, are to be compensated. Seventeen for the bakery, fifteen for the baths.
EDCS-08901176.summary: A military or administrative document detailing personnel numbers and duties, possibly related to rations or pay, from an unspecified date.

EDCS-08901177.text_edition: \n Octavio Festho sic decurioni praeposito meo Aemilius Aemilianus miles salutem transmisi at sic te domine per Macargum siddipia tridici dua quae fiunt viginti quattuor consulibus futuris post Thusco et Basso consulibus accepta XII Kalendas Februarias IT I\n
EDCS-08901177.translation: Aemilius Aemilianus, a soldier, sends greetings to my commander, Octavius Festhus. But, master, through Macargus, I send twenty-four siddipia (a type of garment or cloth) which is twenty-four. Consuls elect, after Tuscus and Bassus were consuls. Received on the twelfth day before the Kalends of February.
EDCS-08901177.summary: A soldier writes to his superior, likely regarding the delivery of goods, with a specific date reference.

EDCS-08901178.text_edition: \n Deo Marti Canapphari Augusto pro salute et incolumitate domini nostri Imperatoris Caesaris divi Septimi Severi nepotis divi Magni Antonini filii Marci Aureli Severi Alexandri Invicti Pii Felicis Augusti pontificis maximi tribuniciae potestatis IIII consulis patris patriae et Iuliae Mammeae Augustae matris Augusti nostri et castrorum totiusque domus divinae per vexillationem legionis III Augustae piae vindicis Severianae curante Tito Flavio Aproniano |(centurione) legionis eiusdem praeposito vexillationis\n
EDCS-08901178.translation: To the god Mars Canappharius Augustus, for the safety and well-being of our lord the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Severus Alexander Invictus Pius Felix Augustus, grandson of the deified Septimius Severus, son of the deified Macrinus Antoninus, pontifex maximus, with tribunician power for the fourth time, father of the country, and of Julia Mammea Augusta, mother of our Augustus and of the entire camp and of the divine household, by the detachment of the III Augustan Pious Vindicating Severian Legion, under the supervision of Titus Flavius Apronianus, centurion of the same legion and commander of the detachment.
EDCS-08901178.summary: A dedication to the god Mars by a military unit under the command of Titus Flavius Apronianus, honoring Emperor Severus Alexander and his mother Julia Mammea, likely from the early 3rd century AD.

EDCS-08901179.translation: To the Emperor Caesar, son of the deified Septimius Severus Pius, Arabicus, Adiabenicus, Parthicus Maximus, Britannicus Maximus, grandson of the deified Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Germanicus Sarmaticus, great-grandson of the deified Antoninus Pius, great-great-grandson of the deified Hadrian, great-great-great-grandson of the deified Trajan Parthicus and the deified Nerva, Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus, Parthicus Maximus, Britannicus Maximus, Germanicus Maximus, pontifex maximus, with tribunician power for the nineteenth time, emperor for the third time, consul for the fourth time, father of the fatherland, proconsul for the forty-third time.
EDCS-08901179.summary: This is an extensive titulary of Emperor Caracalla, dating to his eighteenth year of tribunician power and his fourth consulship, likely around 213 AD, listing his divine ancestry and imperial titles.

EDCS-08901180.translation: To the Emperor Caesar, son of the deified Septimius Severus Pius, Arabicus, Adiabenicus, Parthicus Maximus, Britannicus Maximus.
EDCS-08901180.summary: This is a fragment of an imperial titulary, likely honoring Emperor Caracalla, listing his divine ancestry and some of his major titles, probably from the early 3rd century AD.

EDCS-08901184.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Antia Secura, dutiful, lived 23 years, 11 months; she is buried here.
EDCS-08901184.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Antia Secura, recording her name, piety, age at death, and burial place, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08901185.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Aris Victor, son of Sentius, dutiful, lived 31 years; he is buried here. May the earth be light upon you.
EDCS-08901185.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Aris Victor, son of Sentius, recording his name, piety, age at death, burial place, and a common epitaph, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08901186.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Lucius Arrius Rogatus, dutiful, lived 70 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-08901186.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Lucius Arrius Rogatus, recording his name, piety, age at death, and burial place, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08901187.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Gaius Nunnius Felix, dutiful, lived 62 years; he is buried here. May the earth be light upon you.
EDCS-08901187.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Gaius Nunnius Felix, recording his name, piety, age at death, burial place, and a common epitaph, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08901188.translation: Gaius Julius Felix, freedman of Augustus, son of Accavo, dutiful, lived 65 years; he is buried here. Gaius Julius Felix, freedman of Gaius, made this for his father and his descendants with his own money.
EDCS-08901188.summary: This is a tombstone inscription and funerary monument record, indicating Gaius Julius Felix was buried at 65, and his son, also Gaius Julius Felix (a freedman of another Gaius), erected the monument for his father and descendants, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08901189.text_edition: \n Publio Ennio Titi filio Quirina Saturnino Karo clarissimo viro aedili curuli designato ab actis senatus quaestori urbano flamini perpetuo alumno civi patrono municipii decreto decurionum pecunia publica\n
EDCS-08901189.translation: By public money, according to a decree of the decurions, for Publius Ennius Saturninus Karo, son of Titus, of the Quirina tribe, a most distinguished man, designated curule aedile, quaestor urbanus, perpetual flamen, alumnus, citizen, and patron of the municipality.
EDCS-08901189.summary: A public monument or honor erected from municipal funds to commemorate Publius Ennius Saturninus Karo, who held various important civic and religious offices.

EDCS-08901190.text_edition: \n Ex indulgentia Imperatoris Caesaris Hadriani Augusti patris patriae terminus leugae coloniae Canopitanae III milia passuum\n
EDCS-08901190.translation: By the generosity of the Emperor Caesar Hadrian Augustus, father of the country, the boundary marker of the colony of Canopus, three Roman miles.
EDCS-08901190.summary: A milestone indicating the distance from the Roman colony of Canopus, erected through the emperor's beneficence.

EDCS-09001575.text_edition: \n Saturno Augusto sacrum Caius Calvissius Bullus votum solvit\n
EDCS-09001575.translation: Sacred to Saturn Augustus. Gaius Calvissius Bullus fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-09001575.summary: A votive inscription to the god Saturn by Gaius Calvissius Bullus.

EDCS-09001579.translation: This place holds the sweetest Spesindeum to me, but he lived in the body for 4 years, 3 months, 7 days. His deposition was on the 3rd day before the Nones of December, in the 2nd indiction, during the reign of the Emperor our lord Heraclius.
EDCS-09001579.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Spesindeum, detailing his lifespan and the date of his burial during the reign of Emperor Heraclius, likely in the 7th century AD.

EDCS-09001580.translation: Here lies the unworthy Florentius in a cave, with unshaven beard, submerged by a harsh death; he lived in peace for 22 years, 8 months, and 25 days, buried on the 4th day before the Ides of February, in the 2nd indiction.
EDCS-09001580.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the death and burial of Florentius, dating to the 2nd indiction.

EDCS-09001581.translation: Restitutus, the most blessed bishop, lived in peace for 73 years; his burial was on the Ides of February, in the 15th indiction.
EDCS-09001581.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Bishop Restitutus, indicating his lifespan and burial date in the 15th indiction.

EDCS-09001584.translation: To our lord Flavius Valentinianus Pius Felix Victor and Triumphant Always Augustus, the curator and council of the municipality of Rucumensium, devoted to his divine will and majesty, with public money.
EDCS-09001584.summary: This inscription records a dedication by the municipality of Rucumensium to Emperor Valentinian, likely related to public works funded by the state.

EDCS-09001585.summary: A very brief funerary inscription indicating the repose of someone named Restitutus.

EDCS-09001586.summary: This inscription records the name and title of Accepta, a deaconess.

EDCS-09001587.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Lacaena lived 30 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-09001587.summary: A funerary inscription dedicated to the departed spirits for Lacaena, noting her age and burial.

EDCS-09001588.translation: A gift prepared by Non Optavile for her venerable mother-in-law Tarauta, a young granddaughter, who lived in peace for 40 years; Quodcumque and Ianuaria made it.
EDCS-09001588.summary: This funerary inscription records a dedication by Quodcumque and Ianuaria for their mother-in-law Tarauta, noting her age and peaceful life.

EDCS-09001616.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari Marco Aurelio Claudio Augusto consuli III\n
EDCS-09001616.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Claudius Augustus, in his third consulship.
EDCS-09001616.summary: An inscription honoring Emperor Claudius Gothicus, likely marking a building or public work.

EDCS-09001617.text_edition: \n Domino nostro Flavio Valerio Constantio nobilissimo Caesari \n
EDCS-09001617.translation: To our lord, Flavius Valerius Constantius, the most noble Caesar.
EDCS-09001617.summary: This inscription honors Flavius Valerius Constantius, addressed as Caesar, likely dating to the Tetrarchy or early Constantinian period.

EDCS-09001618.translation: To our lords Valentinianus, Theodosius, and Arcadius, Always Augusti.
EDCS-09001618.summary: This is a dedication to the emperors Valentinianus, Theodosius, and Arcadius, likely from a public monument.

EDCS-09001619.text_edition: \n Imperatori domino nostro Marco Iulio Philippo nobilissimo Caesari milia passuum\n
EDCS-09001619.translation: To our lord Imperator Marcus Julius Philippus, the most noble Caesar, miles.
EDCS-09001619.summary: This inscription honors Marcus Julius Philippus, addressed as Caesar and likely indicating a milestone marking distance.

EDCS-09001620.text_edition: \n Impperatoribus Caessaribus Publio Licinio Valeriano et Licinio Gallieno Invictis Auggustis IIII\n
EDCS-09001620.translation: To the Emperors and Caesars, Publius Licinius Valerianus and Licinius Gallienus, the unconquered Augusti, for the fourth time.
EDCS-09001620.summary: This inscription honors the co-emperors Valerian and Gallienus, indicating a consulship or other significant civic honor during their reign in the mid-3rd century AD.

EDCS-09200547.text_edition: \n [Aureliae Galeriae] [Lucillae Augustae] Imperatoris Caesaris Luci Aureli Veri Augusti Armeniaci Parthici Maximi Medici decreto decurionum pecunia publica\n
EDCS-09200547.translation: To Aurelia Galeria Lucilla Augusta, by decree of the decurions and at public expense.
EDCS-09200547.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Aurelia Galeria Lucilla Augusta, wife of Lucius Aurelius Verus, likely erected by the local town council.

EDCS-09200548.text_edition: \n Aureliae Sabinae Imperatoris Caesaris Marci Aurelii Antonini Augusti Armeniaci Parthici Medici filiae decreto decurionum pecunia publica\n
EDCS-09200548.translation: To Aurelia Sabina, daughter of Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus Armenicus Parthicus Maximus Medicus, by decree of the decurions and at public expense.
EDCS-09200548.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Aurelia Sabina, daughter of Marcus Aurelius, likely erected by the local town council.

EDCS-09200550.text_edition: \n Sabiniae Tranquillinae Augustae coniugi domini nostri Imperatoris Caesaris Marci Antoni Gordi[ani Pii Felicis Invicti Augusti ------\n
EDCS-09200550.translation: To Sabinia Tranquillina Augusta, wife of our lord Emperor Caesar Marcus Antoninus Gordianus Pius Felix Invictus Augustus, [died...].
EDCS-09200550.summary: This inscription honors Sabinia Tranquillina Augusta, wife of Gordian III, likely erected to commemorate her status or death.

EDCS-09200552.text_edition: \n iuridico in! Piceno et Apuliam sic legato legionis XXII Primigeniae Decianae legato legionis XIII geminae Decianae praefecto aerarii Saturni consuli\n
EDCS-09200552.translation: As legal official in Picenum and Apulia, so as legate of the 22nd Legion Primigenia Deciana, as legate of the 13th Legion Gemina Deciana, as prefect of the Saturnian treasury, as consul.
EDCS-09200552.summary: This inscription lists the various high-ranking offices held by an individual, including military commands and political appointments, likely from the 3rd century AD.

EDCS-09200555.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Lollius Munnas civis Belalitanus pius vixit annis LXXXX hic situs est\n
EDCS-09200555.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Lollius Munnas, a citizen of Belalita, pious, lived 90 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-09200555.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lollius Munnas, a citizen of Belalita, recording his piety and age at death.

EDCS-09200556.summary: This fragmentary inscription appears to be a funerary dedication or a record of parentage, but is too incomplete to fully decipher.

EDCS-09200557.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Furius Ianuarius of Arnus, the pious, lived 65 years. Ia [restored: inscription ends].
EDCS-09200557.summary: A funerary inscription dedicated to the departed spirits for Lucius Furius Ianuarius, noting his age and piety.

EDCS-09200558.text_edition: \n Marco Lurio Marci filio Arnensi Fausto Caeciliano equo publico adlecto praefecto cohortis II Bracaraugustanorum \n
EDCS-09200558.translation: To Marcus Lurius Faustus, son of Marcus, of the Arnensian tribe, equo publico adlecto, prefect of the Second Cohort of Bracaraugustani.
EDCS-09200558.summary: This inscription honors Marcus Lurius Faustus, detailing his Roman citizenship status, military command, and tribal affiliation.

EDCS-09200559.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari Tito Aelio Hadriano Antonino Augusto Pio Felicis Arnensis fili sui\n
EDCS-09200559.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Augustus Pius, son of Felix Arnensis.
EDCS-09200559.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Emperor Antoninus Pius, likely from the 2nd century AD.

EDCS-09200560.text_edition: \n Publio Thermestino Crescenti Caeciliano decurioni coloniae Concordiae Iuliae Karthaginis flamini pe[rpetuo ------\n
EDCS-09200560.translation: To Publius Thermestinus Crescens Caecilianus, decurion of the colony of Concordia Julia Karthago, perpetual flamen...
EDCS-09200560.summary: This is a dedication to Publius Thermestinus Crescens Caecilianus, a local official in Roman Africa, probably from the 2nd or 3rd century AD.

EDCS-09200561.text_edition: \n ius Lucius Sc Ianuarius ob honorem magistratus \n
EDCS-09200561.translation: ...Lucius Sc Ianuarius for the honor of the magistracy.
EDCS-09200561.summary: This fragment records Lucius Sc Ianuarius being honored for holding a magistracy, likely in Roman Africa during the Imperial period.

EDCS-09200563.translation: Of Marcus Iulius Felix, son of Caius, from Abdaian.
EDCS-09200563.summary: This inscription records the name and filiation of Marcus Iulius Felix, likely as part of a tomb or dedication.

EDCS-09200564.summary: This epitaph records the lifespan of Fuficius Extricatus, who is described as pious.

EDCS-09200565.summary: This fragmentary inscription likely records the name of Marcus Calpurnius Victor Lutatianus, possibly as a funerary dedication.

EDCS-09200567.translation: Marcus Cincius Victor fulfilled his vow, sacred to Saturn Augustus.
EDCS-09200567.summary: This inscription records Marcus Cincius Victor fulfilling a vow made to the god Saturn Augustus.

EDCS-09200568.translation: Lucius Caecilius Privatus Furnianus willingly fulfilled his vow, sacred to Saturn Augustus.
EDCS-09200568.summary: This inscription records Lucius Caecilius Privatus Furnianus willingly fulfilling a vow made to the god Saturn Augustus.

EDCS-09200569.text_edition: \n Dio sic Mercurio Thermesi Augusto sacrum\n
EDCS-09200569.translation: Sacred to Mercury Thermesis Augustus by Dio.
EDCS-09200569.summary: This is a religious dedication to Mercury by Dio, likely from Roman Africa during the Imperial period.

EDCS-09200570.text_edition: \n Ex iusso sic Iovis Zabazi ara posuit Libero Patri cura Marci Oppi Vitali\n
EDCS-09200570.translation: By order, this altar to Jupiter Zabazus was set up by Libero Patri, under the care of Marcus Oppius Vitalis.
EDCS-09200570.summary: This inscription records the erection of an altar to Jupiter Zabazus, supervised by Marcus Oppius Vitalis, possibly from Roman Africa.

EDCS-09200572.summary: This inscription describes a person named Honoratus as innocent and faithful in peace, likely a funerary epigraph.

EDCS-09200573.summary: This epitaph records the lifespan of Vincemalos, who lived for 49 years.

EDCS-09200574.summary: This epitaph records the lifespan of Bonifatius, who held the office of subdeacon.

EDCS-09200575.translation: Olympia lived 82 years more or less in peace, and Ianuaria, innocent in peace, and Laeta: peace, faith, charity.
EDCS-09200575.summary: This epitaph commemorates Olympia, Ianuaria, and Laeta, highlighting their virtues and peaceful repose.

EDCS-09200576.translation: To Optata lying in the right part for a short time, for she obtained happiness in this present place, buried in a sarcophagus, but let us not say that she has fulfilled fate's gift, because the heir, inscribed in the tomb of the parent, came into no doubt of children born of both sexes. Therefore she lived in the world 80 years, deposited on the sixth day before the Kalends of April, in the 4th indiction.
EDCS-09200576.summary: This complex funerary inscription, dated to the 4th indiction, describes the tomb of Optata, mentioning her lifespan of 80 years, her burial, and the lineage of children.

EDCS-09200578.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Oppia Fortunata.
EDCS-09200578.summary: This funerary dedication is made to the 'Dis Manibus' (Spirits of the Departed) by Oppia Fortunata.

EDCS-09200579.translation: Filvea the faithful lived in peace for 80 years
EDCS-09200579.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Filvea.

EDCS-09200580.translation: Rufius returned [to God] in peace on the 19th day before the Kalends of February
EDCS-09200580.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the death date of Rufius, likely in the late Roman period.

EDCS-09200581.translation: Sabinus the faithful died in peace on the 15th day before the Kalends of September
EDCS-09200581.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the death date of Sabinus.

EDCS-09200582.translation: Blossius Trebonius Eucarpius, a most distinguished man, the faithful, lived for 62 years and 3 months, and died on the 15th day before the Kalends of March
EDCS-09200582.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Blossius Trebonius Eucarpius, recording his lifespan and death date, and indicating his high social standing.

EDCS-09300556.translation: To Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus, with tribunician power for the 9th time, hailed as emperor, consul for the 2nd time, father of the country, and to Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus, with tribunician power for the 4th time, and to Lucius Septimius Geta Caesar Augustus, by Quintus Anicius Faustus, consular legate of the Augusti, [legate of the III Augusta Pia Vindex legion].
EDCS-09300556.summary: This is a dedication to the emperors Septimius Severus, Caracalla, and Geta, erected by Quintus Anicius Faustus, a high-ranking official, likely in North Africa during the early 3rd century AD.

EDCS-09300558.text_edition: \n Numini Praesenti Iulius Vitalis decurio votum solvit libens animo\n
EDCS-09300558.translation: Julius Vitalis, decurion, willingly fulfilled his vow to the Present Divinity.
EDCS-09300558.summary: This inscription records Julius Vitalis, a local official, fulfilling a vow to a divine power, likely in Roman Africa during the Imperial period.

EDCS-09300559.inscription_type: tituli honorarii, tituli operum, tituli sacri
EDCS-09300559.text_edition: \n Genio Gholaiae pro salute Auggustorum Caius Iuulius sic Dignus |(centurio) legionis III Augustae piae vindicis qui primo die quo ad locum ventum est ubi domini nnnostri castra fieri iusserunt locum consecravit et ex p\n
EDCS-09300559.translation: For the health of the Augusti, Caius Julius Dignus, centurion of the III Augusta Pia Vindex legion, consecrated the site on the first day our lords ordered the camp to be established, and from...
EDCS-09300559.summary: This inscription records Caius Julius Dignus, a centurion, consecrating a site for the health of the emperors, likely in Roman Africa during the late 2nd or early 3rd century AD.

EDCS-09300560.translation: Sacred to Augustus by the Bellenenses, from the public funds of the community of Avitna
EDCS-09300560.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Augustus made by the community of Avitna.

EDCS-09300561.translation: The Septimia Aurelia colony, named Sancta Avitina, devoted to the divine majesty of our lord Flavius Claudius Constantinus the Younger, most noble Caesar
EDCS-09300561.summary: This inscription records a dedication by the colony of Avitna to the emperor Constantius II.

EDCS-09301287.translation: Sacred to the Gods of the Caesars, Caius Firmius Heracla and Caius Iulius Tertius, the magistri of the pagus, made [this] at public expense
EDCS-09301287.summary: This inscription records a public work dedicated to the emperors by local officials.

EDCS-09301288.translation: [dedicated to] Iulius Patruinus, a man of consular rank, legate of Numidia, devotedly united to Basilia by love of country
EDCS-09301288.summary: This inscription likely records a dedication or memorial related to Iulius Patruinus, a former legate of Numidia.

EDCS-09400689.translation: In the name of Christ, Aemilianus the deacon in peace
EDCS-09400689.summary: This is a Christian funerary inscription for Aemilianus, a deacon.

EDCS-09400690.translation: To Publius Petronius Victoricus, a most laudable man, by the most splendid order of the colony Aurelia Antoniniana of Carthage and the municipality Aurelia Antoniniana of Abbiritanus Maior, who obtained immunity
EDCS-09400690.summary: This inscription records a dedication or honor bestowed upon Publius Petronius Victoricus by the city councils of Carthage and Abbiritanus Maior.

EDCS-09400691.translation: To our eternal Lords Valentinian, Valens, and Gratian, Augusti, during the proconsulship of Petronius Claudius, clarissimus vir, and Marius Victorinus, legates of Carthage, clarissimi viri, Flavianus Leontius, curator rei publicae of alma Carthago, of the splendid order, decorated the ocean, begun from its foundations and a tidal pool collapsed by ruin, bringing it to completion and maintenance, with new entrances and dedicated with accompanying standards; he initiated, completed, and dedicated it with the contribution of the people and with love.
EDCS-09400691.summary: This inscription records the completion and dedication of port facilities in Carthage by Flavianus Leontius, curator rei publicae, during the proconsulship of Petronius Claudius and Marius Victorinus, and under the perpetual Augusti Valentinian, Valens, and Gratian.

EDCS-09400692.text_edition: \n Positum CA III Idus Iunias Saturno Augusto sacrum Caius Manius Felix Fortunatianus sacerdos in somnis monitus Saturni numine iussus Manius hic votum solvi sacrumque dicavi pro comperta fide et pro servata salute votum solvi libens animo\n
EDCS-09400692.translation: Erected on the third day before the Ides of June, sacred to Saturn Augustus. Caius Manius Felix Fortunatianus, priest, ordered by Saturn's divine power in a dream, dedicated this vow and sacred offering here, willingly fulfilling the vow for proven loyalty and preserved safety.
EDCS-09400692.summary: This is a dedication to Saturn Augustus by the priest Caius Manius Felix Fortunatianus, who was inspired by a dream, likely in Roman Africa during the Imperial period.

EDCS-09400693.translation: To Quintus Latinus Primosus Puniscus, son of Lucius Latinus Felicianus, former duovir, the order of the municipality of Uruensis, as a citizen and patron, for his merits, by decree of the decurions, with public funds.
EDCS-09400693.summary: This is a dedication honoring Quintus Latinus Primosus Puniscus, son of a former duovir, by the decurions of Uruensis for his merits.

EDCS-09400694.translation: The municipality of Uruensis, for all time and posterity, the most splendid and flourishing order of the municipality of Uruensis decreed to a well-deserving citizen, by decree of the decurions, with public funds, for the dedication of which he gave sportulas and a banquet to the decurions and to all the citizens.
EDCS-09400694.summary: This inscription honors a citizen of Uruensis with a decree and public funds, for which he provided gifts and a banquet to the town's officials and citizens.

EDCS-09400695.translation: To Dynamus, son of Lucius Octavius Gallus Atticus Papirius Concessus, son of Quintus Octavius Gallus, egregius vir, and brother of Quintus Octavius Gallus Concessianus, clarissimus puer, for the many merits of his father and grandfather in the fatherland and in the state, and for their honorable munificence and generosity, the most splendid order of the municipality of Uruensis.
EDCS-09400695.summary: The order of the municipality of Uruensis honors Dynamus for the merits and generosity of his father and grandfather.

EDCS-09400696.translation: To Dynamus, Quintus Octavius Gallus Concessianus, clarissimus puer, son of Quintus Octavius Gallus, egregius vir, for the yoke of their house, inherited from their ancestors, and for love of Publius Iunius Felix and his sons, having achieved the most distinguished dignity, for a vow, perpetually, with his father and patron.
EDCS-09400696.summary: This inscription is a perpetual vow made by Publius Iunius Felix and his sons to Dynamus, Quintus Octavius Gallus Concessianus, in recognition of their inherited family status and their love for the donor.

EDCS-09400697.translation: To Lucius Octavius Aurelianus Didasus, clarissimus vir, a citizen by birth, for his unique faithfulness in protecting the citizens and his love for all, he adorned, improved, and dedicated the baths and the water, corrupted after a flood, correctly with his own generosity; the most splendid order and people of the municipality of Uruensium erected a statue to the well-deserving citizen and patron by decree of the decurions, with public funds.
EDCS-09400697.summary: The order and people of Uruensis erected a statue to Lucius Octavius Aurelianus Didasus for his protection of citizens and love for all, and he also generously restored the public baths and water supply after a flood.

EDCS-09400698.translation: To the Defender of the whole world, our Lord Imperator Valerius Licinianus Licinius Pius Felix Invictus Augustus, Pontifex Maximus, holding tribunician power for the 6th time, Consul for the 2nd time, Father of the Fatherland, Proconsul, the municipality of Uruensium, devoted to his divine majesty and power.
EDCS-09400698.summary: The municipality of Uruensis dedicates itself to Emperor Licinius, honoring his titles and power, likely during his sixth tribunician power and second consulship.

EDCS-09400699.translation: For the remarkable and very great merits which shone forth through magnificent generosity in the advancement of the city walls, to Lucius Iunius Iunillus, vir perfectissimus, count of the divine cohort, protector of the province of Mauretania Caesariensis, a citizen and patron, son of Iunius Publianus, vir doctissimus, the order of his splendid municipality of Uruensium and the people erected a marble statue.
EDCS-09400699.summary: The municipality and people of Uruensium erected a marble statue to Lucius Iunius Iunillus, count of the divine cohort and protector of Mauretania Caesariensis, for his outstanding merits and generosity towards the city.

EDCS-09400700.text_edition: \n CA CIBOS NAO agricolae in spl(endidissima) re publica Bihensi Bilta conductori pariatori restitutori fundi Aufidiani et praeter cetera bona quae in eodem fundo fecit steriles quoque oleastri surculos inserendo plurimas oleas instituit puteum iuxta viam pomarium cum trichilis post collectarium vineas novellas sub silva aeque instituit uxor marito incomparabili fecit\n
EDCS-09400700.translation: CIBOSNAO. Bilta, a farmer and conductor of the splendid Republic of Bihensi, an unparalleled husband to his wife, established many olive trees by grafting shoots onto barren oleasters, a well near the road, an orchard with a summerhouse, and young vineyards under the woods, in addition to other improvements he made on the Aufidian estate; his wife made [this] for her incomparable husband.
EDCS-09400700.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Bilta, a farmer and estate manager in Roman Africa, set up by his wife, highlighting his agricultural achievements and their devoted relationship, likely from the late Roman period.

EDCS-09400701.translation: Victoria, may you be in peace.
EDCS-09400701.summary: This is a funerary inscription, likely for a woman named Victoria, dating to the late Roman period.

EDCS-09400702.translation: Sacred to Saturnus Augustus. Caius Coelius Verecundus paid his vow.
EDCS-09400702.summary: This is a dedication of a votive offering to Saturnus Augustus by Caius Coelius Verecundus.

EDCS-09400703.translation: To Hercules, to the Genius of the Saburianenses. Dhamak the priest made and dedicated it at his own expense, Primosus the builder, who built it.
EDCS-09400703.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a structure to Hercules and the Genius of the Saburianenses by the priest Dhamak, built by Primosus at the priest's expense.

EDCS-09400704.translation: Pascasius, subdeacon, lived 22 years and rested on the 15th day before the Kalends of September.
EDCS-09400704.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan and date of rest of Pascasius, a subdeacon.

EDCS-09400705.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Potentius, a subdeacon.

EDCS-09400706.translation: The place of Petressius, in peace.
EDCS-09400706.summary: This inscription marks a burial place, presumably belonging to or for Petressius.

EDCS-09400711.translation: Hildiger was laid here in peace.
EDCS-09400711.summary: This is a funerary epitaph marking the burial of Hildiger.

EDCS-09400714.summary: This inscription marks a burial place, presumably belonging to or for Castalinus.

EDCS-09400715.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the repose of Dinamius.

EDCS-09400716.translation: Bonifatius was laid to rest on the 10th day before the Kalends of March, in peace.
EDCS-09400716.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the date of rest of Bonifatius.

EDCS-09400717.translation: The place of Donatus the priest.
EDCS-09400717.summary: This inscription marks a burial place, presumably belonging to or for Donatus, a priest.

EDCS-09400720.translation: Pimenius lived 32 years and rested in peace on the 4th day before the Nones of August, in the 12th indiction.
EDCS-09400720.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan, date of rest, and indiction year of Pimenius.

EDCS-09400724.translation: Florentia the faithful lived 5 years and rested in peace.
EDCS-09400724.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Florentia, described as 'faithful'.

EDCS-09400725.translation: Dinamius the faithful rested in peace on the Ides of August.
EDCS-09400725.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Dinamius, who rested in peace on the Ides of August.

EDCS-09400726.translation: Germanus the cleric lived 15 years and 2 months, rested in peace on the Ides of July, in the eighth indiction.
EDCS-09400726.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan and repose of Germanus, a cleric, indicating the date by Ides of July and the eighth indiction.

EDCS-09400727.summary: This is a funerary marker indicating the burial place of Innocentius.

EDCS-09400729.translation: Innocentius the faithful rested in peace, lived for some years, interred on the twelfth day before the Kalends of October.
EDCS-09400729.summary: This funerary epitaph records the repose and burial date (twelfth day before the Kalends of October) of Innocentius the faithful.

EDCS-09400730.summary: This is a simple funerary inscription stating that Secundinus rested in peace.

EDCS-09400732.translation: Genazius rested in peace, lived 3 years and 9 months.
EDCS-09400732.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan of Genazius, who lived 3 years and 9 months before resting in peace.

EDCS-09400735.translation: Ivuza rested in peace, lived 10 years.
EDCS-09400735.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan of Ivuza, who lived 10 years before resting in peace.

EDCS-09400736.translation: Castimonialis lived in peace, interred on the eighth day before the Kalends of September, in the eighth indiction.
EDCS-09400736.summary: This funerary inscription records the repose of Castimonialis, specifying her burial date (eighth day before the Kalends of September) and the eighth indiction.

EDCS-09400737.translation: Adeodata the faithful lived in peace for more or less 10 years, interred on the fourteenth day before the Kalends of November, in the ninth indiction.
EDCS-09400737.summary: This funerary epitaph for Adeodata the faithful records her approximate lifespan of 10 years and her burial date (fourteenth day before the Kalends of November) in the ninth indiction.

EDCS-09400738.translation: Abundiola the faithful in Christ rested in peace on the sixth day before the Ides of June, in the thirteenth indiction, lived 4 years.
EDCS-09400738.summary: This funerary inscription for Abundiola the faithful in Christ records her lifespan of 4 years and her burial date (sixth day before the Ides of June) in the thirteenth indiction.

EDCS-09400740.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Abitiana, recording her age at death and her faithful status.

EDCS-09400741.translation: Seberianus rested in peace, lived, buried.
EDCS-09400741.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Seberianus, recording his resting in peace and burial.

EDCS-09400742.translation: Donatus, also called As, lived 67 years, rested in peace on the day before the Kalends of January, in the 9th indiction.
EDCS-09400742.summary: This tombstone inscription records the age at death and burial date of Donatus (also known as As).

EDCS-09400745.translation: Faithful Benantius lived 54 years in peace, buried on the day before the Nones of August, in the sixth indiction.
EDCS-09400745.summary: This tombstone inscription records the age at death and burial date of Benantius, described as faithful.

EDCS-09400746.translation: Place of Teaufilus, to the lector.
EDCS-09400746.summary: This inscription indicates a burial place belonging to Teaufilus and is dedicated to a lector.

EDCS-09400749.translation: Donatilla with her sister in peace.
EDCS-09400749.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Donatilla and her sister, indicating they rest in peace.

EDCS-09400751.summary: This inscription marks a burial place belonging to Vitalis.

EDCS-09400753.summary: This inscription marks a burial place belonging to S. Colonica.

EDCS-09400755.translation: Florentia the faithful lived 64 years, rested in peace on the 15th day before the Kalends of March.
EDCS-09400755.summary: This tombstone inscription records the age at death and burial date of Florentia, described as faithful.

EDCS-09400758.translation: Florentilla in peace, buried on the 11th day before the Kalends of March.
EDCS-09400758.summary: This tombstone inscription records the burial date of Florentilla, who rests in peace.

EDCS-09401239.translation: Sacred to Fruit-Bearing Augustus, for the health of Imperator Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus Armeniacus Medicus Parthicus Maximus and Imperator Caesar Lucius Aurelius Verus Augustus Armeniacus Medicus Parthicus Maximus, the Roman citizens of Almenna, with their own funds, built the temple and porticoes, with Lucius Volussennius Pastor and Gaius Julius Rogatus as curators.
EDCS-09401239.summary: This is a dedication of a temple and porticoes by the Roman citizens of Almenna, built for the health of Emperors Marcus Aurelius Antoninus and Lucius Verus, likely in the mid-2nd century CE.

EDCS-09401240.translation: To the deified Hadrian, according to the will of Publius Sextilius Felix Sulpicianus, from the Roman citizens residing in Ureu.
EDCS-09401240.summary: This inscription records a dedication to the deified Emperor Hadrian, made according to a will by Roman citizens living in Ureu, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-09401241.translation: To our lord Flavius Valerius Constantinus, most noble Caesar Augustus, the municipium of Aurelium Ureu, by decree of the decurions and with public funds, is devoted to his divine majesty.
EDCS-09401241.summary: This inscription is a dedication of the municipium of Aurelium Ureu to Emperor Flavius Valerius Constantinus (Constantine I), likely in the early 4th century CE.

EDCS-09401242.text_edition: \n Magno et invicto principi restitutori orbis sui terrarum Flavio Valerio Constantino Invicto Pio Felici Augusto Asadi devota numini maiestatique eius\n
EDCS-09401242.translation: To Magnus and the unconquered prince, restorer of his world, Flavius Valerius Constantinus Invictus Pius Felix Augustus, Asadi, devoted to his divine majesty.
EDCS-09401242.summary: This is a dedicatory inscription honoring Emperor Constantine I, likely erected by an individual named Asadi, dating to the 4th century CE.

EDCS-09401246.translation: This place holds the illustrious Ebasia, but only her body, for she lives on because she left behind her desired offspring as survivor; she therefore lived happily in this temporal world until the day before she migrated to heaven, for 77 years; laid to rest on the 8th day before the Ides of October, in the 5th indiction.
EDCS-09401246.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Ebasia, recording her lifespan of 77 years and her virtuous life, likely from the late Roman period.

EDCS-09401247.translation: For the prosperity of the blessed times of our lords Theodosius and Valens Valentinianus, perpetual Augusti, Apronius Primus.
EDCS-09401247.summary: This is a dedication by Apronius Primus for the prosperity of the reigns of Emperors Theodosius and Valentinian III, likely in the mid-5th century CE.

EDCS-09401250.translation: To Fridos of good memory, who lived in peace for 20 years.
EDCS-09401250.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Fridos, noting his peaceful life for 20 years, likely from the late Roman or early Christian period.

EDCS-09401251.text_edition: \n Paragorius bixit sic in pace annos IIII\n
EDCS-09401251.translation: Paragorius lived thus in peace for 4 years.
EDCS-09401251.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a child named Paragorius who died at the age of 4, likely dating to the late Roman period.

EDCS-09401252.text_edition: \n Spesinilla innocens fidelis requievit in pace\n
EDCS-09401252.translation: Spesinilla, innocent and faithful, rested in peace.
EDCS-09401252.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a woman named Spesinilla, emphasizing her virtues, likely dating to the late Roman period.

EDCS-09401254.summary: This is a simple funerary epitaph for Fortunata, indicating she died 'in peace', likely from the late Roman or early Christian period.

EDCS-09401255.text_edition: \n Fortunata nurus Sirici sic fidelis vixit in pace annos XXII menses III dies VII\n
EDCS-09401255.translation: Fortunata, daughter-in-law of Siricus, lived faithfully thus in peace for 22 years, 3 months, and 7 days.
EDCS-09401255.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Fortunata, detailing her age at death and relationship to Siricus, likely dating to the late Roman period.

EDCS-09401256.text_edition: \n Memoria Fortunatais sic infanti in pace\n
EDCS-09401256.translation: In memory of Fortunata, an infant, thus in peace.
EDCS-09401256.summary: This is a funerary inscription for an infant named Fortunata, likely dating to the late Roman period.

EDCS-09401257.summary: This is a funerary inscription for an individual named Innocentius, likely dating to the late Roman period.

EDCS-09401258.translation: Iulia Primula rested in peace. Her husband made this.
EDCS-09401258.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Iulia Primula, made by her husband, indicating she died 'in peace', likely from the late Roman or early Christian period.

EDCS-09401259.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Iulius Pascasius lived 60 years and six months.
EDCS-09401259.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Iulius Pascasius, dedicated to the Divine Manes, recording his lifespan of 60 years and 6 months, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09401260.translation: Ponponia Pelagea lived 32 years, with discipline and love.
EDCS-09401260.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Ponponia Pelagea, recording her lifespan of 32 years and commending her character, likely from the late Roman period.

EDCS-09401261.text_edition: \n Memoria Safratis in pace die VIII Idus Nobembres sic\n
EDCS-09401261.translation: In memory of Safratis, in peace, on the 8th day before the Ides of November.
EDCS-09401261.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Safratis, recording the date of death, likely dating to the late Roman period.

EDCS-09401262.text_edition: \n Hic iacet Sitifis qui vixit anno mensibus III\n
EDCS-09401262.translation: Here lies Sitifis, who lived for 1 year and 3 months.
EDCS-09401262.summary: This is a funerary inscription for an individual named Sitifis, recording their age at death, likely dating to the late Roman period.

EDCS-09401263.translation: Innocens named Sofia died, lived for 4 years.
EDCS-09401263.summary: A tombstone recording the death of a young girl named Sofia, who lived for four years.

EDCS-09401264.translation: The gods above, I beseech you.
EDCS-09401264.summary: A very short inscription that may be a prayer or dedication to the gods.

EDCS-09401265.translation: Ursicinus, a man of great vitality.
EDCS-09401265.summary: A fragmentary inscription possibly honoring a man named Ursicinus for his vigor.

EDCS-09401266.translation: Menix, son of Sen, lived for 16 years.
EDCS-09401266.summary: A tombstone recording the death of a young man named Menix, son of Sen, who lived for sixteen years.

EDCS-09401268.translation: Table of the presbyter Cidis, of the Atis.
EDCS-09401268.summary: An inscription possibly related to a table or altar belonging to a presbyter named Cidis, associated with the Atis.

EDCS-09401599.translation: To Lucius Aurellius Hirrius Festus, son of Festus, a singular man, tribune of the First Urban Cohort, an excellent man, an incomparable citizen, for his outstanding benevolence towards his citizens, the citizens of Neferi unanimously erected this.
EDCS-09401599.summary: A dedication by the citizens of Neferi to Lucius Aurellius Hirrius Festus, a tribune of the First Urban Cohort, for his benevolence.

EDCS-09401600.translation: Dedicated to the spirits of the departed. Festa the pious lived for 15 years and 5 days.
EDCS-09401600.summary: A tombstone recording the death of Festa, who lived for fifteen years and five days.

EDCS-09401601.text_edition: \n Nomina quae hoc taurobolio sacrum acceperunt Iulius Felicissimus et Iulia Ianuaria eius et Iulius \n
EDCS-09401601.translation: The names of those who received this sacred taurobolium are Iulius Felicissimus and his Iulia Ianuaria and Iulius...
EDCS-09401601.summary: This is an inscription recording recipients of a taurobolium (a ritual sacrifice of a bull), likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09401604.translation: Dedicated to the spirits of the departed. Flaminius Felix, son of Secundus, from Milza, pious, lived for 75 years.
EDCS-09401604.summary: A tombstone recording the death of Flaminius Felix, son of Secundus, who lived for seventy-five years.

EDCS-09401606.translation: To Lo [---]irius Claudianus, son of Felicis, for his merits, 8 years. Ninius, Tiius,inius Licinianus, Iustinius Didianus, Titus Rutilius Mudidnus, Caius Iulius Iucundus, Caius Datius Tertius, Titus Rutilius Honoratus, Marcus Tadius Sedatus.
EDCS-09401606.summary: A dedication honoring Lo [---]irius Claudianus for his merits, listing several other individuals as well.

EDCS-09401610.translation: Marcus Rutilius lived for 1 year, 6 months, and 4 days, and Quintus Rutilius.
EDCS-09401610.summary: A tombstone recording the lifespan of Marcus Rutilius and mentioning Quintus Rutilius.

EDCS-09401611.translation: Vernensis and Faracus made this for Hermetus Felicitanus.
EDCS-09401611.summary: This text likely records the dedication of a monument by Vernensis and Faracus for Hermetus Felicitanus.

EDCS-09401612.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Amiisivs Vinceni, dutiful, lived 20 years, 6 months, and 5 days.
EDCS-09401612.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the name, piety, and lifespan of Amiisivs Vinceni, dedicated to the underworld deities.

EDCS-09401613.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Caius Arabus Romanus lived...
EDCS-09401613.summary: This is a funerary epitaph, partially preserved, dedicated to the underworld deities and recording the name and lifespan of Caius Arabus Romanus.

EDCS-09401614.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Quintus Fabricius Ri s Honoratianus, dutiful, lived 12 years, 5 months, and 2 hours. Quintus Fabricius Apronianus, a veteran of the 1st Urban Cohort, made this for himself and for his wife, Cominia Rogata.
EDCS-09401614.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Quintus Fabricius Honoratianus, who died young, and his father Quintus Fabricius Apronianus, a veteran, who also dedicated it for his wife.

EDCS-09401615.summary: This is a dedication to the god Saturn of Meddes.

EDCS-09401616.translation: To Saturn Meddensis Augustus, sacred. Caelius Saturninus Nonianus fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-09401616.summary: This inscription records the fulfillment of a vow made to the god Saturn Meddensis Augustus by Caelius Saturninus Nonianus.

EDCS-09401617.translation: To Saturn Meddensis Augustus, sacred. Iulius Sosus Martialis fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-09401617.summary: This inscription records the fulfillment of a vow made to the god Saturn Meddensis Augustus by Iulius Sosus Martialis.

EDCS-09401623.summary: This inscription likely records the dedication of an arch by Gaius Munius Agathopus.

EDCS-09401625.translation: To Marcus Vitius, son of Titus, grandson of Lucius.
EDCS-09401625.summary: This inscription is a dedication or memorial to Marcus Vitius, son of Titus and grandson of Lucius.

EDCS-09401626.summary: This inscription is too fragmentary to provide a meaningful translation or summary.

EDCS-09401627.translation: Dedicated to the spirits of the underworld. Octavia Marchis Secunda lived 5 months.
EDCS-09401627.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Octavia Marchis Secunda, recording her age at death.

EDCS-09401628.translation: Dedicated to the spirits of the underworld. Flaminia, daughter of Marcu Fortunata, lived forty years.
EDCS-09401628.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Flaminia Fortunata, recording her age at death.

EDCS-09401630.translation: Dedicated to Saturn Augustus. Mario willingly fulfilled his vow for his household.
EDCS-09401630.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by Mario to the god Saturn Augustus for the well-being of his household.

EDCS-09401631.translation: Dedicated to the spirits of the underworld. V[---]ipes, a dutiful son, lived 45 years, 5 months, and 15 days, and 2 hours; he is buried here.
EDCS-09401631.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Vrus Ipesi, recording his age at death and burial location.

EDCS-09401637.translation: Dedicated to the spirits of the underworld. Marcus Annius Celer, dutiful, lived 46 years, 3 months, and 13 days, and 3 hours.
EDCS-09401637.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Marcus Annius Celer, recording his age at death.

EDCS-09401638.translation: Dedicated to the spirits of the underworld. Marcus Aelius Madasius Iunior, dutiful, lived 18 years, 10 months, and 4 days; he is buried here.
EDCS-09401638.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Marcus Aelius Madasius Iunior, recording his age at death and burial location.

EDCS-09700369.text_edition: \n Impperatoribus ddominis nnostris Philippis Auggustis Marco Aurelio Cominio Cassiano legato Auggustorum pro praetore clarissimo viro \n
EDCS-09700369.translation: To our Lords Emperors, the Augusti, Marcus Aurelius Cominius Cassianus, clarissimus vir, governor with the authority of the Augusti and propraetor.
EDCS-09700369.summary: This inscription records a dedication by the governor Cassianus to the emperors Philip. It is likely from the mid-3rd century AD.

EDCS-09700371.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription, likely the beginning of a name and potentially a dedication or epitaph.

EDCS-09700372.text_edition: \n legionis III Augustae Vicrius Verus |(centurio) [legionis III Augustae] praepositus vexillationis \n
EDCS-09700372.translation: Vicrius Verus, centurion of the Legio III Augusta, commander of a detachment.
EDCS-09700372.summary: This inscription records the titles and positions held by Vicrius Verus, a centurion in the Legio III Augusta, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-09700378.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Iulia Privata vixit annis LXX\n
EDCS-09700378.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Iulia Privata lived for 70 years.
EDCS-09700378.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Iulia Privata, recording her name and age at death.

EDCS-09700379.translation: Margarita, of good memory, faithful in Christ, rested in peace, lived 38 years, and was buried on the 17th day before the Kalends of October, in the 14th indiction.
EDCS-09700379.summary: This is a Christian funerary inscription for Margarita, recording her age at death and date of burial.

EDCS-09700381.translation: Ferranda, faithful in the service of Christ.
EDCS-09700381.summary: This is a Christian funerary inscription for Ferranda, indicating her devotion.

EDCS-09700764.summary: This is a very brief inscription identifying a centurion named Aurelius.

EDCS-09700765.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Decimus Volasenna Dorotheus pius vixit nnis LXXX mensibus XI diebus VII hic situs est D A pi vixit annis LX mensibus diebus hic sit-- est\n
EDCS-09700765.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Decimus Volasenna Dorotheus, dutiful, lived 80 years, 11 months, 7 days. He is buried here. DA, lived 60 years, months, days. He is buried here.
EDCS-09700765.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the life spans of at least two individuals, Decimus Volasenna Dorotheus and another whose name is incomplete.

EDCS-09700767.translation: To Quintus Aradius Rufinus Optatus Aelianus, consul, Augustalis associate, acting as proconsul of the province of Africa, legate of Augustus with praetorian power for the provinces of Syria Coela, Phoenicia, and Galatia, prefect of the treasury of Saturn, prefect of the military treasury, and legate of the 7th legion.
EDCS-09700767.summary: This is a dedicatory inscription honoring Quintus Aradius Rufinus Optatus Aelianus, listing his numerous high-ranking imperial and military offices.

EDCS-09700768.translation: Whoever chances to pass by our tomb, I beg you to move away from me your complaints about death; he who fled the suffering of this life lived for forty-two years, Probatius, and peacefully rendered his debt to nature.
EDCS-09700768.summary: This is a funerary epigram for Probatius, who lived to the age of 42, possibly dating to the late Roman period based on the style and content.

EDCS-09700769.translation: Crescens, a loyal peregrine, son of Gratiani magister militum, lived for 45 years in peace and was buried on the 11th day before the Ides of October in the fifth indiction.
EDCS-09700769.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Crescens, identified as a peregrine and son of a magister militum, with his age and burial date given.

EDCS-09700770.translation: Traianus, a loyal peregrine tribune, lived for 40 years in peace and was buried on the 8th day before the Kalends of May in the seventh indiction.
EDCS-09700770.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Traianus, a peregrine tribune, stating his age and burial date.

EDCS-09700771.translation: Aristobolus, a loyal man, lived for 37 years and 10 months in peace and was buried on the 9th day before the Kalends of June on the holy Lord's Day in the eleventh indiction.
EDCS-09700771.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Aristobolus, recording his age in years and months, and his burial date.

EDCS-09700772.translation: Gaudibudus, a loyal man, lived for 9 months and was buried on the 3rd day before the Ides of July in the tenth indiction.
EDCS-09700772.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Gaudibudus, stating his lifespan in months and his burial date.

EDCS-09700773.translation: Petrus, a loyal man, lived for 8 years and 3 months and 12 days, and was buried on the day before the Kalends of [Month?] in the fourth indiction.
EDCS-09700773.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Petrus, detailing his age in years, months, and days, and providing a burial date with an incomplete month.

EDCS-09700774.translation: Cosmas, a primicerius, lived for 60 years in peace and was buried on the 11th day before the Kalends of May in the fourth indiction.
EDCS-09700774.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Cosmas, identified as a primicerius, recording his age and burial date.

EDCS-09700775.translation: Gratianus, a deacon, lived for 35 years in peace and was buried on the day of the Nones of July in the fourth indiction.
EDCS-09700775.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Gratianus, a deacon, stating his age and burial date.

EDCS-09700776.translation: Liberatus, a loyal man, lived for 75 years and was buried on the 4th day before the Ides of December in the sixth indiction.
EDCS-09700776.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Liberatus, recording his age and burial date.

EDCS-09700798.translation: To Cornelius Africanus, a veteran of the tenth legion's cavalry.
EDCS-09700798.summary: This is a dedication to Cornelius Africanus, a veteran of the ala X (cavalry unit), likely an honorary or military inscription.

EDCS-09700799.translation: Eucharistus, a slave of Cassius Probus, aged 20, is buried here. His father Charito made this from his own resources.
EDCS-09700799.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a young slave named Eucharistus, set up by his father.

EDCS-09700800.translation: Julius Saturninus of Tipasa made this for himself and his wife Vibía Saturnina while alive.
EDCS-09700800.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Julius Saturninus and his wife, set up by himself during his lifetime.

EDCS-09700801.translation: To the Spirits of the departed. Iulia Spes lived 25 years.
EDCS-09700801.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Iulia Spes, stating her name and age at death.

EDCS-09700802.translation: To the Spirits of the departed. Publius Aelius Teucer, his father, [set this up] for his most beloved son Mauretanicus.
EDCS-09700802.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Mauretanicus, set up by his grieving father.

EDCS-09700803.translation: Severus lived 50 years and is buried here. Tilaucan, daughter of Felix, placed this for her husband. May the earth lie lightly upon you.
EDCS-09700803.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Severus, placed by his wife Tilaucan, including a common Latin epitaph phrase.

EDCS-09700804.translation: To the Spirits of the departed. To Teucrus the Younger, servant and agent of the republic of Tipasa. Felix [set this up] for his most dutiful brother.
EDCS-09700804.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Teucrus the Younger, a civic official, set up by his brother.

EDCS-09701230.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari Lucio Domitio Aureliano Pio Felici Augusto pontifici maximo Germanico maximo Gothico maximo tribuniciae potestatis patri patriae consuli II municipes Uzappenses devoti numini maiestatique eius decreto decurionum pecunia publica\n
EDCS-09701230.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Lucius Domitius Aurelianus Pius Felix Augustus, chief priest, greatest German, greatest Goth, holder of tribunician power, father of the fatherland, consul II. The citizens of Uzappa, devoted to his divine will and majesty, by decree of their decurions, with public funds.
EDCS-09701230.summary: This inscription records a dedication by the citizens of Uzappa to Emperor Aurelian, celebrating his titles and victories, likely from the late 3rd century AD.

EDCS-09701231.translation: Seia Maxima placed this from her own resources by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-09701231.summary: This is a public dedication or funerary monument set up by Seia Maxima on behalf of the town council.

EDCS-09701232.translation: Vesia Rustica placed this from her own resources by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-09701232.summary: This is a public dedication or funerary monument set up by Vesia Rustica on behalf of the town council.

EDCS-09701234.translation: Sacred to Saturnus Augustus. Marcus Gargilius Zabo, the priest, willingly fulfilled his undertaken vow. [This occurred] under the magistracy of Quintus Servenus Primus, during the consulship of Rufinus and Severus, on the sixth day before the Ides of November.
EDCS-09701234.summary: This is a dedication to the deified emperor Saturnus, recording the fulfillment of a vow by a priest during specific consular and magisterial terms.

EDCS-09701235.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the departed. Beccut, joined to her husband Ilon, [died] a virgin. How fate brought me back, a raw maiden, to the seat of death! Thus the Fates decreed. Here I was being sung for with hymn and torch, now covered by urn and earth, I rest. I lived as long as allowed, modest without stain. Through Lucina's favor, I bore a son who bears my name and lives on. Let no one grieve excessively for me whom they hold dear to their heart. Grief at death is common to all. L. Eia Rissima, pious, lived 15 years. Euthesia.
EDCS-09701235.summary: This is a complex funerary epitaph for a young woman named L. Eia Rissima, who died unmarried at 15, lamenting her fate and mentioning her pious life and motherhood before death, possibly written by her mother Euthesia.

EDCS-09701236.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Otacilia Tertia vixit annis LXXX\n
EDCS-09701236.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Otacilia Tertia lived for 80 years.
EDCS-09701236.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Otacilia Tertia, recording her name and age at death.

EDCS-09701237.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Quintus Stagio Lustianus vixit annis XVIII\n
EDCS-09701237.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Quintus Stagio Lustianus lived for 18 years.
EDCS-09701237.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Quintus Stagio Lustianus, recording his name and age at death.

EDCS-09701238.text_edition: \n Marcus Licinius Marci filius Galeria Lugduno Fidelis militavit eques in legione III Augusta nnos XVI factus duplicarius in ala nnoniorum menses IV vixit nnos XXXII hic situs est Quintus Iulius Atticus et Titus nicius Saecularis equites legionis III Augustae heredes eius posuerunt\n
EDCS-09701238.translation: Marcus Licinius, son of Marcus, from the tribe Galeria, from Lugdunum, a loyal soldier, served as an equestrian in the Legio III Augusta for 16 years, became a duplicarius in the ala Norica for 4 months, lived for 32 years. He is buried here. Quintus Iulius Atticus and Titus Iulius Saecularis, equites of the Legio III Augusta, his heirs, placed this.
EDCS-09701238.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcus Licinius, detailing his military service in the Legio III Augusta and his age at death, set up by his heirs.

EDCS-09701239.text_edition: \n Lucius Iulius Luci filius Quirina Tarvillus Avarici miles legionis III Augustae centuria Anchisae vixit nnos XXV militavit annos V hic situs est\n
EDCS-09701239.translation: Lucius Iulius, son of Lucius, from the tribe Quirina, from Tarvillus Avarici, soldier of the Legio III Augusta, in the century of Anchisa, lived for 25 years, served for 5 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-09701239.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Iulius, detailing his military service in the Legio III Augusta and his age at death.

EDCS-09701240.text_edition: \n Sextus Alfius Sexti filius Arnensis Primus Carthagine miles legionis III Augustae centuria Rutili Secundi vixit \n
EDCS-09701240.translation: Sextus Alfius Primus, son of Sextus, of the Arnensis tribe, a soldier of the III Augusta legion, in the century of Rutilius Secundus, lived [unknown duration].
EDCS-09701240.summary: This is a tombstone for Sextus Alfius Primus, a soldier of the III Augusta legion, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-09701241.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Aesopo vikario sic vixit annos XXVI Adventus verna ex dispensatore legionis III Augustae\n
EDCS-09701241.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Aesopus, the deputy official, lived 26 years. Adventus Verna, from the supply officer of the III Augusta legion, [dedicated this].
EDCS-09701241.summary: This is a tombstone for Aesopus, a deputy official, dedicated by Adventus Verna, a supply officer of the III Augusta legion, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-09701242.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Caius Asiaticus Felix paedagogus vixit annos LXXX qui se vivo domum aeternam fecit hic situs est\n
EDCS-09701242.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Caius Asiaticus Felix, the teacher, lived 80 years, who made his eternal home while still alive; he is buried here.
EDCS-09701242.summary: This is a tombstone for Caius Asiaticus Felix, a teacher, who built his own tomb, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-09701243.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Iulia Silleha vixit annos LXXV hic sita est Marius Gaetulicus matri karissimae fecit\n
EDCS-09701243.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Iulia Silleha lived 75 years; she is buried here. Marius Gaetulicus made this for his dearest mother.
EDCS-09701243.summary: This is a tombstone for Iulia Silleha, dedicated by her son Marius Gaetulicus, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-09701244.text_edition: \n Caius Aelius Faustus vixit annos LV menses VI hic situs est Achilleus patri\n
EDCS-09701244.translation: Caius Aelius Faustus lived 55 years and 6 months; he is buried here. Achilleus for his father.
EDCS-09701244.summary: This is a tombstone for Caius Aelius Faustus, dedicated by his son Achilleus, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-09701245.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Annia Hilara vixit annos LXXV hic sita est Sulpicius Pompeius uxori karissimae fecit\n
EDCS-09701245.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Annia Hilara lived 75 years; she is buried here. Sulpicius Pompeius made this for his dearest wife.
EDCS-09701245.summary: This is a tombstone for Annia Hilara, dedicated by her husband Sulpicius Pompeius, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-09701246.text_edition: \n Quinto Aurelio Quinti filio Pio Po militi legionis III Augustae centuria Mestri Vi beneficiario tribuni vixit nnos XXVIII mil[itavit ------\n
EDCS-09701246.translation: To Quintus Aurelius Pius, son of Quintus, a soldier of the III Augusta legion, in the century of Mestrius Vi, an assistant to the tribune, lived 28 years, served [unknown duration].
EDCS-09701246.summary: This is a tombstone for Quintus Aurelius Pius, a soldier and assistant tribune of the III Augusta legion, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-09701247.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Caecilius Rogatianus vixit annos LXX Aemilia Aurelia marito pio Quadrubio sic\n
EDCS-09701247.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Caecilius Rogatianus lived 70 years. Aemilia Aurelia for her devoted husband Quadrubius, thus [lived].
EDCS-09701247.summary: This is a tombstone for Quadrubius, dedicated by his wife Aemilia Aurelia, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-09701248.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Caius Aelius Sabinus vixit annos XCI hic situs est\n
EDCS-09701248.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Caius Aelius Sabinus lived 91 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-09701248.summary: This is a tombstone for Caius Aelius Sabinus, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-09701249.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Fructuosa vixit annos XX hic sita\n
EDCS-09701249.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Fructuosa lived 20 years; she is buried [here].
EDCS-09701249.summary: This is a tombstone for Fructuosa, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-09701250.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Fructo carissimo filius fecit\n
EDCS-09701250.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. His son Fructus made this for his dearest son.
EDCS-09701250.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Fructus, made by his son, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09701251.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Helvius Germanus vixit annos LXX fili posuerunt\n
EDCS-09701251.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Helvius Germanus lived 70 years. His sons erected this.
EDCS-09701251.summary: This is a funerary monument for Helvius Germanus, who lived to 70, erected by his sons, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09701252.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Iulia Quintula vixit annis XXX\n
EDCS-09701252.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Iulia Quintula lived 30 years.
EDCS-09701252.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Iulia Quintula, who lived to 30, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09701253.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Iulia Respectula vixit annos XXXV menses VI Iulius Extricatus coniugi piae fecit hic sita est\n
EDCS-09701253.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Iulia Respectula lived 35 years and 6 months. Iulius Extricatus made this for his pious wife, who is buried here.
EDCS-09701253.summary: This funerary monument records the lifespan of Iulia Respectula and was erected by her husband Iulius Extricatus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09701254.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Iulius Viator vixit annis LXXII filius patri carissimo fecit\n
EDCS-09701254.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Iulius Viator lived 72 years. His son made this for his dearest father.
EDCS-09701254.summary: This is a funerary monument for Iulius Viator, who lived to 72, erected by his son, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09701255.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Caius Laelius Terentianus vixit annis XX mensibus XI diebus XXV hic situs est Laelius Mercurius filio dulcissimo fecit\n
EDCS-09701255.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Caius Laelius Terentianus lived 20 years, 11 months, and 25 days. He lies here. Laelius Mercurius made this for his sweetest son.
EDCS-09701255.summary: This funerary dedication records the life of Caius Laelius Terentianus and was made by his father Laelius Mercurius, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09701256.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Rutilia Marcella vixit nnis duobus mensibus decem hic sita est\n
EDCS-09701256.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Rutilia Marcella lived two years and ten months. She lies here.
EDCS-09701256.summary: This is a funerary monument for Rutilia Marcella, who died at two years and ten months old, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09701257.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum ego Prima Feliciano marito rarissimo memoriam feci et dedicavi qui vixit annos LXX\n
EDCS-09701257.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. I, Prima, made and dedicated this memorial to Feliciano, my most unique husband, who lived 70 years.
EDCS-09701257.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Feliciano, erected by his wife Prima, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09701258.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Ianparila, indicating she died peacefully.

EDCS-09701259.translation: Fortunius, of good memory, lived in peace for 2 years, 11 months.
EDCS-09701259.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Fortunius, who died at the age of 2 years and 11 months.

EDCS-09701260.translation: Gaudentta, who lived in peace for 30 years, Messicius made this for his dearest wife, who died on the 5th day before the Nones of July.
EDCS-09701260.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Messicius for his wife Gaudentta, who died at age 30 on July 2nd.

EDCS-09701261.translation: Maxima, innocent, lived in peace for 11 years, 11 months, and 10 days.
EDCS-09701261.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Maxima, who died at the age of 11 years, 11 months, and 10 days.

EDCS-09701263.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Turibius Victorinus, grandson, adorned this monument for Turibius Marcellus, with respect and good will, as a remembrance of his judgment towards them.
EDCS-09701263.summary: This funerary monument was adorned by Turibius Victorinus for his grandfather Turibius Marcellus, honoring his favorable judgment.

EDCS-09701265.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Modius Quintus lived for 96 years and 3 hours.
EDCS-09701265.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Modius Quintus, who lived 96 years and 3 hours.

EDCS-09701266.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Marcus Ulpius Turannus lived for 60 years; his heirs Ninus and Muttun Fortunatus Gemellus made this.
EDCS-09701266.summary: This funerary monument was made by the heirs of Marcus Ulpius Turannus, who lived to be 60 years old.

EDCS-09701268.translation: You who lead with your looks and do not read this willingly, may no envious person begrudge you; may Victoriani always live in God.
EDCS-09701268.summary: This epitaph is a warning against envy and expresses a wish for the eternal life of Victoriani in God.

EDCS-09701302.text_edition: \n Memoriae Simpliciae coniugis quae vixit annos XXXIII recessit VI Idus Maias (anno) provinciae CCXXVI item Exupi fili vixit annos VI menses VIII dies VI recessit XIII Kalendas supra scriptas (anno) provinciae supra scripto et Monnicae filiae vixit nnos V menses VIIII recessit XIIII Kalendas Iulias (anno) provinciae supra scripto Iulius Exupius piissimis fecit\n
EDCS-09701302.translation: To the memory of my wife Simplicia, who lived 33 years and passed away on the 6th day before the Ides of May in the 226th year of the province; also of my son Exupius, who lived 6 years, 8 months, and 6 days, and passed away on the 13th day before the Kalends of [August, inferred from 'supra scriptas'] in the aforementioned year of the province; and of my daughter Monnica, who lived 5 years, 9 months, and passed away on the 14th day before the Kalends of July in the aforementioned year of the province. Iulius Exupius made this for his most devoted [children and wife].
EDCS-09701302.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Iulius Exupius for his wife Simplicia and two children, Exupius and Monnica, with specific death dates and ages, dating to the provincial year 226 (likely 249 CE).

EDCS-09701303.translation: In memory of the most blessed martyrs Peter and Paul.
EDCS-09701303.summary: This inscription is a memorial to the Christian martyrs Peter and Paul.

EDCS-09701305.translation: In memory of the foreign martyrs who suffered at the trees in the part, whom God brought to this holy place...
EDCS-09701305.summary: This inscription is a memorial to foreign martyrs who suffered and died, possibly near trees, and whose remains were brought to this holy place.

EDCS-09701715.text_edition: \n Neroni Claudio divi Claudi filio Germanici Caesaris nepoti Tiberi Caesaris Augusti pronepoti divi Augusti abnepoti Caesari Augusto Germanico pontifici maximo tribunicia potestate imperatori consuli designato II patri patriae Marcus Pompeius Silvanus Staberius Flavinus XVvir sacris faciundis proconsul III dedicavit Quinto Cassio Grato praetore proconsule Cretae et Cyrenarum legato pro praetore Africae III\n
EDCS-09701715.translation: To Nero Claudius, son of the deified Claudius, grandson of Germanicus Caesar, great-grandson of Tiberius Caesar Augustus, great-great-grandson of the deified Augustus, to Caesar Augustus Germanicus, Pontifex Maximus, holder of tribunician power, Imperator, consul-designate for the second time, father of the country.
