Marcus Pompeius Silvanus Staberius Flavinus, fifteen-man board for performing sacred rites, proconsul for the third time, dedicated this, with Quintus Cassius Gratus as praetor, proconsul of Crete and Cyrene, and legate with proconsular power of Africa for the third time.
EDCS-09701715.summary: This is a dedication by Marcus Pompeius Silvanus Staberius Flavinus, detailing the extensive imperial titles of Nero Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus and mentioning the officials involved in the dedication, likely from the mid-1st century CE.

EDCS-09701716.text_edition: \n Imperatore Caesare Marco Aurelio Antonino Augusto pontifice maximo tribunicia potestate XVI consule III et Imperatore Caesare Lucio Aurelio Vero Augusto pontifice tribunicia potestate II consule II divi Antonini Pii filiis divi Hadriani nepotibus divi Traiani Parthici pronepotibus \n
EDCS-09701716.translation: Under Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus, chief priest, with tribunician power for the 16th time, consul for the 3rd time, and Emperor Caesar Lucius Aurelius Verus Augustus, chief priest, with tribunician power for the 2nd time, consul for the 2nd time, sons of the deified Antoninus Pius, grandsons of the deified Hadrian, great-grandsons of the deified Trajan Parthicus.
EDCS-09701716.summary: This is a formal preamble to an inscription, likely a dedication or honorary monument, dating to the joint reign of Marcus Aurelius and Lucius Verus, around 161-169 AD.

EDCS-09701717.translation: To Aesculapius from Epidaurus, for the health of Augustus, Gaius Fonteius Doryphorus, priest of the Great Mother of the Gods, Idaea, and Attis, gave this gift to Aesculapius from Epidaurus.
EDCS-09701717.summary: A priest of the Great Mother of the Gods and Attis dedicated a gift to Aesculapius from Epidaurus for the health of Emperor Augustus.

EDCS-09701718.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Felix Augusti pius vixit nnos XIII hic situs est\n
EDCS-09701718.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Felix, devoted to the Emperor, lived 13 years; here he lies.
EDCS-09701718.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a boy named Felix, who died at the age of 13, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-09701719.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Rustica Augusti serva pia vixit annis LX hic sita est\n
EDCS-09701719.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Rustica, a devoted slave of the Emperor, lived 60 years; here she lies.
EDCS-09701719.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Rustica, a slave of the emperor, who died at the age of 60, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-09701720.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Cnaeus Tannonius Ingenuus pius vixit nnis XVI mensibus III diebus XVIIII Gavia Sassa mater huius pia vixit nnis XLV mensibus VI hic siti sunt\n
EDCS-09701720.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Gnaeus Tannonius Ingenuus, devoted, lived 16 years, 3 months, and 19 days. Gavia Sassa, his devoted mother, lived 45 years and 6 months. Here they lie.
EDCS-09701720.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Gnaeus Tannonius Ingenuus and his mother Gavia Sassa, recording their ages at death, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-09701722.summary: This is a very brief epitaph for a stonecutter who died in peace.

EDCS-09701723.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the departed. Baerebgbal, son of Baricissus, the dutiful, lived 67 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-09701723.summary: An epitaph recording the death and burial of Baerebgbal, son of Baricissus, who lived 67 years.

EDCS-09701724.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the departed. To R. Baza, the dutiful.
EDCS-09701724.summary: A brief funerary inscription dedicated to R. Baza.

EDCS-09701726.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the departed. Iulius Felix, the dutiful, lived 30 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-09701726.summary: An epitaph recording the death and burial of Iulius Felix, who lived 30 years.

EDCS-09701727.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the departed. Marcus Iulius Rogatus Aelianus, the dutiful, lived 25 years.
EDCS-09701727.summary: An epitaph recording the death of Marcus Iulius Rogatus Aelianus, who lived 25 years.

EDCS-09701728.translation: Iulia, the dutiful, lived 72 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-09701728.summary: An epitaph recording the death and burial of Iulia, who lived 72 years.

EDCS-09701729.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the departed. Maxima lived 40 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-09701729.summary: An epitaph recording the death and burial of Maxima, who lived 40 years.

EDCS-09701730.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the departed. Of Marci Maximi Beregis, lived 66 years.
EDCS-09701730.summary: An epitaph recording the death of Marci Maximi Beregis, who lived 66 years.

EDCS-09701731.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the departed. Octavia Fortunata, freedwoman of Octavius Faustus Minunianus, the dutiful, lived 61 years.
EDCS-09701731.summary: An epitaph recording the death of Octavia Fortunata, a freedwoman, who lived 61 years.

EDCS-09701732.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Pescennius Victor Severianus, son of Caius, of the Papiria tribe, dutiful, lived 32 years and 11 months; he is buried here.
EDCS-09701732.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lucius Pescennius Victor Severianus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09701733.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Pinaria Octavina, daughter of Pinarius Fuscus, dutiful, lived 65 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-09701733.summary: A funerary epitaph for Pinaria Octavina, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09701734.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Potius POESOP
EDCS-09701734.summary: A fragmentary funerary epitaph, the meaning of which is unclear due to abbreviations or damage.

EDCS-09701735.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcus Ricius Saturus Primianus, son of Papiria, dutiful, lived 35 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-09701735.summary: A funerary epitaph for Marcus Ricius Saturus Primianus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09701736.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Rogata Donata, daughter of Publius, dutiful, lived 62 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-09701736.summary: A funerary epitaph for Rogata Donata, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09701738.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Saturninus lived 61 years and 8 months; he is buried here.
EDCS-09701738.summary: A funerary epitaph for Saturninus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09701739.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Septimius Faustinus lived 31 years and 8 months.
EDCS-09701739.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lucius Septimius Faustinus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09701741.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Statienia Secunda, dutiful, lived 85 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-09701741.summary: A funerary epitaph for Statienia Secunda, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09701742.translation: Son of IS lived 85 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-09701742.summary: A fragmentary funerary epitaph recording the lifespan and burial of an unnamed individual, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09701745.translation: Sacred to Aesculapius Augustus for the health of the Emperor Caesar Trajan Hadrianus Parthicus Augustus, father of the country. Gaius Julius Placidus, son of Marcus, of the Cornelia tribe, having promised 10,000 sesterces for the office of perpetual priest and an additional 2,000 sesterces for the office of II vir, adorned the temple with three statues, marble, and paintings; he also made for the adornment of the temple of Pluto a jug and a dish of 6 pounds of silver, and dedicated them by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-09701745.summary: A dedication by Gaius Julius Placidus to Aesculapius and Pluto, detailing his significant financial contributions for religious and civic offices, likely during the reign of Hadrian (AD 117-138).

EDCS-09701746.translation: Sacred to Apollo Augustus. Gaius Julius Placidus, son of Marcius, perpetual priest, made this with his own money.
EDCS-09701746.summary: A dedication to Apollo Augustus by Gaius Julius Placidus, a perpetual priest, funded by himself.

EDCS-09701748.translation: To the deified Hadrian Augustus, by decree of the council of decurions, with public money.
EDCS-09701748.summary: An inscription recording a monument or dedication to Hadrian Augustus, funded by public money and ordered by the local council.

EDCS-09701749.text_edition: \n Dis Mauris Castoribus Auggustis sacrum pro salute Imperatoris Caesaris Luci Septimi Severi Pii Pertinacis patris patriae et Imperatoris Caesaris Marci Aureli Antonini Pii Felicis et Publi Septimi Getae nobilissimi Caesaris Augggustorum et Iuliae Domnae et Fulviae Plautillae Auggustarum Publius Perellius Saturninus IIvir sua pecunia fecit et dedicavit\n
EDCS-09701749.translation: Sacred to the Divine Castores of the Emperors. For the health of the Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax, father of the country, and Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Felix, and Publius Septimius Geta, most noble Caesar, Augusti, and Julia Domna, and Fulvia Plautilla, Augustae. Publius Perellius Saturninus, as aedile, made and dedicated this at his own expense.
EDCS-09701749.summary: This is a dedication to the Divine Castores (Castor and Pollux), likely a public building or monument, by Publius Perellius Saturninus for the health of the Severan imperial family, dating to their reign (c. 198-205 AD).

EDCS-09701750.translation: Sacred to Mercury Augustus, for the welfare of the Emperor Caesar Marcus Opellius Severus Macrinus Pius Felix Augustus, father of the fatherland, and Marcus Opellius Antoninus Diadumenianus Caesar Augustus. Lucius Nonius Rogatianus Honoratianus, annual priest, aedile, twice chief magistrate, perpetual priest, having assessed the cost of the perpetual priesthood at 10,000 sesterces and having paid 5,000 sesterces into the treasury, dedicated the work which he had promised for public use, with augmented funds, with his wife Orfia Fortunata, daughter of Marcius, and his children Orfianus and Fortunatus, having provided a feast for the curiae.
EDCS-09701750.summary: A dedication to Mercury Augustus by Lucius Nonius Rogatianus Honoratianus, a local magistrate and priest, for the welfare of Emperors Macrinus and Diadumenianus, recording his financial contributions and a public feast, likely from the early 3rd century CE.

EDCS-09701751.translation: To the nurse of the gods. Marcus Ovius Maximus willingly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-09701751.summary: A votive offering to the 'nurse of the gods' by Marcus Ovius Maximus.

EDCS-09701752.translation: Sacred to the Pantheon Augustus, for the welfare of the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Severus Alexander Augustus and his entire divine family. The third fleet, from the Augusta curia, restored and adorned the temple, ruined by age, at their own expense, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-09701752.summary: A dedication to the Pantheon Augustus by the third fleet, who restored and adorned a temple at their own expense for the welfare of Emperor Alexander Severus, likely in the 3rd century CE.

EDCS-09701753.translation: Sacred to Pluto Augustus. Lucius Julius Florus, son of Lucius, twice chief magistrate, perpetual priest, made this with his own money.
EDCS-09701753.summary: A dedication to Pluto Augustus by Lucius Julius Florus, a local magistrate and priest, funded by himself.

EDCS-09701754.translation: Sacred to Pluto Frugifer Augustus, to the Genius of Mustis. For the welfare of the Emperor Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Augustus Pius. Marcus Cornelius Laetus, son of Marcius, perpetual priest, twice chief magistrate, public priest of Caelestis and Aesculapius, having assessed the cost for the perpetual priesthood at 10,000 sesterces and for the office of twice chief magistrate at 2,000 sesterces, and having paid 3,000 sesterces into the treasury, erected a bronze statue and made a portico of four columns in the temple of Caelestis with augmented funds, and also dedicated it by decree of the decurions; furthermore, in the same temple, he restored a paternal portico that had collapsed from age, with added funds.
EDCS-09701754.summary: A complex dedication to Pluto Frugifer Augustus and the Genius of Mustis by Marcus Cornelius Laetus, a prominent local official, for the welfare of Emperor Antoninus Pius, detailing his financial contributions towards a statue, a portico, and the restoration of another portico, likely in the mid-2nd century CE.

EDCS-09701755.translation: Sacred to Tellus Augusta, for the welfare of the Emperor Caesar Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Augustus Pius and his children. Marcus Cornelius Laetus, son of Marcius, perpetual priest, five-year chief magistrate, public priest of Caelestis and Aesculapius, built the temple with the statue at his own expense, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-09701755.summary: A dedication to Tellus Augusta by Marcus Cornelius Laetus, a local official, for the welfare of Emperor Antoninus Pius and his children, recording the construction of a temple and a statue at his own expense, likely in the mid-2nd century CE.

EDCS-09701756.translation: Sacred to Vesta Augusta. Publius Valerius Mucianus, son of Marcius of the Arnensi tribe, twice chief magistrate, perpetual priest, made this with his own money.
EDCS-09701756.summary: A dedication to Vesta Augusta by Publius Valerius Mucianus, a local magistrate and priest, funded by himself.

EDCS-09701758.translation: To the Emperor Caesar, son of the deified Nerva, Nerva Trajan Optimus Augustus, Germanicus, Dacicus, Parthicus, chief priest, with tribunician power for the 20th time, imperator for the 11th time, consul for the 6th time, father of his country. Marcus Valerius Fuscus, son of Marcus, of the Arnensis tribe, twice chief magistrate, because of the honor of the perpetual flamenship, spent ten million sesterces and built the middle portico, adding more of his own money; he also built in the Temple of Ceres and in the Temple of Dis porticoes and a shrine with his own money, and dedicated them by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-09701758.summary: This inscription records the construction and dedication of public buildings, including a portico and a shrine, by Marcus Valerius Fuscus, a local magistrate, at his own expense, honoring Emperor Trajan.

EDCS-09701760.translation: To our lord, the Emperor Caesar Flavius Julius Constantius, pious, fortunate, victorious, always Augustus. The municipium Iulium Aurelium Mustitanum, devoted to his divine majesty.
EDCS-09701760.summary: This inscription is a dedication by the municipium of Mustis to Emperor Constantius.

EDCS-09701761.translation: To our lord Theodosius, perpetual and always Augustus, propagator of the Roman Empire, vanquisher of barbarian peoples, founder of laws. Helvius Vindicianus, most distinguished and most eminent man, proconsul of the province of Africa, judging cases by special mandate, together with Gaius Felicius Torquatus, most distinguished man, legate of the province of Numidia, dedicating himself always to his divine majesty.
EDCS-09701761.summary: This inscription is a dedication by Helvius Vindicianus, proconsul of Africa, and Gaius Felicius Torquatus, legate of Numidia, to Emperor Theodosius.

EDCS-09701762.translation: Publius Iulius Respectus, son of Lucius, of the Cornelia tribe, a centurion, [built] a temple with porticoes and statues.
EDCS-09701762.summary: This inscription records the construction of a temple with porticoes and statues by Publius Iulius Respectus, a centurion.

EDCS-09701763.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus Orfius Florentinus, son of Caius, of the Lemonia tribe, dutiful, lived [X] years. He is buried here.
EDCS-09701763.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Quintus Orfius Florentinus, who lived an unspecified number of years and is buried here.

EDCS-09701764.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Caius Orfius Urbanianus, son of Marcus, of the Cornelia tribe, a soldier, a beneficiary of the III Augusta legion, dutiful, lived [X] years.
EDCS-09701764.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Caius Orfius Urbanianus, a soldier of the III Augusta legion, who lived an unspecified number of years.

EDCS-09701767.translation: Bivis, in peace, lived for forty years.
EDCS-09701767.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Bivis, who lived for forty years and is recorded as being in peace.

EDCS-09701768.text_edition: \n En perfecta cito baiarum grata voluptas undantesque fluunt aquae saxi de rupe sub ima nisibus hic nostris prostratus libor sic anhelat quisquis amat fratrum veniat mecumque laetetur\n
EDCS-09701768.translation: Here, pleasure, welcome and abundant, flows from the rocks, springing forth. Whoever loves his brothers, let him come and rejoice with me.
EDCS-09701768.summary: This is a short, possibly poetic, inscription likely associated with a public bath or pleasure resort, possibly at Baiae, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09701769.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Papius Rogatianus, dutiful, lived 26 years. He is buried here. Fagargi made [this] for their dearest comrade.
EDCS-09701769.summary: This tombstone inscription records that Papius Rogatianus, aged 26, is buried here and was commemorated by his colleagues.

EDCS-09701770.translation: Sacred to Saturn, Augustus. Caius Iulius Sarninus paid his vows to the great god Saturn on a good, solemn day.
EDCS-09701770.summary: This inscription records Caius Iulius Sarninus fulfilling a vow to the god Saturn.

EDCS-09701771.translation: Iunianus and Flavius Felicio made a vow to the Great God.
EDCS-09701771.summary: This inscription records a vow made by Iunianus and Flavius Felicio to a deity referred to as the Great God.

EDCS-09701772.translation: Iunius Primus, the priest, fulfilled his vows to Saturnus Augustus on a good, solemn day.
EDCS-09701772.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by Iunius Primus, a priest, to the god Saturnus Augustus.

EDCS-09701773.translation: Sacred to Saturnus Augustus; Massius Victor, his son, fulfilled his vows willingly.
EDCS-09701773.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled willingly by Massius Victor to the god Saturnus Augustus.

EDCS-09701774.translation: Sacred to Saturnus Augustus; Victoriolus Cricinus fulfilled his vows on a good, solemn day.
EDCS-09701774.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled on a solemn day by Victoriolus Cricinus to the god Saturnus Augustus.

EDCS-09701776.summary: This very brief inscription simply records the death of Neoterius.

EDCS-09701777.text_edition: \n Diorus Treboni spectavit Kalendis Decembribus Caio Furnio Caio Silano\n
EDCS-09701777.translation: Diorus, son of Trebonius, watched on the Kalends of December, in the consulship of Gaius Furnius and Gaius Silanus.
EDCS-09701777.summary: This is a record of a date or an event witnessed by Diorus, linked to a specific consular pair, Gaius Furnius and Gaius Silanus, likely dating to their consulship in 45 BC.

EDCS-09701778.translation: Annibonia, Concisus, Laurentius, Piquarius, Felix, Cobbo, Salvius: I ask you from this day forward to be mute and crippled, Dammameneus.
EDCS-09701778.summary: This curse inscription, uttered by Dammameneus, invokes various individuals to inflict muteness and crippling upon others.

EDCS-09701779.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Marcus Caelius Saturninus pius vixit annis XVIIII hic situs\n
EDCS-09701779.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Marcus Caelius Saturninus, devoted, lived 19 years; here he lies.
EDCS-09701779.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcus Caelius Saturninus, who died at the age of 19, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-09701780.summary: This very fragmentary inscription appears to name Fortunatus and suggests a low position or origin.

EDCS-09701781.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades; Lucius Licinius lived 20 years; his father Faustus made this.
EDCS-09701781.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Lucius Licinius at age 20, with the monument erected by his father Faustus.

EDCS-09701782.text_edition: \n Marcus Seius Ianuarius vixit nnos V Seius Ianuariusmia Fortunata filio piissimo\n
EDCS-09701782.translation: Marcus Seius Ianuarius lived 5 years. To their most devoted son, Seius Ianuarius and Fortunata.
EDCS-09701782.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a young boy named Marcus Seius Ianuarius, dedicated by his parents, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-09701783.text_edition: \n Diis Manibus sacrum Publius Sextilius Libycus hic situs vixit pius nnos V\n
EDCS-09701783.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Publius Sextilius Libycus, here he lies, lived 5 devoted years.
EDCS-09701783.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Publius Sextilius Libycus, who died at the age of 5, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-09701784.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Publius Minucius Saturninus vixit nnos L hic situs est\n
EDCS-09701784.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Publius Minucius Saturninus lived 50 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-09701784.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death and burial of Publius Minucius Saturninus, dated to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-09701785.summary: This fragmentary inscription mentions Aemilia and her mother, but the context is incomplete.

EDCS-09701787.text_edition: \n Iussu Csacrum Imperatoris Caesaris Luci Septimi Severi Invicti Pii Pertinacis Augusti Arabici Adiabenici Parthici maximi tribunicia potestate VIII imperatoris XII consulis II patris patriae decreto decurionum pecunia publica\n
EDCS-09701787.translation: By order of the Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Invictus Pius Pertinax Augustus Arabicus Adiabenicus Parthicus Maximus, in his eighth tribunician power, twelfth acclamation as Imperator, second consulship, father of the fatherland, by decree of the decurions, at public expense.
EDCS-09701787.summary: A monumental inscription detailing the titles and honors of Emperor Septimius Severus, likely commemorating a public work funded by the state, dated to his imperial reign.

EDCS-09701788.translation: Marcus Aemilius Rusticus Magonianus, to the good, for the good.
EDCS-09701788.summary: This inscription names Marcus Aemilius Rusticus Magonianus and includes a vague dedication or statement of purpose.

EDCS-09701789.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades; Lucius Labinius Maximus lived 40 years, here he lies. Valeria Felicitas, his sister, made this with Labinius Maximus.
EDCS-09701789.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Lucius Labinius Maximus at age 40 and was erected by his sister Valeria Felicitas and presumably her husband, also named Labinius Maximus.

EDCS-09701791.translation: Amantzia, faithful, lived in peace for seven years. She was laid to rest on the 17th day before the Kalends of August.
EDCS-09701791.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the life and burial of Amantzia.

EDCS-09701792.translation: Faustinus, who was the only son of his widowed mother, lived for eight years. He rested in peace on the 12th day before the Kalends of September, in the 8th indiction.
EDCS-09701792.summary: This funerary inscription commemorates Faustinus, noting his age and burial date.

EDCS-09701794.translation: Paulus, a cleric, lived for eighteen years in peace. He was laid to rest on the 11th day before the Kalends of November, in the seventh indiction.
EDCS-09701794.summary: This inscription records the burial of Paulus, a cleric, and specifies his age and burial date.

EDCS-09701795.translation: Victorinus, bishop of the Vandals, in peace.
EDCS-09701795.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription mentioning Victorinus, a bishop, possibly during the Vandal period.

EDCS-09701796.translation: Victorinus, a cleric, rested in peace.
EDCS-09701796.summary: This brief inscription records the peaceful rest of a cleric named Victorinus.

EDCS-09701797.translation: Fortunius, a subdeacon, lived for twenty-four years. He was laid to rest on the fourth day before the Ides of November.
EDCS-09701797.summary: This funerary inscription details the age and burial date of Fortunius, a subdeacon.

EDCS-09701798.translation: Bellator, also known as Mustelus, the master.
EDCS-09701798.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription identifying a person named Bellator, also known as Mustelus, with the title of "master".

EDCS-09701811.translation: Hildiger was laid to rest here in peace.
EDCS-09701811.summary: This is a simple funerary inscription announcing the burial of Hildiger.

EDCS-09701815.translation: Here lies Asteria, wife of Eugenius, daughter of Tecles, and Asterius.
EDCS-09701815.summary: This inscription records the burial of Asteria, wife of Eugenius and daughter of Tecles, and also mentions Asterius.

EDCS-09701823.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely indicating ownership or dedication by Publius Cornelius Notus.

EDCS-09800351.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari Marco Aurelio Antonino Augusto Armeniaco Medico Parthico Germanico pontifici maximo tribunicia potestate XXVIII imperatori consuli patri patriae arcus ex HS CXX milibus nummum ab Avilio Casto in eum et statuas legatis praeter HS quae de publico adiecta sunt dedicatus Caio Septimio Severo proconsule Lucio Septimio Severo legato pro praetore\n
EDCS-09800351.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus Armeniacus Medicus Parthicus Germanicus, Pontifex Maximus, in his twenty-eighth tribunician power, Emperor, Consul, Father of the Fatherland. An arch, at a cost of 120,000 sesterces from Avilius Castus, in addition to the statues of the legates and the funds added from public money, was dedicated while Gaius Septimius Severus was proconsul and Lucius Septimius Severus was legate pro praetore.
EDCS-09800351.summary: An inscription commemorating the dedication of an arch and statues to Emperor Caracalla, funded by Avilius Castus and public money, with extensive consular and legatine officials named, likely dated to the reign of Caracalla (early 3rd century AD).

EDCS-09800352.text_edition: \n Caio Fulvio Plautiano praefecto praetorio clarissimo viro comiti et necessario dominorum nostrorum Imperatorum Auggustorum Marcus Calpurnius Geta Attianus et Marcus Calpurnius Attianus filius numini devotissimi posuerunt\n
EDCS-09800352.translation: Marcus Calpurnius Geta Attianus and his son Marcus Calpurnius Attianus, most devoted to the divine will, erected [this monument] to Gaius Fulvius Plautianus, praetorian prefect, a most distinguished man, companion and confidant of our lords the Emperors Augusti.
EDCS-09800352.summary: A dedication by Marcus Calpurnius Geta Attianus and his son to Gaius Fulvius Plautianus, a prominent figure and praetorian prefect, likely from the early 3rd century AD.

EDCS-09800353.text_edition: \n Opus doliare ex praediis Lucillae Veri Severo et Sabiniano consulibus\n
EDCS-09800353.translation: Pottery works from the estates of Lucilla, under the consulship of Severus and Sabinianus.
EDCS-09800353.summary: A record of pottery production from the estates of Lucilla, dated by the consulship of Severus and Sabinianus (likely 206 AD).

EDCS-09800354.text_edition: \n Ex praediis Domitiae Lucillae opus doliare Fortunati Lucillae\n
EDCS-09800354.translation: Pottery works from the estates of Domitia Lucilla, belonging to Fortunatus and Lucilla.
EDCS-09800354.summary: An inscription indicating pottery production from the estates of Domitia Lucilla, possibly for her ownership or management, dated to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-09800355.text_edition: \n Opus doliare ex praediis Lucillae Veri Quinti Flavi Apri\n
EDCS-09800355.translation: Pottery works from the estates of Lucilla, belonging to Quintus Flavius Aper.
EDCS-09800355.summary: An inscription documenting pottery production from the estates of Lucilla, associated with Quintus Flavius Aper, dated to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-09800356.text_edition: \n Barbaro et Regulo consulibus ex officina Faviana Flavi Apri opus doliare Fadi Euhelpisti\n
EDCS-09800356.translation: Pottery works from the workshop of Flavius Aper, belonging to Fadius Euhelpistus, under the consulship of Barbarus and Regulus.
EDCS-09800356.summary: An inscription recording pottery production from the workshop of Flavius Aper, attributed to Fadius Euhelpistus, dated by the consulship of Barbarus and Regulus (likely 241 AD).

EDCS-09800357.text_edition: \n Opus doliare ex praediis Caesaris nostri Claudi Secundini\n
EDCS-09800357.translation: Pottery works from the estates of our Caesar Claudius Secundinus.
EDCS-09800357.summary: An inscription indicating pottery production from the estates of Claudius Secundinus, who held the title of Caesar, dated to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-09800358.text_edition: \n Opus doliare ex praediis Aureli Caesaris et Faustinae Augustae Mai servi\n
EDCS-09800358.translation: Pottery works from the estates of Aurelius Caesar and Faustina Augusta Maius Servus.
EDCS-09800358.summary: An inscription detailing pottery production from estates belonging to individuals named Aurelius Caesar and Faustina Augusta Maius Servus, dated to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-09800360.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Marius Ianuarius miles legionis III Augustae vixit annis XXXX\n
EDCS-09800360.translation: Dedicated to the spirits of the departed. Marius Ianuarius, a soldier of the Third Augustan Legion, lived for 40 years.
EDCS-09800360.summary: This is a tombstone for Marius Ianuarius, a soldier of the Third Augustan Legion, who died at the age of 40.

EDCS-09800361.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Iulius Rogatianus filius Rogatiani cornicinis vixit annos XVI menses II dies mo\n
EDCS-09800361.translation: Dedicated to the spirits of the departed. Iulius Rogatianus, son of Rogatianus the cornicen (horn blower), lived for 16 years, 2 months, and some days.
EDCS-09800361.summary: This is a tombstone for Iulius Rogatianus, son of a cornicen, who died at the age of 16.

EDCS-09800362.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Claudius Maxime miles legionis III Augustae stupendiorum sic viginti dua vixit annos XXXX pater ANA fecit\n
EDCS-09800362.translation: Dedicated to the spirits of the departed. Claudius Maxime, a soldier of the Third Augustan Legion, a stupendior (rank/description) of 22, lived for 40 years. His father ANA made this.
EDCS-09800362.summary: This is a tombstone for Claudius Maxime, a soldier of the Third Augustan Legion, erected by his father, dating to his life at age 40.

EDCS-09800363.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Grania Hospita vixit annos XXI hic sita est\n
EDCS-09800363.translation: Dedicated to the spirits of the departed. Grania Hospita lived for 21 years; she lies here.
EDCS-09800363.summary: This is a tombstone for Grania Hospita, who died at the age of 21.

EDCS-09800366.translation: Sextus Classicius Secundinus, procurator of the emperor, restored and dedicated this title, which had been corrupted by age, in the form of the old title and letters. With the city walls razed and smoothed everywhere, as if ruling a rebellious empire, he obtained this throne. Yours, Scipio, yours.
EDCS-09800366.summary: This inscription records the restoration and dedication of a public title by Sextus Classicius Secundinus, a procurator, likely in the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-09800367.translation: Spittaria, Bullarius, Hilarinus, Mamertinus, Victor, Crispinus, Romanus, Luxurius. Through the elected official, may those of my lord receive the reward for the leopard; may your favour donate five hundred denarii to them. Magerius, Magerius. It was acclaimed: by your example, let them learn the gift thus; let future generations hear from what and when. By the example of the quaestors, a gift from your treasury, a gift from your possessions, this day Magerius gives. This is to have, this is to be able, this is now night. Now by your gift, in sacks sent.
EDCS-09800367.summary: This inscription appears to be a record of a public acclamation and distribution of funds, possibly related to games or a spectacle, involving several individuals and a figure named Magerius, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-09800368.summary: This inscription records that the Honoratianii group erected this monument, likely in the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-09800369.summary: This inscription records that the Victorinianii group erected this monument, likely in the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-09800370.summary: This inscription records that the Venerii group erected this monument, likely in the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-09800371.summary: This inscription records that the Venerii group erected this monument, likely in the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-09800372.summary: This inscription records that the Ambivulianii group erected this monument, likely in the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-09800374.summary: This short inscription is a prosperity message for the city of Theveste, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-09800375.summary: This inscription is a loyalty oath or a prayer for the safety of the emperors, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-09800467.inscription_type: inscriptiones christianae, tituli operum, tituli sepulcrales
EDCS-09800467.text_edition: \n Baeatissimorum martyrum speranti EV R DATVA corpora qui A TA saeculi nequitia corona immarcescibile consecuti sunt via Christo regnare hic interim quiescerA scribtura sic declarat fortis Hinna Faustula et Gaudiosa fratres sic fecerunt\n
EDCS-09800467.translation: The bodies of the most blessed martyrs, who, by Christ's grace, attained the unfading crown, left behind by the wickedness of this age, rest here, awaiting reign with Christ; the inscription declares this: Fortis, Hinna, Faustula, and Gaudiosa, siblings, made this.
EDCS-09800467.summary: This is a funerary inscription for martyrs, commemorating their heavenly reward and noting that the tomb was built by siblings.

EDCS-10300002.summary: This inscription is a simple dedication or naming of a monument by Marcus Ulpius Basilius Cerialis, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-10300003.translation: Gaius Claudius Paulus, son of Gaius, of the Collina tribe, honored with the status of veteran, made this for himself.
EDCS-10300003.summary: A funerary monument set up by a veteran for himself.

EDCS-10300007.translation: Lucius Tettius Eutychus donated a cistern to Venus and the people of Leptis with his own money, and had it made under the supervision of Lucius Tettius Comis, his freedman.
EDCS-10300007.summary: A public works project, a cistern donated by a private citizen to Venus and the city of Leptis.

EDCS-10300008.translation: Aemilius Emeritus dedicated an altar to Jupiter Optimus Maximus.
EDCS-10300008.summary: A private dedication of an altar to Jupiter Optimus Maximus.

EDCS-10300009.translation: For the safety of our Emperors, Lucius Septimius Severus Pertinax and Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus, and Lucius Septimius Geta Caesar, Quintus Anicius Faustus, consul-designate, ordered a guard post to be established, under the supervision of Aemilius emeritus, a decurion of the ala, commander of the II Cohort of Flavians of the Africans, and the attached unit.
EDCS-10300009.summary: A military order for the establishment of a guard post, likely issued during the reign of Septimius Severus and Caracalla.

EDCS-10300010.translation: To the departed spirits, Lucius Tarquitius Pudens, devoted, made this monument for himself.
EDCS-10300010.summary: A funerary monument set up by Lucius Tarquitius Pudens for himself.

EDCS-10300012.summary: A simple funerary dedication to the departed spirits.

EDCS-10300013.summary: A funerary inscription with only a name.

EDCS-10300019.translation: To Memmius Cai filius Quirina Messius Pacatus, perpetual priest and holder of all honors in his homeland, an excellent patron, from the fullers of his household.
EDCS-10300019.summary: A funerary monument dedicated by fullers to their deceased patron, Memmius Cai filius Quirina Messius Pacatus.

EDCS-10300020.translation: To Servaeus, son of Quirina, Honoratus, perpetual priest.
EDCS-10300020.summary: A funerary inscription for Servaeus Honoratus, a perpetual priest.

EDCS-10300024.summary: A funerary inscription with only a name, possibly a woman's name.

EDCS-10300026.translation: A sacred offering to Minerva Augusta for the safety of our lords, the Emperors Lucius Septimius Severus and Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Geta, 'Britannicus Parthicus Germanicus Maximus' Augusti, and Julia Augusta, mother of the emperors and of the camps. Julius Zeno, an optio of the III Augusta Legion, erected this altar to his native goddess, fulfilling his vow willingly from a vision.
EDCS-10300026.summary: This inscription records an altar dedicated to Minerva Augusta by Julius Zeno, an optio of the III Augusta Legion, for the safety of the emperors and their family, likely dating to the Severan period.

EDCS-10300029.translation: Fabius M., S., S. and his heirs made and dedicated all these things happily to his wife, S.A.
EDCS-10300029.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a funerary monument by Fabius and his heirs to his wife S.A., likely from a Roman period.

EDCS-10300030.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Quintus Licinius Honoratus Fabricianus lived 18 years, 1 month, 2 days.
EDCS-10300030.summary: This inscription is a tombstone recording the age of Quintus Licinius Honoratus Fabricianus, who died young.

EDCS-10300031.summary: This inscription is likely a tombstone or dedicatory text identifying Lucius Arruntius Suriacus.

EDCS-10300033.translation: Rare such a holy wife. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Iulia Victoria lived thirty years. Passersby, learn what human life is.
EDCS-10300033.summary: This inscription is a tombstone for Iulia Victoria, who died at age 30, with a philosophical reflection on the brevity of life.

EDCS-10300034.translation: In memory of Abedeunis, who lived for seven years.
EDCS-10300034.summary: This is a tombstone recording the death of Abedeunis at the age of seven.

EDCS-10300036.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Aelia Datiba lived 47 years.
EDCS-10300036.summary: This inscription is a tombstone recording the age of Aelia Datiba, who died at age 47.

EDCS-10300037.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Publius Aelius Chrusanthus lived 35 years, 11 months. He made this for his well-deserving wife.
EDCS-10300037.summary: This inscription is a tombstone for Publius Aelius Chrusanthus, who made it for his wife and records his own age at death as 35 years and 11 months.

EDCS-10300038.summary: This inscription is likely a tombstone or dedicatory text identifying Aemilia Paulina.

EDCS-10300041.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Marcus Aemilius Exoratus lived 46 years.
EDCS-10300041.summary: This inscription is a tombstone recording the age of Marcus Aemilius Exoratus, who died at age 46.

EDCS-10300042.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Caius Aemilius Ingenus lived 47 years.
EDCS-10300042.summary: This inscription is a tombstone recording the age of Caius Aemilius Ingenus, who died at age 47.

EDCS-10300043.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Amianthus lived 20 years.
EDCS-10300043.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Amianthus.

EDCS-10300044.translation: To the departed spirits. Lucius Antonius Candidus Exoratianus lived 42 years.
EDCS-10300044.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Lucius Antonius Candidus Exoratianus.

EDCS-10300047.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcus Aurelius Gemellus lived 23 years.
EDCS-10300047.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Marcus Aurelius Gemellus.

EDCS-10300050.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Biator lived 3 years.
EDCS-10300050.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Biator.

EDCS-10300051.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Lived 30 years. Bradua.
EDCS-10300051.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Bradua.

EDCS-10300053.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcus Calpurnius Hipnus lived 80 years.
EDCS-10300053.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Marcus Calpurnius Hipnus.

EDCS-10300054.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcus Calpurnius Victor made this for Datiba, his wife.
EDCS-10300054.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by Marcus Calpurnius Victor for his wife, Datiba.

EDCS-10300055.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Cassius Faustus lived 20 years.
EDCS-10300055.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Cassius Faustus.

EDCS-10300056.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcus Cervius Saturninus lived 35 years.
EDCS-10300056.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Marcus Cervius Saturninus.

EDCS-10300057.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Cerula Ursacia lived 5 years.
EDCS-10300057.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Cerula Ursacia.

EDCS-10300059.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Cornelia Matrona lived 80 years.
EDCS-10300059.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Cornelia Matrona after 80 years of life.

EDCS-10300062.summary: A funerary epitaph consisting solely of a personal name, likely Domitius Florus.

EDCS-10300065.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Gentia Gratilla lived 32 years.
EDCS-10300065.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Gentia Gratilla after 32 years of life.

EDCS-10300068.summary: A funerary epitaph consisting solely of a personal name, likely Lucius Hortensius Protus.

EDCS-10300070.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Iulia Apollonia lived 35 years. Her husband set this up.
EDCS-10300070.summary: A funerary epitaph by a husband for his wife, Iulia Apollonia, who lived 35 years.

EDCS-10300071.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Iulia Fautina lived one year, eleven months, and twenty-five days.
EDCS-10300071.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of the infant Iulia Fautina.

EDCS-10300073.summary: An inscription identifying Iulia Rufina as a priestess of Ceres.

EDCS-10300074.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Quintus Iulius Adiutor rests here. He lived 22 years, 8 months, and 18 days.
EDCS-10300074.summary: A funerary epitaph for Quintus Iulius Adiutor, who lived 22 years, 8 months, and 18 days.

EDCS-10300077.summary: A funerary epitaph consisting solely of a personal name, likely Titus Iulius Paulinus.

EDCS-10300078.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Marcus Iulius Saturninus lived 34 years and 4 months.
EDCS-10300078.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Marcus Iulius Saturninus after 34 years and 4 months of life.

EDCS-10300083.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Licinius Victorinus lived 22 years.
EDCS-10300083.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespan of Licinius Victorinus.

EDCS-10300090.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Plutia Marcella lived 40 years.
EDCS-10300090.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespan of Plutia Marcella.

EDCS-10300094.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Gnaeus Pontius Paulinus Munatianus lived 37 years, 11 months, and 15 days.
EDCS-10300094.summary: This funerary inscription records the detailed lifespan of Gnaeus Pontius Paulinus Munatianus.

EDCS-10300103.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Sposa.
EDCS-10300103.summary: This funerary inscription is a dedication to the departed spirits for Sposa.

EDCS-10300106.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Titas lived 85 years, 3 months, and 7 days.
EDCS-10300106.summary: This funerary inscription records the detailed lifespan of Titas.

EDCS-10300107.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Valeria Pudentilla lived one year.
EDCS-10300107.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespan of Valeria Pudentilla.

EDCS-10300114.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Vernacla lived 22 years.
EDCS-10300114.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespan of Vernacla.

EDCS-10300115.summary: This inscription likely records the name of an individual, Vesolena Felicitas.

EDCS-10300118.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Ziligura lived 25 years.
EDCS-10300118.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespan of Ziligura.

EDCS-10300119.translation: Titus Apronius Telamoenus, a rope-maker from Massilia.
EDCS-10300119.summary: This inscription identifies Titus Apronius Telamoenus by his trade and origin.

EDCS-10300120.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Felix, son of Gallus.

EDCS-10300123.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lusius Cerialis.

EDCS-10300126.translation: Publius Magnius Paulinus gladly and with a willing spirit paid his vow to Caelestius.
EDCS-10300126.summary: This inscription records a votive offering paid by Publius Magnius Paulinus to the deity Caelestius.

EDCS-10300133.translation: For Vitillia Procula, daughter of Lucius, wife of Cnaeus Laetus, grandmother of Sextus Pontilius Vindicus, by the aedile and the four men.
EDCS-10300133.summary: This is a funerary epitaph honoring Vitillia Procula, wife of Cnaeus Laetus and grandmother of Sextus Pontilius Vindicus, likely erected by local officials.

EDCS-10300134.translation: Dedicated and consecrated to Saturn Augustus, and it was given by [---] M.
EDCS-10300134.summary: This inscription records a sacred dedication to Saturn Augustus.

EDCS-10300137.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Lucius Vectimarius, son of Lucius, of the Voltinian tribe, from Reis. Gratus, dutiful, lived 29 years, served 10 years. Vectimarius Frontinnus arranged for this to be made for his most dutiful brother; he lies here.
EDCS-10300137.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Vectimarius, a soldier, who lived 29 years and served 10 years, erected by his brother.

EDCS-10300138.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Quintus Valerius Hostilianus, son of Quintus, of the Galerian tribe, a soldier of the 1st Urban Cohort, dutiful, lived 30 years, served 11 years. His heir arranged for this to be made; he lies here.
EDCS-10300138.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Quintus Valerius Hostilianus, a soldier in the 1st Urban Cohort, who lived 30 years and served 11 years, erected by his heir.

EDCS-10300139.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. For Felicitas, servant of our Augusti. [She] lived 30 years. Faustus, her husband, made [this]; she lies here.
EDCS-10300139.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Felicitas, a servant of the emperors, who lived 30 years, erected by her husband Faustus.

EDCS-10300140.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Philinus, servant of our Caesar, lived 35 years; he lies here. Macrina, his wife, made [this] for her most dutiful husband.
EDCS-10300140.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Philinus, a servant of the emperor, who lived 35 years, erected by his wife Macrina.

EDCS-10300141.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Flavius Crescens.

EDCS-10300142.summary: This inscription records the name of Marcus Herennius Fortunatus.

EDCS-10300143.summary: This inscription records the name of Marcus Messallinus Aliquas.

EDCS-10300145.translation: undus, perpetual priest, further from his own resources.
EDCS-10300145.summary: This inscription mentions undus, a perpetual priest, contributing from his own funds, likely related to a religious dedication or office.

EDCS-10300146.text_edition: \n Quinto Caelio Maximo aedili auguri IIviro quod in magg(istrato) suo ludorum et circensium spectacula exhibuerit munus etiam gladiatorium de suo ediderit et hoc amplius in praesentis tempore HS MMMMMMMMMMMundecim milia rei publicae donaverit ex cuius summae usuris quinssto sic quoque anno semper universis \n
EDCS-10300146.translation: To Quintus Caelius Maximus, aedile, augur, and duovir, for exhibiting games and circus spectacles during his magistracy, for also presenting a gladiatorial munus at his own expense, and furthermore for donating 11,100,000 sesterces to the Republic in the present time, from the interest of which sum each year, forever, to all [the expenses are to be paid].
EDCS-10300146.summary: This is a public inscription honoring Quintus Caelius Maximus for his generosity as aedile and duovir, particularly for funding games, gladiatorial contests, and a significant donation to the state.

EDCS-10300148.translation: Istricatus, a shipowner, lived 35 years and 3 months.
EDCS-10300148.summary: This inscription records the death of Istricatus, a shipowner, who lived 35 years and 3 months.

EDCS-10300149.translation: To Quintus Papius Saturninus Iulianus, son of Quintus, centurion of the II Parthica legion; he lived 60 years. Papia Victoria, his most devoted sister, made this for her brother.
EDCS-10300149.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Quintus Papius Saturninus Iulianus, a centurion, dedicated by his sister Papia Victoria.

EDCS-10300150.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Pulesius, a cloth merchant.
EDCS-10300150.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Pulesius, a cloth merchant, dedicated to the spirits of the dead.

EDCS-10300152.summary: This inscription records the name and age (51) of Processus Vernaclus.

EDCS-10300153.summary: This inscription records the names Pupillus Amator, Cupido, and Aura.

EDCS-10300154.summary: This inscription records the name Aelius Saturninus, with his cognomen Calvus.

EDCS-10300156.summary: This inscription records the names of Aemilia Flora and Trebius Florentinus, likely a dedication or a tombstone.

EDCS-10300158.summary: This is a personal name, likely from a funerary monument or a simple epitaph.

EDCS-10300159.translation: Lucius Erennius Maximus, the oxherd, lived 30 years.
EDCS-10300159.summary: This funerary inscription records the name and age of Lucius Erennius Maximus, identified by his occupation as an oxherd.

EDCS-10300161.translation: For Flavia Faenu, an incomparable woman, for her many distinguished merits towards me, Caus made this for his sweetest wife.
EDCS-10300161.summary: This is a funerary dedication from Caus to his wife Flavia Faenu, praising her virtues and merits.

EDCS-10300163.summary: This is a personal name, likely from a funerary monument or a simple epitaph.

EDCS-10300166.summary: This is a personal name, likely from a funerary monument or a simple epitaph.

EDCS-10300167.summary: This is a personal name, likely from a funerary monument or a simple epitaph.

EDCS-10300170.summary: This is a personal name, likely from a funerary monument or a simple epitaph.

EDCS-10300172.translation: Tertia, daughter of Ammicaris and Botonis, lived [for...]
EDCS-10300172.summary: This is a fragmentary tombstone for Tertia, daughter of Ammicaris and Botonis, recording her lifespan.

EDCS-10300173.translation: Publius Veius Celer, son of Publius, of the Arnensian tribe, lies here; he lived for 32 years.
EDCS-10300173.summary: This is a tombstone for Publius Veius Celer, son of Publius, who died at the age of 32.

EDCS-10300175.translation: To our most indulgent lord, Flavius Claudius Constantinus, Pious, Fortunate, Augustus, born for the good of the state.
EDCS-10300175.summary: This is an honorific inscription dedicating something to Emperor Constantine I, praising his virtues and role in the state.

EDCS-10300176.translation: Heraclius made this to God Liber with his own money.
EDCS-10300176.summary: This is a votive inscription indicating that Heraclius dedicated a monument to the god Liber at his own expense.

EDCS-10300181.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Aelia Saturnina lived 2 years and months. For her most beloved daughter, Caelia Bocontia.
EDCS-10300181.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicating a grave to Caelia Bocontia by her mother Aelia Saturnina, recording the daughter's lifespan.

EDCS-10300182.summary: This is a personal name, likely from a funerary monument or a simple epitaph.

EDCS-10300183.summary: This inscription is a fragmented personal name, likely of a woman named Lollia Baricbalis, with her filiation possibly indicated.

EDCS-10300184.summary: This inscription records the name of a man, Marcus Lollius Iononus, possibly for funerary or commemorative purposes.

EDCS-10300185.summary: This inscription records the name of a woman, Vilia Saturnina, likely for funerary or commemorative purposes.

EDCS-10300186.summary: This inscription records the filiation of an individual, indicating he is the son of Avitus Saturninus, likely for funerary or commemorative purposes.

EDCS-10300187.summary: This inscription records the name of a man, Publius Valerius Pegassius, likely for funerary or commemorative purposes.

EDCS-10300188.summary: This inscription records the name of a woman, Geminia Luciska, likely for funerary or commemorative purposes.

EDCS-10300189.summary: This inscription records the name of a man, Caius Geminius Rufus, likely for funerary or commemorative purposes.

EDCS-10300190.translation: Titus Volusinus Pollius, son of Rufimus
EDCS-10300190.summary: This inscription records the name and filiation of a man, Titus Volusinus Pollius, son of Rufimus, likely for funerary or commemorative purposes.

EDCS-10300192.translation: to the grandson of the deified Hadrian, to the great-grandson of the deified Trajan the Parthian, to the great-great-grandson of the deified Nerva, in the year of the proconsul Sergius Cornelius Scipio Salvidienus Orfitus
EDCS-10300192.summary: This inscription is a dedicatory formula referencing multiple emperors and a specific proconsular year, likely part of a larger monument or honorific inscription from the 2nd century AD.

EDCS-10300195.translation: Vaianae Saturninus the priest performed the sacred rite
EDCS-10300195.summary: This inscription records a religious act performed by Vaianae Saturninus, identified as a priest, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-10300196.translation: By the providence of the gods, with the Molphonii family safe and well.
EDCS-10300196.summary: This inscription records a thanksgiving for the safety of the Molphonii family, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-10300197.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Aviania Rogata lived 38 years.
EDCS-10300197.summary: This is a tomb inscription recording the death of Aviania Rogata at the age of 38.

EDCS-10300198.translation: Quintus C. P. fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-10300198.summary: This inscription records the fulfillment of a vow by Quintus C. P.

EDCS-10300199.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits for Bubali Victorina, and for the tomb and its burdens. Appius, husband and father, ordered this in memory of her, who was snatched away by uterine illness.
EDCS-10300199.summary: This funerary inscription honors Bubali Victorina and was commissioned by her husband and father.

EDCS-10300204.translation: To Aurelius Aristobulus, a man of the highest distinction, proconsul, who discovered and dedicated this monument, [to a man] of incomparable [virtue] and [unparalleled] spirit.
EDCS-10300204.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription from a public monument dedicated to the proconsul Aurelius Aristobulus, likely dating to the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-10300205.translation: Silvana, who was also called Sura.
EDCS-10300205.summary: This inscription simply provides the name of a person, Silvana, also known as Sura.

EDCS-10300206.translation: Sacred to Iuno for Plarilia, daughter of Crepereius Publius. Lucius Flavius Pietas Iulianus Caelius Saturninus Fuscianus [dedicated this] to his most rare and most modest wife.
EDCS-10300206.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the goddess Iuno, made by Lucius Flavius Pietas Iulianus Caelius Saturninus Fuscianus for his wife, Plarilia.

EDCS-10300208.translation: Lucius Pomponius Secundus willingly paid his vow.
EDCS-10300208.summary: This is a votive inscription recording Lucius Pomponius Secundus fulfilling a vow, likely from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-10300211.summary: This inscription simply records the name of a Roman man, Lucius Antonius Extricatus.

EDCS-10300212.summary: This inscription simply records the name of a Roman man, Lucius Volussienius Zella.

EDCS-10300214.summary: This inscription simply records the name of a Roman man, Marcus Iulius Saturninus.

EDCS-10300216.summary: This inscription simply records the name of a Roman man, Publius Aelius Rusticus.

EDCS-10300217.summary: This inscription records the name of Salustia Urbana.

EDCS-10300218.translation: Marcus Cerialis Felix, son of Mevi, among the gods.
EDCS-10300218.summary: This inscription records the deification of Marcus Cerialis Felix.

EDCS-10300219.translation: Publius F. Fronto, Extricatus, and F. Paulina fulfilled their vow willingly.
EDCS-10300219.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by Publius F. Fronto, Extricatus, and F. Paulina.

EDCS-10300221.summary: This inscription records the name of Flavius Datulus.

EDCS-10300222.summary: This inscription records the name of Titus Flavius Saturninus.

EDCS-10300224.summary: This inscription records the name of Iulia Saturnina.

EDCS-10300226.summary: This inscription records the name of Postumia Fortunata.

EDCS-10300227.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Iutinus lived 58 years, 5 months. Festus, to his incomparable and most rare brother, Auspicius, and Lucustius, and Festiva, and Faustina, his left-behind children by their impious and most rare father. Namphula, his wife, grieved even more, herself deceived. Sempronius and Victoricus, taking on the care, erected a small shrine to their most rare parent. Here he is buried.
EDCS-10300227.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Iutinus and praises him, with his children and wife mourning him, and his grandchildren erecting a shrine.

EDCS-10300228.translation: To the August Emperors Lucius Septimius Severus Pertinax Augustus and Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus. The gens Musuniorum Regianorum, under the direction of Thululem Fuae, flamen of the Augusti, by decree of the decurions, with public money, erected an altar.
EDCS-10300228.summary: This inscription records the erection of an altar by the gens Musuniorum Regianorum, funded by public money and approved by the decurions, during the reign of Septimius Severus and Caracalla.

EDCS-10300229.translation: The gens Regianorum made this dedication to the numen of Publius Septimius Geta, most noble Caesar, prince of youth, son of the Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus Arabicus Adiabenicus Parthicus Maximus, brother of the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus Pius Felix, prince of youth.
EDCS-10300229.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by the gens Regianorum to the divine spirit (numen) of Caesar Geta, son of Emperor Septimius Severus and brother of Emperor Caracalla.

EDCS-10300231.translation: Gaius Julius Faustus, son of Selauchanis.
EDCS-10300231.summary: This inscription records the name of Gaius Julius Faustus, son of Selauchanis, likely a funerary dedication or ownership mark.

EDCS-10300238.summary: This inscription records the name of Gaius Pomponius Donatus, likely a funerary dedication or ownership mark.

EDCS-10300239.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Caelius Urbanus lived for 13 years.
EDCS-10300239.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Caelius Urbanus, who died at the age of 13.

EDCS-10300245.translation: Sacred to Mercury Augustus and to the majesty of the divine power; may the good gods [ensure that]. Publius Spiculus, together with his sons, made and dedicated this to our Emperors and Lords Diocletian and Maximian, Augusti.
EDCS-10300245.summary: This is a dedication to Mercury and the imperial divinities made by Publius Spiculus and his sons in honor of Emperors Diocletian and Maximian.

EDCS-10300246.translation: Mathun, son of Massiranis, chief of the Meditanian family, pious, lived for 70 years. He is buried here. His sons attended to the funeral arrangements.
EDCS-10300246.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Mathun, chief of the Meditanian family, who died at 70, with arrangements made by his sons.

EDCS-10300247.translation: Calpurnia Peregrina, you were excessively pious; may the earth be light for you, where you were heavy. Oh, wretched you, you could not live even for a short time away from your homeland, nor be a burden to anyone. She lived for 36 years and 10 months. Thus.
EDCS-10300247.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Calpurnia Peregrina, lamenting her short life and piety, stating she lived 36 years and 10 months.

EDCS-10300249.summary: This inscription records the name of Lucius Julius Felix, likely a funerary dedication or ownership mark.

EDCS-10300250.translation: Quintus Cellius Secundus, son of Quintus, of the Papirian tribe, in his quaestorship with its purple robes, [his] abilities, [his] memory, who indeed also truly, in the minds of men, [honored] his ancestors, he made and dedicated this for himself, his sons, and his daughters, to the town council and the people, that is.
EDCS-10300250.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Quintus Cellius Secundus, likely for public benefit or honor, referencing his civic roles and family.

EDCS-10300251.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Caius Claudius Peregrinus lived for 70 years. Quintus Claudius made this.
EDCS-10300251.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Caius Claudius Peregrinus, who died at 70, made by Quintus Claudius.

EDCS-10300252.translation: vius Julius Victor and Faiania Vitalis Secunda lived for 35 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-10300252.summary: This inscription records the lives of Lucius Julius Victor and Faiania Vitalis Secunda, who lived to 35, with Faiania Vitalis Secunda being buried here.

EDCS-10300253.translation: Gaius Rutilius Felix, pious, lived for 55 years; his wife and sons took care of him. May your bones rest well. He is buried here.
EDCS-10300253.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Gaius Rutilius Felix, recording his lifespan and burial.

EDCS-10300255.translation: Dedicated to the Spirits of the Underworld. Caellia Saturnina lived for 85 years; her sons Flavi Methus and Ceso took care of her.
EDCS-10300255.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Caellia Saturnina, recording her lifespan and mentioning her sons as caretakers.

EDCS-10300256.translation: Telesinus, her husband, bound by love for his dear wife, erected this monument, more because he could than because he wished, in honor of her outstanding chastity.
EDCS-10300256.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Telesinus for his wife in honor of her chastity.

EDCS-10300257.translation: To the Genius of the Senate, preserver of our lords.
EDCS-10300257.summary: This is a dedication to the Genius of the Senate.

EDCS-10300258.text_edition: \n Neptuno Augusto sacrum Lucius Caecilius Maximinus ex summa honoraria flamoni sui posuit idemque dedicavit decreto decurionum\n
EDCS-10300258.translation: Dedicated to Neptune Augustus. Lucius Caecilius Maximinus erected this with funds from his high priestly office and also dedicated it by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-10300258.summary: This is a dedication to Neptune Augustus by Lucius Caecilius Maximinus, funded by his priestly office and authorized by local council, likely from the 2nd-3rd century CE.

EDCS-10300259.translation: Gaius Caecilius Maximinus, duovir, dedicated this sacred offering to Venus Genetrix Augusta.
EDCS-10300259.summary: This is a dedication to Venus Genetrix Augusta by Gaius Caecilius Maximinus, an official.

EDCS-10300261.summary: This inscription records Gaius Aurellius fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-10300262.translation: ESI, priest, made the house. Urbanus, priest, made the gift.
EDCS-10300262.summary: This inscription records two priests, ESI and Urbanus, making a house and a gift respectively.

EDCS-10300266.translation: By decree of the decurions, at public expense: To the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus Armeniacus Medicus Parthicus Maximus, son of the deified Antoninus Pius, grandson of the deified Hadrian, great-grandson of the deified Trajan, further great-grandson of the deified Nerva, pontifex maximus, with tribunician power for the 21st time, imperator for the 3rd time, consul for the 3rd time, proconsul, brother of Lucius Aurellius Verus Augustus Armeniacus Medicus Parthicus Maximus, with tribunician power for the 7th time, imperator for the 3rd time, consul for the 3rd time, proconsul, son of the deified Antoninus Pius, grandson of the deified Hadrian, great-grandson of the deified Trajan, further great-grandson of the deified Nerva.
EDCS-10300266.summary: This lengthy inscription is a dedication to Emperor Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus, listing his titles and lineage, erected by public funds.

EDCS-10300268.translation: To the deified Marcus Antoninus Pius, father of the Emperor Caesar Lucius Aurellius Commodus Augustus Pius Felix.
EDCS-10300268.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the deified Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius, father of Emperor Commodus.

EDCS-10300269.translation: By decree of the decurions, at public expense, with Publius Aelius Rusticus, curator of the state, an outstanding man, dedicating: To Iulia Domna Augusta, wife of the Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus Arabicus Adiabenicus, father of the fatherland.
EDCS-10300269.summary: This inscription dedicates a monument to Julia Domna Augusta, wife of Emperor Septimius Severus, by public decree and with the oversight of Publius Aelius Rusticus.

EDCS-10300270.translation: To Marcus Aurelius Antoninus, Caesar, son of Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus, Arabicus, Adiabenicus, father of the fatherland, Pontifex Maximus, with tribunician power for the 4th time, Imperator for the 8th time, Consul for the 2nd time, Proconsul; dedicated by decree of the decurions and at public expense, with Publius Aelius Rusticus, curator of the republic, an outstanding man, overseeing it.
EDCS-10300270.summary: This inscription dedicates a monument to Marcus Aurelius Antoninus, son of Emperor Septimius Severus, at public expense and by decree of the local council, overseen by a prominent curator.

EDCS-10300273.translation: The entire council, out of their own funds, have set up this inscription to remember Publius Aelius Saturus, a most worthy youth who held the aedileship and the office of duovir, because of his remarkable mildness of character and his full and honorable generosity towards individuals and the community.
EDCS-10300273.summary: This inscription records the erection of a memorial by the entire council to honor Publius Aelius Saturus for his character and generosity.

EDCS-10300274.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcus Aurellius Inventus, freedman of Augustus, procurator of the province of Leptis, is buried here.
EDCS-10300274.summary: This is a tomb inscription for Marcus Aurellius Inventus, a freedman of Augustus and a procurator in the province of Leptis.

EDCS-10300276.translation: The entire populace of the curiae has erected this for Gaius Pompeius Felix Octavianus, son of Lucius, of the tribe Quirina, honored with the public horse, by the divine Severus and Magnus Antoninus.
EDCS-10300276.summary: This inscription records the erection of a statue by the entire populace to honor Gaius Pompeius Felix Octavianus for his equestrian status.

EDCS-10300277.translation: The entire populace of the curiae has made this statue for Lucius Pompeius Ianus, son of Lucius, of the tribe Quirina, a military tribune of the Second Legion Adiutrix for six months, a perpetual flamen, because of his singular and novel example of generosity towards them, a most blameless citizen.
EDCS-10300277.summary: This inscription records the erection of a statue by the entire populace to honor Lucius Pompeius Ianus, a military tribune and perpetual flamen, for his generosity.

EDCS-10300278.translation: To Carpentius Lucius Valgius Fortis, son of Lucius, of the tribe Quirina, perpetual flamen, a man of exceptional affection and excellence towards all individuals and the community, from Antonius Priscianus, Argentius, and Aelius Maiulus, to their incomparable father.
EDCS-10300278.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated by three individuals to their father, Carpentius Lucius Valgius Fortis, a perpetual flamen.

EDCS-10300281.translation: Marius merited honor for his services and efforts, his obedience and diligence, and for the expenses he undertook.
EDCS-10300281.summary: This inscription likely records the merits and services of an individual named Marius, possibly in a public or military context.

EDCS-10300283.translation: The autumn season, the winter season. Author Xenophon.
EDCS-10300283.summary: This inscription appears to be a fragment possibly related to seasons or agricultural cycles, attributed to Xenophon.

EDCS-10300286.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Antestius Felix lived 4 years and 7 months.
EDCS-10300286.summary: This is a tomb inscription recording the short life of Lucius Antestius Felix.

EDCS-10300287.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Antestius Victor lived 75 years.
EDCS-10300287.summary: This is a tomb inscription recording the lifespan of Antestius Victor.

EDCS-10300290.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the age of Decimia Annia Felix, likely from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-10300293.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Octavia Nena, dutiful, lived 18 years and 10 days.
EDCS-10300293.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan of Octavia Nena, dedicated to the Manes.

EDCS-10300294.translation: Hail, Titius! Sacred to the departed spirits. Titus Statilius Satrianus lived 34 years, 9 months, and 27 days; he is buried here.
EDCS-10300294.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan and burial place of Titus Statilius Satrianus, dedicated to the Manes.

EDCS-10300295.translation: A soldier of the 7th Claudian Legion, Rufinus, a most accomplished man, curator of revenues, for the honor and memory of his well-deserving wife.
EDCS-10300295.summary: This inscription honors a soldier's wife, indicating the husband's rank and position, likely on a funerary monument.

EDCS-10300296.summary: This is a simple naming inscription, likely for a tombstone, identifying Servius Cornelius Cerealis.

EDCS-10300297.translation: Flavia Victoria and Lucius Caecilius Victor.
EDCS-10300297.summary: This inscription names two individuals, Flavia Victoria and Lucius Caecilius Victor, likely on a shared funerary monument.

EDCS-10300299.translation: To Iulia Victoria, daughter of Caius. She lived 35 years. Caius Cornelius Cassi erected this for his wife, a virtuous woman well-deserving and an example of piety to their daughter.
EDCS-10300299.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Iulia Victoria, erected by her husband Caius Cornelius Cassi, likely from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-10300301.text_edition: \n Antonio miles legionis III Augustae centuria Sextili vixit nnos XLIV militavit nnos XXV hic situs est Marcus Antonius miles legionis XXI centuria Valeri Prisci frater posuit\n
EDCS-10300301.translation: To Antonius, a soldier of the III Augusta legion, Centuria Sextili. He lived 44 years and served 25 years. Marcus Antonius, a soldier of the XXI legion, Centuria Valeri Prisci, his brother, erected this. He lies here.
EDCS-10300301.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Antonius, a soldier of the III Augusta legion, erected by his brother, also a soldier, likely from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-10300302.text_edition: \n Titi filius Sergia Heridianus tribunus militum legionis X fr<e=I>tensis \n
EDCS-10300302.translation: Heridianus, son of Titus, of the Sergia tribe, tribune of soldiers of the X Fretensis legion.
EDCS-10300302.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely identifying Heridianus, a military tribune, probably from the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-10300303.translation: Sextus Metilius Livi, of the Stellatina tribe, lived 20 years and served 2 years. Tiberius Quintius [erected this].
EDCS-10300303.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Sextus Metilius Livi, who lived 20 years and served 2 years, erected by Tiberius Quintius, likely from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-10300304.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulia Calliope lived 35 years. Her dutiful husband placed this, and the plot, 625 square cubits; she is buried here.
EDCS-10300304.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan of Iulia Calliope, her burial place, and the dimensions of the plot purchased by her husband.

EDCS-10300305.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. You conquered all in beauty, learning, girls. Iulia, dear to me, taken away by fate from my fatherland. Nothing more precious than gold, nor more beautiful than a Tyrian-dyed cylinder, nor more splendid than Laconian marble, nor better or more beautiful than Carystian marble. No Laconian spinner could rival Arachne in song, nor the daughters of Pandion, and you surpassed them in beauty, you who are said to be above all, born of a Greek hero parent. Taken away by lethal fate at the age of sixteen, I, Iulia Paula, now lie buried here. I beg.
EDCS-10300305.summary: This elaborate funerary epitaph praises the deceased Iulia Paula with poetic language, lamenting her early death and beauty.

EDCS-10300306.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. [Iulia Rogatina] lived 25 years, she lies here. Her parents erected [this] for their dearest daughter. // Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Iulia Inventa lived 30 years, she lies here. Her parents erected [this] for their dearest daughter. // Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Lucius Magnius Satur, a hardworking man, not deserving [of such an end], died away from home on the Hadrumetine road. He lived 55 years. Iulia Quinta, his dearest wife, erected [this] for her husband. He lies here.
EDCS-10300306.summary: This is a collection of funerary inscriptions for Iulia Rogatina, Iulia Inventa, and Lucius Magnius Satur, erected by their parents or wives, likely from the 2nd-3rd century CE.

EDCS-10300308.translation: His brothers made a burial for their brother Vitalis. He lived 30 years; having begun a succession of years, he is buried here.
EDCS-10300308.summary: This funerary epitaph records that brothers erected a tomb for their deceased brother, Vitalis, and states his age at death.

EDCS-10300311.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Aemilia Spes lived 30 years; she is buried here. Flavius Victor placed this for his dutiful and most precious wife.
EDCS-10300311.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan of Aemilia Spes and identifies her husband, Flavius Victor, as the dedicator.

EDCS-10300312.translation: Here lies Cnaeus Aemilius Venustus. He placed [this] for his dutiful wife.
EDCS-10300312.summary: This funerary epitaph records that Cnaeus Aemilius Venustus erected a tomb for his dutiful wife.

EDCS-10300313.translation: "Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Annia Sabina lived 60 years, she is buried here. Tadius Felix placed this for his most dutiful wife. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Lucius Tadius Felix lived 90 years, he is buried here."
EDCS-10300313.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Annia Sabina and Lucius Tadius Felix, husband and wife, set up by Tadius Felix for his wife.

EDCS-10300317.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Caecilia Quarta.

EDCS-10300322.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Callonia Aphrodisia.

EDCS-10300346.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Tiberius Iulius Iustus.

EDCS-10300366.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Pompeius Victor.

EDCS-10300382.translation: "Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Caius Clodius Fortunatus lived 45 years, he is buried here. Cornelius Fortunatus, a cavalryman of the 1st Urban Cohort, [placed this] for his dearest uncle."
EDCS-10300382.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Caius Clodius Fortunatus, dedicated by his uncle, Cornelius Fortunatus, a soldier.

EDCS-10300383.translation: "Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Postumius Laetianus, decurion of the colony of Ammaedara, lived 29 years, he is buried here. Quintus Postumius Laetus, decurion of the colony of Ammaedara, a man of quaestorian rank, placed this for his most dutiful son. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Accia Secunda Antonina lived 23 years, she is buried here. Quintus Postumius Laetus, decurion of the colony of Ammaedara, a man of quaestorian rank, placed this for his most unusual daughter-in-law and most holy wife of his son Postumius Laetianus."
EDCS-10300383.summary: This is a double funerary epitaph for Postumius Laetianus and his wife Accia Secunda Antonina, dedicated by Quintus Postumius Laetus, who is both father and father-in-law.

EDCS-10300384.translation: "Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Aemilius M [---]ius Po. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Castulus lived 10 years."
EDCS-10300384.summary: This inscription appears to be a fragmented funerary epitaph, possibly for Aemilius M[---]ius Po and Castulus, who died at age 10.

EDCS-10300386.translation: "Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Asiane lived 8 years, her dutiful father placed [this], she is buried here. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Aelius Domesticus lived 18 years, his dutiful father made [this]. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Aelius Ianuarius lived [---] years, his dutiful father made [this]."
EDCS-10300386.summary: This is a set of funerary epitaphs for Asiane, Aelius Domesticus, and Aelius Ianuarius, all dedicated by their respective fathers.

EDCS-10300388.translation: "Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Calicia Optata, servant, lived 50 years, she is buried here. Aemilius Ianuarius placed [this] for his most excellent wife and for himself."
EDCS-10300388.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Calicia Optata, a servant, set up by her husband Aemilius Ianuarius, also for himself.

EDCS-10300390.translation: Carvilia Donatilla lived 10 years; she is buried here. Carvilius Vindex placed this for his dearest daughter.
EDCS-10300390.summary: A funerary epitaph for Carvilia Donatilla, set up by her father, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10300400.translation: Iulius Secundus, a dutiful father, is buried here.
EDCS-10300400.summary: A simple funerary epitaph for Iulius Secundus, indicating he was a father, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10300402.translation: To eternal sleep. Iunius Paulinus lived 25 years. His brother Gratus placed this for his beloved, dutiful brother.
EDCS-10300402.summary: A funerary epitaph for Iunius Paulinus, erected by his brother, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10300413.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Sempronius Felix placed this for his dearest wife Servilia Solutria, who lived 48 years; she is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Sempronius Elica lived 50 years; he is buried here. His dutiful sons placed this.
EDCS-10300413.summary: A funerary epitaph for a married couple, Servilia Solutria and Lucius Sempronius Elica, erected by their sons, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10300414.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Terentianus. Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulius Felix.
EDCS-10300414.summary: A funerary dedication to the departed spirits, possibly commemorating two individuals, dating to the Roman Imperial period.
