EDCS-10300416.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Varia Maxima lived 65 years. Statilius Quietus placed this for his dutiful wife; she is buried here.
EDCS-10300416.summary: A funerary epitaph for Varia Maxima, erected by her husband, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10300417.translation: Lucius Volturcius Torquatus lived 25 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-10300417.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lucius Volturcius Torquatus, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10300418.summary: A funerary dedication to Volusena Privata, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10300419.translation: Caius Volusenus. Sacred to the departed spirits. Volussena lived 28 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-10300419.summary: A funerary epitaph for Volussena, possibly set up by Caius Volusenus, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10300421.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Caius Tetius Iucundus, a veteran of the XV Apollinaris legion, placed this for himself while alive.
EDCS-10300421.summary: A funerary epitaph for Caius Tetius Iucundus, a veteran of the XV Apollinaris legion, who dedicated it to himself during his lifetime, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10300431.translation: Publius Aelius Crescens and Caius Pompeius Palormus.
EDCS-10300431.summary: This inscription records the names of two individuals, possibly joint dedicants or the subjects of a monument.

EDCS-10300437.translation: She lived 34 years. Here lies a most frugal, most chaste, most obedient wife. Carilius Florentius erected this for his most rare, dutiful sister.
EDCS-10300437.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a woman, erected by her brother, Carilius Florentius, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-10300438.translation: For 40 years I lived as a friend to all, simple, good, generous, as much as I could according to my means. I have now withdrawn to this tomb. While I lived, I did what I could. Here lies Carilius Florentius. He erected this for his dutiful sister.
EDCS-10300438.summary: This funerary epitaph records the life and death of Carilius Florentius, who lived modestly and generously, and was erected by his sister, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-10300439.translation: Spuria ended her life, leaving behind her most wretched natural father and her mother, Aelia Victorina. They gave and made this, dutifully.
EDCS-10300439.summary: This inscription records the death of Spuria, with her natural father and mother being the dedicants, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-10300450.translation: Caius Fabius Ianuarius and Caius Fabius Vetidius Victorinus.
EDCS-10300450.summary: This inscription records the names of two individuals, Caius Fabius Ianuarius and Caius Fabius Vetidius Victorinus, likely brothers or a family commemoration.

EDCS-10300466.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Vibia Caeli lived 40 years. Here she lies. I competed with you, my wife, in dutifulness, virtue, frugality, and love, but death conquered all. May this fate be granted to all. Ianuarianus erected this for his dutiful wife. Sacred to the Divine Shades. Claudius Ianuarianus lived 75 years. Here he lies. Bonosa erected this for her husband.
EDCS-10300466.summary: This funerary inscription records the lives of Vibia Caeli and Claudius Ianuarianus, with their respective spouses Ianuarianus and Bonosa as dedicants, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-10300489.text_edition: \n Saturno et Opi pro salute Impperatorum Caesarum Luci Septimi Severi Pii Pertinacis Augusti Arabici Adiabenici Parthici et Marci Aureli Antonini Augusti Pii [et Publi Septimi Getae nobilissimi Caesaris] totiusque divinae domus victoriaque eorum et Iulia Victorina uxor Secundi mater\n
EDCS-10300489.translation: For Saturn and Ops, for the safety of the Emperors Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus Arabicus Adiabenicus Parthicus and Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus Pius [and Publius Septimius Geta Nobilissimus Caesar], and of their entire divine family, and for their victory, and for Iulia Victorina, wife of Secundus, mother [of Antoninus].
EDCS-10300489.summary: This is a dedication for the safety and victory of the emperors Septimius Severus, Caracalla, and Geta, and their family, including Iulia Victorina, likely from the early 3rd century CE.

EDCS-10300492.translation: Iulia Artemis, freedwoman of Caius. From Alexandria in Egypt. She lived 9 years. Here she lies. Iulius made this for his dutiful daughter.
EDCS-10300492.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a young girl, Iulia Artemis, erected by her father, Iulius, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-10300493.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Flavia Fortunata lived 37 years. Her husband erected this.
EDCS-10300493.summary: This funerary epitaph records the life of Flavia Fortunata, erected by her husband, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-10300502.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Caius Domitius Donatus, a veteran, served as a duplicarius cornicularius. He lived 82 years. Under the care of his son, Gen Rufi.
EDCS-10300502.summary: This funerary inscription records the life of Caius Domitius Donatus, a veteran of the Roman army who served as a duplicarius cornicularius, and was erected by his son, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-10300503.summary: This inscription records the name of Caius Domitius Donatus, possibly a simple dedication or a funerary marker.

EDCS-10300504.summary: This inscription is a name, likely commemorating Domitia Quintula on a monument or tomb.

EDCS-10300506.summary: This inscription is a dedication or memorial, possibly a tomb, from Tunada to Malisua.

EDCS-10300511.translation: Dama, the magistrate, made and dedicated (this) with his own money.
EDCS-10300511.summary: This inscription records a magistrate named Dama who funded and dedicated a public work or structure.

EDCS-10300513.translation: Gaius Cornelius Saturninus and Lucius Petronius Victor made the portico with their own money.
EDCS-10300513.summary: This inscription records the construction of a portico funded by Gaius Cornelius Saturninus and Lucius Petronius Victor.

EDCS-10300514.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Publius Aelius Augendus lived 81 years.
EDCS-10300514.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the death and age of Publius Aelius Augendus.

EDCS-10300515.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Agria Marcella lived 40 years. Sacred to the departed spirits.
EDCS-10300515.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the death and age of Agria Marcella, with a repeated invocation to the departed spirits.

EDCS-10300516.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Bebia Victoria lived 61 years; she rests here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus Agrius Marchelus.
EDCS-10300516.summary: This funerary inscription records the death and age of Bebia Victoria, her burial place, and the name of Quintus Agrius Marchelus, likely a relative or the person commissioning the tomb.

EDCS-10300519.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Considia Prima lived 81 years.
EDCS-10300519.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the death and age of Considia Prima.

EDCS-10300520.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Silvana lived 30 years.
EDCS-10300520.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the death and age of Silvana.

EDCS-10300521.translation: To the Genius of the neighborhood. Lucius Cornelius Ma[---] made (this) with his own money and dedicated it, with Lucius Egnatius Secundus as curator.
EDCS-10300521.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a monument to the Genius of the neighborhood, funded and dedicated by Lucius Cornelius Ma[---] during the curatorship of Lucius Egnatius Secundus.

EDCS-10300522.translation: Flavia Tertulla, daughter of Marcus, priestess, lived 100 years.
EDCS-10300522.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the age of Flavia Tertulla, a priestess.

EDCS-10300525.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Flavius Fortunatus.

EDCS-10300526.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Sextus Lochenius Quintulus.

EDCS-10300528.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Aulus Cossinius Faustus lived 75 years.
EDCS-10300528.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the age of Aulus Cossinius Faustus, dedicated to the Divine Shades.

EDCS-10300529.translation: Caius Cossinius Faustus, son of Romanius, lived 85 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-10300529.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the age and burial place of Caius Cossinius Faustus.

EDCS-10300531.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Fadia Marchiana lived 73 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-10300531.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the age and burial place of Fadia Marchiana, dedicated to the Divine Shades.

EDCS-10300532.translation: Us Repentinus lived 3 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-10300532.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the age and burial place of Us Repentinus.

EDCS-10300533.translation: Valentina, daughter of Rufinus, the pious, lived 80 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-10300533.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the age and burial place of Valentina, daughter of Rufinus.

EDCS-10300535.summary: This is a religious dedication to the god Mercury.

EDCS-10300537.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Aelia Maiorica lived...
EDCS-10300537.summary: This is a tombstone inscription, possibly incomplete, dedicated to the Divine Shades for Aelia Maiorica.

EDCS-10300541.translation: Dedicated to the spirits of the departed. Selicius Saesolianus, son of Selicius, a dutiful man, lived 45 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-10300541.summary: A tombstone recording the death and burial of Selicius Saesolianus, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10300543.summary: A tombstone naming Gargilia Ianuaria, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10300545.summary: A tombstone naming Geminia Luciska, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10300551.translation: Maximus Persicus, who held the tribunician power, on the day of the promise, 200,000 sesterces and gifts to the curial officials.
EDCS-10300551.summary: A fragmentary inscription recording a financial donation by Maximus Persicus, who held tribunician power, likely in the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10300552.text_edition: \n Iussu domini Aesculapi Lucius Numisius Luci filius Vitalis podium de suo fecit quisquis intra podium adscendere volet a muliere a suilla a faba a tonsore a balineo commune custodiat triduo cancellos calciatus intrare nolito\n
EDCS-10300552.translation: By order of our Lord Aesculapius, Lucius Numisius Vitalis, son of Lucius, built the podium at his own expense. Whoever wishes to ascend within the podium must guard it from women, pigsties, beans, and barbers; do not enter the public baths with shoes on for three days.
EDCS-10300552.summary: An inscription from the Roman period recording building rules for a podium dedicated to Aesculapius, likely constructed by Lucius Numisius Vitalis.

EDCS-10300553.translation: Dedicated to the sacred Caelestis Augusta. Titus Iunius Victor made this and set it up at his own expense.
EDCS-10300553.summary: A dedication to the goddess Caelestis Augusta, erected by Titus Iunius Victor at his own expense, likely in the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10300554.translation: To the sacred Goddess Caelestis Augusta, Lucius Rutilius Macer gladly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-10300554.summary: A votive inscription to the goddess Caelestis Augusta, fulfilled by Lucius Rutilius Macer, likely in the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10300555.translation: To the Lady Caelestis Augusta, to her Genius. Titus Titisenus Salutaris made this at his own expense by decree of the council in the year of Daphnius Lupus and Lucius Memmius Felix, from his own resources.
EDCS-10300555.summary: A dedication to the goddess Caelestis Augusta and her Genius, funded by Titus Titisenus Salutaris by order of the town council, dated to the consulship of Daphnius Lupus and Lucius Memmius Felix in the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10300556.translation: To Caelestis Aurelius, by the grace of Augustus, our Lord.
EDCS-10300556.summary: A dedication to Caelestis Aurelius, possibly referencing imperial favor, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10300558.translation: To Juno Caelestis, Marcus Manlius Aptus the younger made a room with columns at his own expense.
EDCS-10300558.summary: A dedication to Juno Caelestis, recording the construction of a room with columns by Marcus Manlius Aptus the younger at his own expense, likely in the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10300563.translation: To Concordia Felix, the Most Loving Patroness.
EDCS-10300563.summary: A dedication to Concordia Felix, describing her as a loving patroness, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10300564.text_edition: \n Dianae Augustae sacrum pro salute Imperatoris Caesaris Traiani Hadriani Augusti Lucius Romanius Publi filius Arnensi Gallus voto posuit idemque dedicavit\n
EDCS-10300564.translation: Lucius Romanius Gallus, son of Publius, of the Arnensis tribe, dedicated this sacred offering to Diana Augusta for the health of the Emperor Caesar Trajan Hadrian Augustus, fulfilling a vow.
EDCS-10300564.summary: A dedication to Diana Augusta by Lucius Romanius Gallus for the health of Emperor Hadrian, likely dating to his reign (117-138 AD).

EDCS-10300565.text_edition: \n Frugifero Augusto sacrum pro salute Imperatoris Caesaris Titi Aeli Hadriani Antonini Augusti Pii Lucius Decianus Marci filius Arnensis Extricatus praefectus iure dicundo sacerdos Cererum annorum CLXXIII nomine suo et Iuliae uxoris et Decianorum Extricati Maniliani Honorati filiorum omnibus ornamentis sua pecunia fecit donum dedit idemque dedicavit\n
EDCS-10300565.translation: Lucius Decianus Extricatus, son of Marcus, of the Arnensis tribe, a former prefect, priest of Ceres, aged 173 years, has made and dedicated this entire offering with his own money in his name and that of his wife Julia, and his sons Decianus Manilianus Honoratus, to the fruitful Augustus.
EDCS-10300565.summary: A dedicatory inscription to 'Frugifer Augustus' (the fruitful Augustus), likely Hadrian, by Lucius Decianus Extricatus, a prominent local official, in the reign of Antoninus Pius (138-161 AD).

EDCS-10300567.translation: Sacred to the genius of the municipality, from the will of Caius Valerius Campanus, centurion of the 13th Gemina Legion, who bequeathed 5,000 sesterces to the genius of his municipality, Julia, perpetual priestess, on behalf of [the following text is corrupt and illegible]... centurion of the 3rd Augustan Legion, centurion of the 2nd [corrupt text].
EDCS-10300567.summary: This inscription records a bequest from Caius Valerius Campanus, a centurion, to the genius of his municipality, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-10300569.translation: Sacred to the genius of the temple, Celer, the priest, made and dedicated this exedra with its statue and all its furnishings in his own name and in the name of his wife Aufidia Quartilla, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-10300569.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a temple exedra by the priest Celer, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10300572.translation: Sacred to Jupiter Optimus Maximus, for the health of the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus Armeniacus, Medicus, Parthicus Maximus, Germanicus, and of his entire divine house, Gaius Octavius Blandus gave this offering in his own name and in the names of his sons Gaius Octavius Blandus Aemilianus and Marcus Octavius Benivolus Aemilianus, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-10300572.summary: This inscription records an offering made by Gaius Octavius Blandus and his sons to Jupiter for the health of Emperor Marcus Aurelius, likely dating to his reign (161-180 CE).

EDCS-10300573.translation: Sacred to the divine power of the Augusti, Primus, a freedman of Augustus, steward of the Upper Thuburbitan and Canopitan districts, placed this at his own expense, and dedicated it.
EDCS-10300573.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a shrine to the divine power of the emperors by Primus, a steward, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10300574.translation: Sacred to Liber Augustus, for the health of the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Commodus Antoninus, Fabius Victor Sestianus, second prefect for administering justice, priest of the genius of the municipality, in his own name and in the name of his wife [MOR - illegible].
EDCS-10300574.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Liber Augustus by Fabius Victor Sestianus, a prefect and priest, for the health of Emperor Commodus, likely dating to his reign (177-192 CE).

EDCS-10300578.translation: Sacred to Mercury Augustus, Quintus, son of Secundus Morinis, willingly fulfilled his vow, deservedly.
EDCS-10300578.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to Mercury Augustus by Quintus, son of Secundus Morinis, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10300580.summary: This is a very brief inscription dedicating something to the deity Pollux by a woman named Julia, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10300581.translation: Sacred to Saturn Augustus, Diophantus, son of Bassus Seris, having held all the offices in his city, placed this marble statue at his own expense, and dedicated it, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-10300581.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a marble statue to Saturn Augustus by Diophantus, a civic official, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10300582.translation: Sacred to Saturn Augustus, Faustus Lupus, son of Daphnis, and [other priests], priests of the genius of the city, made this exedra and all its furnishings at their own expense, and dedicated them, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-10300582.summary: This inscription records the dedication of an exedra to Saturn Augustus and the genius of the city by two priests, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10300583.translation: Sacred to Augustus, Diophantus, son of Cittinus and Diophantus, a craftsman, willingly fulfilled his vow and made this silver palm of 25 denarii at his own expense. And to Saturn.
EDCS-10300583.summary: This inscription records a craftsman named Diophantus making a votive offering of a silver palm to Augustus and Saturn, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10300584.translation: Sacred to Venus Augusta. Titus Carfanius, son of Titus, Pollia Barbarus, and Tiberius Claudius Timonianus, son of Spurius, public officials of the associations of Africans, dedicated this. Venustus, the overseer, rebuilt the small shrine from the ground up at his own expense.
EDCS-10300584.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a rebuilt shrine to Venus Augusta by public officials and its rebuilding by an overseer, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-10300585.translation: Sacred to Vesta Augusta. Umbrius Victoricus, priest, and Aemilia Dativa and F AE CEN MIA ER.
EDCS-10300585.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Vesta Augusta by a priest and two other individuals, possibly from the Imperial period.

EDCS-10300586.translation: Caesia Ianuaria, daughter of [---], fulfilled her vow.
EDCS-10300586.summary: This inscription records a woman fulfilling a vow, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10300588.summary: This inscription records a woman fulfilling a vow, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10300589.translation: Sacred to Augustus. [---]ali, son of [---], fulfilled his vow, and Magnio.
EDCS-10300589.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Augustus and the fulfillment of a vow by two individuals, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10300591.translation: To the pontifex maximus, with tribunician power, and of the entire divine house of them, Germanicus, admitted to the Sarmatic triumph.
EDCS-10300591.summary: This inscription fragment likely refers to an honorific dedication to a high-ranking official, possibly during the reign of Trajan, given the mention of Germanicus and Sarmaticus.

EDCS-10300593.translation: To the greatest, Britannicus, pontifex maximus, with tribunician power for the 11th time, to each of the 300 decurions, a single denarius.
EDCS-10300593.summary: This inscription fragment likely records a distribution of money to decurions in honor of an emperor, possibly Hadrian, given the titles and date range.

EDCS-10300595.translation: For the safety of the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Severus Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus, Parthicus Maximus, Britannicus Maximus, Germanicus Maximus, pontifex maximus, with tribunician power for the 17th time, imperator for the 2nd time, consul for the 4th time, father of the country, proconsul, and of Julia Domna Augusta, Pius Felix, mother of the Augusti, and of the camp, and of the country, and of their entire divine house, the colony Julia Aurelia Commoda of Thuburbo Maius built this from public funds and money from the ground up.
EDCS-10300595.summary: This inscription records the construction of a public building by the colony of Thuburbo Maius in honor of Emperor Caracalla and Empress Julia Domna, likely in the early 3rd century CE.

EDCS-10300603.translation: To Salvianus, patron of blessed Carthage, at the urging of the prosperity of the times of our lords Emperors Arcadius and Honorius, renowned princes, victors everywhere, under the proconsulship of Salvianus Edicius, patron of blessed Carthage, the state of Thuburbo Maius, in honor of its most beloved citizen and lover of himself, granted this statue, which was also due to the merits of his public duties towards it, and he erected the winter baths from the very foundations to the roof, and also, in the time of [---], of all the baths, the end [---] at his own expense and with his own resources, the expenditure with love [---].
EDCS-10300603.summary: This inscription honors Salvianus, a patron of Carthage and Thuburbo Maius, for his public service and his construction of winter baths, likely from the late 4th or early 5th century CE.

EDCS-10300604.translation: Greatest municipium Aelius Hadrianum Augustum Thuburbo Maius.
EDCS-10300604.summary: This inscription fragment likely refers to a dedication to Emperor Hadrian by the municipium of Thuburbo Maius, probably from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-10300605.translation: Of the municipality of Hadrianus Augustus of Thuburbo Maius.
EDCS-10300605.summary: This is an inscription related to the municipality of Thuburbo Maius.

EDCS-10300606.translation: Lucius Magnius Saturninus Sedianus Iunior, to his most beloved patron, was granted a place by decree of the decurions, for Gaius Arrius Quirinus Longinus, a most distinguished boy, son of Gaius Arrius Honoratus, a man of consular rank, and of Oscia Publiana, a most distinguished woman.
EDCS-10300606.summary: This inscription records a place granted by decree to Gaius Arrius Quirinus Longinus, son of a consular man and a distinguished woman, by Lucius Magnius Saturninus Sedianus Iunior.

EDCS-10300607.translation: For Publius Attius Extricationus, son of Publius, of the Arnensis tribe, flamen of the deified Titus, priest of Aesculapius of the colony of Julia Karthago, twice admitted to the equestrian order by the Emperors Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus and Marcus Aurelius Commodus Antoninus Augusti Germanici Sarmatici, the public funds paid for this at the decree of the decurions, in honor of his mother, Julia Bassilia, perpetual flaminica.
EDCS-10300607.summary: An inscription honoring Publius Attius Extricationus, a prominent local magistrate and priest, funded by public money in honor of his mother, dating to the joint reign of Marcus Aurelius and Commodus (177-180 AD).

EDCS-10300608.translation: To Gaius Vettius Sabinianus Iulius Hospitus, son of Gaius, of the Voltinian tribe, who served as consul, as Titian sodalis, as imperial legate with pro-praetorian powers over the three provinces of Dacia and Dalmatia, curator of sacred buildings, also of the public affairs of the Puteolani, commander of detachments sent from Illyricum by the deified Emperor Marcus Aurelius for the defense of the city, honored by the same Emperor with a mural crown and a golden spear and two golden standards for the Germanic and Sarmatian campaigns, as imperial legate with pro-praetorian powers of Pannonia Inferior, prefect of the Saturnian treasury, legate of the Legio XIIII Gemina with jurisdiction over Pannonia Superior, imperial legate for auditing the accounts of the Three Gauls, legate of the Legio III Italica Concordis, juridical official for the regions of Etruria, Aemilia, and Liguria, imperial legate for organizing the affairs of the Cyclades islands, legate of the province of Asia, praetor, tribune of the plebs, quaestor, transferred to the most distinguished order by the deified Emperor Titus Antoninus, tribune of the soldiers of Legio I Italica, prefect of the Cohors II Commagenorum; to the patron of the colony Aurelia Commoda Thuburbo Maius, by decree of the decurions, at public expense.
EDCS-10300608.summary: This extensive inscription honors Gaius Vettius Sabinianus Iulius Hospitus, a high-ranking official and military leader under Marcus Aurelius and Titus Antoninus, who served in various consular, legateship, and administrative roles across the empire and received numerous military honors, and to whom the colony of Thuburbo Maius erected a statue at public expense.

EDCS-10300609.translation: To Lucius Candonius Saturninus Flavius, as aedile, as prefect for administering justice twice, as duovir for five years, as priest of Ceres in the colony, who was the first in his fatherland to achieve [---] N SCIV AIORIV A II curiae C.
EDCS-10300609.summary: This inscription honors Lucius Candonius Saturninus Flavius for his service in various civic and religious offices within the colony, including aedile, prefect, duovir, and priest of Ceres.

EDCS-10300610.translation: To Quintus Fabius Sentius Sentianus Germanus, perpetual flamen, who held all offices, [died at age] 50.
EDCS-10300610.summary: This inscription commemorates Quintus Fabius Sentius Sentianus Germanus, a perpetual flamen who had held all local offices and died at the age of 50.

EDCS-10300611.translation: and of his grandsons, with silver statues and gifts from the ground, and for the dedication.
EDCS-10300611.summary: This fragment likely refers to the erection of silver statues and gifts, possibly related to a dedication ceremony for family members.

EDCS-10300612.translation: He repaired and strengthened with stone a cellar with its floor, including all bronze and lead fixtures, and added a new pool named 'cochlea', restoring the old sumps; dedicated by G. Optatianus, perpetual flamen and curator of public affairs.
EDCS-10300612.summary: This inscription details the repair and renovation of a cellar, pool, and related fixtures by G. Optatianus, the perpetual flamen and curator of public affairs.

EDCS-10300614.summary: This inscription identifies Hono GOR as a perpetual flamen.

EDCS-10300616.summary: This is a maker's mark or ownership inscription from the workshop of Nicentius.

EDCS-10300619.summary: This inscription is a simple dedication or naming of Quintus Aurelius Rogatianus Ioledianus.

EDCS-10300620.summary: This is a funerary inscription or a personal dedication by Gaius Ceppius Sterceius.

EDCS-10300621.summary: This is likely a funerary inscription for Meropia, daughter of Atedius.

EDCS-10300622.text_edition: \n Iuliae Domnae Augustae matri Auggustorum castrorumque nnue victoriis eorum Imperatoris Caesaris Luci Septimi Severi Pii Pertinacis Augusti Arabici Adiabenici Parthici maximi fortissimi felicissimi coniugi civitas Giufitana decreto decurionum dedit posuit eademque dedicavit\n
EDCS-10300622.translation: The citizenship of Giufi has granted and set up this monument to Julia Domna Augusta, mother of the Augusti, of the camps, and of their victories, wife of the Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus Arabicus Adiabenicus Parthicus Maximus, most brave and most fortunate, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-10300622.summary: A civic dedication to Julia Domna, mother of Caracalla and Geta and wife of Septimius Severus, by the city of Giufi, likely erected during the reign of Septimius Severus (193-211 AD).

EDCS-10300623.translation: Marcus Areius Optatus, son of Victoris, and Quintus Minucius Secundus, son of Secundus, veterans, having multiplied the honorary sum for their aedileship, and furthermore on the day of dedication, gave a feast and distributions to the decurions and the people. The site was granted by decree of the decurions. Dedicated on the 3rd Ides of May in the consulship of Pompeianus and Paelignianus.
EDCS-10300623.summary: A record of benefactions by two former officials, Marcus Areius Optatus and Quintus Minucius Secundus, who provided a feast and distributions to the local council and populace upon the completion of their duties, dedicated in 198 AD.

EDCS-10300624.translation: To the Emperor Caesar, son of the deified Septimius Severus Pius Arabicus Adiabenicus Parthicus Maximus Britannicus Maximus, Marcus Aurelius Antoninus.
EDCS-10300624.summary: This is a dedication to the emperor Marcus Aurelius Antoninus, son of Septimius Severus.

EDCS-10300626.translation: To Sextus Asinius Rufus Fabianus, son of Marcus, of the Horatia tribe, former praetor, aedile of Cerealis, from the acts of the consuls, quaestor of the city, priest of the Laurentes, by decree of the decurions, with public money.
EDCS-10300626.summary: This inscription records the public benefactions and career of Sextus Asinius Rufus Fabianus, funded by the local curia.

EDCS-10300628.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Publius Alfius Titianus lived piously for 21 years.
EDCS-10300628.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Publius Alfius Titianus, who died at the age of 21.

EDCS-10300629.summary: This is likely a funerary inscription for Rogata, daughter of Marcus.

EDCS-10300630.translation: For the deified Hadrian, father of the Emperor Caesar Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Augustus Pius, pontifex maximus, with tribunician power for the 8th time, consul for the 2nd time, father of the country, Germanus, son of Passus Germanus, from Sutunurca, on account of the honor of perpetual flaminatus for his fifth daughter Quintae, with 4,000 sesterces, with an additional 1,525 sesterces, has made the statue of the deified Hadrian and of Caesar Lucius Aelius with public money by decree of the decurions. And for the dedication, he gave entrails and a gymnasium to the people.
EDCS-10300630.summary: An inscription recording the erection of statues of Emperors Hadrian and Lucius Aelius, and the donation of a gymnasium, by Germanus in honor of his daughter's perpetual priesthood, likely during the reign of Antoninus Pius (138-161 AD).

EDCS-10300631.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari divi Marci Antonini Pii Germanici Sarmatici filio divi Commodi fratri divi Pii nepoti divi Hadriani pronepoti divi Traiani Parthici abnepoti divi Nervae adnepoti Lucio Septimio Severo Pio Pertinaci Augusto Arabico Adiabenico Parthico maximo pontifici maximo tribunicia potestate IIII imperatori XI consuli III proconsuli patri patriae cives Romani pagani veterani pagi Fortunalis quorum parentes beneficio divi Augusti [] Sutunurca agros acceperunt pecunia publica faciendum curaverunt\n
EDCS-10300631.translation: The Roman citizens, pagans and veterans of the district of Fortunalis, whose parents received land in Sutunurca by the favor of the deified Augustus, have taken care to have this made with public money, for the Emperor Caesar, son of the deified Marcus Aurelius Pius Germanicus Sarmaticus, brother of the deified Commodus, grandson of the deified Pius, great-grandson of the deified Hadrian, great-great-grandson of the deified Trajan Parthicus, great-great-great-grandson of the deified Nerva, Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus Arabicus Adiabenicus Parthicus Maximus, pontifex maximus, with tribunician power for the 4th time, emperor for the 11th time, consul for the 3rd time, proconsul, father of the country.
EDCS-10300631.summary: A public work commissioned by Roman citizens, veterans, and pagans from the district of Fortunalis, whose ancestors benefited from land grants under Augustus, for Emperor Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus, dating to his reign (c. 193-211 AD).

EDCS-10300632.translation: To Julia Augusta, mother of the camp, wife of the Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus Arabicus Adiabenicus Parthicus Maximus, Pontifex Maximus, holder of tribunician power for the 11th time, consul for the 2nd time, proconsul, father of the fatherland, and of the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus, prince of the youth, and of Lucius Septimius Geta nobilissimus Caesar, by the city of Sutunurcensis, by decree of the decurions, with public money.
EDCS-10300632.summary: This inscription honors Julia Domna, mother of Caracalla and Geta, and wife of Septimius Severus, and was commissioned by the city of Sutunurcensis.

EDCS-10300633.translation: To the Emperor Caesar, son of the deified Antoninus Pius, grandson of the deified Hadrian, great-grandson of the deified Trajan Parthicus, great-great-grandson of the deified Nerva, Lucius Aurelius Verus Augustus, Pontifex Maximus, holder of tribunician power for the 2nd time, consul for the 2nd time. Coclius Saturninus Golicus, for the honor of the perpetual priesthood, from 3,000,000 sesterces, also contributed 1,000,000 sesterces to the state, and for the dedication gave a feast and theatrical games, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-10300633.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Coclius Saturninus Golicus to Emperor Lucius Aurelius Verus, for which he provided funds for public games and a feast, and also made a substantial contribution to the state.

EDCS-10300634.translation: Sacred to Fortuna Redux Augusta. For the health of the divine Augustus. Nanius Abonius, perpetual priest, for the honor of his perpetual priesthood and his son Consus Felix Abonius's decurionate, built this temple with all its adornments from 5,000 sesterces, expanded with additional money, on private land, and also placed marble statues of his father and mother in two adjoining rooms, and dedicated them. And for the dedication, he gave a feast and games to all, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-10300634.summary: Nanius Abonius dedicated a temple to Fortuna Redux and provided public entertainment, funded by his own resources and for the honor of his priestly and civic offices, as well as for his family.

EDCS-10300635.translation: To Lucius Cassius Marcellus Florentinus, most excellent boy, son of Lucius Cassius Marcellus, Augustan procurator, a man of distinction, patron, by decree of the decurions, with public money.
EDCS-10300635.summary: This is a public dedication to the memory of Lucius Cassius Marcellus Florentinus, son of a distinguished Roman official.

EDCS-10300636.text_edition: \n Augusto deo cives Romani qui Thinissut negotiantur curatore Lucio Fabricio\n
EDCS-10300636.translation: To the deified Augustus, by the Roman citizens who trade in Thinissut, under the curator Lucius Fabricius.
EDCS-10300636.summary: A dedication to the deified Augustus by Roman merchants of Thinissut, overseen by Lucius Fabricius, likely from the imperial period.

EDCS-10300639.translation: Sacred to Saturn Augustus. Lucius Pompeius Honoratus, son of Arnensis, with his own money made and also dedicated a cistern because of his generosity.
EDCS-10300639.summary: This is a dedication of a cistern to Saturn Augustus by Lucius Pompeius Honoratus, who funded it out of his own pocket due to his munificence.

EDCS-10300642.summary: This inscription records Domnabus Quintus fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-10300643.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus.
EDCS-10300643.summary: This is a dedication to Emperor Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus.

EDCS-10300644.translation: To our lord Arcadius, renowned, pious, happy, Augustus, under the administration of Flavius Macrobianus Maximus, a man of highest rank, count of the first order, acting prefect of the Praetorium, and Flavius Synesius Philo, a man of highest rank, consular of the province of Flavia Valeria Byzacena, Flavius Calbinus, a most devoted man, perpetual flamen, curator of the republic, always most devoted to his divine majesty.
EDCS-10300644.summary: This is a dedication to Emperor Arcadius, likely made by Flavius Calbinus, during the administration of high-ranking officials, indicating an imperial cult context.

EDCS-10300646.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Aurelius Decianus, citizen of Pompeiopolis, lived 5 years, 10 months, 20 days. Aurelius Neophytus, freedman of Augustus, [erected this] for his most sweet son.
EDCS-10300646.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Aurelius Decianus, who died at a young age, set up by his father Aurelius Neophytus.

EDCS-10300647.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Lucius Liberius Julianus, son of Lucius, of the Oufentina tribe, from Forum Flaminii, [now of] Arna, [died in] Carthage, lived eight months, is buried here.
EDCS-10300647.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Lucius Liberius Julianus, a child who died in Carthage and is buried there.

EDCS-10300648.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Lucius Umbilius Felix the elder lived 115 years, 7 months, 15 days, is buried here.
EDCS-10300648.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Lucius Umbilius Felix the elder, noting his exceptional age.

EDCS-10300649.summary: This is a simple inscription bearing the name Cornelius Maximus.

EDCS-10300650.translation: The Curia Poblicia, in honor of Marcus Manlius Quietianus, son of Caius, of the Quirina tribe, Modestus, who was admitted to the public equites and into the five decuries, perpetual flamen, and twice holder of the office of duovir, and curator of the alimenta, a patron who built the theatre at his own expense for his outstanding generosity to his fatherland, [erected this] at his own expense.
EDCS-10300650.summary: This inscription honors Marcus Manlius Quietianus for his public service and munificence in funding the construction of a theatre.

EDCS-10300651.translation: The entire most splendid body of magistrates of the municipality of Vinensium, with Ul [---] as curator, [erected this] to Lucius Domitius Gallicanus Papinianus, a most distinguished man, praetorian prefect of the treasury of Saturn.
EDCS-10300651.summary: This is a dedication by the town council of Vinensium to Lucius Domitius Gallicanus Papinianus, honoring his distinguished career, including his role as prefect of the treasury.

EDCS-10300652.translation: By decree of the town councillors, a place was granted to Titus Scantius Rogatianus, son of Lucius, of the Arnensian tribe, perpetual priest and twice chief magistrate.
EDCS-10300652.summary: This inscription records a grant of public space to a local magistrate, Tito Scantio Rogatiano, by a decree of the local council.

EDCS-10300654.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Statius Statianus and Maximus, brothers, [erected this] for their most devoted and virtuous brother, Gaius Statius Celsus, Roman knight, scribe, and librarian, who lived 36 years, 11 months, and 18 days.
EDCS-10300654.summary: This funerary inscription honors Gaius Statius Celsus, a Roman knight and scribe, by his brothers Statius Statianus and Maximus.

EDCS-10300656.translation: Sacred to Saturn Augustus. Marcus Cominius Felix fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-10300656.summary: This is a votive inscription to Saturn Augustus, indicating Marcus Cominius Felix fulfilled a vow.

EDCS-10300657.translation: Sacred to Saturn Augustus. Gaius Julius Laetus, priest of the god, willingly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-10300657.summary: This is a votive inscription to Saturn Augustus, indicating the priest Gaius Julius Laetus fulfilled his vow.

EDCS-10300658.translation: To the holy Saturn of Sobara. Vettius [dedicated this].
EDCS-10300658.summary: This is a dedication to the local deity Saturn of Sobara by Vettius.

EDCS-10300660.translation: To holy Saturn of CODES R. [He/She] fulfilled [his/her] vow.
EDCS-10300660.summary: This is a votive inscription to Saturn, with "CODES R" likely indicating a place name or tribal affiliation, where a vow was fulfilled.

EDCS-10300664.translation: Titiena Prima rests here. She lived 16 years.
EDCS-10300664.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Titiena Prima, recording her death at the age of 16.

EDCS-10300665.translation: Sacred to Saturn Augustus. Sextus Calavius Victor, son of Publius, priest, willingly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-10300665.summary: This is a votive inscription to Saturn Augustus, indicating the priest Sextus Calavius Victor fulfilled his vow.

EDCS-10300666.translation: To the Nymphs, which chance freely offered.
EDCS-10300666.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the Nymphs, possibly marking a natural spring or source.

EDCS-10300667.translation: Junius Quartus, who served as an assistant in the II Parthica Legion.
EDCS-10300667.summary: This inscription records the service of Junius Quartus as an assistant in the II Parthica Legion.

EDCS-10300668.summary: This inscription is a simple name, likely a funerary epitaph or a label.

EDCS-10300669.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Quintus Mescenius Ianuarius lived 35 years, 6 months, 12 days. May the earth be light upon you, may your bones rest well.
EDCS-10300669.summary: A funerary epitaph for Quintus Mescenius Ianuarius, recording his lifespan and offering a wish for his peaceful repose.

EDCS-10300671.translation: Sacred to Saturn, the Divine. Scribonius, son of Marcius, the priest, gladly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-10300671.summary: A votive inscription dedicated to Saturn by Scribonius, a priest, who gladly fulfilled his vow.

EDCS-10300672.summary: This inscription appears to be a name, possibly an epitaph, with an unclear abbreviation at the end.

EDCS-10300673.translation: Sacred to Caelestis Augusta Graniana. Voltius Senecio moved the temple, which had been snatched away by the force of the river, from the ground and dedicated it.
EDCS-10300673.summary: A dedication to Caelestis Augusta Graniana, recording that Voltius Senecio relocated a temple damaged by a river and rededicated it.

EDCS-10300674.translation: Sacred to Saturn, the Divine. Gaius Octavius Successus gladly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-10300674.summary: A votive inscription dedicated to Saturn by Gaius Octavius Successus, who gladly fulfilled his vow.

EDCS-10300675.translation: To the Divine Saturn of Privatensis, the Divine. Apronius ACO SIS LB and a statue.
EDCS-10300675.summary: A dedication to Saturn of Privatensis, likely by an individual named Apronius, mentioning the dedication of a statue.

EDCS-10300677.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Celia Thyca, placed here.
EDCS-10300677.summary: A funerary inscription for Celia Thyca, indicating her burial place.

EDCS-10300678.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Quintus Sallustius lived 10 years; his most loving mother took care to have this made. He is placed here.
EDCS-10300678.summary: A funerary epitaph for Quintus Sallustius, recording his age and noting that his mother commissioned the monument.

EDCS-10300679.translation: Braciatus Gloriosus Simplicius AlexSandria Fedra Nilus ltus AR NXVI Lusius Morinus
EDCS-10300679.summary: This inscription appears to be a collection of names, possibly a funerary record or a list of individuals, with some unclear elements.

EDCS-10300680.translation: A sacred offering to the divine Caelestis. Lucius Egrilius Felix Maximus, of Praeneste, made this at the command of the goddess.
EDCS-10300680.summary: This votive inscription records an offering made by Lucius Egrilius Felix Maximus to the goddess Caelestis, likely in the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-10300681.translation: To the Augustan family. Publius Perelius Hedylus, perpetual priest, built the temple on private land, the first to do so with his own money.
EDCS-10300681.summary: This inscription records Publius Perelius Hedylus, a perpetual priest, building a temple for the Augustan family on his own land and expense, likely in the imperial period.

EDCS-10300686.summary: A dedication to the god Silvanus Augustus, likely from the imperial period.

EDCS-10300687.translation: Irene the pious lived for 35 years.
EDCS-10300687.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan of a woman named Irene.

EDCS-10300688.translation: Titus Gargilius Valens fulfilled his vow after a vision.
EDCS-10300688.summary: This votive inscription records Titus Gargilius Valens fulfilling a vow made after a divine vision.

EDCS-10300690.summary: An incomplete inscription likely dedicated to an emperor or high official, possibly Valentinian, from the late Roman period.

EDCS-10300691.translation: Flavius Caesar Ulpianus, with tribunician power for the 3rd time, consul for the 4th time, imperator for the 2nd time, also gave from 42,000 sesterces of revenues and from the fees with which he also gave...
EDCS-10300691.summary: This fragmentary inscription records financial contributions and honors bestowed upon Flavius Caesar Ulpianus, likely a high-ranking official, during the reign of Diocletian or Constantine.

EDCS-10300699.translation: The following are inscribed: Gallus Quirina Marullus, son of Publius, son of Praetextatus; Caius, son of Felix Repentinus; Lucius, son of Collina; Macer, son of Caius Arnensis; Probatus Cerennius, son of Lucius; Felix Memmius, son of Quintus Arnensis; Fuscus Marcus Dueldius, son of Marcus Arnensis; Crescens Lucius Manilius, son of Lucius; Quintus Annius, son of Quintus Arnensis; Tertullus Cnaeus Artorius, son of Cnaeus Palatina.
EDCS-10300699.summary: This inscription lists the names of several individuals, possibly members of a collegium or civic body, identified by their gentilicia, cognomina, and tribal affiliations, from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-10300705.summary: A fragmentary inscription mentioning the name Iulius Cassius Cem..., likely part of a longer dedication or epitaph from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-10300709.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Lucius Messius Gallus, a pious veteran, lived for 55 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-10300709.summary: This funerary epitaph records the death and burial of Lucius Messius Gallus, a pious veteran, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-10300710.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcus Clodius Rufus Caecilianus, son of Marcus, of the Arnensian tribe, priest of Ceres for 139 years, a pious man, lived 72 years and 9 months, and Caecilia Quartina, his daughter, a pious woman, lived 84 years. They are buried here.
EDCS-10300710.summary: A funerary epitaph for Marcus Clodius Rufus Caecilianus and his daughter Caecilia Quartina, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10300712.translation: Priest of Ceres for 158 years, aedile, quaestor, prefect for dispensing justice, in addition to 90,000 sesterces for the honor of the aedileship, which he would have cultivated, and furthermore adorned with marbles and for the dedication five days of games, statues, and other cultic expenses from his own funds.
EDCS-10300712.summary: An inscription detailing the financial contributions and public offices held by an individual, likely a local magistrate, in a Roman city.

EDCS-10300715.translation: To Quintus Fadius Fortis, citizen of Carthage.
EDCS-10300715.summary: A dedication or dedication fragment, possibly a tombstone, honoring Quintus Fadius Fortis in Carthage.

EDCS-10300716.translation: To Lucius Octavius Honoratus Avianus Flaccianus, son of Lucius, of the Pollian tribe.
EDCS-10300716.summary: An inscription honoring Lucius Octavius Honoratus Avianus Flaccianus, likely a dedication or funerary marker.

EDCS-10300717.translation: He restored it to a better appearance, under the care of Tertullus, a most distinguished citizen and of Carthage.
EDCS-10300717.summary: An inscription recording the restoration of a public work or building in Carthage, overseen by Tertullus.

EDCS-10300718.translation: To Quintus Voltedius Optatus Aurelianus, son of Lucius, flamen of the deified Nerva, admitted to the equestrian order by the deified Trajan, and by Emperor Caesar Hadrian Augustus to the five decuries, military tribune of the VI Victrix Pia Fidelis legion, aedile, prefect for dispensing justice, master of the rites of Ceres for 179 years, duovir, quinquennial duovir, who, having promised 200,000 sesterces for his honor, bequeathed 38,000 sesterces to the treasury, and with the increased funds provided a spectacle of gladiators and African animals in the amphitheater for four days, at public expense by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-10300718.summary: A lengthy inscription detailing the extensive public career and benefactions of Quintus Voltedius Optatus Aurelianus in a Roman city, likely during the Hadrianic period.

EDCS-10300719.translation: The quinquennial official, perpetual flamen, made this while alive.
EDCS-10300719.summary: An inscription indicating that a quinquennial official and perpetual flamen erected this monument during his lifetime.

EDCS-10300720.summary: A fragment of an inscription, likely funerary or commemorative, containing the words "eternal glory".

EDCS-10300732.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Felicitas, slave of Augustus, a pious woman, lived 20 years and one month. She is buried here.
EDCS-10300732.summary: A funerary epitaph for Felicitas, a slave of Augustus, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10300734.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Ieros, slave of Augustus, a pious man, lived 12 years, 12 days.

EDCS-10300846.translation: To Sextus Caecilius Aemilianus, son of Sextus, of the Quirina tribe, former Xvir for judging disputes, former VIIvir of the Epulones, quaestor, candidate for consul, governor with praetorian powers of the province of Africa, tribune of the plebs, patron by decree of the decurions, with public funds.

EDCS-10300849.translation: To Quintus Marcius Turbo, prefect of the praetorian guard, by decree of the decurions, with public funds.

EDCS-10300850.translation: To Quintus Numerius Rufus, son of Quintus, quaestor of the stipendiary districts of Muxsus, Gususus, and Zeugis.

EDCS-10300854.translation: augur, flamen of the divine [emperor?], admitted to the equestrian order, received into the place of his son, erected for one who deserved well.

EDCS-10300858.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Publius Bucius Celer, dutiful, lived 71 years and six months and twenty-two days. He is buried here. May your bones rest well. May the earth lie lightly upon you.

EDCS-10300860.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Quintus Sextilius Gallonius lived as many years as he could.
EDCS-10300860.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the underworld gods, recording the death of Quintus Sextilius Gallonius.

EDCS-10300862.translation: To Sabinia Tranquillina, Augusta, wife of our lord the Emperor Caesar Marcus Antonius Gordianus Pius Felix Augustus; the municipality of Aelius Thizika, devoted to their divine majesty and their glory, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-10300862.summary: This is a dedication by the town council of Aelius Thizika to Sabinia Tranquillina, wife of Emperor Gordian III, likely on a public monument.

EDCS-10300863.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Octavius Citrasus lived 71 years.

EDCS-10300868.translation: To Marcus Munius Primus Optatianus, Roman knight, perpetual priest, father of Marcus Munius Primus Statianus, most distinguished youth, citizen and patron, by the most splendid order of the citizens of the municipality of Aveddensium, who truly deserved it first.

EDCS-10300869.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Galbia Victoria, dutiful, lived 63 years. May your bones rest well.

EDCS-10300870.summary: This is a name inscription, likely for a tombstone or a dedicatory base.

EDCS-10300871.translation: Marcus Ulpius Menophoon, freedman of Augustus, assistant to Licinius Maximus and Felicior, procurators of Augustus, has paid his vow to the genius of the Trajanic aqueducts.

EDCS-10300882.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Quintus Rubrius, pious, lived 18 years. Buried here, may your bones rest well.
EDCS-10300882.summary: This funerary inscription records the age of Quintus Rubrius and expresses wishes for his repose.

EDCS-10300883.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Marcus Rubrius Melanus, pious, lived 13 years.
EDCS-10300883.summary: This funerary inscription records the age of Marcus Rubrius Melanus.

EDCS-10300884.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Iulius Zabog lived 70 years. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Furia Secunda lived 60 years.
EDCS-10300884.summary: This funerary inscription records the ages of two individuals, Iulius Zabog and Furia Secunda.

EDCS-10300885.translation: Tituleia Paula Rufina, a woman of the highest distinction, gave an altar of bronze as a gift to Augusta Diana.
EDCS-10300885.summary: This is a dedication to Diana Augusta by Tituleia Paula Rufina.

EDCS-10300886.translation: Sacred to Jupiter Optimus Maximus. Praetextatus Augustus [dedicated this].
EDCS-10300886.summary: This is a religious dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Praetextatus.

EDCS-10300887.translation: Lucius Fulvius Faustus, quaestor, former aedile, prefect with judicial authority, twice duovir, pious and dutiful, placed this at his own expense, valued at 5 million sesterces, as a mark of honor for his duovirate, to Publius Septimius Geta, most noble Caesar, prince of youth, son of the Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus Arabicus Adiabenicus Parthicus Maximus, father of the fatherland; brother of the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus Pius Felix, prince of youth, consul three times; nephew of the deified Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Germanicus Sarmaticus; great-nephew of the deified Antoninus Pius; great-great-nephew of the deified Hadrian; great-great-great-nephew of the deified Trajan Parthicus and the deified Nerva.
EDCS-10300887.summary: This extensive inscription is a dedication by Lucius Fulvius Faustus to the deceased Prince Geta, detailing Geta's imperial lineage and Faustus's own public career and expenditures, likely from the early 3rd century CE.

EDCS-10300889.translation: To Gaius Memmius Fidus Julius Albius, son of Gaius, of the Menenian tribe, of most illustrious memory, a man [of notable rank]. OV TP C PIR.
EDCS-10300889.summary: This is a dedication to Gaius Memmius Fidus Julius Albius, honoring his status and memory.

EDCS-10300893.translation: To Publius Marcius Felix, son of Publius, of the Quirina tribe, quaestor, aedile, duovir, and flamen, his most devoted father Caius Marcius Fortunatus made this with his own money.
EDCS-10300893.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by a father for his deceased son who had held several public offices, likely in the late 1st or early 2nd century CE.

EDCS-10300894.text_edition: \n Lucio Iulio Luci filio Quirina Cereali quaestori aedili praefecto iure dicundo flamini Augusti perpetuo municipi sui flamini Augusti provinciae Africae anni XXXX quem honorem ex municipio suo Bullensium Regiorum primus gessit huic cum provinciae Africae leg\n
EDCS-10300894.translation: To Lucius Iulius Cerealis, son of Lucius, of the Quirina tribe, quaestor, aedile, prefect for dispensing justice, perpetual Augustan flamen of his municipality, Augustan flamen of the province of Africa for 30 years, an honor which he was the first from his municipality of Bulla Regia to hold, this man, along with the province of Africa, [received]...
EDCS-10300894.summary: This inscription honors Lucius Iulius Cerealis with various civic and religious titles and outlines his distinguished career serving his municipality and the province of Africa, likely dating to the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-10300896.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcus Gargilius Augustalis, a soldier of the 1st City Cohort, devoted, lived 45 years, is buried here.
EDCS-10300896.summary: This epitaph records the death of a soldier of the 1st City Cohort who died at the age of 45, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-10300897.translation: Faustina, servant of Emperor Titus, Crescentis, her co-slave, lived 27 years, is buried here.
EDCS-10300897.summary: This epitaph commemorates Faustina, a slave belonging to Emperor Titus and a co-slave of Crescentis, who died at the age of 27, likely during the Flavian dynasty.

EDCS-10300898.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Gnaeus Julius Saturus Forticianus, a builder, with his family FV.
EDCS-10300898.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication by Gnaeus Julius Saturus Forticianus, a builder, for himself and his family, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-10300899.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Edinia Flacilla lived 27 years and 10 months, is buried here.
EDCS-10300899.summary: This epitaph records the death of Edinia Flacilla, who died at the age of 27 years and 10 months, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-10300903.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Publius Marcius Victor Hermetianus, devoted.

EDCS-10300905.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Lucius Tenatius Pudens, dutiful, lived for 57 years.

EDCS-10300916.translation: Publius Araneius Faustus, son of Publius, of the Arnensi tribe, a veteran, lived for 75 years. He placed this here for himself while alive.

EDCS-10300917.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Marcus Iulius Commodus, son of Marcus, of the Horatia tribe, former duovir.

EDCS-10300918.translation: Iulia Victoria, daughter of Marcus, a pious priestess, lived for 65 years.

EDCS-10300920.translation: He had undertaken several free legations, and after undertaking the legation of Italica, and a free one, he died in Ostia on his return from its completion. Pious, he lived for 32 years, 3 months, and 11 days.

EDCS-10301026.text_edition: \n Sextiliae Clodiae Fadianianillae filiae Luci Sextili Felicis Clodiani decurionis coloniae Antonianae Karthaginiensis res publica Thibaritanorum ob merita patris eius decreto decurionum pecunia publica dedicata ex VI Kalendas Ianuarias Modesto II et Probo consulibus\n
EDCS-10301026.translation: For Sextilia Clodia Fadianilla, daughter of Lucius Sextilius Felix Clodianus, decurion of the colony of Antoniana Karthago, the community of Thibaritanorum dedicated this from public funds, on the decree of the decurions, on account of the merits of her father, starting from the 6th day before the Kalends of January, when Modestus II and Probus were consuls.
EDCS-10301026.summary: This inscription records a public dedication by the community of Thibaritanorum to Sextilia Clodia Fadianilla, honoring the merits of her father, Lucius Sextilius Felix Clodianus, and is dated by the consulship of Modestus II and Probus in the early 3rd century CE.

EDCS-10301034.translation: Gaius Terentius Iulianus, proconsul, dedicated two colossal statues, which he promised for 30,000 sesterces, to the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus Armeniacus Medicus Parthicus Maximus Germanicus, son of the deified Antoninus Pius, brother of the deified Verus Parthicus Maximus, nephew of the deified Hadrian, great-nephew of the deified Trajan Parthicus, great-great-nephew of the deified Nerva, pontifex maximus, holding tribunician power for the 27th time, acclaimed imperator for the 6th time, consul for the 3rd time, father of the fatherland, for the honor of his priesthood.
EDCS-10301034.summary: This inscription records the dedication of two colossal statues by Gaius Terentius Iulianus to Emperor Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus, honoring his imperial titles and priesthood.

EDCS-10301035.translation: For the safety of the Emperors Caesar [Lucius] Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus Arabicus Adiabenicus Parthicus Maximus, father of the fatherland, and Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Felix [Augustus], and [Publius] Septimius Geta Augustus, and Julia Domna Augusta, mother of the Augusti and of the camps and of their entire divine household, the community of the municipium of Septimius Aurelius Liber, Thugga...
EDCS-10301035.summary: This inscription is a dedication for the safety of the ruling emperors, including Septimius Severus, Caracalla, Geta, and Julia Domna, by the community of the municipium of Thugga, likely dating to the early 3rd century CE.
