EDCS-10701951.translation: To Titus Arranius, son of Titus, of the Quirina tribe, Commodus, for his very cherished wife Crepereia, daughter of Quintus, who deserved exceedingly well of him.
EDCS-10701951.summary: This is a funerary dedication from Titus Arranius Commodus to his wife Crepereia Innula.

EDCS-10701954.translation: To Lord Augustus Saturn, Claudius Donatus gladly paid his vow. To Lord Augustus Saturn, Claudia Donata gladly paid her vow.
EDCS-10701954.summary: This inscription records a vow paid to Lord Augustus Saturn by Claudius Donatus and Claudia Donata, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-10701955.translation: Lucius Flavius Dexter gladly paid his vow to Saturn.
EDCS-10701955.summary: This inscription records Lucius Flavius Dexter paying a vow to Saturn, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10701956.translation: Honoratus and Saturnina to their children, propitious.
EDCS-10701956.summary: This inscription is a dedication by Honoratus and Saturnina to their children, likely a family monument from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10701957.translation: Sacred to Saturn, the Lord. Mas gladly paid his vow.
EDCS-10701957.summary: This inscription records a vow paid to Saturn, the Lord, by Mas, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10701958.translation: Max Ur paid his vow gladly.
EDCS-10701958.summary: This inscription records Max Ur paying a vow, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10702021.text_edition: \n Impperatoribus Diocletiano et Maximiano sennioribus Auggustis et Impperatoribus Constantio et Maximiano Auggustis et Severo et Maximino nobilissimis Caesaribus Marcus Valerius Victor vir perfectissimus praeses provinciae Mauretaniae Caesariensis novas portas turresque dedicavit provinciae CCLXVII\n
EDCS-10702021.translation: Under the Emperors Diocletian and Maximian, elder Augusti, and the Emperors Constantius and Maximian, Augusti, and Severus and Maximinus, most noble Caesars, Marcus Valerius Victor, most perfect man, praeses of the province of Mauretania Caesariensis, dedicated new gates and towers, in the province in the year 267.
EDCS-10702021.summary: This inscription records the dedication of new gates and towers by Marcus Valerius Victor, the governor of Mauretania Caesariensis, under a tetrarchic imperial administration, dated to 267 (likely from the founding of the province or a regnal year).

EDCS-10900694.translation: Of Marcus Laurentius Silanus, the father.
EDCS-10900694.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription that likely records the name of Marcus Laurentius Silanus, father, possibly as part of a funerary monument or a dedication.

EDCS-10900697.summary: This inscription simply records the name Tiberius Claudius Orfitus, likely as an owner or dedicatee of a monument.

EDCS-10900698.text_edition: \n Diis Manibus Aristonis Adrumucus sua pecunia fecit Diodorus Adrumucus frater curavit\n
EDCS-10900698.translation: To the Divine Shades. Aristo Adrumucus made this at his own expense. Diodorus Adrumucus, his brother, arranged it.
EDCS-10900698.summary: This funerary inscription records that Aristo Adrumucus commissioned his tomb at his own expense, and his brother Diodorus Adrumucus oversaw its construction.

EDCS-10900699.text_edition: \n Diis Manibus fecit Marcus Eppi<us=I> sibi et suis et patrona sua \n
EDCS-10900699.translation: To the Divine Shades. Marcus Eppius made this for himself and for his family and for his patroness.
EDCS-10900699.summary: This is a funerary inscription where Marcus Eppius dedicated a tomb for himself, his family, and his patroness.

EDCS-10900700.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Luciae Siliae Luci filiae Piae Lucius Silius Plautius Haterianus vir clarissimus patruus heres fecit\n
EDCS-10900700.translation: To the Divine Shades. For Lucia Silia Pia, daughter of Lucius. Lucius Silius Plautius Haterianus, a most distinguished man, his uncle and heir, made this.
EDCS-10900700.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Lucia Silia Pia and states that the monument was erected by her uncle and heir, Lucius Silius Plautius Haterianus.

EDCS-10900707.translation: Legio III Augusta demarcated during the proconsulship of Gaius Vibius Marsus.
EDCS-10900707.summary: This inscription records a demarcation by Legio III Augusta during the proconsulship of Gaius Vibius Marsus, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10900709.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Aemilia Decimi filia Aprulla pia vixit annis LXXXXIII mensibus II hic sita est Dis Manibus sacrum Nabor Felicis Balsillecis Maraxae pius vixit nnos LXXX hic situs est\n
EDCS-10900709.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Aemilia Aprulla, daughter of Decimus, of the Balsillecis family, pious, lived 93 years and 2 months. She is buried here. Sacred to the Divine Shades. Nabor Felicis Maraxus, pious, lived 80 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-10900709.summary: This funerary inscription records the burials and lifespans of two individuals, Aemilia Aprulla and Nabor Felicis Maraxus, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10900710.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Publius Iulius Sanus Maximinus vixit annum menses III horas IIII caementarius hic situs\n
EDCS-10900710.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Publius Iulius Sanus Maximinus lived for one year, three months, and four hours; a builder, buried here.
EDCS-10900710.summary: This funerary inscription records the death and burial of Publius Iulius Sanus Maximinus, a builder, with details of his age at death.

EDCS-10900711.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Lucius Stiadurius Rogati, dutiful son, lived 70 years; here he rests.
EDCS-10900711.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Stiadurius Rogati, recording his name, parentage, age at death, and burial, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10900712.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Quintus Magnius Felix, a dutiful veteran, lived 70 years; here he rests.
EDCS-10900712.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Quintus Magnius Felix, a veteran, recording his name, age at death, and burial, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10900713.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. The son of Sturius Maximus lived 75 years; here he rests.
EDCS-10900713.summary: This is a funerary inscription for the son of Sturius Maximus, recording his age at death and burial, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10900714.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Acrontia Bereggal lived 58 years; here she rests. Sacred to the Divine Shades. Marcus Caninius Barih lived 68 years; here he rests.
EDCS-10900714.summary: This inscription contains two funerary notices for Acrontia Bereggal and Marcus Caninius Barih, recording their names, ages at death, and burials, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10900715.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Saturninus, son of Paetus, lived 66 years; he is buried here. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Licinia Auriola lived 65 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-10900715.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Saturninus and Licinia Auriola, recording their ages and burial.

EDCS-10900716.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Nonia Rufina, dutiful, lived 70 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-10900716.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Nonia Rufina, recording her age and burial.

EDCS-10900717.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. S[---]nus, son of Faustus and Quintus Verus, pious, lived 62 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-10900717.summary: This is a funerary inscription for S[---]nus, son of Faustus and Quintus Verus, recording his age and burial.

EDCS-10900718.translation: Quintus Geminius Valens, son of Quintus, of the Arnensis tribe, decorated the estate with statues for Manilia.
EDCS-10900718.summary: This inscription records Quintus Geminius Valens decorating an estate with statues for Manilia.

EDCS-10900720.translation: Adeodatus lived 20 years in peace. Died on the Nones of November.
EDCS-10900720.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Adeodatus, recording his age at death and the date of his passing.

EDCS-10900722.translation: To Celesi, a sweet son, while alive, in peace.
EDCS-10900722.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Celesi, referred to as a sweet son.

EDCS-10900723.translation: Cresconia, a faithful virgin, lived 15 years, 6 months, 25 days. Died on the 13th day before the Kalends of August.
EDCS-10900723.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Cresconia, recording her age at death and the date of her passing.

EDCS-10900724.translation: Donata, innocent, while alive, in peace.
EDCS-10900724.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Donata, described as innocent.

EDCS-10900725.translation: Elvia, faithful, lived 16 years, 2 months, 20 days, while alive, in peace. Died on the 4th day before the Nones of March. Saturnina, faithful, lived 16 years, 1 month, 21 days, while alive, in peace. Died on the 14th day before the Kalends of May.
EDCS-10900725.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Elvia and Saturnina, recording their ages at death and the dates of their passing.

EDCS-10900726.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Felix, recording his age at death.

EDCS-10900727.translation: Honorius the father lived 80 years, Honorius the son lived 60 years, Maura the mother lived 90 years, all faithful in peace.
EDCS-10900727.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespans of three individuals: Honorius the father, Honorius the son, and Maura the mother.

EDCS-10900728.translation: ... who was also Iader, finished in peace in September.
EDCS-10900728.summary: This fragmentary funerary inscription records the completion of a life, likely a death date, for an individual named Iader.

EDCS-10900729.translation: Ingeniosa lived 2 years and 9 months, she returned on the 8th day before the Kalends of July.
EDCS-10900729.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespan of Ingeniosa, who died at the age of 2 years and 9 months, and gives her death date.

EDCS-10900730.summary: This funerary inscription records the short lifespan of Lampadia, who lived only 100 days.

EDCS-10900731.summary: This very brief funerary inscription simply states the name Homuncio and that they are 'in peace'.

EDCS-10900732.translation: Paullina lived 60 years, Tutus the innocent, in peace.
EDCS-10900732.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespan of Paullina and mentions Tutus, both 'in peace'.

EDCS-10900733.translation: Primiani the father lived 51 years, Restituta the daughter lived 26 years.
EDCS-10900733.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespans of Primiani the father and Restituta the daughter.

EDCS-10900735.translation: Secunda lived 24 years, Tzelica lived 55 years, faithful in peace.
EDCS-10900735.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespans of Secunda and Tzelica, identified as 'faithful in peace'.

EDCS-10900738.text_edition: \n Clodius Quartus filius ex Taeis vixit annis XXV posuit pietatis causa ex |(centurione) Caius Iulius hic situs est\n
EDCS-10900738.translation: Clodius Quartus, son of Taia, lived for 25 years. Caius Iulius, buried here, erected this out of filial piety. He was a centurion.
EDCS-10900738.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Clodius Quartus, erected by Caius Iulius, a former centurion, out of filial piety.

EDCS-11300842.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription, likely a tombstone, commemorating Corneli Bassus.

EDCS-11300858.translation: Of Lucius Silius Amicus, a most distinguished man.
EDCS-11300858.summary: This inscription likely records the name and status of Lucius Silius Amicus, possibly a tombstone or dedication.

EDCS-11300863.summary: This inscription likely records the name of Marcus Junius Crescens, possibly a tombstone or dedication.

EDCS-11300865.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Geminius Orfitianus miles cohortis XI urbanae vixit annis XXXVIIII hic situs est Geminius Restutus filio pio posuit Dis Manibus sacrum Sornia Maxima vixit annis XXXVI hic sita est Geminius Restutus matri pie posuit Dis Manibus sacrum Lucius Geminius Pusissus vixit annis LVII hic situs est Geminius Restutus patri posuit Dis Manibus sacrum Quintus Geminius Salfenius Quirina vixit annis L filii patri optimo pio posuerunt hic situs est\n
EDCS-11300865.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Geminius Orfitianus, a soldier of the 11th Urban Cohort, lived for 39 years; he is buried here. Geminius Restutus erected this for his pious son. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Sornia Maxima lived for 36 years; she is buried here. Geminius Restutus erected this for his pious mother. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Lucius Geminius Pusissus lived for 57 years; he is buried here. Geminius Restutus erected this for his excellent and pious father. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Quintus Geminius Salfenius and Quirina erected this for their most excellent and pious father; he is buried here.
EDCS-11300865.summary: This extensive funerary inscription records the deaths and burial places of multiple family members, with Geminius Restutus acting as the dedicator for his father, mother, and son.

EDCS-11300866.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Sornia Maxima lived 36 years, she lies here. Geminius Restutus placed this for his pious mother.
EDCS-11300866.summary: This funerary inscription is a dedication by Geminius Restutus to his mother, Sornia Maxima, recording her age at death.

EDCS-11300867.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Geminius Pusissus lived 57 years, he lies here. Geminius Restutus placed this for his father.
EDCS-11300867.summary: This funerary inscription is a dedication by Geminius Restutus to his father, Lucius Geminius Pusissus, recording his age at death.

EDCS-11300868.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus Geminius Salfenius, of the tribe Quirina, lived 50 years. His sons erected this to their most excellent, devoted father. He is buried here.
EDCS-11300868.summary: A funerary epitaph for Quintus Geminius Salfenius, erected by his sons, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-11300870.text_edition: \n Cal Fol Dis Manibus sacrum Mevius Ingenuus vixit nnos XXXIII hic situs est Marcus Mevius Campesis veteranus legionis III Augustae piae vindicis fratri pio posuit Dis Manibus sacrum Marcus Mevius Campesis veteranus legionis III Augustae piae vindicis vixit nnos ipse se vivo fecit\n
EDCS-11300870.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Mevius Ingenuus lived for 33 years; he is buried here. Marcus Mevius Campesis, a veteran of the Third Augustan Legion, pious and victorious, erected this for his pious brother. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Marcus Mevius Campesis, a veteran of the Third Augustan Legion, pious and victorious, made this for himself while alive.
EDCS-11300870.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Mevius Ingenuus, dedicated by his brother, and also records a self-made monument by Marcus Mevius Campesis, a veteran of the Third Augustan Legion.

EDCS-11300873.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Fabia Dativa vixit annis XXXX hic sita est Marcus Mevius Campesis veteranus legionis III Augustae piae vindicis uxori piae fecit\n
EDCS-11300873.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Fabia Dativa lived for 40 years; she is buried here. Marcus Mevius Campesis, a veteran of the Third Augustan Legion, pious and victorious, made this for his pious wife.
EDCS-11300873.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Fabia Dativa, erected by her husband, Marcus Mevius Campesis, a veteran of the Third Augustan Legion.

EDCS-11300874.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Naevius Silanus, a soldier with 6 years of service, lived 30 years. His devoted uncle, Titus Octavius Felix, set this up.
EDCS-11300874.summary: A funerary epitaph for Naevius Silanus, a soldier, erected by his uncle, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-11300875.text_edition: \n Lucius Pacuvius Servatus veteranus legionis III Augustae vixit nnos LXXV militavit nnos hic situs est Pacuvii Felix et Claudia filii patri poserunt\n
EDCS-11300875.translation: Lucius Pacuvius Servatus, a veteran of the Third Augustan Legion, lived for 75 years; he served [for X years]; he is buried here. His children, Pacuvii Felix and Claudia, erected this for their father.
EDCS-11300875.summary: This funerary inscription records the death and military service of Lucius Pacuvius Servatus, a veteran, erected by his children.

EDCS-11300876.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Allius Iucundinus vixit annos XLV hic situs est Ianuaria uxor marito amantissimo pio posuit Dis Manibus sacrum Petilia Romana vixit annos LXV hic sita est Allius Fortunatio uxori piae posuit IVVIT Dis Manibus sacrum Petilius Rusticus miles praetorianus |(duplicarius qui vixit annos XXVIII Allius Fortunatio pater filio p(osuit)\n
EDCS-11300876.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Allius Iucundinus lived for 45 years; he is buried here. Ianuaria, his wife, erected this for her most loving and pious husband. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Petilia Romana lived for 65 years; she is buried here. Allius Fortunatio erected this for his pious wife. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Petilius Rusticus, a praetorian soldier, a duplicarius, lived for 28 years. Allius Fortunatio, his father, erected this for his son.
EDCS-11300876.summary: This funerary inscription records the deaths of Allius Iucundinus and Petilia Romana, with dedications by their spouses, and the death of Petilius Rusticus, a praetorian soldier, dedicated by his father.

EDCS-11300877.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Petilia Romana lived 65 years. Allius Fortunatio erected this to his devoted wife. She is buried here.
EDCS-11300877.summary: A funerary epitaph for Petilia Romana, erected by her husband, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-11300878.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Petilius Rusticus, a praetorian guardsman and duplicarius, who lived 28 years. Allius Fortunatio, his father, erected this to his son.
EDCS-11300878.summary: A funerary epitaph for Petilius Rusticus, a soldier in the Praetorian Guard, erected by his father, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-11300879.text_edition: \n Lucius Regilius Titi filius Galeria Luguduno cornicen legionis III Augustae |(centuria) Gennii Maioris vixit annis X militavit annos XIX hic situs est cornicines commilitoni posuerunt\n
EDCS-11300879.translation: To Lucius Regilius, son of Titus, of the Galeria tribe, from Lugdunum, a cornicen of the Third Augustan Legion, in the century of Gnaeus Maior. He lived 10 years, served 19 years. He is buried here. His fellow soldiers erected this for their comrade.
EDCS-11300879.summary: This funerary monument records Lucius Regilius, a cornicen of the Third Augustan Legion, erected by his fellow soldiers.

EDCS-11300880.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Octaviae Sterceiae Lucius Sempronius Liberalis signifer legionis III Augustae post annos XVI stipendiorum matri posuit\n
EDCS-11300880.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Lucius Sempronius Liberalis, standard-bearer of the Third Augustan Legion, erected this for his mother, Octavia Sterceia, after 16 years of service.
EDCS-11300880.summary: This funerary monument is dedicated by Lucius Sempronius Liberalis, a standard-bearer of the Third Augustan Legion, to his mother Octavia Sterceia.

EDCS-11300881.text_edition: \n miles legionis III Augustae centuria Volusi hic situs est militauit annos XVI vixit annos XXXV Caius Iulius Rufus comanupularis de suo curavit\n
EDCS-11300881.translation: A soldier of the Third Augustan Legion, in the century of Volusius. He is buried here. He served 16 years, lived 35 years. Caius Julius Rufus, a comrade, took care of this from his own funds.
EDCS-11300881.summary: This funerary monument commemorates a soldier of the Third Augustan Legion, who served for 16 years and lived for 35 years, with the expenses covered by a fellow soldier named Caius Julius Rufus.

EDCS-11300884.text_edition: \n Gaius Iulius Africanus i C vixsit sic nnos LI Gaius Iulius Dux |(centurio) pater \n
EDCS-11300884.translation: Gaius Julius Africanus lived 51 years. His father, Gaius Julius Dux, a centurion, [erected this].
EDCS-11300884.summary: This funerary monument records the life of Gaius Julius Africanus, who lived 51 years, and was dedicated by his father, a centurion.

EDCS-11300886.translation: A soldier of the Legio III Augusta lived 35 years.
EDCS-11300886.summary: A fragmentary epitaph for a soldier of the Legio III Augusta, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-11300890.translation: Caius Iulius Philomusus, freedman of Maxsumus, is buried here. He lived 40 years.
EDCS-11300890.summary: A funerary epitaph for Caius Iulius Philomusus, a freedman, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-11300891.text_edition: \n Frugifero Augusto sacrum pro salute Imperatoris Caesaris Luci Septimi Severi Pii Pertinacis Augusti Parthici Arabici Parthici Adiabenici pontificis maximi patris patriae decuriones cives Romani aedem de sportulis fecerunt idemque dedicaverunt\n
EDCS-11300891.translation: Sacred to the fruitful Augustus. For the health of the Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus, Parthicus Arabicus, Parthicus Adiabenicus, pontifex maximus, father of the fatherland. The decurions and Roman citizens built the temple from their contributions and dedicated it.
EDCS-11300891.summary: This inscription records the construction and dedication of a temple to Emperor Septimius Severus by the decurions and citizens for his health.

EDCS-11500953.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Lucius Aelius Saturninus lived 7 years.
EDCS-11500953.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Lucius Aelius Saturninus, who died at the age of seven.

EDCS-11501106.summary: A funerary epitaph for Bassida Crescentia, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-11600225.translation: Montanus, a faithful presbyter, lived 97 years in peace. He was buried on the 4th day before the Nones of July.
EDCS-11600225.summary: A funerary epitaph for Montanus, a Christian presbyter, dating to the Late Roman period based on the mention of 'in pace' and consul dating.

EDCS-11600226.translation: Dalmatia, a sacred virgin, faithful Martiana, faithful, lived [in peace].
EDCS-11600226.summary: A funerary epitaph for Dalmatia, a Christian virgin, likely dating to the Late Roman period.

EDCS-11600227.translation: Alas, how short life is; this order displeases everyone. Hadrian, an infant, killed by a sword by a foe's persuasion. His father Andronicus left [this life]. Your youth will mourn. You lie in Christ, faithful, one year, 2 months, 27 days you lived. Siricus was killed. Buried on the day before the Kalends of January, under consuls Antonio and Syagrio. Andronicus lies here.
EDCS-11600227.summary: A complex Christian funerary epitaph commemorating the infant Hadrian, who was murdered, and his father Andronicus, with a Greek inscription at the end, dating to the consulship of Antonius and Syagrius (likely 305 AD).

EDCS-11600228.text_edition: \n Faustino Felicis Sidiathonis filio flamini Augusti perpetuo civitas Thuggensis ob meritum\n
EDCS-11600228.translation: To Faustinus, son of Felix Sidiathon, perpetual flamen of Augustus. The community of Thugga [honors him] for his merit.
EDCS-11600228.summary: The community of Thugga honors Faustinus, son of Felix Sidiathon and perpetual flamen of Augustus, for his merit.

EDCS-11600230.text_edition: \n L(ucio) Calpurnio Felici civitas Thuggensis ob merita et ipsius et patris eius Faustini curatoribus Iulio Rogato Mucio Kapitone\n
EDCS-11600230.translation: To Lucius Calpurnius Felix. The community of Thugga [honors him] for his merits and those of his father Faustinus, with Julius Rogatus Mucio Capito as curators.
EDCS-11600230.summary: The community of Thugga honors Lucius Calpurnius Felix and his father Faustinus for their merits, with specific curators mentioned.

EDCS-11600232.translation: Sacred to Minerva Augusta, from the will of Quintus Vinnicius Genialis, son of Quintus, of the Arnensian tribe, priest of Ceres, aged 127, quaestor, prefect of justice, duumvir of the colony of Concordia Iulia Karthago, patron of the state of Thugga; from 10,000 sesterces, twenty percent of the tax revenue for the Roman people, he gave this gift to the state, with Gaius Marius Perpetuus, patron of the state, as curator.
EDCS-11600232.summary: This is a dedication to Minerva Augusta funded by the will of Quintus Vinnicius Genialis, a prominent local official and priest, who bequeathed funds for a gift to the state of Karthago, with Gaius Marius Perpetuus serving as curator.

EDCS-11600235.text_edition: \n Mercurio Augusto sacrum Lucius Liconius Rogatianus \n
EDCS-11600235.translation: Sacred to Mercury Augustus. Lucius Liconius Rogatianus [erected this].
EDCS-11600235.summary: This inscription records a sacred dedication to Mercury Augustus, likely erected by Lucius Liconius Rogatianus.

EDCS-11600240.text_edition: \n Aulus Gabinius Quirina Datus patronus pagi et civitatis Thuggensis Marcus Gabinius Quirina Bassus flamen Augusti perpetuus patronus pagi et civitatis nomine suo et Auli Gabini Dati filii in quinque decuriis ab Imperatore Caesare Traiano Hadriano Augusto adlecto sic patroni pagi et civitatis templa solo suo a fundamentis sua pecunia struxerunt itemque dedicaverunt Aulus Gabinius Quirina Datus patronus pagi et civitatis Thuggensis Marcus Gabinius Quirina Bassus flamen Augusti perpetuus patronus pagi et civitatis templa Concordiae Frugiferi Liberi Patris cum reliquis templis et xystis solo suo a fundamentis sua pecunia struxerunt in quod opus cum HS Lmilia promisissent multiplicata pecunia consummaverunt\n
EDCS-11600240.translation: Aulus Gabinius Datus, Quirina tribe, patron of the pagus and community of Thugga, and Marcus Gabinius Bassus, Quirina tribe, perpetual flamen of Augustus, patron of the pagus and community, in his own name and that of his son Aulus Gabinius Datus, who was appointed to the five decuries by the Emperor Caesar Trajan Hadrianus Augustus, [state that] as patrons of the pagus and community, they built the temples of Concordia and Liber Pater Frugiferus, along with other temples and xysti, on their own land from the foundations with their own money, and likewise dedicated them; although they promised 50,000 sesterces for this work, they completed it with the money multiplied.
EDCS-11600240.summary: This inscription details the construction and dedication of several temples, including those of Concordia and Liber Pater Frugiferus, by patrons Aulus Gabinius Datus and Marcus Gabinius Bassus for the community of Thugga, funded substantially from their own resources.

EDCS-11600241.text_edition: \n Lucio Tadio Luci filio Horatia Vero Caeciliano praefecto iure dicundo aedili quaestori equo publico et in quinque decurias adlecto sacerdoti nni CLXXX Uchitani Maiores patrono ob merita\n
EDCS-11600241.translation: To Lucius Tadius Verus Caecilianus, son of Lucius, of the Horatia tribe, who served as praefect, judge, aedile, quaestor, was a member of the equestrian order and appointed to one of the five decuries, priest of the Uchitani Maiores, for his merits as patron.
EDCS-11600241.summary: This inscription is a dedication honoring Lucius Tadius Verus Caecilianus for his public service and patronage, likely erected by the Uchitani Maiores community.

EDCS-11600249.summary: This is a short religious dedication to the goddess Laverna.

EDCS-11600251.translation: To Marcus Attius Cornelianus, admitted to the equestrian order.
EDCS-11600251.summary: This is a dedication to Marcus Attius Cornelianus, who was admitted to the equestrian order.

EDCS-11700293.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Cai Caelei Tharridae Faustiani vixit nnos XVIII semissem hic situs est\n

EDCS-11800655.translation: January, February, June, July, September, November, December, Martian, April, May, August, October.

EDCS-11800743.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Dead. Aemilia Faustilla lived for 100 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-11800743.summary: A funerary inscription for Aemilia Faustilla, stating her age and burial.

EDCS-11800744.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Dead. Quintus Lurius Flaminalis, pious, lived for 75 years. Cerialis made and dedicated this to his father. Sacred to the Spirits of the Dead. Minucia Fundana, pious, lived for 31 years. Cerialis, her son, made and dedicated this.
EDCS-11800744.summary: Two funerary inscriptions side-by-side, one for Quintus Lurius Flaminalis and one for Minucia Fundana, both commissioned by their respective children.

EDCS-12000419.translation: Sacred to Ceres Augusta for the safety of the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Severus Alexander Pius Felix Augustus, and Julia Mamaea Augusta, mother of the Emperor, the senate, the army, and the fatherland. The duty, which Iulia, daughter of Quintus, of honored memory, flaminica, having imitated her parents and ancestors who were benefactors to their fatherland, that is Caius Julius Felinianus, son of Caius, perpetual flamen, who placed a statue of Jupiter Victor in the forum for his fatherland, promised with the decree of the entire order, with the legal sum paid in due time, and more, for the most honorable curia of the first class Augusta, she granted a sum of money worthy, from the interest of which, reduced annually, she would provide a banquet in perpetuity and gave it as a gift, and upon her death she ordered a banquet to be given to the curiae for the dedication. Her brother Quintus Julius Felix, and Julius Homullus and Julius Honoratus, the statue brought by her, they erected and, after giving the banquet to the curiae, dedicated it.
EDCS-12000419.summary: A complex dedication by Iulia, daughter of Quintus and flaminica, for the imperial family's safety, honoring her ancestors, and establishing funds for banquets and a statue to Jupiter Victor, with her family completing the dedication.

EDCS-12200329.translation: For the invincible Augustus, for the safety of our Claudianus. Kalendio, a house-born slave, made this.
EDCS-12200329.summary: A dedication by a slave named Kalendio for the well-being of his master, Claudianus, and the emperor.

EDCS-12200330.translation: Sarus Pomponius Equanus willingly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-12200330.summary: This inscription records Sarus Pomponius Equanus fulfilling a vow, likely on a votive monument, from an unknown date.

EDCS-12200332.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Aurelius Martialis lived 95 years. Aurelius Felix made this for his father.

EDCS-12200348.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Quintilla lived 102 years. C.M. made this for one who deserved well; she is buried here.

EDCS-12200349.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Rufus lived 70 years.

EDCS-12300002.translation: May the earth not press too heavily upon your tender shade, departed Honorata; may the gods above lead you to the lowest realms. Your daughter places her body and soul here for you, Thunderer; I shall depart, a daughter bidding farewell. Having completed twice four years, she rendered the debt of life, laid to rest on the eighth day before the Ides of April, in the 14th indiction.
EDCS-12300002.summary: This epitaph commemorates Honorata, detailing her age at death and the grief of her daughter.

EDCS-12300004.translation: This is the place where Benenata, also called Iambaria, a chaste woman, was laid to rest on the 12th day before the Kalends of December, in the 11th indiction, and she lived in peace for more or less 30 years.
EDCS-12300004.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Benenata (Iambaria), a chaste woman, noting her lifespan and date of burial.

EDCS-12300005.translation: A table for the Holy Spirit of the innocent Nutricosus; he lived 2 years, 10 months.
EDCS-12300005.summary: This epitaph records the short life of Nutricosus, likely a child, possibly associated with a religious context.

EDCS-12300007.translation: Caecilia Victoria lived 70 years, 3 months, 5 days, 2 hours.

EDCS-12300010.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulius Iuilida lived faithfully in peace for 25 years, three months, seventeen days. He is buried here.
EDCS-12300010.summary: This epitaph is a dedication to the departed spirits for Iulius Iuilida, noting his lifespan and faithfulness.

EDCS-12300011.translation: Redemtus lived in peace for 12 years, 5 months, 7 hours.
EDCS-12300011.summary: This epitaph records the lifespan of Redemtus.

EDCS-12300012.summary: This is an incomplete epitaph for Villaticus, only recording his name and the start of his lifespan.

EDCS-12300014.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Mellita, faithful, lived in peace for more or less 75 years, 12 hours.
EDCS-12300014.summary: This epitaph is a dedication to the departed spirits for Mellita, noting her faithfulness and lifespan.

EDCS-12300017.translation: Ematia, faithful, lived for 70 years. She died on the 4th day before the Nones of February, at the first hour.
EDCS-12300017.summary: This epitaph records the lifespan and precise date and hour of death for Ematia.

EDCS-12300018.translation: If there is any honor in life, it is a witness after the gifts of fate; it is revealed by the lot of death when now, at the supreme end, one beholds the infernal temples of the gods of Acheron and sees the tumult of greedy Acheron. For I myself, because I lived always in a pious body, hold the gentle fields of Proserpina, and I know the laws of the gods, the sun above, and the stars. Iulia Mo Benenata, an honorable woman, lived 83 years, 10 months, in peace. She is buried here.
EDCS-12300018.summary: This epitaph for Iulia Mo Benenata, an honorable woman who lived 83 years and 10 months, includes a lengthy poem reflecting on death and the afterlife, typical of late antique Christian or pagan funerary contexts.

EDCS-12300019.translation: Hildeguns lived 40 years and 10 days in peace.

EDCS-12300020.translation: Paulus the faithful lived 13 years, 4 months, and 9 days in peace.
EDCS-12300020.summary: An epitaph for Paulus, identified as faithful, stating he lived 13 years, 4 months, and 9 days.

EDCS-12300021.translation: Honorata the faithful lived about 14 years and 6 hours in peace.
EDCS-12300021.summary: An epitaph for Honorata, described as faithful, recording her lifespan as approximately 14 years and 6 hours.

EDCS-12300023.translation: Paulinus the faithful, son of Iulius Med, lived about [---] years in peace.

EDCS-12300026.translation: Binaticus the cleric lived 14 years, 9 days, and 2 hours in peace.
EDCS-12300026.summary: An epitaph for Binaticus the cleric, stating he lived 14 years, 9 days, and 2 hours.

EDCS-12300027.translation: Bonifaniftia the faithful lived 6 years, 7 days, and 5 hours in peace.

EDCS-12300028.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Biziacinus the faithful lived two years and 10 months in peace.
EDCS-12300028.summary: A funerary inscription dedicated to the 'Dis Manibus' (departed spirits), for Biziacinus the faithful, who lived two years and 10 months.

EDCS-12300029.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Fid [rests] in peace.

EDCS-12300030.translation: Aurelius Nutricosus lived in peace for 35 years, 6 months, and 20 days.
EDCS-12300030.summary: This epitaph records the lifespan of Aurelius Nutricosus, who lived for 35 years, 6 months, and 20 days, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12300031.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulia Fortunata lived in peace for 71 years, 3 months, and 5 hours. May you rest well. Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulia Cattosa lived faithfully with her husband for 50 years, 7 months, and 12 hours. May you rest well.
EDCS-12300031.summary: This funerary inscription honors two women, Iulia Fortunata and Iulia Cattosa, detailing their lifespans and expressing wishes for their peaceful afterlife, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12300032.summary: This is a very brief epitaph commemorating a faithful individual named Musilus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12300034.translation: Constantinus, born of Paulinus and Honorata, overcoming the rage of his enemies with the trophy of faith, destined to reign eternally with Christ, lived 34 years and 8 months, his last day closing, laid to rest on the 13th day before the Kalends of May, in the fourteenth indiction.
EDCS-12300034.summary: This epitaph records the life and death of Constantinus, highlighting his victory through faith and his eternal reign with Christ, with specific dates provided, likely from the Late Roman or Early Byzantine period.

EDCS-12300396.summary: This epitaph records the lifespan of Bonifatius, a priest, who lived for 78 years, likely from the Late Roman or Early Christian period.

EDCS-12300397.translation: Margarita lived in peace for more or less 8 years.
EDCS-12300397.summary: This epitaph states that Margarita lived in peace for approximately 8 years, likely from the Roman Imperial or Early Christian period.

EDCS-12300398.translation: I [A]IARA, the envious, lived for 27 years, 1 month, and 8 days.
EDCS-12300398.summary: This epitaph records the lifespan of I[A]IARA, the envious, who lived for 27 years, 1 month, and 8 days, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12300401.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Vincomalos the presbyter lived for 60 years and in the presbyterate for [---] days.

EDCS-12300402.translation: Here are the names of the holy martyrs Da[---], Dasi, Abdasi, Iacobi, Am[---], and the boy [---] on the day [---].

EDCS-12300404.translation: The presbyter lived for 15 days and 1 hour.

EDCS-12300407.translation: Donatus the faithful lived in peace for 4 years and 10 days.

EDCS-12300408.translation: Tetta the faithful lived for 2 years and 6 months.

EDCS-12300419.translation: Redenta, loyal, lived for 10 years and 8 days.

EDCS-12300424.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Elegius lived here in peace.

EDCS-12300429.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Caecilius Donatus lived here in peace for thirty-five years, 2 months, and 5 days. May you rest in peace.
EDCS-12300429.summary: This is a detailed funerary epitaph for Caecilius Donatus, specifying his age at death and including a common funerary wish, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12300430.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Crescitura the faithful lived here in peace for one year and five hours.
EDCS-12300430.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Crescitura, emphasizing her faithfulness and specifying her very short lifespan, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12300431.translation: Dalmatia the faithful lived for 1 innocent year.
EDCS-12300431.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Dalmatia, highlighting her faithfulness and innocence during her first year of life, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12300432.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Iulia Preiecta lived here in peace for 62 years.
EDCS-12300432.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Iulia Preiecta, recording her peaceful life and age at death, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12300433.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Elpizia lived here in peace for 10 months.
EDCS-12300433.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Elpizia, recording her peaceful life and short lifespan, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12300435.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Promissas, holy one, render unto the homes, best father of the world. Not privately does he desire Rome in the ancient city, he came to Christ. He perished after 3 years, 5 months, and 30 days.

EDCS-12300436.translation: Rupilia Luciana lived in peace, faithful, for 16 years, 5 months, 16 days, and 5 hours.
EDCS-12300436.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Rupilia Luciana, recording her age at death.

EDCS-12300437.translation: In the year of the Lord, Umbria, an honorable woman, faithful, lived for 69 years, 7 months, and 3 days in peace.

EDCS-12400001.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Alexander lived for 70 years and 5 months.

EDCS-12400004.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Cattinosus, faithful, lived in peace for 23 years and 6 months.

EDCS-12400007.translation: EVIPAC IV lived in peace for ... years.

EDCS-12400010.translation: From Tiberia, in peace and rest.

EDCS-12400011.translation: Bassila, faithful, lived in peace for 18 years, 2 months, and 17 days. Sacred to the spirits of the departed.
EDCS-12400011.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to the Manes and records the lifespan of Bassila.

EDCS-12400015.summary: This funerary inscription describes Cassius Vitulus as innocent and faithful, and records his very young age at death.

EDCS-12400016.translation: Christ. Lived in peace for 8 years. Worthy to die. Tomb light and cruel love, which only your parents could [give to] your daughter.

EDCS-12400017.translation: Rupilia Fedosa lived 2 years, 5 months, 10 days, 12 hours.

EDCS-12400019.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Mensa Buci.

EDCS-12400020.translation: Victorinus lived 13 years, 4 months, 8 days, 1 hour in peace.
EDCS-12400020.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Victorinus, dated to the Christian era.

EDCS-12400021.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Fortuna fidelis.

EDCS-12400022.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Morosuus.

EDCS-12400023.translation: QV E lived 60 years and two months, on the seventh day before the Kalends of April.
EDCS-12400023.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of QV E, with a precise date of death.

EDCS-12400031.translation: E IIMINA castimonialis lived 60 years in peace.
EDCS-12400031.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of E IIMINA castimonialis.

EDCS-12400032.translation: Innocentia, untouched by worldly life, holds the Elysian fields with her spouse; our Roman innocence gave birth to us, and Italian soil. She lived in peace from the Kalends of May in the consulship of Flavius tio.

EDCS-12400034.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Redus fidelis, who was also called castimonialis, lived in peace for approximately eighty years.
EDCS-12400034.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Redus fidelis, who was also known as castimonialis.

EDCS-12400035.translation: Accepted by God, he lived 33 years and 6 months.

EDCS-12400419.translation: Iulia Restit, daughter of Caius, lived 30 years. Calpurnius, devoted, placed this for his deserving wife.
EDCS-12400419.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by Calpurnius to his wife Iulia Restit, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-12400420.translation: Cela, a slave woman, lived the years decreed for her by fate, humans, and the holy god. Sacred to the departed spirits, she now holds an eternal seat and suffers endless, deep slumber beside her conjugal partner.
EDCS-12400420.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a slave woman named Cela, invoking the gods of the underworld and lamenting her eternal rest beside her partner, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-12400486.translation: Felix lived 40 years and some months in peace.

EDCS-12400487.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Fasiria lived 35 years and 6 months.

EDCS-12400488.translation: Regatius lived 48 years, 8 months, and 12 days in peace.

EDCS-12400489.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Granius Habetdeus lived 23 years, 5 months, 8 days, and 10 hours in peace and rest.
EDCS-12400489.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the departed spirits, recording the lifespan of Granius Habetdeus, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-12400490.translation: Aulus Lurius Geminius lies here. He was once a master of speaking and of life, and always devoted his faithful life to salutary cares for human bodies. For 80 great months, he completed his faithful life, reaching its end. In this worthy resting place, he has rested in peace.
EDCS-12400490.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Aulus Lurius Geminius, describing his life as a physician or healer and his peaceful death after 80 months (likely a misstatement for years), probably dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-12500001.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Rupilius Serbus lived 75 years and 10 days.
EDCS-12500001.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the departed spirits, recording the lifespan of Rupilius Serbus, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-12500002.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Eukaris the faithful lived 6 years and 8 months in peace.
EDCS-12500002.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the departed spirits, recording the lifespan of Eukaris, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-12500003.translation: Iulia Bictoria lived 18 years, 5 days, and 8 hours in peace.
EDCS-12500003.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Iulia Bictoria, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-12500004.translation: Iulius Donatus lived in peace for 33 years, 5 months, 10 days, and 7 hours.
EDCS-12500004.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Iulius Donatus.

EDCS-12500005.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Laurentius Fidelis lived in peace for 31 years, 8 months, and 3 hours.
EDCS-12500005.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Laurentius Fidelis.

EDCS-12500006.translation: Iulius Felix lived in peace for 11 years, 2 months, 4 days, and 4 hours.
EDCS-12500006.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Iulius Felix.

EDCS-12500007.translation: Licinius Afrodisius lived in peace, faithful, for 43 years, 10 months, and 8 days.
EDCS-12500007.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Licinius Afrodisius.

EDCS-12500008.translation: Licinius Getulus lived for 43 years and 20 days.
EDCS-12500008.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Licinius Getulus.

EDCS-12500009.translation: Petrus lived in peace for more or less 63 years.
EDCS-12500009.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Petrus.

EDCS-12500010.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Tannonia Donata lived in peace for sixty years.
EDCS-12500010.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Tannonia Donata.

EDCS-12500011.translation: Vindemialis lived in peace for 28 years.
EDCS-12500011.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Vindemialis.

EDCS-12500012.translation: ORIVL PPIRI ALS Aprilis IP LSOR lived for...
EDCS-12500012.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of a person named Aprilis, with significant portions missing.

EDCS-12500013.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Honorius.

EDCS-12500014.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Da lived faithfully in peace for 10 years.
EDCS-12500014.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a person named Da, who lived in peace for 10 years.

EDCS-12500015.translation: Afrodisius Menor lived for 8 years, 11 months, and 2 days in peace.
EDCS-12500015.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Afrodisius Menor, detailing his lifespan in years, months, and days.

EDCS-12500016.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. In the name of the father, and of the son, and of the holy spirit, amen. Habetdeus f
EDCS-12500016.summary: This inscription, beginning with a Christian invocation, is a funerary dedication.

EDCS-12500017.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Crispina lived faithfully in peace for twenty years, 2 months, and 3 hours.
EDCS-12500017.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespan of Crispina, who lived faithfully in peace.

EDCS-12500018.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Proiectus lived faithfully in peace for 50 years, 7 months, and 10 days.
EDCS-12500018.summary: This funerary inscription states that Proiectus lived faithfully in peace for 50 years, 7 months, and 10 days.

EDCS-12500019.translation: Serbus lived in peace for 80 years. Sacred to the departed spirits.
EDCS-12500019.summary: This inscription records that Serbus lived in peace for 80 years and is dedicated to the departed spirits.

EDCS-12500020.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Bonifatius the faithful lived in peace for 7 years, 7 months, and 9 hours.
EDCS-12500020.summary: This funerary inscription details the lifespan of Bonifatius, who lived faithfully in peace.

EDCS-12500022.translation: Iulius Na us lived for ten months, five days, and 4 hours. Sacred to the departed spirits.
EDCS-12500022.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespan of Iulius Na us in months, days, and hours.

EDCS-12500023.translation: Bonifatius the faithful lived for 50 years, 6 months, and 10 days.
EDCS-12500023.summary: This inscription records that Bonifatius the faithful lived for 50 years, 6 months, and 10 days.

EDCS-12500025.translation: Assuritana lived in peace for 65 years, 2 months, and 8 days, and 7 hours.
EDCS-12500025.summary: This funerary inscription details the lifespan of Assuritana, who lived in peace.

EDCS-12500027.translation: Julius Nutricosus lived 18 years in peace.
EDCS-12500027.summary: This inscription is a funerary epitaph for Julius Nutricosus, recording his age at death.

EDCS-12500028.summary: This inscription is a funerary epitaph identifying Macarius as faithful, likely a Christian.

EDCS-12500029.translation: Rupilius Julianus, faithful in Christ, lived in peace for 3 years and 5 days.
EDCS-12500029.summary: This inscription is a funerary epitaph for Rupilius Julianus, a Christian, recording his age at death.

EDCS-12500030.translation: Flavia Candida, faithful, lived in peace for 50 years and 3 months and 5 days.
EDCS-12500030.summary: This inscription is a funerary epitaph for Flavia Candida, a Christian, recording her age at death.

EDCS-12500033.translation: In [Christ?], ... lived for years and months.
EDCS-12500033.summary: This inscription is a fragmented funerary epitaph, possibly for a Christian, recording some duration of life.

EDCS-12500036.summary: This inscription is a funerary epitaph for Castinianus, recording his age at death.

EDCS-12500350.translation: Nobellus and Benenata, siblings. Nobellus lived six years and Benenata four years in peace.
EDCS-12500350.summary: This inscription is a funerary epitaph for two siblings, Nobellus and Benenata, recording their ages at death.

EDCS-12500351.translation: Eutropia, faithful, lived ninety years and rested in peace.
EDCS-12500351.summary: This inscription is a funerary epitaph for Eutropia, a Christian, recording her age at death.

EDCS-12500352.translation: In the Lord, Feliciana rested in peace. God [be with?] his daughters. Lived in peace for five years, laid to rest on the 12th of October.
EDCS-12500352.summary: This inscription is a funerary epitaph for Feliciana, a Christian, recording her age and date of burial.

EDCS-12500354.translation: Honorius lived in peace for years
EDCS-12500354.summary: This inscription records the lifespan of Honorius, who lived in peace.

EDCS-12500357.text_edition: \n Vol Calassini kentenaria sic X Caprorenses kentenaria sic DCVII fieri kentenaria sic CCCXIIII R CCLIIII et erunt in conditorio in die XIIII Kalendas Martias centenaria DCCCCXXXI fieri in conditorio |(centenaria) |milleCLXXX XIII Kalendas Martias ad Octobrem |(centenarius) Maurus pondo libras XXXV |(centenarius) Ianuarius pondo libras LV |(centenarius) Felix pondo libras VIIICCXXVI |(centenarius) Vindemialis pondo libras CCC |(centenarius) Victor Mercurialis pondo libras |(duo milia)XCVII |(centenarius) Augustalis pondo libras |milleCCCXCVIII |(centenarius) Maioricus pondo libras |(duo milia)XCVII |(centenarius) Marianus pondo libras IIIIDCLXXVII |(centenarius) Primus pondo libras IIIIDCLX |(centenarius) Murc pondo libras IIICCCCXXV |(centenarius) Evasius pondo libras |milleDCCCLXXII |(centenarius) Restutus pondo libras IIIIXXII |(centenarius) Victorinus pondo libras |(mille) DCCXCIIII fieri numero CCCL pondo libras LXXVIII Vol Calassini kentenaria sic LXXVI\n
EDCS-12500357.translation: Vol(umen) Calassini: 100,000 units. Caprorenses: 607 units. To be made: 314 units. 254. And there will be in the tomb on the 14th day before the Kalends of March, 931 units. To be made in the tomb: 1180 units. On the 18th day before the Kalends of March. At October: Maurus, 35 pounds. Ianuarius, 55 pounds. Felix, 2820 pounds. Vindemialis, 300 pounds. Victor Mercurialis, 2097 pounds. Augustalis, 1398 pounds. Maioricus, 2097 pounds. Marianus, 4677 pounds. Primus, 4660 pounds. Murc, 2425 pounds. Evasius, 1872 pounds. Restutus, 482 pounds. Victorinus, 1794 pounds. To be made, 350 units, 78 pounds. Vol(umen) Calassini, 76 units.
EDCS-12500357.summary: This complex inscription details quantities of goods (likely oil based on later entries) under the heading of Vol(umen) Calassini and specific contributors, with associated weights and dates related to storage and distribution.

EDCS-12500358.text_edition: \n VII Idus Martias ad Octobrem |(centenarius) Felix XXXIII pondo libras LXIIII |(summa) XXXIII pondo libras LXIIII inpletur Vol ascopae a Byzacena numero XXI |(centenaria) XXXIIII fieri in conditorio Zeugitano amphorae gemellariae numero CLXVII ascopae a Byzace(na numero VI |(summa) CCCCXIII pondo libras XX\n
EDCS-12500358.translation: The 7th Ides of March. At October: Felix, 33 units, 64 pounds. Total: 33 units, 64 pounds. Filled by Vol(umen) ascopae from Byzacena: 21 units, 34 units. To be made in the Zeugitan tomb: 167 gemellariae amphorae and 6 ascopae from Byzacena. Total: 413 units, 20 pounds.
EDCS-12500358.summary: This inscription records deliveries of goods (likely oil) on specific dates, detailing quantities from different sources and for different containers, intended for storage.

EDCS-12500359.text_edition: \n VII Kalendas Maias ad Octobrem |(centenarius) Quintus |(centenaria) V pondo libras LX |(centenarius) Victorianus |(centenaria) XX pondo libras LXVII |(centenarius) Bilossus ab Occhi sic |(centenaria) V pondo |(centenarius) Tzelica |(centenaria) X pondo libras XX |(summa) XXXVIII pondo libras XLVII inpletur Vol ascopae a Byzacena numero XXII |(centenaria) XXXVIII pondo libras LXXV fieri in conditorio Zeugitano amphorae gemellariae numero CLXVII et kentenaria sic LXII fisci et Tebelbucitan QZ ascopae a Byzacena numero CCCCXLVI et Vol ascopae a Byzacena numero |(duo milia)CLVI olei Romae canon ascopae numero DCCLVII kentenaria sic |milleCCXXXII |(summa) VIIDCCCLII pondo libras LXXV\n
EDCS-12500359.translation: The 7th day before the Kalends of May. At October: Quintus, 5 units, 60 pounds. Victorianus, 20 units, 67 pounds. Bilossus from Occhi, 5 units. Tzelica, 10 units, 20 pounds. Total: 38 units, 47 pounds. Filled by Vol(umen) ascopae from Byzacena: 22 units, 38 units, 75 pounds. To be made in the Zeugitan tomb: 167 gemellariae amphorae and 62 units. Fisci and from Tebelbucitan QZ, 446 ascopae from Byzacena and 2156 units. Oil from Rome, 757 ascopae, 1232 units. Total: 7852 pounds, 75 pounds.
EDCS-12500359.summary: This inscription details the distribution and quantities of oil from various sources (including Byzacena, Occhi, Tebelbucitan, and Rome) on a specific date and for storage, mentioning different types of containers.

EDCS-12500360.text_edition: \n VII Idus Apriles ad Octobrem |(centenarius) Flabianus sic |(centenaria) X Felix ab Ucubi |(centenaria) VII pondo libras XL |(centenarius) Peregrinus |(centenaria) XIIII pondo libras XC |(centenarius) Felix ab C |(centenaria) X pondo libras XCII |(centenarius) Doianus |(centenaria) pondo libras XXXV |(summa) CLIIII pondo libras LVII inpletur Vol ascopae a Byzacena numero XXI et olei Romae canon ascopae numero CLXI et Macrinenses ascopae a Byzacena numero VI |(centenaria) CLVI fieri in conditorio Zeugitano amphorae gemellariae numero CLXVII et kentenaria sic L fisci et de numero Tebelbucitan QZ ascopae a Byzacena numero CCC et kentenaria sic L de numero Vol ascopae a Byzacena numero |milleDXIIII et olei Romae canon ascopae numero CCLXXII et kentenaria sic |milleXCI |(summa) VCCLXV pondo libras L\n
EDCS-12500360.translation: The 7th Ides of April. At October: Flabianus, 10 units. Felix from Ucubi, 7 units, 40 pounds. Peregrinus, 14 units, 90 pounds. Felix from C, 10 units, 92 pounds. Doianus, units, 35 pounds. Total: 154 units, 57 pounds. Filled by Vol(umen) ascopae from Byzacena: 21 units. And oil from Rome, 161 ascopae. And Macrinenses, 6 ascopae from Byzacena, 156 units. To be made in the Zeugitan tomb: 167 gemellariae amphorae and 50 units. Fisci and from Tebelbucitan QZ, 300 units and 50 units. From Vol(umen) ascopae from Byzacena, 1504 units. And oil from Rome, 272 ascopae, 1091 units. Total: 2265 units, 50 pounds.
EDCS-12500360.summary: This inscription records deliveries of oil and other goods from various regions (Byzacena, Ucubi, Rome, Macrinenses) on a specific date, detailing quantities, weights, and intended storage locations.

EDCS-12500361.text_edition: \n VI Idus Apriles ad Octobrem |(centenarius) Donatilus |(centenaria) XII pondo libras L |(centenarius) Victorianus |(centenaria) VII pondo libras XV |(centenarius) Vanosus |(centenaria) XIIII pondo libras XIIII |(centenarius) Fir |(centenaria) XLVII pondo libras LXV |(centenarius) Kalius |(centenaria) XXIIII |(centenarius) Arus |(centenaria) XXIII pondo libras LIII |(centenarius) Victor |(centenaria) XLVI pondo libras LX |(centenarius) Romanus |(centenaria) LVII pondo libras X |(summa) CCXXXII pondo libras LXVII inpletur Macrinenses ascopae a Byzacena numero XLVIIII et kentenaria sic CXX AFR |(summa) CCXXXV fieri in conditorio Zeugitano amphorae gemellariae numero CLXVII et kentenaria sic L fisci et Tebelbucitan QZ ascopae a Byzacena numero CCC et kentenaria sic L et Macrinenses ascopae a Byzacena numero VI et kentenaria sic CXX olei Romae canon ascopae numero CCCXCI et kentenaria sic |(mille)XCI |(summa) VCCCCI pondo libras XXXV\n
EDCS-12500361.translation: On the sixth day before the Ides of April, to Octobrem, Donatilus the centenarian, with 12 centenaria weighing 50 pounds; Victorianus the centenarian, with 7 centenaria weighing 15 pounds; Vanosus the centenarian, with 14 centenaria weighing 14 pounds; Fir the centenarian, with 47 centenaria weighing 65 pounds; Kalius the centenarian, with 24; Arus the centenarian, with 23 centenaria weighing 53 pounds; Victor the centenarian, with 46 centenaria weighing 60 pounds; Romanus the centenarian, with 57 centenaria weighing 10 pounds; total 232 centenaria, 67 pounds. Filled by the Macrinenses, 49 ascopae from Byzacena, and 120 centenaria. Total 235. Made in the Zeugitan storehouse, 167 twin amphorae and 62 centenaria for the treasury. And Tebelbucitan, 300 ascopae from Byzacena and 50 centenaria. And Macrinenses, 6 ascopae from Byzacena and 120 centenaria. Oil for Rome, 391 ascopae, and 1091 centenaria. Total 4001 pounds, 35 pounds.
EDCS-12500361.summary: This inscription is a record of oil quantities measured and stored, dated to April, likely related to an administrative or logistical record from Roman North Africa.

EDCS-12500362.text_edition: \n Pridie Nonas Maias ad Octobrem |(centenarius) inus |(centenaria) VIIII pondo libras XCIIII |(centenarius) |(centenaria) XIII pondo libras XLII |(centenarius) |(centenaria) VII pondo libras LXVI |(centenarius) nus |(centenaria) IIII pondo libras LXXXVII |(centenarius) Victor a Serue |(centenaria) V pondo libras XVIII |(centenarius) Felix |(centenaria) V pondo libras XIIII |(centenarius) Inventus |(centenaria) XXXV pondo libras LXII |(centenarius) Victor a Nobis sic |(centenaria) XXVII pondo libras XVIII |(summa) CXI pondo libras XI inpletur Vol ascopae a Byzacena numero LXVIII |(centenaria) CXI pondo libras X fieri in conditorio Zeugitano \xcf\x88 numero CLXXXIIII et amphorae gemellariae numero CLXVII kentenaria LXII fisci et Tebelbucitan--- ascopae a Byzacena numero CCCCXLVI et kentenaria sic LXV Macrinenses ascopae a Byzacena LV et kentenaria sic CCLXXXV Vol ascopae a Byzacena numero |(duo milia)CCLXXV olei Romae canon ascopae numero DCCLVII kentenaria sic |milleCCXXXII |(summa) VIIIDCCCII pondo libras LXXV\n
EDCS-12500362.translation: On the day before the Nones of May, to Octobrem, [centenarius] with 9 centenaria weighing 94 pounds; [centenarius] with 13 centenaria weighing 42 pounds; [centenarius] with 7 centenaria weighing 66 pounds; [centenarius] with 4 centenaria weighing 87 pounds; Victor from Serue, with 5 centenaria weighing 18 pounds; Felix, with 5 centenaria weighing 14 pounds; Inventus, with 35 centenaria weighing 62 pounds; Victor from Nobis, with 27 centenaria weighing 18 pounds; total 111 centenaria, 11 pounds. Filled by Vol, 68 ascopae from Byzacena, 111 centenaria, 10 pounds. Made in the Zeugitan storehouse, 184 [units] and 167 twin amphorae, 62 centenaria for the treasury. And Tebelbucitan, 446 ascopae from Byzacena and 65 centenaria. Macrinenses, 55 ascopae from Byzacena and 285 centenaria. Vol, 2275 ascopae from Byzacena. Oil for Rome, 757 ascopae, 1232 centenaria. Total 8882 pounds, 75 pounds.
EDCS-12500362.summary: This inscription details quantities of oil measured and stored, dated to May, likely an administrative or logistical record from Roman North Africa.

EDCS-12600038.translation: With his father Sterceius acting as procurator, the name of the son remains eternal in the tomb; who could say that anyone was happier or more charming than I, who lived for seventy years, and cared neither for the crowds of the forum nor for the laws, but went about with just eyes and a pleasant manner.
EDCS-12600038.summary: This funerary epitaph records the life and virtues of an individual who lived seventy years, expressing contentment with his life and its simple pleasures.

EDCS-12600040.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Cocceius Baribgal, pious, lived 15 years.
EDCS-12600040.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Cocceius Baribgal, who died at the age of 15.

EDCS-12600041.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus Sentius Tires lived 55 years. Fabaria Primosa lived 53 years. They are buried here.
EDCS-12600041.summary: This funerary inscription records the lives of Quintus Sentius Tires and Fabaria Primosa, who died at ages 55 and 53 respectively.

EDCS-12600042.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Plotia Masamonica lived 72 years, by admonition.
EDCS-12600042.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespan of Plotia Masamonica, who died at 72 years old.

EDCS-12600043.text_edition: \n Invicto numini deae Caelestis pro salute et aeternitate imperii domini nostri Marci Aureli Severi Antonini Pii Felicis Augusti et Iuliae Augustae matris Augusti et castrorum et senatus et patriae totiusque domus divinae\n
EDCS-12600043.translation: To the unconquered divine power of the goddess Caelestis, for the safety and eternity of the empire of our lord Marcus Aurelius Severus Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus, and of Julia Augusta, mother of the Augustus and of the camps and of the Senate and of the whole fatherland and of the whole divine house.
EDCS-12600043.summary: This is a dedication to the goddess Caelestis for the well-being and endurance of the Roman Empire and its imperial family, likely from the reign of Emperor Severus Alexander.

EDCS-12600047.translation: To Quintus, son of Gnaeus; to Lucius, son of Cornelius.
EDCS-12600047.summary: This inscription likely records the dedication of a monument or tomb to two individuals, Quintus and Lucius, identified by their patronymic and gentilician names.

EDCS-12600051.translation: Publius Victor, genius Gallus Herennius Felix, Munatius Faustus.
EDCS-12600051.summary: This inscription appears to be a list of names, possibly of individuals associated with a funerary monument or a collegium.

EDCS-12600053.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Caius Sextilius Primus, pious, lived 13 years, 2 months, and 8 days. He is buried here.
EDCS-12600053.summary: This funerary inscription records the life of Caius Sextilius Primus, who died at the age of 13 years, 2 months, and 8 days.

EDCS-12600054.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Sextilia Donata, pious, lived 7 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-12600054.summary: This funerary inscription records the life of Sextilia Donata, who died at the age of 7 years.

EDCS-12600056.text_edition: \n XI Kalendas Augustas navicula Felicis Xeri I Byzacenae VI Kalendas Augustas navicula Byzacenae CXLIIII reprobo IIII\n
EDCS-12600056.translation: On the eleventh day before the Kalends of August, Felix's small boat from Xeri, 1 from Byzacena. On the sixth day before the Kalends of August, a small boat from Byzacena, 144, reprobate 4.
EDCS-12600056.summary: This inscription records the arrival or shipment of small boats, possibly related to trade or transport, dated to July.

EDCS-12600057.translation: Centenarius [weight] pounds; Obbalus [weight] pounds; Metrianus [weight] 8400 pounds; Lampadius [weight] 2300 pounds; Marinus [weight] 7868 pounds; Tutus [weight] 1400 pounds; Livianus [weight] 1500 pounds; [weight] 1000 pounds; B [weight] pounds; N anus [weight] 3114 pounds; du us [weight] 8 pounds; Ignu [weight] 3200 pounds; made in number: 442 centenaria, 93 pounds.
EDCS-12600057.summary: This inscription records the weights in pounds of various individuals, likely related to contributions or rations, possibly for a collegium or a funerary association, with a total count and weight specified at the end.

EDCS-12700096.translation: To the deified spirits. Prima dedicated this to her pious husband Postimus, who was a slave of our Augustus and lived 40 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-12700096.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a slave of the emperor, dedicated by his wife, dating to the imperial period.

EDCS-12700125.translation: To the god Mercury Augustus. For the health of our lord Emperor Caesar Publius Licinius Gallienus Pius Felix Augustus, pontifex maximus, Germanicus maximus, holder of tribunician power for the 9th time, consul for the 4th time, father of the fatherland, proconsul, and of Cornelia Salonina Augusta, wife of our lord, and of their entire divine household, Marcus Tullius Luca, by order of their piety, with his son Primo, made the arch and steps with a frontal wall of stucco at his own expense.
EDCS-12700125.summary: This is a dedication of a public work, including an arch and steps, to the emperor Gallienus and his wife Cornelia Salonina, likely made by a local official in the 3rd century CE.

EDCS-12700131.translation: To our lord Emperor Flavius Julius Constantius, Pius, Felix, ever Augustus. Aurelius Celsinus, most illustrious man, proconsul of the province of Africa, judging vice sacra, devoted to his divine will and majesty.
EDCS-12700131.summary: This is an inscription recording the devotion of Aurelius Celsinus, proconsul of Africa, to Emperor Constantius II, dating to the mid-4th century CE.

EDCS-12700167.inscription_type: tituli operum, tituli sacri, tituli sepulcrales
EDCS-12700167.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Aelius Publius veteranus militavit ala Britannica bis torquata pius vixit annos LV Numpidia sic fecit viro pientissimo et carissimo marito eius sit tibi terra levis VSAL OQB\n
EDCS-12700167.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Aelius Publius, a veteran who served in the winged cavalry regiment Britannica, pious, lived 55 years. Numpidia dedicated this to her most pious and dearest husband. May the earth lie lightly upon you. V(otum) S(olvit) A(nimo) L(ibens) O(b) Q(od) B(e) F(ecisti).
EDCS-12700167.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Aelius Publius, a veteran of the ala Britannica, erected by his wife Numpidia, indicating his service and lifespan.

EDCS-12700179.translation: After the consulship of Modestus and Arintheus, on the 14th day before the Kalends of March. Felix, measurer of oil of the Forum of Carthage, received through the ship of Felix Xerus, from Capua, 208 light centenaria and 13 rejected. The granary of Zeugis, on the 15th day before the Kalends of March.
EDCS-12700179.summary: This is a record of the receipt of olive oil shipments by Felix, an oil measurer in Carthage, likely dating to the late 4th or early 5th century CE.

EDCS-12700180.translation: After the consulship of Modestus and Arintheus, on the 14th day before the Kalends of March. Felix, measurer of oil of the Forum of Carthage, received through the ship of Cilindrus of Capua, 200 light centenaria and eight rejected, and the oil measurer Petrus. The granary of Zeugis.
EDCS-12700180.summary: This is a record of the receipt of olive oil shipments by Felix, an oil measurer in Carthage, likely dating to the late 4th or early 5th century CE.

EDCS-12700198.translation: Adulteress, prostitute, know that I fled from Bulla Regia.
EDCS-12700198.summary: This is a graffiti inscription, likely from the Roman period, expressing personal animosity and indicating a flight from the city of Bulla Regia.

EDCS-12700226.summary: This is a very brief funerary inscription, likely from the Roman period, indicating peace for the deceased Valerius.

EDCS-12700228.text_edition: \n Numini sancto inferno deo votum monitus solvit Cissus\n
EDCS-12700228.translation: To the holy divine power of the underworld god, Cissus fulfilled his vow after being prompted.
EDCS-12700228.summary: This is a votive inscription recording Cissus fulfilling a vow to an underworld deity.

EDCS-12700229.text_edition: \n Diis Mauris Augustis sacrum pro salute Augusti Caesaris Marci Aureli Commodi Antonini toris procurator marmorum Numidicorum io\n
EDCS-12700229.translation: Sacred to the divine Lords of the Underworld. In fulfillment of a vow for the safety of Augustus Caesar Marcus Aurelius Commodus Antoninus, procurator of the Numidian marble quarries.
EDCS-12700229.summary: This is a sacred inscription dedicated to the underworld gods for the safety of Emperor Commodus, mentioning a procurator responsible for Numidian marble.

EDCS-12800189.text_edition: \n Quintus Mirusius votum fecit Saturno votum solvit libens animo\n
EDCS-12800189.translation: Quintus Mirusius made a vow to Saturn and willingly fulfilled it.
EDCS-12800189.summary: This is a votive inscription where Quintus Mirusius declares he made and fulfilled a vow to the god Saturn.

EDCS-12800190.text_edition: \n Fortunatus Heleni filius Saturno votum solvit libens animo pro Severo filio suo\n
EDCS-12800190.translation: Fortunatus, son of Helenus, willingly fulfilled his vow to Saturn for his son Severus.
EDCS-12800190.summary: This is a votive inscription where Fortunatus fulfilled a vow to Saturn for the sake of his son Severus.

EDCS-12800191.translation: Marcus Antonius, priest, paid his vow willingly.
EDCS-12800191.summary: This is a votive inscription by Marcus Antonius, a priest, fulfilling a vow, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-12800192.translation: Lucius Furnius paid his vow willingly to Saturn.
EDCS-12800192.summary: This is a votive inscription by Lucius Furnius to the god Saturn, fulfilling a vow, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-12800321.text_edition: \n ------ legato Kar]thaginis praetori tribuno plebis quaestori provinciae Baeticae viocuro universae curiae impetrato ab ordine loco pecunia sua patrono et alumno coloniae posuerunt\n
EDCS-12800321.translation: [...], legate of Carthage, praetor, tribune of the plebs, quaestor of the province of Baetica, curator of the entire curia, having obtained from the order a place with his own money, as patron and foster-child of the colony, they placed [this].
EDCS-12800321.summary: This inscription, with significant lacunae, likely records the dedication of a public space or monument by officials and citizens of a colony, honoring a benefactor.

EDCS-12800322.translation: To Caia Sulpicia Dymiana, daughter of Caius, most illustrious woman, wife of Quintus Victorinus, most illustrious man, daughter of Caius Sulpicius Justus, most illustrious man. Calpurnius Gabinius [erected this] for his patroness.
EDCS-12800322.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Caia Sulpicia Dymiana, a woman of high social standing, by her client Calpurnius Gabinius, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-12800331.translation: Rmius Pius made this for his friend Trajan Caesar for the Dacian War, with four spears. [---]
EDCS-12800331.summary: This is a dedication from Rmius Pius to Emperor Trajan, likely a military monument given the mention of spears and the Dacian War.

EDCS-12800333.text_edition: \n Bonae Fortunae Dis monumentum Balsilechi Subath qui vixit annorum sic CX et supra\n
EDCS-12800333.translation: A monument to Good Fortune by Balsilechus of Subath, who lived for 110 years and more.
EDCS-12800333.summary: This is a funerary monument dedicated to the goddess Bona Fortuna by Balsilechus, who lived to an advanced age.

EDCS-12800371.translation: Leo, you presumed, you equipped, you dedicated.
EDCS-12800371.summary: This is a short, possibly humorous, dedication or epitaph by Leo, who is credited with preparing and dedicating something.

EDCS-12800681.translation: The People of Acholla, according to the promise of Aulus Terentius Felix.
EDCS-12800681.summary: This inscription records a public work or dedication by the community of Acholla, funded by a promise made by Aulus Terentius Felix.

EDCS-12800682.translation: Vitalio has paid his vow to the Augusti.
EDCS-12800682.summary: This is a votive inscription by Vitalio, dedicating something to the Emperors (Augusti).

EDCS-12800687.text_edition: \n Caius Acrasius Publi filius militavit legione III Augusta vixsit sic nnis XXXV O militavit annis XV heres Helvius rius Quirina H\n
EDCS-12800687.translation: Caius Acrasius, son of Publius, served in the III Augusta legion, lived for 35 years, and served for 15 years. His heir was Helvius [---]rius of the Quirina tribe.
EDCS-12800687.summary: This is a tombstone for Caius Acrasius, a soldier in the III Augusta legion, recording his lifespan and service years.

EDCS-12800688.text_edition: \n Marcus Cornelius Marci filius Maecia Longus Neapole miles legionis III Augustae centuria Sextili vixit nnos LIX militavit nnos XXV hic situs est heredes posuerunt\n
EDCS-12800688.translation: Marcus Cornelius Longus, son of Marcus, of the Maecia tribe, a soldier in the III Augusta legion, in the century of Sextilius, lived for 59 years and served for 25 years. His heirs placed him here.
EDCS-12800688.summary: This funerary inscription records the life and military service of Marcus Cornelius Longus, a soldier of the III Augusta legion.

EDCS-12800689.text_edition: \n Clodius Arnensis Qu miles legionis III AugustaeIFMC \n
EDCS-12800689.translation: Clodius Arnensis, a soldier of the III Augusta legion...
EDCS-12800689.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription identifying Clodius Arnensis as a soldier of the III Augusta legion.

EDCS-12800690.text_edition: \n Caius Iulius Augusti libertus Crestus Samianus \n
EDCS-12800690.translation: Caius Iulius Crestus Samianus, freedman of Augustus.
EDCS-12800690.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Caius Iulius Crestus Samianus, a freedman.

EDCS-12800691.text_edition: \n Diis Manibus sacrum Tiberius Claudius Felix Cilicinenus vixit nnos LI menses hic situs est\n
EDCS-12800691.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Tiberius Claudius Felix of Cilicia lived for 51 years and [some] months. He is buried here.
EDCS-12800691.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Tiberius Claudius Felix, recording his lifespan and burial.

EDCS-12800692.translation: Laetoria Rufina, daughter of Lucius, pious, lived 47 years, her bones are placed here, may you rest well. Sacred to the Divine Shades. Caius Sulpicius Primus, pious, lived 76 years, his bones are placed here, may you rest well.
EDCS-12800692.summary: This is a double epitaph for Laetoria Rufina and Caius Sulpicius Primus, with wishes for their peaceful rest in the afterlife.

EDCS-12800693.translation: Sulpicius Faustus, having taken to wife Sempronia Urbica Masculitana, undertook the raising of a young daughter, Faustina. He wished to join her [in marriage] but was not permitted to achieve his desire. She dies having completed sixty years. Her mother raises her with great distress. To whom she should be joined in marriage, having chosen from many good suitors, he handed her over to a good man. She lived with care for sixty years.
EDCS-12800693.summary: This inscription is a complex epitaph for Sulpicius Faustus, recounting the life and death of his wife Sempronia Urbica Masculitana and their daughter Faustina, with details about their marriages and lifespans.

EDCS-12800694.translation: Sulpicius Primus and Faustina are born, two brothers united in harmony. They are well, by the will of fate, with their mother Urbica. By fate predicting, they mourned their good mother. Without marrying a second wife after his wife's death, he lived eighty years, and his wife joined to him [lived] fifty.
EDCS-12800694.summary: This epitaph for Sulpicius Primus and Faustina recounts their lives, their mother Urbica, and their father's second marriage and lifespans.

EDCS-12800695.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Victor, freedman of the Augusti, lived 47 years. Frunita, his wife, made this. Gemellina, their slave daughter, lived 7 years.
EDCS-12800695.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Victor, a freedman, and his daughter Gemellina, set up by his wife Frunita.

EDCS-12800696.summary: This is a simple epitaph for Africana, indicating her peaceful repose.

EDCS-12800700.translation: Here in peace rest the remains of Avianus and Bavaria.
EDCS-12800700.summary: This is a funerary inscription marking the resting place of Avianus and Bavaria.

EDCS-12800737.summary: This is a personal name inscription, likely a tombstone or dedication by Leontius Caneius.

EDCS-12800738.translation: To Marcus Aemilius, most eminent man, procurator of the Augusti for the XX hereditatium in Umbria, Tuscia, and Picenum, procurator.
EDCS-12800738.summary: This inscription honors Marcus Aemilius, detailing his high-ranking imperial administrative roles as procurator, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-13000602.translation: Sacred to the Departed Gods. Marcus Manilius Vezrunianus, dutiful, lived 62 years.
EDCS-13000602.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the name, piety, and lifespan of Marcus Manilius Vezrunianus.

EDCS-13000603.summary: This is a personal name inscription, likely a tombstone or dedication by Quintus Turius Menonianus.

EDCS-13000604.translation: Zasgia Victoria Cezzonia; Lucius Turius Fabius Lucanianus, her son.
EDCS-13000604.summary: This inscription names Zasgia Victoria Cezzonia and identifies Lucius Turius Fabius Lucanianus as her son, likely a tombstone inscription.

EDCS-13000606.translation: Sacred to Caelestis Augustus. Lucius Furfanius Maximus fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-13000606.summary: This is a votive inscription recording Lucius Furfanius Maximus fulfilling a vow to the goddess Caelestis.

EDCS-13000607.translation: Sutrius Primus, stator of the temple, made the gate for the Lords Ceres and Pluto with his own money.
EDCS-13000607.summary: This inscription records Sutrius Primus, a temple official, dedicating a gate to the deities Ceres and Pluto at his own expense.

EDCS-13000608.text_edition: \n Iovi Augusto sacrum dedicante Cnaeo Suellio Flacco legato Augusti pro praetore Quintus Mantius Quinti filius Camilia Alba Pompeia legio III Augusta de suo fecit\n
