EDCS-13000608.translation: Sacred to Jupiter Optimus Maximus. Dedicated by Gnaeus Suellius Flaccus, governor of the province, Quintus Mantius, son of Quintus, of the Camilia tribe, and Alba Pompeia of the III Augusta legion, made this from his own resources.
EDCS-13000608.summary: This is a dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus made by soldiers of the III Augusta legion under the command of the governor, Gnaeus Suellius Flaccus.

EDCS-13000609.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, Titus Aelius Tyrrhenus from...
EDCS-13000609.summary: This is a dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Titus Aelius Tyrrhenus, likely incomplete.

EDCS-13000610.translation: Sacred to Mercurius Augustus. Lucius Aurunculeius Tertullus.
EDCS-13000610.summary: This is a dedication to the god Mercurius Augustus by Lucius Aurunculeius Tertullus.

EDCS-13000611.translation: Fulfilled his vow willingly to the unconquered divine power of Virtue.
EDCS-13000611.summary: This is a votive inscription expressing a willing fulfillment of a vow to the 'Unconquered Numina of Virtue'.

EDCS-13000612.translation: Ursus and Maxima to their Augustus Serapis.
EDCS-13000612.summary: A dedication to the emperor Serapis by Ursus and Maxima.

EDCS-13000613.translation: Lucius Aemilius Felix dedicated ornaments to the goddess, the esteemed lady, for his curia, and also six hundred [sesterces], which he brought with him, from the interest of which his colleagues may feast on his birthday, which is the Ides of May.
EDCS-13000613.summary: A dedication of ornaments and funds to a goddess by Lucius Aemilius Felix for his collegium, specifying the use of the interest on his birthday.

EDCS-13000622.translation: To the Divine Pius Severus, father of the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Severus Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus, Arabicus Adiabenicus Parthicus Maximus, Britannicus Maximus, Germanicus Maximus, high priest, with tribunician power for the 17th time, consul for the 4th time, proconsul, father of the country.
EDCS-13000622.summary: This is a posthumous dedication honoring Emperor Antoninus Pius (father of Marcus Aurelius), listing his extensive titles and honors.

EDCS-13000623.translation: To Julia Domna Augusta, mother of the camp and of the emperor and of the senate and of the fatherland.
EDCS-13000623.summary: An honorific dedication to Julia Domna, mother of the emperor and the state.

EDCS-13000625.inscription_type: tituli operum, tituli sacri, tituli sepulcrales
EDCS-13000625.text_edition: \n Ex testamento Cai Corneli Egriliani praefecti legionis XIIII geminae quo testamento ex HS CCL milibus nummum arcum cum statuis Auggustorum nnostrorum item tetrastylis duobus cum statuis et Minervae quae in foro fieri praecepit praeter alia HS CCL milia nummum quae rei publicae ita ut certis diebus gymnasia populo publice in thermis praeberentur legavit et ad Kapitolinum argenti libras CLXX id est lances IIII auri libras XIIII id est phialas III scyphos II haece omnia secundum voluntatem eius in contione populi Corneli Fortunatus et Quinta fratres et heredes eius adsignaverunt et opus perfecerunt\n
EDCS-13000625.translation: From the will of Caius Cornelius Egrilianus, prefect of the XIIII Gemina legion, who bequeathed 250,000 sesterces for the construction of an arch with statues of our Augusti, and two tetrastyle buildings with statues and a statue of Minerva, which he ordered to be built in the forum, in addition to other bequests of 250,000 sesterces for public games and access to the baths for the people on specific days. He also left 170 pounds of silver, namely 4 large dishes, and 14 pounds of gold, namely 3 shallow bowls and 2 cups, for the Capitol. All these things, in accordance with his wishes, Cornelius Fortunatus and Quinta, his brothers and heirs, assigned and completed in the public assembly.
EDCS-13000625.summary: This inscription details the fulfillment of the will of Caius Cornelius Egrilianus, a legionary prefect, who left substantial funds for public works, games, and offerings in Rome.

EDCS-13000628.translation: To the most excellent emperor, twice consul, father of the fatherland, begun by indulgence; his wife and IB [perhaps IB=Iulia Balbilla or other name/title].
EDCS-13000628.summary: A dedication to an emperor who held the consulship twice and was father of the fatherland, initiated with clemency.

EDCS-13000630.translation: By divine will, in most fortunate times of our most pious lords Justinian and Theodora, the Augusti, after the Vandals were cut off from Africa and the entire Berber nation extinguished by Solomon, the most glorious and excellent magister militum, ex-consul, prefect of Libya, and patrician, by the providence of the same most eminent man, the city of Theveste was built from its foundations.
EDCS-13000630.summary: An inscription commemorating the rebuilding of the city of Theveste by Solomon under the reign of Justinian and Theodora, following military victories in Africa and Mauretania.

EDCS-13000632.summary: A dedication to unspecified noble Caesars.

EDCS-13000633.translation: To Augustus, holding tribunician power for the 5th time, consul.
EDCS-13000633.summary: An inscription mentioning Augustus with his tribunician power and consulship.

EDCS-13000638.summary: An epithet or dedication to an unnamed divine or imperial figure.

EDCS-13000641.translation: Flavius Rhodinus Primus the younger, a man of consular rank, his son and legate, also placed [this monument].
EDCS-13000641.summary: A record of Flavius Rhodinus Primus the younger, son of a judge of sacred cognition, dedicating a monument.

EDCS-13000642.translation: ...of the [3rd] legion [Claudiae], lived 10[3?] years, served 5 years, is buried here. Lucius Annaeus...
EDCS-13000642.summary: This is a fragment of a tombstone for Lucius Annaeus, a soldier of the III Claudian legion, recording his lifespan and service years.

EDCS-13000643.translation: Flavius Ianuarius, assistant in the office of the cornicularii, made this for Homullius Saturninus, a soldier of the Third Legion Augusta, his fellow soldier.
EDCS-13000643.summary: A memorial stone erected by Flavius Ianuarius, an assistant in the cornicularii office, for his fellow soldier Homullius Saturninus of the Third Legion Augusta.

EDCS-13000644.translation: Quintus Iulius Dioratus, son of Quintus, of the Quirina tribe, soldier of the Third Legion Augusta, century of Lucius Iulius, lived 30 years, served 5 years, is buried here. Titus Flavius Martialis, of the century of Nasidius, his heir, erected this monument.
EDCS-13000644.summary: A tombstone for Quintus Iulius Dioratus, a soldier of the Third Legion Augusta, erected by his heir Titus Flavius Martialis.

EDCS-13000645.translation: X, a veteran, made this tomb for himself and his wife.
EDCS-13000645.summary: A funerary epitaph for a veteran and his wife.

EDCS-13000646.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Repentinus, an Augustan scribe, lived 25 years. His colleagues from the scribal guild made this.
EDCS-13000646.summary: A funerary inscription for Repentinus, a scribe, erected by his colleagues from the scribal guild.

EDCS-13000647.translation: Sacred to [a god], Fructus, freedman, optio of the couriers, PET
EDCS-13000647.summary: This inscription, likely from an altar or a tomb, records Fructus, a freedman serving as an optio for couriers.

EDCS-13000652.translation: Sadunti for services rendered with a sack
EDCS-13000652.summary: This fragmented inscription likely records a dedication or award for services performed, possibly related to a 'saccus' (sack).

EDCS-13000654.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Gaius Audasius Succedens, son of Gaius, of the Papiria tribe, who held the offices of duovir, prefect for dispensing justice, and quaestor, lived 70 years. Audasius Pomptinus Primitius and Ianuaria, his freedmen and heirs, made this for their most excellent and devoted patron. He is buried here.
EDCS-13000654.summary: A funerary inscription for Gaius Audasius Succedens, a local magistrate, erected by his freedmen and heirs.

EDCS-13000656.text_edition: \n Publi Saturnini Saturniani flaminis perpetui filio nepoti Cai Iuli Romuleani equitis Romani pontificis qui primus a condita civitate sua ob honorem flamoni annui munus Idibus omnibus senis paribus curiae suae dedit universae curiae et Augustales pecunia sua locus datus ex decreto ordinis\n
EDCS-13000656.translation: To the son of Publius Saturninus Saturnianus, the perpetual priest, and grandson of Gaius Iulius Romuleanus, a Roman knight and pontiff, who, from the founding of his city, for the honor of the annual priesthood, gave on all the middle days of the month a gift of six each to his senate; and the Augustales, the place was given by his own money, by decree of the order.
EDCS-13000656.summary: A dedication recording the privileges and benefactions of a local dignitary, Publius Saturninus Saturnianus, and his family.

EDCS-13000659.summary: This inscription is highly fragmented, with only a name, Aurelius Florentinus, and some letters remaining, making its purpose unclear.

EDCS-13000661.translation: Flavia built this at her own expense
EDCS-13000661.summary: This inscription records that Flavia funded and constructed something at her own expense.

EDCS-13000665.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Felicitas lived 3 years. She is buried here. Hilarus, freedman of the emperors, made this for his native slave girl.
EDCS-13000665.summary: A funerary inscription for Felicitas, a young girl, erected by Hilarus, an imperial freedman.

EDCS-13000666.translation: Sacred to the Shades Below. Ianuaria, slave of our Emperor Augustus, lived 35 years, 5 months, 2 days. Apollonius, her husband, made this for his pious wife.
EDCS-13000666.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Ianuaria, a slave of Emperor Augustus, who lived to be 35 years old, with her husband Apollonius dedicating the monument.

EDCS-13000667.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Victoria, of Augustus, lived 50 years. She is buried here. Flavius Primus made this for his dearest wife.
EDCS-13000667.summary: A funerary inscription for Victoria, erected by her husband Flavius Primus.

EDCS-13000669.translation: Aelius Venustus, son of Quintus, lived 53 years, 5 months.
EDCS-13000669.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespan of Aelius Venustus, son of Quintus.

EDCS-13000670.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Publius Aelius Viator. He is buried here. Publius Aelius Felix made this for his devoted father.
EDCS-13000670.summary: A funerary inscription for Publius Aelius Viator, erected by his son Publius Aelius Felix.

EDCS-13000671.translation: Sacred to the Shades Below. Aelia Fortunata lived 40 years; she is buried here. Egnatius Rogatianus made this for his dearest wife.
EDCS-13000671.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Aelia Fortunata, who lived 40 years, dedicated by her husband Egnatius Rogatianus.

EDCS-13000672.translation: Sacred to the Shades Below. Annius Gulosus lived 20 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-13000672.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Annius Gulosus at the age of 20.

EDCS-13000673.translation: Sacred to the Shades Below. Annia Lala lived 30 years. Marius Donatus [made this] for his pious mother.
EDCS-13000673.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Annia Lala at the age of 30, dedicated by her son Marius Donatus.

EDCS-13000674.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Gaius Apuleius Gudullus lived 65 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-13000674.summary: A funerary inscription for Gaius Apuleius Gudullus.

EDCS-13000675.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Apuleius Miggin lived 26 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-13000675.summary: A funerary inscription for Apuleius Miggin.

EDCS-13000676.translation: To the departed spirits. Attia Hilariatas lived 27 years, 5 months, 6 days. Iulius Minervalis made this for his most devoted wife.
EDCS-13000676.summary: A funerary epitaph for Attia Hilariatas, recording her age at death and set up by her husband, Iulius Minervalis.

EDCS-13000677.translation: To the departed spirits. Audasius Primitivus and Audasia Ianuaria made this for their most excellent and devoted daughter Audasia Fortunata, who deserved well of us, and lived 16 years, 3 months. She lies here.
EDCS-13000677.summary: A funerary epitaph for Audasia Fortunata, set up by her parents Audasius Primitivus and Audasia Ianuaria, recording her age and death.

EDCS-13000678.translation: To the departed spirits. Audasia Charitu lived 30 years. Pomptinus, her husband, made this for his most devoted wife. She lies here.
EDCS-13000678.summary: A funerary epitaph for Audasia Charitu, recording her age at death and set up by her husband Pomptinus.

EDCS-13000679.translation: Sacred to the Shades Below. Quintus Avidius Noricus lived 53 years, 2 months, 21 days. Avidia Tertia made this for her pious husband; he is buried here.
EDCS-13000679.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespan of Quintus Avidius Noricus and is dedicated by his wife Avidia Tertia.

EDCS-13000680.translation: To the departed spirits. Aurelius Fortunatus placed this for his dearest father Aurelius Victorinus, who deserved well, and for his sweetest mother Aurelia Cara, who deserved well. Mother lived 20 years, Father lived 80 years.
EDCS-13000680.summary: A funerary epitaph for Aurelius Victorinus and Aurelia Cara, set up by their son Aurelius Fortunatus, recording their ages at death.

EDCS-13000681.translation: To the departed spirits. Marcus Caecilius Ianuarius lived 62 years, 11 months, 25 days. Marcus Caecilius Ianuarius made this for his dearest father.
EDCS-13000681.summary: A funerary epitaph for a father, set up by his son Marcus Caecilius Ianuarius, recording the father's age at death.

EDCS-13000682.translation: To the departed spirits. Calpurnia Caesita lived 25 years. She lies here. Calpurnius Felix and Hirria Rogata, her parents, made this for their sweetest daughter.
EDCS-13000682.summary: A funerary epitaph for Calpurnia Caesita, recording her age at death and set up by her parents Calpurnius Felix and Hirria Rogata.

EDCS-13000684.translation: Cassius Aleator, father, and Rutilia Honorata, mother, made this for their most devoted daughter, who lived 16 years and 17 days; she is buried here.
EDCS-13000684.summary: A funerary epitaph for a daughter, recording her lifespan and erected by her parents.

EDCS-13000685.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Caius Claudius Salvianus lived piously for 2 years, 7 months, and 21 days.
EDCS-13000685.summary: A funerary epitaph for a young child, Caius Claudius Salvianus, dedicated to the departed spirits.

EDCS-13000686.translation: To the departed spirits. For Claudia Aphrodisia.
EDCS-13000686.summary: A funerary epitaph fragment for Claudia Aphrodisia.

EDCS-13000687.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcus Cocceius Successus lived 77 years, 4 months, and 10 days. Quintus Cocceius Annianus, his son, made this for his dearest.
EDCS-13000687.summary: A funerary epitaph for Marcus Cocceius Successus, erected by his son, Quintus Cocceius Annianus.

EDCS-13000688.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Cornelius Ianuarianus lived 18 years, 9 months, and 20 days. Cesellia Galla made this for her dearest son.
EDCS-13000688.summary: A funerary epitaph for Cornelius Ianuarianus, erected by his mother, Cesellia Galla.

EDCS-13000689.translation: Aulus Cornelius Longinus made this for himself during his lifetime and for his wife, who reached the end of her allotted span.
EDCS-13000689.summary: A funerary epitaph for Aulus Cornelius Longinus and his wife, made by himself during his lifetime.

EDCS-13000690.translation: Cornelia Afrodisia lived 50 years. Iulius Probus made this for his most devoted wife. She lies here.
EDCS-13000690.summary: A funerary epitaph for Cornelia Afrodisia, recording her age at death and set up by her husband Iulius Probus.

EDCS-13000691.translation: To the departed spirits. Cornificia Fortunata lived [---].
EDCS-13000691.summary: A funerary epitaph fragment for Cornificia Fortunata, recording her name and part of her lifespan.

EDCS-13000692.translation: To the departed spirits. Domitia Primitiva lived 32 years. She lies here. Gaius Domitius Pudens made this for his dearest and most faithful freedwoman.
EDCS-13000692.summary: A funerary epitaph for Domitia Primitiva, recording her age at death and set up by her patron Gaius Domitius Pudens.

EDCS-13000693.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Marcus Faonius Marcellus, son of Caius, lived [unknown years]. He made this monument in his own lifetime.
EDCS-13000693.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcus Faonius Marcellus, who dedicated his tomb during his life, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-13000694.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Titus Flavius Agilis lived eighty years. Flavius, his son, made this for his dutiful father.
EDCS-13000694.summary: This funerary epitaph records Titus Flavius Agilis, who lived to be eighty, with the monument erected by his son, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-13000695.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Flavius Gemellus lived piously for 21 years. Optatus, his father, made this for his most devoted son.
EDCS-13000695.summary: A funerary epitaph for Flavius Gemellus, erected by his father, Optatus.

EDCS-13000696.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Titus Flavius Ianuarius lived twenty years. His heirs made this; he is buried here.
EDCS-13000696.summary: This funerary epitaph for Titus Flavius Ianuarius, who died at twenty, was made by his heirs, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-13000697.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcus Flavius Marcellus lived; he made this for himself during his lifetime.
EDCS-13000697.summary: A funerary epitaph for Marcus Flavius Marcellus, made by himself during his lifetime.

EDCS-13000698.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Flavia Caelia lived 31 years; she is buried here. Xanthinus made this for his devoted wife.
EDCS-13000698.summary: A funerary epitaph for Flavia Caelia, erected by her husband, Xanthinus.

EDCS-13000699.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Flavian[a] lived seventeen years. Demetrianus made this for his dearest wife.
EDCS-13000699.summary: This funerary epitaph records Flavian[a], who died at seventeen, with the monument erected by her husband Demetrianus, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-13000700.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Quintus Folius Felix lived twelve years. Martialis made this for his dutiful son.
EDCS-13000700.summary: This funerary epitaph records Quintus Folius Felix, who died at twelve, with the monument erected by his father Martialis, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-13000701.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Fortunata lived 40 years. Tertiola, her aunt, made this.
EDCS-13000701.summary: A funerary epitaph for Fortunata, erected by her aunt, Tertiola.

EDCS-13000702.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Fortunata lived 56 years; she is buried here. Mun p. placed this.
EDCS-13000702.summary: A funerary epitaph for Fortunata, erected by an individual identified as Mun p. posuit.

EDCS-13000703.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Fusca lived ten months and five days; she is buried here. Gaius Caecilius Cinna[?] made this for his dearest wife.
EDCS-13000703.summary: This funerary epitaph records Fusca, who died at ten months and five days, with the monument erected by her husband Gaius Caecilius Cinna[?], likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-13000705.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Gordius Paetus lived 91 years.
EDCS-13000705.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan of Gordius Paetus.

EDCS-13000706.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Ianuarius lived thirty-six years. His father(?) made this.
EDCS-13000706.summary: This funerary epitaph records Ianuarius, who lived to be thirty-six, with the monument erected by his father(?), likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-13000707.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Ianuarius Halconius(?) the dutiful lived seventy years.
EDCS-13000707.summary: This funerary epitaph records the life of Ianuarius Halconius(?), who lived to be seventy, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-13000708.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Ianuaria lived 5 years, 5 months, and 2 days. VA III AE
EDCS-13000708.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan of Ianuaria, with some unclear abbreviations at the end.

EDCS-13000709.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Caius Iulius Fortis lived 70 years. He is buried here. Agrilia Donata made this for her husband.
EDCS-13000709.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan of Caius Iulius Fortis and states it was made by his wife, Agrilia Donata.

EDCS-13000710.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Iulius Getulicus lived 76 years. His son erected this.
EDCS-13000710.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan of Iulius Getulicus and states it was erected by his son.

EDCS-13000711.translation: Julius Gududio lived eight years; he is buried here. Julia Saturnina made this for her sweetest son.
EDCS-13000711.summary: This funerary epitaph records Julius Gududio, who died at eight, with the monument erected by his mother Julia Saturnina, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-13000712.summary: This is a genitive inscription, likely a tombstone or dedication belonging to Caius Iulius Lucilianus.

EDCS-13000713.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Quintus Julius Minervalis lived seventy years, seven months, and seven days; he is buried here. Tullius Pistus made this.
EDCS-13000713.summary: This funerary epitaph records Quintus Julius Minervalis, who lived to seventy years, seven months, and seven days, with the monument erected by Tullius Pistus, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-13000714.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed, sacred. Gaius Julius Niger lived 65 years. Caecilia Candida made this for her most beloved husband.
EDCS-13000714.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Gaius Julius Niger at age 65 and made by his wife, Caecilia Candida.

EDCS-13000715.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Caius Iulius Rufinus lived 39 years. His mother made this for her son.
EDCS-13000715.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan of Caius Iulius Rufinus and states it was made by his mother.

EDCS-13000716.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed, sacred. Speratus made this for his most beloved daughter, who lived 2 years, 8 months, and 9 days.
EDCS-13000716.summary: A funerary epitaph for a young girl named Speratus, detailing her lifespan and erected by her parent.

EDCS-13000718.translation: Gaius Julius Victorinus lived 60 years; he lies here. Julius Vitalis and Arnobius made this for their dearest father.
EDCS-13000718.summary: A funerary inscription for Gaius Julius Victorinus, who lived to be 60, and was commemorated by his sons, Julius Vitalis and Arnobius.

EDCS-13000719.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Decimus Iulius Capito made this for himself and his wife during his lifetime.
EDCS-13000719.summary: This funerary epitaph records that Decimus Iulius Capito prepared this monument for himself and his wife while he was alive.

EDCS-13000720.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed, sacred. Iulia Eutyche lived 35 years, 10 months, and 12 days; she lies here. Amantius made this for his dearest wife.
EDCS-13000720.summary: A funerary epitaph for Iulia Eutyche, detailing her lifespan and erected by her husband, Amantius.

EDCS-13000721.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed, sacred. Iulia Fortunata lived piously for 60 years, chaste, good, inviolate. This rare gift from a husband, Fortunata, is for you. Worthy of my name Hardalius, as you remain alive and my children's children thrive while you are safe.
EDCS-13000721.summary: A funerary inscription for Iulia Fortunata, who lived 60 years, a dedication from her husband Hardalius, praising her virtues and longevity.

EDCS-13000722.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed, sacred. Iulia Fortunata lived 40 years. Maximus made this for his pious mother.
EDCS-13000722.summary: A funerary epitaph for Iulia Fortunata, who lived 40 years, erected by her son, Maximus.

EDCS-13000723.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Iulia Venusta, daughter of Lucius, lived [years]. Pious, holy.
EDCS-13000723.summary: This funerary epitaph records the name and filial relationship of Iulia Venusta, describing her as pious and holy.

EDCS-13000724.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed, sacred. Iulia Verecunda lived 2 years; she lies here.
EDCS-13000724.summary: A funerary epitaph for a child named Iulia Verecunda, who died at age 2.

EDCS-13000725.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Maiorica lived 24 years. Vitalis, her father, erected this for his pious daughter.
EDCS-13000725.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan of Maiorica and states it was erected by her father, Vitalis.

EDCS-13000726.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Maria Concordia lived 27 years, 10 months, and 7 days. Maria Tertia [made this] for [her] mother.
EDCS-13000726.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan of Maria Concordia and states it was made by Maria Tertia for her mother.

EDCS-13000727.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Martia Cestia lived 40 years. Quintus Acceptus [made this] for his son.
EDCS-13000727.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Martia Cestia, set up by her son Quintus Acceptus.

EDCS-13000728.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Matia Fortunata lived 23 years.
EDCS-13000728.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Matia Fortunata.

EDCS-13000729.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed, sacred. Matronica lived 50 years. Ulpius (?) Rugosus lived 50 years, 6 months, and 2 days. Lupus made this for his parents.
EDCS-13000729.summary: A funerary inscription commemorating two individuals, Matronica and Ulpius Rugosus, and dedicated by their son Lupus.

EDCS-13000730.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Maurica lived 20 years. Extricata made this for her daughter, who is buried here.
EDCS-13000730.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Maurica, set up by her daughter Extricata.

EDCS-13000731.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed, sacred. Lucius Minucius Saturus lived 127 years. Lucius Minucius Felix made this for his excellent father.
EDCS-13000731.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lucius Minucius Saturus, who incredibly lived to 127 years, erected by his son, Lucius Minucius Felix.

EDCS-13000732.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Mustula lived 6 years. Her devoted father made this.
EDCS-13000732.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Mustula, set up by her father.

EDCS-13000733.translation: To M. Fortunata. I pass from life, aged 75 years and 3 months, but I ask and beg you, my dear friends, do not entrust yourselves to such friendships. I commend myself to a new friendship, [a friendship] of affection without enmity, malice, or deceit. [She] departed this life 1 year, 1 month, 12 days, 7 hours ago. Caelius Ianuarius made this for his wife, who is buried here.
EDCS-13000733.summary: A funerary epitaph for M. Fortunata, set up by her husband Caelius Ianuarius, containing a personal reflection on friendships and the deceased's lifespan and time of death.

EDCS-13000734.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed, sacred. Occia Auge lived 37 years; she lies here. Her husband Pomponius Gaetulus made this.
EDCS-13000734.summary: A funerary epitaph for Occia Auge, who lived 37 years, erected by her husband, Pomponius Gaetulus.

EDCS-13000736.translation: Gabia Fausta lived piously for 19 years.
EDCS-13000736.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Gabia Fausta, who died at the age of 19.

EDCS-13000737.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Publius Paetius Abascantius, pious, lived 25 years, 11 months, and 22 days. He is buried here. His father, Publius Paetius Abascantius, made this.
EDCS-13000737.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Publius Paetius Abascantius, who lived to 25 years, 11 months, and 22 days, and was erected by his father.

EDCS-13000738.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Perellia Fortunula lived 12 years. Her parents made this.
EDCS-13000738.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Perellia Fortunula, who died at the age of 12, and was erected by her parents.

EDCS-13000739.translation: Publius Petronius Festus, son of Decimus, pious, lived 7 years, 5 months, and half an hour. He is buried here.
EDCS-13000739.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Publius Petronius Festus, who lived to 7 years, 5 months, and half an hour.

EDCS-13000740.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Petronius Securus lived 22 years. Aventius Augustalis, his heir, set this up.
EDCS-13000740.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Petronius Securus, set up by his heir Aventius Augustalis.

EDCS-13000741.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Gaius Plotius Maximus lived 65 years. Labenia Glauce made this for her pious husband. He is buried here.
EDCS-13000741.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Gaius Plotius Maximus, who lived to 65 years, erected by his wife Labenia Glauce.

EDCS-13000742.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Paetius Augendus, dutiful, lived 30 years and 6 months.
EDCS-13000742.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Paetius Augendus, noting his piety.

EDCS-13000743.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus Pompeius Felix lived 77 years. His sons made this for their dutiful father.
EDCS-13000743.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Quintus Pompeius Felix, set up by his sons.

EDCS-13000744.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus Pompeius Felix lived 3 years, 9 months, and six days. Suricus, his grandfather, set this up.
EDCS-13000744.summary: A funerary epitaph for Quintus Pompeius Felix, set up by his grandfather Suricus, recording his short lifespan.

EDCS-13000745.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Pompeia Margarita, known for her character and modesty, her new and holy piety recognized, lived 56 years, 6 months, and 5 days. Aulus Cornelius Longinus made this for his most rare wife. She is buried here.
EDCS-13000745.summary: A funerary epitaph for Pompeia Margarita, set up by her husband Aulus Cornelius Longinus, praising her virtues and recording her lifespan.

EDCS-13000746.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcus Pomponius Adiutor lived 62 years, 1 month, and 17 days.
EDCS-13000746.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Marcus Pomponius Adiutor, who died at the age of 62 years, 1 month, and 17 days.

EDCS-13000747.translation: Marcus Pomponius Albinus lived 63 years, and 16 days.
EDCS-13000747.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Marcus Pomponius Albinus, who died at the age of 63 years and 16 days.

EDCS-13000748.translation: Pomponia Fortunata lived 15 years. Pomponius Coronta made this for his dearest sister.
EDCS-13000748.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the age of Pomponia Fortunata and dedicating the monument to her by Pomponius Coronta.

EDCS-13000749.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Pomponia Quartilla lived 73 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-13000749.summary: This tombstone inscription records the age of Pomponia Quartilla and states that she is buried at this location.

EDCS-13000750.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. O Pompōsāi, lived 16 years. Hermophilus made this for his dearest daughter. She is buried here.
EDCS-13000750.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Pompōsāi, who lived to 16 years, erected by her father Hermophilus.

EDCS-13000751.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. [Ru]frius(?) [---] A/[---] [P]ompe[ia](?) Ingenua(?) made this for her dearest husband. He is buried here.
EDCS-13000751.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for an unidentified husband, erected by his wife Ingenua(?), with significant lacunae.

EDCS-13000753.translation: Seleucus, heir and fellow freedman, made this.
EDCS-13000753.summary: This inscription records that Seleucus, who was both an heir and a fellow freedman, erected the monument.

EDCS-13000754.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcus Sempronius Amaranthus lived 60 years. His son made this for his pious father.
EDCS-13000754.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcus Sempronius Amaranthus, who lived to 60 years, erected by his son.

EDCS-13000755.translation: To the departed spirits. Sergia Rustica lived 36 years, 7 months. Claudius Titius Crescens [erected this].
EDCS-13000755.summary: A funerary epitaph for Sergia Rustica, who died at age 36 years and 7 months, likely set up by Claudius Titius Crescens.

EDCS-13000757.translation: To the departed spirits. Speratus lived 34 years.
EDCS-13000757.summary: A funerary epitaph for Speratus, who died at age 34.

EDCS-13000758.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Successus lived 35 years. His brother Iulius Chresimus made this.
EDCS-13000758.summary: This tombstone inscription records the age of Successus and dedicates the monument to him by his brother Iulius Chresimus.

EDCS-13000759.translation: To the departed spirits. Tadius Cotronius lived 3 years; his father made this. To the departed spirits. Gaius Tadius Victorinus lived [an unknown age].
EDCS-13000759.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Tadius Cotronius at age 3, set up by his father, followed by a partial epitaph for Gaius Tadius Victorinus.

EDCS-13000760.translation: To the departed spirits. Publius Tanonnius Felix, son of Publius, lived 27 years. Dearest son, he is buried here.
EDCS-13000760.summary: A funerary epitaph for Publius Tanonnius Felix, who died at age 27, likely erected by his children.

EDCS-13000761.translation: To the departed spirits. Valerius Sisa made [this] for himself and his parents while alive. To the departed spirits. Homullia Secundilla lived 40 years. Sisa made [this] for his mother. To the departed spirits. Valerius Natalis lived 75 years. Sisa made [this] for his father. To the departed spirits. Valerius Eupraxius and Iulia Tertia lived [unknown ages]. Sisa made [this]. To the departed spirits. Banasius lived [unknown age]. And Pretiosa lived [unknown age].
EDCS-13000761.summary: A funerary monument with multiple inscriptions, including self-dedications and dedications to family members by Valerius Sisa, recording various individuals' ages at death.

EDCS-13000762.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Iviius rests here, an old and most loving woman, for her most excellent father.
EDCS-13000762.summary: This tombstone inscription records that Iviius rests here, and it is dedicated to her most excellent father.

EDCS-13000763.translation: To the departed spirits. Marcus Vettius Rufus, son of Marcus, of the Papiria tribe, pious, lived 34 years. Marcus Vettius Rufus (his) father and Lucius Vettius Tenax, (his) brother, pious, took care to have this made.
EDCS-13000763.summary: A funerary epitaph for Marcus Vettius Rufus, who died at age 34, erected by his father and brother.

EDCS-13000764.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Vettia Ianuaria lived 11 years. Her parents made this for their pious daughter.
EDCS-13000764.summary: This tombstone inscription records the age of Vettia Ianuaria and dedicates the monument to her by her parents.

EDCS-13000765.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Caius Vibius Achilles lived 17 years, 6 months, and 24 days. The remains of the funeral rites from Carthage rest in this ground. Iulius Faustianus made this for his best friend.
EDCS-13000765.summary: This inscription records the age and burial details of Caius Vibius Achilles, noting his funeral rites originated from Carthage, and it was made by his friend Iulius Faustianus.

EDCS-13000766.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Victor Girmolis lived 60 years. His husband made this for his wife. Sacred to the departed spirits. Donatula lived 68 years. Her husband made this for her. Sacred to the departed spirits. VI NO A LV.
EDCS-13000766.summary: This inscription contains multiple tombstone records, one for Victor Girmolis (aged 60, dedicated by husband) and another for Donatula (aged 68, dedicated by husband), with a fragmented final entry.

EDCS-13000767.translation: To the departed spirits. Vindemia lived 35 years. Ispiculus made [this] for his dearest wife; she is buried here.
EDCS-13000767.summary: A funerary epitaph for Vindemia, who died at age 35, erected by her husband Ispiculus.

EDCS-13000768.translation: To the departed spirits. Ulpius Liberalis lived 15 years, 11 months, 7 days. He is buried here. Marcus Ulpius Vibianus (father) and Aurelia Victoria (mother) made [this] for their incomparable son.
EDCS-13000768.summary: A funerary epitaph for Ulpius Liberalis, who died at age 15 years, 11 months, and 7 days, erected by his parents.

EDCS-13000769.translation: To the departed spirits. Ulpia Quinta lived 40 years. Hortensius Geminius made [this] for his dearest wife.
EDCS-13000769.summary: A funerary epitaph for Ulpia Quinta, who died at age 40, erected by her husband Hortensius Geminius.

EDCS-13000770.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Ulpia Victoria lived 28 years. IICOT OSBOLI made this. She is buried here.
EDCS-13000770.summary: This tombstone inscription records the age of Ulpia Victoria and states she is buried here, with the monument made by IICOT OSBOLI.

EDCS-13000771.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Olca, daughter of Caius, Euporia the dutiful, lived 60 years. Marcus Ulpius Eumelus made this for his most dutiful wife. She is buried here.
EDCS-13000771.summary: This tombstone inscription records the age of Euporia, daughter of Caius, and dedicates the monument to her by her husband Marcus Ulpius Eumelus.

EDCS-13000772.translation: To the departed spirits. [She] was good with good character, urbane and holy, with her Gaius, a worthy wife. I adore your memory. Few are the epitaphs to seek yours. To you, our good and cheerful one. We go to you for many years. We return to you, dear one, unless your good reputation and chaste [innocence]... [illegible]... [illegible]... [illegible]... were noble [illegible]... [illegible] frugal [illegible] NOT enough [illegible] your [illegible] full [illegible] vows [illegible] your [illegible] Oh dear [illegible] will learn and these [illegible] of verses I read and greet you, my sweetest Brea, who lived [illegible] pregnant and returned [her] life to nature. [illegible] [illegible] Brea, farewell, woman. May you fare well, and this sacred [offering]. [For] rare and modest [virtue].
EDCS-13000772.summary: A complex and partially preserved funerary text praising the deceased Brea, noting her virtue, her relationship with Gaius, and her death in childbirth, possibly erected by her family.

EDCS-13000773.translation: Most innocent, incomparable, unhappy father and procurator.
EDCS-13000773.summary: This inscription is a parent's lament for their deceased son, identified as a procurator, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-13000774.summary: This is a simple funerary dedication by parents for a deceased individual, dating to the Roman period.

EDCS-13000775.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. ... lived 25 years for his most dutiful daughter.
EDCS-13000775.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the Divine Shades for a deceased daughter who lived 25 years, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-13000776.translation: Here rests in peace, Palladius the bishop of holy memory, who lived 52 years, of which he lived 12 years in the episcopate.
EDCS-13000776.summary: This epitaph records the life and episcopal service of Bishop Palladius, who lived 52 years and served for 12, likely dating to the Late Roman or early Byzantine period.

EDCS-13000777.translation: Here rested Petronius of good memory, who lived 18 years and departed on the 8th day before the Kalends of November.
EDCS-13000777.summary: This epitaph records the life and death date of Petronius, who died at age 18, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-13000778.translation: Here Marcella lived three years and six months, and rested in peace on the 4th day before the Kalends of November.
EDCS-13000778.summary: This epitaph records the life and death date of a young girl named Marcella, who died at age 3.5, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-13000779.translation: Here rested Quodvultdeus the presbyter of good memory, faithful in peace, who lived 32 years and departed on the 17th day before the Kalends of July.
EDCS-13000779.summary: This epitaph records the life and death date of Quodvultdeus, a faithful presbyter who lived 32 years, likely from the Late Roman or early Byzantine period.

EDCS-13000780.translation: Here rests our son Geminus, faithful in peace, who lived 5 years, 5 months, and 25 days; he was born on the 4th day before the Nones of February in the 7th year of our lord King Trasamund, and departed on the 8th hour of the Sabbath day, on the 17th day before the Kalends of August in the 12th year (of his reign).
EDCS-13000780.summary: This epitaph commemorates a young boy named Geminus, detailing his birth and death dates within the reign of King Trasamund II, likely from the Vandalic kingdom in North Africa (mid-5th to early 6th century CE).

EDCS-13000782.translation: Here Marcellus rested in peace, who lived 75 years.
EDCS-13000782.summary: This epitaph records the life of Marcellus, who lived 75 years, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-13000783.translation: Here rested Silibudi of good memory in peace, who lived 28 years; deposited on the Ides of November.
EDCS-13000783.summary: This epitaph records the life and burial date of Silibudi, who lived 28 years, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-13000784.translation: Ustriut, faithful, lived in peace for 40 years and one month.
EDCS-13000784.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Ustriut, who lived in peace.

EDCS-13000786.translation: Afrodisius lived for 33 years, laid to rest on the 13th day before the Kalends of November.
EDCS-13000786.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan and burial date of Afrodisius.

EDCS-13000800.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Margarita, pious, lived 75 years, is buried here. Gudullus, assistant in the archive of our Emperor, [made this] for his most rare mother-in-law.
EDCS-13000800.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Margarita, who lived 75 years, with her son-in-law Gudullus, an archive assistant, as the dedicator, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-13000801.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Attius Mattius lived 47 years. His sons made [this].
EDCS-13000801.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the life of Lucius Attius Mattius, who lived 47 years, and dedicated by his sons, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-13000802.translation: Amidst the fragrant groves, where Mother Earth rejoices and flourishes with crafted flowers, and barely allows the sunlit day with leaves, here, providentially, Felix Florentinus, an ornament to your chaste and modest wife Hostiliana and your son Splendonillus, constructed this beautiful house...
EDCS-13000802.summary: This is a funerary epigram praising Felix Florentinus and his family, likely commemorating the construction of a tomb or memorial.

EDCS-13000803.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Perellius Felix lived [? number] years. Caecilia [Zaba?] [made this] for her husband.
EDCS-13000803.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lucius Perellius Felix, whose age at death is partially restored, and dedicated by his wife Caecilia, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-13000804.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Rogatina lived for 50 years; her husband made this.
EDCS-13000804.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Rogatina and stating that her husband erected the monument.

EDCS-13000805.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus Septimius Iulianus lived 90 years. Caecilia Paulina made [this] for her most beloved husband.
EDCS-13000805.summary: This funerary epitaph records that Quintus Septimius Iulianus lived 90 years and was dedicated by his wife Caecilia Paulina, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-13000806.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Publius Velleius Tettienus lived for 22 years.
EDCS-13000806.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Publius Velleius Tettienus.

EDCS-13000865.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Aelia Quintula lived for 3 months and 21 days; her father made this.
EDCS-13000865.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Aelia Quintula and stating that her father erected the monument.

EDCS-13000866.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Marcus Volumnius Donatus lived for 71 years.
EDCS-13000866.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Marcus Volumnius Donatus.

EDCS-13000867.translation: Decimus Seius Iuvenis, son of Decimus, of the Quirina tribe, from Burdigala, a soldier of the Third Augustan Legion, in the century of Nepos, lived 46 years, served 23 years, is buried here. Gisatia Seiana made [this] for her husband, who deserved well of her.
EDCS-13000867.summary: This is the funerary epitaph of Decimus Seius Iuvenis, a soldier from Burdigala, who lived 46 years and served for 23 years, dedicated by his wife Gisatia Seiana, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-13000868.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Aemilia Iulia lived for 60 years; she rests here.
EDCS-13000868.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Aemilia Iulia and her burial place.

EDCS-13000869.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Domitius Saturninus lived 25 years and 13 days. Domitia Crescentina arranged for [this] to be made for her dearest brother.
EDCS-13000869.summary: A funerary epitaph for Domitius Saturninus, who lived 25 years and 13 days, dedicated by his sister Domitia Crescentina, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-13000870.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius M. Rogatus lived 95 years. His sons made [this].
EDCS-13000870.summary: This funerary epitaph records the life of Lucius M. Rogatus, who lived 95 years, and was made by his sons, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-13000909.translation: Antonia Aquilina, daughter of Quintus, dutiful and dear, lived for less than 5 years; she rests here. Antonius Martialis, her father, placed this for the deserving.
EDCS-13000909.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the short life of Antonia Aquilina and commemorating her father.

EDCS-13000910.translation: Arrius Saturninus, dutiful, lived for 37 years; he rests here.
EDCS-13000910.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Arrius Saturninus and his burial place.

EDCS-13000911.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Calpurnius Candidus, pious, lived X years; he is buried here. Arrius Magister and Ursacia made this.
EDCS-13000911.summary: A funerary epitaph for Calpurnius Candidus, set up by Arrius Magister and Ursacia, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13000912.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Flavius Antinous lived 55 years. Octavia made this for her husband.
EDCS-13000912.summary: A funerary epitaph for Flavius Antinous, erected by his wife Octavia, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13000913.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Flavius Augurinus, pious, lived 21 years; he is buried here. Fortunatus to his dearest brother: may the earth be light upon you, may your bones rest well.
EDCS-13000913.summary: A funerary epitaph for Flavius Augurinus, set up by his brother Fortunatus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13000914.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Flavius Victor lived 90 years; he is buried here. Fortunatus set this up for his excellent father.
EDCS-13000914.summary: A funerary epitaph for Flavius Victor, erected by his son Fortunatus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13000915.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits for Flavia Dubetata, daughter of Publius, pious, who lived 30 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-13000915.summary: A funerary epitaph for Flavia Dubetata, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13000916.translation: Flavia Spesina, a woman of the rarest character, lived 70 years; she is buried here. Fortunatus, her son, set this up.
EDCS-13000916.summary: A funerary epitaph for Flavia Spesina, erected by her son Fortunatus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13000917.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Mundus lived 40 years; his heirs made this.
EDCS-13000917.summary: A funerary epitaph for Mundus, set up by his heirs, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13000918.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Noventia Satura lived 16 years and 2 months.
EDCS-13000918.summary: A funerary epitaph for Noventia Satura, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13000919.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Satulla, pious, lived 2 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-13000919.summary: A funerary epitaph for the young child Satulla, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13000920.summary: A funerary epitaph for Aemilius Saturninus, likely from the Roman Imperial period, though the end of the text is damaged.

EDCS-13000921.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Victoria lived 63 years; she lies here. Her father Syntropus placed this.
EDCS-13000921.summary: A funerary epitaph for Victoria, likely from the Imperial period, indicating her age and that it was erected by her father.

EDCS-13000922.translation: lived 20 years. Q., his devoted wife.
EDCS-13000922.summary: A fragmentary funerary epitaph, possibly from the Imperial period, recording the age of the deceased and mentioning a surviving wife.

EDCS-13000924.translation: Iunius Super lived 30 years; he lies here.
EDCS-13000924.summary: A funerary epitaph from the Imperial period for Iunius Super, stating his age and burial.

EDCS-13000933.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Lucius Aemilius Severinus qui et Phillyrio vixit annos LXVI plus minus et pro amore Romano quievit ab hoc Capelliano captus memor amicitiae pietatis Victoricus qui et Verota\n
EDCS-13000933.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Aemilius Severinus, also known as Phillyrio, lived 66 years more or less, and rested from this life, captured by Roman affection. Victoricus, also known as Verota, [made this] in memory of his friendship and devotion.
EDCS-13000933.summary: This funerary epitaph records that Lucius Aemilius Severinus, also known as Phillyrio, lived 66 years, and was dedicated by Victoricus (also known as Verota) in memory of their friendship and devotion, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-13000934.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Aelia Nina lived 85 years, is buried here. Aeli S. and P. made [this].
EDCS-13000934.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Aelia Nina, who lived 85 years, dedicated by Aeli S. and P., likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-13000935.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Gaius Apuleius Martis lived 60 years, is buried here.
EDCS-13000935.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the life of Gaius Apuleius Martis, who lived 60 years, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-13000936.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Eppia Exstricata lived 87 years. Eppius made this for his mother.
EDCS-13000936.summary: A funerary epitaph from the Imperial period, indicating Eppia Exstricata's age and that it was dedicated by her son Eppius.

EDCS-13000937.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Iulius Geminius lived 80 years and 17 days.
EDCS-13000937.summary: A funerary epitaph from the Imperial period for Iulius Geminius, detailing his age and days.

EDCS-13000938.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Megonia Rogata lived 74 years. RIELONIT ME 79.
EDCS-13000938.summary: A funerary epitaph from the Imperial period for Megonia Rogata, stating her age and including a possibly corrupted or cryptic second age/identifier.

EDCS-13000939.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Numerius Petronius Successus, aged 85, is buried here.
EDCS-13000939.summary: A funerary epitaph for Numerius Petronius Successus, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13000940.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. I, Marcus P. C., a young man, made this so that I may live as an old man.
EDCS-13000940.summary: A funerary epitaph from the Imperial period where the deceased, Marcus P. C., expresses a desire for a long life after death.

EDCS-13000941.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Tutia Vitalis, daughter of Publius, lived 67 years, is buried here.
EDCS-13000941.summary: A funerary epitaph for Tutia Vitalis, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13000942.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Valeria Nigra lived approximately 90 years.
EDCS-13000942.summary: A funerary epitaph from the Imperial period for Valeria Nigra, indicating her approximate age at death.

EDCS-13000943.translation: Lucius Laelius Silvanus, priest of Saturn, willingly paid his vow.
EDCS-13000943.summary: A dedication from the Imperial period recording Lucius Laelius Silvanus fulfilling a vow as a priest of Saturn.

EDCS-13000944.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Ianuaria lived 25 years. Irso Satur made this for his sister.
EDCS-13000944.summary: A funerary epitaph from the Imperial period for Ianuaria, stating her age and that it was erected by her brother Irso Satur.

EDCS-13000945.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. His sons erected this tombstone for the health of their father Marinus, who lived 80 years and 3 months.
EDCS-13000945.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by sons for their father Marinus, who lived to be 80 years old.

EDCS-13000946.translation: Whose outstanding kindness and prudence were mourned not only by his parents but also by his neighbors. For this reason, his most beloved sons erected a tomb for their most exceptional father with 5,000 sesterces, in his memory. May the living be well disposed to the Divine Shades, so that he may rest in good peace, who lived 53 years.
EDCS-13000946.summary: A funerary epitaph for a man whose sons erected a tomb with 5,000 sesterces, mourning his kindness and prudence, and who lived 53 years.

EDCS-13000947.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Migginn Iatunis lived 75 years.
EDCS-13000947.summary: A funerary epitaph for Migginn Iatunis, who lived 75 years.

EDCS-13000948.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Sarrona lived 90 years.
EDCS-13000948.summary: A funerary epitaph for Sarrona, who lived 90 years.

EDCS-13000950.translation: Mensa Sannasi lived 52 years. Mensa Donatiani lived 81 years. [He/She] departed from [his/her] body.
EDCS-13000950.summary: A funerary inscription recording the ages of two individuals, Mensa Sannasi (52) and Mensa Donatiani (81), with the latter noted as having departed from their body.

EDCS-13000955.translation: And the scepter passed to the king, which he alone held. You, Juno, who summon the storms and winds, it is very easy for you to stir up fears, for you thunder at your quiet brother; you, born of clouds, grant moisture to the lands. Perhaps the ages would have brought death to the gods too, lest you place a crisis through the delicate breezes. Indeed, the very mass of the sky would barely remain firm, this same queen of the gods, lest you, Juno, with rising deep air, support the stars. Unfathomable, you are present to no one's eyes, you command the returning breaths to feel, which you deny the ability to see. You are not known, so familiar to your own, so you block the sky from the rains descending to earth, when you do not close the path of light, nor is it lawful to know why you embrace contrary powers equally. Hail, true ruler of the gods, daughter of Saturn.
EDCS-13000955.summary: A poetic inscription addressing Juno, praising her power over nature and the heavens, and acknowledging her divine authority.

EDCS-13000956.translation: Azrubal Ar tanus had the temple made at his own expense and gladly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-13000956.summary: An inscription recording that Azrubal Ar tanus funded the construction of a temple and fulfilled a vow.

EDCS-13000957.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Cossidia Mazzic, pious, lived 47 years. May your bones rest well; may the earth be light on you.
EDCS-13000957.summary: A funerary epitaph for Cossidia Mazzic, who lived 47 years, with wishes for her peaceful repose.

EDCS-13000958.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Fabia Victoria, pious, lived 21 years. May the bones rest well.
EDCS-13000958.summary: A funerary epitaph for Fabia Victoria, who lived 21 years, with wishes for her peaceful repose.

EDCS-13000959.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Lucius Neratius Rogatianus, son of Lucius, pious, lived 25 years.
EDCS-13000959.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lucius Neratius Rogatianus, son of Lucius, who lived 25 years.

EDCS-13000960.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Dead. Dandas, son of C. Pa iv iis, lived 9 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-13000960.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for a child named Dandas, recording his age at death and burial.

EDCS-13000961.translation: Sacred to Augustus. Lucius Lepidius Primulus, the priest, initiated in this place, erected the altar, paid his vow, and made the offering.
EDCS-13000961.summary: This is a dedication to Augustus by the priest Lucius Lepidius Primulus, who erected an altar.

EDCS-13000962.translation: To Jupiter Stator. Marcus Anniolenus Faustus, a veteran and former decurion of the tribune of the III Augusta legion, erected this at his own expense, fulfilling a vow he made as a soldier upon his honorable discharge.
EDCS-13000962.summary: This is a dedication to Jupiter Stator by Marcus Anniolenus Faustus, a veteran, to fulfill a vow.

EDCS-13000965.translation: For the safety of our lords Diocletian and Maximian Augusti, the oil-room, which had not been in use for many years, was restored and rededicated in their age, under the most distinguished proconsul Aurelius Aristobulus and the most distinguished legate Macrinius Sossianus.
EDCS-13000965.summary: This inscription records the restoration and rededication of an oil-room during the reign of Diocletian and Maximian, mentioning the proconsul and legate.

EDCS-13000967.translation: For the prosperity of the happy times of our lord Flavius Jovian, ever victorious Augustus, under Clodius Octavianus, most distinguished proconsul of the province of Africa, [this was dedicated by] Ulpius Faventinus, a distinguished man.
EDCS-13000967.summary: This is a dedication for the prosperity of Emperor Flavius Jovian, made under the proconsul Clodius Octavianus by Ulpius Faventinus.

EDCS-13000972.translation: Quintus Baebius and Marcus Papirius Rogatus Faustus, the aediles, made the steps at their own expense.
EDCS-13000972.summary: This records the construction of steps by two aediles, Quintus Baebius and Marcus Papirius Rogatus Faustus, at their own expense.

EDCS-13000973.translation: Emeritus, a devoted veteran, lived 70 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-13000973.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for a veteran named Emeritus, recording his age at death and burial.

EDCS-13000974.translation: Marcus Anniolenus Faustus [erected this] to Secundus his grandfather, Faustus his father, Saxona his brother, Faustianus his brother's son, and Nabera Caeci primus.
EDCS-13000974.summary: This is a dedication by Marcus Anniolenus Faustus to his deceased relatives.

EDCS-13000975.translation: Gaius Gabinius Sabinus Fortunatus, son of Publius, made this.
EDCS-13000975.summary: This is a dedication by Gaius Gabinius Sabinus Fortunatus.

EDCS-13000976.translation: Iulia Maxima, devoted, lived 31 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-13000976.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Iulia Maxima, recording her age at death and burial.

EDCS-13000977.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Martialis lived outside the boundaries.
EDCS-13000977.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Martialis and the location of his burial outside the city limits.

EDCS-13000978.translation: Caecilianus made this for his wife Occia Spicula.
EDCS-13000978.summary: This funerary epitaph records that Caecilianus erected a monument for his wife, Occia Spicula.

EDCS-13000979.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Apisia Donatula lived for 8 years and 2 months. Lucius Ortensius Felix made this altar for his most loving and incomparable wife. Lucius is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Ortensius Felix the pious lived for 61 years and 9 months. He is buried here. Lucius Ortensius Iunior the pious lived for 60 years. His wife Sahnamt the pious lived for [unknown duration].
EDCS-13000979.summary: This complex funerary inscription records the deaths and ages of Apisia Donatula, Lucius Ortensius Felix, Lucius Ortensius Iunior, and Sahnamt, likely a family burial plot.

EDCS-13000980.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Peregrinus lived for 3 years. Aelius Victorinus is buried here.
EDCS-13000980.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Peregrinus, who lived for 3 years, and is buried by Aelius Victorinus.

EDCS-13000981.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Perellia Rogata the pious lived for 56 years. Quintus Pompeius Gallus made this for his mother at his own expense. She is buried here.
EDCS-13000981.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Perellia Rogata, aged 56, and was erected by her son Quintus Pompeius Gallus.

EDCS-13000982.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Rusticus the pious lived for [unknown duration]. His most obedient wife made this. His bones rest here in peace.
EDCS-13000982.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Rusticus, whose most obedient wife erected the monument, and offers a wish for his peace.

EDCS-13000983.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Seia Secunde, daughter of Marci, lived for 35 years. [Unknown]. Sacred to the departed spirits. [Unknown name] lived for 4 years.
EDCS-13000983.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Seia Secunde, daughter of Marci, at age 35, and another individual who lived for 4 years.

EDCS-13000984.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. [Unknown name] lived for 40 years. She is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus Secundius Primus the pious lived for 85 years. He is buried here. Secundius Quadratus made this for his dearest parents.
EDCS-13000984.summary: This funerary inscription records the deaths of two individuals and was erected by Secundius Quadratus for his parents.

EDCS-13000985.translation: Lived for 95 years. Quintus Sergius Faustus made this for his father-in-law.
EDCS-13000985.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of an individual who lived for 95 years and was commemorated by his son-in-law, Quintus Sergius Faustus.

EDCS-13000986.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Setonius Victorinus the pious lived for 13 years. Setonia Regilla [made this] for her brother.
EDCS-13000986.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Lucius Setonius Victorinus, aged 13, and was erected by his sister Setonia Regilla.

EDCS-13000987.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Titinia Secunda, dutiful, lived 60 years, is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Caius Titinius Gratus, dutiful, lived 65 years, is buried here. Marcus Titinius Secundianus made this for his own birds.
EDCS-13000987.summary: A funerary epitaph for Titinia Secunda and Caius Titinius Gratus, with Marcus Titinius Secundianus as the maker, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13000988.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Victoria, daughter of Rogatus, dutiful, lived 50 years, is buried here. Rogatus, her husband, made this for his dutiful wife.
EDCS-13000988.summary: A funerary epitaph for Victoria, erected by her husband Rogatus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13000991.translation: To Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Severus Alexander Pius Felix Augustus, for his health, Caius Licinius Ciron Cronha, priest of Caelestis, made and dedicated the altars at his own expense.
EDCS-13000991.summary: A dedication to Emperor Marcus Aurelius Severus Alexander by the priest Caius Licinius Ciron Cronha, likely from the early 3rd century CE.

EDCS-13000992.translation: To Mercury Augustus, for the health of Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Severus, Cocceius Cronha, priest of Caelestis, made this at his own expense.
EDCS-13000992.summary: A dedication to Mercury Augustus by the priest Cocceius Cronha for the health of Emperor Marcus Aurelius Severus, likely from the early 3rd century CE.

EDCS-13000993.translation: Dedicated here lies Apulaeius Datianus Ponponianus, dutiful, lived one year, four months, six days, he lies here.
EDCS-13000993.summary: A funerary epitaph for the infant Apulaeius Datianus Ponponianus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13000994.text_edition: \n Ex auctoritate Imperatoris Nervae Traiani Caesaris Augusti Germanici Dacici Lucius Minicius Natalis legatus Augusti pro praetore inter Madaurenses et Musulamios\n
EDCS-13000994.translation: By the authority of the Emperor Nerva Trajan Caesar Augustus, conqueror of Germany and Dacia, Lucius Minicius Natalis, imperial legate with praetorian power, [intervened] between the people of Madaura and Musulamia.
EDCS-13000994.summary: An inscription recording a legal or administrative decision made by Lucius Minicius Natalis under Emperor Trajan, concerning a dispute between two local communities.

EDCS-13000998.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Claudia Celia, dutiful, lived 40 years. Marcus Annius Victoricus, priest of Pluto, dutiful, lived 1 year. [He/She/They] lived 3 years, is buried here.
EDCS-13000998.summary: A funerary epitaph for Claudia Celia and Marcus Annius Victoricus, with Marcus Annius Victoricus also identified as a priest of Pluto, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13000999.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Titus Clodius Loquella, aedile, duovir, quaestor, perpetual flamen, priest of Liber Pater, lived 49 years, is buried here, adorned with the praise and honors of character and piety, lived honorably, was dear to all, lived a happy 50 years minus one, carried out his duties diligently and enjoyed the honors of his rank, an outstanding man, a dutiful flamen of his homeland, a moderate and generous benefactor of the temple, a cultivator of his own genius and a happy priest of Liber Pater; he added glory and renown to his family. Reader inspecting the beginnings of the verses of Loquella.
EDCS-13000999.summary: A lengthy funerary epitaph for Titus Clodius Loquella, detailing his various magistracies and priesthoods and praising his character, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13001000.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Caius Iulius Laetus, son of Lucius, of the Quirina tribe, priest of Liber Pater, dutiful, lived 91 years, is buried here.
EDCS-13001000.summary: A funerary epitaph for Caius Iulius Laetus, who served as a priest of Liber Pater, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13001001.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulia Miti ta TV, dutiful, lived 2 years. Caius Iulius Urbanus, of the Quirina tribe, aedile, priest of Pluto, dutiful, lived 71 years, are buried here.
EDCS-13001001.summary: A funerary epitaph for Iulia Miti ta TV and Caius Iulius Urbanus, who served as an aedile and priest of Pluto, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13001004.translation: Lucius Caelius Sabinus erected this at his own expense and dedicated it for Noniae Severa, offered by the order.
EDCS-13001004.summary: A monument erected by Lucius Caelius Sabinus at his own expense for Noniae Severa, likely commissioned by a local magistracy, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13001005.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Iulia Victoria, dutiful, lived. Sempronia Spesina, dutiful, lived 16 years. Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Lucius Sempronius Balsille, priest of Pluto, dutiful, lived X years.
EDCS-13001005.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Iulia Victoria and Sempronia Spesina, with Lucius Sempronius Balsille also mentioned as a priest.

EDCS-13001006.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Decimus Aelius Rogatus lived 85 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-13001006.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Decimus Aelius Rogatus, recording his age and burial.

EDCS-13001007.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Caius Aemilius Crescentio, dutiful, lived 21 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-13001007.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Caius Aemilius Crescentio, recording his age and burial.

EDCS-13001008.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. S BASAC V INIA Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Aemilius Quintasius lived 35 years.
EDCS-13001008.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Aemilius Quintasius, recording his age, with a partially illegible name preceding it.

EDCS-13001009.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Antonia Saturnina, dutiful, lived X years; she is buried here. Caius Antonius Crispus.
EDCS-13001009.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Antonia Saturnina, recording that she is buried, with Caius Antonius Crispus also mentioned.

EDCS-13001010.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Antonia Victoria, dutiful, sober, thrifty, lived 43 years; she is buried here. Caius Iulius Saturninus Sabinianus made [this] for his most beloved wife, exceptionally rare in all dutifulness, innocence, and gravity of character, fruitful and cherished, and for himself to perpetuate memory forever. Caius Iulius Saturninus Sabinianus, dutiful, who died from exceptional love for his grandsons, a man of singular virtue, buried in Sitifis, lived 79 years.
EDCS-13001010.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Caius Iulius Saturninus Sabinianus for his deceased wife Antonia Victoria, and also for himself, commemorating his own life and virtue.

EDCS-13001011.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Attilia Tertia, dutiful, lived 43 years; she is buried here. Lucius, dutiful, lived 10 years; he is buried here. Marcus Aemilius Sensus, dutiful, lived 80 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-13001011.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Attilia Tertia, Lucius, and Marcus Aemilius Sensus, recording their ages and burials.

EDCS-13001012.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Quintus Bellenius Secundus, dutiful, lived 55 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-13001012.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Quintus Bellenius Secundus, recording his age and burial.

EDCS-13001013.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Caecilia Spectata, dutiful, lived 25 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-13001013.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Caecilia Spectata, recording her age and burial.

EDCS-13001014.translation: Caelia Getulla, dutiful, lived. Gavius Martialis, dutiful, lived.
EDCS-13001014.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription mentioning Caelia Getulla and Gavius Martialis.

EDCS-13001015.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Caius Cerinius Vitalis, dutiful, lived 71 years; he is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Servilia Numisia, dutiful, lived 85 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-13001015.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Caius Cerinius Vitalis and Servilia Numisia, recording their ages at death.

EDCS-13001017.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Tiberius Claudius Fortunatus, dutiful, lived 30 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-13001017.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Tiberius Claudius Fortunatus, recording his age at death.

EDCS-13001018.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Tiberius Claudius Martialis lived 75 years. Iulia Sapida lived 55 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-13001018.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Tiberius Claudius Martialis and Iulia Sapida, recording their ages at death.

EDCS-13001019.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Tiberius Claudius Rufinus, dutiful, lived 49 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-13001019.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Tiberius Claudius Rufinus, recording his age at death.

EDCS-13001020.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Tiberius Claudius Successus, son of Cogitati Successus, of the Quirina tribe, a lover of good faith and truth, lived 105 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-13001020.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Tiberius Claudius Successus, recording his age at death and mentioning his father and his virtues.

EDCS-13001021.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Claudia Longina, dutiful, lived 75 years; she is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Fabricius Saturninus, dutiful, lived 70 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-13001021.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Claudia Longina and Lucius Fabricius Saturninus, recording their ages at death.

EDCS-13001022.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Clodia Lallina, dutiful, lived [years]. Sacred to the departed spirits. Caius Iulius Donatus Sabinianus, dutiful, lived [years]. Caius Iulius Fessianus, son of Lallina, dutiful, lived 13 years and 1 month; he is buried here.
EDCS-13001022.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Clodia Lallina, Caius Iulius Donatus Sabinianus, and Caius Iulius Fessianus, recording the age of the latter.

EDCS-13001023.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Clodia Stimandra, dutiful, lived [years]. Quintus Clodius Hermocius, dutiful, lived [years]; they are buried here.
EDCS-13001023.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Clodia Stimandra and Quintus Clodius Hermocius, recording their burial.

EDCS-13001024.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Didius Felix, dutiful, lived 61 years. Publius Hordionius Ianuarius, dutiful, lived [years]; he is buried here.
EDCS-13001024.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Didius Felix and Publius Hordionius Ianuarius, recording the age of the former.

EDCS-13001025.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcus Domitius Paulinus, dutiful, lived 31 years; he is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Domitius Sodalis, dutiful, lived 21 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-13001025.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcus Domitius Paulinus and Domitius Sodalis, recording their ages at death.

EDCS-13001026.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Dubila Martialis lived 60 years and is buried here. Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Grania Matrona, devoted, lived 95 years and is buried here. Grania Matrona, devoted.
EDCS-13001026.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Dubila Martialis and Grania Matrona, specifying their ages and devotion.

EDCS-13001027.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Lucius Fabius Alexander, of the Quirina tribe, devoted, lived 30 years and is buried here.
EDCS-13001027.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Lucius Fabius Alexander, specifying his age and tribal affiliation.

EDCS-13001028.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Fabia Ingenua, daughter of Caius, devoted, lived 50 years and is buried here.
EDCS-13001028.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Fabia Ingenua, daughter of Caius, specifying her age.

EDCS-13001029.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Lucius Fabricius Longinianus, devoted, lived 19 years and is buried here.
EDCS-13001029.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Lucius Fabricius Longinianus, specifying his age.

EDCS-13001030.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Fabricia Fausta, devoted, lived 35 years. Lucius Valerius Marchianus, son of Fabricia Fausta, lived 8 years and is buried here.
EDCS-13001030.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Fabricia Fausta and her son Lucius Valerius Marchianus, specifying their ages.

EDCS-13001031.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Faonia Honorata, devoted, lived 23 years and 5 months and is buried here.
EDCS-13001031.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Faonia Honorata, specifying her age in years and months.

EDCS-13001032.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Titus Flavius Ianuarius Laurianus, devoted, lived 107 years and is buried here.
EDCS-13001032.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Titus Flavius Ianuarius Laurianus, specifying his age.

EDCS-13001033.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Titus Flavius Lucinus, devoted, lived 65 years and is buried here.
EDCS-13001033.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Titus Flavius Lucinus, specifying his age.

EDCS-13001034.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Titus Flavius Monimus, devoted, lived 19 years. Titus Flavius Gemellus, devoted, lived 15 years and is buried here.
EDCS-13001034.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Titus Flavius Monimus and Titus Flavius Gemellus, specifying their ages.

EDCS-13001035.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Titus Flavius Novellus, devoted, lived 45 years and is buried here.
EDCS-13001035.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Titus Flavius Novellus, specifying his age.

EDCS-13001036.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Flavia Emerita, daughter of Flavius Achaeus, pious, lived 30 years, is buried here.
EDCS-13001036.summary: A tombstone for Flavia Emerita, daughter of Flavius Achaeus, who lived to be 30 years old.

EDCS-13001037.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Flavia Peregrina, daughter of Titus, pious, lived 70 years, is buried here.
EDCS-13001037.summary: A tombstone for Flavia Peregrina, daughter of Titus, who lived to be 70 years old.

EDCS-13001038.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Flavia Pudentilla, daughter of Titus, of the Quirina tribe, pious, lived 16 years, 6 months, and 22 days, is buried here. May your bones rest well.
EDCS-13001038.summary: A tombstone for Flavia Pudentilla, daughter of Titus, who died at the age of 16 years, 6 months, and 22 days.

EDCS-13001039.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Flavia Sabina lived 60 years.
EDCS-13001039.summary: A tombstone for Flavia Sabina, who lived to be 60 years old.

EDCS-13001040.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Flavia Tertulla, wife of Claudius Lucinus Festianus, pious, lived 53 years, is buried here. Tiberius Claudius Lucinus, son of Tiberius, of the Quirina tribe, pious, lived 56 years.
EDCS-13001040.summary: A tombstone for Flavia Tertulla, wife of Claudius Lucinus Festianus, and for Tiberius Claudius Lucinus, her husband, who lived to 53 and 56 years respectively.

EDCS-13001041.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Publius Mattius Fortunatus Iunior, of the Quirina tribe, of rarest example regarding the reward of his wife, pious, lived 65 years, is buried here. May your bones rest well.
EDCS-13001041.summary: A tombstone for Publius Mattius Fortunatus Iunior, noted for his exceptional behavior towards his wife, who lived to be 65 years old.
