EDCS-13001042.translation: To the Divine Spirits. For Hilara and Oxicarus. Libosus made this for his wife. Hilara, pious, lived 40 years. [Also buried here: Oxicarus who] lived 4 years. They are buried here.
EDCS-13001042.summary: A tombstone dedicated by Libosus for his wife Hilara, who lived 40 years, and their son Oxicarus, who lived 4 years.

EDCS-13001043.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Publius Felix, son of Rufinus, pious, lived 15 years, is buried here. To the Divine Spirits. Hordionia Matrona, pious, lived 95 years, is buried here.
EDCS-13001043.summary: A tombstone commemorating two individuals: Publius Felix, who lived to 15 years, and Hordionia Matrona, who lived to 95 years.

EDCS-13001044.translation: Lived 101 years. Caius Iulius Secundus lived 50 years.
EDCS-13001044.summary: This inscription records the lifespans of two individuals, one living to 101 and Caius Iulius Secundus to 50.

EDCS-13001045.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Caius Iulius C. Agilis, pious, lived 10 years, is buried here.
EDCS-13001045.summary: A tombstone for Caius Iulius C. Agilis, who lived to be 10 years old.

EDCS-13001046.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Gaius Julius Barigbal made this for himself and his wife.
EDCS-13001046.summary: This funerary epitaph records Gaius Julius Barigbal dedicating a monument to himself and his wife.

EDCS-13001047.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Gaius Julius Baric, dutiful, lived 65 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-13001047.summary: This funerary epitaph records the life and burial of Gaius Julius Baric.

EDCS-13001048.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulius Quirina Iucundus, dutiful, lived 70 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-13001048.summary: This funerary epitaph records the life and burial of Iulius Quirina Iucundus.

EDCS-13001049.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Gaius Julius Victor, dutiful, lived 75 years.
EDCS-13001049.summary: This funerary epitaph records the life of Gaius Julius Victor, who died at 75 years old.

EDCS-13001050.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulia Dativa, dutiful, lived 10 years. Iulius Iustus Madaurius, dutiful, lived 4 years. They are buried here, 13 people in total.
EDCS-13001050.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lives of Iulia Dativa and Iulius Iustus Madaurius, with a mention of 13 burials.

EDCS-13001051.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulia Monnina, dutiful, lived 80 years. She is buried here. Claudius, dutiful, lived 15 years. Nundinarius Claudius, dutiful, lived 25 years. Tiberius Claudius Honoratus, dutiful, lived 70 years. Ianus Claudius, dutiful, lived 20 years. Fortunius.
EDCS-13001051.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lives and burials of multiple individuals, including Iulia Monnina, Claudius, Nundinarius Claudius, Tiberius Claudius Honoratus, Ianus Claudius, and Fortunius.

EDCS-13001052.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulia Prima, daughter of Caius, dutiful, lived 61 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-13001052.summary: This funerary epitaph records the life and burial of Iulia Prima, daughter of Caius.

EDCS-13001053.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulia Prima, dutiful, lived 57 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-13001053.summary: This funerary epitaph records the life and burial of Iulia Prima.

EDCS-13001054.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Iunia Maior, dutiful, lived 37 years. She is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcus Domitius Rusticus, dutiful, lived 25 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-13001054.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lives and burials of Iunia Maior and Marcus Domitius Rusticus.

EDCS-13001055.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Publius Licinius Pudens, dutiful, lived 85 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-13001055.summary: This funerary epitaph records the life and burial of Publius Licinius Pudens.

EDCS-13001056.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucceia Hilara, wife of Lucceius Honoratus, lived 75 years. Lucceia Honorata, daughter, lived 30 years. Iulia Honorata lived 7 years. They are buried here.
EDCS-13001056.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucceia Hilara, her daughter Lucceia Honorata, and Iulia Honorata, recording their ages and burial.

EDCS-13001057.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Lutatius Quirina, pious, lived 76 years. Iulia Fausta Quirina, pious, lived 62 years. They are buried here.
EDCS-13001057.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Lutatius Quirina and Iulia Fausta Quirina, recording their ages and burial.

EDCS-13001058.summary: This is a brief funerary epitaph for Marcia Casta, recording her age.

EDCS-13001059.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcia Honorata, pious, lived 9 years. Sacred to the departed spirits. Antonia Namphadora, pious, lived 40 years. Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcia Elpina, pious, lived 4 years.
EDCS-13001059.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for three individuals: Marcia Honorata, Antonia Namphadora, and Marcia Elpina, recording their ages.

EDCS-13001060.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Caius Mattius Quirina Honoratus, pious, lived 60 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-13001060.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Caius Mattius Quirina Honoratus, recording his age and burial.

EDCS-13001061.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Mattia Felicula, daughter of Matti(us) Honoratus, pious, lived 5 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-13001061.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Mattia Felicula, daughter of Matti(us) Honoratus, recording her age and burial.

EDCS-13001062.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Publius Opstorius Africanus, pious, lived [...] years.
EDCS-13001062.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Publius Opstorius Africanus, recording his piety and an incomplete age.

EDCS-13001063.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Obstoria Successa, pious, lived 52 years. She is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Caius Lollius Laetus, pious, lived 95 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-13001063.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for two individuals, Obstoria Successa and Caius Lollius Laetus, recording their ages and burials.

EDCS-13001064.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Obstoria Secura, daughter of Caius, pious, lived 31 years. She is buried here. Her husband Setinus, pious, made (this).
EDCS-13001064.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Obstoria Secura, made by her husband Setinus, recording her age and burial.

EDCS-13001065.translation: Lucius Oclatius Sabinus lived 8 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-13001065.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Oclatius Sabinus, recording his age and burial.

EDCS-13001066.translation: A monument for Pompeius; his heirs of Pomponia Fortunata, aged 6000 [possibly a misprint or symbolic number] and others.
EDCS-13001066.summary: This inscription records a monument established by the heirs of Pomponia Fortunata for Pompeius, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13001067.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Rusticelia Tertulla lived 21 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-13001067.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Rusticelia Tertulla, recording her age at death and burial, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13001068.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Saenia Saturnina the dutiful lived 40 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-13001068.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Saenia Saturnina, noting her piety and age at death, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13001069.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Marcus Scribonius Celsinus, enrolled in the Quirina tribe, dutiful, lived 49 years, is buried here.
EDCS-13001069.summary: A funerary epitaph for Marcus Scribonius Celsinus, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13001070.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulius Securus Claudianus the dutiful lived 26 years; he is buried here, for his most dutiful brother.
EDCS-13001070.summary: This funerary epitaph records the life and death of Iulius Securus Claudianus, who was buried for his brother, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13001071.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcus Servilius Primus the dutiful lived 25 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-13001071.summary: This funerary epitaph for Marcus Servilius Primus records his age at death and burial, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13001072.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus Vettius, son of Quintus, of the Quirina tribe, Innocens the dutiful lived 85 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-13001072.summary: This funerary epitaph records the life of Quintus Vettius Innocens, including his tribal affiliation and age at death, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13001073.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. For Vitruvia Honorata the dutiful, who lived 30 years, and for Publius Fannius, son of Publius, of the Quirina tribe, Sapidus the dutiful, who lived 36 years; they are buried here.
EDCS-13001073.summary: This funerary epitaph commemorates two individuals, Vitruvia Honorata and Publius Fannius Sapidus, noting their ages and tribal affiliation, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13001074.translation: [---]nus the dutiful lived 37 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-13001074.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary epitaph that records the age and burial of an individual identified by a name ending in '-nus', likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13001075.translation: [---]a the dutiful lived 51 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-13001075.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary epitaph recording the age and burial of a female, identified by a name ending in '-a', likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13001076.translation: [---] lived [---]pia lived 95 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-13001076.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary epitaph noting the burial and age of a female, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13001077.translation: Munius Iulius Bargeus, grandson, an honorable man, lived in peace faithfully for 33 years less 13 days. He was buried on the 9th day before the Ides of September; buried here.
EDCS-13001077.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Munius Iulius Bargeus, recording his age and date of burial.

EDCS-13001079.translation: Flaminalis, son of Saturus, who held the office of flaminalis of the city, and also the principate of his city, gave a marble statue to deserving citizens as a gift to Fortune; he made it with his own money and also dedicated it.
EDCS-13001079.summary: This inscription records a dedication of a marble statue to Fortune by Flaminalis, son of Saturus, who held civic offices.

EDCS-13001080.translation: Aurelius Urbanus, a pious veteran, lived 50 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-13001080.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Aurelius Urbanus, a veteran, recording his age and burial.

EDCS-13001081.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Iulia Spei, his most rare and pious wife, lived 40 years. She is buried here. Marcus Iulius Felix, Roman citizen, twice aedile, pious, lived 75 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-13001081.summary: This is a double funerary inscription for Iulia Spei and Marcus Iulius Felix, recording their ages and burial.

EDCS-13001082.translation: Macedo, son of Faustus, priest of Saturn, pious, lived 71 years.
EDCS-13001082.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Macedo, priest of Saturn, recording his age.

EDCS-13001083.translation: Priest of Saturn, lived 40 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-13001083.summary: This is a funerary inscription for an unnamed priest of Saturn, recording his age and burial.

EDCS-13001084.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Lucius Verrius Catullinus lived 60 years. Fabricia Valeria lived 35 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-13001084.summary: This is a double funerary inscription for Lucius Verrius Catullinus and Fabricia Valeria, recording their ages and burial.

EDCS-13001085.translation: Marchellus, son of Arinis, lived 101 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-13001085.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Marchellus, son of Arinis, recording his age and burial.

EDCS-13001086.translation: Ianuaria, wife of Rufinus, lived 5 years.
EDCS-13001086.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Ianuaria, wife of Rufinus, recording her age.

EDCS-13001087.translation: Iulius Zabonis, son, pious, lived 55 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-13001087.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Iulius Zabonis, recording his age and burial.

EDCS-13001088.text_edition: \n no nex sacro praecepto domini nostri Antonini Pii Felicis Augusti et consensum sic utrarumque partium decernente Claudio Iuliano proconsule clarissimo viro\n
EDCS-13001088.translation: ...on account of a divine command not to profane, with the consent of both parties, pronounced by Claudius Julianus, most illustrious proconsul, under our lord Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus.
EDCS-13001088.summary: A fragment of an inscription recording a legal decision made by the proconsul Claudius Julianus during the reign of Antoninus Pius.

EDCS-13001089.translation: To the most holy Mother of the Gods, the Great Idaias, for the health and safety of our lord Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Severus Alexander Pius Felix Augustus, and Augusta Julia Mamaea, and their whole divine family, Publius Caecilius Felix, priest from the order of pontiffs, proclaimed a kriybolium and taurobolium.
EDCS-13001089.summary: A dedication to the Magna Mater by Publius Caecilius Felix, a priest, for the welfare of Emperor Severus Alexander and his mother Julia Mamaea, likely dating to the early 3rd century AD.

EDCS-13001090.translation: The worshippers of Ceres, who are written below: Gaius Julius Lucius, Julius Saturninus, Marcus Sa, Publius Julius Vindex Fronto Iu

EDCS-13001198.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. A son of Cornelius, dutiful, lived 97 years.
EDCS-13001198.summary: This epitaph records the lifespan of an unnamed son of Cornelius, indicating he lived 97 years.

EDCS-13001199.translation: Cornelius, son of Florus, dutiful, lived 31 years, is buried here.
EDCS-13001199.summary: This is an epitaph for Cornelius, son of Florus, recording his age at death and burial, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13001200.translation: Quinti, son of Cornelius Clemens, dutiful, lived 31 years.
EDCS-13001200.summary: This epitaph records the lifespan of Quinti, son of Cornelius Clemens, indicating he lived 31 years.

EDCS-13001201.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus Cornelius Quintasius, dutiful, lived 18 years, is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus Cornelius Nannaricus, dutiful, lived 57 years, is buried here.
EDCS-13001201.summary: This inscription contains two epitaphs for individuals named Quintus Cornelius, Quintasius and Nannaricus, detailing their ages at death and burial.

EDCS-13001202.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Cornelia Bellica, dutiful daughter of Cornelius Meridialis, lived 35 years, is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Ianuarius Laome, dutiful son of Dontis, lived 40 years, is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Agentius Faustinus lived 15 years. Sacred to the departed spirits. Cornelia Matronica lived 41 years. Felicianus, dutiful, lived 14 years. Sacred to the departed spirits. Cornelius Felix lived [an unspecified number of] years.
EDCS-13001202.summary: This funerary inscription records the deaths and burial places of multiple individuals, likely family members, identified by name, parentage, and age at death.

EDCS-13001203.translation: Cornelia Priscilla, dutiful daughter of Caius, lived 14 years, is buried here.
EDCS-13001203.summary: This funerary inscription records the death and burial of Cornelia Priscilla, identified by name, parentage, and age at death.

EDCS-13001204.translation: Curtia Pollitta, dutiful daughter of Lucius, wife of Marcus Iulius Gentilis, lived 55 years.
EDCS-13001204.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Curtia Pollitta, identified by name, parentage, marital status, and age at death.

EDCS-13001205.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Decianus, dutiful son of Rogatus, lived 70 years. Sacred to the departed spirits. Flavia Marcella [lived an unspecified number of years].
EDCS-13001205.summary: This funerary inscription records the deaths of Decianus and Flavia Marcella, identified by name, parentage (for Decianus), and age at death (for Decianus).

EDCS-13001206.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Decimia Matrona, dutiful wife of Felix, lived 31 years, is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Silia Matrona, dutiful daughter of Felix, lived 22 years, is buried here.
EDCS-13001206.summary: This funerary inscription records the deaths and burial places of Decimia Matrona and Silia Matrona, identified by name, relation to Felix, and age at death.

EDCS-13001207.translation: Lucius Didius Macus, dutiful, lived 55 years, is buried here.
EDCS-13001207.summary: This funerary inscription records the death and burial of Lucius Didius Macus, identified by name and age at death.

EDCS-13001208.translation: Lucius Domitius Bellicus, dutiful son of Pacatus, lived 87 years, is buried here.
EDCS-13001208.summary: This funerary inscription records the death and burial of Lucius Domitius Bellicus, identified by name, parentage, and age at death.

EDCS-13001209.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Gaius Domitius Sedatus, dutiful son of Domitius Sedatus, lived 21 years, is buried here.
EDCS-13001209.summary: This funerary inscription records the death and burial of Gaius Domitius Sedatus, identified by name, father's name, and age at death.

EDCS-13001210.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Domitia Matrona, dutiful daughter of Domitius Maximus, lived 15 years, is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Publius Gabinius Secundianus set this up for himself while alive, dutiful, lived 75 years, is buried here.
EDCS-13001210.summary: This funerary inscription records the deaths and burials of Domitia Matrona and Publius Gabinius Secundianus, identified by name, parentage (for Domitia), and age at death, with Secundianus also noted as the self-arranging dedicator.

EDCS-13001211.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Egnatia, dutiful daughter of Publius RESI ARATS, lived [an unspecified number of years]. Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcus Gellius Honoratus, dutiful, lived 85 years.
EDCS-13001211.summary: This funerary inscription records the deaths of Egnatia and Marcus Gellius Honoratus, identified by name, parentage (for Egnatia), and age at death (for Marcus).

EDCS-13001212.translation: Quintus Ennius Iustus of the Papirian tribe lived 19 years.
EDCS-13001212.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Quintus Ennius Iustus.

EDCS-13001213.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcus Fabius Iulius Varus, son of Marcus Fabius Laetus, dutiful, lived 18 years and 9 days. He is buried here.
EDCS-13001213.summary: This funerary inscription records the life and burial of Marcus Fabius Iulius Varus.

EDCS-13001214.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Decimus Fabius Verianus, son of Decimus Fabius, dutiful, lived 30 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-13001214.summary: This funerary inscription records the life and burial of Decimus Fabius Verianus.

EDCS-13001215.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Fabricus Zannulus, dutiful, lived 90 years, dutiful, he is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulia Rogata, daughter of Iustus, wife of Fabricus Zannei, dutiful, lived 65 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-13001215.summary: This is a double funerary inscription recording the lives and burials of Fabricus Zannulus and Iulia Rogata, his wife.

EDCS-13001216.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Gellia Villatici, daughter of Gellus Lupus, wife of Marcellinus of the Farsuleii family, dutiful, lived 55 years. She is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Farsuleius Marcellinus, son of Lucius Farsuleius Rufus, dutiful, lived [---] years.
EDCS-13001216.summary: This is a double funerary inscription recording the lives of Gellia Villatici and Lucius Farsuleius Marcellinus, presumably her husband, with the latter's lifespan incomplete.

EDCS-13001217.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Farsuleia Fortunata, daughter of Farsuleius Marcellinus, dutiful, lived 69 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-13001217.summary: This funerary inscription records the life and burial of Farsuleia Fortunata.

EDCS-13001218.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Farsuleia Nepotia, daughter of Farsuleius Marcellinus, dutiful, lived 23 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-13001218.summary: This funerary inscription records the life and burial of Farsuleia Nepotia.

EDCS-13001219.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Faustina Garici.

EDCS-13001220.translation: Faustinus Iar, son of Silvanus, dutiful, lived 30 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-13001220.summary: This funerary inscription records the life and burial of Faustinus Iar.

EDCS-13001221.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Festa Zabonis, daughter of Baricis, dutiful.
EDCS-13001221.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the name and parentage of Festa Zabonis, with her lifespan not specified.

EDCS-13001223.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Flavia Maia the dutiful lived 35 years; she lies here. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Flavius Crescentianus the dutiful lived 20 years; he lies here.
EDCS-13001223.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the deaths of Flavia Maia and Flavius Crescentianus, who lived 35 and 20 years respectively.

EDCS-13001224.translation: Fronto, son of Florus, the dutiful, lived 65 years.
EDCS-13001224.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the death of Fronto, son of Florus, who lived 65 years.

EDCS-13001225.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. To Romana, wife of Secundus, his most incomparable and most obedient, who lived 39 years. Furius Caelianus, having acquired these plots of rough ground, willingly set up this tomb.
EDCS-13001225.summary: This funerary monument was set up by Furius Caelianus for his wife Romana, who lived 39 years.

EDCS-13001226.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Marcus Furius Lorganus, son of Publius, the dutiful, lived 30 years. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Marcus Furius Mustiolus, the dutiful, lived 28 years.
EDCS-13001226.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the deaths of Marcus Furius Lorganus and Marcus Furius Mustiolus, who lived 30 and 28 years respectively.

EDCS-13001227.translation: Aulus Gabinius Rufinus, son of Aulus, of the tribe Quirina, the dutiful, lived 17 years; he lies here.
EDCS-13001227.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the death of Aulus Gabinius Rufinus, who lived 17 years.

EDCS-13001228.translation: Gabinia Angina, daughter of Marcius, wife of Lucius Iulius Secundus, lived 20 years; she lies here.
EDCS-13001228.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the death of Gabinia Angina, wife of Lucius Iulius Secundus, who lived 20 years.

EDCS-13001229.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Gabinia Casta the dutiful lived [---] years. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Calpurnius Sextianus the dutiful lived [---] years.
EDCS-13001229.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the deaths of Gabinia Casta and Calpurnius Sextianus, whose ages are illegible.

EDCS-13001230.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Lucius Gargilius Pompeianus the dutiful lived 22 years.
EDCS-13001230.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the death of Lucius Gargilius Pompeianus, who lived 22 years.

EDCS-13001231.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Caius Avianius Rogatus the dutiful lived 64 years. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Nina, daughter of Baricbalus, the dutiful, lived 60 years; she lies here.
EDCS-13001231.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the deaths of Caius Avianius Rogatus and Nina, daughter of Baricbalus, who lived 64 and 60 years respectively.

EDCS-13001232.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Gellia Rogata the dutiful lived 26 years; she lies here. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Caius Tuccius Secundus the dutiful lived 7 years; he lies here.
EDCS-13001232.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the deaths of Gellia Rogata and Caius Tuccius Secundus, who lived 26 and 7 years respectively.

EDCS-13001233.translation: Lucius Gellius Terminalis, dutiful, lived 55 years, is buried here.
EDCS-13001233.summary: This is a tombstone for Lucius Gellius Terminalis, who died at age 55.

EDCS-13001234.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Caius Genucius Ianuarius, dutiful, lived 25 years, is buried here.
EDCS-13001234.summary: This is a tombstone for Caius Genucius Ianuarius, who died at age 25.

EDCS-13001235.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Caius Herennius Dativus, son of Cai Herennius Priscus, dutiful, lived 36 years, is buried here.
EDCS-13001235.summary: This is a tombstone for Caius Herennius Dativus, son of Cai Herennius Priscus, who died at age 36.

EDCS-13001236.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcus Herennius Gumina, dutiful, lived 63 years. Sacred to the departed spirits. Herennius Bellicus, dutiful, lived 28 years.
EDCS-13001236.summary: This inscription records the burial of two individuals, Marcus Herennius Gumina (died at 63) and Herennius Bellicus (died at 28).

EDCS-13001237.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Publius Herennius Maximus, dutiful, lived 67 years, is buried here.

EDCS-13001238.translation: Herennia Liberata, dutiful, lived 50 years, is buried here.
EDCS-13001238.summary: This is a tombstone for Herennia Liberata, who died at age 50.

EDCS-13001239.summary: This tombstone is for Herennia Celsina, who died at age 22.

EDCS-13001240.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Hilara Successi, freedwoman, dutiful, lived [unknown age]. Sacred to the departed spirits. Successus, dutiful, lived 81 years, is buried here.
EDCS-13001240.summary: This inscription records the burial of Successus, who died at age 81, and also mentions Hilara Successi.

EDCS-13001241.translation: Honoratus, son of Adiutoris, dutiful, lived 17 years, is buried here.
EDCS-13001241.summary: This is a tombstone for Honoratus, son of Adiutoris, who died at age 17.

EDCS-13001242.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. For Hymentianus, a most bitter youth, snatched away in the flower of youth, a scribe by a cruel fate, who lived 20 years, 8 months, and 5 days, without blemish in his life. His father Postumius Victoricus placed this here. He is buried here.
EDCS-13001242.summary: This tombstone, erected by his father Postumius Victoricus, commemorates Hymentianus, a scribe who died at age 20.

EDCS-13001243.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Ianuaria, pious, lived 67 years.
EDCS-13001243.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the death of Ianuaria, who lived 67 years.

EDCS-13001244.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Ianuaria, wife of Tironis, pious, lived 19 years, is buried here.
EDCS-13001244.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the death of Ianuaria, wife of Tironis, who lived 19 years.

EDCS-13001245.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Ingenuus, son of Seti, pious, lived 75 years, is buried here. Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Clodia Veneria, pious, lived 80 years, is buried here.
EDCS-13001245.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the deaths of Ingenuus, son of Seti (75 years), and Clodia Veneria (80 years).

EDCS-13001246.translation: [---]iria Saturnina, pious, lived 45 years, is buried here.
EDCS-13001246.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the death ofiria Saturnina, who lived 45 years.

EDCS-13001247.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Iulius Crispinus, pious, lived 40 years, is buried here.
EDCS-13001247.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the death of Iulius Crispinus, who lived 40 years.

EDCS-13001248.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Iulius Gemellus lived 83 years. Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Geminia Licinia lived 79 years.
EDCS-13001248.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the deaths of Iulius Gemellus (83 years) and Geminia Licinia (79 years).

EDCS-13001249.summary: This is an incomplete tombstone inscription recording the life of Marcus Iulius Gentilis.

EDCS-13001250.translation: Iulia, daughter of Marcus Iulius Gentilis, GIEL, lived 20 years, is buried here.
EDCS-13001250.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the death of Iulia, daughter of Marcus Iulius Gentilis, who lived 20 years.

EDCS-13001251.translation: Iulius Paternus, son of Faustinus, pious, lived 65 years, is buried here.
EDCS-13001251.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the death of Iulius Paternus, son of Faustinus, who lived 65 years.

EDCS-13001252.translation: Matrona, wife of Faustinus, pious, lived 80 years.
EDCS-13001252.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the death of Matrona, wife of Faustinus, who lived 80 years.

EDCS-13001253.translation: To the departed spirits. Lucius Iulius Privatus, dutiful, lived 25 years. Orfa Munda, dutiful, erected this monument to herself while alive, lived.
EDCS-13001253.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Lucius Iulius Privatus and Orfa Munda, who erected her own monument.

EDCS-13001254.translation: To the departed spirits. Iulius Rufinus, dutiful, lived 75 years, erected and dedicated this while alive. Felicla Antonia, dutiful, lived 70 years, erected and dedicated this while alive. To the good, well done.
EDCS-13001254.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Iulius Rufinus and Felicla Antonia, who erected their own monuments while alive.

EDCS-13001255.translation: To the departed spirits. Caius Iulius Zobicus, freedman, lived 8 years.
EDCS-13001255.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Caius Iulius Zobicus, a freedman who died in childhood.

EDCS-13001256.translation: Iulia Pulyc lived 25 years, 10 months, 12 days. She is buried here. Her husband made this for his dearest wife.
EDCS-13001256.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Iulia Pulyc and was erected by her husband.

EDCS-13001257.translation: Iulia Festa, dutiful daughter of Proculus, lived 13 years.
EDCS-13001257.summary: This funerary inscription records the early death of Iulia Festa.

EDCS-13001258.translation: To the departed spirits. Iulia Festa, dutiful, lived 75 years. She is buried here. To the departed spirits. Vibius Victoricus, dutiful, lived 27 years. He is buried here. Vibius Rogatianus, dutiful son of Rogatianus, lived 17 years.
EDCS-13001258.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of three individuals: Iulia Festa, Vibius Victoricus, and Vibius Rogatianus.

EDCS-13001259.translation: To the departed spirits. Iulia Honorata, wife of Zabonas, dutiful, lived 30 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-13001259.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Iulia Honorata.

EDCS-13001260.translation: To the departed spirits. Iulia Matrona, dutiful daughter of Primus, lived 26 years. Veturius Crescens, her husband, erected this.
EDCS-13001260.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Iulia Matrona and was erected by her husband, Veturius Crescens.

EDCS-13001261.translation: To the departed spirits. Iulia Optata, dutiful daughter of Rosarius, lived 66 years. She is buried here. To the departed spirits. Marcus Aurelius Rosarius, dutiful son of Rosarius, lived 1 year, 1 month. He is buried here.
EDCS-13001261.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Iulia Optata and Marcus Aurelius Rosarius.

EDCS-13001262.translation: To the departed spirits. Iulia Postuma, dutiful, lived 50 years. She is buried here. To the departed spirits. Furfanius Novellus, dutiful son of Furfanius Mac, lived 61 years.
EDCS-13001262.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Iulia Postuma and Furfanius Novellus.

EDCS-13001263.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulia Pusinna, pious, lived 35 years. Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulius Lascivus, pious, lived 41 years. Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulia Frontilla, pious, lived 35 years.
EDCS-13001263.summary: This funerary inscription records the ages at death for three individuals: Iulia Pusinna, Iulius Lascivus, and Iulia Frontilla.

EDCS-13001264.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulia Saturnina, daughter of Caius, of the tribe Quirina, pious, and who lived above all modesty, lived 45 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-13001264.summary: This funerary inscription records the death and age of Iulia Saturnina, emphasizing her piety and modesty.

EDCS-13001265.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Caius Iunius Cornelius Eutyches, pious, lived 94 years; he is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Domitia Secunda, pious, lived 65 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-13001265.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial and ages at death for two individuals: Caius Iunius Cornelius Eutyches and Domitia Secunda.

EDCS-13001266.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Caius Iunius Cornelius Saturninus, pious, lived [age missing]. Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulia Matrona, pious, lived 50 years. Sacred to the departed spirits. V. Fortunatus, pious, lived 20 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-13001266.summary: This funerary inscription records the ages at death for Iulia Matrona and V. Fortunatus, with a missing age for Caius Iunius Cornelius Saturninus.

EDCS-13001267.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Iunius Fronto, son of Iuni Fidus, pious, lived 23 years; he is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Iunius Victoricus, son of Iuni Fidus, pious, lived 35 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-13001267.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial and ages at death for two individuals, Iunius Fronto and Iunius Victoricus, both sons of Iuni Fidus.

EDCS-13001268.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Caius Iunius Saturninus lived 19 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-13001268.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial and age at death of Caius Iunius Saturninus.

EDCS-13001269.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Iunia Festa, daughter of Saturninus, pious, lived 13 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-13001269.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial and age at death of Iunia Festa, daughter of Saturninus.

EDCS-13001270.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Iunia Prisca, daughter of Saturninus, pious, lived 15 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-13001270.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial and age at death of Iunia Prisca, daughter of Saturninus.

EDCS-13001271.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. My body has been laid to rest in this place for Iunia Victoria by her husband Iunius Hyacinthus, an example of rare devotion, who lived 26 years, 3 months, and 23 days, and who showed a chaste conjugal bond to her most pious husband until the last day of her life. You gods above, treat [her] well, live long, and come [to her rites].
EDCS-13001271.summary: This funerary inscription is a dedication by a husband, Iunius Hyacinthus, to his deceased wife, Iunia Victoria, detailing her age and virtuous life.

EDCS-13001272.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Iunia Za, pious wife, lived [age missing]
EDCS-13001272.summary: This fragmented funerary inscription records the name Iunia Za and her status as a pious wife, with a missing age at death.

EDCS-13001273.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Laberia Lucustina, recording her pious nature and age at death.

EDCS-13001274.translation: Laberia Mustela, daughter of Gaetulicus, pious, lived 15 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-13001274.summary: This funerary epitaph records the life and burial of Laberia Mustela, daughter of Gaetulicus.

EDCS-13001275.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Laelia Fortunata, wife of Baric inus, pious, lived 70 years. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Caecilius Antoninus, son of Baric, lived 15 years. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Caecilia Victorina, pious, lived 23 years. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Caecilia N. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Caecilius Faustinus, son of Antoninus, lived 22 years.
EDCS-13001275.summary: This inscription contains multiple funerary notices for members of the Caecilius and Laelia families, recording their piety and ages at death.

EDCS-13001276.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Lavinia, pious, lived 17 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-13001276.summary: This funerary epitaph records the life and burial of Lavinia, noted for her piety.

EDCS-13001277.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Licinia Bellica, pious, lived 70 years; she is buried here. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Festa, wife of Speratus, pious, lived 30 years; she is buried here. Zyonysius Speratus set this up for himself while alive.

EDCS-13001278.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Lucius, son of Gaetulicus, pious, lived 90 years; he is buried here. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Aedinia Rogata, wife of Lucius, pious, lived 60 years; she is buried here.

Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Lucius Vinicius Pudens, son of Iustus, of the Papiria tribe, dutiful, lived 25 years. He lies here.
EDCS-13001372.summary: This funerary inscription records the deaths of Quintus Vinicius Saturninus and Lucius Vinicius Pudens, noting their names, parentage, tribal affiliation, piety, lifespans, and burials.

EDCS-13001373.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Vibia Matrona, dutiful, lived 100 years. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Barichio, son of Victor and Nersanis, dutiful, lived 64 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-13001373.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the ages and burial of two individuals, Vibia Matrona and Barichio.

EDCS-13001374.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Ulpius Ecletus, dutiful, lived 75 years. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Marcus Ulpius Gudullus, dutiful, lived 100 years. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Tita Flavia, dutiful, lived...
EDCS-13001374.summary: This funerary inscription records the ages of three individuals: Ulpius Ecletus, Marcus Ulpius Gudullus, and Tita Flavia.

EDCS-13001375.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Umbrius Soricio, dutiful, lived 57 years. He is buried here. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Mellita, daughter of Calia and Thonis, dutiful, lived 45 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-13001375.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the ages and burial of two individuals, Umbrius Soricio and Mellita.

EDCS-13001376.translation: Urbicus, son of Quintus, dutiful, lived 40 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-13001376.summary: This funerary inscription records the age and burial of Urbicus, son of Quintus.

EDCS-13001377.translation: Baliato, son of Annus, dutiful, lived 70 years. He is buried here. F. placed [this] for his father.
EDCS-13001377.summary: This funerary inscription records the age of Baliato and indicates that his son F. erected the monument.

EDCS-13001378.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Felicitas, dutiful, lived 15 years.
EDCS-13001378.summary: This funerary inscription records the age of Felicitas.

EDCS-13001380.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Alumnus.
EDCS-13001380.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription for Alumnus.

EDCS-13001381.summary: This inscription records the age of an individual identified by the initials A. L. A.

EDCS-13001382.translation: M. A. M. S. F., dutiful, lived 111 years. Sacred to the spirits of the departed.
EDCS-13001382.summary: This funerary inscription records the age of an individual identified by the initials M. A. M. S. F.

EDCS-13001418.translation: Sacred to the divine spirits of the Augusti and the Emperor Caesar, son of the deified Trajan the Parthian, grandson of the deified Nerva, Trajan Hadrianus Augustus, pontifex maximus, with tribunician power for the Vth time, consul for the IIIrd time, father of the fatherland, by decree of the decurions, at public expense.
EDCS-13001418.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by decree of the local council and at public expense, honouring Emperor Hadrian and his predecessors.

EDCS-13001420.translation: To Quintus Domitius Hispanus, son of Publius, of the tribe Quirina, military tribune of the legion XVI Flavia Firma, quaestor of the city, by decree of the decurions, at public expense.
EDCS-13001420.summary: This inscription records a public monument dedicated to Quintus Domitius Hispanus, a military officer and urban quaestor.

EDCS-13001421.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Titus Flavius Ingenuus, honorably discharged from the VI Legion Victrix Pia Fidelis of the province Britannia Inferior, lived 61 years. Iulia Quinta, dutiful, lived 60 years.
EDCS-13001421.summary: This funerary inscription commemorates Titus Flavius Ingenuus and Iulia Quinta, both deceased veterans or associated with the Roman army in Britannia Inferior.

EDCS-13001422.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Lucius Cornelius Gudullus lived 65 years, is buried here. Mucia Fundana lived 70 years, is buried here.
EDCS-13001422.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Lucius Cornelius Gudullus and Mucia Fundana, providing their ages at death and burial location.

EDCS-13001423.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Titus Flavius Pudens lived 25 years.
EDCS-13001423.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Titus Flavius Pudens at the age of 25.

EDCS-13001424.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Flavius Quintilianus, son, lived 25 years, and Flavius Leontius, son, lived 19 years, and Flavia Aemilia, daughter, lived 12 years.
EDCS-13001424.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication for three siblings: Flavius Quintilianus, Flavius Leontius, and Flavia Aemilia, listing their ages at death.

EDCS-13001425.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Spes, wife of Ianuarius, dutiful, lived [--] years. Ianuari, daughter, dutiful, lived 25 years, is buried here.
EDCS-13001425.summary: This funerary inscription honors Spes, wife of Ianuarius, and their daughter Ianuari, providing ages and burial information.

EDCS-13001426.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Valerius Turut lived about 50 years. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Statoria Maxima lived 53 years.
EDCS-13001426.summary: This inscription records the deaths of two individuals, Valerius Turut and Statoria Maxima, noting their approximate ages.

EDCS-13001427.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Valeria Impetrata, dutiful, lived 101 years.
EDCS-13001427.summary: This funerary inscription commemorates Valeria Impetrata, who lived to the age of 101.

EDCS-13001429.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Martialis, son of Quintus, lived 75 years. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Bonosa lived 42 years.
EDCS-13001429.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication for two individuals, Martialis and Bonosa, stating their ages at death.

EDCS-13001430.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Selan lived [--] years. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Saturninus lived 85 years.
EDCS-13001430.summary: This inscription records the deaths of two individuals, Selan and Saturninus, with Saturninus's age at death provided.

EDCS-13001431.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Spes Sinianis lived for 65 years.
EDCS-13001431.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Spes Sinianis.

EDCS-13001432.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Caecilius Primus lived for 73 years. Sacred to the spirits of the underworld.
EDCS-13001432.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Caecilius Primus, with redundant invocation.

EDCS-13001435.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Augurina A lived for 65 years, she is placed here. Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Mescar lived for 55 years, he is placed here.
EDCS-13001435.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespans and burial of Augurina A and Mescar.

EDCS-13001436.translation: Amastra, daughter of Pacrusis, lived for 70 years, she is buried here.
EDCS-13001436.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan and burial of Amastra, daughter of Pacrusis.

EDCS-13001438.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Lucius Otacilius Silvanus, dutiful, lived [---] years, he is buried here.
EDCS-13001438.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the burial of Lucius Otacilius Silvanus, with illegible age.

EDCS-13001439.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Cominia Syra, dutiful, lived for 56 years and 5 months, she is buried here.
EDCS-13001439.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Cominia Syra.

EDCS-13001440.translation: Gaius Julius Getulus, veteran, discharged with the gifts of torcs and armlets, and in his town perpetual flamen, lived for 80 years, he is buried here.
EDCS-13001440.summary: A funerary epitaph for Gaius Julius Getulus, a veteran and local priest, recording his lifespan and burial.

EDCS-13001443.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Aurelia Fortunata, dutiful, lived for 44 years.
EDCS-13001443.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Aurelia Fortunata.

EDCS-13001444.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Bacchus Donatus, dutiful, lived for 90 years.
EDCS-13001444.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Bacchus Donatus.

EDCS-13001445.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. [---] Anistarnus lived for [---] years and 20 months.
EDCS-13001445.summary: A funerary epitaph with incomplete personal name and lifespan.

EDCS-13001446.translation: To the divine Manes. Claudia Ianuaria lived for 42 years and 6 months.
EDCS-13001446.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Claudia Ianuaria, recording her age at death.

EDCS-13001447.translation: Castrensis Honoratus, dutiful, lived for 5 years.
EDCS-13001447.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Castrensis Honoratus, recording his age at death.

EDCS-13001448.translation: Chinidial, son of Wisicir, of the Misiciri tribe, lived for 40 years.
EDCS-13001448.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Chinidial, son of Wisicir, recording his age at death and tribal affiliation.

EDCS-13001449.translation: Nabdhsen, son of Cotuzanis, of the Misictri tribe, lived for 20 years, is buried here.
EDCS-13001449.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Nabdhsen, son of Cotuzanis, recording his age at death, tribal affiliation, and burial.

EDCS-13001450.translation: Rogatus of Amastris lived for 28 years.
EDCS-13001450.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Rogatus of Amastris, recording his age at death.

EDCS-13001451.translation: Sactut, son of Ihimir, lived for 70 years.
EDCS-13001451.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Sactut, son of Ihimir, recording his age at death.

EDCS-13001452.translation: To the divine Manes. Sossia Saturnina, dutiful, lived for 60 years, 8 months, and 8 days, is buried here.
EDCS-13001452.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Sossia Saturnina, recording her age at death and burial.

EDCS-13001453.translation: To the divine Manes. Victor lived for 75 years.
EDCS-13001453.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Victor, recording his age at death.

EDCS-13001454.translation: To the divine Manes. Victoria, daughter of Victor, lived for 75 years.
EDCS-13001454.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Victoria, daughter of Victor, recording her age at death.

EDCS-13001455.translation: To the divine Manes. Victorinus lived for 33 years.
EDCS-13001455.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Victorinus, recording his age at death.

EDCS-13001456.summary: A tombstone inscription recording the age of the deceased.

EDCS-13001460.translation: To Lucius Naevius Flavius Iulianus Tertullus Aquilinus, most distinguished boy, Gaius Maecius Titianus Iunior, a Roman knight, for an incomparable patron; a place was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-13001460.summary: This inscription records the granting of a place by decree of the local council (decurions) to a distinguished young boy, Lucius Naevius Flavius Iulianus Tertullus Aquilinus, in honor of his patron, Gaius Maecius Titianus Iunior.

EDCS-13001461.translation: Buraidus, a soldier from the ranks of the Hipponenses Regii, lived in peace for 40 years, served for 18, and rested on the third day before the Nones of July in the ninth indiction.
EDCS-13001461.summary: This tombstone commemorates Buraidus, a soldier from the Hipponenses Regii, detailing his lifespan, military service, and date of death.

EDCS-13001462.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Marcus Ciarcius Pudens, a soldier of the 14th Urban Cohort, in the century of Silanus, stationed above the bank at Hippo Regius, erected this altar by his will, with the care of his freedman Mercurius; he is buried here.
EDCS-13001462.summary: This tombstone records Marcus Ciarcius Pudens, a soldier of the 14th Urban Cohort, who erected an altar at Hippo Regius and is buried there.

EDCS-13001467.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Publius Aemilius Felix lived for 53 years.
EDCS-13001467.summary: A tombstone inscription recording the name and age of the deceased, Publius Aemilius Felix.

EDCS-13001468.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Marcus Antonius Eutycha lived for 90 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-13001468.summary: This tombstone records the death of Marcus Antonius Eutycha, who lived to be 90 years old.

EDCS-13001469.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Aufidia Colonica lived for 35 years and 4 months; she is buried here.
EDCS-13001469.summary: A tombstone inscription for Aufidia Colonica, stating her age at death and burial location.

EDCS-13001470.translation: Gaius Iulius Aurelius lived for 3 years and 10 months.
EDCS-13001470.summary: This inscription records the short lifespan of a child named Gaius Iulius Aurelius.

EDCS-13001471.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Lucius Aemilius Paternus lived for 55 years, 2 months, and 10 days; he is buried here.
EDCS-13001471.summary: This tombstone records the age and burial details of Lucius Aemilius Paternus.

EDCS-13001472.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Ampliatus lived for 11 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-13001472.summary: A tombstone inscription for Ampliatus, recording his young age at death and burial.

EDCS-13001473.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Anneia Saturnina lived for 60 years.
EDCS-13001473.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Anneia Saturnina, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13001474.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Quintus Caecilius Victor lived for 20 years, 10 months, and 6 days. He is buried here.
EDCS-13001474.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan and burial place of Quintus Caecilius Victor, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13001475.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Caelius Donatus lived for 65 years, 11 months, and 23 days. He is buried here.
EDCS-13001475.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan and burial place of Caelius Donatus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13001476.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Clodia Pollitta the pious lived for 21 years. She is buried here. Wife of Quintus Silicius Martialis.
EDCS-13001476.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan and familial relationship of Clodia Pollitta, wife of Quintus Silicius Martialis, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13001477.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Cornelia Ispenica lived for 75 years, 5 months, and 7 days. She is buried here.
EDCS-13001477.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan and burial place of Cornelia Ispenica, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13001478.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Cresimus, whose first name is partially lost, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13001479.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Gressia Pudentilla lived for 50 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-13001479.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan and burial place of Gressia Pudentilla, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13001480.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Domitia Tyche, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13001481.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Fabius Donatus, also known as Crescens, lived for 48 years, 6 months, and 10 days. He is buried here.
EDCS-13001481.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan and burial place of Fabius Donatus (Crescens), likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13001482.translation: 5 months, 2 days. Hippocrates lived 11 months, 7 days.
EDCS-13001482.summary: This inscription is fragmented and seems to record partial lifespans for Hippocrates, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13001483.translation: To the departed gods. Hygia lived 6 years, 3 months, 12 days.
EDCS-13001483.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Hygia, likely a child, dedicated to the gods of the underworld.

EDCS-13001484.translation: To the departed gods. Tiberius Iulius Syntrophus lived 85 years. Dioscorus for [him], well-deserving.
EDCS-13001484.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan of Tiberius Iulius Syntrophus, set up by Dioscorus, likely a relative or friend.

EDCS-13001485.translation: To the departed gods. For Iulia Corinthia.
EDCS-13001485.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated to Iulia Corinthia.

EDCS-13001486.translation: To the departed gods. Iulia Trepte, also called Salamina, lived 11 years, 4 months, 20 days; she is buried here.
EDCS-13001486.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan of Iulia Trepte (also known as Salamina) and marks her burial place.

EDCS-13001487.translation: To the departed gods. Magnius Mustius lived 31 years, 7 months.
EDCS-13001487.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan of Magnius Mustius.

EDCS-13001488.translation: To the departed gods. Marcus Minthonius Alphius, dutiful, lived 65 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-13001488.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan of Marcus Minthonius Alphius and marks his burial place.

EDCS-13001489.translation: To the departed gods. Munatia Voluptas lived long enough; she is buried here.
EDCS-13001489.summary: This funerary epitaph records that Munatia Voluptas lived a full life and is buried here.

EDCS-13001490.translation: To the departed gods. Illia Rogatilla lived 30 years, 6 months, 8 days; she is buried here.
EDCS-13001490.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan of Illia Rogatilla and marks her burial place.

EDCS-13001491.translation: Septimia Optata lived 45 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-13001491.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan of Septimia Optata and marks her burial place.

EDCS-13001492.translation: To the departed gods. Sittia Veneria, also called Iuniane, lived [a certain number of] years.
EDCS-13001492.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the name Sittia Veneria (also known as Iuniane) and the beginning of her lifespan, with the duration missing.

EDCS-13001494.translation: Aprilia the faithful lived 75 years, departed in peace on the 3rd day before the Kalends of September, in her 24th year in Carthage.
EDCS-13001494.summary: This inscription records the lifespan and peaceful death of Aprilia, an individual who lived 75 years, with a specific mention of her time in Carthage.

EDCS-13001495.translation: Marcellus the faithful lived 28 years, rested in peace on the fifth day before the Kalends of April, in the indiction.
EDCS-13001495.summary: This epitaph commemorates Marcellus the faithful, who lived 28 years and died peacefully on a date specified by the Kalends of April and an indiction cycle.

EDCS-13001496.translation: Reparata the faithful lived for one year, 6 months, and 14 days, rested in peace on the fifth day before the Ides of February, in the fourteenth indiction.
EDCS-13001496.summary: This funerary inscription details the short life of Reparata the faithful, who lived for just over a year and died peacefully on the fifth day before the Ides of February in the fourteenth indiction.

EDCS-13001498.summary: This fragmented inscription names Bonifatius and seems to refer to a construction or effort, but its full meaning is lost.

EDCS-13001499.translation: Felix the builder, a servant, lived 20 years. His wife H. made this.
EDCS-13001499.summary: This inscription records the life of Felix, a builder and servant who lived 20 years, and was commemorated by his wife H.

EDCS-13001500.translation: Enaris the steward lived 65 years. Cerialis, his wife, saw to its construction.
EDCS-13001500.summary: This epitaph records the life of Enaris, a steward who lived 65 years, and was honored by his wife Cerialis who commissioned the monument.

EDCS-13001501.translation: To the divine spirits. Agathoclia, slave of Marcus Salustius, lived 27 years. She is buried here. Agathocles made this for his well-deserving wife.
EDCS-13001501.summary: This funerary inscription honors Agathoclia, a slave of Marcus Salustius who lived 27 years, and was commemorated by her husband Agathocles.

EDCS-13001502.translation: Sacred to the divine spirits. Gemella, slave of Marcus Sallustius, lived 1 year and 6 months. She is buried here. Eventhus and M. L. L. E. made this for their deserving daughter.
EDCS-13001502.summary: This epitaph honors Gemella, a slave of Marcus Sallustius, who lived for a year and a half, and was commemorated by her parents, Eventhus and M. L. L. E.

EDCS-13001503.translation: Passiena Quieta lived 75 years. Her husband D. made this for Felica, deserving of him.
EDCS-13001503.summary: This inscription records the life of Passiena Quieta, who lived 75 years, and was commemorated by her husband D. for Felica.

EDCS-13001504.translation: Felicula lived 35 years. Etruscus, her fellow servant, [honored] her, who was deserving of him.
EDCS-13001504.summary: This funerary inscription honors Felicula, who lived 35 years, and was commemorated by Etruscus, her fellow servant.

EDCS-13001505.translation: Inia Prima lived for 70 years. Her husband, Saenius, made this for her, their fellow slave, buried here.
EDCS-13001505.summary: This is a tombstone for Inia Prima, erected by her husband Saenius, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-13001506.translation: Rogatae, who lived 8 years and 6 months, is buried here as a well-deserving freedwoman of his family.
EDCS-13001506.summary: This is a tombstone for a young girl named Rogatae, erected by her family, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-13001507.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Publius Aelius Chresinus, freedman of Augustus, lived for 71 years. His devoted wife made this. Buried here.
EDCS-13001507.summary: This is a tombstone for Publius Aelius Chresinus, a freedman of the emperor, erected by his wife, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-13001508.translation: To Lucius Postumius Felix Celerinus, holder of military offices, perpetual priest of Augustus, twice chief magistrate, for his magnificence in the gladiatorial show, which he presented to his fellow citizens for three days, surpassing all preceding memories, and for his innocence, brilliance, and incomparable love for his fatherland, each of the curiae erected a statue of their own accord, so that they might match his outstanding willingness with titles of such great honor; the site was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-13001508.summary: This is a public dedication honouring Lucius Postumius Felix Celerinus for his lavish games and civic virtue, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-13001509.translation: To Lucius Postumius Felix Celerinus, holder of military offices, perpetual priest of Augustus, twice chief magistrate, for his magnificence in the gladiatorial show, which he presented to his fellow citizens for three days, surpassing all preceding memories, and for his innocence, brilliance, and incomparable love for his fatherland, each of the curiae erected a statue of their own accord, so that they might match his outstanding willingness with titles of such great honor; the site was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-13001509.summary: This is a public dedication honouring Lucius Postumius Felix Celerinus for his lavish games and civic virtue, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-13001510.translation: Claudia Galla lived for 10 years. Buried here.
EDCS-13001510.summary: This is a tombstone for a young girl named Claudia Galla, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-13001512.translation: Sacred to Baldir Augustus. Macedo, a public official, willingly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-13001512.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to the emperor (or a deified emperor) Baldir Augustus by an official named Macedo, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-13001513.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus Tullius Florus, son of Quintus, of the Arnensis tribe, perpetual priest of Augustus, made this monument in his lifetime for his devoted son Lucius Tullius, who lived for 38 years, and for his devoted daughter Tullia Secunda, who lived for 25 years, and for himself and his descendants.
EDCS-13001513.summary: This is a family tombstone made by Quintus Tullius Florus for himself, his son, and his daughter, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-13001514.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus Tullius Florus, son of Quintus, of the Arnensis tribe, perpetual priest, made this monument in his lifetime for his devoted son Lucius Tullius Florus, who lived for 39 years, and for Tullia Secunda, devoted, who lived for 25 years, for himself and his descendants.
EDCS-13001514.summary: This is a family tombstone made by Quintus Tullius Florus for himself, his son, and his daughter, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-13001515.translation: Cornelius Narsalus lived for 65 years. He is here.
EDCS-13001515.summary: This is a tombstone for Cornelius Narsalus, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-13001516.translation: Gaius Flavius Pax, pious, lived 65 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-13001516.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the death of Gaius Flavius Pax.

EDCS-13001517.translation: Forensis, son of Rogatus, made this monument for himself and his descendants.
EDCS-13001517.summary: This is a funerary monument inscription set up by Forensis for himself and his family.

EDCS-13001518.translation: Otmelc, daughter of Nannemis, pious, lived 65 years. She is buried here. Romanus, her son, placed this with his own money.
EDCS-13001518.summary: This tombstone inscription records the death of Otmelc and notes that her son Romanus paid for the monument.

EDCS-13001519.translation: ---us, son of Quintus Servilianus, lived 70 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-13001519.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the death of Servilianus.

EDCS-13001520.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Tannonia Saturnina, pious girl, lived 13 years, 10 months, and 15 days. Her parents [raised this] with devotion for their beloved daughter.
EDCS-13001520.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a young girl named Tannonia Saturnina, set up by her parents.

EDCS-13001521.translation: [---] to Aesculapius. He set this up and dedicated it.
EDCS-13001521.summary: This is a dedication inscription to the god Aesculapius, likely from a private individual.

EDCS-13001523.translation: Fortuna Victrix, along with images of victories, from an unfrequented and uncultivated place to this site, at private expense, through the distinguished provision of Aurelius Aristobulus, a most distinguished and honored man, in his fourth proconsulship, and of Macrinus Sossianus, a most distinguished legate, in his fourth year, Julius Rusticianus, a citizen and curator of the honorable Kalamensium, moved and placed [it].
EDCS-13001523.summary: This inscription records the relocation and re-dedication of a shrine to Fortuna Victrix by Julius Rusticianus, under the supervision of the proconsul Aurelius Aristobulus and legate Macrinus Sossianus.

EDCS-13001524.translation: Sacred to Hercules Augustus. Gaius Julius, son of Caius, of the Quirina tribe, made a vow.
EDCS-13001524.summary: This is a dedication to Hercules Augustus by Gaius Julius, possibly related to a vow.

EDCS-13001525.translation: Sacred to Hercules Augustus. Lucius Vibius Saturninus, a magistrate of the IIII viri, having promised more than the honorary sum with 3,000 sesterces, placed [this] with his own money from 6,000 sesterces and dedicated it himself.
EDCS-13001525.summary: This is a dedication to Hercules Augustus by Lucius Vibius Saturninus, a magistrate who contributed funds for the monument.

EDCS-13001528.translation: To the Great God, Torquatius fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-13001528.summary: This inscription records Torquatius fulfilling a vow made to the Great God.

EDCS-13001529.translation: To Neptune Augustus. Lucius Flavius Anicius Privatus, priest of Neptune, aedile, duovir, and quinquennial duovir, erected and dedicated the small shrine with all its ornaments at his own expense.
EDCS-13001529.summary: A quinquennial duovir named Lucius Flavius Anicius Privatus erected and dedicated a shrine to Neptune Augustus at his own expense.

EDCS-13001530.translation: To Neptune Augustus. Quintus Nicanius Honoratus, son of Quintus Nicanius Maximus of the Papiria tribe, aedile and duovir, erected and dedicated a statue for the honor of his duovirate, which he had promised for 5,000 sesterces, exceeding the legal sum by 7,340 sesterces.
EDCS-13001530.summary: Quintus Nicanius Honoratus, an aedile and duovir, dedicated a statue to Neptune Augustus, exceeding the promised amount for its erection.

EDCS-13001531.translation: To Apollo Augustus. Whereas Quintus Nicius Annianus, son of Quintus Nicius Pudentis, of the Papiria tribe, decurion and priest of Neptune, had ordered by his written instructions that a statue of Apollo be erected in the new forum for 5,000 sesterces, his heirs Nicani Restitutus Honoratus Maximus, sons of his sister, and his brother Caius Nicius Agrippinus erected it for 5,640 sesterces and dedicated it.
EDCS-13001531.summary: The heirs and brother of Quintus Nicius Annianus erected and dedicated a statue to Apollo Augustus, fulfilling his posthumous instructions at a cost exceeding the original amount.

EDCS-13001532.translation: Quinta Caecilia fulfilled her vow to Saturn.
EDCS-13001532.summary: Quinta Caecilia fulfilled a vow to Saturn.

EDCS-13001533.translation: Sacred to Saturn Augustus. Numidius Marius fulfilled his vow willingly.
EDCS-13001533.summary: Numidius Marius willingly fulfilled a vow to Saturn Augustus.

EDCS-13001534.translation: Sacred to Saturn Augustus. Publius Maximus fulfilled his vow for his son Rufus.
EDCS-13001534.summary: Publius Maximus fulfilled a vow to Saturn Augustus on behalf of his son Rufus.

EDCS-13001535.translation: Sacred to Saturn Augustus. Saturus lived 6 years. Silbana lived 1 year.
EDCS-13001535.summary: This inscription records the ages of two children, Saturus and Silbana, with the dedication 'Sacred to Saturn Augustus'.

EDCS-13001536.translation: Sacred to Saturn Augustus. Caius Silius Nundinarius fulfilled his vow willingly.
EDCS-13001536.summary: Caius Silius Nundinarius willingly fulfilled a vow to Saturn Augustus.

EDCS-13001537.translation: Sacred to Tellus Gilva Augusta. Caius Arrius Sabinius Datus, son of Nepotis, of the Papiria tribe, aedile and priest of Tellus.
EDCS-13001537.summary: Caius Arrius Sabinius Datus, an aedile and priest of Tellus, dedicated this sacred offering to Tellus Gilva Augusta.

EDCS-13001538.translation: Sacred to Victoria Augusta. In the year of the prefecture of Asmunis son of Muthumbbalis and Urbani son of Auchusor, during the principate of Pudentis son of Auchusor, with the care of Clemens Saphiris.
EDCS-13001538.summary: This inscription, dedicated to Victoria Augusta, records the date based on the prefecture of two individuals and the principate of another, with the supervision of Clemens Saphiris.

EDCS-13001539.translation: Aemilius Maximus gladly fulfilled his vow as was deserved.
EDCS-13001539.summary: A private dedication by Aemilius Maximus fulfilling a vow, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-13001540.translation: Aufidia Fundana gladly fulfilled her vow with a willing spirit.
EDCS-13001540.summary: A private dedication by Aufidia Fundana fulfilling a vow, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-13001541.translation: T. Caecilius Lontanustus gladly fulfilled his vow with a willing spirit.
EDCS-13001541.summary: A private dedication by T. Caecilius Lontanustus fulfilling a vow, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-13001542.translation: Caelius Urbanus brought (this) to the god.
EDCS-13001542.summary: A private dedication by Caelius Urbanus to a deity, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-13001543.translation: Felix, son of Baricbalis, gladly fulfilled his vow with a willing spirit.
EDCS-13001543.summary: A private dedication by Felix, son of Baricbalis, fulfilling a vow, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-13001544.translation: Baius Fortunatus gladly fulfilled his vow with a willing spirit.
EDCS-13001544.summary: A private dedication by Baius Fortunatus fulfilling a vow, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-13001545.summary: This inscription appears to be a name inscription, possibly on a tomb or dedication, dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-13001547.translation: Pontius Birzil gladly fulfilled his vow with a willing spirit.
EDCS-13001547.summary: A private dedication by Pontius Birzil fulfilling a vow, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-13001548.translation: Gaius Vibius Fundanus and Vibia Spica gladly fulfilled their vow with a willing spirit.
EDCS-13001548.summary: A joint private dedication by Gaius Vibius Fundanus and Vibia Spica fulfilling a vow, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-13001550.summary: This inscription appears to be a name inscription, possibly on a tomb or dedication, dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-13001558.translation: To Vibia Aurelia Sabina, sister of our Emperor Severus Augustus, daughter of the deified Pius, from Gaius Annius Saturninus, son of Gaius, of the Papiria tribe, patroness.
EDCS-13001558.summary: This inscription dedicates a monument to Vibia Aurelia Sabina, sister of Emperor Severus and daughter of Emperor Pius, likely during the Severan period.

EDCS-13001559.translation: To Vibia Aurelia Sabina, daughter of the deified Marcus, sister of the deified Severus, patroness of the municipality, councilor.
EDCS-13001559.summary: This inscription honors Vibia Aurelia Sabina, daughter of Marcus Aurelius and sister of Septimius Severus, likely in her role as a patroness of the municipality.

EDCS-13001563.translation: To Marcus Aurelius Carinus, most noble Caesar Augustus, prince of youth, consul, son of Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Carinus Invictus Pius Felix Augustus, father of the fatherland, with tribunician power II, chief pontiff, consul II, proconsul, brother of Marcus Aurelius Numerianus, most noble Caesar Augustus, prince of youth; the state of the colony of Kalamensium, administered by Macrinius Sossianus, most illustrious man, curator of the state.
EDCS-13001563.summary: This inscription honors Emperor Carinus, detailing his titles and lineage, and was set up by the colony of Kalamensium under the administration of Macrinius Sossianus.

EDCS-13001569.translation: To our lord Flavius Valentinianus Pius Felix Augustus Victor, during the proconsulship of Publius Ampelius, most illustrious man, the perpetual flamen, augur, and curator of the state, Quintus Basilius Flaccianus, with the most devoted order, placed and dedicated.
EDCS-13001569.summary: This inscription dedicates a monument to Emperor Valentinian I, set up by Quintus Basilius Flaccianus in his various official capacities during the proconsulship of Publius Ampelius.

EDCS-13001570.translation: The splendid order of Kalamensium, with Basilius Cirrenianus Restitutus, priest of the province of Africa, curator of the state, dedicated to our lord Flavius Claudius Julianus, perpetual Victor, always Augustus.
EDCS-13001570.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a monument by the city council of Kalamensium to Emperor Julian, during the curatorship of Basilius Cirrenianus.

EDCS-13001572.translation: The most splendid order of the colony of Kalamensium located and dedicated to our lord Flavius Theodosius, perpetual and Victor, always Augustus, [dedicates this monument] IO.
EDCS-13001572.summary: This inscription records the location and dedication of a monument by the city council of Kalamensium to Emperor Theodosius I.

EDCS-13001573.translation: In the most blessed times of our lords Honorius and Theodosius, always and everywhere victorious, under the administration of Pompeius Proculus, most illustrious and most eminent man, proconsul, and of Thersius Crispinus Megethius, most illustrious man, legate, Valentinus, a most honorable man, curator of the state, reformed the place, which was previously obstructed by ruins and defiled by squalor and filth, to a necessary use and for the hospitality of travelers, with his own funds, into a better form and roof. Happily.
EDCS-13001573.summary: This inscription details how Valentinus, curator of the state, used his own funds to renovate a ruined and filthy area for public use and to accommodate travelers during the reigns of Honorius and Theodosius.

EDCS-13001578.translation: During the proconsulship of Aurelius Symmachus, Basilius Cirrenianus, perpetual flamen and curator of the state, placed [this monument] with the most splendid order.
EDCS-13001578.summary: This inscription records a monument placed by Basilius Cirrenianus, in his capacities as perpetual flamen and curator, during the proconsulship of Aurelius Symmachus.

EDCS-13001579.translation: To Lucius Crepereius Madalianus, a most illustrious man, proconsul of the province of Africa, judging cases by vice sacra, count of the first order, vicar of Italy, prefect of the grain supply of the city, with consular authority and the right of the sword, corrector of Pontus and Bithynia, count of the second order of Flaminia and Picenum, [honored] for his great justice and exceptional moderation.
EDCS-13001579.summary: This inscription honors Lucius Crepereius Madalianus with a long list of his distinguished provincial and imperial offices, recognizing his justice and moderation.

EDCS-13001581.translation: To Marcus Cornelius Fronton, son of Titus, of the Quirina tribe, third man for capital cases, quaestor of the province of Sicily, plebeian aedile, praetor, patron of the citizens of Calama.
EDCS-13001581.summary: This inscription lists the career and honors of Marcus Cornelius Fronton, who served in various judicial and administrative roles and was recognized as a patron by the citizens of Calama.

EDCS-13001582.translation: To Titus Flavius Macro, son of Titus, of the Quirina tribe, twice a priest of the city, perpetual priest of the Ammaedarenses, prefect of the Musulamian tribe, curator for the procurement of grain for the city's food supply, appointed by the deified Nerva Trajan, procurator of the Emperor for the estates of the forests of Hippona and Theveste, procurator of the Emperor for the province of Sicily, by the townspeople of the municipality.
EDCS-13001582.summary: This is a dedication by the townspeople of a municipality to Titus Flavius Macro, listing his various prestigious civic and imperial administrative roles, likely from the late 1st or early 2nd century CE.

EDCS-13001583.translation: Together, sixteen towers grew in a line, the whole structure was seen to be wonderfully constructed quickly; afterwards it is enclosed by the baths with a belt; no evil person will be able to raise a hand. The institution of the patrician Solomon could not be overcome by anyone; the defense of the martyrs protects the structure itself; Clement and Vincent, martyrs, guard the very entrance.
EDCS-13001583.summary: This inscription appears to be a description, possibly allegorical or religious, of a defensive structure or building, mentioning its construction and protection by martyrs, likely dating from the late Roman or early Christian period.

EDCS-13001585.translation: To Quintus Servilius Pudentus, son of Quintus, of the Horatia tribe, tribune of the soldiers of the IV Scythica legion, quaestor of the province of Sicily, tribune of the plebs, praetor, prefect for the distribution of grain, legal advisor for Aemilia and Flaminia, proconsul of Crete and Cyrene, patron of the municipality of Kalamensium, by the municipality.
EDCS-13001585.summary: This is a dedication by the municipality of Kalamensium to Quintus Servilius Pudentus, honoring his various high-ranking military, judicial, and administrative offices, indicating his status as a patron, likely from the late Roman Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-13001587.translation: To Lucius Suanius Victor Vitellianus, who has held all offices, an illustrious man and a consular man, curator of the state and patron of the colony, for his outstanding justice and integrity towards the state and the citizens alike, the most distinguished council of Kalamensium decreed and erected this at public expense.
EDCS-13001587.summary: This is a dedication by the council of Kalamensium to Lucius Suanius Victor Vitellianus, honoring him for his services as curator and patron, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-13001589.translation: As proconsul administering, perpetual priest, from among the curators.
EDCS-13001589.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription mentioning official titles such as proconsul, perpetual priest, and curator, likely part of a longer list of honors or a dedication, the date is uncertain due to its fragmentary nature.

EDCS-13001591.translation: Aeniocle, Ieteua, of his own, of the use, under the consuls Mucianus and Talmus, eight days before the Kalends of July.
EDCS-13001591.summary: This inscription appears to record a date with named consuls (Mucianus and Talmus), possibly related to a legal or administrative event, dating to the Roman Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-13001592.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Tertius Caius Servilius Macro, a scribe, pious, lived 65 years. Benigna, his wife, made this for her deserving husband. May the earth rest lightly upon you here.
EDCS-13001592.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Tertius Caius Servilius Macro, a scribe, set up by his wife, likely from the 1st to 3rd century CE.

EDCS-13001593.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription that appears to mention a gate and consuls, possibly a dedication or marker, the date is highly uncertain.
