EDCS-13001594.translation: To Quintus Domitius Victor, son of Quintus, of the Quirina tribe, prefect of the VI cohort of the Britons, tribune of the soldiers of the X Fretensis legion, tribune of the soldiers of the III Cyrenaica legion, patron of the Calamenses, with money collected.
EDCS-13001594.summary: This is a dedication by the people of Calama to Quintus Domitius Victor, honoring his military and patron status, erected with contributed funds, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13001595.translation: Publius Basilius Rufinus, a soldier of the II cohort of the Sardinians, century of Domitius, lived 50 years, served 17 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-13001595.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Publius Basilius Rufinus, a soldier, recording his age and length of service, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13001596.translation: To Annia Aelia Restituta, perpetual priestess, for her outstanding generosity in pledging 400,000 sesterces for the construction of the theater, and since the town council, because of this, had resolved to erect five statues at public expense, also for the merits of Lucius Annius Aelius Clementis, perpetual priest of Augustus, her father, to whom all the citizens had erected a statue with pooled funds, the entire council by decree.
EDCS-13001596.summary: This inscription records a decree by the town council to erect five statues honoring Annia Aelia Restituta for her generous donation to the theater, and also in memory of her father.

EDCS-13001597.translation: To Annia Aelia Restituta, daughter of Lucius, perpetual priestess of the Augusti, for her exceptional generosity towards her fellow citizens, the entire council, to express gratitude for the theater she promised to adorn with her own money for the benefit of her homeland, resolved to erect five statues at public expense.
EDCS-13001597.summary: This inscription records a decree by the town council to erect five statues honoring Annia Aelia Restituta for her generous promise to fund the adornment of the theater.

EDCS-13001598.translation: To Julius Rusticianus, son of Quintus, of the Papiria tribe, Roman knight, perpetual flamen, former chief magistrate, formeredile, for his innocence, gravity, modesty, as protector, lover of studies, most faithful friend to all, and in all respects a commendable man and a respected father, Julius Lucilianus and Rusticianus Restitutus and Rusticianus, with their own money, have dedicated this, with the offering of an outstanding man, their uncle, the second curator of the city, Julius Rusticianus, our father, marked the memory of his priesthood in the temple by arranging for the hiring of a statue of Hercules, with the approval of the most competent curator of public affairs and the authority of the proconsuls.
EDCS-13001598.summary: This is a dedication of a statue and possibly other honors to Julius Rusticianus, a prominent local official, by his relatives, celebrating his virtues and service.

EDCS-13001599.translation: To Lucius, son of Papirius, Rufinus, perpetual priest of the Augusti, four-time magistrate, first quinquennial magistrate, the town council of the Calamensians, for his merits and generosity, with pooled funds.
EDCS-13001599.summary: This inscription records the recognition of Lucius Papirius Rufinus by the town council of Calamensium for his merits and generosity.

EDCS-13001600.translation: Saturninus, first man of the town, took care to have this erected with his own money.
EDCS-13001600.summary: This short inscription records that Saturninus, a prominent citizen, funded the erection of a monument.

EDCS-13001601.translation: He raised two sons in their early years by his German wife, sent them to their studies, and gave them honors; after such great expenses, he was not honored by anyone at his funeral. When old and laboring, he undertook this task and accomplished all these things. He lived 80 years. His German wife lived 80 years. He also honored the memory of his wife's sister, who was Julia Prima and lived 80 years. Farewell, traveler, reader of my poem.
EDCS-13001601.summary: This epitaph commemorates a man who invested heavily in his sons' education and future, and also honored his deceased wife and her sister, all of whom lived long lives.

EDCS-13001603.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Seia Honorata died in her prime, prudent. She entrusts her children to her most beloved husband. She lost the light of life. She lived twenty-six years.
EDCS-13001603.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Seia Honorata, who died young at 26, leaving behind children and a husband.

EDCS-13001604.translation: Marcus Ulpius Victor Seianus, dutiful decurion of the municipality of the Calamensians, good, modest, studious. He lived 16 years.
EDCS-13001604.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcus Ulpius Victor Seianus, a young decurion of the Calamensians who died at the age of 16.

EDCS-13001605.translation: You desired that you be more abundantly adorned with honor due to the decree of your virtue.
EDCS-13001605.summary: This inscription is a fragmented dedication, likely honoring someone for their virtues and merits, possibly related to a decree.

EDCS-13001607.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcus Ulpius Clarus, dutiful decurion of the municipality of the Calamensians. He lived 23 years and 33 days.
EDCS-13001607.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcus Ulpius Clarus, a young decurion of the Calamensians who died at the age of 23 years and 33 days.

EDCS-13001613.summary: This inscription, likely a funerary marker, is too fragmentary to provide further details beyond the name Rusticus.

EDCS-13001614.translation: Ianuarius, a slave of Nero Claudius Caesar Augustus, lived 30 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-13001614.summary: This is a tombstone for Ianuarius, a slave of Emperor Nero, who died at the age of 30.

EDCS-13001615.translation: Saturnina, housekeeper of Tiberius Claudius Caesar, lived 30 years, and Venusta, her daughter, lived 15 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-13001615.summary: This tombstone commemorates Saturnina, a housekeeper for Emperor Claudius, and her daughter Venusta.

EDCS-13001616.translation: Publius A. Felix lived 25 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-13001616.summary: This is a tombstone for Publius A. Felix, who died at the age of 25.

EDCS-13001617.summary: This inscription records the lifespan of Camarnius, who lived for 40 years, likely on a tombstone.

EDCS-13001618.translation: Aulus Optatus lived 11 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-13001618.summary: This is a tombstone for Aulus Optatus, who died at the age of 11.

EDCS-13001619.translation: Dedicated to the departed spirits. Aemilius Datus lived 72 years. Dedicated to the departed spirits. Domitia Saturnina lived 66 years.
EDCS-13001619.summary: This funerary inscription commemorates two individuals, Aemilius Datus and Domitia Saturnina, with their ages at death.

EDCS-13001620.translation: Dedicated to the departed spirits. Lucius Aemilius Datus the dutiful lived 45 years; he is buried here. Attia Restituta the dutiful lived [---] years; she is buried here.
EDCS-13001620.summary: This funerary inscription records the lives and burials of Lucius Aemilius Datus and Attia Restituta.

EDCS-13001621.translation: Dedicated to the departed spirits. Aemilia Saturnina, daughter of Lucius, lived [---] years. Dedicated to the departed spirits. Lucius Vibius Honoratus the dutiful lived [---] years; he is buried here. Dedicated to the departed spirits. Vibia Saturnina, daughter of Lucius, the dutiful lived 15 years.
EDCS-13001621.summary: This fragmented funerary inscription honors three individuals: Aemilia Saturnina, Lucius Vibius Honoratus, and Vibia Saturnina.

EDCS-13001622.translation: Caius Aponius Dexter lived 6 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-13001622.summary: This is a tombstone for Caius Aponius Dexter, who died at the age of 6.

EDCS-13001623.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Arrius Mustius, dutiful, lived 45 years. Arrius Gudullus, dutiful, lived 22 years. Birictabal Secundus, dutiful, lived 70 years. Pusinna, dutiful, 45 years, is placed here.
EDCS-13001623.summary: A funerary epitaph commemorating four individuals, likely family members, with their ages at death.

EDCS-13001624.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Caius Auficius Restitutus lived 21 years.
EDCS-13001624.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Caius Auficius Restitutus.

EDCS-13001625.translation: The god commanded his servant Siricius. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Eusebius Restuius, dutiful, lived 30 years. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Aurelia Donata, dutiful, lived [duration missing].
EDCS-13001625.summary: A funerary epitaph with a divine command, recording the lifespans of Eusebius Restuius and Aurelia Donata.

EDCS-13001626.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Au[---] Valentina, dutiful, lived 70 years, is placed here. Quintus Caecilius Silvanus lived 65 years, is placed here.
EDCS-13001626.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the burial of Valentina and Quintus Caecilius Silvanus, with their ages at death.

EDCS-13001627.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Baebia Faustina lived 40 years.
EDCS-13001627.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Baebia Faustina.

EDCS-13001628.summary: An inscription likely related to the tomb or memory of Caecilius Atimetus, possibly dedicated by C. Saturnina.

EDCS-13001629.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Caecilius Honoratus lived 25 years, is placed here. [Text possibly incomplete or garbled].
EDCS-13001629.summary: A funerary epitaph for Caecilius Honoratus, stating his age at death and burial.

EDCS-13001630.translation: Caecilia Prima. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Quintus Caecilius Saturninus lived 70 years and [days missing].
EDCS-13001630.summary: A funerary epitaph for Caecilia Prima and Quintus Caecilius Saturninus, recording the latter's age at death.

EDCS-13001631.translation: Caesonia Fellicia lived 75 years, is placed here.
EDCS-13001631.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the burial and lifespan of Caesonia Fellicia.

EDCS-13001633.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Kalpurnia Maximina, dutiful, lived 57 years, 7 months, 18 days, an example of a praiseworthy life. Caecilia Lucilla, daughter-in-law, lived 42 years, 3 months. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Quintus Julius Rusticianus, dutiful, lived 67 years, 8 months.
EDCS-13001633.summary: A funerary epitaph for Kalpurnia Maximina, Caecilia Lucilla, and Quintus Julius Rusticianus, detailing their ages and emphasizing a virtuous life.

EDCS-13001634.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcus Claudius Clemens, pious, lived 75 years; he is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Passenia Celsina, pious, lived 65 years; she is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. [---] Sacred to the departed spirits.
EDCS-13001634.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Marcus Claudius Clemens and Passenia Celsina, likely a couple, with their ages at death.

EDCS-13001635.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Claudia Victoria, pious, lived 23 years; she is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Haterius Iustus, son, pious, lived [---] years.
EDCS-13001635.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Claudia Victoria and Lucius Haterius Iustus, detailing their ages at death.

EDCS-13001636.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Didius Sabinus, pious, lived 20 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-13001636.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Didius Sabinus, specifying his age at death.

EDCS-13001637.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcus Domitius Tutor lived 80 years. Sacred to the departed spirits. Gaia lived 22 years.
EDCS-13001637.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Marcus Domitius Tutor and Gaia, with their ages at death.

EDCS-13001638.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Sacred to the departed spirits. Fabia Saturnina lived 45 years. Sacred to the departed spirits. Caius Iulius Victoricus, pious, lived 40 years, 7 months, and 5 days.
EDCS-13001638.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Fabia Saturnina and Caius Iulius Victoricus, specifying their ages and precise durations of life.

EDCS-13001639.translation: Falconia Fundana lived 27 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-13001639.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Falconia Fundana and her age at death.

EDCS-13001640.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Felix lived 10 years.
EDCS-13001640.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Felix, specifying his age at death.

EDCS-13001641.translation: Flavia Flora lived 26 years. Quintus Iulius, son of Marci, junior, lived 20 years. Iulius Flaminalis, centurion of the II Augusta legion, made this.
EDCS-13001641.summary: This funerary inscription records the burials of Flavia Flora and Quintus Iulius, with their ages, and states that Iulius Flaminalis, a centurion, erected it.

EDCS-13001642.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Flavia Naevilla lived 28 years and 15 days.
EDCS-13001642.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Flavia Naevilla, specifying her age and the number of days she lived.

EDCS-13001643.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcus Fortunius Quintasius, pious, lived 60 years.
EDCS-13001643.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Marcus Fortunius Quintasius, specifying his age at death.

EDCS-13001644.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Fundana Frontonis lived 95 years, is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus Apronius Quintulus lived 72 years. Sacred to the departed spirits. Fundana Pia lived 25 years.
EDCS-13001644.summary: This funerary monument records the burials and ages at death of three individuals: Fundana Frontonis, Quintus Apronius Quintulus, and Fundana Pia.

EDCS-13001645.translation: Gaetulicus, slave of Emperor Domitian, lived 25 years, is buried here.
EDCS-13001645.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial and age at death of Gaetulicus, a slave of Emperor Domitian.

EDCS-13001646.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Helvius Fortunatus lived 66 years. Antonia Optatina lived 46 years.
EDCS-13001646.summary: This funerary inscription records the ages at death of Helvius Fortunatus and Antonia Optatina.

EDCS-13001647.translation: Helvia Fortunata the dutiful lived 30 years, is buried here.
EDCS-13001647.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial and age at death of Helvia Fortunata.

EDCS-13001648.translation: Helvia Fortunata, the mother, dedicated this shrine, her duty fulfilled.
EDCS-13001648.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a shrine by Helvia Fortunata, who fulfilled her maternal duties.

EDCS-13001650.translation: Caius Herennius Iasta the dutiful lived 31 years, is buried here.
EDCS-13001650.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial and age at death of Caius Herennius Iasta.

EDCS-13001651.translation: Herennia Hermiona the dutiful lived 51 years. Valeria Ingenua the dutiful lived 70 years. Marcus Gellius Maximus the dutiful lived 87 years.
EDCS-13001651.summary: This funerary inscription records the ages at death of three individuals: Herennia Hermiona, Valeria Ingenua, and Marcus Gellius Maximus.

EDCS-13001654.translation: Honoratus, son of Urbanus, lived 55 years, is buried here.
EDCS-13001654.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial and age at death of Honoratus, son of Urbanus.

EDCS-13001656.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulius OV. Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulia Urbanosa the dutiful lived [---] years.
EDCS-13001656.summary: This fragmented funerary inscription records part of the names and perhaps ages at death of Iulius OV and Iulia Urbanosa.

EDCS-13001657.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulia Bonosa lived 65 years, 2 months. Caius Iulius Ianuarius lived 20 years, 1 month.
EDCS-13001657.summary: This funerary inscription records the ages at death of Iulia Bonosa and Caius Iulius Ianuarius.

EDCS-13001658.translation: Iulia Borocia and Iulius Primus lived for 76 years.
EDCS-13001658.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespans of Iulia Borocia and Iulius Primus.

EDCS-13001659.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Iulia Ianuaria lived for 75 years; she is buried here. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Faonius Liberalis, dutiful, lived for 50 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-13001659.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the spirits of the departed, recording the lifespans and burial places of Iulia Ianuaria and Faonius Liberalis.

EDCS-13001660.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Iulia Pupa Hospitalis, daughter of [---], lived for 43 years and 7 months. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Iulius Fortunatus, son of Caprarius, lived for 50 years and 4 months.
EDCS-13001660.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the spirits of the departed, recording the lifespans of Iulia Pupa Hospitalis and Iulius Fortunatus.

EDCS-13001661.translation: Marcus Laelius Agrepinus, son of Marcus Acrepinus, lived for 14 years.
EDCS-13001661.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Marcus Laelius Agrepinus.

EDCS-13001662.summary: This is a funerary inscription mentioning Magnius, possibly indicating he commissioned the monument for himself.

EDCS-13001663.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Quintus Manilius Zoboc, dutiful, lived for 81 years; he is buried here. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Quintus Modius Felix, dutiful, lived for 65 years; he is buried here. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Quintus Manilius Maximus, dutiful, lived for 25 years; he is buried here. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Manilia Hilara, dutiful, lived for 5 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-13001663.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the spirits of the departed, recording the lifespans and burial places of Quintus Manilius Zoboc, Quintus Modius Felix, Quintus Manilius Maximus, and Manilia Hilara.

EDCS-13001664.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Marius Saturninus lived for 11 years. Tertia lived for 30 years. Calenus [lived for] 40 years. Marius Marianus lived for 80 years. Marius Felix lived for 30 years. Maria Rogata lived for 12 years.
EDCS-13001664.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the spirits of the departed, recording the lifespans of multiple individuals including Marius Saturninus, Tertia, Calenus, Marius Marianus, Marius Felix, and Maria Rogata.

EDCS-13001665.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Maria Honorata lived for 35 years. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Quintus Auficius Senicio lived for 75 years.
EDCS-13001665.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the spirits of the departed, recording the lifespans of Maria Honorata and Quintus Auficius Senicio.

EDCS-13001666.translation: Marisa, daughter of Silvanus, lived for 31 years.
EDCS-13001666.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Marisa.

EDCS-13001667.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Quintus Messius Saturninus erected this tomb for himself while alive; he lived for [---] years. Caecilia Urbana lived for 10 years. Fulvia Peregrina lived for 63 years.
EDCS-13001667.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the spirits of the departed, where Quintus Messius Saturninus erected a tomb for himself and recording the lifespans of Caecilia Urbana and Fulvia Peregrina.

EDCS-13001668.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Minucia Saturnina lived 45 years. Sacred to the departed spirits. Genti Marcelli, pious, lived 71 years.
EDCS-13001668.summary: This funerary inscription records the lives of two individuals, Minucia Saturnina and Genti Marcelli, who lived 45 and 71 years respectively.

EDCS-13001669.translation: Mithridas, son of Mithridates, lived 9 years. Buried here.
EDCS-13001669.summary: This funerary inscription records the life of Mithridas, son of Mithridates, who died at the age of 9.

EDCS-13001670.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Caius Modius Celer lived 66 years. Buried here.
EDCS-13001670.summary: This funerary inscription records the life of Caius Modius Celer, who died at the age of 66.

EDCS-13001671.translation: Modius Primosus, pious, lived 27 years. Modius Crota lived 13 years, 6 months. Modius Isperatus lived 12 years, 6 months.
EDCS-13001671.summary: This funerary inscription records the lives of three individuals named Modius: Primosus (27 years), Crota (13 years, 6 months), and Isperatus (12 years, 6 months).

EDCS-13001672.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Murosus, son of Honoratus, lived 60 years. Buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Leptinia Festhiva lived 52 years. Buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Borocia, daughter of Honoratus, lived 20 years. Buried here.
EDCS-13001672.summary: This funerary inscription records the lives of three individuals: Murosus (60 years), Leptinia Festhiva (52 years), and Borocia (20 years), with two of them being children of Honoratus.

EDCS-13001674.translation: Nicius Clemens, son of Maximus, pious, lived 23 years. Nicius Maximus and his mother Aedinia.
EDCS-13001674.summary: This funerary inscription records the life of Nicius Clemens, son of Maximus, who died at 23, and mentions his father Nicius Maximus and mother Aedinia.

EDCS-13001675.translation: To Quintus Nicius Fundanus, aged 83, son of Accia Rogata; to Quintus Nicius Anianus, aged 40, son of Nicia Rogata; to Caius Nicius Agrippa, aged 60, son of Nicia Restuta; to Caius Nicius Aniolus, aged 20. Buried here.
EDCS-13001675.summary: This funerary inscription is a family tomb recording the ages at death of Quintus Nicius Fundanus (83), Quintus Nicius Anianus (40), Caius Nicius Agrippa (60), and Caius Nicius Aniolus (20).

EDCS-13001676.translation: Nicius Sufurarius, son of Pudentis, lived 40 years.
EDCS-13001676.summary: This funerary inscription records the life of Nicius Sufurarius, son of Pudentis, who died at the age of 40.

EDCS-13001677.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Ovinius Pudens Lappianus Crescentianus lived 16 years, 4 months, 27 days.
EDCS-13001677.summary: This funerary inscription records the life of Lucius Ovinius Pudens Lappianus Crescentianus, who died at the age of 16 years, 4 months, and 27 days.

EDCS-13001678.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Ovinia Saturnina lived 6 years, 3 months.
EDCS-13001678.summary: This funerary inscription records the life of Ovinia Saturnina, who died at the age of 6 years and 3 months.

EDCS-13001679.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Appius Ianuarius lived 55 years. Sacred to the departed spirits. Postima lived 40 years.
EDCS-13001679.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the ages at death of two individuals, Appius Ianuarius and Postima.

EDCS-13001680.translation: Postima, daughter of Biriamus, lived 41 years.
EDCS-13001680.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the age at death of Postima, daughter of Biriamus.

EDCS-13001681.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Primus, son of Felicis, lived 15 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-13001681.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the age at death of Primus, son of Felicis, who is buried here.

EDCS-13001682.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Pullaenius Rogatus lived 49 years. He is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Licutia Saturnina lived [age missing]. Licutia Saturnina made this for herself and her husband during their lifetime.
EDCS-13001682.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the age at death of Lucius Pullaenius Rogatus and a self-funded burial arrangement made by Licutia Saturnina for herself and her husband.

EDCS-13001683.translation: Marcus Rutilius Rogatus, dutiful, lived 91 years. He made this in his lifetime. He is buried here.
EDCS-13001683.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the age at death of Marcus Rutilius Rogatus, who funded his own burial.

EDCS-13001684.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Satura Paganis lived 62 years. She is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Licinius Martialis lived 55 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-13001684.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the ages at death of two individuals, Satura Paganis and Licinius Martialis.

EDCS-13001685.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Septimia Urbana lived 75 years. She is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus Aemilius Fundanus lived 68 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-13001685.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the ages at death of two individuals, Septimia Urbana and Quintus Aemilius Fundanus.

EDCS-13001686.translation: Septimina the dutiful lived 35 years. Lived [age missing].
EDCS-13001686.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the age at death of Septimina, with a partially repeated or incomplete age entry.

EDCS-13001687.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Sittia Menophila the dutiful lived 25 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-13001687.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the age at death of Sittia Menophila, who is buried here.

EDCS-13001689.translation: THIVAMAC TRABAS, dutiful, lived 60 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-13001689.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the age at death of THIVAMAC TRABAS, who is buried here.

EDCS-13001690.translation: Ovinia Pudentilla, heir and daughter, placed and dedicated this monument to Tonneia Fortunata, whom her husband Ovinius Honoratus ordered to be buried here by his will.
EDCS-13001690.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by a daughter for her mother, following the directions in the deceased's husband's will.

EDCS-13001691.translation: Quintus Trausius, dutiful, lived 25 years. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Cornelia Fortunata, dutiful, lived 40 years. Trausius Saturninus, dutiful, lived 26 years. Trausia Honorata, dutiful, lived 20 years.
EDCS-13001691.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the ages of death for four individuals, likely family members.

EDCS-13001692.translation: The monument which Marcus Turellius Maximus and Ovinia Iba, his wife, built for themselves during their lifetime.
EDCS-13001692.summary: This is a self-funded funerary monument built by a married couple for their own use.

EDCS-13001693.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Valeria Annia Restituta, his devoted wife, lived 71 years and is buried here. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Quintus Bassilius Saturninus, devoted, lived 77 years and is buried here.
EDCS-13001693.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the burial and ages of death for a married couple.

EDCS-13001694.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Caius Vibius Clemens, dutiful, lived 20 years and is buried here.
EDCS-13001694.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the burial and age of death for Caius Vibius Clemens.

EDCS-13001695.translation: Caius Vibius Porcellus, while alive, [built this] for himself and for his wife Postumia Adventa. Postumia Adventa, while alive, [built this]. Caius Vibius Porcellus, her husband, placed [it].
EDCS-13001695.summary: This is a self-funded funerary monument built by a husband for himself and his wife.

EDCS-13001696.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Vibia Valentina, daughter of Lucius, dutiful, lived 20 years. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Pius Aelius Ianuarius, son of Publius, dutiful, lived [unknown] years. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Vibia Constans, daughter, dutiful, lived 23 years and is buried here. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Vibia Honorata, daughter of Lucius, dutiful, lived 17 years and is buried here.
EDCS-13001696.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the burials and ages of death for at least three individuals, likely related.

EDCS-13001697.translation: Victoria, daughter of Montanus, lived [unknown] years.
EDCS-13001697.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription recording the name and parentage of Victoria.

EDCS-13001698.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Iulia Procula lived 70 years.
EDCS-13001698.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the age of death for Iulia Procula.

EDCS-13001699.translation: SIIAIABR ATVRALIS lived 50 years [text missing]. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Marisa, daughter of Mutisanis, lived 120 years and is buried here for 6 months and 5 [days/years?].
EDCS-13001699.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the burial and ages of death for two individuals, one with a remarkably long lifespan recorded.

EDCS-13001702.translation: Tia Quinta, dutiful, lived 61 years. Her son placed this.
EDCS-13001702.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Tia Quinta, placed by her son, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-13001703.summary: This is a simple tombstone inscription recording the lifespan of Restuta, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-13001704.translation: Sacred to the departed gods. N BANIAO
EDCS-13001704.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the Manes (departed spirits), possibly with a name or dedication that is partially illegible, from the Imperial period.

EDCS-13001705.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription, likely funerary, mentioning a person named Gentius and possibly their life, from the Imperial period.

EDCS-13001706.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for an infant named Libertas, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-13001707.translation: Rufus lived 60 years, here he lies.
EDCS-13001707.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the lifespan and burial place of Rufus, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-13001709.translation: OM ROR EXAS FACIQE DOMV IS VIXV DISEX Flavius ESFOICETVS
EDCS-13001709.summary: This is a fragmented inscription that appears to be funerary, mentioning a person named Flavius ESFOICETVS, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-13001710.translation: In this tomb, Adeodatus, pitiable and faithful in Christ, lived 17 years and 3 months, laid to rest on the Ides of July, in the 2nd indiction.
EDCS-13001710.summary: This is a Christian funerary inscription recording the life and burial date of Adeodatus, likely from the Late Roman period.

EDCS-13001711.translation: In this place, Donatianus, servant of God, laid to rest in peace on the 10th day before the Kalends of January, in the 11th indiction.
EDCS-13001711.summary: This is a Christian funerary inscription recording the burial date of Donatianus, a servant of God, likely from the Late Roman period.

EDCS-13001712.translation: In memory of Jana, lived 39 years in peace. Likewise in memory of Flavius Gaetulus. His wife equipped the tomb from the ground up.
EDCS-13001712.summary: This is a tombstone inscription commemorating Jana and Flavius Gaetulus, placed by his wife, likely from the Late Roman or Early Byzantine period.

EDCS-13001713.translation: Matrona, innocent, lived for 1 year and 6 months. She rested in peace on the third day before the Ides of January, in the second indiction.
EDCS-13001713.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Matrona, recording her age at death and the date of her burial in the late Roman period.

EDCS-13001714.translation: Here rests Petrus, innocent and faithful in Christ. He lived for 8 years and 14 days. Amen.
EDCS-13001714.summary: This tombstone inscription records the death and burial of Petrus, a child who lived for 8 years, likely in the early Christian period.

EDCS-13001715.translation: Eirene rested in peace on the tenth day before the Kalends of June, aged 5 years, 9 months, and 27 days.
EDCS-13001715.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Eirene, detailing her age at death and the date of her repose.

EDCS-13002178.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Martius lived for 85 years. His sons and sons-in-law erected this monument.
EDCS-13002178.summary: A tombstone inscription dedicated to the memory of Martius by his sons and sons-in-law, indicating he lived to be 85.

EDCS-13002181.translation: lius Pacatus lived for 36 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-13002181.summary: This is a tombstone inscription forlius Pacatus, stating he lived for 36 years and is buried at this location.

EDCS-13002444.translation: Sacred to Bellona Augusta. Caius Iulius Cattianus willingly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-13002444.summary: A dedication to the goddess Bellona Augusta, recording that Caius Iulius Cattianus fulfilled a vow.

EDCS-13002445.translation: Sacred to Jupiter Optimus Maximus and Saturnus Augustus. Quintus Fabius Pullas and his son Pullaenus, priests, willingly fulfilled their vow.
EDCS-13002445.summary: A dedication to Jupiter and Saturn by priests Quintus Fabius Pullas and his son, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-13002447.translation: Marcus Canteius, soldier of the Legion III Augusta, under Centurion Perpetuus, lived 30 years, served 5 years, is buried here.
EDCS-13002447.summary: A funerary epitaph for Marcus Canteius, a soldier of the Legion III Augusta, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13002448.translation: Sacred to Conservatrix, protector of the Roman people. Marcus Valerius Novius Elpideforus, crowned, a cist-bearer, with his household, made and dedicated this grove from the ground up, with its statues and ornaments.
EDCS-13002448.summary: A dedication of a sacred grove to the goddess Conservatrix by Marcus Valerius Novius Elpideforus and his family.

EDCS-13002449.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Stercula lived 5 years, 2 months, and 7 days. Liberalis, assistant to the scribe of our lord Augustus, and Felicia, made [this] for their dearest daughter, is buried here.
EDCS-13002449.summary: A funerary epitaph for Stercula, a child, with funerary inscriptions by her father and possibly mother, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13002450.translation: Marcus Julius Maternus, son of Marcus, of the Quirina tribe, in the service of Augustus, soldier of the Legion III Augusta, under Centurion Crispinus, lived 27 years, served 5 years, is buried here. Sextus Valerius Atticinus, standard-bearer of the cavalry of the Legion III Augusta.
EDCS-13002450.summary: A combined funerary epitaph for Marcus Julius Maternus and an adjacent inscription for Sextus Valerius Atticinus, both soldiers of the Legion III Augusta, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13002451.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Marco Aurelio Ursiono, freedman of the junior Augustus, lived 90 years, 3 months, and 5 days.
EDCS-13002451.summary: A funerary epitaph for Marco Aurelio Ursiono, a freedman of an emperor, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13002452.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Iulia Celsina, also known as Lampadaria, who lived 6 years and 8 months, rests here. Iulia made this for her most sweet daughter.
EDCS-13002452.summary: A funerary epitaph for a young girl named Iulia Celsina, set up by her mother, Iulia Celsina.

EDCS-13002453.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Secura, the dutiful, lived 64 years, rests here.
EDCS-13002453.summary: A funerary epitaph for a woman named Secura, likely from the 1st or 2nd century AD.

EDCS-13002455.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Vaberia Saturnia, daughter of PII [?], [? from ON Victor?], lived for 26 years. She made this.
EDCS-13002455.summary: A funerary inscription for Vaberia Saturnia, daughter of PII [?], by [? Victor?], who died at the age of 26.

EDCS-13002456.translation: Emerita made this for her son, pious, aged 12.
EDCS-13002456.summary: A tombstone inscription by Emerita for her pious son who died at the age of 12.

EDCS-13002457.translation: Bonosus of good memory rested here in peace, lived 10 years, 8 months, buried on the 14th day before the Kalends of January, in the 10th indiction.
EDCS-13002457.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the burial of Bonosus, who lived 10 years and 8 months, with the date of burial specified.

EDCS-13002458.translation: Donatus, chief centurion, of good memory, lived 60 years, buried on the 11th day before the Ides of October, in the 15th indiction.
EDCS-13002458.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Donatus, a chief centurion, who lived 60 years, with the date of burial provided.

EDCS-13002459.translation: Hilarus of good memory rested here in peace, lived 50 years, buried on the Nones of March, in the 12th indiction.
EDCS-13002459.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Hilarus, who lived 50 years, with the date of burial specified.

EDCS-13002460.translation: The burial of Iohannes, chief centurion, placed in peace, on the 4th day before the Ides of June.
EDCS-13002460.summary: This inscription records the burial of Iohannes, a chief centurion, and gives the date of burial.

EDCS-13002461.translation: Liberatus, a cleric of good memory, rested here in peace, lived 12 years with Christ, was buried on the 8th day before the Ides of February.
EDCS-13002461.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Liberatus, a cleric, who lived 12 years and was buried on a specific date.

EDCS-13002462.translation: Theodorus of good memory, a faithful one, rested here in peace, lived 7 years, buried on the 21st day before the Kalends of October, in the 14th indiction.
EDCS-13002462.summary: This inscription records the burial of Theodorus, who lived 7 years, and specifies the date of burial and indiction.

EDCS-13002485.text_edition: \n Ex auctoritate Imperatoris Caesaris Traiani Augusti Germanici Dacici Lucius Munatius Gallus legatus pro praetore finibus Musulamiorum ectis vetustatis tam abolevit\n
EDCS-13002485.translation: By the authority of Emperor Caesar Trajan Augustus Germanicus Dacicus, Lucius Munatius Gallus, governor with praetorian power, removed the boundaries of the Musulamii which had been erased by age.
EDCS-13002485.summary: A boundary stone dating to the reign of Trajan (98-117 AD), recording the action of the governor Lucius Munatius Gallus regarding the Musulamii tribe.

EDCS-13002497.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the dead. Maria Donata lived 65 years. Sextius Laetus made this for his wife, who is buried here.
EDCS-13002497.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Sextius Laetus for his wife Maria Donata, who lived 65 years.

EDCS-13002498.translation: For great works, from the imminent [danger?], for which reason we render praises in the most fortunate times of our lords Heraclius and Heraclius the Younger, Constantinus and Eudocia Augusti, the most pious [man] together with his companions brought forth [the completion?].
EDCS-13002498.summary: This inscription likely refers to the completion of significant public works during the reigns of Eastern Roman Emperors Heraclius and his son, possibly in the 7th century AD.

EDCS-13002500.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the dead. I Namgedde lived 30 years. Lucius Tekirus made this.
EDCS-13002500.summary: This funerary epitaph was erected by Lucius Tekirus for I Namgedde, who lived 30 years.

EDCS-13002527.translation: Publius Messius Melissus, son of Publius, of the voting tribe Quirina, from Augusta, a soldier of the III Augusta legion, in the century of Lucilius, lived 30 years, served 4 years, rests here. Decimus Clodius, armourer, of the same century, erected this monument.
EDCS-13002527.summary: A funerary epitaph for Publius Messius Melissus, a soldier of the III Augusta legion, with his monument erected by a fellow soldier.

EDCS-13002528.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Valerius Vitalis, a soldier from the ranks of the Martenses, from Gaul, lived 55 years.
EDCS-13002528.summary: A funerary epitaph for Valerius Vitalis, a soldier who served in a unit from Gaul, likely from the 1st or 2nd century AD.

EDCS-13002529.translation: To rino, centurion, lived 13 years and [---] 23 [---] divus MA [---] for perpetual SE [---] rity.
EDCS-13002529.summary: This fragmented inscription appears to be a funerary dedication for a centurion named rino, possibly mentioning his age and military service.

EDCS-13002530.translation: Centurion, armourer of the second Adiutrix legion, promoted into the III Augusta legion, 26 years of service, who lived 46 years, 2 months, and 20 days, rests here. Aurelia Dio[--] made this for her husband [--].
EDCS-13002530.summary: A funerary epitaph for a centurion and armourer, who served in two legions and had 26 years of service, erected by his wife Aurelia Dio[--].

EDCS-13002532.translation: To Aelia Beneaucxidi, wife of Quintus Titinius Securus, priest, quaestor, prefect for administering justice, duovir, munerarius of the curiae and Augustales, who, among his other generous gifts, [gave] sportulas to the decurions...
EDCS-13002532.summary: This is a funerary inscription honoring Aelia Beneaucxidi, wife of Quintus Titinius Securus, a prominent local official, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-13002533.translation: To Aurelia Ianuaria, daughter of Aurelius Exceptus, fiancée and wife of Quintus Crepereius Rufus; to Quintus Crepereius Papiria Rufinus, son of Germanus, augur, aedile, prefect for administering justice, duovir, for his outstanding life and quiet discipline and his prompt generosity in public duties, which he exercised towards his citizens; the entire curia and the Augustales erected this, at his own expense. In order to repay this honor, the same Rufinus gave sportulas of two gold coins each to the decurions and to Caesar's freedmen, and also to the forenses and friends, and to the curiae and Augustales, and gave wine to the people and staged games.
EDCS-13002533.summary: This is a funerary and honorific inscription for Quintus Crepereius Rufinus, a high-ranking local official, detailing his public service and generous donations to the community, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-13002534.translation: Papirius Datus, son, duovir, munerarius, prefect for administering justice, on the day of his public games to all the curiae.
EDCS-13002534.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely recording the public services or benefactions of Papirius Datus, a local official, possibly dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-13002535.translation: To Julianus, a Roman knight, an excellent man, priest, munerarius of the colony of Thevestis, and for his sincere loyalty and integrity with which he deals with the citizens, the entire curia and the Augustales.
EDCS-13002535.summary: This is an honorific inscription dedicated to Julianus, a Roman knight and local official, by the curia and Augustales of Thevestis, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-13002536.translation: To Titinia Iulia, daughter of Quintus Titinius Securus, priest, quaestor, prefect for administering justice, duovir, munerarius, wife of Caius Roinus Petronianus, decorated with the public horse, by the curia and the Augustales for which dedications.
EDCS-13002536.summary: This is a funerary inscription honoring Titinia Iulia, daughter of Quintus Titinius Securus and wife of Caius Roinus Petronianus, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-13002537.translation: To Marcus Valerius Flavius Sabinianus, son of Marcus, of the Papirian tribe, munerarius, and Aurelia Salvilla, for her integrity, [and] simplice and the Augustales, for which dedication sportulas to the curiae and to the Augustales.
EDCS-13002537.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely honoring Marcus Valerius Flavius Sabinianus and Aurelia Salvilla, possibly a couple, for their integrity and benefactions, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-13002538.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Fortunatus, assistant to our Emperor from the office of records, lived 32 years, 1 month, and 17 days, rests here. [---]ATE[---] and Venustula, his wife, made this for their dearest husband. Vegethi.
EDCS-13002538.summary: A funerary epitaph for Fortunatus, an imperial assistant, erected by his wife Venustula and another individual, Vegethi.

EDCS-13002539.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Maxima, servant of our Emperor, lived 5 years, rests here. Victor made this for his most dutiful daughter.
EDCS-13002539.summary: A funerary epitaph for a young girl named Maxima, a servant of the emperor, erected by her father Victor.

EDCS-13002540.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Sallustia Amnubiti(?), freedwoman of our Emperors, lived 18 years, 3 months, and 5 days. Ianua, freedwoman of our Emperors, her mother, made this for her most rare daughter.
EDCS-13002540.summary: A funerary epitaph for Sallustia Amnubiti(?), a young freedwoman, erected by her mother Ianua, who was also a freedwoman of the emperors.

EDCS-13002541.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Cornelius Vincentius, foster-child of the arena, lived [---] years, 3 months, and 10 days. Baberius, father, made this for his dearest son.
EDCS-13002541.summary: A funerary epitaph for Cornelius Vincentius, a gladiator ('foster-child of the arena'), erected by his father.

EDCS-13002542.translation: Youthful love stirs me, no teacher given; I lived for as many years as the fates wrote for me. To me, a wild beast was much more preferable, that with a bridle I kept in my house. If any horse ran under me, which was desirable, I died because I fell from a horn, as was vowed. Now rest my remains in the earth, through which I was known. Caius Iulius Camma.
EDCS-13002542.summary: This is a personal epitaph of Caius Iulius Camma, who expresses a passion for horses and a life lived according to fate and personal vows, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13002543.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription mentioning Publius Aelianus, possibly a dedication or a funerary marker, the date and purpose are uncertain.

EDCS-13002545.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Quintus Aelius Salvianus lived 60 years and is buried here. His sons Aelii Saturninus, Messianus, Octavianus, and Sedatus made this for their father.
EDCS-13002545.summary: A funerary monument records the life and death of Quintus Aelius Salvianus, with dedication by his sons.

EDCS-13002546.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Aemilius Processianus lived 13 years, 2 months, and 16 days and is buried here. His grandfather Manilius Restutus and Aemilius Felicisimus made this for their dearest son.
EDCS-13002546.summary: A funerary monument for a young boy, Aemilius Processianus, with dedication by his grandfather and another relation.

EDCS-13002547.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. [A]emilia Donativa lived 1 year, 4 months, and 13 days and is buried here, who lived sweeter than a rose. Her father Turbo and mother Designata made this for their daughter.
EDCS-13002547.summary: A funerary monument for an infant girl, Aemilia Donativa, with dedication by her parents.

EDCS-13002548.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Aemilia Processa lived 59 years. Her husband Manilius Restutus and her sons Aemilii made this for their dearest mother.
EDCS-13002548.summary: A funerary monument for Aemilia Processa, with dedication by her husband and sons.

EDCS-13002549.translation: Marcus Anneius Salsulus made this for his most devoted son.
EDCS-13002549.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Marcus Anneius Salsulus for his son, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13002550.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Annius Maximus lived 45 years. His sons erected this.
EDCS-13002550.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Annius Maximus, set up by his sons, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13002551.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Annia Stephanicia lived 30 years. Marius Victor made this for his pious wife.
EDCS-13002551.summary: This is a tombstone erected by Marius Victor for his wife Annia Stephanicia, likely in the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13002552.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Antonia Saturnina, daughter of Quintus, lived 60 pious years. Volusianus placed this for his most pious wife; she lies here.
EDCS-13002552.summary: This is a tombstone for Antonia Saturnina, erected by her husband Volusianus, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13002553.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Lucius Apponius Hilarus Tonantius lived 37 years, 4 months, and 9 days and is buried here. Licinia Montana made this for her dearest husband.
EDCS-13002553.summary: A funerary monument for Lucius Apponius Hilarus Tonantius, with dedication by his wife.

EDCS-13002554.translation: Lucius Aridius Fortunatus lies here. With piety, he set up this stone for his most pious father.
EDCS-13002554.summary: This inscription records Lucius Aridius Fortunatus setting up a tombstone for his father, likely in the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13002555.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. For Lucius Atellius Terminalis, son of Lucius, of the Papiria tribe, who lived 80 years and is buried here; I arranged for this to be made while still alive.
EDCS-13002555.summary: A funerary monument for Lucius Atellius Terminalis, who commissioned his own tomb.

EDCS-13002556.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Baebia Aemerita lived 61 years, 3 months, and 5 days. Liberalis, Fuscus, and Emeritus made this for their most beloved mother.
EDCS-13002556.summary: This tombstone was erected by Liberalis, Fuscus, and Emeritus for their mother Baebia Aemerita, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13002557.summary: A brief epitaph for Birsil, possibly a tombstone inscription from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13002558.translation: Gaius Caelius Vi [dedicated this] to the Dacian Datus.
EDCS-13002558.summary: This is a dedication by Gaius Caelius Vi to someone named Datus, possibly a Roman military inscription.

EDCS-13002559.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Caelia Primula lived 7 months and 8 days and is buried here. Lucius Caelius Primulus and Iulia Dativa made this for their dearest daughter.
EDCS-13002559.summary: A funerary monument for an infant girl, Caelia Primula, with dedication by her parents.

EDCS-13002560.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Caelia Victoria lived 3 years and 4 months. Caelius Maximus, her father, made this for his daughter. She is buried here.
EDCS-13002560.summary: A funerary monument for Caelia Victoria, a young girl, with dedication by her father.

EDCS-13002561.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Claudius Abigeus, freedman, lived 8 years, 6 months, and 20 days. Claudius Orion made this for his dearest foster-son. He is buried here.
EDCS-13002561.summary: A funerary monument for a young freedman, Claudius Abigeus, with dedication by his foster-father.

EDCS-13002562.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Coelia Quinta lived 65 years. Avidia Sissonia out of piety, and her son Coelius Caius, placed this; she lies here.
EDCS-13002562.summary: This tombstone for Coelia Quinta was erected by her daughter Avidia Sissonia and grandson Coelius Caius, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13002563.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Cornelius Dativus lived [ ] years and is buried here. [For his most exceptional father] Cornelius Lupercus, as a consolation [after his death].
EDCS-13002563.summary: A funerary monument for Cornelius Dativus, with a partial dedication for his father, Cornelius Lupercus.

EDCS-13002564.translation: Maevius Faustus, with his sons Maevius Octavianus Fortunatus, Petrus Paulus Saturninus, made this for his wife Curtiae Saturninae, who lived here 60 years, for his most faithful wife.
EDCS-13002564.summary: This tombstone for Curtiae Saturninae was erected by her husband Maevius Faustus and their sons, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13002565.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Earbal lived 13 years. Pelusius made this for his student.
EDCS-13002565.summary: This tombstone for the young Earbal was erected by his teacher Pelusius, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13002566.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Esuvia Quintula lived 60 years. Her sons made this; she lies here.
EDCS-13002566.summary: This tombstone for Esuvia Quintula was erected by her sons, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13002567.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Klbli, aged 80 years.
EDCS-13002567.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Klbli, who lived to be 80 years old.

EDCS-13002568.translation: To the gods of the underworld. Gaius F. Felix lived 50 years.
EDCS-13002568.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Gaius F. Felix.

EDCS-13002570.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Flavia Ingenua lived 30 years; she is buried here. A son placed this for his mother.
EDCS-13002570.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Flavia Ingenua, erected by her son.

EDCS-13002571.translation: Lived 7 years. Sacred to the departed spirits. Saturnius of Mellitena lived 5 years, 1 month, and 10 days. TE [possibly an abbreviation or letters of unknown meaning].
EDCS-13002571.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Saturnius of Mellitena, who died at the age of 7 years, 1 month, and 10 days.

EDCS-13002572.translation: Fortunatus lived 55 years. Petronia Quarta had this made for her dearest husband and he is buried here.
EDCS-13002572.summary: A funerary inscription recording the death of Fortunatus and erected by his wife Petronia Quarta.

EDCS-13002574.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Gavilia ittes lived 55 years. Repentinus made this for his most devoted mother.
EDCS-13002574.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Gavilia ittes, erected by her son Repentinus.

EDCS-13002575.translation: To the gods of the underworld. Gavilia Felicula lived 15 years. Her father Flavius Ianuarius made the tomb.
EDCS-13002575.summary: A funerary inscription for Gavilia Felicula, detailing her age and that her father commissioned the tomb.

EDCS-13002576.translation: To the gods of the underworld. Gentia Prima lived 50 years and 2 months. She is buried here.
EDCS-13002576.summary: A funerary inscription stating the lifespan and burial place of Gentia Prima.

EDCS-13002577.translation: To the gods of the underworld. Gaius Julius Donatianus lived 32 years, 4 months, and 6 days. His brother Gaius Julius Felix made this for him, a most devoted brother.
EDCS-13002577.summary: A funerary inscription for Gaius Julius Donatianus, detailing his lifespan and commissioned by his devoted brother.

EDCS-13002578.summary: A short inscription likely referring to a table, possibly part of a funerary monument.

EDCS-13002579.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulius Urbanus lived 46 years, 2 months, and 18 days. Iulius Innocentianus made this for his dearest brother.
EDCS-13002579.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Iulius Urbanus, erected by his brother Iulius Innocentianus.

EDCS-13002580.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. For Iulia Antonia, pious, who lived 35 years. Aurelius Fortunatus made this.
EDCS-13002580.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Iulia Antonia, erected by Aurelius Fortunatus.

EDCS-13002581.translation: To the gods of the underworld. Iulia Castula made this for her husband Donatus, who lived 72 years.
EDCS-13002581.summary: A funerary inscription for Donatus, commissioned by his wife Iulia Castula.

EDCS-13002582.translation: To the gods of the underworld. Iulia Ianuaría lived 23 years, 2 months, and 25 days. Gaius Roius Emeritus made this for his most devoted wife and she is buried here.
EDCS-13002582.summary: A funerary inscription for Iulia Ianuaría, detailing her lifespan and erected by her husband Gaius Roius Emeritus.

EDCS-13002584.translation: To the gods of the underworld. Iulia Vitalis lived 45 years. She is buried here. Her sons made this for their most devoted mother.
EDCS-13002584.summary: A funerary inscription for Iulia Vitalis, stating her age and that her sons commissioned the monument.

EDCS-13002585.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. For Lartidus.
EDCS-13002585.summary: This is a very brief funerary epitaph dedicated to Lartidus.

EDCS-13002586.translation: To the gods of the underworld. Lepidius Congius lived 75 years. His devoted wife made this and he is buried here.
EDCS-13002586.summary: A funerary inscription for Lepidius Congius, recording his lifespan and erected by his devoted wife.

EDCS-13002587.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Liberalis lived for 11 years.
EDCS-13002587.summary: A funerary inscription recording the death of Liberalis at the age of 11.

EDCS-13002588.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Licinia Claudia lived for 12 months. Lucius Licinius Speratus made this for his pious daughter.
EDCS-13002588.summary: A funerary inscription recording the death of Licinia Claudia at 12 months old, dedicated by her father Lucius Licinius Speratus.

EDCS-13002589.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Licinia Quartula lived for 43 years. Her daughter made this for her mother.
EDCS-13002589.summary: A funerary inscription recording the death of Licinia Quartula at 43 years old, made by her daughter.

EDCS-13002590.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Marius Felix, also known as Cucio.
EDCS-13002590.summary: A funerary inscription commemorating Marius Felix, who was also known as Cucio.

EDCS-13002592.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Petronius Victor lived for 60 years. His son made this willingly.
EDCS-13002592.summary: A funerary inscription recording the death of Petronius Victor at 60 years old, made by his son.

EDCS-13002593.translation: Lucius Pompeius Paullinus [set this up] for his son Lucius Pompeius.
EDCS-13002593.summary: This inscription records Lucius Pompeius Paullinus setting up a monument for his son, Lucius Pompeius.

EDCS-13002594.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Pomponia Firmana Mascaradiana lived for 33 years and 4 months.
EDCS-13002594.summary: A funerary inscription recording the death of Pomponia Firmana Mascaradiana at 33 years and 4 months old.

EDCS-13002596.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Porcius Felix lived for 92 years. Porcia Iuliana and Zaba, his heirs, made this; he is buried here.
EDCS-13002596.summary: A funerary inscription recording the death of Porcius Felix at 92 years old, made by his heirs Porcia Iuliana and Zaba.

EDCS-13002597.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Pothus lived for 31 years. His wife Ianuaria made this for her pious husband; he is buried here.
EDCS-13002597.summary: A funerary inscription recording the death of Pothus at 31 years old, made by his wife Ianuaria.

EDCS-13002598.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Lucius Publicius Successus lived for 14 years, 3 months, and 15 days. Successus, his father, made this for his pious son.
EDCS-13002598.summary: A funerary inscription recording the death of Lucius Publicius Successus at 14 years, 3 months, and 15 days old, made by his father.

EDCS-13002599.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Quinquatralis lived for 18 years, 5 months, and 23 days. His sister Tsidina made this.
EDCS-13002599.summary: A funerary inscription recording the death of Quinquatralis at 18 years, 5 months, and 23 days old, made by his sister.

EDCS-13002600.translation: Lived 11 years. Sacred to the departed spirits. Securus [lived].
EDCS-13002600.summary: This funerary epitaph records that Securus lived for 11 years.

EDCS-13002601.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Marcus Sextilius Donatus lived 30 years; he is buried here. His sons made this for their dearest father.
EDCS-13002601.summary: A funerary epitaph for Marcus Sextilius Donatus, set up by his sons, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-13002602.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Sextus, son of..., made this for Rogata Valentia, who lived 45 years.
EDCS-13002602.summary: A funerary epitaph for Rogata Valentia, set up by her son Sextus, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-13002604.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Marcus Valerius lived 50 years.
EDCS-13002604.summary: A funerary epitaph for Marcus Valerius, noting his age, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-13002605.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Caius Valerius Fortis lived 60 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-13002605.summary: A funerary epitaph for Caius Valerius Fortis, noting his age and burial, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-13002607.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Caius Vibius Geminus lived 19 years. Vibius Postumius(?) made this for his most devoted son.
EDCS-13002607.summary: A funerary epitaph for Caius Vibius Geminus, set up by his father Vibius Postumius(?), likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-13002608.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Victoria for father and daughter Q[...]
EDCS-13002608.summary: A funerary epitaph recording Victoria for a father and daughter, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-13002609.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Victorinus lived 22 years.
EDCS-13002609.summary: A funerary epitaph for Victorinus, noting his age, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-13002610.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. [This tomb is for] Evasia, wife of Roi(?), most holy, lived 20 years, 2 months, 15 days; she is buried here.
EDCS-13002610.summary: A funerary epitaph for Evasia, the wife of Roi(?), noting her age and burial, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-13002612.summary: This inscription records Mestrianus setting up a monument.

EDCS-13002615.translation: Fortunatus, a well-deserved veteran, in peace.
EDCS-13002615.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a veteran named Fortunatus, likely dating to the late Roman period.

EDCS-13002616.translation: Antonius, of good memory, was laid to rest here in peace on the fifth day before the Kalends of November in the second indiction.
EDCS-13002616.summary: This funerary epitaph records the burial of Antonius, with a specific date given according to the consular calendar and indiction cycle.

EDCS-13002617.translation: Three brothers were buried here; Cota, of good memory, was laid to rest here in peace on the second day before the Nones of November in the second indiction.
EDCS-13002617.summary: This funerary inscription commemorates the burial of Cota, noting that he was one of three brothers and providing a precise date.

EDCS-13002618.translation: Fortunata, a little child, of good memory, was laid to rest here in peace on the seventh day before the Kalends of July.
EDCS-13002618.summary: This funerary epitaph records the burial of a young child named Fortunata, with the date of death provided.

EDCS-13002619.summary: This is a dedication to a deity or a revered person named Meggenus.

EDCS-13002620.translation: Minarcius rests here in peace; he lived 100 years and was buried on the sixth day before the Ides of July in the ninth indiction.
EDCS-13002620.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Minarcius, who lived to be 100 years old, with the date of burial specified.

EDCS-13002621.translation: Pontus, of good memory, rests here in peace; he lived 4 years, 7 months, and 3 days, and was laid to rest on the fifth day before the Kalends of February on a holy day.
EDCS-13002621.summary: This funerary epitaph details the life and burial of a child named Pontus, including his age and the date of his repose.

EDCS-13002622.inscription_type: inscriptiones christianae, tituli operum, tituli sepulcrales
EDCS-13002622.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Caius Iulius Felix lived 58 years and 7 months. Iulius Felix, his son, made this for his most devoted father; he is buried here. // Mensa Sisatiu.
EDCS-13002622.summary: A funerary epitaph for Caius Iulius Felix, set up by his son, noting his age and burial, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-13002623.translation: Victorinus, of good memory, was laid to rest here in peace on the twelfth day before the Kalends of October in the second indiction.
EDCS-13002623.summary: This funerary epitaph records the burial of Victorinus, specifying the date of his repose according to the consular calendar and indiction.

EDCS-13002625.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Claudius Annius Honoratianus, son of Marcus, of the Papiria tribe, lived 25 years, 2 months, 25 days. Marcus Ann(i)us Octavianus, his unhappy father, made this; he is buried here.
EDCS-13002625.summary: A funerary epitaph for Claudius Annius Honoratianus, set up by his father, noting his age and burial, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-13002626.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Valeria Severa lived 28 years, 7 months; she rests here. Julius Constans made this for his most beloved wife.
EDCS-13002626.summary: A funerary epitaph for Valeria Severa, who died at the age of 28 years and 7 months, erected by her husband Julius Constans.

EDCS-13002627.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. A. Paulina lived 24 years; she lies here, made for her dearest, by herself alone on earth, having gained and departed from life on the same day.
EDCS-13002627.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for A. Paulina, who died at age 24 on the same day she was married or entered a significant phase of life, erected by herself.

EDCS-13002632.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Fufidius Faustus, pious, lived 80 years; he lies here.
EDCS-13002632.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Fufidius Faustus, who lived 80 years and is commemorated for his piety.

EDCS-13002637.translation: A sacred offering to Ceres and Pluto, in honor of Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus and his entire divine family; the Turratenses willingly made this with their own money.
EDCS-13002637.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Ceres and Pluto made by the Turratenses for the health of Emperor Marcus Aurelius Antoninus, likely from the mid-3rd century CE.

EDCS-13002638.translation: A sacred offering to Jupiter Best and Greatest, and to Saturn Augustus.
EDCS-13002638.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Jupiter and Saturn, probably from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13002642.translation: A sacred offering to the spirits of the dead. Munatia Fortunata lived for 16 years, 3 months, and 8 days; Munatia Bonavia made this for her dearest daughter, who is buried here.
EDCS-13002642.summary: This inscription is a tombstone for Munatia Fortunata, who died at the age of 16, and was dedicated by her mother, Munatia Bonavia, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13002644.translation: A sacred offering to Mercury Augustus. Gaius Pompeius Castus willingly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-13002644.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to Mercury Augustus made by Gaius Pompeius Castus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13002645.translation: A sacred offering to the spirits of the dead. Vitalis the shoemaker lived for 35 years; Iucundus made this for his dearest brother.
EDCS-13002645.summary: This inscription is a tombstone for Vitalis the shoemaker, who died at the age of 35, and was dedicated by his brother, Iucundus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13002646.translation: A sacred offering to the spirits of the dead. Aurelius Splendor lived for 47 years; Pompeia Matrona made this for her dearest husband.
EDCS-13002646.summary: This inscription is a tombstone for Aurelius Splendor, who died at the age of 47, and was dedicated by his wife, Pompeia Matrona, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13002647.translation: Barigbalis lived for 41 years; here he lies.
EDCS-13002647.summary: This inscription is a tombstone for Barigbalis, who died at the age of 41, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13002648.translation: A sacred offering to the spirits of the dead. Gaius Flaminius Maximus lived for 70 years; his son made this for his good father.
EDCS-13002648.summary: This inscription is a tombstone for Gaius Flaminius Maximus, who died at the age of 70, and was dedicated by his son, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13002649.translation: A sacred offering to the spirits of the dead. Flavia Salvia lived for 28 years; Modius Mutthun made this for his wife.
EDCS-13002649.summary: This inscription is a tombstone for Flavia Salvia, who died at the age of 28, and was dedicated by her husband, Modius Mutthun, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13002650.translation: A sacred offering to the spirits of the dead for Flavia Successa, his dearest wife.
EDCS-13002650.summary: This inscription is a tombstone dedicated to Flavia Successa, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13002651.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Gaius Julius Donatus lived 91 years. Fundania Victoria made this for her dearest husband.
EDCS-13002651.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Gaius Julius Donatus and was made by his wife, Fundania Victoria.

EDCS-13002652.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Iulius Fortunatus lived 40 years. His wife made this.
EDCS-13002652.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Iulius Fortunatus and was made by his wife.

EDCS-13002653.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Tertulla lived 22 years. Flavius Hipolitus made this for his sweetest wife.
EDCS-13002653.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Tertulla and was made by her husband, Flavius Hipolitus.

EDCS-13002654.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Z... lived 115 years.
EDCS-13002654.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of a person whose name is partially illegible.

EDCS-13002655.translation: Primus made this for his spouse.
EDCS-13002655.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording that Primus made a monument for his spouse.

EDCS-13002656.translation: Gaius Clodius Paterculus willingly paid his vow to Saturn.
EDCS-13002656.summary: This is a dedication recording Gaius Clodius Paterculus fulfilling a vow to the god Saturn.

EDCS-13002657.translation: Marcus Iulius Restus, dutiful, lived 35 years. He lies here.
EDCS-13002657.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Marcus Iulius Restus and his burial place.

EDCS-13002658.translation: Saturnina, daughter of Mutunbalis, dutiful, lived 35 years. She lies here.
EDCS-13002658.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Saturnina and her burial place.

EDCS-13002660.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Sexta Apuleia Fortunata lived 60 years. She made this for her wife.
EDCS-13002660.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Sexta Apuleia Fortunata and that she made this for her wife.

EDCS-13002661.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulius Elianus Pulneus lived 35 years. His wife (?) Felicita (?) made this.
EDCS-13002661.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the age of Iulius Elianus Pulneus as 35 years, with a partially restored dedication by his wife.

EDCS-13002662.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Getula lived approximately 30 years.
EDCS-13002662.summary: A brief funerary epitaph stating that Getula lived for approximately 30 years.

EDCS-13002663.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Lived fifty years. Claudius Fasir made this for Claudius Valerianus, his brother. Firmus made and dedicated this.
EDCS-13002663.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Claudius Valerianus, and it was made and dedicated by his brother Firmus.

EDCS-13002664.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulius [3]nius lived 25 years. Ponponia Ianuaria, his wife, made and dedicated this at her own expense. He rests here.
EDCS-13002664.summary: A funerary epitaph for Iulius [3]nius, who died at 25, erected by his wife Ponponia Ianuaria.

EDCS-13002665.translation: Iulia Tertia lived 26 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-13002665.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the life span of Iulia Tertia.

EDCS-13002666.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Victoria lived 3 years, 5 months. Her dearest parents made this for their sweetest daughter.
EDCS-13002666.summary: A funerary epitaph for Victoria, who died at 3 years and 5 months, erected by her parents.

EDCS-13002668.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the life span of Donatus.

EDCS-13002669.translation: To Iulius Oader, dearest father, in peace.
EDCS-13002669.summary: A funerary inscription honoring a father named Iulius Oader.

EDCS-13002670.translation: The name of the martyr Calendio. The Aiutenses, who completed their vow.
EDCS-13002670.summary: A dedication possibly related to a martyr, made by the Aiutenses.

EDCS-13002672.translation: Gaius Julius Secundus, priest of Saturn, willingly paid his vow to Saturn with good will.
EDCS-13002672.summary: A dedication by Gaius Julius Secundus, priest of Saturn, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-13002673.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Corgra lived 61 years.
EDCS-13002673.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the life span of Corgra, dedicated to the departed spirits.

EDCS-13002674.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Felicia Saturnina lived 52 years. Sulpicius Severus, a dutiful husband, made this.
EDCS-13002674.summary: A funerary epitaph for Felicia Saturnina, made by her husband Sulpicius Severus.

EDCS-13002675.translation: To the revered Mother Goddesses. Quintus T Politicus made statues of the gods, five in number, of the Masidenes and Thililua and Sugganis and Iesdanis and Masiddice, and a temple from the foundations with his own money, costing 8,000 sesterces. He also dedicated it when the matter was overseen and the interested parties were present, with all his people, and willingly fulfilled his vow with good will.
EDCS-13002675.summary: A dedication by Quintus T Politicus, who funded the construction and dedication of a temple and statues of deities at considerable expense.

EDCS-13002676.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. He lived 85 years. Saturninus the priest: if anyone could observe [this], not drinking wine for 38 years and seven months, he himself could be a priest.
EDCS-13002676.summary: A funerary epitaph for Saturninus, a priest, which also includes a curious testament regarding his vow of abstinence from wine.

EDCS-13002677.translation: Table of the presbyter SIDI ATIS
EDCS-13002677.summary: An inscription possibly referring to a table belonging to a Christian presbyter named SIDI ATIS.

EDCS-13002678.summary: This is a funerary inscription commemorating Flavius Cantus, likely indicating a table or tomb associated with him.

EDCS-13002679.translation: Saturninus, son of Baliathon, fulfilled his vow to Mercury Augustus.
EDCS-13002679.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Mercury Augustus by Saturninus, son of Baliathon.

EDCS-13002680.translation: Flamonius Proculus, son of Flamoni, erected this temple...
EDCS-13002680.summary: This is a building inscription indicating that Flamonius Proculus, son of Flamoni, erected a temple.

EDCS-13002682.summary: This is a dedication, likely funerary, to Castrus Crescentius.

EDCS-13002683.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Dead. Aiia Amata lived 75 years. May you rest well here.
EDCS-13002683.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Aiia Amata, who lived 75 years.

EDCS-13002684.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Dead. Amerinus lived 7 years. May your bones rest well here.
EDCS-13002684.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Amerinus, who lived 7 years.

EDCS-13002685.translation: Marcus Antistius Faustus lived 40 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-13002685.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcus Antistius Faustus, who lived 40 years.

EDCS-13002686.translation: The son of Aris Cornelius Capito lived 60 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-13002686.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for the son of Aris Cornelius Capito, who lived 60 years.

EDCS-13002687.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Dead. Quintus Arrius Castus, pious, lived 50 years. May your bones rest well. Sacred to the Spirits of the Dead. Cottia Birihut, pious, lived...
EDCS-13002687.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the ages of Quintus Arrius Castus (50 years) and Cottia Birihut.

EDCS-13002688.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Dead. Aurelius Barigbal, pious, lived 13 years. May your bones rest well here.
EDCS-13002688.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Aurelius Barigbal, who lived 13 years.

EDCS-13002689.summary: A tombstone inscription honoring Aurelius Actus, noting his dutiful nature.

EDCS-13002690.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Publius Aurelius Postumus, dutiful, lived for 30 years. May your bones rest well. Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Marcus Aurelius Clodianus, dutiful, lived [some years]. May your bones rest well.
EDCS-13002690.summary: A funerary inscription recording the ages of Publius Aurelius Postumus and Marcus Aurelius Clodianus, with wishes for their repose.

EDCS-13002691.translation: Capito, son of Arinis, dutiful, lived for 65 years. He is buried here. May your bones rest well.
EDCS-13002691.summary: A tombstone inscription for Capito, son of Arinis, stating his age at death and his burial place.

EDCS-13002692.summary: A tombstone inscription recording the name and age of Aulus Cornelius.

EDCS-13002693.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Cornelia Saturnina, dutiful, lived for 73 years. Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Cornelius Baricbal, dutiful, lived for 85 years.
EDCS-13002693.summary: A funerary inscription recording the ages at death of Cornelia Saturnina and Cornelius Baricbal.

EDCS-13002694.translation: Cornelius Gallicanus, dutiful, lived for 17 years.
EDCS-13002694.summary: A tombstone inscription stating the name and age of Cornelius Gallicanus.

EDCS-13002695.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Cornelius Faustus, dutiful.
EDCS-13002695.summary: A funerary inscription dedicated to Cornelius Faustus.

EDCS-13002696.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Cornelius, dutiful, lived for 95 years. May your bones rest well. Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Lucius Cornelius Privatus, dutiful, lived for 40 years. May your bones rest well.
EDCS-13002696.summary: A funerary inscription recording the ages of Cornelius and Lucius Cornelius Privatus, with wishes for their repose.

EDCS-13002697.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Quintus Cornelius, son Victorinus, lived [some years]. He is buried here. May your bones rest well.
EDCS-13002697.summary: A funerary inscription for Quintus Cornelius, son Victorinus, noting his burial place and age at death.

EDCS-13002698.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Cornelia Victoria, dutiful, lived for 61 years. May the earth rest lightly upon you.
EDCS-13002698.summary: A funerary inscription for Cornelia Victoria, stating her age at death and wishing her peaceful rest.

EDCS-13002699.translation: Curiatius Festus Tabonianus, dutiful, lived 57 years. May your bones rest well.
