EDCS-13003238.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Dead. Quintus Messius TIR ntius lived [---]. Aurelia Honorata lived 41 years. Messius Memorius lived 16 years. Messius Felix lived 22 years. She is placed here.
EDCS-13003238.summary: This funerary inscription records the ages at death of Aurelia Honorata, Messius Memorius, and Messius Felix, and likely Quintus Messius TIR ntius.

EDCS-13003239.translation: Malius Silvanus lived 85 years. He is placed here.
EDCS-13003239.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Malius Silvanus, recording his age at death and indicating his burial.

EDCS-13003242.summary: This inscription records the monument belonging to Caius Iulius Felix.

EDCS-13003243.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Primus Floras, son, recording his age at death.

EDCS-13003244.translation: [---]ius placed [it] for himself and his [family]. [He/She] lived 65 years. [She] is placed here. Potestas, the devoted mother, lived 70 years. Aris, the devoted mother, lived [---]. She is placed here.
EDCS-13003244.summary: This is a complex funerary inscription indicating a monument set up by an individual for their family, with ages at death provided for Potestas and Aris, who are identified as mothers.

EDCS-13003245.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Quintus Manilius Torquatus lived 55 years.
EDCS-13003245.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Quintus Manilius Torquatus, who lived 55 years.

EDCS-13003246.translation: Sisoi, daughter of Selsumis, lived 45 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-13003246.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Sisoi, daughter of Selsumis, who lived 45 years.

EDCS-13003247.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Sitius Fundanus lived 25 years. Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Claudia Matrona lived 64 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-13003247.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Sitius Fundanus (25 years) and Claudia Matrona (64 years), who is buried here.

EDCS-13003248.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. C. Marcus Sthabilius Fortunatus lived [---] years.
EDCS-13003248.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Marcus Sthabilius Fortunatus, with an incomplete record of his age.

EDCS-13003249.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Marcus T. R. Pius. Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Marcus T. Esopus Pius lived 80 years. Lived 70 years. Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. T. R. lived 75 years. Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Didia Maxima, devout, lived 60 years.
EDCS-13003249.summary: This inscription is a collection of funerary notices for Marcus T. R. Pius, Marcus T. Esopus Pius (80 years), T. R. (75 years), and Didia Maxima (60 years).

EDCS-13003250.translation: Titulla, daughter of Baricis, lived 1 year.
EDCS-13003250.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Titulla, daughter of Baricis, who died at the age of 1 year.

EDCS-13003252.summary: This funerary inscription records that Tullianus, who lived 70 years, was devout.

EDCS-13003257.translation: Here is the memoria of Pristinus Altaris.
EDCS-13003257.summary: This inscription marks the memoria, or tomb, of Pristinus Altaris.

EDCS-13003604.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Marcus Govines lived 25 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-13003604.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Marcus Govines, who lived 25 years.

EDCS-13003647.summary: This inscription is a dedication to an individual named Flavius, referred to as 'our lord'.

EDCS-13003649.translation: Quintus Furius Maximus gladly paid his vow to Saturn.
EDCS-13003649.summary: This is a votive inscription by Quintus Furius Maximus to the god Saturn.

EDCS-13003650.summary: This inscription identifies two individuals, Dativus and his wife, as shepherds.

EDCS-13003651.translation: S. Sentius S. gladly paid his vow; Donatus, from the region of the Cri(spian)i.
EDCS-13003651.summary: This is a votive inscription by S. Sentius S., with a note about the dedicator Donatus.

EDCS-13003655.text_edition: \n Caius Iulius Cai filius Quirina Lugudunolus Augustiduno sic centuria Valeri Fidelis vixit annis LV militavit annis XXII heres eius Statutus Popius Saturninus centuria eadem libens merito titulum consecravit\n
EDCS-13003655.translation: Caius Iulius Lugudunolus, son of Caius, of the Quirina tribe, from Augustidunum, of the century of Valerius Fidelis, lived 55 years and served 22 years. His heir, Statutus Popius Saturninus, of the same century, lovingly and deservedly dedicated this monument.
EDCS-13003655.summary: A tombstone erected by an heir for Caius Iulius Lugudunolus, a soldier who lived 55 years and served 22 years.

EDCS-13003656.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Marcus Iulius Statianus, a veteran who served in Pannonia in the First Auxiliary legion, who was apprehended(?), aged 25, was placed here; his heir Iulia Secura made this.
EDCS-13003656.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Marcus Iulius Statianus, a veteran, set up by his daughter Iulia Secura.

EDCS-13003657.text_edition: \n Quintus Lutatius Quinti filius Quirina Viator Autrico miles legionis III Augustae centuria Plaetori vixit annos XXV militavit annos III Titus Flavius centuria Nasidi et Caius Iulius centuria Bruttieni heredes monumentum posuerunt\n
EDCS-13003657.translation: Quintus Lutatius Viator, son of Quintus, of the Quirina tribe, from Autricum, soldier of the III Augusta legion, century of Plaetorius, lived 25 years and served 3 years. Titus Flavius of the century of Nasidius and Caius Iulius of the century of Bruttienus, his heirs, erected this monument.
EDCS-13003657.summary: A tombstone erected by the heirs Titus Flavius and Caius Iulius for Quintus Lutatius Viator, a soldier who lived 25 years and served 3 years.

EDCS-13003658.translation: [...]ius Martialis, veteran of the III Augusta legion, lived 90 years. He rests here.
EDCS-13003658.summary: A funerary epitaph for Martialis, a veteran of the III Augusta legion, who died at the age of 90.

EDCS-13003659.text_edition: \n Sextus Sulpicius Sexti filius Quirina Senilis miles legionis III Augustae centuria Caesoni beneficiarius Tetti Iuliani et Iavoleni Prisci legatorum Augusti vixit annos XXV militavit nnos VI hic situs est Marcus Aurelius Candidus |(centurio) legionis III Augustae heres eius posuit\n
EDCS-13003659.translation: Sextus Sulpicius Senilis, son of Sextus, of the Quirina tribe, soldier of the III Augusta legion, century of Caesoni, beneficiary of the legates of Augustus Tettius Iulianus and Iavolenus Priscus, lived 25 years and served 6 years. Marcus Aurelius Candidus, a centurion of the III Augusta legion, his heir, erected this.
EDCS-13003659.summary: A tombstone erected by Marcus Aurelius Candidus for Sextus Sulpicius Senilis, a soldier and beneficiary, who lived 25 years and served 6 years.

EDCS-13003661.translation: A knight from the ala [of ...], erected by will.
EDCS-13003661.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording a soldier of the cavalry, likely dating to the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-13003662.translation: Vita[lis ...], veteran, lived 80 years. [Family name?]ria MA [erected/dedicated?] this monument; [responsible person?] curavit.
EDCS-13003662.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a veteran named Vitalis who lived to be 80 years old, likely from the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-13003663.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Adaucta lived 21 years. [Date?] XV [erected?].
EDCS-13003663.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a woman named Adaucta who died at the age of 21, likely from the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-13003664.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Titus Aelius Princeps, freedman of the Emperor Augustus, lived 77 years; he lies here. Martialis [erected/dedicated].
EDCS-13003664.summary: This funerary inscription honors Titus Aelius Princeps, a freedman of Emperor Augustus, who lived to be 77, and was set up by Martialis, likely from the 2nd-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-13003665.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Aemilia Marcella, daughter of [VI?], made this.
EDCS-13003665.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Aemilia Marcella, made by her father, dating to the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-13003666.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription recording a dedication made by Aemilia.

EDCS-13003667.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Appius Maximu(s) Saturninus lived 30 years. Gaius Lucius Appius Saturninus made this for his dearest brother; he lies here.
EDCS-13003667.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Appius Maximu(s) Saturninus, who died at 30, and was honored by his brother, likely from the 2nd-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-13003668.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Aponia Polla lived 35 years; she lies here. Cornelius Saturninus made this for his dearest wife.
EDCS-13003668.summary: This funerary inscription records Aponia Polla, who died at 35, and was honored by her husband, Cornelius Saturninus, likely from the 2nd-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-13003669.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Butis made this for her dearest husband. Paris lived 10 years; he lies here.
EDCS-13003669.summary: This funerary inscription honors Butis's husband, Paris, who died at 10 years old, likely from the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-13003671.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus Caecilius Felicior lived 55 years. Caecilius Nundinarius made this for his brother.
EDCS-13003671.summary: This funerary inscription records Quintus Caecilius Felicior, who lived 55 years, and was honored by his brother, likely from the 2nd-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-13003672.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. [Name?] Caecilius Gaetulicus, also known as Pistor, lived 24 years and 9 months. Lucius Caecilius Gaetulus (father) and Caecilia Spesina (mother) made this for their most dutiful son; he lies here.
EDCS-13003672.summary: This funerary inscription records Caecilius Gaetulicus (Pistor), who died at age 24 years and 9 months, honored by his parents, likely from the 2nd-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-13003673.translation: To the departed spirits. Gaius Caecilius Thevestinus lived 52 years. His father made this for his dearest son. [He was] well, happy, and strong.
EDCS-13003673.summary: A funerary inscription for Gaius Caecilius Thevestinus, who lived 52 years, dedicated by his father.

EDCS-13003674.translation: To the departed spirits. Caecilia Cinitia lived 51 years. Caecilius Fortunatus made this monument for his freedwoman and dearest wife. She is buried here.
EDCS-13003674.summary: A funerary inscription recording the life of Caecilia Cinitia (51 years) and stating that Caecilius Fortunatus erected this monument for her as his freedwoman and wife.

EDCS-13003675.translation: To the departed spirits. Caecilia Fortunata lived 42 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-13003675.summary: A funerary inscription for Caecilia Fortunata, who lived 42 years.

EDCS-13003676.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Rutilia Crispilla lived 40 years. Her...
EDCS-13003676.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Rutilia Crispilla, who lived 40 years.

EDCS-13003677.translation: To the departed spirits. Lucius Iulius Octavus lived forty years. His wife Tevestina dedicated this.
EDCS-13003677.summary: A funerary inscription for Lucius Iulius Octavus, who lived 40 years, dedicated by his wife Tevestina.

EDCS-13003678.translation: Marcus Egnatius Vindex, son of Marcus, lived.
EDCS-13003678.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the life of Marcus Egnatius Vindex.

EDCS-13003679.summary: A fragmentary inscription recording a soldier of a Roman legion, with his name partially restored.

EDCS-13003680.translation: To the departed spirits. Erucius lived 13 years.
EDCS-13003680.summary: A fragmentary funerary inscription for Erucius, who lived 13 years.

EDCS-13003682.translation: To the departed spirits. Felix lived 14 years, 5 months, and 19 days. Lixestinus made this for his dearest son.
EDCS-13003682.summary: A funerary inscription for Felix, who lived 14 years, 5 months, and 19 days, dedicated by his father Lixestinus.

EDCS-13003683.translation: To the departed spirits. Flavia Aeregia lived 31 years and 8 months. She is buried here. Gaius Caecilius Cinnas made this for his dearest wife.
EDCS-13003683.summary: A funerary inscription for Flavia Aeregia, who lived 31 years and 8 months, erected by her husband Gaius Caecilius Cinnas.

EDCS-13003684.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the life of Caius Iulius Fortunatus.

EDCS-13003685.translation: To the departed spirits. Quintus Helvius Saturninus, dutiful, lived 50 years. He is buried here. All his sons took care to have this made by Cornelius Optatus.
EDCS-13003685.summary: A funerary inscription for Quintus Helvius Saturninus, who lived 50 years, arranged by his sons and executed by Cornelius Optatus.

EDCS-13003689.translation: To the departed spirits. Gaius Iulius Fortunatianus lived 17 years and 25 days, 8 hours, after his pious mother Fabia Fortunata, who lived 3 years, 6 months, and 21 days, [and] 1 hour. He is buried here.
EDCS-13003689.summary: A funerary inscription for Gaius Iulius Fortunatianus, who lived 17 years and 25 days, and his mother Fabia Fortunata, who lived 3 years, 6 months, and 21 days.

EDCS-13003690.translation: To the departed gods. Gaius Julius Ianvarius lived 40 years. Prima, his wife, made this.
EDCS-13003690.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Gaius Julius Ianvarius, erected by his wife Prima.

EDCS-13003691.translation: Iulia Mese lived 28 years; she is buried here. Annius Felix made this for his dearest wife.
EDCS-13003691.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Iulia Mese, set up by her husband Annius Felix.

EDCS-13003692.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum ut merito in his titulis merenti et generositati suae in sepulcro et extremo loco sit Iulia Perna\n
EDCS-13003692.translation: To the departed gods. So that Iulia Perna may rightfully have a burial place and a final resting spot in these inscriptions, deserving of her nobility.
EDCS-13003692.summary: A funerary inscription intended for Iulia Perna, emphasizing her noble status and right to burial.

EDCS-13003693.translation: To the departed gods. Marcus Iunius Victor lived 80 years. Ianuaria made this for her husband. He is buried here.
EDCS-13003693.summary: A funerary epitaph for Marcus Iunius Victor, erected by his wife Ianuaria, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13003694.translation: To the departed gods. Iunia Optatula lived 35 years. Herennia Ianuaria made this for her daughter. She is buried here.
EDCS-13003694.summary: A funerary inscription for Iunia Optatula, erected by her mother Herennia Ianuaria.

EDCS-13003695.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Lavinia lived 50 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-13003695.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lavinia, who lived 50 years.

EDCS-13003696.translation: To the departed gods. Megatia lived 22 years.
EDCS-13003696.summary: A brief funerary epitaph recording the death of Megatia at the age of 22.

EDCS-13003697.translation: Ronia Quarta had this made for her dearest husband; he is buried here.
EDCS-13003697.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by a wife for her husband, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13003698.translation: To the departed gods. Sada made this. Valeria Quarta lived 30 years.
EDCS-13003698.summary: A funerary inscription recording the death of Valeria Quarta, possibly erected by a person named Sada.

EDCS-13003700.translation: To the departed gods. Sittia Gemellina lived 21 years. Nutrius Ianvarius, her devoted husband, made this. She is buried here.
EDCS-13003700.summary: A funerary epitaph for Sittia Gemellina, erected by her husband Nutrius Ianvarius.

EDCS-13003701.translation: To the departed gods. Vaberius Victor(?)...
EDCS-13003701.summary: A fragment of a funerary inscription, possibly for Vaberius Victor.

EDCS-13003702.translation: To the departed gods. Gaius Valerius Valerianus lived 60 years. Valerius Valens made this for his dearest father. He is buried here. D().
EDCS-13003702.summary: A funerary epitaph for Gaius Valerius Valerianus, erected by his son Valerius Valens.

EDCS-13003703.translation: To the departed gods. Velleia Respecta lived 50 years. She is buried here. Novellianus, her son, made this for his devoted mother.
EDCS-13003703.summary: A funerary epitaph for Velleia Respecta, erected by her son Novellianus.

EDCS-13003704.translation: To the departed spirits. Gaius Vibius Celer lived 20 years. He rests here. Gaius Vibius Novellus made this for his brother, with devotion.
EDCS-13003704.summary: A tombstone recording the death of Gaius Vibius Celer, erected by his brother Gaius Vibius Novellus, likely from the imperial period.

EDCS-13003705.translation: To the departed spirits. Quintus Lutatius Victor lived 60 years.
EDCS-13003705.summary: A tombstone recording the death of Quintus Lutatius Victor, likely from the imperial period.

EDCS-13003706.translation: To the departed spirits. Cotisa(?) lived 21 years. To the departed spirits. Victoria lived 20 years.
EDCS-13003706.summary: A tombstone with two inscriptions, recording the deaths of Cotisa(?) and Victoria, likely from the imperial period.

EDCS-13003707.translation: To the departed spirits. Umbria Victorina lived 35 years. She rests here. Umbrius Adventus made this for his dearest mother.
EDCS-13003707.summary: A tombstone recording the death of Umbria Victorina, erected by her son Umbrius Adventus, likely from the imperial period.

EDCS-13003708.translation: I have escaped, I have fled. Farewell, Hope and Fortune; I have nothing to do with you. Deceive others.
EDCS-13003708.summary: This is a defiant epitaph of an individual who has escaped their fate, possibly from the late Roman Empire.

EDCS-13003709.translation: Iuliana Minor lived for one year.
EDCS-13003709.summary: This is a very brief funerary epitaph recording the short life of a child, Iuliana Minor, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13003716.translation: Privata lived for 13 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-13003716.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the age at death of a female named Privata, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13003717.translation: Victoria, devoted to chastity, live in God.
EDCS-13003717.summary: This is a Christian epitaph for Victoria, a consecrated virgin, likely from the 4th-5th century CE.

EDCS-13003718.translation: Here lies Martiliana, a virgin consecrated to God, laid to rest on the 2nd day before the Kalends of January.
EDCS-13003718.summary: This is a Christian funerary inscription for Martiliana, a consecrated virgin, dated to December 31st, likely from the 4th-5th century CE.

EDCS-13003720.translation: Here lies Axido, who lived for 14 years and then rested in peace, interred on the 16th day before the Kalends of July, in the second indiction.
EDCS-13003720.summary: This is a Christian funerary inscription for Axido, who died at the age of 14, dated to June 16th, likely from the 4th-6th century CE based on the indiction.

EDCS-13003721.translation: Here lies Nonnus of good memory, who lived for 5 years and ten months, interred on the 12th day before the Kalends of August.
EDCS-13003721.summary: This is a Christian funerary inscription for Nonnus, who died at the age of 5 years and 10 months, dated to July 21st, likely from the 4th-6th century CE.

EDCS-13003722.translation: Petronia lived for four years and 16 days in peace.
EDCS-13003722.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the precise age of a child, Petronia, who died at just over four years old, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13003727.translation: Florida, rare in faith, [received into] the grace of God [in the castle] for 7 months and 2 days and 7 days.
EDCS-13003727.summary: This is a fragmented Christian epitaph for Florida, likely recording her death at a young age, possibly from the late Roman period.

EDCS-13003729.translation: To the departed spirits. Marcus Annius Seranus, son of Marcus, of the Papiria tribe, lived 18 years, 11 months, and 12 days. He rests here.
EDCS-13003729.summary: A tombstone recording the death of Marcus Annius Seranus, including detailed age at death, likely from the imperial period.

EDCS-13003730.translation: Gaius Helvius Victor, a veteran, served for 25 years, lived for 56 years.
EDCS-13003730.summary: This is a tombstone recording the life span and military service of a veteran named Gaius Helvius Victor.

EDCS-13003732.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Cosconius Romuleanus (son of) M. lived 25 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-13003732.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Cosconius Romuleanus at the age of 25.

EDCS-13003736.summary: An inscription dedicating something to the god Saturn Augustus, possibly from a public or private shrine, date uncertain but likely imperial period.

EDCS-13003737.translation: Petronius placed (this) with his family. To the Divine Shades.
EDCS-13003737.summary: This brief funerary inscription indicates that Petronius established a monument for himself and his family.

EDCS-13003739.translation: Publius Aurelius Restitutus, son of Marcus, of the Horatia tribe, pious, lived 25 years.
EDCS-13003739.summary: This epitaph records the life span of Publius Aurelius Restitutus, noting his tribal affiliation and piety.

EDCS-13003740.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades for Lucius Fabio Primo, (my) father.
EDCS-13003740.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by an unnamed individual to their father, Lucius Fabio Primo.

EDCS-13003744.translation: Sacred to the august Genius of Thesectus. Maximus, servant of the most distinguished man Annius Percennianus, fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-13003744.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by Maximus, a servant of Annius Percennianus, to the Genius of Thesectus.

EDCS-13003745.translation: Publius Aelius Priscus Magifianus, pious, lived 80 years. His son made and dedicated this monument.
EDCS-13003745.summary: This tombstone records the death of Publius Aelius Priscus Magifianus at the age of 80, with the monument erected by his son.

EDCS-13003746.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Gaius Aelius Iuvenis lived 70 years. His sons made and dedicated this monument.
EDCS-13003746.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Gaius Aelius Iuvenis at the age of 70, with the monument erected by his sons.

EDCS-13003751.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Ulpia Fortunata lived for...
EDCS-13003751.summary: This incomplete funerary inscription records the name Ulpia Fortunata and her age, which is missing.

EDCS-13003752.summary: This brief inscription serves as a memorial for a person named Secunda.

EDCS-13003753.translation: For Alexander, our lord Augustus, for his health and that of [---], the distinguished men of Vesates, under the care of Felix, made this with good intentions.
EDCS-13003753.summary: This is a dedication made by the citizens of Vesates for the health of Emperor Alexander, likely in the 3rd century CE.

EDCS-13003754.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Concordia lived 85 years. T. H. made this for his dearest mother.
EDCS-13003754.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the age of Concordia and set up by her son, T. H., likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13003755.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Crepereia Victorina lived 70 years.
EDCS-13003755.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the age of Crepereia Victorina, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13003756.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Aelia Victoria lived 70 years. Pompeius Felix, her son, made this for his most dutiful mother. She is buried here.
EDCS-13003756.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Aelia Victoria, erected by her son Pompeius Felix, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13003759.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Gavia Maxima lived 55 years. Her heir made this.
EDCS-13003759.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Gavia Maxima, with the monument erected by her heir, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13003760.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Donatus Gabinius lived 75 years.
EDCS-13003760.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the age of Donatus Gabinius, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13003761.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Sextus Iulius Privatus lived 65 years, without any pain, without any reproach in his life. His sons made this dutifully.
EDCS-13003761.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Sextus Iulius Privatus, who lived a life free of pain and reproach, erected by his sons, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13003762.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Urbanus lived 65 years.
EDCS-13003762.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the age of Urbanus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13003763.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Pontilius lived 7 years and 9 months. The monument was made by Pontilius Tutianus and Saturninus for their dearest brother.
EDCS-13003763.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a young Pontilius, who lived 7 years and 9 months, erected by his brothers Tutianus and Saturninus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13003764.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Flavia Herennia, dutiful, lived 54 years. Iulii Herennianus Sentianus Victorinus made this for their most cherished mother. She is buried here.
EDCS-13003764.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Flavia Herennia, erected by her sons Iulii Herennianus Sentianus Victorinus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13003765.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Publius Iulius Victorinus lived 70 years. Flavia Herennia made this for her pious husband. He is buried here.
EDCS-13003765.summary: A tombstone erected by Flavia Herennia for her husband, Publius Iulius Victorinus, who lived 70 years.

EDCS-13003766.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Iulius Ianuarius, son of Caius, pious, lived 50 years. Iulius Victorinus made this for his pious brother. He is buried here.
EDCS-13003766.summary: A tombstone erected by Iulius Victorinus for his pious brother, Lucius Iulius Ianuarius, who lived 50 years.

EDCS-13003767.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Caius Iulius Probatus, son of Caius, pious, lived 48 years. Iulius Victorinus made this for his pious brother. He is buried here.
EDCS-13003767.summary: A tombstone erected by Iulius Victorinus for his pious brother, Caius Iulius Probatus, who lived 48 years.

EDCS-13003768.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulia Ingenua, daughter of Caius, pious, lived 55 years. Iulius Victorinus made this for his pious sister. She is buried here.
EDCS-13003768.summary: A tombstone erected by Iulius Victorinus for his pious sister, Iulia Ingenua, who lived 55 years.

EDCS-13003769.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Caelia Fausta lived sixteen years.
EDCS-13003769.summary: A tombstone for Caelia Fausta, who died at the age of sixteen.

EDCS-13003770.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Marci Magni Felicis lived 67 years. His son made this for his most pious father. He is buried here.
EDCS-13003770.summary: A tombstone erected by a son for his most pious father, Marci Magni Felicis, who lived 67 years.

EDCS-13003771.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Postimius Felicus lived 90 years. His son Iulianus made this.
EDCS-13003771.summary: A tombstone erected by Iulianus for his father, Postimius Felicus, who lived 90 years.

EDCS-13003772.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Aretia Secunda lived 75 years. Her son Victor made this monument for her. She is buried here.
EDCS-13003772.summary: A tombstone erected by Victor for his mother, Aretia Secunda, who lived 75 years.

EDCS-13003773.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Aelius Saxa, pious, lived 30 years. Aelius Mamon made this monument for his pious son.
EDCS-13003773.summary: A tombstone erected by Aelius Mamon for his pious son, Aelius Saxa, who lived 30 years.

EDCS-13003778.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Titus Flavius Quirina Satluc Mathacianus lived 80 years. Successus, his freedman, made this final resting place for his most pious patron. He is buried here.
EDCS-13003778.summary: A tombstone erected by Successus, a freedman, for his most pious patron, Titus Flavius Quirina Satluc Mathacianus, who lived 80 years.

EDCS-13003779.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Caelius Paulinus, his sons, have paid their due. He lived ninety years.
EDCS-13003779.summary: A funerary monument dedicated to Caelius Paulinus by his sons, who fulfilled a debt, dating to the imperial period.

EDCS-13003781.text_edition: \n Pro salute Imperatoris Caesaris Marci Aureli Antonini Augusti Armeniaci Medici Parthici maximi liberorumque eius Iuliani Bitinenses posuerunt\n
EDCS-13003781.translation: For the safety of the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus Armeniacus Medicus Parthicus Maximus and his children. The people of Bitinienses set this up.
EDCS-13003781.summary: A dedication for the well-being of Emperor Marcus Aurelius Antoninus and his children, set up by the inhabitants of Bitinienses, likely mid-2nd century CE.

EDCS-13003782.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Hateria Ianuaria lived 40 years. Cerdonius made this for his most beloved nurse.
EDCS-13003782.summary: A funerary epitaph for Hateria Ianuaria, who lived 40 years, dedicated by her nurse Cerdonius, dating to the imperial period.

EDCS-13003783.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Florus made this with his sons. He lived 75 years. He lies here.
EDCS-13003783.summary: A funerary inscription for Florus, who lived 75 years, set up by himself and his sons, dating to the imperial period.

EDCS-13003787.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Ulpius Donatus lived 28 years. His mother, Ulpia Marcella, made this memorial.
EDCS-13003787.summary: A funerary monument for Ulpius Donatus, who lived 28 years, made by his mother Ulpia Marcella, dating to the imperial period.

EDCS-13003788.translation: Hail Dativa. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Aurelia Dativa, buried here, lived [X] years.
EDCS-13003788.summary: A funerary epitaph for Aurelia Dativa, who was buried here and lived an unstated number of years, dating to the imperial period.

EDCS-13003789.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. I, Cirrus, made this. Inspect my monument. I lived 50 years.
EDCS-13003789.summary: A funerary inscription for Cirrus, who lived 50 years, indicating he made his own monument, dating to the imperial period.

EDCS-13003790.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Conductor lived 6 years and two months.
EDCS-13003790.summary: A funerary epitaph for Conductor, who lived 6 years and two months, dating to the imperial period.

EDCS-13003791.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Maria lived 41 years. Caesellius Africanus made this for his wife.
EDCS-13003791.summary: A funerary monument for Maria, who lived 41 years, dedicated by her husband Caesellius Africanus, dating to the imperial period.

EDCS-13003792.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Maten lived one year, six months, and six days. Atilius made this for his son.
EDCS-13003792.summary: A funerary epitaph for Maten, who lived one year, six months, and six days, dedicated by his father Atilius, dating to the imperial period.

EDCS-13003793.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Quintus Sabinus lies here. He lived 91 years. His sons made this.
EDCS-13003793.summary: A funerary monument for Quintus Sabinus, who lived 91 years, erected by his sons, dating to the imperial period.

EDCS-13003794.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Urbana lived 88 years. Her son made this tomb for his mother.
EDCS-13003794.summary: A funerary inscription recording the death of Urbana, set up by her son, likely from the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-13003795.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Datus lived 65 years and [name illegible] lived... for a dutiful father and mother.
EDCS-13003795.summary: A funerary inscription mentioning individuals named Datus and others, possibly for a father and mother, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13003796.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus Caecilius Paulus lived 85 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-13003796.summary: A funerary inscription recording the death of Quintus Caecilius Paulus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13003797.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Ianuarianus lived 80 years [illegible text].
EDCS-13003797.summary: A funerary inscription recording the death of Ianuarianus, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13003799.summary: A dedication to the goddess Venus and a person named Rufina, purpose unknown, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-13003800.translation: We bought and built. Cassianus and Victor for his father Renovatus, who had passed away.
EDCS-13003800.summary: A funerary inscription by Cassianus and Victor for their father Renovatus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13003801.translation: To the departed spirits. Flavius Vindex lived 80 years. He rests here.
EDCS-13003801.summary: A tombstone recording the death of Flavius Vindex, likely from the imperial period.

EDCS-13003802.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Vitellia Ianuaria lived 90 years. Her sons Cinitius and Secundus made this.
EDCS-13003802.summary: A funerary inscription for Vitellia Ianuaria, set up by her sons Cinitius and Secundus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13003803.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Caius Iulius Felix Pulex, perpetual flamen, made this for himself and for his wife Aurelia Victoria and their descendants. He lived as many years as he could; the remainder he spent [illegible].
EDCS-13003803.summary: A funerary inscription and self-dedication by Caius Iulius Felix Pulex, a perpetual flamen, for himself, his wife Aurelia Victoria, and descendants, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13003804.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Camerius Datus lived 60 years. His wife Rustica made this.
EDCS-13003804.summary: A funerary inscription for Camerius Datus, set up by his wife Rustica, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13003805.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Flavia Ianuaria lived 21 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-13003805.summary: A funerary inscription recording the death of Flavia Ianuaria, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13003806.translation: To the departed spirits. Iulius Ianuarius lived 36 years.
EDCS-13003806.summary: A tombstone recording the death of Iulius Ianuarius, likely from the imperial period.

EDCS-13003807.translation: To the departed spirits. Iulius Mamari lived 26 years.
EDCS-13003807.summary: A tombstone recording the death of Iulius Mamari, likely from the imperial period.

EDCS-13003808.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulia Saturnina lived 70 years.
EDCS-13003808.summary: This is a tombstone for Iulia Saturnina, recording her name and age at death, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13003809.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Olia Rustica lived 71 years, 10 months, and 11 days; she lies here.
EDCS-13003809.summary: This is a tombstone for Olia Rustica, recording her name, lifespan, and burial, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13003810.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Popilia Secunda lived 45 years.
EDCS-13003810.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the age of the deceased, Popilia Secunda.

EDCS-13003811.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Boroct, the priest.
EDCS-13003811.summary: A funerary inscription identifying Boroct as a priest and dedicating the monument to the spirits of the departed.

EDCS-13003812.translation: Donatus [set up this monument for] Agrudana, [who lived] 44 years.
EDCS-13003812.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the age of Agrudana, likely set up by Donatus.

EDCS-13003813.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Victorinius, son of Gentia Tertulla, made this monument for his mother, who lived 80 years.
EDCS-13003813.summary: A funerary epitaph where Victorinius commemorates his mother, Gentia Tertulla, and notes her age.

EDCS-13003814.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Galla Cliana lived 13 years, 1 month. Her parents set [this up].
EDCS-13003814.summary: A funerary epitaph by parents for their daughter Galla Cliana, recording her age and the monument's erection.

EDCS-13003815.translation: Saturnina, wife of Zamensis, lived 65 years. Victorinna Zamensis lived 70 years.
EDCS-13003815.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the ages of two women, Saturnina and Victorinna, likely related.

EDCS-13003820.summary: An inscription identifying Titus Clodius Fortunatus as a priest, possibly on a monument or honorary base.

EDCS-13003822.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Datiana lived 85 years.
EDCS-13003822.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the age of the deceased, Datiana.

EDCS-13003823.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Flavia Eutuchia lived 52 years, 10 months, 9 days. Flavius Demetrius [set this up] for his sweetest wife.
EDCS-13003823.summary: A funerary epitaph by Flavius Demetrius for his wife Flavia Eutuchia, recording her age and the monument's dedication.

EDCS-13003824.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. For Gemellae, daughter, who lived 6 years, 2 months. Her parents made [this].
EDCS-13003824.summary: A funerary epitaph by parents for their young daughter Gemellae, recording her age and the monument's erection.

EDCS-13003825.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Opimianus and Augurinus for their most sweet and dutiful mother Flavia Sozusa, who lived 80 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-13003825.summary: A funerary epitaph for Flavia Sozusa, set up by her children Opimianus and Augurinus, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13003826.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Palustris, who lived 105 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-13003826.summary: A funerary epitaph for Palustris, recording his exceptionally long life and burial, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13003827.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Publius Octavius Marinus, who lived 70 years. He is buried here. His dutiful sons made this.
EDCS-13003827.summary: A funerary epitaph for Publius Octavius Marinus, erected by his sons, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13003828.translation: Zosima, servant of Caesar Augustus, daughter of Felicio, who lived [---] years. She is buried here.
EDCS-13003828.summary: A funerary epitaph for Zosima, a freedwoman of the imperial household, recording her age and parentage, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13003830.translation: Sacred to the Great Mother of the Gods. Euphrates, procurator of the province, built the temple with statues and a portico at his own expense and also dedicated it.
EDCS-13003830.summary: A dedication by Euphrates, a provincial procurator, of a temple complex to the Great Mother of the Gods, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13003831.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Caius Aurelius Saturninus, veteran, who lived 60 years. He is buried here. Iulia Aurelia made this for her most rare husband.
EDCS-13003831.summary: A funerary epitaph for Caius Aurelius Saturninus, a veteran, erected by his wife Iulia Aurelia, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13003832.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Titus Flavius Nundinarius, veteran, made this for his granddaughter Pet Nundinaria, who lived 3 years and 5 months. She is buried here.
EDCS-13003832.summary: A funerary epitaph for the young Pet Nundinaria, erected by her grandfather Titus Flavius Nundinarius, a veteran, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13003833.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Titus Statilius Viator, son of Titus, dutiful, who lived 70 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-13003833.summary: A funerary epitaph for Titus Statilius Viator, recording his filial piety and age, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13003838.summary: A votive inscription recording the fulfillment of a vow by Tutia Bonosa, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13003840.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Innocens Aemilianus, who died on the 8th day before the Kalends of April, lived eight months and thirteen days.
EDCS-13003840.summary: A funerary epitaph for Innocens Aemilianus, detailing his premature death and age, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13003841.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Lucius Pontius Iahin lived 59 years, 3 months, 20 days. Lucius Pontius Silunus, his son, made this.
EDCS-13003841.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the life and maker of Lucius Pontius Iahin, made by his son.

EDCS-13003843.translation: Honorata lived well for 48 years, buried on the 4th day before the Kalends of May in the 7th year.
EDCS-13003843.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan and burial date of Honorata.

EDCS-13003844.translation: To my most sweet daughter Flabana. Her father made this. She lived 4 years, 12 months, 17 days, 7 hours.
EDCS-13003844.summary: A funerary epitaph for a young girl named Flabana, made by her father.

EDCS-13003846.translation: Table of Donatilla, a girl. She lived in peace for 13 years, 9 months.
EDCS-13003846.summary: A funerary epitaph for a young girl named Donatilla, recording her lifespan.

EDCS-13003847.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Ulpius Donot lived 65 years. His wife made this. Ulpius Donatus lived 25 years, his son, is buried here.
EDCS-13003847.summary: A funerary epitaph for Ulpius Donot, made by his wife, and also mentioning his son Ulpius Donatus.

EDCS-13003848.translation: [...] lived 70 years. Caius Ulpius Gustatus made this.
EDCS-13003848.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of an unnamed individual and made by Caius Ulpius Gustatus.

EDCS-13003849.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Octavia Celsina lived 60 years. Secundus placed this for his wife.
EDCS-13003849.summary: A funerary epitaph for Octavia Celsina, placed by her husband Secundus.

EDCS-13003850.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Attius Rogatus the pious lived 8 years. May your bones rest well.
EDCS-13003850.summary: A funerary epitaph for a child named Attius Rogatus, expressing a wish for his repose.

EDCS-13003851.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Herennia Matronica the pious lived 15 years. May your bones rest well. May the earth be light upon you.
EDCS-13003851.summary: A funerary epitaph for Herennia Matronica, expressing wishes for her repose and a light burial.

EDCS-13003852.translation: Iulia Fortunata the pious lived 60 years.
EDCS-13003852.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Iulia Fortunata.

EDCS-13003853.translation: Occius Martialis, son of Macrinus, pious, lived 18 years, is buried here.
EDCS-13003853.summary: This is a tombstone recording the life and death of Occius Martialis, who lived for 18 years.

EDCS-13003854.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Octavius Pinna, pious, lived 65 years, is buried here.
EDCS-13003854.summary: This is a tombstone dedicated to the Manes, recording the death of Octavius Pinna, who lived for 65 years.

EDCS-13003855.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Paccius Sextus lived 3 years.
EDCS-13003855.summary: This tombstone is dedicated to the Manes and records the death of Paccius Sextus, who lived for 3 years.

EDCS-13003857.translation: Valeria Luperca, pious, lived 70 years, is buried here.
EDCS-13003857.summary: This is a tombstone recording the life and death of Valeria Luperca, who lived for 70 years.

EDCS-13003858.translation: Valeria Secunda, daughter of Pacatus, pious, lived 45 years, is buried here.
EDCS-13003858.summary: This is a tombstone recording the life and death of Valeria Secunda, daughter of Pacatus, who lived for 45 years.

EDCS-13003861.translation: O.M. lived 65 years, may your bones rest well, may the earth be light upon you, from the time of the 6th consulship of the Emperor and 6th consulship of the Father of the Fatherland. Caius Pomponius Rufus Acilius, son.
EDCS-13003861.summary: This tombstone, likely from the late Roman Empire, records the death of Caius Pomponius Rufus Acilius after living 65 years and includes a wish for his peaceful repose.

EDCS-13003863.translation: Constantinus and Constantius, most noble and most blessed Caesars, after an honorable discharge from the rank of centurion, [built?] the baths for 400,000 sesterces.
EDCS-13003863.summary: This inscription records that the Emperors Constantinus and Constantius financed the construction of baths for 400,000 sesterces after a centurion's honorable discharge, likely from the 4th century CE.

EDCS-13003864.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Lucius Botarius Felix Ianuarianus, pious, lived 8 years and 14 days, is buried here.
EDCS-13003864.summary: This tombstone dedicated to the Manes records the short life of Lucius Botarius Felix Ianuarianus, who lived for 8 years and 14 days.

EDCS-13003865.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Modia Quarta, pious, lived 65 years. Sacred to the spirits of the underworld.
EDCS-13003865.summary: This tombstone, dedicated to the Manes, records the death of Modia Quarta, who lived for 65 years.

EDCS-13003866.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Prima, daughter of Zabonis, lived 35 years, is buried here. Marcus Namphamonis, son of Rogatus, lived 50 years, is buried here. Marcus Laelius Martialis, the heir, for the dearest.
EDCS-13003866.summary: This tombstone records the deaths of Prima and Marcus Namphamonis, with Marcus Laelius Martialis acting as the heir, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13003867.translation: Sacred to Neptune Augustus. Flavius Emeritianus, his priest, gladly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-13003867.summary: A vow fulfilled to Neptune by a priest named Flavius Emeritianus.

EDCS-13003868.text_edition: \n Ex auctoritate Imperatoris Nervae Traiani Caesaris Augusti Germanici Dacici consulis VI imperatoris XIII Lucius Acilius Strabo Clodius Nummus legatus Augusti pro praetore inter Musulamios et Madaurenses\n
EDCS-13003868.translation: By the authority of the Emperor Nerva Traianus Caesar Augustus Germanicus Dacicus, consul for the 6th time, Imperator for the 13th time. Lucius Acilius Strabo Clodius Nummus, imperial legate with praetorian power, between the Musulamii and Madaurenses.
EDCS-13003868.summary: This inscription records an official act by the legate Lucius Acilius Strabo Clodius Nummus, under Emperor Trajan, concerning boundary disputes between tribes, likely from the early 2nd century AD.

EDCS-13003869.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Crescens lived for 5 years.
EDCS-13003869.summary: A funerary inscription recording the short life of Crescens.

EDCS-13003870.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcus Munatius Maximus made this for himself while alive.
EDCS-13003870.summary: A funerary inscription by Marcus Munatius Maximus, made during his lifetime.

EDCS-13003871.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Matih, son of Siddinis, lived for 33 years and is buried here.
EDCS-13003871.summary: A funerary inscription recording the life and burial of Matih, son of Siddinis.

EDCS-13003874.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulia Secura, dutiful, lived for 45 years and is buried here. Priscus, son of Urbanus, dutiful, lived for 61 years and is buried here.
EDCS-13003874.summary: A funerary inscription for two individuals, Iulia Secura and Priscus, son of Urbanus.

EDCS-13003875.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Titinia Fortunata, dutiful, lived for 48 years and is buried here. May your bones rest well. Sacred to the departed spirits. Titus Flavius Quirina Pudens Maximianus, son of Titus Flavius, dutiful, lived for 83 years and 11 months and is buried here. May your bones rest well. Flavius is buried here, a great-grandfather who, counting many years of life in old age, deserved to be often called this. He lived as an example for the lives of his descendants and was like a father in virtue, for he often used to surpass great streams with fairness, and the old man would point out a hare to the hounds. Thus, strong, he counted a hundred years of life. I, the great-grandson, send these verses, testing a life through many ages. Flavius Pudens.
EDCS-13003875.summary: A complex funerary inscription for multiple generations of the Flavius family, commemorating the long and virtuous life of the great-grandfather, Flavius Pudens.

EDCS-13003876.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. [---]ius, priest, lived for 75 years. Sacred to the departed spirits. Ianuaria Arinis, dutiful daughter, lived for 85 years.
EDCS-13003876.summary: A funerary inscription for two individuals, a priest and Ianuaria Arinis, daughter of Arinis.

EDCS-13003877.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Festus Natalis, son of Dubb, of the tribe V [---].
EDCS-13003877.summary: A funerary inscription for Festus Natalis, son of Dubb, likely from the tribal territory of V[---].

EDCS-13003878.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Flora, dutiful daughter of Antonius, lived for 11 years and is buried here.
EDCS-13003878.summary: A funerary inscription for Flora, dutiful daughter of Antonius, who died at the age of 11.

EDCS-13100001.text_edition: \n Helvius Fuscus Luci filius Quirina Emerita militavit legione III Augusta vixit annos militavit annos XXXIIII hic situs est EIus ProculusAVI \n
EDCS-13100001.translation: Helvius Fuscus, son of Lucius, of the Quirina tribe, from Emerita, served in the III Augusta legion, lived 34 years, served 34 years, lies here. His [relative] Proculus [made this].
EDCS-13100001.summary: This is a military tombstone for Helvius Fuscus, a soldier of the III Augusta legion, recording his tribal affiliation, origin, service duration, and age, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13100004.text_edition: \n eus Cai filius Arnensis miles legionis III Augustae centuria Curti vixit annosXVI militavit nnos hic situs est R\n
EDCS-13100004.translation: [Name], son of Caius, of the Arnensis tribe, soldier of the III Augusta legion, [in the] century of Curtius, lived 16 years, served [number] years, lies here. R [made this].
EDCS-13100004.summary: This is a tombstone for a soldier of the III Augusta legion, recording his tribal affiliation, unit, age, and service duration, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13100005.text_edition: \n lusio O vixsit sic nnos XLIII militavit nnos XXIII hic situs est curam egerunt Caius Catellius \n
EDCS-13100005.translation: [Name], lived 43 years, served 23 years, lies here. Caius Catellius [made this] with care.
EDCS-13100005.summary: This is a tombstone for an individual who served in the military, recording their age and service years, with Caius Catellius noted as the one who arranged it, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13100006.text_edition: \n s Cai filius Celer --- mil(es) legionis III Augustae \n
EDCS-13100006.translation: [Name], son of Caius Celer, soldier of the III Augusta legion.
EDCS-13100006.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription identifying a soldier, Caius Celer, of the III Augusta legion, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13100007.translation: [Name], soldier of the III Augusta legion, [in the] century of [name], lived 67 years, served 24 years.
EDCS-13100007.summary: This is a tombstone for a soldier of the III Augusta legion, recording his age and service years, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13100008.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcus Aemilius Aemilianus, consecrated, lived for 4 years, 2 months, and 28 days. Pompeia Quarta, dutiful, placed [this]. He is buried here.
EDCS-13100008.summary: A funerary inscription for Marcus Aemilius Aemilianus, who died at a very young age, placed by Pompeia Quarta.

EDCS-13100009.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Quintus C. Felico, dutiful, lived 30 years; whose body is buried here.
EDCS-13100009.summary: A funerary inscription recording the burial of Quintus C. Felico, who lived 30 years.

EDCS-13100010.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Carvilla Africana lived 67 years; she is buried here. Sulgia Marcia set this up for her dutiful mother.
EDCS-13100010.summary: A funerary inscription recording the burial of Carvilla Africana, who lived 67 years, and dedicated by her daughter Sulgia Marcia.

EDCS-13100011.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Hateria Dativa lived about 80 years; she is buried here. Lucius Geminius Fortunatianus set this up for his dearest mother.
EDCS-13100011.summary: A funerary inscription recording the burial of Hateria Dativa, who lived about 80 years, and dedicated by her son Lucius Geminius Fortunatianus.

EDCS-13100012.translation: Herennius Maximus, son of [---], of the Quirina tribe, lived 38 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-13100012.summary: A funerary inscription recording the burial of Herennius Maximus, who lived 38 years.

EDCS-13100013.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Vit Cancael lived 56 years.
EDCS-13100013.summary: A funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Vit Cancael, who lived 56 years.

EDCS-13100014.summary: A funerary inscription fragment indicating a son set up a monument for a parent.

EDCS-13100015.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Sergia Secunda lived 86 years. Roman Figel made [this] for his dutiful wife.
EDCS-13100015.summary: A funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Sergia Secunda, who lived 86 years, and dedicated by her husband Roman Figel.

EDCS-13100018.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Quintus Caecilius Bassileus made [this] for Petronia Vitalis.
EDCS-13100018.summary: A funerary inscription indicating Quintus Caecilius Bassileus dedicated a monument to Petronia Vitalis.

EDCS-13100020.translation: Macurta Macurgum, Vihinna, Bonchor, Varsissima, Matila, Iuna. Marcus Aemilius Ianuarius and Quintus Aelius Felix made and dedicated [this] from their own resources.
EDCS-13100020.summary: An inscription recording the dedication of a monument by Marcus Aemilius Ianuarius and Quintus Aelius Felix for a group of individuals, possibly family members.

EDCS-13100023.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Aris Storacis filius vixit annos LXX hic situs est Dis Manibus sacrum Arest pia vixit nnos\n
EDCS-13100023.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Aris, son of Storax, lived 70 years, lies here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Arest [pious, made this], lived [years].
EDCS-13100023.summary: This is a tombstone for Aris, son of Storax, recording his age and burial, with a partial second inscription possibly for Arest, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13100024.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Caelia Maxima, dutiful daughter of Caelia Hilari, lived 37 years, 2 months, and 23 days. For her merits, her betrothed, Tertullus, made [this] and set up his own image.
EDCS-13100024.summary: A funerary inscription recording the life of Caelia Maxima, who lived 37 years, 2 months, and 23 days, and dedicated by her betrothed Tertullus, who also placed his own image.

EDCS-13100026.translation: The atrium of the Antonine Baths, begun by our ancestors, with cisterns and supports in the same place, which, due to incomplete work, had become damaged and defiled by rubble, the divine Honoratianus, perpetual flamen and curator rei publicae twice, with a statue and image of the fortunate Emperors, restored and dedicated.
EDCS-13100026.summary: This inscription records the restoration and dedication of the atrium of the Antonine Baths by Honoratianus, a perpetual flamen and curator rei publicae, likely in the later Roman period.

EDCS-13100028.translation: Marcus Oppius Hospes made a vow.
EDCS-13100028.summary: This inscription records a votive offering made by Marcus Oppius Hospes.

EDCS-13100031.summary: This is a fragment, possibly a milestone, indicating a distance of 8 Roman miles from a location identified as SFI.

EDCS-13100032.translation: RAMB O, from his beloved husband, with the character of his father-in-law, of ancient purity of life, the last of his line, with goodwill.
EDCS-13100032.summary: This is a funerary inscription, likely a dedication or epitaph, praising the character and lineage of the deceased.

EDCS-13100033.translation: Caius Titurnius Quartio, a cavalryman of the III Gallica legion, served for 35 years. The August Emperors awarded him a torque and armlets in the Parthian War at Seleucia and Babylon. He repaid his vow.
EDCS-13100033.summary: This inscription details the military service of Caius Titurnius Quartio, a cavalryman awarded for his bravery in the Parthian War, who fulfilled a vow.

EDCS-13100034.translation: Sacred to Saturn Augustus. Our benefactor Cuttinus, with his goods, gladly paid his vow.
EDCS-13100034.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to Saturn Augustus, paid by Cuttinus.

EDCS-13100035.translation: Iulia Faustilla lived 80 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-13100035.summary: This is a simple epitaph recording the name, age, and burial location of Iulia Faustilla.

EDCS-13100036.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucilianus made this for Mamidia Felicitas, his incomparable wife.
EDCS-13100036.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Lucilianus to his wife, Mamidia Felicitas.

EDCS-13100037.translation: To our lord Flavius Constantius Pius Felix Augustus, 60,000 [denarii?].
EDCS-13100037.summary: This inscription records a dedication or payment of 60,000 units (likely denarii) to Emperor Constantius II.

EDCS-13100043.translation: To the Great Mother of the Gods, Cybele, and Attis Augustus.
EDCS-13100043.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the Great Mother of the Gods (Cybele) and Attis.

EDCS-13100045.translation: Flavius Arcadius, son oflius Bonifatius Maiorinus.
EDCS-13100045.summary: This inscription appears to be a fragmentary dedication or memorial to Flavius Arcadius, son oflius Bonifatius Maiorinus.

EDCS-13100047.translation: Sacred to the gods. Maxima lived 77 years. Donatus SCCA made this willingly, having lived 85 years.
EDCS-13100047.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the ages of Maxima and Donatus SCCA, with Donatus explicitly stating he made the monument.

EDCS-13100049.translation: In the 8th and 2nd year, they made [this] for Aelius Saturninus, who rests here.
EDCS-13100049.summary: This funerary inscription records the construction of a monument for Aelius Saturninus, with a dating reference to consular years.

EDCS-13200001.text_edition: \n Caio Iunio Serio Augurino Marco Trebio Sergiano consulibus Caius Caelius Saturninus structor ab Avitinis sic votum solvit columnas duas in cella Caelestis deae sua pecunia fecit? et dedicavit\n
EDCS-13200001.translation: During the consulship of Caius Iunius Serius Augurinus and Marcus Trebius Sergianus, Caius Coelius Saturninus, a builder from Avitinis, fulfilled a vow and made and dedicated two columns in the cella of the goddess Caelestis with his own money.
EDCS-13200001.summary: This inscription records a religious dedication by Caius Coelius Saturninus, a builder, who fulfilled a vow by providing two columns for the temple of the goddess Caelestis, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13200004.translation: Of Gratian and Valentinian, always Emperors.
EDCS-13200004.summary: This is a dedication or inscription referencing the imperial authority of Gratian and Valentinian, likely from the late 4th century.

EDCS-13200016.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription mentioning a colleague, possibly related to an official or a shared duty.

EDCS-13200017.summary: This inscription records the title 'curator rei publicae', indicating an official responsible for public affairs in a city or region.

EDCS-13200283.translation: Salonius Felix, the superior priest, with his wife, fulfilled a vow.
EDCS-13200283.summary: This is a votive inscription recording Salonius Felix, a priest, fulfilling a vow with his wife.

EDCS-13300147.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Lucius Aurelius Narcissus, dutiful, lived 60 years, rests here.
EDCS-13300147.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the life and burial of Lucius Aurelius Narcissus.

EDCS-13300148.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Lucius Marcellus, son of Minutus, lived 66 years, rests here.
EDCS-13300148.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the life and burial of Lucius Marcellus.

EDCS-13300149.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Nevia Gemista, dutiful, chaste, lived 22 years, 6 months, 11 hours, rests here.
EDCS-13300149.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the life, including precise age, and burial of Nevia Gemista.

EDCS-13300150.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Publius Pomponius lived for [X] years.
EDCS-13300150.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Publius Pomponius.

EDCS-13300151.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Sulpicia Maior, pious, lived for 95 years. She rests here.
EDCS-13300151.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan and burial of Sulpicia Maior.

EDCS-13300152.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Caricilia Victoria, pious, lived for 22 years, 5 months, and 1 day. She rests here.
EDCS-13300152.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan and burial of Caricilia Victoria.

EDCS-13300153.translation: [---]inius, son of T. N. N. R., [---].
EDCS-13300153.summary: This is a fragmented inscription that likely records a name and filiation.

EDCS-13300154.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari Augusto tribunicia potestate XVIII Lucius Asprenas \n
EDCS-13300154.translation: To Emperor Caesar Augustus, in his eighteenth tribunician power. Lucius Asprenas.
EDCS-13300154.summary: This is a dedication to Emperor Augustus, initiated by Lucius Asprenas, likely on a public monument, dated to his 18th tribunician power.

EDCS-13300155.summary: This is a dedication, possibly funerary, to Imilcho.

EDCS-13300156.translation: Gaius Julius Hospes, freedman, to Gaius Julius Successus, patron.
EDCS-13300156.summary: This is a dedication, likely funerary, from a freedman to his patron.

EDCS-13300185.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription with barely legible words.

EDCS-13300187.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Canisia Sosusa lived for 10 years.
EDCS-13300187.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Canisia Sosusa.

EDCS-13300189.translation: Castula, a girl of 48 years, on the 6th day before the Ides of March, hastened to receive the rewards of chastity, she deserved an imperishable crown; God will grant grace to the persevering in peace.
EDCS-13300189.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Castula, emphasizing her chastity and promising heavenly rewards.

EDCS-13300190.translation: Cresconia, innocent, in the peace of Christ.
EDCS-13300190.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Cresconia, indicating a Christian burial.

EDCS-13300191.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Ebentia, who is described as innocent and at peace.

EDCS-13300192.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Pelagius, noting his state of peace.

EDCS-13301698.translation: To Caecilia Saturnina, my most holy wife; she lived 60 years; she is laid here.
EDCS-13301698.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Caecilia Saturnina, commemorating her life and placing her remains.

EDCS-13302421.translation: Marcus Eustorgius Heraclamon Leonides, husband, to his most rare and unique wife, a philosopher, of exemplary character, modesty, and excellence, in peace.
EDCS-13302421.summary: This is a funerary epitaph from a husband to his wife, a philosopher, praising her virtues.

EDCS-13302422.translation: Drink, play, give gifts. Eustorgius says: God hates a wife of bad character and her son in poverty and usury. Eustorgius says: God loves a true and beautiful virgin and good friends. Eustorgius says: Understand this: expect a friend, for you will quarrel with him. Eustorgius says: Drink, young men, while you can drink. Eustorgius says: Drink. Eustorgius says: Go straight ahead. Eustorgius says:
EDCS-13302422.summary: This inscription contains a series of moralizing sayings and exhortations, likely from a tombstone or building inscription, attributed to Eustorgius.

EDCS-13302423.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Cotbuldeus, noting his state of peace.

EDCS-13302432.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari Marco Annio Floriano Pio Felici Augusto pontifici maximo fortissimo adque sic indulgentissimo principi restitutori orbis potestate consuli II patri patriae procons(uli) res publica coloniae Hipponensium Regiorum\n
EDCS-13302432.translation: To Emperor Caesar Marcus Annius Florianus Pius Felix Augustus, pontifex maximus, most brave and most indulgent prince, restorer of the world, consul for the second time, father of the country, proconsul. The Republic of the colony of Hippona Regia.
EDCS-13302432.summary: This is a dedication from the city of Hippona Regia to Emperor Annius Florianus, praising his virtues and titles, likely an honorific inscription on a public building.

EDCS-13302437.summary: This is a dedication to the god Liber Pater, also known as Bacchus, in his august form.

EDCS-13302440.translation: The pronaos of the curia and the people, of the pious, fortunate, unconquered.
EDCS-13302440.summary: This inscription likely records a public works project or dedication related to a curia (town hall or meeting place) and its people, emphasizing piety and good fortune.

EDCS-13302442.translation: Africa, consul of all, with Rea assisting.
EDCS-13302442.summary: This inscription records some administrative or public event involving Africa and a consul, with assistance from Rea.

EDCS-13302448.translation: Aelia Silvano, life with her family.
EDCS-13302448.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Aelia Silvano, indicating her peaceful repose with her family.

EDCS-13302452.translation: To Quintus Domitius Marsianus, son of Lucius, of the voting tribe Quirina, procurator of the Emperor for the patrimony of the province of Narbonensis, procurator of the Emperor for iron mines, procurator of the Emperor for receiving census in Gaul for the provinces of Belgica through the regions of the Tungri and Frisavones and Lower Germany and the Batavi, prefect of soldiers, admitted to the order of equestrians at public expense by the Emperors Marcus Aurelius Antoninus and Lucius Aurelius Verus Caesar, for whom when the equestrian order decreed that a monument be erected at public expense, his brother Lucius Domitius Fabianus, remitting the public expense, erected it at his own cost, following the example of the imperial rescripts. Caesar Antoninus Augustus to his Marsianus greeting: I have long wished to advance you to the splendor of the ducenary procuratorship and am using the opportunity that now presents itself. Succeed Marius Pudentius, with as much hope of my perpetual favor as you have maintained conscientiousness, diligence, and experience. Farewell, my dearest Marsianus, my friend.
EDCS-13302452.summary: This is a funerary inscription honoring Quintus Domitius Marsianus, a high-ranking imperial official, erected by his brother who took over the expense after the state had planned to fund it, and includes a rescript from Emperor Marcus Aurelius Antoninus. The inscription is dated to the co-reign of Marcus Aurelius and Lucius Verus, before Marsianus' death.

EDCS-13302472.translation: To Quintus Flavius Lappianus, son of Caius Flavius Lappianus, perpetual priest of the municipality of Kalamensium, most distinguished Roman knight, for his outstanding and exceptional generosity and liberality towards the citizens, by which, among other things, he removed all burden of care from them, surpassing in this regard the generosity of his parents, the people of Thabarbusus offered a statue costing 6,661 sesterces; this offering, having been gladly and gratefully accepted, Lappianus himself, after all the money was returned, content with the honor alone, dedicated it to the citizens with a feast and gymnasium.
EDCS-13302472.summary: This is a dedicatory inscription by the people of Thabarbusus to Quintus Flavius Lappianus, honoring his generosity with a statue, which he then rededicated after repaying the cost and providing a feast and gymnasium.

EDCS-13302476.translation: Filtered oil lamps from the workshop of Donatus.
EDCS-13302476.summary: This is a maker's mark or inscription indicating the origin of oil lamps from Donatus' workshop.

EDCS-13302506.translation: Marcus Aurelius Ianuarius, centurion of the III Augusta Pia Vindex legion, willingly paid this to Fortuna Augusta.
EDCS-13302506.summary: A private dedication to Fortuna Augusta by Marcus Aurelius Ianuarius, a centurion, dated to the period of the legion's activity.

EDCS-13302578.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari divi Nervae filio Nervae Traiano Augusto Germanico Dacico pontifici maximo tribunicia potestate XVII imperatori VII consuli VI patri patriae civitates LXIIII pagi Thuscae et Gunzuzi pecunia sua fecerunt idemque dedicaverunt curatore Victore Martialis sic praefecto earum e |(centurione)\n
EDCS-13302578.translation: To Emperor Caesar, son of the deified Nerva, Nerva Trajan Augustus Germanicus Dacicus, pontifex maximus, in his seventeenth tribunician power, imperator for the seventh time, consul for the sixth time, father of the country. Sixty-four communities and the pagi of Thusca and Gunzuzi made this at their own expense and dedicated it. Victor Martialis, curator and prefect of them, acted as supervisor.
EDCS-13302578.summary: This is a dedication to Emperor Trajan by sixty-four communities and pagi, financed and dedicated by them, with Victor Martialis serving as supervisor, dated to Trajan's 17th tribunician power.

EDCS-13302579.summary: A milestones inscription indicating the distance to Carthage.

EDCS-13302601.translation: In the temple of Pluto, they made a portico; Felix Imilis, son of Iamon, and Zrubalis, son of Anonis, sufetes of the Sucubensians, built it in the year of Izazcus and...; Felix, Iamo, Bolmicar, Ioli, Surus, Zuresius, Felicio, Diomedes, Baliato, Anterotis, Fortunatus, son of Diomedes, Assan, Cilo, Abdilim, Caledius, Rusticus, son of Ioli, Namcido, Cadaius, Ibubalis, Aninus, Felix, son of Aesopus, Cadaius, Suaeo, Primicenius, Secundaes, built it; and with their own funds, they established it with three columns, along with Fortunatus, Adnlinis, Caledii, Mutumbal, Nassaius, Miscadaius, Banocilo.
EDCS-13302601.summary: This is a dedication of a portico in a temple of Pluto, listing numerous builders and financiers, including the sufetes of the Sucubensians, with an approximate date derived from the names of the sufetes.

EDCS-13302609.text_edition: \n Lutatius Gai filius Iulius vixit annos XLI\n
EDCS-13302609.summary: This is a simple epitaph recording the name and age of the deceased, Gaius Lutatius Iulius.

EDCS-13302610.translation: With our lords Flavius Lucretius Florentinus Rusticus, most excellent man, governor, in good health, placed.
EDCS-13302610.summary: An inscription indicating that Flavius Lucretius Florentinus Rusticus, a governor, installed something, possibly a statue or monument, while wishing well to his superiors.

EDCS-13302611.translation: To good memory, Segundianus lived in peace more or less 65 years, rested in peace.
EDCS-13302611.summary: A funerary inscription commemorating Segundianus, noting his age and peaceful rest.

EDCS-13302651.translation: To Marcus Lepidus, for the third time emperor, high priest, Triumvir for Restoring the Republic, twice consul, again patron, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-13302651.summary: An inscription honoring Marcus Lepidus, listing his numerous high offices, likely related to a public monument or dedication.

EDCS-13302652.translation: This is the Fortuna of Curaria Fortunata.
EDCS-13302652.summary: A short inscription identifying a statue or shrine dedicated to Fortuna, belonging to Curaria Fortunata.

EDCS-13302734.translation: To Vetranio, most distinguished man, son, legate.
EDCS-13302734.summary: A dedication or commemoration of Vetranio, identified as a distinguished man, son, and legate.

EDCS-13302735.text_edition: \n Germanico maximo tribunicia potestate XVI imperatori XV consuli VII patri patriae proconsuli Caius Servilius Marsus consul curator rei publicae regionis Tripolitanae devotus numini maiestatique eius\n
EDCS-13302735.translation: To Germanicus Maximus, in his sixteenth tribunician power, imperator for the fifteenth time, consul for the seventh time, father of the country, proconsul. Caius Servilius Marsus, consul, curator of the Republic of the Tripolitana region, devoted to his divine majesty.
EDCS-13302735.summary: This is a dedication by Caius Servilius Marsus to Germanicus Maximus, likely a general or imperial figure, in his capacity as curator of the Tripolitana region, dated to Germanicus' 16th tribunician power.

EDCS-13302750.summary: This inscription records that Rufenus made a monument or object, likely of personal significance.

EDCS-13302752.translation: If you have washed, here is...
EDCS-13302752.summary: This inscription appears to be incomplete and its meaning is unclear, possibly relating to a ritual cleansing or a funerary context.

EDCS-13302753.translation: This is Fortuna, wife of Curarius, for Fortunata.
EDCS-13302753.summary: This inscription seems to be a dedication or memorial, possibly related to a family or an individual named Fortuna, connected to Curarius and Fortunata.

EDCS-13302782.summary: This inscription is a simple naming, likely identifying an individual named Tyrannus Cyprianus, possibly on a tomb or dedication.

EDCS-13302783.translation: Melleus, bishop of unity, rested in peace. He lived about 80 years, was laid to rest on the 5th day before the Ides of August in the 12th indiction.
EDCS-13302783.summary: This is a Christian funerary inscription for Melleus, a bishop, recording his death date and approximate age.

EDCS-13302784.translation: Pascasius, a subdeacon, lived 22 years. He rested on the 15th day before the Kalends of September.
EDCS-13302784.summary: This is a Christian funerary inscription for Pascasius, a subdeacon, recording his death date and age.

EDCS-13302785.summary: This is a Christian funerary inscription for Potentius, a subdeacon, recording his age at death.

EDCS-13302786.translation: Martialis, a priest, lived 30 years. He rested in peace.
EDCS-13302786.summary: This is a Christian funerary inscription for Martialis, a priest, recording his age at death and his peaceful rest.

EDCS-13302788.translation: Reparatus, faithful in Christ, rested in peace on the 9th day before the Kalends of May in the 12th indiction.
EDCS-13302788.summary: This is a Christian funerary inscription for Reparatus, recording his death date and affirming his faith.

EDCS-13302789.translation: Stefanus, living in God, lived 10 months. He was laid to rest on the 13th day before the Kalends of May in the 8th indiction. He rested in peace.
EDCS-13302789.summary: This is a Christian funerary inscription for Stefanus, recording his short life, death date, and peaceful rest.

EDCS-13302791.summary: This is a boundary marker or property designation associated with Vindicianus Albucius.

EDCS-13302792.summary: This is a boundary marker or property designation associated with Quintianus.

EDCS-13302793.translation: The place of the sons of Zotimus.
EDCS-13302793.summary: This is a boundary marker or property designation associated with the sons of Zotimus.

EDCS-13302794.summary: This is a boundary marker or property designation associated with Silbanianus.

EDCS-13302795.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Valerius.

EDCS-13302796.translation: Felix fell asleep in peace; he lived 47 years; he was buried on the Nones of December, in the 11th indiction.
EDCS-13302796.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Felix, his age at death, and the date of his burial, likely from the 4th century AD.

EDCS-13302797.translation: Gentilis was buried in peace on the 5th day before the Kalends of March, in the 11th indiction; he lived 49 years.
EDCS-13302797.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Gentilis, his age at death, and the date of his burial, likely from the 4th century AD.

EDCS-13302799.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Superius.

EDCS-13302801.summary: This is a boundary marker or property designation associated with Reparatus Potens.

EDCS-13302802.translation: Dinamius rested in peace on the 8th day before the Ides of July, in the 8th indiction; he lived 3 years.
EDCS-13302802.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Dinamius, his age at death, and the date of his burial, likely from the 4th century AD.

EDCS-13302803.translation: Theodorus rested in peace on the day before the Nones of May, in the second indiction.
EDCS-13302803.summary: This inscription records the death of Theodorus, including the date and indiction, likely from a tombstone or funerary context.

EDCS-13302804.translation: Hildiger was placed here in peace.
EDCS-13302804.summary: This inscription marks the burial place of Hildiger, indicating they were laid to rest peacefully.

EDCS-13302805.translation: The distinguished Albucius lived in peace for 40 years.
EDCS-13302805.summary: This inscription records the life and peaceful death of the distinguished Albucius, specifying his age at death.

EDCS-13302806.translation: The place of Donatus Belianus in peace.
EDCS-13302806.summary: This inscription designates a burial place belonging to Donatus Belianus, suggesting a funerary context.

EDCS-13302808.summary: This inscription commemorates Marciana, noting her innocence and peaceful rest, likely on a tombstone.

EDCS-13302809.summary: This inscription marks a location associated with Castalinus, possibly a burial plot or property marker.

EDCS-13302810.summary: This inscription records the peaceful rest of Dinamius, likely from a funerary monument.

EDCS-13302811.translation: The virgin Iulia lived for 11 years and 3 months, rested in peace on the 6th day before the Nones of March, in the twelfth indiction.
EDCS-13302811.summary: This inscription commemorates the virgin Iulia, detailing her age at death, the date, and the indiction, from a funerary monument.

EDCS-13302812.translation: Bonifatius was placed [here] on the 10th day before the Kalends of March in peace.
EDCS-13302812.summary: This inscription records the burial of Bonifatius on a specific date, indicating his peaceful repose, likely from a tombstone.

EDCS-13302813.translation: The place of Donatus the priest.
EDCS-13302813.summary: This inscription designates a burial place or property belonging to Donatus, identified as a priest.

EDCS-13302814.translation: Pontica, faithful in Christ, rested in peace on the 10th day before the Ides of May, in the 14th indiction. She lived for 5 years.
EDCS-13302814.summary: This funerary inscription records the death and age of Pontica, a Christian woman.

EDCS-13302815.translation: Bonis rested in peace on the 8th day before the Kalends of April, in the 6th indiction.
