EDCS-13302815.summary: This funerary inscription records the repose of Bonis, dated by indiction.

EDCS-13302816.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Maurianus, identified by his military rank of optio.

EDCS-13302817.translation: Theudorus, cleric, in peace, lived for 18 years, buried on the 16th day before the Kalends of February.
EDCS-13302817.summary: This funerary inscription records the death and burial date of Theudorus, identified as a cleric.

EDCS-13302818.translation: Felix, Catholic deacon, rested in peace.
EDCS-13302818.summary: This funerary inscription records the repose of Felix, identified as a Catholic deacon.

EDCS-13302819.translation: Victor, deacon, rested in peace on the 11th day before the Kalends of July. He lived for 29 years.
EDCS-13302819.summary: This funerary inscription records the death and age of Victor, identified as a deacon.

EDCS-13302820.translation: Cresconia rested in peace. She lived for one year and 4 months.
EDCS-13302820.summary: This funerary inscription records the death and age of Cresconia, who died in infancy.

EDCS-13302821.translation: Florentia rested in peace. She lived for three years and 4 months.
EDCS-13302821.summary: This funerary inscription records the death and age of Florentia, who died in early childhood.

EDCS-13302822.summary: This funerary inscription records the age of Barbara at death.

EDCS-13302823.summary: This funerary inscription records the name and clerical rank of Crescentianus.

EDCS-13302824.translation: Florentinus the subdeacon lived in peace, buried on the day before the Kalends of February.
EDCS-13302824.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the burial of Florentinus, a subdeacon.

EDCS-13302826.translation: Egiptius the deacon rested in peace, lived 38 years, buried on the day of the Nones of September, in the eighth indiction.
EDCS-13302826.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the burial of Egiptius, a deacon, with his lifespan and the indiction year.

EDCS-13302827.translation: Pimenius a faithful one in Christ lived 22 years, buried on the day of the Ides of July.
EDCS-13302827.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the burial of Pimenius, identified as a faithful Christian, with his lifespan.

EDCS-13302828.translation: Pimenius lived 32 years, rested in peace on the fourth day before the Nones of August, in the twelfth indiction.
EDCS-13302828.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the burial of Pimenius, with his lifespan and the indiction year.

EDCS-13302829.translation: Altina rested in peace the day before the Ides of December.
EDCS-13302829.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the burial of Altina.

EDCS-13302830.translation: Onorata rested in peace, lived for one year and 6 months, was buried on the third day before the Ides of March.
EDCS-13302830.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the burial of Onorata, with her lifespan.

EDCS-13302831.translation: Genazius rested in peace, lived 3 years and 9 months.
EDCS-13302831.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Genazius.

EDCS-13302832.translation: Lucillus rested in peace, lived 55 years, buried.
EDCS-13302832.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Lucillus.

EDCS-13302834.translation: Polibius a faithful one in peace.
EDCS-13302834.summary: A funerary epitaph identifying Polibius as a faithful person at peace.

EDCS-13302835.translation: Terentinus a faithful one in peace.
EDCS-13302835.summary: A funerary epitaph identifying Terentinus as a faithful person at peace.

EDCS-13302840.translation: Ivuza rested in peace, lived 10 years.
EDCS-13302840.summary: This is a tomb inscription for Ivuza, who lived 10 years and rested in peace.

EDCS-13302841.translation: Fortunatus the faithful [rested] in peace on the 10th day before the Kalends of October.
EDCS-13302841.summary: This is a tomb inscription for Fortunatus, a faithful person who died on September 22nd.

EDCS-13302842.summary: This is a tomb inscription for Fla, a faithful person who rested.

EDCS-13302844.translation: Barbara the chaste rested in peace.
EDCS-13302844.summary: This is a tomb inscription for Barbara, a chaste person who rested in peace.

EDCS-13302848.translation: Adeodata the faithful lived for 10 years more or less, placed [here] on the 14th day before the Kalends of November in the 9th indiction.
EDCS-13302848.summary: This is a tomb inscription for Adeodata, a faithful person who lived approximately 10 years and was buried on October 19th.

EDCS-13302851.translation: Castalinus the lector rested in peace, lived six years [and] 4 months, was placed [here] on the day before the Kalends of January in the 3rd indiction.
EDCS-13302851.summary: This is a tomb inscription for Castalinus, a lector, who lived 6 years and 4 months and was buried on December 31st.

EDCS-13302852.translation: Iuliana, wife of the magistratus, faithful in Christ, rested in peace, lived 50 years, placed [here] on the 8th day before the Kalends of November in the 6th indiction.
EDCS-13302852.summary: This is a tomb inscription for Iuliana, wife of a magistratus, who lived 50 years and was buried on October 25th.

EDCS-13302853.translation: Abundiola the faithful in Christ rested in peace on the 6th Ides of June in the 13th indiction, lived 4 years.
EDCS-13302853.summary: This is a tomb inscription for Abundiola, a faithful person in Christ, who lived 4 years and was buried on June 7th.

EDCS-13302854.translation: Quodbuldeus the faithful in Christ rested in peace on the 14th day before the Kalends of February in the 13th indiction, lived 10 months.
EDCS-13302854.summary: This is a tomb inscription for Quodbuldeus, a faithful person in Christ, who lived 10 months and was buried on January 19th.

EDCS-13302856.translation: Pregepta the faithful in Christ rested in peace on the fifth Ides of November, lived 9 years.
EDCS-13302856.summary: This is a tomb inscription for Pregepta, a faithful person in Christ, who lived 9 years and was buried on November 9th.

EDCS-13302857.translation: Restituta, faithful in Christ, rested in peace on the 11th day before the Ides of June, in the 2nd indiction; she lived 3 years.
EDCS-13302857.summary: This is a Christian epitaph recording the death of Restituta, who lived for 3 years and died on June 2nd in the 2nd indiction.

EDCS-13302858.translation: Abundiola, faithful in Christ, rested in peace on the Ides of June, in the 2nd indiction; she lived 5 years.
EDCS-13302858.summary: This is a Christian epitaph recording the death of Abundiola, who lived for 5 years and died on June 13th in the 2nd indiction.

EDCS-13302859.translation: Adeodata, faithful in Christ, rested in peace on the 2nd day before the Kalends of June, in the 8th indiction; she lived 3 years.
EDCS-13302859.summary: This is a Christian epitaph recording the death of Adeodata, who lived for 3 years and died on May 31st in the 8th indiction.

EDCS-13302860.translation: Cresconia, faithful in Christ, rested in peace on the 2nd day before the Kalends of June, in the 8th indiction; she lived 6 years.
EDCS-13302860.summary: This is a Christian epitaph recording the death of Cresconia, who lived for 6 years and died on May 31st in the 8th indiction.

EDCS-13302861.translation: Guitifrida lived 32 years more or less; she rested in peace on the Kalends of February, in the 14th indiction.
EDCS-13302861.summary: This is a Christian epitaph recording the death of Guitifrida, who lived approximately 32 years and died on February 1st in the 14th indiction.

EDCS-13302862.translation: Maria, faithful, rested in peace on the 3rd day before the Ides of November.
EDCS-13302862.summary: This is a Christian epitaph recording the death of Maria, who died on November 11th.

EDCS-13302863.translation: Marcinus, cleric, rested in peace; he lived 4 years and 5 months; he was buried on the 3rd day before the Ides of May.
EDCS-13302863.summary: This is a Christian epitaph recording the death of Marcinus, a cleric, who lived 4 years and 5 months and was buried on May 13th.

EDCS-13302864.translation: Ornatus patriae, defender of the city, you are covered by the tomb of Mustela. You who were pleasing to the people with a kind mind deserved to receive eternal life after this life. Warrior who also was Mustelus, master, lived in peace.
EDCS-13302864.summary: This is a pagan epitaph for Mustelus (also called Ornatus patriae and Bellator), a defender of the city, who is praised for his kindness and military service.

EDCS-13302865.translation: Rogatina, faithful in Christ, rested in peace on the 5th day before the Ides of June, in the 7th indiction; she lived 4 years.
EDCS-13302865.summary: This is a Christian epitaph recording the death of Rogatina, who lived for 4 years and died on June 9th in the 7th indiction.

EDCS-13302866.translation: Abitziana, faithful, lived 44 years in peace; she was buried.
EDCS-13302866.summary: This is a Christian epitaph recording the burial of Abitziana, who lived 44 years and was faithful.

EDCS-13302867.translation: Seberianus rested in peace, lived, was buried.
EDCS-13302867.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the death and burial of Seberianus, likely from late antiquity.

EDCS-13302868.translation: Donatus, also known as As, lived for 67 years, rested in peace, was buried on the day before the Kalends of January in the 9th indiction.
EDCS-13302868.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the death of Donatus, who lived 67 years, and specifies the date of his burial in the 9th indiction.

EDCS-13302869.translation: Basa, faithful in Christ, rested in peace, lived for 13 years, was buried on the 8th day before the Kalends of March in the 9th indiction.
EDCS-13302869.summary: This funerary epitaph records the death of Basa, a faithful Christian, who lived 13 years, and gives the date of her burial in the 9th indiction.

EDCS-13302871.translation: In the 7th indiction, Flavianilla, faithful in peace, was buried, lived for 58 years, on the 6th day before the Nones of March.
EDCS-13302871.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Flavianilla, a faithful Christian, specifying her age as 58 years and the date in the 7th indiction.

EDCS-13302872.translation: Curri, who was of the light of ORI, I deserved him from all, I fulfilled both customs for him, and God knew him to be a worthy man by his morals, with a noble friend, and constant, truthful in his ways, rested in peace.
EDCS-13302872.summary: This is a fragmented epitaph praising the deceased Curri for his character and constancy, noting he rested in peace.

EDCS-13302873.translation: Flabiana, faithful, lived in peace for 15 years minus 14 days, rested on the 14th day before the Kalends of September in the 15th indiction.
EDCS-13302873.summary: This funerary epitaph records the life and death of Flabiana, a faithful Christian, who lived for 15 years less 14 days, with the burial date specified in the 15th indiction.

EDCS-13302874.translation: Benantius, faithful, lived for 54 years in peace, was buried on the day before the Nones of August in the sixth indiction.
EDCS-13302874.summary: This epitaph records the death of Benantius, a faithful Christian, who lived 54 years, and specifies the date of his burial in the sixth indiction.

EDCS-13302878.translation: Magnificus rested in peace, lived for 57 years more or less, was buried on the fourth day of the Ides of September in the 8th indiction.
EDCS-13302878.summary: This funerary epitaph states that Magnificus rested in peace and lived for approximately 57 years, with his burial date noted in the 8th indiction.

EDCS-13302879.translation: Caupis, faithful in Christ, rested in peace on the 5th day of the Ides of December in the 6th indiction.
EDCS-13302879.summary: This epitaph records the death of Caupis, a faithful Christian, specifying the date of his repose in the 6th indiction.

EDCS-13302880.translation: Petrus the innocent rested in peace.
EDCS-13302880.summary: This short epitaph records the peaceful rest of Petrus, described as innocent.

EDCS-13302881.translation: Pieta, Ama, Titus: all have been judged.
EDCS-13302881.summary: This is a funerary inscription with a judgement theme, likely from the late Roman period.

EDCS-13302882.translation: Margherita, faithful in Christ, rested in peace. She lived 38 years, buried on the 17th day before the Kalends of October in the 14th indiction.
EDCS-13302882.summary: This is a Christian funerary inscription recording the death and burial details of Margherita.

EDCS-13302883.translation: Crescentinus, faithful in Christ, rested in peace. He lived 59 years, buried on the 3rd day before the Ides of October in the third indiction.
EDCS-13302883.summary: This is a Christian funerary inscription recording the death and burial details of Crescentinus.

EDCS-13302889.translation: Amis, having left IS, was buried in peace on the [date?] of May.
EDCS-13302889.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the burial of Amis in May.

EDCS-13302893.translation: Liberatus, faithful in peace, lived 5 years, buried on the Kalends of June.
EDCS-13302893.summary: This is a Christian funerary inscription recording the death and burial details of Liberatus.

EDCS-13302894.translation: Biola lived seven years in Christ and rested in peace.
EDCS-13302894.summary: This is a Christian funerary inscription recording the lifespan and peaceful rest of Biola.

EDCS-13302895.translation: Batzu the innocent lived six years in Christ and rested in peace.
EDCS-13302895.summary: This is a Christian funerary inscription recording the lifespan and peaceful rest of Batzu, described as innocent.

EDCS-13302896.translation: Marcianus rested in peace, lived 5 years.
EDCS-13302896.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan and peaceful rest of Marcianus.

EDCS-13302897.translation: Reparatus, a cleric, lived 15 years, rested in peace on the 7th day before the Ides of July in the eighth indiction, in the 34th year.
EDCS-13302897.summary: This is a Christian funerary inscription for Reparatus, a cleric, recording his age, date of burial, and regnal year.

EDCS-13302898.translation: Victoria rested in peace on the Ides of May in the 6th indiction.
EDCS-13302898.summary: This is a Christian funerary inscription recording the burial date of Victoria.

EDCS-13302899.translation: Florentia the faithful lived 5 years and rested in peace.
EDCS-13302899.summary: This epitaph records the life and peaceful rest of Florentia, a faithful individual.

EDCS-13302900.summary: This inscription likely commemorates Valerius, a victor in Christ, possibly on a personal marker or a Christian monument.

EDCS-13302901.translation: Frumentianus, son of Adeodatus, rested in peace on the 13th day before the Kalends of January, in the second indiction, having lived 15 years.
EDCS-13302901.summary: This epitaph records the death of Frumentianus, son of Adeodatus, detailing his age, date of rest, and the second indiction, likely from the 4th century CE or later.

EDCS-13302902.translation: John the lector rested in peace, lived six years and eight days, buried on the Ides of July.
EDCS-13302902.summary: This epitaph records the death of John, identified as a lector, providing his age, burial date, and repose in peace.

EDCS-13302904.summary: This fragment likely refers to an individual who rested in Christ, possibly continuing a nearby inscription.

EDCS-13302905.translation: Dinamius the faithful rested in peace on the Ides of August.
EDCS-13302905.summary: This epitaph records the death of Dinamius, a faithful individual, noting his peaceful rest on the Ides of August.

EDCS-13302906.translation: Germanus the cleric lived 15 years and 2 months, rested in peace, buried on the Ides of July, in the eighth indiction.
EDCS-13302906.summary: This epitaph records the life and peaceful rest of Germanus, a cleric, specifying his age, date of burial, and the eighth indiction.

EDCS-13302907.summary: This inscription marks a burial place belonging to or designated for Innocens.

EDCS-13302909.summary: This epitaph records the peaceful rest of Ianes.

EDCS-13302910.translation: Innocentius, son of Lucilla, rested in peace on the 2nd day before the Nones of August, in the eighth indiction, having lived 22 years and 6 months.
EDCS-13302910.summary: This epitaph records the death of Innocentius, son of Lucilla, detailing his age, date of rest, and the eighth indiction.

EDCS-13302912.translation: Donatus the reader was laid to rest in peace on the 14th day before the Kalends of May, in the eighth indiction, in the month of April.
EDCS-13302912.summary: This inscription records the burial of Donatus, identified as a reader, with a specific date of death.

EDCS-13302914.translation: Dinamius fell asleep in Christ in peace; he lived 80 years, laid to rest the day before the Nones of December in Christ, in peace.
EDCS-13302914.summary: This inscription records the death and age of Dinamius, specifying his burial date and emphasizing his peaceful rest in Christ.

EDCS-13302915.translation: Flabiana, faithful in Christ, lived 11 years; she rested in peace on the 3rd day before the Ides of July.
EDCS-13302915.summary: This inscription records the life and death of Flabiana, a faithful Christian, noting her age and date of rest.

EDCS-13302916.translation: Innocentius, faithful, rested in peace; he lived [unknown number of] years, laid to rest on the 12th day before the Kalends of October.
EDCS-13302916.summary: This inscription records the peaceful rest of Innocentius, a faithful individual, with a specific burial date but an unknown lifespan.

EDCS-13302917.translation: Felix rested in peace; he lived 5 years and 6 months, laid to rest on the 7th day before the Kalends of November.
EDCS-13302917.summary: This inscription records the death of Felix, a child, noting his age (in years and months) and the date of his peaceful repose.

EDCS-13302918.summary: This is a very brief inscription recording the peaceful rest of Secundinus.

EDCS-13302919.translation: Batocius rested in peace on the 17th day before the Kalends of November.
EDCS-13302919.summary: This inscription records the peaceful repose of Batocius, specifying the date of death.

EDCS-13302921.translation: Satura rested; she lived in peace 67 years, laid to rest on the 3rd day of the Nones of November.
EDCS-13302921.summary: This inscription records the death of Satura, stating her age in years and the date of her burial.

EDCS-13400125.translation: Marcus Sallvius Hamillus erected this sacred monument at his own expense.
EDCS-13400125.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by Marcus Sallvius Hamillus, who funded the construction of a sacred monument.

EDCS-13400131.summary: This is a very brief dedication to a person named Septidonius, likely on a small monument or marker.

EDCS-13400134.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Migin, a pious soldier of the III Augusta legion, lived 111 years and served 9 years; his tent-mates made this.
EDCS-13400134.summary: This funerary inscription records the life and service of Migin, a soldier of the III Augusta legion, and was erected by his fellow soldiers.

EDCS-13400154.translation: The entire populace with their sincere votes, and the most distinguished council with its most solemn judgment, decreeing Burrenius Felix, by his diligent care as curator of our state, to have placed this in addition to his other merits, because of his presentation of games at public expense, as the first to do so. For Quintus Silicius Victorinus, son of Lucius, of the Quirina tribe, Cornelianus Honoratianus, perpetual priest, former duovir, aedile.
EDCS-13400154.summary: A public monument erected by the council and people to Quintus Silicius Victorinus, aedile and perpetual priest, for funding games, likely in the 2nd century AD.

EDCS-13400163.translation: Gentius Proculus Rogatianus, perpetual priest of Lucius Genti Zebucianus, a perpetual priest of excellent memory, dedicated this statue of Marsyas, at a cost of 7,000 sesterces, for which he provided a two-day theatrical performance and a banquet for all the decurions and curiae. A place was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-13400163.summary: A statue dedication by Gentius Proculus Rogatianus, a perpetual priest, to Marsyas, with accompanying public games and a banquet, likely in the 2nd century AD.

EDCS-13400164.translation: Sacred to Mercury Augustus. Lucius Numisius Vitalis built this temple from the ground up at his own expense for the health of the Emperor Hadrian Caesar Augustus.
EDCS-13400164.summary: A temple dedicated to Mercury Augustus, built by Lucius Numisius Vitalis at his own expense for the health of Emperor Hadrian, likely during Hadrian's reign (117-138 AD).

EDCS-13400165.translation: To Venus. Lucius Vinnicius Fuscus, priest of the Genius of the municipality.
EDCS-13400165.summary: A dedication to Venus by Lucius Vinnicius Fuscus, functioning as a priest of the Genius of the municipality, possibly in the 2nd century AD.

EDCS-13400167.text_edition: \n ------ cons]uli VIIviro epulonum fetiali sodali Augustali proconsuli Africae legato Augustorum pro praetore provinciarum Moesiae item Dalmatiae curatori operum publ[icorum ------\n
EDCS-13400167.translation: To consul for the seventh time, member of the college of pontiffs, fetialis, member of the college of Augustales, proconsul of Africa, legate of the Augusti, governor with praetorian authority of the provinces of Moesia and also Dalmatia, curator of public works.
EDCS-13400167.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription listing the high offices held by an unnamed individual, including consulship, proconsulship of Africa, and legateship of Moesia and Dalmatia.

EDCS-13400181.text_edition: \n Victoriae Augustae Publius Cornelius Dolabella consul VIIvir epulonum sodalis Titiensis proconsul occiso Tacfarinate posuit\n
EDCS-13400181.translation: To Victoria Augusta. Publius Cornelius Dolabella, consul, member of the college of pontiffs, member of the college of Titius, proconsul, erected this after killing Tacfarinate.
EDCS-13400181.summary: This is a dedication to Victoria Augusta by Publius Cornelius Dolabella, a Roman official and military figure, commemorating his victory over Tacfarinate, and likely erected after his proconsulship in Africa.

EDCS-13400182.text_edition: \n Dolabella Rom proconsul Tacfarinate debellato civitas sic Oeam restituit pace conservata POP APHR PROT et consecravit\n
EDCS-13400182.translation: Dolabella to Rome, proconsul. After conquering Tacfarinate and preserving peace, the city of Oeam restored and consecrated this.
EDCS-13400182.summary: This inscription records that the city of Oeam was restored and consecrated by Dolabella, proconsul, after he defeated Tacfarinate and secured peace, likely referring to Dolabella's actions in North Africa.

EDCS-13400209.translation: For the deified Hadrian, father of Emperor Caesar Antoninus Augustus Pius, father of the country. The heirs of Barcula, son of Barminon, placed this, costing 400,000 sesterces, in honor of their father's magistracy, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-13400209.summary: A monument honoring the deified Emperor Hadrian, funded by the heirs of Barcula Barminonis to mark his father's magistracy, likely in the mid-2nd century AD.

EDCS-13400210.translation: The council of the Vinians and all citizens to their most beloved Aurelius Flavius, decurion, former aedile, quaestor, duovir, Roman equestrian, who has been proven by countless services to us and our state.
EDCS-13400210.summary: A public monument erected by the council and citizens of Vina to Aurelius Flavius, a prominent local official and Roman equestrian, likely in the 2nd or 3rd century AD.

EDCS-13400211.text_edition: \n Matri Magnae Ideae sacrum [[]] [[]] [[]] [[]] [] Quintus Latinius Victor et Quintus Latinius Egregius filius eius dendrofori cerno et criobolio de suo acceptis aram pecunia sua fecerunt et consacraverunt tradente Caio Raecio Aprile et Pompeia Satria Fortunata eius sacerdotibus Matris Deum Magnae Ideae coloniae Utikensis astantibus dendroforis et sacratis ministrante Caio Rombio Felice dendroforo atparatore sic dedicata X Kalendas Iulias\n
EDCS-13400211.translation: Sacred to the Great Mother Goddess Cybele. Quintus Latinius Victor and his son Quintus Latinius Egregius, dendrophores (tree-bearers), having paid the cost of a ram and bull sacrifice from their own funds, made and consecrated this altar with their own money, with Gaius Raecius Aprilis and his wife Pompeia Satria Fortunata, priests of the Great Mother Goddess Cybele of the colony of Utica, presiding, with the dendrophores and sacred attendants standing by, and Gaius Rombius Felix, a dendrophore and attendant, officiating, was dedicated thus on the tenth day before the Kalends of July.
EDCS-13400211.summary: This inscription records the dedication of an altar to the Great Mother Goddess Cybele by two dendrophores in Utica, dated to June 22nd.

EDCS-13400212.translation: Guntha, youth, may the god protect you.
EDCS-13400212.summary: A brief personal dedication or prayer for the youth Guntha, possibly a tomb inscription, date uncertain.

EDCS-13400214.translation: Sabinianus Senurianus paints and paves. May you wash well.
EDCS-13400214.summary: A functional inscription, possibly by an artist named Sabinianus Senurianus, relating to painting and paving, with an instruction for use, date uncertain.

EDCS-13400215.translation: From the hands of Sabinianus, without a painter.
EDCS-13400215.summary: A self-referential inscription by someone named Sabinianus, implying their work is of high quality even without a professional painter, date uncertain.

EDCS-13400216.translation: Maximus, son of Verecundus, the Zurmetinus, has sketched and whitewashed successfully.
EDCS-13400216.summary: An inscription by Maximus, son of Verecundus, identifying his artistic work of sketching and whitewashing, likely a workshop or artist's signature, date uncertain.

EDCS-13400226.translation: A sacred offering to the Consenting gods and goddesses. In the year of the most distinguished man, Acilius Glabrio, proconsul, Gaius Lutius Priscus of Forum Livii and Lucius Octavius Serenus of Brixellum willingly erected this altar.
EDCS-13400226.summary: This is a dedication of an altar to deities by two individuals during the proconsulship of Acilius Glabrio.

EDCS-13400237.translation: From the workshop of Lucius Acilius.
EDCS-13400237.summary: This inscription records the maker of an object, identified as Lucius Acilius.

EDCS-13500218.translation: The holy martyrs Protasius, Gerbasius, and Triphon were laid to rest on the fourth day before the Kalends of December. Here, the memory of Saint Triphon on the eighth day before the Kalends of December.
EDCS-13500218.summary: This inscription records the burial dates of three martyrs: Protasius, Gerbasius, and Triphon.

EDCS-13500219.translation: Serbius lived faithfully with his patrons in peace for 33 years. He was laid to rest on the nineteenth day before the Kalends of September, in the sixth indiction.
EDCS-13500219.summary: This epitaph records the lifespan and peaceful death of a freedman named Serbius.

EDCS-13500220.translation: Alexandria lived for four years, four months, and twenty-five days in peace.
EDCS-13500220.summary: This epitaph records the lifespan of Alexandria.

EDCS-13500221.translation: Let the subdeacon Victoricus return his gift to the Lord.
EDCS-13500221.summary: This inscription is a devotional statement by a subdeacon named Victoricus.

EDCS-13500222.translation: To Saint Cyprian, most blessed bishop and pontiff, together with Saint Adelfius, priest of this community, Aquinius and his wife Iuliana, along with Villa and Deogratias, placed this tessera for eternal peace.
EDCS-13500222.summary: This is a dedication of a tessera to Bishops Cyprian and Adelfius by Aquinius, his wife Iuliana, and two others.

EDCS-13500226.translation: Gaius Julius Valens, son of Gaius, of the voting tribe Quirina, decurion of the colonia Aelia Augusta Tipasensium, was arranged to be buried by his brother and heir Iulius Masculus in accordance with his will.
EDCS-13500226.summary: This is a funerary monument inscription stating that Iulius Masculus arranged the burial of his brother, Gaius Julius Valens, a decurion.

EDCS-13500227.translation: Lucius Turranius Honoratus, having retired from military service, for the sake of the honor owed to his most rare wife Masculina, in her memory.
EDCS-13500227.summary: This is a dedication by Lucius Turranius Honoratus to his deceased wife Masculina.

EDCS-13500228.translation: To Iulia Saturnina, daughter of Lucius, Tiberius Claudius Saturninus for her merits.
EDCS-13500228.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Tiberius Claudius Saturninus to his mother, Iulia Saturnina.

EDCS-13500230.translation: and for his son Valens, a flaminate priest of the city of Rome, patron of the province, his most dutiful father, Gaius Julius Masculus, pontifex.
EDCS-13500230.summary: This inscription is a dedication by a pontifex and father to his son, who held priestly and patronal offices in Rome and its province, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13500232.translation: From the will of Lucius Assellus Honoratus, son of Lucius, of the voting tribe Quirina, by decree of the town councillors.
EDCS-13500232.summary: This inscription records a posthumous honor granted by decree of the town councillors, stemming from the will of Lucius Assellus Honoratus, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13500233.translation: To Gnaeus Sentius Pudentus, son of Lucius, of the voting tribe Quirina, by decree of the town councillors.
EDCS-13500233.summary: This inscription is an honorific dedication to Gnaeus Sentius Pudentus, granted by decree of the town councillors, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13500234.translation: The council of Hipponensium Regiorum, concerning the gifts from the trust funds of their dependants, decreed and dedicated a statue to Lucius Baburius Iuvenis, a most distinguished young man, son of Lucius Baburius Iuvenis, a most distinguished man, patron of the colony.
EDCS-13500234.summary: This inscription records a statue decreed and dedicated by the local council of Hipponensium Regiorum to Lucius Baburius Iuvenis, a young man honored for his father's patronage and trust funds, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13500235.translation: The council of Hipponensium Regiorum, concerning the gifts from the trust funds of their dependants, decreed and dedicated a statue to Gaius Baburius Herculanius, a most distinguished boy, son of Lucius Baburius Iuvenis, a most distinguished man, patron of the colony.
EDCS-13500235.summary: This inscription records a statue decreed and dedicated by the local council of Hipponensium Regiorum to Gaius Baburius Herculanius, a boy honored for his father's patronage and trust funds, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13500241.translation: On the 3rd day before the Ides of September, Ermengon, spouse, of sweet memory, departed in peace, having lived 35 years, with her husband Ingomaris.
EDCS-13500241.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Ermengon, a married woman who lived 35 years and is remembered as 'sweet', likely dating to the Late Roman or early post-Roman period.

EDCS-13500242.translation: Supserika the faithful lived in peace. Arcura the faithful lived in peace, for 10 years.
EDCS-13500242.summary: This is a short funerary inscription mentioning two individuals, Supserika and Arcura, both described as 'faithful' and 'in peace', with Arcura's age noted as 10 years, likely from the Late Roman or early post-Roman period.

EDCS-13500243.translation: Supserik the faithful lived in peace for 41 years. Germana his wife lived.
EDCS-13500243.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Supserik, described as 'faithful' and 'in peace', who lived 41 years, and also mentions his wife Germana, likely dating to the Late Roman or early post-Roman period.

EDCS-13500304.translation: Giuliaruna the presbyteress reposed in peace, lived 50 years.
EDCS-13500304.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Giuliaruna, identified as a 'presbyteress', who lived 50 years and reposed in peace, likely dating to the Late Roman or early post-Roman Christian period.

EDCS-13500307.translation: Egyptzuius the presbyter, faithful in peace.
EDCS-13500307.summary: This brief funerary inscription records Egyptzuius, identified as a 'presbyter', who is described as 'faithful' and 'in peace', likely dating to the Late Roman or early post-Roman Christian period.

EDCS-13500308.summary: This inscription is a simple epitaph for Valila, identified as faithful, resting in peace.

EDCS-13500309.summary: This inscription is a simple epitaph for Quinta, identified as faithful, resting in peace.

EDCS-13500311.summary: This inscription is a brief epitaph for Izzaca, identified as faithful.

EDCS-13500312.translation: Margarita the faithful lived 25 years, rested in peace on the 6th day before the Ides of May, leaving the grief of her parents, on the 6th day before the Ides of May.
EDCS-13500312.summary: This inscription records the death of Margarita, who lived 25 years and died on May 10th, leaving her parents grieving.

EDCS-13500313.translation: Sacred to Saint Saturninus. Numisius Gratus lived 1 year and 7 months, an innocent infant without fault, released.
EDCS-13500313.summary: This inscription is a memorial for Numisius Gratus, the infant son of Numisius Gratus, who died after 1 year and 7 months.

EDCS-13500329.translation: In peace. Felix Argenti, at that memory. Sons made it. Lived 75 years.
EDCS-13500329.summary: This inscription is a memorial for Felix Argenti, created by his sons, who lived to be 75 years old.

EDCS-13500330.translation: The place of Teophilus, deceased. To the reader.
EDCS-13500330.summary: This inscription marks the burial place of Teophilus, identified as deceased, and is addressed to the reader.

EDCS-13500331.translation: Redentus the subdeacon lived 21 years, rested on the [---] day.
EDCS-13500331.summary: This inscription records the death of Redentus, a subdeacon, who died at the age of 21.

EDCS-13500332.translation: Memorial to Isperatia the kind, in peace. Lived 86 years, 6 months, 7 days.
EDCS-13500332.summary: This inscription is a memorial to Isperatia, who lived a long life of 86 years, 6 months, and 7 days.

EDCS-13500333.translation: Who also Gni, placed in peace.
EDCS-13500333.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription indicating that 'Gni' was placed in peace, likely in a burial context.

EDCS-13500336.translation: Donatilla with her sister, in peace.
EDCS-13500336.summary: A funerary epitaph for Donatilla and her sister, dating to the early Christian period.

EDCS-13500341.summary: This inscription marks a designated burial plot, likely in a Christian cemetery, referencing the city of Antioch, possibly due to a connection or a symbolic name.

EDCS-13500342.summary: This inscription marks a designated burial plot, likely in a Christian cemetery, referencing the city of Colonia, possibly due to a connection or a symbolic name.

EDCS-13500344.summary: This inscription marks a designated burial plot, likely in a Christian cemetery, referencing the city of Florence, possibly due to a connection or a symbolic name.

EDCS-13500345.translation: Place of Liberata, granddaughter of Romanus the presbyter.
EDCS-13500345.summary: This inscription marks a designated burial plot, likely in a Christian cemetery, belonging to Liberata, granddaughter of a priest named Romanus.

EDCS-13500353.translation: Astius Dinamius, priest of the province of Africa.
EDCS-13500353.summary: An inscription identifying Astius Dinamius, who held a significant priestly office in the Roman province of Africa.

EDCS-13500354.translation: Florentia, faithful, lived 64 years, rested in peace on the 15th day before the Kalends of March.
EDCS-13500354.summary: A funerary epitaph for Florentia, recording her lifespan and date of death on February 15th, suggesting a late Roman or early Christian context.

EDCS-13500355.translation: Innocentius rested in peace, died on the 4th day before the Ides of March, lived 72 years.
EDCS-13500355.summary: A funerary epitaph for Innocentius, recording his lifespan and date of death on March 11th, suggesting a late Roman or early Christian context.

EDCS-13500356.translation: Ferranda, faithful in the service of Christ.
EDCS-13500356.summary: A funerary epitaph for Ferranda, indicating her devotion as a Christian.

EDCS-13500358.translation: Florentilla, placed in peace on the 11th day before the Kalends of March.
EDCS-13500358.summary: A funerary epitaph for Florentilla, recording her date of repose on February 19th, suggesting a late Roman or early Christian context.

EDCS-13500382.translation: My hope is in my God.
EDCS-13500382.summary: This is a short religious inscription expressing personal faith.

EDCS-13600153.summary: A very brief inscription, possibly a greeting or dedication.

EDCS-13600154.translation: And having constructed and fabricated all the honors deserved, and for the public of the town of Bobbio, the perpetual flamen and citizen, they had a perpetual statue of the town erected by decree and confirmed by Flavius Eusignius, a most excellent and most ample proconsul of the province of Africa.
EDCS-13600154.summary: This inscription records the erection of a perpetual statue in Bobbio, honoring a local official and confirmed by the proconsul of Africa, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-13600155.summary: This is a brief dedication to the goddess Diana, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-13600159.translation: Sacred to Sol Invictus, the Restorer.
EDCS-13600159.summary: A dedication to the sun god Sol Invictus, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-13600160.translation: To Emperor Caesar Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Augustus Pius, and to Aelius Aurelius Verus Caesar, and to Lucius Aelius Caesar, sons of Emperor Caesar Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Augustus Pius, Caius Antonius, aedile and flamen of Augustus, erected three statues, which he had promised to Augustus and his children for the honor of his aedileship, costing 12,000 sesterces, at a cost of 10,407 sesterces and 400 asses, and to supplement the sum of his promise, a silver image of Faustina, wife of Aurelius Verus Caesar, son of Emperor Antoninus Augustus Pius, the Second...
EDCS-13600160.summary: This inscription details the dedication of three statues and a silver image by Caius Antonius, an aedile and flamen, to honor the imperial family, likely dating to the mid-2nd century AD.

EDCS-13600173.translation: To Domitius Fronton, Stoic philosopher, citizen of Hipponium, by decree of the decurions, with public money.
EDCS-13600173.summary: This inscription records a public monument erected by the town council in honor of Domitius Fronton, a Stoic philosopher from Hipponium.

EDCS-13600226.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Dead. Hospita, servant of our Caesar, lived 30 years. Mario made this for his most pious wife.
EDCS-13600226.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Hospita, wife of Mario, who lived 30 years and was a servant of the emperor.

EDCS-13600227.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Dead. Aelia Leporina lived 37 years, 4 months, and 27 days. Marcus Aurelius Maximus, freedman of Augustus, made this for his deserving wife. She is buried here.
EDCS-13600227.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Aelia Leporina, wife of Marcus Aurelius Maximus, a freedman of Augustus, detailing her age and burial.

EDCS-13600228.translation: The Senate and the people decreed that Jupiter Optimus Maximus should be placed in this location for the health of the Augusti, under the supervision of Caius Umbrius Tertullus, a distinguished man, the curator of the public affairs.
EDCS-13600228.summary: This inscription records a public decree to erect a statue of Jupiter Optimus Maximus for the well-being of the emperors, overseen by a local official.

EDCS-13600239.translation: Sacred to Saturn Augustus. Lucius Aemilius Maximus, priest, paid his vow willingly.
EDCS-13600239.summary: This is a dedication to Saturn Augustus by a priest named Lucius Aemilius Maximus, who is fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-13600240.text_edition: \n Dominis sanctis martyribus Silvano et Fortunato T Bonifatius votum solvit a quibus petimus ut orationes nostras in mente habeatis martyres cum comites vestros\n
EDCS-13600240.translation: To the holy lords Silvanus and Fortunatus. Bonifatius fulfilled his vow and asks that you, martyrs, remember our prayers, along with your companions.
EDCS-13600240.summary: This inscription is a votive dedication to the martyrs Silvanus and Fortunatus, requesting their intercession.

EDCS-13600241.inscription_type: inscriptiones christianae, tituli sacri, tituli sepulcrales
EDCS-13600241.translation: The memorial of Victorinus, who died a martyr in peace, having held the office of 'professus' (likely a religious or administrative role), on the eighth day before the Ides of May, on a Sunday, at the eighth hour, in the province in the year 271.
EDCS-13600241.summary: This inscription marks the memorial of Victorinus, a martyr, and provides details about his death date and possibly a provincial dating system.

EDCS-13600242.translation: The master fulfilled the vow of Amacius Restitutus Secundianus.
EDCS-13600242.summary: This is a votive inscription from an unknown location, recording the fulfillment of a vow.

EDCS-13600260.translation: Sequens, a memorator of OECIS, son of M. Neorum Mon, erected this for all his parents, and also presented his day of victories with sacrifices for his ancestors, fifty-one bulls and thirty-eight goats.
EDCS-13600260.summary: This inscription from an unknown location records a dedication and a funerary feast with animal sacrifices, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13600296.translation: The town council of Hippo Regius dedicated this to Marcus Aurelius Consius Quartus, a man most distinguished in all glories, excellent in administration, admirable in virtue, outstanding in integrity, a most illustrious decurion, corrector of the Flaminia and Picenum, corrector of Venetia and Istria, consular governor of Belgica Prima, vicar of the Spains, proconsul of the province of Africa, and judging with vice-sacred authority.
EDCS-13600296.summary: This dedication from Hippo Regius (modern Annaba, Algeria) honors Marcus Aurelius Consius Quartus, a high-ranking official, likely in the late Roman period.

EDCS-13600413.translation: Quintus Salinius Sabinus erected the altar in fulfillment of a vow.
EDCS-13600413.summary: This is a votive inscription from an unknown location, recording the erection of an altar.

EDCS-13600418.translation: Iobius, a most distinguished and loyal man, lived for 51 years and 6 months and departed in peace on the 4th day before the Ides of November in the 20th year at Carthage.
EDCS-13600418.summary: This is a funerary epitaph from Carthage, recording the lifespan and death date of Iobius.

EDCS-13700309.text_edition: \n Africanus Fabius Quinti filius Maximus consul VIIvir epulonum pro consule XXCVII\n
EDCS-13700309.translation: Africanus Fabius Maximus, son of Quintus, consul, member of the college of seven epulones (priests who supervised banquets), served as proconsul [for the province of X].
EDCS-13700309.summary: This inscription records the career of Africanus Fabius Maximus, a Roman official who held several important positions.

EDCS-13700311.translation: In memory of the most blessed martyrs Peter and Paul.
EDCS-13700311.summary: This is a dedicatory inscription, likely from an ecclesiastical building, honoring Saints Peter and Paul, probably dating to the post-Constantinian era.

EDCS-13700314.translation: During the happy age of our lords Flavius Constantius the greatest victorious Augustus, in his seventh consulship, and Julian the most noble Caesar, in his second consulship, Quintus Licinius Aurintius Victorinus, curator of the state, erected and dedicated this with the most splendid council.
EDCS-13700314.summary: This inscription from an unknown location records the erection and dedication of a monument by Quintus Licinius Aurintius Victorinus, curator rei publicae, during the consulships of Constantius II and Julian, likely in the mid-4th century CE.

EDCS-13700315.translation: In the most eminent age of our lords Valentinian, Valens, and Gratian, always Augusti, with the most noble boy [and Augustus] always Augusti, under the administration of Petronius Claudius, a most distinguished proconsul, and his most distinguished legates, Fulvius Quodvultdeus, curator of the state, completed and dedicated this most beautiful praetorium from its foundations, with his own initiative and the entire council, happily.
EDCS-13700315.summary: This inscription from an unknown location records the completion and dedication of a praetorium by Fulvius Quodvultdeus, curator rei publicae, during the reign of Valentinian, Valens, and Gratian, likely in the late 4th century CE.

EDCS-13700317.translation: Sacred to Saturn Augustus. Lucius Sulpicius Secundinus made the column with his own money, contributed to the expense, and dedicated it.
EDCS-13700317.summary: This is a dedication to Saturn Augustus from an unknown location, recording the construction and dedication of a column by Lucius Sulpicius Secundinus at his own expense, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13700345.translation: To Aelius Silvanus with his family.
EDCS-13700345.summary: This is a dedication or funerary inscription from an unknown location, honoring Aelius Silvanus and his family.

EDCS-13700355.translation: To Calpurnia Clara, a most rare maiden. Sextus Calpurnius Aponianus, son of Sextus, of the Quirina tribe, perpetual priest of Augustus, priest of the deified Severus, who had held all offices, granted a plot to his most cherished daughter by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-13700355.summary: A funerary monument for a daughter, indicating the father held public office and religious positions.

EDCS-13700356.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Dead. Volcius Messor, by my will, I have given a legacy to the Germanian Curia, I give and bequeath 250 denarii; I give and bequeath 250 denarii to the Marian Curia. I ask of you, best curials, and entrust to your good faith, that you honor my memory at least five times each year, a promise I have made to you. He lived 20 years. Here lies Volcius Maurus, his freedman, who made this for his patron.
EDCS-13700356.summary: A will bequeathing funds for funeral rites and stipulating annual remembrances for the deceased Volcius Maurus, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-13700357.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Dead. Iulius Gallianus, cavalryman of the I Augusta Ituraeorum ala, lived 45 years, served 23 years. C. Beliabo, heir, and Mantaeus Secundus, heir, from the army of Lower Pannonia.
EDCS-13700357.summary: A funerary inscription for Iulius Gallianus, a cavalryman in a Roman auxiliary unit, dating to the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-13700358.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Dead. MI, of the I ala of Roman citizens, 47 years old, with 28 years of service. Iulius Martialis, duplicarius of the Britannica miliaria ala, his heir, and Primitius, his freedman.
EDCS-13700358.summary: A funerary inscription for a soldier of the I ala of Roman citizens, identified as MI, with his heir and freedman listed, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-13700367.translation: Sacred to Mercurius Augustus, which the god Victor heard; I have rendered my vow and made the offering.
EDCS-13700367.summary: A votive inscription to Mercurius Augustus by Victor, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-13700368.summary: A dedication to Ceres Augusta, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-13700371.summary: An inscription recording the title of Lucius Vehilius, who held the office of quaestor pro praetore, likely from the Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-13700372.text_edition: \n ------ legato iu]ridico dioceseos Hipponensis curatori rei publicae Hipponensium regiorum item municipiorum Thubursicensium Kalamensium Tipasitanorum Marcus Ulpius Spenicus Iunior cliens domus eius locus datus decreto decurionum\n
EDCS-13700372.translation: To Marcus Ulpius Spenicus Junior, client of the imperial household, who was legal official of the diocese of Hippo, curator of the public affairs of the people of Hippo Regius, and also of the municipalities of Thubursicum, Kalamenses, and Tipasa. The place was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-13700372.summary: This inscription grants land to Marcus Ulpius Spenicus Junior, a high-ranking imperial official, by decree of the local councils.

EDCS-13700373.translation: To Gaius Annius Titianus, perpetual flamen of Augustus, aedile twice, Roman knight. Bennius Rufus Pacatianus, designated aedile, and Gaius Allius Renatus Tessellius, to their friend of the rarest example.
EDCS-13700373.summary: A dedication to Gaius Annius Titianus, a prominent local official, by his colleagues and friends, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-13700374.translation: To a most splendid Roman knight, who most innocently discharged all his offices. Marcus Ulpius Felix Charidius, who surpassed fraternal love towards him, to his dearest friend from his earliest age, granted a plot by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-13700374.summary: A funerary monument for a Roman knight, honoring his integrity and friendship, with burial space granted by local authorities.

EDCS-13700407.text_edition: \n Dei Herculis simulacrum Marcus Pacatus Amil\n
EDCS-13700407.translation: The statue of the god Hercules. Marcus Pacatus [erected it].
EDCS-13700407.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a statue of the god Hercules by Marcus Pacatus.

EDCS-13700408.translation: To the divine spirit of Nimira, daughter of Proculus, son of Imibal.
EDCS-13700408.summary: A funerary dedication to a deceased individual named Nimira, likely from a period of Roman provincial administration.

EDCS-13700435.translation: The town council, recognizing her civic spirit, decreed that a statue should be publicly erected in honor of her. Vibia Severa, content with the honor, erected it at her own expense. In order to reward the excellent affection, piety, and generosity of his daughter, he (or she) established that the decurions should annually receive donations of money for feasts in honor of Augustus, and that the body of Augustales should receive two gold coins each year for feasts.
EDCS-13700435.summary: This inscription records a decree by town councilors to honor Vibia Severa with a statue and her subsequent erection of it, along with provisions for annual feasts and gifts for the Augustales, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-13800077.translation: Marcius Mansuetus, a soldier of the First Urban Cohort, stationed in the century of Kapiton, gladly paid his vow to Balamon Augustus.
EDCS-13800077.summary: This inscription is a dedication by a soldier of the First Urban Cohort to the deity Balamon Augustus, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-13800079.translation: To Marcus Asinius Horatius Rufinus Valerius Verus Sabinianus, son of Sextus, admitted among the praetorians by the Emperor Marcus Aurelius Commodus Antoninus Augustus Pius, honored with the priesthood of the Fetiales, curator of the Appian Way, and consul, by the devotees of his household, for his merits.
EDCS-13800079.summary: This inscription is a dedication honoring Marcus Asinius Rufinus Valerius Verus Sabinianus for his distinguished career under Emperor Commodus, likely from the late 2nd century CE.

EDCS-13800172.translation: To our Lord Diocletian the Emperor.
EDCS-13800172.summary: This is a short dedication to Emperor Diocletian, likely from the Tetrarchic period (late 3rd to early 4th century CE).

EDCS-13800173.translation: To the president of the same province, devoted to his divinity and majesty.
EDCS-13800173.summary: This inscription records devotion to a provincial governor, likely from the Imperial period, possibly connected to the previous inscription.

EDCS-13800212.translation: Behold here our funeral, our wounds, our newborn, forever remaining immortal in our hearts. Alas, you deserved it, and you left a sweet, great sorrow; I move a greater work, a greater work I move, a greater order is born for me. Who took you from your own, this mother who rejoiced for her future marriage to a husband? Who would not weep at such misfortunes, for a beloved child, beautiful, and not yet having completed twelve full years? Thus she met a fatal fate, an untimely death, now ready for a husband, now in her nubile years. Constantina the faithful lived in peace for 12 years.
EDCS-13800212.summary: This is an epitaph for Constantina, a faithful woman who died at the age of 12, lamenting her untimely death and expressing enduring grief, likely from the late Roman Empire.

EDCS-13900042.translation: Flavius Nucidus gave this gift to Mercury Augustus.
EDCS-13900042.summary: This is a dedication by Flavius Nucidus to the god Mercury Augustus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13900043.translation: Publius Sextilius Fel Amplius, apparitor, for the honor of A.
EDCS-13900043.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Publius Sextilius Amplius, an apparitor, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13900059.text_edition: \n Domino nostro Flavio Iulio Constantio Pio Felici Augusto Furnos devota XXXVI\n
EDCS-13900059.translation: To our lord Flavius Julius Constantius, the Pious, Fortunate, August. Thirty-six offerings from Furnos.
EDCS-13900059.summary: This is a dedication to the emperor Constantius, possibly related to a religious cult or offering.

EDCS-13900063.translation: In these estates, Suzen, the vicarius in charge of the inherited properties of Auctus and the Boritani.
EDCS-13900063.summary: This inscription identifies Suzen as a vicarius managing inherited properties, likely from a private estate during the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13900064.translation: Legal official for Italy in the Transpadane region, praetorian legate for the province of Africa, aedile, quaestor for the province of Asia, tribune of the broad stripe in the II Augusta legion.
EDCS-13900064.summary: This inscription lists the distinguished career of an unnamed individual holding various high-ranking administrative and military positions, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13900065.translation: To Celsinilla, most illustrious woman, and
EDCS-13900065.summary: This is a fragment of a dedication, likely to a woman of high status, with the recipient and purpose incomplete.

EDCS-13900066.translation: To our Lord Flavius Julius Constantius Pius Felix, Lord of the Forum and Victory
EDCS-13900066.summary: This is a dedication to the emperor Constantius II, likely from a public or private individual, dating to his reign (337-361 AD).

EDCS-13900067.translation: To the Native God, Flavius Eusebius, most distinguished man, citizen
EDCS-13900067.summary: This inscription is a dedication to a 'Native God' by Flavius Eusebius, a prominent citizen, possibly dating to the late Roman period.

EDCS-13900068.translation: To the Lord of all things, our Lord Flavius Gratianus Victor and triumphant, ever Augustus; the entire order of the colony of Bullensium Regiorum, devoted to his divine majesty
EDCS-13900068.summary: This is a dedication by the town council of Bullensium Regiorum to Emperor Gratian, expressing their devotion and likely dating to his reign (367-383 AD).

EDCS-13900098.summary: This inscription is a very brief dedication or epitaph, possibly naming or honoring individuals associated with the cult of Invictus.

EDCS-13900099.translation: Hegerit, your servant, made this as a gift of God and Saint Felix
EDCS-13900099.summary: This is a votive inscription by Hegerit, dedicating a work to God and Saint Felix, likely from the later Roman or early Christian period.

EDCS-13900100.summary: This is likely an epitaph for an infant named Pantaleo, possibly associated with a Christian context due to the use of 'Saint'.

EDCS-13900306.translation: Sacred to the Fruit-Bearing God. Marcus Volusius Ampliatus made the temple from the ground up with his own money, and dedicated it himself.
EDCS-13900306.summary: This is a dedication of a temple built and funded by Marcus Volusius Ampliatus to a 'Fruit-Bearing God', likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-13900307.translation: For the health and victory of the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Severus Antoninus Augustus Pius Felix, greatest victor of Parthia, greatest victor of Britain, chief priest, with tribunician power for the 15th time, emperor for the 2nd time, consul for the 3rd time. Sacred to the August Mother of the Gods. The republic of the city of R., by decree of the decurions, with public money, restored the temple with its sanctuary and portico from the ground up.
EDCS-13900307.summary: This inscription records the restoration of a temple to the Mother of the Gods by the city of R. at public expense, under Emperor Caracalla, likely around 212 AD.

EDCS-13900309.translation: For Publius Septimius Geta, most noble Caesar, prince of youth, Augustus, son of Emperor Caesar divus Marcus Antoninus Pius Germanicus Sarmaticus, brother of divus Commodus, grandson of divus Antoninus Pius, great-grandson of divus Hadrianus, great-great-grandson of divus Traianus Parthicus, great-great-great-grandson of divus Nerva, brother of Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus, chief priest, with tribunician power for the 10th time, consul for the 2nd time, proconsul, promoter of the empire, the very strong and most fortunate prince, father of the country; the republic of the city of R., with its own money, made and likewise dedicated [this monument].
EDCS-13900309.summary: This is a dedication by the city of R. to Geta, brother of Caracalla, likely commemorating an event or his elevation, with an extensive genealogy tracing imperial lineage, possibly dating to around 209-211 AD.

EDCS-13900382.translation: Ovillia Iunia, pious, lived 33 years and 5 days. Pelagi.
EDCS-13900382.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Ovillia Iunia, indicating her name, piety, age at death, and possibly a connection to a person named Pelagi.

EDCS-13900439.translation: In the tenth year of the reign of our lord King Guntamund, on the day before the Nones of March (March 6th), Julius Quintianus and Gilesa his wife sold from their Mancian fields in the Tuletianensis estate, under the ownership of Flavius Geminius Catullinus, the flamen, forever, in its own places and names, a place called in Vuresa, a well-site, one masseria with one caprificus tree named ernassoneu oxuno odore and six young fig trees. Among its boundaries on the sea side, water from the aquarius rising, and from the south, leaving behind Lucianus. Quintianus, the seller, and from this day, Geminius Felix bought it for 340 folles. Messius Quintianus and Gilesa his wife received them and took them with them, and in the presence of witnesses, they responded that they sought nothing more from the said price. On the day before they sold, they held, possessed, and it was theirs. And from this day, in the name of Felix, the buyer, they transferred their ownership, they or their heirs, forever. And if anyone wishes to make a claim or declare it his own concerning the aforesaid property, when it is proven, then he shall give the price paid or another equal to it or whatever the property was worth at that time, as compensation for the evicted property, to be given rightly and without malice. Malice is absent, will be absent, and will be future. Geminius Felix, the buyer, stipulated. Quintianus and Gilesa his wife, the sellers, promised. Acted in Tuletianos in the year and day above written. I, Quadratianus, notary, requested by Quintianus and Gilesa his wife, who do not know letters, making their signs below, sold and received the full price. Sign of Quintianus. Sign of Gilesa. I, Paulinianus, by order of my father Quintus, was present at this instrument. I, Urbanianus, was present at this instrument. I, Quadratianus, by order of my father Ianuarius, wrote and signed this instrument. Instrument concerning Quintianus's caprificus from Vuresa.
EDCS-13900439.summary: This is a legal document detailing the sale of land and a caprificus tree in the Tuletianos region during the reign of King Guntamund, involving Julius Quintianus and Gilesa as sellers and Geminius Felix as the buyer, with notarization and witness attestations.

EDCS-13900455.text_edition: \n Flabius sic Saicham bn Macharcum Sonmon tribynus bymysiyrir aban Machrus useb\n
EDCS-13900455.translation: Flabius erected this. Saicham, son of Macharcus Sonmon, tribunes.
EDCS-13900455.summary: This inscription records a dedication or construction by Flabius, mentioning military tribunes named Saicham and others.

EDCS-13900459.translation: Flavius Dasama, son of Uybinim Macrine, the centurion, [served] with the sea-soldiers of Sabare, [in the province] of Sau.
EDCS-13900459.summary: This inscription likely records a military man, Flavius Dasama, a centurion in a naval unit ('sea-soldiers') from the province of Sau.

EDCS-13900475.summary: This is a votive dedication of a gift to the goddess Latona Augusta.

EDCS-13900476.translation: To Valerius Firmus, an equestrian of the Thracian ala, from the rank of the singulares, from the province of Mauretania Caesariensis, for 5 years of service. He lived 25 years. Valerius Victor, his brother, contributed.
EDCS-13900476.summary: This is a funerary monument for Valerius Firmus, an equestrian soldier of the Thracian ala, who served in Mauretania Caesariensis and died at age 25, with the monument erected by his brother.

EDCS-13900477.translation: His relative Fortunatus, good and faithful, buried in his own land.
EDCS-13900477.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Fortunatus, described as a good and faithful relative, buried on his own property.

EDCS-13900478.text_edition: \n Sabinae Augustae Hadriani Augusti decreto decurionum pecunia publica\n
EDCS-13900478.translation: To Sabina Augusta, wife of Hadrian Augustus. By decree of the decurions, at public expense.
EDCS-13900478.summary: This inscription records the erection of a monument to Empress Sabina at public expense, by order of the local council.

EDCS-13900479.translation: To Lucius Aelius Caesar, son of Emperor Caesar Trajan Hadrianus Augustus, Pontifex Maximus, with tribunician power for the 21st time, Father of the Fatherland, grandson of the deified Trajan Parthicus, great-grandson of the deified Nerva, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-13900479.summary: This is an honorary inscription dedicating something to Lucius Aelius Caesar, son of Emperor Hadrian, highlighting his lineage and political/religious titles, erected by a decree of the local council.

EDCS-13900480.translation: He who conceals the king's secrets, whom the world adores, here finds rest and here eternal peace. May the house of the Villatic man, the toga-clad, the prefect, and God [show] mercy.
EDCS-13900480.summary: This is an inscription with religious and perhaps funerary connotations, speaking of secrets, adoration, rest, and peace, with a plea for mercy directed towards God and possibly a deceased 'Villatic man'.

EDCS-13900484.translation: From the workshop of Titus Cornelius Saturninus.
EDCS-13900484.summary: This inscription indicates the origin or maker of an object, stating it comes from the workshop of Titus Cornelius Saturninus.

EDCS-13900485.translation: To Lucius Caesennius, son of Publius, Secundio Furianus, praefectus iure dicundo, quaestor, duovir, permanent flamen, by his will, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-13900485.summary: This is an honorary inscription for Lucius Caesennius Secundio Furianus, a local magistrate and priest, likely dedicated posthumously by a decree of the decurions in accordance with his will.

EDCS-13900486.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Nonnia Primitiva, priestess of the Punic Ceres, pious and fortunate, lived 97 years, 3 months, and 7 days.
EDCS-13900486.summary: A tombstone for Nonnia Primitiva, a priestess of Ceres, giving her age at death.

EDCS-13900500.translation: To Gaius Marius, son of Gaius, seven times consul, founder of the colony. Quintus Furfanius Bellicus, son of Quintus, of the Lemonia tribe, who held all the offices in his colony, as perpetual priest of Augustus, in the name of Caninia Tertia, daughter of Lucius, his wife and perpetual priestess of Augustus, erected this at his own expense by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-13900500.summary: A dedication by Quintus Furfanius Bellicus for his wife, Caninia Tertia, honoring her role as perpetual priestess of Augustus, and listing his own civic achievements.

EDCS-13900612.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Adiutoris, an equestrian of the first wing of the Cannanafates, lived 41 years and served for 23 years. Placed by his freedman Cabanus, his heir, who deserved well.
EDCS-13900612.summary: A tombstone for Adiutoris, an equestrian soldier, giving his age and length of service, erected by his freedman heir.

EDCS-14000033.translation: To our lord Flavius Valens Pius, triumphant victor, ever Augustus. The council of the municipium of Nattabutum erected and dedicated this.
EDCS-14000033.summary: A dedication by the town council of Nattabutum to the emperor Flavius Valens.

EDCS-14000035.translation: Martialis, priest of Saturn, lived 65 years.
EDCS-14000035.summary: A tombstone for Martialis, a priest of Saturn, giving his age at death.

EDCS-14000038.translation: Baric, son of Muc, lived 46 years. He lies here.
EDCS-14000038.summary: A tombstone for Baric, giving his age at death.

EDCS-14000039.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Caecilius Aquensis lived [duration missing] years.
EDCS-14000039.summary: An incomplete tombstone for Caecilius Aquensis, recording his dedication to the Divine Manes and giving his name.

EDCS-14000040.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Quintus Calpurnius [details missing].
EDCS-14000040.summary: An incomplete tombstone for Quintus Calpurnius, dedicated to the Divine Manes.

EDCS-14000041.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Kasta Victoria lived 75 years. She lies here.
EDCS-14000041.summary: A tombstone for Kasta Victoria, giving her age at death.

EDCS-14000042.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Publius Clodius Priscus lived 30 years. He lies here.
EDCS-14000042.summary: A tombstone for Publius Clodius Priscus, giving his age at death.

EDCS-14000044.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Gargilia Pacata lived for...
EDCS-14000044.summary: A funerary inscription for Gargilia Pacata, recording her age at death.

EDCS-14000045.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Helvonia Pantia lived for 43 years; she lies here.
EDCS-14000045.summary: A funerary inscription for Helvonia Pantia, recording her age at death and burial.

EDCS-14000046.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Iulia Spes lived for 35 years; may your bones rest well.
EDCS-14000046.summary: A funerary inscription for Iulia Spes, recording her age at death and a wish for her repose.

EDCS-14000047.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Livia Urbica lived for...
EDCS-14000047.summary: A funerary inscription for Livia Urbica, recording her age at death.

EDCS-14000048.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Publius Marius Priscus, *COR O VC* (perhaps 'consul' or similar honorific).
EDCS-14000048.summary: A funerary inscription for Publius Marius Priscus, possibly including an honorific title.

EDCS-14000049.translation: Modia Optata lived for 85 years; she lies here.
EDCS-14000049.summary: A funerary inscription for Modia Optata, recording her age at death and burial.

EDCS-14000050.translation: Salv lived for...; he lies here.
EDCS-14000050.summary: A funerary inscription for Salv, recording his burial and an incomplete lifespan.

EDCS-14000051.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Selecus lived for 70 years; he lies here.
EDCS-14000051.summary: A funerary inscription for Selecus, recording his age at death and burial.

EDCS-14000052.translation: Quintus Tertilius Felix lived for 30 years; he lies here.
EDCS-14000052.summary: A funerary inscription for Quintus Tertilius Felix, recording his age at death and burial.

EDCS-14000054.translation: Marcus Vibius Montanus lived 35 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-14000054.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the life and burial of Marcus Vibius Montanus.

EDCS-14000057.translation: IIC Pius, his brother, lived for...
EDCS-14000057.summary: A funerary epitaph fragment recording the name and incomplete lifespan of a brother named Pius.

EDCS-14000059.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Marcus Caesius Audentius lived 71 years.
EDCS-14000059.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Marcus Caesius Audentius, dedicated to the spirits of the departed.

EDCS-14000060.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Caius I...
EDCS-14000060.summary: A funerary epitaph fragment dedicated to the spirits of the departed, beginning with the name Caius I...

EDCS-14000061.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Iulius Gaeminius.
EDCS-14000061.summary: A funerary epitaph dedicated to the spirits of the departed, recording the name Iulius Gaeminius.

EDCS-14000062.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Verna the dutiful lived 60 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-14000062.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the life and burial of Verna, dedicated to the spirits of the departed.

EDCS-14100252.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Quintus Iulius Terox lived for...
EDCS-14100252.summary: A funerary epitaph fragment dedicated to the spirits of the departed, recording the name Quintus Iulius Terox and an incomplete lifespan.

EDCS-14100253.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Caius Domitius Maximus.
EDCS-14100253.summary: A funerary epitaph dedicated to the spirits of the departed, recording the name Caius Domitius Maximus.

EDCS-14100254.summary: A funerary epitaph fragment recording a lifespan of 87 years, with the name of the deceased missing.

EDCS-14100255.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Iulius Baric, son of Caius, lived 36 years.
EDCS-14100255.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the name, parentage, and lifespan of Iulius Baric.

EDCS-14100256.translation: To Publius Rusticus, son of Pomponius Garta.
EDCS-14100256.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication for Publius Rusticus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-14100257.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. For Popillia Sphaerata, aged ten years.
EDCS-14100257.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a young girl named Popillia Sphaerata, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-14100259.translation: Sacred to Saturn and the Emperor. Marcus Flavius Tertius made this for the well-being of his lord, the Emperor Gaius Julius Verus Maximinus Augustus.
EDCS-14100259.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Saturn and Emperor Maximinus, made by Marcus Flavius Tertius for the emperor's well-being, likely during Maximinus' reign (235-238 AD).

EDCS-14200004.translation: To Aurelius Caesar, son of Antoninus Augustus Pius. Vitalis, his freedman (?), home-born, X months old.
EDCS-14200004.summary: This is a dedication to Aurelius Caesar, likely a young imperial prince, by a freedman's household slave.

EDCS-14200007.summary: This inscription is a tribal or communal designation, likely related to the inhabitants of Lepcimagna in Roman North Africa.

EDCS-14200008.summary: This inscription is a dedication or dedication fragment to the 'fatherland', possibly from Roman Africa.

EDCS-14200010.text_edition: \n Dis sacrum Manibus Claudius Stiddin monimentum sic fecit se vivo posterius suis Dis sacrum Manibus Claudius Ladas monimentum sic fecit se vivo posterisque suis\n
EDCS-14200010.translation: Sacred to the departed gods. Claudius Stiddin made this monument for himself while alive, and for his descendants later. Claudius Ladas made this monument for himself while alive, and for his descendants.
EDCS-14200010.summary: This is a funerary monument inscription recording the construction of a tomb by Claudius Stiddin and Claudius Ladas for themselves and their families.

EDCS-14200016.text_edition: \n Incomparabilis virtutis et innocentiae viro Lucio Clodio Clodiano veterano ex decurione qui vixit annis XLVIIII mensibus VIII Valeria Processa uxor et Clodius Victor Clodianus Processus V emeritus patri piissimo\n
EDCS-14200016.translation: To a man of incomparable virtue and integrity, Lucius Clodius Clodianus, a veteran ex-decurion, who lived 49 years and 8 months. His wife Valeria Processa and his son Clodius Victor Clodianus Processus V emeritus, to their most devoted father.
EDCS-14200016.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Lucius Clodius Clodianus, a veteran, set up by his wife and son.

EDCS-14200019.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Quintus Porcius Iovinus lived for 10 years. Quintus Porcius Reginus, a most devoted father, made this for his peaceful son.
EDCS-14200019.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Quintus Porcius Iovinus, set up by his father, Quintus Porcius Reginus, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-14200020.text_edition: \n Diis Manibus sacrum Balynae vixsit sic annorum sic XXXVIII Caius Caecilius Lupus uxori suae obsequentissimae feccit sic structorique sic\n
EDCS-14200020.translation: Sacred to the departed gods. Balyna lived 38 years. Caius Caecilius Lupus made this for his most obedient wife and for the builder.
EDCS-14200020.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Balyna, set up by her husband Caius Caecilius Lupus, also mentioning the builder.

EDCS-14200021.text_edition: \n IV militabo in laboro obsequius per quae ista omnia perfecta sunt a me sic FV ARE felix Vrbanus Donatinaq(ue) eius qui patrem exuperant\n
EDCS-14200021.translation: I will serve and labor diligently, by which all these things were accomplished by me. Felix Urbanus and his Donatina. (These children) surpass their father.
EDCS-14200021.summary: This is a dedication, possibly to a deity or for a public work, by Felix Urbanus and his wife Donatina, celebrating their children who surpass their father.

EDCS-14200023.translation: Greek inscription of uncertain meaning, possibly related to personal names or deities.
EDCS-14200023.summary: This inscription appears to be in Greek and possibly features personal names or deities, with its exact meaning unclear due to its brevity and possible damage.

EDCS-14200024.translation: Sequens, the memorialist of Oecis, is the son of Monos, Vocis. He dedicated this to all his parents and also exhibited sacrifices on the day of his victories: fifty-one bulls and thirty-eight goats.
EDCS-14200024.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Sequens, son of Monos and Vocis, commemorating his parents and listing sacrifices of bulls and goats, likely related to a victory celebration during the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-14200026.translation: Fragmentary inscription, possibly Punic or Liby-Punic, with unclear names and dedications.
EDCS-14200026.summary: This inscription is fragmentary and likely in Punic or Liby-Punic, containing unclear names and potential dedicatory phrases from Roman North Africa.

EDCS-14200127.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Memory of Morna, son of Mocimemtu, who was taken by Culia, Eiciimioivbom made this.
EDCS-14200127.summary: This is a funerary inscription, possibly in Punic or a related language, recording the death of Morna and a dedication by Eiciimioivbom, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-14200130.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Iulia Faustina lived piously for 28 years, 11 months, and 25 days. Iulius Honoratus, her freedman, took care of the arrangements.
EDCS-14200130.summary: A funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Iulia Faustina and mentioning her freedman who arranged her burial, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-14200131.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari Lucio Septimio Severo Pio Pertinaci Augusto tribunicia potestate VIIII imperatori consuli II patri patriae et Imperatori Caesari Marco Aurelio Antonino Augusto tribunicia potestate IIII et Lucio Septimio [Getae] Caesari Augusto Quinto Anicio Fausto legato Augustorum consulare legionis III Augustae piae vindicis\n
EDCS-14200131.translation: To Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus, holding tribunician power for the 9th time, consul for the 2nd time, father of the fatherland, and to Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus, holding tribunician power for the 4th time, and to Lucius Septimius [Geta] Caesar Augustus. To Quintus Anicius Faustus, consular legate of the 3rd Augustan Legion, pious and avenging.
EDCS-14200131.summary: This is a dedication to the emperors Septimius Severus, Caracalla, and Geta, and to the legate Quintus Anicius Faustus, likely on a military monument or building.

EDCS-14200135.text_edition: \n Imperatore Caesare divi Traiani Parthici filio divi Nervae nepote Traiano Hadriano Augusto pontifice maximo tribunicia potestate IIII consule III Quintus Servilius Candidus sua inpensa aquam quaesitam et elevatam in coloniam perduxit\n
EDCS-14200135.translation: While Emperor Caesar Trajan Hadrianus Augustus, son of the deified Trajan Parthicus, nephew of the deified Nerva, was pontifex maximus, consul for the 3rd time, holding tribunician power for the 4th time, Quintus Servilius Candidus, at his own expense, brought water, which had been sought and raised, into the colony.
EDCS-14200135.summary: This inscription records that Quintus Servilius Candidus funded the bringing of a water supply to a colony during the reign of Emperor Hadrian.

EDCS-14200136.translation: To our divine-born lord, our most courageous prince, Valentinian, victorious, pious, blessed, and ever triumphant Augustus, Flavius Vivius Benedictus, a most accomplished man, governor of the province of Tripolitana, forever devoted to his divine majesty and authority.
EDCS-14200136.summary: A dedication to Emperor Valentinian by Flavius Vivius Benedictus, governor of Tripolitana, likely from the 4th century CE.

EDCS-14200137.translation: Quintus Pomponius Rufus, consul, pontifex, sodalis Flavialis, curator of public works, imperial legate with praetorian power of the provinces of Moesia, Dalmatia, and Hispania, legionary legate of the V legion, prefect of the maritime coast of Hispania Citerior and Gallia Narbonensis during the war which Emperor Galba waged for the Republic, proconsul of the province of Africa, through Lucius Asinius Rufus, his legate with praetorian power.
EDCS-14200137.summary: An extensive career summary inscribed for Quintus Pomponius Rufus, detailing his high-ranking political and military offices under Emperor Galba and later as proconsul of Africa, probably from the late 1st century CE.
