EDCS-14900270.text_edition: \n Senatus consultum de nundinis saltus Beguensis in territorio Casensi descriptum et recognitum ex libro sententiarum in senatu dictarum Kani Iuni Nigri Cai Pomponi Camerini consulum in quo scripta erant Africani iura et id quod infra scriptum est Idibus Octobribus in comitiorum sic in curia Iulia scribundo adfuerunt Quintus Gargilius Quinti filius Quirina Antiquus Tiberius Claudius Tiberi filius Palatina Quartinus Caius Oppius Cai filius Velina Severus Caius Herennius Cai filius Palatina Caecilianus Marcus Iulius Marci filius Quirina Clarus Publius Cassius Publi filius Claudia Dexter quaestor Publius Nonius Marci filius Oufentina Macrinus quaestor in senatu fuerunt CC senatus consultum per discessionem factum quod Publius Cassius Secundus Publius Delphius Peregrinus Alfius Alennius Maximus Curtius Valerianus Proculus Marcus Nonius Mucianus conssules verba fecerunt desiderio amicorum Lucili Africani clarissimi viri qui petunt ut ei permittantur in provincia Africa regione Beguensi territorio Musulamiorum ad Casas nundinas IIII Nonas Novembres et XII Kalendas Decembres ex eo omnibus mensibus IIII Nonas et XII Kalendas sui cuiusque mensis instituere habere quid fieri placeret de ea re ita censuerunt permittendum Lucilio Africano clarissimo viro in provincia Africa regione Beguensi territorio Musulamiorum ad Casas nundinas IIII Nonas Novembres et XII Kalendas Decembres et ex eo omnibus mensibus IIII Nonas et XII Kalendas sui cuiusque mensis instituere et habere eoque vicinis advenisque nundinandi dumtaxat causa coire convenire sine iniuria et incommodo cuiusquam liceat actum Idibus Octobribus Publio Cassio Secundo Marco Nonio Muciano eodem exemplo de eadem re duae tabellae signatae sunt signatores Titi Flavi Comini scribae Cai Iuli Fortunati scribae Marci Caesi Helvi Euhelpisti Quinti Metili Onesimi Cai Iuli Periblepti Luci Verati Philerotis Titi Flavi Crescentis\n
EDCS-14900270.translation: A decree of the Senate concerning the market days of the Beguensis estate in the territory of Casensi, inscribed and reviewed from the record of decisions made in the Senate during the consulship of Kanius Junius Niger and Caius Pomponius Camerinus. In it were written the rights of Lucilius Africanus and what is written below. On the Ides of October, in the Julian Curia, the following were present for the recording: Quintus Gargilius Antiquus, son of Quintus, of the Quirina tribe; Tiberius Claudius Quartinus, son of Tiberius, of the Palatina tribe; Caius Oppius Severus, son of Caius, of the Velina tribe; Caius Herennius Caecilianus, son of Caius, of the Palatina tribe; Marcus Julius Clarus, son of Marcus, of the Quirina tribe; Publius Cassius Dexter, son of Publius, of the Claudia tribe, quaestor; Publius Nonius Macrinus, son of Marcus, of the Oufentina tribe, quaestor. There were 200 senators present. A decree of the Senate was made by division, because Publius Cassius Secundus, Publius Delphius Peregrinus, Alfius Alennius Maximus, Curtius Valerianus Proculus, and Marcus Nonius Mucianus, consuls, spoke at the request of the friends of Lucilius Africanus, a most distinguished man, who asks that he be permitted to establish two market days in the province of Africa, in the Beguensis region, in the territory of the Musulamii, near Casas: the Nones of November and the Kalends of December, and thereafter on the fourth day before the Nones and the twelfth day before the Kalends of each month, and to hold them. Regarding this matter, they decreed as follows: It shall be permitted to Lucilius Africanus, a most distinguished man, in the province of Africa, in the Beguensis region, in the territory of the Musulamii, near Casas, to establish and hold market days on the fourth day before the Nones of November and the twelfth day before the Kalends of December, and thereafter on the fourth day before the Nones and the twelfth day before the Kalends of each month, and that neighbors and visitors may come together for the sole purpose of trading, without injury or inconvenience to anyone. This was acted upon on the Ides of October. Two tablets were signed by Publius Cassius Secundus and Marcus Nonius Mucianus, on the same principle concerning the same matter. Signatories: Titi Flavi Comini, scribe; Cai Iuli Fortunati, scribe; Marci Caesi Helvi Euhelpisti; Quinti Metili Onesimi; Cai Iuli Periblepti; Luci Verati Philerotis; Titi Flavi Crescentis.
EDCS-14900270.summary: This inscription records a Senate decree from the consulship of Kanius Junius Niger and Caius Pomponius Camerinus, granting permission to Lucilius Africanus to establish two market days per month in a specific region of the province of Africa, detailing the process, participants, and signatories.

EDCS-14900271.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Rogata lived for 29 years, Donata lived for 27 years, Secunda lived for 5 years. Rogatus with his own money, most dutiful.
EDCS-14900271.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespans of Rogata, Donata, and Secunda, with Rogatus paying for the monument.

EDCS-14900272.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Gaius Aurelius Cuttitanus, aged 45, is buried here. His cousin Gaius Aurelius Saturninus made this.
EDCS-14900272.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the death and burial of Gaius Aurelius Cuttitanus, set up by his cousin.

EDCS-14900276.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Aemilia Secunda lived for 58 years.
EDCS-14900276.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Aemilia Secunda.

EDCS-14900277.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Gessius Aevasius lived for 72 years.
EDCS-14900277.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Gessius Aevasius.

EDCS-14900278.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Gaius Gessius Rogatus lived for 65 years and Iulia Saturnina lived for 55 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-14900278.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespans of Gaius Gessius Rogatus and Iulia Saturnina, indicating her burial.

EDCS-14900279.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Martialis lived for 40 years. Pedania erected this for her excellent husband.
EDCS-14900279.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Martialis, erected by his wife Pedania.

EDCS-14900280.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Ialnoas, augur of the vicus.
EDCS-14900280.summary: This is a funerary inscription mentioning Ialnoas, who held the position of augur within his neighborhood (vicus).

EDCS-14900281.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Caresius Rufus lived 80 years, his wife
EDCS-14900281.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Caresius Rufus and mentioning his wife.

EDCS-14900282.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Fesiva lived 60 years.
EDCS-14900282.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Fesiva.

EDCS-14900283.translation: Marcianus, son of Miginis, lived 75 years.
EDCS-14900283.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Marcianus, son of Miginis.

EDCS-14900284.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Nargeudud lived to 80 years and Maior lived 70 years; their sons made this for their father and mother.
EDCS-14900284.summary: A funerary epitaph made by sons for their parents, recording their lifespans.

EDCS-14900285.translation: Speronis, a dutiful daughter, lived 82 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-14900285.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Speronis, a daughter, and stating her burial place.

EDCS-14900286.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Ianuaria, lived 38 years; her daughter made this for her daughter; she is buried here.
EDCS-14900286.summary: A funerary epitaph made by a daughter for her mother, recording her lifespan and burial place.

EDCS-14900288.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Hexitus Flavius Antonius Marchianus, a soldier, lived 42 years. Marctia, his dutiful wife, placed this for her departed and deserving husband.
EDCS-14900288.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by a wife for her deceased husband, a soldier, recording his lifespan.

EDCS-14900290.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Lucius Agrius Vitalis, a priest, lived 93 years; his son placed this for his excellent father; he is buried here.
EDCS-14900290.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by a son for his priest father, recording his lifespan and burial place.

EDCS-14900291.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Secunda, a priestess, lived 63 years; her sons placed this for their dutiful mother.
EDCS-14900291.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by sons for their priestess mother, recording her lifespan.

EDCS-14900292.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Catilius made this for himself while alive; he lived 100 years.
EDCS-14900292.summary: A funerary epitaph where an individual set up their own monument while alive, recording their lifespan.

EDCS-14900293.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Iulia Rogatea lived 40 years. Her dutiful children placed [this]; she rests here.
EDCS-14900293.summary: A funerary epitaph for Iulia Rogatea, set up by her children.

EDCS-14900294.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Lucius Nunnius Quirina Ianuarius lived 80 years. His sons set this up for a good father; he rests here.
EDCS-14900294.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lucius Nunnius Quirina Ianuarius, set up by his sons.

EDCS-14900295.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Caius Nunnius Secundinus, son of Marcus, of Quirina, lived 90 years. His sons set this up; he rests here.
EDCS-14900295.summary: A funerary epitaph for Caius Nunnius Secundinus, set up by his sons.

EDCS-14900296.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Nunnius Secundinus, son of Marcus, of Quirina, Luciolus, lived 89 years. His wife and sons set this up; he rests here. Sacred to the Divine Manes. Sperontia Saturnina lived 76 years. Her sons set this up for a most sweet mother; she rests here.
EDCS-14900296.summary: A funerary epitaph for Nunnius Secundinus, set up by his wife and sons, and another for Sperontia Saturnina, set up by her sons.

EDCS-14900297.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Marcus Volussius Filica lived 70 years. Felix his son and Quarta his wife made this.
EDCS-14900297.summary: A funerary epitaph for Marcus Volussius Filica, made by his son and wife.

EDCS-14900298.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Lucius Caecilius Rogatianus lived 76 years; he rests here. Nia his wife and Caecius set this up for a most sweet father.
EDCS-14900298.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lucius Caecilius Rogatianus, set up by his wife Nia and Caecius.

EDCS-14900299.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Clodia Urbana, dutiful, lived 28 years and two months. Memmius Sextanus placed this with sorrow for his good wife, in remembrance.
EDCS-14900299.summary: A funerary epitaph for Clodia Urbana, placed by her husband Memmius Sextanus.

EDCS-14900301.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Bonia, a maiden, lived 51 years.
EDCS-14900301.summary: A funerary epitaph for Bonia, a maiden.

EDCS-14900303.translation: Sacred to Victoria Augusta. Marcus Domitius Donatus, priest, fulfilled his vow willingly.
EDCS-14900303.summary: A dedication to the goddess Victoria Augusta by the priest Marcus Domitius Donatus.

EDCS-14900305.translation: Sacred to the deified Pius Marcus Antoninus Augustus, father of the Emperor Caesar Lucius Aurelius Commodus Pius Felix Augustus Sarmaticus Germanicus Maximus Britannicus, father of the fatherland. The Augustales set this up from their own funds.
EDCS-14900305.summary: A dedication to the deified Emperor Marcus Aurelius, erected by the Augustales.

EDCS-14900306.translation: To Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pertinax Augustus, chief priest, with the tribunician power for the 3rd time, commander for the 5th time, consul for the 2nd time, father of the country, conqueror of Parthia, Arabia, and Adiabene, by decree of the decurions, at public expense.
EDCS-14900306.summary: This inscription records a public monument dedicated to Emperor Septimius Severus, likely erected by local officials in Emerita Augusta.

EDCS-14900308.translation: To Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Valerius Maximianus Pius Felix Invictus Augustus, the colony of Flavia Augusta Emerita Ammaedara, by decree of the decurions, at public expense.
EDCS-14900308.summary: This inscription is a public dedication to Emperor Maximian by the colony of Emerita Ammaedara, funded by the local treasury.

EDCS-14900312.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Publius Petilius Victorinus, son of Publius, of the Quirina tribe, a soldier of the cohort, lived 33 years.
EDCS-14900312.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Publius Petilius Victorinus, a soldier who died at the age of 33.

EDCS-14900319.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Aelia Festula lived 24 years, 9 months, and 18 days. Herennius Victor, with his sons, placed this for his most beloved wife. She is laid here.
EDCS-14900319.summary: A funerary epitaph for Aelia Festula, placed by her husband Herennius Victor and sons, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-14900320.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Aelia Fortunata lived 43 years and 8 months. She is laid here. Lucius Cascellius Rufus placed this for his most pious and chaste wife. To the Spirits of the Departed.
EDCS-14900320.summary: A funerary epitaph for Aelia Fortunata, erected by her husband Lucius Cascellius Rufus, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-14900321.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Gaius Aelius Naphamos lived 38 years. His devoted wife placed this.
EDCS-14900321.summary: A funerary epitaph for Gaius Aelius Naphamos, erected by his wife, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-14900322.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Publius Aelius Rogatus lived 66 years. He is laid here. Aelius Rogatus placed this for his devoted father.
EDCS-14900322.summary: A funerary epitaph for Publius Aelius Rogatus, erected by his son Aelius Rogatus, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-14900324.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Flavia Hilara lived 22 years. Annius Severus placed this for his most unique wife. She is laid here. To the Spirits of the Departed. Annius Severus lived 32 years, and 11 days. He is laid here.
EDCS-14900324.summary: A double funerary epitaph recording the lives of Flavia Hilara and her husband Annius Severus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-14900325.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Anthus and Sabina placed this for their dearest son. Sabinus lived one year. He is buried here.
EDCS-14900325.summary: This funerary epitaph records the burial of a child named Sabinus, who died at the age of one, dedicated by his parents Anthus and Sabina.

EDCS-14900326.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Modia Saturnina lived 90 years. She is laid here. Her daughters placed this for their dearest mother. To the Spirits of the Departed. Lucius Atilius Macedo lived 70 years. He is laid here. Lucius Atilius Extricatus and Antilia placed this for their devoted father.
EDCS-14900326.summary: A double funerary epitaph for Modia Saturnina, erected by her daughters, and for Lucius Atilius Macedo, erected by his son and daughter, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-14900327.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Antonia Hilara Modiana, daughter of Quintus, lived approximately 30 years. Magnianus placed this for his sister.
EDCS-14900327.summary: A funerary epitaph for Antonia Hilara Modiana, erected by her brother Magnianus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-14900328.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Gaius Camurenus Victoricus lived 70 years. Publius, his son, made this. To the Spirits of the Departed. Gaius Victorinus lived 22 years. His devoted brother made this. To the Spirits of the Departed. Antonia lived 55 years. Her devoted son made this.
EDCS-14900328.summary: A triple funerary epitaph recording the lives and dedications for Gaius Camurenus Victoricus, Gaius Victorinus, and Antonia, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-14900329.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Lucius Aquilius Suavis, son of Lucius, of the Quirina tribe, lived 75 years. His son placed this for his devoted father. He is laid here.
EDCS-14900329.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lucius Aquilius Suavis, erected by his son, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-14900330.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Arria Sperata lived 53 years. She is laid here. Apuleius Licinianus placed this for his devoted wife.
EDCS-14900330.summary: A funerary epitaph for Arria Sperata, erected by her husband Apuleius Licinianus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-14900331.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Alia Victoria lived 55 years. Assidonius Victoricus set this up for his excellent mother. She is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Assidonius Ingenuus lived 18 years and 6 months. Assidonius Liberalis, a devoted father, set this up for his excellent son. He is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Assidonius Liberalis lived about 60 years. Assidonius Victoricus set this up for his dearest father. He is buried here.
EDCS-14900331.summary: This inscription is a tombstone recording the deaths and ages of three individuals: Alia Victoria, Assidonius Ingenuus, and Assidonius Liberalis, with familial relationships and dedications noted.

EDCS-14900332.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Assidonius Liberalis lived 47 years, 4 months, and 5 days. He is buried here. Assidonius Calvus set this up for his dearest brother, my lord.
EDCS-14900332.summary: This tombstone records the death of Assidonius Liberalis, who lived 47 years, 4 months, and 5 days, and was commemorated by his brother, Assidonius Calvus.

EDCS-14900333.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Assidonia Aerope, devout, lived 25 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-14900333.summary: This tombstone records the death of Assidonia Aerope, who lived 25 years, and was noted as devout.

EDCS-14900334.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Aufidius Marius Castulus lived 25 years. He is buried here. A devoted father set this up.
EDCS-14900334.summary: This tombstone records the death of Aufidius Marius Castulus, who lived 25 years, and was commemorated by his father.

EDCS-14900335.translation: Quintus Aveius made this, grieving, for his most sweet and most chaste wife. She is buried here.
EDCS-14900335.summary: This epitaph records a husband's grief and dedication for his deceased wife, Quintus Aveius for his wife.

EDCS-14900337.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus Aurelius Impetratus lived 50 years. His sons set this up for their devoted father. He is buried here.
EDCS-14900337.summary: This tombstone records the death of Quintus Aurelius Impetratus, who lived 50 years, and was commemorated by his sons.

EDCS-14900338.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Aurelia Rogata lived [X] years. Caius Iulius Felix placed this for his pious mother. She is buried here.
EDCS-14900338.summary: This is a funerary epitaph where Caius Iulius Felix honors his deceased mother, Aurelia Rogata.

EDCS-14900339.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Numisia Donata lived 34 years. She is buried here. Lucius Bolanus Felix set this up for his devout wife. Sacred to the departed spirits. Bolana Primula lived 52 years. She is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Bolanus Caelestinus lived 8 years. Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Bolanus lived about 3 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-14900339.summary: This inscription is a tombstone recording the deaths of four individuals from the Bolanus family: Numisia Donata, Bolana Primula, Lucius Bolanus Caelestinus, and Lucius Bolanus, with ages and familial relationships indicated.

EDCS-14900340.translation: Caecilius Fortunatianus Quintanus lived 33 years. His father erected the burial for his son. He is buried here. Victoricus lived 80 years. His sons erected the burial for their father. He is buried here.
EDCS-14900340.summary: This epitaph records two burials: Caecilius Fortunatianus Quintanus, buried by his father, and Victoricus, buried by his sons.

EDCS-14900341.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Caelia Donata, devout, lived 100 years. Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcus Caecilius Ianuarius lived 90 years.
EDCS-14900341.summary: This inscription records the extreme longevity of two individuals, Caelia Donata (100 years) and Marcus Caecilius Ianuarius (90 years), likely on a shared monument or as separate entries.

EDCS-14900342.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Helvia Gemellina lived 50 years. Matrona set this up for her mother. Sacred to the departed spirits. Caelius Datus, a boy, lived 2 years. Matrona set this up. Sacred to the departed spirits. Helvia Maior lived 31 years. Matrona set this up.
EDCS-14900342.summary: This monument commemorates three individuals: Helvia Gemellina, Caelius Datus, and Helvia Maior, with ages and dedications by Matrona, suggesting family relationships.

EDCS-14900343.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Caelius Epicurus, devout, lived 32 years and 6 months. He is buried here. Publius Caelius Numisianus for his excellent brother.
EDCS-14900343.summary: This tombstone records the death of Lucius Caelius Epicurus, who lived 32 years and 6 months, and was commemorated by his brother, Publius Caelius Numisianus.

EDCS-14900344.translation: Marcus Caelius Quadratus, son of Publius, of the Arnensis tribe, lived 50 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-14900344.summary: This tombstone records the death of Marcus Caelius Quadratus, son of Publius, of the Arnensis tribe, who lived 50 years.

EDCS-14900345.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Publius Caelius Victor Praetoricius lived [X] years. He is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Numisia Secunda lived 45 years. Caelia Victorina lived 10 years. A pious father placed this.
EDCS-14900345.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Publius Caelius Victor Praetoricius and two daughters, Numisia Secunda and Caelia Victorina, all honored by a pious father.

EDCS-14900346.translation: To the departed spirits. Sacred. Calpurnia Victorina, also called Faeda, lived 80 years. Gaius Julius Proculus, her husband, placed this for his dutiful wife. She is buried here. To the departed spirits. Sacred. Gaius Julius Proculus lived 101 years, 7 months. He is buried here.
EDCS-14900346.summary: A double tombstone recording the deaths of a wife, Calpurnia Victorina, and her husband, Gaius Julius Proculus, who both died and were buried in this location.

EDCS-14900348.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Sempronia Fortunata lived 55 years. She is buried here. Lucius Camurenus Saedus lived 28 years. Sempronia Fortunata, the mother, placed this for her most pious and dearest son. He is buried here.
EDCS-14900348.summary: This funerary epitaph records the burial of Lucius Camurenus Saedus, dedicated by his mother Sempronia Fortunata, who is also buried there.

EDCS-14900349.translation: To the departed spirits. Sacred. Lucius Carvilius Albinus lived 100 years. To the departed spirits. Sacred. Carvilia Albina lived 18 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-14900349.summary: A tombstone for Lucius Carvilius Albinus and Carvilia Albina, likely father and daughter, recording their ages at death and burial.

EDCS-14900350.translation: He is buried here. Lucius Carvilius Exsoratus placed this for his pious father. [X] years.
EDCS-14900350.summary: This epitaph records Lucius Carvilius Exsoratus dedicating a burial for his father.

EDCS-14900351.translation: To the departed spirits. Sacred. Lucius Cassius Faustus, son of Lucius, of the Quirina tribe, lived 44 years, a good man and indispensable to people and affairs. He is sought by his country, the greatest people; the earth covers him. He left a happy but ungrateful life. Lucius Cassius, his brother, dutifully placed this.
EDCS-14900351.summary: A tombstone for Lucius Cassius Faustus, a man of importance to his community, erected by his brother.

EDCS-14900352.translation: To the departed spirits. Sacred. Claudius Lucanus Tzaninus lived 17 years, 10 months, and 5 days. Claudius Sextilius Lucanus and Claudia Novella placed this for their dearest son.
EDCS-14900352.summary: A tombstone erected by Claudius Sextilius Lucanus and Claudia Novella for their son, Claudius Lucanus Tzaninus, who died at the age of 17.

EDCS-14900353.translation: To the departed spirits. Sacred. Tiberius Claudius Victor lived 70 years. Agria Rogata placed this for her sweetest husband. He is buried here. Whoever lives will live forever.
EDCS-14900353.summary: A tombstone for Tiberius Claudius Victor, erected by his wife Agria Rogata, with a pious inscription about eternal life.

EDCS-14900354.translation: To the departed spirits. Sacred. Cluvius Donatus lived 31 years. His parents placed this for their son. He is buried here.
EDCS-14900354.summary: A tombstone for Cluvius Donatus, erected by his parents after his death at the age of 31.

EDCS-14900356.translation: The most splendid order, by its decree, honored Marcus Cornelius Proculeianus, son of Cornelius Rogatianus, a Roman knight and priest of the old province of Africa, with a statue, on account of his studies, character, modesty, and obedience towards his fellow citizens; a place was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-14900356.summary: This inscription records a statue erected by the town council to honor Marcus Cornelius Proculeianus for his character and service.

EDCS-14900357.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Cornelius Marcellus, son of Quirinus, pious, lived 33 years. Sereta Saturnina, daughter of Caius, wife of Lucius Cornelius Verris, pious, lived 20 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-14900357.summary: This is a tombstone recording the deaths of Cornelius Marcellus and Sereta Saturnina, noting their ages and familial relationships.

EDCS-14900358.translation: To the departed spirits. Sacred. Cornelia Clodiana lived 3 years, 8 months, and 25 days. Her dutiful father placed this for his sweetest daughter.
EDCS-14900358.summary: A tombstone erected by a father for his young daughter, Cornelia Clodiana, who died at the age of three.

EDCS-14900359.translation: To the departed spirits. Sacred. Cornelia Crispina lived 52 years. She is buried here. Gaius Pinarius Vitalis placed this for his dutiful mother.
EDCS-14900359.summary: A tombstone for Cornelia Crispina, erected by her son Gaius Pinarius Vitalis, recording her age at death.

EDCS-14900360.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Cornelia Licinia sacerdos Cererum publica vixit annos LXV hic sita est filii pii posuerunt\n
EDCS-14900360.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Cornelia Licinia, priestess of Ceres, lived 65 years. She is buried here. Her dutiful sons placed this.
EDCS-14900360.summary: A tombstone for Cornelia Licinia, a priestess of Ceres, erected by her sons, recording her age at death.

EDCS-14900361.translation: To the departed spirits. Sacred. Cornelia Romana, daughter of Marcus, lived 25 years. Messius Saturninus placed this for his excellent wife. She is buried here.
EDCS-14900361.summary: A tombstone for Cornelia Romana, erected by her husband Messius Saturninus, recording her age at death.

EDCS-14900362.translation: To the departed spirits. Domitia Veneria lived 95 years and is buried here. Fortunata erected this for her pious mother.
EDCS-14900362.summary: A tombstone recording the death of Domitia Veneria, dedicated by her daughter Fortunata.

EDCS-14900363.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Marmaris lived 47 years. She is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Donatus lived 6 years and 7 months. He is buried here.
EDCS-14900363.summary: This tombstone records the burials and ages of two individuals, Marmaris and Donatus.

EDCS-14900364.translation: To the departed spirits. Duronius Neptunalis lived 25 years and is buried here. To the departed spirits. Duronius Successor lived 13 years and is buried here.
EDCS-14900364.summary: A tombstone recording the deaths of two individuals, Duronius Neptunalis and Duronius Successor, possibly father and son.

EDCS-14900365.translation: To the departed spirits. Aetria Victoria lived 44 years. Her devoted parents erected this; she is buried here.
EDCS-14900365.summary: A tombstone recording the death of Aetria Victoria, erected by her parents.

EDCS-14900366.translation: To the departed spirits. Euplius lived 37 years and 7 days and is buried here. Valeria Concordia erected this for her dearest father.
EDCS-14900366.summary: A tombstone recording the death of Euplius, erected by his daughter Valeria Concordia.

EDCS-14900367.translation: Facundus and Maecenas erected this for their pious brother.
EDCS-14900367.summary: This is a dedication by two individuals, Facundus and Maecenas, for their brother.

EDCS-14900368.translation: Thus I receive the rewards for my services and my name as a salutor, and I am fortunate after death; my dear comrades have fixed my name for eternity on this monument; fare well, and may you always please the arena. I lived 40 years.
EDCS-14900368.summary: This epitaph records the life and posthumous fame of a gladiator or performer who lived 40 years.

EDCS-14900369.translation: To the departed spirits. Flavia Primitiva Crescentina lived 1 year [...].
EDCS-14900369.summary: A tombstone recording the death of Flavia Primitiva Crescentina, who died in her first year.

EDCS-14900370.translation: To the departed spirits. Flavia Secura, who lived 18 years, is buried here.
EDCS-14900370.summary: A tombstone recording the death of Flavia Secura, who died at the age of 18.

EDCS-14900371.translation: To the departed spirits. Gaius Gabinius Ingeneuus lived [...] years.
EDCS-14900371.summary: A tombstone fragment recording the death of Gaius Gabinius Ingeneuus.

EDCS-14900372.translation: Gargilia Saturnina the pious lived 80 years and is buried here. Postumiae Pacata Sperata Quieta erected this for their pious mother.
EDCS-14900372.summary: A tombstone recording the death of Gargilia Saturnina, erected by her daughters.

EDCS-14900373.translation: To the departed spirits. Geminius Fortunatianus lived 22 years, 7 months, and 14 days. His devoted father erected this. To the departed spirits. Pinar[ia He]donin[a vi]/xit a[nnos] / XXXX[3] / man[3] / p[.
EDCS-14900373.summary: A tombstone recording the death of Geminius Fortunatianus, erected by his father, alongside a fragment likely for a woman named Pinar[ia].

EDCS-14900374.translation: To the departed spirits. Publius Geminius Laetus, son of Publius, of the Quirina tribe, lived 66 years and is buried here.
EDCS-14900374.summary: A tombstone recording the death of Publius Geminius Laetus, son of Publius.

EDCS-14900375.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Titus Herennius, son of Quintus, of the Quirina tribe, lived 25 years, 4 months, and 20 days; he lies here. Quintus Herennius, his father, placed this for his devoted son.
EDCS-14900375.summary: A funerary epitaph for Titus Herennius, set up by his father, Quintus Herennius, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-14900376.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Herennia Celsiana, devoted, lived 40 years and 6 months; she lies here.
EDCS-14900376.summary: A funerary epitaph for Herennia Celsiana, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-14900377.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Julius Felix lived 60 years and 3 months. Augendus, his son, placed this for his dearest father.
EDCS-14900377.summary: A funerary epitaph for Julius Felix, set up by his son Augendus, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-15000100.translation: To Gaius Bruttius Praesens, son of Lucius, of the Pomptina tribe, consul, proconsul of the province of Africa, XV vir sacris faciundis, curator of sacred buildings, public works, and places, legatus pro praetore of Emperor Caesar Trajan Hadrianus Augustus of the province of Cappadocia, likewise legatus pro praetore of Emperor Caesar Trajan Hadrianus Augustus of the province of Moesia Inferior, legatus pro praetore of Emperor divine Trajan Augustus of the province of Cilicia, curator of the Via Latina, legatus of the VI Ferrata legion, honored with military decorations by Emperor Trajan Augustus for the Parthian war, praetor, plebeian aedile, quaestor of the province of Hispania Baetica Ulterior, tribuni laticlavii of the I Minervia legion, honored with military decorations by Emperor Augustus for the Marcomannic war, triumvir capitalis, patron, by decree of the decurions, with public funds.
EDCS-15000100.summary: This inscription honors Gaius Bruttius Praesens, detailing his extensive political and military career from quaestor to consul and his numerous imperial appointments and military honors, likely marking a public monument erected by the town council of Mactaris.

EDCS-15000134.text_edition: \n Centenarum sic Mufelthiana Marci Caecili Bumupal ffecerunt semper Dunbanem Bucubuom Salonema\n
EDCS-15000134.translation: The Centenari, Mufelthiana and Marci Caecili, made it always for Dunbanem, Bucubuom, Salonema.
EDCS-15000134.summary: An inscription recording a dedication made by the 'Centenari,' possibly a local group or administrative unit, to individuals named Dunbanem, Bucubuom, and Salonema, with uncertain dating.

EDCS-15100007.text_edition: \n Lucio Iulio Luci filio Papiria Victori |(centurioni) cohortis I urbanae Severianae laterculensi ostiario scriniario praeffectorum praetorio eemminentissimorum vvirorum innocentissimo viro ob nimia merita IIORORVMI admirabilem benevolentiam erga singulos universosque optimo civi Maracitani sua pecunia fecerunt dedicaverunt\n
EDCS-15100007.translation: Lucius Iulius Victor, son of Lucius, of the Papiria tribe, centurion of the first urban cohort Severiana, doorkeeper and scribe of the most eminent prefects of the praetorium, an innocent man, for his admirable benevolence towards individuals and the community as a whole, the best citizen, the people of Maracita ('Maracitani') made and dedicated this with their own money.
EDCS-15100007.summary: A dedication of a monument by the citizens of Maracita to Lucius Iulius Victor, a centurion and official, honoring his merits and benevolence, likely dating to the Severan period.

EDCS-15100013.translation: Tito Flavio Symphoro, freedman of Augustus, procurator of the Augustan public revenues of Africa, Nasennia Haeresis had this constructed on his own land with his own money for her most pious father and for herself and her family.
EDCS-15100013.summary: This inscription records the construction of a monument by Nasennia Haeresis for her father, Tito Flavio Symphoro, an imperial procurator.

EDCS-15100014.translation: To Avidius Vitalis, daughter of Gaius, perpetual flaminica of the colony Concordia Julia Karthago, Gnaeus Salvius Saturninus, perpetual flamen, [erected this] for her merits.
EDCS-15100014.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Gnaeus Salvius Saturninus, a perpetual flamen, to Avidius Vitalis, a perpetual flaminica of Carthage, likely in recognition of her service.

EDCS-15100016.text_edition: \n ? Aemilio Quinti filio Papiria Pudenti centurioni legionis III Augustae item legionis II Augustae item iterum legionis II Augustae item legionis XI Claudiae adlecto in comitatu Imperatoris Commodi Augusti Pii Felicis IIviro q(uin)q(uennali) coloniae Thaenitanae fratri Quinti Aemili Laeti praefecti praetorio ob singularem innocentiam et in promerendis singulis universisque civibus examina tam adfectionem ordo Thaenensium statuam equestrem ponendam de publico decreto decreto decurionum pecunia publica\n
EDCS-15100016.translation: To Aemilius Pudentus, son of Quintus, of the Papiria tribe, centurion of the III Augustan legion, also of the II Augustan legion, again of the II Augustan legion, also of the XI Claudian legion, admitted into the retinue of the Emperor Commodus Augustus Pius Felix, quinquennial duovir of the colony of Thaena, for his brother Quintus Aemilius Laetus, prefect of the praetorium, because of singular innocence and his careful attention to individuals and the citizens as a whole, the council of the Thaenitani, by public decree of the decurions, with public money, [ordered to erect] an equestrian statue.
EDCS-15100016.summary: A decree by the council of Thaena to erect an equestrian statue to Aemilius Pudentus, a military officer and local magistrate, in honor of his brother Quintus Aemilius Laetus, a prefect of the praetorium, likely dating to the reign of Commodus.

EDCS-15100017.translation: Lucius Helvius Barigbal promised and also donated a column to his fellow tribules in his own name and in the name of his sons.
EDCS-15100017.summary: Lucius Helvius Barigbal, acting on behalf of himself and his sons, dedicated a column to his fellow tribules.

EDCS-15100018.translation: To Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus, prince of youth, son of Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus Arabicus Adiabenicus Parthicus Maximus, most strong, most fortunate, father of the country, with tribunician power, consul V, proconsul, by decree of the decurions of the colony Aelia Aurelia Mactaris, with public funds.
EDCS-15100018.summary: This inscription records a dedication by the decurions of Mactaris, using public funds, to Emperor Marcus Aurelius Antoninus, son of Septimius Severus, acknowledging his various titles and honors.

EDCS-15100020.translation: For the safety of our lords the Emperors Constantine the Great and Constantine and Constantius, the most noble Caesars, an unusual work was erected on the height, constructed over a long course by Florentius, a most perfect man, procurator, most devoted patron; they were dedicated.
EDCS-15100020.summary: This inscription records a monumental work erected for the safety of the Emperors Constantine the Great, Constantine, and Constantius, overseen by Florentius, a procurator.

EDCS-15100021.translation: Gaius Pompeius Gallus willingly made a statue of the Lady of the Earth and a temple.
EDCS-15100021.summary: Gaius Pompeius Gallus willingly dedicated a statue of Tellus and a temple.

EDCS-15100023.translation: Sacred to Saturn. Secundus Octavius Felix willingly entered under the yoke.
EDCS-15100023.summary: This inscription, sacred to Saturn, records Secundus Octavius Felix willingly submitting to a ritualistic 'yoke'.

EDCS-15100024.translation: Sacred to Augustus Saturn. Publius Petronius Proculus, priest.
EDCS-15100024.summary: Publius Petronius Proculus, a priest, dedicates this inscription to Augustus Saturn.

EDCS-15100026.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. The will of Flavius is declared in these verses. He built this tomb for himself while alive and provided a place for his family. Uncertain as to when he would be deprived of light, the remains of bodies are placed therein. Lucius Flavius Felix lived 40 years, here he lies. Of Felix.
EDCS-15100026.summary: This tomb inscription records the self-funded construction by Lucius Flavius Felix for himself and his family, and notes his lifespan of 40 years.

EDCS-15100027.translation: Gaius Paccius Africanus, pontifex, consul, proconsul, patron of the municipality, dedicated this; Lucius Domitius Fuscus Chunnurio, flamen Augusti, contributed it in honor, through the agency of Quintus Servilius Pudens, legate as propraetor.
EDCS-15100027.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a monument by Gaius Paccius Africanus and its contribution by Lucius Domitius Fuscus Chunnurio, with the involvement of Quintus Servilius Pudens.

EDCS-15100028.translation: The citizens of Maracitania made this for their son Papirius Optatus, aedile, with their own money, because of his affection for each individual and for all.
EDCS-15100028.summary: The citizens of Maracitania funded the construction of this monument for their aedile, Papirius Optatus, in recognition of his affection.

EDCS-15100322.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Julius Licinianus lived 19 years and 8 months; he lies here. Julius Secundianus, his devoted father, placed this. Sacred to the departed spirits. Manilia Saturnina lived 2 years and 10 months; she lies here. Julius Secundianus, her devoted grandfather, placed this. Sacred to the departed spirits. Cornelia Iulia Crescentia lived 22 years; she lies here. Julius Secundianus, her dearest husband, placed this.
EDCS-15100322.summary: A complex funerary monument with three epitaphs, recording the deaths of Julius Licinianus, Manilia Saturnina, and Cornelia Iulia Crescentia, with two of them set up by Julius Secundianus in his roles as father and husband, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-15100324.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus Iulius Saturninus, devoted, lived 35 years; he lies here. Quintus Iulius Fortunatus placed this for his devoted brother, a good man.
EDCS-15100324.summary: A funerary epitaph for Quintus Iulius Saturninus, set up by his brother Quintus Iulius Fortunatus, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-15100325.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Caius Iulius [illegible] lived [illegible]... lived 85 years; he lies here.
EDCS-15100325.summary: A damaged funerary epitaph recording the death of a Caius Iulius, with only his age at death partially preserved, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-15100326.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Julius [illegible]nus lived 32 years and [illegible] months; he lies here. Iulius Liberalis placed this for his brother.
EDCS-15100326.summary: A funerary epitaph for an unnamed Julius, set up by his brother Iulius Liberalis, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-15100327.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulia Nampamina lived 80 years. Iulius Antiochenus set this up. Here she lies. [Sacred to the departed spirits] Iulia [lived]...
EDCS-15100327.summary: A funerary inscription for Iulia Nampamina, erected by Iulius Antiochenus, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-15100330.translation: Iunia Fructuosa, daughter of Marcus, lived 22 years and 11 months. Here she lies. Pleminius Donatus set this up for his dearest wife.
EDCS-15100330.summary: A funerary monument erected by Pleminius Donatus for his wife, Iunia Fructuosa, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15100331.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Memia Quietula lived [X] years. Here she lies. Liberalis for himself and the same Quietula for herself while alive set this up. Sacred to the departed spirits. Liberalis lived [X] years. Here he lies. He himself set this up for himself while alive.
EDCS-15100331.summary: A double funerary inscription, possibly for a couple, recording the lives of Memia Quietula and Liberalis, who prepared their tombs in advance.

EDCS-15100332.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Licinius Donatus lived 60 years. Here he lies. Licinia Tertiola set up this tomb for her father, out of dutiful affection.
EDCS-15100332.summary: A funerary monument set up by Licinia Tertiola for her father, Licinius Donatus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15100333.translation: To the departed spirits. Ligarius,(?) son of Ligarius,(?) Ligarianus lived 30 years. Ligarius Liberalis set this up for his devoted brother. Here he lies.
EDCS-15100333.summary: A funerary inscription for Ligarius Liberalis, erected by his brother, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15100334.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Sextus Magnius Verus lived 53 years. Here he lies. Quintus Magnius Hilarius(?) set this up for his devoted father.
EDCS-15100334.summary: A funerary monument erected by Q. Magnius Hilarius(?) for his father, Sex. Magnius Verus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15100335.translation: [Manilius Longus, son of Lucius, lived 54 years. Here he lies.] Quintus Manilius Maximus set this up for [his] best and devoted [father/son/brother].
EDCS-15100335.summary: A funerary inscription, partially restored, for Manilius Longus, with a dedication likely by Quintus Manilius Maximus.

EDCS-15100336.translation: Quintus Manilius Maximus, possibly a perpetual flamen, lived 52 years and 5 months. Here he lies. Iulia Stolis set this up for her devoted husband.
EDCS-15100336.summary: A funerary inscription for Quintus Manilius Maximus, possibly a local religious official, erected by his wife Iulia Stolis.

EDCS-15100337.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Manilia Rufina lived 45 years. Vinnius Silo set this up for his most devoted wife. Here she lies.
EDCS-15100337.summary: A funerary monument erected by Vinnius Silo for his wife, Manilia Rufina, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15100338.translation: [This tomb is for] Mantia Lucisca, daughter of Publius, [his] excellent grandmother. She lived 80 years.
EDCS-15100338.summary: A funerary inscription for Mantia Lucisca, honoring her as an excellent grandmother, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15100339.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Publius Marius Pasi[3] lived 75 years. Publius Marius Saturninus, his son, placed this for his father.
EDCS-15100339.summary: This is a tombstone recording the death of Publius Marius Pasi[3] and erected by his son, Publius Marius Saturninus, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-15100340.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcia Fortuna lived 90 years and is buried here. Marci Fortunatus Secundinus Ampliatus Honoratus, her sons, placed this for their dutiful mother.
EDCS-15100340.summary: This tombstone records the burial of Marcia Fortuna, who lived 90 years, and was erected by her sons, Marci Fortunatus Secundinus Ampliatus Honoratus, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-15100341.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Margarita lived 20 years and is buried here. Venustus placed this for his wife.
EDCS-15100341.summary: This tombstone records the burial of Margarita, who lived 20 years, and was erected by her husband, Venustus, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-15100342.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus Marius Felix lived 67 years and is buried here. Perellia Saturnina placed this for her husband.
EDCS-15100342.summary: This tombstone records the burial of Quintus Marius Felix, who lived 67 years, and was erected by his wife, Perellia Saturnina, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-15100345.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Memmia Saturnina [---]. Sacred to the departed spirits. Q(uintus) Memmius Saturninus lived 83 years and is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Aemilia Donata lived 90 years and is buried here. Memmius Aemilianus placed this for his dutiful mother.
EDCS-15100345.summary: This inscription appears to be a composite epitaph, recording the deaths of Memmia Saturnina, Quintus Memmius Saturninus, and Aemilia Donata, with Memmius Aemilianus erecting a monument for his mother, Aemilia Donata; it likely dates to the Imperial period.

EDCS-15100346.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Mevia Felicitas lived 40 years. Quintus Calpurnius Fortunatus placed this for his dearest wife, a most unworthy spouse who too quickly departed this life; miserable one, you ought to have lived a hundred years. For you were more beautiful than others, and possessed eloquence and modesty beyond compare, and I will not say that such qualities existed or will exist to be surpassed. But since the spirits exist, may the earth lie lightly upon you. She is buried here.
EDCS-15100346.summary: This is a tombstone for Mevia Felicitas, who died at 40, erected by her husband Quintus Calpurnius Fortunatus, who laments her early death and praises her beauty, eloquence, and modesty, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-15100347.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Felicitas lived 4 years and 4 months. Her dutiful mother placed this.
EDCS-15100347.summary: This is a tombstone for Felicitas, who died at the age of 4 years and 4 months, erected by her mother, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-15100348.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Gaius Sentius Fortunatus lived 90 years. Gaius Sentius Rogatianus, his son, placed this for his dutiful father. He is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Gaius Minucius Valentinus lived 88 years. His dutiful sons placed this for their father. He is buried here.
EDCS-15100348.summary: This inscription is a composite tombstone recording two burials: Gaius Sentius Fortunatus, who lived 90 years and was honored by his son Gaius Sentius Rogatianus, and Gaius Minucius Valentinus, who lived 88 years and was honored by his sons; it likely dates to the Imperial period.

EDCS-15100349.translation: [---]tia, daughter of Sextus [---]. Sacred to the departed spirits. Modia Maxima, daughter of Caius, dutiful, lived 24 years and is buried here. Caius Modius Maximus placed this for his excellent daughter. Sacred to the departed spirits. Gaius Modius Maximus, son of Gaius, lived 24 years and 2 months and is buried here. Caius Modius Maximus placed this for his son.
EDCS-15100349.summary: This inscription records multiple burials, including Modia Maxima, who died at 24 and was honored by her father Caius Modius Maximus, and Gaius Modius Maximus, who also died at 24 and was honored by his father also named Caius Modius Maximus; it likely dates to the Imperial period.

EDCS-15100352.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Nonia Suriscina, daughter of Marcu[s], is buried here.
EDCS-15100352.summary: This tombstone records the burial of Nonia Suriscina, daughter of Marcu[s], likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-15100353.translation: To the divine spirits. Quintus Orbius Salutaris Connari lived for 28 years, one month, and 26 days. He lies buried here. His adopted son placed this.
EDCS-15100353.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Quintus Orbius Salutaris Connari, who lived for 28 years, one month, and 26 days, with the monument erected by his adopted son.

EDCS-15100355.translation: To the spirits, here Passiena Casta rests in peaceful shades. She lived 45 years, pious, generous, kind. Her father and brothers erect this tomb for her.
EDCS-15100355.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Passiena Casta, who lived 45 years, erected by her father and brothers.

EDCS-15100356.translation: To the divine spirits. Petronia Casta lived for 75 years. She lies buried here. Kastus, her son, placed this for his mother.
EDCS-15100356.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Petronia Casta, who lived 75 years, erected by her son Kastus.

EDCS-15100357.translation: To the divine spirits. Plotius Alexander lived...
EDCS-15100357.summary: This is an incomplete funerary epitaph for Plotius Alexander.

EDCS-15100358.translation: To the divine spirits. Pompeia Fortunata lived for 85 years. Her devoted sons placed this. To the divine spirits. Publius Sextilius Donatus lived for 60 years, a devoted wife. She placed this for her husband.
EDCS-15100358.summary: This inscription is a double epitaph, recording Pompeia Fortunata, who lived 85 years and was commemorated by her sons, and Publius Sextilius Donatus, who lived 60 years and was commemorated by his wife.

EDCS-15100359.translation: To the spirits. Pomponia Quarta, daughter of Caius, pious, lived for 18 years.
EDCS-15100359.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Pomponia Quarta, daughter of Caius, who lived 18 years.

EDCS-15100360.translation: To the divine spirits. Pomponia Valeria lived for 15 years...
EDCS-15100360.summary: This is an incomplete funerary epitaph for Pomponia Valeria, who lived 15 years.

EDCS-15100362.translation: To the divine spirits. Publius Praecilius Pollio, son of Marcus, of the Quirina tribe, lived for [3] years. He lies buried here. His brothers, Praecilius Fidus and Vitalis, saw to its construction.
EDCS-15100362.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Publius Praecilius Pollio, son of Marcus, who lived an unspecified number of years and was commemorated by his brothers, Fidus and Vitalis.

EDCS-15100363.translation: To the divine spirits. Refrius Successus lived for 47 years. He lies buried here. Refrius Nundinarius placed this for his devoted brother.
EDCS-15100363.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Refrius Successus, who lived 47 years, erected by his brother Refrius Nundinarius.

EDCS-15100364.translation: To the divine spirits. Gaius Remmius Felix, son of Caius, a rope maker, pious, lived for 21 years.
EDCS-15100364.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Gaius Remmius Felix, son of Caius, a rope maker, who lived 21 years.

EDCS-15100365.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Remmia Tertullina Mustelica lived 23 years. Gaius Titius Clemens, a dutiful man, erected this for his dutiful wife, who rests here.
EDCS-15100365.summary: A funerary epitaph for Remmia Tertullina Mustelica, erected by her husband, Gaius Titius Clemens.

EDCS-15100366.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. For Remmia Secunda, daughter of Caius, who lived 28 years.
EDCS-15100366.summary: A funerary epitaph for Remmia Secunda, daughter of Caius, with an incomplete line indicating the mother's name.

EDCS-15100367.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Publius Rutilius Vitalis, son of Publius, of the Quirina tribe, lived 38 years and rests here. Publius Rutilius Fortunatus erected this for his excellent brother.
EDCS-15100367.summary: A funerary epitaph for Publius Rutilius Vitalis, erected by his brother, Publius Rutilius Fortunatus.

EDCS-15100368.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Quintus Sempronius Lucifer, son of Quintus, of the Quirina tribe, lived a dutiful 80 years. His heirs, Quintus Sempronius Antenor and Sempronia Mallina, erected this for their patron.
EDCS-15100368.summary: A funerary epitaph for Quintus Sempronius Lucifer, erected by his heirs, Quintus Sempronius Antenor and Sempronia Mallina.

EDCS-15100369.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Sempronia Mallina lived 80 years.
EDCS-15100369.summary: A funerary epitaph for Sempronia Mallina, with an incomplete line.

EDCS-15100370.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Sextia Fortunata lived...
EDCS-15100370.summary: A funerary epitaph for Sextia Fortunata, with incomplete life span and name restoration.

EDCS-15100371.translation: Tannonius Marcellus lived 70 years. Tannonius Sterceius erected this for his dutiful father, who rests here.
EDCS-15100371.summary: A funerary epitaph for Tannonius Marcellus, erected by his son, Tannonius Sterceius.

EDCS-15100372.translation: Gaius Thar[---], son of Titus TTAR[---], 1 year and 1 month and [---] days old, is buried here. His ancestor...
EDCS-15100372.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription for Gaius Thar[---] who died at the age of 1 year and 1 month.

EDCS-15100373.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Marcus Titinius Fuscus lived 80 years and rests here. Gaius Titinius Fuscus erected this for his father. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Agria Extricata lived 70 years and rests here. Gaius Titinius made this for his mother. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Iulia Victoria lived 50 years. Gaius Titinius Fuscus erected this for his wife.
EDCS-15100373.summary: A funerary monument with three epitaphs: Marcus Titinius Fuscus (erected by son Gaius), Agria Extricata (erected by son Gaius), and Iulia Victoria (erected by husband Gaius Titinius Fuscus).

EDCS-15100374.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Gaius Trebius Ianuarius lived 15 years and rests here. Annia Maxima erected this for her dutiful son. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Gaius Trebius Maximus lived 45 years and rests here. His dutiful wife erected this.
EDCS-15100374.summary: A funerary monument with two epitaphs: Gaius Trebius Ianuarius (erected by mother Annia Maxima) and Gaius Trebius Maximus (erected by his wife).

EDCS-15100375.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Marcus Valerius Institor lived 55 years and rests here.
EDCS-15100375.summary: A funerary epitaph for Marcus Valerius Institor.

EDCS-15100376.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Valeria Dubitata lived 5 years and 20 days; her father placed [this] for his daughter.
EDCS-15100376.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a young girl named Valeria Dubitata, who died at the age of 5 years and 20 days, and was commemorated by her father.

EDCS-15100377.translation: Here lies Varius, known as Frontonianus, whom his delightful wife Cornelia Galla placed here, restoring the sweet comforts of a former life; she set up marble likenesses of his face, eyes, and spirit, so that she could satisfy her love for him more deeply through his image. This will be her solace, for as long as she lives, her husband will be in her whole heart, and it is no wonder, for what woman has such qualities? [---] he was pious, [---] indulgent, [---] and happy, [---] but [---] snatched away [---] for he [---] and not [---] in the year [---].
EDCS-15100377.summary: This is a lengthy funerary epitaph for Varius Frontonianus, commemorating his character and the deep love of his wife Cornelia Galla, who erected the monument.

EDCS-15100378.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Venustus, pious, lived 80 years; he lies here. [---] placed for his most pious father.
EDCS-15100378.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Venustus, who died at the age of 80, and whose monument was erected by his son.

EDCS-15100379.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Vibia Ispica lived for 17 years, 2 months, and 14 days; her mother placed this for her daughter. She is buried here.
EDCS-15100379.summary: This funerary inscription records the life and burial of Vibia Ispica, who died at age 17, placed by her mother.

EDCS-15100380.translation: To the Divine Shades. Vettia Pollitta, daughter of Lucius, lived for 68 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-15100380.summary: This funerary inscription records the life and burial of Vettia Pollitta, who died at age 68.

EDCS-15100381.translation: Caia Ve/tutia, a respectable matron, lived [---] years.
EDCS-15100381.summary: This is a funerary epitaph fragment for Caia Vetutia, a matron, recording her name and an incomplete lifespan.

EDCS-15100382.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Volussena Ianuar(i)a lived 38 years; she lies here. Lucius Granius Victor placed [this] for his most excellent wife. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Volussena Gududia lived 96 years; she lies here. Lucius Granius Victor placed [this] for his daughter.
EDCS-15100382.summary: This funerary monument records two women, Volussena Ianuar(i)a and Volussena Gududia, both honored by Lucius Granius Victor, one as his wife and the other as his daughter.

EDCS-15100384.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. [Nia] Mon lived for 8 years and 5 days. [Her mother/father] placed this.
EDCS-15100384.summary: This funerary inscription records the life of [Nia] Mon, who died at age 8 years and 5 days.

EDCS-15100386.translation: To the Divine Shades. Onpius, pious, lived for 66 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-15100386.summary: This funerary inscription records the life and burial of Onpius, who died at age 66.

EDCS-15100388.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription indicating a parent placed a monument for their daughter.

EDCS-15100389.translation: [---] lived for 40 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-15100389.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription recording the burial of an individual who died at age 40.

EDCS-15100390.translation: Lived for 18 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-15100390.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of an individual who died at age 18.

EDCS-15100391.summary: This is a very short inscription, possibly a religious dedication or inscription related to a church.

EDCS-15100393.translation: Flavius Silbanianus the Illustrious lived for 80 years and rested under the Ides of August in the eighth indiction.
EDCS-15100393.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Flavius Silbanianus Illustris at the age of 80, with a specific date (Ides of August, 8th indiction) and likely dating to the later Roman Empire.

EDCS-15100394.translation: Valerius Innocenti lived 61 years, rested in the peace of Christ.
EDCS-15100394.summary: This is a tomb inscription recording the lifespan and peaceful rest of Valerius Innocenti, likely from the Christian era.

EDCS-15100395.translation: Vitalis, a lector, lived 5 years, buried on the 3rd day before the Nones of May, in the first indiction.
EDCS-15100395.summary: This is a tomb inscription for Vitalis, identified as a lector, recording his age at death and burial date.

EDCS-15100396.translation: Argentia the faithful lived 23 years, buried in peace on the 5th day before the Kalends of May.
EDCS-15100396.summary: This tomb inscription records the lifespan and burial date of Argentia, described as 'faithful'.

EDCS-15100397.translation: Ciprianus lived 7 years, rested in peace.
EDCS-15100397.summary: This is a tomb inscription stating the age at death and peaceful rest of Ciprianus.

EDCS-15100398.summary: This inscription records the lifespan of Felix, likely from a tomb.

EDCS-15100399.translation: Perpetua rested in peace on the Ides of April, in the first indiction, lived 5 years.
EDCS-15100399.summary: This tomb inscription records the peaceful rest and age at death of Perpetua, with a specific burial date.

EDCS-15100400.translation: Victor Nepos rested in peace on the Ides of August, lived 11 months, 25 days.
EDCS-15100400.summary: This tomb inscription records the peaceful rest of Victor Nepos, specifying his age at death in months and days.

EDCS-15100401.translation: Victor went into peace, rested, lived 40 years, buried on the 11th day before the Kalends of March.
EDCS-15100401.summary: This tomb inscription records the lifespan and burial date of Victor, indicating his peaceful transition.

EDCS-15100405.translation: Of the faithful Donatus, in peace.
EDCS-15100405.summary: This inscription likely commemorates Donatus, described as faithful and at peace, possibly on a tomb.

EDCS-15100406.translation: Florida lived one year, 4 months, 5 days.
EDCS-15100406.summary: This inscription records the lifespan of Florida, likely from a tomb, indicating she died in infancy.

EDCS-15100407.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Marcus Attius Castrensis, a devoted son, lived 85 years; his sons erected this to their most excellent father. To his excellent sister, who lived 35 years, her brothers erected this.
EDCS-15100407.summary: This is a funerary epitaph erected by brothers for their sister and by sons for their father, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15100408.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Gaius Clodius Faustinus lived 30 years; his devoted mother placed him here. Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Gaius Clodius Fabianus lived 25 years; his devoted mother placed him here.
EDCS-15100408.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lives and burial of two individuals, Gaius Clodius Faustinus and Gaius Clodius Fabianus, whose mother placed them here.

EDCS-15100409.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Iulia Secunda lived 48 years and 20 days; she is buried here. Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Quinta lived 14 years, 1 month, and 25 days; her devoted father placed her here, buried.
EDCS-15100409.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lives and burial of two individuals, Iulia Secunda and Quinta, with Quinta's father being the dedicant.

EDCS-15100410.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Quintus Vibius Saturninus lived 65 years; his sons erected this to their devoted father.
EDCS-15100410.summary: This funerary epitaph records the life of Quintus Vibius Saturninus, for whom his sons erected the monument.

EDCS-15100411.translation: [---] Rufus, a veteran of the III Augusta legion, lived 94 years; he lies here. Marcus Nunnius Secundinus placed [this] for his dear uncle.
EDCS-15100411.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Rufus, a veteran of the III Augusta legion, who lived to 94, and was commemorated by his nephew, Marcus Nunnius Secundinus.

EDCS-15100412.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Quintus Caelius Felix, priest, lived 60 years. Quintus Caelius Felix, his son, placed [this] for his pious father.
EDCS-15100412.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Quintus Caelius Felix, a priest who died at 60, erected by his son of the same name.

EDCS-15100413.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Aelia Victoria, to Nunnius Secundinus, her most rare husband, she erected this.
EDCS-15100413.summary: This funerary epitaph is dedicated by Aelia Victoria to her husband, Nunnius Secundinus.

EDCS-15100414.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Caius Antonius Fortunatus lived 35 years.
EDCS-15100414.summary: This is a brief funerary epitaph recording the life of Caius Antonius Fortunatus.

EDCS-15100415.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Atilia Quartilla lived 35 years; she lies here. Cornelius Saxo placed [this] for his dearest wife.
EDCS-15100415.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Atilia Quartilla, who died at 35, and was commemorated by her husband, Cornelius Saxo.

EDCS-15100416.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Caecilia Concordia, dutiful, lived 32 years; she lies here.
EDCS-15100416.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Caecilia Concordia, who died at the age of 32.

EDCS-15100417.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Caecilia Optata, daughter of Quintus, lived 37 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-15100417.summary: This funerary epitaph records the life and burial of Caecilia Optata, daughter of Quintus.

EDCS-15100418.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Lucius Cascellius Rufus, son of Lucius, of the Quirina tribe, lived 80 years; he is buried here. Cascelli Saturninus and Rufus erected this to their most excellent father.
EDCS-15100418.summary: This funerary epitaph records the life of Lucius Cascellius Rufus and was erected by his sons, Cascelli Saturninus and Rufus.

EDCS-15100419.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Cascillia Maxima lived 47 years; she is buried here. Cascelli Saturninus and Rufus erected this to their dearest sister.
EDCS-15100419.summary: This funerary epitaph records the life of Cascillia Maxima and was erected by her brothers, Cascelli Saturninus and Rufus.

EDCS-15100420.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Cornelia Restituta lived 40 years; she is buried here. Her devoted father erected this.

EDCS-15100422.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Opilius Iunius Aratus lived 50 years and is buried here. Saturnina set this up for her devoted husband.

EDCS-15100424.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Flavia Secundina, a chaste virgin, lived 19 years and 7 months; she lies here. Whoever reads this, may you know that [---] made this.

EDCS-15100427.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Nonia Prima lived 23 years. Julius Donatus erected this for his devoted wife.

EDCS-15100428.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Postumia Mustacia, freedwoman of Caius, lived 41 years. Pullimer erected this for his most devoted wife here.

EDCS-15100429.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Caius Remius Aprilis lived 40 years. His religious wife Cattula set this up out of devotion from her own resources.

EDCS-15100430.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Caius Veturius Modestianus lived 19 years and is buried here. His devoted father set this up.

EDCS-15100431.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Victor lived 40 years and is buried here.
EDCS-15100431.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Victor, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15100432.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Volusena Magna lived 30 years. Messorianus set this up for his sister. She is buried here. Sacred to the Divine Manes. Caius Iulius Vi lived [---] years and is buried here.

EDCS-15100433.translation: Volusena Privata lived 33 years, 11 months, and 13 days. She is buried here. Volusenus Lucifer set this up for his devoted wife.

EDCS-15100434.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Nonius Daphinus, son of Nonius, piously set this up.

EDCS-15100436.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Fructuosa lived 24 years and 5 months. Manilius Messallinus erected this for his devoted daughter here.
EDCS-15100436.summary: A funerary epitaph for Fructuosa, erected by her father, Manilius Messallinus, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15100437.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulius Maximianus lived 47 years. Helvia Sperata and Lucia Saturnina set this up for their devoted husband and father. He is buried here.
EDCS-15100437.summary: A funerary monument set up by Helvia Sperata and Lucia Saturnina for their husband and father, Iulius Maximianus.

EDCS-15100438.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Caius Iulius Memor lived 95 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-15100438.summary: A funerary monument for Caius Iulius Memor, who lived 95 years.

EDCS-15100439.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Plotia, a chaste and modest woman, lived 54 years. Julius Generosus erected this for his most remarkable wife here.
EDCS-15100439.summary: A funerary epitaph for Plotia, erected by her husband, Julius Generosus, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15100440.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Aemilia Fortunata lived 43 years. Agrius Rufinus made this for his dearest mother here. She rests here. EDCS-15100440.summary: A double funerary epitaph, recording the burials of Aemilia Fortunata, erected by her son Agrius Rufinus, and Marcus Agrius Quartus, erected by his husband, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15100441.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Gaius Gabinius Gentilis lived 65 years and, while alive, arranged for this tomb for himself and his wife Ianuaria. He rests here. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Pompeia Ianuaria lived 60 years. She rests here. Gabinia Adauctula arranged for the inscription for her exceedingly devoted parents.
EDCS-15100441.summary: A double funerary epitaph recording self-funded burials for Gaius Gabinius Gentilis and Pompeia Ianuaria, with an additional note about parents by Gabinia Adauctula, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15100442.translation: While our lords Diocletian and Maximian, unconquered Augusti, reign. Decimus Amullius Victorinus, perpetual priest, out of his generosity built this portico at his own expense.
EDCS-15100442.summary: A dedication by Decimus Amullius Victorinus, a perpetual priest, for the construction of a portico during the reign of Diocletian and Maximian.

EDCS-15100443.translation: Of Lucius Calpurnius, son of Marcus, of the Tromentina tribe, from Aquae Statiellae. He lived 35 years, served 13 years as a soldier in the III Augusta legion. Philmusus Eutychus Amaranthus, his freedman and heir, rests buried here.

EDCS-15100444.translation: Publius Vettius, son of Publius, of the Velina tribe, a soldier in the III Augusta legion, a trumpeter, rests here.

EDCS-15100445.translation: Titus Pompeius Macrinus, son of Titus, veteran of the III Augusta legion, lived 85 years. He rests here.

EDCS-15100446.translation: [...]lia Amata, high priestess, lived 100 years. She rests here. II Felix III were there.

EDCS-15300090.translation: Cubelia, daughter of Caius, lived 20 years; she rests here.

EDCS-15300091.translation: Baebius Restutus, a most excellent man. Lucius Oppius Martialis, a most excellent man, son of Oppius, made this tombstone with his own money.
EDCS-15300091.summary: This is a funerary epitaph indicating that Lucius Oppius Martialis commissioned a tombstone for Baebius Restutus.

EDCS-15300106.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Valeria Quarta lived for 45 years.

EDCS-15300107.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Valeria Victoria lived for 83 years.

EDCS-15300108.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Lucius Volusinius Maximus lived 55 years; he is buried here.

EDCS-15300109.translation: [...]us Iuscus lived 57 years; he is buried here.

EDCS-15300111.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Postumia Secunda lived 45 years; she is buried here, a freedwoman of Postumius, to her mother and mistress.
EDCS-15300111.summary: A funerary inscription recording the death of Postumia Secunda at the age of 45, set up by her freedman son to his mother and mistress.

EDCS-15300113.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Arranius Fortunatus lived 8 years; he is buried here. Arranius Augustalis [erected this] for his son, a man worthy of respect.

EDCS-15300114.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Servilia Rogatiana lived 30 years; she is buried here. Arranius Augustalis set up this monument to his most rare wife.

EDCS-15300116.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Felix, a slave of our Emperor, lived 50 years.

EDCS-15300117.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Lollius Felix lived 62 years; he is buried here.

EDCS-15300130.translation: Dedicated to the Divine Spirits. Agellania Donata, daughter of Lucius, dutiful, lived 70 years, is buried here.

EDCS-15300139.translation: Dedicated to the Divine Spirits. Appius Fortunatus lived 52 years.

EDCS-15300140.translation: Dedicated to the Divine Spirits. Felix, who lived piously for 30 years. Marcus Germanicus Saturninus [erected this] for his dearest brother.
EDCS-15300140.summary: A funerary monument erected by Marcus Germanicus Saturninus for his brother Felix, who lived piously for 30 years.

EDCS-15300145.translation: Dedicated to the Divine Spirits. [---]naspeatu camo, dutiful, lived for [---] year. Dedicated to the Divine Spirits. Lucius Iulius Kastus, dutiful, lived 21 years.
EDCS-15300145.summary: This inscription contains two separate funerary dedications, one incomplete and another for Lucius Iulius Kastus, recording his age at death.

EDCS-15300146.translation: Dedicated to the Divine Spirits. Marcus Porcius Extricatus, son of Lucius, dutiful, lived 25 years, 4 months, and 10 days, is buried here.
EDCS-15300146.summary: A funerary inscription for Marcus Porcius Extricatus, son of Lucius, detailing his age at death and burial.

EDCS-15300147.translation: To the most fortunate era of our Lords Caius Aurelius Valerius Diocletianus Pius Felix Invictus Augustus and Marcus Aurelius Valerius Maximianus Pius Felix Invictus Augustus and Marcus Flavius Valerius Constantius and Caius Galerius Valerius Maximianus, most noble Caesars and consuls, by whose virtue and foresight all things are reformed for the better, the portico with its arch, which was missing for the circuit of the forum, was begun from the ground and completed with public money by Aurelius Aristobulus, a most distinguished man, proconsul of Africa, by the initiative of Macrinus Sossianus, a most distinguished man, governor, and was dedicated with the same governor, under the administration of the Republic of the Calamenses, by decree of the decurions, with public money.
EDCS-15300147.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a public portico and arch in a forum, built with public funds during the reign of Diocletian and Maximian and their Caesars, and initiated by the proconsul of Africa.

EDCS-15300148.translation: Papius, his son, [built] these at his own expense on his private land for his city of Mididita and for his fatherland.
EDCS-15300148.summary: This inscription records a private citizen, Papius, building structures at his own expense for the city of Mididita, likely a tomb or commemorative monument.

EDCS-15300149.translation: Sextus Volussius Maximus, with his children, dedicated this to Caius Mevius Silus Crescentius Fortunatianus, a most distinguished boy, patron, son of Caius Iulius Fortunatianus, an eminent man, patron.
EDCS-15300149.summary: This is a dedication by Sextus Volussius Maximus to his patron's son, Caius Mevius Silus Crescentius Fortunatianus, likely on a monument or tomb.
