EDCS-15300150.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Quintus Caecilius Martialis, recording his age and burial.

EDCS-15300151.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Laria Ornata lived for 10 years.
EDCS-15300151.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Laria Ornata, recording her age.

EDCS-15300152.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Iulius Dexter and Latinius Rogatianus made this monument for Octavius Fortunatianus, who lived for 30 years.
EDCS-15300152.summary: This funerary inscription records the creation of a monument by Lucius Iulius Dexter and Latinius Rogatianus for Octavius Fortunatianus.

EDCS-15300155.translation: Iulia Galli daughter lived for 60 years, deserving [of this remembrance].
EDCS-15300155.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Iulia Galli daughter, recording her age and a pious sentiment.

EDCS-15300156.translation: Lucius Volusius Saturninus the Younger, son of Lucius Volusius Saturninus, made this monument for his most dutiful father, and for Julia Severa his wife, and for their descendants.
EDCS-15300156.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording Lucius Volusius Saturninus the Younger's construction of a family monument for his father, mother, and descendants.

EDCS-15300157.translation: Resting here lies Honoratus, faithful, resting in peace. He lived 67 years and 2 months.
EDCS-15300157.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Honoratus, recording his lifespan and peace in death.

EDCS-15300158.translation: Sacred to Apollo the Father and Augustus. Tiberius Plautius, son of Tiberius, Papiria, Felix Ferruntianus, prefect of the First Wing of Thracian Veteran Archers, procurator for supplies and granaries, tribune of soldiers of the First Italian Legion, commander of detachments of Pontus in Scythia and Taurica, commander of detachments of the Third Augustan Legion among the Marcomanni, awarded military decorations D.
EDCS-15300158.summary: This is a dedication to Apollo and Augustus by Tiberius Plautius Felix Ferruntianus, listing his extensive military and administrative career and decorations, likely marking a public building or shrine.

EDCS-15300160.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari divi Nervae filio Nervae Traiano optimo Augusto Germanico Parthico pontifici maximo tribunicia potestate XX imperatori XII consuli Vl Caecilius Faustinus proconsul dedicavit decreto decurionum pecunia publica\n
EDCS-15300160.translation: Caecilius Faustinus, proconsul, dedicated this at the decree of the town councillors with public money to Emperor Caesar Nerva Traianus Optimus Augustus Germanicus Parthicus, son of the deified Nerva, Pontifex Maximus, with tribunician power for the 20th time, Imperator for the 12th time, Consul for the 6th time.
EDCS-15300160.summary: An official dedication to Emperor Trajan, likely from a provincial capital, commissioned by the proconsul Caecilius Faustinus on behalf of the local council.

EDCS-15300161.translation: To Emperor Caesar Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Augustus Pius, son of the deified Hadrian, grandson of the deified Trajan the Parthian, great-grandson of the deified Nerva, pontifex maximus, holder of tribunician power for the 20th time, imperator for the 2nd time, consul for the 4th time, father of the fatherland. Publius [---] concerning the honor of the prefecture... [---]
EDCS-15300161.summary: This inscription records honors for Emperor Antoninus Pius, possibly related to a prefecture, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-15300165.translation: To Cocceia Bassula Numisia Procula, by decree of the local councilors, at public expense.
EDCS-15300165.summary: This inscription is a public dedication to Cocceia Bassula Numisia Procula, likely a woman of high status, funded by the town council, probably from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15300166.translation: To Quintus Rupilius Honoratus, son of Quintus, of the Papiria tribe, appointed to the equestrian ranks by the deified Alexander, perpetual flamen, by Lucius Popilius Saturninus, his incomparable patron.
EDCS-15300166.summary: This inscription honors Quintus Rupilius Honoratus, who was appointed to equestrian rank and served as perpetual flamen, and is dedicated by his patron, Lucius Popilius Saturninus, likely from the 3rd century CE.

EDCS-15300167.translation: Publius Honoratus, son of Publius, a veteran of Legio III Augusta, lived 70 years. He lies here.
EDCS-15300167.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Publius Honoratus, a veteran of Legio III Augusta, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15300168.translation: To Lucius Iulius Victor Optatianus, son of Quintus, of the Horatia tribe, a most distinguished citizen of the curia.
EDCS-15300168.summary: This inscription honors Lucius Iulius Victor Optatianus, a prominent citizen associated with the local council (curia), likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15300169.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Gaius Verrius Rogatus, son of Quintilius, of the Quirina tribe, perpetual flamen and quinquennial official, who discharged all honors, lived piously for 65 years. He lies here.
EDCS-15300169.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Gaius Verrius Rogatus, a local religious and civic official, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15300170.translation: To Quintus Iulius Victor Virrius Rogatus, for his service as a duovir and aedile of the colony of Assur. Iulius Optatianus and Victor, his children, [dedicate this] to their most excellent father.
EDCS-15300170.summary: This inscription is a dedication by children to their father, Quintus Iulius Victor Virrius Rogatus, who held local magistracies in the colony of Assur, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15300174.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Annius Datianus lived 17 years.
EDCS-15300174.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Lucius Annius Datianus, who died at the age of 17, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15300175.translation: Gaius Annius Faustinus lived 60 years. He lies here.
EDCS-15300175.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Gaius Annius Faustinus, who died at the age of 60, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15300176.translation: Lucius Antonius Saturninus the dutiful lived 30 years.
EDCS-15300176.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Lucius Antonius Saturninus, who died at the age of 30, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15300177.translation: Apollinaris, son of Caius, of the voting tribe Quirina, lived for 42 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-15300177.summary: A funerary inscription recording the lifespan and burial of Apollinaris.

EDCS-15300178.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Aurelius Honoratus lived for 2 years, 6 months, and 5 days.
EDCS-15300178.summary: A funerary inscription recording the short lifespan of Aurelius Honoratus.

EDCS-15300180.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Bassidia Fortunata, dutiful, lived for 69 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-15300180.summary: A funerary inscription recording the lifespan and burial of Bassidia Fortunata.

EDCS-15300181.translation: M. A. Fortunata made this for her husband O. A. Victor, who lived for 50 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-15300181.summary: A funerary inscription commemorating a husband, made by his wife.

EDCS-15300182.translation: Gaius Julius, of the voting tribe Quirina.
EDCS-15300182.summary: A fragmentary inscription likely recording a name and tribal affiliation.

EDCS-15300183.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus Julius Felix, dutiful, lived for 60 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-15300183.summary: A funerary inscription recording the lifespan and burial of Quintus Julius Felix.

EDCS-15300185.translation: His father restored this tombstone to Gaius Julius Proculus Fortunatianus, his son, who had been snatched away, having lived twenty-two years, which the Fates had decreed, and he gave back all of his age by the gift of innumerable praises of his life, for in a short time he gave the best examples of youth and manhood by living well, he exhibited the beginnings of manhood with a youthful heart, he adorned the life of youth with the greatest glory, so indeed as if he had lived many years in a short time, as a boy strong in intellect, as a youth modest, as a young man he was an orator and delighted the public ears with his studies in the toga; thus indeed in a short time in life with many praises and in this paternal work, as a young man now as an old man he rests in perpetual peace, a welcome spirit to the maker.
EDCS-15300185.summary: A lengthy funerary epitaph praising the deceased, Gaius Julius Proculus Fortunatianus, highlighting his brief but virtuous life, intellectual talents, and oratorical skills.

EDCS-15300186.translation: Iulius Maximus dedicated this structure to his Pallia Saturnina, formerly his own, so that he might always have it as a gift and at the same time a memorial of his dutiful wife, and that the reader might conclude his own time within it along with her, in the thirty years in which she was given to him, she lived very well with her husband, desiring nothing more than that her home should rejoice in her possessions, for in her husband's and her own affairs, she was a common mother to the young, living with a simple spirit, she claimed little of the feminine world for herself, she was religious towards her husband, modest in herself, a mother in the family, she never knew how to be angry or to plot against anyone, neglecting the adornment of her body, she adorned herself with her character and accompanied no one from the family except by her own modesty.
EDCS-15300186.summary: A funerary monument dedicated by Iulius Maximus to his deceased wife, Pallia Saturnina, praising her virtues, domesticity, and modesty during their thirty-year marriage.

EDCS-15300187.translation: In obedience he surpassed him, fire which he always desired for himself, and his brother with V virgins lived twice ten orbits, MOSVA, light ones, buried here, she lives forever for herself.
EDCS-15300187.summary: A fragmented and difficult funerary inscription, possibly mentioning obedience, a brother, virgins, and the deceased's eternal life.

EDCS-15300188.summary: An inscription recording the full name and filiation of Marcus Iulius Maximus Flavianus.

EDCS-15300265.translation: Dedicated to the Divine Shades. Sextus Rocius Bassus, son of Marcus, of the Horatia tribe, twice chief magistrate, quinquennial chief magistrate, perpetual priest, prefect of engineers, a dutiful man, lived 75 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-15300265.summary: A funerary epitaph for Sextus Rocius Bassus, detailing his numerous public offices and lifespan, likely from the late Roman Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-15300266.translation: Two miles from Philippi, son of Augustus.
EDCS-15300266.summary: A milestone marker indicating a distance of two miles from Philippi, likely related to imperial road infrastructure.

EDCS-15300267.summary: A fragmentary inscription likely referring to an emperor, possibly part of a dedication or title.

EDCS-15300269.translation: Sacred to the god Mercury Augustus.
EDCS-15300269.summary: A dedication to the god Mercury, incorporating the imperial title 'Augustus', suggesting a date from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15300270.translation: It was decided that the names of those who built the portico with collected funds should be inscribed; they paid from their own expenses. Donatus and Salus Barih, and Octavius Adaer, and Biricius Tertius, and Rogatianus Varius, and Fortunatus Venustus, and Silvanus made it with their own money.
EDCS-15300270.summary: An inscription recording the collective funding and construction of a portico by several individuals, likely a public benefaction.

EDCS-15300271.translation: Defender of the city, you are covered by the tomb of a weasel.
EDCS-15300271.summary: A pithy epitaph, possibly sarcastic, for a defender of the city buried in a humble grave.

EDCS-15300274.translation: The place of Reparatus the presbyter.
EDCS-15300274.summary: A funerary marker indicating a burial plot belonging to Reparatus, a presbyter (an early Christian elder).

EDCS-15300275.translation: Reparatus the cleric lived 15 years, laid to rest in peace on the Ides of July.
EDCS-15300275.summary: A Christian epitaph for Reparatus, a cleric, recording his age at death and burial date.

EDCS-15300277.translation: Florentius the subdeacon lived [until] the Kalends of February.
EDCS-15300277.summary: A Christian epitaph for Florentius, a subdeacon, indicating the date of his death.

EDCS-15300279.translation: Donatus the lector was laid to rest in peace on the 4th day before the Kalends of May, in the eighth indiction, in the month of April.
EDCS-15300279.summary: A Christian epitaph for Donatus, a lector, specifying his burial date and the imperial 'indiction' cycle, suggesting a Late Roman or Byzantine date.

EDCS-15300280.translation: Agricola, a man of the highest distinction, governor of the province and supervisor of public works, restored the temple of the god PFE by his own generosity.
EDCS-15300280.summary: This inscription records the restoration of a temple by Agricola, who served as provincial governor and supervisor of public works, likely in the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-15300281.translation: Sextus Vitellius, the pontifex, made this at his own expense for the almighty Jupiter and Ceres.
EDCS-15300281.summary: This inscription records a private dedication of a religious offering or structure to Jupiter and Ceres by Sextus Vitellius, a pontifex, likely in the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15300286.translation: Rogatus Dini Pantoni erected this statue for the Emperor Caesar Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Augustus Pius, father of the fatherland, using 800 sesterces which he owed for the honor of the office of suffete, and he also dedicated it.
EDCS-15300286.summary: This inscription records the erection and dedication of a statue to Emperor Antoninus Pius by Rogatus Dini Pantoni, using funds owed for the office of suffete, likely in the mid-2nd century CE.

EDCS-15300287.translation: On the eleventh day before the Kalends of January, in memory of the saints Heraclius, Donatus, Zebbecis, Secundianus, Victor, and Publicia Meggenis.
EDCS-15300287.summary: This inscription records a commemoration of martyrs or saints on a specific date, likely from the later Roman Empire or early Christian period.

EDCS-15300288.translation: Novellus, the deacon, fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-15300288.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by Novellus, identified as a deacon, likely from the early Christian period.

EDCS-15300290.summary: This inscription is a short epitaph for Donatus, identified as a lector, indicating his peaceful passing, likely from the early Christian period.

EDCS-15300292.summary: This inscription is a short epitaph recording the lifespan of an individual as 19 days, likely from the Roman Imperial or early Christian period.

EDCS-15300293.translation: Here lies Ilia Hospita; Bassilica made (this) from the workshop of Catti Laggi of Thibica.
EDCS-15300293.summary: This inscription is an epitaph for Ilia Hospita, stating she was made by Bassilica from the workshop of Catti Laggi of Thibica, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15300294.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Iulius Rogatianus, an equestrian of the Pannonian cavalry, lived for 22 years.
EDCS-15300294.summary: This inscription is an epitaph for Iulius Rogatianus, an equestrian serving in the Pannonian cavalry, who died at the age of 22, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15400775.summary: This inscription is a very brief epitaph for Pallia Saturnina, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15400776.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Gaius Julius Fortunatianus.

EDCS-15400778.translation: Of Marcus Julius Maximus, the builder.
EDCS-15400778.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Marcus Julius Maximus, identified as a builder.

EDCS-15400779.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Aucronia Rogatiana.

EDCS-15400780.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Gaius Julius Montanus the Younger lived for [---]. Gaius Julius Primus lived for 4 years, is buried here. [His parents] Iulius Secundianus and Coronata [placed this].
EDCS-15400780.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Gaius Julius Primus, who lived for 4 years, and was placed here by his parents, Iulius Secundianus and Coronata, also mentioning Gaius Julius Montanus the Younger.

EDCS-15400781.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Magnia Maxima lived for 85 years. Gaius Valerius Felix, honored by his skill, pious, lived for 80 years, is buried here. Valeria Maximilla lived for 2 years and 1 month. Gaius Valerius Vindemialis lived for 1 year, 11 months, and 23 days.
EDCS-15400781.summary: This funerary inscription records the lives and burials of Magnia Maxima, Gaius Valerius Felix, Valeria Maximilla, and Gaius Valerius Vindemialis.

EDCS-15400782.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Mantia Tertulla, daughter of Publius, pious, lived for 53 years, is buried here.
EDCS-15400782.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Mantia Tertulla, daughter of Publius, who lived for 53 years.

EDCS-15400783.translation: Lucius Naevius Maximus, pious, lived for 20 years and 11 months, is buried here.
EDCS-15400783.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Lucius Naevius Maximus, who lived for 20 years and 11 months.

EDCS-15400784.translation: Porcius Maximus Humilis, pious, lived for 20 years.
EDCS-15400784.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespan of Porcius Maximus Humilis, who lived for 20 years.

EDCS-15400785.translation: Quintus Refrius Africanus, son of Caius, of the Aemilia tribe, pious, lived for 77 years, is buried here. May the earth lie lightly upon you.
EDCS-15400785.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Quintus Refrius Africanus, son of Caius, and includes a wish for his peaceful rest.

EDCS-15400786.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Sempronius Saturninus lived for 45 years, is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits, to my most excellent wife Sempronia Victoria.
EDCS-15400786.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Sempronius Saturninus and includes a dedication to his wife, Sempronia Victoria.

EDCS-15400787.translation: Pious Terentia Prima lived 80 years, she is buried here.
EDCS-15400787.summary: This is a tombstone epitaph for Terentia Prima, recording her age at death.

EDCS-15400788.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Pious Vesta Ianuaria lived 66 years. Pious Quintus Caecilius Secundus.
EDCS-15400788.summary: This epitaph is dedicated to the departed spirits and records the lifespan of Vesta Ianuaria and mentions Quintus Caecilius Secundus.

EDCS-15400789.translation: Lucius Victrius Polybius, freedman of Lucius, lived 25 years, he is buried here.
EDCS-15400789.summary: This tombstone epitaph records the lifespan of Lucius Victrius Polybius, a freedman.

EDCS-15400792.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Iulius Fasir lived 45 years, he is buried here.
EDCS-15400792.summary: This epitaph is dedicated to the departed spirits and records the lifespan of Iulius Fasir.

EDCS-15400795.translation: Flabius Argutio lived 30 years, one month, and 24 days in peace.
EDCS-15400795.summary: This epitaph records the lifespan of Flabius Argutio, noting his age in years, months, and days.

EDCS-15400796.translation: Licinius Gulosus the faithful lived 58 years, 8 months, and 5 days in peace. He was laid to rest on the 6th day before the Kalends of July.
EDCS-15400796.summary: This epitaph records the lifespan and burial date of the faithful Licinius Gulosus.

EDCS-15400797.translation: Paulinus the faithful lived about 10 years, 10 months, and 5 hours in peace.
EDCS-15400797.summary: This epitaph records the lifespan of Paulinus the faithful, noting his age in years, months, and hours.

EDCS-15400798.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Pompeius Cercadio lived 15 years and 5 months in peace.
EDCS-15400798.summary: This epitaph is dedicated to the departed spirits and records the lifespan of Pompeius Cercadio.

EDCS-15400799.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Triaria lived 9 years.
EDCS-15400799.summary: This epitaph is dedicated to the departed spirits and records the lifespan of Triaria.

EDCS-15400803.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Antonius Optatianus lived 30 years and 4 months and a day.
EDCS-15400803.summary: This epitaph is dedicated to the departed spirits and records the lifespan of Antonius Optatianus.

EDCS-15400804.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Aurelia Vindicta, priestess of Venus, lived 80 years. Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Marcus Aurelius Dativos of Esucis lived 70 years.
EDCS-15400804.summary: This is a funerary inscription for two individuals, Aurelia Vindicta and Marcus Aurelius Dativos, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15400805.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription that records the name Iulia Rogata and mentions her lifespan, but the duration is missing.

EDCS-15400806.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Licinius Maurus, founder of this work, dedicated it of his own will for himself and his descendants, so that the Manes might always inhabit a secure place. He dedicated this construction of his work to Licinia Vestalica, once his wife, so that he might always have it as a dedication and at the same time make a memorial of his dutiful wife, and in that time conclude himself with her, in the 14 years in which it was granted that they might live alike. Also to Fortunata, his dutiful mother, he lived 85 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-15400806.summary: This is a complex funerary inscription by Licinius Maurus, who built a monument for himself, his wife Licinia Vestalica, and his mother Fortunata, likely during the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15400807.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Liciniae Vindemiae, the dutiful, lived 40 years. Licinius Burianus for his incomparable wife. She is buried here.
EDCS-15400807.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by Licinius Burianus to his wife Licinia Vindemia, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15400808.translation: Umbrius Victorianus, so that it might never be doubted in later times who among mortals had been buried in this earth, took care to inscribe "Victorianus"; he left his fame to posterity with great piety, having divided all his wealth. He lived 69 years. Umbria Veia lived in peace 14 years and 5 months. Umbria C... lived in peace 44 years and 3 months.
EDCS-15400808.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Umbria Victorianus and two other Umbrias, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period, emphasizing piety and lasting fame.

EDCS-15400809.translation: Sacred to Rome and to the Emperor Tiberius Caesar Augustus. On the 7th day before the Kalends of November. Tribune of the Plebs.
EDCS-15400809.summary: This is a dedication to Emperor Tiberius Caesar Augustus, likely a public inscription possibly related to a magistracy, dating to his reign (14-37 AD).

EDCS-15400810.translation: Mactaritanus, duovir quinquennalis, made this alive for myself and my descendants.
EDCS-15400810.summary: This is a funerary or dedicatory inscription by Mactaritanus, a high-ranking local magistrate (duovir quinquennalis), likely dating to the Roman Imperial period in a provincial town.

EDCS-15400811.translation: Aemilia Rogata, the dutiful, lived [missing years]
EDCS-15400811.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription that records the name Aemilia Rogata and mentions her lifespan, but the duration is missing.

EDCS-15400812.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Namphamus, son of Homullus, made a mausoleum for himself and his wife, extending to the public wall and the neighborhood path.
EDCS-15400812.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Namphamus and his wife, who built a mausoleum, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15400813.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Sextus Valerius Extricatus, son of Sextus, the dutiful, lived 57 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-15400813.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Sextus Valerius Extricatus, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15400814.translation: Marcus Valerius Victor lived 105 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-15400814.summary: A tombstone inscription recording the lifespan and burial of Marcus Valerius Victor.

EDCS-15400815.translation: Son of M. Itfilarus, pious, lived 35 years.
EDCS-15400815.summary: A tombstone inscription recording the lifespan of a man identified by his patronymic and piety.

EDCS-15400822.translation: Saturninus, son of Muthunsachon, perpetual priest, appointed with the consent of the entire citizenry of Chusira, made this altar at his own expense, during the reign of Emperor Caesar Vespasian Augustus, pontifex maximus, holding tribunician power, consul for the third time.
EDCS-15400822.summary: An altar dedication by Saturninus, son of Muthunsachon, a perpetual priest, during the reign of Vespasian.

EDCS-15400825.translation: To Ianus, a man of consular rank, proconsul of Africa.
EDCS-15400825.summary: An inscription honoring Ianus, a former proconsul of Africa.

EDCS-15400826.translation: Iulius Ingenus died in Gaul; his wife entrusts his body to the embrace of his homeland. Virula earned her place in Germany, serving as a speculator and cornicularius of the legion. The beginning of his life was its end.
EDCS-15400826.summary: A funerary inscription for Iulius Ingenus, a soldier who died in Gaul, and his wife Virula, with a philosophical reflection on life and death.

EDCS-15400827.translation: Quintus Arranius Regulus, son of Caius, perpetual priest, built this at his own expense for the convenience of the people and also dedicated it.
EDCS-15400827.summary: An inscription recording the construction and dedication of a public work by Quintus Arranius Regulus, a perpetual priest.

EDCS-15400828.translation: Danius, perpetual priest, Roman knight, curator of the state.
EDCS-15400828.summary: An inscription listing the offices held by Danius: perpetual priest, Roman knight, and curator rei publicae.

EDCS-15400833.translation: Ausanius the faithful lived 72 years in peace.
EDCS-15400833.summary: A tombstone inscription recording the lifespan and peaceful death of Ausanius.

EDCS-15400837.translation: For the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Severus Alexander Pius Felix Augustus, son of the deified great Antoninus Pius, grandson of the deified Severus; he adorned (this) with his own money.
EDCS-15400837.summary: An inscription indicating that someone financed decorations or a monument for Emperor Severus Alexander.

EDCS-15400839.translation: Marcus Lorenius Lorenianus, having held all honors, when he had requested the order to erect a statue in the forum of his municipality to his son Publius Lorenianus Pudentius, a pious aedile, and the order had decreed it to his father, he himself, with the expense remitted and offered to him, erected the statue of his son and dedicated it. With public money, on the seventh day before the Kalends of April, when Lupo and Maximo were consuls.
EDCS-15400839.summary: An inscription detailing the circumstances under which Marcus Lorenius Lorenianus erected a statue to his son, a deceased aedile, using public funds during the consulship of Lupo and Maximo.

EDCS-15400841.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Aelia Gallitta lived piously for 33 years and 4 months; she is buried here. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Caius Cosconius Victor lived piously for [---] years; he is buried here.
EDCS-15400841.summary: Two tombstone inscriptions, one for Aelia Gallitta and one for Caius Cosconius Victor, recording their lifespans and burial.

EDCS-15400842.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Gaius Amullius Donatianus, dutiful, lived 22 years, 4 months, 5 days; he is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Amullia Victoria, dutiful, lived 15 years, 2 days; she is buried here.
EDCS-15400842.summary: This epitaph records the deaths of Gaius Amullius Donatianus and Amullia Victoria, likely siblings or family members, who died at young ages.

EDCS-15400843.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Gaius Amullius Silvanus, dutiful, lived 75 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-15400843.summary: This epitaph records the death of Gaius Amullius Silvanus, who died at the age of 75.

EDCS-15400844.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Amullius Tertullus Rogatianus lived 3 years, 2 months; he is buried here.
EDCS-15400844.summary: This epitaph records the death of Amullius Tertullus Rogatianus, who died at a very young age.

EDCS-15400846.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Amullia Urbana, dutiful, lived 4 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-15400846.summary: This epitaph records the death of Amullia Urbana, who died at the age of 4.

EDCS-15400847.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcus Antonius Faustianus, grandson, dutifully lived 43 years, 7 months, 15 days; he is buried here.
EDCS-15400847.summary: This epitaph records the death of Marcus Antonius Faustianus, who died at the age of 43.

EDCS-15400850.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Caledius Saturninus, dutiful, lived 30 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-15400850.summary: This epitaph records the death of Caledius Saturninus, who died at the age of 30.

EDCS-15400851.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Clarus Bonicianus, a youth refined in all respects, incomparable in modesty, renowned for his morals and intellect, delightful in all simplicity, always dear to his parents, he lived with their highest affection, 21 years, 1 month; he is buried here.
EDCS-15400851.summary: This epitaph records the death of Clarus Bonicianus, a young man praised for his virtues, who died at the age of 21.

EDCS-15400852.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcus C Vilaticus, dutiful, lived 20 years, 15 days. Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcus C Maximus Iunior, dutiful, lived 10 years, 9 months, 5 days.
EDCS-15400852.summary: This epitaph records the deaths of two individuals, Marcus C Vilaticus and Marcus C Maximus Iunior, likely family members, who died at young ages.

EDCS-15400853.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Publius Domitius Brutius lived 73 years.
EDCS-15400853.summary: This epitaph records the death of Publius Domitius Brutius, who lived to be 73 years old.

EDCS-15400854.translation: Titus Ennius Gratus lived 50 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-15400854.summary: This epitaph records the death and burial of Titus Ennius Gratus, who died at the age of 50.

EDCS-15400857.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Marcus Insteius Ianuarius, dutiful, lived 70 years and 7 months; he is buried here.
EDCS-15400857.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Marcus Insteius Ianuarius, who lived 70 years and 7 months.

EDCS-15400858.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Marcus Iunius Victor Maculianus, dutiful, lived 5 years.
EDCS-15400858.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Marcus Iunius Victor Maculianus, who died at the age of 5.

EDCS-15400859.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Lucius Kaledius Victor, dutiful, lived 5 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-15400859.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Kaledius Victor, who died at the age of 5.

EDCS-15400860.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld, in memory of his parents Caius Marius of Rome and Magna, daughter of Publius.
EDCS-15400860.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the parents of an unnamed individual.

EDCS-15400861.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Lucius Messius Honoratus lived 18 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-15400861.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Messius Honoratus, who died at the age of 18.

EDCS-15400862.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Percenia Romanilla, dutiful, lived 16 years, 7 months, and 15 days; she is buried here.
EDCS-15400862.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Percenia Romanilla, who died at the age of 16 years, 7 months, and 15 days.

EDCS-15400864.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Titus Petronius Avitus, dutiful, lived 18 years and 10 months; he is buried here.
EDCS-15400864.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Titus Petronius Avitus, who died at the age of 18 years and 10 months.

EDCS-15400865.translation: CIL I [or perhaps other context suggests CIL, not EDCS-ID] Saturninus Torianus lived 53 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-15400865.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Saturninus Torianus, who died at the age of 53.

EDCS-15400866.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Gaius Sipius Rufinus, to his most loving Primigenius, and Antonia Ingenua, his mother, and Antiochis, his grandmother, and his dutiful grandfather, lived 18 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-15400866.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Gaius Sipius Rufinus, dedicated by his mother, grandmother, and grandfather, who died at the age of 18.

EDCS-15400867.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Sulpicia Crescentia, dutiful, lived 85 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-15400867.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Sulpicia Crescentia, who died at the age of 85.

EDCS-15400869.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Titus Tissenius Honoratus, dutiful, lived 70 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-15400869.summary: A funerary epitaph for Titus Tissenius Honoratus, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15400870.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Tissen.
EDCS-15400870.summary: A funerary epitaph fragment for someone named Tissen, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15600004.translation: By order of the Emperor Caesar Trajan Hadrian Augustus, the boundary markers were restored by Capiton Pomponianus, through Peregrinus, a freedman of the Emperor sent by him, a surveyor, between the communities of the Suppenses and the Vofricenses.
EDCS-15600004.summary: An inscription recording the restoration of boundary markers by an imperial surveyor under Emperor Hadrian, likely in the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-15600014.translation: To the deified Hadrian, father of the Emperor Caesar Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Augustus Pius, chief priest, with tribunician power for the 9th time, consul for the 4th time, father of his country. Germanus, son of Passus of Sutunurca, on account of the honor of the perpetual priesthood for his daughter Quinta, made a legitimate statue of the deified Hadrian and Caesar Aelius with 4,000 sesterces, adding 525 sesterces from his own funds, by decree of the decurions, with his own money, and gave a gymnasium to the people.
EDCS-15600014.summary: A dedication for a statue and gymnasium made by Germanus in honor of his daughter's perpetual priesthood, honoring Emperor Hadrian and Aelius Caesar, dating to the reign of Antoninus Pius (mid-2nd century CE).

EDCS-15600019.summary: A dedication by Lucius, son of Cesennius, likely for a religious or public monument, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15600039.text_edition: \n Memoria marturum sic Rogati Vitalis IESTES animas s perenn \n
EDCS-15600039.translation: In memory of the martyrs, Rogatus Vitalis, your souls live on forever.
EDCS-15600039.summary: A memorial inscription for martyrs, possibly referring to Rogatus Vitalis, invoking their eternal remembrance.

EDCS-15600040.summary: A short epitaph for a person named Maxima, indicating peaceful rest.

EDCS-15600041.translation: In memory of Amantius the priest, worshipper of the true God, who also rests in Abraham's bosom with the martyrs, with Hilara, his companion. In memory of Amantius the priest, Hilara, and Aurelia.
EDCS-15600041.summary: A Christian funerary inscription commemorating Amantius the priest, his wife Hilara, and Aurelia, likely dating to the 3rd or 4th century CE.

EDCS-15600042.summary: A simple epitaph stating the burial place of Sabina.

EDCS-15600043.translation: In memory of Crescens, Victor, [offering] to God.
EDCS-15600043.summary: A funerary inscription for Crescens and Victor, with a possible Christian or late Roman pagan dedication, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15600044.translation: Urbana of Lambdia departed on the 13th day before the Kalends of December, to one who deserved well.
EDCS-15600044.summary: A funerary epitaph for Urbana of Lambdia, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15600846.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus Veianius Rufinianus, dutiful, lived 31 years and 1 month and 5 days. He is buried here.
EDCS-15600846.summary: A funerary epitaph for Quintus Veianius Rufinianus, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15600847.translation: Marcus Domitius Antoninus lived 73 years and 5 months in peace.
EDCS-15600847.summary: A funerary epitaph for Marcus Domitius Antoninus, likely a Christian given the phrase 'in pace', dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15600848.translation: Privatianus lived in peace for 41 years and 5 days.
EDCS-15600848.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Privatianus, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15600849.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. V. R. T. Opta M. Redaco V. lived for 60 years, is buried here.
EDCS-15600849.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Opta M. Redaco V., dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15600852.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Perellia Maior, a dutiful daughter of Lucius, lived for 46 years, is buried here.
EDCS-15600852.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Perellia Maior, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15600853.translation: Sacred to Fortuna Redux Augusta, for the health of the Emperor Caesar, son of the deified Marcus Antoninus Pius Germanicus Sarmaticus, brother of the deified Commodus, nephew of the deified Antoninus Pius, great-nephew of the deified Hadrian, great-great-nephew of the deified Trajan Parthicus, great-great-great-nephew of the deified Nerva, Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus Arabicus Adiabenicus, pontifex maximus, holding tribunician power for the 4th time, imperator for the 8th time, consul for the 2nd time, father of the country, and of Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Caesar, his son, and of their entire divine family. Marcus Pinarius Fortunatus, perpetual flamen, who had promised from his own flaminate funds of 7,000 sesterces to distribute 1,000 sesterces for the temple of Fortuna, completed the temple, which was built on public land, with his own funds increased, and dedicated it himself. Furthermore, for the dedication, he gave gifts to the decurions, and also a feast and gymnasium to all the citizens, and presented a spectacle of stage plays.
EDCS-15600853.summary: This is a dedication of a temple to Fortuna Redux Augusta by Marcus Pinarius Fortunatus, a perpetual flamen, for the health of Emperor Septimius Severus and his son Caracalla, likely dating to the early 3rd century CE.

EDCS-15600857.translation: With just votes and a decree, the most distinguished Galibus and the beloved homeland erected a statue with outstanding adornment to the most brilliant Calipodius, acknowledging his sweet virtue and the eternal memory of his excellent duty for all time.
EDCS-15600857.summary: This inscription records the erection of a statue honoring Flavius Calipodius for his distinguished service, likely from the late Roman Empire.

EDCS-15600858.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcus Iulius Seranianus, perpetual flamen, an honorable man, lived for 76 years and 5 months, is buried here.
EDCS-15600858.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Marcus Iulius Seranianus, a perpetual flamen, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15600859.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcus Iulius Seranianus, an honorable man, perpetual flamen, lived for 70 years and one month and 21 days, is buried here.
EDCS-15600859.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Marcus Iulius Seranianus, a perpetual flamen, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15600860.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcus Iulius Seranianus, perpetual flamen, lived for 67 years and 5 months, is buried here.
EDCS-15600860.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Marcus Iulius Seranianus, a perpetual flamen, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15600861.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Fabia Furniermitalis Vincentia lived for 25 years, 2 months, and 15 days.
EDCS-15600861.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Fabia Furniermitalis Vincentia, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15600862.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Titissenia Saturnina lived for 35 years, is buried here.
EDCS-15600862.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Titissenia Saturnina, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15600864.translation: Sacred to Aesculapius Augustus, for the safety of the Emperor Caesar Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Augustus Pius and his children, the city of Thibica made this by decree of the decurions, with public funds, under the supervision of Felix Victor, son of a suffete.
EDCS-15600864.summary: This is a dedication to Aesculapius Augustus made by the city of Thibica for the health of the emperor and his children.

EDCS-15600868.translation: Lucius Plancius Victorianus, son of Lucius, perpetual flamen, and Caius Volussius Statianus, perpetual flamen, elected by law, for the honor of their fatherland, through their great liberality, having been granted distinguished honors for their aedileship, made this; and on the day of dedication they gave gifts to the decurions and a banquet and a gymnasium to the citizens; the place was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-15600868.summary: This inscription records a public works project funded by two perpetual flamines in honor of their city, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15600869.translation: Felicula, daughter of Terius Sterceianus, wife and mother of their sons; Caius Aedinius Sterceianus, son of Felicis Sterceianus, father of a son, made this with repeated tears. She lived 35 years, 2 months, 10 days, 1 hour. She is buried here. Caius Aedinius Felix Renatus, son of Sterceianus, grandson of Felicis, and Aedinia Ca Rufa, daughter of Sterceianus, granddaughter of Felicis.
EDCS-15600869.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Felicula and her husband Caius Aedinius Sterceianus, detailing family relationships and lifespans, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15600870.translation: Marcus Cornelius Felicis lived 30 years. Sextus Cornelius Felix, Cornelia Tertia, daughter of Corneli Surus.
EDCS-15600870.summary: This is a brief epitaph recording the names and lifespans of Marcus Cornelius Felicis and others, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15600871.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Dead. Septimia Honorata, devoted, lived 35 years. She is buried here. Quintus made this for his most devoted wife.
EDCS-15600871.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Quintus for his wife Septimia Honorata, indicating her devotion and lifespan, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15600872.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Dead. Caius Turranius Honoratus, son of Caius, devoted, lived 10 years and 2 days. He is buried here. Caius Turranius Adiutor, a soldier in the stationed garrison, set this up for his most obedient son.
EDCS-15600872.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Caius Turranius Honoratus, a young boy, erected by his father Caius Turranius Adiutor, a soldier, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15600873.translation: The local god, where the auspices of dignity are such, the elders of the municipium of Apisa.
EDCS-15600873.summary: This is a very brief inscription mentioning a local deity and the elders of Apisa, possibly related to a religious or civic act.

EDCS-15600876.translation: For the Emperor Caesar, son of the deified Marcus, brother of the deified Commodus, grandson of the deified Pius, great-grandson of the deified Hadrian, great-great-grandson of the deified Trajan Parthicus, great-great-great-grandson of the deified Nerva, Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus Arabicus Adiabenicus, father of the fatherland, holding tribunician power for the 9th time, imperator for the 8th time, consul for the 2nd time, proconsul, the city of Apisa Maius by decree of the decurions, with public funds.
EDCS-15600876.summary: This is a dedication to Emperor Septimius Severus by the city of Apisa Maius, listing his extensive imperial titles and honors, likely dating to his reign (193-211 AD).

EDCS-15600877.translation: To Emperor Caesar Pius Felix Augustus Severus Alexander.
EDCS-15600877.summary: This is a dedication or reference to Emperor Severus Alexander, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15600878.translation: To our Lord Emperor Augustus Flavius Valentinianus Pius Felix victor and perpetual triumphator, the devoted order of the municipium of Apisa Maior, with Valerius Marinus, curator of the public affairs.
EDCS-15600878.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Emperor Valentinian I (reigned 364-375 AD) by the city of Apisa Maior and its curator, Valerius Marinus.

EDCS-15600879.translation: The devoted council of the municipality of Apisensium Maiorum, with Valerius Marinus as curator of the state, to our lord Emperor Flavius Valens Pius Felix, victorious and triumphant forever.
EDCS-15600879.summary: This inscription records a dedication by the local council of Apisensium Maiorum to Emperor Valens, likely in the late 4th century CE.

EDCS-15600882.translation: Acting as deputy prefect of the praetorian guard, in response to the clemency of the age.
EDCS-15600882.summary: This fragmented inscription likely refers to an official acting under the authority of a prefect of the praetorian guard, possibly in the later Roman Empire.

EDCS-15600884.translation: To Julianus Pius the Emperor V.
EDCS-15600884.summary: This short inscription is a dedication to Emperor Julian (known as Julian the Apostate), likely dating to his reign in the mid-4th century CE.

EDCS-15600888.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Marcus Gorcius Victor Honoratianus, dutiful, lived 4 years, 9 months, 23 days; he is buried here.
EDCS-15600888.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a young boy named Marcus Gorcius Victor Honoratianus, providing his age at death and burial location.

EDCS-15600889.translation: Caius Julius Felix Primus Tert, Marcus Aulenius, shepherd, BAN Ceparius Magni Magni IAFICI AFIC.
EDCS-15600889.summary: This inscription appears to be a list of names, possibly related to a business or collegium, with some illegible abbreviations.

EDCS-15600890.summary: This is a simple epitaph indicating that Aurelia Sallustia has died and is now 'in peace', likely from the Christian period.

EDCS-15600891.translation: Publius Ennius, son of Titus, grandson of Eppillus, of the tribe Quirina, from Paccianus, having received benefits from the Legio II Augusta under Emperor Domitian Caesar Augustus Germanicus, consul for the 13th time.
EDCS-15600891.summary: This inscription records Publius Ennius, a soldier from Legio II Augusta, who received benefits from Emperor Domitian, likely dating to Domitian's reign (81-96 CE).

EDCS-15600892.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Gadaeus, son of Felix, dutiful, lived 66 years; he is buried here. Secunda, daughter of Secundus, lived [years]; Gadaeus [dedicated this] to his most dutiful father.
EDCS-15600892.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Gadaeus, who lived 66 years, and his wife Secunda, dedicated by their son Gadaeus.

EDCS-15600895.translation: Sacred to the eternal, outstanding, and propitious divine power. Victor, the priest, and Arrius Servilius, administering affairs, and also paved the entire sanctuary with flagstones on the fifth day before the Ides of March, in the consulship of Ursius and Pollemius.
EDCS-15600895.summary: This inscription records a dedication to a deity and the paving of a sanctuary by a priest and another official, dated by the consulship of Ursius and Pollemius.

EDCS-15600896.translation: To Victoria Augusta. The citizenry of Avitta, by decree of the decurions, at public expense. Manlius Honoratus and Julius Metellus, sufetes, saw to its construction.
EDCS-15600896.summary: This inscription records a public work dedicated to Victoria Augusta, funded by the city of Avitta and overseen by officials named Manlius Honoratus and Julius Metellus, likely in a Punic-influenced region.

EDCS-15600897.translation: To Faustina Augusta, by decree of the local council and at public expense, from the property of the Emperor Caesar Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Augustus Pius, father of the fatherland.
EDCS-15600897.summary: This inscription records a public dedication to Faustina Augusta, wife of Antoninus Pius, likely on a monument or building funded by the state, dated to the reign of Antoninus Pius (138-161 CE).

EDCS-15600904.translation: To Speratus Speratianus, son of Quintus Agrinius, of the Arnensis tribe, priest of Ceres, in the 197th year [of the colony]; although the order had decreed a new statue for him at public expense because of his portico which he had built with his generosity, he erected it at his own expense by decree of the local council.
EDCS-15600904.summary: This is a dedicatory inscription from the colony of Carthage honoring Speratus Speratianus, a priest of Ceres, who funded the construction of a public portico and was granted a statue by the local council.

EDCS-15600905.translation: To Salus (Health) and the healing arts, from Geminia, daughter of Dativus, curator of the state for the second time, perpetual sole [something].
EDCS-15600905.summary: This fragmentary inscription honors Salus and medicine, possibly dedicated by Geminia, a local official, in a city of North Africa, likely dating to the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-15600909.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus Fabius Urbanus Venustinus, pious, lived 35 years, 2 months. Axia Saturnina, mother, to her son. Sacred to the departed spirits. Axia Saturnina, daughter of Axius Rusticus, pious, lived [certain age]. While she was still healthy, she prepared this for herself and her family.
EDCS-15600909.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Quintus Fabius Urbanus Venustinus, who died at age 35, and also for Axia Saturnina, his mother, who prepared her own tomb.

EDCS-15600910.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Octavia Rogata, daughter of Octavius Severus, pious, lived 70 years, 2 months. Masupius Rogatianus, her husband, pious, lived 70 years, 2 months. Aelius Primus, Felix, and Secundianus, sons of Aelius Primus Masupianus, and Secundianus Didda and Campani, heirs, had this made for 5,000 sesterces, plus ground purchased by themselves.
EDCS-15600910.summary: This funerary epitaph records the deaths of Octavia Rogata and her husband Masupius Rogatianus, who both lived to 70, and details the cost and arrangements for their burial by their heirs.

EDCS-15600911.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Suania Rutilla, pious, lived 60 years. Sacred to the departed spirits. [Name] son of Saturninus, pious, lived 65 years. Sacred to the departed spirits. Faustus Gulebianus, pious, lived 35 years, 1 month, 10 days.
EDCS-15600911.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lives and deaths of three individuals: Suania Rutilla, an unnamed son of Saturninus, and Faustus Gulebianus, with their ages at death.

EDCS-15600912.translation: Titus Volussenus Felix, pious, lived 70 years. Sulpicia Victoria, 70 years old. Here she lies. May your bones rest well.
EDCS-15600912.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Titus Volussenus Felix and Sulpicia Victoria, both aged 70, with a wish for their peaceful rest.

EDCS-15600916.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Canicia Secunda, pious, lived 67 years. Here she lies.
EDCS-15600916.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Canicia Secunda, who died at the age of 67.

EDCS-15600918.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus Gallonius Victorianus, pious, lived [age].
EDCS-15600918.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary epitaph for Quintus Gallonius Victorianus, recording his name and piety.

EDCS-15600921.translation: To Gaius Attius Alcimus Felicissimus, most excellent man, who served as deputy prefect of the Praetorian Guard, prefect of the grain supply, prefect of the Vigiles, master of the *summa privata*, master of the *summae rationes*, curator of the work on the amphitheater, procurator of inheritances in Rome, procurator of the sacred mint, procurator of the iron mines, procurator of the grain supply of the Narbonensian province, procurator of private property along the Salarian, Tiburtine, Valeria, and Tuscia roads, also deputy procurator of the customs duties of the Gallic provinces, procurator of the alimentary funds in Transpadana, Istria, and Liburnia, advocate of the treasury of 11 provinces, by the most splendid order of the city as patron, because of his exceptional love for his country.
EDCS-15600921.summary: This extensive inscription honors Gaius Attius Alcimus Felicissimus for his numerous high-ranking administrative and financial posts throughout the Roman Empire, likely dating to the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-15600922.text_edition: \n Caio Vettio Grato Attico Sabiniano clarissimo puero filio Cai Vetti Grati Sabiniani clarissimi viri tribuni militum legionis VII Claudiae quaestoris kandidati nepotis sic Cai Vetti Sabiniani Hospitis clarissimae memoriae viri proconsulis municipium Aurelium Cpatrono decreto decurionum pecunia publica\n
EDCS-15600922.translation: Dedicated by the Municipality of Aurelium, as patron, by decree of the town councillors with public money, to Gaius Vettius Gratus Atticus Sabinianus, a most distinguished boy and son of Gaius Vettius Gratus Sabinianus, a most distinguished man and tribune of the soldiers of the Legio VII Claudia, candidate for quaestor, grandson of Gaius Vettius Sabinianus Hospes, a man of most distinguished memory and proconsul.
EDCS-15600922.summary: A public monument erected by a municipality to honor a young boy, Gaius Vettius Gratus Atticus Sabinianus, the son and grandson of distinguished officials.

EDCS-15600924.translation: To Quintus Geminius Sabinus, son of Quintus, of the Arnensian tribe, centurion of the Legio VII Gemina, Legio VI Ferrata, Legio XIV Martia, Legio III Cyrenaica, Legio Pia Fidelis C II.
EDCS-15600924.summary: This inscription lists the military career of Quintus Geminius Sabinus, a centurion who served in five Roman legions.

EDCS-15600925.translation: To Quintus Considius Repostus Areianus, son of Nymphamon, who held the office of aedile twice and duovir, for his outstanding administration as duovir and his singular love for the citizens, the entire curia. Dedicated on the 11th day before the Kalends of March, when Agricola and Clementianus were consuls.
EDCS-15600925.summary: An honorific inscription to Quintus Considius Repostus Areianus for his service as aedile and duovir, dedicated by the town council during the consulship of Agricola and Clementianus.

EDCS-15600926.translation: To Titus Racilius Tertullus Dativus, son of Lucius Racilius Felix, the lampmaker, perpetual flamen, by his father's goodwill, friendly association, and charitable consortium, Salvius Honoratus, for his friend's son.
EDCS-15600926.summary: This inscription is a dedication by Salvius Honoratus to Titus Racilius Tertullus Dativus, honoring his father's friend and his son, likely a funerary monument or a token of friendship.

EDCS-15600927.translation: Quintus Vetulenius Urbanus Herennianus, perpetual flamen and curator of the republic, constructed at his own expense a new changing room on the right as one exits from the foundations, two pools, and other facilities, restored the rest, and adorned it with statues, marble slabs, painted panels, columns, entrances to the rooms, and other furnishings, along with his most flourishing and wisest son, Magnilianus, according to the vow of all citizens; he completed and dedicated it and also provided a feast for the entire populace for three days, and furthermore presented theatrical games.
EDCS-15600927.summary: This inscription records the extensive public works and dedications undertaken by Quintus Vetulenius Urbanus Herennianus and his son Magnilianus for the city, including a new changing room, pools, and entertainment, likely dating to the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-15600928.translation: To Tertullus Dativus, quaestor, former duovir, perpetual flamen, for his outstanding love for the fatherland and his excellent faithfulness with which he deserved the favor of individuals and the community, Caelestia, for her patron.
EDCS-15600928.summary: This inscription honors Tertullus Dativus, a former local magistrate, for his civic virtues and loyalty, dedicated by Caelestia, possibly as a posthumous honor or a public commendation.

EDCS-15600929.translation: Then he gave the tenth gift, and again to him presenting splendid gifts, to Armatus Senorius.
EDCS-15600929.summary: This very brief inscription seems to record a sequence of gifts or honors given to Armatus Senorius, possibly within a civic or familial context.

EDCS-15600933.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Lucius Clodius Felix, dutiful, lived 30 years, 10 months. He is buried here.
EDCS-15600933.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the death and age of Lucius Clodius Felix.

EDCS-15600934.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Lucius Licinius Felix Egnatianus, dutiful, lived 69 years. He is buried here. Sacred to the Divine Manes. Lucius Licinius Victorinus Ampelianus, a most sweet infant, dutiful, lived 7 years. Sacred to the Divine Manes. Suillia Firmina, his dutiful daughter-in-law, lived 25 years.
EDCS-15600934.summary: This is a funerary inscription commemorating three members of the same family: Lucius Licinius Felix Egnatianus, his grandson Lucius Licinius Victorinus Ampelianus, and his daughter-in-law Suillia Firmina.

EDCS-15600935.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Quintus Tadius Rufus, dutiful, lived 86 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-15600935.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the death and age of Quintus Tadius Rufus.

EDCS-15600936.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Victorianus, dutiful, lived 37 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-15600936.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the death and age of Victorianus.

EDCS-15700002.translation: Envious envy, may it not harm a pure and clean soul.

EDCS-15700005.translation: Envy, envious envy, may the one who made himself the sky by night suffer envy. Nothing displease a pure and clean soul who is called Istefania.

EDCS-15700006.translation: Gabriel, unconquered goddess, you conquered the lion of the tribe of Judah with an envious, infuriating victory; you will be sated. Whoever does not build your cella for himself will be this.

EDCS-15800289.translation: In the name of the Lord, this inscription against hail begins: O good Lord Capituline, who grants us wisdom in the face of God, who was there when the German brother of God was born, when Christ was born with blood, there are these things. Remember three times when there was a great drought and no spring had water. What were you doing at the spring drinking? Drink pure water. The snake came out to free you, and the little man said to it, 'Free me from the bad water, from the bad hail.' 'I free you from the bad water and from the bad hail.' There are these things. Remember three times while this boundary holds the curse: INCAD BIRACTIMATIS INCAD TAIDA INCAD BALORENV INCAD SENTV MAXIMV INCAD CAPRARA INCAD PASSA SECOR INCAD CASTRVM MAMVNASSEN INCAD BILLA DE ABDELLA ET DIFATAN. Then the hail came from the evil cloud, and from the vineyards, and from the orchards, and the fruit, and the holm-oaks, and from the olive trees. In the name of the Lord, the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit of God, your holy name, because it is powerful, what I chant: Holy, holy, holy. Amen. Amen. Hallelujah. Hallelujah. In the name of the Lord, this inscription against hail begins: O good Capituline, you promised me before the face of God, there where this and hail... was. When the German brother of God was born, when Christ was born with blood, there are these things. Remember three times when there was a great drought and no spring had water. What were you doing at the spring drinking? Drink pure water. The snake came out to free you, and the little man said to it, 'Free me from the bad water, from the bad hail.' 'I free you from the bad water and from the bad hail.' There are these things. Remember three times while this boundary holds the curse: DE INCAD BIRACTIMATIS INDEV DE INCAD TA IDA DE INCAD BALORENV INCAD SENTV MAXIMV INCAD B CAPRARA DE INCAD POSSA DESECOR INCAD BILLA PISI DE INCAD CASTRV MAMVNASSEN DE INCAD POSSA ABDELLA ET INCAD. Then the hail came from the evil cloud, and from the vineyards, and from the fruit trees, and from the orchards, and the olive trees, and the holm-oaks. In the name of the Lord, the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit of God, your holy name, because it is powerful, what I chant: Holy, holy, holy. Amen. Amen. Hallelujah.
EDCS-15800289.summary: This complex and repetitive inscription is a magical spell or curse text, likely from late antiquity, intended to ward off hail and drought, invoking Christian and possibly pagan deities and using a series of incantations and place names.

EDCS-15800296.translation: To Publius Messius Saturninus, most perfect man, a trecenarius in Latin declamations, an advocate of the treasury, a member of the sacred consistory, a centenarian and sexagenarian in studies, prefect of the ala of Roman citizens, tribune of the second legion Adjutrix, and to Publius Messius Augustinus Maecianus, most illustrious boy, who performed the equestrian tribunate with three honors, to the whole senate, citizens, and patrons.

EDCS-15900341.inscription_type: inscriptiones christianae, tituli operum, tituli sepulcrales
EDCS-15900341.text_edition: \n In hok sic tumulo iaket sic korpus bonae memoriae RV pectore carus qui per gladium indomitem sic okisum sic bixit sic in pake sic plus minus annos XXV rekessit sic de hok sic saekulo sic sub die VI mensis Dekember sic indictione XIII amen\n
EDCS-15900341.translation: In this tomb lies the body of good memory, dear to my heart, who died by the sword, lived and rested in peace for more or less 25 years, departed from this world on the 6th day of the month of December, in the 13th indiction. Amen.
EDCS-15900341.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the violent death and age of approximately 25 years of an individual, dated by indiction.

EDCS-15900346.translation: Sacred to eternal Rome. Lucius Accius Vitalis fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-15900346.summary: A dedication to the goddess Roma Aeterna, with Lucius Accius Vitalis fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-15900348.translation: Numisius Iunior made this dimidium (a measure of grain).
EDCS-15900348.summary: An inscription recording the making of a measure of grain by Numisius Iunior.

EDCS-15900349.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Euphrosynus, deputy of theAugustus's treasurer, dutiful, lived for 35 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-15900349.summary: A funerary inscription for Euphrosynus, a deputy treasurer to the emperor, who lived 35 years.

EDCS-15900395.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. To Iuvenalis, a household slave, belonging to Mercurius. He lived one year, five months, and three days. May the earth lie lightly on you.
EDCS-15900395.summary: A funerary dedication to the gods of the underworld for a young slave named Iuvenalis, with a wish for a light earth.

EDCS-15900396.translation: In memory of Verus of Icosium, who was also called Iom.
EDCS-15900396.summary: A memorial inscription for Verus of Icosium.

EDCS-15900397.translation: In memory of Venustus of Mesarfelt, the faithful merchant. He rests here in peace. Ianuarius, his son, made this. He died in God and Christ on the Kalends of November at the age of 60.
EDCS-15900397.summary: A Christian funerary monument erected by a son for his merchant father, recording his death date and age.

EDCS-16000003.translation: [...]rius Tertullus, procurator of the province, restored and dedicated [this monument] which had been corrupted by age, with his own money.
EDCS-16000003.summary: A procurator named Tertullus restored and dedicated a damaged monument using his own funds.

EDCS-16000275.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Tertius, a slave of our Caesar, made this for his mother, Ulpia Quita.

EDCS-16000276.translation: Flavius Silvanus made a window for Minerva.
EDCS-16000276.summary: This is a dedication to Minerva by Flavius Silvanus.

EDCS-16000277.summary: This is a curse or epitaph mentioning a murderer named Bonifatius.

EDCS-16000279.translation: Sacred to Ceres Maurusia Augusta, Marcus Pusillius Securus and his wife Auteia Adauta, perpetual priestess.

EDCS-16100214.translation: Flavius Acotius Storacis Silanius Polionis Felix, who is also Goddos, son of Marsus Iaderis, I wrote. Asmun, Faustus, Rogatus, son of Mamo, Lucius Octavius Victor, Coccæius Bargbalis, Celer, Hilari.

EDCS-16100216.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the departed. Caius Vibius Masof lived 51 years. He is buried here.

EDCS-16100219.translation: Gallus, Lunus, Fausca, Placus, Meius, Rupila, Rupilia, Licinius, Maxima, Salbao, Marta, Septemius, Amia, Saturina, Speratus, so that if anyone does otherwise, Cleopatra.

EDCS-16100221.translation: O Artulailam, Semesilam, Aehio, Bakhukh, Bakakhukh, Menebaikhukh, Abraxas, Bazabakhukh, Menebaikhukh, Abraxas. Lord gods, hold and restrain the Falernian baths, let no one approach them, bind and secure them. Let no person approach the Falernian baths from this day forward.
EDCS-16100221.summary: A magical inscription invoking deities to protect the Falernian baths from unauthorized access, possibly from a public bath complex.

EDCS-16100222.translation: Let him go there to wash. Bind the Falernian baths from this day forward, bind and secure the Falernian bath, let no one go there from this day forward.

EDCS-16100354.translation: For Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus Parthicus Maximus Britannicus Maximus, son of the Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Arabicus Adiabenicus Parthicus Maximus Britannicus Maximus, grandson of the Divine Antoninus Pius Germanicus Sarmaticus, great-grandson of the Divine Antoninus Pius, great-great-grandson of the Divine Hadrian, great-great-great-grandson of the Divine Trajan Parthicus and the Divine Nerva, pontifex maximus, with tribunician power for the 19th year, consul for the 3rd time, father of the fatherland, proconsul, [at] 33 miles.
EDCS-16100354.summary: An honorific inscription likely associated with a milestone or roadside monument, detailing the extensive imperial titles of Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius, son of Septimius Severus.

EDCS-16100355.translation: Nassaeus, son of Iuzgagis, lived 91 years. Longinus, son of Iuzgao, and Temrirmas, daughter of Sadufai, managed the affairs. She lived 80 years. Longinus, son of Iuzgao, managed the affairs.
EDCS-16100355.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespans and caretakers of Nassaeus and Temrirmas, likely family members, with a probable date in the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-16100357.text_edition: \n Hic corpus iacet pueris Nominandi o benedicte puer paucis te terra diebus infantem tenuit caeliquae sic in regna remisit propterea et natus ut caperes tanta renatus\n
EDCS-16100357.translation: Here lies the body of the child Nominandus, blessed child. The earth held you only a few days; heaven recalled you, reborn, so that you might grasp such things.
EDCS-16100357.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for an infant named Nominandus, emphasizing his brief life and immediate ascension to heaven.

EDCS-16100358.translation: For Lucius Caesernius Honoratus, aedile, twice chief magistrate, an excellent citizen. The town councillors of the colony of Madaure set this up for him on account of his merits.

EDCS-16100360.translation: Crinitus, faithful in peace, lived 22 years. He departed this life on the 10th day before the Kalends of March.

EDCS-16100401.translation: Aris, son of Aristoinis, pious, lived 71 years. Fuza, daughter of Victor Senti, pious, lived 65 years. Aris, their grandson, pious, lived 65 years. Here lie their bones. May you rest well.
EDCS-16100401.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Aris, Fuza, and another Aris (possibly son/grandson), detailing their ages and offering a wish for their peaceful rest, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-16100403.translation: Deed of Sale of Serbunis. In the tenth year of the reign of King Ginttabund, on the 5th day before the Ides of May. Adeudata and Innulus, his son, are selling from their own cultivated lands of Manciana, from the estate of Tuletianensis, under the ownership of Flavius Geminius Catullinus, perpetual priest. In the place called Sem, a small stream, there are thirteen fig trees and six young vines with their tendrils. Neighboring the same land on the south are the sons of Januariani, on the east Quintus Pontiani, on the west Marino. The sellers Adeudata and Innulus, the heirs of Serbunis, received three hundred coins from Geminius Felix, the buyer, for these properties, which they had held and possessed with all their rights from the day before the sale. They declared that they owed nothing further to themselves from the said price. They sold and transferred these properties from this day in perpetuity to their buyer, Felix, and his heirs. If anyone should raise a question or claim ownership of the aforementioned property, they will pay the price of the property at that time, or double the price, or whatever the property is worth at that time, as compensation for eviction, without malice. Malice is absent, will be absent, and will not be present. Geminius Felix, the buyer, stipulated. Adeudata and Innulus, heirs of Serbunis, pledged security in the year and on the day written above. I, Donatianus, requested by Adeudata and Innulus, her son, witnessed them making their marks, having received the full price. Mark of Adeudata. Mark of Innulus. I, Saturninus, was present. Mark of Saturninus. I, Donatianus, inscribed and subscribed this deed.
EDCS-16100403.summary: This is a detailed legal deed of sale from the 10th year of King Ginttabund, recording the sale of land with fig trees and vines from Adeudata and Innulus to Geminius Felix, witnessed by Donatianus and Saturninus.

EDCS-16100404.translation: To Emperor Caesar Vespasian Augustus, son of Emperor Titus Caesar Vespasian Augustus.

EDCS-16201197.summary: This is a sacred dedication to the Great Mother Idaea made by V. Sempronius, a public priest, for the health and safety of the imperial family, including Septimius Severus, Caracalla, Geta, and Julia Domna.

EDCS-16201258.translation: Lucius Iulius Cupitianus Mellitus established and dedicated this mausoleum for myself and for Viria Rogata, my wife, for both of us while alive, and for our posterity, and in memory of Cupitus, my father, and Venusta, my excellent parents. The same Felix, when he was 60 years old, completed and dedicated this work for himself and Rogata, his wife. He additionally lived 6 years, making the total of his life 66 years. Rogata, his wife, also when she was 47 years old, dedicated this work with Mellitus, her husband. She additionally lived 24 years, making the total of her life 73 years. Take away the garlands from your hair and forget your loves; sad, poor, in a short garment, Thalia, come; let not the unchaste Idalian wand dally, nor let the bright veil flow before your feet. I, Iulius, who am called Mellitus, made this for myself, for my father Cupitus, for my mother Venusta, and I placed my wife Rogata with me, that her fame may be eternally established in this place. We lived our fill, we both fulfilled our duty, we produced a double female offspring. You too, who read these verses and approve of these deeds, learn to honor your parents deservedly, so that I may cultivate you, Glafrianus, and leave titles. The fates allowed me to do this while alive. I, Iulius, now ask this of you, ruler of the Underworld: when I die, may my bones lie undisturbed. I.
EDCS-16201258.summary: This extensive funerary inscription dedicates a mausoleum built by Lucius Iulius Cupitianus Mellitus for himself, his wife Rogata, their descendants, and in memory of his parents, recounting their ages and wishes for the afterlife; it includes poetic verses and requests to the god of the underworld. It likely dates to the Imperial Roman period.
