EDCS-16201517.summary: A funerary epitaph fragment for Memmius Orcelus, recording only his name.

EDCS-16201518.translation: To the Divine Manes. Memmia Getula, dutiful, lived 10 years.
EDCS-16201518.summary: A funerary epitaph for Memmia Getula, recording her name, dutifulness, and age at death.

EDCS-16201519.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Memmia Maia, dutiful, lived 55 years, is buried here.
EDCS-16201519.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Memmia Maia, who lived 55 years.

EDCS-16201520.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Aulus Menius Amillus Nepos, dutiful, lived 2 years, is buried here.
EDCS-16201520.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Aulus Menius Amillus Nepos, who died at the age of 2.

EDCS-16201521.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Lucius Messius Rogatus lived.
EDCS-16201521.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Messius Rogatus, recording his life but not his death or burial.

EDCS-16201522.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Messor, dutiful, lived 17 years, is buried here.
EDCS-16201522.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Messor, who lived 17 years.

EDCS-16201523.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Mesus Arovicius, aged 3.
EDCS-16201523.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Mesus Arovicius, who died at the age of 3.

EDCS-16201524.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Minatia Rogatula, dutiful, lived [for X] years.
EDCS-16201524.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Minatia Rogatula, recording her life but not her death or burial.

EDCS-16201525.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Mincius Venerius, who lived 65 years, is buried here.
EDCS-16201525.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Mincius Venerius, who lived 65 years.

EDCS-16201526.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Mindius Cimber lived 30 years, is buried here.
EDCS-16201526.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Mindius Cimber, who lived 30 years.

EDCS-16201527.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Modius, recording his age at death as 50 years.

EDCS-16201528.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Marcus Modius Fortu[natus?].
EDCS-16201528.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcus Modius Fortunatus, recording his name and dedication to the gods of the underworld.

EDCS-16201529.translation: To the good memory of Mustula, light of my life. She lived 20 years, 5 months, and 12 days. She rests in peace. The Ides of June.
EDCS-16201529.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Mustula, recording her lifespan and date of repose in peace, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-16201530.translation: In the spirit of Calendionis, in peace. In the spirit of Fortunatas, in peace.
EDCS-16201530.summary: This inscription, likely funerary, invokes the spirits of Calendionis and Fortunatas, indicating their peaceful repose, possibly from late antiquity.

EDCS-16201659.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Carvilia Sophe, who was also called Issa, a dutiful wife, lived 31 years. Her most dutiful husband made this for his wife.
EDCS-16201659.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Carvilia Sophe (Issa), recording her age at death and dedicating the monument to her by her husband, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-16201671.translation: Arifridos, in peace. Lived 20 years. Buried on the Ides of November.
EDCS-16201671.summary: A funerary inscription recording the lifespan and burial date of Arifridos, indicating rest in peace, likely from late antiquity.

EDCS-16201672.translation: He repaired and strengthened the communal bath, named 'Snail', with all its equipment of bronze and lead, and added a new pool, returning the old cisterns. Dedicated by Gaius Optatianus, perpetual priest and curator of public affairs.
EDCS-16201672.summary: This inscription records the renovation and expansion of a public bath complex, including a new pool and cisterns, by Gaius Optatianus, a local official, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-16201677.translation: Sacred to Hercules Augustus. The community of the 102 Numidians of the people of Vazalitani.
EDCS-16201677.summary: This is a dedication to Hercules Augustus by a community identified as 102 Numidians from Vazalitani, likely a military or veteran group, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-16201755.summary: A very brief inscription, likely funerary, indicating 'Vincetdeus' rests in peace, possibly from late antiquity.

EDCS-16201759.translation: The Pontifex Maximus with tribunician power for the fourth time, and of their entire divine household, Publius Petronius Felix, chief centurion from the Praetorian Guard, and his son Publius Petronius Felix Fuscus, a Roman Equites, and Publius Petronius Severus, made these at their own expense by decree of the decurions; and for the dedication of this work, they gave individual denarii to the decurions and fifty denarii each to the curae.
EDCS-16201759.summary: This inscription details the construction or dedication of a work by Publius Petronius Felix and his family, including members of the Praetorian Guard and equestrian order, with a record of their financial contributions to local officials, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-16201852.translation: Marcus Enius Octavi fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-16201852.summary: This is a votive inscription recording Marcus Enius Octavi fulfilling a vow, likely dedicated to a deity, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-16201854.summary: This is a very short inscription, possibly a name on a monument or tomb, belonging to Annius Saturnini, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-16201856.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Sexsus sic Volcacius Marsus vixit annis CXV Antonia Urbana vixit annis LX Helvia Urbana vixit annis LXX\n
EDCS-16201856.translation: To the departed spirits. Sexsus sic Volcacius Marsus lived for 115 years. Antonia Urbana lived for 60 years. Helvia Urbana lived for 70 years.
EDCS-16201856.summary: A tombstone for three individuals named Sexsus sic Volcacius Marsus, Antonia Urbana, and Helvia Urbana, recording their ages at death, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-16201857.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Aelius Honoratus pius vixit annis LXXXIII mensibus V Gratus Gaius Cuminus Donatus filii fecerunt\n
EDCS-16201857.translation: To the departed spirits. Aelius Honoratus, a dutiful man, lived for 83 years and 5 months. Gratus Gaius Cuminus Donatus, his sons, made this.
EDCS-16201857.summary: A tombstone for Aelius Honoratus, who died at 83 years and 5 months, erected by his sons, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-16201858.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Fortunatus Donati filius vixit annis XXII mensibus sexs sic Donatus pater fecit\n
EDCS-16201858.translation: To the departed spirits. Fortunatus, son of Donatus, lived for 22 years and six months. Donatus, his father, made this.
EDCS-16201858.summary: A tombstone for Fortunatus, son of Donatus, who died at 22 years and 6 months, erected by his father, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-16201859.text_edition: \n Minervae Victoriae Augustae sacrum pro salute Auggg(ustorum) Imppp(eratorum) Severi et Antonini et Getae et Iuliae Domnae Augustae coloni Gamoniensis sua pecunia fecerunt\n
EDCS-16201859.translation: Sacred to Minerva Victoria Augusta for the safety of the Emperors Augustus, Severus, Antoninus, Geta, and Augusta Julia Domna; the colonists of Gamundia made this with their own money.
EDCS-16201859.summary: A dedication to Minerva Victoria Augusta by the colonists of Gamundia, praying for the safety of Emperors Severus, Antoninus, Geta, and Julia Domna, dated to their reigns (early 3rd century CE).

EDCS-16201860.summary: This inscription is a simple place name, likely the designation of a Roman colony.

EDCS-16201864.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Iulia Felicitas, high priestess, lived. Iulia Felicitas, freedwoman, erected this for her most excellent patroness; she lies here.
EDCS-16201864.summary: This is a funerary dedication by a freedwoman for her patroness, likely from the imperial period.

EDCS-16201865.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Cornelia Aegia, also called Nice, lived 32 years and 3 months. Baburia Ianuaria, also called priestess of Ceres, a pious mother, erected this. Sacred to the Divine Shades. Quintus Cornelius Genialis lived 75 years. Baburia Ianuaria, also called priestess of Ceres, erected this for her pious husband and daughter; he lies here.
EDCS-16201865.summary: This is a complex funerary inscription recording the deaths and burial arrangements of multiple individuals, including a priestess of Ceres, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-16201867.text_edition: \n Hygiae Augustae sacrum pro salute et victoriis Impperatorum Caessarum Luci Septimii Severi Pii Pertinacis Augusti et Marci Aureli Antonini Pii Felicis Augusti et Luci Septimii Getae nobilissimi Caesaris et Iuliae Domnae Augustae matris Aug(ustorum) et castrorum totiusque divinae domus eorum Lucius Baebius Secundus et Iulia Victorina uxor eius votum solverunt\n
EDCS-16201867.translation: Sacred to Hygieia Augusta for the safety and victories of the Emperors Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus, Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus, and Caesar Lucius Septimius Geta Nobilissimus, and Julia Domna Augusta, mother of the Augusti and of the camp, and of their entire divine family. Lucius Baebius Secundus and his wife Iulia Victorina fulfilled their vow.
EDCS-16201867.summary: A votive dedication to Hygieia Augusta by Lucius Baebius Secundus and his wife Iulia Victorina, praying for the safety and victories of Emperors Septimius Severus, Caracalla, Geta, Julia Domna, and their family, dated to their reigns (early 3rd century CE).

EDCS-16201868.translation: Sacred to Jupiter Best and Greatest Dolichenus Augustus. The priests Flavius Clarus and Pompeianus dedicated this temple, built from the ground up, out of favor for themselves and their descendants.
EDCS-16201868.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a temple to Jupiter Dolichenus by two priests, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-16201869.summary: This is a dedicatory inscription to a "Nutrix Augustae", possibly a deified empress or a personification associated with the imperial family.

EDCS-16201870.translation: Sacred to Saturn Augustus. Titus Cornelius Italus.
EDCS-16201870.summary: This is a dedicatory inscription to the god Saturn, possibly with an imperial connection ('Augustus'), by Titus Cornelius Italus, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-16201871.translation: Sacred to Saturn Augustus. Quintus Fulvius Julianus Victorinus, son of Quintus, of the Quirina tribe, aedile, prefect with the power of a city magistrate, acting as duumvir for two terms and quinquennial augur, with his wife and children, preserved by his own will, gladly made and dedicated the marble statue he had promised; this place was granted by decree of the decurions. Arnobii.
EDCS-16201871.summary: This inscription details the career and dedications of Quintus Fulvius Julianus Victorinus, an important local official in the town of Arnobii, likely dating to the late Roman Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-16201878.text_edition: \n Publio Attio Deciano Felici Matutino clarissimo puero civi et patrono \n
EDCS-16201878.translation: To Publius Attius Decianus Felix Matutinus, a most distinguished boy, citizen and patron.
EDCS-16201878.summary: This is a dedication to a young boy named Publius Attius Decianus Felix Matutinus, identified as a citizen and patron, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-16201880.translation: [...]ano, Roman eques, augur, perpetual flamen, aedile, for his outstanding administration of the aedileship, the people, by curiae and the Augustales, presented him with gifts and honours.
EDCS-16201880.summary: This inscription honors an individual, identified as an eques, augur, flamens, and aedile, for his excellent service, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-16201883.text_edition: \n Splendonii Lucio Clodio Luci filio Quirina Titiano qui in IANI et IIviratu admodum floret IIOR cultoribusque ium ediderunt \n
EDCS-16201883.translation: To Lucius Clodius Titianus, son of Quirinus, son of Splendonius, who flourishes greatly in the office of IANVS and IIvirate, and his cult-followers, they dedicated.
EDCS-16201883.summary: This inscription records the dedication by cult followers of Lucius Clodius Titianus, who held the IIvirate office and was a flourishing figure, likely in a provincial town.

EDCS-16201886.translation: [...]X Romuli X. Sacred to the Divine Shades. Caius Iulius Optatianus lived 66 years. He lies here. Caius Iulius Valens Fortunatus [erected this] for his dearest father.
EDCS-16201886.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Caius Iulius Optatianus, dedicated by his son, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-16201887.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Caius Iulius Titienus Maximus, son of Caius, of the Quirina tribe, of honourable memory, a youth, lived 25 years. He lies here. Caius Iulius Fortunatus erected [this] for his dutiful brother. X
EDCS-16201887.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a young man named Caius Iulius Titienus Maximus, erected by his brother, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-16201890.translation: Theodosius the cleric rested in peace on the fourth day before the Ides of February.
EDCS-16201890.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Theodosius, a cleric, indicating his date of rest.

EDCS-16201891.translation: Petrus, faithful in Christ, rested with his patron; he was loved, lived for 10 years, 10 months, and 15 days, resting on the seventh day before the Kalends of May in the ninth indiction.
EDCS-16201891.summary: A funerary inscription for Petrus, detailing his lifespan and date of rest, along with his relationship to a patron.

EDCS-16201892.translation: Dinamius, faithful, lived for 3 years and rested in peace on the seventh day before the Kalends of December in the fourth indiction.
EDCS-16201892.summary: This inscription records the short life and peaceful rest of Dinamius, specifying his age and date of death.

EDCS-16201893.translation: Flavius Cresconius, son of Gallus, lived for 29 years and 6 months, rested in peace on the eleventh day before the Kalends of December in the second indiction, in the fourth year of the reign of Lord Justinian the Emperor.
EDCS-16201893.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Flavius Cresconius, providing his age at death and the date of his repose during the reign of Emperor Justinian.

EDCS-16201894.translation: Gemellinus was laid to rest on the Kalends of August in the tenth indiction; he lived for fifty-five years.
EDCS-16201894.summary: A funerary inscription for Gemellinus, stating his age at death and the date of his repose.

EDCS-16201895.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Saturninus, former chief magistrate and prefect of the Musulamiorum tribe, lived 92 years. His sons Saturninus and Commodus erected this for their father. He is buried here.
EDCS-16201895.summary: This funerary inscription honors Saturninus, a prominent official and leader of the Musulamiorum, and was erected by his sons.

EDCS-16201896.translation: By the authority of Emperor Nerva Trajan Caesar Augustus Germanicus Dacicus, consul for the sixth time, emperor for the fourteenth time. Lucius Acilius Strabo Clodius Nummus, imperial legate with praetorian power, [settled a dispute] between the Musulamii and the Bullamenses.
EDCS-16201896.summary: This inscription records an official act by the legate Lucius Acilius Strabo Clodius Nummus concerning a dispute between two tribes, issued under the authority of Emperor Trajan.

EDCS-16201897.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Quintus Considius Rufus, son of Arnabio of Arna, lived 50 years and 9 days.
EDCS-16201897.summary: A funerary inscription for Quintus Considius Rufus, stating his age and lifespan.

EDCS-16201898.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Fortunata lived 75 years. Marcus Gallius Valens, his son, [erected this] for his parents.
EDCS-16201898.summary: This funerary inscription honors Fortunata and was erected by her son Marcus Gallius Valens.

EDCS-16201899.translation: Rogata, daughter of Felix, lived [number] years.
EDCS-16201899.summary: A funerary inscription for Rogata, daughter of Felix, recording her lifespan but with missing age details.

EDCS-16201900.summary: A funerary inscription recording the lifespan of a child named Victorinus.

EDCS-16201901.summary: A funerary inscription for Lucius Valerius Vitalis, likely part of a longer epitaph.

EDCS-16201902.translation: Bibius Mustulus, with all love, completed the paving.
EDCS-16201902.summary: A dedication for paving work completed by Bibius Mustulus, motivated by affection for the community.

EDCS-16201904.translation: Sacred to Aesculapius Augustus. Marcus Aufidius Extricatus, with his family, fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-16201904.summary: A votive inscription to Aesculapius Augustus by Marcus Aufidius Extricatus.

EDCS-16201905.text_edition: \n Pro salute Augusti Quintus Bennius Felix Palus Victor filius Aesculapio vota reddiderunt\n
EDCS-16201905.translation: For the safety of Augustus, Quintus Bennius Felix Palus Victor, son, paid vows to Aesculapius.
EDCS-16201905.summary: This is a votive inscription by Quintus Bennius Felix Palus Victor, dedicating a promise to the god Aesculapius for the health of the Emperor (Augustus), likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-16201906.translation: Sacred to Aesculapius Augustus. Caius Asinius Datinus, priest, fulfilled and dedicated his vow for the vaulted ceiling with columns and ornaments, along with his family, in good health.
EDCS-16201906.summary: A dedication to Aesculapius Augustus by the priest Caius Asinius Datinus, recording the completion of a vaulted ceiling with associated elements.

EDCS-16201907.translation: Sacred to Aesculapius Augustus. Marcus Orbius Felix, with his family, fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-16201907.summary: A votive inscription to Aesculapius Augustus by Marcus Orbius Felix.

EDCS-16201908.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Publius Peticius Ianuarius vixit annis LXVII et Peticia Procula uxor eius vixit annis Publius Peticius Martialis filius parentibus praestantissimis fecit et dedicavit ex officina Cittini\n
EDCS-16201908.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Publius Peticius Ianuarius lived for 67 years, and his wife Peticia Procula lived for [XX] years. Publius Peticius Martialis, their son, made and dedicated this for his most excellent parents, from the workshop of Cittinus.
EDCS-16201908.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Publius Peticius Ianuarius and his wife Peticia Procula, set up by their son, indicating the date of death and provenance from a workshop, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-16201909.text_edition: \n Quirino deo Patri Genio municipii Augusto sacrum pro salute Imperatoris Caesaris Marci Aureli Severi Alexandri Pii Felicis Augusti pontificis maximi tribunicia potestate consulis patris patriae proconsulis et Iuliae Mamaeae Augustae matris Augusti et castrorum et senatus et patriae totiusque domus divinae Lucius Turius Martialis et Quintus Cornelius Felix Emeritus aediles inlatis rei publicae summis honorariis aedilitatis suae amplius statuam aeream ex SS VIIIImilibus nummum et basim patriae dono dederunt et dedicaverunt ob quam dedicationem ludos scaenicos sic ediderunt et gymnasium biduo dederunt\n
EDCS-16201909.translation: Sacred to Quirinus the Father God, to the Genius of the municipality, and to Augustus. For the safety of the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Severus Alexander Pius Felix Augustus, Pontifex Maximus, holder of tribunician power, consul, father of the fatherland, proconsul, and to Julia Mamaea Augusta, mother of Augustus, of the camp, of the senate, and of the whole fatherland, and of the entire divine house, Lucius Turius Martialis and Quintus Cornelius Felix Emeritus, aediles, having presented the highest honorary gifts of their aedileship to the state, donated and dedicated a bronze statue weighing 8000 pounds and a base to the fatherland, and for this dedication they presented theatrical games and a gymnasium for two days.
EDCS-16201909.summary: This lengthy inscription details the dedication of a bronze statue and base by aediles Lucius Turius Martialis and Quintus Cornelius Felix Emeritus, for the safety of Emperor Severus Alexander and Julia Mamaea, which included public games and a gymnasium, dating to the reign of Severus Alexander (222-235 CE).

EDCS-16201910.text_edition: \n Bonifatius Ianuarius Montius Eurialus Candurius Victor Eulogius Anfio Ninficus Fortunio Preiectus Anastasus Amor Nymficus\n
EDCS-16201910.translation: Bonifatius Ianuarius, Montius Eurialus, Candurius Victor, Eulogius Anfius, Nymficus, Fortunius, Praeiectus, Anastasius, Amor Nymficus.
EDCS-16201910.summary: This inscription is a list of names, possibly of officials, members of a group, or individuals associated with an event, without further context.

EDCS-16201926.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Quintus Camerius, son of Quintus, a soldier of the 13th Urban Cohort, under the centuria of Aelius Dexter, lived 25 years, served 17 years. Buried here at the care of his heir.
EDCS-16201926.summary: A funerary inscription for Quintus Camerius, a soldier who served in the 13th Urban Cohort.

EDCS-16201927.text_edition: \n Caelesti sacrum Decimus Valerius Phoenix libens animo votum solvit\n
EDCS-16201927.translation: Sacred to Caelestis. Decimus Valerius Phoenix willingly paid his vow.
EDCS-16201927.summary: This is a votive inscription by Decimus Valerius Phoenix, dedicating a promise to the goddess Caelestis, likely from Roman North Africa.

EDCS-16201940.summary: A fragmentary inscription, possibly an epitaph or a name associated with a monument.

EDCS-16201945.summary: A very brief inscription indicating that Sphaerus was the maker of an object or monument.

EDCS-16201951.text_edition: \n Divo Lucio Septimio Severo Pio Pertinaci patri Imperatoris Caesaris Marci Aureli Severi Antonini Pii Felicis Augusti Parthici Arabici maximi Britannici maximi pontificis maximi patris patriae ordo Mustitanus Pacatori deo decreto decurionum pecunia publica\n
EDCS-16201951.translation: To the deified Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax, father of the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Severus Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus Parthicus Arabicus Maximus Britannicus Maximus, Pontifex Maximus, father of the fatherland, the council of Mustitana, to the god Pacator, by decree of the decurions, with public money.
EDCS-16201951.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a monument to the deified Emperor Septimius Severus by the council of Mustitana, using public funds, likely dating to the reign of his son Caracalla (211-217 CE).

EDCS-16201952.translation: For the health and safety of the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Severus Alexander Pius Felix Augustus and their entire divine family, Caius Caelius Felix, aedile of Libertatis, completed and dedicated the statue which he had promised to erect for the distribution of games and the quaestorship, with enlarged funds, and he also gave a feast to all the citizens. Caius Caelius Fortunatus, son of Septimianus, the father, paid for all these things.
EDCS-16201952.summary: A complex dedication by Caius Caelius Felix, an aedile, for a statue and public works honoring Emperor Severus Alexander and his family, funded by his father, Caius Caelius Fortunatus.

EDCS-16201953.translation: Macrinus, a distinguished man, dedicated [this] with his own money.
EDCS-16201953.summary: This is a dedication of a monument or object by Macrinus, an esteemed individual, funded by himself.

EDCS-16201954.translation: To the Pious Fortunate Emperor Macrinus.
EDCS-16201954.summary: This is an inscription honoring Emperor Macrinus, likely an acclamation of his imperial titles.

EDCS-16201957.summary: This is a short epitaph for a person named Zabullica, indicating her peaceful repose, likely from a tomb.

EDCS-16201959.text_edition: \n Pro salute Imperatoris Caesaris divi Severi Pii nepotis divi Magni Antonini Pii filii Marci Aureli Severi Alexandri Pii Felicis Augusti pontificis maximi tribunicia potestate VIIII consulis III patris patriae proconsulis Caius Timuleius Honoratus Felix Petronianus eques Romanus in urbe Roma Imperatoris domini nostri Alexandri Augusti sacerdos bidentalis iussus fecit\n
EDCS-16201959.translation: For the safety of the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Severus Alexander Pius Felix Augustus, Pontifex Maximus, holder of tribunician power for the 9th time, consul for the 3rd time, father of the fatherland, proconsul, descendant of the deified Severus Pius, son of the deified Magnus Antoninus Pius, Caius Timuleius Honoratus Felix Petronianus, a Roman knight, priest of our lord Emperor Alexander Augustus, performed this iussus (command).
EDCS-16201959.summary: This inscription records a religious act performed by Caius Timuleius Honoratus Felix Petronianus, a Roman knight and priest, for the safety of Emperor Severus Alexander, detailing his prestigious lineage and titles, likely dating to Severus Alexander's reign (222-235 CE).

EDCS-16201964.translation: To the god Saturn, Apronius Aco, his freedman, and Sta, [dedicated this].
EDCS-16201964.summary: This is a dedication to the god Saturn by Apronius Aco and Sta, identifying Apronius as a freedman.

EDCS-16201967.translation: Prima, to my dear Iseddinio, what you owe me for the price of wine, which you bought from me, I sent you a note for two thousand in the sacks, not sesterces but denarii, I sent you a note for three thousand in the sacks.
EDCS-16201967.summary: This inscription appears to be a personal note or record of debt related to the purchase of wine, possibly from a merchant or creditor.

EDCS-16201968.translation: To the Emperor Caesar, son of the divine Septimius Severus Pius Arabicus Adiabenicus Parthicus Maximus Britannicus Maximus, grandson of the divine Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Germanicus Sarmaticus, great-grandson of the divine Antoninus Pius, descendant of the divine Hadrian, descendant of the divine Trajan Parthicus, and descendant of the divine Nerva, Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus Parthicus Maximus Britannicus Maximus Germanicus Maximus, Pontifex Maximus, holding tribunician power for the 19th time, Imperator for the 3rd time, Consul for the 4th time, Father of the Fatherland, Proconsul, 56,000 [units of currency/soldiers/etc.].
EDCS-16201968.summary: This is a lengthy imperial titulature inscription for Emperor Caracalla, listing his extensive titles and achievements, possibly associated with a monument or military donation.

EDCS-16201969.translation: To Lusius Septimius Julianus, most illustrious man, son of Quintus Lusius Laberius Geminius Rutilianus, consular, decemvir for judging litigation, military tribune of the IV Flavia Felix Moesia Superior legion, quaestor of the city, tribune of the plebs candidate, patron of the Emperor Caesar R. CAN., by decree of the town council, with public funds.
EDCS-16201969.summary: This is a public dedication or honorific inscription for Lusius Septimius Julianus, detailing his distinguished career and public service.

EDCS-16201976.translation: In the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, Amen. Vitalis the presbyter lived in the peace of God for 78 years. I rest here today, placed here in peaceful repose, preserved in dust, but great hope remains for me, for I hope for the Lord who created all things to come, that you may raise these ashes, you who are powerful. This is more beautiful than the sun and is found to be superior to the arrangement of all the stars when compared to light, since it is one, all-powerful, and permanent in itself, renewing all things. Born in the 28th year of King Genserich, the day before the Ides of September.
EDCS-16201976.summary: This is a Christian epitaph for Vitalis the presbyter, dating his birth to the 28th year of King Genserich, and expressing hope for resurrection.

EDCS-16201977.translation: Consul for the 3rd time, Father of the Fatherland, son of the divine Antoninus. [Dedicated by] Cocceius Severianus Honorius.
EDCS-16201977.summary: This inscription likely refers to an imperial figure and is dedicated by Cocceius Severianus Honorius, possibly honoring the emperor.

EDCS-16201981.translation: To Sextus Caecilius Sextus son of Quirina Aemilianus, decemvir for judging litigation, septemvir of the epulones, quaestor of the emperor designate, governor of the province of Africa with the emperor's authority, tribune of the plebs, patron by decree of the town council, with public funds.
EDCS-16201981.summary: This is an honorific inscription for Sextus Caecilius Sextus Aemilianus, detailing his significant public and political career and honors bestowed by a town council.

EDCS-16201990.translation: To Aelia Celsinilla, the consular lady, her perpetual patroness, mother of Celsinianus, a consular man, her curator, the entire council of the most splendid colony of Octavii Thuburbitana.
EDCS-16201990.summary: This is a dedication by the town council of Thubursic (Tunisia) to Aelia Celsinilla, honoring her as a patroness and mother.

EDCS-16300010.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Aelius Saturninus, called Calvus, my dearest son, lived for 34 years and 4 months; overcome by fate, you could not do for us what you ought to have done.
EDCS-16300010.summary: A funerary epitaph for Aelius Saturninus, recording his age and expressing grief and unfulfilled familial obligations.

EDCS-16300012.translation: After the consulship of our lords Honorius for the 12th time and Theodosius for the 8th time, on the 16th day before the Kalends of August. Aurelius Iuntes Sasucthanus established [this] from the price of oil sold, [worth] one thousand eight hundred pounds of oil. This record was issued.
EDCS-16300012.summary: An administrative record from the late Roman period, possibly relating to the sale of oil and its revenue, dated to the consulship of Honorius and Theodosius.

EDCS-16300013.translation: Sessufa to Severus, contractor, from your record of expenses for wine, eighteen amphorae.
EDCS-16300013.summary: An accounting record detailing the expenditure of 18 amphorae of wine by Severus, a contractor.

EDCS-16300016.translation: To the Emperor Caesar, son of the deified Hadrian, grandson of the deified Trajan the Parthian, great-grandson of the deified Nerva, Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Augustus Pius, invested with tribunician power, designated consul for the second time. The pagus and the civitas of Thugga, by decree of the decurions, at public expense.
EDCS-16300016.summary: A dedication from the community of Thugga (Tunisia) to Emperor Antoninus Pius, funded by public money and approved by the local council.

EDCS-16300021.translation: Quintus Pacuvius Saturus, perpetual flamen and augur of the Colony Julia Karthago, and Nahania Victoria, perpetual flaminica, made [this], and also expanded the cult, with their own money. Likewise, the portico and the market area in the home pagus.
EDCS-16300021.summary: A dedication by a perpetual flamen and flaminica of Carthage, likely funded by them personally, to improve public amenities like a portico and market area.

EDCS-16300210.translation: Of Marcus Planus, son of Lucius, of Russinus.
EDCS-16300210.summary: A simple ownership or funerary inscription, identifying Marcus Planus, son of Lucius.

EDCS-16300213.translation: Silbester to Africanus: You disbursed for the acceptors 11 pounds of sheep meat. On the 11th day before the Kalends of May, in the year of King B, I subscribed for sheep meat.
EDCS-16300213.summary: A record of a transaction involving the disbursement of 11 pounds of sheep meat by Silbester to Africanus, dated to a specific day and an unspecified regnal year.

EDCS-16300214.translation: Urbanilla disbursed for the tithes six pounds of sheep meat. On the Ides of July, I subscribed for sheep meat: 8 L.
EDCS-16300214.summary: A record of Urbanilla's disbursement of six pounds of sheep meat for tithes, with a personal subscription note for eight pounds.

EDCS-16300215.translation: Urbanilla disbursed one amphora of wine. In August, I subscribed for one amphora of wine.
EDCS-16300215.summary: A record of Urbanilla's disbursement of one amphora of wine, with a personal subscription note for another amphora in August.

EDCS-16300216.translation: I paid three measures of wine for sheep meat.
EDCS-16300216.summary: This is a record of a payment for meat and wine, likely a private note or receipt.

EDCS-16300217.translation: Urbanilla, you paid out, I paid.
EDCS-16300217.summary: This appears to be a personal note or receipt concerning a payment made by Urbanilla.

EDCS-16300226.translation: Covuldus will build the market at his own expense.
EDCS-16300226.summary: This records an individual's promise to build a market at his own expense.

EDCS-16300227.translation: Domnabus Quintus fulfilled his vow with his own [resources].
EDCS-16300227.summary: This records the fulfillment of a vow by Domnabus Quintus.

EDCS-16300229.text_edition: \n [] [] [] [] municipium Septimium Aurelium Severianum Antoninianum frugiferum concordium liberum Thibursicensium bure thermas Gallienianas[3] reformatas et excultas pecunia publica perfecit et dedicavit proconsule Lucio Naevio Aquilino clarissimo viro patrono municipi dedicantibus Naevio Balbino Aquilino legato Karthaginis cclarissimis vviris patronis publicis ad cuius operis musaeum plerique decuriones HS XLI milia CC conl[atis ------\n
EDCS-16300229.translation: [...] the municipality of Septimium Aurelium Severianum Antoninianum, fruitful, harmonious, free, of Thibursicensians, [...] the Gallienian baths, reformed and improved, completed and dedicated with public money, under the proconsul Lucius Naevius Aquilinus, most distinguished man, patron of the municipality, with Naevius Balbinus Aquilinus, legate of Carthage, most distinguished men, public patrons, towards which work, the museum, many decurions contributed 41,000 sesterces and 200 [...]
EDCS-16300229.summary: This inscription records the completion and dedication of reformed baths in the municipality of Thibursicensium by public funds, under the proconsul Lucius Naevius Aquilinus and with contributions from decurions, likely dating to the period of Gallienus (mid-3rd century CE).

EDCS-16300235.translation: Alceta, procurator of Numidian marbles, made this goblet.
EDCS-16300235.summary: This is a maker's signature for a goblet, likely made of marble, by Alceta, a procurator.

EDCS-16300369.translation: By the authority of the Emperor Vespasian Caesar Augustus, father of the country, the boundaries of the new and old province were delimited where the royal ditch was, under Rutilius Gallicus, consul, pontifex, and Sentius Caecilianus, praetor and legates of the emperor pro praetore.
EDCS-16300369.summary: This inscription records the delimitation of provincial boundaries under the authority of Emperor Vespasian, overseen by specific officials.

EDCS-16300371.translation: By the authority of the Emperor Vespasian Caesar Augustus, father of the country, the boundaries of the new and old province were delimited where the royal ditch was, under Rutilius Gallicus, consul, pontifex, and Sentius Caecilianus, praetor, legates of the emperor pro praetore.
EDCS-16300371.summary: This inscription records the delimitation of provincial boundaries under the authority of Emperor Vespasian, overseen by specific officials.

EDCS-16300380.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Urbana and indicating her son erected the tomb.

EDCS-16300384.translation: Natalika the faithful lived in peace for 55 years, laid to rest on the day of the Augustas, in the 10th indiction.

EDCS-16300399.translation: Sacred to Saturn Augustus. Diophantus, son of Bassiseris, having held all the offices in his city, erected this marble statue at his own expense, and he also dedicated it.
EDCS-16300399.summary: This is a dedication to Saturn Augustus by Diophantus, who had held various civic offices, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-16300401.translation: For the health of the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Severus Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus, the greatest victor in Parthia, Britain, and Germany, chief priest, consul four times, father of the country, proconsul, and of Julia Domna Augusta Pia Felix, mother of the Augusti and of their entire divine house, the colony Julia Aurelia Commoda Thuburbo Maius, the exceptional iana, built from the public treasury from the ground up.
EDCS-16300401.summary: This is a public building inscription from the colony of Thuburbo Maius, dedicated to Emperor Caracalla and Empress Julia Domna, likely dating to the early 3rd century CE.

EDCS-16300411.text_edition: \n Claudio Chresto viro egregio patrono perpetuo civitatis Hadrumetinae Dyscoli liberti patrono bene merenti qui vixit annos plus minus LV\n

EDCS-16400315.translation: To Mars Augustus, and to your divine majesty, good gods. The Emperor Caesar Nerva Traianus Augustus Germanicus Dacicus, son of the deified Nerva, pontifex maximus, holder of tribunician power for the 9th time, imperator for the 4th time, consul for the 5th time, father of the country, [has granted to] Lucius Minicius Natalis, legate of the emperor with the power of a propraetor, the citizenship of the Nybgeniorum, 29 [denarii?].
EDCS-16400315.summary: An inscription recording the grant of citizenship and possibly a financial award by Emperor Trajan to Lucius Minicius Natalis, his legate in Germania, dated to around 103-104 CE.

EDCS-16400473.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Lucius Magnius Saturus, a hardworking man, not worthy of his resting place, died away from home on the Hadrumetine road. He lived 55 years. Iulia Quina placed this for her dearest husband. He is buried here.
EDCS-16400473.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lucius Magnius Saturus, detailing his life, death, and the placement of the monument by his wife.

EDCS-16400475.text_edition: \n Caius Hil Felix sacerdos Saturni cultor dei exegit V Kalendas Novembres Sabino et Anullino consulibus per Baricem magg(istrum)\n
EDCS-16400475.translation: Gaius Hil[i]us Felix, priest of Saturn, devotee of the god, completed this on the 5th day before the Kalends of November, when Sabinus and Anullinus were consuls, through Barices, the magistrate.
EDCS-16400475.summary: A dedication recording the completion of a work by Gaius Hil[i]us Felix, priest of Saturn, during the consulship of Sabinus and Anullinus.

EDCS-16400496.translation: During the consulship of Tiberius Claudius (IIII) and Lucius Vitellius (III), by order of the aediles, it was exacted at the Articuleian weights, for the third time.
EDCS-16400496.summary: A fragmentary inscription likely related to fiscal matters or public works, dated by consuls in the early imperial period.

EDCS-16400497.text_edition: \n Ex auctoritate Quinti Iuni Rustici praefecti urbis\n
EDCS-16400497.translation: By the authority of Quintus Junius Rusticus, prefect of the city.
EDCS-16400497.summary: A legal or administrative statement issued under the authority of Quintus Junius Rusticus, the prefect of the city.

EDCS-16400501.summary: A simple funerary dedication for a daughter named Perpetua.

EDCS-16400502.translation: For the glory of our lords Honorius and Theodosius, wherever they are victorious. During the proconsulship of Caius Aelius Pomponius Porfiry Proculus, a man of highest rank and notable, judging by vice sacra, Marcus Senius Caripa, patron, devoted to the municipality, by his own declaration, completed a new fountain.
EDCS-16400502.summary: An inscription commemorating the completion of a new fountain by Marcus Senius Caripa during the proconsulship of Caius Aelius Pomponius Porfiry Proculus, dedicated to the emperors Honorius and Theodosius.

EDCS-16400529.translation: To Quintus Julius Severus Proculianus, a man of highest rank.

EDCS-16400530.translation: To Marcus Memmius Caecilianus, a man of highest rank, our patron, by the Gigthesians, publicly, by decree of the decurions, with public money.
EDCS-16400530.summary: A public dedication by the people of Gigthis to their patron, Marcus Memmius Caecilianus, authorized by a decree of the decurions and funded by public money.

EDCS-16400546.translation: Attia Quieta [dedicates this] to our Emperor Caesar Augustus.
EDCS-16400546.summary: A dedication by Attia Quieta to Emperor Caesar Augustus.

EDCS-16400547.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Olus Cosinius Fortis miles cohortis VI praetoriae piae vindicis Severianae praepo[situs ------\n
EDCS-16400547.translation: To the departed gods, sacred. Olus Cosinius Fortis, soldier of the VI Praetorian cohort, pious, vindicating, Severian, appointed [---].
EDCS-16400547.summary: A dedication to the departed gods for Olus Cosinius Fortis, a soldier in the VI Praetorian cohort.

EDCS-16400554.summary: A dedication to a 'Hero Augustus', likely a deified emperor or a person honored with heroic status.

EDCS-16400556.summary: A fragmentary inscription mentioning Marcus Pri[---] and 'urceus', possibly related to a person and a type of vessel or building feature.

EDCS-16500019.translation: To Sallustius and Livius Silanus, vows paid, by C(aius) M(arcus?).

EDCS-16500020.summary: This inscription likely refers to Sulla in his consular year, with a possible reference to a military or administrative unit identified as 'Vetavf III', dating to the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-16500072.translation: To Tiberius Caesar Augustus, son of Augustus, pontifex maximus, consul V, imperator VIII, with tribunician power XXXIIII, Gaius Septimius, flamen, made these four columns at his own expense, with Lucius Lurius, son of Quintus Rufus, as curator.
EDCS-16500072.summary: This is a dedication of four columns by Gaius Septimius, a flamen, to Emperor Tiberius, likely dating to Tiberius' reign (14-37 CE).

EDCS-16500076.translation: Saturnius, a sailor, citizen of Rome. Let the master pay the bronze tribute, let the master fall.

EDCS-16500102.translation: Sacred to Saturn Augustus. Publius Valerius Celsus gladly fulfilled his vow.

EDCS-16500144.translation: What is given by parents is to be preserved for good fortune; to amplify is of virtue. Flavius Fuscenillus, father, a man of the highest distinction, and his son, a man of the highest distinction, and Aemiliana, a most distinguished woman, and his daughter, a most distinguished girl, enlarged the shop. SA
EDCS-16500144.summary: This inscription details the expansion of a shop by a father and son, both of high status, along with female members of the family, emphasizing virtue and good fortune, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-16500195.translation: The gens Regianorum made [this] to the divine spirit of the son of Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus Arabicus Adiabenicus Parthicus Maximus, brother of Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus Pius Felix, prince of youth.
EDCS-16500195.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by the gens Regianorum to the divine spirit of Emperor Caracalla, honoring him and his father Septimius Severus, dating to the reign of Caracalla (early 3rd century CE).

EDCS-16500223.translation: From the workshop of Bassus, the tile-maker, of Agger, with his apprentices.

EDCS-16500258.translation: To our lord the emperor, Flavius Valerius Constantius, the unconquered, dutiful, fortunate Augustus.

EDCS-16600217.translation: Guest of the angels, companion of martyrs, and breathing a peaceful life, Crescentinus the deacon, with grateful piety as he is accustomed, has departed to you, O saint, remembering us, and has returned [this offering] on the 3rd day before the Kalends of August.

EDCS-16600268.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Primitivos sic pius vixit annis V mensibus VI hic situs est alumno bene merito Anicetus ex dispensatore fecit regionis sibi et suis\n
EDCS-16600268.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Primitivos lived piously for 5 years and 6 months, is buried here; Anicetus, formerly a quartermaster, made this for his well-deserving foster-son and his own family.
EDCS-16600268.summary: This tombstone records the burial of Primitivos, who died at a young age, and was dedicated by his foster-father Anicetus, possibly around the 3rd century CE.

EDCS-16600272.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Lived eight months minus [some number of] days. Badumas, in peace.
EDCS-16600272.summary: A funerary inscription recording the short lifespan of Badumas and dedicating it to the Manes.

EDCS-16600284.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Marcus Valerius Petao, a sesquiplicarius (senior auxiliary soldier) of the Gemellian ala (cavalry unit), from the province of Tingitana, lived 30 years, he is buried here.
EDCS-16600284.summary: A funerary inscription for Marcus Valerius Petao, a military man, recording his age and origin.

EDCS-16600317.translation: Boundary marker number VIII of Tanius Ampliatus. Boundary marker number VIII of Iulius Flaccus and Celsus.
EDCS-16600317.summary: An inscription marking boundaries and naming property owners, likely from the 1st or 2nd century AD.

EDCS-16600394.translation: Although the council of Segermitae had decreed a statue for Decimus Iulius, son of Decimus, of the Arnensian tribe, using public money, Decimus Iulius Saturninus and Marcus Arcis, grateful for the money, remitted the funds and erected [the statue] at their own expense.
EDCS-16600394.summary: A decree by the council of Segermitae to erect a statue, with the cost later covered by two individuals who returned the public funds.

EDCS-16600417.translation: Acana, Satrasamacna, Basilius, Amor, Pretiosus, Profugus, Pelops, Clarus, Salutaris.
EDCS-16600417.summary: A list of names, possibly from a funerary inscription or a dedicatory text, with no further context provided.

EDCS-16600420.translation: To the virtue of the holy martyrs Caelianuns, Sass, and the Limineres.
EDCS-16600420.summary: This is an altar dedicated to the virtue of martyrs.

EDCS-16600421.translation: The Emperor Caesar, son of Augustus, with tribunician power for the 16th time, Lucius Asprenas, consul and proconsul, governor of the VII Viri Epulonum, took care to fortify the road from the winter camp to Tacapes, with Legio III Augusta, 154 [paces?].
EDCS-16600421.summary: A military inscription recording the road construction from winter camps to Tacapes by Legio III Augusta under proconsul Lucius Asprenas, likely during the reign of Augustus.

EDCS-16600422.translation: To the Emperor Caesar, son of the deified Septimius Severus Pius Arabicus Adiabenicus Parthicus Maximus Britannicus Maximus, grandson of the deified Antoninus Pius Germanicus Sarmaticus, great-grandson of the deified Pius, great-great-grandson of the deified Hadrian, great-great-great-grandson of the deified Trajan and the deified Nerva, Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus Parthicus Britannicus Maximus, with tribunician power for the 19th time, imperator for the 3rd time, consul for the 4th time, father of the fatherland, proconsul, 33 [miles] from Tacapes.
EDCS-16600422.summary: A long titulary inscription honoring Emperor Caracalla, likely marking a distance of 33 miles from Tacapes.

EDCS-16600424.translation: To the Emperor Caesar, Gaius Valerius Diocletianus Pius Felix Augustus, consul for the 4th time, 40 [miles] from Tacapes.
EDCS-16600424.summary: An inscription honoring Emperor Diocletian, marking a distance of 40 miles from Tacapes, likely from the Tetrarchic period.

EDCS-16600425.translation: To the Emperor Caesar, Gaius Valerius Aurelius Maximianus Pius Felix Augustus, consul for the 3rd time, 44 miles from Tacapes.
EDCS-16600425.summary: An inscription honoring Emperor Maximian, marking a distance of 44 miles from Tacapes, likely from the Tetrarchic period.

EDCS-16600427.translation: Good fortune to our Lords, Marcus Flavius Valerius Constantius Pius Felix semper Augustus and Marcus Valerius Severus nobilissimus Caesar, 35 miles from Tacapes.
EDCS-16600427.summary: An inscription dedicated to Emperors Constantius I and Severus, indicating a distance of 35 miles from Tacapes, likely from the early 4th century.

EDCS-16600428.translation: Under the rule of our Lord, Marcus Flavius Valerius Constantinus Pius Felix semper Augustus, born for the good of the state.
EDCS-16600428.summary: An inscription honoring Emperor Constantine the Great, likely a milestone or dedication marker.

EDCS-16700004.translation: To the Augusti, under the proconsulship of Flavius Euxinus, most brilliant man, and by the legation of Flavius Clodianus, most brilliant man, Iulius Rusticius Vesper, curator of the republic.
EDCS-16700004.summary: An inscription recording the activities of Iulius Rusticius Vesper, curator rei publicae, under the proconsulship of Flavius Euxinus and the legation of Flavius Clodianus.

EDCS-16700058.translation: Caelestis, most holy one, may you be favorable to us. AMA.
EDCS-16700058.summary: A short votive inscription appealing to the goddess Caelestis for favor.

EDCS-16700083.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. I, Titus Crescens Vesdrunus, here myself preserve my bones and remains covered by this urn, a small tower made as a tomb. Piously, I lived 77 years. Felix, his son, made this.
EDCS-16700083.summary: A funerary epitaph for Titus Crescens Vesdrunus, erected by his son Felix, detailing his life and burial.

EDCS-16700084.translation: Sacred to Caelestis Augusta, he made this offering in fulfillment of a vow for the safety of Lucius Anniolus Albanus.
EDCS-16700084.summary: This is an ex-voto inscription dedicated to Caelestis Augusta for the safety of Lucius Anniolus Albanus.

EDCS-16700085.translation: Erienus Pudens and Iulia Fida built this temple to Ceres Augusta from the ground up at their own expense, in fulfillment of a vow.
EDCS-16700085.summary: This inscription records the construction of a temple to Ceres Augusta by Erienus Pudens and Iulia Fida, likely in the Imperial period.

EDCS-16700101.text_edition: \n Pro salute Imperatorum dominorum nostrorum Luci Septimi Severi Pertinacis Augusti et Marci Aurelli sic Antonini Bassiani Caesaris Imperatoris destinati templum Victoriae Augustorum cultores eius numinis fecerunt Iulius Emeritus flamen perpetuus impensis suis fecit anno provinciae CLVIII\n
EDCS-16700101.translation: For the health of our Emperors and Lords, Lucius Septimius Severus Pertinax Augustus and Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Bassianus Caesar, destined Emperor, the devotees of their divine power built this temple to Victoria Augusta; Julius Emeritus, perpetual priest, built it at his own expense in the 158th year of the province.
EDCS-16700101.summary: This inscription records the construction of a temple to Victoria Augusta by the devotees of the imperial cult and the perpetual priest Julius Emeritus, likely in the early 3rd century CE, during the reign of Septimius Severus and Caracalla.

EDCS-16700182.summary: This is a very brief inscription, likely the ownership mark of Marcus Staius Agathangelus.

EDCS-16700295.summary: This inscription, likely from a chariot racing context, lists names of people and horses, and includes curses against opponents and wishes for victory for Sarbamisarab and associated parties, possibly dating to the late Roman Empire.

EDCS-16700296.translation: Feiub Sarbamisarab, Delicaltanus, Capria Volucer Nervicus, Basilius, Nilus, Scintilla, Hilarinus, Polidromus, Delicatus, Marrusius, Blandus, Profugus, Pretiosus, Gemmatus, Amor, Pelops, Zefurus, Alcastrus, Attonitus, Roseus, Germanicus, Celestinus, Clarus, Salutaris, Socrates, the count, these names of men and horses which I have given to you, may they fall, I beg you, Sarbamisarab.
EDCS-16700296.summary: This inscription, likely related to chariot racing, lists numerous names of men and horses, potentially invoking them for success or cursing opponents associated with Sarbamisarab, possibly dating to the late Roman Empire.

EDCS-16800172.translation: To the divine spirits. Vetula, priestess, daughter of Saturninus, dutiful, lived 91 years and is buried here.
EDCS-16800172.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Vetula, priestess and daughter of Saturninus, who lived for 91 years.

EDCS-16800173.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Voltidia Augustina, who lived for 25 years.

EDCS-16800174.translation: To the divine spirits. Morasius Rogatus, dutiful, lived 4 years and is buried here.
EDCS-16800174.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Morasius Rogatus, who lived for 4 years.

EDCS-16800175.translation: To the divine spirits. Sergia Fortunata, dutiful, lived 80 years and is buried here.
EDCS-16800175.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Sergia Fortunata, who lived for 80 years.

EDCS-16800176.translation: [Name missing], dutiful, lived 73 years and is buried here.
EDCS-16800176.summary: This is a funerary epitaph with a missing name, recording a dutiful person who lived for 73 years.

EDCS-16800178.translation: To the divine spirits. Pompeius Victorinus Zenaratianus, son of Candidus, dutiful, lived 25 years and is buried here.
EDCS-16800178.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Pompeius Victorinus Zenaratianus, son of Candidus, who lived for 25 years.

EDCS-16800179.translation: To the divine spirits. Natalis, dutiful, lived 3 years and is buried here.
EDCS-16800179.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Natalis, who lived for 3 years.

EDCS-16800180.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Satria A
EDCS-16800180.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication to the deified spirits of the dead, mentioning Satria A.

EDCS-16800181.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Vibia Fortunata, dutiful, lived 75 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-16800181.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication to the deified spirits of the dead, recording the life and burial of Vibia Fortunata.

EDCS-16800182.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Vitellia Prima, daughter of Primus, dutiful, lived 30 years.
EDCS-16800182.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication to the deified spirits of the dead, recording the life of Vitellia Prima.

EDCS-16800183.translation: Aulus Pompeius Auspicalis, dutiful, lived 85 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-16800183.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication to the deified spirits of the dead, recording the life and burial of Aulus Pompeius Auspicalis.

EDCS-16800184.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Caius Saufeius Victor, dutiful, lived 77 years and 11 months; he is buried here. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Pompeia Euhodia, dutiful, lived 70 years and 6 months.
EDCS-16800184.summary: This inscription is a double funerary dedication to the deified spirits of the dead, recording the lives and burials of Caius Saufeius Victor and Pompeia Euhodia.

EDCS-16800185.translation: Sacred to all the spirits of the departed. Verus Barbarus lived 25 years.
EDCS-16800185.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication to all the deified spirits of the dead, recording the life of Verus Barbarus.

EDCS-16800186.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Plautia Lucilla, dutiful, lived 41 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-16800186.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication to the deified spirits of the dead, recording the life and burial of Plautia Lucilla.

EDCS-16800187.translation: Dedicated to the spirits of the departed. Saturnina the pious lived for 56 years and 10 months.
EDCS-16800187.summary: A funerary epitaph for Saturnina, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-16800188.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Victoria, daughter of Mena, daughter of Adiutor, dutiful, lived 60 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-16800188.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication to the deified spirits of the dead, recording the life and burial of Victoria.

EDCS-16800189.translation: Dedicated to the spirits of the departed. Lucius Morasius, son of Aevidus, pious, lived for 51 years.
EDCS-16800189.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lucius Morasius, son of Aevidus, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-16800190.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Quintus Mucius Rogatianus, dutiful, lived 24 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-16800190.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication to the deified spirits of the dead, recording the life and burial of Quintus Mucius Rogatianus.

EDCS-16800191.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Pompeius Victorinus, dutiful, lived 25 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-16800191.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication to the deified spirits of the dead, recording the life and burial of Pompeius Victorinus.

EDCS-16800192.translation: To the Divine Manes. Quintus Sirifius Candidus, dutiful, lived 70 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-16800192.summary: A funerary epitaph for Quintus Sirifius Candidus, dated by its content to be from Roman Imperial times.

EDCS-16800202.translation: I adjure you, demon, whoever you are, and I demand of you from this hour, this day, this moment, that you kill the green and white horses and the charioteers Clarum, Felicem, Primulum, and Romanum, strike them down, and leave them no breath. I adjure you by him who loosed you, the sea and air god, Iao, Iasdaō, ophiō, ēia, Cuigeu, censeu, cinbeu, perfleu, diarunco, deasta, bescu, berebescu, arurara, bazagra, Noctivagus, Tiberis, Oceanus, Antmoaraitto.
EDCS-16800202.summary: A powerful curse invoking a demon to cause harm to specific horses and charioteers, likely from a magical papyrus.

EDCS-16800231.translation: I commend to you my beloved Vettia, whom Optata bore, so that you may send her to infernal demons, so that they may not allow her to despise me, but may she do whatever I desire. For with your help, may she not be able to sleep, eat, or take food because of her love for me. Come to me, Karkē, Mōkthie, Oōdd, Oke, Entimoithespe. I bind Vettia, whom Optata bore, with sense, wisdom, and intellect, and the will to love me, Felix, whom Fructa bore, from this day, this hour, so that she may forget her father and mother, all her family and friends, and other men, and for my love, Felix, whom Fructa bore, Vettia, whom Optata bore, may she think only of me, frenzied, watchful, burning, chilled, aflame, for the sake of my love and desire.
EDCS-16800231.summary: A love spell inscribed on an object, intended to compel Vettia to love Felix, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-16800347.translation: Pottery work from the estates of Commodus Augustus, our lord, from the kilns of Marcus Adi Speratus.
EDCS-16800347.summary: An inscription on a pottery work, likely from the late 2nd century AD, indicating its origin and the producer.

EDCS-16800371.translation: Ilauc, son of Haitibalis, lived 33 years.
EDCS-16800371.summary: A funerary epitaph for Ilauc, son of Haitibalis, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-16900159.translation: Sacred to Caelestis Augusta, from the people of SVC.
EDCS-16900159.summary: A dedication to the goddess Caelestis Augusta, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-16900161.translation: For the Emperor Caesar Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Augustus Pius, son of the divine Hadrian, grandson of the divine Trajan the Parthian, great-grandson of the divine Nerva, pontifex maximus, with tribunician power for the 21st time, imperator for the 2nd time, consul for the 4th time, father of the fatherland. Publius A ctus, prefect of 12 cities, erected this at his own expense, according to his promise, and dedicated it by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-16900161.summary: A dedication monument for Emperor Antoninus Pius, erected by Publius A ctus, a prefect, likely in the mid-2nd century AD.

EDCS-16900163.translation: For the safety of the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Severus Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus, prince of youth, pontifex maximus, Germanicus maximus, with tribunician power for the 19th time, imperator for the 3rd time, consul for the 4th time, proconsul, grandson of the divine Severus, great-grandson of the divine Antoninus Pius. From the people of... by decree of the decurions, at public expense.
EDCS-16900163.summary: A public dedication for the safety of Emperor Caracalla, likely from the early 3rd century AD, funded by the state.

EDCS-17000036.translation: ... erected by Dumius, a centurion of the 13th urban cohort, between the Thaborenses and the Thimisuenses.
EDCS-17000036.summary: An inscription indicating a boundary or marker, set up by a centurion, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-17000039.translation: Sacred to the Fructiferous Augustus, the Nurse. Sacred to Janus Pater Augustus. For the safety of our lords, the Augusti. Publius Iunius Solutorius, having fulfilled his vow of religious duty, made and dedicated this.
EDCS-17000039.summary: A dedication to the deified emperors Augustus as 'Nurse' and 'Janus Pater', offered by Publius Iunius Solutorius, likely from the 1st or 2nd century AD.

EDCS-17700347.inscription_type: tituli honorarii, tituli operum, tituli sacri
EDCS-17700347.text_edition: \n Marco Fannio Marci filio Papiria Vitali |(centurioni) cohortis IIII Sygambrorum cohortis I Hispanorum misso honesta missione a divo Hadriano praefecto iuris dicundo flamini perpetuo qui ob honorem flaminatus HS X milia nummum rei publicae intulit et amplius ludorum scaenicorum diem et epulum dedit cui cum ordo statuam decrevisset titulo contentus sua pecunia posuit dono dedit\n
EDCS-17700347.translation: To Marcus Fannius Vitalis, son of Marcus, of the Papirian tribe, centurion of the IV Cohort of Sygambrians and the I Cohort of Hispaniards, honorably discharged by the deified Hadrian, perpetual priest, who for the honor of the priesthood contributed 10,000 sesterces to the public treasury and also provided a day of theatrical games and a banquet, and for whom the council decreed a statue, but content with the inscription, he erected it at his own expense. He gave it as a gift.
EDCS-17700347.summary: A dedicatory inscription honoring Marcus Fannius Vitalis, a prominent local official and military officer, who funded public works and games, likely dating to the 2nd century AD.

EDCS-17700348.translation: To Gaius Faltonius Fuscus, son of Lucius, of the Arnian tribe; although the town council had decreed a statue to him, Lucius Faltonius Valens, his father, content with the inscription, erected this at his own expense to his most devoted son.
EDCS-17700348.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by a father for his son, likely in the Imperial period, to commemorate a decreed but not yet erected statue.

EDCS-17700349.translation: Sacred to the departed gods. Orcivia Casta lived piously for 20 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-17700349.summary: A funerary epitaph for Orcivia Casta, dating from the Roman Imperial period, recording her name, piety, age, and burial.

EDCS-17700352.translation: Sacred to the Augustan Apollo. Decimus Fundanius Primianus, son of Papiria Fundani Felicis and grandson of Fundanius Primi, a perpetual priest, and himself an aedile, in imitation of his father's example, erected this statue at his own expense, having paid 8,000 sesterces, for the honor of the aedileship which his town council decreed to him by vote; he dedicated it and, upon its dedication, along with his colleague Annius Memmianus, gave theatrical games and a banquet to the people and the decurions. The site was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-17700352.summary: A dedication to Apollo by an aedile, Decimus Fundanius Primianus, likely in the 2nd century CE, detailing the cost of the statue, his honors, and public benefactions upon dedication.

EDCS-17700353.translation: Sacred to Leontis Dardani Caelestis, the Augustan goddess. Publius Iddibalius Victorinus, son of the quaestorian flamen Felicis and of Papiria, and Marcus Domitius Victor, son of the aedile Processanus and of Papiria, made this at their own expense, and upon dedication gave a banquet to the decurions. The site was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-17700353.summary: A dedication by two officials, a quaestor and an aedile, to a goddess, likely in the 2nd or 3rd century CE, including a banquet for the town council upon dedication.

EDCS-17700355.translation: Sacred to Liber Pater, the Augustan Pluto. Quintus Cervius Celerianus, son of Felix Celer and of Papiria, and Publius Cornelius Dativus, son of Marcellus and of Papiria, as aediles, made this at their own expense, and upon dedication gave a banquet to the decurions. The site was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-17700355.summary: A dedication to Liber Pater by two aediles, likely in the 2nd or 3rd century CE, specifying their families and including a banquet for the town council upon dedication.

EDCS-17700356.translation: Sacred to the Augustan Victory. Marcus Cimbrius Saturninus, son of Felicis and of Papiria, a quaestor and twice duovir, erected this at his own expense, having paid 8,000 sesterces, for the honors of his interrupted aedileship and his term as duovir, and gave a banquet to the council upon its dedication. The site was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-17700356.summary: A dedication to Victory by a prominent local official, Marcus Cimbrius Saturninus, likely in the 2nd or 3rd century CE, who paid for honors related to his magistracies and provided a banquet for the council.

EDCS-17700357.translation: Sacred to the Augustan Victory. Gaius Gemnius Felix, son of Felicis and of Papiria, a duovir, erected this at his own expense, having paid 8,000 sesterces, for the honors of his interrupted aedileship and his term as duovir, and gave a banquet to the council upon its dedication. The site was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-17700357.summary: A dedication to Victory by a local official, Gaius Gemnius Felix, likely in the 2nd or 3rd century CE, who paid for honors related to his magistracies and provided a banquet for the council.

EDCS-17700358.translation: To his divine majesty, by decree of the decurions and at public expense, the municipality of Giufitanum, devoted to him who holds tribunician power for the third time, is emperor for the fifth time, consul, father of the country, proconsul.
EDCS-17700358.summary: A dedication by the municipality of Giufitanum to the emperor, likely Hadrian or Antoninus Pius, likely in the mid-2nd century CE, highlighting his multiple titles and powers.

EDCS-17700359.translation: The town council erected this at its own expense to Boncius Ma, Roman knight, curator of the state of the municipality of Alexandriana Giufitana, a duumviral decurion of the most distinguished colony, and curator of many cities, for his singular love and justice and for the benefits conferred upon the state and its citizens.
EDCS-17700359.summary: An honorary inscription to Boncius Ma, a Roman knight and high-ranking official, likely in the late 2nd or 3rd century CE, commissioned by the town council for his service to various municipalities.

EDCS-17700360.translation: To Licinia Saturnina, wife of Aurellius Dionysius, patron of the citizens of the municipality of Aurelia Alexandriana Augusti Magni Giufitani.
EDCS-17700360.summary: An honorary inscription to Licinia Saturnina, wife of a patron, likely in the Roman Imperial period, by the citizens of the municipality.

EDCS-17700361.translation: The two men M. Ritaius and Prio dedicated [this monument]; and on the occasion of the dedication, they gave a feast to the decurions and presented theatrical games for two days; the place was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-17700361.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a monument by two individuals, who also provided a feast and games, with the location granted by the decurions.

EDCS-17700362.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Publius Aelolius Felix lived 41 years and 4 days. Driven by love for the sea and its deadly trade, I have come to eternal silence.
EDCS-17700362.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Publius Aelolius Felix, detailing his age and his profession related to maritime trade, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-17700363.translation: Marcus Curiolus Secundus lived 56 years. Marcus Curiolus Felix pious lived 33 years.
EDCS-17700363.summary: This funerary inscription records the ages of two individuals, Marcus Curiolus Secundus and Marcus Curiolus Felix.

EDCS-17700364.translation: Pescennia Quodvultdeus, a woman of honorable memory, born of noble birth, married like a matron, a chaste wife, a pious mother, bore 3 sons and 2 daughters, lived 30 years. Pescennia Victorina lived 7 years. Pescennius Sunnius lived 3 years. Pescennius Marcus lived 2 years. Pescennius Marcelus lived 1 year. Pescennia Fortunata lived 13 years and 8 months. Pescennius Marcellus made this memorial for his worthy wife and for our children, sons and daughters, while I am still alive, so that it may be perpetual for all.
EDCS-17700364.summary: This funerary inscription commemorates Pescennia Quodvultdeus, her deceased children, and was erected by her husband Pescennius Marcellus, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-17700365.translation: Sacred to Saturn Augustus. Labienus Pudens Caecilianus, a most illustrious man, gladly paid his vow.
EDCS-17700365.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Saturn Augustus by Labienus Pudens Caecilianus, a prominent man, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-17700366.translation: Sacred to Saturn, Lord. Lucius Sullius Firmulus, priest of the god Saturn, gladly paid his vow.
EDCS-17700366.summary: This votive inscription is dedicated to Saturn by Lucius Sullius Firmulus, who identifies himself as a priest of Saturn, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-17700367.translation: Sacred to Saturn Augustus. Sextus Valerius Festus, priest, gladly paid his vow.
EDCS-17700367.summary: This votive inscription is dedicated to Saturn Augustus by Sextus Valerius Festus, identified as a priest, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-17700370.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. For Insteia Diogenia, a deserving woman. Insteius Tertullus, a most illustrious man.
EDCS-17700370.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated by Insteius Tertullus, a distinguished man, to Insteia Diogenia.

EDCS-17700371.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulia Gadaia, mother, and Quartina Pupenia and Amantius Quartinus, [made this] for their most loving sister.
EDCS-17700371.summary: This funerary inscription was made by Iulia Gadaia, Quartina Pupenia, and Amantius Quartinus for their beloved sister.

EDCS-17700372.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Maia Aphrodisia lived 103 years. Aphrodisius, her son, made [this] for his pious mother. She is buried here.
EDCS-17700372.summary: This funerary epitaph records the long life of Maia Aphrodisia, stating that it was erected by her son Aphrodisius.

EDCS-17700373.translation: Romanus, bishop, laid to rest in peace, 11 days before the Kalends of [---]. Rusticus, bishop, laid to rest in peace, on the Kalends of [---]. Exitiosus, bishop, laid to rest in peace, 9 days before the Kalends of December.
EDCS-17700373.summary: This is a funerary inscription for three bishops, Romanus, Rusticus, and Exitiosus, with the last burial dated to before the Kalends of December.

EDCS-17700374.translation: Constantinus, subdeacon, lived 70 years, laid to rest 16 days before the Kalends of February.
EDCS-17700374.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Constantinus, a subdeacon, who died at the age of 70 and was buried 16 days before the Kalends of February.

EDCS-17700377.text_edition: \n Hymetii Caio Iulio Regino decurioni Karthaginis aedili IIviro quinquennalicio gentis Severianae Alexandrianae Augustae flamini flamini perpetuo curatori splendidissimae reipublicae Thimidensium Regiorum ordo decurionum ex sportulis suis ob merita dono dedit\n
EDCS-17700377.translation: To Gaius Julius Reginus of Hymetii, councilor, aedile, duovir for five years, of the Severian Alexandrian Augustan tribe, perpetual priest, curator of the most distinguished republic of the Thimidensian Regians, the council of decurions gave this gift from their sportulae for his merits.
EDCS-17700377.summary: A dedicatory inscription honoring Gaius Julius Reginus, a high-ranking local official in Thimidis, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-17700378.translation: To Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus, Parthicus Maximus, Prince of Youth, with tribunician power for the second time, consul, son of Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Pius Pertinax Augustus Arabicus Adiabenicus Parthicus Maximus, grandson of the deified Antoninus Pius Germanicus Sarmaticus, great-grandson of the deified Antoninus Pius, great-great-grandson of the deified Hadrian, great-great-great-grandson of the deified Trajan Parthicus and great-great-great-great-grandson of the deified Nerva. Gnaeus Cal[---] [---]
EDCS-17700378.summary: A fragmentary imperial titulature inscription, likely recording titles of Caracalla and possibly Severus, dating to the early 3rd century AD.

EDCS-17700379.translation: To Julia Domna Augusta, mother of the camps, mother of the Augusti, wife of Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus. Quintus Silicius Victor and Gaius Tadius Fortunatus, because of their perpetual priesthood office, made and dedicated a statue with a base for 2,000 sesterces, with legal funds properly collected, from the decree of the pagani of the pagus Mercurialis of the veterans of Medelitanus, with their own money.
EDCS-17700379.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a statue with a base to Julia Domna by two officials, Quintus Silicius Victor and Gaius Tadius Fortunatus, likely during the reign of Septimius Severus (late 2nd/early 3rd century CE).

EDCS-17700380.translation: Publius, son of Caius, from Norba, centurion of the [---] legion, [---], by decree of the decurions, with public money.
EDCS-17700380.summary: This inscription likely records a military honor or benefaction by a centurion named Publius, funded by public money and decreed by local officials.

EDCS-17700386.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that likely refers to a judicial official responsible for religious affairs.

EDCS-17700387.summary: This inscription identifies the 'civitas Abbircellensis,' likely referring to the community or territory of Abbircella.

EDCS-17700388.translation: To Migatia Victoria, incomparable wife. Silanius Crescens, perpetual flamen, erected this. The place was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-17700388.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Silanius Crescens, a perpetual flamen, to his wife Migatia Victoria, with the burial site granted by local authorities.

EDCS-17700389.translation: To Mars Augustus Protector, lord of our Emperor Caesar Marcus Antonius Gordianus Pius Felix Augustus, pontifex maximus, with tribunician power for the 2nd time, consul, father of the country. Quintus Calvius Rufinus, in his role as aedile, with his own funds and those of Titus Aelius Annus Litor, his former colleague, for the honor of their aedileship in compensation for games provided, made this with communal money. Calvius Rufinus, as aedile, dedicated it. Because of the dedication of this statue, the same Rufinus also provided a show of boxers and a gymnasium at his own expense. The place was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-17700389.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a statue to Mars Augustus Protector and the provision of public games and a gymnasium by two aediles, Quintus Calvius Rufinus and Titus Aelius Annus Litor, during the reign of Gordian III (mid-3rd century CE).

EDCS-17700391.translation: In the time of the most brave and most pious princes, under the administration of the proconsul of the province of Africa, originating from a noble family, perfected, cultivated, gave games, dedicated.
EDCS-17700391.summary: This inscription, likely from Roman Africa, describes the completion and dedication of games and construction during the reign of 'brave and pious princes', possibly the Severans or later emperors.

EDCS-17700392.translation: To Felix, restorer of this city, with Bonifacius the Conqueror, a most distinguished man.
EDCS-17700392.summary: This is a dedication to two prominent individuals, 'Felix, restorer of this city' and 'Bonifacius the Conqueror', likely honoring their achievements or leadership.

EDCS-17700396.translation: Aemilius Maurus and Flaminia Victorina made and completed this.
EDCS-17700396.summary: This is a dedication made by Aemilius Maurus and Flaminia Victorina, likely a married couple given the names, perhaps related to a building or a public work.

EDCS-17700402.translation: To Flavius Quadratus Laetianus, prefect of the I IMV cohort in the province of Tingi, for Flavius Felix, perpetual flamen and quinquennial duovir.
EDCS-17700402.summary: This is a dedication to Flavius Quadratus Laetianus, a military official, likely by or for Flavius Felix, who held important civic and religious offices in Tingis.

EDCS-17700407.summary: This is a tombstone recording the life span of Rogata, with Dionysius potentially being the deceased or the person who erected the stone.

EDCS-17700408.translation: Public vows. For the two-year term, administered by Quintus Mycius Endulcentius, perpetual priest, curator of the republic of the Biienses. [---] a temple begun many ages ago, from the ground up, in the two-year term of Gaius Aurelius Galosus and Marcus Favonius Macedon, completed in the year of the duovirate of Splendon Restutianus and Publius Aurelius Robur. Expenses partly from public funds, partly from offerings. [---] dedicated by Victorinus, a man of consular rank, governor of the province of Valeria Byzacena, with the care of [---] Arrius Secundianus. By sacred indulgence of our lords Constantius and Constans, the greatest Augusti.
EDCS-17700408.summary: A lengthy inscription detailing the completion and dedication of a public temple in Biienses, funded by public money and offerings, completed under the reign of Constantius and Constans, dating to the mid-4th century AD.

EDCS-17700409.translation: Rusticus, perpetual flamen and former magistrate, curator of the public affairs of the Botrians, has [given this] to the citizens, after the long age of almost a century.
EDCS-17700409.summary: This records Rusticus, a perpetual flamen and curator, dedicating something to the citizens of Botriensium after a significant period, likely honoring his service or the town's history.

EDCS-17700410.translation: Quintus Cornelius Secundus Gentianus, dutiful, lived 41 years. Aemilia Fuscula made this for her most dutiful husband.
EDCS-17700410.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Aemilia Fuscula for her husband, Quintus Cornelius Secundus Gentianus, who died at the age of 41.

EDCS-17700411.translation: To [his] father, who lived 78 years, and to his mother Tertulla, Titus Aelius Aemilius Nargisus, Titus Aelius Aemilius Melanthus, Marcus Aelius Aemilius Fuscus, Publius Aelius Aemilius Hospes, for themselves and their children and descendants and freedmen.
EDCS-17700411.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Titus Aelius Aemilius Nargisus and his brothers for their parents and for themselves and their descendants, indicating a family burial plot.

EDCS-17700412.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld for Satrius Rufus.
