EDCS-17700412.summary: This is a funerary dedication to the spirits of the underworld (Dis Manibus) for Satrius Rufus, likely a tombstone or a marker for his burial.

EDCS-17700416.translation: By decree of the decurions, by order of Lucius Sisenna, son of Lucius, Basso, who gave 22,000 sesterces from his return to the public treasury, also ordered that in the seventh year a statue be erected for himself for 3,200 sesterces, and in the name of a feast, that 5 denarii be provided for the decurions and 60 denarii for the curials on the Kalends of May, his birthday.
EDCS-17700416.summary: This decree records a public benefactor, Lucius Sisenna Basso, who left a significant sum for public works and amenities, including a statue and distributions to officials on his birthday.

EDCS-17700417.translation: Caecilius Nov made this work with his own money.
EDCS-17700417.summary: This records a construction project completed by Caecilius Nov at his own expense, possibly a public or private building.

EDCS-17700419.summary: This is a very brief inscription, possibly a dedication or an epitaph, with 'Julius Caesar' being a name and 'occasio' meaning opportunity or occasion.

EDCS-17700420.translation: To Valentiniani, Theodosi, and Arcadi, most distinguished perpetual legates of the alma Karthago, by senatorial decree, which concerning what was desired in the Capitoline temples, [let them run] through the spaces which had been empty. Mutilius, son of R., [made this] for himself.
EDCS-17700420.summary: This inscription records a senatorial decree concerning the use of space in the Capitoline temples, with a contribution from Mutilius.

EDCS-17700422.translation: To babylli, son of Papirius, [erected this] for the respublica from his own resources. He lived 13 years.
EDCS-17700422.summary: This is a dedication from babylli, son of Papirius, for the respublica, likely a funerary monument.

EDCS-17700423.translation: Dedicated to the Divine Shades. Publius Domitius Secundus, dutiful, lived 57 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-17700423.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Publius Domitius Secundus, recording his name, piety, age at death, and burial.

EDCS-17700424.translation: Dedicated to the Divine Shades. Domitia, dutiful daughter of Titus, lived 43 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-17700424.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Domitia, daughter of Titus, recording her name, piety, age at death, and burial.

EDCS-17700425.translation: Dedicated to the Divine Shades. To his wife Veneria.
EDCS-17700425.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated by an unnamed person to his wife, Veneria.

EDCS-17700428.translation: To the Pious, Fortunate, Ever-Victorious Augustus.
EDCS-17700428.summary: This is a dedicatory inscription to an emperor, likely Trajan given the context of the following inscription, praising him as victor.

EDCS-17700429.translation: By testament of Caius Memmius Felix Armenianus, admitted to the public equestrian order, a citizen of excellent memory, an arch was made. For its decoration, his mother Armenia Auge and his sister Bebenia Pauliana generously contributed 25,000 sesterces. On the day of dedication, they gave gifts to the decurions, a banquet, and games to the townspeople. Furthermore, the municipality of Seressos, to augment the decorations, constructed a quadriga at public expense.
EDCS-17700429.summary: This inscription records the erection of an arch and other public works in honor of Caius Memmius Felix Armenianus, funded by his family and the municipality of Seressos, likely in the early 2nd century AD.

EDCS-17700430.translation: Sacred to Saturninus Augustus. Marcus Tannonius Felix, perpetual priest, willingly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-17700430.summary: This is a votive inscription to Saturninus Augustus by Marcus Tannonius Felix, a perpetual priest, who fulfilled a vow.

EDCS-17700431.translation: Tertulus, a most distinguished man, restored the temple from its foundations at his own expense by vow, under the supervision of Alcibiades, the steward.
EDCS-17700431.summary: This inscription records the restoration of a temple by Tertulus, a distinguished man, with supervision by Alcibiades, likely in the 2nd century AD.

EDCS-17700432.translation: For the safety of Apthonetus, under the Emperor Caesar Trajan.
EDCS-17700432.summary: This is a dedication for the well-being of Apthonetus, likely a freedman or client, during the reign of Emperor Trajan.

EDCS-17700435.summary: This funerary inscription records the peaceful life of Paulus.

EDCS-17700437.translation: Honoratus Gaudentius [brought] the pavement and structures to completion for him.
EDCS-17700437.summary: This inscription records the completion of pavement and structures by Honoratus Gaudentius.

EDCS-17700438.translation: before you, triumphant flamen perpetuus, curator of affairs
EDCS-17700438.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription mentioning a triumphant flamen perpetuus and curator.

EDCS-17700439.translation: To Invictus Augustus, the most splendid order of the municipality of Tubernuc, devoted to his divinity and majesty.
EDCS-17700439.summary: This inscription records the devotion of the municipal council of Tubernuc to Emperor Invictus Augustus.

EDCS-17700442.translation: placed upon the columns, he perfected and improved it from another opening.
EDCS-17700442.summary: This fragment describes the placement of columns and subsequent improvements.

EDCS-17700443.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Aelius Germanus made this at his own expense for his Aelia, a pious woman who lived for [X] years.
EDCS-17700443.summary: This is a funerary inscription by Aelius Germanus for his wife Aelia, noting her piety and lifespan.

EDCS-17700445.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Quintus P. Arius Fortunatus, pious, lived for 76 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-17700445.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Quintus P. Arius Fortunatus at the age of 76.

EDCS-17700446.translation: Quintus Pompeius Balbus, a most distinguished man, proconsul of the province of Sicily, began [this]; Albia, daughter of Marcius, completed [it].
EDCS-17700446.summary: This inscription records the initiation of a project by Quintus Pompeius Balbus and its completion by Albia, daughter of Marcius.

EDCS-17700447.translation: Sacred to Diana Augusta. For the health of the Emperors, Caesars, Augusti, Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius and Aurelius Verus. Rogatus Thermus made and dedicated this in his own name and that of his children, with permission from the proconsul, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-17700447.summary: This dedication to Diana Augusta was made by Rogatus Thermus for the health of the emperors, with official approval.

EDCS-17700449.translation: Vincentia lived for 79 years in peace.
EDCS-17700449.summary: This funerary inscription records the peaceful life of Vincentia, who lived to 79.

EDCS-17700451.translation: Sacred to the divine power of the Augusti. Caius Aurelius Saturninus, from the tribe Papiria, holding the office of II vir (duovir) for the second time, as an honorary II vir, with more than his share, erected a statue of the She-Wolf with its insignia, and at the people's request, he staged a day of theatrical games, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-17700451.summary: This inscription records a statue of the She-Wolf and a day of games dedicated by Caius Aurelius Saturninus, an official of the state, possibly in the 2nd or 3rd century AD.

EDCS-17700452.translation: The municipium of Aurelia Vina, devoted to the divine power and majesty of our Emperor Caesar Publius Licinius Gallienus Pius Felix Augustus, pontifex maximus, holding tribunician power for the 4th time, consul for the 2nd time, proconsul, by decree of the decurions, at public expense.
EDCS-17700452.summary: This inscription records the devotion of the municipium of Aurelia Vina to Emperor Gallienus, likely around 260-268 AD.

EDCS-17700453.translation: The municipium of Aurelia Vina, devoted to the divine power and majesty of our lords, Cornelia Salonina, wife of our lord Emperor Caesar Publius Licinius Egnatius Gallienus Pius Felix Augustus, and him, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-17700453.summary: This inscription records the devotion of the municipium of Aurelia Vina to Empress Cornelia Salonina and Emperor Gallienus, likely around 253-268 AD.

EDCS-17700454.translation: The municipium of Aurelia Vina, devoted to the divine power and majesty of our lord Flavius Valerius Constantinus, most pious Caesar, by decree of the decurions, at public expense.
EDCS-17700454.summary: This inscription records the devotion of the municipium of Aurelia Vina to Caesar Constantine, likely dating to his rise to power before 306 AD.

EDCS-17700457.translation: To Augusta Felicitas (Prosperity). The community of the Siagitani, by decree of the decurions, at public expense.
EDCS-17700457.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the divine personification of Prosperity (Felicitas Augusta) by the community of the Siagitani, funded by public money.

EDCS-17700458.translation: Sacred to Victoria Armeniaca, Parthica, Medica, of the Augusti. The community of the Siagitani, by decree of the decurions, at public expense.
EDCS-17700458.summary: This inscription dedicates a monument to Victoria Armeniaca, Parthica, Medica, likely commemorating military victories of the emperors, by the community of the Siagitani.

EDCS-17700459.translation: To our lord Emperor Caesar, son of the deified Septimius Severus Pius Arabicus Adiabenicus Parthicus Maximus Britannicus Maximus, grandson of the deified Marcus Antoninus Pius Germanicus Sarmaticus, great-grandson of the deified Antoninus Pius, great-great-grandson of the deified Hadrian, great-great-great-grandson of the deified Trajan Parthicus and the deified Nerva, Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus Parthicus Maximus Britannicus Maximus Germanicus Maximus, holding tribunician power for the 18th time, consul for the 3rd time, governor of the provinces (for the 4th time), father of the country, proconsul, the best princeps. The community of the Siagitani, by decree of the decurions, at public expense.
EDCS-17700459.summary: This lengthy inscription is a dedication to Emperor Caracalla (Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus), detailing his extensive titulature and lineage, made by the community of the Siagitani, likely during his reign (198-217 AD).

EDCS-17700461.translation: To our lord Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Caro Pius Felix Augustus, pontifex maximus, holding tribunician power, consul, father of the country, proconsul. The colonia Iulia Neapolis, devoted to his divine power.
EDCS-17700461.summary: This inscription records the devotion of the colonia Iulia Neapolis to Emperor Carus, likely around 282-283 AD.

EDCS-17700462.translation: To the health of our lords, the illustrious and always Augusti Arcadius and Honorius, while the honorable lord Gabinius Barbarus Pompeianus, proconsul of the province of Africa, judging in place of the sacred authority, Coelius Titianus, most honorable man, former procurator and shipowner, former curator of public affairs, with his most honorable son Coelius Restitutus, dedicated at his own expense, at his insistence, while Publianus, most honorable man, perpetual priest and curator of public affairs, was administering.
EDCS-17700462.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a monument by Coelius Titianus and his son Coelius Restitutus, with the approval of the proconsul and local officials, likely in the late 4th or early 5th century AD.

EDCS-17700463.translation: To the health of our lords, while Marius Vindicis, most illustrious man, was proconsul, judging in place of the sacred authority, Marius Rusticus, procurator and shipowner, (dedicated something) during his second (term/year).
EDCS-17700463.summary: This incomplete inscription records a dedication by Marius Rusticus, a procurator and shipowner, during the proconsulship of Marius Vindicis, likely in the late Roman period.

EDCS-17700464.translation: To Marcus Aurelius Seranus, son of Marcus, of the Arnensian tribe, a most distinguished man, candidate for plebeian aedile, quaestor of the province of Crete, a citizen and patron, by decree of the decurions, at public expense.
EDCS-17700464.summary: This is a public dedication honoring Marcus Aurelius Seranus, likely for his local offices and patronage, paid for by public funds.

EDCS-17700465.translation: Quintus Coelius Laetus, son of Laetus, and Marcus Coelius Pacatus, son of Syllae, as aediles, having recovered from many sources the amount exceeding the budget, and adding another equal amount from their own funds, erected this, a site having been granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-17700465.summary: Two aediles, Quintus Coelius Laetus and Marcus Coelius Pacatus, funded the erection of a monument from a combination of public funds and their own money, with the site granted by local authorities.

EDCS-17700466.translation: Marcus Coelius Pacatus, son of Syllae, and Quintus Coelius Laetus, son of Laetus, having recovered from many sources the amount exceeding the budget, and adding another equal amount from their own funds, erected this, a site having been granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-17700466.summary: Two aediles, Marcus Coelius Pacatus and Quintus Coelius Laetus, funded the erection of a monument from a combination of public funds and their own money, with the site granted by local authorities.

EDCS-17700467.translation: To the memory of Marcus Numisius Clodianus, a decurion and augur, a good man, who, upon his death, by his will left 10,000 sesterces to reward the curiales of the Aelia Curia, the same curiales erected this statue at their own expense in his honor.
EDCS-17700467.summary: This inscription records a statue erected by the curiales of the Aelia Curia to honor the deceased decurion and augur Marcus Numisius Clodianus, who had bequeathed funds for this purpose.

EDCS-17700468.translation: To the memory of Aemilia Ebuciana Postuma, a most praised girl, daughter of Fabia Maiana, most beloved.
EDCS-17700468.summary: This is a funerary inscription commemorating Aemilia Ebuciana Postuma, a young girl, likely set up by her mother.

EDCS-17700470.translation: During the consulship of Gaius Caesar, Imperator, for the fourth time. Lucius Pomponius Malchus (?), freedman of Lucius, duovir, oversaw the construction of the entire town wall made of squared stone.
EDCS-17700470.summary: An inscription recording the construction of a town wall by the duovir Lucius Pomponius Malchus, likely dating to the late Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-17700471.translation: During the consulship of Marcus Appuleius and Publius Silius. As duovir for five years, Gnaeus Domitius Malchio. As aediles, Lucius Sertorius Alexander and Lucius Vitruvius Alexander constructed a permanent platform, two porticoes, a sundial, [---] and improved the road.
EDCS-17700471.summary: An inscription recording public works, including a permanent platform, porticoes, a sundial, and road improvement, funded by the duovir Gnaeus Domitius Malchio and aediles Lucius Sertorius Alexander and Lucius Vitruvius Alexander, likely dating to the early Imperial period.

EDCS-17700472.text_edition: \n Publius Attius Publi filius Vaarus sic legatus pro praetore Caius Considius Cai filius Longus legatus pro praetore murum turres posteicuus sic fossam faciundum coeraverunt Titus Tettius Titi filius Velina praefectus\n
EDCS-17700472.translation: Publius Attius Varus, son of Publius, legate pro praetore. Gaius Considius Longus, son of Caius, legate pro praetore. They oversaw the construction of the wall, towers, and rear fosse. Titus Tettius Velina, son of Titus, prefect.
EDCS-17700472.summary: An inscription recording the construction of a defensive wall, towers, and fosse by two legates pro praetore and a prefect, likely in a frontier context, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-17700473.translation: To Gaius Helvius Honoratus, son of Caius, of the Arnensian tribe, aedile twice, duovir twice, quinquennial duovir, and curator of the distribution of grain, a good man, by decree of the decurions of the Colonia Iulia Curubis, at public expense, for his outstanding generosity and love for the state and its citizens.
EDCS-17700473.summary: This is a public dedication to Gaius Helvius Honoratus of Colonia Iulia Curubis, honoring his civic service and generosity, erected at public expense.

EDCS-17700474.translation: To Herennia Cluchia of Patavium and Septimia and their sons.
EDCS-17700474.summary: This is a fragmented funerary inscription mentioning Herennia Cluchia and Septimia, possibly a dedication to them and their sons.

EDCS-17700475.summary: This is a brief funerary inscription simply stating the name and age of the deceased, Bonifatius.

EDCS-17700476.translation: Iobiana, faithful, lived 65 years, laid to rest on the 13th day before the Kalends of December.
EDCS-17700476.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the name, lifespan, and burial date of Iobiana.

EDCS-17700481.translation: To the Emperor Caesar, son of the deified Hadrian, grandson of the deified Trajan the Parthian, great-grandson of the deified Nerva, Hadrian Antoninus Augustus Pius, father of the country.
EDCS-17700481.summary: This is a dedication to Emperor Antoninus Pius, listing his lineage and the title 'father of the country', likely part of a public monument.

EDCS-17700482.translation: The citizens of Missua erected this statue to the eternal commemoration of the merits of Flavius Arpagius, a most illustrious man, who served as permanent priest of this city, who was an agent-in-the-ranks, a most illustrious man, an assistant to the illustrious Master of Offices, a most respectable tribune and notary, because of his outstanding services to the state and especially because of his benefactions as patron.
EDCS-17700482.summary: This inscription is a statue base erected by the citizens of Missua to honor Flavius Arpagius for his public service and patronage.

EDCS-17700483.translation: Quintus Mucius Lesbius is buried here. He lived piously for 98 years.
EDCS-17700483.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Quintus Mucius Lesbius, recording his name and age at death.

EDCS-17700485.translation: Adeodatus made [this] from the gifts of God and Christ.
EDCS-17700485.summary: This is a short inscription indicating a dedication made by Adeodatus, attributing it to divine gifts.

EDCS-17700486.translation: Sextilius Martialis, the husband, a public priest who had held all offices, and his son Martialis, permanent priest, decorated the temple, which Cassia Maximula, the priestess, had vowed to the divine Plotina Caelestis, a goddess, with marble, mosaics, a statue of Pudicitia Augusta, and a breastplate of Caelestis Augusta, at their own expense, built from the ground up, by decree of the decurions, and on the day of dedication they gave gifts to the decurions.
EDCS-17700486.summary: This inscription records the completion and decoration of a temple, originally vowed by Cassia Maximula and built by her husband Sextilius Martialis and son Martialis, with funds and honors provided by the decurions.

EDCS-17700487.translation: Dedicated to our lord Flavius Julius Constantinus, Pious, Fortunate, Always Augustus, by the devoted Karpis, who set this up under the proconsulship of Virius Lupus, a most illustrious man, proconsul of the province of Africa.
EDCS-17700487.summary: This is a dedication set up by Karpis to Emperor Flavius Julius Constantinus during the proconsulship of Virius Lupus in the province of Africa.

EDCS-17700488.translation: To our lord Gratianus, Pious, Fortunate, Always Augustus, the most peace-loving Sextius Rusticus Valianus, a most illustrious man, second-time proconsul of the province of Africa, established this to his peaceful divine majesty.
EDCS-17700488.summary: This inscription records the establishment of something to the divine majesty of Emperor Gratianus by Sextius Rusticus Valianus, a second-time proconsul of Africa.

EDCS-17700490.translation: To Aesculapius, Titus Julius Perseus, contractor for four public works in Africa.
EDCS-17700490.summary: This is a dedication to Aesculapius by Titus Julius Perseus, who was a contractor for public works in Africa.

EDCS-17700491.translation: Sacred to Saturn Augustus. Lucius Caesonius Victor decorated the epistyle with his own money and dedicated it, and contributed to the expenses with the priests.
EDCS-17700491.summary: This inscription records Lucius Caesonius Victor decorating and dedicating an epistyle to Saturn Augustus at his own expense, also contributing to associated costs.

EDCS-17700821.translation: Valeria Stacte gave a gift to Diana Caelestis Augusta.
EDCS-17700821.summary: This is a votive offering inscription by Valeria Stacte to the goddess Diana Caelestis Augusta.

EDCS-17700822.translation: Sacred to Mercury Augustus. Pompeius Iulianus fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-17700822.summary: This is an inscription recording the fulfillment of a vow to Mercury Augustus by Pompeius Iulianus.

EDCS-17700824.translation: Sacred to Sarapis Neptune Augustus, dedicated by Publius Aurelius Pasinicus with his family, at his own expense, by decree of the town council.
EDCS-17700824.summary: This is a dedication to Sarapis Neptune Augustus, funded by Publius Aurelius Pasinicus and approved by local officials, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-17700826.translation: Tiberius Claudius Sarapiacus, the priest, with his family, gave this offering to the greatest god Sarapis, by decree of the town council.
EDCS-17700826.summary: This is an offering to the god Sarapis by the priest Tiberius Claudius Sarapiacus and his family, sanctioned by local authorities, probably dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-17700831.translation: Crescens fulfilled a vow to the Lord Baal, who heard his voice and granted him good fortune.
EDCS-17700831.summary: This is a votive inscription recording Crescens' fulfillment of a vow to the deity Baal, likely from a period when Baal cults were present in Roman territories.

EDCS-17700832.translation: Lucius Vibius Datus willingly paid a vow to Saturn, the Lord Augustus.
EDCS-17700832.summary: This is a votive inscription of Lucius Vibius Datus to the god Saturn, indicating a personal offering made with willing intent, likely during the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-17700833.summary: This is a brief votive inscription by Niger, expressing the voluntary fulfillment of a vow, probably from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-17700834.summary: This is a short votive inscription stating that Rogatus fulfilled a vow with willingness, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-17700835.translation: Gaius Decrius Celadus willingly paid a vow.
EDCS-17700835.summary: This is a votive inscription recording Gaius Decrius Celadus fulfilling a vow with sincere intention, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-17700839.translation: To our Lord Flavius Constantinus Maximus Pius Felix Invictus Augustus. Domitius Latronianus, clarissimus vir, proconsul of the province of Africa, and Vettius Piso Severus, clarissimus vir, curator of the republic of Carthage, ever most devoted to his divinity.
EDCS-17700839.summary: An inscription dedicated to Emperor Constantine the Great by the proconsul of Africa and the curator of Carthage, dating to the 4th century AD.

EDCS-17700840.translation: To the greatest Arabicus, Parthicus, Adiabenicus, father of the fatherland, and to Julia Domna Augusta, mother.
EDCS-17700840.summary: This inscription honors Emperor Caracalla (implied by epithets) and his mother Julia Domna, likely dating to the early 3rd century CE.

EDCS-17700843.translation: Dedicated by devoted Carthage to our lord Justinus Felicis semper Augustus, with Lucius Map, most illustrious proconsul of the province of Africa, presiding.
EDCS-17700843.summary: This is a dedication to Emperor Justin I by the city of Carthage, overseen by the proconsul Lucius Map, likely dating to the 6th century CE.

EDCS-17700847.translation: For Arrianus, most brilliant man, prefect of the city, and perpetual flamens, for his merits.
EDCS-17700847.summary: This inscription honors Arrianus, the city prefect, and perpetual flamens for their commendable services, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-17700848.translation: Gaius Regilius Priscus, son of Caius, of the Voltinian tribe, a veteran of this cohort, [dedicated this to the centuria] of Clodius Rufus of the First Urban Cohort.
EDCS-17700848.summary: This inscription identifies a veteran and his tribal affiliation, likely associated with a military unit, possibly dating to the early imperial period.

EDCS-17700849.translation: To the departed spirits. Restored by T. Nepius Velocis, his heir, for his freedman Rufrius Adiutor, son of Decimus, of the Oufentina tribe, from Milan. He served in the 13th urban cohort, in the century of Pubilius, for 15 years. He lived for 40 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-17700849.summary: This is a tombstone for Rufrius Adiutor, a soldier in the urban cohort, paid for by his heir.

EDCS-17700850.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Quintus Vilanius Quinti filius Voltinia Nepos Philippis |(centurio) cohortis XIII urbanae donis donatus a Domitiano ob bellum Dacicum item ab eodem ob bellum Germanicum item torquibus armillis ob bellum Dacicum vixit nnos L militavit annos XXXII Marcus Silius Quintianus optio bene merenti posuit\n
EDCS-17700850.translation: To the departed spirits. Quintus Vilanius Nepos, son of Quintus, of the Voltinia tribe, a centurion in the 13th urban cohort, honored with gifts by Domitian for the Dacian War and also for the German War, and also with torques and armillae for the Dacian War. He lived for 50 years and served for 32 years. Marcus Silius Quintianus, optio, erected this for the deserving.
EDCS-17700850.summary: This tombstone commemorates Quintus Vilanius Nepos, a decorated centurion of the urban cohort, erected by his optio.

EDCS-17700851.translation: To the departed spirits. Antigona will live and feast. Vitalis, the courier of our Emperor, will live and feast. While I, Vitalis, am alive and well, I made this tomb; and as I pass through and read these lines, I myself, having circumnavigated the whole land region with diplomas and caught hares and foxes with dogs, and afterward willingly enjoyed drinks and feasts, having done many things in youth because I am about to die, whoever of you young men is wise, erect a tomb for yourself while alive.
EDCS-17700851.summary: This is an unusual funerary epigram by Vitalis, a courier, who erected his own tombstone and urges the living to do the same.

EDCS-17700852.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Hermaes, freedman of Augustus, an administrator of taxes, lived piously for 57 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-17700852.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Hermaes, a freedman and tax administrator for the emperor, who lived to be 57.

EDCS-17700854.translation: To the departed spirits. Aelia Rufina lived for 43 years.
EDCS-17700854.summary: This is a simple tombstone for Aelia Rufina, recording her name and age at death.

EDCS-17700855.translation: To the departed spirits. For Lucius Antonius Martialis, most devoted brother. [Restored text implies a dedication.]
EDCS-17700855.summary: This is a tombstone dedicated to Lucius Antonius Martialis, their most devoted brother, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-17700856.summary: This is a very short inscription, likely a name on a tombstone or monument, identifying Titus Appuleius, possibly dating from the Roman Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-17700857.translation: To the departed spirits. Caius Aufidius Maximus, pious, lived for 70 years. May the earth be light for you, may your bones rest well.
EDCS-17700857.summary: This is a tombstone for Caius Aufidius Maximus, recording his name, piety, age at death, and a standard closing formula.

EDCS-17700859.translation: To the departed spirits. Caius Caecilius Paulinus, son of Marcus, of the Arnensis tribe, pious, lived for 23 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-17700859.summary: This tombstone records the burial of Caius Caecilius Paulinus, a young man, including his tribe and age.

EDCS-17700860.translation: To the departed spirits. Commorianus, the pious, lived for 75 years. He is buried here. May your bones rest well, may the earth be light for you.
EDCS-17700860.summary: This is a tombstone for Commorianus, noting his piety and age at death, with a common closing formula.

EDCS-17700861.translation: To the departed spirits. Caelia Prima lived for 40 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-17700861.summary: This tombstone records the burial of Caelia Prima, giving her name and age at death.

EDCS-17700863.translation: Caesetia Ingenua, daughter of Marcus. [This monument] for Caesetia Ingenua, daughter of Marcus, who is also buried here. She lived for 13 years, whose bones are in the altar of the monument within the enclosure. The rest is [illegible] outside, where he lies. May the earth be light for you.
EDCS-17700863.summary: This is a tombstone for a young girl, Caesetia Ingenua, indicating the location of her remains and a standard closing.

EDCS-17700864.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Sacred. To Caria Galla, daughter of Quintus. She lived seven years, ten months, and twelve days.
EDCS-17700864.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the death of Caria Galla, who died at a young age, approximately in the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-17700865.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Sacred. [3]dia Cerealis, [3] pious, lived seventeen years.
EDCS-17700865.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary epitaph recording the death of a woman named [3]dia Cerealis, who lived to be seventeen, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-17700867.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Sacred. Concordia Quieta, pious, lived twenty-two years. She rests here. May her bones rest well.
EDCS-17700867.summary: This funerary epitaph records the life of Concordia Quieta, who died at age twenty-two, approximately in the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-17700868.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Sacred. Daphnis Candida, pious, lived thirty-five years. She rests here. Nicetes made this for his most pious companion.
EDCS-17700868.summary: This funerary epitaph records the death of Daphnis Candida, who lived to be thirty-five, and was set up by her companion Nicetes, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-17700869.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Sacred. [3]s Felicio, lived [---] years.
EDCS-17700869.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary epitaph recording the death of a person named Felicio, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-17700872.translation: Iasucta, son of Selidius, lived honorably for 63 years.
EDCS-17700872.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the name, parentage, lifespan, and honorable life of Iasucta.

EDCS-17700873.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Sacred. Iulia Durmi[ana] lived twenty-one years. She rests here.
EDCS-17700873.summary: This funerary epitaph records the death of Iulia Durmi[ana], who lived to be twenty-one, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-17700874.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Sacred. Licinius Crescens, pious, lived thirty-five years.
EDCS-17700874.summary: This funerary epitaph records the life of Licinius Crescens, who lived to be thirty-five, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-17700875.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Sacred. Mania Certula, pious, lived thirty years. She rests here.
EDCS-17700875.summary: This funerary epitaph records the death of Mania Certula, who lived to be thirty, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-17700876.translation: Maximilla, daughter of Bassus, pious, lived nineteen years. She rests here.
EDCS-17700876.summary: This funerary epitaph records the death of Maximilla, daughter of Bassus, who died at the age of nineteen, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-17700877.translation: Lucius Otavius Epaphroditus, freedman of Liguris, [erected this] for Octavia Optata, his freedwoman, and for himself while alive.
EDCS-17700877.summary: This is an funerary dedication set up by a freedman for his freedwoman and himself, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-17700878.translation: [3] Octavius Primus, innocent, lived twenty years and seven months.
EDCS-17700878.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary epitaph recording the death of Octavius Primus, who lived twenty years and seven months, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-17700879.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Primigenius lived piously for 22 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-17700879.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the age and burial of Primigenius, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-17700881.summary: This inscription is a name, likely from a funerary monument, identifying Romanus Victor Balbus, possibly dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-17700882.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Rufus Bamseus lived for 60 years; he is buried here. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Secunda, daughter of Rogatianus, lived for 70 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-17700882.summary: A double funerary epitaph recording the ages and burials of Rufus Bamseus and Secunda, daughter of Rogatianus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-17700883.translation: Sabinus Suganus placed [this] for his mother.
EDCS-17700883.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Sabinus Suganus for his mother, likely dating from the Imperial period.

EDCS-17700886.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Lucius Saturninus lived for 50 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-17700886.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the age and burial of Lucius Saturninus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-17700887.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Publius Saturninus [died...]
EDCS-17700887.summary: An incomplete funerary epitaph that begins with a dedication to the spirits of the departed and the name Publius Saturninus.

EDCS-17700889.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Saturninus, son of Rufus Faustus, lived piously for 65 years; he is buried here. May your bones rest well. May the earth lie lightly upon you.
EDCS-17700889.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the age and burial of Saturninus, son of Rufus Faustus, and including a wish for his peaceful rest.

EDCS-17700890.translation: Marcus Silius Maximus made this tomb for his dearest wife. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Vibia Saturnina lived for 33 years, two months, and sixteen days.
EDCS-17700890.summary: A funerary inscription where Marcus Silius Maximus dedicates a tomb to his wife, Vibia Saturnina, who died at the age of 33.

EDCS-17700891.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Sulvia Castula lived...
EDCS-17700891.summary: An incomplete funerary epitaph beginning with a dedication to the spirits of the departed and the name Sulvia Castula.

EDCS-17700892.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Publius Sufenas Felix lived piously for [3?] years and [3?] days. He is buried here. May your bones rest well. May the earth lie lightly upon you.
EDCS-17700892.summary: A funerary epitaph for Publius Sufenas Felix, recording his age in years and days, and including a wish for his peaceful rest.

EDCS-17700894.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Publius Volussienus Pacatus Saturnianus, son of Proculus, lived for 2 years and 4 months. May it happen for you as you wish, that you do not violate this sacred vow.
EDCS-17700894.summary: A funerary inscription for Publius Volussienus Pacatus Saturnianus, who died at a young age, with a curse against anyone who would disturb the grave.

EDCS-17700895.translation: [She] made [this] for [her] most pious wife in 24 days.
EDCS-17700895.summary: This is a funerary dedication, possibly by a surviving spouse, noting the completion of the monument within a short timeframe.

EDCS-17700896.translation: On the 24th day, we dedicated the foundations of the temple. See, friends, the servant of God invoking him, who heard him, rejoicing. The lord exalted you. Fastilanus completed the imminent [work] with joy.
EDCS-17700896.summary: This inscription appears to be a Christian dedication celebrating the completion of a temple foundation, possibly dating to the late Roman or early Byzantine period.

EDCS-17700902.translation: [He] is buried piously. Lived for 15 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-17700902.summary: An incomplete funerary epitaph recording the age and burial of an individual, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-17700907.translation: Colonicus lived in peace for 9 months.
EDCS-17700907.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Colonicus in months, suggesting a very young age and likely dating to the Christian period.

EDCS-17700908.translation: Constantia lived in peace for 10 years.
EDCS-17700908.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Constantia.

EDCS-17700909.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Gratiosus Vitalis.

EDCS-17700910.translation: Rogata the innocent lived in peace for 19 years.
EDCS-17700910.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Rogata.

EDCS-17700911.translation: Lucillus the faithful was laid to rest in peace on the Ides of January.
EDCS-17700911.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucillus, with a date of death.

EDCS-17700912.translation: Paula the pious lived 23 years and 1 [day?].
EDCS-17700912.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Paula.

EDCS-17700914.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Valeria Candida.

EDCS-17700915.translation: May Victorinus rest in peace and in harmony.
EDCS-17700915.summary: A short epitaph, likely from a tombstone, wishing peace and harmony for Victorinus, possibly dating to the Late Roman or Early Christian period.

EDCS-17700916.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Victorina.

EDCS-17700917.translation: Vincentius the faithful (is) in peace; Ber ta the faithful.
EDCS-17700917.summary: This is a funerary inscription for two individuals, Vincentius and Ber ta.

EDCS-17700918.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Vitalica.

EDCS-17700919.translation: To Vitalis, son of Cai, (is) in peace.
EDCS-17700919.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Vitalis, son of Cai.

EDCS-17700920.translation: To Vitalis, grandson of Lucius, in peace.
EDCS-17700920.summary: A funerary dedication to Vitalis, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-17700921.translation: Vitalis, son of Publius, in peace.
EDCS-17700921.summary: A funerary inscription for Vitalis, son of Publius, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-17700922.translation: Vitalis, son of Titus, in peace.
EDCS-17700922.summary: A funerary inscription for Vitalis, son of Titus, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-17700923.translation: Vitalis, son of Sextus, in peace.
EDCS-17700923.summary: A funerary dedication for Vitalis, son of Sextus, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-17700924.translation: [...] lived V days before the Kalends of August.
EDCS-17700924.summary: A funerary inscription recording the lifespan of an individual, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-17700927.translation: Innocens was laid to rest on the Kalends of May.
EDCS-17700927.summary: A funerary inscription recording the burial date of Innocens, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-17700928.summary: A short funerary inscription possibly referring to a person named Fidelis, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-17700930.translation: In this sign you will live forever, Caius M. Lu[...]
EDCS-17700930.summary: A funerary inscription with a religious or philosophical message, possibly for Caius M. Lucius, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-17700944.translation: VI son of Marcius, son of Publius. CVI PPII
EDCS-17700944.summary: A fragmented inscription recording family lineage, likely funerary, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-17700948.translation: NORE LESIS E CODVM IVA RATI
EDCS-17700948.summary: A highly fragmentary inscription with illegible content, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-17700951.summary: A funerary inscription recording the lifespan of a faithful individual.

EDCS-17700953.summary: A funerary inscription for a faithful individual who lived in peace.

EDCS-17700962.translation: Augusta, faithful, lived 5 years in peace.
EDCS-17700962.summary: A funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Augusta.

EDCS-17700976.summary: A funerary inscription recording the age of a freedman.

EDCS-17700977.summary: A funerary inscription lamenting a short and perhaps unfulfilled life.

EDCS-17700987.translation: This inscription is too fragmentary to translate or summarize.
EDCS-17700987.summary: This inscription is too fragmentary to translate or summarize.

EDCS-17700989.translation: The council of magistrates of the people of Tabuda erected this in honour of the Emperor Caesar Publius Licinius Valerianus Pius Felix Invictus Augustus, Pontifex Maximus, with tribunician power V, Consul III, Father of the Fatherland, Proconsul.
EDCS-17700989.summary: A dedication by the local council of Tabuda to Emperor Valerian.

EDCS-17700990.translation: Iar Moderatus, moderate and deserving, lived 50 years in peace. Departed on the Ides of January.
EDCS-17700990.summary: A funerary inscription recording the age and date of death of Iar Moderatus.

EDCS-17700991.translation: By decree of the council of magistrates, at public expense: To the Emperor Caesar Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Pius Augustus, son of the deified Hadrian, grandson of the deified Trajan Parthicus, great-grandson of the deified Nerva, Pontifex Maximus, with tribunician power XX, Consul IIII, Father of the Fatherland.
EDCS-17700991.summary: A public dedication to Emperor Antoninus Pius, likely erected by a local council.

EDCS-17700993.translation: Onomastus, overseer of the highest officials of the associated public works of Africa, is buried here.
EDCS-17700993.summary: A funerary inscription for Onomastus, an overseer of public works in Africa.

EDCS-17700994.translation: Felicula, a pious slave of our Caesar, lived 25 years. Festus, her father, and Epitynchanus, her fellow slave, made this from their own means. She is buried here.
EDCS-17700994.summary: A funerary epitaph for a slave named Felicula, set up by her father and a fellow slave, likely dating to the imperial period.

EDCS-17700995.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Annaria Fructa, a most dear and pious wife, lived 35 years. She is buried here. May your bones rest well; may the earth lie lightly upon you.
EDCS-17700995.summary: A funerary epitaph for Annaria Fructa, set up by her husband, likely dating to the imperial period.

EDCS-17700996.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Apronia Victoria, a pious woman, lived 48 years, 2 months, and 11 days. She is buried here. May the earth lie lightly upon you; may your bones rest well.
EDCS-17700996.summary: A funerary epitaph for Apronia Victoria, likely dating to the imperial period, specifying her lifespan in years, months, and days.

EDCS-17700997.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. A most happy and sweet houseborn slave lived 11 months and 20 days. He is buried here. May your bones rest well; may the earth lie lightly upon you.
EDCS-17700997.summary: A funerary epitaph for a young houseborn slave, likely dating to the imperial period, detailing his short lifespan.

EDCS-17700998.translation: Lucius Marcius Severus, son of Lucius, a dutiful man, lived 3 years. Lucius Marcius, a dutiful man, lived [unknown age]. Quintus M, a dutiful man, lived 50 years.
EDCS-17700998.summary: A fragmented funerary inscription likely commemorating multiple family members, noting their lifespans and piety, possibly from the early imperial period.

EDCS-17700999.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus Pinarius, the son, lived 33 years and 11 months and 15 days.
EDCS-17700999.summary: A funerary epitaph for Quintus Pinarius, likely dating to the imperial period, specifying his lifespan.

EDCS-17701000.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Saturus, a dutiful man, lived 22 years and 11 months. He is buried here.
EDCS-17701000.summary: A funerary epitaph for Saturus, likely dating to the imperial period, recording his lifespan and burial place.

EDCS-17701001.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. To my most sweet wife Victorina, who lived 28 years.
EDCS-17701001.summary: A funerary epitaph for Victorina, set up by her husband, likely dating to the imperial period, stating her age at death.

EDCS-17701002.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. [Iu]laria Mucia, a most worthy and pious wife, lived 31 years. She is buried here. May your bones rest well; may the earth lie lightly upon you.
EDCS-17701002.summary: A funerary epitaph for Iularia Mucia, set up by her husband, likely dating to the imperial period, specifying her age at death.

EDCS-17701003.summary: A very fragmentary inscription, possibly naming individuals, its purpose and date are uncertain.

EDCS-17701005.translation: To Iuno Sallustia, daughter of Marcus, Luperca, priestess of Ceres.
EDCS-17701005.summary: This is an epitaph for Luperca, a priestess of Ceres, who is honored with a dedication to Iuno Sallustia.

EDCS-17701006.translation: The priest of Aesculapius, of Jupiter Best and Greatest, adorned the temple with an altar and whitewashed work, and freely exhibited it by decree of the decurions, at his own expense.
EDCS-17701006.summary: This inscription records that a priest of Aesculapius, at his own expense and by decree of the town council, adorned and exhibited a temple to Jupiter Best and Greatest, including an altar and whitewashed decoration.

EDCS-17701008.translation: Bellicus, son of Maximu, willingly fulfilled his vowed promise.
EDCS-17701008.summary: This is a votive inscription recording Bellicus, son of Maximu, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-17701009.translation: Rogatus willingly fulfilled his vowed promise.
EDCS-17701009.summary: This is a votive inscription recording Rogatus fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-17701010.summary: This is a dedication or epitaph for Lucius Julius Urbanus.

EDCS-17701011.translation: To the Emperor Caesar, son of the deified Trajan, conqueror of Parthia, grandson of the deified Nerva.
EDCS-17701011.summary: This is a dedication to Emperor Caesar, son of Trajan and grandson of Nerva, highlighting his titles and lineage.

EDCS-17701012.translation: To Quintus, son of Saturninus, twice appointed as a duovir, promoted by the deified Pius to the equestrian orders and to the college of judges.
EDCS-17701012.summary: This inscription honors Quintus, son of Saturninus, who held the office of duovir twice and was elevated to the equestrian order and the judicial bench by Emperor Antoninus Pius.

EDCS-17701015.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the dead. Cornelia Rogata, dutiful, lived 35 years; she is buried here. May your bones rest well.
EDCS-17701015.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Cornelia Rogata, who lived 35 years, with a wish for her repose.

EDCS-17701016.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the dead. Fanius Saturninus lived 20 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-17701016.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Fanius Saturninus, who lived 20 years.

EDCS-17701017.translation: Gadaia, daughter of Icchnanis, sister of Nargududis, dutiful, lived 35 years.
EDCS-17701017.summary: This is an epitaph for Gadaia, daughter of Icchnanis and sister of Nargududis, who lived 35 years.

EDCS-17701018.translation: To the spirits of the departed; Mellita lived for 6 months.
EDCS-17701018.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Mellita, who died at six months old.

EDCS-17701020.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed; Orcivia Caia Pia lived, she is buried here.
EDCS-17701020.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Orcivia Caia Pia, indicating she lived and was buried here.

EDCS-17701021.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Receptus, stating he lived in peace.

EDCS-17701024.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed; Lucius Vitellius Felix, dutiful, lived for 15 years, he is buried here.
EDCS-17701024.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Vitellius Felix, who died at 15 years of age.

EDCS-17701034.translation: To Lucius Flavius Felicis Gabinianus, an outstanding man, perpetual priest and former chief magistrate of the distinguished colony of Carthage, our most abstinent patron, [dedication by] AI IS.
EDCS-17701034.summary: This is a dedication to Lucius Flavius Felicis Gabinianus, honoring his public service in Carthage, likely erected by his patrons.

EDCS-17701036.translation: Cambulus the faithful was laid to rest on the 2nd day before the Kalends of September.
EDCS-17701036.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Cambulus, recording his death date.

EDCS-17701037.translation: Potitus' freedman, [named?] rtus, dutiful, lived for 50 years; Lucius' freedwoman, Chreusis, dutiful, lived for 50 years; Gargilia, Lucius' daughter, Secunda, dutiful, lived for [unspecified years]; Gargilia, Lucius' daughter, Potita, dutiful, lived for [unspecified years]; Gargilius, Lucius' son, Primus, dutiful, lived for [unspecified years]; Gargilius, Lucius' son, Potitus, made [this monument].
EDCS-17701037.summary: This funerary inscription records the lives and ages of several individuals, with Gargilius Potitus erecting the monument for his family.

EDCS-17701038.translation: Alcius the faithful in peace; Iohanna the faithful in peace; Iohannes in peace lived for [unspecified years].
EDCS-17701038.summary: This funerary inscription records the peaceful passing of Alcius, Iohanna, and Iohannes.

EDCS-17701039.translation: Prima the faithful in peace lived for 50 years, laid to rest on the 3rd day before the Nones of March.
EDCS-17701039.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Prima, who died at 50 years old on March 4th.

EDCS-17701040.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari Lucio Septimio Severo Pertinaci Augusto pontifici maximo tribunicia potestate consuli designato II patri patriae civitas Ucres pecunia publica fecit et dedicavit anno Corneli Anullini proconsulis clarissimi viri et Valeri Festi legati eius\n
EDCS-17701040.translation: The city of Ucres built and dedicated this with public money to Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pertinax Augustus, pontifex maximus, holding tribunician power, consul-designate for the second time, father of the country, in the year of the proconsul Cornelius Anullinus, a most distinguished man, and of Valerius Festus, his legate.
EDCS-17701040.summary: This is a public building inscription from the city of Ucres dedicated to Emperor Septimius Severus, dated by the consuls of the year, likely the late 2nd or early 3rd century CE.

EDCS-17701044.translation: To Sextus Caecilius Crescentius Volusianus, son of Quintus, of the Quirina tribe, former praefectus fabrum, priest of the Arval Brethren responsible for sacred rites, advocate of the imperial treasury in Rome, procurator of inheritances and of the private correspondence of the deified Antoninus and of the emperors, patron of the municipality, by decree of the decurions, with public money.
EDCS-17701044.summary: This is a funerary and honorary inscription for Sextus Caecilius Crescentius Volusianus, detailing his distinguished career in imperial administration and his patronage of a municipality, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-17701045.translation: To Gaius Porcius Saturninus Minor, son of Gaius, of the Quirina tribe, tribune of the 13th Legion Gemina, tribune of the 12th Legion Fulminata, for his constant services to the state, by decree of the decurions, at public expense.
EDCS-17701045.summary: This is a dedication honoring Gaius Porcius Saturninus Minor for his military service and contributions to the state, funded by the local government.

EDCS-17701046.translation: Sacred to the divine spirits, in memory of the most holy woman Septimia Donata, who lived 41 years and 9 months.
EDCS-17701046.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Septimia Donata, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-17701048.summary: This is a dedication to the god Liber Pater, possibly during the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-17701049.translation: Maecilius Hilarianus, vir clarissimus, proconsul and judging with vice sacra, dedicated this to the divine power and perpetuity of our lord Constantine the Great, Pious, Victorious, Perpetual, Ever Augustus, founder and also amplifier of the whole Roman world and of all individual cities, increasing their state and adornment by his liberality and clemency.
EDCS-17701049.summary: This is a dedication by a high-ranking official to Emperor Constantine the Great, likely from the 4th century CE.

EDCS-17701050.text_edition: \n Lucius Domitius Ahenobarbus pro consule trimodium posuit qua civitates salem emetirentur\n
EDCS-17701050.translation: Lucius Domitius Ahenobarbus, proconsul, erected this three-modius measure so that the communities could measure out salt.
EDCS-17701050.summary: This inscription records the erection of a public measure for salt by Lucius Domitius Ahenobarbus, a proconsul, likely dating to the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-17701051.translation: The colony Julia Aelia Hadriana Augusta Utica, by decree of the decurions and with public money, [dedicated this] to their perpetual patrons Lucius Accius Iulianus Asclepiānus, vir clarissimus, consul, curator of the republic of Utica, and Gallonia Octavia Marcella, clarissima femina, their wife, and their daughters Accia Heuresis Venantius, puella clarissima, and Accia Asclepiānilla Castora, puella clarissima.
EDCS-17701051.summary: This is a public dedication by the colony of Utica to its patrons, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-17701053.translation: The splendidissima colonia Utica, while Silis Tertullus, vir clarissimus, their curator, was overseeing and dedicating, restored with its own funds a temple of three chambers that had collapsed from age, with added finer decoration of the coffered ceiling.
EDCS-17701053.summary: This records the rebuilding and renovation of a temple in Utica by the colony and its curator, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-17701055.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription possibly recording the erection of a monument by Aurelius Luper, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-17701056.translation: Aurelius Alexander Aibiseeius took care to set this up.
EDCS-17701056.summary: This records Aurelius Alexander Aibiseeius as the person responsible for setting up a monument, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-17701057.translation: Sacred to the divine spirits. Balbus lived 21 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-17701057.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Balbus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-17701058.translation: Sacred to the divine spirits. Gaius Blandus lived 73 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-17701058.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Gaius Blandus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-17701059.translation: Sacred to the divine spirits. Cassius lived 40 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-17701059.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Cassius, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-17701060.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Marius, son of Marcus, lived 52 years. He lies here.
EDCS-17701060.summary: A funerary inscription recording the death of Marius.

EDCS-17701062.translation: Terentius P. O[---] O V X N I A N V [---]
EDCS-17701062.summary: An incomplete inscription, likely funerary, mentioning a name and possibly ages or dates.

EDCS-17701063.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Tulia Lenna, dutiful, lived 20 years. She lies here.
EDCS-17701063.summary: A funerary inscription recording the death of Tulia Lenna.

EDCS-17701067.summary: An incomplete inscription, possibly a dedication or mention of imperial figures.

EDCS-17701074.summary: A funerary inscription recording the lifespan of M. Plancus.

EDCS-17701076.translation: From the Emperor Pius HE [---] father of Caius Stranius TV, curator of the state of the most splendid, sacred Cotuza, Valerius Ianuarius ADLLOSE [---]
EDCS-17701076.summary: An incomplete inscription mentioning imperial favor and a local official, possibly a dedication.

EDCS-17701078.translation: Sacred to the Genius of the colony of Julia Hippon Diarrhytus. From the colonists of the colony of Julia Carpitana, kinsmen, to the just, best, and most equitable judges, by decree of the decurions, with public money.
EDCS-17701078.summary: A dedication by colonists to the Genius of their colony, honoring its judges.

EDCS-17701082.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Marcus Artorius Festus Concessianus, dutiful, lived 75 years. He lies here.
EDCS-17701082.summary: A funerary inscription recording the death of Marcus Artorius Festus Concessianus.

EDCS-17701083.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Gaius Julius Gallicanus, dutiful, lived 14 months. He lies here.
EDCS-17701083.summary: A funerary inscription recording the death of Gaius Julius Gallicanus.

EDCS-17701084.translation: Muthumbal, son of Baliatho the Labrecan, a Thisitanian, priest of Adonis, lived 92 years. May your bones rest well. May the earth be light upon you.
EDCS-17701084.summary: A funerary inscription for a priest of Adonis, with a common epitaph wishing peace to the deceased.

EDCS-17701085.summary: A dedication to Porcius Avitus, likely a local notable from Histani, possibly on a tomb or honorary monument.

EDCS-17701086.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Garcilia the dutiful lived 80 years. Lucius Atius Rufinus made the burial arrangements for his mother-in-law.
EDCS-17701086.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Garcilia and commemorating her mother-in-law, with her son-in-law Lucius Atius Rufinus as the dedicator.

EDCS-17701088.translation: To Theodosius, Father of the Fatherland, Emperor Caesar, curator of the republic, procurator...
EDCS-17701088.summary: An incomplete inscription honoring Theodosius, who held the titles 'Father of the Fatherland', Emperor Caesar, and served as curator of the republic and procurator, likely a high-ranking official.

EDCS-17701090.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari divi Marci Antonini Pii Germanici Sarmatici filio divi Commodi fratri divi Antonini Pii nepoti divi Hadriani pronepoti divi Traiani Parthici abnepoti divi Nervae adnepoti Lucio Septimio Severo Pio Pertinaci Augusto Arabico Adiabenico Parthico maximo pontifici maximo tribunicia potestate XVII imperatori XII consuli III patri patriae et Imperatori Caesari Luci Septimi Severi Pii Pertinacis Augusti Arabici Adiabenici Parthici maximi filio divi Marci Antonini Pii Germanici Sarmatici nepoti divi Antonini Pii pronepoti divi Hadriani abnepoti divi Traiani Parthici et divi Nervae adnepoti Marco Aurelio Antonino Pio Felici Augusto tribunicia potestate XI imperatori II consuli III et Publio Septimio Severo Getae [nobilissimo Caesari principi iuventutis et Iuliae Domnae Augustae] matri Auggustorum et castrorum colonia Septimia Vaga nomini et auspiciis divinis eorum inlustrata per Titum Flavium Decimum proconsulem clarissimum virum colonia deducta arcum fecit et numini Augusti eorum dicavit\n
EDCS-17701090.translation: Colonia Septimia Vaga, in the name and under the divine auspices of Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus Arabicus Adiabenicus Parthicus Maximus, pontifex maximus, holding tribunician power for the 17th time, imperator for the 12th time, consul for the 3rd time, father of the country; and of Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus, son of Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus Arabicus Adiabenicus Parthicus Maximus, grandson of the deified Marcus Aurelius Pius Germanicus Sarmaticus, great-grandson of the deified Antoninus Pius, great-great-grandson of the deified Hadrian, great-great-great-grandson of the deified Trajan Parthicus, and great-great-great-great-grandson of the deified Nerva, holding tribunician power for the 11th time, imperator for the 2nd time, consul for the 3rd time; and of Publius Septimius Severus Geta, most noble Caesar, prince of youth; and of Julia Domna Augusta, mother of the emperors and of the camps, illuminated by their divine names and auspices, through Titus Flavius Decimus, a most distinguished proconsul, erected this arch and dedicated it to their divine majesty.
EDCS-17701090.summary: This is a monumental inscription by Colonia Septimia Vaga commemorating the construction of an arch dedicated to the emperors Septimius Severus, Caracalla, Geta, and Empress Julia Domna, likely erected during Severus' reign (193-211 CE).

EDCS-17701093.translation: to the most noble Caesar of the colony of Concordia Iulia Aurelia Antoniniana of Carthage.
EDCS-17701093.summary: An incomplete dedication or honorific inscription to a Caesar associated with the colony of Carthage, likely from the Antonine period.

EDCS-17701095.translation: To Lucius Pomponius Dextrus Celerinus, a most distinguished man, consul Aurelian Antoninian, the most distinguished order of the colony of Septimia Vaga, to its perpetual patron and curator; to Gaius Sergius Primianus, Roman knight, perpetual priest.
EDCS-17701095.summary: A complex dedication honoring Lucius Pomponius Dextrus Celerinus as patron and curator of the colony of Septimia Vaga, and Gaius Sergius Primianus as priest, likely from the late 2nd or 3rd century.

EDCS-17701097.translation: To Marcus Julius Maximus Felix, son of Marcus, of the Fabian tribe, decurion, appointed aedile and priest for 14 years, prefect for judicial matters, twice chief magistrate, twice quinquennial chief magistrate, and perpetual priest, for whom the most distinguished order decreed that a statue be made at public expense due to his merits; Quintus Agrius Iulius Maximus Felix, his uncle, made it at his own expense in a place given to him by the order, as a great tribute to his filial piety, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-17701097.summary: A public monument honoring Marcus Julius Maximus Felix with a statue, funded by his uncle, for his many civic and religious offices in the colony, highlighting his piety and merits.

EDCS-17701098.translation: To Titus Rutilius Iunior Iulianus, aedile and priest, quinquennial chief magistrate, and curator of the public games.
EDCS-17701098.summary: An inscription detailing the civic and religious offices held by Titus Rutilius Iunior Iulianus, including aedile, priest, quinquennial duovir, and curator of games.

EDCS-17701099.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcus Trebius Ribianus Silonianus, tribune of the people, lived 57 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-17701099.summary: A funerary epitaph for Marcus Trebius Ribianus Silonianus, a tribune of the people, recording his age and burial location.

EDCS-17701100.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Abinia Secunda the dutiful lived 45 years. She is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcia Secura the dutiful lived 31 years. She is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus Marcius Saedius the dutiful lived [---] years. He is buried here.
EDCS-17701100.summary: A funerary inscription recording the deaths and ages of three individuals: Abinia Secunda, Marcia Secura, and Quintus Marcius Saedius, likely from the same family or burial plot.

EDCS-17701101.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. To Aemilius Fortunatus.
EDCS-17701101.summary: A dedication to Aemilius Fortunatus, likely on a tomb or funerary monument.

EDCS-17701102.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Aemilius Fabia Marcellus, dutiful, lived 33 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-17701102.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Aemilius Fabia Marcellus, who lived 33 years.

EDCS-17701103.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Caius Caninius Felix, son of Caius, dutiful, lived 60 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-17701103.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Caius Caninius Felix, who lived 60 years.

EDCS-17701104.translation: To the memory of Marcus Aurelius and Vibia.
EDCS-17701104.summary: This is a dedication to the memory of Marcus Aurelius and Vibia.

EDCS-17701105.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Caecilia Honorata, daughter of Quintus, dutiful, lived 13 years and [illegible portion indicating months or days]; she is buried here.
EDCS-17701105.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Caecilia Honorata, who lived 13 years.

EDCS-17701106.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Euhemeris, dutiful and fortunate, lived 14 years and 8 months; she is buried here. Nicerus, her husband, made this for his incomparable wife.
EDCS-17701106.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Nicerus for his wife Euhemeris, who lived 14 years and 8 months.

EDCS-17701107.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Caius Granius Victor, dutiful, lived 40 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-17701107.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Caius Granius Victor, who lived 40 years.

EDCS-17701108.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Caius Iulius Fortunatus, dutiful, lived 80 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-17701108.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Caius Iulius Fortunatus, who lived 80 years.

EDCS-17701109.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Caius Iulius Poludeuces, freedman, and...
EDCS-17701109.summary: This is the beginning of a funerary epitaph for Caius Iulius Poludeuces, a freedman.

EDCS-17701110.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Iulia Maiorica, dutiful, lived 70 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-17701110.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Iulia Maiorica, who lived 70 years.

EDCS-17701111.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Quintus Laelius Helenus Sextianus, dutiful, lived 14 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-17701111.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Quintus Laelius Helenus Sextianus, who lived 14 years.

EDCS-17701112.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Marcus Lollius Primulus, dutiful, lived 66 years, is buried here. Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Marcus Lollius Lampadarius, dutiful, lived 45 years, is buried here.
EDCS-17701112.summary: This is a tombstone recording the deaths of two individuals, Marcus Lollius Primulus and Marcus Lollius Lampadarius, with their ages at death.

EDCS-17701113.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Lucius Mamnius Primulus, dutiful, lived 77 years, is buried here.
EDCS-17701113.summary: This is a tombstone recording the death of Lucius Mamnius Primulus, with his age at death.

EDCS-17701114.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Mersitana, dutiful, lived 33 years, is buried here.
EDCS-17701114.summary: This is a tombstone recording the death of Mersitana, with her age at death.

EDCS-17701115.translation: Marcus Gavius Felix, son of Sabrutto, dutiful, lived 65 years, is buried here.
EDCS-17701115.summary: This is a tombstone recording the death of Marcus Gavius Felix, with his age at death and patronymic.

EDCS-17701116.summary: This inscription fragment likely refers to a deceased woman, identified by her marital relationship to a Statilius.

EDCS-17701117.translation: Vulcia Flora lived 80 years. May your bones rest well.
EDCS-17701117.summary: This is a tombstone for Vulcia Flora, stating her age at death and including a common funerary wish.

EDCS-17701119.translation: Festa the faithful lived 110 years in peace.
EDCS-17701119.summary: This is a tombstone recording the exceptionally long life of Festa, emphasizing her faithfulness and peaceful passing.

EDCS-17701120.translation: Whoever trusts in God will live forever. Galatea the faithful.
EDCS-17701120.summary: This epitaph records the name Galatea and expresses a Christian sentiment about eternal life.

EDCS-17701122.translation: Balsillec, son of Imilcon of Tituris, lived 75 years, is buried here.
EDCS-17701122.summary: This is a tombstone recording the death of Balsillec, with his age at death and tribal affiliation.

EDCS-17701124.translation: Sacred to the gods of the underworld. Capras lived 10 years.
EDCS-17701124.summary: A brief funerary inscription dedicated to the gods of the underworld for a child named Capras who lived for 10 years.

EDCS-17701125.translation: Caius Domitius Secundus, son of Caius, dutiful, lived 73 years, is buried here.
EDCS-17701125.summary: This is a tombstone recording the death of Caius Domitius Secundus, with his age at death and patronymic.

EDCS-17701126.translation: Lucius Paccius Fortunatus, son of Lucius, pious, lived 25 years, is buried here.
EDCS-17701126.summary: A funerary inscription for Lucius Paccius Fortunatus, dating to the Roman period.

EDCS-17701127.translation: Salitthu, daughter of Liliecis, pious, lived 25 years, is buried here.
EDCS-17701127.summary: A funerary inscription for Salitthu, dating to the Roman period.

EDCS-17701128.summary: A funerary inscription for Sextus Staberius Hospes, dating to the Roman period.

EDCS-17701129.translation: Dedicated to the departed spirits. Victorca, pious, lived 65 years.
EDCS-17701129.summary: A funerary inscription dedicated to the departed spirits, for Victorca, dating to the Roman period.

EDCS-17701130.translation: To the gods. Verus Augustus, for the honors of the FEA OR family, VVT.
EDCS-17701130.summary: A dedication to the gods, possibly related to imperial honors, dating to the Roman period.

EDCS-17701134.translation: For the health of his son Veturio, son of Lucius, of the Quirina tribe, Fortunatus, because of his supreme affection for daily life and his incomparable administration of the duovirate and his singular integrity exhibited for public benefits and advantages, the town councillors of the colony of Julia Augusta of Simithensian Numidia, for his many and great merits, erected this with a collection of money, on land granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-17701134.summary: A public monument erected by the town councillors of Simithensian Numidia to honor Veturio Fortunatus for his public service and integrity, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-17701135.translation: The pious wife of Quintus Volcius Ianuarius, Gargilia Tiburtina, daughter of Quintus Volcius Ianuarius, lived 102 years. She lies here. Sacred to the gods of the underworld.
EDCS-17701135.summary: A funerary inscription for Gargilia Tiburtina, wife of Quintus Volcius Ianuarius, who lived 102 years, dedicated to the gods of the underworld.

EDCS-17701136.translation: Dedicated to the departed spirits. Iulius Honoratus Inerius. Dedicated to the departed spirits. Nesta, pious, lived.
EDCS-17701136.summary: A fragmented funerary inscription possibly honoring two individuals, Iulius Honoratus Inerius and Nesta, dating to the Roman period.

EDCS-17701137.translation: Dedicated to the departed spirits. Iulius Honoratianus, pious, lived 35 years, is buried here.
EDCS-17701137.summary: A funerary inscription for Iulius Honoratianus, dating to the Roman period.

EDCS-17701139.translation: Dedicated to the departed spirits. Guddem, son of Pardali, pious, lived 93 years. The heir took care of it.
EDCS-17701139.summary: A funerary inscription for Guddem, son of Pardali, with his heir arranging the burial, dating to the Roman period.

EDCS-17701140.translation: For the health of the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus Germanicus Sarmaticus, of the divine family and household, Lucius Memmius Felix, priest of the temple of the lord Aesculapius, made this altar, a bronze caldron, a jug, and a bronze lamp with his own money, and he himself dedicated them.
EDCS-17701140.summary: A dedication by Lucius Memmius Felix, a priest of Aesculapius, for the health of Emperor Marcus Aurelius Antoninus and his family, likely dating to the mid-2nd century CE.

EDCS-17701142.translation: To Titus Flavius Gallicus, son of Titus, of the Quirina tribe, procurator Augusti of the province of Africa, prefect of the harbour district of Carthage, appointed by the Emperor Caesar Hadrianus Augustus, by the decurions and fellow citizens of Thisiduenus.
EDCS-17701142.summary: This is a dedication by the decurions and citizens of Thisiduenus to Titus Flavius Gallicus, an imperial official, likely on a public monument.

EDCS-17701143.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Lusias Fortunatiana, who was aedile and munerarius, also duovir and munerarius acting in place of curators of the state, lived piously for 46 years, here always in peace.
EDCS-17701143.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lusias Fortunatiana, who held several local magistracies, dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-17701144.translation: Herennia Quartata, an eques of Arnus, for the honour of the Emperor Augustus Besicanus Armeniacus Aurelianus Antoninianus Maximus, the decurions of [city name] by his magnificence and SPECT Martini Perpetus, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-17701144.summary: This inscription records the erection of a statue to Emperor Aurelian by the decurions of an unknown city, honoring his military victories.

EDCS-17701147.translation: To the most noble Caesar, devoted to him, the colony of Vallis Numinis.
EDCS-17701147.summary: This is a dedication by the colony of Vallis Numinis to a noble Caesar, likely a ruler of the Roman Empire.

EDCS-17701148.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Augustus, to Marcus Antonius, the most noble Caesar, devoted to him, the colony of Vallis Numinis.
EDCS-17701148.summary: This is a dedication by the colony of Vallis Numinis to Emperors Augustus and Marcus Antonius, likely Caracalla.

EDCS-17701149.summary: This is a dedication to Emperor Valentinianus, likely Valentinian I or II.

EDCS-17701150.translation: During the proconsulship of Petronius Probianus, a man of consular rank, while judging in place of the highest pontiff, Julius Tullius Priscus, a man of consular rank, the legate, in the prosperous Carthage, with Aemilius Victor, an excellent man, the perpetual priest and curator of the state, having overseen it, placed it.
EDCS-17701150.summary: This inscription records the placement of a monument in Carthage during the proconsulship of Petronius Probianus, overseen by Aemilius Victor, a perpetual priest and curator.

EDCS-17701151.translation: To Publius Metilius Secundus, legate Augusti pro praetore, [from the men] of the third Augustan legion.
EDCS-17701151.summary: This is a dedication by soldiers of the Legio III Augusta to their governor, Publius Metilius Secundus.

EDCS-17701152.translation: Marcus Arellius Victor, perpetual priest, son of Acis, and [his son], the first duovir, and Publius Bellicus Secundus, perpetual priest, gave and dedicated this marble statue.
EDCS-17701152.summary: This is a dedication of a marble statue by Marcus Arellius Victor and Publius Bellicus Secundus, both perpetual priests and local magistrates, likely in the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-17701153.translation: The decurions of the municipality of Vallis made this at their own expense for Vettia Quinia, daughter of Quintus, perpetual priestess of the municipality of Vallis, wife of Cluvius Tertullinus, curator of the state.
EDCS-17701153.summary: This inscription records a monument erected by the decurions of Vallis for Vettia Quinia, wife of the state curator Cluvius Tertullinus and herself a perpetual priestess.

EDCS-17701154.translation: He dedicated at his own expense and with his diligent effort, together with the most distinguished order, the columns, marble slabs, and statues, which had been designated and were in better condition, for their improvement.
EDCS-17701154.summary: This inscription records the dedication of public works, including columns, marble, and statues, by a designated curator at his own expense.

EDCS-17701155.translation: The order of decurions made this by public decree to repay the affection which Optatus, patron of their municipality, Vallitani, shows generously to his homeland and citizens.
EDCS-17701155.summary: This inscription records a public decree by the decurions of the municipality of Vallitani honoring their patron, Optatus, for his generosity.

EDCS-17701156.translation: The portico and the curia of our lords, Honorius and Theodosius, perpetual Augusti, were constructed from their bounty, under the administration, dedication, and care of Lucius Geminius Ianuarius, an honorable man and perpetual priest.
EDCS-17701156.summary: This inscription records the construction of a portico and curia, funded by Emperors Honorius and Theodosius, under the supervision of Lucius Geminius Ianuarius, a perpetual priest.

EDCS-17701159.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Ancuria Victoria lived piously for [---] years.
EDCS-17701159.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Ancuria Victoria, recording her piety and age at death.

EDCS-17701160.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Lucius Bellicius Bellicianus lived piously for 70 years, 1 month, and 5 days. Here lies Bellicius Repostus, his dearest father.
EDCS-17701160.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Bellicius Bellicianus, recording his lifespan and that his father, Bellicius Repostus, is buried there.

EDCS-17701161.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Lucius Caecilius Rogatus, son of Lucius, of the Papiria tribe, pious and most frugal, a praiseworthy father of his sect, a man of integrity, innocence, and loyalty, lived for 73 years, 11 months, and 9 days. Here lies Constantius, his son.
EDCS-17701161.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Caecilius Rogatus, detailing his virtues, lifespan, and mentioning his son Constantius.

EDCS-17701162.translation: Lucius Caelius Aurelianus, son of Lucius, of the Papiria tribe, pious, lived for 60 years. Alfidia Quartina, daughter of Lucius, pious, lived for 48 years and [---] months.
EDCS-17701162.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Caelius Aurelianus and Alfidia Quartina, recording their respective ages at death.

EDCS-17701163.translation: Modius Ianuarius, son of Primus, pious, lived for 65 years, 3 months, and 6 days. He lies here.
EDCS-17701163.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Modius Ianuarius, recording his lifespan and burial location.

EDCS-17701164.translation: Liber, pious, lived for 65 years and 24 days. He lies here.
EDCS-17701164.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Liber, recording his pious life and lifespan.

EDCS-17701167.translation: For the safety of the Emperor Caesar Marcus Antoninus. [Someone] enthusiastically built the apodyterium and exedra [---] individually with marble columns, because of the dedication of these things.
EDCS-17701167.summary: This inscription likely records the construction or renovation of bathing facilities, possibly an apodyterium and exedra, for the well-being of Emperor Marcus Antoninus.

EDCS-17701168.translation: By grace of our lords Gratian, Valentinian, and Theodosius, most invincible princes, two decrees having been established according to ancient custom, the dedication of a statue confirmed greater judgments; first by divine command, under Titus Cassius Veturius, proconsul, and now, under Secundus Audentius Aemilianus, most distinguished man, acting proconsul, with magnificent and most worthy authority, and by the decree of the senate [or emperor], for his merits and benefits bestowed upon the citizens and the state, Calicius Honoratianus, our most worthy patron, has erected a statue in his own marble, and in his glory.
