EDCS-17701168.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a statue to the patron Calicius Honoratianus, likely in the late 4th century CE, by officials under the emperors Gratian, Valentinian, and Theodosius.

EDCS-17701170.translation: Julius Saturus, perpetual priest and curator of the state, his children and heirs, at their own expense.
EDCS-17701170.summary: This inscription records a dedication or monument erected at personal expense by Julius Saturus, a perpetual priest and state curator, and his heirs.

EDCS-17701171.translation: At the beginning of the work, abandoned to Honoratus and Caelius Sperantius, perpetual priests.
EDCS-17701171.summary: This inscription likely records a dedication or a phase of construction associated with the perpetual priests Honoratus and Caelius Sperantius.

EDCS-17701172.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Annaeus Saturninus Appellianus lived for 31 years, he is buried here.
EDCS-17701172.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Annaeus Saturninus Appellianus, who died at the age of 31.

EDCS-17701173.translation: To Honoratus, a Roman knight, who lived for [number] years.
EDCS-17701173.summary: This is a funerary inscription fragment for Honoratus, a Roman knight, indicating his lifespan.

EDCS-17701174.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcus Terentius Saturninus lived for 31 years.
EDCS-17701174.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Marcus Terentius Saturninus, who died at the age of 31.

EDCS-17701175.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription that likely refers to Titus Saturninus, possibly in a funerary context.

EDCS-17701177.translation: Pious, lived for 80 years, he is buried here.
EDCS-17701177.summary: This is a funerary inscription fragment for an unnamed individual who lived to be 80 years old.

EDCS-17701178.translation: To Severus Optatus, of the tribe [name missing].
EDCS-17701178.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that likely refers to Severus Optatus, possibly dedicating a monument or being honored.

EDCS-17701179.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcus Aemilius Receptus Rogatianus, dutiful, lived for 63 years, he is buried here. To him, Aemilia Recepta, his wife, and Publius Sexticius Appollinaris and Aemilius Saturninus, friends and heirs, made this monument.
EDCS-17701179.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Marcus Aemilius Receptus Rogatianus, who died at 63, with his wife, friends, and heirs dedicating the monument.

EDCS-17701181.translation: Sacred to Hercules Augustus. Fabius Larini Stachumelis, his son, the arch-maker, dedicated this with a tiled roof and the father's seal, and dedicated it himself.
EDCS-17701181.summary: A dedication to Hercules Augustus by Fabius Larini Stachumelis, who was an arch-maker.

EDCS-17701187.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Caelius Felicianus, son of Secundus, lived for 19 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-17701187.summary: A funerary inscription for Caelius Felicianus, who died at age 19.

EDCS-17701188.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Curia Felicla the pious lived for 85 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-17701188.summary: A funerary inscription for Curia Felicla, who died at age 85.

EDCS-17701189.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Modia Sabina the pious lived for 12 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-17701189.summary: A funerary inscription for Modia Sabina, who died at age 12.

EDCS-17701190.translation: Sacred to Caelestis Augusta. Quintus Mattius Primus donated 125 denarii for the expansion of the temple and the steps, and gladly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-17701190.summary: A dedication by Quintus Mattius Primus for temple improvements, likely during the 2nd century AD.

EDCS-17701191.summary: A dedication to Cibbercia Fortunata, likely a funerary or honorary inscription from a child.

EDCS-17701193.translation: For the safety of the Emperors Caesars Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus and Lucius Aurelius Commodus Augustus and their entire household. Gaius Volcius Quietus made an altar from the ground up for 500 sesterces with his own money, and dedicated it himself. Also, for the dedication, he gave entrails and a feast to his relatives and priests.
EDCS-17701193.summary: A dedication of an altar by Gaius Volcius Quietus for the safety of Emperors Marcus Aurelius and Commodus, likely from the late 2nd century AD.

EDCS-17701194.translation: To Gaius Sulgius Caecilianus, son of Lucius, of the Papiria tribe, prefect of the III Cyrenaica legion, primus pilus of the XX Valeria Victrix legion, supervisor of the reserve fleet of Misenum Piae Vindicis and the imperial treasuries and of the baggage trains for transporting troops, centurion of the III Augusta, VII Gemina, I Parthica, XVI Flavia Firma, and XIII Gemina legions in the province of Dacia, naval officer of the reserve fleet of Misenum Piae Vindicis, optio of the peregrini, trainer of the frumentarii soldiers, and to Sulgia AE and Sulgius Aper, his father and husband.
EDCS-17701194.summary: A complex funerary epitaph for Gaius Sulgius Caecilianus, detailing his extensive military career and familial relationships, likely from the late 2nd or early 3rd century AD.

EDCS-17701196.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Geminia Artemisia, daughter of Aulus.
EDCS-17701196.summary: A funerary inscription for Geminia Artemisia, daughter of Aulus.

EDCS-17701197.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Marcus Iulius Ithimbal Amulianus lived for 70 years.
EDCS-17701197.summary: A funerary inscription for Marcus Iulius Ithimbal Amulianus, who died at age 70.

EDCS-17701200.translation: Sacred to Mars Augustus. Lucius Aemilius Honoratus, son of Lucius, of the Voltinia tribe, a centurion, made this at his own expense in fulfillment of a vow.
EDCS-17701200.summary: A centurion dedicated a monument to Mars Augustus at his own expense, likely in the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-17701204.translation: To Hadrian's son, the Hibbienses [crossed out?] for single [individuals?].
EDCS-17701204.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription potentially related to a dedication or a list of individuals associated with Hadrian, possibly from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-17701209.translation: For the health of the Emperor Caesar. Quintus Martius Felix, son of a god, of Liber Pater.
EDCS-17701209.summary: Quintus Martius Felix made a dedication for the health of the Emperor Caesar, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-17701210.translation: For the health of the Emperor Caesar Pius. Marcus Volussius Donatus, perpetual priest, [dedicated?] the timberwork.
EDCS-17701210.summary: Marcus Volussius Donatus, a perpetual priest, dedicated timberwork for the health of Emperor Caesar Pius, likely during the Antonine period.

EDCS-17701213.summary: A very fragmentary inscription mentioning Constantius, likely a name from the late Roman period.

EDCS-17701218.translation: Luria Posilla, daughter of Caius Victor, pious, aged 20, lies here.
EDCS-17701218.summary: A tombstone inscription for Luria Posilla, who died at the age of 20, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-17701219.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Memmius Ianuarius, pious, lived 36 years, lies here.
EDCS-17701219.summary: A tombstone inscription for Memmius Ianuarius, who died at the age of 36, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-17701220.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Petronia Donata, pious, lived 85 years and 1 month; for her merits, her most benevolent daughter Oppia Celsina made this memorial; may you rest well here.
EDCS-17701220.summary: A tombstone inscription for Petronia Donata, erected by her daughter Oppia Celsina, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-17701221.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Pomponius Arbilensis Rogatus lived 73 years.
EDCS-17701221.summary: A tombstone inscription for Pomponius Arbilensis Rogatus, who died at the age of 73, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-17701222.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Saturninus Felicius, son of Quintus Sisenna, pious, lived 73 years.
EDCS-17701222.summary: A tombstone inscription for Saturninus Felicius, son of Quintus Sisenna, who died at the age of 73, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-17701225.translation: Sacred to Saturn, Augustus. Marcus Afrinius Felix, priest, gladly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-17701225.summary: A private religious dedication to the god Saturn and the emperor Augustus, made by Marcus Afrinius Felix, a priest.

EDCS-17701226.translation: Antonius Victor gladly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-17701226.summary: A private religious vow fulfillment by Antonius Victor.

EDCS-17701228.translation: To our lord, Emperor Valerius Licinianus Licinius Augustus, greatest Sarmaticus, greatest Germanicus, holding tribunician power for the 10th time, consul for the 5th time, imperator for the 10th time, father of the fatherland, proconsul. The colony of Bisica Lucana is devoted to his divine majesty.
EDCS-17701228.summary: An official dedication by the colony of Bisica Lucana to Emperor Licinius, attesting to his titles and power.

EDCS-17701229.translation: Under the unending rule of our lords Honorius and Theodosius, perpetual always Augusti, with Felice Ennodio, most illustrious and most magnificent proconsul of the province of Africa, judging in place of the emperor, with his most illustrious legate Firmus, [repaired] the baths which were so greatly damaged by age and ruin.
EDCS-17701229.summary: A dedication recording the repair of baths in the province of Africa during the joint rule of Emperors Honorius and Theodosius, overseen by the proconsul Felice Ennodio and his legate Firmus.

EDCS-17701230.translation: Probus, who fell in battle against the Numidians, a lover of valor, died in the service. I have inscribed these verses for him, dictated by sorrow, blaming Fortune because she did not arrange such things for me by birth, and dedicated them after our obsequies.
EDCS-17701230.summary: A funerary epigram lamenting the death of Probus in battle, written by a grieving friend who questions fate.

EDCS-17701231.translation: Rubrius Rogatus Belalitanus, priest of Caelestis, lived seventy years.
EDCS-17701231.summary: A tombstone inscription for Rubrius Rogatus Belalitanus, a priest of the goddess Caelestis, stating his name, origin, priesthood, and age at death.

EDCS-17701237.translation: Sacred to the Shades below. Antonius Felix, son of Fronto, pious, lived twenty-four years. He rests here. May your bones rest well; may the earth lie lightly upon you.
EDCS-17701237.summary: A funerary epitaph for Antonius Felix, son of Fronto, recording his piety, age, and standard funerary wishes for repose.

EDCS-17701238.translation: Lucius Pontitius Felix, pious, lived eighty years. He rests here. May your bones rest well; may the earth lie lightly upon you.
EDCS-17701238.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lucius Pontitius Felix, recording his piety, age, and standard funerary wishes for repose.

EDCS-17701239.translation: Sacred to the Shades below. Fortunatus, son of Victor, pious, lived fifty years. He rests here.
EDCS-17701239.summary: A funerary epitaph for Fortunatus, son of Victor, recording his piety, age, and that he rests here.

EDCS-17701240.translation: Sacred to the Shades below. Marcus Hortensius Faustinus, dearest brother, pious, lived sixty years. He rests here. May your bones rest well; may the earth lie lightly upon you.
EDCS-17701240.summary: A funerary epitaph for Marcus Hortensius Faustinus, described as a dearest and pious brother, recording his age and standard funerary wishes for repose.

EDCS-17701241.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Iulia Cornelia lived for 92 years and is buried here.
EDCS-17701241.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Iulia Cornelia at the age of 92.

EDCS-17701242.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Iulia Galla lived for 10 years and is buried here.
EDCS-17701242.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Iulia Galla at the age of 10.

EDCS-17701243.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Iulia Satura, dutiful, lived [here]; may your bones rest well; may the earth lie lightly upon you.
EDCS-17701243.summary: A funerary epitaph for Iulia Satura, including a wish for her peaceful repose.

EDCS-17701244.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Caius Laetorius Marcellus, dutiful, lived for 55 years and 9 months and is buried here; may your bones rest well; may the earth lie lightly upon you.
EDCS-17701244.summary: A funerary epitaph for Caius Laetorius Marcellus, detailing his age at death and a wish for his peaceful rest.

EDCS-17701245.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Caius Lurius Argolicus, son of Vabocuteenus, Messius, dutiful, lived for 4 years and 5 months and is buried here; may your bones rest well. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Caius Lurius Argolicus, Messius, dutiful, lived.
EDCS-17701245.summary: A funerary epitaph for Caius Lurius Argolicus, giving his age at death and also repeated in a slightly different form.

EDCS-17701246.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Luria Quarta, daughter of S., lived for [years] and 5 months and is buried here. To Caius Clodius, his dearest wife.
EDCS-17701246.summary: A funerary epitaph for Luria Quarta, with a dedication from her husband Caius Clodius.

EDCS-17701247.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Lucius Manlius Sergius lived for 30 years and is buried here.
EDCS-17701247.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Lucius Manlius Sergius at the age of 30.

EDCS-17701248.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Caius Memmius Felix lived for 82 years, five months, and seven days and is buried here.
EDCS-17701248.summary: A funerary epitaph detailing the age of Caius Memmius Felix at his death.

EDCS-17701249.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Nuptialis, dutiful, lived for 21 years and is buried here; may your bones rest well; may the earth lie lightly upon you.
EDCS-17701249.summary: A funerary epitaph for Nuptialis, who died at the age of 21, including a wish for his peaceful repose.

EDCS-17701250.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Caius Ovinius Felix Lurianus, dutiful, lived for 4 years and is buried here.
EDCS-17701250.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Caius Ovinius Felix Lurianus at the age of 4.

EDCS-17701251.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Patulcius Primus, dutiful, lived for 85 years. He is buried here. May your bones rest well.
EDCS-17701251.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Patulcius Primus, a man who lived 85 years, with a dedication to the underworld spirits and a wish for his bones to rest well.

EDCS-17701252.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Marcus Potitius Aurelianus, dutiful, lived for 85 years. May your bones rest well.
EDCS-17701252.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Marcus Potitius Aurelianus, a man who lived 85 years, with a dedication to the underworld spirits and a wish for his bones to rest well.

EDCS-17701254.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Quintus Sentius Marcianus, dutiful, lived for 58 years, 1 month, and 2 days. He is buried here. May your bones rest well.
EDCS-17701254.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Quintus Sentius Marcianus, who lived 58 years, 1 month, and 2 days, with a dedication to the underworld spirits and a wish for his bones to rest well.

EDCS-17701255.translation: Turius Gemellus made this for her most dutiful son.
EDCS-17701255.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Turius Gemellus to her son.

EDCS-17701256.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Lucius Valerius Victor Lucanianus lived for 23 years, 3 months, and 25 days.
EDCS-17701256.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Lucius Valerius Victor Lucanianus, who lived 23 years, 3 months, and 25 days, with a dedication to the underworld spirits.

EDCS-17701257.translation: Volussena Castula, dutiful, lived for 50 years. She is buried here. May your bones rest well and may the earth be light upon you.
EDCS-17701257.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Volussena Castula, who lived 50 years, with a dedication to the underworld spirits and wishes for her peaceful rest.

EDCS-17701258.translation: Lived 45 years. S. F. Saïus Nartialus and Ianuarius made this for their son.
EDCS-17701258.summary: This is a funerary dedication by S. F. Saïus Nartialus and Ianuarius for their son, who lived 45 years.

EDCS-17701259.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Coc T. N. ius, sister, [made this?], dutiful, lived for...
EDCS-17701259.summary: This is a fragmented tombstone inscription dedicating to the underworld spirits, mentioning a sister named Coc T. N. ius.

EDCS-17701260.translation: Enatianus Diachonus departed in peace in his 68th year, buried on the day before the Kalends of August.
EDCS-17701260.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Enatianus Diachonus, who died in peace at age 68, with a specific burial date.

EDCS-17701261.translation: Gaudiosa the faithful lived in peace for 23 years.
EDCS-17701261.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Gaudiosa, who lived 23 years and is described as faithful and having lived in peace.

EDCS-17701262.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Ignicia, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-17701263.translation: To the holy three, Maxima, Donatilla, and Secunda, good girls. Stefanus [dedicated this].
EDCS-17701263.summary: This inscription is a dedication to three girls, Maxima, Donatilla, and Secunda, likely by Stefanus, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-17701264.translation: Died in peace on the Ides of April. Brecon Coris [something] Commodus.
EDCS-17701264.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of someone on the Ides of April and mentions a location (Brecon Coris) and a name (Commodus), likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-17701266.translation: To our lords, the Flavians, Valentinian and Valens, pious, happy, victorious, ever-Augusts, the municipality of Mizaeoterenense [dedicated this].
EDCS-17701266.summary: This is a dedication by the municipality of Mizaeoterenense to the emperors Valentinian and Valens, dating to the late 4th century AD.

EDCS-17701268.translation: For the memory of the Atelii: he erected this at his own expense for Chlara, his piously devoted wife, and son, and for Publius Ateius Valerianus, grandson of Marcus.
EDCS-17701268.summary: This funerary monument was erected by an individual for his wife Chlara, son, and grandson Publius Ateius Valerianus, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-17701269.translation: Sacred to Ceres Augusta. Fabius Caecilius Praetextatus, perpetual priest and curator of public affairs, erected [this].
EDCS-17701269.summary: This is a dedication to Ceres Augusta by Fabius Caecilius Praetextatus, who held religious and civic offices, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-17701271.translation: Sacred to Mercury Augustus. Decimus Clodius, son of Torquatus, erected and dedicated this statue, having promised it for 3,000 sesterces, with an additional 5,000 sesterces, in his own name and in the name of his children Felix Torquatus and Honoratus.
EDCS-17701271.summary: This is a dedication of a statue to Mercury Augustus by Decimus Clodius, specifying the costs and his children, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-17701272.translation: To Caesar. Lucius Annius Perpetuus, son of Lucius, of the Quirina tribe, erected and dedicated this statue, which their father Lucius Annius had promised for 2,000 sesterces in his own name and that of his children, with additional funds, in his own name and in the names of his children, his sister Annia, and his brother Iulianus. The site was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-17701272.summary: This inscription records the erection and dedication of a statue to Caesar by Lucius Annius Perpetuus, honoring his family and specifying land allocation by local authorities, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-17701277.translation: Under Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Severus Alexander Pius Felix Augustus, son of the deified Severus Pius, grandson of the deified Severus Pius, pontifex maximus, holding tribunician power for the 8th time, consul for the 3rd time, father of the country; and of [Julia Mammaea] Augusta, mother of the emperors and of the camps and of the senate and of the fatherland, the municipality of Septimium Aurelium Antoninianum [Alexandrianum] Herculeum frugiferum Thignica, devoted to their divine majesty and power, rebuilt the macellum, which had collapsed from age, from the ground with public money and dedicated it.
EDCS-17701277.summary: This inscription records the rebuilding of a market (macellum) in the municipality of Septimium Aurelium Antoninianum by public funds during the reign of Severus Alexander and his mother Julia Mammaea, likely around 224-227 CE.

EDCS-17701278.translation: For the safety(?) of our lords Diocletian and Maximian Augusti and Constantius and Maximian, most noble Caesars. [Name/title?] Caecilianus [title?] performed the taurobolium (?)
EDCS-17701278.summary: This inscription likely records a dedication, possibly a taurobolium (a ritual sacrifice), for the safety of the Tetrarchic emperors (Diocletian, Maximian, Constantius, and Galerius), with the name of the dedicator partially preserved.

EDCS-17701282.translation: To the divine lords, our Emperors Caesar Diocletian and Maximian Augusti, and the most noble Caesars Constantius and Maximian. The public entity of the municipality of Thignica dedicated [this], with Gaius Annius Anullinus serving as proconsul.
EDCS-17701282.summary: This is a dedication by the municipality of Thignica to the emperors Diocletian, Maximian, Constantius, and Maximian, under the proconsul Gaius Annius Anullinus, dating to the Tetrarchy (late 3rd/early 4th century AD).

EDCS-17701288.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. He lived piously for 38 years. He lies here. May your bones rest well. May the earth be light upon you.
EDCS-17701288.summary: This is a funerary epitaph invoking the Di Manes, stating the deceased's age, and offering wishes for a peaceful afterlife, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-17701289.translation: Gaius Calvius Privatus, priest of Jupiter, Sextus Fac...
EDCS-17701289.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription naming a priest of Jupiter, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-17701290.translation: To Gaius Memmius Felix, perpetual flamen of the Augusti of both parts of the community of Thignica, Gaius Memmius Fortunatus, perpetual flamen of the Augusti of both parts of the community of Thignica, placed this because of his exceptional piety and brotherly affection which he shows towards himself and his children.
EDCS-17701290.summary: This is a dedication by Gaius Memmius Fortunatus to Gaius Memmius Felix, likely a prominent civic and religious official in Thignica, set up due to affection and piety, probably from the Imperial period.

EDCS-17701291.translation: To the priest and master of the temples, very pious, he lived 66 years. He is buried here. May your bones rest well. May the earth be light upon you.
EDCS-17701291.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a pious priest and temple master who lived 66 years, likely from the Roman Empire.

EDCS-17701292.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Fausta Servia lived 30 years. She is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits.
EDCS-17701292.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Fausta Servia, who died at the age of 30, likely from the Roman Empire.

EDCS-17701293.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Salierna the pious lived 77 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-17701293.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Salierna, who died at the age of 77, likely from the Roman Empire.

EDCS-17701295.translation: IIRIS I lived 10 years. He is buried here. May your bones rest well. May the earth be light upon you.
EDCS-17701295.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a child named IIRIS I, who died at the age of 10, likely from the Roman Empire.

EDCS-17701296.translation: Sacred to Juno Caelestis Augusta. Modia Victoria, with her family, fulfilled her vow willingly.
EDCS-17701296.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Juno Caelestis Augusta by Modia Victoria, likely from the Roman Empire.

EDCS-17900343.translation: To the Prince of Youth and restorer of public liberty, our lord Flavius Claudius Julianus Pius Felix Augustus, the colony of Tibursicum Bure...
EDCS-17900343.summary: This inscription honors Emperor Julian (Flavius Claudius Julianus) as Prince of Youth and restorer of public liberty, likely erected by the colony of Tibursicum Bure during his reign in the mid-4th century CE.

EDCS-17900345.translation: While our most Christian and invincible Emperors Justin and Sophia Augusti reign, Thomas, the most excellent prefect, has happily built this fortification.
EDCS-17900345.summary: This inscription records the construction of a fortification by Thomas, a prefect, under the reign of Emperors Justin and Sophia, likely dating to the 6th century CE.

EDCS-17900348.text_edition: \n Sexto Cocceio Anicio Fausto Paulino proconsuli provinciae Africae res publica coloniae [][] Augustae \n
EDCS-17900348.translation: The Republic of the colony [ Colonia Augusta?] to Sextus Cocceius Anicius Faustus Paulinus, proconsul of the province of Africa.
EDCS-17900348.summary: This inscription records a dedication by the 'Republic' (i.e., the city government) of Colonia Augusta to Sextus Cocceius Anicius Faustus Paulinus, proconsul of Africa, likely from the 3rd century CE.

EDCS-17900349.translation: To Maevia Agathoclia, wife of Pompeius Faustinus Severianus, the clarissimus vir, consul, the municipium Septimium V...
EDCS-17900349.summary: This is a dedication from the municipium Septimium to Maevia Agathoclia, wife of Pompeius Faustinus Severianus, a man of senatorial rank (clarissimus vir) and consul, likely from the late Roman period.

EDCS-17900350.translation: To Quintus Acilius Fuscus, son of Caius, of the Papirian tribe, an outstanding man, procurator of the annona of our Augusti, procurator of the work of the theatre of Pompey, advocate of the treasury, codicillary official of the hereditates, curator of adjacent properties, priest of the Laurentes Lavinates, to whom the municipality of Severiana Antoniniana granted citizenship and the patronage of Tibur, for his merits as a citizen and patron.
EDCS-17900350.summary: This inscription honors Quintus Acilius Fuscus, detailing his various administrative and financial roles in Ostia and Rome, and his civic honors from Severiana Antoniniana.

EDCS-17900351.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. To Quintus Urvinus Crescentius Livianus, honored with equestrian rank, a noble and most devoted young man, who was dear to his parents.
EDCS-17900351.summary: This is a tomb inscription for Quintus Urvinus Crescentius Livianus, a young man of equestrian rank, dedicated by his parents.

EDCS-17900352.translation: Quintus Cornificius, son of Quintus, of the Arnensian tribe, made this temple and statue from his own funds and dedicated them himself.
EDCS-17900352.summary: This inscription records Quintus Cornificius of the Arnensian tribe funding and dedicating a temple and statue.

EDCS-17900361.summary: This fragment likely refers to Emperor Trajan, possibly part of a dedicatory inscription praising him.

EDCS-17900362.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. To Lucius Abidius Faustus Lucilianus, devoted, who lived 20 years and 20 days, he is buried here.
EDCS-17900362.summary: This is a tomb inscription for Lucius Abidius Faustus Lucilianus, who died at the age of 20 years and 20 days.

EDCS-17900363.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. To Fabius Faustinus, devoted, who lived 75 years, he is buried here.
EDCS-17900363.summary: This is a tomb inscription for Fabius Faustinus, who died at the age of 75.

EDCS-17900364.translation: Zibucis' son Fortunatus, devoted, who lived 30 years, he is buried here.
EDCS-17900364.summary: This is a tomb inscription for Fortunatus, son of Zibucis, who died at the age of 30.

EDCS-17900365.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. To Caius Herculeius Abidianus, devoted, who lived 12 years, he is buried here.
EDCS-17900365.summary: This is a tomb inscription for Caius Herculeius Abidianus, who died at the age of 12.

EDCS-17900366.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. To Caius Herculeius Ianuarius, devoted, who lived 65 years, he is buried here.
EDCS-17900366.summary: This is a tomb inscription for Caius Herculeius Ianuarius, who died at the age of 65.

EDCS-17900367.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. To Marcus Herculeius Ianuarius, devoted, who lived 55 years, he is buried here.
EDCS-17900367.summary: This is a tomb inscription for Marcus Herculeius Ianuarius, who died at the age of 55.

EDCS-17900368.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Caius Herculeius Victor, dutiful, lived 13 years, is buried here.
EDCS-17900368.summary: This is a tombstone recording the death of Caius Herculeius Victor at the age of 13.

EDCS-17900369.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Herculeia Marciana, dutiful, lived 12 years, is buried here.
EDCS-17900369.summary: This is a tombstone recording the death of Herculeia Marciana at the age of 12.

EDCS-17900370.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Quintus Heredius Fortunatus, dutiful, lived 70 years, is buried here.
EDCS-17900370.summary: This is a tombstone recording the death of Quintus Heredius Fortunatus at the age of 70.

EDCS-17900371.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Magnius Felix, dutiful, lived 85 years, is buried here. May the earth lie lightly upon you.
EDCS-17900371.summary: This is a tombstone recording the death of Magnius Felix at the age of 85, with a common epitaph wishing him peace.

EDCS-17900372.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. F. Mellus Ausumilus, dutiful, lived 55 years, is buried here.
EDCS-17900372.summary: This is a tombstone recording the death of F. Mellus Ausumilus at the age of 55.

EDCS-17900373.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Otacilia Sura, dutiful, lived 70 years, is buried here.
EDCS-17900373.summary: This is a tombstone recording the death of Otacilia Sura at the age of 70.

EDCS-17900374.translation: He beautified and completed with every detail the temple, which Titus Palatius Honoratus, in the name of his wife Bonifatia, had undertaken for 20,000 sesterces, with the money multiplied according to his will.
EDCS-17900374.summary: This dedicatory inscription records Titus Palatius Honoratus completing a temple, funded by his wife Bonifatia's inheritance, possibly in the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-17900375.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Marcus Sallustius Celer, dutiful, lived 47 years, is buried here.
EDCS-17900375.summary: This is a tombstone recording the death of Marcus Sallustius Celer at the age of 47.

EDCS-17900376.translation: I, Sallustia Primula, was the first born daughter of Tityrus, given away in marriage to my master Sisennius Atticius Barbarus. I was sold to Sallustius Carosus, whom fate moved to join me to himself in marriage. I kept the spirit, I returned the breath, I held the bones in one tomb.
EDCS-17900376.summary: This epitaph, likely from the 2nd century CE, tells the life story of Sallustia Primula, a slave who was married, bore children, and died, expressing her devotion to her last owner.

EDCS-17900377.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Severina, daughter of Marcus, lived 20 years, is buried here.
EDCS-17900377.summary: This is a tombstone recording the death of Severina, daughter of Marcus, at the age of 20.

EDCS-17900378.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Ticcienia Galla, dutiful, lived 73 years, is buried here.
EDCS-17900378.summary: A funerary epitaph for Ticcienia Galla, dating from antiquity.

EDCS-17900379.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Turrania Ianuaria, dutiful, lived 65 years, is buried here.
EDCS-17900379.summary: A funerary epitaph for Turrania Ianuaria, dating from antiquity.

EDCS-17900380.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Lucius Valerius Valens, dutiful, lived 65 years, is buried here.
EDCS-17900380.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lucius Valerius Valens, dating from antiquity.

EDCS-17900381.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Publius Crepereius Suriacus of Arna, dutiful, lived 40 years.
EDCS-17900381.summary: A funerary epitaph for Publius Crepereius Suriacus of Arna, dating from antiquity.

EDCS-17900382.translation: Sacred to Jupiter Optimus Maximus, Juno Regina, and Minerva, the August ones. For the health of the Emperors Caesars Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus and Lucius Aurelius Verus Augustus, conquerors of Armenia, Media, and Parthia, and of their divine house, Lucius Marcius Simplex and Lucius Marcius Simplex Regillianus made this at their own expense. // Lucius Marcius Simplex and Lucius Marcius Simplex Regillianus made this at their own expense.
EDCS-17900382.summary: This inscription is a dedication of a religious shrine to several gods for the health of Emperors Marcus Aurelius and Lucius Verus, funded by Lucius Marcius Simplex and Lucius Marcius Simplex Regillianus, likely dating to their joint reign (161-169 AD).

EDCS-17900384.text_edition: \n Pietati Augustae sacrum Pompeius Rogatus testamento Cai Pompei Nahani fratris sui ex HS XXX milibus nummum solo suo exstruxit itemque dedicavit curatoribus Marco Morasio Donato Caio Pompeio Cossuto\n
EDCS-17900384.translation: Sacred to Pietas Augusta. Pompeius Rogatus built and dedicated this, as per his will, from his brother Caius Pompeius Nahani's 30,000 sesterces, using his own land, with Marcus Morasius Donatus and Caius Pompeius Cossutus as curators.
EDCS-17900384.summary: This inscription records the construction and dedication of a monument to Pietas Augusta, funded by Pompeius Rogatus in memory of his brother and completed by appointed curators.

EDCS-17900385.translation: Sacred to Caelestis Augusta. Quintus Gabinius Rufus Felix Beatianus increased and cultivated the gifts of his parents, and dedicated them.
EDCS-17900385.summary: An dedication to the goddess Caelestis Augusta by Quintus Gabinius Rufus Felix Beatianus, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-17900389.text_edition: \n Imperatori Tiberio Claudio Caesari Augusto Germanico pontifici maximo tribunicia potestate consuli imperatori II Lucius Iulius Luci filius Cornelia Crassus aedilis ornamentarius tribunus militum legionis XXI rapacis in Germania praefectus fabrum IIvir augur IIvir quinquennalis designatus? patronus pagi dedit Caius Caesetius Cai filius Arnensi perpetuus sacerdos patronus pagi Thuggensis nomine suo et fili et perpetui arcum de sua pecunia faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-17900389.translation: Lucius Iulius Crassus, son of Lucius of the Cornelia tribe, an ornamental aedile, tribune of the soldiers of the XXI Rapax legion in Germany, prefect of engineers, twice duovir, augur, designated quinquennial duovir, and patron of the village, dedicated to Emperor Tiberius Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus, pontifex maximus, with tribunician power, consul for the second time. Caius Caesetius Arnensis, son of Caius of the Arnensi tribe, perpetual priest and patron of the Thugga village, on his own behalf and that of his son and perpetual successors, saw to the construction of this arch at his own expense.
EDCS-17900389.summary: This inscription details a dedication of an arch to Emperor Tiberius Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus by Lucius Iulius Crassus, with Caius Caesetius Arnensis also noted as a patron and priest who oversaw its construction at his own expense, likely from the 1st century AD.

EDCS-17900390.translation: For the Emperor Caesar, Trajan Hadrian Augustus, grandson of the deified Nerva, son of Trajan Dacicus and Parthicus, chief priest, holding tribunician power, consul for the second time, father of his country, by the Thuggaean city, by decree of the decurions, at public expense.
EDCS-17900390.summary: A public dedication by the city of Thugga to Emperor Hadrian, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-17900393.translation: For the safety of the Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pertinax Augustus Arabicus Parthicus Adiabenicus, chief priest, holding tribunician power for the third time, consul for the second time, father of his country, and of Caesar Decimus Clodius Septimius Albinus, and of Julia Domna Augusta, mother of the camps. The work of the temple of Saturn, which Lucius Octavius Victor Roscianus bequeathed fifty thousand sesterces from his highest honorific account towards the completion of that work, and which was paid by his heirs and publicly contributed, the pagus and the city of Thugga, by decree of the decurions, dedicated.
EDCS-17900393.summary: A dedication of the temple of Saturn by the pagus and city of Thugga, funded in part by a bequest from Lucius Octavius Victor Roscianus and dedicated during the reigns of Septimius Severus and Clodius Albinus, likely around 200 CE.

EDCS-17900394.text_edition: \n Pro salute Imperatoris Caesaris divi Septimi Severi Pii Arabici Adiabenici Parthici maximi Britannici maximi filii divi Marci Antonini Germanici Sarmatici nepotis divi Antonini Pii pronepotis divi Hadriani abnepotis divi Traiani Parthici et divi Nervae adnepotis Marci Aureli Antonini Pii Felicis Augusti Parthici maximi Britannici maximi Germanici maximi pontificis maximi tribunicia potestate XVII imperatoris III consulis IIII patris patriae proconsulis et Iuliae Domnae Piae Felicis Augustae matris Augusti et castrorum et senatus et patriae totiusque divinae domus eorum templum Victoriae Augustae domini nostri quod Gabinia Hermiona testamento suo ex |(sestertium) C milibus nummum fieri iussit perfectum et dedicatum est suo testamento die dedicationis et deinde quodannis epulum decurionibus ab heredibus suis dari praecepit item agrum qui appellatur circus ad voluptatem populi rei publicae remisit\n
EDCS-17900394.translation: For the health of Emperor Caesar Septimius Pius Arabicus Adiabenicus Parthicus Maximus Britannicus Maximus, son of the deified Marcus Antoninus Germanicus Sarmaticus, grandson of the deified Antoninus Pius, great-grandson of the deified Hadrian, great-great-grandson of the deified Trajan Parthicus and the deified Nerva, Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus Parthicus Maximus Britannicus Maximus Germanicus Maximus, pontifex maximus, with tribunician power for the 17th time, imperator for the 3rd time, consul for the 4th time, father of the country, proconsul, and of Julia Domna Pia Felix Augusta, mother of the Augusti, of the camp, of the senate, and of the whole fatherland, and of their entire divine house, the temple of Victoria Augusta, our lord, which Gabinia Hermiona ordered to be built by her will from 100,000 sesterces, was completed and dedicated according to her will. On the day of dedication, and thereafter every year, she ordered a feast to be given to the decurions by her heirs. She also remitted the land called Circus to the Republic for the pleasure of the people.
EDCS-17900394.summary: This extensive inscription records the dedication of a temple to Victoria Augusta, along with associated provisions for public enjoyment and distributions, funded by Gabinia Hermiona through her will for the health of Emperor Septimius Severus and his family, likely in the early 3rd century AD.

EDCS-17900397.translation: For the safety of Marcus Aurelius Severus Alexander Pius Felix Augustus, father of his country, chief priest. At the request of the entire populace, Marcus Aebutius Honoratus and Publius Labonius Institor, the duovirs, promised.
EDCS-17900397.summary: A record of a promise made by two duovirs for the safety of Emperor Severus Alexander, likely from the early 3rd century CE.

EDCS-17900398.translation: The colony of Licinia Septimia Aurelia Alexandriana Thuggensis, devoted to the divine majesty of Emperor Caesar Publius Licinius Gallienus Germanicus Pius Felix Augustus, father of the country, pontifex maximus, with tribunician power for the 10th time, imperator for the 10th time, consul for the 2nd time, designated for the 5th time, proconsul, dedicates this.
EDCS-17900398.summary: This inscription records the colony of Thuggensis dedicating itself to the divine majesty of Emperor Gallienus, likely dating to his reign between 253-268 AD.

EDCS-17900401.translation: To our lords, the Augusti Valentinian and Gratian, and Valentinian. During the proconsulship and under the authority of Decimus Hilarianus Hesperius, a most distinguished man, judging with vice-sacred power, the channel, which had fallen into disrepair due to age and was not serving the water channels, to its complete form; also the nymphaeum, which discharged the returned waters for the use of the city, with surrounding porticoes, was begun, completed, and cultivated by Lucius Napotius Felix Antonianus, formerly curator of the public affairs, for the honor of perpetual flamonicatorship, as a favor to his homeland.
EDCS-17900401.summary: A dedication of a restored water channel and nymphaeum by Lucius Napotius Felix Antonianus, likely during the joint reign of Valentinian I, Valens, and Gratian in the late 4th century CE.

EDCS-17900403.translation: For the safety of the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Severus Alexander Pius Felix Augustus, chief priest, holding tribunician power for the third time, consul, father of his country, and of Lucius Septimius Caesar, our Augustus, our father-in-law, and of their entire divine family. Because, at the request of the entire populace, Publius Labonius Publi filius Institor and Marcus Aebutius Honoratus Pacatianus, the aediles, made and dedicated with their own money.
EDCS-17900403.summary: A record of a public work funded and dedicated by the aediles Publius Labonius Institor and Marcus Aebutius Honoratus Pacatianus for the safety of Emperor Severus Alexander and his family, likely from the early 3rd century CE.

EDCS-17900404.translation: For the health of Emperor Caesar Trajan Hadrianus Augustus. Aulus Gabinius Datus, patron of the village and city, and Marcus Gabinius Bassus, perpetual flamen of Augustus, patron of the village and city, built from their own land and at their own expense, from the foundations, the temples of Concordia, Liber Pater, along with other temples and colonnades. They promised 50,000 sesterces for this work and completed it with increased funds, and dedicated it with Fortunatus, Lucius Instanius Fortunatus, and Marcus Vibius Gemellus as curators.
EDCS-17900404.summary: This inscription records the construction and dedication of several temples and porticoes by Aulus Gabinius Datus and Marcus Gabinius Bassus, patrons and a flamen of Augustus, for the health of Emperor Hadrian, funded significantly by their own wealth, likely in the mid-2nd century AD.

EDCS-17900405.translation: To Lucius Marcius Simplex, son of Quintus, of the Arnian tribe, patron of the village and the community, perpetual priest and perpetual priest of the Divine Augustus of the colony of Julia Karthago, aedile, chosen by the Emperor Antoninus Augustus into the board of fifteen for his outstanding munificence, the village and community of Thuggensium, by decree of the decurions and at public expense, with Gaius Modius Rusticus, Lucius Numissius Honoratus, and Lucius Julianus Sallustius, son of Quintus, as curators.
EDCS-17900405.summary: This inscription records a dedication by the community of Thuggensium to Lucius Marcius Simplex, honoring his munificence and public service, likely in the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-17900406.translation: The people of Thuggenses to Asicia Victoria, flaminica. For her munificence and singular generosity to the public affairs, for which she promised 100,000 sesterces for the priesthood of her daughter Vibia Asician(a), from whose income theatrical games and gifts to the decurions were to be provided. The decurions of both orders erected this.
EDCS-17900406.summary: This inscription honors Asicia Victoria, a flaminica, for her generous donation to the public which funded games and gifts for the decurions, likely in the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-17900408.translation: Quintus Pacuvius Saturus, perpetual priest and augur of the colony of Julia Karthago, and his wife Nahania Victoria, perpetual priestess, made this at their own expense.
EDCS-17900408.summary: This is a dedication for a structure or monument made by Quintus Pacuvius Saturus and his wife Nahania Victoria, who held priestly offices in the colony of Julia Karthago.

EDCS-17900412.text_edition: \n Quintus Pacuvius Saturus flamen perpetuus augur coloniae Iuliae Karthaginis et Nahania Victoria uxor eius flaminica perpetua opus templi Mercuri quot sic Marcus Pacuvius Felix Victorianus filius eorum codicillis suis ex HS L milibus fieri iussit amplius ipsi ob honorem flamonii perpetui ex HS LXX milibus pollicitis summis templum Mercuri et cellas duas cum statuis et porticibus et ornamentis omnibusae exstruxerunt et excoluerunt item civitati Thuggae HS XXV milia Quintus Pacuvius Saturus flamen perpetuus daturum se pollicitus est ex cuius summae reditu quotannis decurionibus sportulae darentur et ob diem dedicationis ludos scaenicos et sportulas decurionibus utriusque ordinis et universo populo dedit\n
EDCS-17900412.translation: Quintus Pacuvius Saturus, perpetual flamen and augur of the colony of Iulia Karthago, and Nahania Victoria, his wife, perpetual flaminica, ordered the work of the temple of Mercury to be carried out by their son Marcus Pacuvius Felix Victorianus in his codicils from 50,000 sesterces. Furthermore, for the honor of his perpetual priesthood, he promised an additional 70,000 sesterces, constructed and embellished the temple of Mercury with two chapels, statues, porticoes, and all ornaments. Quintus Pacuvius Saturus, perpetual flamen, also promised to give 25,000 sesterces to the city of Thugga, from the income of which gifts were to be provided annually to the decurions. On the day of dedication, he gave theatrical games and gifts to the decurions of both orders and to the entire populace.
EDCS-17900412.summary: This inscription details a substantial construction project for the temple of Mercury and related amenities, funded by Quintus Pacuvius Saturus and his family, with significant public distributions and games, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-17900413.translation: Sacred to Caelestis Augusta. Quintus Gabinius Rufus Felix Beatianus multiplied and improved the benefactions of his parents and dedicated them.
EDCS-17900413.summary: This inscription records Quintus Gabinius Rufus Felix Beatianus dedicating improved benefactions originating from his parents to the goddess Caelestis Augusta.

EDCS-17900414.translation: For the health of Emperor Caesar Publius Licinius Egnatius Gallienus Germanicus Pius Felix Augustus, pontifex maximus, conqueror of Germany, with tribunician power for the 10th time, consul for the 4th time, father of the country, proconsul, and of Cornelia Salonina Augusta, and of their entire divine house. Botria Fortunata, daughter of Victor, perpetual flaminica, built and embellished the temple of Tellus from her own funds from the ground up, in honor of her high priestly office, and dedicated it, providing gifts to the decurions and a feast to the entire populace.
EDCS-17900414.summary: This inscription records the construction and dedication of a temple to Tellus by Botria Fortunata, a perpetual flaminica, funded by her own wealth and dedicated to the imperial family, likely during the reign of Gallienus (253-268 AD).

EDCS-17900416.translation: Sacred to the shades below. Dolabellius Felix, son of Candidus, pious, lived 43 years, is buried here.
EDCS-17900416.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the death and burial of Dolabellius Felix, providing his age and indicating his piety.

EDCS-17900418.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the departed. Maodius Veniteriani, a dutiful son, lived for [M] months. May he rest here; he is buried here.
EDCS-17900418.summary: This is a tomb inscription for Maodius Veniteriani, noting his lifespan in months and his burial place.

EDCS-17900419.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Volceia Victoria lived 65 years, she lies here. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Quintus Cornelius Solutor, a pious man, lived 33 years, he lies here. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Botuvia Victoria pious lived [years]
EDCS-17900419.summary: This inscription is a funerary monument recording the lives of at least three individuals, Volceia Victoria, Quintus Cornelius Solutor, and Botuvia Victoria.

EDCS-17900422.translation: For the honor of his perpetual priesthood and Ummidius Caelestinus.
EDCS-17900422.summary: This fragmentary inscription appears to be a dedication or commemoration related to a perpetual priesthood and mentions Ummidius Caelestinus.

EDCS-17900425.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the departed. Arrinia Victoria, a woman of great character, whose ways cannot be emulated, is buried here. But you are in spirit, and surely you are in mind, because you will never leave mine. I, Marcus Motasius, declare: this tomb which is yours shall be the same for me. She lived piously for 35 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-17900425.summary: This is a tomb inscription for Arrinia Victoria, expressing deep affection and loss by her husband Marcus Motasius, who states she lived 35 years.

EDCS-17900426.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the departed. Quintus Arsacius Quadratus, dutiful, lived for 99 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-17900426.summary: This is a tomb inscription for Quintus Arsacius Quadratus, stating he lived 99 years and is buried here.

EDCS-17900427.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the departed. Cassia Victoria, daughter of Honoratus, dutiful, lived for 62 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-17900427.summary: This is a tomb inscription for Cassia Victoria, daughter of Honoratus, stating she lived 62 years and is buried here.

EDCS-17900428.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the departed. Caecilia Fortunata, dutiful, lived for 82 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-17900428.summary: This is a tomb inscription for Caecilia Fortunata, stating she lived 82 years and is buried here.

EDCS-17900429.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the departed. Flavianus lived for [X] years. He is buried here.
EDCS-17900429.summary: This is a tomb inscription for Flavianus, indicating his burial place but with a missing lifespan.

EDCS-17900430.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Macer, son of Imilco Abdismunis, dutiful, lived 80 years, is buried here.
EDCS-17900430.summary: A funerary inscription for Macer, son of Imilco Abdismunis, who lived 80 years.

EDCS-17900431.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Magnianus Iulius, dutiful, lived 12 years, is buried here.
EDCS-17900431.summary: A funerary inscription for Magnianus Iulius, who lived 12 years.

EDCS-17900432.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Marcus Iunius Iustus, dutiful, lived 25 years, is buried here.
EDCS-17900432.summary: A funerary inscription for Marcus Iunius Iustus, who lived 25 years.

EDCS-17900433.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Q. Morassina Felicia, dutiful, lived 30 years. BAISAM.
EDCS-17900433.summary: A funerary inscription for Q. Morassina Felicia, who lived 30 years.

EDCS-17900434.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Quintus Morasius Felicianus Annianus, dutiful son, lived 50 years, is buried here. His wife Euvodii made this for her most loving husband.
EDCS-17900434.summary: A funerary inscription for Quintus Morasius Felicianus Annianus, who lived 50 years, set up by his wife.

EDCS-17900435.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Paccia Tertia, dutiful, lived 19 years, is buried here.
EDCS-17900435.summary: A funerary inscription for Paccia Tertia, who lived 19 years.

EDCS-17900436.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Caius Valasenius Successus, dutiful, lived 70 years, is buried here.
EDCS-17900436.summary: A funerary inscription for Caius Valasenius Successus, who lived 70 years.

EDCS-17900437.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Decimus Valerius Fortunatianus, dutiful, lived 15 years, is buried here.
EDCS-17900437.summary: A funerary inscription for Decimus Valerius Fortunatianus, who lived 15 years.

EDCS-17900438.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Viia Victoria, lived 84 years, is buried here.
EDCS-17900438.summary: A funerary inscription for Viia Victoria, who lived 84 years.

EDCS-17900439.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Cipotenus Honoratus, perpetual flamen, dutiful, lived 60 years, is buried here.
EDCS-17900439.summary: A funerary inscription for Cipotenus Honoratus, a perpetual flamen, who lived 60 years.

EDCS-17900440.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Lucius Marcidius Surus, son of Lucius, of the Arnensian tribe, a dutiful man, lived 91 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-17900440.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Marcidius Surus, stating his age and burial place.

EDCS-17900441.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Marcidia Restituta, a dutiful woman, lived 26 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-17900441.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcidia Restituta, stating her age and burial place.

EDCS-17900442.text_edition: \n Fortunae Augustae sacrum Imperatori Caesari Marco Aurelio Antonino Augusto Armeniaco et Imperatori Caesari Lucio Aurelio Vero Augusto Armeniaco templum quod Caius Iulius Cai filius Cornelia Galba |(centurio) legionis XXII Primigeniae hastatus ex HS XXX milibus nummum testamento suo fieri iussit Lucius Iulius Luci filius Cornelia Rogatus Kappianus frater patruelis et heres eius adiectis ob honorem flamonii perpetui sui HS X milibus nummum et amplius quae professus est HS XXX milibus nummum cum fratribus Potito Natale Honorata faciendum curavit Lucius Iulius Titisenus Rogatus Kappianus filius sororis et heres eius consummavit et cum Aulo Titiseno Honorato Kappiano filio suo dedicavit et ob dedicationem triduo ludos decurionibus sportulas populo epulum et gymnasium dedit\n
EDCS-17900442.translation: Sacred to Fortuna Augusta. Caius Iulius Galba, son of Caius, a centurion of the 22nd Legion Primigenia, ordered a temple to be built in his will for 30,000 sesterces. Lucius Iulius Rogatus Kappianus, son of Lucius, of the Cornelia tribe, his cousin and heir, added 10,000 sesterces for the honor of his perpetual priesthood, and more than 30,000 sesterces which he declared, supervised its construction with his brothers Potitus, Natale, and Honorata. Lucius Iulius Titisenus Rogatus Kappianus, son of his sister and his heir, completed it and dedicated it with Aulus Titisenus Honoratus Kappianus, his son. For the dedication, he gave games for three days, gifts to the decurions, a feast for the people, and a gymnasium.
EDCS-17900442.summary: This inscription records the construction and dedication of a temple to Fortuna Augusta, financed and overseen by multiple family members including Lucius Iulius Rogatus Kappianus and his son Lucius Iulius Titisenus Rogatus Kappianus, honoring the emperors Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus Armeniacus and Lucius Aurelius Verus Augustus Armeniacus.

EDCS-17900443.translation: Sacred to Juno Augusta, and the front wall. Lucius Iulius Rufinus, Ba[---], Marcus Iulius Florus, son of Lucius, Cornelia [---]icio, Marcus Senius [---] Nonius Maximus, [---]ndidus, [---]catus, [---] R C T D.
EDCS-17900443.summary: This inscription appears to be a dedication to Juno Augusta, possibly related to the construction or repair of a building, with multiple dedicants.

EDCS-17900444.translation: To the deified Publius Helvius Pertinax. Caius Iulius Crescentianus Instanianus, son of Caius, of the Cornelia tribe, admitted to the public equestrian order and to the quinque decuriae, perpetual priest, [---] in the aerarium, with the highest legal entitlement.
EDCS-17900444.summary: This is a dedication to the deified emperor Pertinax by Caius Iulius Crescentianus Instanianus, a prominent figure holding multiple official and religious positions.

EDCS-17900447.translation: To the most invincible and most fortunate Emperor Augustus Caesar, pacifier of the world, by decree of the decurions of the Musticenses.
EDCS-17900447.summary: This is a dedicatory inscription honoring an unnamed Emperor Augustus Caesar, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE, by the local council (decurions) of Musticenses.

EDCS-17900450.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Caius Licinius Ingenus, a soldier of the 13th Urban Cohort, in the century of Tavis, a dutiful man, lived 25 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-17900450.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Caius Licinius Ingenus, a soldier, stating his age and burial place.

EDCS-17900455.translation: ITV [---]. [---] pia lived 9 years; she is buried here. Sacred to the Divine Manes. Iovius Honoratus, having fulfilled all offices, a dutiful man, lived 70 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-17900455.summary: This inscription contains two funerary epitaphs, one for a young girl named ITV and another for Iovius Honoratus, who held public offices.

EDCS-17900456.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Caius Aemilius Lania, a dutiful man, lived 25 years; he is buried here. Alchides, the new one.
EDCS-17900456.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Caius Aemilius Lania, stating his age and burial place, with an additional note about 'Alchides'.

EDCS-17900457.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Baburia Quartinula, daughter of Marcus, a most dutiful mother, lived 52 years and 2 months; she is buried here. Sacred to the Divine Manes. Baburius Quartinus, son of Marcus, of the Cornelia tribe, a dutiful man, lived 75 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-17900457.summary: This inscription contains two funerary epitaphs for members of the Baburia family, a mother and son, detailing their ages and burial.

EDCS-17900458.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Publius Cornelius Vitalis, son of Quintus, of the Cornelia tribe, lived 31 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-17900458.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Publius Cornelius Vitalis, stating his age and burial place.

EDCS-17900459.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Quintus Cossutius, son of Lucius, of the Cornelia tribe.
EDCS-17900459.summary: This is the beginning of a funerary epitaph for Quintus Cossutius, son of Lucius, of the Cornelia tribe, likely incomplete.

EDCS-17900460.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Lucius D. Victorianus, dutiful, lived 27 years. She lies here. Dutiful, he lived 23 years. He lies here.
EDCS-17900460.summary: This inscription records the burial of two individuals, Lucius D. Victorianus and another person, with their ages at death.

EDCS-17900461.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Quintus Egnatius, son of Marcus, and Cornelia Simplicius, dutiful, lived 35 years and 5 months. She lies here.
EDCS-17900461.summary: This inscription records the burial of Quintus Egnatius and Cornelia Simplicius, with their ages and the duration of their lives.

EDCS-17900462.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Fulvia, daughter of Caius, Bonifatia, dutiful, lived 45 years. She lies here.
EDCS-17900462.summary: This inscription records the burial of Fulvia Bonifatia, daughter of Caius, with her age at death.

EDCS-17900463.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Caius Iulius Fructosus, dutiful, lived 25 years. He lies here. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Caius Iulius Primus Egassius, dutiful, lived 43 years. He lies here.
EDCS-17900463.summary: This inscription records the burial of two individuals named Caius Iulius, Fructosus and Primus Egassius, with their ages at death.

EDCS-17900464.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Caius Iulius Strato Sabinianus, dutiful, lived 80 years. He lies here. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Cornelia Fructa, daughter of Lucius, dutiful, lived 51 years. She lies here.
EDCS-17900464.summary: This inscription records the burial of two individuals, Caius Iulius Strato Sabinianus and Cornelia Fructa, with their ages at death.

EDCS-17900465.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Iulia Concordia, daughter of Publius, dutiful, lived 21 years.
EDCS-17900465.summary: This inscription records the burial of Iulia Concordia, daughter of Publius, with her age at death.

EDCS-17900466.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Iunius Saturus, dutiful, lived 45 years. He lies here. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. [He] lies here.
EDCS-17900466.summary: This inscription records the burial of Iunius Saturus, with his age at death, and a partial record of another burial.

EDCS-17900467.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Caius Liburnius Felix and Cornelia Mustitanus, dutiful, lived 32 years, 5 months, and 5 days. He lies here.
EDCS-17900467.summary: This inscription records the burial of Caius Liburnius Felix and Cornelia Mustitanus, with their precise ages at death.

EDCS-17900468.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Licinia Bonifatia, dutiful, lived 46 years. She lies here. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Caius Fulvius Felix, son of Caius, dutiful, lived 65 years. She lies here.
EDCS-17900468.summary: This inscription records the burial of two individuals, Licinia Bonifatia and Caius Fulvius Felix, with their ages at death.

EDCS-17900469.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Melin Fortunata, dutiful, lived 47 years and 3 months. She lies here. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. P. Defundanianus, dutiful, lived 61 years. He lies here.
EDCS-17900469.summary: This inscription records the burial of two individuals, Melin Fortunata and P. Defundanianus, with their ages at death.

EDCS-17900470.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Cai's daughter Namphamina, dutiful, lived 57 years, is buried here. Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Titus Nonius Datus Albanus, dutiful, lived 84 years, is buried here.
EDCS-17900470.summary: This is a funerary monument recording the burial of two individuals, Titus Nonius Datus Albanus and Namphamina.

EDCS-17900471.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Nonia Zabulla, daughter of Lucius, dutiful, lived 90 years, is buried here.
EDCS-17900471.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Nonia Zabulla.

EDCS-17900472.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Octavia Honorata, dutiful, lived 35 years, is buried here. Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Gaius Ovius Saturninus, dutiful, lived 80 years, is buried here.
EDCS-17900472.summary: This funerary monument records the burial of two individuals, Gaius Ovius Saturninus and Octavia Honorata.

EDCS-17900473.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Lucius Ostilius Rusticianus, dutiful, lived 31 years, is buried here.
EDCS-17900473.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Lucius Ostilius Rusticianus.

EDCS-17900474.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Gaius Paccius, son of Caius, from the Cornelia tribe, Tamurianus, dutiful, lived 40 years, is buried here. Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Quintilia Iusta, daughter of Marcus, dutiful, lived 49 years, is buried here.
EDCS-17900474.summary: This funerary monument records the burial of two individuals, Gaius Paccius and Quintilia Iusta.

EDCS-17900475.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Silicia Fortunata, dutiful, lived 47 years, is buried here. Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Lucius Petreius, son of Lucius, from the Cornelia tribe, Octavianus, dutiful, lived 85 years, is buried here. Heracli.
EDCS-17900475.summary: This funerary monument records the burial of two individuals, Lucius Petreius and Silicia Fortunata, with a possible additional name or reference to Heraclius.

EDCS-17900476.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Tertia, dutiful, lived 20 years, is buried here. Lived 70 years, is buried here.
EDCS-17900476.summary: This funerary inscription appears to record two different individuals named Tertia, one who lived 20 years and another who lived 70 years.

EDCS-17900477.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Aulus Valerius Agilis, dutiful, lived 103 years, is buried here.
EDCS-17900477.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Aulus Valerius Agilis.

EDCS-17900478.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Lucius Valerius Rogatianus Areugi, dutiful, lived 22 years, is buried here. Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. CAI [---], lived 80 years, is buried here.
EDCS-17900478.summary: This funerary monument records the burial of Lucius Valerius Rogatianus Areugi and another individual identified as CAI, whose full details are lost.

EDCS-17900479.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Lucius Vetius Aticus, dutiful, lived 19 years, is buried here.
EDCS-17900479.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Lucius Vetius Aticus.

EDCS-17900480.translation: Pious Umbria Rogata lived 87 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-17900480.summary: A tombstone inscription recording the lifespan and burial of Umbria Rogata.

EDCS-17900481.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Marcus Cornelius Rufus lived 55 years and...
EDCS-17900481.summary: A tombstone inscription fragment recording the lifespan of Marcus Cornelius Rufus, dedicated to the Manes.

EDCS-17900482.translation: The elders of the fort established and gave this to the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Augustus Felix, conqueror of Parthia, conqueror of Britain, conqueror of Germany, chief priest, with tribunician power for the 16th time, general for the second time, consul for the fourth time, father of the country, proconsul, and to the best and greatest prince.
EDCS-17900482.summary: An inscription dedicated by the elders of a fort to Emperor Marcus Aurelius, detailing his numerous titles and honors.

EDCS-17900483.translation: The elders of the fort established and dedicated this to Julia Augusta Pia Felix, mother of the emperor, of the camps, of the Senate, and of the fatherland.
EDCS-17900483.summary: An inscription dedicated by the elders of a fort to Julia Augusta Pia Felix, honoring her titles related to the emperor and the state.

EDCS-17900485.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Cameria Namphame lived 82 years; she is buried here. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Caius Iulius Namphamo lived 15 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-17900485.summary: A double tombstone inscription recording the lifespans and burials of Cameria Namphame and Caius Iulius Namphamo.

EDCS-17900486.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Quintus Munatius BARIII lived 35 years I I
EDCS-17900486.summary: A tombstone inscription fragment recording the lifespan of Quintus Munatius, dedicated to the Manes.

EDCS-17900487.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Pacius Rogatianus lived 20 years.
EDCS-17900487.summary: A tombstone inscription recording the lifespan of Pacius Rogatianus, dedicated to the Manes.

EDCS-17900488.translation: Lucius Quintius Rogatus, son of Publius, of the Quirina tribe, pious, lived 65 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-17900488.summary: A tombstone inscription recording the lifespan and burial of Lucius Quintius Rogatus.

EDCS-17900490.translation: Sacred to Augusta Ceres. Valeria Saturnina, the senior priestess and flaminica, erected this.
EDCS-17900490.summary: A religious dedication to Augusta Ceres, erected by Valeria Saturnina, a priestess.

EDCS-18300004.translation: Sacred to Hercules. Marcus Tuticius Proculus, procurator of the emperor, made this at his own expense.
EDCS-18300004.summary: A religious dedication to Hercules, funded by Marcus Tuticius Proculus, an imperial procurator.

EDCS-18300005.translation: To the honor and valor of the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Carus, son of Publius, the Invincible.
EDCS-18300005.summary: This is a dedication to Emperor Carus, likely honoring his virtues, possibly on a public monument.

EDCS-18300006.translation: Sacred to Jupiter. Gaius Cassius Macer, procurator of the Emperor, made this at his own expense.
EDCS-18300006.summary: A dedication to Jupiter by Gaius Cassius Macer, a procurator, funded by himself.

EDCS-18300007.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, Protector of our most holy princes, our lords the Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus Arabicus Adiabenicus Parthicus Maximus, most brave, most fortunate, chief priest, in his sixteenth year of tribunician power, hailed Imperator twelve times, consul three times, father of his country; and of the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Augustus Parthicus, in his eleventh year of tribunician power, hailed Imperator twice, consul three times, father of his country; and of Julia Augusta, mother of the emperor and of the camps, on account of their preservation, after conspiracies of public enemies were discovered, by decree of the decurions, at public expense.
EDCS-18300007.summary: A grand dedication to Emperors Septimius Severus and Caracalla, and Julia Domna, for their safety, funded by public money and ordered by local officials.

EDCS-18300008.translation: Sacred to the New Gate. Quintus Junius Terminianus made this from a vision.
EDCS-18300008.summary: A dedication to the 'New Gate' by Quintus Junius Terminianus, who claims to have been inspired by a divine vision.

EDCS-18300010.translation: To the Emperor Caesar, grandson of the deified Septimius Severus, son of the deified Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius.
EDCS-18300010.summary: An inscription honoring Emperor Severus Alexander, tracing his lineage to his deified predecessors.

EDCS-18300012.translation: To our lady Flavia Helena Augusta. Marcus Valerius Gypasius, most distinguished man, curator of the state and duovir, devoted to her divine majesty.
EDCS-18300012.summary: A dedication to Flavia Helena Augusta by Marcus Valerius Gypasius, an official of the city.

EDCS-18300015.translation: To our lord the Emperor Caesar Flavius Valentinianus Pius Felix Victor, always Augustus. Aemilius Iulius Cassius Donatus, priest, curator of the state, and the council of Siccensium, devoted to his divine majesty.
EDCS-18300015.summary: A dedication to Emperor Valentinian III by a local priest and the town council of Siccensium, expressing devotion.

EDCS-18300017.translation: To the seventh consul, sixth consul, and quinquennial aedile ON Rufus, his grandfather.
EDCS-18300017.summary: An inscription honoring a public official named Rufus who held multiple magistracies, dedicated by his grandfather.

EDCS-18300018.text_edition: \n Marco Flavio Marci filio Sabarro Vettio Severo clarissimo viro proconsuli provinciae Africae decreto decurionum pecunia publica\n
EDCS-18300018.translation: To Marcus Flavius Vettius Severus, son of Marcus, of the Sabarra family, a most distinguished man, proconsul of the province of Africa, by decree of the decurions, with public funds.
EDCS-18300018.summary: This inscription honors Marcus Flavius Vettius Severus, proconsul of Africa, with a dedication by the decurions using public funds.

EDCS-18300020.translation: To Publius Licinius Marcus son, of the Quirina tribe, Papirianus, procurator of the Emperors Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus, Germanicus, Sarmaticus, Maximus, father of his country, and of the deified Verus, in charge of accounts, to whom the most distinguished council of the Siccensians, because of his merits and care for my municipalities of Cirta and Siccensium, my dearest fellow citizens, I wish to give 1,300,000 sesterces; I entrust this sum to your fidelity, my dearest fellow citizens, so that from the interest, at the rate of five percent annually, 300 boys and 200 girls may be supported, boys from three years of age to fifteen, and each boy shall receive two and a half denarii per month; girls from three years of age to thirteen, and two denarii; the colonists must also be enrolled, indeed only colonists who reside within the buildings of our colony; and if it seems best to you, it must be attended to by the duovirs each year, and it is necessary that for an adult or deceased person, another be immediately substituted, so that the full number may always be supported.
EDCS-18300020.summary: A complex endowment by Publius Licinius Papirianus, a procurator, to fund the support of orphaned children in the municipalities of Cirta and Siccensium, with detailed instructions for management and substitution.

EDCS-18300021.translation: Lucius Annius Fidelis, son of Lucius, of the Quirina tribe, a soldier of the Third Augustan Legion Vindex, served for 20 years, lived for 20 years, is buried here.
EDCS-18300021.summary: A soldier's tombstone, Lucius Annius Fidelis, detailing his military service and lifespan.

EDCS-18300022.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. To Iulius Castus Armorianus, Roman knight, Cubernius, who lived 17 years. Iulius Fortunatus Armorianus Cubernius and Homulia Saturnina, parents, gave the place, granted by his parent, Iulius Ianuarius.
EDCS-18300022.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Iulius Castus Armorianus, a Roman knight, and dedicates his burial place.

EDCS-18300023.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Sextus Laelius Honoratus Terminianus, son of Honoratus, of the Quirina tribe, who lived 65 years, an honored man, is buried here.
EDCS-18300023.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Sextus Laelius Honoratus Terminianus, an honored man, and his age at death.

EDCS-18300024.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Glucus, soldier of the VIII Augusta legion, who lived 41 years, is buried here.
EDCS-18300024.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Glucus, a soldier of the VIII Augusta legion, and his age at death.

EDCS-18300025.translation: To Quintus Octavius Rufus Erucianus, Roman knight, perpetual priest, an excellent man, father of Quintus Octavius Fortunatus Erucianus Stellae Stratoniani, a most distinguished youth. Lucius Sallustius Saturninus, having fulfilled all honors, a just man, because of his outstanding goodness towards all, by which he is eternally preserved.
EDCS-18300025.summary: This honorary inscription honors Quintus Octavius Rufus Erucianus, a Roman knight and priest, for his character and virtue, erected by Lucius Sallustius Saturninus.

EDCS-18300026.translation: To Victor, legionary centurion, formerly a Roman knight, for his generosity, the town council of Siccensium, a fellow citizen and colleague, by decree of the decurions, from public funds.
EDCS-18300026.summary: This inscription records a public dedication by the town council of Siccensium to Victor, a former Roman knight and centurion, in recognition of his generosity.

EDCS-18300027.translation: To Quintus Cassius Capito, son of Quintus, of the Quirina tribe, quaestor, prefect for administering justice. For the colonists of the colony Iulia Cirta Nova, because he alleviated the grain supply from his own funds, Aemilia Cerealis, daughter of Lucius, his great-niece, transferred this statue by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-18300027.summary: This inscription honors Quintus Cassius Capito, a former official, for subsidizing grain for the colonists of Cirta Nova, with a statue erected by his great-niece Aemilia Cerealis.

EDCS-18300028.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Quintus Valerius Hilarianus, son of Quintus, of the Quirina tribe, a pious priest, lived 18 years, 3 months, and 13 days, is buried here. Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Quintus Valerius Severus Platiensis, priest of the Great Mother, a pious man, lived 55 years, is buried here.
EDCS-18300028.summary: This inscription contains two funerary notices for Quintus Valerius Hilarianus and Quintus Valerius Severus Platiensis, detailing their ages and piety.

EDCS-18300029.translation: Vindemania, priestess, lived 75 years, is buried here.
EDCS-18300029.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Vindemania, a priestess, and her age at death.

EDCS-18300030.translation: The town council of the Cirtensians and Siccensians [honors] their patron, a man of the highest integrity and justice, a man of unique excellence, the curator of the state, for his deference towards the entire order and all the people.
EDCS-18300030.summary: This inscription is a dedication by the town councils of Cirtensium and Siccensium to their patron, praising his integrity and service as curator rei publicae.

EDCS-18300031.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription honoring a distinguished man.

EDCS-18300034.translation: Lucius Aedinius Saturninus, son of Lucius, of the Quirina tribe, lived 83 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-18300034.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Aedinius Saturninus, dating from the Roman period.

EDCS-18300035.translation: Aeliseus, son of Cornelius, erected a temple in the year 126, on the 9th day of March.
EDCS-18300035.summary: This is a dedication inscription for a temple, likely erected by Aeliseus, dated to 126 (year unspecified, likely AUC or a local era).

EDCS-18300036.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Statia Sabina, the dutiful, lived 79 years; she is buried here. Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Caius Aemilius Atho, the dutiful, lived 85 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-18300036.summary: This is a double funerary inscription for Statia Sabina and Caius Aemilius Atho, dating from the Roman period.

EDCS-18300037.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Aemilius Donatus lived 30 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-18300037.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Aemilius Donatus, dating from the Roman period.

EDCS-18300038.translation: Lucius Aemilius Optatus, son of Lucius, of the Quirina tribe, lived 25 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-18300038.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Aemilius Optatus, dating from the Roman period.

EDCS-18300039.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Caius Aemilius Polittio, son of Publius, the dutiful, lived [X] years; he is buried here.
EDCS-18300039.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Caius Aemilius Polittio, dating from the Roman period, with a lacuna for his age.

EDCS-18300040.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Aemilia, wife of Archiptolemus, lived 51 years; she is buried here. Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Caius Aemilius Fuscinus lived 55 years.
EDCS-18300040.summary: This is a double funerary inscription for Aemilia and Caius Aemilius Fuscinus, dating from the Roman period.

EDCS-18300041.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. II B duovir [Name illegible] lived 23 years; he is buried here. Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Aemilia Berechi, the dutiful grandmother, lived 81 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-18300041.summary: This is a double funerary inscription, one for a duovir and another for Aemilia Berechi, dating from the Roman period.

EDCS-18300042.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Statius Lupercus lived 43 years; he is buried here. Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Agrius Ianuarianus, a most holy youth, lived 18 years; he is buried here.
