EDCS-18300042.summary: This is a double funerary inscription for Statius Lupercus and Agrius Ianuarianus, dating from the Roman period.

EDCS-18300043.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Lucius Annius Rufus Maximianus lived 23 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-18300043.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Annius Rufus Maximianus, dating from the Roman period.

EDCS-18300044.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Annia Saturnina, devoted daughter of Sextus, lived 65 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-18300044.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Annia Saturnina, recording her age at death and burial.

EDCS-18300045.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Antistia Zosime, devoted daughter of Lucius, lived 70 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-18300045.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Antistia Zosime, recording her age at death and burial.

EDCS-18300046.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Decimus Antonius Baebianus lived 18 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-18300046.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Decimus Antonius Baebianus, recording his age at death and burial.

EDCS-18300047.translation: To Gaius Antonius Quirinus, son of Chuinis, lived 83 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-18300047.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Gaius Antonius Quirinus, recording his age at death and burial.

EDCS-18300048.translation: Quirina, devoted daughter of Gaius Antonius and Flaminalis, lived 50 years.
EDCS-18300048.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Quirina, daughter of Gaius Antonius and Flaminalis, recording her age at death.

EDCS-18300049.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Quintus Antonius Fortunatus Florianus, devoted, lived 30 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-18300049.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Quintus Antonius Fortunatus Florianus, recording his age at death and burial.

EDCS-18300051.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Gaius Antonius Taratara, devoted, lived 18 years.
EDCS-18300051.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Gaius Antonius Taratara, recording his age at death.

EDCS-18300052.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Quintus Antonius Victor, devoted, lived 53 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-18300052.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Quintus Antonius Victor, recording his age at death and burial.

EDCS-18300053.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Appia Galla, devoted daughter of Lupus, lived 12 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-18300053.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Appia Galla, recording her age at death and burial.

EDCS-18300054.translation: To Aquilta Salvianilla, devoted daughter of Sextus, [---] daughter of Iavillius, [---] of the tribe Quirina, daughter of [---] Pomp[---], [---] Avinius [---] Draonir [---] Parvi [---].
EDCS-18300054.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary epitaph for Aquilta Salvianilla, daughter of Sextus, recording her parentage and tribal affiliation, with significant lacunae.

EDCS-18300055.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Quintus Arrius Surus, dutiful, lived 75 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-18300055.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the death and burial of Quintus Arrius Surus.

EDCS-18300056.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Aselia Fabia.

EDCS-18300057.translation: Publilia, daughter of Publius, wife of Asellia, lived 30 years.
EDCS-18300057.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Publilia, daughter of Publius.

EDCS-18300058.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Avatia Victoria, who was also called Monna, lived 20 years.
EDCS-18300058.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the death of Avatia Victoria, who was also known as Monna.

EDCS-18300059.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Aviania Matidia, dutiful, lived 50 years; she is buried here. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Titus Avianius Hilarianus lived 13 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-18300059.summary: This is a double funerary epitaph recording the deaths and burials of Aviania Matidia and Titus Avianius Hilarianus.

EDCS-18300060.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Titus Avianius Messor, son, lived 21 years and 6 months; he is buried here.
EDCS-18300060.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the death and burial of Titus Avianius Messor, son.

EDCS-18300061.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. For Fabia Romula, daughter of Quintus, lived 30 years.
EDCS-18300061.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Fabia Romula, daughter of Quintus.

EDCS-18300062.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Publius Calicius Rufulus, dutiful, lived 45 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-18300062.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the death and burial of Publius Calicius Rufulus.

EDCS-18300063.translation: Lucius Caiecinus Victor lived 35 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-18300063.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the death and burial of Lucius Caiecinus Victor.

EDCS-18300064.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Caius Calpurnius Saturus Rogatianus lived 37 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-18300064.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the death and burial of Caius Calpurnius Saturus Rogatianus.

EDCS-18300065.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Quintus Cassius Saturninus, son of Quintus, of the Quirina tribe, lived 5 years.
EDCS-18300065.summary: A tombstone recording the death of a young boy named Quintus Cassius Saturninus, who lived for 5 years.

EDCS-18300066.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Publius Castronius Verus, son of Caius, of the Quirina tribe, lived 45 years.
EDCS-18300066.summary: A tombstone recording the death of Publius Castronius Verus, who lived for 45 years.

EDCS-18300067.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Fabia Tertullina lived 55 years; she lies here. Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Marcus Claudius Firmulus lived 17 years; he lies here.
EDCS-18300067.summary: A tombstone recording the deaths of two individuals, Fabia Tertullina and Marcus Claudius Firmulus, with their ages at death.

EDCS-18300068.translation: Tiberius Claudius Aeschines, son of [---], lived 18 years; he lies here.
EDCS-18300068.summary: A tombstone recording the death of Tiberius Claudius Aeschines, who lived for 18 years.

EDCS-18300069.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Lucius Clodius CALDVS [lived...].
EDCS-18300069.summary: A tombstone fragment dedicated to the Divine Spirits, mentioning Lucius Clodius CALDVS.

EDCS-18300070.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Lucius Clodius Epiphra pius lived years...
EDCS-18300070.summary: A tombstone fragment dedicated to the Divine Spirits, mentioning Lucius Clodius Epiphra and his piety.

EDCS-18300071.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Lucius Clodius Fuscinus, of the Quirina tribe, lived 31 years; he lies here.
EDCS-18300071.summary: A tombstone recording the death of Lucius Clodius Fuscinus, who lived for 31 years.

EDCS-18300072.summary: A tombstone recording the death of Lucius C. Iovinus, who lived for 19 years.

EDCS-18300073.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Clodia Serana lived 63 years; she lies here.
EDCS-18300073.summary: A tombstone recording the death of Clodia Serana, who lived for 63 years.

EDCS-18300074.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Colonica pia lived 19 years; she lies here.
EDCS-18300074.summary: A tombstone recording the death of Colonica pia, who lived for 19 years.

EDCS-18300075.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. F. Cordius Iunior lived for 10 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-18300075.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of F. Cordius Iunior at the age of 10.

EDCS-18300076.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Cornelia Felicissima, daughter of Lucius, lived for 52 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-18300076.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Cornelia Felicissima at the age of 52.

EDCS-18300078.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Grania Nice, daughter of Titus, lived for 97 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-18300078.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Grania Nice at the age of 97.

EDCS-18300079.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Credduta lived for 31 years; may the earth lie lightly upon you.
EDCS-18300079.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Credduta at the age of 31, with a common epitaphic wish.

EDCS-18300080.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Quintus Erucius Maximus, son of Quintus, lived for 9 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-18300080.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Quintus Erucius Maximus at the age of 9.

EDCS-18300081.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Caius Erucius Saturninus, son of Quintus, of the tribe Quirina, dutiful, lived for 71 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-18300081.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Caius Erucius Saturninus at the age of 71.

EDCS-18300082.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Caius Erucius Serus Sabinianus, of the tribe Quirina, lived for 16 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-18300082.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Caius Erucius Serus Sabinianus at the age of 16.

EDCS-18300083.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Publius Fabius Lupercus lived for 30 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-18300083.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Publius Fabius Lupercus at the age of 30.

EDCS-18300084.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Quintus Fabius Saturninus Iunior lived for 37 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-18300084.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Quintus Fabius Saturninus Iunior at the age of 37.

EDCS-18300085.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Fabius lived for 17 years and 2 months.
EDCS-18300085.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Fabius at the age of 17 years and 2 months.

EDCS-18300087.translation: To the Divine Shades. Faustus, son of Honoratus, a dutiful man, lived 26 years; he lies buried here.
EDCS-18300087.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Faustus, son of Honoratus, who lived 26 years, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-18300088.translation: To the Divine Shades. Felicitas, also called Ururia, a dutiful woman, lived 22 years; she lies buried here.
EDCS-18300088.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Felicitas (Ururia), who lived 22 years, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-18300089.summary: This is a very brief funerary epitaph for Fortunata, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-18300090.translation: To the Divine Shades. Germanus, a dutiful man, lived 17 years; he lies buried here.
EDCS-18300090.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Germanus, who lived 17 years, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-18300091.translation: Grania Tertulla, daughter of Caius, lived 43 years; she lies buried here.
EDCS-18300091.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Grania Tertulla, daughter of Caius, who lived 43 years, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-18300092.translation: To the Divine Shades. Gressia Ciana, daughter of Gressius Saturninus, lived 17 years; she lies buried here.

EDCS-18300222.summary: A funerary monument for Faustina, erected by her husband Publius Aelius Iulianus, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-18300223.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Lucius Herennius Evasius, pious, lived 2 years and 5 months. Titus Sapienus Purpurius, his uncle, placed this. He is buried here.
EDCS-18300223.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Lucius Herennius Evasius, who died in childhood, and was set up by his uncle Titus Sapienus Purpurius, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-18300224.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Iulius Quirina Fortunatus lived 65 years. Iulia Donata, his daughter, made this.
EDCS-18300224.summary: A funerary epitaph for Iulius Quirina Fortunatus, dedicated by his daughter Iulia Donata, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-18300225.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Iulia Fortunata Tiberia lived 71 years, for her pious mother.
EDCS-18300225.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication to Iulia Fortunata Tiberia, likely set up by her children, and dates to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-18300226.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Octavius Fazai lived 36 years, suddenly snatched away, without fault, without pain. And you who read, he asks that you say, may the earth be light for you. Octavius Felix and Iulia Urbana made this for their son. He is buried here.
EDCS-18300226.summary: A tombstone for Octavius Fazai, who died young and unexpectedly, set up by his parents Octavius Felix and Iulia Urbana, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-18300227.translation: Marcus Pomponius Getulus lived 87 years, 4 months, and 2 days. He is buried here.
EDCS-18300227.summary: A funerary inscription for Marcus Pomponius Getulus, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-18300229.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Ulpia Prima lived 65 years. Bibius Martialis made this for his dearest wife. She is buried here.
EDCS-18300229.summary: A funerary monument for Ulpia Prima, erected by her husband Bibius Martialis, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-18300230.translation: Here lies, who lived 95 years. C.B.B.E., a pious wife, lies here, 102 years old, for deserving parents. Urbanus and Napamo, son.
EDCS-18300230.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of C.B.B.E. and her parents, with details about their ages and the dedication by her son.

EDCS-18300231.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Quintus Aelius Laetianus lived 18 years. In memory of Caius Iulius Saturninus, son of Caius, of the Papiria tribe, Cilonianus, who held all offices in the colony of Sufetula, and [his] grandsons.
EDCS-18300231.summary: This inscription is a funerary monument commemorating Caius Iulius Saturninus, a prominent local official in Sufetula, and also recording the life of Quintus Aelius Laetianus.

EDCS-18500202.summary: This inscription records an epithet for the Third Augustan Legion, highlighting its loyalty and devotion.

EDCS-20300002.translation: Mauricelus, faithful, lived in peace for 60 years, buried on the 7th day before the Ides of October.
EDCS-20300002.summary: This is a tomb inscription recording the name, lifespan, and burial date of Mauricelus, likely from the late Roman period.

EDCS-20900085.translation: Keep this work for me, Patelaria Minor. Love sluggish for us. From the magical workshop of Donatus. We wish you, Victor, a colonist of the colony of Nova, a craftsman, to see us. We wish for you. Hail Mother, Hail.
EDCS-20900085.summary: This is an inscription from a workshop, possibly a funerary one, mentioning a magical workshop, its owner Donatus, and clients, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-20900086.translation: Triumphant, Votalis, Glorious congratulator. Why do you eat pale food? Enjoy the Baiae which you denied existed.
EDCS-20900086.summary: This is a funerary epigram, likely for a wealthy individual named Gratulator Triumfator Votalis Gloriosus, satirizing their supposed asceticism, probably from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-20900090.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Fortunatus qui et Samracius vixit annos XVII\n
EDCS-20900090.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Fortunatus, also called Samracius, lived 17 years.
EDCS-20900090.summary: This is a short funerary inscription recording the death of Fortunatus Samracius at the age of 17.

EDCS-20900091.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Ael Antulla vixit annis XXV piissime Honorata vixit annis IX\n
EDCS-20900091.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Ael Antulla lived 25 years, most pious Honorata lived 9 years.
EDCS-20900091.summary: This funerary inscription records the lives of two individuals, Ael Antulla and Honorata.

EDCS-20900092.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus fixit sic Iluma Mathlicis monimento sic FACM anno(s LXXXXV\n
EDCS-20900092.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Iluma Mathlicis set up this monument, lived 95 years.
EDCS-20900092.summary: This funerary inscription records that Iluma Mathlicis erected a monument for herself and lived to the age of 95.

EDCS-20900093.translation: To the Divine Shades. Appius Adiutor lived for 31 years. He rests here.
EDCS-20900093.summary: This is a standard tomb inscription for Appius Adiutor, indicating his age at death and burial location, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-20900094.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Considia Saturnina lived for 93 years. She rests here. Sacred to the Divine Shades. Considia Victoria lived for 21 years. She rests here.
EDCS-20900094.summary: This is a double tomb inscription for Considia Saturnina and Considia Victoria, recording their ages at death and burial, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-20900095.translation: Clodius Victor lived for 100 years. He rests here.
EDCS-20900095.summary: This is a tomb inscription for Clodius Victor, recording his exceptional age at death and burial, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-20900097.translation: Lucius Baebius, son of Lucius, [lived] 20 years. He rests here.
EDCS-20900097.summary: This is a tomb inscription for Lucius Baebius, son of Lucius, recording his age at death and burial, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-20900098.summary: This is a tomb inscription recording the name and age at death of Pinnia Pitinnina, likely from the Roman imperial period, with the burial place unstated.

EDCS-20900099.translation: From the Vindimialis workshop, at the instance of Primulus and his household.
EDCS-20900099.summary: This inscription indicates a commission or order from the Vindimialis workshop, likely related to funerary objects, at the request of Primulus and his family, probably from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-20900100.translation: Of Quintus, son of Aelius, a most distinguished man.
EDCS-20900100.summary: This is an epitaph for Quintus, son of Aelius, identified as a man of high standing, likely from the Roman elite.

EDCS-20900101.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Septimius Gaipa lived 80 years, twice a month.
EDCS-20900101.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Septimius Gaipa, who lived to the age of 80.

EDCS-20900102.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Cathadata lived 35 years; she lies here.
EDCS-20900102.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Cathadata, who lived to the age of 35 and is buried here.

EDCS-20900103.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Valeria Sperata lived 80 years. Sacred to the departed spirits. Saturninus, son of Coponius, lived 96 years. The sons made this for a dutiful father.
EDCS-20900103.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Valeria Sperata and Saturninus, son of Coponius, with the latter's sons erecting the monument for their devoted father.

EDCS-20900106.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Osenius, a dutiful son, lived 85 years.
EDCS-20900106.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Osenius, described as a dutiful son, who lived to the age of 85.

EDCS-20900107.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Ochius Marcus lived 51 and a half years.
EDCS-20900107.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Ochius Marcus, who lived to the age of 51 and a half.

EDCS-20900108.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Caius T. Baric, who died at the age of 12.

EDCS-20900110.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Antus lived 35 years.
EDCS-20900110.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Antus, who lived to the age of 35.

EDCS-20900111.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Aurelius Migin lived one year.
EDCS-20900111.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Aurelius Migin, who died at the age of one year.

EDCS-20900112.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Marcus Quadratus, who died at the age of 11.

EDCS-20900115.translation: Nitus, son of the perpetual flamen, having received the gifts of his father Iulius Fannius Delphus Victorinus Anicianus, the priesthood and the burden undertaken by his son Iucundus, with all the steps and honours of their family.
EDCS-20900115.summary: This inscription records the honours and priesthoods received by Nitus and his son Iucundus, likely dating to the late Roman Empire.

EDCS-20900116.summary: This is a dedication to the emperor Magnus Maximus, likely from the late 4th century CE.

EDCS-20900117.translation: Caius Mamilius Daceus lived for 55 years.
EDCS-20900117.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Caius Mamilius Daceus, recording his lifespan.

EDCS-20900118.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Gaius Julius Barigbal lived for 57 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-20900118.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Gaius Julius Barigbal, recording his lifespan and burial place.

EDCS-20900119.translation: Honoratus, son of Protus, lived for 2 years.
EDCS-20900119.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for the child Honoratus, recording his short lifespan.

EDCS-20900120.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Manilia Marcia lived for 75 years; she is buried here. Marcia.
EDCS-20900120.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Manilia Marcia, recording her lifespan and burial place, with a repetition of her name.

EDCS-20900121.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Quintus Papirius Junior lived for 45 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-20900121.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Quintus Papirius Junior, recording his lifespan and burial place.

EDCS-20900122.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Gududia, daughter of Barigbalis, lived for 85 years; the heir arranged for this to be made. Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Quintus Papirius Mesor lived for 103 years; the heir arranged for this to be made.
EDCS-20900122.summary: This inscription contains two funerary epitaphs, one for Gududia and one for Quintus Papirius Mesor, recording their exceptional lifespans and noting that their heirs commissioned the monuments.

EDCS-20900123.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Fortunata the devoted lived for 35 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-20900123.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Fortunata, recording her lifespan and burial place.

EDCS-20900124.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Gududia Massivena, daughter of Sei, the devoted, lived for 27 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-20900124.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Gududia Massivena, recording her lifespan and burial place.

EDCS-20900125.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Felix Kaprilius, dutiful, lived 25 years.
EDCS-20900125.summary: A funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Felix Kaprilius, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-20900126.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Secundus and Victoriae, his children, made this from their own means.
EDCS-20900126.summary: A funerary inscription recording a dedication made by children for their parents, Secundus and Victoriae, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-20900127.translation: Marcus Ulpius Quartio, freedman of Augustus and procurator, made this for his slave Salutaris.
EDCS-20900127.summary: A funerary inscription recording a dedication made by Marcus Ulpius Quartio for his slave Salutaris, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-21000539.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Autronia Honorata, daughter of Satiarae, lived 25 years.
EDCS-21000539.summary: A funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Autronia Honorata, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-21000540.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Marcus Chelihius Donatus lived X years. Caia Anicia Spica, his wife, lived 51 years. Chelihia Recchira set this up.
EDCS-21000540.summary: A funerary inscription recording the lives of Marcus Chelihius Donatus and his wife Caia Anicia Spica, with a dedication by Chelihia Recchira, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-21000541.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Livia Laetina. Marcus Spurius Secundus lived 42 years.
EDCS-21000541.summary: A funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Marcus Spurius Secundus, and also mentioning Livia Laetina, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-21000542.summary: A funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Baric Malatis, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-21000543.summary: A funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Bizizi Manan, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-21000545.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Marcus Flavius Constantius vixit nnos XVIIII menses IIII\n
EDCS-21000545.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Marcus Flavius Constantius lived 19 years and 4 months.
EDCS-21000545.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the life of Marcus Flavius Constantius, who died at the age of 19 years and 4 months.

EDCS-21000546.translation: dedicated by the authority of the most excellent Volusius Calpurnianus, curator, for the perpetual victory of the emperors and all who conquer.
EDCS-21000546.summary: An inscription recording a dedication made by Volusius Calpurnianus, a curator, likely related to public works or a monument, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-21000547.translation: The emperor's restorer of the walls... of Africa, a deputy, honored with greater affection by his homeland... Mussianus, most distinguished man, and by his own labor restored the ruined heights.
EDCS-21000547.summary: An inscription commemorating Mussianus, a distinguished man and deputy of Africa, who restored ruined structures, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-21000548.translation: To our lord Flavius Valentius, Pious, Fortunate, ever Augustus, by decree of the decurions, with public money.
EDCS-21000548.summary: This inscription records a public dedication to Emperor Flavius Valentius (likely Valentinian I) made by the town council.

EDCS-21000549.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Lucius Lollius Honoratus lived 46 years.
EDCS-21000549.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Lucius Lollius Honoratus, who died at the age of 46.

EDCS-21000550.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Lollius Honoratus lived 11 years.
EDCS-21000550.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Lollius Honoratus, who died at the age of 11.

EDCS-21000551.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Iafi c.
EDCS-21000551.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for a person named Iafi c.

EDCS-21000552.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Iafic.
EDCS-21000552.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for a person named Iafic.

EDCS-21000553.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Iulius Euasius lived 10 and a half years.
EDCS-21000553.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Iulius Euasius, who died at the age of 10 and a half.

EDCS-21000554.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Iulius Felix, son of Rogatus.
EDCS-21000554.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Iulius Felix, son of Rogatus.

EDCS-21000555.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Saturninus lived 25 years.
EDCS-21000555.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Saturninus, who died at the age of 25.

EDCS-21000556.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Vergilia Saturnina, dutiful, lived 65 years.
EDCS-21000556.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Vergilia Saturnina, who died at the age of 65.

EDCS-21000557.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Coricus.
EDCS-21000557.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for a person named Coricus.

EDCS-21000558.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of a woman named Maximina.

EDCS-21000560.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Quintus Silvanius.
EDCS-21000560.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicating a burial to the underworld spirits, mentioning Quintus Silvanius.

EDCS-21000561.translation: IVA, son of I and Desmidis.
EDCS-21000561.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription recording a parentage relationship, likely funerary or commemorative.

EDCS-21000562.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Saturninus.
EDCS-21000562.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicating a burial to the underworld spirits, mentioning Saturninus.

EDCS-21000563.summary: This is a very brief inscription, possibly a name on a monument or grave marker.

EDCS-21000565.translation: The house of Crescentianus, son of Attius Crescentis.
EDCS-21000565.summary: This inscription likely marks ownership of a house, identifying the owner as Crescentianus, son of Attius Crescentis.

EDCS-21000566.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Iulia Donata lived for 51 years. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Aurelius Victor, son of Apini, lived for 62 years.
EDCS-21000566.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespans of two individuals, Iulia Donata and Aurelius Victor.

EDCS-21000567.summary: This is a very brief inscription, likely a name on a monument or grave marker.

EDCS-21000568.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Octavia Rogata lived for 45 years, is buried here. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Publius Manlius Fidelis lived for 71 years, is buried here.
EDCS-21000568.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespans and burials of two individuals, Octavia Rogata and Publius Manlius Fidelis.

EDCS-21000569.translation: Here lies Popi Liberatus, faithful, in peace. Lived four years, four months, and six days.
EDCS-21000569.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the death of a child, Popi Liberatus, with details of their age at death.

EDCS-21000570.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Honoratus Victor, who rested here, lived in faith for 53 years.
EDCS-21000570.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Honoratus Victor, who lived 53 years.

EDCS-21000571.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Pompeius Marcellus lived for 5 years.
EDCS-21000571.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Pompeius Marcellus, who died at the age of 5.

EDCS-21000572.translation: Here lies Theodorus, a man worthy of remembrance, lived 30 years.
EDCS-21000572.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Theodorus, who lived 30 years.

EDCS-21000573.text_edition: \n Pro salute Imperatoris Caesaris Marci Aureli Commodi Augusti Quintus Volusius Maximus Maximianus sacerdos quod nania Maxima uxor sua hoc munus fieri una secum voverat id Volusius Maximianus votum solvit\n
EDCS-21000573.translation: For the safety of the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Commodus Augustus. Quintus Volusius Maximus Maximianus, a priest, fulfilled a vow that his wife Nania Maxima had pledged to make together with him; Volusius Maximianus fulfilled the vow.
EDCS-21000573.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by the priest Quintus Volusius Maximus Maximianus and his wife Nania Maxima for the well-being of Emperor Commodus.

EDCS-21000574.translation: The colony Flavia Augusta Emerita Ammaedara.
EDCS-21000574.summary: This inscription appears to be an administrative or geographical designation, possibly related to the colony of Emerita Ammaedara.

EDCS-21000576.translation: The aedile, quaestor, prefect for dispensing justice, ordered that his daughter be his heir.
EDCS-21000576.summary: This inscription records a legal or testamentary disposition concerning inheritance, mentioning various magistracies.

EDCS-21000581.translation: Trajan gave this, with tribunician power for the 10th time.
EDCS-21000581.summary: This inscription records an act by Emperor Trajan, dated by his tribunician power, likely related to a dedication or grant.

EDCS-21000585.translation: To Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus, conqueror of Arabia and Adiabene...
EDCS-21000585.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely honoring Emperor Septimius Severus, dating to his reign (late 2nd/early 3rd century CE).

EDCS-21000590.summary: This is a votive inscription by Aphrodisia, indicating the fulfillment of a religious promise.

EDCS-21000597.text_edition: \n Titi Camidieni Atimeti doliare ex praediis Plotinae Augustae\n
EDCS-21000597.translation: Doliar work from the estates of Plotina Augusta, made by Titus Camidienus Atimetus.
EDCS-21000597.summary: This records dolia (large earthenware jars) produced from the estates of Plotina Augusta, likely during the Hadrianic period (mid-2nd century CE).

EDCS-21000598.text_edition: \n Opus doliare ex praediis Domitiae Lucillae Flavi Probi Pontiano et Atiliano consulibus\n
EDCS-21000598.translation: Doliar work from the estates of Domitia Lucilla, by Flavius Probus and Pontianus and Atilianus, consuls.
EDCS-21000598.summary: This inscription records dolia produced from the estates of Domitia Lucilla, dating to the consulship of Flavius Probus and Pontianus and Atilianus, likely in the mid-2nd century CE.

EDCS-21000601.translation: It was decaying with age. Quintus Sentius Fabricius Iulianus, curator of the public resources, with...
EDCS-21000601.summary: This inscription seems to be part of a larger text concerning the restoration or maintenance of public property under the curator Quintus Sentius Fabricius Iulianus.

EDCS-21000603.translation: Sacred to Lord Saturn. Cetronius Saturninus, priest, gladly fulfilled his vow from the flock.
EDCS-21000603.summary: This is a religious inscription recording a vow fulfilled by Cetronius Saturninus, a priest of Saturn.

EDCS-21000604.text_edition: \n Silvano Augusto sacrum Marcus Manlius Felix sacerdos dono dedit dedicavit\n
EDCS-21000604.translation: Sacred to Silvanus Augustus. Marcus Manlius Felix, the priest, gave and dedicated this offering.
EDCS-21000604.summary: This is a dedication to the god Silvanus Augustus by the priest Marcus Manlius Felix, likely dating to the late 2nd or early 3rd century CE.

EDCS-21000608.translation: To Marcus Attius Cornelius, most eminent prefect of the praetorian guard, a good man, Ius Felix Pe... on account of special...
EDCS-21000608.summary: This is an honorary inscription dedicated to Marcus Attius Cornelius, a high-ranking prefect, likely by Ius Felix.

EDCS-21000609.translation: The state of the people of Uchita Maius, by decree of the decurions, has granted this to the priest of the eternal city of Rome for his outstanding loyalty in matters of the fatherland and his affection towards all citizens.
EDCS-21000609.summary: This inscription records a public grant from the community of Uchita Maius to a priest of Rome, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-21000610.text_edition: \n Areti Quinto Apronio Longino Mamiano clarissimo puero Quinti Aproni Mamiani Marciani egregi viri filio Cai Aproni Fortunati Mamiani egregi viri nepoti ordo coloniae Marianae Augustae Alexandrianae Uchitanorum Maiorum patrono et alumno suo\n
EDCS-21000610.translation: To Aretus, Quintus Apronius Longinus Mamianus, a most distinguished boy, son of Quintus Apronius Mamianus Marcianus, an excellent man, grandson of Caius Apronius Fortunatus Mamianus, an excellent man; to the patron and pupil of the town council of Colonia Mariana Augusta Alexandriana Uchitanorum Maiorum.
EDCS-21000610.summary: This is a dedication to a young boy named Aretus by the town council of Colonia Mariana Augusta Alexandriana Uchitanorum Maiorum, honoring him as a patron and pupil, likely dating to the late 2nd or early 3rd century CE.

EDCS-21000612.translation: As chief magistrate of the colony of Concordia Iulia Karthago.
EDCS-21000612.summary: This inscription likely records the holding of a magistracy in the Roman colony of Carthage, probably from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-21000613.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari Lucio Aurelio Commodo Augusto Imperatoris Antonini Augusti filio divi Pii nepoti divi Hadriani pronepoti divi Traiani Parthici abnepoti divi Nervae atnepoti Germanico Sarmatico tribunicia potestate IIII imperatori IIII consuli II patri patriae res publica Uchitanorum Maiorum sua pecunia fecit itemque dedicavit decreto decurionum\n
EDCS-21000613.translation: The Republic of the Uchitanorum Maiorum, by decree of the decurions and with public funds, made and also dedicated this to Emperor Caesar Lucius Aurelius Commodus Augustus, son of Emperor Antoninus Augustus, grandson of divine Pius, great-grandson of divine Hadrian, great-great-grandson of divine Parthicus Trajan, great-great-great-grandson of divine Nerva, Germanicus, Sarmaticus, holding tribunician power for the 4th time, emperor for the 4th time, consul for the 4th time, father of the country.
EDCS-21000613.summary: This inscription records the public works funded and dedicated by the town of Uchitanorum Maiorum to Emperor Commodus, celebrating his imperial titles and lineage, dating to his 4th tribunician power (179 CE).

EDCS-21000614.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari Marco Aurelio Antonino Pio Felici Augusto principi iuventutis tribunicia potestate V consuli proconsuli patri patriae Imperatoris Caesaris Luci Septimi Severi Pii Pertinacis Augusti Parthici maximi Arabici Adiabenici fortissimi felicissimi principis sena et Iuliae Domnae Augustae matris Augustorum et castrorum filio et Publi Septimi Getae nobilissimi Caesaris fratri divi Marci Antonini Pii nepoti divi Antonini Pii pronepoti divi Hadriani abnepoti divi Traiani et divi Nervae a<d=T>nepoti res publica Uchitanorum Maiorum decreto decurionum pecunia publica \n
EDCS-21000614.translation: The Republic of the Uchitanorum Maiorum, by decree of the decurions and with public funds, [dedicated this] to Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus, prince of youth, holding tribunician power for the 5th time, proconsul, father of the country, son of Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus Parthicus Maximus Arabicus Adiabenicus, the most valiant and fortunate prince, and of Iulia Domna Augusta, mother of the emperors and of the camp, and brother of Publius Septimius Geta nobilissimus Caesar, grandson of divine Marcus Antoninus Pius, great-grandson of divine Antoninus Pius, great-great-grandson of divine Hadrian, great-great-great-grandson of divine Trajan and divine Nerva.
EDCS-21000614.summary: This inscription records public works funded by the town of Uchitanorum Maiorum dedicated to Emperor Caracalla, celebrating his titles and imperial ancestry, dating to his 5th tribunician power (202 CE).

EDCS-21000615.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari Caio Valerio Diocletiano Pio Felici Augusto et \n
EDCS-21000615.translation: To Emperor Caesar Gaius Valerius Diocletian Pius Felix Augustus and...
EDCS-21000615.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription honoring Emperor Diocletian, likely dating to his reign (284-305 CE).

EDCS-21000617.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Quintus Tuscilius Luci filius Quintianus miles cohortis XI urbanae stipendiorum trium pius vixit annis XXIII hic situs est\n
EDCS-21000617.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Dead. Quintus Tuscilius Quintianus, son of Lucius, a soldier of the 11th Urban Cohort, with three years of service, pious, lived 23 years, is buried here.
EDCS-21000617.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Quintus Tuscilius Quintianus, a soldier of the 11th Urban Cohort, who died at the age of 23, likely dating to the late 2nd or early 3rd century CE.

EDCS-21000618.translation: Sacred to Saturnus Augustus. Caecilius Salus, priest, willingly fulfilled his vow in his 15th year.
EDCS-21000618.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Saturnus Augustus by a priest named Caecilius Salus, dating to his 15th year of service or the 15th year of an emperor, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-21000619.translation: Sacred to Saturnus Augustus. Lucius Cornelius Verna willingly fulfilled his vow in his 56th year.
EDCS-21000619.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Saturnus Augustus by Lucius Cornelius Verna, dating to his 56th year of life or service, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-21000620.summary: This inscription likely refers to a person or group associated with Baiae, possibly a family or a community group, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-21000621.translation: By order of the merciful goddess, Iscrispina made this from the measurements of Victor.
EDCS-21000621.summary: This inscription records a construction or dedication made by Iscrispina, possibly related to a religious cult or a building project, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-21000624.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Gaius Titinius Cabalus lived for fifty years.
EDCS-21000624.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the name and age of Gaius Titinius Cabalus, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-21000625.translation: Domnianus Miter lived for 3 years before the Kalends of October.
EDCS-21000625.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the name and age of a child, Domnianus Miter, who died shortly before October 1st, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-21000626.translation: To Pontica and Titiana, honorable and faithful women, may they have good memory in peace.
EDCS-21000626.summary: This is a funerary inscription honoring two women, Pontica and Titiana, emphasizing their faithfulness and wishing them a good remembrance, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-21000634.translation: To the Emperor Caesar, son of the deified Marcus Antoninus Pius, conqueror of the Germans and the Sarmatians.
EDCS-21000634.summary: This is a dedication to an emperor, identified by his lineage and military titles, likely commemorating a victory and dating to the Roman Imperial period, possibly relating to Marcus Aurelius.

EDCS-21000635.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the emperor Septimius Severus, likely from the Severan period (late 2nd to early 3rd century CE).

EDCS-21000639.translation: To our lord Flavius Claudius Constantius, the most noble Caesar, forever victorious.
EDCS-21000639.summary: This is an honorific inscription for the Caesar Flavius Claudius Constantius, likely dating to the mid-4th century CE.

EDCS-21000640.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely part of a larger dedication to an emperor named Caesar, possibly from the early imperial period.

EDCS-21000641.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the deified emperor Augustus, the father of the imperial family, likely from the early imperial period.

EDCS-21000644.translation: [---] established this by his expenditure and his care.
EDCS-21000644.summary: This inscription records the establishment of something by an unnamed individual through their own resources, likely a public benefaction.

EDCS-21000646.summary: This is a dedication to Aemilius Prudentis, potentially a public official or benefactor, with further details missing.

EDCS-21300240.translation: to the perpetual priest and curator of the republic
EDCS-21300240.summary: This inscription names an individual holding the offices of perpetual priest and curator rei publicae, indicating a significant civic role, likely from a provincial city.

EDCS-21300241.translation: completed in the second year of the duovirate of Caius Aurelius Galosus and Marcus Favonius Macedo, in the year of the duovirate
EDCS-21300241.summary: This inscription records the completion of a work during the second year of the joint duovirate of Caius Aurelius Galosus and Marcus Favonius Macedo, dating the event to their term of office.

EDCS-21300242.translation: Gymnicus of [---] years, an unworthy deed
EDCS-21300242.summary: This inscription refers to a 'Gymnicus' related to years and an 'unworthy deed', possibly connected to athletic games or a scandal.

EDCS-21300244.translation: To Quintus Octavius Volusius Thruscenius, most distinguished man, consul, Salian priest of the Colline tribe, praetor candidate, prefect of the Roman knights, decemvir for settling lawsuits, and to Geminia Vulcacia Mira, a woman of admirable goodness and exceptional innocence, Utica, with the people as patron, from her parents
EDCS-21300244.summary: This extensive dedication honors Quintus Octavius Volusius Thruscenius for his numerous high public offices and Geminia Vulcacia Mira for her virtues, set up in Utica by her parents and the town.

EDCS-21300247.translation: CCV, a pious wife, lived 35 years.
EDCS-21300247.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of a pious wife, CCV.

EDCS-21300250.translation: Artinius Ianuarius dedicated this sacred object from his own resources.
EDCS-21300250.summary: This is a dedication of a sacred object made by Artinius Ianuarius at his own expense.

EDCS-21300251.translation: For the safety of the Emperor Antoninus Augustus Pius and his children, Cincius Cai filius Arnensi Victor, after he had long before been made patron of the state with the consent of all the decurions, restored the temple portico of Ceres, consumed by age, from the ground up, and placed a statue of the Genius of the curia in the curia at a cost of 4,000 sesterces. On the day of the dedication, he gave gifts of eight asses each to the decurions and a banquet to all the citizens. And because they had requested and made Marcus Cincius Felix Iulianus, his son, patron because of the merits which the same Cincius Victor had shown towards his state and all the citizens, Cincius Victor, his father, in order to extend his generosity, had promised a statue of Fortuna and then placed it with increased funds from his own resources, and dedicated it. On that day, he also gave gifts of eight asses each to the decurions of the district and the state, and a banquet to all the citizens.
EDCS-21300251.summary: This inscription records the extensive public benefactions of Cincius Victor, including the restoration of a temple portico, the dedication of statues, and the provision of gifts and banquets for the decurions and citizens, likely dating to the reign of Antoninus Pius.

EDCS-21300252.translation: Of Decimus Clodius Septimus Albinus Caesar.
EDCS-21300252.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription referring to Decimus Clodius Septimus Albinus Caesar, possibly an official title or ownership marker.

EDCS-21300253.translation: To our great and invincible lords Diocletian and Maximian, perpetual Augusti, and to Constantius and Maximian, most noble Caesars, the state of the municipium of Agbia dedicates this, with Marcus Tullius T. proconsul of the province of Africa dedicating it to their majesty.
EDCS-21300253.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a monument by the municipium of Agbia to the emperors Diocletian, Maximian, Constantius, and Maximian, under the proconsulship of Marcus Tullius T. in Africa.

EDCS-22000652.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari Lucio Septimio Severo Pio Pertinaci Augusto tribunicia potestate IX imperatori consuli II patri patriae et Imperatori Caesari Marco Aurelio Antonino Augusto tribunicia potestate IIII et Lucio Septimio [Getae] Caesari Augusto Quinto Anicio Fausto legato Augustorum consulari [legionis III Augustae piae vindicis]\n
EDCS-22000652.translation: To Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus, holding tribunician power for the 9th time, emperor for the 2nd time, consul for the 2nd time, father of the country, and to Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus, holding tribunician power for the 4th time, and to Lucius Septimius [Geta] Caesar Augustus, by Quintus Anicius Faustus, consular legate of the Legio III Augusta Pia Vindex.
EDCS-22000652.summary: This inscription records the dedication of something by Quintus Anicius Faustus, legate of Legio III Augusta, to Emperors Septimius Severus, Caracalla, and Geta, dating to Severus's 9th tribunician power (201 CE) and Caracalla's 4th (201 CE).

EDCS-22000655.text_edition: \n Tiberio Claudio Caesari Augusto Germanico pontifici maximo tribunicia potestate consul II imperator III Quintus Marcius Cai filius Barea consul XVvir sacris faciundis fetialis proconsul dedicavit\n
EDCS-22000655.translation: To Emperor Tiberius Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus, chief priest, with tribunician power for the fifth time, consul for the second time, hailed as emperor for the third time, Quintus Marcius Barea, son of Gaius, consul for the fifteenth time, member of the college of fifteen for sacred rites, fetial priest, proconsul, dedicated this.
EDCS-22000655.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a monument by Quintus Marcius Barea, honoring Emperor Claudius.

EDCS-22000656.summary: This is a dedication to Germanicus, who held the office of pontifex maximus.

EDCS-22000660.translation: To Gaius Memmius Gaius filius Quirina Africanus, grandson of Gaius, who was enrolled in the ranks of the Roman equites by the deified Hadrian, [in the] first [place/rank] VO.
EDCS-22000660.summary: This inscription honors Gaius Memmius Quirinus Africanus, a member of the equestrian order admitted by Emperor Hadrian, with a partial indication of his rank or achievement.

EDCS-22000661.translation: For Quintus Plautius Titianus, who faithfully discharged his magistracy and other honors, the Curia Faustina [dedicates this] because of his merits.
EDCS-22000661.summary: This inscription is a dedication by the Curia Faustina to Quintus Plautius Titianus, honoring his public service and merits.

EDCS-22000662.translation: Although the order decreed a statue to Lucretius and [his] most valiant [colleague], he made [it] with his own funds because of his merits and dedicated it with public games.
EDCS-22000662.summary: This inscription records that Lucretius funded and dedicated a statue, likely in honor of himself and a colleague, after the order had decreed it.

EDCS-22000668.translation: [---] son, to the most noble Caesar Divi [---] MFI RCI IIIER IA.
EDCS-22000668.summary: This is a heavily damaged inscription likely intended as a dedication to a noble Caesar, possibly related to the imperial family.

EDCS-22000671.translation: To Victoria, conqueror of the Britons, by public decree of the people of Gighta, in honor of the Emperors Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax and Marcus Aurelius Antoninus and Publius Septimius Geta, Augusti.
EDCS-22000671.summary: This inscription is a public dedication by the people of Gighta to Victoria, likely celebrating military victories by the emperors Septimius Severus, Caracalla, and Geta, probably dating to their joint reign (c. 209-211 AD).

EDCS-22000674.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pertinax Augustus.
EDCS-22000674.summary: This is an imperial dedication to Emperor Lucius Septimius Severus Pertinax, likely part of a larger monument.

EDCS-22000675.text_edition: \n Quinto Egrilio Plariano legato pro praetore patrono Gigthenses publice\n
EDCS-22000675.translation: To Quintus Egrilius Plarianus, governor with praetorian power, their patron, by public decree of the people of Gigthis.
EDCS-22000675.summary: This inscription records a public dedication by the people of Gigthis to their patron, Quintus Egrilius Plarianus.

EDCS-22000679.translation: By public decree of the people of Gighta, to Quintus Egilius Plarianus, proconsul and patron.
EDCS-22000679.summary: This is a public dedication by the people of Gighta to their patron, the proconsul Quintus Egilius Plarianus.

EDCS-22000680.translation: The council and people of the municipium of Gighta have gratefully erected this statue to Flavius Archontius Nilus, a most distinguished man, governor and count of the province of Tripolitana, who conquered the king of the Austurians and is the sole and primary authority in this region.
EDCS-22000680.summary: This inscription records the grateful erection of a statue by the people of Gighta to their governor, Flavius Archontius Nilus, likely in the 3rd century AD.

EDCS-22000681.translation: To Servilius Primus, patron, from Publius Curtius, son of Publius, of the voting tribe Quirina, a scribe of the quaestorian rank, who served as one of the three decuries, with public equestrian status, squadron IIII.
EDCS-22000681.summary: This is a dedication to Servilius Primus, patron, by Publius Curtius, who held several public offices and equestrian rank.

EDCS-22000682.translation: Lucius Aemilius, with his own funds, by decree of the decurions, was granted a place.
EDCS-22000682.summary: This inscription records that Lucius Aemilius was granted a place, likely for a tomb or monument, at his own expense by local officials.

EDCS-22400591.translation: Publius Hortensius Pietas erected this to his most devoted father, Gaius Hortensius, son of Publius, of the voting tribe Quirina, as a gift from his own funds.
EDCS-22400591.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Publius Hortensius Pietas for his father, Gaius Hortensius Pietas, using private funds.

EDCS-22400593.translation: The senate and people of Gighta decreed that a monument be erected with public funds to Lucius Servaeus Firmus, son of Quintus, of the voting tribe Quirina, for his merits in the republic and his unique generosity to individuals and the community; but when he remitted [the funds], the council and people, content with the honor, had it erected with their own funds along with the local inhabitants.
EDCS-22400593.summary: This inscription records a public monument decreed for Lucius Servaeus Firmus by the people of Gighta for his public service and generosity, which he refused payment for, so they erected it at communal expense.

EDCS-22400594.translation: The senate and people of Gighta decreed that a monument be erected with public funds to Quintus Servaeus Fuscus, son of Lucius, of the voting tribe Quirina, for his merits in the republic and his unique generosity to individuals and the community; but when he remitted [the funds], the council and people, content with the honor, erected it with their own funds along with the local inhabitants.
EDCS-22400594.summary: This inscription records a public monument decreed for Quintus Servaeus Fuscus by the people of Gighta for his public service and generosity, which he refused payment for, so they erected it at communal expense.

EDCS-22400595.translation: Servaeus Insertor made the base for his excellent patron.
EDCS-22400595.summary: This inscription records that Servaeus Insertor commissioned a base for his patron.

EDCS-22400599.summary: This inscription records that Asius was the maker of the object, likely a dedication or building.

EDCS-22400601.translation: To the Divine Manes. Prosper and Candida, freedmen of their patron Iulius Callistus.
EDCS-22400601.summary: This funerary inscription records the dedication to the Divine Manes by the freedmen Prosper and Candida for their patron Iulius Callistus.

EDCS-22400602.summary: This inscription appears to be a simple list of three names, likely identifying individuals, possibly from a tomb or monument.

EDCS-22400607.translation: Egnatia Leas, a girl, lived in peace in this world for 21 years, 4 months, and 4 days.
EDCS-22400607.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Egnatia Leas, recording her age at death and her peaceful repose.

EDCS-22400609.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Petronius Crescens lived for 75 years.
EDCS-22400609.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to the Divine Manes and records the lifespan of Petronius Crescens.

EDCS-22400610.summary: This inscription consists of a single name, Valerius Vovius, likely an epitaph or identification marker.

EDCS-22400611.translation: To the father of the fatherland.
EDCS-22400611.summary: This fragment likely refers to an honorific inscription dedicated to a figure of great importance, possibly an emperor, given the title 'father of the fatherland'.

EDCS-22400612.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Eufrosine lived for 70 years.
EDCS-22400612.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to the Divine Manes and records the lifespan of Eufrosine.

EDCS-22400613.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Licinius Felix lived for 65 years and 4 months and 11 days.
EDCS-22400613.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to the Divine Manes and records the lifespan of Licinius Felix.

EDCS-22400614.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Lusia Maia lived for 36 years.
EDCS-22400614.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to the Divine Manes and records the lifespan of Lusia Maia.

EDCS-22400615.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Valerius Annianus lived 35 years.
EDCS-22400615.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Valerius Annianus.

EDCS-22400616.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Maridius Venustus made and dedicated this from his own resources for his beloved Volunteia Albia Secunda Terentia Secunda.
EDCS-22400616.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Lucius Maridius Venustus for his beloved Volunteia Albia Secunda Terentia Secunda.

EDCS-22400617.translation: To a good memory. Attia Quintula rests in peace, departed on the twelfth day before the Kalends of August, having lived 23 years, 18 days, and 3 hours.
EDCS-22400617.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan and death date of Attia Quintula.

EDCS-22400618.translation: Here lie your most holy ashes, to the departed spirits, a good woman of good memory, Aurelia.
EDCS-22400618.summary: This is a funerary inscription stating that the ashes of the good woman Aurelia are interred here.

EDCS-22400619.translation: To a good memory. Balsamius lived 40 years and 5 months.
EDCS-22400619.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Balsamius.

EDCS-22400620.translation: To a good memory. Crispina lived 8 years, 10 months, 24 days, and 6 hours, and rests in peace.
EDCS-22400620.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan and date of death of Crispina.

EDCS-22400621.translation: Iulius Maximus lived 60 years, 5 months, and 6 hours, in peace.
EDCS-22400621.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Iulius Maximus.

EDCS-22400622.translation: To a good memory. Pascasa lived 2 years and 7 months, in peace.
EDCS-22400622.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Pascasa.

EDCS-22400623.translation: To a good memory. Paulina lived 3 months, rests in peace in Christ.
EDCS-22400623.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Paulina, indicating a Christian burial.

EDCS-22400624.translation: To a good memory. Priscianus the faithful lived 35 years, died in peace on the tenth day before the Kalends of February, in the [Xth] indiction.
EDCS-22400624.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan and death date of Priscianus, a faithful individual, potentially from the 4th century onwards due to the mention of 'in pace' and 'indiction'.

EDCS-22400625.translation: To good memory, Rogata lived 4 years, 11 months, 3 days, 7 hours; she sleeps in peace.
EDCS-22400625.summary: This epitaph records the lifespan of Rogata, who died in peace.

EDCS-22400628.translation: To the Divine Manes, Vergilius Atticus lived 7 days and 6 hours; in peace.
EDCS-22400628.summary: This epitaph records the lifespan of Vergilius Atticus, who died in peace.

EDCS-22400629.translation: To good memory, Verna lived 7 days; sleeps in peace.
EDCS-22400629.summary: This epitaph records the lifespan of Verna, who died in peace.

EDCS-22400636.translation: To eternal memory, Consortiola, in peace.
EDCS-22400636.summary: This epitaph commemorates Consortiola, whose life ended in peace.

EDCS-22400638.translation: Maximianus, in peace, lived 3 months, 3 days.
EDCS-22400638.summary: This epitaph records the lifespan of Maximianus, who died in peace.

EDCS-22400639.translation: Sacred to the departed gods. Nonia Faustina, daughter of Gaius, lived for 5 years.
EDCS-22400639.summary: This is a tombstone recording the death of Nonia Faustina, a child of five years old.

EDCS-22400640.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Marcus Rasinius Martialis, son of Sextus Rasinius, lived two years, four months. May you achieve what you desire and not violate this sacred offering.
EDCS-22400640.summary: This epitaph is a dedication to the Divine Manes for Marcus Rasinius Martialis, including a warning against disturbing the grave.

EDCS-22400644.translation: To the procurator of the patrimony for the region of Leptis, to the procurator of the imperial treasury for the region of Tripolitania, a man of all virtues and of all justice, the incomparable prefect, by the freedmen and household of our Caesars.
EDCS-22400644.summary: This is a dedication to an official who held two procuratorial roles in Roman North Africa, likely in the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-22400645.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. To Gaius Tanusius Lupus, soldier of the 13th Urban Cohort, stationed at Post 1.
EDCS-22400645.summary: This epitaph is a dedication to the Divine Manes for Gaius Tanusius Lupus, a soldier serving in Rome.

EDCS-22400646.translation: [...] my name, wife, father, [who lived] months and year under the yoke of marriage, who gave birth and died. If you wish to pour tears for my buried self, [do not].
EDCS-22400646.summary: This is a fragment of a funerary inscription from a wife to her husband, expressing her marital life and perhaps her own impending death or sorrow.

EDCS-22400647.translation: To the Divine Manes, Romana lived 7 months.
EDCS-22400647.summary: This epitaph records the lifespan of Romana, who died in peace.

EDCS-22400648.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Vitalis, son of Vitalis, lived for 5 years.
EDCS-22400648.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a child named Vitalis, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22400649.translation: The return of Castula on the third day before the Ides of July.
EDCS-22400649.summary: This inscription records a date related to a person named Castula, possibly a legal or administrative return, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22400652.translation: To Simplicius Lucius Septimius Malchio Fortunatus, Roman knight, imperial priest, freedman of the Augusti, his paternal uncle, from Rome.
EDCS-22400652.summary: This is an inscription honouring Lucius Septimius Malchio Fortunatus, detailing his social and religious standing, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22400654.translation: Adeodata rests in peace. She lived for 25 years.
EDCS-22400654.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a woman named Adeodata, likely from the late Roman or early Christian period.

EDCS-22400655.translation: Antistia sleeps in peace. She lived for 6 years.
EDCS-22400655.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a child named Antistia, likely from the late Roman or early Christian period.

EDCS-22400656.translation: Asterius lived for 25 years, minus [some amount]; he sleeps in peace.
EDCS-22400656.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a person named Asterius, likely from the late Roman or early Christian period.

EDCS-22400657.translation: Cresconius sleeps in peace. He lived for 25 years and 6 months.
EDCS-22400657.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a person named Cresconius, likely from the late Roman or early Christian period.

EDCS-22400658.translation: Geganius Secundinius lived for 33 years and 7 months. He rested in peace on the day before the Kalends of October.
EDCS-22400658.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Geganius Secundinius, providing his age and date of death, likely from the late Roman or early Christian period.

EDCS-22400660.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a person named Maurusius, likely from the late Roman or early Christian period.

EDCS-22400661.translation: Medden rests in peace. He lived for 35 years, more or less. He departed on the 8th day before the Ides of January.
EDCS-22400661.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a person named Medden, providing his age and date of death, likely from the late Roman or early Christian period.

EDCS-22400662.translation: Victor lived in peace for 30 years more or less, 8 days before the Kalends of December, under Hierius and Artaburus.
EDCS-22400662.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Victor and the consuls under whom he died.

EDCS-22400663.translation: Billatica lived for 18 years more or less and rested in peace on the 6th day before the Kalends of July in the 29th year.
EDCS-22400663.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Billatica and a regnal year.

EDCS-22400664.translation: my mother sleeps in peace, lived for more than 44 years, under the consulship of Florentius and Dionysius.
EDCS-22400664.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a mother, noting her lifespan and the consuls.

EDCS-22400667.translation: Here, Lauro's workshop, may you build more and better things, if God is for us, who can be against us? The one whose name God knows, fulfilled his vow with his people Geon, Fison, Tigris, Euphrates.
EDCS-22400667.summary: This is a dedication to God from a workshop owner, wishing prosperity and listing his associates.

EDCS-22400668.translation: Cresconia lived in peace for 22 years, 2 months, and 10 days, and for this holy place, she gave her soul to God and his Christ.
EDCS-22400668.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespan of Cresconia and her devotional act.

EDCS-22400669.translation: For Parthica Victoria, by decree of the decurions, with public funds.
EDCS-22400669.summary: This records a public dedication or monument in honor of Parthica Victoria.

EDCS-22400677.translation: To the underworld spirits. Pusinnica was buried here, she lived for three years, 10 months, and 21 days. Her dearest mother Donata made this.
EDCS-22400677.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a young child, Pusinnica, dedicated by her mother.

EDCS-22400678.translation: To the underworld spirits. Secundinus lived for [X] years.
EDCS-22400678.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Secundinus.

EDCS-22400679.translation: To the underworld spirits. Lucius Sulpicius Marcellus was placed here, he lived for 21 years. His father made this.
EDCS-22400679.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Sulpicius Marcellus, made by his father.

EDCS-22400683.translation: To Danacia Quartilla Aureliana, the most illustrious lady.
EDCS-22400683.summary: This is a dedication or epitaph honoring the distinguished lady Danacia Quartilla Aureliana.

EDCS-22400684.translation: Iatepraetaca, rarest of mothers, is buried here after death.
EDCS-22400684.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Iatepraetaca, identified as a mother, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22400685.translation: Quintus Otacilius lived for ninety years. Cuntus Tituleius set this up as patron.
EDCS-22400685.summary: This funerary monument records the long life of Quintus Otacilius, and it was erected by Cuntus Tituleius, acting as patron, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22400686.translation: To the departed spirits. Quintus Helvius Rogatus lived for 2 years.
EDCS-22400686.summary: A funerary epitaph for Quintus Helvius Rogatus, who died at the age of two, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22400688.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Flavius Valerius Constantinus, Pious, Fortunate, Unconquered, Augustus, chief priest, holder of tribunician power, the colony of Uppenna, devoted to his divine majesty, at the decree of the decurions, with public money.
EDCS-22400688.summary: This is a dedication by the colony of Uppenna to Emperor Constantine I, celebrating his imperial titles and authority, likely from the 4th century CE.

EDCS-22400689.translation: To the departed spirits, sacred. Ceselius Martis lived for 70 years.
EDCS-22400689.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Ceselius Martis, who lived for 70 years, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22400691.summary: This fragmentary inscription likely refers to an individual named Bassus, who held the office of herald, possibly a dedication or funerary marker.

EDCS-22400692.translation: To the departed spirits, sacred. Suellius Quartus, son of Marcius Suellius Quarti, lived for 36 years and thirty days, is buried here.
EDCS-22400692.summary: A funerary epitaph for Suellius Quartus, detailing his age at death and burial location, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22700623.translation: Many years ago, Esra, son of the son of [---] urbit.
EDCS-22700623.summary: This very fragmentary inscription seems to record a person named Esra and an action, possibly related to construction or ownership, with an uncertain date.

EDCS-22700624.translation: M. Flaminius, 82 years old, and his wife Cornelia, with his own money.
EDCS-22700624.summary: This funerary inscription records the ages of M. Flaminius and his wife Cornelia, with the burial expenses covered by Flaminius, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22700628.translation: To Claudius the Unconquered Emperor, by decree of the decurions, with public money.
EDCS-22700628.summary: This inscription is a dedication by the decurions to Emperor Claudius, possibly commemorating an event or honoring his authority, likely from the 1st century CE.

EDCS-22700630.translation: To Philippianus, a man of equestrian rank, admitted by the Emperors Antoninus and Verus Augusti, by decree of the councilors, with public funds.
EDCS-22700630.summary: This inscription records a public monument erected to Philippianus, likely a local official, at public expense, dating to the reign of Marcus Aurelius and Lucius Verus.

EDCS-22700631.translation: To the protector, Gaius Postumius Saturninus Flavianus, an excellent man, procurator of the hundredth [rank] of the province of Hadrumetum, who also held the two-hundredth [rank], by sacred command, in the same province; Lucius Sempronius Maximus, perpetual priest, [erects this] to his patron.
EDCS-22700631.summary: This is a dedication by a perpetual priest to his patron, Lucius Sempronius Maximus, honoring Gaius Postumius Saturninus Flavianus, a high-ranking procurator in the province of Hadrumetum.

EDCS-22700632.translation: To the protector, Gaius Postumius Saturninus Flavianus, an excellent man, procurator of the hundredth [rank] of the province of Hadrumetum, who also held the two-hundredth [rank], by sacred command, in the same province; Victor, freedman of the Augusti and client, [erects this].
EDCS-22700632.summary: This inscription honors Gaius Postumius Saturninus Flavianus, a procurator in Hadrumetum, erected by his freedman and client, Victor.

EDCS-22700633.translation: And to his citizens, they provided for themselves in memory; Gaia Fortunata, perpetual priestess of the same municipality, in solace for her most beloved lost husband, erected this statue with her own money; the site was granted by decree of the councilors.
EDCS-22700633.summary: This inscription records the erection of a statue by Gaia Fortunata, a local priestess, in memory of her husband, with the site provided by the municipal council.

EDCS-22700634.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Publius Aelius Pius, son of Publius, lived.
EDCS-22700634.summary: This is a simple funerary inscription (dis manibus) for Publius Aelius Pius.

EDCS-22700635.translation: Julius Sicivus, for love of his father, for instruction c
EDCS-22700635.summary: This fragmented inscription likely records an offering or a memorial related to Julius Sicivus and his father.

EDCS-22700637.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Numisius Felix, pious, lived 80 years.
EDCS-22700637.summary: This is a funerary inscription (dis manibus) for Numisius Felix, who lived to be 80 years old.

EDCS-22700642.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Ingenius Cilonianus, the father, lived 76 years and 4 months.
EDCS-22700642.summary: This is a funerary inscription (dis manibus) for Ingenius Cilonianus, who lived to be 76 years and 4 months old.

EDCS-22700643.translation: To Antoninus Augustus, father, and to Beben [son of] Antoninus, Augusti.
EDCS-22700643.summary: This inscription is an honorific dedication to the Emperors Antoninus (likely Caracalla) and his son (Geta or another co-emperor).

EDCS-22700644.translation: Sacred to the god Pluto. For the health of our lords Diocletian and Maximian, and of Constantius and Maximian, the most noble Caesars, the temple of Pluto, collapsed, was dedicated through the initiative of Felix Caius Aelius Fortunatus and Lucius Caius Antonius Marsuatanus, magistrates of the fundus Iubaltianensis, and Fortunatus Aliqautis, treasurer, who also cared for the power and majesty of this deity.
EDCS-22700644.summary: This inscription records the rededication of a dilapidated temple to Pluto, commissioned by local officials on a rural estate (fundus Iubaltianensis), during the Tetrarchy.

EDCS-22700646.translation: Sissoi, freedwoman of Tarafani, lived 100 years. Fortunatus, son of Babba, of Sufetana, lived 80 years. Their son Donatus made this for them out of piety at his own expense.
EDCS-22700646.summary: A funerary monument erected by a son for his parents, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22700647.summary: A simple dedication or memorial possibly for Lucius Iulius Homullus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22700650.translation: Frontonius Fortis Abidianus, perpetual priest, pious, lived 34 years. May your bones rest well.
EDCS-22700650.summary: A funerary epitaph for Frontonius Fortis Abidianus, a perpetual priest, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22700651.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the short life of Allius Caprasius, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22700652.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Aelius Gubula lived 32 years, with his wife Pomponnia Secunda dutifully managing. Pomponnia Secunda lived 50 years and 11 days.
EDCS-22700652.summary: A funerary monument dedicated to the departed spirits, recording the lives of Aelius Gubula and his wife Pomponnia Secunda, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22700653.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Aelia Sisso lived 22 years. May your bones rest well.
EDCS-22700653.summary: A funerary epitaph dedicated to the departed spirit of Aelia Sisso, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22700654.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Aelia Victoria Zaracaia lived 9 years and 106 days.
EDCS-22700654.summary: A funerary epitaph dedicated to the departed spirit of Aelia Victoria Zaracaia, recording her young age, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22700655.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Fortunatianus lived 44 years. May your bones rest well.
EDCS-22700655.summary: A funerary epitaph dedicated to the departed spirit of Fortunatianus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22700656.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. P. C. lived [some years]; Nicone, Felix, and the other sons took care [of the burial]. He lies here.
EDCS-22700656.summary: A funerary epitaph mentioning the care of sons for a deceased parent, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22700657.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Crescentia lived 42 years and 9 months. Caius Pomponius Saturninus to his dearest wife. Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Caius Pomponius Saturninus lived 55 years; his son took care of this out of piety. Pomponius Castus lived [some] months. Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Pomponius Cillo lived 35 years. May your bones rest well. Publius Pomponius Carus Venerius lived 3 years. Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Aelia Victoria lived 2 years.
EDCS-22700657.summary: A complex funerary monument with multiple epitaphs for various family members, including Crescentia, Caius Pomponius Saturninus, Pomponius Castus, Pomponius Cillo, Publius Pomponius Carus Venerius, and Aelia Victoria, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22700658.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. [He/She] lived 30 years. May your bones rest well. Sacred to the departed spirits. [He/She] lived 58 years. May your bones rest well.
EDCS-22700658.summary: A funerary inscription recording the age at death of at least two individuals, invoking the departed spirits.

EDCS-22700660.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits, to a wife of reverence and memory, Claudia Auguriva, who lived 90 years. [Her] husband lived 6 years. Donatus lived 1 year, 4 months. May your bones rest well.
EDCS-22700660.summary: A funerary inscription honoring Claudia Auguriva and Donatus, recording their ages at death and mentioning the husband's lifespan.

EDCS-22700662.summary: A funerary inscription simply stating the name of Iulia Saturnina.

EDCS-22700663.summary: A funerary inscription that names Marcus Aurelius Primasius and states he lived, likely indicating his death.

EDCS-22700664.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulius Successus lived 7 years. May your bones rest well.
EDCS-22700664.summary: A funerary inscription for a child, Iulius Successus, recording his age at death and invoking the departed spirits.

EDCS-22700665.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulia Getulica lived 44 years. May your bones rest well.
EDCS-22700665.summary: A funerary inscription for Iulia Getulica, recording her age at death and invoking the departed spirits.

EDCS-22700666.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulia Quinta lived years.
EDCS-22700666.summary: A funerary inscription for Iulia Quinta, with incomplete information about her age at death, invoking the departed spirits.

EDCS-22700667.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits, in memory of Sextus Iulius Rogatianus, who lived 6 years and 15 days.
EDCS-22700667.summary: A funerary inscription for Sextus Iulius Rogatianus, recording his age at death, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22700668.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus Iunius Quintianus lived 14 years. His wife Monna restored [this].
EDCS-22700668.summary: A funerary inscription for Quintus Iunius Quintianus, recording his age at death and stating it was restored by his wife Monna.

EDCS-22700669.translation: Caius Valerius Neos lived 60 years, and his wife Canneia Variana lived [years], and his other wife Aurellia Mustula lived 30 years. Caius, farewell.
EDCS-22700669.summary: A funerary inscription recording the ages at death of Caius Valerius Neos and his two wives, Canneia Variana and Aurellia Mustula.

EDCS-22700675.translation: To the underworld gods. Gaius Cassius Secundus.
EDCS-22700675.summary: This is a funerary dedication to the underworld gods by Gaius Cassius Secundus.

EDCS-22700676.summary: This records a votive offering to a deity named Isarbosa.

EDCS-22700677.translation: Sacred to the underworld gods. Satria Silvana lived for 9 years and 4 months; she is buried here.
EDCS-22700677.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the age at death and burial location of Satria Silvana.

EDCS-22700679.translation: I, Teodora, daughter of Giliissupon, wrote this in the sixth indiction and dedicated it to Christ.
EDCS-22700679.summary: This is a Christian inscription where Teodora records her act of writing and dedication in the sixth indiction.

EDCS-22700680.translation: Hear, O God, my prayer; give ear to the words of my mouth. Holy ones, pray for me.
EDCS-22700680.summary: This is a Christian prayer invoking God and requesting prayers from the saints.
