EDCS-22700681.translation: Dedicated to the holy ones, January and his companions. Flavius Annius Pusinnus, with his family, happily completed his vow.
EDCS-22700681.summary: This is a votive inscription by Flavius Annius Pusinnus and his family, dedicated to saints January and his companions.

EDCS-22700682.translation: Nonnius lived in peace for years.
EDCS-22700682.summary: This is a funerary inscription that records the name of the deceased, Nonnius, and the duration of his life in peace, though the exact number of years is missing.

EDCS-22700685.translation: Sacred to the underworld gods. Aemilia Donata lived for 52 years.
EDCS-22700685.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Aemilia Donata, stating her age at death and dedicating the inscription to the underworld gods.

EDCS-22700686.translation: To the underworld gods. Gaius Caecilius Iulianus lived for 14 years.
EDCS-22700686.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Gaius Caecilius Iulianus, stating his age at death and dedicating the inscription to the underworld gods.

EDCS-22700687.translation: Sacred to the underworld gods. C. Saturnina lived for 102 years.
EDCS-22700687.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for C. Saturnina, stating her age at death and dedicating the inscription to the underworld gods.

EDCS-22700688.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the Manes, with illegible text following.

EDCS-22700689.translation: To the departed spirits. Flavius Urbanus lived 30 years. Flavia Fortunata made this.
EDCS-22700689.summary: This is a funerary inscription by Flavia Fortunata commemorating her husband, Flavius Urbanus, who died at age 30.

EDCS-22700690.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Flavius Victorin lived 1 month.
EDCS-22700690.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Flavius Victorin, who died at one month of age.

EDCS-22700691.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Manovius lived 1 year.
EDCS-22700691.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Manovius, who died at one year of age.

EDCS-22700692.translation: To the departed spirits. Lucius Munatius [---] Magnianus, his colleague in the contubernium, lived [---] years.
EDCS-22700692.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Munatius Magnianus, likely a soldier, who died after an unspecified period of service as a beneficiarius and contubernalis.

EDCS-22700693.summary: This is a funerary inscription for [---]uscocus Ia mus, who died at age 52.

EDCS-22700694.translation: Quintus Caecilius Paulus lived 85 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-22700694.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Quintus Caecilius Paulus, who died at age 85.

EDCS-22700695.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Tettius Quietus, dutiful, lived 55 years. [---]
EDCS-22700695.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Tettius Quietus, who died at age 55, with illegible text following.

EDCS-22700696.translation: [---]lia ti VAI lived [---] years. Maximus Plancius lived 23 years; he made this for himself and his sons.
EDCS-22700696.summary: This funerary inscription records Maximus Plancius, who died at age 23, and was made for himself and his sons.

EDCS-22700698.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Postumia Matronilla, incomparable wife, good mother, most dutiful grandmother, modest, religious, hardworking, efficient, vigilant, solicitous, faithful to one husband, sharing one marriage bed, a matron of all industry and fidelity, lived 53 years, 5 months, and 3 days.
EDCS-22700698.summary: This is a detailed funerary inscription for Postumia Matronilla, who died at age 53 years, 5 months, and 3 days, praising her virtues as a wife, mother, and grandmother.

EDCS-22700699.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Ianuaria lived 45 years; her husband arranged for this monument to be erected, and for Cerdon, her dearest son, who lived 5 years.
EDCS-22700699.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Ianuaria and her son Cerdon, likely dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22700701.translation: To Adiabenicus Parthicus, son of Ulpius.
EDCS-22700701.summary: This is a dedicatory inscription to a military figure named Adiabenicus Parthicus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22700702.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Aelius Metunus lived 26 years; his parents made this tombstone.
EDCS-22700702.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Aelius Metunus, set up by his parents, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22700705.translation: His children arranged for this [monument] for the priestess of the Great Ceres, their most chaste and dearest mother.
EDCS-22700705.summary: This is a funerary inscription honoring a priestess of Ceres, erected by her children, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22700706.translation: Dubbaina, daughter of Gadais, from Cillita, lived 20 years; she lies here.
EDCS-22700706.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Dubbaina, a woman from Cillita, likely dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22700707.translation: Masac, son of Alurusae, lived 45 years; he lies here. His children arranged for this [monument].
EDCS-22700707.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Masac, son of Alurusae, erected by his children, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22700708.translation: Farisa, daughter of Codra, from Cillita, wife of Masac, son of Alurusae, from Cillita, lived 40 years; her children arranged for this [monument] for their mother.
EDCS-22700708.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Farisa, wife of Masac, and mother of two sons, likely dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22700709.translation: Masul, son of Masac, pious, lived 60 years. [---] son of [---] ...
EDCS-22700709.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Masul, son of Masac, likely dating from the Roman Imperial period, with lacunae.

EDCS-22700710.translation: Saturninus, son of Masac, lived 70 years. Flavia Fortunata lived 65 years. Their son Flavius Fortunatus arranged for this monument.
EDCS-22700710.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Saturninus and Flavia Fortunata, erected by their son Flavius Fortunatus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22700711.translation: Fusca, daughter of Fortunatus, lived 50 years; her husband Saturninus arranged for this [monument].
EDCS-22700711.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Fusca, daughter of Fortunatus, erected by her husband Saturninus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22700713.translation: I, Amoriona, most beautiful AMM, moved by DREVE, since I was defrauded of AI, then with my husband I added an honorable tomb for ES years.
EDCS-22700713.summary: This is a funerary epitaph, likely from the Roman Empire, recording the burial of Amoriona with her husband.

EDCS-22700714.summary: This is a maker's mark or inscription indicating the origin of an object from the workshop of Cricitolanus.

EDCS-22700716.translation: To Victoria of our Augustus, the Emperor Caesar, of the deified Aurelianus Pius Felix Invictus, by decree of the decurions, with public money.
EDCS-22700716.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Victoria, likely commissioned by local officials (decurions) and funded by public money, in honor of Emperor Aurelian.

EDCS-22700718.translation: To Marcus Annius Verus Caesar, son of the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus Armenicus Medicus Parthicus Maximus and of Faustina Augusta, by decree of the decurions, with public money.
EDCS-22700718.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Marcus Annius Verus Caesar, son of Marcus Aurelius and Faustina, commissioned by local officials (decurions) and funded by public money.

EDCS-22700720.translation: To Emperor Caesar Marcus Antonius Gordianus Pius Felix Invictus Augustus, with tribunician power for the second time, consul, father of the country, by decree of the decurions, at public expense.
EDCS-22700720.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Emperor Gordian III, funded by public money and decreed by the local council.

EDCS-22700721.translation: For the health and ORF of the Emperor Caesar, with his own money within the space of a year.
EDCS-22700721.summary: This inscription records a dedication for the health of the Emperor Caesar, made with private funds within a year.

EDCS-22700722.translation: For the blessedness of the most invincible princes, with Gelius, curator of the republic, urging, for eternal times.
EDCS-22700722.summary: This inscription records a dedication for the prosperity of the emperors, overseen by Gelius, the curator of the state, intended to last for eternity.

EDCS-22700723.translation: The entire curia, recognizing his merits, his outstanding clemency and singular excellence towards individuals and the public alike, his integrity, his generous moderation in the matter of grain supply, and his unique pre-eminence in all virtues, have marked by the eternity of this title the honor of statues for Lucius Caelio Plautius Catullinus, a most distinguished man, a tribune, and curator of the republic.
EDCS-22700723.summary: This inscription records the award of honorary statues by the entire town council to Lucius Caelio Plautio Catullino, acknowledging his virtues, clemency, administrative skills, and public service.

EDCS-22700728.translation: Lucius Valgius Mauricus, an excellent man, made this for Pomponius Gallus, son of Gaius, of the Papiria tribe, a distinguished man who had served as advocate for the Spanish treasury for three years, and administrator of the province of Carthage, and was a commentator for the praetorian prefects, and a procurator of Augusti nostrae with a salary of 200,000 sesterces in the diocese of Hadrumetum, because of exceptional friendship as fellow students.
EDCS-22700728.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Lucius Valgius Mauricus to his friend Pomponius Gallus, honoring his distinguished career in various financial and administrative roles within the Roman Empire.

EDCS-22700729.translation: The most splendid order of Sufetula has marked by the eternity of this title for Marcus Valgius Aemilianus, son of Marcus, of the Quirina tribe, a Roman knight and tribune of the Palmyrene cohort, because of his exceptional liberality towards his state.
EDCS-22700729.summary: This inscription records the honoring of Marcus Valgius Aemilianus by the city of Sufetula for his generous contributions to the state.

EDCS-22700730.translation: For Quintus Julius Rogatianus, son of Quintus, of the Quirina tribe, because of the honor of the aedileship and his medical profession, and his generous liberality in staging games twice for the priesthood of the freedmen and the entire curia.
EDCS-22700730.summary: This inscription honors Quintus Julius Rogatianus for his service as an aedile, his medical practice, and his generous funding of public games.

EDCS-22700731.translation: To Marco Magnius Severus, perpetual priest, incomparable citizen, on account of his splendid merits, the council of Sufetula decreed with public funds.
EDCS-22700731.summary: This inscription records a public monument erected by the town council of Sufetula to honor Marco Magnius Severus for his merits.

EDCS-22700732.translation: To Quintus Octavius Lucullus Honoratianus, son of Caius Octavius Asprius, for his singular munificence and generous liberality, a place in the whole curia was granted by decree of the council, [as a gift from] his father Caius Octavius Asprius.
EDCS-22700732.summary: This inscription records the granting of a place in the curia to Quintus Octavius Lucullus Honoratianus, honoring his generosity, gifted by his father.

EDCS-22700733.translation: To Lucius Rasinius Saturninus Maximianus, son of Lucius Rasinius, aedile and quinquennial duumvir, for his exemplary character and steadfast kindness in both his public offices, and for his sons' presentation of priesthood games and their constant generosity towards individual citizens, the entire populace of the curiae has erected this perpetual testimony of their gratitude and has also dedicated it.
EDCS-22700733.summary: This inscription records a monument of gratitude erected by the populace to Lucius Rasinius Saturninus Maximianus, honoring his character, public service, and his sons' contributions.

EDCS-22700737.translation: To Severus, consular governor of the province of Flavia Valeria Byzacena.
EDCS-22700737.summary: This inscription records the name of Severus, a consular governor of Flavia Valeria Byzacena, likely on a public monument.

EDCS-22700738.summary: This is a very brief inscription, possibly indicating ownership or a dedication by Victorinus Sikillus.

EDCS-22700750.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Aelius Optatulus lived 50 years. His dearest wife made this.
EDCS-22700750.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the death of Aelius Optatulus at age 50, dedicated by his wife.

EDCS-22700751.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Aelia Felicitas lived 2 years and 13 months.
EDCS-22700751.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the death of Aelia Felicitas at the age of 2 years and 13 months.

EDCS-22700752.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Aelia Honorata.
EDCS-22700752.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the name of Aelia Honorata.

EDCS-22700754.translation: Aelia Victoria lived 2 years and 2 months.
EDCS-22700754.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the death of Aelia Victoria at the age of 2 years and 2 months.

EDCS-22700755.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the death of Aemilius Victorinus at the age of 22 months.

EDCS-22900072.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Donata lived 45 years.
EDCS-22900072.summary: A funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Donata, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22900073.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Arruntia Tecusa, dutiful, lived for three years.
EDCS-22900073.summary: A funerary inscription recording the short lifespan of Arruntia Tecusa, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22900074.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Aurelius [---]
EDCS-22900074.summary: A funerary inscription for Aurelius, with the text incomplete, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22900075.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Aurelius Ianuarius Victor lived for 15 months.
EDCS-22900075.summary: A funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Aurelius Ianuarius Victor, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22900076.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Caecilius V. VI [---]
EDCS-22900076.summary: A funerary inscription for Caecilius, with the text incomplete, possibly recording a lifespan, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22900077.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Caecilius Datus lived for [---] years.
EDCS-22900077.summary: A funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Caecilius Datus, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22900079.translation: To the spirits of the departed. So[---]us Calendio, aged III years.
EDCS-22900079.summary: A funerary inscription recording the age of So[---]us Calendio, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22900080.translation: To the spirits of the departed. So[---]atus Gallonius, a child, lived for 1 year and 6 days.
EDCS-22900080.summary: A funerary inscription recording the short lifespan of the child So[---]atus Gallonius, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22900081.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Clepia Donatulla lived for 55 years and 10 months.
EDCS-22900081.summary: A funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Clepia Donatulla, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22900082.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Cornelia Saturnina, daughter of Saturninus Maior, lived for 32 years.
EDCS-22900082.summary: A funerary inscription recording the lifespan and parentage of Cornelia Saturnina, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22900084.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Curba.
EDCS-22900084.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a person named Curba, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22900085.translation: Flavia Tertullina lived for one year and 5 months.
EDCS-22900085.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Flavia Tertullina, recording her short lifespan, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22900086.translation: To the Divine Manes. Aius Flavianus lived for 65 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-22900086.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Aius Flavianus, recording his death and burial place, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22900087.translation: To the Manes. Estus lived for 2 years. Esia Victoria lived for 3 years. Antestius Fortunatus lived for 2 years and 7 months. They are buried here.
EDCS-22900087.summary: This is a funerary inscription for multiple individuals, likely family members, recording their lifespans and burial, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22900088.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Fortunata lived for 1 year, [---] months.
EDCS-22900088.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Fortunata, recording her short lifespan with missing details, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22900089.translation: Fortunata lived for 3 years and 10 days.
EDCS-22900089.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Fortunata, recording her young age at death, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22900091.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Iulius Claudius lived for 2 years, 7 months, and 6 days. He is buried here.
EDCS-22900091.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Iulius Claudius, recording his lifespan and burial, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22900092.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Quintus Iulius Datus lived for 15 years, 2 months, and 14 days.
EDCS-22900092.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Quintus Iulius Datus, recording his lifespan, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22900093.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Iulius Lucinianus lived for 3 years, 5 months, and 19 days. His father Iulius Buricus made this for his dearest son.
EDCS-22900093.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Iulius Lucinianus, dedicated by his father, recording his young age and burial, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22900094.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Iulia Saturnina lived for 14 years.
EDCS-22900094.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Iulia Saturnina, recording her lifespan, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22900095.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Iulia Saturnina lived for 24 years and 4 days.
EDCS-22900095.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Iulia Saturnina.

EDCS-22900096.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Iustius Iunius Ianuarius lived for 40 years and is buried here.
EDCS-22900096.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan and burial of Iustius Iunius Ianuarius.

EDCS-22900097.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the life of Licin Cuia Victo.

EDCS-22900098.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Luci Septimi Saturni lived for 1 year, 5 months, and 17 days.
EDCS-22900098.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Luci Septimi Saturni.

EDCS-22900099.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Ulpius Athenaeus lived for 76 years, 3 months, and 26 days and is laid to rest here.
EDCS-22900099.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan and burial of Ulpius Athenaeus.

EDCS-22900101.translation: To the spirits of the departed. [Name illegible] lived for 3 years, 3 months.
EDCS-22900101.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of an unnamed individual, likely a child.

EDCS-22900102.translation: Lived for 2 years, 5 months, and 10 days.
EDCS-22900102.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of an unnamed individual, likely a child.

EDCS-22900104.translation: To the gods of the underworld. [Name illegible] in the year [date illegible], [lived/was buried] for 5 months.
EDCS-22900104.summary: A funerary epitaph with partial information about a burial and a duration of 5 months.

EDCS-22900107.translation: To Emperor Caesar, Egnatianus, perpetual priest.
EDCS-22900107.summary: An inscription dedicating something to the Emperor Caesar by Egnatianus, a perpetual priest.

EDCS-22900108.translation: Marcus Gentius Quartinus, a veteran, made this for Marcus Gentius Quartus, a citizen of the town of Sufetula.
EDCS-22900108.summary: A funerary monument set up by a veteran for his father, a citizen of Sufetula.

EDCS-22900109.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Silus Tertullus, decurion of the Ala Flavia, lived 40 years.
EDCS-22900109.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Silus Tertullus, a decurion, who lived 40 years.

EDCS-22900110.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Lucius Cassius Fortunatus lived 70 years.
EDCS-22900110.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Cassius Fortunatus, who lived 70 years.

EDCS-22900111.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Aulus Cossinius Iucundus lived [number of] years.
EDCS-22900111.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Aulus Cossinius Iucundus, with the age missing.

EDCS-22900112.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Quintus Iulius Crispinus, named Celerius, a boy of excellent disposition, snatched away in his tender age, lived 13 years, 11 months, and 12 days.
EDCS-22900112.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Quintus Iulius Crispinus (also called Celerius), a boy who died at the age of 13.

EDCS-22900113.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Issidba, who lived 30 years.

EDCS-22900114.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Magnia made [this].
EDCS-22900114.summary: This is a funerary epitaph, possibly a dedication by Magnia.

EDCS-22900115.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Pomponius Saturninus, who lived 25 years.

EDCS-22900116.translation: Vales Nicois lived 35 years; he is here.
EDCS-22900116.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Vales Nicois, who lived 35 years.

EDCS-22900120.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the death of an individual after 21 years.

EDCS-22900122.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Titus Aelius Saturninus lived 32 years. His father made [this].
EDCS-22900122.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Titus Aelius Saturninus, who lived 32 years, dedicated by his father.

EDCS-22900127.translation: Hermias lived 80 years. Aelius Getulicus Quintasius.
EDCS-22900127.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Hermias, with a possible dedicant or second individual named Aelius Getulicus Quintasius.

EDCS-22900128.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Aelia Ianuaria lived 80 years. Sacred to the departed spirits. Aelia IA lived 4 years. Publius Aelius Narcissus made this for his parents.
EDCS-22900128.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespans of Aelia Ianuaria and Aelia IA, dedicated by Publius Aelius Narcissus to his parents.

EDCS-22900129.translation: Labrius Euforion lived 75 years. Flavia Donata made this for her husband and for Labrius Eucarus Eucarus Optabilis, his most dutiful father, while they were alive.
EDCS-22900129.summary: This is a funerary inscription detailing the lifespan of Labrius Euforion and commissioned by Flavia Donata for her husband and father-in-law.

EDCS-22900130.translation: crius Barici lived 70 years, with his wife attending to the arrangements.
EDCS-22900130.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespan of crius Barici, with his wife overseeing the burial arrangements.

EDCS-22900131.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Flavia Ianuaria lived 39 years.
EDCS-22900131.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Flavia Ianuaria.

EDCS-22900132.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. ntius Germanianus lived 20 years and 4 months; he rests here.
EDCS-22900132.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespan of ntius Germanianus and states that he rests here.

EDCS-22900133.translation: Marcus Magnius Donatus lived 60 years; his wife took care of the arrangements.
EDCS-22900133.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespan of Marcus Magnius Donatus, with his wife overseeing the burial arrangements.

EDCS-22900134.translation: Iulia Cattula, dutiful, 2 children. Caius Marius Secundus, dutiful, lived 80 years. CE MT I I.
EDCS-22900134.summary: This inscription records the lifespans and family details of Iulia Cattula and Caius Marius Secundus.

EDCS-22900135.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Numisia Mevia lived 80 years, for her dearest daughter. Martialis, her husband.
EDCS-22900135.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespan of Numisia Mevia and is dedicated by her husband, Martialis, for their daughter.

EDCS-22900136.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Saturnia lived 36 years. Vibius Gigans made this for his wife, so that she would not forget him.
EDCS-22900136.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespan of Saturnia and was made by her husband, Vibius Gigans, with a request for remembrance.

EDCS-22900137.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Marcus Calpurnius Regulus lived 4 years and 1 month.
EDCS-22900137.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the age of death of Marcus Calpurnius Regulus, likely for a child.

EDCS-22900138.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Caius Gessius Dativus lived...
EDCS-22900138.summary: This is a funerary epitaph, now incomplete, recording the name of Caius Gessius Dativus and the beginning of his age at death.

EDCS-22900139.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Publius Aulus Victor Boicin(us) lived 70 years; his sons made (this).
EDCS-22900139.summary: This is a funerary epitaph where sons dedicated a monument to their father, Publius Aulus Victor Boicin(us), who lived 70 years.

EDCS-22900140.translation: Felix, son of Victor, grandson of Speron.
EDCS-22900140.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the name and lineage of Felix.

EDCS-22900141.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Macus Tunini lived 70 years and Venusta lived 90 years; their sons made (this).
EDCS-22900141.summary: This is a funerary epitaph where sons dedicated a monument to their parents, Macus Tunini (70 years) and Venusta (90 years).

EDCS-22900142.translation: Tunninus lived 85 years; Victoria lived 70 years.
EDCS-22900142.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the ages at death of Tunninus (85 years) and Victoria (70 years).

EDCS-22900143.translation: To the Divine Spirits. His sons made (this) for their mother Getulia, who lived 70 years. To the Divine Spirits. Victor lived 85 years, 3 months, and 5 days; his sons made this monument for him, under the care of N...
EDCS-22900143.summary: This is a complex funerary inscription with separate dedications for Getulia (70 years) and Victor (85 years, 3 months, 5 days), both by their sons.

EDCS-23100011.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Caius Iulius Cai filius Norbanus, perpetual priest and veteran, lived 85 years.
EDCS-23100011.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Caius Iulius Norbanus, who served as a perpetual priest and veteran, and lived 85 years.

EDCS-23100012.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Lucius Granius Rogati filius Honoratus, of the Quirina tribe, lived 70 years.
EDCS-23100012.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Granius Honoratus, a member of the Quirina tribe, who lived 70 years.

EDCS-23100013.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Iulius Paulus lived 75 years. To the Divine Spirits. Iulia Marciosa lived 25 years.
EDCS-23100013.summary: This funerary inscription records the ages at death for two individuals, Iulius Paulus (75 years) and Iulia Marciosa (25 years).

EDCS-23100014.translation: To the Divine Shades. Tiberius Claudius Urbanus erected this for his most dutiful mother, Julia Quinta, repaying her piety.
EDCS-23100014.summary: A son honors his mother with a funerary monument.

EDCS-23100015.summary: A tombstone records the lifespan of Lia Marcia.

EDCS-23100016.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Aelia lived 51 years. Caius Vibius Urbanus lived 86 years.
EDCS-23100016.summary: A funerary monument records the lifespans of two individuals, Aelia and Caius Vibius Urbanus.

EDCS-23100017.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. D. Iulia Spes lived X years.
EDCS-23100017.summary: A funerary inscription records the name and lifespan of D. Iulia Spes.

EDCS-23100018.translation: Sexti Iuli, who was also called Puia, lived 45 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-23100018.summary: A tombstone records the name, alias, lifespan, and burial place of Sexti Iuli (Puia).

EDCS-23100019.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Caesia Gennila the pious lived 115 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-23100019.summary: A tombstone records the name, piety, lifespan, and burial place of Caesia Gennila.

EDCS-23100020.translation: Through Christ, near the martyrs, Felix, father, you have worthy rewards of your excellent life, and your fame resounds with perpetual renown and your praise is approved by common voice. Pomponianus, who lived a fortunate 78 years, [erected this] with kind heart to all, [showing] love in [his] prayer.
EDCS-23100020.summary: A Christian funerary inscription by Pomponianus for Felix, mentioning his virtuous life and praising him.

EDCS-23100309.summary: A tombstone records the lifespan of Flavia Florentina.

EDCS-23100310.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Marcus Octavius Marcutius lived 45 years. Emerita, his devoted wife, made this for her deserving husband.
EDCS-23100310.summary: A wife, Emerita, dedicated a funerary monument to her husband, Marcus Octavius Marcutius.

EDCS-23100311.translation: To the departed spirits, Popilia Fortunata lived 40 years.
EDCS-23100311.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Popilia Fortunata.

EDCS-23100312.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Valerius S lived 82 years. Sacred to the departed spirits. Vibia Spicula lived 70 years.
EDCS-23100312.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespans of Valerius S and Vibia Spicula.

EDCS-23100313.translation: May you use it happily, may you buy from there.
EDCS-23100313.summary: This is a very brief inscription, possibly related to a shop or market stall, wishing prosperity to users and buyers.

EDCS-23200231.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Nonia Tertula lived [X] years. Sacred to the departed spirits. Rogatae lived 65 years.
EDCS-23200231.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan of Rogatae and mentions Nonia Tertula.

EDCS-23200232.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus C Aurelius lived 3 years. Quintus S placed [this] for his most devoted son; he lies here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus C Commodus lived 6 years. Quintus S placed [this] for his most devoted son; he lies here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulia Gemellina lived 32 years. Quintus S placed [this] for his incomparable wife; she lies here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulia Donata lived 27 years. Quintus S placed [this] for his most obedient sister-in-law; she lies here.
EDCS-23200232.summary: This complex funerary monument records the deaths of Quintus C Aurelius, Quintus C Commodus, Iulia Gemellina, and Iulia Donata, all seemingly related to Quintus S, likely a father and brother-in-law.

EDCS-23200233.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Domitia Victoria lived 31 years. Domitius, her devoted son and heir, placed [this].
EDCS-23200233.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan of Domitia Victoria and its dedication by her son and heir.

EDCS-23200234.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Nunnia Iulia lived 15 years; she lies here. Her devoted father placed [this].
EDCS-23200234.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan of Nunnia Iulia and its dedication by her father.

EDCS-23200235.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Caius Iulius Crispinus lived 19 years. His devoted father placed [this].
EDCS-23200235.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan of Caius Iulius Crispinus and its dedication by his father.

EDCS-23200236.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Caius Iulius Crispus lived 99 years. His devoted sons placed [this].
EDCS-23200236.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan of Caius Iulius Crispus and its dedication by his sons.

EDCS-23200237.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Flavia Venusta lived 123 years. Her son and grandson [dedicated this]. Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcus Iulius Crispus lived 65 years. His son placed [this] for his devoted father; he lies here.
EDCS-23200237.summary: This funerary monument records the lifespans of Flavia Venusta and Marcus Iulius Crispus, with dedications by their descendants.

EDCS-23200238.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Gaius Julius Saturninus lived 75 years. His son placed this for his most dutiful father. He lies here.
EDCS-23200238.summary: A son erected a tombstone for his devoted father, Gaius Julius Saturninus, who lived to be 75.

EDCS-23200247.text_edition: \n Iuliae Flaviae Herenniae Caeciliae Honoratianae Optatae clarissimae puellae filiae Flavi Pollionis Flaviani clarissimi viri curatoris rei publicae praetoris kandidati decreto decurionum pecunia publica\n
EDCS-23200247.translation: By decree of the decurions, at public expense, to Julia Flavia Herennia Caecilia Honoratiana Optata, most illustrious girl, daughter of Flavius Pollio Flavianus, most illustrious man, curator of the state, candidate for praetor.
EDCS-23200247.summary: This inscription records a public dedication to Julia Flavia Herennia Caecilia Honoratiana Optata, a young girl, daughter of a prominent official.

EDCS-23200248.summary: A funerary dedication to a son named Quintilius.

EDCS-23200253.translation: For Rufus, son of Quintus Julius Caius, of the Quirina tribe, decorated with equestrian military distinctions; first of all patrons. He lived 55 years. The Iulii are buried here, for services well rendered.
EDCS-23200253.summary: A monument dedicated to Rufus, son of Quintus Julius Caius, a man of equestrian rank and a patron, who lived 55 years.

EDCS-23200256.translation: Priest of the divinity, all... A T V T O T A N...
EDCS-23200256.summary: An inscription referencing a priest of a divinity, with partial text remaining.

EDCS-23200257.translation: Sacred to the departed gods. Aecia the pious lived 14 years. Mapalicus set this up for his daughter. She rests here.
EDCS-23200257.summary: This is a tombstone recording the death of Aecia, a 14-year-old girl, set up by her father Mapalicus.

EDCS-23200258.translation: Sacred to the departed gods. Aelia Cyrpe, also called Eutycia, lived 42 years. Her husband set [this up] for his wife.
EDCS-23200258.summary: This is a tombstone recording the death of Aelia Cyrpe (also known as Eutycia), who lived 42 years, set up by her husband.

EDCS-23200260.translation: Aemilius Ianuarius placed this for his uncle out of dutiful affection. He lived 35 years. He lies here.
EDCS-23200260.summary: An uncle, Aemilius Ianuarius, erected a tombstone for his nephew, who lived 35 years.

EDCS-23200261.translation: Sacred to the departed gods. Aemilia Marcella the pious lived 7 years. [...] Romanus [...] rests here.
EDCS-23200261.summary: This is a tombstone recording the death of Aemilia Marcella, a child of seven years, with partial information about a relative.

EDCS-23200262.translation: Sacred to the departed gods. Marcus Antonius Concessus lived 95 years. He rests here. // Sacred to the departed gods. [...] lived [...] years. Marcus Antonius Concessus set [this up] for his most beloved wife.
EDCS-23200262.summary: This inscription is a double tombstone, first recording the death of Marcus Antonius Concessus at 95, and then a second dedication by him to his wife.

EDCS-23200263.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Malia Modia lived 43 years. She lies here. Arranius Felix made this for his wife. Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Arranius Felix lived 50 years.
EDCS-23200263.summary: Arranius Felix dedicated a tomb to his wife Malia Modia, who lived 43 years, and also recorded his own lifespan of 50 years.

EDCS-23200264.translation: Sacred to the departed gods. Arrania Sperata lived [3 years, 3 months] [...]. [...] her most beloved and pious daughter made this. She rests here.
EDCS-23200264.summary: This is a tombstone recording the death of Arrania Sperata, with partial details of her age and a dedication by her daughter.

EDCS-23200265.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Asidonia Victoria lived 65 years and is buried here; her sons placed this. To the Spirits of the Departed. Asidonius December lived 70 years and is buried here; his sons placed this.
EDCS-23200265.summary: This inscription records two separate burials for Asidonia Victoria and Asidonius December, with their respective sons acting as dedicants, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-23200266.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Marcus Assidonius Marianus, pious, lived [X] years and is buried here; Iu[3]O placed [this] for [his] pious [father].
EDCS-23200266.summary: This funerary inscription honors Marcus Assidonius Marianus, who lived an unknown number of years and was memorialized by his son, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-23200267.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Lucius Atilius Maioricus lived 40 years. Atilius Faustianus placed this for his dearest brother; he is buried here. To the Spirits of the Departed. [X] Atilius Clodianus lived 23 years; his son placed [this]; he is buried here.
EDCS-23200267.summary: This inscription contains two funerary notices, one for Lucius Atilius Maioricus commemorating his brother Atilius Faustianus, and another for Atilius Clodianus memorialized by his son, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-23200270.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. For Gaius Natus.
EDCS-23200270.summary: A funerary dedication to Gaius Natus, sacred to the spirits of the underworld.

EDCS-23200271.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. C() Pescenia lived 2 years and is buried here; Ianuarius placed this for his daughter. To the Spirits of the Departed. Augendus lived 4 years and is buried here.
EDCS-23200271.summary: This inscription records the burial of two young children, C() Pescenia and Augendus, with Ianuarius dedicating the former and likely a parent the latter, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-23200272.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Titus Caecilius Macer, son of Caius, of the tribe Quirina, lived 20 years and is buried here.
EDCS-23200272.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Titus Caecilius Macer, a young man who died at the age of 20, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-23200273.translation: [IA] sis. Caelius Respectulus, his grandson, placed this. He lies here.
EDCS-23200273.summary: A grandson, Caelius Respectulus, erected a monument for his relative, identified by the partial name IA[---]sis.

EDCS-23200274.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Aemilia Restutula lived 21 years and is buried here. To the Spirits of the Departed. Caelius Marius lived 60 years; Claudia Donata placed this for her husband.
EDCS-23200274.summary: This inscription records two burials: Aemilia Restutula and Caelius Marius, the latter memorialized by his wife Claudia Donata, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-23200276.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. For Caelia Octavia, who lived [X]3 years and 10 months, and is buried here, [3]ius Aq[3]/[3]s placed [this] for [his] most chaste and dearest wife.
EDCS-23200276.summary: This funerary inscription honors Caelia Octavia, who died at the age of 30-something and was memorialized by her husband, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-23200277.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Caninia Verecunda Italica lived 21 years and is buried here; Pompeius Aemilianus placed this for his incomparable wife. To the Spirits of the Departed. Pompeia Fortunata lived 27 years and is buried here; her pious father placed [this].
EDCS-23200277.summary: This inscription records two burials: Caninia Verecunda Italica, memorialized by her husband, and Pompeia Fortunata, memorialized by her father, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-23200278.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Cutullus lived 48 years and is buried here; his pious sister placed [this].
EDCS-23200278.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Cutullus, who died at the age of 48, and was memorialized by his sister, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-23200279.translation: Quintus Cornelius Inminus, his father, placed this for his son. He lived... FIDE...
EDCS-23200279.summary: A father, Quintus Cornelius Inminus, erected a monument for his son, with partially preserved details.

EDCS-23200280.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Iulia Memoria lived 25 years and is buried here; Iulius Secundianus placed [this] for his dearest mother. To the Spirits of the Departed. Publius Cornelius Massuricus lived 3 years and 5 months; Caius Massuricus, his pious father, placed [this] for his son. Aelia Crescentia lived 70 years and is buried here; Cornelius Massuricus placed [this].
EDCS-23200280.summary: This inscription records three burials: Iulia Memoria memorialized by her son, Publius Cornelius Massuricus by his father Caius Massuricus, and Aelia Crescentia by Cornelius Massuricus, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-23200281.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Publius Cornelius Secundianus lived 5 years and is buried here. Iulius Saturninus placed [this] for his pious son. Sacred to the departed spirits. Publius Cornelius Victor, also called Massuricus, lived 46 years and is buried here. Iulia Saturnina placed [this] for her pious husband. Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulia Prima lived 15 years and is buried here. Iulia Saturnina placed [this] for her devoted foster-daughter.
EDCS-23200281.summary: This is a triple tombstone recording the deaths of three individuals, Publius Cornelius Secundianus, Publius Cornelius Victor, and Iulia Prima, with dedications by family members.

EDCS-23200282.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Concordia Pia lived 7 years and 7 months. Ianuarius placed [this] for his pious daughter and she is buried here.
EDCS-23200282.summary: This tombstone records the death of Concordia Pia, who lived 7 years and 7 months, and was dedicated by her father Ianuarius.

EDCS-23200284.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Clodia Secunda lived 20 years and is buried here. Iulius Maximus Barda placed [this] for his pious wife.
EDCS-23200284.summary: This tombstone records the death of Clodia Secunda, who lived 20 years, and was dedicated by her husband Iulius Maximus Barda.

EDCS-23200285.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Clodia Dativa, most chaste woman, lived 36 years. She lies here. Clodius Libosus made this eternal home for his most rare wife.
EDCS-23200285.summary: Clodius Libosus dedicated a tomb to his "most rare" wife, Clodia Dativa, who lived 36 years.

EDCS-23200286.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Steia Donatula and Rupila lived 50 years and are buried here. Titus Lartius Quintulus placed [this] for his most devoted wife.
EDCS-23200286.summary: This tombstone records the death of Steia Donatula (with a partial name Rupila), who lived 50 years, and was dedicated by her husband Titus Lartius Quintulus.

EDCS-23200287.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Fabia Secunda lived 16 years and is buried here. Her parents placed [this] for their sweetest daughter. Na[---] lived [---] years.
EDCS-23200287.summary: This tombstone records the death of Fabia Secunda, who lived 16 years, and was dedicated by her parents, with a second, incomplete inscription for another individual.

EDCS-23200288.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulia Aemiliana lived 48 years and is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus Fannius Longinus lived 52 years and is buried here.
EDCS-23200288.summary: This is a double tombstone recording the deaths of Iulia Aemiliana (aged 48) and Quintus Fannius Longinus (aged 52).

EDCS-23200289.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Flavia Dativa lived 60 years. Flavia Restuta placed [this] for her dearest sister. I, Flavia Restuta, and Flavia Pulla [dedicated this].
EDCS-23200289.summary: This tombstone records the death of Flavia Dativa, who lived 60 years, and was dedicated by her sister Flavia Restuta and Flavia Pulla.

EDCS-23200290.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. [Munatius Quintasius lived ---] years and is buried here. [---] placed [this] for his pious [---]. Sacred to the departed spirits. Flavia Cai Piscenila lived 25 years and 4 months and is buried here. Munatius Quintasius placed [this] for his dearest wife.
EDCS-23200290.summary: This is a double tombstone recording the deaths of an unnamed individual who died sometime after Munatius Quintasius and Flavia Cai Piscenila, who lived 25 years and 4 months and was dedicated by her husband Munatius Quintasius.

EDCS-23200291.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Geminius Felix lived 51 years and 12 [months---].
EDCS-23200291.summary: This tombstone records the death of Geminius Felix, who lived 51 years and 12 months, with an incomplete dedication.

EDCS-23200292.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Germanus lived [---] years.
EDCS-23200292.summary: This tombstone records the death of Germanus, with an incomplete lifespan and dedication.

EDCS-23200293.translation: To the Divine Shades. Lucius Helvius Donatus lived for [3] years; he is buried here. His most devoted sons erected this.
EDCS-23200293.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Helvius Donatus, erected by his sons, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-23200294.text_edition: \n Barasi X X X Dis Manibus sacrum Quintus Iulius Bucianus vixi interim annis LXXII de bonis X\n
EDCS-23200294.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Quintus Iulius Bucianus lived for 72 years. [Erected] from his own property.
EDCS-23200294.summary: A funerary inscription recording the death of Quintus Iulius Bucianus, who lived to 72 and whose monument was funded by his own means, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-23200295.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Caius Iulius Donatus lived for 22 years; his parents placed him here, a pious son.
EDCS-23200295.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Caius Iulius Donatus, who died at 22 and was commemorated by his parents, probably from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-23200296.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Pudentilla lived for 85 years. Her dearest daughter made [this] for her mother. Sacred to the Divine Shades. Caius Iulius Felix lived for 82 years and 7 months. Unworthily, Felix, you left life; you should have lived for almost 100 years. May the earth be light on you, if the shades exist. He is buried here. His dearest wife.
EDCS-23200296.summary: This complex inscription records the deaths of Pudentilla, commemorated by her daughter, and Caius Iulius Felix, whose monument was erected by his wife, with laments about his premature death, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-23200297.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Gaius Julius Fortunatus lived 10 years, is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Gaius Julius Mesius lived 60 years, is buried here. His devoted wife placed this. Sacred to the departed spirits.
EDCS-23200297.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lives and burial of two individuals, Gaius Julius Fortunatus and Gaius Julius Mesius, with the latter's epitaph placed by his devoted wife.

EDCS-23200298.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulius Fortunatianus lived 13 years. His husband placed this for his spouse.
EDCS-23200298.summary: This funerary epitaph records the life of Iulius Fortunatianus, who lived 13 years, and was placed by his husband.

EDCS-23200299.translation: To Iulius Gallonius, after seventy years, and after he had lived as many autumns. Three born to you. We fix for you, a good father, this tomb which seems to be pleasing. My dear mother urges that this honor of death be made for you. Farewell now, father, having left us. Now the cruel underworld will not hold you, but the Elysian field has taken you, from which it is now right for you to return. As a good and upright father, he is buried here.
EDCS-23200299.summary: This epitaph is a poetic dedication to a father named Iulius Gallonius, celebrating his long life and good character, and expressing grief at his passing and hope for his afterlife.

EDCS-23200300.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Flavia Ingenua lived 30 years, is buried here. Her son placed this for his mother. Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulia Redducta lived 12 years, is buried here. Her brother placed this for his pious sister. Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulius Iubeus Fortunatus lived 40 years. Iulius Nundinarius placed this for his father.
EDCS-23200300.summary: This funerary inscription contains three separate epitaphs, recording the lives and burials of Flavia Ingenua, Iulia Redducta, and Iulius Iubeus Fortunatus, with familial dedications.

EDCS-23200301.translation: In memory. Sacred to the departed spirits. Gaius Iulius Memorialis lived 50 years, is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulia Bonosa lived 63 years, is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulius Saturninus lived 30 years, is buried here.
EDCS-23200301.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lives and burials of three individuals: Gaius Iulius Memorialis, Iulia Bonosa, and Iulius Saturninus.

EDCS-23200302.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulia lived 30 years, is buried here. Her parents placed this for their dearest daughter.
EDCS-23200302.summary: This funerary epitaph records the life of Iulia, who lived 30 years, and was placed by her parents.

EDCS-23200303.translation: Iulia Casta lived for 36 years and 9 months. Iuli[...]. Vic[...]
EDCS-23200303.summary: This is a fragment of a funerary epitaph for Iulia Casta, recording her lifespan of 36 years and 9 months, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-23200304.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulia Restuta the pious lived 36 years. Gaius Iulius Annianus placed this for his pious daughter. She is buried here.
EDCS-23200304.summary: This funerary epitaph records the life of Iulia Restuta, who lived 36 years, and was placed by her father, Gaius Iulius Annianus.

EDCS-23200305.translation: Iulia Romana placed this for her dutiful son.
EDCS-23200305.summary: This funerary epitaph is a dedication placed by Iulia Romana for her dutiful son.

EDCS-23200306.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulia Silvana the pious lived 30 years, is buried here. Quintus Caecilius Primatus placed this for his most rare and modest wife.
EDCS-23200306.summary: This funerary epitaph records the life of Iulia Silvana, who lived 30 years, and was placed by her husband, Quintus Caecilius Primatus.

EDCS-23200307.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus Laetorius Conventalis merited for himself from himself. Sacred to the departed spirits. Memmia Rufina merited for herself from herself, placed now by the cohort. Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus La [---] Vigi
EDCS-23200307.summary: This funerary inscription records three individuals, Quintus Laetorius Conventalis, Memmia Rufina, and Quintus La [---] Vigi, with the latter two possibly associated with a cohort and indicating self-dedication or posthumous honors.

EDCS-23200308.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Libosa lived 20 years, here she lies. Manilius Frutuosus placed [this] for his devoted wife.
EDCS-23200308.summary: A tombstone for Libosa, erected by her husband Manilius Frutuosus, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-23200309.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. M. lived 80 years. Pr. Marcianus placed [this] for his devoted mother. Here she lies.
EDCS-23200309.summary: A tombstone for an unnamed mother, erected by her son Pr. Marcianus, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-23200310.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Quintus Magnius Peregrinus lived 77 years, here he lies. His freedmen erected [this] for their devoted patron.
EDCS-23200310.summary: A tombstone for Quintus Magnius Peregrinus, erected by his freedmen, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-23200311.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Caius Marius Cassio Pius lived 75 years. Gnaeus his son erected [this] for his most devoted father. Here he lies.
EDCS-23200311.summary: A tombstone for Caius Marius Cassio Pius, erected by his son Gnaeus, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-23200312.translation: [This] for his dearest sister. [He/She] lived 51 years. Maurusius erected [this].
EDCS-23200312.summary: A tombstone for an unnamed sister, erected by Maurusius, possibly dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-23200313.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Memmius Martalis lived 40 years. Caecilia Donata placed [this] for her husband. Here he lies.
EDCS-23200313.summary: A tombstone for Memmius Martalis, erected by his wife Caecilia Donata, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-23200314.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Neria Primigenia lived 70 years. Here she lies. I sought a fair resting place and joyful repose; my son, who was dear to me, wished [this] to be done. Her devoted son erected [this] for his dear mother.
EDCS-23200314.summary: A tombstone for Neria Primigenia, erected by her son, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-23200315.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Tertullus lived 71 years. Here he lies. Nonius Victor his son erected [this] for his devoted father.
EDCS-23200315.summary: A tombstone for Tertullus, erected by his son Nonius Victor, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-23200316.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Maxima lived 21 years. Here she lies. Pompeius Attus her husband erected [this].
EDCS-23200316.summary: A tombstone for Maxima, erected by her husband Pompeius Attus, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-23200317.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Pomponia lived 4 years. Here she lies. Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Pomponia Celsina lived 9 years. Here she lies. Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Aelia Tallusa lived 73 years. Here she lies. Her devoted daughter and son-in-law erected [this].
EDCS-23200317.summary: A tombstone recording the deaths of three individuals: Pomponia (4), Pomponia Celsina (9), and Aelia Tallusa (73), erected by Aelia Tallusa's daughter and son-in-law, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-23200318.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Prima lived piously for 1 year and 2 months. Fortunatus placed [this] for his pious daughter. Sacred to the departed spirits. Concordia lived piously for 37 years; she is laid here.
EDCS-23200318.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Prima and Concordia, placed by Fortunatus for his daughter, and recording their ages at death.

EDCS-23200319.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Sira Pudentilla lived piously for 15 years; she is laid here. Onnus Ades placed [this].
EDCS-23200319.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Sira Pudentilla, who died at age 15, placed by Onnus Ades.

EDCS-23200320.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Racilius Restutus lived for 53 years; he is laid here. Socra placed [this].
EDCS-23200320.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Racilius Restutus, who died at age 53, placed by Socra.

EDCS-23200321.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Refria Victorina lived for 22 years. Refrius N [placed this].
EDCS-23200321.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Refria Victorina, who died at age 22, likely placed by Refrius.

EDCS-23200322.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Restitutus lived for many years; he is laid here for his dearest, pious son.
EDCS-23200322.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Restitutus, placed by his parents for their very dear and pious son.

EDCS-23200323.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Rutunda lived piously for 87 years; she is laid here.
EDCS-23200323.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Rutunda, who died at age 87.

EDCS-23200325.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Domitia Fortunata lived for 85 years; her pious sons placed [this]. Sacred to the departed spirits. Publius Servilius Donatus lived for 60 years; his pious wife placed [this] for her husband.
EDCS-23200325.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Domitia Fortunata, placed by her sons, and for Publius Servilius Donatus, placed by his wife, recording their ages at death.

EDCS-23200326.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Ispesina lived for 20 years; she is laid here. Her pious husband placed [this].
EDCS-23200326.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Ispesina, who died at age 20, placed by her pious husband.

EDCS-23200327.summary: This is a very brief inscription, likely a funerary dedication placed by Successus.

EDCS-23200328.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Titia Tertullina lived for 14 years; she is laid here.
EDCS-23200328.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Titia Tertullina, who died at age 14.

EDCS-23200329.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Trahia lived 50 years. Her devoted wife set this up.
EDCS-23200329.summary: A funerary dedication for Trahia, set up by her wife, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-23200330.summary: A funerary dedication for Lucius Valerius Fructuosus, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-23200331.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Furnia Felicula lived 70 years and is buried here. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Lucius Valerius Severus lived 102 years and is buried here. Furnia A [---]
EDCS-23200331.summary: A double funerary dedication, likely for members of the same family, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-23200332.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Valeria Ingenua lived 40 years and is buried here. Caius Caelius Lupercus set this up for his devoted wife.
EDCS-23200332.summary: A funerary dedication for Valeria Ingenua, set up by her husband Caius Caelius Lupercus, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-23200333.translation: Victorinus Felicianus for his dearest sister.
EDCS-23200333.summary: A dedication for a sister by Victorinus Felicianus, the exact nature of the monument is unclear but it is likely funerary, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-23200334.translation: Vitalis lived 3 years and 3 months. Publius Pe[---] set this up. He is buried here.
EDCS-23200334.summary: A funerary dedication for a child named Vitalis, set up by Publius Pe[---], likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-23200335.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Fervida, while she could, played [---]
EDCS-23200335.summary: A funerary dedication for Fervida, the full context of which is lost, but suggests a life that was enjoyed, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-23200336.translation: [---]rius, son of Caius, a devoted father.
EDCS-23200336.summary: A fragment of an inscription, possibly a funerary dedication or a description of a status, referring to a 'devoted father', likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-23200337.translation: [...]uriia [...]onilla [lived for] 1 year and 11 months. She is buried here.
EDCS-23200337.summary: A fragmentary funerary epitaph recording the burial of a child named possibly Uriia/Onilla who lived for 1 year and 11 months, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-23200339.translation: Nepotianus set this up for his very dear brother.
EDCS-23200339.summary: A dedication for a brother by Nepotianus, likely funerary, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-23200351.summary: A funerary dedication for a child named Baza, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-23200352.summary: This is a simple funerary epitaph for Charaeha.

EDCS-23200353.translation: Festa rested in peace on the eighth day before the Kalends of March in the fourteenth year of the reign of King Thrasamund.
EDCS-23200353.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the death of Festa during the reign of King Thrasamund.

EDCS-23200354.translation: Life is good and death is evil, holding neither of these; understand, if you are wise, which is more beneficial. But since the Manes exist, may the earth be light for you. Iulia Lucilla, daughter of Titus, lived 14 years and 5 months. From which time she lived 18 months and 30 days until her death. Fabius Exsuperantius made this for his innocent, devout wife.
EDCS-23200354.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Iulia Lucilla, detailing her age at death and commemorating her devotion, with her husband Fabius Exsuperantius as the dedicator.

EDCS-23200356.translation: Materna lived 60 years and rested on the Kalends of September.
EDCS-23200356.summary: This funerary epitaph records the death of Materna, including her age and date of rest.

EDCS-23200359.translation: Flavius Amon, faithful, lived for [X] years.
EDCS-23200359.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Flavius Amon, indicating his faithfulness and age at death.

EDCS-23200362.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Musa lived 21 years, here she lies. Her mother Pompeia Successa placed this.
EDCS-23200362.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Musa, erected by her mother Pompeia Successa, and it includes her age at death.

EDCS-23200363.translation: To the Divine Manes. Messia Fortunata, daughter of Caius, devout, lived for [X] years. Here she lies.
EDCS-23200363.summary: This funerary epitaph records the death of Messia Fortunata, daughter of Caius, noting her piety and age at death.

EDCS-23200365.translation: Quintius Ingenuus lived 98 years, here he lies. His son placed this.
EDCS-23200365.summary: This funerary epitaph records the death of Quintius Ingenuus, noting his age and that it was erected by his son.

EDCS-23200368.translation: Caius Coelius Victor began the arch, which he promised to his fatherland out of his own generosity in his year of aedileship; the duumvir dedicated it.
EDCS-23200368.summary: This inscription records the construction and dedication of a public arch by Caius Coelius Victor during his term as aedile.

EDCS-23200405.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Cornelia Ingenua lived 30 years, here she lies.
EDCS-23200405.summary: This funerary epitaph records the death of Cornelia Ingenua, stating her age and location of burial.

EDCS-23200406.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Gaius Minius Iunius lived 65 years.
EDCS-23200406.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the death of Gaius Minius Iunius after living 65 years.

EDCS-23200407.translation: Lucius Caecilius Martialis lived 11 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-23200407.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Lucius Caecilius Martialis at the age of 11.

EDCS-23200408.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Maxima Pia lived 24 years. Helenus and Aquilina, freedmen of Augustus, made this for their most dutiful daughter and for themselves, taken from the light.
EDCS-23200408.summary: This funerary inscription records that Helenus and Aquilina, freedmen of Augustus, dedicated this monument to their daughter Maxima Pia, who died at 24.

EDCS-23200411.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Asellia Optata lived 70 years. Lucceius Rogatus made this for his wife. She is buried here.
EDCS-23200411.summary: This funerary inscription records that Lucceius Rogatus dedicated this monument to his wife Asellia Optata, who lived 70 years.

EDCS-23200412.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Publius Cacius Optatus lived 61 years.
EDCS-23200412.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the death of Publius Cacius Optatus after living 61 years.

EDCS-23200413.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Marcus Cestius Optatus lived 52 years.
EDCS-23200413.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the death of Marcus Cestius Optatus after living 52 years.

EDCS-23200414.translation: Iulius Calventius lived 55 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-23200414.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Iulius Calventius at the age of 55.

EDCS-23200415.summary: This is a very brief inscription, possibly a funerary epitaph, honoring Marcus Lucceius Rogatus.

EDCS-23200416.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Curtia Fronima, dutiful, lived 26 years. Domitius Crepereianus placed this for his most unique wife. She is buried here.
EDCS-23200416.summary: This funerary inscription records that Domitius Crepereianus dedicated this monument to his wife Curtia Fronima, who died at 26.

EDCS-23200417.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Gaius Gentius Extricatus lived 97 years. His dutiful son made this. IA us Fo ua lived 65 years. His son made this.
EDCS-23200417.summary: This funerary inscription records the deaths of Gaius Gentius Extricatus (age 97) and IA us Fo ua (age 65), both with monuments dedicated by their dutiful sons.

EDCS-23200418.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Varia Fortunata, also called Monna, who lived for 43 years, diligent in every respect and of moderate character, Publius Magnius Pontianus, son of Caius, set up for his well-deserving wife; she is buried here.
EDCS-23200418.summary: A funerary epitaph for Varia Fortunata, set up by her husband, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-23200419.translation: Here lies. Pious brothers set up for their brother, 13 years old. Pious parents set up.
EDCS-23200419.summary: A fragmented funerary inscription likely recording the burial of a young boy, set up by his siblings and parents.

EDCS-23200420.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Maria Rogata, daughter of Lucius, dutiful, lived for 75 years. She is buried here. Her dutiful husband set [it] up.
EDCS-23200420.summary: A funerary epitaph for Maria Rogata, set up by her husband, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-23200421.summary: A brief funerary epitaph recording the age of Aphrodisia.

EDCS-23200422.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Aelia Urbana lived for 85 years. Caius Caesius Bonus Gallonius is buried here. Caesius A set [it] up for his incomparable brother, who lived for 60 years.
EDCS-23200422.summary: A funerary epitaph for Aelia Urbana and Caesius Bonus Gallonius, set up by the latter for his brother, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-23200423.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Rogatus. Sacred to the departed spirits. Clodius Lucius Clusus, freedman of Lucius, M [5?] V [5?].
EDCS-23200423.summary: A fragmented inscription to the departed spirits, possibly a funerary dedication, with names including Rogatus, Clodius Lucius Clusus, and numerical indications possibly related to age or status.

EDCS-23200424.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Maximia Felicitas lived for 25 years.
EDCS-23200424.summary: A funerary epitaph for Maximia Felicitas, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-23200425.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Monument for Serdon Sanis, who lived for 14 years.
EDCS-23200425.summary: A funerary epitaph for Serdon Sanis, likely a child, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-23200426.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Tonneia Faustina lived for 60 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-23200426.summary: A funerary epitaph for Tonneia Faustina, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-23200429.translation: To the great-grandson of the deified Nerva.
EDCS-23200429.summary: An inscription honoring a descendant of the Roman Emperor Nerva, likely a dedication or commemorative marker.

EDCS-23200431.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Antonia Secundina lived for 36 years. Caius Cornelius Victor [dedicates this] to his wife.
EDCS-23200431.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Antonia Secundina, dedicated by her husband Caius Cornelius Victor.

EDCS-23200432.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Pompeia Tice lived for 20 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-23200432.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Pompeia Tice, recording her age and burial.

EDCS-23200433.summary: This is a fragmented funerary epitaph recording an age.

EDCS-23200434.translation: In memory of Caius Iunius Faustinus Postumianus, consul, governor of the provinces of Hispania and Britannia. Iunius Flaccus and Paulina [dedicate this] to their most loving father.
EDCS-23200434.summary: This is a funerary dedication from Iunius Flaccus and Paulina to their father, Caius Iunius Faustinus Postumianus, a former consul and governor, likely from the 3rd century CE.

EDCS-23200435.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Fortunatus Natalis, son of PI BI II CON.
EDCS-23200435.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Fortunatus Natalis, son of PI BI II CON, the meaning of the abbreviation is unclear.

EDCS-23200437.translation: Aurelius Aristobulus, proconsul of Africa, [acting] through the intervention of Caius Macrinus Sossianus, clarissimus vir, legate.
EDCS-23200437.summary: This inscription records an action taken by the proconsul of Africa, Aurelius Aristobulus, at the request of the legate Caius Macrinus Sossianus.

EDCS-23200440.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Flavius Felix.
EDCS-23200440.summary: This is a funerary epitaph simply stating the name Flavius Felix.

EDCS-23200441.summary: This is a simple inscription identifying Secundus as the son of Felix.

EDCS-23200443.translation: Sacred to the Good August Goddess. Iulia Casta Felicitas gladly fulfilled her vow.
EDCS-23200443.summary: This is a religious dedication from Iulia Casta Felicitas to the Bona Dea, recording the fulfillment of a vow.

EDCS-23200445.inscription_type: tituli honorarii, tituli operum, tituli sacri
EDCS-23200445.text_edition: \n Pro restituta salute Imperatoris Caesaris Marci Aureli Antonini Augusti Armeniaci Parthici Medici pontificis maximi patris patriae tribunicia potestate XXIII consulis III imperatoris V civitas Mactaritanorum extruxit anno Sexti Laterani proconsulis clarissimi viri Lucius Rupilius Au legatus eius dedicavit\n
EDCS-23200445.translation: For the restored health of the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus Armeniacus Parthicus Medicus, Pontifex Maximus, Father of the Fatherland, with tribunician power for the 23rd time, consul for the 3rd time, and Imperator. The city of Mactaritanorum erected [this] in the year of Sextus Lateranus, most illustrious proconsul. Lucius Rupilius Au, his legate, dedicated it.
EDCS-23200445.summary: This inscription records the erection of a monument by the city of Mactaritanorum to commemorate the health of Emperor Marcus Aurelius Antoninus, under the proconsulship of Sextus Lateranus, likely dating to the late 2nd century CE.

EDCS-23200447.translation: To Publius Septimius Geta Caesar, son of Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus Arabicus Adiabenicus Parthicus Maximus, strongest, happiest, pontifex maximus, with tribunician power for the 7th time, imperator for the 11th time, consul for the 2nd time, father of the fatherland, proconsul; brother of Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus, with tribunician power for the 2nd time, proconsul; nephew of the deified Marcus Antoninus Pius Germanicus Sarmaticus; great-nephew of the deified Antoninus Pius; grand-nephew of the deified Hadrian; great-great-nephew of the deified Trajan Parthicus and the deified Nerva. By decree of the decurions of the colonia Aelia Aurelia Mactaris, with public funds.
EDCS-23200447.summary: This is a monumental inscription from the colonia Aelia Aurelia Mactaris dedicating a public work to Geta, brother of Caracalla and son of Septimius Severus, likely erected during the reign of Septimius Severus.

EDCS-23200450.translation: To our lord Flavius Valerius Constantinus, most noble Caesar, the city of Mactaris, devoted to their divine power and majesty, by decree of its decurions and at public expense.
EDCS-23200450.summary: This inscription from the colony of Mactaris dedicates a monument to Emperor Constantine, enacted by the town council and funded by public money.

EDCS-23200451.translation: To our lord Flavius Claudius Julianus, Pious, Fortunate, always Augustus, Quintus Licinius Faustus, perpetual priest and curator of the republic, together with the most splendid order, dedicated to his divine power and majesty.
EDCS-23200451.summary: This inscription records the dedication to Emperor Julian by Quintus Licinius Faustus, a perpetual priest and civic official, alongside the town council.

EDCS-23200452.translation: To our lord Flavius Valentinianus, Pious, Fortunate, always Augustus, Quintus Julius Moderatus, perpetual priest and curator of the republic, together with the most splendid order, most devoted to his divine power and majesty.
EDCS-23200452.summary: This inscription dedicates a monument to Emperor Valentinian I by Quintus Julius Moderatus, a perpetual priest and civic official, with the approval of the town council.

EDCS-23200453.translation: To our lord Flavius Valentinianus, Pious, Fortunate, always Augustus, Quintus Julius Moderatus, perpetual priest and curator of the republic, together with the most splendid order, most devoted to his divine power and majesty.
EDCS-23200453.summary: This inscription dedicates a monument to Emperor Valentinian I by Quintus Julius Moderatus, a perpetual priest and civic official, with the approval of the town council.

EDCS-23200454.translation: To our lord Flavius Gratianus, Pious, Fortunate, always Augustus, Lucius Popilius Honoratus, perpetual priest and curator of the republic, together with the most splendid order, placed and dedicated to his divine power and majesty.
EDCS-23200454.summary: This inscription records the placement and dedication of a monument to Emperor Gratian by Lucius Popilius Honoratus, a perpetual priest and civic official, with the town council.

EDCS-23200455.translation: To our lord Diocletian Augustus, the colony of Mactaris, devoted to his divine power and majesty.
EDCS-23200455.summary: This inscription from the colony of Mactaris expresses devotion to Emperor Diocletian, likely on behalf of the city.

EDCS-23200457.translation: To Marcus Valerius Quadratus, son of Marcus, of the Quirina tribe, decemvir for judging lawsuits, broad-striped tribune of the Legio III Augusta, quaestor of the Emperor, patron of the municipality, by decree of the decurions, at public expense.
EDCS-23200457.summary: This is a dedication of a public monument to Marcus Valerius Quadratus, detailing his distinguished career in various civic and military offices, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-23200459.translation: To Gaius Sextius, son of Gaius, of the Papiria tribe, Martialis, tribune of the soldiers of the IV Scythica Legion, procurator of the Emperor from the city's records, procurator of the Emperor for the tax farmers of the Quadragesima Galliarum, and merchants; procurator of Macedonia; who, in memory of his brother Titus Sextius Alexander, ordered a public banquet from the income of 50,000 sesterces to be given annually to his home town of Mactaris on his brother's birthday, from curial revenues; for which generosity, the entire curia, by decree of the decurions, erected this statue at his expense.
EDCS-23200459.summary: This inscription honors Gaius Sextius Martialis, a prominent official, who endowed a public banquet in memory of his brother, for which the town council erected a statue.

EDCS-23200463.translation: Iccius, son of Rogatus, Inus AT
EDCS-23200463.summary: This inscription appears to be a fragment, possibly a tombstone, with the names Iccius and Inus.

EDCS-23200466.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus Amicius Rogatianus, a pious priest, lived for 42 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-23200466.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Quintus Amicius Rogatianus, a priest, indicating his age and burial.

EDCS-23200467.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Caius Mulceius Maximus lived for 30 years. Sacred to the Divine Shades. Sextus Aurelius F[...]-nus lived for 40 years.
EDCS-23200467.summary: This is a funerary inscription that appears to be a composite monument, originally an epitaph for a freedman who rose to wealth and status through agriculture and public service, with additional, later funerary dedications to Caius Mulceius Maximus and Sextus Aurelius F[...]-nus, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-23200468.translation: Canneia Optata, pious, lived for 60 years; she is buried here. Gaius Cassius Imi, son of Gaius, public defender, at his own expense. Whoever shall disturb me will have the wrath of the gods and will burn alive. Lived for 114 years. Quadratianus, public defender, son of the public defender, lived for 34 years; he is buried here. Cassia Fria, pious, lived for 10 years.
EDCS-23200468.summary: This tombstone records the burial of Canneia Optata, with a curse for desecration, and her son Quadratianus, also a public defender, as well as Cassia Fria, with ages provided for each.

EDCS-23200469.translation: Numisia, pious priestess of Ceres, lived 80 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-23200469.summary: A funerary inscription for Numisia, a priestess of Ceres, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-23200470.translation: Agria Peregrina, freedwoman of Caius, lived 34 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-23200470.summary: A funerary inscription for Agria Peregrina, a freedwoman, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-23200471.translation: Turpilia Fausta lived 50 years; she is buried here. Quintus Albicius Montanus lived 50 years; he is buried here. Montanus made this for his parents.
EDCS-23200471.summary: A funerary inscription set up by Quintus Albicius Montanus for his parents, Turpilia Fausta and another individual, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-23200472.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Lucius Antistius Honoratus lived 80 years.
EDCS-23200472.summary: A funerary inscription dedicated to Lucius Antistius Honoratus, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-23200473.translation: Apsennia Secunda, daughter of Marcus, lived 30 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-23200473.summary: A funerary inscription for Apsennia Secunda, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-23200474.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Avidia Felicitas, pious, lived 5 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-23200474.summary: A funerary inscription for Avidia Felicitas, a child, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-23200475.translation: Caelia Maxima, daughter of Caius, pious, lived 80 years. Lucius Ga... is buried here.
EDCS-23200475.summary: A funerary inscription for Caelia Maxima and Lucius Ga[---], dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-23200476.translation: [Daughter] of Caliganis, pious, lived 85 years; she is buried here. May your bones rest well; may the earth be light upon you.
EDCS-23200476.summary: A funerary inscription with wishes for the deceased, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-23200477.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Titus Cornelius Optatianus lived 50 years; he is buried here. Aquilia Namgedde lived [---] years with her most rare husband.
