EDCS-23200477.summary: A funerary inscription for Titus Cornelius Optatianus and his wife Aquilia Namgedde, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-23200478.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Naevia Vindicta, pious, lived 27 years and 15 days; she is buried here. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Lucius Domitius Secundianus, pious, lived 58 years, 2 months, and 25 days; he is buried here. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Antistia Victoria, pious, lived 85 years; she is buried here. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Lucius Domitius Rogatus Veranus, pious, lived 65 years; he is buried here. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Domitia Victoria, pious, sister of Domitii Rogatianus and Secundianus, lived [---].
EDCS-23200478.summary: A complex funerary inscription recording the deaths of several members of the Domitii family and others, including Antistia Victoria and Naevia Vindicta, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-23200479.translation: Pompeius Ianuarius lived 70 years. Flavia Fausta, pious and good, lived 75 years.
EDCS-23200479.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespans of Pompeius Ianuarius and Flavia Fausta.

EDCS-23200480.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Flavia Iula.

EDCS-23200481.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Fortunatia.

EDCS-23200482.translation: Dedicated to the spirits of the departed. Geminia Macrina, pious, lived 15 years and one month.
EDCS-23200482.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the spirits of the departed, recording the lifespan of Geminia Macrina.

EDCS-23200483.translation: Dedicated to the spirits of the departed. Ianuarius, pious, lived 38 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-23200483.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the spirits of the departed, recording the lifespan and burial of Ianuarius.

EDCS-23200484.translation: Quintus Iulius Martialis [and] Zama and Sileha his wife lived 65 years. C. Anni [erected this].
EDCS-23200484.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespans of Quintus Iulius Martialis and his wife Sileha, possibly erected by C. Anni.

EDCS-23200485.translation: Iulius Felix, the son, erected and dedicated this out of piety to his parents. Dedicated to the spirits of the departed. Caius Iulius Saturninus and Pomponia Victoria lived 80 years; they are buried here.
EDCS-23200485.summary: This funerary inscription records that Iulius Felix erected this monument for his parents, Caius Iulius Saturninus and Pomponia Victoria, who lived 80 years and are buried here.

EDCS-23200486.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Iulius Victor.

EDCS-23200487.translation: Iulia Paeonia lived 37 years, 3 months, and 4 days.
EDCS-23200487.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Iulia Paeonia.

EDCS-23200488.translation: Marcus Iunius Crescens, pious, lived 27 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-23200488.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan and burial of Marcus Iunius Crescens.

EDCS-23200489.translation: Lucilius Pius lived 70 years, is buried here; Cossinia Quinta, pious, lived 60 years, is buried here.
EDCS-23200489.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucilius Pius and Cossinia Quinta, recording their ages at death and burial.

EDCS-23200490.translation: Lucilius Saturninus, pious, lived 51 years, is buried here.
EDCS-23200490.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucilius Saturninus, recording his age at death and burial.

EDCS-23200491.translation: Magna lived 90 years, is buried here.
EDCS-23200491.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Magna, recording her age at death and burial.

EDCS-23200492.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Selicia Ingenua, pious, lived 76 years and 2 months, is buried here. Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Mamurius Postimus, pious, lived 70 years, is buried here.
EDCS-23200492.summary: This is a funerary inscription honoring Selicia Ingenua and Mamurius Postimus, providing their ages and burial information.

EDCS-23200494.translation: Maximus, son of L. Mintho, S.
EDCS-23200494.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely recording the name and parentage of Maximus.

EDCS-23200495.translation: Maxima, daughter of Maximus, pious, lived 30 years, is buried here.
EDCS-23200495.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Maxima, daughter of Maximus, recording her age at death and burial.

EDCS-23200496.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Minucius Rogatus, recording his age at death.

EDCS-23200497.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Lucius Minucius Secundus lived 3 years.
EDCS-23200497.summary: This is a funerary inscription for the young child Lucius Minucius Secundus, recording his age.

EDCS-23200498.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Mulleia Victoria lived 63 years and 1 month and 10 days.
EDCS-23200498.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Mulleia Victoria, recording her age at death.

EDCS-23400687.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Lucius Naevius Maximus, pious, lived 98 years, is buried here. For Lucius Naevius Felix, most pious and kind father.
EDCS-23400687.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Lucius Naevius Maximus by his son Lucius Naevius Felix, recording the former's age.

EDCS-23400688.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Lucilia Sabina, a dutiful daughter of Lucius, made this for herself and her husband. She lived 50 years. Quintus Octavius Felix Burdonianus, dutiful, lived 50 years.
EDCS-23400688.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated to Lucilia Sabina and her husband, with their ages at death provided.

EDCS-23400689.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Octavia Spes, dutiful, lived 30 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-23400689.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the death of Octavia Spes, who lived 30 years.

EDCS-23400690.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Octavia Sra lived [X] years.
EDCS-23400690.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the death of Octavia Sra, though her age is incomplete.

EDCS-23400691.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Lucius Rammius Ianuarius lived 85 years; he is buried here. Manlia Saturnina, his wife, lived 88 years. Lucius Manlius Victor made this for his most devoted parents from his own resources.
EDCS-23400691.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Lucius Manlius Victor for his parents, Lucius Rammius Ianuarius and Manlia Saturnina, with their ages at death.

EDCS-23400692.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Aulus Rupilius Saturninus, a dutiful son of Lucius of the Papiria tribe, lived 86 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-23400692.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the death of Aulus Rupilius Saturninus, who lived 86 years.

EDCS-23400693.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Sallustius Rogatus, dutiful, lived [X] years.
EDCS-23400693.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Sallustius Rogatus, though his age is incomplete.

EDCS-23400694.translation: Satura, daughter of Florus, lived 68 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-23400694.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the death of Satura, daughter of Florus, who lived 68 years.

EDCS-23400695.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. For Aelius Saturninus, father, and Octavia Matrona, dutiful mother, daughter of Lucius.
EDCS-23400695.summary: This is a funerary dedication by a daughter for her deceased parents, Aelius Saturninus and Octavia Matrona.

EDCS-23400696.translation: Saturninus, son of Fronto, from Zaigula, lived 27 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-23400696.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the death of Saturninus, son of Fronto, a native of Zaigula, who lived 27 years.

EDCS-23400697.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Sedia Nina, daughter of Bisilis, lived 80 years; she is buried here. Bisil lived 100 years.
EDCS-23400697.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Sedia Nina and Bisil, recording their ages at death as 80 and 100 years respectively.

EDCS-23400698.translation: Quintus Seius Mustus, dutiful, lived 30 years, is buried here.
EDCS-23400698.summary: A tombstone recording the life and burial of Quintus Seius Mustus.

EDCS-23400699.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Aelia Victoria lived 41 years. Lucius Septimius Saturnus lived [some years]. Sacred to the departed spirits. Pullaenia Rogata lived 41 years. Septimius Rufus lived 53 years.
EDCS-23400699.summary: A funerary inscription recording the lives of Aelia Victoria, Lucius Septimius Saturnus, Pullaenia Rogata, and Septimius Rufus.

EDCS-23400700.translation: Sileca, daughter of Laetus, dutiful, lived 15 years, is buried here.
EDCS-23400700.summary: A tombstone recording the life and burial of Sileca.

EDCS-23400701.translation: Staberia Calmasa lived 5 years, is buried here.
EDCS-23400701.summary: A tombstone recording the life and burial of Staberia Calmasa.

EDCS-23400702.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Sulpicia Saturnina lived 82 years.
EDCS-23400702.summary: A funerary inscription recording the life of Sulpicia Saturnina.

EDCS-23400703.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Tadius Castulus, dutiful, lived 35 years.
EDCS-23400703.summary: A funerary inscription recording the life of Tadius Castulus.

EDCS-23400704.translation: Terentius Rogatus, dutiful, lived 45 years, is buried here.
EDCS-23400704.summary: A tombstone recording the life and burial of Terentius Rogatus.

EDCS-23400705.translation: Quintus Titurius Saturninus, father, dutiful, lived 85 years, is buried here.
EDCS-23400705.summary: A tombstone recording the life and burial of Quintus Titurius Saturninus.

EDCS-23400706.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Caius Valerius lived 10 years, lived happily 26 years, is buried here.
EDCS-23400706.summary: A tombstone recording the life and burial of Caius Valerius, possibly indicating two different age counts or periods of life.

EDCS-23400707.translation: Titus Vaternius, son of Caius, of the Stellatina tribe.
EDCS-23400707.summary: An inscription identifying Titus Vaternius, son of Caius, and his tribal affiliation, likely from a public record or monument.

EDCS-23400709.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. To Lucius Virius Tertullus, my brother, and to Vibius Materna Sissina, daughter of Lucius, my dearest sisters.
EDCS-23400709.summary: A funerary dedication by a sibling to their deceased brother and sister, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-23400710.translation: As much good fortune as fortune can bestow upon a man from his predecessors, so much good I brought to you, a young man who died with renown.
EDCS-23400710.summary: A funerary epitaph lamenting the death of a renowned young man and attributing his positive qualities to fortune, likely Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-23400711.summary: A short, epigrammatic inscription on a tomb, possibly Roman Imperial period, referring to the deceased's spirit.

EDCS-23400714.translation: He lived 85 years. Here lie. He lived 81 years. Here lie.
EDCS-23400714.summary: A funerary inscription recording the lifespans of two individuals, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-23400717.summary: A brief funerary inscription stating the age of the deceased, likely Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-23400719.translation: Once worthy of God, here in his tomb lies Bishop Germanus; he lived in the episcopate [X] years, [Y] months, [Z] days.
EDCS-23400719.summary: A funerary inscription for Bishop Germanus, detailing his lifespan and time in office, likely from the Late Roman or Early Christian period.

EDCS-23400720.translation: Rutilius, bishop, lived in the episcopate 23 years, 2 months, 10 days.
EDCS-23400720.summary: A funerary inscription for Bishop Rutilius, stating his age and tenure as bishop, likely from the Late Roman or Early Christian period.

EDCS-23400721.translation: Bonispera, faithful, lived in peace 9 years, 3 days.
EDCS-23400721.summary: A funerary inscription for Bonispera, recording her age and peaceful repose, likely from the Late Roman or Early Christian period.

EDCS-23400722.translation: Cersciturus lived in peace 14 years, 11 months, 25 days, 3 hours.
EDCS-23400722.summary: A funerary inscription for Cersciturus, detailing his age and duration of life, likely from the Late Roman or Early Christian period.

EDCS-23400723.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Grunnitus lived in peace 55 years, 4 months.
EDCS-23400723.summary: A funerary inscription dedicated to the spirits of the departed, recording the lifespan of Grunnitus, likely Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-23400724.translation: Dominicellus lived in peace for one month and one hour.
EDCS-23400724.summary: This inscription records the lifespan of Dominicellus, who lived for one month and one hour.

EDCS-23400725.translation: Geminius lived in peace for sixty-four years, ten months, and ten days. He was laid to rest on the 13th day before the Kalends of December.
EDCS-23400725.summary: This inscription records the lifespan and burial date of Geminius.

EDCS-23400726.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Iulia Victoria, an honorable and faithful woman, lived for 25 years, five months, and three days. She departed this life on the 15th day before the Kalends of November.
EDCS-23400726.summary: This inscription records the lifespan and death date of Iulia Victoria, dedicated to the Spirits of the Departed.

EDCS-23400728.translation: Restitutus lived in peace for thirty years.
EDCS-23400728.summary: This inscription records the lifespan of Restitutus, who lived for thirty years.

EDCS-23400729.summary: This inscription records the incomplete lifespan of Victorinus.

EDCS-23400730.translation: ARIA ISTE lived for years STE.
EDCS-23400730.summary: This inscription records the incomplete lifespan of someone named ARIA ISTE.

EDCS-23400731.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. CTA lived in peace for seventy-one years and three months.
EDCS-23400731.summary: This inscription records the lifespan of CTA, dedicated to the Spirits of the Departed.

EDCS-23400734.summary: This inscription records the lifespan of an unnamed individual who lived for sixty-seven years.

EDCS-23400737.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Lucius Apertius Tertullianus, dutiful, lived for thirteen years, eight months, and six days. He was laid to rest here.
EDCS-23400737.summary: This inscription records the lifespan and burial of Lucius Apertius Tertullianus, dedicated to the Spirits of the Departed.

EDCS-23400738.translation: Marcus Apuleius Fortunatus, dutiful, lived for thirty years. He was laid to rest here.
EDCS-23400738.summary: This inscription records the lifespan and burial of Marcus Apuleius Fortunatus.

EDCS-23400739.translation: Bellicus, son of Maximi Nanni, lived 33 years.
EDCS-23400739.summary: This is a tombstone recording the lifespan of Bellicus, son of Maximi Nanni.

EDCS-23400740.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Munatius Cududus lived 51 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-23400740.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Munatius Cududus, who lived 51 years.

EDCS-23400741.translation: Optatus Iuzgagis lived 85 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-23400741.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Optatus Iuzgagis, who lived 85 years.

EDCS-23400742.translation: Popillia Vitalis, dutiful daughter of Lucius, lived 28 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-23400742.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Popillia Vitalis, daughter of Lucius, who lived 28 years.

EDCS-23400743.translation: Vibia Rogata, dutiful, lived 11 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-23400743.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Vibia Rogata, who lived 11 years.

EDCS-23400744.translation: A dutiful slave lived 60 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-23400744.summary: This is a funerary inscription for an unnamed dutiful slave who lived 60 years.

EDCS-23400747.translation: Sacred to Juno Augusta. Lucius Vibius Latinianus Valens, tribune of the VI Legion, made this.
EDCS-23400747.summary: This is a dedication to Juno Augusta made by Lucius Vibius Latinianus Valens, a tribune of the VI Legion.

EDCS-23400748.translation: To the Divine Marcus Antoninus Pius, father, by decree of the local council and at public expense, in his sixth year of tribunician power, second consulship, fourth acclamation as emperor, a father of the fatherland.
EDCS-23400748.summary: This is a public dedication to Emperor Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius, likely erected during his reign (c. 175-180 AD).

EDCS-23400749.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Lucius Aurelius Verus Augustus, conqueror of Armenia, son of the divine Antoninus, grandson of the divine Hadrian, great-grandson of the divine Trajan Parthicus, great-great-grandson of the divine Nerva, pontiff maximus, in his first year of tribunician power, second consulship, a father of the fatherland, by decree of the local council and at public expense.
EDCS-23400749.summary: This is a public dedication to Emperor Lucius Aurelius Verus, likely erected during his consulship and tribunician power, around 161 AD.

EDCS-23400751.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Severus Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus. The city of Uzappa erected [this] by decree of the decurions, at public expense.
EDCS-23400751.summary: This inscription records the erection of a monument by the city of Uzappa in honor of Emperor Marcus Aurelius Severus Antoninus (Caracalla), funded by public decree, likely dating to the early 3rd century CE.

EDCS-23400753.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Probus Pius Felix Augustus, pontifex maximus, conqueror of the Germans, conqueror of the Sarmatians, with tribunician power, father of the fatherland, consul for the third time, the citizens of Uzappa.
EDCS-23400753.summary: This inscription honors Emperor Probus with a full titulature and indicates it was erected by the citizens of Uzappa.

EDCS-23400754.translation: Lucius Avidius [erected/dedicated] to the most invincible Emperors Augustus [and others], the flamonium perpetuum [which had collapsed] due to age, out of civic affection and honor towards them, which was awarded to Quinto Avidio Felicio, consul of the province of Byzacena.
EDCS-23400754.summary: This inscription records Lucius Avidius restoring a flamonium perpetuum in the province of Byzacena, honoring the emperors and the consul Quinto Avidio Felicio.

EDCS-23400755.translation: The order of the city of Uzappa arranged for the erection and dedicated a statue to Sextus Anicius Faustus Paulinianus, a most distinguished youth, patron and son of a patron.
EDCS-23400755.summary: A statue was erected and dedicated by the city of Uzappa to Sextus Anicius Faustus Paulinianus, honoring his status as patron.

EDCS-23400757.translation: The order of the municipality of Uzappa arranged for the erection of a statue at public expense and dedicated it to Gaius Valerius Gallianus Honoratianus, a most distinguished youth, son of a patron, because of his affection and that of his grandfather Valerius Gallianus, his father Rogatianus, and his brother V. Pa.
EDCS-23400757.summary: A statue was erected by the municipality of Uzappa to Gaius Valerius Gallianus Honoratianus, honoring his familial connections and personal affection.

EDCS-23400820.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Iunia Fausta lived for 80 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-23400820.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Iunia Fausta, recording her age at death.

EDCS-23400821.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Saturninus, son of Victor Ceras, lived for [unknown age]; he is buried here. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Eiri tus lived for 2 years.
EDCS-23400821.summary: This inscription appears to be a composite funerary text, mentioning Saturninus and Eiri tus, the latter of whom died at the age of two.

EDCS-23400822.translation: He lived 40 years and 1 month. He is buried here.
EDCS-23400822.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan and burial of an unnamed individual.

EDCS-23400823.translation: Sextia Diodora, dutiful, lived 80 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-23400823.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan and burial of Sextia Diodora.

EDCS-23400824.translation: Rossia Rogata lived 20 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-23400824.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan and burial of Rossia Rogata.

EDCS-23400826.translation: The bronze statue of a god with a horse, from the old temple, belonging to Marcus Aurelius Licinius, was transferred to this temple through the munificence of Publius Opstorius Saturninus, perpetual flamen, with the permission of the Republic of the Vazitani and the most distinguished proconsul Valerius Pudens, and placed in the basilica purchased by the same Opstorius.
EDCS-23400826.summary: This inscription records the transfer and reinstallation of a bronze statue of a deity and horse, funded by Publius Opstorius Saturninus, with official permission, likely in the 3rd or 4th century CE.

EDCS-23400827.translation: Quintus Magnius Eutyches, a Roman equestrian, made an altar with its ornaments and statues for the god Hercules and dedicated it himself with his own.
EDCS-23400827.summary: This is a dedication of an altar and statues to Hercules by Quintus Magnius Eutyches, a Roman equestrian, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-23400830.translation: For the Father God, Lucius Antistius Maximianus, lover of priests, together with his granddaughter Antistia Maxima Postima Aemiliana, from Lucius Antistius Maximianus Licinianus, his son.
EDCS-23400830.summary: This inscription is a dedication to a Father God, made by Lucius Antistius Maximianus and his granddaughter, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-23400833.text_edition: \n Pro salute Imperatoris Caesaris divi Septimi Severi Pii Arabici Adiabenici Parthici maximi Britannici maximi fili divi Marci Antonini Pii Germanici Sarmatici nepotis divi Antonini Pii pronepotis divi Hadriani abnepotis divi Traiani Parthici et divi Nervae adnepotis Marci Aureli Antonini Pii Felicis principis iuventutis Augusti Parthici maximi Brittannici maximi pontificis maximi tribunicia potestate XV imperatoris II consulis III patris patriae et Iuliae Domnae Augustae Piae Felicis matris Augusti et castrorum et senatus totiusque domus divinae Publius Opstorius Saturninus flamen perpetuus sacerdos Mercuri cum patriae suae Vazitanae triplicata summa flamoni perpetui HS III milibus nummum aedem Mercurio Sobrio pollicitus fuisset ampliata liberalitate eandem aedem cum pronao et ara fecit et ob dedicationem aepulum sic et gymnasium dedit loco dato decreto decurionum idem iam ante hoc ob honorem XI primatus aedem Aesculapio deo promissam bassilicam sic cohaerentem multiplicata pecunia fecit\n
EDCS-23400833.translation: For the well-being of the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Felix, prince of the youth, Augustus, conqueror of the Parthians, conqueror of the Britons, pontifex maximus, with tribunician power for the 15th time, imperator for the 2nd time, consul for the 3rd time, father of the fatherland, son of the deified Septimius Severus Pius Arabicus Adiabenicus Parthicus maximus Britannicus maximus, grandson of the deified Marcus Antoninus Pius Germanicus Sarmaticus, great-grandson of the deified Antoninus Pius, great-great-grandson of the deified Hadrian, great-great-great-grandson of the deified Trajan Parthicus and the deified Nerva; and of Julia Domna Augusta Pia Felix, mother of the Augusti and of the camp and of the entire divine house, Publius Opstorius Saturninus, perpetual flamen, priest of Mercury, with his homeland Vazitana, having promised 3,000 sesterces for the triple sum of the perpetual flamonic office, built the same temple with a pronaos and altar, having amplified his generosity; and for the dedication, he gave a banquet and a gymnasium, in a place granted by decree of the decurions; he had already previously, for the honor of his 11th primary office, promised a temple to the god Aesculapius, and with multiplied funds, built an adjoining basilica.
EDCS-23400833.summary: This long inscription records the extensive dedications made by Publius Opstorius Saturninus, a perpetual flamen, including a temple to Mercury and a basilica to Aesculapius, for the health of Emperor Caracalla and Empress Julia Domna, likely dating to the early 3rd century CE.

EDCS-23400835.translation: To our lord Flavius Gratianus Maximus Pius Felix Victor, always Augustus.
EDCS-23400835.summary: This is an acclamation or dedication to the emperor Gratian, dating to his reign (367-383 CE).

EDCS-23400837.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Dead. Marcus Florius Maximus Iulianus lived 46 years and 6 months. He is buried here.
EDCS-23400837.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan and burial of Marcus Florius Maximus Iulianus.

EDCS-23400838.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Dead. Lucius Germanius Nannaricus, son of Publius, dutiful, lived 22 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-23400838.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan and burial of Lucius Germanius Nannaricus.

EDCS-23400840.translation: This is a tomb monument for burial. Sacred to the Spirits of the Dead. Pomponius Rogatianus, dutiful, lived 83 years and 24 days. He is buried here. Sacred to the Spirits of the Dead. Pomponius Faustinianus, dutiful, lived 34 years, 10 months and 23 days. Pomponia Quinta, dutiful, lived 31 years, 10 months and 12 days. She is buried here.
EDCS-23400840.summary: This is a multi-person funerary inscription recording the lifespans and burials of Pomponius Rogatianus, Pomponius Faustinianus, and Pomponia Quinta.

EDCS-23500042.text_edition: \n Victoriae Augustae ducatu instantiaque Claudi Constantis procuratoris Augusti contigit des et Musulamios gentesque aliasnminmerumptest anno usque\n
EDCS-23500042.translation: To Augusta Victoria, by the command and at the instance of Claudius Constans, procurator of Augustus, the Cetus and Musulamii and numerous other peoples...
EDCS-23500042.summary: This inscription, likely from North Africa, records a dedication to Augusta Victoria by Claudius Constans, a procurator, and mentions various peoples, possibly related to military achievements or administrative divisions.

EDCS-23500043.translation: Rasinia Secunda returned on the 17th day before the Kalends of November in the 157th year.
EDCS-23500043.summary: This short inscription records the return of a person named Rasinia Secunda on a specific date, possibly in reference to a public office or a historical era.

EDCS-23500044.translation: The decurions of the colony of Tipasa, by decree of the council, erected and dedicated this to Marcus Cocceius Romanus, an equestrian of Rome, a primipilar, for his outstanding love and defense of the state, which he has shown to his fatherland and his fellow citizens.
EDCS-23500044.summary: This inscription records a dedication by the town council of Tipasa to Marcus Cocceius Romanus, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-23500045.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Flavius Tutor, imaginifer of the I Contarii cavalry unit, erected this for his most devoted friend Ulpius Tertius, a curator of the same unit.
EDCS-23500045.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Ulpius Tertius, a curator, set up by his friend Flavius Tutor, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-23500046.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Adiutor, a duplicarius from the troop of singulares, who was killed on Mount Zelel, lived 36 years, 4 months, and 10 days. His mother made this for her excellent son. [Restored text follows]
EDCS-23500046.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Adiutor, a soldier, and was erected by his mother, probably from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-23500047.translation: Lucius Marcius Ferox erected this mausoleum on land granted to her by the most distinguished council for his exceedingly rare wife, Cornelia Flora, daughter of Lucius.
EDCS-23500047.summary: This inscription records the erection of a mausoleum by Lucius Marcius Ferox for his wife Cornelia Flora, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-23500050.translation: From the will of Gaius Critius Felix, son of Gaius, of the voting tribe Quirina.
EDCS-23500050.summary: This is a dedication from the will of Gaius Critius Felix, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-23500051.translation: Dedicated from the will of Critius Felix, with Claudia Fabiola officiating.
EDCS-23500051.summary: This inscription records a dedication from the will of Critius Felix, overseen by Claudia Fabiola, probably from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-23500053.translation: To the spirits of the departed Honoratus.
EDCS-23500053.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Honoratus, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-23500054.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Iulia Severa lived 2 years, [number] months, and 25 days.
EDCS-23500054.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Iulia Severa, likely a child, from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-23500055.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription identifying Iulia Aemilia, daughter of Gaius, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-23500056.translation: To the spirits of the departed Rogata [restored text follows]
EDCS-23500056.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Rogata, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-23500057.translation: Samaita and Immi made this for their mother.
EDCS-23500057.summary: This is a simple funerary inscription recording that Samaita and Immi erected a memorial for their mother.

EDCS-23500058.translation: Tertulla Honorata, aged 80, to her most devoted husband
EDCS-23500058.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a woman named Tertulla Honorata, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-23500062.summary: This inscription is a dedication to an individual named Iani Innocentissimus, possibly a deity or a deceased person, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24000030.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Iulia Urbana, pious wife of Saturus Felix, lived [X] years. Julius Musteolus, pious son of Saturus Felix, lived 42 years. Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Saturus Felix, pious son of Iustus, lived [X] years.
EDCS-24000030.summary: This is a complex funerary epitaph for multiple members of the Saturus Felix family, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24100001.summary: This is a very brief inscription, possibly a greeting or dedication, with numerical elements, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24100002.translation: Marchius and his parents, father and mother, [dedicated this] to Marchius Nimmirus and Maccurasa, who made this memorial for them. We have examined the accounts and the money expended on it amounts to forty-five thousand six hundred denarii in cash, in addition to the food for the workers. May sons and grandsons happily read and visit.
EDCS-24100002.summary: This inscription records the construction of a memorial by Marchius and his parents for Marchius Nimmirus and Maccurasa, detailing the significant cost of its erection, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24100003.translation: Marchius Nasif and Marchia Mathlich [made this] for their dear parents, Marchius Nimirus and Fydel, sons.
EDCS-24100003.summary: This is a funerary epitaph where sons Marchius Nasif and Marchia Mathlich honor their parents, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24100004.summary: This inscription is too fragmented or written in an unknown script to be fully translated or summarized, but it appears to be a Roman-era inscription.

EDCS-24100005.translation: anaꞩiba ys fel Udruna lobuthem ulybanem Duniad Osilim Sebuinan uSysan uIlun NANAA ixeb Calamdas MΣNA UARIA Micauran
EDCS-24100005.summary: This inscription is challenging to translate due to its potentially non-Latin or highly abbreviated nature, but it appears to be a dedication or funerary marker from the Roman period.

EDCS-24100006.text_edition: \n Aurellio Nazmuri parenti et matri Aurelli Maior et Magnus et Arcadius fili parentibus piissimis fecerunt\n
EDCS-24100006.translation: Aurellius Nazmur, to his parents, and to his mother, Aurellius Maior, Magnus, and Arcadius, his sons, made this for their most devoted parents.
EDCS-24100006.summary: This is a funerary inscription where sons Aurellius Maior, Magnus, and Arcadius honor their parents, including Aurellius Nazmur and his mother.

EDCS-24100007.text_edition: \n x templum de sua pecunia Titus Flavius Quirina Capito Io \n
EDCS-24100007.translation: Titus Flavius Quirina Capito Io made a temple at his own expense.
EDCS-24100007.summary: This inscription records Titus Flavius Quirina Capito Io dedicating a temple built at his own expense.

EDCS-24100008.summary: This inscription is very short and difficult to interpret, possibly a personal dedication or marker, from the Roman period.

EDCS-24100009.text_edition: \n Mercurio et Minervae Animosa Symmachi filia dedit dedicavit\n
EDCS-24100009.translation: Animosa, daughter of Symmachus, gave and dedicated this to Mercury and Minerva.
EDCS-24100009.summary: This is a dedication to the gods Mercury and Minerva by Animosa, daughter of Symmachus.

EDCS-24100011.text_edition: \n [Fulviae Plau][tillae Augustae] Antonini Augusti Pii sponsae dedicante Flavio Celere procuratore liberti et familia splendidissimi vectigalis IIII publicorum Africae\n
EDCS-24100011.translation: To Fulvia Plautilla Augusta, wife of Antoninus Augustus Pius, dedicated by Flavius Celer, procurator, freedmen and staff of the most distinguished tax collectors of Africa.
EDCS-24100011.summary: This inscription records the dedication to Fulvia Plautilla Augusta, wife of Emperor Antoninus Pius, by Flavius Celer, a procurator, and his associated staff.

EDCS-24100012.text_edition: \n Imperator Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus Arabicus Adiabenicus Parthicus maximus Britannicus maximus pontifex maximus tribuniciae potestatis decem sic et octies imperator duodecies consul ter pater patriae proconsul coepit et ex maiore parte perfecit Imperator Caesar divi Septimi Severi Pii Arabici Adiabenici Parthici maximi Britannici maximi filius divi Marci Antonini Pii Germanici Sarmatici nepos divi Antonini Pii pronepos divi Hadriani abnepos divi Traiani Parthici et divi Nervae adnepos Imperator Caesar Marcus Aurellius sic Antoninus Pius Augustus Parthicus maximus Britannicus maximus Germanicus maximus pontifex maximus tribuniciae potestatis decem sic novies imperator ter consul quater pater patriae proconsul perfici curavit\n
EDCS-24100012.translation: Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus Arabicus Adiabenicus Parthicus maximus Britannicus maximus, pontifex maximus, with tribunician power for the 18th time, imperator for the 12th time, consul for the third time, father of the fatherland, proconsul, began and for the most part completed. Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Augustus Parthicus maximus Britannicus maximus Germanicus maximus, pontifex maximus, with tribunician power for the 19th time, imperator for the third time, consul for the fourth time, father of the fatherland, proconsul, had completed.
EDCS-24100012.summary: This inscription details the construction of a public work initiated by Emperor Septimius Severus and completed under Emperor Caracalla, outlining their extensive imperial titles and consulships.

EDCS-24100014.text_edition: \n Imperatore Caesare Vespasiano Augusto pontifice maximo tribunicia potestate III imperatore X consule IIII designato V patre patriae Quintus Manlius Ancharius Tarquitius Saturninus proconsul patronus dedicavit Volumnius Memor Felix legatus pro praetore Iddibal Balsillecis filius Annobalis nepos Asmunis proneposus templum Matris Magnae et exornavit ex HS CC milibus nummum de sua pecunia dedit is et Passienus Maris E\n
EDCS-24100014.translation: Under Emperor Caesar Vespasian Augustus, Pontifex Maximus, holding tribunician power for the 3rd time, Imperator for the 10th time, Consul for the 4th time, designated Consul for the 5th time, Father of the Country, Quintus Manlius Ancharius Tarquitius Saturninus, Proconsul, Patron, dedicated this temple to the Great Mother. Volumnius Memor Felix, legate with praetorian authority, son of Iddibal, grandson of Balsilles, great-grandson of Asmunis, also adorned it and gave it from his own funds, 200,000 sesterces. He also and Passienus Maris...
EDCS-24100014.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a temple to the Great Mother by the proconsul Quintus Manlius Ancharius Tarquitius Saturninus and its adornment by the legate Volumnius Memor Felix, dating to the reign of Vespasian (AD 69-79).

EDCS-24100015.text_edition: \n NI OMM honestissim cognoscendi perpenso qu MEATO ob qurem publicam exquisitisisionum generibus fecerit ampliorem instauratori moenium publicorum quod eius innumera circa se ac suos officia supra genitalis civis affectum Lepcis magna inclita fide devotione praestans multifariam senserit meritorum eius tenacissime memor per ordinis sui et populi viros Flavio Victori Calpurnio viro perfectissimo praesidi provinciae Tripolitanae patrono suo statuam decrevit et ob individuum mutui amoris affectum eamdem sic se propter constituit ac dedicavit\n
EDCS-24100015.translation: The most honest men, after careful consideration of the public records and examination of various issues, decided to erect a statue for him, the restorer of public works, because of his countless services to the city and to his family, and because, above the natural affection of a citizen, Lepcis Magna, outstanding in loyalty and devotion, has recognized his merits in many ways. They decreed a statue to Flavius Victor Calpurnius, a most accomplished man, governor of the province of Tripolitana, their patron, and, because of the indivisible affection of mutual love, they erected and dedicated the same statue in his presence.
EDCS-24100015.summary: This decree from Lepcis Magna records the erection of a statue to the provincial governor Flavius Victor Calpurnius by the local elites and people, honoring his services and their mutual affection, likely in the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24100016.translation: To Quintus Pompeius Cerealis, by decree of the council.
EDCS-24100016.summary: This inscription records a public honor or dedication to Quintus Pompeius Cerealis, likely made by a local council, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24100017.translation: To the gods of the underworld and to the memory of Aoge, honored for his generous gifts for the year, who lived 22 years and 3 months, and to the well-being of his fellow citizens.
EDCS-24100017.summary: This funerary inscription honors Aoge and celebrates his generosity and life, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-24100020.translation: Calpurnia Licinia Sadith made this for Calpurnia Bargydden, Calpurnius Cerealis, and Calpurnius Candidus, her parents and brother, out of devotion.
EDCS-24100020.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by a daughter for her parents and brother, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-24100021.translation: To the departed spirits of Claudia Sabina Soteris.
EDCS-24100021.summary: This is a brief funerary dedication to Claudia Sabina Soteris, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-24100022.translation: To the departed spirits of Claudia Salvia.
EDCS-24100022.summary: This is a brief funerary dedication to Claudia Salvia, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-24100023.translation: Publius Lucretius Rogatinus, the father, made this for his son Publius Lucretius Crescentis, a good son and good brother.
EDCS-24100023.summary: This funerary monument was erected by a father for his deceased son, who is praised for his filial and fraternal qualities, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-24100024.summary: This inscription records the lifespan of a young individual named Rutilius Victor, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-24100026.translation: To the goddesses of the crossroads and to the good memory of Bia, who lived 16 years with virginal chastity.
EDCS-24100026.summary: This funerary inscription honors Bia, who died at 16 and is praised for her chastity, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-24100028.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Aelia Arisuth vixit annos sexaginta plus minus Dis Manibus sacrum Aelios Ma Iurathani bixit sic annosaginta quinque plus minus\n
EDCS-24100028.translation: Sacred to the departed gods. Aelia Arisuth lived sixty years, more or less. Sacred to the departed gods. Aelios Ma Iurathani lived sixty-five years, more or less.
EDCS-24100028.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the ages at death of two individuals, Aelia Arisuth and Aelios Ma Iurathani, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24100030.translation: To Caelestis Augustus, by Annius Istrugis, priest, in the year when Carmeius Noricus and Gabinius Gemellus were magistrates.
EDCS-24100030.summary: This dedication to the deity Caelestis Augustus was made by a priest during a specific magistracy, providing a precise date within the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-24100031.translation: To the departed spirits of Caius Marius Rufus; the monument for himself and for Maria Venusta, his wife.
EDCS-24100031.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Caius Marius Rufus for himself and his wife Maria Venusta, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-24100040.summary: This is likely the name of an individual, possibly an owner or a subject of a dedication, from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-24100043.inscription_type: tituli honorarii, tituli operum, tituli sacri
EDCS-24100043.text_edition: \n Quintus Servaeus Quinti filius Quirina Macer adlectus in quinque decurias a divo Hadriano lupam aeream quam ad ornamentum municipii promiserat cum Romulo et Remo dedit idemque dedicavit\n
EDCS-24100043.translation: Quintus Servaeus Macer, son of Quintus, of the Quirina tribe, admitted to the five decuries by the divine Hadrian, dedicated the bronze she-wolf, which he had promised for the adornment of the municipality, along with Romulus and Remus. He also dedicated it himself.
EDCS-24100043.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a bronze she-wolf statue, along with Romulus and Remus, to the municipality by Quintus Servaeus Macer, who had been appointed to a judicial role by Emperor Hadrian, likely dating to Hadrian's reign (AD 117-138).

EDCS-24100044.translation: Marcus Servilius Plautus, the aedile, erected the abacus and the statue at his own expense.
EDCS-24100044.summary: An aedile named Marcus Servilius Plautus dedicated a statue and an abacus at his own expense, likely in a public space.

EDCS-24100049.translation: To Emperor Caesar Traianus Hadrianus Augustus, son of the deified Trajan the Parthian, grandson of the deified Nerva, founder of the municipality of Gigthes, erected by public funds.
EDCS-24100049.summary: This is a public dedication by the people of Gigthes to Emperor Hadrian, recognizing him as the founder of their municipality.

EDCS-24100051.translation: To Aurelius Ver Caesar, by public funds of the people of Gigthes.
EDCS-24100051.summary: A public dedication by the people of Gigthes to the co-emperor Marcus Aurelius, who was adopted as Caesar by Antoninus Pius.

EDCS-24100055.translation: To the deified Commodus Augustus, by public funds of the people of Gigthes.
EDCS-24100055.summary: A public dedication by the people of Gigthes to the deified emperor Commodus.

EDCS-24100061.translation: To Quintus Julius Severus Proculianus, most distinguished man.
EDCS-24100061.summary: An inscription honoring Quintus Julius Severus Proculianus, a prominent individual, possibly a dedication or a commemoration.

EDCS-24100062.translation: To Marcus Memmius Caecilianus, most distinguished man and patron, by public decree of the decurions of Gigthes, with public money.
EDCS-24100062.summary: The people of Gigthes, by decree of their town council and with public funds, dedicated this to Marcus Memmius Caecilianus, honoring him as patron.

EDCS-24100063.translation: To Quintus Memmius Pudentius, most distinguished man and patron, by public decree of the decurions of Gigthes, with public money.
EDCS-24100063.summary: The people of Gigthes, by decree of their town council and with public funds, dedicated this to Quintus Memmius Pudentius, honoring him as patron.

EDCS-24100064.translation: To Lucius Messius Rufus, son of Lucius, III vir capitalis, quaestor of province CC.
EDCS-24100064.summary: An inscription honoring Lucius Messius Rufus, detailing his career as a monetary official and a provincial quaestor.

EDCS-24100065.translation: To Quintus Servaeus Fuscus Cornelius, most distinguished man, legate of the province of Galatia, legate of Legio I Italica, legate of Legio XIII Gemina, praetor hastarius, also by delegation juridical over civil cases and over supreme matters, curator of the Via Salaria, tribune of the plebs, urban quaestor, to the curia in its entirety, supported by annual endowments by his freedmen, freedwomen, and their sons.
EDCS-24100065.summary: This inscription details the extensive career of Quintus Servaeus Fuscus Cornelius, a high-ranking official, and records a public endowment provided by his freedpersons and their children.

EDCS-24100066.translation: Quintus Servaeus Fuscus, son of Lucius, and Quintus Servaeus Felix, son of Lucius, erected this at their own expense to their most devoted mother, Aurelia Antonia, daughter of Lucius, for her singular piety.
EDCS-24100066.summary: Two sons, Quintus Servaeus Fuscus and Quintus Servaeus Felix, erected a monument at their own expense to their mother, Aurelia Antonia, in recognition of her exceptional devotion.

EDCS-24100067.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Caecina, daughter of Quintus, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24100068.translation: Publius Hortensius Pietas made this for his most dutiful brother, Quintus Hortensius Placidus, son of Caius, with his own money.
EDCS-24100068.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Publius Hortensius Pietas for his brother Quintus Hortensius Placidus, funded by the brother himself, probably in the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24100069.translation: Publius Hortensius Pietas, son, made this for his most dutiful mother, Hortensia Placidus, daughter of Quintus, with his own money, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-24100069.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Publius Hortensius Pietas for his mother Hortensia Placidus, funded by the son and authorized by local officials, likely in the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24100072.translation: The order erected this for Marcus Julius Mando, son of Cia, of the Quirina tribe, perpetual flamen, because of his manifold generosity towards the state, at the request of the entire populace.
EDCS-24100072.summary: This public monument honors Marcus Julius Mando, a perpetual flamen, for his services to the state, erected by official decree and popular demand, likely in the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24100073.translation: The people of Chinithus have erected this with their own money for Lucius Memmius Messius Pacatus, son of Lucius, of the Quirina tribe, perpetual flamen of the deified Trajan, admitted into the five decuriae by the deified Hadrian, because of his merits and his singular devotion which he shows to his people.
EDCS-24100073.summary: This public monument was funded by the community of Chinithus to honor Lucius Memmius Messius Pacatus, a perpetual flamen and official admitted by Hadrian, for his contributions to the community, likely in the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24100074.translation: [...]pernas erected [this] for the daughter of Quintus.
EDCS-24100074.summary: This is a fragment of a funerary epitaph, mentioning a dedicator ending in '-pernas' and a daughter of Quintus, probably from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24100075.translation: The order and the people of Gigthensis have erected this at their own expense for Quintus Satrius Lupercus, son of Caius, because of his many merits to the state and his distinguished administration as duovir.
EDCS-24100075.summary: This public monument honors Quintus Satrius Lupercus, a duovir, for his service to the state, funded by the local government and populace, likely in the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24100076.translation: Quintus Servaeus Fuscus, son of Quintus, grandson of Quintus, of the Quirina tribe, made this for his most dutiful brother, Quintus Servaeus Fuscus, son of Quintus, grandson of Quintus, of the Quirina tribe, with his own money; the place was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-24100076.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Quintus Servaeus Fuscus for his brother Quintus Servaeus Fuscus, funded by the brother and with a burial plot granted by local officials, likely in the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24100077.translation: The place was granted by decree of the decurions for Quintus Servaeus Macro, son of Quintus, of the Quirina tribe, admitted into the five decuriae by the deified Hadrian Augustus; Quintus Servaeus Fuscus and Lucius Servaeus Firmus, sons, [erected this] for their most indulgent father.
EDCS-24100077.summary: This funerary monument, with a plot granted by local officials, was erected by the sons Quintus Servaeus Fuscus and Lucius Servaeus Firmus for their father Quintus Servaeus Macro, who had been honored by Emperor Hadrian, likely in the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24100078.text_edition: \n Marco Servilio Publi filio Quirina Draconi Albuciano IIviro flamini perpetuo quod super multa in rem publicam merita et amplissimum munificentiae studium legationem urbicam gratuitum ad Latium maius petendum duplicem susceperit tandemque feliciter renuntiaverit ordo publice ponendam censuit et cum is honore contentus pecuniam rei publicae remisisset populus de suo posuit\n
EDCS-24100078.translation: For Marcus Servilius Draconi, son of Publius, of the Quirina tribe, Albucianus, twice chief magistrate (duumvir), and perpetual priest, because of his many services to the state and his most ample zeal for munificence, he undertook the urban legation to seek the greater Latium region twice, and finally successfully announced its return. The council decreed that a statue should be publicly erected. Since he was content with this honor and remitted the money to the state, the people erected it at their own expense.
EDCS-24100078.summary: This inscription records the erection of a statue to Marcus Servilius Draconi, a local official honored for his public services and munificence, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period when such municipal offices were common.

EDCS-24100079.translation: The order and the people have erected this at their own expense, having remitted the money to the state, for Marcus Servilius Draco Albucianus, son of Publius, of the Quirina tribe, because of his merits; the place was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-24100079.summary: This public monument honors Marcus Servilius Draco Albucianus for his merits, funded by the local government and populace, with a plot granted by decree, likely in the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24100080.translation: The Senate and people of Gigthis decreed that statues be erected for Gaius Servilius Quirina Maurinus, perpetual priest, son of Marcus Servilius Plautus, perpetual priest, and for his wife Paulina, with individual contributions, in recognition of his merits and generosity; Tani and Ioco, approving, contributed.
EDCS-24100080.summary: This inscription records a decree by the Senate and people of Gigthis to erect statues for Gaius Servilius Maurinus and his wife Paulina, honoring his merits and generosity as a perpetual priest.

EDCS-24100081.translation: Erected with the magnificence of her husband, Gaius Servilius Maurinus, perpetual priest, with public money.
EDCS-24100081.summary: This inscription records a monument erected at public expense by Gaius Servilius Maurinus, perpetual priest, in honor of his wife.

EDCS-24100082.translation: To Servilia Mae, daughter of Gaius Servilius Serenus, of excellent memory, wife of Gaius Servaeus, son of Gaius, of the Quirina tribe, Messia Pacai, a Roman knight and perpetual priest, an excellent patroness; by the elders of her household.
EDCS-24100082.summary: This funerary inscription honors Servilia Mae, daughter of Gaius Servilius Serenus and wife of Gaius Servaeus Messius Pacai, a Roman knight and perpetual priest.

EDCS-24100084.translation: At the request of Marcus Ummidius Quirina Sedatus, ornament of the fatherland, with the consent of the people and the order of decurions, the council decreed a statue for him publicly; Marcus Ummidius Sedatus, pleased with this honor, erected and dedicated it with his own money.
EDCS-24100084.summary: This inscription records that the council decreed a public statue for Marcus Ummidius Sedatus, an ornament of the fatherland, which he then paid for and dedicated himself.

EDCS-24100085.translation: To Gaius, son of O., aedile.
EDCS-24100085.summary: This inscription records the dedication by Gaius, son of O., in his capacity as an aedile.

EDCS-24100093.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Gaius Messius Hermet made this for his wife Messia Spicula and for himself.
EDCS-24100093.summary: This is a funerary inscription where Gaius Messius Hermet dedicated a monument to his wife Messia Spicula and himself.

EDCS-24100102.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Quintus Apuleius Maxssimus, also called Rideus, son of Iuzale, grandson of Iurathe, lived 90 years. His most dutiful sons, Pudens, Severus, and Maxsimus, and his most loving wife Thanubra, made this for their most loving father with their own money.
EDCS-24100102.summary: This funerary inscription records the dedication of a tomb by the family of Quintus Apuleius Maxssimus (also called Rideus), who lived to be 90 years old.

EDCS-24100103.translation: Sacred to the Genius of Tisavar Augustus. Ulpius Paulinus, centurion of the III Augusta legion, fulfilled his vow with the detachment he commanded, under Vibianus and Myron as optio.
EDCS-24100103.summary: This inscription records the fulfillment of a vow by Ulpius Paulinus, a centurion of the III Augusta legion, to the Genius of Tisavar Augustus.

EDCS-24100107.translation: The Centenarium of Tibubuci, which Valerius Vibianus, a most accomplished man, commissioned to be begun, Aurelius Quintianus, a most accomplished man and governor of the province of Tripolitana, saw completed.
EDCS-24100107.summary: This inscription records the construction of a building called the Centenarium of Tibubuci, commissioned by Valerius Vibianus and completed under the supervision of the provincial governor Aurelius Quintianus.

EDCS-24100111.translation: Emperor Caesar Publius Licinius Gallienus Pius Felix Invictus Augustus Germanicus Persicus Maximus, supreme pontiff, holding tribunician power for the 12th time, consul V, father of the country, proconsul, established the camp of the 8th Cohort of Fida in a suitable location from the ground up, with his bravest soldiers working from the Tripolitanian frontier.
EDCS-24100111.summary: This inscription records the establishment of a military camp for the 8th Cohort of Fida by Emperor Gallienus, built by his soldiers from the Tripolitanian frontier.

EDCS-24100115.translation: To the Divine Shades and the Genius of Tarquitia Marcella, most devoted mother. Aemilia Rusilla, her daughter, made this with her own money for her most holy mother, who lived 61 years, more or less.
EDCS-24100115.summary: This funerary inscription, dedicated by a daughter to her mother, likely dates from the Imperial period and records the creation of a monument for the deceased.

EDCS-24100116.translation: To the Divine Shades. Cuemobeius Faustus made this tomb for himself and his wife.
EDCS-24100116.summary: This funerary inscription, likely from the Imperial period, records a man making a tomb for himself and his wife.

EDCS-24100119.translation: For the Manilii and Arellii. On these estates, Marcus Manilius Ingenuus, a most devoted man, and Arellia Nepotilla, his respectable wife, and their sons, grandsons, and great-grandsons, may they live, grow old, and achieve greater things. The tower was completed in its arrangement by them, through the diligent effort of their slave, Rufinus, the estate manager, with construction carried out by Rufinus, the stonemason, and Sigo, lovers of their household.
EDCS-24100119.summary: This inscription, likely from the Imperial period, records the completion of a tower on estates owned by the Manilii and Arellii families, with specific mention of the overseeing slave and builders.

EDCS-24100125.translation: Rania gave seven hundred thousand sesterces.
EDCS-24100125.summary: This very brief inscription, likely from the Imperial period, records a donation of money by an individual named Rania.

EDCS-24100126.translation: To the Divine Shades. Gargilius Victorinus made this for his wife Antonia Pollica and for himself.
EDCS-24100126.summary: This funerary inscription, likely from the Imperial period, records a husband dedicating a monument to his wife and himself.

EDCS-24100127.summary: This very brief inscription, likely from the Imperial period, is a dedication or memorial to an individual named Decimus Aelius.

EDCS-24100128.translation: To the Divine Shades. For Arellia LyIsistratenis.
EDCS-24100128.summary: This funerary inscription, likely from the Imperial period, is a dedication to an individual named Arellia LyIsistratenis.

EDCS-24100129.translation: To the Divine Shades. For Valeria Procula, Lucius Caecilius Cerealis, her husband, lived 73 years.
EDCS-24100129.summary: This funerary inscription, likely from the Imperial period, records a husband dedicating a monument to his wife Valeria Procula and states her lifespan.

EDCS-24100130.summary: This inscription, likely from the Imperial period, identifies an individual named Ianuarius and his military rank.

EDCS-24100137.text_edition: \n Legio III Augusta leimitavit sic Caio Vibio Marso proconsule III dextra decumanum LXX ultra kardinem CCLXXX\n
EDCS-24100137.translation: Legio III Augusta marked out [the boundary] as follows, under the proconsul Gaius Vibius Marsus for the third time: seventy paces on the right, 280 paces beyond the cardo.
EDCS-24100137.summary: A boundary marker inscription set up by Legio III Augusta during the proconsulship of Gaius Vibius Marsus, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24100141.translation: Legio III Augusta honored Gaius Vibius Marsus, proconsul, for the third time.
EDCS-24100141.summary: This inscription, likely from the Imperial period, records an honor bestowed by Legio III Augusta upon Gaius Vibius Marsus, a proconsul, for the third occasion.

EDCS-24100147.translation: To the Divine Manes. Emianus and his son dedicated this to Marcus Clementinus, son of Aulus, and Hinit, his wife.
EDCS-24100147.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Marcus Clementinus and his wife Hinit, set up by Emianus and his son.

EDCS-24100148.translation: To the Divine Manes, sacred. Quintus Petronius Felix, son of Lucius Senti, lived 95 years. Petronius Quintillus Restitus and his grandsons dedicated this to their most dutiful father.
EDCS-24100148.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Quintus Petronius Felix, set up by his grandson and great-grandsons, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24100149.translation: To the Divine Manes, sacred. [---] and his sons of the Third Augustan Legion. [---] to his sons.
EDCS-24100149.summary: This is a funerary inscription, likely for a soldier of the Third Augustan Legion, dedicated to his sons.

EDCS-24100150.translation: To the Divine Manes, sacred. R. VAN. His heirs, the freedmen and freedwomen of their procurator, to them.
EDCS-24100150.summary: This is a funerary inscription for an individual identified by the initials R. VAN., set up by his heirs and freedmen.

EDCS-24100153.translation: Sacred to Augustus for the safety of the Emperor Nerva Trajan Caesar Augustus Germanicus Dacicus, by the sufetes Atticus and Fronto, Maslae.
EDCS-24100153.summary: This is a dedication made to Emperor Trajan for his safety by the sufetes Atticus and Fronto, likely during Trajan's reign (98-117 AD).

EDCS-24100155.translation: To the Divine Manes. Valeria Celerina, daughter of Rusticus Gergos, priestess of the colony of Thaenae, lived 75 years.
EDCS-24100155.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Valeria Celerina, a priestess of the colony of Thaenae, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24100156.translation: To the Divine Manes. Lucius Aemilius Felix lived 72 years.
EDCS-24100156.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Aemilius Felix, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24100157.translation: To the Divine Manes. Lucius Antonius Elegans lived 6 years.
EDCS-24100157.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Antonius Elegans, a child who died at the age of six.

EDCS-24100158.translation: To the Divine Manes, sacred. Quintus Aurelius Hospes lived 33 years.
EDCS-24100158.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Quintus Aurelius Hospes, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24200112.translation: Lucius Aemilius Adiutor, president of the sacred rites of Liber Pater of the Augusta curia, [donated] with his own money for his merits, [in the] year of the Augusta curia.
EDCS-24200112.summary: This is a dedication by Lucius Aemilius Adiutor, a religious official, to the Augusta curia for his merits, likely during the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24200113.translation: To Quirina, for Catullus, who served as aedile, quaestor of the treasury, pontifex, prefect for administering justice, president of sacred rites, and patron of the Youth of the Ulpian Curia.
EDCS-24200113.summary: This inscription honors Catullus, listing his various public and religious offices, likely on a monument dedicated by the Youth of the Ulpian Curia.

EDCS-24200114.translation: To Marcia Pompeiana, daughter of Sextus, of the Caesienus tribe, an eternal priestess from Leptis, an excellent woman; Marcus Caecilius Lurianus and Publius Postumius Marianus [dedicate this].
EDCS-24200114.summary: This is a dedication to Marcia Pompeiana, an eternal priestess, likely by her family or friends, indicating her status and origin.

EDCS-24200115.translation: To Marcus Nonius Capito, son of Lucius, of the Papiria tribe, honored with all offices in his state; Marcus Caecilius Lurianus and Publius Postumius Marianus [dedicate this].
EDCS-24200115.summary: This inscription honors Marcus Nonius Capito for his distinguished career in public service within his community.

EDCS-24200117.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Marcus Caelius Fuscus lived 70 years.
EDCS-24200117.summary: A brief funerary epitaph recording the name and age at death of Marcus Caelius Fuscus.

EDCS-24200187.translation: Freed and unburdened, you endured the underworld by your sister's care, deserted by life, separated forever, you shun the gentle light and sad labors, received in the earth of father Pluto's hall. You were troubled by earthly concerns while life remained, and by wretched worries, not yet mindful of Orcus. The Fates, separating us from our blood kin, wished to cast us down by cruel grief. Only peace keeps you in the tomb, remaining in the earth. We have placed ashes and bones in hidden places and perfumes. You lived thirty years and two months and six days. Both father and mother have you as a youth, and hurrying. Therefore, may you be favorable to me as a god forever for your merits. Peregrinus, your brother, adorns you with song. Lucius Ummidius rests here. May any passerby read this with goodwill.
EDCS-24200187.summary: An elaborate funerary poem for Lucius Ummidius, erected by his brother Peregrinus, likely from the Roman Imperial period, lamenting his early death and celebrating his character.

EDCS-24200632.translation: In good memory of Adiutoris, who lived in peace for 35 years, 5 months, and 5 days.

EDCS-24200633.translation: In good memory of Aurelius Hospitalis, who lived 37 years; his guardians made this.
EDCS-24200633.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespan of Aurelius Hospitalis and states that his guardians erected the monument.

EDCS-24200638.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription that attempts to record the lifespan of Pompo.

EDCS-24200639.translation: In good memory of Innocens Rustica, who lived two years, ten months, and twenty-one days; she sleeps in peace.
EDCS-24200639.summary: This funerary inscription records the short lifespan and peaceful repose of Innocens Rustica.

EDCS-24200640.translation: Atticus lived 6 years, 3 months, 5 days, and 7 hours.
EDCS-24200640.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of a child named Atticus.

EDCS-24200643.translation: To the Divine Female Spirits, 22 years of age. Cittinus, son of N. TH., lived 10 years and 4 days.
EDCS-24200643.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Cittinus, indicating his age at death and the duration of his life.

EDCS-24200644.translation: For Luna, for the safety of the Emperor Caesar Augustus, father of the fatherland, Manius Gavius Tetricius, son of Marcus, augur.
EDCS-24200644.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the goddess Luna, possibly by the augur Manius Gavius Tetricius, for the safety of Emperor Augustus.

EDCS-24200645.translation: To the holy god Mercury, and the Genius of the colony of Thysdritanum, Flavius Vinnus, son of Faustinus, willingly and deservedly fulfills a promised vow.
EDCS-24200645.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Mercury and the Genius of the colony of Thysdritanum by Flavius Vinnus.

EDCS-24200649.summary: This records a votive offering by Substantius, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24200650.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely a funerary monument, bearing only the name Marcus Helvius Felix.

EDCS-24200652.translation: The entire curia, owing him twenty-one chariot races and every kind of public show, set up this (monument) for Aurelius Felix, the Emperor Maximianus Augustus, first magistrate, as a reward for his abundant generosity, benevolence, and example of integrity.
EDCS-24200652.summary: This inscription records a monument erected by a municipal council to honor Aurelius Felix, likely a magistrate, for his munificence in providing public games and spectacles.

EDCS-24200655.translation: Flavius Martialis, centurion, lived 36 years in peace.
EDCS-24200655.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Flavius Martialis, a centurion, stating his age at death.

EDCS-24200656.translation: [...] ordered games with twelve palm fronds for the birthdays of his daughters Victorina and Macedonia, and also prize baskets and a feast for the people, which he commanded to be given annually, from his own money, as a good citizen.
EDCS-24200656.summary: This inscription, likely from a public monument, records the endowment by a citizen for games and distributions to the populace in honor of his daughters, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24200669.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription that appears to record the name of Lucius Iulius Eg...

EDCS-24200674.translation: To the Divine Spirits, Cornelia Honorata, mother, (set this up)...
EDCS-24200674.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription begun by Cornelia Honorata, identified as a mother.

EDCS-24200675.translation: To the Divine Spirits, Lucius Gessius, son of Sextus, lived...
EDCS-24200675.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription for Lucius Gessius, son of Sextus, indicating his lifespan.

EDCS-24200676.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed, sacred. Ianuarius lived for 50 years. To Rufia Callicora, his dearest wife.
EDCS-24200676.summary: This is a tombstone recording the death of Ianuarius at age 50, erected by his wife Rufia Callicora, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24200677.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Lucius Pomponius Amandulus lived for 1 year, 6 months, and 11 days. Lucius Pomponius Urbanus for his dearest son.
EDCS-24200677.summary: This is a tombstone recording the death of Lucius Pomponius Amandulus at age 1 year, 6 months, and 11 days, erected by his father Lucius Pomponius Urbanus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24200682.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription mentioning Peregrinus and invoking divine refreshment, likely from a funerary context.

EDCS-24200686.summary: This inscription records a land grant or ownership of 202 iugera by Hermonius Saturninus.

EDCS-24200689.translation: To Annonis, son of Annonis, from Minthon, a wolf, aged 75 years.
EDCS-24200689.summary: This inscription is likely a funerary text for Annonis, son of Annonis, who lived to be 75 years old.

EDCS-24200690.summary: This inscription is a funerary record for Murena, who died at the age of 27.

EDCS-24200691.summary: This inscription is a funerary record for Iannuarius, stating he lived for twenty years.

EDCS-24200692.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Caesellia Nina lived for 70 years. Her pious sister Eleutheris made this.
EDCS-24200692.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Caesellia Nina at age 70, dedicated by her sister Eleutheris.

EDCS-24200693.translation: To the Divine Shades. I, Fabius Saturninus, lived for about 106 years.
EDCS-24200693.summary: This inscription is a funerary text for Fabius Saturninus, who is said to have lived for approximately 106 years.

EDCS-24200694.summary: This inscription likely records the name and parentage of L. Tutpate.

EDCS-24200697.translation: In memory of Abbot Iader, who lived in peace for 50 years, rested on the day of the Ides of December.
EDCS-24200697.summary: This funerary inscription commemorates Abbot Iader, who lived for 50 years and died on the Ides of December.

EDCS-24200698.translation: Of Plotina Augusta, wife of Emperor Caesar Nerva Traianus.
EDCS-24200698.summary: This inscription is a dedication or memorial fragment related to Plotina Augusta, wife of Emperor Trajan.

EDCS-24200699.text_edition: \n Lucio Silicio Luci filio Claudia Saturnino militi legionis III Augustae centuria Iuli Liguris vixit annos XL militavit annos XVIIII defunctus in pugna sub Lucilio centurione inter Aras et Vatari Rerrichae Rustici Romani filiae Silicius Luci filius Felix matri et fratri de sua inpensa fecit\n
EDCS-24200699.translation: To Lucius Silicius, son of Lucius, a soldier of the III Augusta legion, from the century of Iulius Liguris. He lived 40 years and served 19 years, died in battle under Centurion Lucilius between Aras and Vataris. Silicius Felix, son of Lucius, made this for his mother and brother at his own expense.
EDCS-24200699.summary: This is a tombstone for Lucius Silicius, a soldier of the III Augusta legion who died in battle, erected by his surviving son Silicius Felix for his mother and brother, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24300059.translation: These are the names of the martyrs: Petrus, Paulus, Saturninus the presbyter, the same Saturninus, Bindemius, Saturninus, Donatus, Saturninus, Gududa, Paula, Clara, Lucilla, Fortunata, Iader, Caecilius, Aemilius, who suffered on the day of the Nones of August and were buried on the 6th day before the Ides of November. Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace to men.
EDCS-24300059.summary: This inscription lists the names of martyrs, their feast days and burial dates, likely from a Christian context.

EDCS-24300060.translation: Bishop Honorius lived for 90 years, buried on the 8th day before the Ides of August.
EDCS-24300060.summary: This epitaph records the lifespan and burial date of Bishop Honorius, likely from a late Roman or early medieval period.

EDCS-24300061.translation: Bishop Baleriolus lived for 82 years, buried on the 8th day before the Kalends of October.
EDCS-24300061.summary: This epitaph records the lifespan and burial date of Bishop Baleriolus, likely from a late Roman or early medieval period.

EDCS-24300062.translation: Emeritus the priest lived for 64 years in peace.
EDCS-24300062.summary: This epitaph records the lifespan of Emeritus, a priest, suggesting a late Roman or early Christian burial context.

EDCS-24300063.translation: Crescentius the deacon lived for 65 years in peace, and his son Bruttanicus lived for 28 years in peace.
EDCS-24300063.summary: This epitaph records the lifespans of Crescentius, a deacon, and his son Bruttanicus, suggesting a family burial from a late Roman or early Christian context.

EDCS-24300064.translation: Quintus the lector lived for 22 years and one month and 17 days.
EDCS-24300064.summary: This epitaph records the lifespan of Quintus, a lector, indicating a burial from a late Roman or early Christian community.

EDCS-24300065.translation: Julius Honorius, perpetual priest, lived for 62 years in peace.
EDCS-24300065.summary: This epitaph records the lifespan of Julius Honorius, a perpetual priest, from a late Roman or early Christian context.

EDCS-24300066.translation: Aripectus of Zarzio lived for 70 years in peace; let those who are worthy receive [this blessing?].
EDCS-24300066.summary: This epitaph records the lifespan of Aripectus of Zarzio and includes a somewhat enigmatic religious exhortation, likely from a late Roman or early Christian period.

EDCS-24300067.translation: Aprilis lived for 16 years in peace.
EDCS-24300067.summary: This epitaph records the lifespan of Aprilis, suggesting a burial from a late Roman or early Christian context.

EDCS-24300068.translation: Babelo lived for 50 years in peace.
EDCS-24300068.summary: This epitaph records the lifespan of Babelo, suggesting a burial from a late Roman or early Christian context.

EDCS-24300069.translation: S. Audiens lived for [?] years and two months in Christ; Bonifatia Audiens lived for one year and 4 months in the peace of Christ.
EDCS-24300069.summary: This epitaph records the lifespans of S. Audiens and Bonifatia Audiens, likely from a late Roman or early Christian burial.

EDCS-24300070.translation: Cilonia Grata lived in peace for 60 years, 6 months, and 20 days.
EDCS-24300070.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Cilonia Grata.

EDCS-24300071.translation: Crescentia lived in peace for four years; Secunda lived in peace for ten years.
EDCS-24300071.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespans of two individuals, Crescentia and Secunda.

EDCS-24300072.translation: Donatianus lived in peace for 60 years.
EDCS-24300072.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan of Donatianus.

EDCS-24300073.translation: Fabia Restituta lived in peace for 34 years and 5 months.
EDCS-24300073.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan of Fabia Restituta.

EDCS-24300074.translation: May Faonius rest in peace; he lived for 85 years.
EDCS-24300074.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan of Faonius, with a plea for his repose.

EDCS-24300075.translation: Fastiditus lived in peace for 22 years and rested.
EDCS-24300075.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan of Fastiditus and notes his rest.

EDCS-24300076.translation: Faustina the faithful lived in peace for 53 years.
EDCS-24300076.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan of Faustina, described as faithful.

EDCS-24300078.translation: Felicianus lived in peace for 50 years and 13 days.

EDCS-24300079.translation: Felicitas the faithful lived in peace for 7 years; she rested on the day before the Ides of August.
EDCS-24300079.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan and repose date of Felicitas, described as faithful.

EDCS-24300080.translation: Felix the faithful lived in peace for eight years.
EDCS-24300080.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan of Felix, described as faithful.

EDCS-24300082.translation: Fortunatus lived in peace for 53 years; he departed four days before the Kalends of June.
EDCS-24300082.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan and death date of Fortunatus.

EDCS-24300083.translation: Gaudentia lived in peace for twenty years.
EDCS-24300083.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Gaudentia.

EDCS-24300085.summary: A very brief funerary epitaph for Irene.

EDCS-24300086.translation: Julia, most holy girl, in peace.

EDCS-24300087.translation: Lucilianus lived in peace for fifty-two years.
EDCS-24300087.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Lucilianus.

EDCS-24300088.translation: Maioricus lived in peace for five years and thirteen days.
EDCS-24300088.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Maioricus.

EDCS-24300089.summary: A funerary epitaph for Maxima, described as faithful.

EDCS-24300090.translation: To the good memory of Optantius, who lived in peace for 68 years.
EDCS-24300090.summary: A funerary epitaph with a wish for good memory and the lifespan of Optantius.

EDCS-24300091.translation: Pascasius lived in peace for 32 years; he departed eight days before the Kalends of December.
EDCS-24300091.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan and death date of Pascasius.

EDCS-24300092.translation: Petrus rested in peace four days before the Kalends of March; he lived 55 years; he rested in peace on the Kalends of January.
EDCS-24300092.summary: A funerary epitaph for Petrus, recording his death date, lifespan, and another death date, likely indicating a complex burial history or inscription error.

EDCS-24300093.translation: Filocalus lived in peace for 50 years; he departed on the 6th day before the Kalends of February.
EDCS-24300093.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan and death date of Filocalus.

EDCS-24300094.translation: Quadratianus, faithful, lived in peace for 2 years and 5 months; he departed on the 8th day before the Kalends of May.
EDCS-24300094.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan and death date of Quadratianus.

EDCS-24300095.translation: Quadratianus lived in peace for 60 years; he was laid to rest on the 15th day before the Kalends of October.
EDCS-24300095.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan and burial date of Quadratianus.

EDCS-24300097.translation: Reparatus, faithful, lived in peace for 1 year and 3 months; he departed on the 15th day before the Kalends of March.
EDCS-24300097.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan and death date of Reparatus.

EDCS-24300098.translation: Restutus lived in peace for 60 years.
EDCS-24300098.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Restutus.

EDCS-24300099.translation: Rusticilla, faithful, lived for nine years.
EDCS-24300099.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Rusticilla.

EDCS-24300100.translation: Saturninus lived in peace for 7 years; he was laid to rest on the 13th day before the Kalends of July.
EDCS-24300100.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan and burial date of Saturninus.

EDCS-24300101.translation: Secundianus and his wife Restuta, in peace.

EDCS-24300102.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Sperendeu.

EDCS-24300103.translation: Varius Donatianus lived for 20 years and 45 days.
EDCS-24300103.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Varius Donatianus.
