EDCS-24300104.translation: Vernacula lived in peace for 14 years.
EDCS-24300104.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Vernacula, who lived for 14 years.

EDCS-24300105.translation: Bernaculus the faithful lived in peace for 80 years.
EDCS-24300105.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Bernaculus, who lived for 80 years.

EDCS-24300106.translation: Victoria the faithful lived in peace for 20 years.
EDCS-24300106.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Victoria, who lived for 20 years.

EDCS-24300108.translation: [Name] lived in peace for 75 years, departed on the 15th day before the Kalends of March.
EDCS-24300108.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of an individual and their date of death, estimated to be in the later Roman Empire due to the phrasing 'lived in peace'.

EDCS-24300114.summary: This is a dedication to a woman named Sufetula, likely a benefactress or patron.

EDCS-24300116.translation: Iola the faithful lived in peace for 34 years; rested on the 3rd Ides of October.
EDCS-24300116.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan and date of death of Iola, a faithful individual.

EDCS-24300117.translation: Mamma Donata lived faithfully in peace for more or less seventy years.
EDCS-24300117.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Mamma Donata, stating she lived faithfully in peace for approximately 70 years.

EDCS-24300118.translation: Rufina the faithful lived in peace for 37 years; conclusion on the day of the Kalends of February.
EDCS-24300118.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Rufina, who lived for 37 years and whose end is noted on the Kalends of February.

EDCS-24300119.translation: I, Marcus Fabius Eutyches, fulfilled [my] vow.
EDCS-24300119.summary: This is a votive inscription where Marcus Fabius Eutyches dedicates a fulfillment of a vow, likely to a deity.

EDCS-24300124.translation: To [the emperor] from the tribune of the 32nd Volunteer Cohort, tribune of the 13th Gemina Legion, prefect of cavalry of the Vettones' Wing, prefect of cavalry of the 2nd Flavian Wing (Miliaria), curator of the Pedana road, procurator of the Augusti of the province of Upper Pannonia, procurator of the Augusti of the Hadrumetine region, by decree of the decurions, with public money.
EDCS-24300124.summary: This inscription lists the extensive career of a high-ranking Roman official who held numerous military and administrative posts, funded by public money and approved by local councils.

EDCS-24300125.translation: Although the council of Segermes had decreed a statue of Decimus Julius Saturninus, son of Decimus, of the Arnensis tribe, a tribune of the legion, at public expense, his parents Decimus Julius Saturninus and Marcia Pacata remitted the money and erected it at their own expense.
EDCS-24300125.summary: This inscription records the erection of a statue by parents who replaced a public monument with one funded privately.

EDCS-24300128.translation: By the sacred indulgence of our lords Constantius and Constans, Maxim[...
EDCS-24300128.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely related to imperial authority and potentially a dedication or grant, dating to the mid-4th century CE.

EDCS-24300130.translation: Caius Aurelius Rogatus Karpianus [paid] 200 sesterces; Titus Aurelius Numidius, his son, [paid] 300 sesterces.
EDCS-24300130.summary: This inscription records two individuals' payments, possibly for a public work or a shared expense, from an unspecified location and date.

EDCS-24300132.translation: Of Decimus Avianius, son of Decimus.
EDCS-24300132.summary: This is a very short inscription that likely served as a dedication or ownership marker, possibly for a tomb or monument.

EDCS-24300137.translation: Iianus lived for 67 years. Apocidia Urbana lived for 35 years. Quintus Caelius Saturninus, the son, made [this] for his most dutiful parents. They are buried here.
EDCS-24300137.summary: This is a tomb inscription commemorating the lives of Iianus, Apocidia Urbana, and the son Quintus Caelius Saturninus who erected it for his parents.

EDCS-24300138.translation: Sacred to Saturn Augustus. Quintus Caecilius, son of Quintus, of the Arnensis tribe.
EDCS-24300138.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the god Saturn Augustus by Quintus Caecilius, son of Quintus, of the Arnensis tribe.

EDCS-24300141.translation: For Gaius Julius Maximus, honored with public equestrian rank, having held the office of aedile and quaestor in the most splendid colony of Iulia Aurelia Antoniana Karthago, and curator of the state in the most splendid municipium of Abthugna, the council, at its own expense, erected [this] because of his notable affection and sincerity towards the state, the council, and all citizens.
EDCS-24300141.summary: This inscription records the erection of a monument by the council of Abthugna in honor of Gaius Julius Maximus for his public service and integrity.

EDCS-24300143.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Dead. Domitia Concessa, dutiful daughter of Lucius, lived for 43 years. She is buried here. Sacred to the Spirits of the Dead. S. A., dutiful daughter of Lucius, Fortunata, lived for 18 years and 2 months. She is buried here.
EDCS-24300143.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the deaths and ages of two women, Domitia Concessa and Fortunata, likely family members.

EDCS-24300144.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Dead. Caius Bennius Quintianus lived for 60 years, 3 months, and 10 days. He is buried here.
EDCS-24300144.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the death and age of Caius Bennius Quintianus.

EDCS-24300145.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Dead. Iulia Caelia Tertia, wife of Magnus Saturninus, dutiful, lived for 20 years and 11 [months]. She is buried here.
EDCS-24300145.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the death and age of Iulia Caelia Tertia, wife of Magnus Saturninus.

EDCS-24300146.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Marcus Aelius Strator, in accordance with the terms of the will, made this monument to Memoria, wife of Marcus Aelius Maevius Primus, at his own expense.
EDCS-24300146.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Marcus Aelius Strator for Memoria, wife of Marcus Aelius Maevius Primus, as stipulated in her will.

EDCS-24300147.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Lucius Mussius Balbus Placidianus, dutiful, lived 19 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-24300147.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Mussius Balbus Placidianus, who died at the age of 19.

EDCS-24300148.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Sabinia Marciana, dutiful daughter of Marcus and wife of Bullius Curius Saturninus, lived 10 years, 4 months, and 6 days; she is buried here.
EDCS-24300148.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Sabinia Marciana, who died at the age of 10 years, 4 months, and 6 days.

EDCS-24300149.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Iana lived 1 year, 7 months, and 2 days; she is buried here.
EDCS-24300149.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a child named Iana, who died at the age of 1 year, 7 months, and 2 days.

EDCS-24300150.summary: This is an incomplete funerary inscription recording the name Geminia Prima and the beginning of her age.

EDCS-24300151.summary: This is a very brief inscription recording the name Izdon and his filiation.

EDCS-24300153.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Quintus Calicius Pudens, soldier, lived [age incomplete]; he is buried here.
EDCS-24300153.summary: This is an incomplete funerary inscription for Quintus Calicius Pudens, a soldier.

EDCS-24300154.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Publius Considius Donatus Victorinus, dutiful, lived 17 years, 9 months, and 17 days; he is buried here.
EDCS-24300154.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Publius Considius Donatus Victorinus, who died at the age of 17 years, 9 months, and 17 days.

EDCS-24300156.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Lucius Vibius Quintianus lived 15 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-24300156.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Vibius Quintianus, who died at the age of 15.

EDCS-24300157.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Liberia lived 2 years.
EDCS-24300157.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Liberia, who died at the age of 2.

EDCS-24300162.translation: To the Divine Manes. Gaius Licinius Martinus lived 75 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-24300162.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan and burial of Gaius Licinius Martinus.

EDCS-24300163.translation: To the Divine Manes. Lucius Aufidius Saturninus Iulianus lived 44 years, 9 months, and 25 days. Aucanus and Fructus...
EDCS-24300163.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Lucius Aufidius Saturninus Iulianus and mentioning dedicants Aucanus and Fructus.

EDCS-24300166.translation: To the Divine Manes. Annaeus Nonianus the pious lived 77 years and 6 months. Gaius Annaeus Nonianus Quartianus the pious [and] Quartilla to their most pious husband and son...
EDCS-24300166.summary: A funerary epitaph for Annaeus Nonianus and his son, dedicated by Quartilla.

EDCS-24300167.translation: To Ulpia Severina Pia, wife of our lord the Emperor Caesar Lucius Domitius Aurelianus Pius Felix Augustus. The municipality of Augusti Semta, devoted to his divine majesty and greatness.
EDCS-24300167.summary: An inscription dedicating a monument by the municipality of Augusti Semta to Ulpia Severina Pia, wife of Emperor Aurelian.

EDCS-24300168.translation: To Flavius Valerius Constantius, most noble Caesar Augustus. The people of Semta, by public decree of the decurions and at public expense.
EDCS-24300168.summary: A dedication by the people of Semta to Caesar Flavius Valerius Constantius.

EDCS-24300169.translation: To the Invincible Divine Power of Augustus. Annius Bassianus, son of Raclae Ann, Amip D...
EDCS-24300169.summary: A dedication to the divine power of Augustus by Annius Bassianus.

EDCS-24300170.translation: To the Invincible Divine Power of Augustus. Annius Bassianus, son of Raclae Ann, Amip D...
EDCS-24300170.summary: A dedication to the divine power of Augustus by Annius Bassianus.

EDCS-24300172.translation: Quintus Aemilius Pastor, son of Lucius, of the Arnensian tribe, lived 65 years. Quintus Aemilius Secundus, a soldier of the III Augusta legion, set this up for his father.
EDCS-24300172.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by a soldier for his father, recording his lifespan.

EDCS-24300173.translation: Publius Helvidius Ma, a column, spiral, and other works of column construction, at his own expense.
EDCS-24300173.summary: A record of a private commission for a column, spiral, and other decorative architectural elements.

EDCS-24300174.text_edition: \n Caius Geminius Rufus pius vixit annos LVII hic situs est\n
EDCS-24300174.translation: Gaius Geminius Rufus, dutiful, lived 57 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-24300174.summary: A tombstone recording the life and burial of Gaius Geminius Rufus, likely dating to the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-24300177.translation: To the Emperor Caesar, son of the deified Trajan Parthicus, grandson of the deified Nerva, Trajan Hadrian Augustus, pontifex maximus, with tribunician power for the 13th time, consul for the 3rd time, father of the country. The Roman citizens who reside in the village of Hateria.
EDCS-24300177.summary: A dedication to Emperor Hadrian by Roman citizens residing in the village of Hateria.

EDCS-24300178.translation: The gentile name of Ulpius Speratus.
EDCS-24300178.summary: This inscription records the gentile name of Ulpius Speratus, likely on a tombstone.

EDCS-24300179.translation: Ulpius Speratus, next to his wife.
EDCS-24300179.summary: This inscription mentions Ulpius Speratus and his wife, possibly indicating their burial place.

EDCS-24300183.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Haerennia Victoria, dutiful, lived 90 years.
EDCS-24300183.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Haerennia Victoria, recording her name, piety, and age at death.

EDCS-24300184.translation: His sons Aemilius and Felix Maximus made this for him because of his merits.
EDCS-24300184.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by sons to their father in recognition of his merits.

EDCS-24300185.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Meintia lived 60 years.
EDCS-24300185.summary: This funerary epitaph records the name and age at death of Meintia.

EDCS-24300189.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Lucius Caecilius Silvanus, son of Quintus, lived 6 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-24300189.summary: A tombstone for a young child, Lucius Caecilius Silvanus, who died at the age of six, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-24300192.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Aemilius Saturninus lived 3 years, 4 months, and 3 days.
EDCS-24300192.summary: This funerary epitaph records the name and very young age at death of Lucius Aemilius Saturninus.

EDCS-24300193.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, sacred. Lucius Rasinius Celer lived 85 years. Quintus Rasinius Saturninus, his most dutiful son, made this for his father. He is buried here.
EDCS-24300193.summary: A tombstone dedicated by a son to his deceased father, Lucius Rasinius Celer, who lived to the age of 85, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-24300194.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, sacred. Vibia Donata lived [...]
EDCS-24300194.summary: A partial tombstone for Vibia Donata, recording her name and the beginning of her lifespan, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-24300199.translation: Dominus Iannarius, from whom he was released from chains, gave thanks, bound by your goodness, O Christ.
EDCS-24300199.summary: This inscription is a votive thanksgiving from Dominus Iannarius for his release from chains, crediting Christ.

EDCS-24300201.text_edition: \n VI Kalendas Iulias Valeriano et Lucilo consulibus domino Augusto sacrum Concessurus Luci Memnonis votum solvit\n
EDCS-24300201.translation: On the sixth day before the Kalends of July, in the consulship of Valerianus and Lucilus, Concessurus, a freedman of Lucius Memnon, fulfilled his vow to the divine emperor.
EDCS-24300201.summary: A dedication to the emperor, made by a freedman named Concessurus, dated to the consulship of Valerianus and Lucilus, likely in the late 3rd century CE.

EDCS-24300202.translation: Lucius Aemilius Saturninus paid his vow to Augustus.
EDCS-24300202.summary: This inscription records Lucius Aemilius Saturninus fulfilling a vow made to the emperor Augustus.

EDCS-24300204.summary: This inscription records Gaius Caecilius Crispinus as the maker of a monument or object.

EDCS-24300206.summary: This inscription records Datus fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-24300207.summary: This is a personal name, likely a tombstone inscription, of Felix Fuschus.

EDCS-24300208.summary: This is a patronymic, likely a tombstone inscription, identifying Fuschus as the son of Ianuarius Fuscus.

EDCS-24300209.summary: This is a personal name, likely a tombstone inscription, of Marcus Iulius Saturus Ping.

EDCS-24300210.translation: Lucius Iunius Saturninus restored it for himself and his family.
EDCS-24300210.summary: This inscription records Lucius Iunius Saturninus fulfilling an obligation for himself and his family, possibly related to a public building or offering.

EDCS-24300213.summary: This inscription records Primi Popili fulfilling a vow, likely a dedication to a deity.

EDCS-24300214.summary: This inscription records Quintus fulfilling a vow, likely a dedication to a deity.

EDCS-24300215.summary: This is a patronymic, likely a tombstone inscription, identifying Saturus as the son of Rogatus Maior.

EDCS-24300216.summary: This inscription records Silvani Donati fulfilling a vow, likely a dedication to a deity.

EDCS-24300217.translation: For the health of our patron and of Passienilla and their children, Macrinus, their freedman, whitewashed the stone of Saturn.
EDCS-24300217.summary: This inscription records the freedman Macrinus dedicating an act of whitewashing a stone of Saturn for the health of his patrons and their children.

EDCS-24300222.summary: This inscription appears to be a series of personal names, possibly a tombstone inscription, for Aliso Ruuluci Aemili Faufi.

EDCS-24300229.translation: [...], II, [consul], designated IX, X, father of the fatherland, to Lucius Iavolenus Priscus, imperial legate pro praetore. The community of the Thigenses.
EDCS-24300229.summary: A fragmentary inscription honoring Lucius Iavolenus Priscus, an imperial legate, by the community of the Thigenses, with a date indicated by consular titles, likely from the early Imperial period.

EDCS-24300230.text_edition: \n Imperatore Nerva Caesare Augusto pontifice maximo tribunicia potestate consule III Quinto Fabio Barbaro Valerio Magno Iuliano legato Augusti pro praetore castellus sic Thigensium\n
EDCS-24300230.translation: Under Emperor Nerva Caesar Augustus, pontifex maximus, in his third tribunician power, consul, with Quintus Fabius Barbarus Valerius Magnus Iulianus, imperial legate pro praetore: the fort of the Thigenses.
EDCS-24300230.summary: An inscription marking a location as the fort of the Thigenses, dated to the consulship of Emperor Nerva and Quintus Fabius Barbarus Valerius Magnus Iulianus, likely from the late 1st century CE.

EDCS-24300233.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Aelius lived 9 years.
EDCS-24300233.summary: A funerary dedication for Aelius, who died at age 9.

EDCS-24300234.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. CNVIMIIA Bonosa lived 20 years. Her sons arranged for the construction of this monument. May your bones rest well. Iula Mari lived 48 years. Her sons arranged for the construction of this monument. May your bones rest well. Lived [---].
EDCS-24300234.summary: A funerary dedication for CNVIMIIA Bonosa and Iula Mari, detailing their ages at death and that their sons erected monuments for them.

EDCS-24300235.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Sexta Clodia lived 18 years.
EDCS-24300235.summary: A funerary dedication for Sexta Clodia, who died at age 18.

EDCS-24300236.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Flavia Nina lived 80 years, Nstantia her freedwoman.
EDCS-24300236.summary: A funerary dedication for Flavia Nina, who died at age 80, and her freedwoman.

EDCS-24300237.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Quintus Gellius Secundus lived 16 years.
EDCS-24300237.summary: A funerary dedication for Quintus Gellius Secundus, who died at age 16.

EDCS-24300238.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Clodia Saturnina lived 50 years.
EDCS-24300238.summary: A funerary dedication for Clodia Saturnina, who died at age 50.

EDCS-24300239.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Caius Urbius Fortunatus lived 80 years. Pis Lucroni.
EDCS-24300239.summary: A funerary dedication for Caius Urbius Fortunatus, who died at age 80.

EDCS-24300240.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Julius Barbarus, soldier of the third Augustan legion, lived 40 years.
EDCS-24300240.summary: A funerary dedication for Julius Barbarus, a soldier of the Legio III Augusta, who died at age 40.

EDCS-24300241.translation: Julius M[---] lived 70 years. His sons made it for him from his own property.
EDCS-24300241.summary: A funerary dedication for Julius M[---], noting that his sons erected the monument using his own funds.

EDCS-24300242.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Caius Julius Ianurius, veteran, lived 85 years. Adiutor, Fructus, and Victor Tertius Felix dedicated this monument to him.
EDCS-24300242.summary: A funerary dedication for the veteran Caius Julius Ianurius, who died at age 85, by Adiutor, Fructus, and Victor Tertius Felix.

EDCS-24300243.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius lived 5 years.
EDCS-24300243.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius, who died at the age of 5.

EDCS-24300244.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Paccius Felix lived 40 years.
EDCS-24300244.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Paccius Felix, who died at the age of 40.

EDCS-24300245.text_edition: \n Genio dddominorum nnnostrorum Diocletiani et Maximiani Auggustorum et Constanti et Maximiani nobillissimorum Caessarum Varius Flavianus vir perfectissimus praeses provinciae Valeriae Byzacenae\n
EDCS-24300245.translation: To the genius of our lords Diocletian and Maximian Augusti, and of Constantius and Maximian, most noble Caesars, Varius Flavianus, a most accomplished man and governor of the province of Valeria Byzacena.
EDCS-24300245.summary: A dedication by Varius Flavianus, governor of Valeria Byzacena, to the Augusti Diocletian and Maximian, and the Caesars Constantius and Maximian, likely from the late 3rd or early 4th century CE.

EDCS-24300247.translation: Fortunula, wife of Valentinus, a centurion of the Second Flavia Legion, made (this) in gratitude to your divinity, and she lived 40 years; she made (this) for her most sweet wife, who had a father Laomedon and a mother Olympia, in the city of Sarra.
EDCS-24300247.summary: This funerary inscription records Fortunula's commemoration of her wife, who died at 40, mentioning her parents and husband's military affiliation.

EDCS-24300249.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription recording the life of Res Conia Colomi.

EDCS-24300254.translation: Felix, son of Fallus, lived 30 days. Sucita.
EDCS-24300254.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Felix, son of Fallus, who died at 30 days old.

EDCS-24300255.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Postumius R Oc N lived...
EDCS-24300255.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription mentioning Postumius.

EDCS-24300256.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription recording the lifespan of an individual described as a citizen.

EDCS-24300258.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Cnaeus Cornelius Terpnus lived 67 years. Terpnus his son made (this).
EDCS-24300258.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Cnaeus Cornelius Terpnus, erected by his son.

EDCS-24300259.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulius Rogatus, who lived 25 years, for Venusta his wife and for their daughter Iulia Venusta, and Iulius Sa...
EDCS-24300259.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription for Iulius Rogatus, his wife Venusta, and daughter Iulia Venusta.

EDCS-24300260.translation: The gens Musuniorum of Regianum made and dedicated (this) to the Emperor Caesar Marcus Antonius Gordianus Pius Felix Augustus and Tranquillina Augusta, his wife.
EDCS-24300260.summary: This inscription records a dedication by the gens Musuniorum of Regianum to Emperor Gordian III and Empress Tranquillina.

EDCS-24300261.translation: To the Divine Manes. Antonia Prima lived 30 years, at the urging of her father-in-law.
EDCS-24300261.summary: A funerary dedication for Antonia Prima, set up by her father-in-law, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24300262.translation: To the Divine Manes. Lucius Cerellius Fortunatus lived 62 years. His sons dedicated this.
EDCS-24300262.summary: A funerary monument dedicated by sons for their father, Lucius Cerellius Fortunatus, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24300263.translation: To the Divine Manes. Donatus lived 35 years and 30 days.
EDCS-24300263.summary: A funerary dedication for Donatus, who lived 35 years and 30 days, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24300299.summary: This is likely a name inscription, possibly a tombstone or dedication fragment, with no further context.

EDCS-24300300.translation: Catullus Nundiminus, 3 days before the Ides of October, [or] the Kalends of October, in the time of Maximinius.
EDCS-24300300.summary: This inscription appears to record a date and possibly a person's name or a reference to an official, possibly related to legal or administrative matters.

EDCS-24300301.summary: This inscription seems to record a date and a personal name, possibly a tombstone fragment.

EDCS-24300302.summary: This inscription records a date and a personal name or abbreviation, likely part of a larger text such as a calendar or record.

EDCS-24300303.translation: The day before the Kalends of October. Novellus.
EDCS-24300303.summary: This inscription records a specific date and a personal name, likely part of a record or funerary text.

EDCS-24300304.translation: 17th day before the Kalends of June. Onunusa.
EDCS-24300304.summary: This inscription records a specific date and a personal name, possibly a tombstone fragment.

EDCS-24300305.translation: 6th day before the Ides of December. P. da[tavit?]
EDCS-24300305.summary: This inscription records a date and the beginning of a name or verb, possibly a dedication or record.

EDCS-24300306.translation: On the fifteenth day before the Kalends of August, Paula [dedicated this].
EDCS-24300306.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Paula on July 18th, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24300307.translation: On the third Ides of May, Paulus [dedicated this].
EDCS-24300307.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Paulus on May 13th, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24300310.translation: On the fourteenth day before the Kalends of October, Privata [dedicated this].
EDCS-24300310.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Privata on September 18th, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24300311.translation: On the day before the Kalends of November, Restutus [dedicated this].
EDCS-24300311.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Restutus on October 31st, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24300312.translation: On the sixth day before the Kalends of May, Rustica [dedicated this].
EDCS-24300312.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Rustica on April 26th, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24300314.translation: On the seventh day before the Kalends of August, Saturnina [dedicated this].
EDCS-24300314.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Saturnina on July 26th, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24300315.translation: On the fifteenth day before the Kalends of September, Saturninus [dedicated this].
EDCS-24300315.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Saturninus on August 18th, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24300316.translation: Sausa on the day before the Ides of October [dedicated this].
EDCS-24300316.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Sausa on October 14th, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24300317.translation: On the ninth day before the Kalends of October, Secundina [dedicated this].
EDCS-24300317.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Secundina on September 23rd, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24300318.translation: On the fifteenth day before the Kalends of July, Seroti Seroti [dedicated this].
EDCS-24300318.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Seroti Seroti on June 17th, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24300319.translation: On the third day before the Nones of May. Serv[---]
EDCS-24300319.summary: This inscription records a date and the beginning of a name, likely part of a formal dedication or record, possibly from the Imperial period.

EDCS-24300321.translation: On the Ides of September. Victoria
EDCS-24300321.summary: This inscription records a date and the name Victoria, suggesting a personal dedication or a commemoration, possibly from the Imperial period.

EDCS-24300322.translation: Vimiasius on the third day before the Kalends of May
EDCS-24300322.summary: This inscription records a personal name and a date, likely part of a dedication or memorial, possibly from the Imperial period.

EDCS-24300323.summary: This inscription is a funerary text recording the name Vincentius and the phrase 'in pace' (in peace), common on early Christian burials.

EDCS-24300324.translation: On the eighth day before the Ides. Urbanus Urbanus
EDCS-24300324.summary: This inscription records a date and a repeated personal name, possibly a dedication or a memorial from the Imperial period.

EDCS-24300329.translation: On the seventh day before the Kalends of May. Sia
EDCS-24300329.summary: This inscription records a date and a name, likely part of a dedication or memorial, possibly from the Imperial period.

EDCS-24300331.translation: On the fifth day before the Kalends of May. Rom[---]
EDCS-24300331.summary: This inscription records a date and the beginning of a name or place, likely part of a formal dedication or record, possibly from the Imperial period.

EDCS-24300334.translation: For the safety of the Emperors and Caesars Augusti, Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Armeniacus, and their children, and Lucius Aurelius Verus Armeniacus, the people of the fundus Itani built the wall of the domina Ceres with their own money and dedicated it with Publius Statius Silvanus as magistrate, who also...
EDCS-24300334.summary: This is a dedication by the tenant farmers of an estate (fundus Itani) to the goddess Ceres and for the safety of Emperors Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Armeniacus and Lucius Aurelius Verus Armeniacus, dating to their joint reign (161-169 AD).

EDCS-24300335.summary: This inscription records a personal name, Marcus Caecilius, likely the subject of a dedication, epitaph, or legal document from the Roman period.

EDCS-24300336.translation: Fortunatus. From his son. He lived for 9 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-24300336.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the name Fortunatus, his age at death (9 years), and indicating it was set up by his son, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-24300337.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Victoria lived 10 years.
EDCS-24300337.summary: A funerary dedication for Victoria, who died at the age of 10.

EDCS-24300338.summary: A dedication to the god Mercury Augustus, with names and titles that are partially preserved.

EDCS-24300339.translation: Felix, 65 years old, is buried here.
EDCS-24300339.summary: A funerary inscription recording the burial of Felix and his age.

EDCS-24300342.translation: Publius Annius Donatus, priest of Saturn, fulfilled and made a vow to the gods.
EDCS-24300342.summary: A dedication by Publius Annius Donatus, a priest of Saturn, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-24300343.translation: Lucius Iunius Pudens, priest of Saturn Augustus.
EDCS-24300343.summary: An inscription identifying Lucius Iunius Pudens as a priest of Saturn Augustus.

EDCS-24300344.translation: Quintus Muleius Felix, priest of Saturn Augustus, fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-24300344.summary: A record of Quintus Muleius Felix, a priest of Saturn Augustus, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-24300345.translation: Lucius Numitorius Felix Burri, priest of Saturn Augustus, happily fulfilled his vows.
EDCS-24300345.summary: An inscription stating that Lucius Numitorius Felix Burri, a priest of Saturn Augustus, fulfilled his vows.

EDCS-24300346.translation: Caius Octavius Bassus, priest of Saturn Augustus, fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-24300346.summary: This inscription records that Caius Octavius Bassus, a priest of Saturn Augustus, fulfilled a vow.

EDCS-24300347.translation: Lucius Octavius Severus, priest of Saturn Augustus, fulfilled his vow to Saturn Augustus.
EDCS-24300347.summary: A dedication by Lucius Octavius Severus, a priest of Saturn Augustus, fulfilling a vow to the deity.

EDCS-24300348.translation: Paulus, bishop of the first see of the province of Mauretania, rested in peace on the 15th day before the Kalends of March.
EDCS-24300348.summary: A funerary inscription for Paulus, a bishop in Mauretania, indicating his death date.

EDCS-24300349.translation: Faustinus the presbyter lived in peace for 56 years and rested on the 10th day of February.
EDCS-24300349.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan and death date of Faustinus, a presbyter.

EDCS-24300350.translation: Felicissimus the presbyter was placed in peace on the 5th day before the Kalends of June.
EDCS-24300350.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the burial date of Felicissimus, a presbyter.

EDCS-24300351.translation: Iitalis, servant of God and hermit, lived in peace for 75 years and was laid to rest on the 7th day before the Ides of March.
EDCS-24300351.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan and burial date of Iitalis, a hermit and servant of God.

EDCS-24300352.translation: Agathe the faithful lived in peace for 15 years and was placed in peace on the 13th day before the Kalends of March.
EDCS-24300352.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan and burial date of Agathe, identified as faithful.

EDCS-24300353.translation: Bellator lived in peace for 75 years and rested on the 4th Ides of May.
EDCS-24300353.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan and death date of Bellator.

EDCS-24300354.translation: Honoria lived in peace for 67 years and was laid to rest on the Nones of January.
EDCS-24300354.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan and burial date of Honoria.

EDCS-24300356.translation: Renobatus departed in peace on the 9th day before the Kalends of April.
EDCS-24300356.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the departure date of Renobatus.

EDCS-24300357.translation: Vincentia the faithful lived in peace for 41 years and was laid to rest on the 7th Ides of August.
EDCS-24300357.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan and burial date of Vincentia, identified as faithful.

EDCS-24400001.translation: To Quinto Servilio Pudenti, son of Quinto Servilio Pudentis, the proconsul, patron of the municipality, by decree of the decurions, with public money.
EDCS-24400001.summary: This is a dedication of a public monument or honorific inscription in honor of Quinto Servilio Pudenti, son of a proconsul and patron of the municipality.

EDCS-24400003.translation: To the divine Virtue and Security, by decree of the decurions, with public money, by order of the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Severus Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus, Parthicus Maximus, Britannicus Maximus, Pontifex Maximus, holding tribunician power for the 15th time, Imperator for the 2nd time, Consul for the 3rd time, Father of the Fatherland, grandson of the divine Marcus Antoninus Pius Germanicus Sarmaticus, great-grandson of the divine Antoninus Pius, great-great-grandson of the divine Hadrian, great-great-great-grandson of the divine Trajan Parthicus and the divine Nerva.
EDCS-24400003.summary: This is a dedication of a public monument to the virtues of the emperor Septimius Severus, listing his titles and ancestry, funded by public money.

EDCS-24400006.translation: To Marcus Cornelius Octavianus, a most accomplished man, prefect of the praetorian fleet of Misenum, leader throughout Africa, Numidia, and Mauretania, an incomparable patron; the most distinguished council of the municipality of Bisicensis honors him for his merits.
EDCS-24400006.summary: This is a dedication by the council of Bisicensis to Marcus Cornelius Octavianus, praising his military and administrative achievements.

EDCS-24400007.translation: The council of Bisicensis made this for Quintus Ennius Eppillus, son of Titus, of the Quirina tribe, centurion of the III Augusta legion, perpetual flamen, their patron.
EDCS-24400007.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by the council of Bisicensis to Quintus Ennius Eppillus, a military officer and priest, honoring him as their patron.

EDCS-24400008.translation: To Marcus Caecilius Secundus Arnensis Honoratus, son and grandson of perpetual flamines of his municipality.
EDCS-24400008.summary: This is a dedication to Marcus Caecilius Secundus Honoratus, noting his distinguished family lineage of perpetual priests in his municipality.

EDCS-24400009.translation: For the prosperity of the times, Lucius Calavius Germanianus, from the citizenry, perpetual flamen, twice curator of public affairs, erected this.
EDCS-24400009.summary: This inscription records the erection of a monument by Lucius Calavius Germanianus, a civic official and priest, to ensure the prosperity of the times.

EDCS-24400010.translation: To the memory of Marcus Caecilius Felix Martialis, son of Caius Caecilius Felix, a distinguished man and perpetual flamen; the decurions and the Cereales erected this.
EDCS-24400010.summary: This inscription is a memorial erected by the decurions and the Cereales to Marcus Caecilius Felix Martialis, a prominent citizen and priest.

EDCS-24400012.translation: Zopyrus, son of Tiron, of Bisicensis, from the leading citizens. He lived 89 years. Here he lies. May your bones rest peacefully in the urn, and may the earth be not burdensome, but light upon your ashes. May your bones rest well. May the earth be light upon you.
EDCS-24400012.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Zopyrus, a prominent citizen of Bisicensis, who lived to be 89 years old.

EDCS-24400014.translation: To Curtia, daughter of Publius, Auctilla Gargiliana.
EDCS-24400014.summary: This is a dedication to Curtia Auctilla Gargiliana, daughter of Publius.

EDCS-24400015.translation: Gidius Primus lived 55 years. Mamia Secunda lived 55 years. He made this for his father and mother.
EDCS-24400015.summary: This inscription records the ages of Gidius Primus and Mamia Secunda, who jointly erected a monument for their parents.

EDCS-24400016.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcus Zascius Ennianus, son of Ennianus, dutiful, lived 13 years, 10 months, and days.
EDCS-24400016.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Marcus Zascius Ennianus, a young boy who died at the age of 13.

EDCS-24400017.translation: Marcus Zascius, son of Primulus, dutiful, lived 65 years, 6 months, and 5 days. Here he lies.
EDCS-24400017.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Marcus Zascius Primuli, who died at the age of 65.

EDCS-24400021.translation: She lived piously for 68 years; she rests here.
EDCS-24400021.summary: This is a tombstone recording the life and death of a woman who lived for 68 years.

EDCS-24400024.translation: To Venus Augusta, Delius Abascanti, deputy of the emperor's estate manager, restored and enlarged the toll-house from its foundations at his own expense.
EDCS-24400024.summary: This is a dedication to the goddess Venus Augusta, recording the restoration and enlargement of a toll-house by Delius Abascanti, a subordinate official.

EDCS-24400026.translation: For Modia Quintilla, daughter of Quintus Modius Felix, perpetual priestess, the town council decreed that she, for the honor of her priesthood, having added money beyond the legal assessment, adorned the portico with marbles, coffered ceilings, and columns, and improved the aqueduct; and the council decreed a statue for her at public expense.
EDCS-24400026.summary: This inscription records a decree by the town council honoring Modia Quintilla, a perpetual priestess, for her contributions to public works and for adorning a portico and aqueduct.

EDCS-24400027.translation: For Gaius Sulpicius Perenis, son of Gaius Sulpicius, of the Arnensis tribe, priest of the Ceres of Carthage, aged 130 years, by decree of the decurions at public expense.
EDCS-24400027.summary: This is a funerary inscription honoring Gaius Sulpicius Perenis, a priest of Ceres, who lived to the age of 130.

EDCS-24400028.translation: To Quintus Cornelius Pudentus, a friend of noble spirit and ancient [lineage]...
EDCS-24400028.summary: This is a dedication to Quintus Cornelius Pudentus, honoring him as a friend of noble spirit and ancient lineage.

EDCS-24400030.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Flavius Valentinianus, the Pious, Fortunate, Victorious, ever Augustus, chief priest, holder of tribunician power...
EDCS-24400030.summary: This is an inscription honoring Emperor Valentinian III, listing his imperial titles and powers.

EDCS-24400031.translation: Balithon, son of Methunilim, Marinianus, lived piously for 80 years, buried at Saturn's [place]...
EDCS-24400031.summary: This is a tombstone recording the life and death of Balithon, son of Methunilim, who lived for 80 years.

EDCS-24400032.translation: Clodius Honor Valerianus lived for 28 years, 3 months, and 5 days.
EDCS-24400032.summary: This is a tombstone recording the lifespan of Clodius Honor Valerianus.

EDCS-24400033.translation: Namgedde, daughter of Metthunis, son of Dischunis, lived piously for 56 years, she rests here.
EDCS-24400033.summary: This is a tombstone recording the life and death of Namgedde, who lived for 56 years.

EDCS-24400034.summary: This is a fragmentary dedication, likely funerary, to a wife and daughter.

EDCS-24400037.translation: Primus the younger is on the base which joins this column and the bronze of Homer.
EDCS-24400037.summary: This fragmentary inscription likely records a statue or monument dedicated to Homer, with Primus the younger noted as being part of its base, probably from the Imperial period.

EDCS-24400040.translation: To Saturn, sacred to Achaea, Augustus. For the safety of Emperor Caesar Antoninus Augustus Pius, father of the fatherland. The gens Bacchuiana built the temple with their own money and likewise dedicated it. Candidus, son of Balsamon, from the first eleven, donated additional space in which the temple was built.
EDCS-24400040.summary: A dedication to Saturn and for the health of Emperor Antoninus Pius, recording the construction and endowment of a temple by the gens Bacchuiana and a donation of space by Candidus, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-24400041.translation: A sacred offering to Ceres and Tellus Augusta: Aebutius Saturninus and Victor, sons of Titus Aebutius, made the gate with all its adornments with their own money and dedicated it.
EDCS-24400041.summary: This inscription records a dedication of a gate and its adornments to the goddesses Tellus and Ceres, made by two sons, Aebutius Saturninus and Victor, during the Imperial period.

EDCS-24400044.translation: Aemilia Amotmicar, priestess of Ceres, lived 75 years and served as priestess for 35 years.
EDCS-24400044.summary: This funerary inscription records the life and service of Aemilia Amotmicar, a priestess of Ceres, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-24400045.translation: To Caecilia, wife of Ho Saturninus, most holy.
EDCS-24400045.summary: This dedication is a tomb inscription for Caecilia, the "most holy" wife of Ho Saturninus, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-24400046.translation: A sacred offering to the Spirits of the Underworld: Lucius Clodius Primanus, dutiful, lived 70 years. Valeria Rogata, daughter of Rufus, dutiful, lived 15 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-24400046.summary: This funerary inscription records the lives of Lucius Clodius Primanus and Valeria Rogata, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-24400047.translation: Decimius, for 12 days and 20 hours. May the earth lie lightly upon you.
EDCS-24400047.summary: This funerary epitaph records the short lifespan of Decimius and expresses a wish for the earth to lie lightly upon him, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-24400048.translation: A sacred offering to the Spirits of the Underworld: Modius Victor Quietus lived 60 years. A sacred offering to the Spirits of the Underworld: Iulia Sedata lived 80 years.
EDCS-24400048.summary: This double funerary inscription records the lives of Modius Victor Quietus and Iulia Sedata, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-24400050.translation: To the divine Augustus, pontifex maximus, holder of tribunician power, consul, father of the fatherland, proconsul, the municipality of Septimius Aurelius Severianus Augustalis of Sululitanum, devoted to his divine majesty and greatness.
EDCS-24400050.summary: This inscription records the devotion of the municipality of Sululitanum to Emperor Septimius Severus (Severianus Augustalis), likely from the late 2nd or early 3rd century CE.

EDCS-24400101.translation: A sacred offering to the Spirits of the Underworld: Discun Felicis Sesonis, dutiful, lived 85 years, 2 months, and 21 days.
EDCS-24400101.summary: This funerary inscription records the life of Discun Felicis Sesonis, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-24400102.translation: A sacred offering to the Spirits of the Underworld: Marcus Geminius Quintianus, dutiful, lived 27 years, 9 months, and 2 days.
EDCS-24400102.summary: This funerary inscription records the life of Marcus Geminius Quintianus, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-24400106.translation: For the safety of the Emperor Caesar Gaius Messius Quintus Traianus Decius and
EDCS-24400106.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription likely dedicating something for the well-being of Emperor Trajan Decius.

EDCS-24400109.translation: For the safety of the Augusti, the city of Tepeltensis by decree of the decurions, with public money
EDCS-24400109.summary: This inscription records a dedication by the city of Tepeltensis for the safety of the Augusti, funded by public money and approved by the decurions.

EDCS-24400110.translation: For the Emperor Caesar Hadrianus Augustus, son of the deified Trajan Parthicus, grandson of the deified Nerva, pontifex maximus, with tribunician power for the 14th time, consul for the 3rd time, the city of Tepeltensis by decree of the decurions, with public money, Maximus, son of Saturus, and Lucius, son of Luciscus, sufetes, carried this out.
EDCS-24400110.summary: This is a dedication to Emperor Hadrian by the city of Tepeltensis, mentioning local magistrates and funded by public money, likely from the period of Hadrian's reign.

EDCS-24400111.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription possibly commemorating or dedicating something to Emperor Severus.

EDCS-24400112.translation: For Sabinia Tranquillina Augusta, wife of our lord Emperor Caesar Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus, the city of Tepeltensis, devoted to their divine majesty, by decree of the decurions, with public money
EDCS-24400112.summary: This inscription records a dedication by the city of Tepeltensis for Empress Sabinia Tranquillina, wife of Antoninus Pius, funded by public money and decreed by the decurions.

EDCS-24400114.translation: For Gaius Galerius Valerius Maximianus, most noble Caesar, the municipality of Tepeltensium
EDCS-24400114.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Caesar Galerius Valerius Maximianus by the municipality of Tepeltensium.

EDCS-24400116.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription likely dedicating something to Emperor Antoninus Pius.

EDCS-24400117.translation: Marcus Aurelius Antoninus, veteran, marble columns
EDCS-24400117.summary: This inscription records a dedication of marble columns by Marcus Aurelius Antoninus, a veteran.

EDCS-24400122.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Mecenatia Secundula, a Christian woman, faithful and honorable, wife of Manilius Faustinianus, lived 40 years, 2 months. Sacred to the departed spirits. Manilius Faustinianus, son of Manilius and Fortunata, aedilician and duoviral official, an honorable and pious man, lived for himself and his own while alive. Sacred to the departed spirits. Manilius Fortunatianus, son of Manilius Faustinianus, aedilician and duoviral official, an honorable and pious man, lived 32 years, 1 month.
EDCS-24400122.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the deaths of Mecenatia Secundula, her husband Manilius Faustinianus, and their son Manilius Fortunatianus, noting their piety and official positions, with a Christian reference for the wife.

EDCS-24400123.translation: GEN A C made VVS DE tius H B CIS AECAI IA S PTVI ETI RIS AV NETI for the fatherland, its law, the proconsul L, perpetual priest of the people of Favorum, and the entire league and order, this inscription has placed him eternally.
EDCS-24400123.summary: This inscription records honors bestowed upon an individual (possibly named Lucius) who held various prestigious religious and civic offices, including proconsul and perpetual priest, and was honored by the people of Favorum and a broader league.

EDCS-24400124.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus Aelius Primus, a soldier of the 14th urban cohort, dutiful, lived 50 years. Pompeia Satura, his wife.
EDCS-24400124.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Quintus Aelius Primus, a soldier, likely from the late 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-24400125.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Publius Aventinius Ticianus lived 71 years, 3 months, 12 days. He is buried here.
EDCS-24400125.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Publius Aventinius Ticianus, recording his lifespan, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24400130.translation: To our lord Flavius Honorius, the Unconquered Emperor, ever Augustus, the municipality of Avitta Bibba, devoted to his divine majesty, by decree of the decurions, with public money.
EDCS-24400130.summary: This is a dedication to Emperor Honorius, likely from the early 5th century CE, funded by the municipality of Avitta Bibba.

EDCS-24400132.translation: Established with joy and by Gemini's love for his father Triumphalis, continuing his journey, by the care of Dativus, you will remain in eternal place.
EDCS-24400132.summary: This text appears to be a dedication or inscription related to a memorial or monument, possibly referencing a person named Triumphalis and the care of Dativus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24400136.translation: Iunius Urbanus, son of Clarus, is buried here. He lived 78 years.
EDCS-24400136.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Iunius Urbanus, recording his name, parentage, and lifespan, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24400137.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Caius Mitius Victor, dutiful, lived [X] years. He is buried here.
EDCS-24400137.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Caius Mitius Victor, recording his name and lifespan, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24400138.translation: which ancient decay and most foul neglect had possessed to such an extent that the very summit of the work repelled the gaze; he restored it to its former splendor and magnificence by laying foundations and the portico, and Geminius Aurelius Auctor, perpetual priest and curator of the state, and the love of the most splendid council and of the entire people, completed and dedicated it through labor.
EDCS-24400138.summary: This inscription records the restoration of a public building, likely a portico, by Geminius Aurelius Auctor, who held religious and civic offices, funded by public contributions, probably from the 3rd century CE.

EDCS-24400139.translation: For the safety of the Emperor Caesar, son of the deified Antoninus, grandson of the deified Hadrian, great-grandson of the deified Trajan Parthicus, great-great-grandson of the deified Augustus, Pius Felix Augustus, and for his children. The community of the Biracsaccenses made this vow to Jupiter, Juno, and Minerva in the year of the suffetes Honoratus Fortunatus, son of [Magistrate], and Flavius Victor, son of [Magistrate], Rirensis and Vetuleni, and Similis, on behalf of their brothers, with public money, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-24400139.summary: This is a votive inscription by the community of Biracsaccenses to the Capitoline Triad and for the emperor's safety, likely from the mid-2nd century CE, during the reign of Antoninus Pius.

EDCS-24400140.translation: To the Emperor Caesar, son of the deified Antoninus, grandson of the deified Hadrian, great-grandson of the deified Trajan Parthicus, great-great-grandson of the deified Augustus, Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus, pontifex maximus, with tribunician power for the 15th time, consul for the 3rd time, by decree of the decurions, with public money.
EDCS-24400140.summary: This is a dedication to Emperor Marcus Aurelius, likely from around 177/178 CE, sponsored by local authorities.

EDCS-24400141.translation: To the Emperor Caesar, son of the deified Antoninus, grandson of the deified Hadrian, great-grandson of the deified Trajan Parthicus, great-great-grandson of the deified Augustus, Lucius Aurelius Verus Augustus, with tribunician power, consul for the 2nd time, by decree of the decurions, with public money.
EDCS-24400141.summary: This is a dedication to Emperor Lucius Verus, likely from around 166/167 CE, sponsored by local authorities.

EDCS-24400142.translation: To Faustina Augusta, wife of Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus, pontifex maximus, in his fifteenth tribunician power, consul for the third time, by decree of the decurions, with public funds.
EDCS-24400142.summary: An inscription honoring Faustina Augusta, wife of Marcus Aurelius, erected by public funds as decided by the local council, dated to Marcus Aurelius's 15th tribunician power and 3rd consulship, likely around 175 CE.

EDCS-24400146.translation: Sacred to the Deities of the Underworld. Carbania Ianuaria lived 13 years and 2 months.
EDCS-24400146.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Carbania Ianuaria, recording her age at death.

EDCS-24400147.translation: To Apollo Augustus. Pescennius Rogatianus and Felix.
EDCS-24400147.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Apollo Augustus by Pescennius Rogatianus and Felix.

EDCS-24400148.translation: Sacred to Pluto the Great King. Caius Pescennius Saturus, son of Saturinus, of the Palatine tribe, perpetual priest of the deified Hadrian, quaestor, prefect with judicial power for two terms, quinquennial duovir of the colony of Zama, in recognition of his priesthood, enlarged with 4,000 sesterces and by a taxation, placed two statues and provided a feast twice, and also dedicated these things by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-24400148.summary: This is a dedicatory inscription by Caius Pescennius Saturus to Pluto, detailing his civic and priestly offices and the honors bestowed upon him by the colony of Zama.

EDCS-24400150.translation: For Quintus Julius Maximo Demetrianus, a man of exceptional memory, advocate of the treasury, procurator of the 40th tax of the Gallic provinces, procurator of the 20th inheritance tax through Umbria and Tuscany, prefect of the transport services through Belgium and the two Germanies, a man of singular integrity, and public patron. Lucius Munatius Saturninus, his maternal uncle, with the place obtained from the town council, erected this at his own expense.
EDCS-24400150.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Lucius Munatius Saturninus for his uncle Quintus Julius Maximo Demetrianus, listing his impressive administrative career.

EDCS-24400151.translation: To Marcus, whose body lies here. Although the town council had decreed that a statue be erected at public expense for him, due to the merits of his ancestors and his own character, he, Pomponius Martialis, son of Octavianus, at his own expense, with the money returned to the Republic, and in the place obtained from the town council, erected it.
EDCS-24400151.summary: This inscription records that Pomponius Martialis erected a statue for himself at his own expense, although the town council had previously decreed it be a public monument, possibly due to the family's ancestral merits.

EDCS-24400152.translation: To Marcus Pescennius Faustus. Pescennia Ria, daughter of Acaadis.
EDCS-24400152.summary: This is a funerary epitaph, possibly for Marcus Pescennius Faustus, with the dedicant identified as Pescennia Ria, daughter of Acaadis.

EDCS-24400153.translation: Sacred to the Deities of the Underworld. Cassia, daughter of Caius, called Data.
EDCS-24400153.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Cassia Data, daughter of Caius.

EDCS-24400154.translation: Sacred to the Deities of the Underworld. Gallus Victor Maximinus lived 10 years.
EDCS-24400154.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Gallus Victor Maximinus, recording his age at death.

EDCS-24400155.translation: Caius Julius Maximianus lived piously for 27 years. Sacred to the Deities of the Underworld.
EDCS-24400155.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Caius Julius Maximianus, recording his age and a statement of his piety.

EDCS-24400156.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Juno Regina Sarmatica.

EDCS-24400159.translation: Publius Mummius Saturninus made and dedicated this, having tribunician power.
EDCS-24400159.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by Publius Mummius Saturninus, who held tribunician power.

EDCS-24400165.translation: In the name of the Lord, we built a tower in the time of Lord Maurice the Emperor, under Patrician Gennadius and John the Prefect. The three brothers Maximianus, Istefanus, and Mellosus built it.
EDCS-24400165.summary: This inscription records the construction of a tower during the reign of Emperor Maurice, initiated by Patrician Gennadius and Prefect John, and built by three brothers.

EDCS-24400166.translation: The Limisenses, by decree of the decurions, with public money, Julius Perpetuus and Saturninus, son of Masopis, two of the sufetes, made this, under the supervision of Faustus, son of Maximi.
EDCS-24400166.summary: This inscription records a public work funded by the decurions of Limisenses and executed by Julius Perpetuus and Saturninus Masopis, supervised by Faustus.

EDCS-24400169.translation: To Publius Mummius Saturninus, son of Lucius, of the Papiria tribe, priest of the province of Africa, 113 years old, decurion and formerly duovir of the municipality of Furni. When the ordo offered him the honor of the flamonic priesthood, he made the pronaos with its ornaments of the temple of Mercury at his own expense, in lieu of the honor. For its dedication, the people voted 1,000,000 sesterces for the baths.
EDCS-24400169.summary: This inscription honors Publius Mummius Saturninus, a prominent local official and priest, who funded the construction of a pronaos and temple ornaments for Mercury, with the community later voting funds for baths in his honor.

EDCS-24400171.translation: S. Victor Cassius, Evasius Rectus, Marcus Caecilius Marc, Lucius Sudius Felix, Lucius Sudius Nundinarius, Decimus Concessius Felix, Geminius Saturninus, Paccius Saturninus, A. Sin. N. Secundianus, Servilius Victor, Lucius Limisius Rogatianus, Lucius Servilius Felicianus, Lucius Umbrius Saturninus, Ceionius Felix, Sulpicius Felix, Ulpius Rogatianus, Caelius Ianuarius, Caecilius Eranius, Octavius Honoratus.
EDCS-24400171.summary: This inscription is a list of names, likely recording a group of individuals associated with a particular event or community, possibly a dedication or membership list.

EDCS-24400172.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Caecilia Pusilla, daughter of Caius, dutiful, lived 27 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-24400172.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Caecilia Pusilla, recording her name, parentage, piety, age at death, and burial location.

EDCS-24400173.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Flavius Severinus, son of Marcius, dutiful, lived [X] years.
EDCS-24400173.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Flavius Severinus, recording his name, parentage, piety, and lifespan, with the exact age missing.

EDCS-24400174.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Quintus Ge Fortunatus, dutiful, lived [X] M.
EDCS-24400174.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Quintus Ge Fortunatus, recording his name, piety, and lifespan, with the exact age missing.

EDCS-24400175.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Geminia Spes, daughter of Gaius, dutiful, lived 57 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-24400175.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Geminia Spes, recording her name, parentage, piety, age at death, and burial location.

EDCS-24400176.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Lucius Iulius Victor, dutiful, lived 64 years, 7 months, and 16 days; he is buried here.
EDCS-24400176.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Iulius Victor, recording his name, piety, exact age at death, and burial location.

EDCS-24400177.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Publius Helvius Fuscus, dutiful, lived 25 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-24400177.summary: A tombstone recording the death of Publius Helvius Fuscus at the age of 25.

EDCS-24400178.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Helvia Saturnina, dutiful, lived 33 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-24400178.summary: A tombstone recording the death of Helvia Saturnina at the age of 33.

EDCS-24400180.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Iunia Donata, daughter of Lucius, dutiful, lived 21 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-24400180.summary: A tombstone recording the death of Iunia Donata at the age of 21.

EDCS-24400181.translation: Pelusius, son of Masopis, lived dutifully 50 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-24400181.summary: A tombstone recording the death of Pelusius at the age of 50.

EDCS-24400182.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Pinaria Saturnina, daughter of Caius, dutiful, lived 75 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-24400182.summary: A tombstone recording the death of Pinaria Saturnina at the age of 75.

EDCS-24400183.summary: A fragment of an inscription possibly naming Caius, context unclear.

EDCS-24400184.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Saturia Victoria, daughter of Lucius, dutiful, lived 14 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-24400184.summary: A tombstone recording the death of Saturia Victoria at the age of 14.

EDCS-24400185.translation: ... dutiful, lived 25 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-24400185.summary: A fragment of a tombstone recording the death of an unnamed female at the age of 25.

EDCS-24400186.translation: ... lived 60 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-24400186.summary: A fragment of a tombstone recording the death of an unnamed male at the age of 60.

EDCS-24400187.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. O O
EDCS-24400187.summary: A fragment of an inscription with illegible names or titles.

EDCS-24400188.translation: Sacred to Apollo Augustus. The temple, which Gaius Clodius Saturninus had promised to construct and complete from the ground up with the doubled sum of his decurionate honor and that of his brother Clodius Celer, was erected from the ground and completed with every amenity by his granddaughter Clodia Macrina, a most distinguished lady, with an additional sum of 5,600 sesterces beyond his 6,400 sesterces honorarium, a total of 12,000 sesterces, through her generosity. The public affairs were managed by E MC, and she spontaneously adorned it with marble statues and dedicated them.
EDCS-24400188.summary: This inscription records the construction and dedication of a temple to Apollo Augustus, financed by Clodia Macrina and initiated by her grandfather and uncle.

EDCS-24400189.translation: Sacred to the Genius of the state and Augustus, for the health of the Emperor Caesar Antoninus Augustus Pius and his children.
EDCS-24400189.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the Genius of the state and Augustus for the well-being of the emperor and his family.

EDCS-24400190.translation: To the deified Great Antoninus Pius, founder of the municipality, the citizens of Muzucenses, by decree of the decurions, at public expense.
EDCS-24400190.summary: This inscription honors Emperor Antoninus Pius as the founder of the municipality of Muzucenses and was erected by the town council.

EDCS-24400191.translation: To the most invincible and most indulgent prince, Emperor Caesar Pius Felix Invictus Augustus, the council of the municipality of Muzucenses, devoted to his divine will and majesty, by decree of the decurions, at public expense.
EDCS-24400191.summary: This inscription is a dedication by the council of Muzucenses to Emperor Caesar Pius Felix Invictus Augustus, honoring his divine majesty.

EDCS-24400192.translation: To our lord Flavius Valerius Constantius, Invictus and most noble Caesar, the council of the municipality of Muzucenses, devoted to his divine will and majesty, by decree of the decurions, at public expense.
EDCS-24400192.summary: This inscription is a dedication by the council of Muzucenses to Caesar Flavius Valerius Constantius.

EDCS-24400193.translation: To the most invincible and most indulgent prince, Emperor Caesar Flavius Valerius Constantinus Pius Felix Invictus Augustus, the council of the municipality of Muzucenses, devoted to his divine will and majesty, by decree of the decurions, at public expense.
EDCS-24400193.summary: This inscription is a dedication by the council of Muzucenses to Emperor Caesar Flavius Valerius Constantinus.

EDCS-24400195.translation: To Marcus Annaeus Maximus Aquila Fulvianus.
EDCS-24400195.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Marcus Annaeus Maximus Aquila Fulvianus.

EDCS-24400196.translation: To Marcus Clodius Faustus Secundus, son of Marcus Clodius, of the voting tribe Quirina, sent to purchase grain for the province during the Mauric war, who was appointed to military honors on the German campaign and honored with a vexillum and a pure spear, and to Clodius Quirinus Iucundianus, a Roman knight, and to Quintus Clodius.
EDCS-24400196.summary: This inscription honors Marcus Clodius Faustus Secundus and others for military service and a mission to purchase grain during wartime.

EDCS-24400197.translation: Plautius Faustus and Auge, the heirs, completed the temple, which Plautia Ep had promised to build from the ground up with statues for the honor of her perpetual priesthood, for 10,000 sesterces, with increased funds.
EDCS-24400197.summary: This inscription records the completion of a temple and statues, originally promised by Plautia Ep for her perpetual priesthood, by her heirs.

EDCS-24400198.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a priestess of Venus, recording her lifespan.

EDCS-24400200.translation: To the Avi, citizens, for singular merit.
EDCS-24400200.summary: This is an inscription honoring the Avi for their exceptional service, likely a dedication on a public monument.

EDCS-24400201.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely a dedication or memorial, recording 'to them always'.

EDCS-24400202.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Aelia Adiecta, dutiful, lived 79 years, is buried here.
EDCS-24400202.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Aelia Adiecta, recording her life span and burial.

EDCS-24400204.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Barigbal Cisi lived 60 years, here.
EDCS-24400204.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Barigbal Cisi, recording his age and burial.

EDCS-24400205.translation: Bellinia Rogata, lived 53 years, is buried here.
EDCS-24400205.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Bellinia Rogata, recording her age and burial.

EDCS-24400206.translation: To Quintus Clodius Mercatus and Clodia Iucunda.
EDCS-24400206.summary: This is a dedication, likely on a tomb or monument, to Quintus Clodius Mercatus and Clodia Iucunda.

EDCS-24400207.translation: Consulia Rosa, dutiful, lived 2 years, is buried here.
EDCS-24400207.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for the child Consulia Rosa, recording her short life span and burial.

EDCS-24400208.translation: Cornelius Rogatinus, dutiful, lived 40 years, is buried here.
EDCS-24400208.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Cornelius Rogatinus, recording his life span and burial.

EDCS-24400209.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Titus Flavius Priscus, dutiful, lived 80 years, is buried here.
EDCS-24400209.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Titus Flavius Priscus, recording his life span and burial.

EDCS-24400210.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Gallus, son of Gallus, a Numidian, dutiful, lived 47 years.
EDCS-24400210.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Gallus Galli Numidae, recording his age, parentage, and ethnic origin.

EDCS-24400211.translation: Titus Livius lived piously for 15 years, 8 months, and 32 days; he is buried here.
EDCS-24400211.summary: This is a tombstone recording the life and burial of Titus Livius, who died at a young age.

EDCS-24400212.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Lucius Laelius Adiectus lived piously; he is buried here.
EDCS-24400212.summary: This is a tombstone dedicated to the Manes, recording the burial of Lucius Laelius Adiectus.

EDCS-24400213.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Quintus Maevius Iulianus lived 27 years, 9 months, and 14 days. The most loving fellow soldiers made this enormous monument for their extremely dear fellow soldier; he is buried here.
EDCS-24400213.summary: This tombstone, erected by fellow soldiers, records the life and burial of Quintus Maevius Iulianus.

EDCS-24400214.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Pomponius lived piously for 22 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-24400214.summary: This tombstone records the life and burial of Pomponius, who died at age 22.

EDCS-24400215.translation: Popilius Iunius lived piously for 27 years; Popilius Maximus lived piously for 24 years.
EDCS-24400215.summary: This tombstone records the lives of two individuals, Popilius Iunius and Popilius Maximus, who died at relatively young ages.

EDCS-24400216.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Postumia Secunda, daughter of Donatus, lived piously for 23 years; she is buried here. Her brother Silvanus made this.
EDCS-24400216.summary: This tombstone, erected by her brother Silvanus, records the life and burial of Postumia Secunda.

EDCS-24400217.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Rosa Guduis lived piously for 41 years.
EDCS-24400217.summary: This tombstone records the life of Rosa Guduis, who died at age 41.

EDCS-24400218.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Saturnina, daughter of Rogatus, lived piously.
EDCS-24400218.summary: This tombstone records the life of Saturnina, daughter of Rogatus.

EDCS-24400219.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Lucius Ulpius Fidelis lived piously for 56 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-24400219.summary: This tombstone records the life and burial of Lucius Ulpius Fidelis.

EDCS-24400220.translation: Mianus lived piously for 57 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-24400220.summary: This tombstone records the life and burial of Mianus, who died at age 57.

EDCS-24400222.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Venustus Maximianus, dutiful, lived 2 years and 5 days; he is buried here.
EDCS-24400222.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Venustus Maximianus, who died at a young age.

EDCS-24400224.translation: Sacred to Mercury Augustus. For the safety of the Emperors Caesars Lucius Septimius Severus Pertinax Augustus Arabicus Adiabenicus, father of the fatherland, and Imperator Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus, Gaius Iulius Glaucus built this temple at his own expense. [Built] 102 years after the founding of the city.
EDCS-24400224.summary: This is a dedication of a temple to Mercury Augustus by Gaius Iulius Glaucus, likely during the reign of Septimius Severus and Caracalla.

EDCS-24400226.translation: To a friend of everyone, of the entire senate.
EDCS-24400226.summary: This is a dedication or epitaph to a respected individual known for their popularity and service to the curia.

EDCS-24400227.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Lucius Antistius Caesianus, dutiful, lived 84 years.
EDCS-24400227.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Antistius Caesianus, who lived a long life.

EDCS-24400228.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Cassia Bonosa, dutiful, lived 17 years, 10 months; she is buried here.
EDCS-24400228.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Cassia Bonosa, who died in her late teens.

EDCS-24400229.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Flavia Donatula, daughter of Marcus, dutiful, lived 5 years, 8 months, and 2 days; she is buried here.
EDCS-24400229.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Flavia Donatula, a young child.

EDCS-24400230.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Titus Gaetulius Secundianus lived 13 years and 6 months; he is buried here.
EDCS-24400230.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Titus Gaetulius Secundianus, who died in his early teens.

EDCS-24400233.translation: I brought back my love and willingly returning what is mine, I now give voice to my fatherland in this empty tomb, having met the fate that compels, I departed from life, happy.
EDCS-24400233.summary: This is a personal epitaph expressing the deceased's love for their homeland and the circumstances of their death.

EDCS-24400235.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Flavia Victorina lived 36 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-24400235.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Flavia Victorina, who died in adulthood.

EDCS-24400236.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Cattenius Felicio, dutiful, lived 80 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-24400236.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Cattenius Felicio, who lived a long life.

EDCS-24400237.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Lucius Laelius Maximus Ferianus lived for 60 years.
EDCS-24400237.summary: A funerary dedication for Lucius Laelius Maximus Ferianus, who lived to be 60.

EDCS-24400238.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Aemilia Donata the dutiful lived for 10 years.
EDCS-24400238.summary: A funerary dedication for Aemilia Donata, who died at the age of 10.

EDCS-24400239.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Prima, daughter of Pularius, lived for 65 years.
EDCS-24400239.summary: A funerary dedication for Prima, daughter of Pularius, who lived to be 65.

EDCS-24400240.translation: Epius lived for 74 years. Aemilius Saturus and Felix Maximus, his sons, made this for him because of his merits.
EDCS-24400240.summary: A funerary monument erected by sons for their father, Epius, who lived to be 74.

EDCS-24400241.translation: Sacred to Mercury for the safety of the Emperor Caesar. Lucius Aemilius Donatus, a veteran, built the shrine with steps with his own money.
EDCS-24400241.summary: A dedication to Mercury by Lucius Aemilius Donatus, a veteran, for the emperor's safety and including construction details of a shrine.

EDCS-24400243.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Aelia Leonia lived for 20 years, 2 months, and 5 hours.
EDCS-24400243.summary: A funerary dedication for Aelia Leonia, who lived to be 20 years, 2 months, and 5 hours.

EDCS-24400244.translation: Sevic Numen made this for his pious wife. She is buried here.
EDCS-24400244.summary: A funerary dedication made by Sevic Numen for his wife.

EDCS-24400245.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Rusticus, son of Rusticus, lived for 58 years.
EDCS-24400245.summary: A funerary dedication for Rusticus, son of Rusticus, who lived to be 58.

EDCS-24400247.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Iulia Secunda is buried here. She lived for 33 years. Servilis Marcienus made this for his wife.
EDCS-24400247.summary: A funerary monument erected by Servilis Marcienus for his wife, Iulia Secunda, who lived to be 33.

EDCS-24400248.translation: He who was once among the living, the mighty Mossius, now a slender soul, wanders through the Elysian fields. Here he was born, here he is buried. If you who pass by care for eighteen and three, farewell forever.
EDCS-24400248.summary: A funerary epitaph for Mossius, lamenting his death and addressing passersby with a plea and a farewell.

EDCS-24400249.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Aelia Felicitas, daughter of Quintus, pious, lived 10 years, 2 months; she is buried here.
EDCS-24400249.summary: This is a tombstone for Aelia Felicitas, who died at a young age.

EDCS-24400250.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Marcus Claudius Scas dedicated this to Titus Claudius Maximianus, a most worthy youth, who met a miserable end, having lived 21 years.
EDCS-24400250.summary: This is a tombstone for Titus Claudius Maximianus, a young man, dedicated by Marcus Claudius Scas.

EDCS-24400252.translation: He made and dedicated this at his own expense for the benefit of the people, as decurio, aedile, quaestor, and duovir of the colony.
EDCS-24400252.summary: This inscription records the benefactions of an unnamed official who served multiple civic roles in the colony of Thelepte.

EDCS-24400254.translation: To Nicia, our most sweet mistress, illuminated by Christ, the light of justice; Master, receive us and mine, for whom the holy one will grant deserving reward according to merits.
EDCS-24400254.summary: This is a Christian inscription addressed to Nicia, a mistress figure, and invokes Christ as a judge of merits.

EDCS-24400256.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Herenus Castus lived 8 years, 3 months, 6 days; he is buried here.
EDCS-24400256.summary: This is a tombstone for Herenus Castus, who died at a very young age.

EDCS-24400257.translation: To Venus Augusta, Gaius C llius Mulianus, son of Publius, dedicated this at his own expense.
EDCS-24400257.summary: This is a dedication to the goddess Venus Augusta by Gaius C llius Mulianus.

EDCS-24400259.translation: In return for the love he has shown, by his own means he has approved the temple of the Emperor the triumphant victor for the vicus.
EDCS-24400259.summary: This inscription records a private donation to a temple, likely for an imperial triumph, and praises an individual named Iulius Maximus.

EDCS-24400265.summary: This is a brief dedication or mention of Saturninus Pertinax, possibly as a recipient or honoree.

EDCS-24400266.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Lucius Baebius Barbarus, a student in Carthage, died having lived 20 years, 7 months; he is buried here.
EDCS-24400266.summary: This is a tombstone for Lucius Baebius Barbarus, a student who died young in Carthage.

EDCS-24400267.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Marcus Fabius Restutus, a good man, a physician, lived piously for 62 years, 3 months; he is buried here.
EDCS-24400267.summary: This is a tombstone for Marcus Fabius Restutus, a physician who lived a pious life.

EDCS-24400268.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Aemilius Secundus Mestrianus, dutiful, lived 40 years and 5 days; he is buried here.
EDCS-24400268.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Aemilius Secundus Mestrianus, recording his age at death and burial.

EDCS-24400269.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Caius Amulius Rogatus Commodianus, dutiful, lived 18 years, 6 months.
EDCS-24400269.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Caius Amulius Rogatus Commodianus, recording his age at death.

EDCS-24400270.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Antonius Donatianus, dutiful, lived 73 years, 6 months, and 10 days; he is buried here. Grania Maxima, dutiful, lived 70 years, 8 months, and 2 days; she is buried here.
EDCS-24400270.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Antonius Donatianus and Grania Maxima, recording their ages at death and burial.

EDCS-24400271.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Marcus Antonius Faustianus Nepos, dutiful, lived 44 years, 7 months, and 15 days; he is buried here.
EDCS-24400271.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcus Antonius Faustianus Nepos, recording his age at death and burial.

EDCS-24400272.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Marcus Antonius Faustianus Nepos Principinus, endowed with outstanding dutifulness, renowned for his character and intellect, beloved, skilled in public speaking, cherished by his parents with the highest honor, lived dutifully 18 years and 6 days.
EDCS-24400272.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcus Antonius Faustianus Nepos Principinus, detailing his virtues and lifespan.

EDCS-24400273.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Lucius Antonius Proculus, dutiful, lived 70 years.
EDCS-24400273.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Antonius Proculus, recording his age at death.
