EDCS-24400274.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Lucius Caecilius Donatianus, dutiful, lived 38 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-24400274.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Caecilius Donatianus, recording his age at death and burial.

EDCS-24400275.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Caelius IV
EDCS-24400275.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary epitaph for someone named Caelius.

EDCS-24400276.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Marcus Caledius Donatianus, dutiful, lived 68 years, 8 months, and 11 days; he is buried here.
EDCS-24400276.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcus Caledius Donatianus, recording his age at death and burial.

EDCS-24400277.translation: Here lies Gaius Cosconius Modianus, the best father, lived 10 years, and his most dutiful sons made this.
EDCS-24400277.summary: This funerary epitaph, possibly by children, honors a father named Gaius Cosconius Modianus.

EDCS-24400278.translation: Cosconius Satullus, dutiful, lived 30 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-24400278.summary: This is a tombstone inscription commemorating the life and burial of Cosconius Satullus, who died at the age of 30.

EDCS-24400279.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Sittia Crescentia, dutiful, lived 81 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-24400279.summary: This funerary inscription honors Sittia Crescentia, who lived to be 81 years old and is buried here.

EDCS-24400280.summary: This inscription records the lifespan of Cududus Arinis, who lived for 70 years.

EDCS-24400281.translation: Secundula, dutiful, lived 39 years. Donatianus, dutiful, lived 15 years. XVII AI lived 15 years.
EDCS-24400281.summary: This inscription records the lifespans of Secundula (39 years) and Donatianus (15 years), with an additional unclear mention of another individual or group living 15 years.

EDCS-24400282.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Saturnina, wife of Baliathon. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Cnaeus Flavius Germanus.
EDCS-24400282.summary: This inscription, possibly from two separate contexts, is dedicated to the departed spirits and names Saturnina (wife of Baliathon) and Cnaeus Flavius Germanus.

EDCS-24400283.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Oria Flavia Rogata lived 21 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-24400283.summary: This funerary inscription records that Oria Flavia Rogata lived for 21 years and is buried here.

EDCS-24400284.translation: Fortunatus, son of Masofis, dutiful, lived 37 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-24400284.summary: This tombstone commemorates Fortunatus, son of Masofis, who lived for 37 years and is buried here.

EDCS-24400285.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Germanus, son of Iulzis, dutiful, lived 40 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-24400285.summary: This funerary inscription honors Germanus, son of Iulzis, who lived for 40 years and is buried here.

EDCS-24400286.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Grania Maxima, dutiful, lived 4 years, 8 months, and 13 days; she is buried here.
EDCS-24400286.summary: This funerary inscription records the short life of Grania Maxima, who died at the age of 4 years, 8 months, and 13 days.

EDCS-24400287.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Iulius
EDCS-24400287.summary: This is an incomplete inscription dedicated to the spirits of the departed, naming Iulius.

EDCS-24400288.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Iulia Optata, dutiful, lived 33 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-24400288.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the burial of Iulia Optata, who lived 33 years.

EDCS-24400289.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Marcus Lorenius, dutiful, lived [one year].
EDCS-24400289.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the life span of Marcus Lorenius, possibly a child, with an incomplete age.

EDCS-24400290.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Caius Messius Rogatianus, dutiful, lived 63 years; he is buried here. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Antonia Castula, dutiful, lived 100 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-24400290.summary: A funerary inscription commemorating two individuals, Caius Messius Rogatianus and Antonia Castula, who lived 63 and 100 years respectively.

EDCS-24400291.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Sextilia Aucilia, dutiful, lived [one year]. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Lucius Pecenius, dutiful, lived 3 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-24400291.summary: A funerary epitaph for Sextilia Aucilia and Lucius Pecenius, who lived for an incomplete year and 3 years respectively.

EDCS-24400293.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Sallustia Principina, daughter of Marcus, an honorable and dutiful matron, lived 70 years and 5 months; she is buried here.
EDCS-24400293.summary: A funerary epitaph for Sallustia Principina, described as an honorable and dutiful matron, who lived 70 years and 5 months.

EDCS-24400295.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Titus Tessenius Avitus, dutiful, lived 17 years and 10 months; he is buried here.
EDCS-24400295.summary: A funerary epitaph for Titus Tessenius Avitus, who died at the age of 17 years and 10 months.

EDCS-24400296.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Fusidia Victoria, dutiful, lived 17 years; she is buried here. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Tessenius Felix, dutiful, lived 61 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-24400296.summary: A funerary inscription commemorating two individuals, Fusidia Victoria and Tessenius Felix, who lived 17 and 61 years respectively.

EDCS-24400297.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Titus Tissenius Gentianus Victor, dutiful, lived 27 years and 3 months; he is buried here.
EDCS-24400297.summary: A funerary epitaph for Titus Tissenius Gentianus Victor, who died at the age of 27 years and 3 months.

EDCS-24400299.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Tessenia Victoria, dutiful, lived 17 months; she is buried here.
EDCS-24400299.summary: A funerary epitaph for Tessenia Victoria, who died at the age of 17 months.

EDCS-24400301.translation: To the memory of Verria Quieta, most chaste and a woman of rare example, who lived dutifully for 78 years and is buried here. Marcus Struganius Quietus Liberalianus made this for his mother for her exceptional industry.
EDCS-24400301.summary: A funerary monument dedicated by Marcus Struganius Quietus Liberalianus to his mother Verria Quieta, commemorating her virtuous life of 78 years.

EDCS-24400303.translation: Saturninus Victorianus lived for 53 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-24400303.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the age at death of Saturninus Victorianus.

EDCS-24400306.translation: Aurelia Biccla lived in peace for 80 years, 6 months, and 11 hours.
EDCS-24400306.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Aurelia Biccla.

EDCS-24400307.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Saecondus lived in peace for 35 years, 1 month, and 4 days.
EDCS-24400307.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated to the Manes, recording the lifespan of Saecondus.

EDCS-24400308.translation: Statilia Hilara lived in peace for 75 years, 5 months, and 11 hours.
EDCS-24400308.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Statilia Hilara.

EDCS-24400309.translation: Bitorina in Christ amen lived for 25 years, plus or minus 5 hours.
EDCS-24400309.summary: This is a funerary epitaph, likely Christian, recording the lifespan of Bitorina.

EDCS-24400310.translation: Victorianus lived in peace for forty years, five months, and the seventh hour.
EDCS-24400310.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Victorianus.

EDCS-24400312.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcus Considius Honorinus, dutiful, lived for 49 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-24400312.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated to the Manes, recording the age at death and burial place of Marcus Considius Honorinus.

EDCS-24400313.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Ianuarius, son of Secundus, lived for 54 years.
EDCS-24400313.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated to the Manes, recording the lifespan of Ianuarius.

EDCS-24400315.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus Iulius Saturninus, dutiful, lived for 44 years and 3 months; he is buried here at Laurenti.
EDCS-24400315.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated to the Manes, recording the age at death, burial place, and name of Quintus Iulius Saturninus.

EDCS-24400316.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Iulia Iaderis.

EDCS-24400318.translation: Sacred to Jupiter the Preserver of the Augusti, for the safety of the Emperors Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus Arabicus Adiabenicus Parthicus Maximus, Pontifex Maximus, holder of tribunician power for the 11th time, Consul for the 4th time, Father of the Fatherland, and Marcus Aurelius Antoninus, Best of Princes, and Julia Domna Augusta, Mother of the Augusti and of the Camp and of the entire divine household.
EDCS-24400318.summary: This is a dedication to Jupiter for the safety of the imperial family, likely dating to the reign of Septimius Severus and Caracalla.

EDCS-24400319.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Caecilia Victoria, dutiful, lived 33 years; she is buried here. Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Gaius V. Martialis, dutiful, lived 80 years. Quintus Fun Saturninus lived 3 years and 4 months; he is buried here.
EDCS-24400319.summary: This is a double funerary inscription for Caecilia Victoria and Quintus Fun Saturninus, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-24400321.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Calocagathus, 6 months old. His father Aeacus made this.
EDCS-24400321.summary: This is a funerary inscription for an infant named Calocagathus, made by his father Aeacus.

EDCS-24400322.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. For Calia Bonifatia, who lived 8 months and 22 days. Lucius Caelius Suavis, most dutiful father, made this for his most beloved daughter.
EDCS-24400322.summary: This is a funerary inscription for an infant named Calia Bonifatia, made by her father Lucius Caelius Suavis.

EDCS-24400323.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Ovidia Sancta, daughter of Lucius, is buried here. She lived 14 years. Gaius Ovidius Cupitus [made this] for his most dutiful daughter.
EDCS-24400323.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Ovidia Sancta, made by her father Gaius Ovidius Cupitus.

EDCS-24400324.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Pontia Donata is buried here. She lived 25 years. Priscus [made this] for his most dutiful wife.
EDCS-24400324.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Pontia Donata, made by her husband Priscus.

EDCS-24400325.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits and to the memory of Urbicus, who lived 9 months and 8 days. His most longed-for son, Paris, his father, made this.
EDCS-24400325.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Urbicus, made by his father Paris, who also mourned his son's short life.

EDCS-24400848.translation: Aurelius Pasinicus with his people gave and dedicated this gift to Serapis Augustus.
EDCS-24400848.summary: This is a dedication of a gift to the god Serapis Augustus by Aurelius Pasinicus and his group.

EDCS-24400850.translation: Sacred to Serapis Augustus for the safety of the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Commodus Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus and his entire divine household. Iulianus, son of Rogatus Gemnius Sardanus, in his own name and in the name of his sons Rogatianus, Primulus, Iulianus, and Secundianus, promised a statue out of his own generosity to adorn it, having pledged 3,000 sesterces, and he made and dedicated it, and on account of the dedication.
EDCS-24400850.summary: This is a dedication of a statue to Serapis Augustus for the emperor's safety by Iulianus, who also contributed funds and dedicated it.

EDCS-24500538.summary: This is an incomplete inscription that begins by identifying 'Cresconius the faithful'.

EDCS-24500541.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a person named Dalmatius, who is described as faithful and at peace, likely dating from the late Roman or early Christian period.

EDCS-24500542.translation: Paschasius, faithful, lived in peace for 7 years. Datiba lived, faithful, in peace for 4 years.
EDCS-24500542.summary: This funerary inscription records the ages of two individuals, Paschasius and Datiba, both described as faithful and at peace, suggesting a late Roman or early Christian context.

EDCS-24500544.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Dorsi, described as faithful and indicating an age of 1 year, likely from the late Roman or early Christian period.

EDCS-24500546.summary: This is a simple funerary inscription for Egiptia, indicating her peaceful repose, likely dating from the late Roman or early Christian period.

EDCS-24500547.translation: Emerita, faithful, lived in peace for 33 years.
EDCS-24500547.summary: This funerary inscription records the age of Emerita, who is described as faithful and at peace, likely dating from the late Roman or early Christian period.

EDCS-24500551.summary: This is a simple funerary inscription for Felicia, indicating her peaceful repose, likely dating from the late Roman or early Christian period.

EDCS-24500552.translation: Februarias [daughter of] Felic, lived for 3 years and 6 months.
EDCS-24500552.summary: This funerary inscription records the age of Februarias, the daughter of Felic, who died at the age of 3 years and 6 months, likely dating from the late Roman or early Christian period.

EDCS-24500553.translation: Felicissimus, lived in peace for 70 years and 6 months.
EDCS-24500553.summary: This funerary inscription records the age of Felicissimus, who lived for 70 years and 6 months and is described as being in peace, likely dating from the late Roman or early Christian period.

EDCS-24500554.summary: This inscription records the name and office of Felicissimus, who served as an administrator, possibly indicating an official or funerary context from the Roman period.

EDCS-24500555.translation: Victor, in peace, was buried on the 6th day before the Kalends of June. Lucianus [and] Felicitas [commemorate?] Victor, faithful.
EDCS-24500555.summary: This funerary inscription marks the burial date of Victor, who is described as faithful and at peace, and includes the names of Lucianus and Felicitas, likely dating from the late Roman or early Christian period.

EDCS-24500557.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a person named Mem, stating they lived in peace.

EDCS-24500559.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Florida, stating they lived in peace.

EDCS-24500572.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Jugurtha, stating they lived in peace.

EDCS-24500573.translation: Liber the faithful lived for [---] years.
EDCS-24500573.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Liber, recording his faithful life and lifespan.

EDCS-24500574.translation: Lula, a faithful one, lived in peace, buried on the 3rd day before the Kalends of September.
EDCS-24500574.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lula, detailing her faithful life and burial date.

EDCS-24500575.translation: Melosus the innocent lived for 4 years, buried on the 8th day before the Ides [of ---].
EDCS-24500575.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Melosus, recording his innocence, lifespan, and burial date.

EDCS-24500576.summary: This is a funerary inscription for an unidentified person who was faithful and lived in peace.

EDCS-24500578.translation: Paulus in peace. Aquisa in peace.
EDCS-24500578.summary: This is a funerary inscription mentioning two individuals, Paulus and Aquisa, both of whom lived in peace.

EDCS-24500581.summary: This is an inscription, possibly funerary, mentioning the name Deogratias.

EDCS-24500584.translation: Primula the faithful lived for 35 years in peace.
EDCS-24500584.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Primula, detailing her faithful life and lifespan.

EDCS-24500586.summary: This is a fragmentary epitaph for a person named PROIV A, described as faithful.

EDCS-24500588.summary: This is an epitaph for Quodvultdeus, described as faithful and resting in peace.

EDCS-24500591.summary: This is an epitaph for Renata, described as faithful and resting in peace.

EDCS-24500592.summary: This is an epitaph for Renatus, who is resting in peace.

EDCS-24500594.translation: Bitalis, faithful, in peace; Codbul, faithful, in peace; Restitutus lived 80 years, in peace.
EDCS-24500594.summary: This epitaph records three individuals: Bitalis and Codbul, described as faithful, and Restitutus, who lived to be 80 years old, all resting in peace.

EDCS-24500595.translation: Restitutus, in peace, lived for five years.
EDCS-24500595.summary: This epitaph records that Restitutus lived for five years and is now in peace.

EDCS-24500610.summary: This is an epitaph for Simplicius, who is resting in peace.

EDCS-24500611.summary: This epitaph records Successus resting in peace, with an additional, possibly related, personal name 'Aiut'.

EDCS-24500612.translation: Memorial to Sura and B, in peace.
EDCS-24500612.summary: This inscription marks a memorial for two individuals, Sura and B, who are resting in peace.

EDCS-24500613.translation: Theodora, faithful, in peace, lived one year, seven months, and seven days; buried on the 18th day before the Kalends of October.
EDCS-24500613.summary: This epitaph records the burial date and lifespan of Theodora, who lived for one year, seven months, and seven days and was described as faithful and at peace.

EDCS-24500616.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Varica, identified as faithful and at peace, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-24500617.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Vernaclus, stating he is at peace, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-24500619.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Victor, described as innocent and at peace, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-24500621.translation: Victoria, unharmed, in peace. C. I. Ericdius Ovinus, Incarnatus [?]
EDCS-24500621.summary: This inscription likely records Victoria, unharmed and at peace, possibly with a dedication or reference to C. I. Ericdius Ovinus, dating to the Roman period.

EDCS-24500622.translation: Victoria, faithful, lived 65 years, in peace.
EDCS-24500622.summary: This tombstone inscription for Victoria states she was faithful, lived 65 years, and is now at peace, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-24500623.translation: Victorinus lived X years and his daughter Vict[oria?].
EDCS-24500623.summary: This inscription records the lifespan of Victorinus and mentions his daughter Vict[oria?], likely a tombstone from the Roman period.

EDCS-24500624.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Bincamus, identified as faithful and at peace, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-24500625.summary: This inscription likely names two individuals, Vincent and Curu[s?], possibly related to a tomb or dedication, dating to the Roman period.

EDCS-24500626.translation: Vin, faithful, lived more or less.
EDCS-24500626.summary: This tombstone inscription for Vin states he was faithful and lived an unspecified duration, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-24500627.translation: Vincentiolus and Bonifatia, faithful, in peace.
EDCS-24500627.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for the faithful couple Vincentiolus and Bonifatia, who are now at peace, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-24500630.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the age of Fidelis.

EDCS-24500642.summary: This is a funerary inscription of Fidelis.

EDCS-24500643.translation: Ada Fidelis lived [and was] placed in peace on the Nones of August.
EDCS-24500643.summary: This funerary inscription records Ada Fidelis's death and burial date.

EDCS-24500691.summary: This is a funerary inscription of Arnesus.

EDCS-24500701.summary: This is a funerary inscription of Sidonius, possibly with a numerical code or abbreviation.

EDCS-24500706.translation: Aurelia Sirvata, innocent, lived in peace; [she lived] one year, four months, twenty-three days. Secundosa, faithful, [rests] in peace.
EDCS-24500706.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Aurelia Sirvata, detailing her age at death, and a separate mention of Secundosa.

EDCS-24500708.translation: Antonius the presbyter [was placed] in peace, [died] 13 days before the Kalends of October; Quintus the deacon [was placed] in peace, [died] 2 days before the Kalends of October; Cyprianus the presbyter [was placed] in peace, [died] 1 June; Apronianus the deacon [was placed] in peace.
EDCS-24500708.summary: This inscription from a burial site lists the death and burial dates of several clergy members: Antonius, Quintus, Cyprianus, and Apronianus.

EDCS-24500716.summary: This funerary inscription identifies Albula and her place of origin, Lipara.

EDCS-24500717.summary: This is a funerary inscription of Alomius.

EDCS-24500720.summary: This is a funerary inscription of Benenata.

EDCS-24500721.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for an unnamed individual, indicating their peaceful repose.

EDCS-24500722.translation: Benenata, faithful, in peace, lived 83 years. Tianus, in peace, lived 50 years. Laid to rest in April.
EDCS-24500722.summary: This epitaph records the ages at death of two individuals, Benenata and Tianus, and specifies the month of burial for Tianus.

EDCS-24500727.summary: This is a simple funerary epitaph for Cornelius, stating his peaceful rest.

EDCS-24501001.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Romanus, a devoted slave and steward, lived 64 years.
EDCS-24501001.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Romanus, a slave and steward, dedicated to the household gods.

EDCS-24501002.text_edition: \n Extricata Imr serva Felicis saltuari filia pia vixit annis IIII hic sita\n
EDCS-24501002.translation: Extricata, the devoted slave girl of Felix, daughter of Saltuarius, lived for 4 years and is buried here.
EDCS-24501002.summary: This is a tombstone for a young slave girl named Extricata, dating from antiquity.

EDCS-24501003.translation: In the most blessed and flourishing times of our lords Valentinian, Valens, and Gratian, ever invincible Augusti, whose kindness and clemency we see daily increasing their world, during the proconsulship of Paulus Constantius, a most distinguished man, and of Paulinus, a most distinguished man, again legate of the illustrious Carthage, with all the territories belonging to it, the curator of the public works of the fortress of Biracsaccara, with his own resources, began to build it from its foundations and dedicated it along with his order.
EDCS-24501003.summary: This inscription celebrates the construction and dedication of a fortress's public works, initiated and completed by a curator under the authority of proconsuls and legates during the reign of Valentinian, Valens, and Gratian, likely in the late 4th century.

EDCS-24501004.translation: Saturus, son of Saturus, son of Acastus, devoted, lived 80 years. Cusanras, son of Arinis Gaitulis, lived 75 years.
EDCS-24501004.summary: This epitaph records the ages at death of two individuals, Saturus and Cusanras, likely from the same family or community.

EDCS-24501005.translation: Crescentianus, son of Lucius, devoted, lived 60 years. He lies here.
EDCS-24501005.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Crescentianus, son of Lucius, stating his age at death and burial location.

EDCS-24501006.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. I, Titus, am here. Crescens Vesdrunus himself keeps my bones and remains in a jar; my little tower, made as a tomb, holds seventy-seven years. My devoted son Felix made this.
EDCS-24501006.summary: This funerary epitaph, dedicated to the departed spirits, records that Titus lived 77 years and was buried in a jar within a small tower built by his devoted son Felix.

EDCS-24501007.translation: Numerius Caesius, son of Felix, among the leading men of Bisicensis, devoted, lived 71 years. He lies here. May your bones rest well. May the earth lie lightly upon you.
EDCS-24501007.summary: This epitaph for Numerius Caesius, son of Felix and a prominent figure in Bisicensis, records his age at death and burial, including wishes for his repose.

EDCS-24501008.translation: Sempronia, daughter of Lucius, Albina, devoted, lived 32 years.
EDCS-24501008.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Sempronia Albina, daughter of Lucius, stating her age at death.

EDCS-24501009.summary: This inscription records a dedication or ownership by Marcus Julius, son of Iulus, likely on a monument or property. The date is uncertain but falls within the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-24501010.translation: To Julia, daughter of Lucius, Postuma.
EDCS-24501010.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Julia Postuma, daughter of Lucius. The context of the dedication is not specified, but it is likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-24501011.summary: This is a dedication of a sacred object or place to Fortuna Augusta, a deified aspect of the Roman imperial cult, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-24501012.translation: Sacred to Caelestis Augusta, made by vow for the safety of Lucius Anniolenus Albanus.
EDCS-24501012.summary: This is a votive dedication to Caelestis Augusta, made by Lucius Anniolenus Albanus for his own safety, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-24501013.translation: Pudens and his daughter Iulia Fida, devotedly and with a willing spirit, built the temple from the ground up at their own expense as a vow to Imperial Ceres.
EDCS-24501013.summary: This inscription records the construction and dedication of a temple to Ceres Augusta by Pudens and his daughter Iulia Fida, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-24501014.translation: Sacred to Caelesta Augusta, the city [made this] for T...
EDCS-24501014.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Caelesta Augusta, made by the city for an individual whose name is incomplete, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-24501015.translation: For the safety of the Emperor, Caesar Traianus Hadrianus Augustus, Pontifex Maximus, holding tribunician power for the 15th time, Consul for the 3rd time, Imperator for the 2nd time, Father of the Fatherland; the priest of the countryside made the temple from the foundations and dedicated it himself, because of the honor of perpetual flamen.
EDCS-24501015.summary: This inscription records the construction and dedication of a temple by a priest from the countryside, for the safety of Emperor Hadrian, during his 15th tribunician power and 3rd consulship, likely in the mid-2nd century CE.

EDCS-24501018.translation: To our lord Flavius Honorius, the Unconquered, ever Augustus, Emperor.
EDCS-24501018.summary: This is an inscription honoring Emperor Flavius Honorius, likely on a public monument or building, dating to his reign in the late 4th to early 5th century CE.

EDCS-24501021.translation: Acapitul of rocks, three middle columns in the portico: Acidonius son of Nargaus, Orcu son of Sirimbatis, Nagud son of Barigbal, Barigbal son of Felicis, Lucanus son of Aris, Oricufonius son of Secundus, Lactuca son of Nis, Lucanus son of Sufetum, Sufetes son of Nis, made these from their own money as a vow.
EDCS-24501021.summary: This inscription records the construction of architectural elements (columns and portico) by a group of individuals, identified by patronymic and tribal affiliations, who were likely local officials (sufetes), probably dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-24501022.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Lucius Fabius Saturninus lived 80 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-24501022.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Fabius Saturninus, recording his name, age at death, and burial, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-24501023.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Lucius Pullaienus Papias pius vixit annos XVIII hic situs est Primigenius pater posuit\n
EDCS-24501023.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Lucius Pullaienus Papias, devoted, lived for 18 years and is buried here. His father Primigenius erected this.
EDCS-24501023.summary: This is a tombstone for Lucius Pullaienus Papias, erected by his father, dating from antiquity.

EDCS-24501024.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Gaius Aurelius Namphamo Nebridianus, dutiful, lived 60 years. Gaius Aurelius Paladianus, dutiful, lived 26 years. He is buried here. Berebgal, dutiful, lived [---] years. She is buried here. Gaius Aurelius Paladius, dutiful, lived 7 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-24501024.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the ages and burial of several individuals, likely family members, from the Aurelius family.

EDCS-24501025.translation: Marcus Caecilius Perpetuus and Papia Sulpicia lived 35 years. Quintus Caecilius Perpetuus lived 103 years. Quintus Caecilius made this monument for his most excellent and dutiful father and wife.
EDCS-24501025.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the ages of Marcus Caecilius Perpetuus and Quintus Caecilius Perpetuus, and stating that Quintus Caecilius dedicated the monument to his father and wife.

EDCS-24501026.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Fausta, dutiful daughter of Baribgalis, lived 75 years. Sacred to the departed spirits. For my dutiful daughter Tertia, lived 70 years. For a dutiful freedwoman, lived 2 years and 6 months.
EDCS-24501026.summary: A funerary epitaph for Fausta and her daughter Tertia, also commemorating a freedwoman, likely from the late Roman period given the context of 'Dis Manibus'.

EDCS-24501027.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Cimbrius Rogatianus, dutiful, lived 75 years, 1 month, and 11 days.
EDCS-24501027.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Lucius Cimbrius Rogatianus, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-24501028.translation: Azrubal, son of Baisillis, Chian, Saturninus lived 40 years. Saturninus.
EDCS-24501028.summary: A brief funerary epitaph recording the name and age of Saturninus, son of Azrubal and Baisillis, likely from North Africa.

EDCS-24501029.translation: Under our lords, Arcadio, Honorio, and Theodosio, perpetual always Augusti, during the proconsulship of Flavius Pionius Diotimus, a man of highest distinction, judging with vice-sacred authority.
EDCS-24501029.summary: An inscription recording the names of the reigning emperors and a proconsul, likely from the Eastern Roman Empire around the early 5th century AD.

EDCS-24501032.translation: Gidius Felix, son of Primus, priest of Caelestis, lived 71 years. Monument from his own funds for himself.
EDCS-24501032.summary: A funerary epitaph for Gidius Felix, a priest of Caelestis, who built his own tomb, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-24501033.translation: Caius Aedinius Repentinus lived 25 years. Aedinus Felix.
EDCS-24501033.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the name and age of Caius Aedinius Repentinus, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-24501034.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Aelius Felix Faustinus Maximinus, son of Felicis, dutiful, lived 1 year, 5 months, and 17 days. They are buried here.
EDCS-24501034.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lucius Aelius Felix Faustinus Maximinus, a child, recording his short lifespan.

EDCS-24501035.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus Apuleius Martialis, son of Caius, dutiful, lived 71 years. May your bones rest well. May the earth lie lightly upon you.
EDCS-24501035.summary: A funerary epitaph for Quintus Apuleius Martialis, including a common Latin epitaph wish for the deceased.

EDCS-24501036.translation: Quintus Caecilius Felix, son of Zoprus, and Pompeia Rogatula, daughter of Rogatus, with Lucius Caecilius...
EDCS-24501036.summary: This inscription appears to be a dedication or familial record naming Quintus Caecilius Felix and Pompeia Rogatula, possibly as a couple or related individuals, with a partial mention of Lucius Caecilius.

EDCS-24501037.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Marcus Ennius Acmazon, son of Protogenis, lived 52 years; he is buried here. May his bones rest well; may the earth lie lightly upon you.
EDCS-24501037.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the death of Marcus Ennius Acmazon, son of Protogenis, who lived 52 years, and includes wishes for his peaceful rest.

EDCS-24501038.translation: Sacred to the August Emperors. Quintus Gargilius, freedman of Quintus, restored [this] with his own money.
EDCS-24501038.summary: This inscription records the restoration of something sacred to the August Emperors by Quintus Gargilius, a freedman, at his own expense.

EDCS-24501039.translation: Sacred to Mercury the Fateful, the August. Marcus Lollius Gemellus vowed and willingly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-24501039.summary: This is a votive inscription recording that Marcus Lollius Gemellus vowed and fulfilled a vow to Mercury Fatale Augustus.

EDCS-24501040.translation: To our lord Flavius Honorius Pius, Victorious, ever August prince.
EDCS-24501040.summary: This is an honorific inscription dedicated to the Emperor Flavius Honorius, addressing him with various imperial titles.

EDCS-24501041.summary: This is a very brief inscription, likely naming Lucius Manilius Turia Maxima, possibly on a tomb or monument.

EDCS-24501043.translation: To Augusta Venus, T. Us Pes, freedman.
EDCS-24501043.summary: This is a dedication to Augusta Venus by T. Us Pes, who is identified as a freedman.

EDCS-24501044.translation: To the Emperor Caesar, son of the divine Trajan Particus, grandson of the divine Nerva, Hadrian Augustus, pontifex maximus, with tribunician power for the 18th time, consul for the 3rd time, father of the fatherland. Sextus Calvius Primus, Lucilius Victor, M.S. Surrentinus Saturninus, Primus, At.VS. S. Primus, Mogondineus, Dinius Maximus, S. Rianeus, M.E. R. Vict. Bens, Saturninus, Ma. US Brihis, B. Ecundus, US Faustus, Ves. Secundus, nus Saturninus, Iustus, US Plocamus, Ter. Ni. US O. Ni. US Prin. US Ni.
EDCS-24501044.summary: This extensive inscription lists the imperial titles of Emperor Hadrian and is dedicated by numerous individuals, including Sextus Calvius Primus and others, likely commemorating an imperial visit or achievement.

EDCS-24501045.translation: To our Emperor Caesar Flavius Valerius Constantinus, Pious, Fortunate, Victorious Augustus, pontifex maximus, with tribunician power for the 8th time, emperor for the 7th time, consul for the 3rd time, father of the fatherland, proconsul. The municipality of Felix Thaborra is devoted to his divine majesty and authority.
EDCS-24501045.summary: This inscription records the devotion of the municipality of Felix Thaborra to Emperor Constantine the Great, listing his numerous imperial titles and dignities.

EDCS-24501050.translation: To Aulus Ammicaris, son of Pius, lived 83 years; he is buried here. May his bones rest well; may the earth lie lightly upon you.
EDCS-24501050.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the death of Aulus Ammicaris, son of Pius, who lived 83 years, and includes wishes for his peaceful rest.

EDCS-24501051.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Datus, son of Saturninus Giddinis, lived 56 years. Saturnina, wife of Rogatus Flaminianus, lived 37 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-24501051.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the Divine Shades, recording the ages of two individuals, Datus and Saturnina, who are buried here.

EDCS-24501052.text_edition: \n Amodb Secundi IAI ASAE pia vixit annos XVI Lucius Secundus Mutthuni LIMBENE pius vixit annos LXXXV Felix filius parentibus fecit\n
EDCS-24501052.translation: Amodb Secundi (devoted), lived for 16 years. Lucius Secundus Mutthuni (devoted), lived for 85 years. Felix, their son, erected this for his parents.
EDCS-24501052.summary: This is a tombstone for Lucius Secundus Mutthuni and his unnamed spouse, erected by their son Felix, dating from antiquity.

EDCS-24501053.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Memius Secundus lived [age] years.
EDCS-24501053.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the Divine Shades, recording the lifespan of Memius Secundus, though the exact age is lost.

EDCS-24501054.translation: Mutthun, son of Aris, lived 52 years. Nu lived 92 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-24501054.summary: This funerary inscription records the ages of two individuals, Mutthun and Nu, with Nu being buried here.

EDCS-24501055.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Petronius Viceminens, father of Carus, pious, lived 57 years.
EDCS-24501055.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to the Divine Shades and records the lifespan and piety of Petronius Viceminens, father of Carus.

EDCS-24501056.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Rogatus, son of Saturnina daughter of Saturninus Censor, and his most frugal, most diligent, pious son, lived 22 years and 8 months. He is buried here.
EDCS-24501056.summary: This funerary inscription dedicated to the Divine Shades records the lifespan of a pious son, identified by his mother Rogatus and grandfather Saturninus Censor.

EDCS-24501057.translation: Fortunata the girl lived 32 years in peace.
EDCS-24501057.summary: This is a tombstone for Fortunata, a young girl who lived 32 years.

EDCS-24501058.translation: A boundary stone placed while the [---] form was [---] through Publius Tettius Sepiminus, centurion of the 13th urban cohort, between the people of Thabor and the people of Thimisus.
EDCS-24501058.summary: This inscription records the placement of a boundary stone, likely marking land or territory, overseen by a centurion and concerning two communities.

EDCS-24501060.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Lucius Aurelius Commodus Rogatianus, pious, lived 27 years, 6 months, and 13 days. He is buried here.
EDCS-24501060.summary: This funerary inscription dedicated to the Divine Shades records the lifespan and burial of Lucius Aurelius Commodus Rogatianus.

EDCS-24501061.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Quintus Caelius Maximus, pious, lived 76 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-24501061.summary: This funerary inscription dedicated to the Divine Shades records the lifespan and burial of Quintus Caelius Maximus.

EDCS-24501062.summary: This is a brief epitaph for Quinta Annia Fausta, indicating her peaceful rest.

EDCS-24501063.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Publius Antistius Secundus lived 13 years, is buried here. M. Successa lived 30 years, is buried here. Publius Antistius Secundus, dutiful, lived 12 years. Publius Antistius, 20?
EDCS-24501063.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of members of the Antistius family.

EDCS-24501066.translation: Felicitas in peace, 9 years. [---] on the base.
EDCS-24501066.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the age at death of Felicitas.

EDCS-24501067.translation: Naborianus departed in peace on the fourth day before the Nones of October.
EDCS-24501067.summary: This funerary inscription records the death date of Naborianus.

EDCS-24501068.translation: Table of martyrs. Here the venerable relics of the blessed martyrs Maena and Sebastian were deposited in peace on the third day before the Ides of November, in the fourth indiction, by the hands of the most blessed bishop Iulianus, priest, and Victor, monk. They had made a vow to God.
EDCS-24501068.summary: This inscription records the deposition of the relics of martyrs Maena and Sebastian by clergy and monks, likely in the 4th century.

EDCS-24501071.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Aris Clementis, son of Cullube, dutiful, lived 21 years, is buried here.
EDCS-24501071.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Aris Clementis.

EDCS-24501072.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Babit Silvani, son of Aterus, lived 40 years, is buried here. May the earth rest lightly upon you.
EDCS-24501072.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Babit Silvani, with a wish for a light burial.

EDCS-24501073.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Celer, son of Celeris Galli Celeris, dutiful, lived [number] years.
EDCS-24501073.summary: This funerary inscription records the name and parentage of Celer, with an incomplete lifespan.

EDCS-24501074.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Marcus Fabius Fuscus lived 85 years. Antonia Gallari, daughter of Sammius, lived 70 years. Marcus Fabius Fuscus Valerianus lived 25 years. Dutiful, he is buried here. May your bones rest well.
EDCS-24501074.summary: This funerary inscription records the deaths of three members of the Fabius family, with wishes for their peaceful repose.

EDCS-24501075.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Lucius Pontius Felix Pompeianus, dutiful, lived 66 years. May the earth rest lightly upon you. May your bones rest well.
EDCS-24501075.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Lucius Pontius Felix Pompeianus and expresses wishes for his peaceful afterlife.

EDCS-24501076.translation: Sacred to Mercury Augustus, for the health of the emperors Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus and Lucius Aurelius Verus. Aius Arinis Occonis made and dedicated this with his own money, with a willing spirit.
EDCS-24501076.summary: This dedication to Mercury was made by Aius Arinis Occonis for the health of Emperors Marcus Aurelius Antoninus and Lucius Aurelius Verus, likely in the mid-2nd century AD.

EDCS-24501077.translation: To the portico of the porch, next to the COL, for the decurions and other citizens, a gift of Marcus Aurelius Severus Alexander, grandson of the deified Lucius Septimius Severus Pius.
EDCS-24501077.summary: This inscription records a public dedication of a portico to decurions and citizens, made in honor of Emperor Alexander Severus, likely in the 3rd century CE.

EDCS-24501078.translation: To the Divine Shades. For a son of exceptional piety, who lived [only?] to the very last [daughter?], by his parents.
EDCS-24501078.summary: This is a funerary dedication to a deceased son, expressing the parents' grief and piety, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24501079.translation: The house of Titus Valerius Vennis, to Valerius.
EDCS-24501079.summary: This inscription appears to indicate ownership or a dedication related to a house belonging to Titus Valerius Vennis, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24501080.translation: To Marcus Aufidius, son of Marcus, and Cornelia Caia, his wife Exoptata.
EDCS-24501080.summary: This inscription lists a couple, Marcus Aufidius and his wife Cornelia Exoptata, likely a tombstone or dedication, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24501081.translation: Valeria Tertia, daughter of Augusta and Castrorum and Senatus, [dedicated this] with her own money.
EDCS-24501081.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by Valeria Tertia, possibly honoring her mother or other significant figures, using her own funds, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24501083.translation: Sentius Sentius Futinis, a dutiful son, lived 20 years.
EDCS-24501083.summary: This inscription is a tombstone for Sentius Sentius Futinis, noting his age at death and his filial piety, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24501084.translation: To the Divine Shades. Cossinia Fuscula, lived 75 years, is buried here.
EDCS-24501084.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Cossinia Fuscula, stating her age and that she is buried here, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24501085.summary: This inscription indicates that Ianuarius Bostricianus, a son, erected this monument, likely a tombstone, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24501086.translation: By the Sululitanian community, by decree of the decurions, with public funds: to Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus, Armenian, Median, Parthian the Greatest, Pontifex Maximus, with tribunician power for the 22nd time, Imperator for the 6th time, Consul for the 3rd time, Father of the Fatherland, and to Emperor Caesar Lucius Aurelius Verus Augustus, Armenian, Median, Parthian the Greatest, with tribunician power for the 8th time, Imperator for the 5th time, Consul for the 2nd time, Father of the Fatherland, sons of the deified Antoninus, grandsons of the deified Hadrian, great-grandsons of the deified Trajan Parthicus, and great-great-grandsons of the deified Nerva.
EDCS-24501086.summary: This extensive inscription records a dedication by the community of Sullulitana to Emperors Marcus Aurelius Antoninus (Caracalla) and Lucius Aurelius Verus (Geta), detailing their extensive titles and honors, likely from the early 3rd century CE.

EDCS-24501092.translation: To Gaius Attius Alximus Felicissimus, a most accomplished man, prefect of the grain supply, prefect of the Praetorian guard, vice-prefect of the Vigiles, master of the highest private office, master of the highest accounts, curator of the work of the amphitheater, procurator of inheritances in Rome, procurator of the sacred mint, procurator of the iron mines, procurator of the grain supply of the province of Narbonensis, procurator of the private [estate?] through the Salarian and Tiburtine roads, procurator of [estates?] through the Flaminian, Umbrian, and Picene regions.
EDCS-24501092.summary: This lengthy inscription details the numerous high-ranking administrative and financial positions held by Gaius Attius Alximus Felicissimus, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24501093.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Nonius Privatus, dutiful, lived 65 years, 4 months, 7 days; he is buried here and dedicated this.
EDCS-24501093.summary: A tombstone for Nonius Privatus, who lived to be 65 years old, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24501094.translation: To the memory of Aninia Rusticula, his most chaste, obedient, and frugal wife. Pinatius Lucianus, her husband, [erected this].
EDCS-24501094.summary: A memorial erected by Pinatius Lucianus for his wife Aninia Rusticula, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24501095.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus Caelius, deceived by fate, lived 66 years, 9 months; Caelius Secundianus [erected this] for his father here.
EDCS-24501095.summary: A tombstone for Quintus Caelius, who lived to be 66 years old, erected by his son Caelius Secundianus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24501096.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Caius Cominius Felicianus, a most rare man, lived 34 years, 7 months, 3 days; Caius Cominius Felix [erected this] for his son here.
EDCS-24501096.summary: A tombstone for Caius Cominius Felicianus, who died at 34 years old, erected by his father Caius Cominius Felix, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24501097.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulia Semp, lived 10 years; her son Rogatus dedicated this to his most rare wife.
EDCS-24501097.summary: A tombstone for Iulia Semp, who died at 10 years old, dedicated by her son Rogatus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24501099.text_edition: \n Imperatore Caesare Marco Aurelio Commodo Antonino Augusto V Manio Acilio Glabrione II consulibus pridie Kalendas Februarias et possessorum civium ibi Victor Callitiosi filius et Honoratus filius um quaestos quod agri suorum pecoribus ovium devastarentur et tem conrosas sic esse quod ipsum initium honoris nostri at sit facta etiam mentione sacrarum litterarum ONnostramque denuntiationem initium honoris nostrit nec debeat eis contumacia eorum prodesse et aliter ea res s secundum sacras constitutiones actum fuerit sic quae decreto subiciendam existimavimus et aecum mihi desiderium vestrum videtur et exemplo adiuvari --- in? agrum vestrum invitis vobis pecora pascendi gratia induccare quod si ignorante domino servus induxerrit pecora in ipsum servum proconsul severe constituet si iusso sic domini etiam praetium sic servi ex forma censoria |(denarios) D dominus dare debebit si sua sponte id admiserint a proconsule flectentur sic ita ut in relegentur quit sic fieri placeret de ea re universi censuerunt passim in territorio unius cuiuscumque pecora pascendi facultatemncentur et cum etiam post ex constitutione \n
EDCS-24501099.translation: Under the emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Commodus Antoninus Augustus, and Manius Acilius Glabrio, consuls for the second time, on the day before the Kalends of February...[This inscription appears to be a legal decree or dispute regarding grazing rights and penalties, dating to the consulship of Commodus and Acilius Glabrio in the late 2nd century CE.]
EDCS-24501099.summary: This inscription is a legal text concerning grazing rights and penalties, dated to the consulship of Commodus and Acilius Glabrio (c. 185 CE).

EDCS-24501100.translation: Together with Murnia, he happily gave [this] for the games.
EDCS-24501100.summary: A dedication for games, possibly related to a public event or a private benefactor, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24501102.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Boncia Galla, mother, lived [XX] years; Quintus Iulius Saturninus, father, lived [XX] years.
EDCS-24501102.summary: A tombstone fragment for Boncia Galla and Quintus Iulius Saturninus, indicating a couple's shared burial plot, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24501104.summary: A fragmentary inscription that likely refers to members of the family of Magnii Galli, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24501105.summary: A fragmentary inscription possibly commemorating or related to the emperor Antoninus Pertinax, dating to the late 2nd century AD.

EDCS-24501106.translation: Quintus Vetulenius Urbanus Herennianus, perpetual priest and curator of the republic, completed and dedicated a new changing room on the right as one exits the cells, and two swimming pools, and restored other things, adorned with marble statues, painted panels, columns, at the entrance of the cells, and with other things, at his own expense, together with his most flourishing and most prudent son Magnilianus, a youth, fulfilling the vow of all the citizens, and he gave a banquet to the entire populace for three days and theatrical games.
EDCS-24501106.summary: A dedication by Quintus Vetulenius Urbanus Herennianus and his son for public works including a changing room and swimming pools, along with games and a banquet for the populace, likely in the 2nd or 3rd century AD.

EDCS-24501108.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Gaius Claudius Quintatus lived 35 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-24501108.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan and burial of Gaius Claudius Quintatus.

EDCS-24501110.translation: and all the materials and wood brought and transported here from Renis.
EDCS-24501110.summary: A fragment of an inscription, likely detailing materials acquired for construction or a project, originating from Renis.

EDCS-24501111.translation: was desired by all. IXIR MATORE
EDCS-24501111.summary: An incomplete inscription, possibly a dedication or a wish, with an unclear personal name or title.

EDCS-24501112.translation: The municipality of Thagaria Maius, devoted to the divine numen and majesty of the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Valerius Claudius Pius Felix Augustus, pontifex maximus, with tribunician power twice, consul twice, proconsul, dedicated this with public money by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-24501112.summary: An inscription recording the dedication of a monument by the municipality of Thagaria Maius to Emperor Marcus Aurelius Valerius Claudius.

EDCS-24501113.translation: Vitriasius Restutus, flamen perpetuus and curator rei publicae, along with the council, devoted to the divine numen and majesty of our lord Flavius Valens Maximus Pius Felix Victor semper Augustus.
EDCS-24501113.summary: An inscription recording the devotion of Vitriasius Restutus, a local official, to Emperor Flavius Valens Maximus.

EDCS-24501118.translation: To the memory of Adventus, a good man and actor. He is buried here.
EDCS-24501118.summary: A funerary epitaph commemorating Adventus, described as a good man and an actor.

EDCS-24501119.translation: Sacred to Hercules Augustus. Iulia Bas...
EDCS-24501119.summary: A fragment of a dedication to Hercules Augustus, initiated by Iulia Bas.

EDCS-24501124.translation: from the legion Gallica, dismissed as a standard-bearer. But an unhappy father erected this for his son. Lived 12 years. Pavioinciarininio andoni. His paternal grandmother lived 1 year. To the departed spirits. His paternal grandfather Flavius Callio Zaecoi lived 2 years.
EDCS-24501124.summary: A complex funerary inscription for multiple family members, including a son who lived 12 years, and his grandparents, with a father and grandmother also mentioned.

EDCS-24501126.inscription_type: tituli honorarii, tituli operum, tituli sacri
EDCS-24501126.text_edition: \n Mercurio Augusto sacrum pro salute Imperatoris Caesaris Marci Aurelli sic Severi Alexandri Pii Felicis Augusti pontificis maximi patris patriae tribunicia potestate XII proconsulis et Iuliae Mamaeae Augustae matris Augusti et senatus et patriae totiusque domus divinae eorum Quintus Cervius Luci filius Lucretius Maximus et Caius Geminius Cai filius Victoricus aediles sua pecunia fecerunt et ob dedicationem epulum decurionibus et missilia populo dederunt et fistula plumbea cum epitonio aereo ad labrum lapideum aqua ut saliret aeque sua pecunia curaverunt locus datus decreto decurionum\n
EDCS-24501126.translation: Sacred to Mercury Augustus for the health of the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Severus Alexander Pius Felix Augustus, Pontifex Maximus, Father of the Fatherland, holder of tribunician power for the 12th time, proconsul, and Julia Mamaea Augusta, Mother of Augustus and the Senate and of the whole Fatherland, and of their divine household. Quintus Cervius Lucretius Maximus, son of Lucius, and Caius Geminius Victoricus, son of Caius, aediles, made this at their own expense and for the dedication, they provided a feast for the decurions and distributed gifts to the people, and they also took care, at their own expense, to have a lead pipe with a bronze fitting so that water would flow to a stone basin. The site was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-24501126.summary: This is a dedication of a public work, likely a fountain, to Mercury Augustus for the health of Emperor Severus Alexander and Julia Mamaea, funded by the aediles Quintus Cervius Lucretius Maximus and Caius Geminius Victoricus, dating to the early 3rd century CE.

EDCS-24501127.translation: Sacred to Mercury Augustus. Publius Iulius Ro...
EDCS-24501127.summary: A fragment of a dedication to Mercury Augustus, initiated by Publius Iulius Ro...

EDCS-24501128.translation: The city of Giufitana, devoted to the divine numen and majesty of the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus, prince of the youth, with tribunician power twice, father of the fatherland, proconsul, son of Emperor Caesar Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus Arabicus Adiabenicus Parthicus Maximus, the most strong and most fortunate, great-grandson of divine Marcus Aurelius Pius, great-great-grandson of divine Hadrian, great-great-great-grandson of divine Trajan Parthicus and divine Nerva, dedicated this temple with public money by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-24501128.summary: An inscription by the city of Giufitana dedicating a temple to Emperor Marcus Aurelius Antoninus, listing his imperial lineage and titles.

EDCS-24501129.translation: To the Emperor Caesar, son of the divine Magnus Antoninus Pius, grandson of the divine Septimius Severus Pius, Marcus Aurelius Severus Alexander Pius Felix Augustus, supreme pontiff, father of the fatherland, in his eighth year of tribunician power, consul for the second time designated, the city of Giufi funded this with public money by decree of its decurions.
EDCS-24501129.summary: This is a dedication to Emperor Severus Alexander by the city of Giufi, likely set up on a public building or monument.

EDCS-24501130.translation: To Aurelia Dionysia, daughter of her patron Aurellius Alexandrianus Augustus Magnus Giufitanus, from the townswomen of the municipality of Aurelia Alexandriana.
EDCS-24501130.summary: This is an epitaph or dedication for Aurelia Dionysia, honoring her relationship to her patron and her civic connections.

EDCS-24501132.translation: Mamon, son of Safotis and Athon, erected this column with its capital and spire at his own expense.
EDCS-24501132.summary: This is a private dedication of a column, funded by Mamon, son of Safotis and Athon.

EDCS-24501133.translation: For the safety of our Lords. Ianuarius, a slave, fulfilled his vow to Mercury Silvanus.
EDCS-24501133.summary: This is a votive inscription by a slave named Ianuarius to Mercury Silvanus for the well-being of his masters.

EDCS-24501134.translation: Sacrates made (this) at their own expense.
EDCS-24501134.summary: This is a brief dedication indicating that Sacrates funded a project at their own cost.

EDCS-24501135.summary: This is a simple inscription, likely an epitaph, for Fortunatus Tutus.

EDCS-24501136.summary: This is a simple inscription, likely an epitaph, for Sarganis.

EDCS-24501137.translation: To Marcus Aelius Aurelius Verus Caesar, son of the Emperor Caesar Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Augustus Pius, supreme pontiff, in his ninth year of tribunician power, consul for the fourth time, father of the fatherland, son of Aufidius Felix; Sutunurcensian Felix Felicionis Pancrati son, grandson, whom the decurions of his city, as perpetual priest and decurion, adopted as his son, transferred to him, gave equestrian statues and, in addition, for the dedication, a public feast, costing 8,000,000 sesterces, the total sum for his magistracy.
EDCS-24501137.summary: This inscription records a significant financial endowment by Aufidius Felix for the erection of equestrian statues and a public feast in honor of Marcus Aurelius (as Caesar), whose father was Antoninus Pius.

EDCS-24501138.translation: To the Emperor Caesar, son of the divine Marcus Antoninus Pius Germanicus Sarmaticus, grandson of the divine Antoninus Pius, great-grandson of the divine Hadrian, great-great-grandson of the divine Trajan Parthicus, great-great-great-grandson of the divine Nerva, Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus Arabicus Adiabenicus, father of the fatherland, supreme pontiff, in his third year of tribunician power, emperor for the seventh time, consul for the second time, proconsul, the city of Sutunurca funded this with public money by decree of its decurions.
EDCS-24501138.summary: This is a dedication to Emperor Septimius Severus by the city of Sutunurca, likely set up on a public building or monument.

EDCS-24501139.summary: This is a dedication or address to the governor of Mauretania.

EDCS-24501140.translation: To Corinthia, daughter of Cerialis, perpetual flamen.
EDCS-24501140.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Corinthia, daughter of Cerialis, who held the position of perpetual flamen, likely on a tomb or religious monument.

EDCS-24501141.translation: Sacred to Saturn Augustus. Gaius Valerius Felix gladly paid his vow.
EDCS-24501141.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicating something to the god Saturn Augustus, with Gaius Valerius Felix fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-24501142.translation: Sacred to the god Saturn. Decimus Insteius Merianus, priest, gladly paid his vow.
EDCS-24501142.summary: This votive inscription records that the priest Decimus Insteius Merianus gladly fulfilled a vow made to the god Saturn.

EDCS-24501148.translation: To Gaius Egnatius Cosminus, son of the perpetual flamen Gaius Egnatius Cosminus, admitted to the public horse by Emperor Hadrian for his father's merit, who among other bequests left to the state in his will also gave 75 denarii annually to each curia, so that the curiae might feast in public on his birthday; the curiae as a whole made this with their own money.
EDCS-24501148.summary: This inscription records a public monument erected by the curiae to Gaius Egnatius Cosminus, honoring his father's significant bequests to the community, likely dating to Hadrian's reign.

EDCS-24501149.translation: To Egnatia Honorata, daughter of Gaius, wife of Quintus Cassius Frontonianus Iustianus, perpetual flamen, by decree of the decurions, with public money.
EDCS-24501149.summary: This inscription records a monument or honor for Egnatia Honorata, wife of a perpetual flamen, funded by public money and decreed by the local council.

EDCS-24501150.translation: Masurius in the estates of Laberius, of Laberianus and Paulinus Masurius.
EDCS-24501150.summary: This inscription likely indicates ownership or property boundaries relating to Masurius on the estates of Laberius and others.

EDCS-24501151.summary: This is a very brief inscription, possibly a name or a dedication by Ederatus to Mustela, perhaps on a tomb or object.

EDCS-24501155.summary: This inscription lists three names, Myro, Fructus, and Victor, likely a list of individuals, possibly freedmen or workers, or owners of an object.

EDCS-24501156.translation: To Quintus Billenus, son of Quintus, Helvius Valens.
EDCS-24501156.summary: This inscription appears to be a dedication or dedication to Quintus Billenus, son of Quintus, possibly by Helvius Valens.

EDCS-24501161.translation: Vincentius Optatus, restored to peace, the day before the Kalends of November.
EDCS-24501161.summary: This inscription records the death and burial of Vincentius Optatus, noting his peaceful rest and the date of his passing, likely from the 4th century AD or later.

EDCS-24501162.translation: Quintus Marcius Protomachus, son of Herakleides, physician, made a table for Lucius Marcius, consul. (Greek text: Quintus Marcius Protomachus, son of Herakleides, physician).
EDCS-24501162.summary: This inscription, partly in Greek, records a medical practitioner named Quintus Marcius Protomachus who dedicated a table during the consulship of Lucius Marcius.

EDCS-24501163.text_edition: \n Adoni Augusto sacrum pro salute Imperatoris Caesaris Luci Septimi Severi Pertinacis Augusti et Imperatoris Caesaris Marci Aureli Antonini Pii Felicis Augusti et Iuliae Domine sic Augustae\n
EDCS-24501163.translation: Sacred to Adonis Augustus for the health of the Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pertinax Augustus and the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus and Julia Domna Augusta.
EDCS-24501163.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Adonis Augustus for the health of Emperors Septimius Severus, Caracalla, and Julia Domna, likely dating to the early 3rd century CE.

EDCS-24501165.translation: Fulvius Repostus, priest, willingly paid his vow to the lord of Sobara.
EDCS-24501165.summary: This dedication records Fulvius Repostus, a priest, fulfilling a vow to a local deity or lord of Sobara.

EDCS-24501166.translation: Sacred to Saturn Augustus. Caius Memmius Pudens, priest, willingly entered under the yoke.
EDCS-24501166.summary: This inscription indicates that Caius Memmius Pudens, a priest, dedicated something to Saturn Augustus, possibly as part of a ritual involving passing 'under the yoke'.

EDCS-24501167.translation: Sacred to Saturn Augustus. Petronius Restutus, priest, willingly paid his vow.
EDCS-24501167.summary: Petronius Restutus, a priest, willingly fulfilled a vow made to Saturn Augustus.

EDCS-24501169.translation: Voltia Nuptialica and Petronius Bucculus, son and husband of Petronius Proculina, who made a track for a vow, paid their vow to Saturn Augustus.
EDCS-24501169.summary: Voltia Nuptialica and Petronius Bucculus fulfilled a vow to Saturn Augustus, related to a track and made on behalf of Petronius Proculina.

EDCS-24501170.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Caius Pisonius Victor, a pious veteran, lived in his own property for 70 years.
EDCS-24501170.summary: This funerary inscription records the life and death of Caius Pisonius Victor, a veteran who lived to be 70 years old.

EDCS-24501171.translation: Covuldus built the market from his own property.
EDCS-24501171.summary: This inscription records Covuldus financing and constructing a market building at his own expense.

EDCS-24501172.translation: Coelianus, all of it Greek, 82 years.
EDCS-24501172.summary: This very brief inscription possibly records the age of a person named Coelianus, noting their Greek origin.

EDCS-24501174.translation: To Flavius Valerius Constantinus, most noble Caesar.
EDCS-24501174.summary: This is a dedication to Flavius Valerius Constantinus, referred to as a 'most noble Caesar', likely dating to the 4th century CE.

EDCS-24501176.translation: Under the Augusti Valentinianus, Theodosius, and Arcadius, Innocentius, perpetual flamen and curator of the city, opened the neglected curia, which had been restored to its former appearance in the proconsulate of Flavius Primus, a most distinguished and illustrious man, and of Lucius Tor[…], perpetual flamen and curator of the public affairs, and dedicated it to the city and the people.
EDCS-24501176.summary: This inscription details the restoration and rededication of a neglected curia (meeting hall) by Innocentius, who served as both flamen and city curator, during the reigns of multiple emperors and under the supervision of imperial officials.

EDCS-24501177.translation: During the proconsulship of... priest for life, a citizen and... of the most distinguished Polibus, by our notice and decree.
EDCS-24501177.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription mentioning a priest for life and a distinguished individual named Polibus.

EDCS-24501178.translation: From 100,000 sesterces, which for public use... by the united effort of the whole council.
EDCS-24501178.summary: This inscription records the use of a sum of money, likely for a public project, contributed by a council.

EDCS-24501179.translation: Sacred to Ceres Augusta. Lucius Titius Metrianus, priest, along with Lucius Titius Felix and Lucius Titius Victor, his sons, gladly made the altar with its foundations.
EDCS-24501179.summary: This is a dedication of an altar and its foundations to Ceres Augusta by a priest and his sons.

EDCS-24501180.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Tuccius Ianianus lived 24 years and 8 months. Lucius Tuccius Rogatus lived 38 years. Marcus Tuccius Severus lived 12 years.
EDCS-24501180.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the ages of death for three individuals: Tuccius Ianianus, Lucius Tuccius Rogatus, and Marcus Tuccius Severus.

EDCS-24501182.translation: To Fidens, to Lucio Apertio Fidus, our good citizen of Capua. Apertio Gaetulicus to his brother, Caviolus Secundus, honored.
EDCS-24501182.summary: This is a dedication honoring Fidens and Apertio Gaetulicus for his brother, Caviolus Secundus, who is described as a good citizen of Capua.

EDCS-24501186.summary: This inscription records Nargius fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-24501187.translation: To Quintus Appaeus Saturninus Iuventianus, son of Publius, of the Teretina tribe, an excellent man, father of Quintus Appaeus Felix Flavius, of most distinguished memory, a young priest of eternal Rome, and perpetual priest.
EDCS-24501187.summary: This is a dedication to Quintus Appaeus Saturninus Iuventianus, honoring him as a father and a perpetual priest of Rome.

EDCS-24501189.translation: Sacred to Saturn. M. Abdazi, son, fulfilled his vow gladly.
EDCS-24501189.summary: This inscription records M. Abdazi fulfilling a vow to Saturn.

EDCS-24501190.summary: This inscription records Paederos fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-24501191.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription mentioning the name Gaius Considius.

EDCS-24501197.translation: Septimianus, a man of singular and military distinction, advocate of the treasury of the patrimony of the province of Carthage, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-24501197.summary: This inscription honors Septimianus, an advocate for the treasury in Carthage, with a decree from the town council.

EDCS-24501198.translation: Leander, be a lamp to me, don't be rough.
EDCS-24501198.summary: This inscription is a personal, perhaps pedagogical, instruction from Leander.

EDCS-24501201.translation: Faithful in peace, placed [here] in the year of the Januaries.
EDCS-24501201.summary: This inscription records a person named Ianuarias who died faithful in peace.

EDCS-24501202.translation: Which befitted the most splendid times, with our lords Theodosius and Valentiniano ruling, for the proconsulate, for the vicar and proconsul of the province of Africa, then for the municipality, by SV Rufinianus, a most distinguished man, perpetual flamen, and by P. Maurusius, a most honorable man, twice curator of public affairs, and Iter.
EDCS-24501202.summary: This inscription details civic and religious honors granted during the proconsulate of Africa under Emperors Theodosius and Valentiniano, enacted by Rufinianus and Maurusius.

EDCS-24501203.summary: This inscription records Rufina, identified as a young girl, at peace.

EDCS-24501206.translation: Most perfect... under the care of Flavius, the freedman.
EDCS-24501206.summary: This inscription mentions something 'most perfect' being overseen by a freedman named Flavius.

EDCS-24501207.translation: He made [this] for his most chaste wife, his dearest spouse.
EDCS-24501207.summary: This inscription is a dedication made by a husband to his beloved and chaste wife.

EDCS-24501208.translation: Saturinus the presbyter lived 53 years in peace.
EDCS-24501208.summary: This epitaph records the death of Saturinus, a presbyter, who lived 53 years in peace.

EDCS-24501209.summary: This epitaph records the death of Facra, who lived 80 years in peace.

EDCS-24501211.translation: To the Emperor Caesar, son of the divine Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Magnus, grandson of the divine Severus Pius.
EDCS-24501211.summary: This is a dedication to an Emperor, identifying him through his lineage from Marcus Aurelius and Severus.

EDCS-24501212.translation: For the safety of our unconquered lord the Emperor Caesar Licinius Gallienus Augustus and Cornelia Salonina Augusta, his wife, Caius Licinius Felix, freedman of Postumius, erected this from the ground at his own expense, according to a vision of the divine powers of the goddesses Ceres.
EDCS-24501212.summary: This inscription records the erection of a monument by Caius Licinius Felix for the safety of Emperor Licinius Gallienus and Cornelia Salonina, likely in the 3rd century CE.

EDCS-24501213.translation: Quintus Aufidius Melior gladly paid his vow.
EDCS-24501213.summary: This is a votive inscription by Quintus Aufidius Melior, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24501215.summary: This is a simple votive inscription by Fabius Fabullus, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24501218.summary: This inscription is a simple personal dedication or identification by Marcus Furfianius Sabinus, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24501219.summary: This inscription provides a personal identification with patronymic by Imilcho, son of Nisazru, likely of North African origin.

EDCS-24501221.translation: Lucius Rodienus Gallus gladly paid his vow.
EDCS-24501221.summary: This is a votive inscription by Lucius Rodienus Gallus, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24501222.summary: This inscription is a simple personal dedication or identification by Stenius Quartio, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24501225.translation: For the safety of the Emperors, Caesars, and Marcus Aurelius Domna Augusta.
EDCS-24501225.summary: This is a dedication for the safety of the reigning emperors and Marcus Aurelius Domna Augusta, likely from the 3rd century CE.

EDCS-24501227.translation: The colony Aurelia Commoda Pia Felix Augusta Pupput, most devoted to the majesty of the divine being of the great and most powerful prince, the Emperor Caesar Licinius Pius Felix Invictus Augustus.
EDCS-24501227.summary: This inscription expresses the devotion of the colony of Pupput to Emperor Licinius, likely dating from the early 4th century CE.

EDCS-24501228.translation: To Lucius Octavius Cornelius Salvius Iulianus Aemilianus, son of Publius, Xvir quaestorius, quaestor of the Emperor Hadrian, to whom the deified Hadrian doubled the salary of the quaestorship because of his outstanding learning, tribune of the plebs, praetor, prefect of the treasury of Saturn, also military quaestor, consul, pontiff, member of the Hadrianic fellowship, member of the Antonine fellowship, curator of sacred buildings, legate of Emperor Antoninus Augustus Pius in Lower Germany, legate of Emperors Antoninus Augustus and Verus Augustus in Further Spain, proconsul of the province of Africa, patron, by decree of the decurions, with public money.
EDCS-24501228.summary: This is a lengthy cursus honorum inscription honoring Lucius Octavius Cornelius Salvius Iulianus Aemilianus, detailing his extensive political and military career and public benefactions, likely dating to the mid-2nd century CE.

EDCS-24501229.text_edition: \n Thoraci mirae integritatis et innocentiae inimitabilis exempli viro Caelio Severo viro clarissimo patricio consulari curatori rei publicae et patrono coloniae Puppitanorum qui solus sua liberalitate forum vetustate conlapsum cum aedibus et capitolio et curia meliori cultu restituit et dedicavit ordo Puppitanorum patrono perpetuo dedicata VIIII Kalendas Iunias Imperatore Probo Augusto V et Victorino consulibus\n
EDCS-24501229.translation: To Thorac, a man of wondrous integrity and inimitable example of innocence, to Caelus Severus, a most distinguished man, a patrician, curator of the Republic, and patron of the colony of Puppita, who alone, with his own generosity, restored and dedicated the forum, which had collapsed from age, along with the buildings, the Capitol, and the curia, with better craftsmanship. The ordo of the Puppitans to their perpetual patron. Dedicated on the 9th day before the Kalends of June, when Emperor Probus Augustus was consul for the 5th time and Victorinus was consul.
EDCS-24501229.summary: This inscription honors Caelus Severus, a distinguished patron of the colony of Puppita, for his restoration of the forum and public buildings, dating to the reign of Emperor Probus (276-282 CE).

EDCS-24501231.translation: Nardus the elder, Turassus the younger, Restitutus the younger departed the day before the Ides of May, in peace.
EDCS-24501231.summary: This inscription records the death of three individuals, possibly a family, with a date implied by their passing in peace.

EDCS-24501232.translation: Lucius Statius Aurelianus, son of Marcus, of the Arnensian tribe, a Roman knight, with his generosity above the legal limit...
EDCS-24501232.summary: This inscription fragment likely records the generosity of Lucius Statius Aurelianus, a Roman knight, possibly related to a legal or financial matter.

EDCS-24501233.summary: This inscription fragment likely records a dedication or monument funded by the generous contribution of someone named Ponti.

EDCS-24501234.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus, conqueror of Parthia, greatest pontiff, with the tribunician power for the 21st time, general for the 5th time, consul for the 3rd time, father of the country, son of Livius [---].
EDCS-24501234.summary: This is a formal dedication to Emperor Marcus Aurelius Antoninus, listing his numerous titles and honors, suggesting it accompanied a public monument or statue.

EDCS-24501235.translation: While our lords Honorius and Theodosius are perpetually everlasting Augusti, Stertinius Carcedonius, perpetual priest, recalling the traditions of his ancestors, restored statues, placed from the offering of his own family's generosity out of love for his country.
EDCS-24501235.summary: This inscription records the restoration of statues by Stertinius Carcedonius, a perpetual priest, under the reigns of Emperors Honorius and Theodosius, motivated by family generosity and patriotism.

EDCS-24501236.translation: Similis, son of Marcus, of the Arnensian tribe.
EDCS-24501236.summary: This is a very brief inscription likely identifying an individual, Similis, by name, filiation, and tribal affiliation.

EDCS-24501238.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Marcus Julius Sedatus lived 58 years, died in Caesarea.
EDCS-24501238.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the death of Marcus Julius Sedatus, his age, and place of death.

EDCS-24501239.translation: Decimus Laelius Balbus, son of Decimus, quaestor pro praetore, arranged for the making of a sundial and a solar [clock].
EDCS-24501239.summary: This inscription records that Decimus Laelius Balbus, a quaestor pro praetore, commissioned the construction of timekeeping devices, likely a sundial and a solar clock.

EDCS-24501241.summary: This is a brief funerary inscription stating the name and age of Simplicia.

EDCS-24501242.summary: This inscription, possibly funerary, states the name and age of Obaia and includes a phrase about believing in peace.

EDCS-24501243.translation: Livinius gave his vow to Saturn Augustus, willingly.
EDCS-24501243.summary: A private individual named Livinius dedicates a votive offering to Saturn Augustus.

EDCS-24501244.translation: Lucius Pomponius Curius, also called Cacca, the priest, fulfilled his vow to Saturn Augustus, willingly.
EDCS-24501244.summary: A priest named Lucius Pomponius Curius, also known as Cacca, dedicates a votive offering to Saturn Augustus.

EDCS-24501251.translation: On the Kalends of June and under the consulship of Condianus.
EDCS-24501251.summary: This inscription records a date defined by consuls and a specific day.

EDCS-24501256.translation: In the fourth consulship of Emperor Caesar Commodus Augustus and the second of Victorinus, Saturn Balcaranensis [received a dedication from] Atus M.

EDCS-24501262.translation: Lucius Sextilius Communis, outstanding and admonished by a vision, willingly fulfilled his vow to Saturn Augustus Balcaranensis.

EDCS-24501335.translation: The community of Galensis, led by the sufetes Aris and Manius Celeris, built the temple to Mercury and commissioned it. Satur Celeris's son, the builders Caius Manius and Gaius Aemilius.

EDCS-24501336.translation: Quarta Nyptanis, daughter of Galensis, wife of Celeris Mantis, the chief priestess, made her burial place with her own money, with the curators Saturus Rogatus Brutione Manius Namphamone Valens, son of Celeris, and the builders Rufus and Imilco Tuleses. She lived 59 years.
EDCS-24501336.summary: This funerary inscription records the construction of a burial place by Quarta Nyptanis, daughter of Galensis and chief priestess, mentioning various officials and builders, and her age at death.

EDCS-24501337.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcus Ampelius Ampelianus lived 34 years, 2 months; he is buried here.
EDCS-24501337.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the life and burial of Marcus Ampelius Ampelianus.

EDCS-24501338.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcus Iulius Rogatianus Seranianus lived...

EDCS-24501340.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Livia Restuta is here; she lived 40 years, 2 months; she is buried here.

EDCS-24501341.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Titus Paetius Papius the pious lived 52 years; he is buried here. P. Victoria the pious lived 111 years; she is buried here.

EDCS-24501345.translation: In the flourishing reign of the most invincible emperors. Helvius Tertullus, perpetual priest, curator of the public business.

EDCS-24501348.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Donata lived 60 years, daughter of Titus, lived 60 years. Gaius T. Aristus lived 32 years.
