EDCS-24501362.translation: Dedicated to the departed spirits. Optata, daughter of Optatus, lived forty-five years.

EDCS-24501363.translation: To the divine Commodus Augustus, brother of Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pertinax Augustus Arabicus Adiabenicus Parthicus, father of the fatherland, by decree of the decurions, with public money.
EDCS-24501363.summary: An inscription dedicating a monument to the deified emperor Commodus, funded by the local council.

EDCS-24501364.translation: To Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Severus Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus Parthicus Maximus Britannicus Maximus, son of the divine Septimius Severus Arabicus Adiabenicus Parthicus Maximus Britannicus Maximus, grandson of the divine Marcus Antoninus Pius Germanicus Sarmaticus, great-grandson of the divine Antoninus Pius, descendant of the divine Hadrian, descendant of the divine Trajan Parthicus and the divine Nerva, Pontifex Maximus, holder of tribunician power for the 16th time, Imperator for the 2nd time, Consul for the 4th time, father of the fatherland, proconsul, the best and greatest prince, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-24501364.summary: A lengthy imperial titulature for Caracalla, likely part of a public monument funded by the local council.

EDCS-24501365.translation: Dedicated to the departed spirits. Marcus Pomponius Saturninus Antonianus, son of Marcus Pomponius Maximus Antonianus, lived 16 years. He is buried here. Dedicated to the departed spirits. Marcus Pomponius Maximus Antonianus, son of Marcus Pomponius Li Antonianus, lived 51 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-24501365.summary: A double funerary dedication for a father and son, both named Marcus Pomponius, recording their ages at death.

EDCS-24501366.translation: Dedicated to the departed spirits. Vitalis Piaetita, the innocent, lived 91 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-24501366.summary: A funerary dedication for Vitalis Piaetita, recording her age at death and burial.

EDCS-24501367.translation: I have escaped the harshest burdens of life, leaving behind a tomb to grant me perpetual memory. I possess this even in death. I beg that I may be with my dear wife, born [here].
EDCS-24501367.summary: A personal epitaph expressing a desire for remembrance and companionship with his wife in the afterlife.

EDCS-24501402.translation: Sacred to Mercury Augustus. By decree of the decurions and at public expense, for the health of the Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pertinax Arabicus Adiabenicus, father of the country, and of the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus.

EDCS-24501403.translation: To the god Mercury Augustus. Servilius Felix, Servilius Rogatianus, Tadius Victorinus, Flavius Flavianus, Lucius Rufinus, Gnaeus Castius Biz...
EDCS-24501403.summary: This is a dedication to the god Mercury Augustus, listing several dedicator names, likely from the late Roman period.

EDCS-24501404.translation: For the health of the Emperor Caesar, son of the deified Septimius Severus Pius Arabicus Adiabenicus Parthicus Maximus Britannicus Maximus, grandson of the deified Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Germanicus Sarmaticus, great-grandson of the deified Antoninus Pius, great-great-grandson of the deified Hadrian, great-great-great-grandson of the deified Trajan Parthicus and the deified Nerva, Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Felix, prince of youth, Augustus, Parthicus Maximus, Britannicus Maximus, high priest, with tribunician power 15 times, imperator twice, consul 3 times, father of the country, and of Julia Domna Augusta Pia Felix, mother of the emperor, mother of the camps, mother of the senate and of the entire divine house, Gaius Octavius Rogatus, perpetual flamen, priest of Mercury, in his own name and in the name of his son, Caius Octavius Rogatianus, constructed and dedicated the arch with its steps from his own generosity and funds by decree of the decurions. He also, using doubled funds, constructed the bronze statue of the god Mercury seated on a rock, and also, in honor of his priesthood, the statue of Emperor Severus.
EDCS-24501404.summary: This inscription records the construction and dedication of an arch and two statues by Gaius Octavius Rogatus, a perpetual flamen and priest of Mercury, honoring Emperor Septimius Severus and his family.

EDCS-24501405.translation: The civic community of Vazitana Sarara, by decree of the decurions and with public funds, made and dedicated this for Septimius Severus, high priest and Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus Pius Felix, prince of youth, and for Julia Domna Augusta, mother of the emperors, mother of the camps, mother of the senate, and mother of the country and of the entire divine house.
EDCS-24501405.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a monument by the civic community of Vazitana Sarara to Emperor Septimius Severus, his son Caracalla, and Julia Domna.

EDCS-24501406.translation: Quintus Antistius Felix Furianus and Lucius Antistius Maximus Furianus placed this in memory of their kinsman, Quintus Magnius Furianus, son of Quintus, a dutiful man, for his outstanding example of kinship love towards them.
EDCS-24501406.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Quintus Antistius Felix Furianus and Lucius Antistius Maximus Furianus for their kinsman Quintus Magnius Furianus.

EDCS-24501407.translation: Iulia Galla, pious daughter of Caius, is buried here; she lived 50 years.
EDCS-24501407.summary: This is a simple tombstone recording the death of Iulia Galla.

EDCS-24501408.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus Magnius Secundus, dutiful, lived 31 years. Minininia Venusta, dutiful, lived 31 years. They are buried here.
EDCS-24501408.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Quintus Magnius Secundus and Minininia Venusta, who died at the same age.

EDCS-24501409.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Magnia Fortunata, dutiful, lived 58 years. She is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus Magnius Saturninus lived 66 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-24501409.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Magnia Fortunata and Quintus Magnius Saturninus.

EDCS-24501410.translation: He lived 21 years. He is buried here. Magnia Amitata, dutiful, lived 23 years.
EDCS-24501410.summary: This is a tombstone for two individuals, one unnamed and Magnia Amitata.

EDCS-24501411.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Rudionia Iulia, also known as Gudugia, lived 61 years. Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Rudionius Maximianus Iulianus lived 36 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-24501411.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Rudionia Iulia and Lucius Rudionius Maximianus Iulianus.

EDCS-24501412.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Boncia Germana lived 54 years. She is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcus Apronius Felix Aurelianus lived 55 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-24501412.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Boncia Germana and Marcus Apronius Felix Aurelianus.

EDCS-24501413.translation: Flavia Galla, dutiful daughter of Faustus, lived 51 years.
EDCS-24501413.summary: This is a tombstone recording the death of Flavia Galla.

EDCS-24501414.translation: Mitun, daughter of Bal Rogatus, lived 40 years, is buried here. Calpurnius Saturninus lived 25 years, is buried here.
EDCS-24501414.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lives and burials of two individuals, Mitun and Calpurnius Saturninus.

EDCS-24501415.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Saturnina, daughter of Muthum Balis, lived 85 years, is buried here. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Gaius Fabius Donatus lived 75 years, is buried here.
EDCS-24501415.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lives and burials of two individuals, Saturnina and Gaius Fabius Donatus, with a dedication to the spirits of the departed.

EDCS-24501416.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Victor, son of Astrennius, lived 20 years, is buried here.
EDCS-24501416.summary: This funerary epitaph records the life and burial of Victor, son of Astrennius, dedicated to the spirits of the departed.

EDCS-24501417.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Victoria, daughter of Licinus, lived 85 years, is buried here.
EDCS-24501417.summary: This funerary epitaph records the life and burial of Victoria, daughter of Licinus, dedicated to the spirits of the departed.

EDCS-24501418.translation: Sacred to Augustus. Rufinianus Saturninus, the priest, saw to its construction by decree of the decurions, with public money, for the son of Chenius, Probius.
EDCS-24501418.summary: This inscription records the construction of a monument or building sacred to Augustus, commissioned by the priest Rufinianus Saturninus through a decree of the local council and public funds.

EDCS-24501419.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Fusnus lived 85 years.
EDCS-24501419.summary: This is a fragment of a funerary epitaph recording the age of Fusnus, dedicated to the spirits of the departed.

EDCS-24501420.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Marcus Antonius Secundinus Hilarianus, son of Marcus Antonius Marci, pious, lived 75 years, is buried here.
EDCS-24501420.summary: This funerary epitaph records the life and burial of Marcus Antonius Secundinus Hilarianus, son of Marcus Antonius Marci, who lived 75 years.

EDCS-24501421.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Iulia Victoria lived 21 years.
EDCS-24501421.summary: This is a fragment of a funerary epitaph recording the age of Iulia Victoria, dedicated to the spirits of the departed.

EDCS-24501423.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Gaius Valerius Sabinianus lived 58 years and 5 months, is buried here. His sons made this for their most devoted father.
EDCS-24501423.summary: This funerary epitaph records the life of Gaius Valerius Sabinianus, who lived 58 years and 5 months, and was buried here, with the monument erected by his sons.

EDCS-24501425.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Oratius Frumentius lived 2 years, 11 months, 12 days, and 3 hours.
EDCS-24501425.summary: This funerary epitaph records the very young age of Oratius Frumentius, who lived 2 years, 11 months, 12 days, and 3 hours.

EDCS-24501427.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Honorata, likely from late antiquity.

EDCS-24501429.translation: Recepta lived for 5 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-24501429.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the life and burial of Recepta.

EDCS-24501430.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. He is buried here. Silus Titus lived for 33 years, by order of Ro, 3 feet.
EDCS-24501430.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Silus Titus, who lived 33 years, and specifies burial depth.

EDCS-24501431.translation: To the god Hercules, Firmia, daughter of Marcus, gave this offering.
EDCS-24501431.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicating a gift to the god Hercules by Firmia.

EDCS-24501432.translation: To the Great God, Firmia, daughter of Marcus.
EDCS-24501432.summary: This is a votive inscription to the 'Great God' by Firmia.

EDCS-24501433.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Quintus Considius Valens lived piously for 49 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-24501433.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Quintus Considius Valens, who lived piously for 49 years.

EDCS-24501435.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Faustina, daughter of Mutthunis, lived piously for 23 years. Her son Helvius Cogitans made this for his wife.
EDCS-24501435.summary: This is a funerary inscription made by Helvius Cogitans for his wife Faustina, who lived piously for 23 years.

EDCS-24501436.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Iulius Nundinus lived.
EDCS-24501436.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the name of Iulius Nundinus and stating that he lived.

EDCS-24501437.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Gaius Tertul[...]
EDCS-24501437.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription for Gaius Tertul[...].

EDCS-24501438.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Lucius Aurelius Aebutianus lived piously for 45 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-24501438.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Aurelius Aebutianus, who lived piously for 45 years.

EDCS-24501439.translation: To the Divine Manes. Gaius Julius Saturninus Victorianus lived 53 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-24501439.summary: A funerary epitaph for Gaius Julius Saturninus Victorianus, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24501440.translation: To the Divine Manes. Minsilius Ianuarius, dutiful, lived 70 years and 4 months; he is buried here.
EDCS-24501440.summary: A funerary epitaph for Minsilius Ianuarius, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24501441.translation: To the Divine Manes. Lucius Sempronius Iulianus, dutiful, lived 22 years, 6 months, and 7 days; he is buried here.
EDCS-24501441.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lucius Sempronius Iulianus, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24501442.translation: To the Divine Manes. Lucius Septimius Mustulus, who was also called Sosus, lived piously for 25 years.
EDCS-24501442.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lucius Septimius Mustulus, also known as Sosus, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24501443.translation: S. Rucanus, son of Quintus, lived 61 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-24501443.summary: A funerary epitaph for S. Rucanus, son of Quintus, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24501444.translation: To the Divine Manes. Tessenia Rogatianilla, dutiful, lived 38 days; she is buried here.
EDCS-24501444.summary: A funerary epitaph for Tessenia Rogatianilla, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24501445.translation: To the Divine Manes. Quintus Considius Extricatus, dutiful, lived 41 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-24501445.summary: A funerary epitaph for Quintus Considius Extricatus, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24501446.translation: To the Divine Manes. Marcus Domitius Cududus lived 30 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-24501446.summary: A funerary epitaph for Marcus Domitius Cududus, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24501447.translation: To the Divine Manes. Lucius Rogatus Arinis, dutiful, lived 105 years.
EDCS-24501447.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lucius Rogatus Arinis, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24501448.translation: Gaius Julius Maximus Claudianus lived 60 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-24501448.summary: A funerary epitaph for Gaius Julius Maximus Claudianus, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24501449.translation: To Julia Augusta, daughter of Germanicus, by public money.
EDCS-24501449.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Julia Augusta, likely funded by public money, possibly related to the imperial family.

EDCS-24501450.translation: To Lucius Virius Lupus, clarissimus vir, ordinary consul, legate of the province of Lycia, patron of the municipality by decree of the decurions, by public money.
EDCS-24501450.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Lucius Virius Lupus, a high-ranking official and consul, honoring his role as patron of the municipality.

EDCS-24501451.translation: To Cassia Manilia, a woman of the first rank, grandmother. By Cassius Manilianus, clarissimus vir.
EDCS-24501451.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Cassia Manilia by her grandson, Cassius Manilianus, a prominent man.

EDCS-24501452.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus Caecilius Tertullus Caecilianus lived 29 years, 8 months, and 18 days; he is buried here.
EDCS-24501452.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan and burial of Quintus Caecilius Tertullus Caecilianus.

EDCS-24501453.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Cassius Rufus Lollianus, dutiful, lived 76 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-24501453.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan and burial of Lucius Cassius Rufus Lollianus.

EDCS-24501454.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Cassius Rusticianus, dutiful, lived 51 years and 3 months; he is buried here.
EDCS-24501454.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan and burial of Lucius Cassius Rusticianus.

EDCS-24501455.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcus Cocceius Saturninus Iulianus lived 71 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-24501455.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan and burial of Marcus Cocceius Saturninus Iulianus.

EDCS-24501456.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Egnatia Secunda, dutiful, lived 38 years.
EDCS-24501456.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Egnatia Secunda.

EDCS-24501457.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Fabia Rutula lived 32 years and 6 months; she is buried here.
EDCS-24501457.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan and burial of Fabia Rutula.

EDCS-24501458.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulius Secundianus, dutiful, lived 20 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-24501458.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan and burial of Iulius Secundianus.

EDCS-24501459.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. To Junia Repentina, daughter of Quintus, a most virtuous woman and most dutiful wife to her husband.
EDCS-24501459.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Junia Repentina, likely set up by her husband.

EDCS-24501460.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Lucius Lutatius Serinus, dutiful, lived 80 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-24501460.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Lutatius Serinus, recording his age at death.

EDCS-24501461.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Lucius Modius Prudentianus lived 47 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-24501461.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Modius Prudentianus, recording his age at death.

EDCS-24501462.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Lucius Rithulius Felix Lollianus lived 75 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-24501462.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Rithulius Felix Lollianus, recording his age at death.

EDCS-24501463.translation: Crescens, dutiful, lived 65 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-24501463.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Crescens, recording his age at death.

EDCS-24501465.translation: Modia Staberia lived one hundred years; she is buried here.
EDCS-24501465.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Modia Staberia, recording her age at death.

EDCS-24501466.translation: Sextus Staberi us, son of Sextus, Se RC Laet, lived 25 years.
EDCS-24501466.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Sextus Staberi us, recording his age at death.

EDCS-24501467.translation: Terentia Secundula, dutiful, lived 52 years and 5 months; Lucius Sentius Secundus, dutiful, lived [---]
EDCS-24501467.summary: This inscription records the lifespan of Terentia Secundula and begins to record that of Lucius Sentius Secundus.

EDCS-24501468.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Publius Iulius Saturninus Maximianus lived 51 years, 3 months, 3 hours; Crement (?) is buried here.
EDCS-24501468.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Publius Iulius Saturninus Maximianus, recording his age at death and possibly another individual.

EDCS-24501469.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Decimus Marcius Rogatianus lived 67 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-24501469.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Decimus Marcius Rogatianus, recording his age at death.

EDCS-24501470.translation: To Imperator Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pertinax Augustus, son of the deified Marcus Antoninus Germanicus Sarmaticus, brother of the deified Commodus, nephew of the deified Antoninus Pius, great-nephew of the deified Hadrian, great-great-nephew of the deified Trajan Parthicus, great-great-great-nephew of the deified Nerva; pontifex maximus, with the tribunician power for the 3rd time, imperator for the 8th time, consul for the 2nd time, father of the fatherland, at the decree of the decurions, with public funds.
EDCS-24501470.summary: This is an honorific inscription dedicated to Emperor Septimius Severus, likely erected by a city at public expense.

EDCS-24501471.translation: Although the town council had decreed that a statue be publicly erected to Publius Iulius Gibba, son of Publius, of the Arnensis tribe, because of his singular devotion to the state, Publius Iulius Gibba, priest of Ceres of the colony of Concordia Iulia Karthago in its 198th year, and his sons Lucius Iulius Maximus, Caius Iulius Urbanus, and Marcus Iulius Felix, content with honoring their most dutiful father, erected this statue.
EDCS-24501471.summary: This inscription records the erection of a statue to Publius Iulius Gibba by his sons, likely in Roman Africa.

EDCS-24501472.translation: For 13 years a citizen of Sarad, of his parents and of the distinguished men of Deciana, the town council of Sarad established this at its own expense by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-24501472.summary: This inscription seems to record a dedication or monument established by the town council of Sarad for one of its citizens, potentially referencing a period of 13 years.

EDCS-24501473.translation: The town council and people of Sarad erected this to Marcus Valerius Caelianus, son of Marcus, of the Iulia tribe, for his outstanding justice towards the state and the people, especially in the face of the treasury's demands and in general towards all citizens.
EDCS-24501473.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a monument by the town council and people of Sarad to Marcus Valerius Caelianus, a curator rei publicae, for his just administration.

EDCS-24501474.translation: Sacred to Frugifer Augustus, by the will of Caius Mutilius Felix Annaeianus, public defender, under the care of Caius Mutilius Optatus, relative and heir, from his public feast given to the decurions.
EDCS-24501474.summary: This inscription records a sacred dedication to Frugifer Augustus, established by the will of Caius Mutilius Felix Annaeianus, with his heir overseeing its execution.

EDCS-24501475.translation: To the deified Antoninus Pius, son of the deified Hadrian, grandson of the deified Trajan Parthicus, great-grandson of the deified Nerva, pontifex maximus, with the tribunician power for the 23rd time, imperator for the 3rd time, consul for the 4th time, father of the fatherland, at the decree of the decurions, with public funds.
EDCS-24501475.summary: This is an honorific inscription dedicated to the deified Emperor Antoninus Pius, likely erected by a city at public expense.

EDCS-24501477.summary: This is a very brief inscription, possibly the names of two individuals, perhaps related to a tomb or dedication.

EDCS-24501478.summary: This is a short dedication to the goddess Tellus Augusta.

EDCS-24501479.translation: The community of Avioccalensis erected this to Imperator Caesar Marcus Aurelius Commodus Antoninus Augustus Germanicus Sarmaticus, son of the deified Marcus Antoninus Pius Germanicus Sarmaticus, grandson of the deified Pius, great-grandson of the deified Hadrian, great-great-grandson of the deified Trajan Parthicus, great-great-great-grandson of the deified Nerva; pontifex maximus, with the tribunician power for the 6th time, imperator for the 4th time, consul for the 3rd time, father of the fatherland, with public funds.
EDCS-24501479.summary: This inscription records a public dedication by the community of Avioccalensis to Emperor Commodus.

EDCS-24501482.text_edition: \n Caio Arrio Cai filio Quirina Calpurnio Longino clarissimo viro consuli legato Karthaginis auguri praetori urbano quaestori tribuno legionis triumviro auro argento flando feriundo Avioccalenses civi et patrono\n
EDCS-24501482.translation: To Gaius Arrius Calpurnius Longinus, son of Gaius, of the Quirina tribe, most distinguished man, consul, legate of Carthage, augur, urban praetor, quaestor, tribune of the legion, triumvir for striking gold and silver coinage, as a citizen and patron of the Avioccalenses.
EDCS-24501482.summary: This inscription honors Gaius Arrius Calpurnius Longinus, a prominent Roman official and patron, by the people of Avioccalenses.

EDCS-24501483.translation: To Oscia Modesta, Cornelia Patruina Publiana, a most illustrious woman, citizen and patron, for her distinguished merits by which she brought glory to her homeland, the citizens of Avioccalenses, at the decree of the decurions, with public funds.
EDCS-24501483.summary: This inscription records a dedication by the citizens of Avioccalenses to Oscia Modesta, a distinguished woman and patron, at public expense.

EDCS-24501768.translation: Fabricius Bonifa lived in peace for 43 years, 2 months, and 4 hours; he died on the Kalends of October.
EDCS-24501768.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespan and date of death of Fabricius Bonifa, likely from the late antique period.

EDCS-24501769.translation: Felicissima lived in peace for 43 years.
EDCS-24501769.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespan of Felicissima, who lived in peace.

EDCS-24501770.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Here lies Fortunatianus; he lived for 62 years, 5 months, and 15 days.
EDCS-24501770.summary: This funerary inscription, dedicated to the Dis Manibus, records the lifespan of Fortunatianus and marks his burial place.

EDCS-24501771.translation: Ianariana lived for 56 years and 2 [units of time, likely months or days]; her spirit rests in holy [peace].
EDCS-24501771.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespan of Ianariana and mentions her spirit resting in peace, suggesting a late antique or early Christian context.

EDCS-24501772.translation: Iohannes the faithful lived for 8 years, 4 months, and 6 days.
EDCS-24501772.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespan of Iohannes the faithful, likely a child.

EDCS-24501773.translation: Iulius Fortunatus the faithful lived in peace for 62 years and 9 days.
EDCS-24501773.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespan of Iulius Fortunatus the faithful, indicating a peaceful life and death.

EDCS-24501774.translation: Iulius Pascasi lived in peace for 21 months.
EDCS-24501774.summary: This funerary inscription records the short lifespan of Iulius Pascasi, who lived for 21 months.

EDCS-24501775.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Iulia Fortunata lived for [unknown years], 5 days, and 7 hours in peace.
EDCS-24501775.summary: This funerary inscription, dedicated to the Dis Manibus, records the lifespan of Iulia Fortunata, emphasizing her peaceful passing.

EDCS-24501776.translation: Iulia Restuta lived in peace. Calpurnius [Ti?] placed this for his wife.
EDCS-24501776.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespan of Iulia Restuta and was set up by her husband, Calpurnius.

EDCS-24501777.translation: Olimpia the faithful lived in peace for 3 years, 9 months, 10 days, and 2 hours.
EDCS-24501777.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespan of Olimpia, a faithful individual, likely from the late antique period.

EDCS-24501778.translation: Cenova was given as an innocent and placed among the saints; she lived 20 months and 6 days.
EDCS-24501778.summary: This inscription records the burial of a child named Cenova, who died at a very young age.

EDCS-24501779.translation: A faithful servant lived in peace for 87 years, 1 month, and 11 days; he was buried on the 8th day before the Kalends of June.
EDCS-24501779.summary: This inscription records the death and burial dates of a faithful servant who lived to an advanced age.

EDCS-24501780.translation: Siliquesis, faithful in peace, lived 28 years, 10 months, and 3 hours.
EDCS-24501780.summary: This inscription records the lifespan of Siliquesis, a faithful individual who died in peace.

EDCS-24501781.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Soric, faithful in peace, lived 4 years, 11 months, 7 days, and 5 hours.
EDCS-24501781.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication to the departed spirits for Soric, a child who died at the age of four.

EDCS-24501782.translation: Ispes, faithful, lived in peace for 15 years, 5 months, and 7 hours, passing away on the 13th day before the Kalends of January.
EDCS-24501782.summary: This inscription records the lifespan and death date of Ispes, a faithful individual.

EDCS-24501783.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Tyranus, faithful, rested in peace for 35 years, 4 months, and 13 days, and 15 hours.
EDCS-24501783.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Tyranus, a faithful individual who died at the age of 35.

EDCS-24501784.translation: Urbana, faithful, lived in peace for 5 years, 2 months, and 2 hours.
EDCS-24501784.summary: This inscription records the short life of Urbana, a faithful child.

EDCS-24501785.translation: Victoria, faithful, lived in peace for 22 years, 8 months, 13 days, and 12 hours.
EDCS-24501785.summary: This inscription records the lifespan of Victoria, a faithful individual.

EDCS-24501786.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Ursacius, faithful, lived in peace for 18 years and 5 months.
EDCS-24501786.summary: This funerary inscription records the life of Ursacius, a faithful individual who died at age 18.

EDCS-24501787.translation: Lived in peace for 55 years, 10 months, and 25 days, departing on the 8th day before the Ides of November.
EDCS-24501787.summary: This inscription records the death date and lifespan of an individual who lived in peace.

EDCS-24501788.translation: Faithful in peace, she lived for 40 years, 1 month, 14 days, and 2 hours. He thrust a sword into us until the day of our death.
EDCS-24501788.summary: This epitaph records the lifespan and a poignant personal detail about a woman, likely from the late Roman period.

EDCS-24501791.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits: to Lucius Sextilius Felix, a man of strong spirit, for his memory.
EDCS-24501791.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Lucius Sextilius Felix, praising his character.

EDCS-24501792.translation: Iulia Paeonia lived for 37 years, 3 months, and 4 days.
EDCS-24501792.summary: This epitaph records the lifespan of Iulia Paeonia.

EDCS-24501794.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits: Matus Sentius Ianuarius lived for 58 years and 7 days.
EDCS-24501794.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Matus Sentius Ianuarius, recording his lifespan.

EDCS-24501795.translation: To the Emperor Caesar, son of the deified Hadrian, grandson of the deified Trajan the Parthian, great-grandson of the deified Nerva, Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Augustus Pius, chief priest, with tribunician power for the 21st time, general for the 2nd time, consul for the 4th time, father of the fatherland. Publius I Adiectus, prefect of 62 districts, according to his promise, placed this with his own money and also dedicated it by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-24501795.summary: This is a public dedication of a monument by Publius I Adiectus, a prefect, honoring Emperor Antoninus Pius, likely from the mid-2nd century AD.

EDCS-24501797.translation: To Quintus Cassius Agrippianus Aelianus, a most distinguished man, consul, praetor, candidate for tribune, candidate for quaestor, moneyer, member of the board of six for the deployment of troops, curator of the public affairs of the colonies of Mactaris, Zama, and Regius.
EDCS-24501797.summary: This is a dedication honoring Quintus Cassius Agrippianus Aelianus for his various public offices, likely from Roman North Africa.

EDCS-24501798.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits: Rupilia Natalica lived for 13 years and 8 months.
EDCS-24501798.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Rupilia Natalica, recording her lifespan.

EDCS-24501800.translation: Aelius Septimius Veratianus, dutiful, lived for 40 years.

EDCS-24501802.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits: Caecilia Optata, dutiful, lived for 70 years; her bones are placed in this monument.

EDCS-24501803.summary: This epitaph records the lifespan of Caecilia Spes.

EDCS-24501814.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Flavia Secundula.

EDCS-24501816.translation: Fortunata, a devoted woman, lived for 65 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-24501816.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan and burial place of Fortunata.

EDCS-24501817.translation: To the Divine Manes, Julius V...
EDCS-24501817.summary: This is a funerary inscription fragment, likely dedicated to the Divine Manes.

EDCS-24501818.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Quintus Iulius Felix, devoted, lived for 21 years.
EDCS-24501818.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Quintus Iulius Felix, dedicated to the Divine Manes.

EDCS-24501819.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Iulius Florianus lived for 25 years.
EDCS-24501819.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Iulius Florianus, dedicated to the Divine Manes.

EDCS-24501821.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Iulia Optata, daughter of Quintus, devoted, lived for 80 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-24501821.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan and burial place of Iulia Optata, daughter of Quintus.

EDCS-24501822.summary: This is a funerary inscription fragment mentioning Lucius and his father Vindicis.

EDCS-24501823.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Nia Maior.
EDCS-24501823.summary: This is a funerary inscription fragment dedicated to the Divine Manes for Nia Maior.

EDCS-24501824.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Manius Paulinus, devoted, lived for 65 years.
EDCS-24501824.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Manius Paulinus, dedicated to the Divine Manes.

EDCS-24501825.translation: To Matuta, who lived 61 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-24501825.summary: This is a tombstone for Matuta, who lived 61 years.

EDCS-24501827.summary: This inscription records the lifespan of Munatia Fortunata, who lived 40 years.

EDCS-24501828.translation: Ingenua lived 2 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-24501828.summary: This is a tombstone for Ingenua, who lived 2 years.

EDCS-24501829.translation: Fal Fo, daughter of Namgidde, pious, lived 90 years. She is buried here, placed in purchased land from Quintus Minatius Felix, near the Pomarian boundary, and Procusio, his grandson.
EDCS-24501829.summary: This is a tombstone for Fal Fo, daughter of Namgidde, specifying her lifespan and burial location purchased from Quintus Minatius Felix.

EDCS-24501830.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Dead. Numisia Saturnina lived 25 years.
EDCS-24501830.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to the spirits of the dead for Numisia Saturnina, who lived 25 years.

EDCS-24501831.summary: This inscription records the lifespan of Quinta, who lived 35 years.

EDCS-24501832.summary: This inscription is a simple name inscription, likely for Marcus P. Rogatus.

EDCS-24501833.translation: Rufus Anobalis, pious, lived 85 years. He is buried here.

EDCS-24501834.translation: Saturnius, son of Asuris, lived 90 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-24501834.summary: This is a tombstone for Saturnius, son of Asuris, who lived 90 years.

EDCS-24501835.translation: ac Saturnina lived 25 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-24501835.summary: This is a tombstone for Saturnina, who lived 25 years.

EDCS-24501837.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Secunda, dutiful daughter of Viator, lived here.
EDCS-24501837.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a woman named Secunda, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-24501838.translation: Marcus Valerius Felicio, dutiful, lived 75 years, is buried here.
EDCS-24501838.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Marcus Valerius Felicio, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-24501840.translation: ucius is T cull lived 60 years, is buried.
EDCS-24501840.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-24501841.translation: ii, dutiful, lived 10 years, is buried. tus, dutiful, lived 10 years, is buried.
