EDCS-24502055.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Flavia Lucusta, an excellent woman, wife of Flavi Mulsutus, lived 36 years.
EDCS-24502055.summary: A funerary inscription recording the life and virtues of Flavia Lucusta, wife of Flavi Mulsutus.

EDCS-24502056.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Lududio made [this]. AI [aged?] 1 year.
EDCS-24502056.summary: A funerary inscription indicating that Lududio made the monument and recording the age of an infant named AI.

EDCS-24502057.summary: A partial funerary inscription recording the short life of Gududio.

EDCS-24502058.translation: Ilaucha, son of Itibalis, lived 33 years.
EDCS-24502058.summary: A funerary inscription recording the life of Ilaucha, son of Itibalis.

EDCS-24502059.translation: Istatan, son of Iston, is buried here.
EDCS-24502059.summary: This is a tombstone marking the burial place of Istatan, son of Iston.

EDCS-24502060.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Julius Donatus lived 15 years.
EDCS-24502060.summary: This is a tombstone recording the life and death of Julius Donatus, who died at the age of 15.

EDCS-24502061.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Laninius Fortunatus lived 51 years.
EDCS-24502061.summary: This is a tombstone recording the life and death of Laninius Fortunatus, who died at the age of 51.

EDCS-24502062.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Labinius Rogat [is buried here/lived here].
EDCS-24502062.summary: This is a tombstone recording the name of Labinius Rogat, dedicated to the spirits of the departed.

EDCS-24502063.summary: This inscription simply records the name Licinius Marianus, possibly on a tombstone or other marker.

EDCS-24502064.translation: Lucius Lollius Adiutor, son of Tironis.
EDCS-24502064.summary: This inscription records the name Lucius Lollius Adiutor, son of Tironis, likely on a tombstone or monument.

EDCS-24502065.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Micurenus Iunior lived [x] years.
EDCS-24502065.summary: This is a tombstone recording the name Micurenus Iunior, dedicated to the spirits of the departed, with an incomplete age.

EDCS-24502066.summary: This is a tombstone marking the burial place of Mustus M.

EDCS-24502067.summary: This inscription records the name Caius Musstus Restitulus, likely on a tombstone or monument.

EDCS-24502068.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Mutthunus, son of Sereni, lived 55 years, is buried here.
EDCS-24502068.summary: This is a tombstone recording the life and death of Mutthunus, son of Sereni, who died at the age of 55.

EDCS-24502069.translation: Narsus, son of Rogatus, of the Rufria tribe.
EDCS-24502069.summary: This is a funerary inscription identifying the deceased by name, father's name, and tribal affiliation, likely from the Roman Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-24502071.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the name and age at death of Aia Saturia, likely from the Roman Empire.

EDCS-24502072.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed; Securus, of the Massive clan.
EDCS-24502072.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicating the monument to the spirits of the dead and identifying the deceased, likely from the Roman Empire.

EDCS-24502073.translation: Successus lived 95 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-24502073.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the name and age at death of Successus, stating he is buried here, likely from the Roman Empire.

EDCS-24502074.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed; Thiaethus dedicated.
EDCS-24502074.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicating the monument to the spirits of the dead and indicating the dedicator, likely from the Roman Empire.

EDCS-24502075.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed; Victoria, wife of Utis.
EDCS-24502075.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicating the monument to the spirits of the dead and identifying the deceased by name and marital relationship, likely from the Roman Empire.

EDCS-24502076.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed; Tidus lived 21 years.
EDCS-24502076.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicating the monument to the spirits of the dead and recording the name and age at death of Tidus, likely from the Roman Empire.

EDCS-24502077.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the name, a character epithet, and age at death of M. Tilpius, likely from the Roman Empire.

EDCS-24502078.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed; Iaficus.
EDCS-24502078.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicating the monument to the spirits of the dead and identifying the deceased, likely from the Roman Empire.

EDCS-24502081.translation: Resting in peace, Liberatus the faithful lived 23 years and two months.
EDCS-24502081.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the name, epithets, and precise age at death of Liberatus, likely from the late Roman Empire or early Christian period.

EDCS-24502082.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Ofisia Cattula, priestess, lived 80 years.
EDCS-24502082.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Ofisia Cattula, a priestess who lived to 80 years of age.

EDCS-24502084.translation: Paulinianus lived 30 years, [his son/daughter?] lived 12 years.
EDCS-24502084.summary: This epitaph records the lifespans of at least two individuals, Paulinianus and another, likely a younger relative, who lived 12 years.

EDCS-24502086.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Albius Pullaienus Salvillus, pious, lived 63 years, lies here. Vibia Secunda [lies here too].
EDCS-24502086.summary: This is a funerary monument for Albius Pullaienus Salvillus, who lived 63 years, and Vibia Secunda.

EDCS-24502088.translation: To the Divine Manes. Secunda, wife of Barachon, lived 72 years piously, lies here.
EDCS-24502088.summary: This funerary epitaph records that Secunda, wife of Barachon, lived 72 years and is buried here.

EDCS-24502089.translation: To the Genius of the district, from the promise of the neighbourhood officials, Publius Geminius Saturninus [made this] to Publius Geminius Martialus and Critus.
EDCS-24502089.summary: This inscription records a dedication to the Genius of the district by Publius Geminius Saturninus, made to officials Publius Geminius Martialus and Critus.

EDCS-24502090.translation: Sacred to Liber Augustus. From the fullers who contributed to the building: Caius Iulius Saturninus, Lucius Lucilius Musicus, Marcus Pomponius Primulius, Caius Iulius Rogatus, Lucius Cominius Rogatus, Marcus Aquilius Victor, Publius Iulius Florus, Lucius Modius Rufus, Caius Cominius Rogatus, Caius Marius Rogatus, Caius Iulius Datus, Caius Aquilius Capito, Quintus Rasinius Saturninus, son of Gabba Maximi Galbae, [and] Servius Gallus Cordius Meridianus Saturninus. Sextus Nonius Iuvenalis, in his own name and that of his sons Noni and Luci, made a column pouring wine at his own expense, and he also dedicated it.
EDCS-24502090.summary: This inscription records a dedication of a column pouring wine to Liber Augustus, made by Sextus Nonius Iuvenalis and funded by a group of fullers, likely in the late 1st or early 2nd century CE.

EDCS-24502091.translation: Sacred to the Great Mother of the Gods, Idaea Augusta. For the safety of the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Probus Pius Felix Augustus and his entire divine family. Quintus Arellius Optatianus, a Roman knight and priest, having completed the sacred rites of the lamb and bull sacrifices, with the approval of the order of his colony of Mactaris, has been approved as chief priest, at his own expense, with Rannius Salvio, a Roman knight and pontiff, and Claudius Faustus, priests, handing over the proceedings, along with all the dendrophori and consecrated persons of both sexes. He has willingly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-24502091.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by Quintus Arellius Optatianus, a Roman knight and priest, to the Great Mother of the Gods, Idaea Augusta, for the well-being of Emperor Probus, and was approved by the local council of Mactaris.

EDCS-24502092.text_edition: \n Matri Deum Magnae Ideae Augustae sacrum pro salute Impperatorum Caessarum Cai Valeri Diocletiani Pii Felicis Augusti et Marci Aureli Valeri M[axi][miani] Pii Pii Felicis Augusti totiusque divinae domus eorum Quintus Minthonius Fortunatus sacerdos perfectis ritae sic sacris cernorum crioboli et tauroboli suffragio ordinis coloniae suae Mactaritanae comprobatus antistes sumptibus suis tradente Claudio Bono sacerdote una cum universis dendroforiis sic et sacratis utriusque sexus votum solvit libens animo\n
EDCS-24502092.translation: Sacred to the Great Mother of the Gods, Idaea Augusta. For the safety of the Emperors Caesar Gaius Valerius Diocletian Pius Felix Augustus and Marcus Aurelius Valerius Maximian Pius Pius Felix Augustus and their entire divine family. Quintus Minthonius Fortunatus, a priest, having completed the sacred rites of the lamb and bull sacrifices, with the approval of the order of his colony of Mactaris, has been approved as chief priest, at his own expense, with Claudius Bonus, priest, handing over the proceedings, along with all the dendrophori and consecrated persons of both sexes. He has willingly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-24502092.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by Quintus Minthonius Fortunatus, a priest, to the Great Mother of the Gods, Idaea Augusta, for the well-being of Emperors Diocletian and Maximian, with the approval of the council of Mactaris.

EDCS-24502095.translation: To Venus. Menophilus, slave of the public officials of Africa, freed from his obligation, willingly, as deserved.
EDCS-24502095.summary: This is a votive inscription to Venus by Menophilus, a slave associated with public officials in Africa.

EDCS-24502096.translation: Sacred to Augusta Venus, for the health and safety of the Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus, father of the fatherland, and of the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus, the first Caesar, and of Julia Domna, mother of the Augusti, and of the camps, and of the fatherland. Terentia Spra, priestess, freed from her obligation, willingly, as deserved.
EDCS-24502096.summary: This is a votive inscription to Augusta Venus, made by the priestess Terentia Spra for the health and safety of Emperor Septimius Severus, his son Caracalla, and Julia Domna.

EDCS-24502098.translation: Through Cardelus the new priest, for the songs and gatherings of the temple.
EDCS-24502098.summary: This inscription records a dedication by a new priest, Cardelus, related to temple rituals of singing and gathering.

EDCS-24502105.translation: Arruntia Sperata, daughter of a veteran, made this monument of stone; her father Arruntius made it, as deserved. May the earth lie lightly on you, as I hoped you would do for me. She lived 28 years, lies here.
EDCS-24502105.summary: This funerary epitaph records Arruntia Sperata, daughter of a veteran, who lived 28 years, and mentions her father Arruntius's role in her burial.

EDCS-24502106.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the life span of Aufidius Saturninus, a veteran.

EDCS-24502107.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Lucius Antonius Saturninus, priest of Diana, lived 70 years.
EDCS-24502107.summary: This funerary inscription commemorates Lucius Antonius Saturninus, a priest of Diana, and records his age.

EDCS-24502108.translation: To Licinia Antulla, daughter of Quintus, wife of Marcus Minthonius Tertullus, by decree of the decurions, at public expense.
EDCS-24502108.summary: This is a dedication of a monument or tomb to Licinia Antulla, funded by public money as decided by the local council.

EDCS-24502109.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. His son, Papirius Tiprunitanus, prefect for administering justice in place of the duumvirs, [lived] 32 years. His wife, Pomponia Saturnina, daughter of Lucius, dutiful, lived 52 years.
EDCS-24502109.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Papirius Tiprunitanus, a judicial official, and his wife Pomponia Saturnina, recording their ages.

EDCS-24502110.translation: Quintus Vibius Salaga, son of Caius, with all expenses contributed, erected this table for me and mine.
EDCS-24502110.summary: This dedication records Quintus Vibius Salaga paying for the construction of a funerary table for himself and his family.

EDCS-24502115.translation: Caius Gessius Florus, son of Caius, from Abella, lived 49 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-24502115.summary: This funerary epitaph records the life span and burial place of Caius Gessius Florus from Abella.

EDCS-24502116.translation: Sobos, son of Sernus, from Mididitas, lived 63 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-24502116.summary: This funerary epitaph records the life span and burial place of Sobos from Mididitas.

EDCS-24502117.translation: Lived 45 years. Caius Agr Dia arranged for this to be made at his own expense.
EDCS-24502117.summary: This inscription records that Caius Agr Dia paid for a monument or tomb to be constructed for someone who lived 45 years.

EDCS-24502118.translation: Aucharia Quinta, dutiful daughter of Caius, lived [many] years.
EDCS-24502118.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary epitaph for Aucharia Quinta, recording her name and dutiful nature.

EDCS-24502119.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Antistius Marinus lived 43 years and 6 months.
EDCS-24502119.summary: This funerary inscription commemorates Antistius Marinus and records his age at death.

EDCS-24502120.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Antonius Cududus lived 27 years.
EDCS-24502120.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Antonius Cududus, who died at the age of 27.

EDCS-24502121.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Maior, 80 years. Lucius Antonius Marcellus lived 55 years.
EDCS-24502121.summary: This funerary epitaph records the ages of Maior (80) and Lucius Antonius Marcellus (55).

EDCS-24502122.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Lucius Antonius Maximus.
EDCS-24502122.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Antonius Maximus.

EDCS-24502123.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Lucius Antonius Narizal lived 95 years. Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Octavia Rufina lived 77 years.
EDCS-24502123.summary: This funerary epitaph records the ages of Lucius Antonius Narizal (95) and Octavia Rufina (77).

EDCS-24502124.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Antonia Maxima lived 27 years and 3 months.
EDCS-24502124.summary: This funerary epitaph records the age of Antonia Maxima, who died at 27 years and 3 months.

EDCS-24502125.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Antonia Saturnina, dutiful, lived 18 years.
EDCS-24502125.summary: This funerary epitaph records the age of Antonia Saturnina, who died at 18 years.

EDCS-24502126.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Antonia Celin, dutiful, lived 10 years and 2 months.
EDCS-24502126.summary: This funerary epitaph records the age of Antonia Celin, who died at 10 years and 2 months.

EDCS-24502127.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. For Antulla, daughter of Minthonia Pastor, lived 30 years. For Iulia Aufida, daughter of Quintus Aufidius, lived 11 years.
EDCS-24502127.summary: This funerary epitaph records the deaths of Antulla (daughter of Minthonia Pastor, 30 years old) and Iulia Aufida (daughter of Quintus Aufidius, 11 years old).

EDCS-24502128.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Apronia Prima.

EDCS-24502130.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Aristobolus lived [---] years.
EDCS-24502130.summary: This funerary epitaph records the name Aristobolus, but the age is incomplete.

EDCS-24502131.translation: Marcus Aufidius Rogatus, dutiful, lived 27 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-24502131.summary: This is a tombstone for Marcus Aufidius Rogatus, who died at the age of 27.

EDCS-24502132.translation: Aufidia Silvana lived [?] years. Marau Chubudis, son, lived 82 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-24502132.summary: This tombstone records the life and death of Marau Chubudis, who lived to be 82, and also mentions Aufidia Silvana.

EDCS-24502133.translation: Aufidius Iustus, dutiful, lived 80 years. Tu lived 85 years.
EDCS-24502133.summary: This tombstone records the lives of two individuals, Aufidius Iustus and Tu, who lived to be 80 and 85 years old, respectively.

EDCS-24502134.translation: Aula Zdrumae Amicaris, dutiful, lived 70 years.
EDCS-24502134.summary: This is a tombstone for Aula Zdrumae Amicaris, who lived to be 70 years old.

EDCS-24502135.translation: Marcus Bennius, son of Extricatus, lived 9 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-24502135.summary: This tombstone records the death of Marcus Bennius, son of Extricatus, at the age of 9.

EDCS-24502136.translation: Cecilia Soluta, dutiful, daughter of Quinctus, lived 65 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-24502136.summary: This tombstone records the death of Cecilia Soluta, daughter of Quinctus, at the age of 65.

EDCS-24502137.translation: Caius Luscelus, dutiful, lived 55 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-24502137.summary: This tombstone records the death of Caius Luscelus at the age of 55.

EDCS-24502138.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Quinto Camellio Optato Fausto lived 57 years, and Flavia Primae lived 97 years. To their most dutiful parents, Camelli Faustus and Caeler made this.
EDCS-24502138.summary: This tombstone was erected by Camelli Faustus and Caeler to honor their parents, Quinto Camellio Optato Fausto (died at 57) and Flavia Primae (died at 97).

EDCS-24502139.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Casus Onoratus lived 18 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-24502139.summary: This tombstone records the death of Casus Onoratus at the age of 18.

EDCS-24502140.translation: Cassia Potita, daughter of Caius, lived 25 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-24502140.summary: This tombstone records the death of Cassia Potita, daughter of Caius, at the age of 25.

EDCS-24502141.translation: Cassia Rogata lived piously for 80 years, she is placed here. Tiberius Claudius Faustus lived piously for 91 years, he is placed here.
EDCS-24502141.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the ages of Cassia Rogata and Tiberius Claudius Faustus.

EDCS-24502142.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the age of Colr Celsus.

EDCS-24502143.translation: Chubud, son of Masmaconis, lived piously for 75 years, he is placed here.
EDCS-24502143.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the age of Chubud, son of Masmaconis.

EDCS-24502144.translation: Claudia Tertulla lived piously for 14 years, she is placed here.
EDCS-24502144.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the age of Claudia Tertulla.

EDCS-24502145.translation: Lucius Coelius lived piously for 65 years, he is placed here.
EDCS-24502145.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the age of Lucius Coelius.

EDCS-24502146.translation: Cornelius lived piously for 25 years, he is placed here.
EDCS-24502146.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the age of Cornelius.

EDCS-24502149.translation: Cutia Tertulla lived piously for 35 years, she is placed here.
EDCS-24502149.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the age of Cutia Tertulla.

EDCS-24502150.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the burial of Titus Egnatius.

EDCS-24502151.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Egnatius Birzilianus lived for 30 years.
EDCS-24502151.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the age of Lucius Egnatius Birzilianus.

EDCS-24502152.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus Egnatius Optatus, son of Quintus Egnatius Rogatus, lived for 30 years, he is placed here.
EDCS-24502152.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the age of Quintus Egnatius Optatus, son of Quintus Egnatius Rogatus.

EDCS-24502153.translation: Lucius, son of Victor, lived 65 years. [duration of life]
EDCS-24502153.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespan of Lucius.

EDCS-24502154.translation: Felix lived 60 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-24502154.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespan and burial of Felix.

EDCS-24502155.translation: Felix, son of Saturninus, lived 3 years.
EDCS-24502155.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespan of a child named Felix.

EDCS-24502156.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Flavius Adventus, pious, lived 65 years. Minucia Amanda, his wife, with her own money placed this small altar on her own land for herself and her husband. She is buried here.
EDCS-24502156.summary: This funerary inscription records the lives of Flavius Adventus and his wife Minucia Amanda, who erected a monument for them.

EDCS-24502157.translation: Fortunata, wife of Phamus, lived 50 years. She made [this] for her husband. She is buried here.
EDCS-24502157.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespan of Fortunata and indicates she erected the monument for her husband.

EDCS-24502159.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespan of Fortunata.

EDCS-24502160.translation: Gargilia Saturnina, pious, lived 96 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-24502160.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespan and burial of Gargilia Saturnina.

EDCS-24502161.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Geminius Felix lived 73 years.
EDCS-24502161.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespan of Lucius Geminius Felix.

EDCS-24502162.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Grania Pa[ter]...
EDCS-24502162.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription dedicated to the departed spirits, likely for Grania Pa[ter...].

EDCS-24502164.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Ianuaria, daughter of Fortunatus, pious, lived 35 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-24502164.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespan and burial of Ianuaria, daughter of Fortunatus.

EDCS-24502165.translation: Quintus Instius Maca lived for 70 years.
EDCS-24502165.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Quintus Instius Maca.

EDCS-24502166.translation: Caius Iulius Felicianus lived for 2 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-24502166.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the short lifespan and burial of Caius Iulius Felicianus.

EDCS-24502167.translation: Iulius Felix Sabinus Maximus Victoricus made this monument with his own funds for himself and his family.
EDCS-24502167.summary: This funerary monument was constructed by Iulius Felix Sabinus Maximus Victoricus for himself and his family.

EDCS-24502168.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Dead. Iulius Maximus Magnianus lived piously for 48 years, 5 months, and 20 days; he is buried here.
EDCS-24502168.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan and burial of Iulius Maximus Magnianus, dedicated to the Spirits of the Dead.

EDCS-24502169.translation: Caius Iulius Optatus lived for 50 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-24502169.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan and burial of Caius Iulius Optatus.

EDCS-24502170.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Dead. Caius Iulius Saturninus Marianus lived for 75 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-24502170.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan and burial of Caius Iulius Saturninus Marianus, dedicated to the Spirits of the Dead.

EDCS-24502171.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Dead. Iulius Secundianus lived for 60 years; he is buried here. Sacred to the Spirits of the Dead. M.
EDCS-24502171.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan and burial of Iulius Secundianus, with a repeated dedication to the Spirits of the Dead.

EDCS-24502172.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Dead. Iulius SyriRus Tittalus lived for 15 years, 1 month, and 11 days.
EDCS-24502172.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan of Iulius SyriRus Tittalus, dedicated to the Spirits of the Dead.

EDCS-24502174.translation: Iulia, daughter of Lucius, pious Aebutia, is buried here.
EDCS-24502174.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the burial of Iulia, daughter of Lucius.

EDCS-24502175.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Dead. Iulia Florida lived for 27 years.
EDCS-24502175.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan of Iulia Florida, dedicated to the Spirits of the Dead.

EDCS-24502176.translation: Dedicated to the spirits of the underworld. Iulia Maxima, dutiful, lived for 52 years.
EDCS-24502176.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Iulia Maxima.

EDCS-24502177.translation: Dedicated to the spirits of the underworld. Quintus Licinius Aurentius Victorinus, a junior prior, dutiful and pious, lived for 49 years, 10 months, and 3 days.
EDCS-24502177.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan and name of Quintus Licinius Aurentius Victorinus, noting his rank as 'junior prior'.

EDCS-24502179.translation: Dedicated to the spirits of the underworld. Caius Licinius Felix, son of Caius and Horatia, dutiful, lived for 77 years; he is buried here. Staberia Saturnina, daughter of Lucius, dutiful, lived for 70 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-24502179.summary: A double funerary epitaph recording the lifespans and burial places of Caius Licinius Felix and Staberia Saturnina.

EDCS-24502180.translation: Dedicated to the spirits of the underworld. Lucilius Fortunatus lived for 50 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-24502180.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan and burial place of Lucilius Fortunatus.

EDCS-24502181.translation: Dedicated to the spirits of the underworld. M. Honoratus, dutiful, lived for 70 years.
EDCS-24502181.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of M. Honoratus.

EDCS-24502182.translation: Dedicated to the spirits of the underworld. Lucius Mius Datianus lived for 17 years.
EDCS-24502182.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Lucius Mius Datianus.

EDCS-24502183.summary: An incomplete funerary epitaph mentioning Quintus Magnius and his lifespan.

EDCS-24502184.translation: Dedicated to the spirits of the underworld. Caius Manlius Homullinus lived for... Saturninus lived for... and to his brother.
EDCS-24502184.summary: An incomplete funerary epitaph mentioning Caius Manlius Homullinus and Saturninus, possibly related.

EDCS-24502185.summary: A fragmentary inscription likely identifying Marcella as the daughter of Saturus.

EDCS-24502186.translation: Dedicated to the spirits of the underworld. Marsidius Fortunatus lived for 70 years.
EDCS-24502186.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Marsidius Fortunatus.

EDCS-24502187.translation: Masculus lived 73 years, he is buried here. Sacred to the Divine Shades. Iulia Faustina lived 10 years, she is buried here.
EDCS-24502187.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the ages and burial of two individuals, Masculus and Iulia Faustina, under the dedication to the Divine Shades.

EDCS-24502188.translation: Maximus, son of Caius, lived 40 years, he is buried here.
EDCS-24502188.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the age and burial of Maximus, son of Caius.

EDCS-24502189.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Modia Montana the dutiful lived 72 years and 6 months.
EDCS-24502189.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated to the Divine Shades, recording the age of Modia Montana.

EDCS-24502190.translation: Monius Saturninus, son of Lucius, [lived] 3 years, he is buried here.
EDCS-24502190.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the age and burial of Monius Saturninus, son of Lucius.

EDCS-24502191.translation: Narsidius Murracius lived dutifully 25 years, he is buried here.
EDCS-24502191.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the age and burial of Narsidius Murracius.

EDCS-24502192.translation: Lucius Nunnius Secundus, son of Caius, is buried here.
EDCS-24502192.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the burial of Lucius Nunnius Secundus, son of Caius.

EDCS-24502193.translation: Nunnia Prima, daughter of Lucius, is buried here.
EDCS-24502193.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the burial of Nunnia Prima, daughter of Lucius.

EDCS-24502194.translation: Octavia Faustina lived 75 years, she is buried here.
EDCS-24502194.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the age and burial of Octavia Faustina.

EDCS-24502195.translation: Octavia Gafiuta, daughter of Marcus, the dutiful, lived 15 years, she is buried here.
EDCS-24502195.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the age and burial of Octavia Gafiuta, daughter of Marcus.

EDCS-24502196.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Helius [erected this] for Orfiae Statiae, his dearest companion in barracks, who lived 20 years, she is buried here.
EDCS-24502196.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated to the Divine Shades, recording the burial of Orfiae Statiae and her age, set up by her companion Helius.

EDCS-24502197.translation: Lucius Paci Fortunatus lived 75 years and is buried here. Insteia Optata, daughter of Lucius, devoted, lived 51 years and is buried here.
EDCS-24502197.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lives and burial of Lucius Paci Fortunatus and Insteia Optata.

EDCS-24502199.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Pomponia Romana, devoted, lived 35 years and is buried here. Marcus Tadius Rogatus lived 70 years. Iulia Saturnina, devoted, lived 11 years and is buried here. Lucius Pomponius Donatus placed this for his most devoted parents to preserve their memory.
EDCS-24502199.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Lucius Pomponius Donatus for his parents, Marcus Tadius Rogatus and Pomponia Romana, and a relative, Iulia Saturnina.

EDCS-24502200.translation: Possessor, son of Lucius, of the Quirina tribe, devoted.
EDCS-24502200.summary: This fragmentary inscription appears to record the name, parentage, tribe, and a virtue (devoted) of a person named Possessor.

EDCS-24502201.translation: Quarta, daughter of Babbalis, devoted, lived 85 years and is buried here.
EDCS-24502201.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the life and burial of Quarta, daughter of Babbalis.

EDCS-24502202.translation: Quinta Quintia, devoted, lived 30 years. Gemella, daughter, 6 years. Buried here.
EDCS-24502202.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lives and burial of Quinta Quintia and her daughter Gemella.

EDCS-24502203.translation: Marcus Quintius Florus, son of Titus, of the Galeria tribe, devoted, lived 40 years and is buried here.
EDCS-24502203.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the life and burial of Marcus Quintius Florus.

EDCS-24502204.translation: Quintia Tertulla, daughter of Publius, devoted, lived 25 years and is buried here.
EDCS-24502204.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the life and burial of Quintia Tertulla.

EDCS-24502205.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Ramius Cicero lived 64 years. Ramius Victor placed this for his father. May the earth lie lightly on you.
EDCS-24502205.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Ramius Victor for his father, Ramius Cicero, with a standard epitaph wish.

EDCS-24502206.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Rocius Pullus lived 91 years and 11 months.
EDCS-24502206.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Rocius Pullus.

EDCS-24502207.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Romana Matussenia, devoted, lived 25 years and is buried here.
EDCS-24502207.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the life and burial of Romana Matussenia.

EDCS-24502208.translation: Selicia Saturnina, daughter of Publius, lived 50 years and is buried here. Vestali lived 71 years and is buried here. 15 years and is buried here. Lived here and buried here. Marcus Gargilius Fortunatus made this for his most dutiful parents, his brother, his wife, himself, his wife, his sons and their descendants with his own money and land.
EDCS-24502208.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Marcus Gargilius Fortunatus for his family, including Selicia Saturnina and Vestali, and himself.

EDCS-24502209.translation: Saturninus Martialis, son, dutiful, lived 25 years.
EDCS-24502209.summary: This is a tombstone recording the death of Saturninus Martialis at the age of 25.

EDCS-24502210.translation: Saturninus, son of Sextus, dutiful, lived 75 years and is buried here. Non, dutiful daughter, lived 62 years.
EDCS-24502210.summary: This tombstone records the burial of Saturninus, son of Sextus, and his daughter Non.

EDCS-24502211.summary: This is a tombstone recording the death of Saturnina at the age of 10.

EDCS-24502212.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Gaius Selicius Rogatus lived 13 years and is buried here.
EDCS-24502212.summary: This is a tombstone recording the burial of Gaius Selicius Rogatus at the age of 13.

EDCS-24502213.translation: Sempronia Maxima, daughter of Marcus, lived 35 years and is buried here.
EDCS-24502213.summary: This is a tombstone recording the burial of Sempronia Maxima at the age of 35.

EDCS-24502214.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Serotina is buried here for her merits.
EDCS-24502214.summary: This funerary inscription honors Serotina for her merits.

EDCS-24502215.translation: Gnaeus Servilius Advena, dutiful, lived 80 years. Gnaeus Servilius Romanus, dutiful, lived 50 years and is buried here.
EDCS-24502215.summary: This tombstone records the lives and burials of Gnaeus Servilius Advena and Gnaeus Servilius Romanus.

EDCS-24502216.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Sextia Fortunata, daughter of Caius, dutiful, is buried here.
EDCS-24502216.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Sextia Fortunata.

EDCS-24502217.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. For Sextilia Florentilla, because of her merits.
EDCS-24502217.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to Sextilia Florentilla in recognition of her merits.

EDCS-24502218.translation: Lucius Staberius, son of Quintus, of the Arnensis tribe, pious, lived, is buried here.
EDCS-24502218.summary: This is a tombstone for Lucius Staberius, son of Quintus, indicating his name, tribal affiliation, pietas, and that he is buried here.

EDCS-24502219.translation: Saturnius Staberius, son of Lucius, lived 27 years, is buried here.
EDCS-24502219.summary: This is a tombstone for Saturnius Staberius, son of Lucius, stating his age at death and burial location.

EDCS-24502220.translation: Titus Staberius, son of Lucius, lived 25 years, is buried here.
EDCS-24502220.summary: This is a tombstone for Titus Staberius, son of Lucius, stating his age at death and burial location.

EDCS-24502221.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Terentia Prima, daughter of Marcus, of the Papiria tribe, pious, lived 25 years, is buried here. Marcus Iulius Vitalis, of the Papiria tribe, pious, lived 98 years and 10 months.
EDCS-24502221.summary: This inscription records the burial of Terentia Prima and Marcus Iulius Vitalis, likely a family tomb, noting their pietas and ages at death.

EDCS-24502222.translation: Toneia Rogata, daughter of Lucius, pious, lived 80 years, is buried here.
EDCS-24502222.summary: This is a tombstone for Toneia Rogata, daughter of Lucius, noting her pietas, age at death, and burial location.

EDCS-24502223.translation: Caius Velleius Theodotus lived 75 years, is buried here.
EDCS-24502223.summary: This is a tombstone for Caius Velleius Theodotus, stating his age at death and burial location.

EDCS-24502224.translation: Velleia Secunda, called Asella, daughter of Caius, of the Velleia family, pious, lived 26 years, is buried here.
EDCS-24502224.summary: This is a tombstone for Velleia Secunda, also known as Asella, daughter of Caius, noting her pietas, age at death, and burial location.

EDCS-24502225.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Vetulenius Secundianus lived 30 years.
EDCS-24502225.summary: This inscription is dedicated to the departed spirits and records that Lucius Vetulenius Secundianus lived for 30 years, likely a funerary dedication.

EDCS-24502226.translation: Victoria, daughter of Bassus, is buried here.
EDCS-24502226.summary: This is a tombstone for Victoria, daughter of Bassus, indicating her burial location.

EDCS-24502227.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcus Ulpius Grilus lived 6 years, is buried here.
EDCS-24502227.summary: This inscription, dedicated to the departed spirits, records the burial of the young Marcus Ulpius Grilus, who died at the age of 6.

EDCS-24502228.translation: Ulpia Victoria, dutiful, lived 60 years, is buried here. Marcus Ulpius Pirric, dutiful, lived 70 years, is buried here. Lucius Blossius Luperci, for the honour of the monument, gave the place from his own funds and set it up for them as children.
EDCS-24502228.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Ulpia Victoria and Marcus Ulpius Pirric, with a statement about Lucius Blossius Luperci dedicating land for their monument.

EDCS-24502229.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Umbrius Fortunatus lived 50 years.
EDCS-24502229.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Umbrius Fortunatus.

EDCS-24502230.translation: Donata, freedwoman of Usumia Quintus, dutiful, lived 30 years, is buried here.
EDCS-24502230.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan and burial of Donata, a freedwoman.

EDCS-24502233.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Annonia lived 18 years and 23 days.
EDCS-24502233.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Annonia.

EDCS-24502242.summary: This is a very brief funerary epitaph identifying Oreius as a freedman of Caius.

EDCS-24502256.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of an individual identified only by a partial name.

EDCS-24502261.translation: Table of the martyrs Saint Januarius and Saint Felix.
EDCS-24502261.summary: This inscription refers to a table associated with the martyrs Saint Januarius and Saint Felix, likely in a Christian context.

EDCS-24502262.translation: Faustinus, priest, lived 34 years in the diaconate and 2 years and 6 months in the presbyterate.
EDCS-24502262.summary: This epitaph records the service duration of Faustinus, a priest, in both diaconate and presbyterate roles.

EDCS-24502263.translation: Iobianus, priest, lived 35 years in the presbyterate.
EDCS-24502263.summary: This epitaph records the service duration of Iobianus, a priest, in the presbyterate.

EDCS-24502264.translation: Abeddeus and Maximus, his sons, lived in peace, innocent. Sacred to the Divine Shades. Aurelia Victoriola lived in peace 50 years, 7 days, and 9 hours.
EDCS-24502264.summary: This is a dual funerary epitaph for Abeddeus, Maximus, and Aurelia Victoriola, noting their peaceful and innocent lives.

EDCS-24502265.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Badumas lived eight months less some days, in peace.
EDCS-24502265.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the short lifespan of Badumas.

EDCS-24502266.translation: Fidelis Bonifatia lived sixteen years, more or less, in peace.
EDCS-24502266.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Fidelis Bonifatia, likely from the Roman Imperial period or Late Antiquity.

EDCS-24502267.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Bonifatia lived seventy years and five months.
EDCS-24502267.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Bonifatia, likely from the Roman Imperial period or Late Antiquity.

EDCS-24502268.translation: Citeus lived seventy years, two months, and two days, in peace. Sacred to the Divine Manes.
EDCS-24502268.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Citeus, likely from the Roman Imperial period or Late Antiquity.

EDCS-24502269.translation: Claudius Nutricosus lived two years, six months, and twenty-two days, in peace.
EDCS-24502269.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Claudius Nutricosus, likely from the Roman Imperial period or Late Antiquity.

EDCS-24502270.summary: This is a very brief inscription, possibly an epitaph or a dedication, for Fidelis Egiptia.

EDCS-24600712.summary: This inscription records Occius fulfilling a vow, likely a votive offering.

EDCS-24600714.summary: This inscription identifies Quintus as a priest and son of Pom, possibly with an indication of his age (LII).

EDCS-24600715.translation: Pontienus Samardacus, priest, willingly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-24600715.summary: This inscription records Pontienus Samardacus, a priest, fulfilling a vow, likely a votive offering.

EDCS-24600716.translation: Sacred to Saturnus Augustus. Lucius Pontius Faustinus, priest, willingly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-24600716.summary: This inscription records Lucius Pontius Faustinus, a priest, dedicating something to Saturnus Augustus and fulfilling his vow.

EDCS-24600717.translation: Sacred to Augustus Saturn. Caius Popilius Vitalis willingly paid his vow.
EDCS-24600717.summary: This votive inscription records the payment of a vow to the deified emperor Saturn by Caius Popilius Vitalis.

EDCS-24600720.summary: This is a very brief inscription, likely indicating a dedication or belonging to Saturn, attributed to Quietus.

EDCS-24600725.translation: Sacred to Augustus Saturn Balcaranensis. Quintus Sallustius Felix, priest, made this in fulfillment of a vow according to a dream, willingly.
EDCS-24600725.summary: This inscription records a votive offering made by Quintus Sallustius Felix, a priest, to the local deity Saturn Balcaranensis, inspired by a dream.

EDCS-24600737.summary: This is a simple dedication to the local god Saturn Balcaranensis.

EDCS-24600738.translation: Sacred to Augustus Saturn Balcaranensis. Priest.
EDCS-24600738.summary: This inscription identifies a priest who dedicated something to Augustus Saturn Balcaranensis.

EDCS-24600741.summary: This is a concise dedication to the local deity Saturn Balcaranensis.

EDCS-24600742.summary: This is a concise dedication to the local deity Saturn Balcaranensis.

EDCS-24700291.translation: Faustus, son of Asprenas, of the tribe Mitilci, lived 75 years.
EDCS-24700291.summary: This epitaph records the name, parentage, tribal affiliation, and age at death of Faustus.

EDCS-24700292.summary: This is a Greek epitaph indicating the burial place of Apollinaris and Herodo.

EDCS-24700293.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely a dedication or honorific, to Lucius Gabinius Primigenius Labonius.

EDCS-24700294.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Rogatula, devout, lived 17 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-24700294.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the life and burial of Rogatula, who died at age 17, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24700295.text_edition: \n Karthagini Augustae sacrum ex testamento Quinti Aproni Quinti filii Arnensi Vitalis honestae memoriae viri qui rei publicae Uchitanorum maiorum at sic statuam milia et in epulationem sui HS II milia ndam adfectionem amplificationem HMIL epulationis concessit et ex HS V milibus fieri curavit Caius Apronius Extricatus ad exornandam munificentiam fratris basem cum impensa perferendae et constituendae statuae suo sumptu et cura posuit donum dedit\n
EDCS-24700295.translation: Sacred to Carthage Augusta. From the will of Quintus Apronius Vitalis, son of Quintus, of the Arnensian tribe, a man of honorable memory, who granted 2,000 sesterces for a statue and 2,000 sesterces for a banquet for himself for the public affairs of the people of Uchita. Caius Apronius Extricatus, to adorn the generosity of his brother, erected the base for the statue and its expenses at his own expense and care, and presented it as a gift.
EDCS-24700295.summary: This inscription records a posthumous dedication by Quintus Apronius Vitalis to Carthage Augusta, with his brother Caius Apronius Extricatus completing the monument and statue base.

EDCS-24700297.text_edition: \n Saturno Augusto pro salute Imperatoris Nervae Quintus Urvinius Quinti libertus Callistus templum a solo donum dedit pecunia publica fecit\n
EDCS-24700297.translation: To Saturn Augustus. For the safety of the Emperor Nerva. Quintus Urvinius Callistus, freedman of Quintus, dedicated a temple from the ground up; he also constructed it with public funds.
EDCS-24700297.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a temple to Saturn Augustus by Quintus Urvinius Callistus, freedman of Quintus, for the safety of Emperor Nerva, built with public funds.

EDCS-24700300.text_edition: \n Victoriae Parthicae Britannicae Germanicae maximae Augustae Imperatoris Caesaris divi Septimi Severi Pii Arabici Adiabenici Parthici maximi Britannici maximi fili divi Marci Antonini Pii Germanici Sarmatici nepotis divi Antonini Pii pronepotis Marci Aureli Severi Antonini Pii Felicis Augusti Parthici maximi Britannici maximi Germanici maximi pontificis maximi tribuniciae potestatis XVII imperatoris II consulis IIII patris patriae pecunia publica Uchitanorum maiorum decreto decurionum\n
EDCS-24700300.translation: To Victoria Parthica Britannica Germanica Maxima Augusta, daughter of Emperor Caesar divus Septimius Severus Pius Arabicus Adiabenicus Parthicus Maximus Britannicus Maximus, granddaughter of divus Marcus Antoninus Pius Germanicus Sarmaticus, great-granddaughter of divus Antoninus Pius, great-great-granddaughter of Marcus Aurelius Severus Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus Parthicus Maximus Britannicus Maximus Germanicus Maximus, Pontifex Maximus, with tribunician power for the 17th time, Imperator for the 2nd time, Consul for the 4th time, Father of the Country. Erected with public funds by decree of the decurions of the people of Uchita.
EDCS-24700300.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Victoria Augusta, commemorating military victories under Emperor Caracalla, and was funded by the people of Uchita.

EDCS-24700303.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus, Pontifex Maximus, with tribunician power for the 22nd time, Armenian, Mede, Parthicus Maximus, Imperator for the 5th time, Consul for the 3rd time, Father of the Country, son of divus Antoninus, grandson of divus Hadrianus, great-grandson of divus Traianus Parthicus, great-great-grandson of divus Nerva.
EDCS-24700303.summary: This is a dedication to Emperor Caracalla, listing his numerous titles and lineage, likely dating to his 22nd year of tribunician power.

EDCS-24700305.translation: To the Emperor Caesar, son of divus Antoninus, brother of divus Verus Parthicus Maximus, grandson of divus Hadrianus, great-grandson of divus Traianus Parthicus, great-great-grandson of divus Nerva, Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus Germanicus Sarmaticus, Pontifex Maximus, with tribunician power for the 31st time, Imperator for the 8th time, Consul for the 3rd time, Father of the Country. Fortunatus, by virtue of his many offices, [at his own expense]...
EDCS-24700305.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Emperor Caracalla, listing his titles and tribunician power, with a partial mention of Fortunatus and his extensive magisterial duties.

EDCS-24700308.translation: [For the safety(?)] of the Emperor Caesar Lucius Aurelius Commodus Augustus Germanicus Sarmaticus, Pontifex Maximus, with tribunician power for the 4th time, Imperator for the 4th time, Consul for the 2nd time, Father of the Country. The public administration of the people of Uchita Maiora made it at its own expense and dedicated it by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-24700308.summary: This inscription records a dedication, likely for the safety of Emperor Commodus, erected by the public administration of Uchita Maiora at their own expense.

EDCS-24700309.translation: To Emperor Caesar Lucius Aurelius Commodus Augustus Germanicus Sarmaticus, Pontifex Maximus, with tribunician power for the 4th time, Imperator for the 4th time, Consul for the 2nd time, Father of the Country. The public administration of Uchita Maiora made it at its own expense and dedicated it by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-24700309.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Emperor Commodus, listing his titles and tribunician power, erected by the public administration of Uchita Maiora.

EDCS-24700310.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari Lucio Septimio Severo Pio Pert<i=E>naci Augusto Parthico Arabico Parthico Adiabenico tribunicia potestate V imperatori VIIII consuli II patri patriae divi Marci filio divi Commodi fratri divi Antonini nepoti divi Hadriani pronepoti divi Traiani abnepoti divi Nervae adnepoti res publica Uchitanorum maiorum pecunia publica posuit in quam rem Caius Lucilius Cai filius Athenaeus sacerdos Cereris coloniae Iuliae Karthaginis anni CCXXXV flamen perpetuus depensis in curam supra scriptam quam ipse gessit HS XII milibus nummum summae suae honorariae et amplius pecunia publica erogata basem cum ornamentis suis sua pecunia fecit et epulo decurionibus dato dedicavit decreto decurionum \n
EDCS-24700310.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus Parthicus Arabicus Parthicus Adiabenicus, with tribunician power for the 5th time, Imperator for the 9th time, Consul for the 2nd time, Father of the Country, son of divus Marcus, brother of divus Commodus, grandson of divus Antoninus, great-grandson of divus Hadrianus, great-great-grandson of divus Traianus, great-great-great-grandson of divus Nerva. The public administration of the people of Uchita Maiora placed it with public funds. Caius Lucilius Athenaeus, son of Caius, priest of Ceres of the colony of Iulia Karthago in the year 235, perpetual flamen, contributed 12,000 sesterces from his own funds for the aforementioned care which he himself managed, in addition to public funds, and made the base with its ornaments at his own expense and dedicated it after providing a banquet for the decurions, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-24700310.summary: This inscription records the erection of a monument to Emperor Septimius Severus by the people of Uchita Maiora, with significant personal contributions from Caius Lucilius Athenaeus, a local priest and flamen.

EDCS-24700311.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Arabicus Adiabenicus Augustus, father of the fatherland, pontiff, maximum, holding tribunician power for the 5th time, imperator for the 8th time, consul for the 2nd time, son of the deified Marcus Antoninus Pius Germanicus Saramaticus, brother of the deified Commodus, grandson of the deified Antoninus Pius, great-grandson of the deified Hadrian, and great-great-grandson of the deified Trajan Parthicus, and great-great-great-grandson of the deified Nerva, by decree of the decurions, at public expense.
EDCS-24700311.summary: This is a dedication to Emperor Septimius Severus, likely on a public building or monument, as indicated by the phrase 'by decree of the decurions, at public expense'.

EDCS-24700312.translation: To Julia Domna Augusta, mother of the camps, wife of the Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Arabicus Adiabenicus Augustus, by decree of the decurions, at public expense.
EDCS-24700312.summary: This is a dedication to Julia Domna, wife of Septimius Severus, likely on a public building or monument, as indicated by the phrase 'by decree of the decurions, at public expense'.

EDCS-24700314.translation: To Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Caesar, destined Emperor, son of the Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Arabicus Adiabenicus Augustus, father of the fatherland, by decree of the decurions, at public expense.
EDCS-24700314.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Marcus Aurelius Antoninus (Caracalla), son of Septimius Severus, likely on a public building or monument, as indicated by the phrase 'by decree of the decurions, at public expense'.

EDCS-24700315.translation: To Publius Septimius Geta, most noble Caesar, brother of Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus, Father of the Fatherland, Prince of Youth, by decree of the decurions, with public money.
EDCS-24700315.summary: A dedication honoring Publius Septimius Geta, brother of Caracalla, likely for a public monument erected by local officials.

EDCS-24700319.translation: Under the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Claudius Pius Felix Augustus.
EDCS-24700319.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription indicating a date during the reign of Emperor Claudius Gothicus.

EDCS-24700324.translation: To Valeria, daughter of Publius Marianilla, most illustrious woman, from the Uchitani Maiores, for her outstanding generosity, by decree of the decurions, with public money.
EDCS-24700324.summary: A dedication honoring Valeria Marianilla for her generosity, erected by the Uchitani Maiores through a public decree, likely in the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24700328.translation: After he had asked for the base to be made at his own expense, also for the memory of the munificence of his household, with which he had adorned the Genius of the Fatherland with statues and given a banquet three times, Pullaienus Bassus decreed a statue for himself, his father, his conjugal partner, and his children, so that he might satisfy the desires of the citizens; content with the fourth banquet given by himself, he placed and also dedicated a statue at his own expense.
EDCS-24700328.summary: A lengthy inscription detailing the civic benefactions of Pullaienus Bassus, who funded statues and banquets to honor his family and the community, likely in the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24700333.translation: buried 25th, deposited 3 days before the Kalends of May, faithful in peace, lived 40 years, deposited Decembres, cleric in peace, lived 30 years, deposited 7 days before the Ides of March.
EDCS-24700333.summary: A fragmentary epitaph listing individuals, likely clergy, buried with their ages and dates of deposition, indicating a Christian context from the Late Roman or Byzantine period.

EDCS-24700334.summary: A very brief inscription identifying someone as the son of Sarchus, possibly a funerary or ownership marker.

EDCS-24700335.summary: A simple epitaph identifying Vindemius as an exorcist and marking his peaceful repose, indicating a Christian burial.

EDCS-24700336.summary: An epitaph for Adeodata, described as 'faithful,' suggesting a Christian burial, with the location 'Augustas' possibly indicating a specific cemetery or region.

EDCS-24700337.summary: A concise epitaph for Agate, identified as 'faithful' and at peace, characteristic of early Christian funerary inscriptions.

EDCS-24700342.translation: Boinus, faithful, in peace, lived 60 years, deposited 16 days before the Kalends of January.
EDCS-24700342.summary: A Christian epitaph recording the death and burial of Boinus, who lived 60 years and was buried in early January.

EDCS-24700344.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the age of Bonifatius at death.

EDCS-24700345.translation: Campratius the faithful lived 65 years in peace, buried on the Nones of July.
EDCS-24700345.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the age and burial date of Campratius.

EDCS-24700347.translation: Dida the faithful, on the Kalends of September. Victor.
EDCS-24700347.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the name of Dida and possibly the dedicator or another person named Victor, with a date.

EDCS-24700348.translation: Cersconius the faithful lived 50 years in peace, buried on the Kalends of November.
EDCS-24700348.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the age and burial date of Cersconius.

EDCS-24700349.translation: Datibus, buried on the 7th day before the Kalends of July, the faithful.
EDCS-24700349.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the burial date of Datibus, who is described as faithful.

EDCS-24700351.translation: Deogratias the faithful lived [---] years in peace, buried on the 3rd day before the Ides, in the 7th indiction.
EDCS-24700351.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the burial date and indiction year of Deogratias.

EDCS-24700352.summary: This is a brief funerary inscription identifying Deushabet as faithful.

EDCS-24700354.translation: Dicentius the faithful lived 60 years in peace, buried on the Kalends of November; he is faithful and lies here.
EDCS-24700354.summary: This funerary inscription records the age and burial date of Dicentius, with a Greek epitaph.

EDCS-24700355.translation: Euticia the faithful in peace, buried on the 15th day before the Kalends of May. Feli[x?].
EDCS-24700355.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the burial date of Euticia, with a possible name at the end.

EDCS-24700356.summary: This is a funerary inscription with a term of endearment for Eutychius.

EDCS-24700357.summary: This is a simple epitaph for a woman named Fania, indicating her faithfulness and peaceful repose in death.

EDCS-24700359.summary: This is a simple epitaph for a woman named Felicia, indicating her faithfulness and peaceful repose in death.

EDCS-24700366.summary: This epitaph records the peaceful rest of two individuals, Fortunatus and Iuliana.

EDCS-24700368.summary: This epitaph records the lifespan of a faithful individual named Gelasius.

EDCS-24700369.summary: This epitaph commemorates a young girl named Generosa, indicating her peaceful rest.

EDCS-24700370.translation: Gulosus, lived 76 years, buried faithful, in peace. Felix lived [X] years.
EDCS-24700370.summary: This epitaph records the age of Gulosus at death and mentions his faithfulness, also noting the lifespan of Felix.

EDCS-24700371.summary: This is a simple epitaph for an individual named Helenus, indicating his peaceful repose in death.

EDCS-24700372.summary: This is a simple epitaph for an individual named Herclanius, indicating his peaceful repose in death.

EDCS-24700377.translation: Publius Iunius Maximus, faithful, lived [X] years.
EDCS-24700377.summary: This epitaph records the lifespan of Publius Iunius Maximus, a faithful individual.

EDCS-24700378.summary: This inscription identifies a person named Lampas as 'religious', likely indicating a devotee or someone of pious character.

EDCS-24800764.text_edition: \n VS SILVEVS Lammiani et Domitiani Thusdritano iunctae sunt ius Marinus et Doryphorus Primigenio suo salutem exemplum epistulae scriptae nobis a Tutilio Pudente egregio viro ut notum haberes et id quod subiectum est celeberrimis locis propone nulla VII proximis annis scriptam iubeas sermo procuratorum Imperatoris Caesaris Traiani Hadriani Augusti quia Caesar noster infatigabili cura sua per quam adsidue pro humanis utilitatibus excubat omnes partes agrorum quae tam oleis quam frumentis aptae sunt excoli iubet idcirco permissum providentiae eius potestas fit omnibus etiam eas partes occupandi quae in centuriis elocatis saltus Blandiani et Udensis et in illis partibus sunt quae ex saltu Lamiano et Domitiano iunctae Thusdritano sunt nec a conductoribus exercentur isque qui occupaverint possidendi ac fruendi heredique suo relinquendi id ius datur quod et lege Hadriana comprehensum de rudibus agris et iis qui per decem annos continuos inculti sunt nec ex Blandiano et Udensi saltu maiores partes fructuum exigentur a possesoribus quam quartas ideo qua cetera omnia iussa Caesaris nostri augeri quam ullo m diu minui sinis si quis in ea loca neglecta ab conductoribus occupaverit quae rigari solent si tertias partes fructuum dabit de his quoque regionibus quae ex Lamiano et Domitiano saltu iunctae Thusdritano sunt tantundem dabit de oleis quas quisque aut in scrobibus posuerit aut oleastris inseruerit captorum fructuum nulla decem proximis exigetur sed nec de pomis septem annis proximis nec alia poma in divisionem umquam cadent quam quae venibunt a possessoribus quas partes aridas fructuum quisque debebit dare eas proximo quinquennio ei dabit in cuius conductione agrum occupaverit post it tempus rationi Caesaris nostri in fsis e lege relocan\n
EDCS-24800764.translation: VS SILVEVS to Lammianus and Domitianus, joined to Thusdritus, sends greetings from Marinus and Doryphorus Primigenius. Let it be known by you, as we have been informed by an example of an epistle written to us by Tutilius Pudens, an excellent man, and let it be proposed in the most frequented places. In the last seven years, because our Caesar, with his tireless care, through which he unceasingly watches over human interests, orders all parts of the lands, which are suitable for both olives and grains, to be cultivated. For this reason, his foresight permits the power to extend to everyone, even to occupy those parts which are in the leased centuriae of the Blandian and Udens pastures, and in those parts which are joined from the Lamian and Thusdritan pastures, and are not worked by contractors. And to him who shall occupy them, the right is given to possess and enjoy, and to leave to his heir, which is also comprehended in the Hadrianic law concerning uncultivated lands, and those which have been uncultivated for ten continuous years. Nor shall larger portions of the fruits be exacted from the possessors than a quarter from the Blandian and Udens pastures. Therefore, as all other commands of our Caesar are to be increased, do not allow any to be diminished for a long time. If anyone shall occupy in those places, neglected by the contractors, which are usually irrigated, he shall give a third part of the fruits. He shall give the same from those regions which are joined from the Lamian and Domitian pastures to Thusdritus. For the olive trees which anyone has planted either in pits or grafted from wildings, no fruits shall be exacted for the nearest ten years, but also for the fruits of apples for the nearest seven years, nor shall other apples ever fall into division than those which are sold by the possessors. The proportions of dry fruits which anyone shall owe, he shall give them in the next five years to him in whose lease he occupied the land. After that time, they will be relocated to the accounts of our Caesar according to the law. The area is 100 iugera.
EDCS-24800764.summary: This is a rescript from Emperor Trajan Hadrian to Tutilius Pudens, concerning the cultivation and occupation of lands in the Blandian and Udens pastures, outlining terms for settlers and harvest shares.
