EDCS-24800792.summary: This dedication records Caius Carusius Longus as the builder of steps for a shrine dedicated to 'Hero Augustus', likely a deified emperor or a heroic figure associated with Augustus.

EDCS-24800793.translation: To Jupiter Hammon the Barbaric and Silvanus, the priests Sempronia Salsula, mother of the sacred rites, Caius Iunius Mercurius, Lucius Pistorius Suavis, Caius Graecinius Auspicialis, Publius Iulius Felix, Lucius Pistorius Silvanus, Lucius Valerius Fortunatus, Lucius Caelius Peregrinus, Titus Valerius Primitius, Publius Tettius Saturninus, Marcus Pomponius Crescens, Marcus Pomponius Felix, Lucius Caelius Dexter, Quintus Liberius Proculus, the priestess Valeria Paulina, mother of the sacred rites, Quintus Caecilius Honoratus, and five other priests of the barbaric god Silvanus.
EDCS-24800793.summary: This lengthy inscription lists numerous priests and priestesses, including designated 'mothers of the sacred rites', dedicating a shrine to Jupiter Hammon and Silvanus, possibly a syncretic deity, in a context of polytheistic worship.

EDCS-24800794.translation: Sacred to Liber, from the vintners of the most flourishing Carthage, with all their merchandise.
EDCS-24800794.summary: This inscription records a dedication to the god Liber (Bacchus) by the vintners of Carthage, indicating a religious observance related to their trade and commerce.

EDCS-24800796.translation: Sacred to Pluto. Quintus Pullaienus Clinia, priest of Ceres, set this up at his own expense.
EDCS-24800796.summary: This inscription records Quintus Pullaienus Clinia, a priest of Ceres, dedicating a monument at his own expense to Pluto, possibly in connection with chthonic deities or funerary rites.

EDCS-24800798.translation: Sacred to Saturn Augustus. Quintus Fabius Saturninus, priest of Mars the 'temenorus', of the temple of memory, and his wife Fortunula, with their sons, fulfilled a vow.
EDCS-24800798.summary: This inscription records Quintus Fabius Saturninus, a priest of Mars, and his family fulfilling a vow to Saturn Augustus, possibly in relation to a family mausoleum or memorial ('temenorus aedis memoriae').

EDCS-24800801.translation: To Tellus Augusta. Soma Felix R. Three locations. Under the consulship of [---].
EDCS-24800801.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Tellus Augusta, likely mentioning a donor named Soma Felix and possibly referring to land ('loca III'), dated by consuls.

EDCS-24800802.translation: Sacred to Venus Erucina Augusta. Lucius Cassius Apolaustus fulfilled his vow willingly.
EDCS-24800802.summary: This inscription records Lucius Cassius Apolaustus willingly fulfilling a vow to Venus Erucina Augusta, a specific cult of Venus, likely during the imperial period.

EDCS-24800804.translation: Lucius Ofillius Felix, procurator of Augustus, consecrated the altar and rendered his vow.
EDCS-24800804.summary: This inscription records Lucius Ofillius Felix, an imperial official (procurator Augusti), consecrating an altar and fulfilling a vow, likely during the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-24800805.translation: Sacred. The litter-bearer fulfilled his vow willingly and dedicated it himself.
EDCS-24800805.summary: This inscription records a 'lecticarius' (litter-bearer) fulfilling a vow and dedicating a monument, indicating a devotion from a person of a specific trade or social standing.

EDCS-24800806.translation: Gnaeus Lurius Abascantianus, a hunter of 'taelegeniorum' (a type of performance or game), willingly set this up in fulfillment of a vow.
EDCS-24800806.summary: This is a votive inscription set up by Gnaeus Lurius Abascantianus, a hunter.

EDCS-24800807.translation: For the health of the Augusti (emperors), CLCIA cchus, a hunter, fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-24800807.summary: This is a votive inscription for the health of the emperors, dedicated by a hunter named CLCIA cchus.

EDCS-24800808.translation: [Text incomplete]... the third turma, Tinos, priest, the entire D, consuls.
EDCS-24800808.summary: This inscription appears to record officials or units, possibly military or religious, with the mention of consuls.

EDCS-24800809.translation: On behalf of the most distinguished proconsul Lucius Clodius Amplitus Naevianus and the most distinguished legate pro praetore Cocceius Honorinus, what was undertaken by the priestess Honorata, likewise what was undertaken by the priestess of Aesculapius, was built by Gaius Mu[---] during the consulship of [---] [---] MLCII [---].
EDCS-24800809.summary: This inscription records a building project or undertaking related to provincial administration and religious officials, likely from the 2nd century AD.

EDCS-24800810.translation: Having undergone the taurobolium, the priest dedicated (it).
EDCS-24800810.summary: This is a short dedication by a priest who has undergone the taurobolium, a ritual sacrifice.

EDCS-24800811.translation: Aemilius Primigenianus and Pompeius Sisinnus fulfilled their vow for Quintas.
EDCS-24800811.summary: This is a votive inscription by Aemilius Primigenianus and Pompeius Sisinnus.

EDCS-24800812.summary: This is a votive inscription by a woman named Donata.

EDCS-24800813.translation: Titus Modius Felix fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-24800813.summary: This is a votive inscription by Titus Modius Felix.

EDCS-24800814.translation: S Stabi willingly set this up.
EDCS-24800814.summary: This is a votive inscription set up by S. Stabi.

EDCS-24800815.summary: This is a votive inscription by Ursianus.

EDCS-24800816.translation: Aquilo and T. gladiator willingly fulfilled their vow to Augustus.
EDCS-24800816.summary: This is a votive inscription by two gladiators, Aquilo and T. gladiator, dedicated to Augustus.

EDCS-24800818.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Augustus by Aginis.

EDCS-24800820.summary: This dedicatory inscription records the erection of a monument by priests.

EDCS-24800822.translation: For my divine Augustus, I made this while alive.
EDCS-24800822.summary: This is a funerary or dedicatory inscription made by an individual for the divine Augustus.

EDCS-24800825.summary: This is a dedicatory inscription, likely for a monument, honoring Aurelius Antoninus.

EDCS-24800835.summary: This inscription refers to the emperor Septimius Severus Augustus.

EDCS-24800842.translation: To our Lords, Caesar Flavius Julius Crispus and Caesar Flavius Claudius Constantine.
EDCS-24800842.summary: This is a dedicatory inscription honoring the Caesars Crispus and Constantine.

EDCS-24800848.translation: To Theodosius, perpetual Augustus, and to the most glorious men.
EDCS-24800848.summary: This inscription honors the emperor Theodosius I and other distinguished men.

EDCS-24800854.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription mentioning Publius Cae[---].

EDCS-24800856.summary: This inscription refers to the titles of emperors, emphasizing their invincibility.

EDCS-24800857.summary: This inscription refers to the titles of emperors, emphasizing their status as unconquered lords.

EDCS-24800858.summary: An inscription honoring two emperors, likely from the Late Roman period.

EDCS-24800860.summary: An inscription fragment possibly referring to Caesar Augustus as the son of a divine emperor.

EDCS-24800861.translation: To the Emperor Caesar, son of the divine
EDCS-24800861.summary: A fragmentary inscription honoring an emperor, likely from the imperial period, mentioning his divine parentage.

EDCS-24800862.summary: A fragmentary inscription possibly honoring Emperor Augustus, mentioning his fatherhood and a possible official title.

EDCS-24800863.summary: A fragmentary inscription mentioning 'Augustus' and what appears to be a title or an abbreviation.

EDCS-24800867.translation: Aconius Catullinus, a most distinguished man, dedicated these excellent baths, adorned with fitting splendor, from the very foundation.
EDCS-24800867.summary: This inscription records the dedication of excellent public baths by Aconius Catullinus, a prominent man, likely in the 1st or 2nd century AD.

EDCS-24800868.translation: Quintus Aurelius Symmachus, a most distinguished man, while proconsul of the province of Africa and judging in place of the emperor, ordered this to be set up.
EDCS-24800868.summary: This inscription records an order by Quintus Aurelius Symmachus, a distinguished man and proconsul of Africa, to erect a monument, likely in the late 4th century AD.

EDCS-24800869.translation: To C.I. Faustinus, a most distinguished man
EDCS-24800869.summary: A fragmentary inscription honoring a prominent individual named Faustinus, likely from the imperial period.

EDCS-24800870.summary: A very brief inscription, possibly a legal or administrative record, mentioning Julius Asper.

EDCS-24800871.translation: Marcus Servilius Nonianus, a member of the board of seven epulones, consul, proconsul, patron of the town, dedicated this.
EDCS-24800871.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a monument by Marcus Servilius Nonianus, a distinguished Roman official with multiple high-ranking roles, likely in the 1st or 2nd century AD.

EDCS-24800872.translation: The priests of Ceres, in their entirety, made this at their own expense, in honour of their descendant Lucius Memmius Tuscillus, great-grandson of Memmius Senecio the consular.
EDCS-24800872.summary: This inscription is a dedication by the priests of Ceres to a distinguished ancestor.

EDCS-24800874.translation: Virius Audentius Aemilianus, a man of the highest rank, judging in the stead of the proconsul of the province of Africa, carried out the restoration of the theatre with its statues.
EDCS-24800874.summary: This inscription records the restoration of a theatre by Virius Audentius Aemilianus, a high-ranking official in Roman Africa, possibly in the 3rd century CE.

EDCS-24800875.translation: Virius Audentius Aemilianus, a man of the highest rank, judging in the stead of the proconsul of the province of Africa.
EDCS-24800875.summary: This inscription names Virius Audentius Aemilianus, a high-ranking official in Roman Africa, possibly in the 3rd century CE, exercising judicial authority.

EDCS-24800878.translation: To the legate of the Fifth Trajan Legion.
EDCS-24800878.summary: This is a dedication to a legate of the Fifth Trajan Legion.

EDCS-24800879.translation: As tribune of the plebs by decree of the decurions, at public expense.
EDCS-24800879.summary: This inscription likely records an official act or monument funded by the public and approved by the town council, related to a tribune of the plebs.

EDCS-24800880.translation: To Pullaenius, proconsul of the province of Africa.
EDCS-24800880.summary: This is a dedication to Pullaenius, who served as proconsul of Africa.

EDCS-24800882.translation: for the province of Sicily, when he served as legate.
EDCS-24800882.summary: This inscription refers to someone who served as legate in the province of Sicily.

EDCS-24800886.translation: Proconsul of the province of Africa, judging in the stead of the highest authority, Victoria the faithful lived in peace for 60 years, buried on the 9th of June. Placidus the faithful lived in peace for 80 years, buried on the 28th of December.
EDCS-24800886.summary: This inscription records the burial dates and ages of Victoria and Placidus, associated with a proconsul of Africa, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-24800887.translation: Judging in the stead of the highest authority, O.
EDCS-24800887.summary: This inscription fragment refers to someone judging in a high official capacity.

EDCS-24800888.translation: ius Acanus, a man of the highest rank.
EDCS-24800888.summary: This inscription fragment identifies 'ius Acanus' as a man of high rank.

EDCS-24800891.translation: during the insistence of the count P.O.
EDCS-24800891.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription mentioning a count P.O. and the context of their insistence, likely from an administrative or legal record.

EDCS-24900130.translation: The proconsul Ingenus, Felix, Felix, Secundus.
EDCS-24900130.summary: This inscription lists names, including a proconsul named Ingenus, likely related to a list of officials or a dedication.

EDCS-24900132.translation: from Nea Probus of Sabinis, Donatus from Hadrumetum, [---]ici inus Her [---]
EDCS-24900132.summary: This inscription appears to record individuals, possibly with their origins in Sabinis and Hadrumetum, with fragmented personal names and place names.

EDCS-24900133.translation: from Perinthus, [---]ulus from Berytus, [---]erus from Carthage, Titus Lucius A[---]
EDCS-24900133.summary: This inscription lists individuals and their places of origin: Perinthus, Berytus, and Carthage, along with Roman personal names.

EDCS-24900136.translation: Lucius Lappius, Caius Iulius, Marcus Pupius [---]rius.
EDCS-24900136.summary: This inscription lists several Roman personal names, suggesting it might be part of a dedication, funerary monument, or list of officials.

EDCS-24900138.translation: [---]us Caius Mac Quintus Furfanius Quintus Vegilius Marcus Ulpius Lucius Iulius Marcus Pontius Marcus
EDCS-24900138.summary: This is a long list of Roman personal names, likely part of a monument or record commemorating multiple individuals.

EDCS-24900146.translation: Sacred to the Dis Manes. Lucius Cornelius Maximus, son of Lucius, of the Papiria tribe, a soldier of the first urban cohort, century of Aelius Longus. He served for 18 years and lived piously for 40 years. Livius Maternus, a soldier of the same cohort, century of Castor, his relative and heir, and Petronius Tiro and Beturius Maximus, his fellow soldiers of the same unit, friends and co-heirs, had this made. He is buried here.
EDCS-24900146.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Cornelius Maximus, a soldier of the first urban cohort, detailing his service, lifespan, and the individuals who arranged his burial.

EDCS-24900147.translation: Sacred to the Dis Manes. Lucius Ammonius Paternus, a soldier for 20 years in the second praetorian cohort. Ammonius.
EDCS-24900147.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Ammonius Paternus, a soldier in the second praetorian cohort, who served for 20 years.

EDCS-24900148.translation: Sacred to the Dis Manes. Quintus Domitius Inventus, a soldier of the first urban cohort, century of B. Domitius Liburnus, his heir, made this.
EDCS-24900148.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Quintus Domitius Inventus, a soldier of the first urban cohort, erected by his heir.

EDCS-24900149.translation: Caius Iulius Severus, a veteran, lived piously for 60 years. P. pia Aucta, his freedwoman, set this up.
EDCS-24900149.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Caius Iulius Severus, a veteran, and his freedwoman, P. pia Aucta, who erected the monument.

EDCS-24900150.translation: Sacred to the deified spirits. Licinius Germullus, soldier of the I Urbana cohort, served 19 years, lived [---].
EDCS-24900150.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Licinius Germullus, a soldier of the I Urbana cohort, recording his service and lifespan.

EDCS-24900151.summary: This inscription mentions Plotius, likely a soldier from a cohort, with no further context provided.

EDCS-24900153.translation: Gloriosa lived one year faithfully in peace. Sacred to the Divine Manes. Marcus Valerius Peta, a sesquiplicarius of the ala Gemelliana from the province of Tingitana, lived 30 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-24900153.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcus Valerius Peta, a cavalry soldier from Tingitana, who lived 30 years, and for his wife Gloriosa, who lived only one year, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24900155.translation: of the III Augusta legion. He is buried here.
EDCS-24900155.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription mentioning a soldier of the III Augusta legion, indicating he is buried at this location.

EDCS-24900157.summary: This inscription fragment refers to a veteran who accomplished a destructive act, the full context of which is lost.

EDCS-24900158.translation: to his son Musclosianus Arnensis Quintilianus, flamen of the deified Pius, whose father Musclosianus, elected aedile by the suffrage of all and with legitimate funds, donated 50,000 sesterces and a show for the same office to the treasury.
EDCS-24900158.summary: This inscription records a father's honoring of his son Quintilianus, who served as a flamen, and details the son's father's significant financial contributions to the aedileship.

EDCS-24900159.translation: Marcus Servilius Arnensis, priest of the VARINIARI, for his merit by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-24900159.summary: This inscription honors Marcus Servilius Arnensis, a priest, for his merits, as decided by the local council (decurions).

EDCS-24900160.translation: For his outstanding goodness, Secundus Iulianus, an excellent man, was granted a place by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-24900160.summary: This inscription records that Secundus Iulianus, recognized for his goodness, was granted a place of honor by a decree of the decurions.

EDCS-24900162.translation: of our lord Augustus, a decurion of the colony of Carthage, with funds.
EDCS-24900162.summary: This inscription fragment mentions a decurion of the colony of Carthage and refers to funds, possibly related to a dedication or public work.

EDCS-24900169.translation: I am born, under the care of Cornelius.
EDCS-24900169.summary: This inscription fragment, possibly part of a larger text, mentions an individual who is 'born' or 'arisen' under the care of Cornelius.

EDCS-24900172.translation: priest, I made this; I lived 50 years and months.
EDCS-24900172.summary: This is a funerary epitaph of a priest who records having made the monument and lived 50 years and some months.

EDCS-24900176.translation: Vitalis, of most happy arrival, made with his own money the approach for his children, where the mountain, its paving, its stairs, and its structure would be made strong, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-24900176.summary: This inscription records Vitalis funding the construction of an approach with stairs and paving, likely a public work, following a decurial decree.

EDCS-24900187.translation: For Petronius Carus Victorinus, a man of note, formerly vicar of Africa.
EDCS-24900187.summary: This is a dedication, likely to Petronius Carus Victorinus, who held a significant administrative post in Roman Africa.

EDCS-24900210.translation: For the most distinguished youth Crescens, son of Lucius.
EDCS-24900210.summary: This inscription honors Crescens, son of Lucius, described as a distinguished youth.

EDCS-24900218.translation: To Lucius Rufinianus, of the Vivt family.
EDCS-24900218.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Lucius Rufinianus.

EDCS-24900228.translation: For the most distinguished man T. [---]
EDCS-24900228.summary: This is a partial inscription honoring a 'most distinguished man' with the initial T.

EDCS-24900230.translation: From the Imperial treasury of the province of Africa.
EDCS-24900230.summary: This inscription indicates a source of funding from the imperial treasury for the province of Africa.

EDCS-24900231.summary: This is a dedication to Volussius Aemilianus Prudentis.

EDCS-24900232.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription possibly related to a family of Flavius, with illegible portions.

EDCS-24900271.translation: For Marcus Annius, a man of distinction.
EDCS-24900271.summary: This inscription honors Marcus Annius, described as a man of distinction.

EDCS-24900273.translation: For Lucius Aemilius, aged III [?] years, from Castres [?].
EDCS-24900273.summary: This inscription possibly records the name and age of a young individual, Lucius Aemilius, possibly from Castres.

EDCS-24900278.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription indicating property owned by Marcus, likely from a boundary stone or land division marker.

EDCS-24900280.translation: Here is Leo whom no one conquers
EDCS-24900280.summary: This inscription appears to be a funerary epitaph or a marker for a tomb, possibly for a person or animal named Leo.

EDCS-24900287.translation: Brumalis, Ianuarius, Februarius, Martius, Aprilis, the equinoctial (month), Maius, Iunius, the solstice (month)
EDCS-24900287.summary: This inscription lists names of months, possibly related to a calendar, agricultural cycle, or astronomical observations.

EDCS-24900288.text_edition: \n Lucius Atilius Luci libertus Hiero furnarius Valeria |(mulieris) liberta Euterpe furnaria vivit Caius Valerius Cai libertus Dionisius sic triarius vivit\n
EDCS-24900288.translation: Lucius Atilius Hiero, freedman of Lucius, baker. Valeria Euterpe, freedwoman of [---], baker, lives. Caius Valerius Dionisius, freedman of Caius, a veteran, lives.
EDCS-24900288.summary: This is a funerary inscription for several individuals, including bakers and a veteran, indicating their familial relationships and occupations.

EDCS-24900289.translation: Asyllia Polla, daughter of Lucius, physician, lies here. She lived 65 years. Euscius, her freedman, made this at his own expense.
EDCS-24900289.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Asyllia Polla, a physician, recording her age at death and stating it was paid for by her freedman.

EDCS-24900290.translation: Secundus, a veterinary slave of Marcus Benni, is buried here. He lived 45 years.
EDCS-24900290.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Secundus, a veterinary slave, recording his name, occupation, owner, and lifespan.

EDCS-24900291.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Titus Aelius Fortunatus, a soldier of the 1st Urban Cohort, lived 20 years and 8 months. He is buried here.
EDCS-24900291.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Titus Aelius Fortunatus, a soldier in the 1st Urban Cohort, recording his lifespan and burial.

EDCS-24900292.translation: To the deified spirits. Quintus Julius Ingenuus, soldier of Legion VII Gemina Felix, lived 43 years, served 21 years. Flavius Marinus, his heir, erected this index.
EDCS-24900292.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Quintus Julius Ingenuus, a soldier of the VII Gemina Felix legion, recording his age at death and length of service, and noting it was erected by his heir.

EDCS-24900293.translation: To Cornelius Marcellus, soldier of the 13th Urban Cohort. Cornelius Crescens lived 30 years, deserving of his patron.
EDCS-24900293.summary: A funerary inscription for Cornelius Marcellus, a soldier in the 13th Urban Cohort, set up by Cornelius Crescens.

EDCS-24900296.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Felix Caesaris nostri cursor servus pius vixit nnos XVIII collegium mulionum ob merita\n
EDCS-24900296.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Felix, a faithful servant and courier of our emperor, lived 18 years. The guild of muleteers [set this up] for his merits.
EDCS-24900296.summary: A funerary inscription for Felix, a servant and courier of the emperor, honored by the guild of muleteers.

EDCS-24900298.translation: Terentia Successa, dutiful, lived 28 years and 18 days. She is buried here. Fortunatus, a scribe slave of Augustus, made this for his most dutiful wife. May the earth be light for you, may your bones rest well.
EDCS-24900298.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Terentia Successa, made by her husband Fortunatus, a scribe slave, expressing wishes for her peaceful afterlife.

EDCS-24900299.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Aurelius [name illegible], a faithful attendant born in the imperial household, lived 34 years and 8 months and 9 days. He lies here.
EDCS-24900299.summary: A funerary inscription for Aurelius, a domestic attendant to the emperors, who died at the age of 34.

EDCS-24900300.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Romanus, a faithful land surveyor of the emperor, lived 50 years. He lies here.
EDCS-24900300.summary: A funerary inscription for Romanus, an imperial land surveyor, who died at the age of 50.

EDCS-24900301.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Vitalis, a dutiful household slave of Augustus, a steward of our Caesar, lived 25 years. He is buried here. Thalamus, his father, made this for the deserving man.
EDCS-24900301.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Vitalis, a slave and steward, likely from the imperial household, stating his age and that it was erected by his father.

EDCS-24900302.text_edition: \n Lascivus Augusti servus nomenclator pius vixit nnos XXII hic situs est\n
EDCS-24900302.translation: Lascivus, a faithful servant of the emperor and a nomenclator (official list-keeper), lived 22 years. He lies here.
EDCS-24900302.summary: A funerary inscription for Lascivus, an imperial servant and nomenclator, who died at the age of 22.

EDCS-24900304.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Fortunatus, a dutiful notary slave of Augustus, lived 26 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-24900304.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Fortunatus, a notary slave of Augustus, recording his age and burial.

EDCS-24900305.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Salvius, a dutiful notary slave of Augustus, lived 19 years. He is buried here. Flavius Salvius and Flavia Tertia made this for the most noble boy.
EDCS-24900305.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Salvius, a notary slave of Augustus, recording his age and burial, erected by Flavius Salvius and Flavia Tertia for him.

EDCS-24900306.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Felix, a faithful servant and attendant of our emperor, lived 48 years. He lies here. Aelia Melpomene made this for her most devoted husband.
EDCS-24900306.summary: A funerary inscription for Felix, an imperial servant, set up by his wife Aelia Melpomene.

EDCS-24900307.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. For Florentinus, a dutiful attendant of Augustus, who lived 64 years. Icara, his companion, made this. He is buried here.
EDCS-24900307.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Florentinus, an attendant of Augustus, recording his age and burial, erected by his companion Icara.

EDCS-24900309.translation: Dedicated to the Spirits of the Departed. Stephanio, forest ranger and slave of our Caesar, lived 49 years and 4 months. Phaenippus, assistant of tabularii for Augustus, his brother, made this.
EDCS-24900309.summary: A funerary dedication for Stephanio, a forest ranger and slave of Caesar, made by his brother Phaenippus, an assistant tabularius for Augustus.

EDCS-24900310.translation: Dedicated to the Spirits of the Departed. Placida, a pious slave of Augustus, lived 28 years. Romanus, a messenger for Augustus, made this for his most pious sister.
EDCS-24900310.summary: A funerary dedication for Placida, a slave of Augustus, made by her brother Romanus, a messenger for Augustus.

EDCS-24900311.translation: Primus, servant of Caesar, lived 3 years. He lies here. Nicodicus, servant of Caesar and a messenger, made this for his devoted son.
EDCS-24900311.summary: A funerary inscription for Primus, son of Nicodicus, a servant and messenger of Caesar.

EDCS-24900312.translation: Dedicated to the Spirits of the Departed. Saccar, a pious messenger and slave of our Caesar, lived 30 years. Hortrus, a pious messenger and slave of our Caesar, lived 20 years. His devoted mother made this.
EDCS-24900312.summary: A funerary dedication for Saccar and Hortrus, both slaves and messengers of Caesar, made by their mother.

EDCS-24900313.translation: Dedicated to the Spirits of the Departed. Sabina, a pious slave of the Emperors, lived 19 years and 8 months. Here she rests. Her pious father Nicarchus, a messenger for Augustus, made this.
EDCS-24900313.summary: A funerary dedication for Sabina, a slave of the Emperors, made by her father Nicarchus, a messenger for Augustus.

EDCS-24900314.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Publius Aelius Optatus, a faithful freedman of the emperor and a scribe, lived 30 years. He lies here. His sister made this.
EDCS-24900314.summary: A funerary inscription for Publius Aelius Optatus, an imperial freedman and scribe, set up by his sister.

EDCS-24900315.translation: Dedicated to the Spirits of the Departed. Successa lived 17 years, 5 months, and 8 days. A virgin. Ionicus, freedman and tabularius for Augustus of tribute collections, made this.
EDCS-24900315.summary: A funerary dedication for Successa, a virgin, made by Ionicus, an Augustus' freedman and tabularius of tribute collections.

EDCS-24900316.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Cladus, a faithful servant of the emperor and assistant to the scribe, lived 27 years and 4 months. He lies here. His devoted wife Quietula made this.
EDCS-24900316.summary: A funerary inscription for Cladus, an imperial servant and scribe's assistant, set up by his wife Quietula.

EDCS-24900317.translation: Dedicated to the Spirits of the Departed. Primigenius, an assistant tabularius for Augustus, lived 31 years and 41 days. His devoted mother and wife made this for the most pious.
EDCS-24900317.summary: A funerary dedication for Primigenius, an assistant tabularius for Augustus, made by his mother and wife.

EDCS-24900318.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Saturninus, a faithful servant and assistant to the scribe of our emperor, lived 40 years and 7 months and 5 days. He lies here.

EDCS-24900319.summary: A fragmented inscription likely recording a dedication or funerary commemoration, mentioning an assistant tabularii.

EDCS-24900321.translation: Dedicated to the Spirits of the Departed. Aelius Felix Sextius, pious, lived 24 years. Here he rests.

EDCS-24900322.translation: Dedicated to the Spirits of the Departed. Aelia.

EDCS-24900323.translation: Dedicated to the Spirits of the Departed. Aelia Casta, pious, lived 58 years. Here she rests.

EDCS-24900324.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Evangellis lived piously for 20 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-24900324.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Evangellis, recording her pious life and age at death.

EDCS-24900325.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Agatho, a devoted slave, lived 45 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-24900325.summary: A tombstone for Agatho, a slave, who lived 45 years, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24900326.translation: Agathopus, vicarius and slave of the Emperor, lived 24 years. He is buried here.

EDCS-24900329.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Asia, a pious servant of Augustus, lived 24 years; she is buried here. Asiaticus, father, and Cupita, mother, and Privatus, a fellow servant, made this.

EDCS-24900331.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Attis, a slave of the Emperor, lived 11 years. She is buried here. Spendo for his most sweet fellow freedwoman.
EDCS-24900331.summary: A tombstone for Attis, a slave of the Emperor, who lived 11 years, possibly erected by Spendo, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24900332.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Marcus Aurelius Felicior lived piously for 75 years, 3 months, and 5 days; he is buried here.
EDCS-24900332.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcus Aurelius Felicior, recording his pious life and precise age at death.

EDCS-24900333.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Aurelius Felix lived for 21 years, 8 months, and 16 days; he is buried here.
EDCS-24900333.summary: This funerary epitaph records the life and precise age at death of Aurelius Felix.

EDCS-24900334.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Aurelius Maxsimus lived for 37 years, 3 months, 8 days, and 3 hours; he is buried here.
EDCS-24900334.summary: This funerary epitaph records the life and precise age at death of Aurelius Maxsimus.

EDCS-24900336.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Pantagathus, a servant of Augustus, made this for his wife Caecilia Nia, who lived for 40 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-24900336.summary: This funerary epitaph records the marriage and death of Caecilia Nia, with her husband Pantagathus, a servant of Augustus, as the dedicator.

EDCS-24900337.translation: Callistus is buried here. Curtia Peculiaris [made this?].
EDCS-24900337.summary: This funerary epitaph records the burial of Callistus and likely indicates Curtia Peculiaris as the maker or related person.

EDCS-24900338.translation: Campanus, a devoted slave of Caesar, lived 14 years. He is buried here. Gargilia Veneria, his wife, made this for her devoted husband.
EDCS-24900338.summary: A tombstone for Campanus, a slave of Caesar, who lived 14 years, erected by his wife Gargilia Veneria, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24900340.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Casius lived for 10 years, 9 months, and 7 days.
EDCS-24900340.summary: This funerary epitaph records the life and precise age at death of Casius, son of Caesar.

EDCS-24900341.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Lucius Geminius Victor lived piously for 37 years and 11 days.
EDCS-24900341.summary: This funerary epitaph records the pious life and age at death of Lucius Geminius Victor.

EDCS-24900342.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Chrestus, a most devoted slave of the Emperors, lived 5 years, 11 months, and 14 days. He is buried here.
EDCS-24900342.summary: A tombstone for Chrestus, a slave of the Emperors, who lived 5 years, 11 months, and 14 days, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24900345.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Marcus Claudius Primigenius lived piously for 22 years.
EDCS-24900345.summary: This funerary epitaph records the pious life and age at death of Marcus Claudius Primigenius.

EDCS-24900346.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Claudia Eugenia lived 24 years and 6 months. Claudia Cratiste lived 15 years. They are buried here.
EDCS-24900346.summary: A tombstone for Claudia Eugenia and Claudia Cratiste, who lived 24 years, 6 months, and 15 years respectively, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24900348.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. [---]fio, freedman of the Emperor, [---]fo Cocceia.
EDCS-24900348.summary: A funerary monument fragment recording a freedman of the Emperor and Cocceia, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24900350.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Concordia lived 18 years. Her devoted mother Primigenia made this. She rests here.
EDCS-24900350.summary: A funerary epitaph for Concordia, set up by her mother, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24900351.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Cornelia Tilla.
EDCS-24900351.summary: A funerary epitaph for Cornelia Tilla, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24900353.translation: Crescens lived 2 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-24900353.summary: A tombstone for Crescens, who lived 2 years, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24900354.translation: Crito, a devoted slave of Caesar, lived 40 years. He is buried here. His devoted sons made this.
EDCS-24900354.summary: A tombstone for Crito, a slave of Caesar, who lived 40 years, erected by his sons, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24900355.text_edition: \n Daphnis ego Hermetis coniunx sum libera facta cum dominus vellet primus Hermes liber ut esset fato ego facta prior fato ego rapta prior quae tuli quod gemui gemitus viro saepe reliqui quae domino invito vitam dedi proxime nato nunc quis alet natum quis vitae longa ministrat me Styga sic quod rapuit tam cito eni<m=A> a superos sic pia vixit annis XXV hic sita est \n
EDCS-24900355.translation: I, Daphnis, wife of Hermes, was freed, being freed by my master's wish that Hermes should be freed first. Fate freed me sooner, fate snatched me away sooner. What I bore and what I groaned for, I often left my husband. Forcing my life away from my master, for my son recently born. Who will now nourish my child? Who will provide for his life? As the one whom Death snatched so quickly, so did I, who lived piously, lie here for 25 years.
EDCS-24900355.summary: A funerary epitaph for Daphnis, a freedwoman, recounting her life and premature death after her husband Hermes was freed, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24900356.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Datius the devoted lived 11 years. He rests here. Made.
EDCS-24900356.summary: A funerary epitaph for Datius, stating his age and that it was made, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24900357.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Dionysia, a pious slave of Caesar, lived for 3 years. She is buried here. Her mother Tertia made this.
EDCS-24900357.summary: A tombstone for Dionysia, a pious slave of Caesar, who died at the age of three, erected by her mother Tertia, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24900358.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Donata the devoted lived [XX?] years. She rests here. Made by Ianuarius.
EDCS-24900358.summary: A funerary epitaph for Donata, set up by Ianuarius, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24900359.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Egnatia Secunda the devoted lived 40 years. She rests here.
EDCS-24900359.summary: A funerary epitaph for Egnatia Secunda, stating her age, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24900360.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Elegans lived piously for 40 years.
EDCS-24900360.summary: A funerary inscription for Elegans, who lived piously for 40 years, likely dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24900362.translation: Erucia Vitalis lived piously for 34 years. She is buried here. Vitalis, a slave of our Caesar, made this for his pious wife.
EDCS-24900362.summary: A tombstone for Erucia Vitalis, erected by her husband Vitalis, a slave of Caesar, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24900363.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Eutaxia, a pious slave of our Caesar, lived for 9 years and 4 months. She is buried here. May your bones rest well. May the earth lie lightly on you.
EDCS-24900363.summary: A funerary epitaph for Eutaxia, a pious slave of Caesar, who died at the age of 9 years and 4 months, with standard wishes for the deceased, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24900364.translation: She rests here, Eutychia, a freedwoman, having earned this.
EDCS-24900364.summary: A funerary epitaph for Eutychia, a freedwoman, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24900365.translation: Publius Fabius Secundus lived piously for 75 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-24900365.summary: A tombstone for Publius Fabius Secundus, who lived piously for 75 years, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24900366.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Fausta, devoted follower of Augustus, lived 80 years and 11 days. Martialis and Primus for their mother. She rests here.
EDCS-24900366.summary: A funerary epitaph for Fausta, set up by her sons Martialis and Primus, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24900367.translation: Faustilla, a pious slave of our Caesar, lived for 60 years. Her daughter Helena for 30 years. Felix lived for 2 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-24900367.summary: A funerary inscription commemorating Faustilla, her daughter Helena, and a child named Felix, all associated with Caesar's household, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24900369.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Faustus, devoted servant of Augustus, lived more than 100 years. Redducta the devoted, his granddaughter, lived 1 year and 3 months and 11 days. She rests here.
EDCS-24900369.summary: A funerary epitaph for Faustus and his granddaughter Redducta, noting Faustus's long life, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24900370.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Faustus and Saturninus Secundus, brothers and pious slaves of our Caesar, lived for 18 and 6 years respectively. They are buried here. Saturninus and Ianuaria, parents, made this for their most pious sons.
EDCS-24900370.summary: A tombstone for two brothers, Faustus and Saturninus Secundus, slaves of Caesar, erected by their parents, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24900371.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Felicissima the devoted lived 19 years and 6 months. She rests here.
EDCS-24900371.summary: A funerary epitaph for Felicissima, stating her age, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24900372.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Felicitas the devoted lived 37 years and 2 months. She rests here.
EDCS-24900372.summary: A funerary epitaph for Felicitas, stating her age, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24900373.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Felicula, a pious slave of Augustus, lived for 25 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-24900373.summary: A tombstone for Felicula, a pious slave of Augustus, who died at the age of 25, dated to the early Imperial period.

EDCS-24900374.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Felix, faithful servant of Augustus, lived 68 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-24900374.summary: A funerary epitaph for Felix, a servant of Augustus, who lived 68 years, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24900375.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Felix, faithful servant of Augustus, lived 7 months and 3 days; he is buried here.
EDCS-24900375.summary: A funerary epitaph for Felix, a servant of Augustus, who lived 7 months and 3 days, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24900376.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Felix lived piously for 90 years and 5 months. He is buried here.
EDCS-24900376.summary: A funerary inscription for Felix, who lived a pious life for 90 years and 5 months, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24900379.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Titus Flavius Faustulus, faithful, lived 17 years, 7 months, and 26 days; he is buried here. His most dutiful parents made this. To the Divine Spirits. Veratius, faithful servant of our Caesars, lived 18 years, 8 months, and 14 days; he is buried here. For his most dutiful and deserving uncle.
EDCS-24900379.summary: A complex funerary epitaph with two individuals, Titus Flavius Faustulus and Veratius, likely from the Roman Imperial period, commemorating the lives and deaths of both.

EDCS-24900380.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Titus Flavius Nivalis, faithful, lived approximately 70 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-24900380.summary: A funerary epitaph for Titus Flavius Nivalis, who lived approximately 70 years, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24900382.translation: Flavia Magnia Callippina, devout, lived for 2 years and 4 months; she is buried here.
EDCS-24900382.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the death of Flavia Magnia Callippina at a young age.

EDCS-24900383.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Flavia Safsula lived for 22 years, 25 days, and 9 hours; she is buried here.
EDCS-24900383.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the death of Flavia Safsula at the age of 22.

EDCS-24900384.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Flavia Tertia, freedwoman of Augustus, devout, lived for 80 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-24900384.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the death of Flavia Tertia, a freedwoman of the emperor, at the age of 80.

EDCS-24900386.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Gaius Fuficius Nobilis, devout, lived for 46 years, 7 months, and 9 days. Maxima made this for her most devout husband; he is buried here.
EDCS-24900386.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the death of Gaius Fuficius Nobilis, erected by his wife Maxima.

EDCS-24900387.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Lucius G. Iucundus, faithful, lived 24 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-24900387.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lucius G. Iucundus, who lived 24 years, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24900388.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. [Name missing]us, devout, lived for 40 years. Gemellus made this for his most devout brother; he is buried here.
EDCS-24900388.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the death of an unnamed man who lived 40 years, erected by his brother Gemellus.

EDCS-24900389.translation: And Gratius for his most dutiful brother, aged 25.
EDCS-24900389.summary: A funerary epitaph fragment commemorating a brother named Gratius who died at the age of 25, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24900390.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Heraclida, devout, lived for 62 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-24900390.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the death of Heraclida at the age of 62.

EDCS-24900391.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Hilarus, servant of our Caesar, devout, lived for 11 years; likewise Elix, his brother, devout, lived for 2 years. Elix, their father, made this for his most devout sons; they are buried here.
EDCS-24900391.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the deaths of two brothers, Hilarus and Elix, who lived to ages 11 and 2 respectively, erected by their father.

EDCS-24900392.translation: [Name missing] Hygia, devout, lived for 30 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-24900392.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the death of Hygia at the age of 30.

EDCS-24900394.translation: Ianuarius, servant of Augustus, lived for 5 years.

EDCS-24900395.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Ianuarius, servant of Augustus, lived 25 years; he is buried here. His devoted wife Tertia made this.
EDCS-24900395.summary: A funerary epitaph for Ianuarius, a servant of Augustus, erected by his wife Tertia, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24900396.translation: [Name missing]us Inginus F[---], lived for [---] years, [---] days, 5 days.
EDCS-24900396.summary: This is a fragmentary tombstone inscription that likely records the name and lifespan of an individual.

EDCS-24900398.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Iucunda, faithful, lived 17 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-24900398.summary: A funerary epitaph for Iucunda, who lived 17 years, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24900399.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Iulia Rogata, faithful, lived 26 years, 1 month, and 13 days; she is buried here.
EDCS-24900399.summary: A funerary epitaph for Iulia Rogata, who lived 26 years, 1 month, and 13 days, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24900400.translation: Iulia Tertulla the pious lived 55 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-24900400.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Iulia Tertulla, recording her name, piety, age at death, and burial place.

EDCS-24900401.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Licinia Tertulla, daughter of Marcus, the pious, lived 28 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-24900401.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Licinia Tertulla, recording her name, parentage, piety, age at death, and burial place.

EDCS-24900402.translation: Lucinus the pious lived 5 years, 2 months, and 10 days.
EDCS-24900402.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Lucinus, recording his name, piety, and age at death in years, months, and days.

EDCS-24900403.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Luculentus, who is also called Adaucta, faithful, lived 17 years, 9 months, and 15 days; she is buried here.
EDCS-24900403.summary: A funerary epitaph for Luculentus (also known as Adaucta), who lived 17 years, 9 months, and 15 days, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24900405.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Marciana, freedwoman of Augustus, dutiful, lived 22 years, is buried here.
EDCS-24900405.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Marciana, a freedwoman of Augustus, recording her age at death.

EDCS-24900406.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Maximus lived for 1 year and 5 months.

EDCS-24900407.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Modia Egloge, dutiful, lived 47 years, 8 months, and 25 days. Lucius Modius Crysopaes made this for his dearest and most sacred wife.
EDCS-24900407.summary: This is a funerary inscription made by Lucius Modius Crysopaes for his wife Modia Egloge, recording her age and lifespan.

EDCS-24900408.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Montana, dutiful, lived 55 years. Her son Donatus made this.
EDCS-24900408.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Montana, stating her age at death and that it was made by her son Donatus.

EDCS-24900409.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Munatius Valerius, dutiful, lived 1 year, 6 months, and 8 days. He is buried here.
EDCS-24900409.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Munatius Valerius, recording his age at death.

EDCS-24900410.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Munatia Apsens, daughter of Lucius, the pious, lived 15 years, 10 months, and 24 days; she is buried here.
EDCS-24900410.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Munatia Apsens, recording her name, parentage, piety, age at death in years, months, and days, and burial place.

EDCS-24900411.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Murrania Maia, the pious, lived 50 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-24900411.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Murrania Maia, recording her name, piety, age at death, and burial place.

EDCS-24900413.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Norbania Saturnina the pious. As fame proves, I surpassed twice six hundred years of light and also the part of the year we mentioned, twice three combined with ten days. I kept chastity and modesty throughout my life. Happy now I rest in the African soil. You too, passing by, whoever reads this tomb, spare my ashes from being trampled by reckless feet. Thus may much light overflow for you into the heavenly air.
EDCS-24900413.summary: This is a metrical tombstone inscription for Norbania Saturnina, recording her name, piety, a poetic recounting of her lifespan (24 years) and virtues, her burial in Africa, and a plea to passersby.

EDCS-24900414.translation: For himself. Publius Octav lived [X] years. He is buried here. From CA omin.
EDCS-24900414.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Publius Octav, likely a self-funded tomb or epitaph, recording his lifespan.

EDCS-24900415.translation: Publius Octavius Metro[---], freedman, out of dutifulness (?).
EDCS-24900415.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription mentioning Publius Octavius Metro[---], a freedman, possibly for a funerary dedication.

EDCS-24900416.summary: This is a very brief inscription identifying an individual, Oppius T. Secundus, likely a name on a tomb or monument.

EDCS-24900417.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Optata Piata, the pious, lived 2 years, 3 months, and 8 days; she is buried here.
EDCS-24900417.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Optata Piata, recording her name, piety, age at death in years, months, and days, and burial place.

EDCS-24900418.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Optatus, servant of Augustus, dutiful, lived 60 years, is buried here. Salvia, dutiful, his wife, made this. Faustus, servant of Augustus, dutiful, lived 1 year, 5 months, is buried here. Optatus made this.
EDCS-24900418.summary: This funerary inscription records the deaths of two servants of Augustus, Optatus and Faustus, noting their ages and who made their respective epitaphs.

EDCS-24900419.translation: Dutiful servant, lived [X] years. She is buried here. Optatus, the father, made this for his daughter.
EDCS-24900419.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a daughter, made by her father Optatus, recording her lifespan.

EDCS-24900420.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Paetina the dutiful lived 10 years and is buried here.
EDCS-24900420.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Paetina, recording her age at death and burial.

EDCS-24900421.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Pantea the dutiful lived 1 year and 20 days and is buried here.
EDCS-24900421.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Pantea, recording her age at death and burial.

EDCS-24900423.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Phaenippus, a pious servant of Augustus, lived 33 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-24900423.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Phaenippus, a servant of Augustus, recording his name, piety, age at death, and burial place.

EDCS-24900424.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Philo, a servant of Augustus, lived 33 years. Laetina, his sister, made this. He is buried here.
EDCS-24900424.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Philo, a servant of Augustus, recording his name, age at death, and that it was erected by his sister, Laetina.

EDCS-24900425.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus Pompeius Victoricus lived 55 years and 7 months and 12 days and is buried here.
EDCS-24900425.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Quintus Pompeius Victoricus, recording his age at death and burial.

EDCS-24900426.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Prepusa, a servant of Caesar, the pious, lived 7 years and 3 months; she is buried here.
EDCS-24900426.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Prepusa, a servant of Caesar, recording her name, piety, age at death in years and months, and burial place.

EDCS-24900429.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Prima, dutiful, lived for 1 year, 9 months, and 14 days; she rests here.
EDCS-24900429.summary: This is a tombstone for Prima, who died in infancy, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24900430.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Primigenia lived 30 years; Ianuarius the dutiful lived 23 years and is buried here.
EDCS-24900430.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Primigenia and Ianuarius, recording their ages at death and burial.

EDCS-24900431.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Princeps Augusti the dutiful lived 25 years and is buried here. Ulpia Veneria, his dutiful mother, made this.
EDCS-24900431.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Princeps Augusti, noting his age at death and that his mother, Ulpia Veneria, erected it.

EDCS-24900432.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Priscianus the dutiful lived 3 years, 8 months, and 21 days. Redemtus, father, made this. Redemtus the dutiful lived...
EDCS-24900432.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Priscianus, detailing his age and noting his father Redemtus as the maker, with an incomplete mention of Redemtus' own life.

EDCS-24900434.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Romanus, a dutiful slave of our Caesar, lived for 15 years; he rests here.
EDCS-24900434.summary: This is a tombstone for Romanus, a slave of the emperor, who died as a youth, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24900435.translation: Salvia, a dutiful slave of Caesar, lived for 30 years; she rests here.
EDCS-24900435.summary: This is a tombstone for Salvia, a slave of the emperor, who died in adulthood, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24900436.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Salvia, a dutiful slave of Augustus, lived for 38 years; she rests here. Titus Flavius Salvius had this made out of duty.
EDCS-24900436.summary: This is a tombstone for Salvia, a slave of Augustus, with a dedication by Titus Flavius Salvius, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24900437.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Salvia, Augusti's slave, the dutiful, lived 5 years and 5 months. Saturninus, father, made this for his daughter who deserved well of him.
EDCS-24900437.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Salvia, a slave, recording her age at death and noting that her father, Saturninus, erected the monument.

EDCS-24900438.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Salvius, a slave of our Caesar, lived for two years and eight months; he rests here. Salvius, his father, had this made for his deserving son.
EDCS-24900438.summary: This is a tombstone for Salvius, the son of Salvius, a slave of the emperor, who died in early childhood, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24900439.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Sannacrio, dutiful, lived for 7 years; he rests here.
EDCS-24900439.summary: This is a tombstone for Sannacrio, who died in childhood, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24900440.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Saturnina, a dutiful slave of our Caesar, lived for 10 years; she rests here.

EDCS-25000981.text_edition: \n Sexto Caecilio Sexti filio Quirina Aemiliano Xviro stlitibus iudicandis VIIviro epulonum quaestori Augusti candidato legato pro praetore provinciae Africae tribuno plebis praetori patrono decreto decurionum pecunia publica\n
EDCS-25000981.translation: To Sextus Caecilius Aemilianus, son of Sextus, of the Quirina tribe, member of the college of the Xviri stlitibus iudicandis, member of the college of the VIIviri epulonum, quaestor of the Emperor, candidate for the consulship, governor with praetorian power of the province of Africa, tribune of the plebs, praetor, patron, honoured by decree of the local council with public funds.
EDCS-25000981.summary: An honorary inscription honoring Sextus Caecilius Aemilianus, detailing his extensive career in Roman public life and political offices, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25000983.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Asterius, who died at the age of 96.

EDCS-25000986.translation: CI RIO CV C contributed to his homeland and his fellow citizens with simple love. Marcus Paetius Victor, perpetual flamen, twice chief magistrate, for his pious mother.
EDCS-25000986.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by Marcus Paetius Victor to his mother, commemorating his public service.

EDCS-25000987.translation: To Marcus Plotus Verus, citizen, on account of his father's merits.
EDCS-25000987.summary: This inscription honors Marcus Plotus Verus, a citizen, for his father's merits.

EDCS-25000988.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Octavius Mustulus lived 35 years; he is buried here. May your bones rest well; may the earth be light upon you.
EDCS-25000988.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Octavius Mustulus, recording his age and a wish for a peaceful afterlife, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25000990.translation: Because of Publius Cluvius Felix Tertullianus, perpetual priest of the colony of Iulia Aurelia Antoniniana Karthago, through the splendid request of the entire populace, they erected this bronze statue by public subscription, honoring his incomparable justice, integrity, goodness, and clemency in his administration.
EDCS-25000990.summary: This inscription records the erection of a bronze statue by public subscription in honor of Publius Cluvius Felix Tertullianus, a perpetual priest of Karthago, for his virtuous administration, likely from the Antonine period.

EDCS-25000991.translation: For the glory of our lords Honorius and Theodosius, victorious everywhere, during the proconsulate of Gaius Aelius Pomponius Proculus, a most distinguished and notable man, judging with vice-regal authority, Marcus Sinius Caripa, patron, devoted to the municipality, completed the construction of a new fountain at his own expense.
EDCS-25000991.summary: This inscription records Marcus Sinius Caripa's completion of a new fountain at his own expense for the glory of the emperors Honorius and Theodosius and during the proconsulate of Gaius Aelius Pomponius Proculus, dating it to the late Roman period.

EDCS-25001164.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Tyche, devoted, lived 40 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-25001164.summary: A funerary dedication for Tyche, who lived to be 40 years old.

EDCS-25001166.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Valeria, a servant of the Emperor, dutiful, lived 25 years and three months; she rests here.
EDCS-25001166.summary: A funerary epitaph for Valeria, an imperial servant, recording her age and lifespan at death and indicating she is buried here, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25001167.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Venustus, devoted, lived 12 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-25001167.summary: A funerary dedication for Venustus, who died at the age of 12.

EDCS-25001168.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Victor, a devoted servant of our Caesar, lived 22 years; he is buried here. May the earth lie lightly upon you; may your bones rest well.
EDCS-25001168.summary: A funerary dedication for Victor, a servant of Caesar, who died at the age of 22, with wishes for a peaceful afterlife.

EDCS-25001169.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Victor, a devoted servant of Augustus, lived 9 years and 8 months; he is buried here.
EDCS-25001169.summary: A funerary dedication for Victor, a servant of Augustus, who died at the age of 9 years and 8 months.

EDCS-25001170.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Victor lived piously for 8 years. Ianuaria lived piously for 12 years.
EDCS-25001170.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the ages of two children, Victor and Ianuaria, dedicated to the Divine Shades.

EDCS-25001171.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Victoria, devoted, lived 15 years and 6 months; she is buried here.
EDCS-25001171.summary: A funerary dedication for Victoria, who died at the age of 15 years and 6 months.

EDCS-25001172.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Victoria, devoted, lived 13 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-25001172.summary: A funerary dedication for Victoria, who died at the age of 13.

EDCS-25001173.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Victoria, a devoted servant of Augustus, lived 1 year, 5 months, and 4 days; she is buried here.
EDCS-25001173.summary: A funerary dedication for Victoria, a servant of Augustus, who died at the age of 1 year, 5 months, and 4 days.

EDCS-25001174.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Victoria, devoted, lived 3 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-25001174.summary: A funerary dedication for Victoria, who died at the age of 3.

EDCS-25001175.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Victoria, devoted, lived 35 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-25001175.summary: A funerary dedication for Victoria, who lived to be 35 years old.

EDCS-25001176.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Victoricus the pious lived for 5 years, 7 months, 20 days, and 9 hours.
EDCS-25001176.summary: A tombstone recording the lifespan of Victoricus, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25001177.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Marcus Ulpius Euphemus lived for 50 years and Ulpia Trophime the pious lived for 60 years; he made this altar for himself while alive. Let malicious intent be absent from this altar; she is buried here.
EDCS-25001177.summary: A tombstone for Marcus Ulpius Euphemus and Ulpia Trophime, who constructed their own altar and burial place, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25001178.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Umbonia Secundula the pious lived for 28 years and 7 months; Felix made this for his wife who deserved well of him. Aurelius Felix the pious lived for 4 years, 2 months, and 10 days; Felix made this for his son who deserved well of him. She is buried here.
EDCS-25001178.summary: A tombstone set up by Felix for his wife Umbonia Secundula and son Aurelius Felix, both deceased, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25001179.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Unio lived for 4 years, 2 months, and 20 days.
EDCS-25001179.summary: A tombstone recording the short lifespan of Unio, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25001180.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Urbana, daughter, lived for 19 years, here she lies.
EDCS-25001180.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the age of Urbana, daughter, dedicated to the Divine Shades.

EDCS-25001181.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Urbana the pious lived for [unknown years], 2 months; she made this for her sister who deserved well of her.
EDCS-25001181.summary: A tombstone set up by Urbana for her sister, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25001182.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Urbica the pious lived for 25 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-25001182.summary: A tombstone recording the lifespan of Urbica, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25001184.translation: Zosa the slavewoman lived for 12 years; her pious mother made this. Freedwoman of the Emperors.
EDCS-25001184.summary: A tombstone for Zosa, a slavewoman, erected by her mother, indicating her status as a freedwoman of the emperors, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25001185.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Zosimus lived for 55 years.
EDCS-25001185.summary: A tombstone recording the lifespan of Zosimus, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25001186.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Zosime lived piously for 85 years, here she lies.
EDCS-25001186.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the age of Zosime, dedicated to the Divine Shades.

EDCS-25001187.translation: ON lived for 60 years, more or less. Most loving of his own. He is buried here.
EDCS-25001187.summary: A tombstone for ON, recording his approximate age and expressing affection, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25001188.translation: Halia, slavewoman, deservedly [mourned?], lived for 16 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-25001188.summary: A tombstone for Halia, a slavewoman, erected likely by a family member, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25001189.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. S. died aged 33 years and 8 months, and is buried here.
EDCS-25001189.summary: A funerary inscription for S., freedman of Augustus, stating his age at death.

EDCS-25001191.translation: Ilia Enas, pious, died aged 30 years, and is buried here.
EDCS-25001191.summary: A funerary inscription for Ilia Enas, stating her age at death.

EDCS-25001195.translation: A slave died aged 14 years and 6 months.
EDCS-25001195.summary: A funerary inscription for a slave, stating their age at death.

EDCS-25001196.translation: Sius, pious, died aged 25 years, and is buried here.
EDCS-25001196.summary: A funerary inscription for Sius, stating his age at death.

EDCS-25001198.translation: Pius, aged 60 years, Verna, pious, aged 10 years.
EDCS-25001198.summary: A fragmented funerary inscription mentioning two individuals, Pius and Verna, with their ages at death.

EDCS-25001199.translation: Marcus, freedman of Augustus, [died aged] 11 months.
EDCS-25001199.summary: A fragmented funerary inscription for Marcus, freedman of Augustus, stating his age at death.

EDCS-25001204.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Titus Aelius Libycus, freedman of Augustus, assistant to the clerks at the Thuisiduensis table, died aged 78 years, and is buried here.
EDCS-25001204.summary: A funerary inscription for Titus Aelius Libycus, freedman of Augustus and an official, stating his age at death.

EDCS-25001205.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Caecilia Felicitas lived piously for 21 years, here she lies. Viator, servant and assistant of the Emperor's record office, made this for his deserving wife.
EDCS-25001205.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Caecilia Felicitas, made by her husband Viator, a servant and assistant in the imperial record office.

EDCS-25001206.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Chrestus, custodian of the Emperor's grain warehouses, lived piously for 80 years.
EDCS-25001206.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the age of Chrestus, a custodian of imperial grain warehouses.

EDCS-25001207.summary: A fragmented funerary inscription for Gellia, a nurse, indicating her age at death.

EDCS-25001208.translation: Freedman of Augustus, a chamberlain, pious, died aged 2 months and 1 day, and is buried here.
EDCS-25001208.summary: A funerary inscription for a freedman of Augustus who served as a chamberlain, stating his age at death.

EDCS-25001209.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Agathopus, freedman of Augustus, pious, died aged 90 years and 9 months, and is buried here.
EDCS-25001209.summary: A funerary inscription for Agathopus, freedman of Augustus, stating his age at death.

EDCS-25001211.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Publius Considianus Eurocles lived 20 years and 8 months.
EDCS-25001211.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan of Publius Considianus Eurocles.

EDCS-25001212.translation: Repentina, pious wife, lived 80 years; here he lies.
EDCS-25001212.summary: This fragmentary funerary epitaph records the lifespan of a woman named Repentina and mentions her husband.

EDCS-25001213.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Lucius Cornelius Dorion, pious, lived 43 years; here he lies.
EDCS-25001213.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan and burial place of Lucius Cornelius Dorion.

EDCS-25001214.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Fortunatus, a pious slave of our emperor, lived 63 years; his pious wife made this; here he lies.
EDCS-25001214.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan of Fortunatus, a slave of the emperor, and notes his wife as the dedicator.

EDCS-25001216.translation: Iuala, daughter of Pudentis, 27 years old.
EDCS-25001216.summary: This inscription records the name and age of Iuala, daughter of Pudentis.

EDCS-25001217.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Lucius Pacon lived...
EDCS-25001217.summary: This fragmentary funerary epitaph begins the record of Lucius Pacon's life.

EDCS-25001218.translation: [---]. Perelius lived piously for [---] years, here he lies.
EDCS-25001218.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription recording the life of Perelius.

EDCS-25001221.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Pupia Asella, pious, lived 42 years, 7 months, and 15 days; here she lies.
EDCS-25001221.summary: This funerary epitaph records the full lifespan and burial place of Pupia Asella.

EDCS-25001224.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Veneria lived piously for 70 years, here she lies.
EDCS-25001224.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the age of Veneria, dedicated to the Divine Shades.

EDCS-25001227.translation: ... slave lived ... years; here he lies.
EDCS-25001227.summary: This fragmentary funerary epitaph records a slave's burial place and mentions their lifespan.

EDCS-25001228.summary: This very fragmentary inscription likely records the name or status of a slave.

EDCS-25001236.summary: This fragmentary inscription records Aemilianus' lifespan, indicating uncertainty about the exact duration.

EDCS-25001242.translation: Artoria Harmonia lived piously for 2 years, here she lies.
EDCS-25001242.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the age of the child Artoria Harmonia.

EDCS-25001245.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a freedman named Felix, identified by his master Hilauctus.

EDCS-25001247.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Aurelius Candidus lived 3 years. Aurelius Quirinalis to his well-deserving son and Aureli.
EDCS-25001247.summary: A funerary epitaph where Aurelius Quirinalis set up a monument for his son Aurelius Candidus, who lived only 3 years.

EDCS-25001248.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Marcus Aurelius Nomadius Pius, freedman of Augustus, lived 32 years and 11 months. Nice made this for her husband.
EDCS-25001248.summary: A funerary epitaph for Marcus Aurelius Nomadius Pius, a freedman of Augustus, set up by his wife Nice.

EDCS-25001253.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Caecilia Primitiva, dutiful, lived 43 years and 5 months and 2 days. She is buried here.
EDCS-25001253.summary: A funerary epitaph for Caecilia Primitiva, recording her age at death and burial.

EDCS-25001254.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely serving as an epitaph for Caeladius Aemilius.

EDCS-25001255.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Marcus Caelius Felix, dutiful, lived 28 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-25001255.summary: A funerary epitaph for Marcus Caelius Felix, recording his age at death and burial.

EDCS-25001258.summary: A fragmentary funerary epitaph for Celest, mentioning her dutifulness and incomplete age.

EDCS-25001262.translation: Considius Felicitas took care to have this made.
EDCS-25001262.summary: This inscription records Considius Felicitas arranging for a monument or construction to be made.

EDCS-25001265.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. S. Crescens, dutiful, lived years...
EDCS-25001265.summary: A fragmentary funerary epitaph for S. Crescens, mentioning his dutifulness and incomplete age.

EDCS-25001267.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Cuppia Secunda, dutiful, lived 25 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-25001267.summary: A funerary epitaph for Cuppia Secunda, recording her age at death and burial.

EDCS-25001268.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Donatus, identified by his praenomen and a filiation or cognomen.

EDCS-25001269.translation: Egrilia Romana, daughter of Aulus, lived piously for 20 years, here she lies.
EDCS-25001269.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the age of Egrilia Romana, daughter of Aulus.

EDCS-25001270.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Fabia Repulsula, dutiful, lived 10 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-25001270.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the life and death of Fabia Repulsula, who died at the age of 10.

EDCS-25001271.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Via Fau, who died at the age of 21.

EDCS-25001273.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Titus Flavius.
EDCS-25001273.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Titus Flavius.

EDCS-25001278.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription mentioning Fulvia Donata.

EDCS-25001279.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Titus Furfanius Amphio, dutiful, lived 16 months.
EDCS-25001279.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Titus Furfanius Amphio, who died at the age of 16 months.

EDCS-25001280.translation: [---] lived 8 years. Furiana, dutiful, lived [---] years; she is buried here.
EDCS-25001280.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary epitaph for two individuals, one of whom is Furia(na).

EDCS-25001283.translation: I beg you, whoever reads this inscription, do not depart from Aphrocras.
EDCS-25001283.summary: This is a peculiar inscription which seems to be a curse or a plea to ensure the deceased remains undisturbed.

EDCS-25001285.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. [---]onia Hilara.
EDCS-25001285.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Hilara, likely with a missing praenomen or nomen.

EDCS-25001287.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Caius Hosidius Optatus, dutiful, lived 27 years, 10 months, 7 days; he is buried here.
EDCS-25001287.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the life and death of Caius Hosidius Optatus, who died at the age of 27 years, 10 months, and 7 days.

EDCS-25001288.translation: To Lucius Hostilius Flaccus, son of Lucius, of the Arnensis tribe, father; to Lucius Hostilius [---]
EDCS-25001288.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Hostilius Flaccus, likely indicating a family monument.

EDCS-25001289.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Hymen.
EDCS-25001289.summary: This is a funerary dedication to the gods of the underworld by Hymen.

EDCS-25001290.translation: Ianuarius lived 50 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-25001290.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the age and burial of Ianuarius.

EDCS-25001291.translation: Farsuleia Victrix, devout, lived 38 years; she rests here.
EDCS-25001291.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Farsuleia Victrix, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25001292.summary: This memorial was set up by Ingenuus.

EDCS-25001294.summary: This funerary inscription records the age of the deceased Inventa.

EDCS-25001295.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Iltius Iucundus [lived] 11 months and 10 days.
EDCS-25001295.summary: This funerary dedication records the short life of Iltius Iucundus.

EDCS-25001298.translation: Iulia Quieta, devout, lived 35 years; she rests here.
EDCS-25001298.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Iulia Quieta, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25001302.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Marmoraria [lived] ... years.
EDCS-25001302.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to the gods of the underworld and records part of the age of Marmoraria.

EDCS-25001303.summary: This is a fragmented inscription, possibly funerary, mentioning the name Martialis.

EDCS-25001304.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Caius Messius Eulogius, dutiful, lived 23 years, 11 months, and 7 days. Ligni.
EDCS-25001304.summary: This funerary inscription records the age at death of Caius Messius Eulogius.

EDCS-25001306.translation: Modia Grata, freedwoman of Caius, devout, lived 40 years; she rests here.
EDCS-25001306.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Modia Grata, a freedwoman, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25001307.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Antonius lived 85 years. Muttunius, son of Marcus, lived [...] years.
EDCS-25001307.summary: This funerary inscription records the ages of two individuals, Antonius and Muttunius.

EDCS-25001310.translation: Numisia Tertia, dutiful daughter of Caius, is buried here. She lived [...] years.
EDCS-25001310.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial and age of Numisia Tertia.

EDCS-25001311.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Pacata lived for [some number of] years.
EDCS-25001311.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespan of a woman named Pacata.

EDCS-25001313.translation: Quintus Pompeius Naus, devout, lived 18 years; he rests here. Quintus Pompeius Quietus, devout, lived 10 years; he rests here.
EDCS-25001313.summary: This is a paired funerary inscription recording the deaths of Quintus Pompeius Naus and Quintus Pompeius Quietus, likely father and son, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25001317.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Prima the dutiful lived for 55 years. Datus lived for 80 years. Secunda lived for 65 years.
EDCS-25001317.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespans of three individuals: Prima, Datus, and Secunda.

EDCS-25001319.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that likely identifies an individual named Proculus.

EDCS-25001322.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcus Quintilius Asinus, the dutiful, lived for one year and 5 months. He is buried here.
EDCS-25001322.summary: This funerary inscription records the short life of Marcus Quintilius Asinus.

EDCS-25001323.translation: A Restuta lived for 40 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-25001323.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespan and burial of a woman named Restuta.

EDCS-25001327.summary: This fragmentary inscription likely refers to an individual named Septimius Rusticus.

EDCS-25001328.translation: Marcus Rutilius Liber, devout, lived sixty years.
EDCS-25001328.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Marcus Rutilius Liber, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25001332.summary: This dedication is addressed to an individual named Saturo.

EDCS-25001333.summary: This fragmentary inscription appears to name two individuals, Saturninus and Medubia.

EDCS-25001334.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Saufeius Iucundus lived for [some number of] years.
EDCS-25001334.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespan of Saufeius Iucundus.

EDCS-25001335.summary: This fragmentary inscription likely refers to an individual named Saturninus.

EDCS-25001343.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Lucius Tadius Germullianus Caecilis Copiola lived 39 years; she is buried here. Tadius Germullianus lived 11 years; he is buried here. Tadia lived [age not specified]; she is buried here.
