EDCS-25001343.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the deaths of Lucius Tadius Germullianus Caecilis Copiola and two others, likely family members.

EDCS-25001344.translation: To the divine power, Taintida IODO presented this sacred offering.
EDCS-25001344.summary: A dedication to a deity by Taintida IODO, likely a votive offering.

EDCS-25001345.translation: Tharsicius, a caregiver, mourning him snatched away in tender youth, abroad.
EDCS-25001345.summary: A commemorative inscription for a deceased youth, Tharsicius, mourned by his caregiver.

EDCS-25001346.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Thevest lived 10 years.
EDCS-25001346.summary: A funerary epitaph for Thevest, who died at the age of 10.

EDCS-25001350.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Valeria Atiliana, pious and from Magontia, lived 31 years and 5 months.
EDCS-25001350.summary: A funerary epitaph for Valeria Atiliana, specifying her age and piety.

EDCS-25001351.translation: Valeria Secunda, daughter of Quintus, devout, lived 22 years; she rests here.
EDCS-25001351.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Valeria Secunda, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25001352.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Vene...
EDCS-25001352.summary: A fragmentary funerary inscription beginning with a dedication to the Divine Spirits.

EDCS-25001356.translation: Of the urban cohort, Mela S. lived...
EDCS-25001356.summary: A fragmentary inscription possibly referring to a soldier of the urban cohort.

EDCS-25001357.summary: A fragmentary inscription recording the age of a deceased person, possibly a brother.

EDCS-25001362.summary: A fragmentary inscription recording a duration of life, 40 years and 3 months.

EDCS-25001365.translation: Campanus lived 10 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-25001365.summary: A funerary epitaph for Campanus, who died at the age of 10.

EDCS-25001370.translation: To Ranilla, daughter of Ianus, a Tianan.
EDCS-25001370.summary: This is an epitaph for Ranilla, daughter of Ianus, who was from Tianum.

EDCS-25001374.translation: The slave lived 12 years, is buried here.
EDCS-25001374.summary: An epitaph for an unnamed slave who died at the age of 12.

EDCS-25001376.translation: To Ae, the freedwoman, lived 20 years.
EDCS-25001376.summary: An epitaph for Ae, a freedwoman who died at the age of 20.

EDCS-25001380.translation: O incomparable, pious one, lived 39 years.
EDCS-25001380.summary: An epitaph honoring an "incomparable, pious one" who lived 39 years.

EDCS-25001382.summary: A fragmentary epitaph for a man named S, who was 50 years old and a consul.

EDCS-25001384.summary: A fragmentary epitaph for a pious individual who lived to be 82 years old.

EDCS-25001389.translation: To AL, she brings sacred offerings, adorns.
EDCS-25001389.summary: A dedication to AL, likely a deity, for bringing sacred offerings and adorning.

EDCS-25001392.translation: Os A, lived X years, was buried here.
EDCS-25001392.summary: A fragmentary epitaph for someone named Os A, who lived an unknown number of years and was buried here.

EDCS-25001400.translation: Son of the divine Antoninus Magnus Pius.
EDCS-25001400.summary: An inscription identifying someone as the son of Emperor Antoninus Pius.

EDCS-25001402.translation: To Gallia Optata, wife of Publius Modius Felix, daughter of Primus, to reward the generosity of her husband, this perfect work of the market hall for the entire curia.
EDCS-25001402.summary: A dedication from Publius Modius Felix to his wife Gallia Optata, likely commissioning a market hall as a testament to her virtue and his generosity.

EDCS-25001403.translation: To Publius Modius Primus, son of Felix, former quaestorian, former duovir, to reward his generosity and to perpetuate his memory forever, the entire curia.
EDCS-25001403.summary: This inscription honors Publius Modius Primus, a former quaestorian and duovir, for his generosity by the entire curia.

EDCS-25001404.translation: To Racilia Saturnina, daughter of Titus Racilius Felix Lampadius, perpetual flamen, for the dutiful love she owed her sister and for the affection of her own kin, her brother.
EDCS-25001404.summary: A brother dedicates this monument to his sister, Racilia Saturnina, a daughter of a perpetual flamen, recognizing her familial love.

EDCS-25001407.translation: To our lord Flavius Gratianus Maximus Pius Felix Victor, always Augustus, Vitrasius Restutus, perpetual flamen and curator of the state, devoted with the order to his divine majesty.
EDCS-25001407.summary: Vitrasius Restutus, a perpetual flamen and curator, dedicates this inscription to Emperor Gratian, expressing his devotion.

EDCS-25001415.translation: Sacred to Deus Mercurius Augustus, which Caius Imbrius Saturus, contractor, and Quintus Gemnius, and Caius Calpurnius Optatus, and Bargius Secundus, and Rufinus Coini, and Primus Idilis, and Primus Curunni, and Felix Cai Gemni, and Primus Burros, and Fabius Honoratus, and Secundus Deana, and Sempronius Severianus, and Cerius Felix, partners, made at their own expense in the year of the duovirs Publius Iulius Mai Primianus and Caius Annaeus Namphamon.
EDCS-25001415.summary: This is a dedication to Deus Mercurius Augustus made by a group of contractors and partners during the tenure of duovirs Publius Iulius Mai Primianus and Caius Annaeus Namphamon.

EDCS-25001416.translation: Sacred to Probantius, Laodicus, Pacius, and Augustus. Lucius Publicius Optatus, son of Optatus the veteran, of the Papiria tribe, and Publius Goddaeus Victor, son of Victor, of the Papiria tribe, quaestorian aediles, made this at their own expense with the considerable sum for the state, and for the dedication they gave a feast to the order; the site was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-25001416.summary: Two quaestorian aediles, Lucius Publicius Optatus and Publius Goddaeus Victor, dedicate a monument and provide a feast to the order, with the site granted by decree of the decurions.

EDCS-25001417.translation: Sacred to Pluto Augustus, whose munificence Lucius Iacchirius Rogatus, of honored memory, had promised in the years of his aedileship, that same promise was fulfilled by Quintus Fullonius Felix, his friend and heir appointed by him, as sole heir.
EDCS-25001417.summary: Quintus Fullonius Felix fulfills a promise made by his deceased friend Lucius Iacchirius Rogatus, who had served as aedile, to dedicate this monument to Pluto Augustus.

EDCS-25001418.translation: Sacred to Pluto Augustus. Quintus Rutilius Communis, son of Proculianus, perpetual flamen, and Quintus Filonius Maximus, son of Victor, aediles, made this at their own expense and for the dedication gave a gymnasium to the people; the site was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-25001418.summary: The perpetual flamen Quintus Rutilius Communis and the aedile Quintus Filonius Maximus dedicate a gymnasium to the people in honor of Pluto Augustus, with the site granted by decree of the decurions.

EDCS-25001419.translation: To Carnuntum, to Quintus Furfanius Moderatianus, I [dedicate this].
EDCS-25001419.summary: This is a dedication to Quintus Furfanius Moderatianus at Carnuntum.

EDCS-25001421.translation: Sacred to Saturnus Augustus. Lucius Apronius Martialis, priest, fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-25001421.summary: Lucius Apronius Martialis, a priest, dedicates this inscription to Saturnus Augustus, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-25001422.translation: Sacred to Saturnus Augustus. Quintus Aquilius Felicio fulfilled his vow willingly.
EDCS-25001422.summary: Quintus Aquilius Felicio dedicates this inscription to Saturnus Augustus, willingly fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-25001423.translation: Gaius Baesius Buricus fulfilled his vow to Augustus Saturn, the god of Sobar.
EDCS-25001423.summary: This inscription records Gaius Baesius Buricus fulfilling a vow to Saturn, the god of Sobar.

EDCS-25001424.translation: Gaius Baesius Victor, the priest, willingly made this sacred offering to Augustus Saturn.
EDCS-25001424.summary: This inscription records the priest Gaius Baesius Victor making a sacred offering to Augustus Saturn.

EDCS-25001425.translation: Quintus Herennius Felix fulfilled his vow to his lord of Sobar.
EDCS-25001425.summary: This inscription records Quintus Herennius Felix fulfilling a vow to his lord of Sobar.

EDCS-25001426.translation: Octavius Ianuarius, the priest, willingly made this sacred offering to Augustus Saturn.
EDCS-25001426.summary: This inscription records the priest Octavius Ianuarius making a sacred offering to Augustus Saturn.

EDCS-25001427.translation: Publius Petronius, the priest, made this sacred offering to Saturn of Sobar.
EDCS-25001427.summary: This inscription records the priest Publius Petronius making a sacred offering to Saturn of Sobar.

EDCS-25001428.translation: onius Ba willingly made this sacred offering to Augustus Saturn.
EDCS-25001428.summary: This inscription records a partial dedication to Augustus Saturn by someone named 'onius Ba'.

EDCS-25001429.translation: Gaius Petronius Bassus, the priest, willingly made this sacred offering to Augustus Saturn.
EDCS-25001429.summary: This inscription records the priest Gaius Petronius Bassus making a sacred offering to Augustus Saturn.

EDCS-25001430.translation: Gaius Petronius Felix, the priest, willingly made this sacred offering to Augustus Saturn.
EDCS-25001430.summary: This inscription records the priest Gaius Petronius Felix making a sacred offering to Augustus Saturn.

EDCS-25001431.translation: Lucius Petronius Proculus willingly made his vow and this sacred offering to Augustus Saturn.
EDCS-25001431.summary: This inscription records Lucius Petronius Proculus fulfilling a vow and making a sacred offering to Augustus Saturn.

EDCS-25001433.translation: Publius Petronius Proculinus and Papiria Nuptialica, parents of Petroniun Zosimus and Petroniun Bucculus, who made the mosaic floor and the border, and wished to have eternal inscriptions through their sons, from the colony of Uthina.
EDCS-25001433.summary: This inscription records Publius Petronius Proculinus and Papiria Nuptialica commissioning a mosaic floor and border in memory of their sons, with the wish for eternal inscriptions, originating from the colony of Uthina.

EDCS-25001434.translation: To the Emperor Caesar, son of the deified Marcus Aurelius Pius Antoninus Germanicus Sarmaticus, brother of the deified Commodus, nephew of the deified Antoninus Pius, great-nephew of the deified Hadrian, great-great-nephew of the deified Trajan Parthicus, great-great-great-nephew of the deified Nerva, Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus Arabicus Adiabenicus, pontifex maximus, with tribunician power for the 4th time, imperator for the 8th time, consul for the 2nd time, proconsul, father of the fatherland. The citizenship of Neferitana [erected this] by decree of the decurions, with public funds.
EDCS-25001434.summary: A public dedication by the citizenship of Neferitana to Emperor Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus, likely from his reign (193-211 AD).

EDCS-25001435.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Augustus, pontifex maximus, with tribunician power for the 6th time, consul, proconsul for the 1st time, father of the fatherland, son of Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus Arabicus Adiabenicus Parthicus Maximus, grandson of the deified Marcus Aurelius Pius Germanicus Sarmaticus, great-grandson of the deified Antoninus Pius, great-great-grandson of the deified Hadrian, great-great-great-grandson of the deified Trajan Parthicus and the deified Nerva. The citizenship of Neferitana [erected this] by decree of the decurions, with public funds.
EDCS-25001435.summary: A public dedication by the citizenship of Neferitana to Emperor Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Augustus (Caracalla), likely from his sixth tribunician power grant (around 201 AD).

EDCS-25001437.translation: To the Emperor Caesar, grandson of the deified Septimius Severus Pius, son of the deified Magnus Antoninus, Marcus Aurelius Severus Alexander.
EDCS-25001437.summary: A dedication to Emperor Marcus Aurelius Severus Alexander (reigned 222-235 AD), possibly erected by a local authority or an individual.

EDCS-25001438.translation: Sacred to Saturn Augustus. Lucius Lusius Sperseius, priest, made [this] by dream.
EDCS-25001438.summary: A dedication to the god Saturn Augustus by a priest named Lucius Lusius Sperseius, who was inspired by a dream, likely from the imperial period.

EDCS-25001439.translation: [...]inius, son of [...]us, servant of Saturn Sicingensis. Uchmaris, priest, the first.
EDCS-25001439.summary: A fragmentary inscription recording a priest named Uchmaris and possibly another individual, dedicated to Saturn Sicingensis, dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-25001441.summary: A very fragmentary inscription, possibly a dedication or funerary text, with names or epithets.

EDCS-25001442.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Felix Varus lived for [...] years.
EDCS-25001442.summary: A funerary inscription for Felix Varus, recording his age at death, from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-25001443.summary: A short epitaph or devotional text mentioning 'Victoria' and 'in pace', likely from the Roman imperial period or early Christian era.

EDCS-25001445.translation: To Saturn the god. Messius Iucundus fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-25001445.summary: A votive inscription to the god Saturn by Messius Iucundus, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-25001447.translation: The steward of the two Iulii Aquilinus and Rusticinus fulfilled his vow with his family.
EDCS-25001447.summary: A votive inscription by the steward of the Iulii Aquilini and Rusticiani, dedicating something with his family, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-25001448.translation: The builders, sons of a consul, made [this].
EDCS-25001448.summary: This is a dedication by builders, sons of a consul, likely for a public work.

EDCS-25001449.translation: The prefect, exercising judicial power, a former *duovir*, made this and dedicated it because of the honor of his amplified *duovirate*, with his own money. The place was granted by decree of the town council.
EDCS-25001449.summary: This is a dedication by a prefect who had previously served as a *duovir*, commemorating his enhanced office.

EDCS-25001450.translation: Lucius Apronius, son of Lucius, a soldier of the Third Augustan Legion, is buried here.
EDCS-25001450.summary: This is a tombstone for Lucius Apronius, a soldier of the Third Augustan Legion.

EDCS-25001451.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Castus, rare and good man, master of the guilds, who passed his 70th year of age and months, [is buried here].
EDCS-25001451.summary: This is a tombstone for Marcus Picarius Turranianus, a guild master who died after the age of 70.

EDCS-25001454.translation: For the surveyor Publius Ligarius Maximus, son of Ligarius Potitus, decurion and annual magistrate of his city of Goritia, who out of his own generosity promised to contribute 4,000 sesterces to his republic, so that from the income of this sum, that is, the interest, on the 16th day before the Kalends of January, his birthday, for boxers and the gymnasium, and also a banquet for the decurions each year in perpetuity, would be spent by the same republic. Publius Ligarius Securus placed [this] out of dutiful regard for his father. The place was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-25001454.summary: This is a dedication by Publius Ligarius Securus honoring his father, Publius Ligarius Maximus, a decurion and magistrate who endowed public games and banquets.

EDCS-25001455.translation: For Marius Marinus, son of Felix, perpetual priest, because of his outstanding generosity to his homeland and his citizens, who by his will gave 12,000 sesterces to his republic of Goritia, from the interest of which, on his birthday on the Ides of September, the decurions would receive provisions each year and the gymnasium for all citizens, because of his generosity. Although the council decreed a statue for him at public expense, Maria Victoria, his daughter and heir, content with the inscription and place, placed [this] with her own money, and with Ofelius Primus, *sufes* and perpetual priest, gave a banquet to her order.
EDCS-25001455.summary: This is a dedication by Maria Victoria honoring her father, Marius Marinus, a perpetual priest who bequeathed funds for public provisions and a gymnasium, with a statue also decreed by the council.

EDCS-25001457.translation: To Venus Augusta, Anniolenus Crescentianus and Marcus Simminius Mistlita, *aediles*, having gone beyond the limits of their poverty to adorn their homeland, made [this] with their own money in compensation for the *missilia*. And because of the dedication, they provided boxers. CROM [likely an abbreviation for a place or group].
EDCS-25001457.summary: This is a dedication to Venus Augusta by two *aediles* who funded public games and adornments for their city.

EDCS-25001458.translation: Salutaris paid his vow from his own funds.
EDCS-25001458.summary: This is a dedication by Salutaris fulfilling a votive offering.

EDCS-25001459.translation: His officials had it placed at their own expense for Lucius Plautius Italus, procurator of Augustus.
EDCS-25001459.summary: This is a dedication by the officials of Lucius Plautius Italus, a procurator of Augustus.

EDCS-25001462.translation: Publius Lorenius S, from the collectors, restored the water system to a permanent state.
EDCS-25001462.summary: This is a record of the restoration of a water system by Publius Lorenius S, likely a public official or contractor.

EDCS-25001463.translation: The aedile, out of love for his fatherland, provided festivities costing 20,000 sesterces, and for the dedication ceremony he provided a banquet for everyone at a cost of 5 sesterces.
EDCS-25001463.summary: An inscription recording the public works and expenses of an aedile, likely from the Roman Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-25001466.text_edition: \n Caio Memmio Cai filio Quirina Fido Iulio Albio consuli sodali Titio legato Augusti pro praetore provinciae Noricae curatori viae Flaminiae praefecto Miniciae proconsuli provinciae Baeticae legato Augusti legionis VII Claudiae iuridico per Italiam regionis Transpadanae praetori legato pro praetore provinciae Africae aedili Ceriali quaestori provinciae Asiae tribuno laticlavio legionis II Augustae Caius Annius Iulius Secundus [][] amico rarissimo ob eximiam eius erga se benivolentiam sua pecunia posuerunt et dedicaverunt decreto decurionum\n
EDCS-25001466.translation: Caius Annius Iulius Secundus erected and dedicated this at his own expense with a decree of the decurions, for Gaius Memmius Fidus Iulius Albius, son of Caius, of the Quirina tribe, consul, Titian sodalis, legate of the emperor as proconsul of Noricum, curator of the Flaminian Way, prefect of the Minicia, proconsul of Baetica, legate of Emperor Augustus with the VII Claudia legion, iuridicus for the Transpadane region in Italy, praetor, legate as proconsul of Africa, cereal aedile, quaestor of the province of Asia, broad-striped tribune of the II Augusta legion, his very rare friend, because of his exceptional kindness towards him.
EDCS-25001466.summary: This is a public monument erected by Caius Annius Iulius Secundus to honor Caius Memmius Fidus Iulius Albius, a prominent Roman official, likely dating to the late 1st or early 2nd century CE.

EDCS-25001468.translation: Gaius Otacilius Africanus, dutiful, lived 22 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-25001468.summary: A funerary epitaph for Gaius Otacilius Africanus, providing his name, a character assessment, age at death, and burial location.

EDCS-25001469.translation: Gaius Bullatius Felix and Octavius Primus dedicated the temple.
EDCS-25001469.summary: A dedication inscription by two individuals, Gaius Bullatius Felix and Octavius Primus, for the dedication of a temple.

EDCS-25001470.translation: The colony of Iulia Curubis, by decree of its decurions and with public funds, [dedicated this] to the Emperor Caesar Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Augustus Pius, son of the deified Hadrian, grandson of the deified Trajan the Parthian, great-grandson of the deified Nerva, pontifex maximus, in his 24th year of tribunician power, Imperator for the second time, consul for the fourth time, father of the fatherland.
EDCS-25001470.summary: A lengthy dedication inscription from the colony of Iulia Curubis to Emperor Antoninus Pius, likely dating to his reign (138-161 AD) based on his titles.

EDCS-25001471.translation: The Curubitan ordo, at the people's request, decreed the honor of a statue to OSI, aedile, holder of the duumvirate, munerarius for this year, in recognition of his simple life and generous love for the citizens and the fatherland, and in gratitude for the games provided by his father and brother.
EDCS-25001471.summary: A decree from the town of Curubis honoring OSI with a statue for his civic virtues and his family's generosity in providing public games, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25001472.translation: Your servant Juliana, a girl, tiled the sacred synagogue of the Naronites for her own salvation with her own property.
EDCS-25001472.summary: An inscription detailing a private donation by a freedwoman, Juliana, to the synagogue of Narona for her salvation.

EDCS-25001473.translation: The tools of your servant, from Narona.
EDCS-25001473.summary: A very brief inscription possibly marking the ownership or dedication of tools belonging to a servant from Narona.

EDCS-25001475.text_edition: \n Asterius filius Rustici archosinagogi sic margaritarii domus dei partem portici tesselavit\n
EDCS-25001475.translation: Asterius, son of Rusticus, the archosinagogus, a pearl merchant, tiled a part of the portico of the house of God.
EDCS-25001475.summary: This inscription records the donation of Asterius, son of Rusticus, a synagogue official and pearl merchant, to a Jewish community building, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25001476.translation: To Sabina Augusta, wife of Emperor Hadrian Augustus.
EDCS-25001476.summary: A dedication or honorific inscription to Empress Vibia Sabina, wife of Emperor Hadrian (reigned 117-138 AD).

EDCS-25001477.translation: To Lucius Aelius Dionysius, most distinguished man, proconsul of the province of Africa, for his four years of service and his love for the order of Aequa Maxula, for his many services to them, the entire obedient and grateful order of Maxula decreed this.
EDCS-25001477.summary: An honorific inscription from the town of Aequa Maxula to Lucius Aelius Dionysius, a former proconsul of Africa, recognizing his services and affection for the community, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25001479.summary: A very short epitaph, likely Christian, commemorating a person named Don.

EDCS-25001482.translation: Claudius Mucatra of the colony gives this gift to Jupiter Best and Greatest Cernenus.
EDCS-25001482.summary: This is a votive dedication to Jupiter, likely by a colonist named Claudius Mucatra.

EDCS-25001484.translation: Afrania Ianuaria fulfilled her vow to Mercury Augustus.
EDCS-25001484.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by Afrania Ianuaria to the god Mercury Augustus.

EDCS-25001485.translation: Gaius Aburrius Felix Aburrianus willingly fulfilled his vow to Saturn Augustus.
EDCS-25001485.summary: This is a votive inscription by Gaius Aburrius Felix Aburrianus to Saturn Augustus.

EDCS-25001489.translation: Tiberius Claudius Helis with his family.
EDCS-25001489.summary: A simple dedication or memorial inscription for Tiberius Claudius Helis and his household.

EDCS-25001491.translation: Titus Minucius Felix, priest of Saturn, also known as Rogatus, willingly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-25001491.summary: This inscription records Titus Minucius Felix, a priest of Saturn, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-25001497.translation: I ask you who hold the underworld to you I commend Iulia Faustilla, daughter of Marius, that you may quickly take her away and have her among your number.
EDCS-25001497.summary: This is a magical invocation to a chthonic deity, asking for the soul of Iulia Faustilla to be taken into the underworld.

EDCS-25001498.translation: I ask you who hold the underworld to you I commend Iulia Faustilla, that you may quickly take her away and have her in the underworld among your number.
EDCS-25001498.summary: This is a magical invocation to a chthonic deity, asking for Iulia Faustilla to be taken into the underworld.

EDCS-25001500.translation: Let Successa be burned by love or desire for Successus...
EDCS-25001500.summary: This appears to be a love charm or curse, possibly intended to cause obsessive love, with some garbled or foreign text.

EDCS-25001501.translation: I adjure you, death-dweller, whatever you are, by the mighty names Salbathalab Authgerotabal Basutatheo Aleo Samabethor, bind the horses whose names and attributes I entrust to you in this vessel: Roseon, Silvanus, Servatus, Love, Zephyrus, Blandus, Imbraeus, Deiuitas, Mariscus, Rapidus, Orientus, Arborustus, and of the Venetians: Heminentes, Dignes, Leno, Paizon, Chrysaspas, Argutus, Dereisor, Phrugiphorus, Euphrates, Sanctus, Aethops, Praeclarus. Bind for them their speed, their strength, their spirit, their impetus, their swiftness. Take away their victory, impede their feet, cripple them, disable them, so that tomorrow in the hippodrome they may not be able to run, nor walk, nor win, nor exit the gates of the stables, nor advance in the arena, nor round the turning posts, but may they fall with their charioteers: Euprepes, the son of Telesphorus, also known as Gentius, and Phileikos, and Dionysius the drinker and insatiable. I command you Ablathanalabas and Anchrephronephiphoubin, bind the horses whose names and attributes I have entrusted to you in this vessel: Roseon, Silvanus, Servatus, Love, Zephyrus, Blandus, Imbraeus, Deiuitas, Mariscus, Rapidus, Orientus, Arborustus, and of the Venetians: Heminentes, Dignes, Leno, Paizon, Chrysaspas, Argutus, Dereisor, Phrugiphorus, Euphrates, Sanctus, Aethops, Praeclarus. Bind for them their speed, their strength, their spirit, their impetus, their swiftness. Take away their victory, impede their feet, cripple them, disable them, so that tomorrow in the hippodrome they may not be able to run, nor walk, nor win, nor exit the gates of the stables, nor advance in the arena, nor round the turning posts, but may they fall with their charioteers: Protus, and Phileikos, and Narcissus. Bind their hands for them. Wrap their reins into the harnesses. Take away their victory, their dismount, and their sight, so that they may not be able to see their opponents while driving, but rather snatch them from their chariots and throw them to the ground, so that they may fall by themselves in any part of the hippodrome, dragging themselves, especially at the turning posts, with injury to their bodies and their horses, already, quickly.
EDCS-25001501.summary: This is a complex magical curse inscribed on a tablet, intended to cripple the horses and charioteers of opposing factions in a chariot race, ensuring victory for the patron's faction.

EDCS-25001502.translation: I adjure you, death-dweller, whatever you are, by the mighty names Insydunasoi parac oaina agiathea simouebuarre karopasi ounethka seurōai echmasiroul aebbo r iaompsonpa. Bind the horses of the green faction whose names I entrust to you: Dareius, Agilus, Pardus, Pougiones, Dardanos, Einachos, Pretiōsus, Prunicus, Nimbus, Maurus, Victor, Prophicius, Aegyptius, Tingitanus. Bind for them their speed, their strength, their spirit, their impetus, their swiftness. Take away their victory, impede their feet, cripple them, dislocate their limbs, so that tomorrow in the hippodrome they may not be able to come and run, nor walk, nor win, nor exit the gates of the stables, nor advance in the arena, nor round the turning posts, but may they fall with their charioteers: Protus, and Phileikos, and Narcissus. I command you Ablathanalaas and Anchrephronephiphoubin, bind the horses of the green faction whose names I have entrusted to you: Dareius, Agilus, Pardus, Pougiones, Dardanos, Einachos, Pretiōsus, Prunicus, Nimbus, Maurus, Victor, Prophicius, Aegyptius, Tingitanus. Bind for them speed, feet, victory, impetus, spirit, swiftness. Cripple them, dislocate their limbs, so that tomorrow in the hippodrome they may not be able to run, nor walk, nor win, nor exit the gates of the stables, nor advance in the arena, nor round the turning posts, but may they fall with their charioteers: Protus, and Phileikos, and Narcissus. Bind their hands for them. Wrap their reins into the harnesses. Take away their victory, their dismount, and their sight, so that they may not be able to see their opponents while driving, but rather snatch them from their chariots and throw them to the ground, so that they may fall in any part of the hippodrome, especially at the turning posts, with injury to their bodies and legs, already, quickly, quickly, quickly, quickly, bind, bind, bind them.
EDCS-25001502.summary: This is a long and detailed magical curse tablet, similar to EDCS-25001501, aimed at causing the downfall of horses and charioteers, specifically targeting the 'green' faction in a chariot race.

EDCS-25001507.translation: to the divine Nerva, chief priest
EDCS-25001507.summary: This is a dedication to Emperor Nerva, who held the office of pontifex maximus.

EDCS-25001513.summary: This is a title likely referring to a military victory against the Sarmatians, possibly belonging to an emperor.

EDCS-25001514.translation: in the power of the Parthian
EDCS-25001514.summary: This phrase refers to imperial authority over the Parthian region, likely part of an emperor's titulature.

EDCS-25001515.translation: to the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Caro Pius Felix Invictus Augustus, chief priest, greatest Parthian, greatest German, with tribunician power for the second time, consul for the second time, father of the country, proconsul; Gaius Valerius Gallianus Honoratianus, a most distinguished man, curator of the affairs of Carthage, dedicated to his divine will and majesty.
EDCS-25001515.summary: This is a dedication by a high-ranking official, Gaius Valerius Gallianus Honoratianus, to Emperor Carus, praising his titles and power.

EDCS-25001518.translation: of the region and to the people of his province of Africa
EDCS-25001518.summary: This fragment likely refers to a dedication or grant related to the province of Africa.

EDCS-25001524.translation: to our lord Flavius Valentinus Victor and Triumphant, always Augustus, a most distinguished man, the proconsul of the province of Africa, judging in sacred authority.
EDCS-25001524.summary: This is a dedication to Emperor Valentinian, honoring him and mentioning the proconsul of Africa, Julius Festus.

EDCS-25001527.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely part of a dedication to one or more emperors, referring to them as 'our Lords'.

EDCS-25001531.summary: This is a dedication to the syncretic Greco-Egyptian deity Pluto Sarapis.

EDCS-25001533.translation: Sextius Rusticus, a most distinguished man, proconsul of the province of Africa, completed this at his own expense.
EDCS-25001533.summary: This is a dedication by Sextius Rusticus, the proconsul of Africa, who funded the construction or completion of a monument.

EDCS-25001534.translation: augur, quaestor, fought with the Transpadanes; with thousands of enemies slain, he captured them and captives.
EDCS-25001534.summary: This inscription likely commemorates the military achievements of an augur and quaestor who fought and captured enemies in the Transpadane region.

EDCS-25001536.translation: He restored it into a better form, proconsul of the province of Africa.
EDCS-25001536.summary: This inscription records the restoration of something by the proconsul of Africa, likely during the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-25001537.translation: To the quaestor, tribune of the plebs, proconsul of Africa.
EDCS-25001537.summary: This is a dedication to an official who held multiple significant political offices, including quaestor, tribune of the plebs, and proconsul of Africa, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-25001538.translation: Consul-designate, vicar of the city of Rome.
EDCS-25001538.summary: This inscription mentions a consul-designate and a vicar of the city of Rome, suggesting a context of Roman political hierarchy, possibly from the late Roman Republic or early imperial period.

EDCS-25001540.text_edition: \n Raniae Flaviae Iulianae Optatae clarissimae feminae matri Flaviorum Flaviani clarissimi pueri et Optatae clarissimae filiae et Flavianillae clarissimae puellae colonia Ammaedarensium sua pecunia fecit\n
EDCS-25001540.translation: The colony of Ammaedarum, at its own expense, made this for Rania Flavia Iuliana Optata, most distinguished woman, mother of Flavius Flavianus, most distinguished boy, and of Optata, most distinguished daughter, and of Flavianilla, most distinguished girl.
EDCS-25001540.summary: This is a public dedication by the colony of Ammaedarum honoring Rania Flavia Iuliana Optata and her children, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25001541.translation: Sabinus the patrician to the sweetest.
EDCS-25001541.summary: This is a personal dedication from Sabinus, a patrician, to an unspecified recipient, likely a personal inscription or a dedication of a gift, possibly from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-25001545.summary: This inscription records Artemidorus, who served as a procurator (an imperial financial official) under Augustus, dating it to the early imperial period.

EDCS-25001553.translation: Pompeius Faustinus to his fatherland, Carthage.
EDCS-25001553.summary: This is a dedication by Pompeius Faustinus to his homeland, Carthage, likely expressing civic pride or devotion, possibly from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-25001558.summary: This inscription simply states 'priest forever', likely referring to a religious office and expressing perpetual dedication to a deity or cult, possibly from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-25001571.translation: Alexander, freedman of Alexander, priest, elected, also put on games by decree of the decurions in the place of his grandfather Gnaeus Calvinius Alexander.
EDCS-25001571.summary: This inscription records a freedman named Alexander who served as a priest and sponsored games in honor of his grandfather, by decree of the local council, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-25001576.translation: S. Claudius Quin Celad Felix V Faustus Iulius A.
EDCS-25001576.summary: This inscription appears to be a list of names, possibly related to a family or a group, with Roman cognomina and gentilicia, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-25001577.translation: Herculanus, son of Narius, Aurelius An Bassus Quintus Felix, consul.
EDCS-25001577.summary: This inscription lists individuals, including Herculanus and Aurelius An Bassus Quintus Felix, who held a consulship, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-25001578.translation: Marcius Sextilius Ho, from Pulla, nicknamed Apelles, son of Flavius H.
EDCS-25001578.summary: This inscription appears to be an incomplete funerary epitaph or a name on a monument, mentioning personal names and tribal affiliations.

EDCS-25001579.translation: His heirs erected this for Sextus Atilius Rogatianus, a primipilaris, with the care of Publius Nonius Felix, a distinguished primipilaris and his father-in-law.
EDCS-25001579.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by the heirs of Sextus Atilius Rogatianus, with the monument overseen by his father-in-law, also a primipilaris.

EDCS-25001582.summary: This is a very brief inscription identifying 'Clutorianus' as a Roman knight.

EDCS-25001583.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that praises an individual as a distinguished man.

EDCS-25001585.translation: [---] was settled, enrolled, prefect with the power of delivering judgment, duovir, curator of the republic.
EDCS-25001585.summary: This fragmentary inscription lists several high-ranking civic and judicial offices held by an individual, possibly dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-25001586.summary: This inscription records an individual's priestly role in the first year of their tenure.

EDCS-25001587.translation: The public decreed a statue for the funeral.
EDCS-25001587.summary: This inscription records a public decree for a statue to honor a funeral.

EDCS-25001588.translation: Autumn, winter, spring, summer; September, October, November, December, January, February, March, April, May, June, July, August.
EDCS-25001588.summary: This inscription lists the names of the seasons and months, possibly related to a calendar or a symbolic representation of time.

EDCS-25001589.summary: This inscription mentions a person named Scorpianus, with an unclear reference to 'adamatum'.

EDCS-25001591.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Flavius Fraternus, soldier of the VII Gemina Felix legion, centuria of Apulo, lived 28 years, served 9 years, is buried here. Valerius Flavius, of the centuria of the primipilaris, had this made.
EDCS-25001591.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Flavius Fraternus, a soldier who served in the VII Gemina Felix legion, detailing his age, service length, and burial location, with the monument prepared by Valerius Flavius.

EDCS-25001592.translation: Caius Iulius Rogatus, veteran, devout, lived 80 years; he rests here.
EDCS-25001592.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Caius Iulius Rogatus, a veteran, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25001593.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Quintus Iulius Victorinus, a soldier of the I Urban Cohort, lived 29 years and 3 months; he is buried here.
EDCS-25001593.summary: This is a tombstone for Quintus Iulius Victorinus, a soldier, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25001594.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Publius Licinius Themistocles, also known as Probatus, freedman of Publius Licinius Crispinus, procurator of the Augusti, made a cup for him who deserved well; he is buried here.
EDCS-25001594.summary: This tombstone records Publius Licinius Themistocles, a freedman and procurator's freedman, who made a cup for someone deserving, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25001595.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Priscus, a dutiful slave of the procurator Alexandrus, lived 4 years, 4 months, and 26 days; Felix, his father, made this [monument].
EDCS-25001595.summary: This tombstone records Priscus, a slave of a procurator, and notes his lifespan and the maker of the tombstone, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25001596.translation: Dedicated to the spirits of the departed. Titus Flavius Laetus, freedman of the Emperor, a clerk, dutiful, lived for 70 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-25001596.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Titus Flavius Laetus, a freedman and clerk, who lived to be 70 years old.

EDCS-25001597.translation: Dedicated to the spirits of the departed. Titus Flavius Tertius, freedman of the Emperor, a clerk, dutiful, lived for 70 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-25001597.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Titus Flavius Tertius, a freedman and clerk, who lived to be 70 years old.

EDCS-25001598.translation: Fortunatus, a dutiful slave and keeper of the archive of Caesar, lived 45 years; Victoria made this for her dutiful companion.
EDCS-25001598.summary: This tombstone records Fortunatus, a slave and archive keeper, and was made by his companion Victoria, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25001599.translation: Dedicated to the spirits of the departed. Donatus, freedman of the Emperor, assistant clerk, dutiful, lived for 50 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-25001599.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Donatus, a freedman and assistant clerk, who lived to be 50 years old.

EDCS-25001600.translation: Dedicated to the spirits of the departed. To Eminenti, assistant clerk of the Emperor, who lived for 30 years, 9 months, and 6 days. His brother Phaenippus erected this.
EDCS-25001600.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Eminenti, an assistant clerk, erected by his brother Phaenippus.

EDCS-25001601.translation: Dedicated to the spirits of the departed. Eugramus, a slave and assistant clerk of the Emperors, dutiful, lived for 33 years and 5 months. He is buried here.
EDCS-25001601.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Eugramus, an imperial slave and assistant clerk, who lived to be 33 years old.

EDCS-25001602.translation: Dedicated to the spirits of the departed. Julius Terminalis, dutiful, lived for 81 years and 5 months and 4 days. This was arranged by Terminalis his grandson, through Phaenippus, assistant clerk of our Emperor. He is buried here.
EDCS-25001602.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Julius Terminalis, who lived to be 81 years old, arranged by his grandson Terminalis via an imperial assistant clerk.

EDCS-25001603.translation: Dedicated to the spirits of the departed. Primus, a slave and assistant clerk of the Emperor, dutiful, lived for 43 years. Victoria, his dutiful daughter, lived for 8 years. Primigenia, his dutiful daughter, lived for 3 years. Fortunata, freedwoman of the Emperor, erected this for her deserving husband and children. They are buried here.
EDCS-25001603.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Primus, his two daughters, and his wife Fortunata, erected by Fortunata for her family, all of whom were associated with imperial service.

EDCS-25001604.translation: Dedicated to the spirits of the departed. Priscus, a slave of our Emperor, assistant clerk, lived for 22 years, 3 months, and 7 days. He is buried here.
EDCS-25001604.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Priscus, an imperial slave and assistant clerk, who lived to be 22 years old.

EDCS-25001605.translation: Dedicated to the spirits of the departed. Quietus, a slave of the Emperor, assistant clerk, dutiful, lived for 43 years and 7 months. He is buried here.
EDCS-25001605.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Quietus, an imperial slave and assistant clerk, who lived to be 43 years old.

EDCS-25001606.translation: Dedicated to the spirits of the departed. Salvius, a slave of the Emperor, assistant clerk, lived for 40 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-25001606.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Salvius, an imperial slave and assistant clerk, who lived to be 40 years old.

EDCS-25001607.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Simplex, a dutiful slave and assistant in the archives of our Caesar, lived 25 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-25001607.summary: This tombstone records Simplex, a slave and assistant in the archives, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25001608.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Vindex, a dutiful slave and assistant in the archives of Augustus, lived 50 years; Silvanus, his colleague, made this for him who deserved well; he is buried here.
EDCS-25001608.summary: This tombstone records Vindex, a slave and archive assistant, and was made by his colleague Silvanus, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25001610.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Africanus, assistant to Caesar's tabularii of the military treasury, lived piously for 22 years. His father, Africanus, made this.
EDCS-25001610.summary: This is a tombstone for Africanus, an assistant to the imperial treasury's scribes, erected by his father.

EDCS-25001611.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Primigenius, a dutiful slave and assistant from the records of Augustus, lived 45 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-25001611.summary: This tombstone records Primigenius, a slave and assistant from the records, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25001612.translation: Processus, a dutiful slave and assistant from the records of our Caesar, lived 40 years; Numisia Benedicta, his daughter, supervised his burial here.
EDCS-25001612.summary: This tombstone records Processus, a slave and assistant from the records, whose burial was supervised by his daughter, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25001613.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Victor, a dutiful slave and assistant from the records of Augustus, lived 26 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-25001613.summary: This tombstone records Victor, a slave and assistant from the records, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25001614.translation: To the spirits of the departed. To Victor and Urbica, dutiful slaves of Augustus, their most dutiful parents. Iucundus, freedman of Augustus, assistant from the imperial correspondence, renovated the space permitted by [the law]. Victor lived 102 years, and Urbica lived 80 years; they are buried here.
EDCS-25001614.summary: This tombstone records the exceptionally long lives of Victor and Urbica, slaves and parents, and was renovated by their son Iucundus, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25001615.translation: Attalus, servant of Caesar, a scribe, lived piously for 19 years. His pious mother made this.
EDCS-25001615.summary: This tombstone is for Attalus, a scribe and servant of Caesar, dedicated by his mother.

EDCS-25001616.translation: Dedicated to the Divine Spirits. Castus, a pious freedman librarian of the emperors, lived 45 years, 11 months, and 24 days; he is buried here.
EDCS-25001616.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Castus, a freedman librarian of the emperors, who lived to be 45 years old.

EDCS-25001617.translation: Clarus, servant of our Caesar, a scribe, lived for 25 years. He rests here.
EDCS-25001617.summary: This is a tombstone for Clarus, a scribe and servant of Caesar, who lived for 25 years.

EDCS-25001618.translation: Fortunatus, a pious freedman librarian of the emperor, lived 39 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-25001618.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Fortunatus, a freedman librarian of the emperor, who lived to be 39 years old.

EDCS-25001619.translation: Heliodorus, a pious freedman librarian of the emperor, lived 21 years.
EDCS-25001619.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Heliodorus, a freedman librarian of the emperor, who lived to be 21 years old.

EDCS-25001620.translation: Dedicated to the Divine Spirits. Receptus, a freedman librarian of the emperor, lived 26 years and 5 months. Receptus, his father, [dedicated this].
EDCS-25001620.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Receptus, a freedman librarian of the emperor, who lived to be 26 years old, dedicated by his father.

EDCS-25001621.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Alexander, servant of our Caesar, a scribe, lived piously for 40 years. He rests here. Flavia Atalante made this for her husband from her own means.
EDCS-25001621.summary: This tombstone records Alexander, a scribe and servant of Caesar, who lived for 40 years, and was dedicated by his wife Flavia Atalante.

EDCS-25001622.translation: Dedicated to the Divine Spirits. Cilix, a pious verna (born in the household) and notary of our emperors, lived 30 years and 5 days; he is buried here.
EDCS-25001622.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Cilix, a verna and notary of the emperors, who lived to be 30 years old.

EDCS-25001623.translation: Dedicated to the Divine Spirits. Primus, a pious freedman and trainer of couriers of our emperor, made this for Rogatus, his dearest brother. He lived 70 years, 3 months, and 15 days; he is buried here.
EDCS-25001623.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Primus, a freedman and trainer of couriers of the emperor, who lived to be 70 years old, dedicated by his brother.

EDCS-25001624.translation: Dedicated to the Divine Spirits. Alexander, a pious freedman courier of the emperor, lived 25 years; he is buried here. Primigenia, his mother, made this.
EDCS-25001624.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Alexander, a freedman courier of the emperor, who lived to be 25 years old, dedicated by his mother.

EDCS-25001625.translation: Dedicated to the Divine Spirits. Coetus Chorentus, a pious courier, lived 23 years and 9 months; he is buried here.
EDCS-25001625.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Coetus Chorentus, a courier, who lived to be 23 years old.

EDCS-25001626.translation: Crescens, servant of Augustus, formerly a courier, lived piously for 45 years. His daughter Felicitas made this for her pious father. He rests here.
EDCS-25001626.summary: This tombstone is for Crescens, a courier and servant of Augustus who lived for 45 years, erected by his daughter Felicitas.

EDCS-25001627.translation: Dionysius, a scribe, lived piously for 50 years. His son Dionysius made this out of piety.
EDCS-25001627.summary: This tombstone honors Dionysius, a scribe, who lived for 50 years, and was dedicated by his son.

EDCS-25001628.translation: Dedicated to the Divine Spirits. Primula the pious lived one year, 2 months, and 10 days; she is buried here. Facetianus, a tabularius (clerk or accountant) of the emperors, made this.
EDCS-25001628.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Primula, a child, who lived for just over one year, dedicated by Facetianus, an imperial tabularius.

EDCS-25001629.translation: Dedicated to the Divine Spirits. Faustus, a pious verna (born in the household) and tabularius (clerk or accountant) of the emperor, lived [XX] years. Victoricus, a pious verna and tabularius of the emperor, lived 11 years, 4 months, and 5 days. His father made this for his most pious son; he is buried here.
EDCS-25001629.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Victoricus, a young son of an imperial tabularius, who lived to be 11 years old, dedicated by his father.

EDCS-25001630.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Felix, a scribe, son of Donata, servant of our Caesar, pious, lived about 40 years. Victoria, his wife, made this. He is buried here.
EDCS-25001630.summary: This is a tombstone for Felix, a scribe and servant of Caesar, erected by his wife Victoria.

EDCS-25001631.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Gallus, a scribe, servant of our Caesar, pious, lived 28 years and 12 days. Eugenia, wife of Gallus, servant of our Caesar, also lived 28 years and 3 months. He is buried here.
EDCS-25001631.summary: This is a tombstone for Gallus, a scribe and servant of Caesar, and his wife Eugenia, also a servant of Caesar.

EDCS-25001632.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Eusebes, lived piously for 4 years, 11 months, and 17 days. Hermeros made this for his subordinate, Eusebes, a scribe of Augustus.
EDCS-25001632.summary: This tombstone records Eusebes, who lived for 4 years, 11 months, and 17 days, and was dedicated by his superior, Hermeros, an imperial scribe.

EDCS-25001633.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Natalis, a scribe, servant of Augustus, lived [some years]. He is buried here.
EDCS-25001633.summary: This is a tombstone for Natalis, a scribe and servant of Augustus, with incomplete life details.

EDCS-25001634.translation: Flavia Fortunata, his most pious mother. Primigenius, a scribe of Augustus, made this at his own expense. She rests here.
EDCS-25001634.summary: This tombstone honors Flavia Fortunata, erected by her son Primigenius, an imperial scribe.

EDCS-25001635.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Saturninus, a scribe of Augustus, lived piously for 25 years. He rests here.
EDCS-25001635.summary: This tombstone is for Saturninus, a scribe and servant of Augustus, who lived for 25 years.

EDCS-25001636.translation: Tertius, a scribe of our Caesar, pious, lived 28 years. Euprasia made this for her pious companion.
EDCS-25001636.summary: This is a tombstone for Tertius, a scribe of Caesar, erected by his companion Euprasia.

EDCS-25001637.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Publius Aelius Victor mesor agrorum pius vixit annis XXXXVIIII Quartio frater pius fecit hic situs est\n
EDCS-25001637.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Publius Aelius Victor, surveyor of lands, lived piously for 49 years. His brother Quartio, also pious, made this. He rests here.
EDCS-25001637.summary: This tombstone records Publius Aelius Victor, a land surveyor, who lived for 49 years, and was erected by his brother Quartio.

EDCS-25001638.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Didymus, a slave of the Emperor, a land surveyor, devout, lived 46 years; he lies here. Iulia Primiginia, his wife, made this from her own means.
EDCS-25001638.summary: A tombstone recording the death of Didymus, an imperial slave and land surveyor, erected by his wife.

EDCS-25001639.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Titus Flavius Apsens, a land surveyor, pious, lived 26 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-25001639.summary: This is a tombstone for Titus Flavius Apsens, a land surveyor.

EDCS-25001640.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Titus Flavius Dapnus, a freedman of the Emperor, a land surveyor, devout, lived 90 years. Iulia Fortunata made this for her most devoted husband; he lies here.
EDCS-25001640.summary: A tombstone commemorating Titus Flavius Dapnus, an imperial freedman and land surveyor, erected by his wife.

EDCS-25001641.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Victor, in charge of the Emperor's pack animals, devout, lived 60 years; he lies here.
EDCS-25001641.summary: A tombstone recording the death of Victor, who was responsible for the Emperor's pack animals, noting his piety and age.

EDCS-25001642.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Anteros, a slave of the Emperor, a runner, devout, lived 40 years. Flavia Tyche made this for her companion from her own means; he lies here.
EDCS-25001642.summary: A tombstone for Anteros, an imperial slave and runner, erected by his female companion Flavia Tyche.

EDCS-25001643.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Campanus, a slave of our Emperor, a runner, devout, lived 55 years; he lies here. Flavia made this for her devout companion.
EDCS-25001643.summary: A tombstone for Campanus, an imperial slave and runner, erected by his companion Flavia.

EDCS-25001644.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Chryseros, a slave of the Emperor, a runner, lived 60 years; he lies here.
EDCS-25001644.summary: A tombstone for Chryseros, an imperial slave and runner, stating his age at death.

EDCS-25001645.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Donatus, a household slave (verna) and footman of Augustus, pious, lived 68 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-25001645.summary: This is a tombstone for Donatus, a household slave and footman of Augustus.

EDCS-25001646.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Felix, son of Spica, footman, servant of Augustus, pious, lived 70 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-25001646.summary: This is a tombstone for Felix, a footman and servant of Augustus.

EDCS-25001647.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Fortunatus, footman, servant of Augustus, pious, lived 39 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-25001647.summary: This is a tombstone for Fortunatus, a footman and servant of Augustus.

EDCS-25001648.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Fortunatus, footman, servant of Augustus, pious, lived 20 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-25001648.summary: This is a tombstone for Fortunatus, a footman and servant of Augustus.

EDCS-25001649.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Fructus, a slave of our Emperor, a runner, devout, lived 31 years; he lies here.
EDCS-25001649.summary: A tombstone for Fructus, an imperial slave and runner, noting his piety and age at death.

EDCS-25001650.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Fortunatus, a tutor, servant of Caesar, pious, lived 95 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-25001650.summary: This is a tombstone for Fortunatus, a tutor and servant of Caesar.

EDCS-25001651.translation: Dedicated to the departed spirits. Optatus, devoted freedman of Augustus, a devoted teacher, lived 45 years and 4 months; he is buried here.
EDCS-25001651.summary: A funerary inscription for Optatus, a freedman of Augustus and a paedagogus, who lived 45 years and 4 months.

EDCS-25001652.translation: Dedicated to the departed spirits. Nus, a teacher.
EDCS-25001652.summary: A funerary inscription recording the name of Nus, identified as a paedagogus.

EDCS-25001653.translation: Dedicated to the departed spirits. Dexter, servant and temple attendant of our Emperor, devoted, lived about 85 years; his body was properly cremated and honorably buried by his son; he is buried here.
EDCS-25001653.summary: A funerary inscription for Dexter, a servant and temple attendant of the Emperor, who lived about 85 years and was buried by his son.

EDCS-25001654.translation: Faustus, son of Speratus, a slave of Caesar and keeper of the temple stores, lived 5 years; he lies here.
EDCS-25001654.summary: A tombstone for Faustus, the son of an imperial temple keeper, who died at a very young age.

EDCS-25001655.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Synhetus, a temple keeper for the Emperor, lived 95 years; he lies here.
EDCS-25001655.summary: A tombstone for Synhetus, an imperial temple keeper, recording his long lifespan.

EDCS-25001656.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. For Marcus Cocceius Verecundus and Verus, worthy of remembrance for Pythagoras, freedman and procurator of the Emperor, who served well; he lies here.
EDCS-25001656.summary: A tombstone honoring two individuals, Marcus Cocceius Verecundus and Verus, for Pythagoras, an imperial freedman and procurator, likely erected by colleagues or subordinates.

EDCS-25001657.translation: Flavia Successa, freedwoman of Augustus, First Lady, and Princeps, servant of Augustus, made this from her own resources for her most loving wife, pious, lived 45 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-25001657.summary: A funerary inscription set up by Flavia Successa for her wife, Princeps, a servant of Augustus, who lived 45 years.

EDCS-25001658.translation: Dedicated to the departed spirits. To Claudia Euresis, devoted daughter of Tiberius, who lived 17 years. Valentinus, from the cohort of the Emperor's chamberlains, made this for his most beloved wife, pious, who followed him to the province of Africa; she is buried here.
EDCS-25001658.summary: A funerary inscription set up by Valentinus for his wife, Claudia Euresis, who lived 17 years and followed him to Africa.

EDCS-25001659.translation: Dedicated to the departed spirits. Abascantulus, devoted freedman of Augustus, lived 1 year and 11 months; he is buried here. Abascantus, his father and freedman of Augustus, made this for his most devoted son.
EDCS-25001659.summary: A funerary inscription for Abascantulus, son of Abascantus, both freedmen of Augustus, who died aged 1 year and 11 months.

EDCS-25001660.translation: Dedicated to the departed spirits. Abascantus, devoted, lived 60 years. Secundina, his daughter, devoted, lived 32 years; they are buried here.
EDCS-25001660.summary: A funerary inscription for Abascantus, who lived 60 years, and his daughter Secundina, who lived 32 years.

EDCS-25001661.translation: Dedicated to the departed spirits. Publius Acutilius Ampliatus, devoted, lived 35 years and 7 days; he is buried here.
EDCS-25001661.summary: A funerary inscription for Publius Acutilius Ampliatus, who lived 35 years and 7 days.

EDCS-25001662.translation: Dedicated to the departed spirits. Acutilia Monica, devoted, lived 22 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-25001662.summary: A funerary inscription for Acutilia Monica, who lived 22 years.

EDCS-25001663.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Adaucta lived 45 years.
EDCS-25001663.summary: A tombstone recording the death of Adaucta at the age of 45.

EDCS-25001664.translation: To Caesar, lived 40 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-25001664.summary: A funerary inscription for an individual who lived 40 years and was dedicated to Caesar.

EDCS-25001665.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Aecus lived piously for 65 years and 7 months. Felix, his pious son, lived for 25 years and 7 months. Urbanus, his pious son, lived for 22 years and 4 months. His pious mother made this.
EDCS-25001665.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lives of Aecus and his two sons, Felix and Urbanus, with the epitaph erected by their mother.

EDCS-25001666.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Aelius Amphion lived piously for 40 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-25001666.summary: A funerary epitaph for Aelius Amphion, recording his pious life and burial.

EDCS-25001667.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Publius Aelius Benenatus lived 4 years.
EDCS-25001667.summary: A tombstone recording the death of Publius Aelius Benenatus at the age of 4.

EDCS-25001668.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Publius Aelius Felix, freedman of the Emperor, lived for 76 years, 9 months, 3 days, and 12 hours. He is buried here for Ostoria Procula, his well-deserving wife, concerning whom he made no complaint.
EDCS-25001668.summary: A funerary epitaph for Publius Aelius Felix, a freedman of the Emperor, and his wife Ostoria Procula, likely erected by her.

EDCS-25001669.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Aelius Primitivus lived for 30 years and 2 months and 15 days. Iulia Euplia made this for her well-deserving wife, concerning whom she made no complaint. She is buried here.
EDCS-25001669.summary: A funerary epitaph for Aelius Primitivus, erected by his wife Iulia Euplia.

EDCS-25001670.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Publius Aelius Primus, dearest son, lived for 23 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-25001670.summary: A funerary epitaph for Publius Aelius Primus, a young man, likely erected by his parents.

EDCS-25001671.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Aelia N
EDCS-25001671.summary: An incomplete funerary epitaph for Aelia N.

EDCS-25001672.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Aelia Venusta lived piously for 24 years. Saturus made this for his well-deserving wife.
EDCS-25001672.summary: A funerary epitaph for Aelia Venusta, erected by her husband Saturus.

EDCS-25001673.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Aemilia Quinta lived 31 years and rests here.
EDCS-25001673.summary: A tombstone recording the death of Aemilia Quinta at the age of 31.

EDCS-25001674.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Agileius Ampliatus lived 9 years and rests here.
EDCS-25001674.summary: A tombstone recording the death of Lucius Agileius Ampliatus at the age of 9.

EDCS-25001675.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Publius Albonius Ianuarius lived piously for 20 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-25001675.summary: A funerary epitaph for Publius Albonius Ianuarius, recording his pious life and burial.

EDCS-25001676.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Alethia, a pious servant of the Emperor, lived for 23 years. She is buried here. Primigenius, husband of the Emperor's servant, piously made this for his dutiful wife.
EDCS-25001676.summary: A funerary epitaph for Alethia, a servant of the Emperor, erected by her husband Primigenius.

EDCS-25001677.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Alexander, a pious servant of the Emperor, lived for 3 years and 11 months. He is buried here.
EDCS-25001677.summary: A funerary epitaph for Alexander, a young servant of the Emperor, recording his short life.

EDCS-25001678.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Alexander lived 22 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-25001678.summary: A funerary inscription recording the death and burial of Alexander, who lived 22 years.

EDCS-25001679.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Amabilis, devoted to Augustus, lived 39 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-25001679.summary: A funerary inscription recording the death and burial of Amabilis, who lived 39 years and was devoted to Augustus.

EDCS-25001680.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Amandus, a devoted slave of our Caesar, lived [X] years; he is buried here.
EDCS-25001680.summary: A funerary inscription recording the death and burial of Amandus, a devoted slave of Caesar, whose age is lost.

EDCS-25001681.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Amantianus the devoted lived 10 years, 3 months, and 10 days.
EDCS-25001681.summary: A funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Amantianus, who lived 10 years, 3 months, and 10 days.

EDCS-25001682.translation: Here is buried Ania Amoena, a devoted wife; she made [this].
EDCS-25001682.summary: A funerary inscription stating that Ania Amoena, a devoted wife, was buried here and likely commissioned the monument.

EDCS-25001683.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Anicetus, a devoted servant of the Emperor, lived 2 years and rests here. Felix and Laetina, his parents, made this.
EDCS-25001683.summary: A tombstone for Anicetus, a young imperial freedman, made by his parents.

EDCS-25001684.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Anneia Aphrodisia the devoted lived 40 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-25001684.summary: A funerary inscription recording the death and burial of Anneia Aphrodisia, who lived 40 years.

EDCS-25001685.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Anteros lived 4 years and 7 months.
EDCS-25001685.summary: A tombstone recording the death of Anteros at the age of 4 years and 7 months.

EDCS-25001686.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Aprilis, a devoted servant of the Emperor, lived 60 years and rests here. Iucundus made this for his deserving wife.
EDCS-25001686.summary: A tombstone for Aprilis, an imperial freedwoman, made by her husband Iucundus.

EDCS-25001687.translation: Attica, a devoted servant of Caesar, lived 10 years and rests here. Victoria made this for her dearest sister.
EDCS-25001687.summary: A tombstone for Attica, a freedwoman of Caesar, made by her sister Victoria.

EDCS-25001688.translation: Aucta, a devoted servant of our Emperor, lived 28 years and rests here. Dionysius, a fellow servant, made this for her merits.
EDCS-25001688.summary: A tombstone for Aucta, an imperial freedwoman, made by a fellow freedman, Dionysius.

EDCS-25001689.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Marcus Aufidius Rusticus the devoted lived 1 year, 7 months; he is buried here.
EDCS-25001689.summary: A funerary inscription recording the death and burial of Marcus Aufidius Rusticus, who lived 1 year and 7 months.

EDCS-25001690.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Aurelius Gemellus the devoted lived 36 years; his most devoted wife made [this]; he is buried here.
EDCS-25001690.summary: A funerary inscription recording the death and burial of Aurelius Gemellus, who lived 36 years, with his wife as the dedicator.

EDCS-25001691.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Aurelius Primitivus the devoted lived 22 years, 11 months; he is buried here.
EDCS-25001691.summary: A funerary inscription recording the death and burial of Aurelius Primitivus, who lived 22 years and 11 months.

EDCS-25001692.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Aurelia Harmonia lived 5 years.
EDCS-25001692.summary: A funerary inscription recording the death of Aurelia Harmonia, who lived 5 years.

EDCS-25001693.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Aurelia Crescentia, dutiful, lived 55 years and 9 months. Aurelius Victoricus, dutiful, lived 2 years and 9 months. He lies here buried.
EDCS-25001693.summary: A tombstone recording the ages of Aurelia Crescentia and Aurelius Victoricus, likely family members.

EDCS-25001694.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Baebia Nemesis, dutiful, lived 30 years. She lies here.
EDCS-25001694.summary: A tombstone recording the age of Baebia Nemesis.

EDCS-25001695.translation: Bathyllus, servant of the Emperor, lived 7 years and rests here.
EDCS-25001695.summary: A tombstone recording the death of Bathyllus, an imperial freedman, at the age of 7.

EDCS-25001696.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Blandus, a dutiful slave of our emperor, lived 35 years. He lies here.
EDCS-25001696.summary: A tombstone for Blandus, a slave of the emperor, recording his age.

EDCS-25001697.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Blandus, dutiful, lived 18 years and 33 days, who after the death of his mother lived 6 months and 23 days. He lies here. May the earth be light on you, may your bones rest well.
EDCS-25001697.summary: A tombstone for Blandus, recording his age and noting his death after his mother's.

EDCS-25001698.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Caecilius Felix lived 5 years, 2 months, and 11 days.
EDCS-25001698.summary: A tombstone recording the brief life of Lucius Caecilius Felix.

EDCS-25001699.translation: To the divine spirits. Sacred. Caecilia Nemesis, dutiful, lived for 4 years, 8 months, and [number] days.
EDCS-25001699.summary: A funerary epitaph for Caecilia Nemesis, recording her age at death, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25001700.translation: Caletyche, a dutiful servant of Augustus, lived for 30 years; she is laid here. Faustus for his dutiful fellow servant.
EDCS-25001700.summary: A funerary epitaph for Caletyche, a freedwoman of Augustus, with a dedication from Faustus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25001701.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Cambius Privatus, dutiful, lived 35 years. He lies here.
EDCS-25001701.summary: A tombstone recording the age of Cambius Privatus.

EDCS-25001702.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus Camurcius Fortunatus, dutiful, lived 53 years. He lies here.
EDCS-25001702.summary: A tombstone recording the age of Quintus Camurcius Fortunatus.

EDCS-25001703.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Cilnia Flora, dutiful, lived 52 years. Flavius Lupus made this for his most dutiful wife. She lies here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Ianuarius, dutiful, lived 1 year, 2 months, and 5 days. He lies here.
EDCS-25001703.summary: A tombstone dedicated by Flavius Lupus to his wife Cilnia Flora, also recording the death of Ianuarius.

EDCS-25001704.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Cinnas, a dutiful slave of our emperor, lived 12 years. He lies here.
EDCS-25001704.summary: A tombstone for Cinnas, a slave of the emperor, recording his age.

EDCS-25001705.translation: To the divine spirits. Sacred. Clemens, a dutiful servant of our emperor, lived for 33 years; he is laid here.
EDCS-25001705.summary: A funerary epitaph for Clemens, a slave of the emperor, recording his age at death, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25001706.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Clemens, a dutiful slave of Augustus, lived 1 year and 6 months. Optatus made this for his deserving son from his own property.
EDCS-25001706.summary: A tombstone dedicated by Optatus to his son Clemens, recording his age and the father's provision for the burial.

EDCS-25001707.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Communis lived piously for 8 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-25001707.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the burial of Communis, who died at the age of 8.

EDCS-25001708.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Cocceia Calethice lived piously for 32 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-25001708.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the burial of Cocceia Calethice, who died at the age of 32.

EDCS-25001709.translation: To the divine spirits. Sacred. Quintus Cornelius Felix Macrianus, dutiful, lived for 27 years; he is laid here. Appia Quadratilla, his dutiful wife, made this.
EDCS-25001709.summary: A funerary epitaph for Quintus Cornelius Felix Macrianus, with a dedication by his wife, Appia Quadratilla, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25001710.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Crescens, a pious slave of our emperor, lived for 81 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-25001710.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the burial of Crescens, a pious slave of the emperor, who died at the age of 81.

EDCS-25001711.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Dama, a slave of our emperor, lived for 70 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-25001711.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the burial of Dama, a slave of the emperor, who died at the age of 70.

EDCS-25001712.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Doryphorus lived piously for 10 years; he is buried here. Sacred to the Divine Shades. Veneria lived piously for 25 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-25001712.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the burial of two individuals, Doryphorus (aged 10) and Veneria (aged 25).

EDCS-25001713.translation: To the divine spirits. Sacred. Epaphroditus, a dutiful child-slave of Augustus, lived for one year and 17 days. O sweet little cheeks! He is laid here.
EDCS-25001713.summary: A funerary epitaph for Epaphroditus, a young slave of Augustus, noting his very early death and affectionately recalling his features, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25001714.translation: To the divine spirits. Sacred. Eugenes, a dutiful servant of Augustus, lived for 9 years; he is laid here.
EDCS-25001714.summary: A funerary epitaph for Eugenes, a slave of Augustus, recording his age at death, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25001715.translation: To the divine spirits. Sacred. Eutyches, dutiful, lived for 80 years; he is laid here. // To the divine spirits. Sacred. Amandus, dutiful, a servant of Augustus, lived for 80 years; he is laid here.
EDCS-25001715.summary: A funerary epitaph with two identical entries for Eutyches and Amandus, both dutiful and 80 years old, likely slaves of Augustus, suggesting perhaps a shared tomb or adjacent burials.

EDCS-25001716.translation: To the divine spirits. Sacred. Extricata, a dutiful servant of Augustus, lived for 40 years; she is laid here. Primus for his deserving wife.
EDCS-25001716.summary: A funerary epitaph for Extricata, a slave of Augustus, with a dedication from her husband Primus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25001717.translation: To the divine spirits. Sacred. Favor, a dutiful servant of Augustus, lived for 70 years; he is laid here.
EDCS-25001717.summary: A funerary epitaph for Favor, a slave of Augustus, recording his age at death, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25001718.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Faustilla lived piously for 48 years. Didymus, her pious son, is buried here.
EDCS-25001718.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the burial of Faustilla, who died at the age of 48, and mentioning her son Didymus.

EDCS-25001719.translation: To the divine spirits. Sacred. Faustinus, a dutiful servant of Augustus, lived for 18 years; he is laid here.
EDCS-25001719.summary: A funerary epitaph for Faustinus, a slave of Augustus, recording his age at death, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25001720.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Faustus, servant of the Emperor, lived piously for 21 years, 10 months, and 25 days; he rests here. Fortunatus, his father, made this for his pious son.
EDCS-25001720.summary: A tombstone set up by a father for his deceased son, Faustus, a freedman of the emperor, who died at the age of 21.

EDCS-25001721.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Felicula, a wife well-deserving, pious, lived 37 years and 4 months. Aelius Saturus made this for her; she rests here.
EDCS-25001721.summary: A tombstone for Felicula, the deceased wife of Aelius Saturus, who died at the age of 37.

EDCS-25001722.translation: Felix, servant of our Emperor, lived piously for 2 years; he rests here. Dassius and Nymphe, his parents, made this.
EDCS-25001722.summary: A tombstone for Felix, the deceased young son of Dassius and Nymphe, who was a servant of the emperor.

EDCS-25001723.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Felix, a pious slave of Augustus, is buried here.
EDCS-25001723.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the burial of Felix, a pious slave of Augustus.

EDCS-25001725.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Felix, servant of our Emperor, lived piously for 5 years; he rests here. Amiantus, his father, made this.
EDCS-25001725.summary: A tombstone for Felix, the deceased young son of Amiantus, who was a servant of the emperor.

EDCS-25001726.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Felix, servant of the Emperor, lived piously for 22 years; he rests here.
EDCS-25001726.summary: A tombstone for Felix, a servant of the Emperor, who died at the age of 22.

EDCS-25001728.translation: Felix of Hermes, deputy of the Emperor, lived for 30 years; he rests here.
EDCS-25001728.summary: A tombstone for Felix, deputy of the Emperor (vicarius Augusti), who died at the age of 30.

EDCS-25001729.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Titus Flavius Anicetus, a pious freedman of Augustus, lived for 77 years, 10 months, and 5 days; he is buried here.
EDCS-25001729.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the burial of Titus Flavius Anicetus, a freedman of Augustus, who died at the age of 77 years, 10 months, and 5 days.

EDCS-25001730.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Flavius Doryphorus lived piously for 70 years; he rests here.
EDCS-25001730.summary: A tombstone for Flavius Doryphorus, who died at the age of 70.

EDCS-25001731.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Titus Flavius Quartio lived piously for 50 years; he rests here.
EDCS-25001731.summary: A tombstone for Titus Flavius Quartio, who died at the age of 50.

EDCS-25001732.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Titus Flavius Successus lived piously for 35 years; he rests here.
EDCS-25001732.summary: A tombstone for Titus Flavius Successus, who died at the age of 35.

EDCS-25001733.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Flavia Doris lived piously for 24 years; she rests here. May your bones rest well; may the earth be light upon you.
EDCS-25001733.summary: A tombstone for Flavia Doris, who died at the age of 24, with a common epitaph wishing her a peaceful afterlife.

EDCS-25001734.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Flavia Felicula, dutiful, lived 70 years; she rests here.
EDCS-25001734.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Flavia Felicula, recording her lifespan and burial.

EDCS-25001735.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Flavia Maxima lived for 83 years. Venusta, her pious [daughter/relative], made this; she is buried here.
EDCS-25001735.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the burial of Flavia Maxima, who died at the age of 83, with the monument erected by Venusta.

EDCS-25001736.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Flavia Quarta lived piously for 40 years, 3 months, and 20 days. Salvius made this for his pious wife; she is buried here.
EDCS-25001736.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the burial of Flavia Quarta, who died at the age of 40 years, 3 months, and 20 days, with the monument erected by her husband Salvius.

EDCS-25001737.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Flavia Spes, freedwoman of Augustus, dutiful, lived 30 years; she rests here. May your bones rest well.
EDCS-25001737.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Flavia Spes, a freedwoman of Augustus, noting her lifespan and burial, with a wish for her repose.

EDCS-25001738.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Flavia Tyche, dutiful, lived 77 years. Quintus Bennius Restutus made this for his wife. She rests here.
EDCS-25001738.summary: This funerary epitaph records the death of Flavia Tyche, erected by her husband Quintus Bennius Restutus.

EDCS-25001739.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Fortunatus, servant of Augustus, lived 26 years; he rests here.
EDCS-25001739.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Fortunatus, a servant of Augustus, detailing his age at death and burial.

EDCS-25001740.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Fortunatus, a dutiful servant of the Emperor, lived 70 years. He rests here.
EDCS-25001740.summary: This funerary epitaph records the death of Fortunatus, a servant of the Emperor.
