EDCS-25001741.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Fortunatus, dutiful, lived 12 years. Primus, his brother and fellow servant, made this. He rests here.
EDCS-25001741.summary: This funerary epitaph records the death of Fortunatus, erected by his brother and fellow servant Primus.

EDCS-25001742.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Fortunatus, servant of Augustus, dutiful, lived 1 year, 6 months, 10 days; he rests here.
EDCS-25001742.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Fortunatus, a servant of Augustus, recording his very young age at death and burial.

EDCS-25001743.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Fortunatus, a dutiful native-born servant of the Emperor, lived 13 years, 6 months, 28 days. He rests here.
EDCS-25001743.summary: This funerary epitaph records the death of Fortunatus, a native-born servant of the Emperor, specifying his age in years, months, and days.

EDCS-25001744.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Fortunatus, dutiful, lived 1 year, 47 days. He rests here.
EDCS-25001744.summary: This funerary epitaph records the death of Fortunatus, specifying his age in years and days.

EDCS-25001745.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Fortunata, dutiful, lived 8 years, 1 month, 20 days. Fortunatus her father made this for his dutiful daughter; she rests here.
EDCS-25001745.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Fortunata, set up by her father Fortunatus, recording her young age and burial.

EDCS-25001746.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Fortunata, dutiful, lived 15 years. She rests here. Made with the care of her most dutiful father.
EDCS-25001746.summary: This funerary epitaph records the death of Fortunata, erected by her father.

EDCS-25001748.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Fructuosa, a well-deserving servant of our Emperor, dutiful wife, lived 32 years, 5 months. Aelius Primigenius made this for her. She rests here.
EDCS-25001748.summary: This funerary epitaph records the death of Fructuosa, a servant of the Emperor and wife, erected by her husband Aelius Primigenius.

EDCS-25001749.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Fuscus, a dutiful native-born servant of the Emperor, lived 69 years. He rests here.
EDCS-25001749.summary: This funerary epitaph records the death of Fuscus, a native-born servant of the Emperor.

EDCS-25001750.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Gaius, dutiful, lived 27 years, 6 months.
EDCS-25001750.summary: This funerary epitaph records the death of Gaius, specifying his age in years and months.

EDCS-25001751.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Gemellus, a dutiful servant, lived 12 years. He rests here.
EDCS-25001751.summary: This funerary epitaph records the death of Gemellus, a servant.

EDCS-25001753.translation: Gemellus lived 5 years, he is buried here, Gemellus, servant of Augustus.
EDCS-25001753.summary: This inscription records the burial of Gemellus, a servant of Augustus, who died at the age of 5.

EDCS-25001754.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Caius Geminius Asiaticus, dutiful, lived 6 years. His dutiful father, Asiaticus, made this. He is buried here.
EDCS-25001754.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Caius Geminius Asiaticus, who died at the age of 6, set up by his father.

EDCS-25001755.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Hecate, dutiful, lived 29 years, 7 months, 5 days; she rests here.
EDCS-25001755.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Hecate, detailing her age at death and burial.

EDCS-25001756.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Heliodorus, servant of Augustus, dutiful, lived 40 years; he rests here. Victoria his wife made this.
EDCS-25001756.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Heliodorus, a servant of Augustus, erected by his wife Victoria, recording his lifespan and burial.

EDCS-25001757.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Hilarus, dutiful servant of Augustus, lived 10 years, 6 months, and 6 days. He is buried here.
EDCS-25001757.summary: This funerary inscription commemorates Hilarus, a servant of Augustus, who lived for 10 years, 6 months, and 6 days.

EDCS-25001758.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Hilara, dutiful freedwoman of Augustus, lived 42 years, 5 months. Felix, servant of Augustus, made this for his well-deserving wife. She is buried here.
EDCS-25001758.summary: This inscription records the burial of Hilara, a freedwoman of Augustus, who lived to be 42 years and 5 months old, and was memorialized by her husband Felix.

EDCS-25001759.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Hospes, dutiful servant of our emperors, lived 18 years, 3 months, and 17 days. His brother made this for his deserving relation.
EDCS-25001759.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Hospes, a servant of the emperors, who died at the age of 18 years, 3 months, and 17 days, erected by his brother.

EDCS-25001760.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Ianuarius, dutiful homeborn servant of the Augusti, lived 6 years, 6 months, and 2 days. He is buried here.
EDCS-25001760.summary: This inscription records the burial of Ianuarius, a homeborn servant of the emperors, who died at the age of 6 years, 6 months, and 2 days.

EDCS-25001761.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Ianuarius, dutiful, lived 9 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-25001761.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Ianuarius, who died at the age of 9.

EDCS-25001762.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Ianuarius, dutiful, lived 45 years, six months, and 22 days. He is buried here.
EDCS-25001762.summary: This inscription records the burial of Ianuarius, who lived for 45 years, 6 months, and 22 days.

EDCS-25001763.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Ianuarius, dutiful servant of Augustus, lived 28 years, and 10 months. He is buried here.
EDCS-25001763.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Ianuarius, a servant of Augustus, who died at the age of 28 years and 10 months.

EDCS-25001765.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Ianuaria, dutiful, lived 21 years and 15 days. She is buried here.
EDCS-25001765.summary: This inscription records the burial of Ianuaria, who died at the age of 21 years and 15 days.

EDCS-25001766.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Ianuaria, dutiful, lived 18 years, 8 months; she rests here.
EDCS-25001766.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Ianuaria, recording her age at death and burial.

EDCS-25001767.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Imilia Rufina, dutiful, lived for 35 years, more or less.
EDCS-25001767.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Imilia Rufina, who lived for approximately 35 years.

EDCS-25001768.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Irene, dutiful, lived 5 months and 2 days, she is buried here.
EDCS-25001768.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Irene, who lived for 5 months and 2 days.

EDCS-25001769.translation: Her dutiful father made this for Iucundus, aged 20.
EDCS-25001769.summary: This is a funerary epitaph, likely a tombstone, for Iucundus who died at the age of 20.

EDCS-25001770.translation: Julius Heracleon to Julia Zosima, his well-deserving mother.
EDCS-25001770.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Julius Heracleon for his mother, Julia Zosima.

EDCS-25001771.translation: Gaius Julius Herma, freedman of Gaius, dutiful, lived 60 years; he rests here.
EDCS-25001771.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Gaius Julius Herma, a freedman, recording his lifespan and burial.

EDCS-25001772.translation: Iulius Rogatus made this. Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulia Rogata lived 30 years, 4 months. Iulius V[---]nus, 5 years old, rests here.
EDCS-25001772.summary: This inscription records the funerary monument erected by Iulius Rogatus, dedicating it to the departed spirits and listing the ages and burial of Iulia Rogata and Iulius V[---]nus.

EDCS-25001773.translation: To the spirits of the departed, sacred. Julius Valerius lived for 1 year, 2 months, 15 days.
EDCS-25001773.summary: A funerary inscription recording the short lifespan of a child named Julius Valerius, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25001774.translation: To the spirits of the departed, sacred. Iulia Campana, dutiful, lived for 35 years, 6 months, 8 days. She rests here.
EDCS-25001774.summary: A funerary epitaph for Iulia Campana, a woman who lived to 35 years, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25001775.translation: To the spirits of the departed, sacred. Iulia Campanu[la], lived for 5 years, 5 months, 10 days. She rests here.
EDCS-25001775.summary: A funerary epitaph for Iulia Campanula, a child who lived to 5 years, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25001776.translation: To the spirits of the departed, sacred. Iulia Gamice, dutiful, lived for 2 years. Iulius Caelestinus, her dutiful brother, lived for 1 year, 1 month. He rests here.
EDCS-25001776.summary: A funerary inscription for two siblings, Iulia Gamice and Iulius Caelestinus, likely children, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25001778.translation: To the spirits of the departed, sacred. Iulia Sissonia, dutiful, lived for 35 years. She rests here. Titus Flavius Romanus made [this] for his most dutiful, most holy, most indulgent wife, and also for Fundania Minor, his mother-in-law. [She] lived for 90 years. She rests here.
EDCS-25001778.summary: A tombstone set up by Titus Flavius Romanus for his wife Iulia Sissonia and his mother-in-law Fundania Minor, both deceased, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25001779.translation: To the spirits of the departed, sacred. Iulia Ultrix, dutiful, lived for 28 years. She rests here. Her foster children made [this] for her, on account of her merits.
EDCS-25001779.summary: A funerary inscription by the foster children of Iulia Ultrix, honoring her merits, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25001780.translation: To the sacred spirits of the departed. Laches, slave of our Caesar, dutiful, lived for 90 years. He rests here. Martialis made [this] for his deserving [father-in-law]. May his bones rest well.
EDCS-25001780.summary: A funerary monument for Laches, a slave of Caesar, erected by his son-in-law Martialis, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25001781.translation: Laeta, slave of Caesar, dutiful, lived for 40 years. Dionysius made [this] for his dutiful wife. She rests here. May your bones rest well. May the earth be light on you.
EDCS-25001781.summary: A tombstone for Laeta, a slave of Caesar, erected by her husband Dionysius, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25001782.translation: Sacred to Laevius A., who lived 51 years, PV; he is buried here.
EDCS-25001782.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Laevius A., who lived 51 years and is buried here.

EDCS-25001783.translation: To the sacred spirits of the departed. Lesbia, slave of Augustus, dutiful, lived for 26 years. She rests here.
EDCS-25001783.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lesbia, a slave of Augustus, who died at 26, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25001784.translation: To the spirits of the departed, sacred. Liberal[is...
EDCS-25001784.summary: An incomplete funerary inscription beginning with the name Liberalis, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25001785.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Licinia Ianuaria, devoted, lived for 37 years and 8 months.
EDCS-25001785.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Licinia Ianuaria, recording her age at death, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25001786.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Lucanus, devoted slave of our Caesar, lived for 85 years. Iulia Fortunata, devoted, lived for 65 years. They are laid here.
EDCS-25001786.summary: A joint funerary inscription for Lucanus and Iulia Fortunata, both slaves of Caesar, detailing their ages and burial, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25001787.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Lucilla Felicitas, devoted, lived for 13 years and 6 months. She is laid here.
EDCS-25001787.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucilla Felicitas, recording her young age at death, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25001788.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Lucillus, dutiful, lived 2 years, 3 months, and 7 days.
EDCS-25001788.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucillus, who lived for 2 years, 3 months, and 7 days.

EDCS-25001789.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Martialis, a dutiful freedman of Augustus, lived 35 years and 7 months; his spouse made this; he is buried here.
EDCS-25001789.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Martialis, a freedman of Augustus, erected by his spouse.

EDCS-25001790.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Marcus Optatus Amillus, dutiful, lived 35 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-25001790.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcus Optatus Amillus, who lived for 35 years.

EDCS-25001791.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Maxima, devoted to Augustus, lived for 2 years, 8 months, and 9 days. She is laid here. Primigenius made this for his most devoted and dearest daughter, belonging to Augustus.
EDCS-25001791.summary: A funerary inscription for Maxima, daughter of Primigenius and likely a member of the imperial household (indicated by 'Aug(usti)'), recording her very young age and the dedication by her father.

EDCS-25001792.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Mercurius lived 28 years, 10 days, and 7 hours; his dutiful father made this; he is buried here.
EDCS-25001792.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Mercurius, who lived 28 years, 10 days, and 7 hours, erected by his father.

EDCS-25001793.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Minucia Prima, who lived for 26 years. Nicodromus made this for his devoted wife, belonging to Augustus, and well-deserving. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Minicia Prima, who lived for 26 years. Nicodromus made this for his devoted wife, belonging to Augustus, and well-deserving. You were snatched away in your youth, my dearest wife. Life proved itself for you for twice ten years and six. Rome is your origin; it was your fate to be a Libyan. Now, pitiable one, you are led to the Stygian boat, and sorrowful Lethe dwells in your heart, so that you do not recognize me, pitiable one, the devoted one. It was Fortune's gift to keep you chaste, and you could have given both of us to Italy. You will renew many things with tears, O good and simple one, when I do not have you in sight as a companion. She is laid here. Prima.
EDCS-25001793.summary: A complex funerary epitaph for Minucia Prima, who died at 26, including a poem by her husband Nicodromus, who served Augustus, lamenting her death and their shared life.

EDCS-25001912.translation: A dutiful messenger lived 29 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-25001912.summary: This brief inscription commemorates a messenger who died at the age of 29.

EDCS-25001913.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Felix, a dutiful slave and land surveyor of the Emperor, lived 35 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-25001913.summary: This funerary text honors Felix, an imperial slave and land surveyor, who lived for 35 years.

EDCS-25001914.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Victor, a dutiful slave and land surveyor of our Emperor, lived 65 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-25001914.summary: This inscription records the burial of Victor, an imperial slave and land surveyor, who lived to the age of 65.

EDCS-25001915.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. S., a dutiful chorographer of the Emperor, lived 66 years; his wife made it for her husband who deserved well of her; his bones may rest here; may the earth lie lightly on you.
EDCS-25001915.summary: This tombstone was erected by a wife for her husband S., an imperial chorographer, who lived to be 66.

EDCS-25001916.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Publius Aelius Primus, freedman of Augustus, a craftsman, dutiful, lived 94 years. He is buried here. Aelia Eutychis made this for her deserving patron.
EDCS-25001916.summary: A funerary epitaph for Publius Aelius Primus, a craftsman and freedman of Augustus, set up by his freedwoman Aelia Eutychis.

EDCS-25001917.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Felix, a footman of Augustus, dutiful, lived 40 years. Fortunata, dutiful, lived 3 years and 9 months. Tertulla, dutiful, lived 3 years and 9 months. They are buried here.
EDCS-25001917.summary: A funerary epitaph for Felix, a footman of Augustus, and two children, Fortunata and Tertulla, likely his family.

EDCS-25001919.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Felix, a servant and guardian of the household gods of our Caesar, dutiful, lived 76 years and 3 months and 15 days. Aelia Ianuaria, a fellow servant, dutiful, made this.
EDCS-25001919.summary: A funerary epitaph for Felix, a servant and guardian of household gods of Caesar, set up by his fellow servant Aelia Ianuaria.

EDCS-25001920.translation: Maior, a basket-maker, dutiful, lived 35 years. Primigenius made this for his deserving wife. She is buried here.
EDCS-25001920.summary: A funerary epitaph for Maior, a basket-maker, set up by her husband Primigenius.

EDCS-25001921.translation: Of Hymnus, a soldier of the fourth legion of the province of Africa, a treasurer, lived 2 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-25001921.summary: A funerary epitaph for Hymnus, a treasurer in the fourth legion of Africa, likely a soldier who died young.

EDCS-25001922.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed, sacred. Gessia Luscina, dutiful, lived 30 years. She rests here. Tiberius Claudius Matrillus, the physician, made this for his dutiful wife.
EDCS-25001922.summary: A tombstone for Gessia Luscina, erected by her husband Tiberius Claudius Matrillus, a physician.

EDCS-25001923.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Marcus Macrius Trophimus, freedman of Augustus, a physician, dutiful, lived 45 years. His freedmen made this for their patron who deserved well of them.
EDCS-25001923.summary: A funerary epitaph for Marcus Macrius Trophimus, a physician and freedman of Augustus, set up by his freedmen.

EDCS-25001924.translation: Secundus, physician of Augustus, dutiful, lived 17 years, 11 months, and 10 days.
EDCS-25001924.summary: A funerary epitaph for Secundus, a physician of Augustus, who died at a young age.

EDCS-25001926.translation: Thyas, the dancer, lived 14 years. For Thalamus, his betrothed.
EDCS-25001926.summary: A funerary epitaph for Thyas, a dancer, set up by his betrothed Thalamus.

EDCS-25001927.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Adiutor, servant of our Caesar, dutiful, lived 105 years. Adiutor and Cale made this. He is buried here.
EDCS-25001927.summary: A funerary epitaph for Adiutor, a servant of Caesar, who lived to a remarkable age, set up by Adiutor (likely his son) and Cale.

EDCS-25001929.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Titus Aelius Epaphroditus, dutiful, lived 30 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-25001929.summary: A funerary epitaph for Titus Aelius Epaphroditus.

EDCS-25001930.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Aelius Restitutus, dutiful, lived for 3 years and 6 months. He rests here.
EDCS-25001930.summary: A tombstone recording the short life of Aelius Restitutus, likely a child, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25001931.translation: Dedicated to the departed spirits. Aelius Saggeus, dutiful, lived 60 years and 4 months. Aelia Felixima lived 40 years and 2 months.
EDCS-25001931.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the ages at death of Aelius Saggeus and Aelia Felixima.

EDCS-25001932.translation: Dedicated to the departed spirits. Aelia Felicitas, dutiful, lived 37 years and 2 months; she is buried here. Dedicated to the departed spirits. Aelius Salvianus, dutiful, lived 1 year, 4 months, and 22 days; his most dutiful mother made this.
EDCS-25001932.summary: This tombstone records the ages at death of Aelia Felicitas and Aelius Salvianus, with the latter's monument erected by his mother.

EDCS-25001933.translation: To the Divine Spirits, sacred. Aelius Viator, dutiful, lived for 36 years. He rests here.
EDCS-25001933.summary: A tombstone for Aelius Viator, who died at the age of 36, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25001934.translation: Dedicated to the departed spirits. Aelius Viator, CIORLOLIOETO, to his dearest son, who lived 11 years and 10 months; he is buried here.
EDCS-25001934.summary: This tombstone records the death of Aelius Viator, a young boy, and is dedicated by his father.

EDCS-25001935.translation: Dedicated to the departed spirits. Aelia Adiutrix, dutiful, lived 42 years and 7 months. Artema made this for her deserving wife; she is buried here.
EDCS-25001935.summary: This tombstone records the age at death of Aelia Adiutrix and was erected by her wife, Artema.

EDCS-25001936.translation: Dedicated to the departed spirits. Aelia Asella, dutiful, lived 26 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-25001936.summary: This tombstone records the age at death of Aelia Asella.

EDCS-25001937.translation: Dedicated to the departed spirits. For Aelia Bellica, an excellent and most dutiful woman, Caius Fulvius Venustus made this in recognition of her merits.
EDCS-25001937.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by Caius Fulvius Venustus to his wife, Aelia Bellica, for her merits.

EDCS-25001938.translation: Dedicated to the departed spirits. Aelia Campestra, freedwoman of Augustus, also called Bona, dutiful, lived 62 years; she is buried here. Dedicated to the departed spirits. Fortunata, servant of Augustus, dutiful, lived 25 years and 6 months; she is buried here.
EDCS-25001938.summary: This tombstone records the ages at death of two women, Aelia Campestra (a freedwoman of Augustus) and Fortunata (a servant of Augustus).

EDCS-25001939.translation: Dedicated to the departed spirits. Aelia Charis, dutiful, lived 1 year, 6 months, and 9 days; she is buried here.
EDCS-25001939.summary: This tombstone records the age at death of Aelia Charis.

EDCS-25001940.translation: Dedicated to the departed spirits. Aelia Cupita, freedwoman of Augustus, dutiful, lived 50 years; she is buried here. Castrensis, a fellow freedman, made this for her deserving associate.
EDCS-25001940.summary: This tombstone records the age at death of Aelia Cupita, a freedwoman of Augustus, and was erected by a fellow freedman.

EDCS-25001941.translation: Dedicated to the departed spirits. Aelia Felicula, freedwoman of Augustus, dutiful, lived 60 years, 5 months, and 8 days, 6 hours. Geminius Rogatus, dutiful, lived 71 years, 10 months, and 3 days, 10 hours. Aurelius Successus, dutiful, lived 23 years, 8 months.
EDCS-25001941.summary: This tombstone records the ages at death of three individuals: Aelia Felicula (a freedwoman of Augustus), Geminius Rogatus, and Aurelius Successus.

EDCS-25001942.translation: To the Divine Spirits, sacred. Aelia Felicula, dutiful, lived for 80 years. Felix and Caletyche, her sons, made this for their dutiful mother. She rests here.
EDCS-25001942.summary: A tombstone set up by sons for their mother, Aelia Felicula, who lived to 80, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25001943.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Aelia Primitiva lived 23 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-25001943.summary: A funerary epitaph for Aelia Primitiva, recording her age at death and burial location.

EDCS-25001944.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Aelia Tychis, freedwoman of Augustus, pious, lived 92 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-25001944.summary: A funerary epitaph for Aelia Tychis, a freedwoman of Augustus, recording her age at death and burial location.

EDCS-25001945.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Africanus, slave of Augustus, pious, lived 38 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-25001945.summary: A funerary epitaph for Africanus, a slave of Augustus, recording his age at death and burial location.

EDCS-25001946.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Alfia Secundula, also called Cosina, lived one year and seven months.
EDCS-25001946.summary: A funerary epitaph for Alfia Secundula (also known as Cosina), recording her age at death.

EDCS-25001947.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Ampedia Primigenia, pious, lived 18 years, 1 month, 14 days, and 7 hours.
EDCS-25001947.summary: A funerary epitaph for Ampedia Primigenia, recording her age at death in years, months, days, and hours.

EDCS-25001950.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Publius Annius Dicaeus lived for 50 years. Publius Annius Natalis, his freedman, made this for his well-deserving patron.
EDCS-25001950.summary: A tombstone erected by a freedman, Publius Annius Natalis, for his patron Publius Annius Dicaeus, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25001951.translation: To the Divine Spirits, sacred. The dutiful servant of the Emperor lived for 17 years. He rests here.
EDCS-25001951.summary: A tombstone for a male imperial slave who died at age 17, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25001952.translation: To the Divine Spirits, sacred. Antonia Haline, dutiful, lived for 72 years and 10 months. Publius Aelius Euhodus, freedman of the Emperor, for his well-deserving wife, with whom he lived for 40 years. She rests here.
EDCS-25001952.summary: A tombstone set up by Publius Aelius Euhodus, an imperial freedman, for his wife Antonia Haline, whom he had been married to for 40 years, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25001953.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Apronia Victoria lived 80 years. Her pious daughter made this.
EDCS-25001953.summary: A funerary epitaph for Apronia Victoria, recording her age at death and noting that it was made by her daughter.

EDCS-25001954.translation: To the Divine Spirits, sacred. Arbuscula, dutiful, of our Emperor, lived for 53 years. She rests here.
EDCS-25001954.summary: A tombstone for Arbuscula, a woman associated with the imperial household, who died at age 53, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25001956.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Arnesis, pious, lived one year and two months. He is buried here.
EDCS-25001956.summary: A funerary epitaph for Arnesis, recording his age at death and burial location.

EDCS-25001958.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Atheneus, freedman of Augustus, pious, lived 60 years and 4 months and 15 days. He is buried here.
EDCS-25001958.summary: A funerary epitaph for Atheneus, a freedman of Augustus, recording his age at death and burial location.

EDCS-25001959.translation: To the Divine Spirits, sacred. Atimetianus, dutiful, lived for 3 years and 6 months. He rests here.
EDCS-25001959.summary: A tombstone recording the short life of Atimetianus, likely a child, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25001960.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Aufidia Restituta, pious, lived 25 years. She is buried here. Aufidius Aprilis, pious, lived 22 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-25001960.summary: A paired funerary epitaph for Aufidia Restituta and Aufidius Aprilis, recording their ages at death and burial locations.

EDCS-25001961.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Augustianus, pious, lived 2 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-25001961.summary: A funerary epitaph for Augustianus, recording his age at death and burial location.

EDCS-25001962.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Augustianus lived 37 years.
EDCS-25001962.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Augustianus, who died at the age of 37.

EDCS-25001964.translation: To the spirits of the departed, sacred. Aurelius I, aged 29 years, lies here.
EDCS-25001964.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Aurelius I, who died at the age of 29.

EDCS-25001965.translation: To the spirits of the departed, sacred. Marcus Aurelius Demetrius, dutiful, lived 40 years, 10 months, 5 days; he lies here.
EDCS-25001965.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcus Aurelius Demetrius, who died at the age of 40 years, 10 months, and 5 days.

EDCS-25001966.translation: To the spirits of the departed, sacred. Aurelius Proculianus, dearest infant, who lived 1 year, 6 months, 8 days; he lies here.
EDCS-25001966.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Aurelius Proculianus, an infant who died at the age of 1 year, 6 months, and 8 days.

EDCS-25001967.translation: To the spirits of the departed, sacred. Aurelia Floscula, dutiful, lived 34 years, 3 months; she lies here.
EDCS-25001967.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Aurelia Floscula, who died at the age of 34 years and 3 months.

EDCS-25001968.translation: To the spirits of the departed, sacred. Aurelia Hilara lived 2 years, 11 months; she lies here.
EDCS-25001968.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Aurelia Hilara, who died at the age of 2 years and 11 months.

EDCS-25001969.translation: To the spirits of the departed, sacred. Aurelia Victoria, dutiful, lived 25 years, five months; she lies here.
EDCS-25001969.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Aurelia Victoria, who died at the age of 25 years and five months.

EDCS-25001970.translation: To the spirits of the departed, sacred. Gaius Caecilius, son of Caius, of the Papiria tribe, Catullus, dutiful, lived 48 years; he lies here.
EDCS-25001970.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Gaius Caecilius Catullus, who died at the age of 48.

EDCS-25001971.translation: To the spirits of the departed, sacred. Marcus Caecilius Felix, dutiful, lived 6 months, 20 days; he lies here.
EDCS-25001971.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcus Caecilius Felix, who died at the age of 6 months and 20 days.

EDCS-25001972.translation: Caius Caecilius Restutus, dutiful, lived for 19 years. He rests here.
EDCS-25001972.summary: A tombstone for Caius Caecilius Restutus, who died at age 19, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25001973.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Cale.
EDCS-25001973.summary: This is a very fragmentary funerary epitaph, only the name Cale is preserved.

EDCS-25001974.translation: To the Divine Spirits, sacred. Cale, dutiful, servant of our Emperor, lived for 40 years. She rests here.
EDCS-25001974.summary: A tombstone for Cale, a female imperial slave, who died at age 40, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25001975.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Callistus, a devoted slave, lived for 30 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-25001975.summary: A tombstone inscription recording the death of Callistus, a slave, who lived for 30 years.

EDCS-25001976.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Carchedonia lived for 3 years and 10 months.
EDCS-25001976.summary: A tombstone inscription recording the death of Carchedonia, who lived for 3 years and 10 months.

EDCS-25001977.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Cassius Africanus, son of Lucius, devoted, lived 30 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-25001977.summary: A funerary inscription recording the death of Lucius Cassius Africanus, who lived 30 years.

EDCS-25001978.summary: A milestone inscription indicating distance, and that Casta lived.

EDCS-25001979.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Casta the devoted lived for 18 years and 4 months; she is buried here.
EDCS-25001979.summary: A tombstone inscription recording the death of Casta, who lived for 18 years and 4 months.

EDCS-25001980.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Castula, a devoted native girl, lived for 15 years; her loving masters made this for her merit; she is buried here.
EDCS-25001980.summary: A tombstone inscription for Castula, a native girl, stating her masters erected it due to her merit.

EDCS-25001981.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Chrysogonus lived for 4 years, 1 month, and 24 days.
EDCS-25001981.summary: A tombstone inscription recording the death of Chrysogonus, who lived for 4 years, 1 month, and 24 days.

EDCS-25001982.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Clarus, devoted servant of the Emperor, lived 40 years. Ianuarius, his son, made this for his most devoted father. He is buried here.
EDCS-25001982.summary: A funerary inscription recording the death of Clarus, a devoted imperial freedman, erected by his son Ianuarius.

EDCS-25001983.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Titus Claudius Rufinulus, devoted, lived for 14 years, 5 months, and 21 days; he is buried here.
EDCS-25001983.summary: A tombstone inscription recording the death of Titus Claudius Rufinulus, who lived for 14 years, 5 months, and 21 days.

EDCS-25001984.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Claudia Felicissima, devoted, lived for 6 years and 6 months.
EDCS-25001984.summary: A tombstone inscription recording the death of Claudia Felicissima, who lived for 6 years and 6 months.

EDCS-25001985.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Claudia Nape, devoted, lived 86 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-25001985.summary: A funerary inscription recording the death of Claudia Nape, who lived 86 years.

EDCS-25001986.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Marcus Clodius Plautianus, devoted, lived for 42 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-25001986.summary: A tombstone inscription recording the death of Marcus Clodius Plautianus, who lived for 42 years.

EDCS-25001987.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Clodia Victoria, devoted, lived for 30 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-25001987.summary: A tombstone inscription recording the death of Clodia Victoria, who lived for 30 years.

EDCS-25001988.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Cocceia Alche, pious, lived 100 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-25001988.summary: A funerary epitaph for Cocceia Alche, who lived 100 years, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25001989.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Cocceia Dromas is buried here.
EDCS-25001989.summary: A funerary epitaph for Cocceia Dromas, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25001990.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Cocilia Veneria, pious, lived 43 years. May your bones rest well. May the earth lie lightly upon you.
EDCS-25001990.summary: A funerary epitaph for Cocilia Veneria, who lived 43 years, including a common Latin funerary formula, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25001991.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Colobonius Licinianus lived 27 years, 7 months, and 16 days. His most pious wife made this. He is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Domitius Primus, pious, lived 2 years and 4 months. He is buried here.
EDCS-25001991.summary: A funerary epitaph commemorating two individuals, Colobonius Licinianus and Lucius Domitius Primus, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25001992.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcus Cominius Basileus, pious, lived 28 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-25001992.summary: A funerary epitaph for Marcus Cominius Basileus, who lived 28 years, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25001993.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Caius Cominius Nobilis, pious, lived 8 years and 11 months. He is buried here.
EDCS-25001993.summary: A funerary epitaph for Caius Cominius Nobilis, who lived 8 years and 11 months, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25001994.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Caius Cominius Restutulus lived 17 years and 3 days. He is buried here.
EDCS-25001994.summary: A funerary epitaph for Caius Cominius Restutulus, who lived 17 years and 3 days, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25001995.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Comisator, devoted servant of our Emperor, lived 25 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-25001995.summary: A funerary inscription recording the death of Comisator, a devoted imperial freedman, who lived 25 years.

EDCS-25001996.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Concordia, pious, lived 37 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-25001996.summary: A funerary epitaph for Concordia, who lived 37 years, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25001998.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Publius Cornelius Hiilarus, pious, lived 26 years and 7 months. He is buried here.
EDCS-25001998.summary: A funerary epitaph for Publius Cornelius Hiilarus, who lived 26 years and 7 months, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25001999.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Cossinius Callistus lived 5 months. He is buried here.
EDCS-25001999.summary: A funerary epitaph for Cossinius Callistus, who lived 5 months, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25002000.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Cottius Felix, dutiful, lived for 8 years and 23 days; he is buried here.
EDCS-25002000.summary: A funerary epitaph for Cottius Felix, who lived 8 years and 23 days.

EDCS-25002001.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Cuccas, dutiful, lived for 21 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-25002001.summary: A funerary epitaph for Cuccas, who lived 21 years.

EDCS-25002002.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Cusp[---], devoted, lived 1 year and 10 months. He is buried here.
EDCS-25002002.summary: A funerary inscription recording the death of Lucius Cusp[---], who lived 1 year and 10 months.

EDCS-25002003.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Cuttia Felicula, dutiful, lived for 43 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-25002003.summary: A funerary epitaph for Cuttia Felicula, who lived 43 years.

EDCS-25002004.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Danae, lived 1 year, 6 months, and 20 days. She is buried here.
EDCS-25002004.summary: A funerary inscription recording the death of Danae, who lived 1 year, 6 months, and 20 days.

EDCS-25002005.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Daphnus, a dutiful freedman of Augustus, lived for about 25 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-25002005.summary: A funerary epitaph for Daphnus, a freedman of Augustus, who lived about 25 years.

EDCS-25002006.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Dellia Flaccilla, devoted, lived 20 years and 8 months. She is buried here.
EDCS-25002006.summary: A funerary inscription recording the death of Dellia Flaccilla, who lived 20 years and 8 months.

EDCS-25002007.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Dioscorus, a dutiful freedman of our Emperor, lived for 74 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-25002007.summary: A funerary epitaph for Dioscorus, a freedman of the Emperor, who lived 74 years.

EDCS-25002008.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Domitius Rufus, son of Martial, dutiful, lived for 54 years, 5 months, and 8 days.
EDCS-25002008.summary: A funerary epitaph for Domitius Rufus, son of Martial, who lived 54 years, 5 months, and 8 days.

EDCS-25002009.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Domitia Castula lived for 20 years and 24 days; her father placed this here for his daughter; she is buried here.
EDCS-25002009.summary: A funerary epitaph for Domitia Castula, who lived 20 years and 24 days, dedicated by her father.

EDCS-25002010.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Domitia Maurica lived for 2 years, 9 months, and 21 days; she is buried here.
EDCS-25002010.summary: A funerary epitaph for Domitia Maurica, who lived 2 years, 9 months, and 21 days.

EDCS-25002011.summary: A fragmentary inscription mentioning a dictator and the number VIII.

EDCS-25002012.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Eucarpus, also called Gittus, lived for 2 years and 7 months, and Satura, dutiful, lived for 21 years and 8 months.
EDCS-25002012.summary: A funerary epitaph for Eucarpus (Gittus) and Satura, recording their ages at death.

EDCS-25002013.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Euprepes lived 25 years.
EDCS-25002013.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Euprepes, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25002014.translation: Euphrosyna, daughter of Marci and Euphrosyna, is laid here.
EDCS-25002014.summary: A funerary epitaph identifying Euphrosyna, daughter of Marci, and stating she is buried here, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25002015.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Eurytus, Augustus's devoted household slave, lived 82 years; he is laid here.
EDCS-25002015.summary: A funerary epitaph for Eurytus, a devoted household slave of Augustus, who lived 82 years, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25002016.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Eutycha, devoted, lived 15 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-25002016.summary: A funerary inscription recording the death of Eutycha, who lived 15 years.

EDCS-25002017.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Extricatus, devoted servant of the Emperor, lived 81 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-25002017.summary: A funerary inscription recording the death of Extricatus, a devoted imperial freedman, who lived 81 years.

EDCS-25002018.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Extricata, devoted, lived 33 years; she is laid here. May your bones rest well; may the earth be light upon you.
EDCS-25002018.summary: A funerary epitaph for Extricata, including a common wish for the deceased's peaceful rest, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25002019.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Fabia Iucunda, devoted, lived 34 years, 10 months, and 1 day. Fabius Felix, devoted, lived 33 years. They are buried here.
EDCS-25002019.summary: A funerary inscription recording the deaths of Fabia Iucunda and her brother Fabius Felix, likely in the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-25002020.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the short lifespan of Fausti (4 months), dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25002021.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Faustus, devoted, lived 80 years; he is laid here. His son made this.
EDCS-25002021.summary: A funerary epitaph for Faustus, who lived 80 years, dedicated by his son, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25002024.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Felicia the dutiful lived 50 years, and Badaeus the dutiful lived 60 years; here he lies buried.
EDCS-25002024.summary: This is a tombstone recording the deaths of Felicia and Badaeus, who lived 50 and 60 years respectively, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25002025.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Felicio, devoted, lived 46 years and 4 months; he is laid here.
EDCS-25002025.summary: A funerary epitaph for Felicio, who lived 46 years and 4 months, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25002026.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Felicitas, devoted household slave of Augustus, lived 14 years, 4 months, and 24 days; she is laid here.
EDCS-25002026.summary: A funerary epitaph for Felicitas, a household slave of Augustus, who died at the age of 14 years, 4 months, and 24 days, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25002027.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Felicula, devoted servant of Augustus, lived 33 years; she is laid here. Felix made this for his cherished wife.

EDCS-25002133.translation: To the Divine Spirits, sacred. Senila lived piously for one year and eight months. She is buried here.

EDCS-25002134.translation: To the Divine Spirits, sacred. You whoever reads this inscription, whether pious or unkind, weep for my age, which I ought not to have left such light nor such underworld gods. For what reason do you speak? I was obedient to my dear husband, whose character and chastity I always served out of timidity, and whose affection I preserved, because he truly deserved me, who loved me so chastely. I lived simply and chastely, in whose modesty no one could boast or be angry with my dear husband. Whatever you, a chaste woman, can do, live so chastely; for I know you can be dearly loved if you live chastely according to my custom. For after my death, I leave the memory of many years to my husband. But I give thanks to the gods above that while I lived, they denied me nothing of my pleasures, because I myself deserved them. Severa, a pious servant of Augustus, lived 24 years, 6 months, and 11 days. She is buried here. Her husband made this for her, who deserved it.
EDCS-25002134.summary: A lengthy epitaph for Severa, a pious servant of Augustus, detailing her virtuous life and devotion to her husband, and serving as a moral guide for other women; she lived 24 years, 6 months, and 11 days. The inscription was made by her deserving husband, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25002166.translation: In the consulship of Lucius Cassius and Gaius Marius.
EDCS-25002166.summary: This inscription records a date based on the consuls Lucius Cassius and Gaius Marius.

EDCS-25002177.translation: In honor of Lucius Cassius Athenaeus, son of Lucius, former aedile, former duovir, a youth, former municipal priest, perpetual priest, Roman knight, who held the imperial procuratorship for correspondence due to his outstanding clemency of character and his liberality towards all citizens individually and the blameless and exceptional administration of his duovirate and his enjoyment, and in honor of his son Caecilius Donatus Aufidianus, perpetual priest, the most distinguished order and the entire populace of the curiae of the colony of Sufetula have erected this eternal testament of their gratitude and have also dedicated it.
EDCS-25002177.summary: This is a dedication by the colony of Sufetula honoring Lucius Cassius Athenaeus for his public service and character, and possibly also his son.

EDCS-25002180.translation: Rufinus' daughter Rufina, a virgin of 15 years.
EDCS-25002180.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Rufina, recording her age and familial relationship.

EDCS-25002183.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Flavius Zoilus is buried here. He lived 43 years and 8 months. His sons made this for their most dutiful father.
EDCS-25002183.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Flavius Zoilus, erected by his sons, recording his age at death.

EDCS-25100217.translation: Agoniosus the acolyte lived 45 years, was buried on the 13th day before the Kalends of September.
EDCS-25100217.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Agoniosus, an acolyte, recording his age at death and burial date.

EDCS-25100221.translation: Bonifatius, faithful, was laid to rest in peace on the 17th day before the Kalends of January.
EDCS-25100221.summary: This inscription records the burial of Bonifatius, a faithful individual, on a specific date.

EDCS-25100222.translation: Bonosula lived in peace for 2 years. Consortius.
EDCS-25100222.summary: This inscription records the lifespan of Bonosula, who lived for 2 years, and is associated with Consortius.

EDCS-25100224.translation: Quirillus, faithful, lived in peace for 50 years.
EDCS-25100224.summary: This inscription records the lifespan of Quirillus, a faithful individual, who lived for 50 years.

EDCS-25100225.summary: This inscription indicates that Egisia Eddeora is at peace, likely a funerary marker.

EDCS-25100230.translation: Iucunda, innocent, lived in peace for [unclear] years, on the Kalends of July, indiction VIII; innocent, lived in peace for [unclear] years, was laid to rest on the Kalends of June, indiction XII.
EDCS-25100230.summary: This inscription records the lifespan and burial of Iucunda, described as innocent, with dates specified by Kalends and indictions.

EDCS-25100232.translation: Musa, faithful, lived in peace for 5 years, was laid to rest on the 8th day before the Ides of March; [name unclear], faithful, lived in peace for 2 years, was laid to rest on the 10th day before the Kalends of [month unclear]; Fortunatus, faithful, lived in peace for 50 years.
EDCS-25100232.summary: This inscription records the lifespans and burials of at least three individuals: Musa, an unnamed faithful person, and Fortunatus.

EDCS-25100235.summary: This inscription commemorates Perpetua, described as faithful and a martyr, noting she lived for 7 months.

EDCS-25100236.translation: Redempta, faithful, lived in peace for [unclear] years.
EDCS-25100236.summary: This inscription records the lifespan of Redempta, a faithful individual, who lived for an unspecified number of years.

EDCS-25100237.translation: Restituta, faithful, lived in peace for 6 years.
EDCS-25100237.summary: This inscription records the lifespan of Restituta, a faithful individual, who lived for 6 years.

EDCS-25100239.translation: Stefanus lived in peace for 70 years, buried on the 3rd day before the Kalends of August in the first indiction.
EDCS-25100239.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Stefanus, noting his lifespan and burial date, likely from the late Roman or Byzantine period.

EDCS-25100243.translation: Victor the faithful, buried on the 2nd Ides.
EDCS-25100243.summary: A brief funerary inscription recording the burial of Victor.

EDCS-25100247.summary: A very short inscription identifying Secundus as a husband, likely a tombstone epitaph.

EDCS-25100249.translation: Robius, you would have asked for V.
EDCS-25100249.summary: This inscription is fragmentary and difficult to interpret, possibly a personal note or a request.

EDCS-25100250.translation: To Lucius Calpurnius Fidus Aemilianus, a most distinguished man, quaestor of Crete and Cyrenaica, tribune of the plebs, praetor; from Publius Sicinius Pescennius Hilarianus, his candidate, an incomparable friend.
EDCS-25100250.summary: A dedication from Publius Sicinius Pescennius Hilarianus to Lucius Calpurnius Fidus Aemilianus, listing his high offices and praising him as a friend and candidate, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-25100253.translation: To Aulus Lucius Felix Blaesianus, admitted into the quinque decuriae, aedile, duovir, perpetual flamen, priest of the province of Africa, by the city of the Thubbensians.
EDCS-25100253.summary: An honorary inscription by the city of Thubursicum Bure (modern Mactar) honoring Aulus Lucius Felix Blaesianus for his various civic and religious offices, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-25100255.summary: A fragmentary inscription mentioning the actions of a duovir, possibly related to public works or supply.

EDCS-25100257.summary: This is a very short and obscure inscription, possibly referring to a person, a measure, or an object.

EDCS-25100262.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Licinia Victoria, a devout midwife, lived 49 years, 6 months, 14 days; she is laid here. May the earth be light on you, may your bones rest well. Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Valerius Valerianus, devout, lived 62 years, 5 months, 7 days. Licinia Victoria, a devout midwife, lived 49 years, 6 months, 14 days. May your bones rest well, may the earth be light on you.
EDCS-25100262.summary: A double funerary inscription honoring Licinia Victoria and Lucius Valerius Valerianus, providing their ages at death and standard wishes for the deceased, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-25100263.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcus Aemilius Irenaeus, devout, lived 70 years; may the earth be light on you, may your bones rest well.
EDCS-25100263.summary: A funerary inscription for Marcus Aemilius Irenaeus, stating his age at death and invoking blessings for his afterlife, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-25100265.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Ianuaria, devout, lived 32 years, more or less. May your bones rest well. May the earth lie lightly upon you.
EDCS-25100265.summary: A funerary epitaph for Ianuaria, recording her age at death.

EDCS-25100266.translation: Licinia Quieta, daughter of Quintus, devout, lived 22 years and 5 months. She is buried here. May your bones rest well. May the earth lie lightly upon you. Claudius Rhyter, devout, lived 22 years and 6 months. He is buried here. May your bones rest well. May the earth lie lightly upon you.
EDCS-25100266.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the ages and burial of Licinia Quieta and Claudius Rhyter.

EDCS-25100267.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Reposta, devout, lived 37 years, 10 months, and 7 days. She is buried here. May your bones rest well. May the earth lie lightly upon you.
EDCS-25100267.summary: A funerary epitaph for Reposta, recording her age at death and burial.

EDCS-25100268.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Sirosus, devout, lived 40 days. He is buried here. May the earth lie lightly upon you. May your bones rest well.
EDCS-25100268.summary: A funerary epitaph for Sirosus, recording his very short lifespan in days.

EDCS-25100269.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Successa, devout, lived 27 years and 9 months. She is buried here. May your bones rest well. May the earth lie lightly upon you.
EDCS-25100269.summary: A funerary epitaph for Successa, recording her age at death and burial.

EDCS-25100270.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Tanonius Victorianus lived 10 years, 10 months, and 7 days. He is buried here. May the earth lie lightly upon you. May your bones rest well.
EDCS-25100270.summary: A funerary epitaph for Tanonius Victorianus, recording his age at death and burial.

EDCS-25100271.translation: Vipsania Nymphe lived 69 years. She is buried here. May your bones rest well. May the earth lie lightly upon you.
EDCS-25100271.summary: A funerary epitaph for Vipsania Nymphe, recording her age at death and burial.

EDCS-25100277.summary: A funerary epitaph for Crementia, likely from an early Christian context.

EDCS-25100278.summary: A funerary epitaph for Marsianus, likely from an early Christian context.

EDCS-25100279.translation: Quodbuldeus, faithful, in peace and rests with your children.
EDCS-25100279.summary: A funerary epitaph for Quodbuldeus, likely from an early Christian context, mentioning rest with children.

EDCS-25100283.translation: Clodia Saturnina is placed here. She lived [many?] years. May your bones rest well.
EDCS-25100283.summary: A funerary epitaph for Clodia Saturnina, likely from the Roman Imperial period, expressing a wish for her repose.

EDCS-25100284.translation: [Someone named?] Crescens lived more or less 35 years. The business [was done?].
EDCS-25100284.summary: A fragmentary funerary inscription mentioning Crescens and an approximate lifespan, possibly Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25100291.text_edition: \n Tesseram pagi Minervi Marcus Grattius Marci filius Papiria magister pagi de sua pecunia dedit\n
EDCS-25100291.translation: The marker of the district of Minerva. Marcus Grattius, son of Marcus, of the Papiria tribe, as district magistrate, dedicated this at his own expense.
EDCS-25100291.summary: A dedication of a boundary marker for the district of Minerva by Marcus Grattius, a district magistrate, funded from his own money, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25100292.translation: The roofs of the Bassiana estate shine, known by the name Baiae, and gleam even more with the brightness of the light. Sidonius (?) arranged to make... for the honored dedication... opposite...
EDCS-25100292.summary: An incomplete inscription that seems to describe the shining roofs of the Bassiana estate, named Baiae, and mentions a dedication arranged by someone named Sidonius (?), likely related to a building or property improvement in the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25100293.summary: A very brief inscription possibly naming two individuals, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25100294.summary: A highly fragmentary inscription, possibly related to a religious or civic event, Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25100298.translation: Caecilia Sanaemonis, daughter of Auge, pious, lived 18 years.
EDCS-25100298.summary: A funerary epitaph for Caecilia, daughter of Sanaemonis and Auge, who died at the age of 18, likely Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25100299.translation: Lucius Pist, priest, entered [office?] under the emperor Commodus Augustus for the seventh time.
EDCS-25100299.summary: An inscription recording the entrance of Lucius Pist into office as priest under Emperor Commodus, indicating a date around 177-192 AD.

EDCS-25100300.summary: A fragmentary funerary inscription for Licinia, likely Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25100301.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Caius Sergius Iunianus lived 28 years, 11 months, and 27 days. He is buried here.
EDCS-25100301.summary: A funerary epitaph for Caius Sergius Iunianus, providing his age at death and burial details, likely Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25100303.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Minervalis Honorati [son?], the attendant, lived 95 years and 4 months. His sons made this for their father.
EDCS-25100303.summary: A funerary epitaph for Minervalis Honorati, set up by his sons, indicating his age at death, likely Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25100304.translation: Publius Pescennius, son of Lucius, a veteran of the Third Augustan Legion, lived 85 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-25100304.summary: A funerary epitaph for Publius Pescennius, a veteran of the Third Augustan Legion, detailing his age and burial, likely Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25100305.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Tufienius Speratus, a soldier of the VI Praetorian Cohort, stationed at the bank of Utica, lived for 35 years, served for 15 years. May your bones rest well. May the earth lie lightly on you.
EDCS-25100305.summary: A funerary epitaph for Tufienius Speratus, a Praetorian soldier, providing his age and years of service.

EDCS-25100307.translation: To Sapritus, incomparable. Lived for 7 years, 6 months, 3 days, and 8 hours. [He/She] made this monument.
EDCS-25100307.summary: A funerary epitaph for Sapritus, likely a child, detailing their lifespan and indicating the monument was erected by someone else.

EDCS-25100308.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Simplicius Successus lived for 38 years, 3 months, and 15 days. May your bones rest well. May the earth lie lightly on you.
EDCS-25100308.summary: A funerary epitaph for Simplicius Successus, providing his age at death.

EDCS-25100310.translation: Sacred to Pluto Augustus. Lucius Caecilius Dexter Iovianus, a veteran formerly a decurion, gave this altar according to his vow and dedicated it himself.
EDCS-25100310.summary: A votive altar dedicated to Pluto Augustus by a veteran former decurion named Lucius Caecilius Dexter Iovianus.

EDCS-25100314.translation: [---] and Licem [---] of the deified Augustus. Felix and his wife [---] gave this gift.
EDCS-25100314.summary: A dedication of a gift, possibly by Felix and his wife, to a deified emperor, with a damaged text.

EDCS-25100317.summary: A very brief Christian epitaph for Paulina.

EDCS-25100318.translation: To Marcus Julius Probatus, son of Caius Julius Probus Sabinianus, who held all offices in his homeland of Carthage, for his exceptional and outstanding benevolence towards us, the order of the Chiniavensian expatriates, [dedicate this] to their patron.
EDCS-25100318.summary: A dedication by the expatriate community of Chiniavensis to their patron, Marcus Julius Probatus, honoring his public service and benevolence.

EDCS-25100321.summary: A tombstone or dedication mentioning two individuals, Sextilius Mercurius and Primitivus.

EDCS-25100322.summary: A brief Christian epitaph for Vicentia.

EDCS-25100323.translation: Fidelis lived for 70 years. Fidelis lived for 75 years.
EDCS-25100323.summary: A funerary epitaph recording two different lifespans for an individual named Fidelis, possibly indicating two separate records or an error.

EDCS-25100324.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Minucius Liberalis, dutiful, lived for 86 years and 2 months. He is buried here.
EDCS-25100324.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the burial of Minucius Liberalis, who lived for 86 years and 2 months.

EDCS-25100325.translation: To his great-grandson of the deified Antoninus Pius, his grand-nephew, holder of tribunician power for the 5th time, imperator for the 2nd time, consul for the 3rd time, designated for the 4th time, father of the fatherland, proconsul, mother of the camp and of the senate and of the fatherland, mother of the Emperor Antoninus Augustus.
EDCS-25100325.summary: This is a dedication, likely part of a larger inscription, to members of the imperial family, referencing titles and relationships.

EDCS-25100327.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Senia Victoria lived for 54 years and 10 months.
EDCS-25100327.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Senia Victoria.

EDCS-25100328.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Picin [died].
EDCS-25100328.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription mentioning the name Picin.

EDCS-25100329.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Suffiix lived for 12 years.
EDCS-25100329.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Suffiix, who lived for 12 years.

EDCS-25100330.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Su us CR NV lived for approximately [---] years.
EDCS-25100330.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription recording the approximate lifespan of Su us.

EDCS-25100332.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Latinia Prima lived for 71 years and 3 months. T.B.C.
EDCS-25100332.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Latinia Prima, who lived for 71 years and 3 months.

EDCS-25100334.translation: Sacred to Saturn Augustus. Caius Caecilius Secundus, priest, fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-25100334.summary: This is a votive inscription by Caius Caecilius Secundus, a priest, dedicating it to Saturn Augustus.

EDCS-25100335.translation: Sacred to Saturn Augustus. Quintus Vesperius Saloninus, priest, willingly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-25100335.summary: This is a votive inscription by Quintus Vesperius Saloninus, a priest, dedicating it to Saturn Augustus.

EDCS-25100336.inscription_type: tituli honorarii, tituli operum, tituli sacri
EDCS-25100336.text_edition: \n Pro salute Imperatoris Caesaris Marci Aureli Antonini divi Antonini filii et Imperatoris Caesaris Luci Aureli Augustorum liberorumque Antonini Augusti Agrius Samsera ob honorem decurionatus sui inlatis legitimis ex HS CCducentis milibus nummum ampliata pecunia statuas memoriae temporum quattuor decreto decurionum posuit item dedicationis die epulum decurionibus dedit\n
EDCS-25100336.translation: For the safety of the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus, son of the divine Antoninus, and of the Emperor Caesar Lucius Aurelius, and of Antoninus Augustus and his children. Agrius Samsera, in honor of his magistracy, with the legal contribution of two hundred thousand sesterces, and with additional funds, erected statues as a memorial of the times, by decree of the decurions. On the day of the dedication, he also provided a feast for the decurions.
EDCS-25100336.summary: Agrius Samsera dedicated statues and provided a feast for the decurions for the safety of the Emperors Marcus Aurelius Antoninus and Lucius Aurelius, using his own funds supplemented by legal contributions, in honor of his magistracy, dating to the reign of Marcus Aurelius and Commodus.

EDCS-25100337.summary: This is an inscription identifying Lucius Gargillius Fortunatus as a priest.

EDCS-25100338.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Maecius Felix, perpetual priest and one of the four officials responsible for public affairs, lived for 63 years and 11 months.
EDCS-25100338.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Maecius Felix, recording his age and civic offices.

EDCS-25100339.translation: Lucius Gargillius Fortunatus, dutiful, gave thanks, lived for 84 years.
EDCS-25100339.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Gargillius Fortunatus, noting his age and piety.

EDCS-25100341.translation: Aemilius Ia, dutiful, lived for 60 years.
EDCS-25100341.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Aemilius Ia, recording his age and piety.

EDCS-25100342.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Flavista Solutrix, dutiful, lived for 13 years, 3 months, and 10 days; she lies here.
EDCS-25100342.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Flavista Solutrix, detailing her age and place of burial.

EDCS-25100343.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulius Primulus lived for 20 years; he lies here.
EDCS-25100343.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Iulius Primulus, noting his age and burial.

EDCS-25100344.translation: Titus Iunius Fortunatus lived for 53 years, 2 months, and 10 days; he lies here.
EDCS-25100344.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Titus Iunius Fortunatus, recording his age and burial.

EDCS-25100345.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Maius Cerdubis lived for 80 years.
EDCS-25100345.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Maius Cerdubis, noting his age.

EDCS-25100347.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely a tombstone or dedication, mentioning Lutatius Apuleius.

EDCS-25100348.translation: Caecilia Fausta, daughter of Lucius, chaste, dutiful, lived for 33 years; she lies here.
EDCS-25100348.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Caecilia Fausta, detailing her age, parentage, virtues, and burial place.

EDCS-25100349.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Manilius Primus Charitonianus, dutiful, lived for 80 years; may your bones rest well.
EDCS-25100349.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Manilius Primus Charitonianus, noting his age and offering a wish for his repose.

EDCS-25100352.translation: Manilius Apicius, laid to rest in peace on the third day before the Ides of June.
EDCS-25100352.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the burial of Manilius Apicius in peace.

EDCS-25100358.translation: Valeria Maxima, daughter of Quintus, dedicated this with her own funds, having adorned all places with cult and decoration.
EDCS-25100358.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a monument by Valeria Maxima, daughter of Quintus, who funded the adornment of places.

EDCS-25100361.translation: New ones and paving for years, dedicated by Herennius.
EDCS-25100361.summary: This inscription records the dedication of new paving by Herennius over a period of years.

EDCS-25100362.translation: For his son Marcus, 25 sesterces. Aurelianus...
EDCS-25100362.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely recording a payment or donation of 25 sesterces for Marcus, son of Marcus, made by Aurelianus.

EDCS-25100363.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Petronia Bana lived for 38 years, by care of...
EDCS-25100363.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Petronia Bana, who lived 38 years, dedicated to the departed spirits.

EDCS-25100364.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Victor Manilianus, a man of pious memory, lived for 60 years, paying nature's debt. Now he lives in the best way. May the earth be light upon you; may your bones rest well here.
EDCS-25100364.summary: This is a detailed funerary inscription for Victor Manilianus, who lived 60 years, expressing wishes for his afterlife and the repose of his bones.

EDCS-25100365.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Titus Ron Felix, an old man, pious, lived for 25 years. [Dedicated by] Sonia Honorata.
EDCS-25100365.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Titus Ron Felix, who lived 25 years and is described as pious, likely dedicated by Sonia Honorata.

EDCS-25100366.translation: Sullia Prima, daughter of Siicus, pious, lived for 35 years. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Abviaz... Basicus... eta.
EDCS-25100366.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Sullia Prima, who lived 35 years and is described as pious, with repeated invocations to the spirits of the departed.

EDCS-25100367.translation: N DV V PI lived for 70 years. May the earth be light upon you; may it be light for you. Victor I DO lived for 60 years.
EDCS-25100367.summary: This inscription records the ages of two individuals, N DV V PI (70 years) and Victor I DO (60 years), with a wish for the earth to be light upon them.

EDCS-25100373.translation: The great priestess, pious, lived for 95 years. She lies here.
EDCS-25100373.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a great priestess who lived 95 years and is stated to be buried here.

EDCS-25100374.translation: Sextus Iulius Primulus lived for 21 years.
EDCS-25100374.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the age of Sextus Iulius Primulus at the time of his death.

EDCS-25100375.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Iulia Rogata lived for 75 years.
EDCS-25100375.summary: A funerary epitaph dedicated to the Divine Shades, recording the age of Iulia Rogata.

EDCS-25100376.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Gnaeus Iunius Severianus, good and pious, lived for [X] years, 4 months.
EDCS-25100376.summary: A funerary epitaph dedicated to the Divine Shades, recording the lifespan of Gnaeus Iunius Severianus.

EDCS-25100377.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Pontia Berecta, pious, lived for 75 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-25100377.summary: A funerary epitaph dedicated to the Divine Shades, recording the age and burial of Pontia Berecta.

EDCS-25100378.translation: To the avenging god, pious [name] lived and is buried.
EDCS-25100378.summary: A funerary inscription dedicated to an avenging deity, noting the piety and burial of an individual.

EDCS-25100380.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades, from Diagr [---] V.
EDCS-25100380.summary: A fragmentary funerary inscription dedicated to the Divine Shades, possibly indicating a period of 5 days for a burial or sacrifice.

EDCS-25100382.summary: A dedication to the god Apollo Augustus.

EDCS-25100383.translation: Sacred to the Father God Apollo Augustus.
EDCS-25100383.summary: A religious dedication to Apollo Augustus, referred to as the Father God.

EDCS-25100387.translation: For the safety of the Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus Arabicus Adiabenicus, supreme pontiff, with tribunician power for the 4th time, consul for the 2nd time, father of the fatherland, son of the deified Marcus Antoninus Pius Germanicus Sarmaticus, great-grandson of the deified Hadrian, grandson of the deified Antoninus Pius, great-great-grandson of the deified Trajan Parthicus, great-great-great-grandson of the deified Nerva, and of Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Caesar, and of the entire divine house; the public administration of the colony of Bullensium Regiorum has erected this temple to Diana Corollitica, which Marcius Tertullus of most distinguished memory, an alumnus and patron of the public administration, ordered to be built among other outstanding examples of his generosity to his homeland, and which was completed with money raised from his heir.
EDCS-25100387.summary: A public building inscription from the colony of Bullensium Regiorum, dedicated to Diana Corollitica, commissioned by Marcius Tertullus and completed by his heir, with a lengthy titulature for Emperor Septimius Severus and Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus, likely dating to the early 3rd century CE.

EDCS-25100388.translation: Celsus, the aedile, made the portico with 4 columns from his own money for Tiberius Caesar Augustus' son, Augustus, supreme pontiff, with tribunician power for the 36th time, consul for the 5th time.
EDCS-25100388.summary: A public works inscription recording the construction of a portico with four columns by Celsus, an aedile, at his own expense, for Emperor Tiberius Caesar Augustus, likely dating to the late 1st century CE or early 2nd century CE.

EDCS-25100390.translation: For Vero Augusto, great-grandson of Emperor [Nerva?], governor, his father and sons [dedicated this].
EDCS-25100390.summary: This inscription is a dedication by a father and sons to a governor named Vero Augusto, likely from the late 2nd or early 3rd century.

EDCS-25100391.translation: To Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus, Prince of Youth, son of Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus Arabicus Adiabenicus Parthicus Maximus, grandson of the deified Marcus Antoninus Pius Germanicus Sarmaticus, great-grandson of the deified Antoninus Pius, great-great-grandson of the deified Hadrian, great-great-great-grandson of the deified Trajan Parthicus and the deified Nerva, by decree of the decurions, at public expense.
EDCS-25100391.summary: This is a dedication honoring Marcus Aurelius Antoninus (likely Caracalla) with extensive imperial titulature, erected by the decurions at public expense, probably in the early 3rd century.

EDCS-25100392.translation: For the safety of our Lords Emperors Diocletian and Maximian Augusti, Lucius Munatius Sabinus, a man of consular rank, curator of the public affairs, reconstructed and dedicated the public temple, which had collapsed due to age, with vaults, paintings, and marbles, at public expense.
EDCS-25100392.summary: This inscription records the reconstruction and dedication of a public temple by Lucius Munatius Sabinus, curator of the city, funded by public money, during the reign of Diocletian and Maximian (late 3rd century).

EDCS-25100394.translation: The colonia Aelia Hadriana Augusta Bulla Regia, devoted to his divine numen and majesty, [dedicated this] to the Emperor, with tribunician power, father of the fatherland, governor.
EDCS-25100394.summary: This inscription is a dedication by the colonia of Bulla Regia to an emperor, likely Hadrian given the colony's name, expressing devotion and acknowledging his imperial titles and role as governor, probably from the 2nd century.

EDCS-25100395.translation: For the vital interests of the state, to Agria Tannonia, a most distinguished girl, daughter of Agri Celsinianus, her consular husband and curator.
EDCS-25100395.summary: This inscription is a dedication for the well-being of the state, honoring Agria Tannonia, daughter of a consular official, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century.

EDCS-25100396.translation: The most splendid ordo of the colonia Bulla Regia erected [this] to Antonio Marcellinus, a most distinguished man, governor of the province of Africa, and their patron, whose integrity and justice Africa has approved, [as he was] of an illustrious family.
EDCS-25100396.summary: This inscription is a dedication by the city council of Bulla Regia to their patron, Antonio Marcellinus, a former governor of Africa, praising his integrity, likely from the late 2nd or 3rd century.

EDCS-25100397.translation: The most splendid ordo of Bulla Regia erected [this] to Ceionius Iulianus, a most distinguished man, governor, also hearing cases in place of the emperor, and patron, [as he was] of consular rank, from a family of patrons, and to [this] patron from his parents.
EDCS-25100397.summary: This is a dedication by the city council of Bulla Regia to their patron, Ceionius Iulianus, a former governor who also judged cases, likely from the 3rd century.

EDCS-25100400.translation: The most splendid ordo of the colonia Bulla Regia [erected this] to the man of most distinguished and excellent rank, governor for a second time, hearing cases in place of the emperor, and perpetual patron.
EDCS-25100400.summary: This inscription is a dedication by the city council of Bulla Regia to a governor, honored for his second term, his judicial role, and his status as a perpetual patron, likely from the 3rd century.

EDCS-25100401.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Gaius Julius Marinus, veteran, lived 51 years, 2 months, 9 days. He is buried here.
EDCS-25100401.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Gaius Julius Marinus, a veteran, recording his age and burial place, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-25100402.translation: Caius Sallustius Praenestinus dedicated [this] at his own expense to his mother Minia Procula, daughter of Caius, wife of Caius Sallustius Dextrus, perpetual flamen, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-25100402.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a monument by Caius Sallustius Praenestinus to his mother, Minia Procula, funded by himself and approved by the decurions, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century.

EDCS-25100404.translation: Sabinius Ianuarius Extricatianus in the year of his aedileship, by a religious promise.
EDCS-25100404.summary: This inscription records a vow made by Sabinius Ianuarius Extricatianus during his year as aedile.

EDCS-25100405.translation: Livineius Victor, son of Livineius, of the Quirina tribe, perpetual priest, for the honor of the perpetual priesthood freely offered to him, decorated all the marble columns, the clock tower, the rostral monuments, the facades, and the porticoes with marble and stucco work at his own expense, and dedicated them.
EDCS-25100405.summary: This inscription details the generous public works funded by Livineius Victor, a perpetual priest, likely during the Imperial period.

EDCS-25100413.translation: Of our lord Hadrian Augustus, 220 years [after the founding of Rome?], with Agrippa as consul for the third time.
EDCS-25100413.summary: This inscription is a dating clause referring to Emperor Hadrian and mentioning a consul named Agrippa, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-25200049.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Lucius Pompeius Faustulus, dutiful, lived 5 years and 6 months. He is buried here.

EDCS-25200051.summary: A tombstone recording the death of Priscilia at the age of 9.

EDCS-25200063.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Pious Quintus Stella Felix lived for 76 years; he is buried here.

EDCS-25200094.text_edition: \n Hadriani Augusti domini locus Camerino et Nigro consulibus sub cura Agathae liberti\n
EDCS-25200094.translation: The property of Hadrian Augustus, lord. In the consulship of Camerinus and Niger, under the supervision of Agathus, a freedman.
EDCS-25200094.summary: A boundary or ownership inscription indicating land belonging to Hadrian Augustus, supervised by his freedman Agathus, dating to the consulship of Camerinus and Niger (likely in the early 2nd century AD).

EDCS-25200095.translation: [...] of Emperor Hadrian Augustus, our lord, in the consulship of Camerinus and Niger.
EDCS-25200095.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely commemorating an event or building project under Emperor Hadrian, mentioning consuls for dating.

EDCS-25200096.translation: Of Emperor Antoninus Augustus... No. 751, workshop... Under Emperor Antoninus and... under the supervision of Agatha.
EDCS-25200096.summary: An incomplete inscription mentioning Emperor Antoninus Augustus, a workshop number, and supervision by Agatha, likely related to imperial administration or property during Antoninus Pius's reign.

EDCS-25200097.translation: In the consulship of Orfitus and Priscinus, from the account of Callistus. No. 61. Certus...
EDCS-25200097.summary: An incomplete inscription mentioning the consuls Orfitus and Priscinus, an account of Callistus, and a number, likely an administrative record or ledger entry from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25200099.translation: From the accounts of the workshop of Agens Callistus, freedman of Augustus, number 444.
EDCS-25200099.summary: This inscription records an accounting detail from a workshop belonging to Agens Callistus, a freedman of Augustus.

EDCS-25200100.summary: This inscription records a person named Callistus, possibly identifying a group or a count.

EDCS-25200101.translation: From the account of Felix, 1st August, number 724.
EDCS-25200101.summary: This inscription appears to be a record of an account or inventory related to an individual named Felix, possibly during the reign of an emperor named Augustus.

EDCS-25200113.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Flavius Domitianus, may your bones rest well, may the earth lie lightly upon you. Titus Flavius VETE, legate of Augustus Trajan, from [---].
