EDCS-25200728.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespans of two individuals, Banus Guddem and Ancia Victorina.

EDCS-25200729.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Lucius Octavius Sabb[---] TIMI[---]
EDCS-25200729.summary: A fragmentary funerary inscription dedicated to Lucius Octavius Sabb[---] dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25200732.translation: Helvia Commoda, dutiful, lived 35 years. Caius Julius Bitus, her husband, a veteran of the II Cohort of Thracians, set this up.
EDCS-25200732.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Helvia Commoda, set up by her husband Caius Julius Bitus, a veteran.

EDCS-25200734.translation: Felix Zobbori, generous to himself with... Felix Zobbori, generous to himself with.
EDCS-25200734.summary: This is a fragmented inscription, possibly a dedication or funerary text, mentioning an individual named Felix Zobbori and a sense of generosity.

EDCS-25200738.translation: Lucius Geminius Saturianus erected this for his patron, a military tribune of the III Cyrenaic Legion, and a decemvir for judging lawsuits, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-25200738.summary: This is a funerary or honorary inscription honoring a patron who held significant military and judicial positions, erected by his client Lucius Geminius Saturianus with official approval.

EDCS-25300036.translation: Flavia Faustiana, 20 iugera and 6 feet of land at Diana's. Likewise Sabinius Munianus, the Sextian farm, 28 iugera and 8 feet of land.
EDCS-25300036.summary: This inscription records a land transaction or property division, detailing plots belonging to Flavia Faustiana and Sabinius Munianus.

EDCS-25300037.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Dead. Iulius Fortunatus, a good man, a multiplier, invincible, lived 24 years, 10 months, 1 day, 6 hours.
EDCS-25300037.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Iulius Fortunatus, detailing his lifespan and praising his character.

EDCS-25300039.translation: Caius Herennius Secundus, dutiful, lived 5 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-25300039.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a young child, Caius Herennius Secundus, recording his age and burial.

EDCS-25300040.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Marcus Iulius Borodes.
EDCS-25300040.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to the spirits of the underworld by Marcus Iulius Borodes.

EDCS-25300041.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Quintus Licinius Dativus lived 28 years, 7 months, and 10 days. May your bones rest well; may the earth lie lightly upon you.
EDCS-25300041.summary: This funerary inscription records the life span of Quintus Licinius Dativus and includes wishes for his afterlife.

EDCS-25300042.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Octavianus Miccasi lived 80 years and 3 months; he is buried here.
EDCS-25300042.summary: This funerary inscription records the life span of Octavianus Miccasi and states he is buried here.

EDCS-25300043.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Tanonia Arthemis the pious lived 19 years, 10 months, and 11 days. Sacred to the spirits of the underworld; may the earth lie lightly upon you; may your bones rest well.
EDCS-25300043.summary: This funerary inscription records the life span of Tanonia Arthemis and includes wishes for her afterlife.

EDCS-25300044.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Valeria Maior the pious lived 40 years, 8 months, and 8 days; she is buried here.
EDCS-25300044.summary: This funerary inscription records the life span of Valeria Maior and states she is buried here.

EDCS-25300046.translation: He lived 10 years; he is buried here. May the earth lie lightly upon you; may your bones rest well.
EDCS-25300046.summary: This funerary inscription records the age of a person and includes wishes for their afterlife.

EDCS-25300049.summary: This inscription, possibly funerary, commemorates Candida's faithfulness and peaceful rest.

EDCS-25300051.translation: Felix, in peace, may your spirit be well.
EDCS-25300051.summary: This inscription, likely funerary, wishes Felix peace and well-being for his spirit.

EDCS-25300056.translation: To Marcus Porcius, son of Flaminalis, of the Quirina tribe, Dextrianus, aedile and perpetual flamen, who bequeathed 100 sesterces of his own property to his fatherland, so that from the interest of 200,000 sesterces, a theatrical performance might be presented each year on his birthday, and to each of the decurions a gift of five denarii, by decree of the decurions, from public funds.
EDCS-25300056.summary: This inscription records a posthumous endowment by Marcus Porcius to fund annual games and gifts to officials, established by a decree of the decurions.

EDCS-25300058.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Elucius Roc[...], son of Rinis, the pious, lived 105 years.
EDCS-25300058.summary: This funerary inscription records the age of Elucius Roc[...], son of Rinis, who lived to 105 years.

EDCS-25300063.translation: To our rulers, the Augusti, Salvis and Valent, Felix, freedman of Vlagius, paid.
EDCS-25300063.summary: This is a dedication made by Felix, a freedman, likely to the emperors Valent and Salvis, possibly referencing a financial contribution.

EDCS-25300065.translation: To Megethus, son of Lucius, of the Papiria tribe, a decurion, who was promoted to aedilician rank, served as flamen perpetuus, and held all other offices, and who, on account of his office of aedilician rank, staged theatrical games, and furthermore, for his aedileship, spent more than 300,000 sesterces.
EDCS-25300065.summary: This inscription honors Megethus, detailing his cursus honorum and significant financial contributions to public games and his aedileship, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25300066.translation: Publius Memmius Octavianus, a veteran, erected this for his incomparable son, Memmius Victorinus, who was honored with the public horse, a man of esteemed memory, because of his exceptional and tireless devotion to his father. The site was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-25300066.summary: This monument, erected by a veteran father for his son, records the son Memmius Victorinus's honor and filial piety, with the site granted by local authorities.

EDCS-25300067.translation: Lucius Licinius Rogatianus, son of Lucius, of the Papiria tribe, a decurion who was promoted.
EDCS-25300067.summary: This is a simple dedication or record of office for Lucius Licinius Rogatianus, a decurion promoted to higher rank.

EDCS-25300069.translation: To the departed spirits, Lucius Bionius Felix lived 110 years.
EDCS-25300069.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespan of Lucius Bionius Felix, who lived to be 110 years old.

EDCS-25300071.translation: Sacred to Minerva Augusta. Honoratus Rogati, a citizen of Vazaritanus, because of the decurionate of Rogatus, his son, donated and arranged for the construction of a statue for 900 sesterces, adding 400 sesterces from his own funds. He also dedicated it.
EDCS-25300071.summary: This dedication to Minerva Augusta records a donation by Honoratus Rogati for the construction and dedication of a statue in honor of his son's decurionate, indicating a transaction involving currency.

EDCS-25300072.summary: This is a simple dedication to the goddess Victoria Augusta.

EDCS-25300077.translation: To our lord Flavius Gratianus, perpetual Augustus, the municipium of Septimius Liberum Aulodes, most devoted to his divinity and majesty.
EDCS-25300077.summary: This inscription declares the devotion of the municipium of Septimius Liberum Aulodes to the emperor Flavius Gratianus, likely dating to his reign in the late 4th century AD.

EDCS-25300078.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Cassius Honorius lived 2 years, 5 months, 12 days.
EDCS-25300078.summary: This funerary inscription records the short lifespan of Lucius Cassius Honorius, who died at the age of 2 years, 5 months, and 12 days.

EDCS-25300081.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus Fannius Primulus lived seventy years and four months. He lies here.
EDCS-25300081.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespan of Quintus Fannius Primulus as seventy years and four months, indicating his burial place.

EDCS-25300084.translation: For the safety of the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius, son of [---], of the Arnensian tribe, from Carthage, AT, after it was enlarged from its entirety, O.
EDCS-25300084.summary: This inscription, likely from Carthage, records a dedication for the safety of Emperor Marcus Aurelius, possibly on a public building enlarged at that time.

EDCS-25300086.translation: The community of Uccula, by decree of the Africans, erected [this monument] for Gaius Anniolenus Gallianus, son of Gaius, of the Arnensian tribe, from Carthage, flamen of the deified Titus.
EDCS-25300086.summary: This inscription records a public dedication made by the community of Uccula for Gaius Anniolenus Gallianus, a local magistrate and priest, likely from the late 1st or early 2nd century AD.

EDCS-25300087.inscription_type: carmina, tituli fabricationis, tituli operum, tituli sacri
EDCS-25300087.translation: [---] many citizens have always enjoyed [---] in civic life, and the majesty of the unconquered divine Mars, crafted by hand, stands firm; the divine power of Ingenui saw something similar to himself, which was reformed into something better, a certain image with a more venerable countenance, and all the signs demonstrate that such a work, perfected, is religion itself, which makes his own camp shine perpetually, with Cilonius as the maker, whose love still grows in number among the great, because he prepares this for him to have a happy life and at the same time shows it with better fame, and he also made a vow willingly with his spirit. For he gave a gymnasium and wine to Martensibus, and thus not undeservedly, because he paid the offering to be presented to the deity as it certainly commanded, and he produced his own image with his money. // To Mars the Unconquered by Cilonius // To Mars the Unconquered by Cilonius
EDCS-25300087.summary: This dedication, made by Cilonius to Mars the Unconquered, records the construction of a gymnasium and the donation of wine, intended to enhance the prosperity and reputation of the soldiers' camp.

EDCS-25300088.translation: Caelus Primus and Victor, from the bequest of Caelus Primus, erected [this monument] for their father, Marcus Valerius Cestianus Publianus, son of Marcus, of the Arnensian tribe.
EDCS-25300088.summary: This inscription records a funerary monument erected by two individuals for their father, Marcus Valerius Cestianus Publianus, likely dating to the 2nd century AD.

EDCS-25300089.translation: Marcus Valerius, son of Marcus, of the Arnensian tribe, Cestianus Publianus, the council.
EDCS-25300089.summary: This inscription seems to be a fragmented dedication or record related to Marcus Valerius Cestianus Publianus and the local council.

EDCS-25300090.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Marcus Attius Tulinus lived for 33 years, 3 months, and 25 days; he is buried here.
EDCS-25300090.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the name, age at death, and burial location of Marcus Attius Tulinus, a private individual.

EDCS-25300092.translation: For the Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus, Parthicus Arabicus, Parthicus Adiabenicus, with tribunician power for the fourth time, emperor for the eighth time, consul for the second time, proconsul. Alfius Secundus, perpetual priest, erected two equestrian statues, worth 12,000 sesterces, which Lucius Alfius Felix, his father, had promised for double the sum as an honorary gift for the perpetual priesthood, by permission of the council, from his own liberality.
EDCS-25300092.summary: This inscription records the erection of two equestrian statues by Alfius Secundus, honoring his father Lucius Alfius Felix, and commemorating the emperor Septimius Severus, likely dating to the early 3rd century CE.

EDCS-25300093.translation: Caesar Augustus, Imperator, Consul for the fourth time, Tribune of the Plebs for the second time, O II OI O VC EIIC A I IIAV ICIIIS II, made this statue which his same father had promised, and for the dedication he gave a feast to the council.
EDCS-25300093.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Caesar Augustus, likely referring to his adoptive father, Julius Caesar, involving the erection and dedication of a statue with a public banquet.

EDCS-25300094.translation: For Tiberius Apraius Felix, son of Quintus, of the Papiria tribe, Paratus, aedile, perpetual priest, a good man, lover and protégé of his municipality, because of his incomparable gift of projectiles, in honor of his aedileship, and also for the great construction of a bathing establishment from his sheer liberality, the people, with contributions of money, erected this; the site was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-25300094.summary: This monument, erected by public subscription and approved by the decurions, honors Tiberius Apraius Felix for his generosity as an aedile and for funding the construction of a bathing complex.

EDCS-25300095.translation: To Marcus Munius Primus Optatianus, Roman knight, perpetual flamen, most generous and magnificently munificent citizen, patron.
EDCS-25300095.summary: This inscription is a dedication or honorific text for Marcus Munius Primus Optatianus, a prominent local citizen and magistrate, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century AD.

EDCS-25300096.summary: This fragmented inscription likely records a decree or grant of rights by Secundus, a member of the town council (decurion).

EDCS-25300099.translation: Sacred to Saturn Augustus. Lucius Remmius Faustus, with his son Avitus, built this temple and his statue from his own funds from the foundations and also dedicated it by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-25300099.summary: This inscription records the private construction and dedication of a temple and statue to Saturn Augustus by Lucius Remmius Faustus and his son, approved by the town council.

EDCS-25300101.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. To Livia Honorata, faithful, simple, devout, pious, such as never was and never can be, her husband erected this monument, a gift of grateful memory. She lived 57 years, months.
EDCS-25300101.summary: This tombstone inscription honors Livia Honorata, recording her virtues and the gift of the monument from her grieving husband, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century AD.

EDCS-25300102.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Marcus Iulius Amicus, dutiful, lived for 73 years, 5 months, and 59 hours.
EDCS-25300102.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Marcus Iulius Amicus.

EDCS-25300106.translation: While Emperor Caesar Augustus was consul for the 13th time, and Marcus Plautius Silvanus was consul, Marcus Titurnius Africanus, son of Marcus, of the Arnensian tribe, rebuilt the temple of Tellus. HNC [perhaps 'honoris causa' - as an honor].
EDCS-25300106.summary: This inscription records the rebuilding of the temple of Tellus by Marcus Titurnius Africanus during the consulship of Augustus and Marcus Plautius Silvanus.

EDCS-25300109.translation: He made and dedicated [this] with his own money, the conqueror of Adiabene and Parthia.
EDCS-25300109.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by an individual who was honored for military victories, likely a private dedication.

EDCS-25300113.translation: Marcus Aurelius Amaonius, a soldier of the First Urban Cohort.
EDCS-25300113.summary: This is a military inscription identifying Marcus Aurelius Amaonius as a soldier in the First Urban Cohort.

EDCS-25300114.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Aemilia Cogitata, dutiful, lived for 9 years.
EDCS-25300114.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the short lifespan of Aemilia Cogitata.

EDCS-25300115.translation: Caius Annius Martialis Sicinianus, dutiful, lived for 53 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-25300115.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan and burial place of Caius Annius Martialis Sicinianus.

EDCS-25300116.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Antius, also called Fuscus, lived for 5 years, 5 months, and 15 days.
EDCS-25300116.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Antius Fuscus.

EDCS-25300117.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Apronius lived for 68 years.
EDCS-25300117.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Apronius.

EDCS-25300119.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Caecilius Crescens, dutiful, lived for [unknown duration].
EDCS-25300119.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the name and dutiful nature of Caecilius Crescens, with an incomplete lifespan.

EDCS-25300120.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Caecilia Victoria, dutiful, lived for 40 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-25300120.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan and burial place of Caecilia Victoria.

EDCS-25300121.translation: Quintus Caninius Felix, son of Gaius, dutiful, lived 15 years, is buried here.
EDCS-25300121.summary: This is a tombstone recording the life and burial of Quintus Caninius Felix, who died at the age of 15.

EDCS-25300122.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Gaius Caninius Victoricus, a freedman, lived 1 year.
EDCS-25300122.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to the Divine Shades and records the short life of Gaius Caninius Victoricus, a freedman who died at age 1.

EDCS-25300123.translation: Gaius Cornelius Lucidus, dutiful, lived 21 years, is buried here.
EDCS-25300123.summary: This tombstone records the life and burial of Gaius Cornelius Lucidus, who died at the age of 21.

EDCS-25300124.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Iulia Rioda, dutiful, lived 20 years.
EDCS-25300124.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to the Divine Shades and records the life of Iulia Rioda, who died at the age of 20.

EDCS-25300125.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Oppius Solutor lived 36 years, is buried here.
EDCS-25300125.summary: This tombstone is dedicated to the Divine Shades and records the burial of Oppius Solutor, who died at the age of 36.

EDCS-25300126.translation: Servilius Callistus lived 80 years, 6 months, 8 days.
EDCS-25300126.summary: This inscription records the lifespan of Servilius Callistus, who lived to be 80 years, 6 months, and 8 days old.

EDCS-25300127.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Gaius Trebius Fuscus Felix, son of Gaius, dutiful, lived.
EDCS-25300127.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to the Divine Shades and records the life of Gaius Trebius Fuscus Felix, son of Gaius.

EDCS-25300128.summary: This inscription appears to be the beginning of a funerary dedication or a public record, possibly for Gaius Valerius Nampamo.

EDCS-25300129.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Volussia Privata, dutiful, lived 3 years, is buried here.
EDCS-25300129.summary: This tombstone is dedicated to the Divine Shades and records the burial of Volussia Privata, who died at the young age of 3.

EDCS-25300130.translation: [...]rino, an excellent drinker, good, lived 40 years, is buried here.
EDCS-25300130.summary: This tombstone records the burial of an individual, possibly named [... ]rino, known for drinking, who died at the age of 40.

EDCS-25300134.summary: This inscription is a simple epitaph for a person named Marcianus.

EDCS-25300136.translation: For the safety of the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus, Armenian, Mede, Parthian the Great, Germanicus, and of Augusta Faustina, and of their children, two victories, which Gaius Annedius Severus had promised for the honor of the decurionate of Gaius Annedius Honoratus Severus Terentianus and Gaius Annedius Severus, his sons, according to the assessed legal requirements before the acts, Gaius Annedius Honoratus Severus Terentianus, his son, set up with increased funds and himself dedicated it; the site was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-25300136.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by Gaius Annedius Honoratus Severus Terentianus, likely during the reign of Marcus Aurelius Antoninus (likely Caracalla, given the titles), for the safety of the emperor and his family, commemorating a donation made for the decurionate.

EDCS-25300137.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Quintus Octavius, son of Quintus, of the Cornelia tribe, Primus, a young man of excellent character, designated aedile, pious, lived 23 years, 6 months, 17 days, is buried here.
EDCS-25300137.summary: This is a tombstone for Quintus Octavius Primus, who died at a young age before holding the office of aedile, dating likely to the Imperial period.

EDCS-25300139.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Mamilia Rufilla, a pious sambuca player, lived 80 years.
EDCS-25300139.summary: This is an epitaph for Mamilia Rufilla, who played the sambuca, an ancient musical instrument, and lived to be 80 years old.

EDCS-25300140.translation: A man, pious, lived 69 years, is buried here on his own land.
EDCS-25300140.summary: This is a tombstone for an unnamed man who was pious and lived to 69 years old, buried on his own property.

EDCS-25300141.summary: This is a very brief inscription, likely a name marker on a tomb or monument.

EDCS-25300142.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Marcus Allius, duovir.
EDCS-25300142.summary: This is an epitaph for Marcus Allius, who held the office of duovir, likely in a municipal context.

EDCS-25300143.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Lucius Antonius Festus, pious, lived 40 years.
EDCS-25300143.summary: This is an epitaph for Lucius Antonius Festus, who lived to 40 years of age.

EDCS-25300144.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Antonia Quarta, pious, lived 75 years.
EDCS-25300144.summary: This is an epitaph for Antonia Quarta, who lived to 75 years of age.

EDCS-25300145.translation: Arruntia Victoria, pious, excellent, faithful, lived 65 years, is buried here.
EDCS-25300145.summary: This is a tombstone for Arruntia Victoria, who was remembered for her piety, excellence, and faithfulness, and lived to 65 years.

EDCS-25300146.translation: Avial Fecanea lived 30 years, she is buried here.
EDCS-25300146.summary: This is a tombstone recording the life and burial of Avial Fecanea.

EDCS-25300147.translation: Gaius Aufidius, son of Quintus, of the Horatia tribe, pious, lived 25 years.
EDCS-25300147.summary: This is a tombstone recording the life of Gaius Aufidius, son of Quintus.

EDCS-25300148.translation: Aufidia Horn, lived 75 years, they are buried here.
EDCS-25300148.summary: This is a tombstone recording the life and burial of Aufidia Horn.

EDCS-25300149.translation: Marcus Cecilius, son of Marcus, to his father, with all his belongings.
EDCS-25300149.summary: This is a funerary dedication from Marcus Cecilius to his father.

EDCS-25300150.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Caecilius Namfami, pious, lived 21 years, he is buried here.
EDCS-25300150.summary: This is a tombstone recording the life and burial of Caecilius Namfami.

EDCS-25300151.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Caelia Sissin lived 2 years, she is buried here.
EDCS-25300151.summary: This is a tombstone recording the life and burial of Caelia Sissin.

EDCS-25300152.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Titus Cor[...]
EDCS-25300152.summary: This is a funerary dedication to the departed spirits, likely for Titus Cornelius.

EDCS-25300153.translation: Marcus Cornelius Qua[...], of the Ummidia family, to his father [or mother/brother/sister/etc.].
EDCS-25300153.summary: This is a funerary dedication from Marcus Cornelius to a family member.

EDCS-25300154.summary: This is a tombstone recording the life of Cornelius Vitalis.

EDCS-25300155.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Gaius Domitius Colonicus, pious, lived 70 years, he is buried here.
EDCS-25300155.summary: This is a tombstone recording the life and burial of Gaius Domitius Colonicus.

EDCS-25300156.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Domitius Festus lived 80 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-25300156.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Domitius Festus, who lived to be 80 years old.

EDCS-25300157.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Domitia Urbica, daughter of Caius, lived 8 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-25300157.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Domitia Urbica, aged 8.

EDCS-25300158.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Fabius Faustus, pious, lived 5 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-25300158.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Fabius Faustus, aged 5.

EDCS-25300159.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Fortunata, who lived to be 80 years old.

EDCS-25300160.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Gargilia, pious wife, lived [XX] years.
EDCS-25300160.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Gargilia, a pious wife, with an incomplete age.

EDCS-25300161.translation: Lucius Granius, son of Cnaeus, of the Fabia tribe, lived 60 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-25300161.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Lucius Granius, who lived to be 60 years old.

EDCS-25300162.translation: Quintus Granius, son of Quintus, Siccus, lived 15 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-25300162.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Quintus Granius Siccus, aged 15.

EDCS-25300163.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. M. amus Ingenus, pious, lived 21 years.
EDCS-25300163.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Ingenus, who lived to be 21 years old.

EDCS-25300164.translation: Caius Iulius Priami filius lived 80 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-25300164.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Caius Iulius Priami filius, who lived to be 80 years old.

EDCS-25300165.translation: Caius Iulius Saturninus, pious, lived 70 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-25300165.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Caius Iulius Saturninus, who lived to be 70 years old.

EDCS-25300166.translation: Iulius Victor, son of Caius, of the Quirina tribe, dutiful, lived 60 years; he rests here.
EDCS-25300166.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the death of Iulius Victor, who lived to be 60 years old.

EDCS-25300167.translation: Marcus Lepidius Crispus, dutiful, lived 75 years; he rests here.
EDCS-25300167.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the death of Marcus Lepidius Crispus, who lived to be 75 years old.

EDCS-25300168.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Licinia Aufilia Nevia, AN, rests here.
EDCS-25300168.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the departed spirits, commemorating Licinia Aufilia Nevia.

EDCS-25300169.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. M. Primus, dutiful, lived 30 years; he rests here.
EDCS-25300169.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the departed spirits, recording the life of M. Primus who lived to be 30 years old.

EDCS-25300170.translation: Lucius Marcius, son of Quintus, of the Fabia tribe, lived dutifully 70 years. May his bones rest well.
EDCS-25300170.summary: This tombstone records Lucius Marcius, son of Quintus, who lived a dutiful life of 70 years and expresses a wish for his remains.

EDCS-25300171.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Maria Prima, dutiful, lived 75 years; she rests here.
EDCS-25300171.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the departed spirits, recording the death of Maria Prima, who lived to be 75 years old.

EDCS-25300172.translation: Memmia Candida, daughter of Lucius, lived 3 years; she rests here.
EDCS-25300172.summary: This tombstone records the short life of Memmia Candida, daughter of Lucius, who died at the age of 3.

EDCS-25300173.translation: Miccra Sallutia, daughter of Lucius, lived 33 years; she rests here on her own property.
EDCS-25300173.summary: This tombstone records that Miccra Sallutia, daughter of Lucius, lived 33 years and is buried on her own land.

EDCS-25300175.translation: Octavia, daughter of Aulus, [of the tribe] Via.
EDCS-25300175.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription identifying Octavia, daughter of Aulus, and her tribal affiliation.

EDCS-25300176.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Orbia Fortunata, daughter of Marcius, dutiful, lived 20 years; she rests here.
EDCS-25300176.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the departed spirits, recording the death of Orbia Fortunata, who lived to be 20 years old.

EDCS-25300177.translation: Pinaria Urbana, daughter of Marcus, dutiful, lived 30 years, is buried here.
EDCS-25300177.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the life and burial of Pinaria Urbana, who died at the age of 30.

EDCS-25300178.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Pompei SICV.
EDCS-25300178.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the Manes (spirits of the dead), possibly naming the deceased as Pompei or a location related to Pompei.

EDCS-25300179.translation: Sallustia Gemella, daughter of Caius, dutiful, lived 85 years, is buried here.
EDCS-25300179.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the life and burial of Sallustia Gemella, who died at the age of 85.

EDCS-25300180.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Sesia, dutiful, lived 12 years, is buried here.
EDCS-25300180.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the life and burial of Sesia, who died at the age of 12.

EDCS-25300181.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Sextilia Ianuaria, daughter of Lucius, dutiful, lived 39 years, is buried here.
EDCS-25300181.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the life and burial of Sextilia Ianuaria, who died at the age of 39.

EDCS-25300182.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Silicia Ianuaria, dutiful, lived 70 years, is buried here.
EDCS-25300182.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the life and burial of Silicia Ianuaria, who died at the age of 70.

EDCS-25300183.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Silvanus lived 4 years, is buried here.
EDCS-25300183.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the life and burial of Silvanus, who died at the age of 4.

EDCS-25300184.summary: This is a tombstone inscription identifying the deceased as Lucius Velonius Clemens.

EDCS-25300185.translation: Quintus Vellonius Clemens lived 53 years, is buried here.
EDCS-25300185.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the life and burial of Quintus Vellonius Clemens, who died at the age of 53.

EDCS-25300186.summary: This inscription appears to be a funerary text for Publius Velonius Lemonia, though part of the text is illegible or incomplete.

EDCS-25300187.translation: Velonia Fortunata, daughter of Quintus, dutiful, lived 21 years, is buried here. Publius Grosanius Marsus made this for his wife.
EDCS-25300187.summary: A funerary epitaph for Velonia Fortunata, dedicated by her husband Publius Grosanius Marsus.

EDCS-25300188.translation: Vibia, daughter of Publius, lived 74 years, is buried here.
EDCS-25300188.summary: A funerary epitaph for Vibia, daughter of Publius.

EDCS-25300189.translation: To Ulpia, his dearest and deserving wife, Excitatus made this. [She was] dutiful, lived 25 years.
EDCS-25300189.summary: A funerary epitaph for Ulpia, dedicated by her husband Excitatus.

EDCS-25300190.translation: Gaius Volussenius Vitalis, son of Caius, of the Arnensian tribe, lived 80 years, is buried here.
EDCS-25300190.summary: A funerary epitaph for Gaius Volussenius Vitalis.

EDCS-25300192.translation: Minus, dutiful, lived 26 years, is buried here.

EDCS-25300193.translation: Marci's freedwoman, dutiful, lived 80 years, is buried here.
EDCS-25300193.summary: A funerary epitaph for Marci's freedwoman.

EDCS-25300194.translation: Quintus Caecilius Bassus, son of Quintus, of the Collina tribe, lived 94 years, is buried here.
EDCS-25300194.summary: A funerary epitaph for Quintus Caecilius Bassus.

EDCS-25300328.translation: The sons placed this for the well-deserving, sacred to the departed spirits. Pacuia Felicissima, dutiful, lived 89 years, is buried here. May your bones rest well. Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus Aurelius Zabullus, dutiful, lived 80 years, is buried here. May the earth rest lightly upon you.
EDCS-25300328.summary: A funerary monument for Pacuia Felicissima and Quintus Aurelius Zabullus, placed by their sons.

EDCS-25300332.translation: [To] Ieriae, sacred to Augusta. [Quintus] Furfanius Martialialis, son of Quintus, of the Lemnian tribe, paid for the statues to be made with his own money [for his honors] as dual magistrate and flamen of Augustus, by decree [of the decurions], beyond the sum [---] for the honor of the quinquennality, and moreover [he provided] games and a banquet twice and 10,000 modii of wheat, with the cost at ten denarii each from [---] denarii, [given] by Bellicus, his father, to the people in his name. [Likewise also] sportulas to the order twice.
EDCS-25300332.summary: An inscription recording the public benefactions of Quintus Furfanius Martialialis, including funding statues and public amenities, likely during the late 1st or early 2nd century CE.

EDCS-25300334.translation: Lucius Aemilius Crescens fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-25300334.summary: An inscription recording Lucius Aemilius Crescens fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-25300335.translation: Titus Anicius willingly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-25300335.summary: A dedication fulfilling a vow by Titus Anicius.

EDCS-25300336.summary: A dedication fulfilling a vow by Lucius Caeus.

EDCS-25300337.summary: An inscription that appears to be a name, possibly of a person or a dedication recipient.

EDCS-25300338.translation: Quintus Clodius Amarantus willingly fulfilled his vow with a willing spirit.
EDCS-25300338.summary: A dedication fulfilling a vow by Quintus Clodius Amarantus.

EDCS-25300339.translation: Diodore fulfilled his vow to Saturn.
EDCS-25300339.summary: A dedication fulfilling a vow to the god Saturn by Diodore.

EDCS-25300340.summary: An inscription that appears to be a dedication to Iulius Caius Fabius.

EDCS-25300341.translation: Caius Anicius Faustus fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-25300341.summary: A dedication fulfilling a vow by Caius Anicius Faustus.

EDCS-25300342.summary: A dedication fulfilling a vow by Fausta.

EDCS-25300344.translation: Caius Iulius Lare fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-25300344.summary: A dedication fulfilling a vow by Caius Iulius Lare, likely to a deity.

EDCS-25300347.summary: A dedication fulfilling a vow by Lucius Lollius.

EDCS-25300349.summary: This is a votive inscription recording Lucius Marcius fulfilling a vow, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-25300350.translation: [---]estius, husband, and his wife, fulfilled their vow willingly.
EDCS-25300350.summary: A fragmentary inscription recording a vow fulfilled by a husband and wife, likely a funerary or dedicatory monument.

EDCS-25300352.translation: Lucius Octavius willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-25300352.summary: This votive inscription records Lucius Octavius willingly fulfilling a vow, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-25300353.translation: Marcus, son of Publius, fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-25300353.summary: This is a votive inscription recording Marcus, son of Publius, fulfilling a vow, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-25300355.translation: Aulus Pomponius Asclepius fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-25300355.summary: This is a votive inscription recording Aulus Pomponius Asclepius fulfilling a vow, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-25300356.summary: This is a votive inscription recording Upelusus fulfilling a vow, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-25300358.translation: [...]ius, son of C[---]nus, willingly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-25300358.summary: This is a votive inscription recording the fulfillment of a vow by an individual whose name is partially lost, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-25300359.translation: Lucius, son of Lucius, of the tribe Cornelia, fulfilled his vow willingly.
EDCS-25300359.summary: This votive inscription records Lucius, son of Lucius, of the tribe Cornelia, fulfilling his vow, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-25300368.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Caius Iulius Herennianus lived for 13 years and is buried here. Sacred to the Divine Shades. Caius Iulius Martialis, a veteran of the II Adiutrix Pia Fidelis legion, which is stationed in Lower Pannonia at Aquincum.
EDCS-25300368.summary: This funerary inscription records the life and death of a young boy, Caius Iulius Herennianus, and also mentions his father, Caius Iulius Martialis, a veteran stationed in Aquincum, likely dating to the 2nd century AD.

EDCS-25300369.translation: Titus Trebius, son of Titus, of the Camilia tribe, from Pisaurum, a veteran, lived for 81 years and is buried here.
EDCS-25300369.summary: This funerary inscription records the life and death of Titus Trebius, a veteran from Pisaurum, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-25300370.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Caius Domitius Primus Iulianus, son of Caius, of the Quirina tribe, who served as aedile and quaestor in his own colony.
EDCS-25300370.summary: This funerary inscription records the life and public service of Caius Domitius Primus Iulianus, who held magistracies in his home colony, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-25300371.translation: Quintus Furfanius Felix Bellicus, having fulfilled all offices in his colony, as perpetual priest of Augustus, having contributed money for the perpetual priesthood, dedicated this by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-25300371.summary: This is a public dedication by Quintus Furfanius Felix Bellicus for his perpetual priesthood in his colony, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-25300385.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Rogata, dutiful, lived 125 years.
EDCS-25300385.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Rogata, recording her name, filial piety, and long lifespan, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25300386.translation: Quintus Stallus Extricatus, dutiful, lived 20 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-25300386.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Quintus Stallus Extricatus, recording his name, piety, age, and burial place, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25300418.translation: To the Prince of Youth, our lord Flavius Valentinianus Invictus Augustus, dedicated by the devoted Thibiuca.
EDCS-25300418.summary: This is a dedication to the Emperor Valentinian III by a woman named Thibiuca, likely dating to the 5th century CE.

EDCS-25300419.text_edition: \n Quinto Caecilio Quinti filio Arnensi Marcello Dentiliano Xviro stlitibus iudicandis tribuno militum legionis XI Claudiae piae fidelis quaestori provinciae Africae aedili curuli candidato divi Hadriani praetori candidato eiusdem legato provinciae Cretae Cyrenarum legato provinciae Hispaniae proconsuli provinciae Cretae Cyrenarum legato legionis XII fulminatae legato Augusti pro praetore provinciae Galliae Aquitanicae coloniae patrono Thibiucenses aere conlato\n
EDCS-25300419.translation: To Quintus Caecilius Quintus son Arnensis Marcellus Dentilianus, member of the XV viri for judging lawsuits, military tribune of the XI Claudian Pia Fidelis legion, quaestor of the province of Africa, curule aedile, candidate for the same, praetor, candidate for the same, legate of the province of Crete and Cyrene, legate of the province of Hispania, proconsul of the province of Crete and Cyrene, legate of the XII Fulminata legion, legate of Augustus as proconsul of the province of Gallia Aquitania, patron of the colony. The people of Thibiuca, with contributions of money, erected this.
EDCS-25300419.summary: This extensive honorary inscription celebrates the extensive career of Quintus Caecilius Quintus son Arnensis Marcellus Dentilianus, detailing his military, judicial, and administrative posts, and his patronage of the colony of Thibiuca, likely dating to the Hadrianic or Antonine period.

EDCS-25401715.translation: SE having fulfilled his offices in his colony, dutiful, lived for [unknown number of] years.
EDCS-25401715.summary: This incomplete tombstone inscription records a man's service to his colony and his lifespan, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25401716.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Sextus Iulius Victor Aniceanus, dutiful, lived 35 years; he is buried here. Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Terentia Zosima, dutiful, lived 105 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-25401716.summary: This is a double tombstone inscription for Sextus Iulius Victor Aniceanus and Terentia Zosima, recording their lifespans and burial, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25401717.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Memmia Maxima, daughter of Lucius, dutiful, lived 5 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-25401717.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for the young child Memmia Maxima, recording her name, parentage, age, and burial, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25401718.translation: Vettia Ammia, daughter of Caius, dutiful, lived 20 years.
EDCS-25401718.summary: This tombstone inscription records the name, parentage, and age of Vettia Ammia, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25401719.translation: [Unclear text] ... dutiful, lived 39 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-25401719.summary: This incomplete tombstone inscription records a woman's lifespan and burial, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25401720.translation: Gaius Cocceius Festus, dutiful, lived 63 years.
EDCS-25401720.summary: This tombstone inscription records the name and lifespan of Gaius Cocceius Festus, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25401721.translation: Lucius Iulius Salvianus, son of Quintus, of the Palatina tribe, dutiful, lived 23 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-25401721.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Lucius Iulius Salvianus, recording his age at death and burial place.

EDCS-25401722.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Castis Blanda, dutiful, lived 27 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-25401722.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Castis Blanda, recording her age at death and burial place.

EDCS-25401723.translation: Quinta, daughter of Caius, dutiful, lived 60 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-25401723.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Quinta, recording her age at death and burial place.

EDCS-25401724.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Quintus ETIIVS E A lived. Sacred to the Divine Spirits. I Bieia MA M N A I lived for years. He is buried here. Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Mapia Mima, dutiful, lived 70 years. P Q XX I.
EDCS-25401724.summary: This inscription, though fragmented, records the lives and burials of at least two individuals, Quintus ETIIVS E A and Mapia Mima, who lived to 70 years old.

EDCS-25401726.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Demetrius Ianuarius lived 80 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-25401726.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Demetrius Ianuarius, recording his age at death and burial place.

EDCS-25401727.translation: X, dutiful, lived 42 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-25401727.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for an individual identified only as 'X', recording his age at death and burial place.

EDCS-25401728.translation: Lucius Licinius Rufus, son of Lucius, of the Quirina tribe, aedile, dutiful, lived 70 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-25401728.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Lucius Licinius Rufus, an aedile, recording his age at death and burial place.

EDCS-25401729.translation: ius, physician, dutiful, lived 28 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-25401729.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for an individual identified by his profession as a physician, recording his age at death and burial place.

EDCS-25401730.translation: Marcus Gallius Cal iius, dutiful, lived 58 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-25401730.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Marcus Gallius Cal iius, recording his age at death and burial place.

EDCS-25401731.summary: This inscription is too fragmented to provide a meaningful translation or summary.

EDCS-25401732.translation: Sacred to Saturn Augustus; Publius Octavius Fortunatus, the priest, built the temple from the ground up and enclosed it with a wall, and dedicated it at his own expense.
EDCS-25401732.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a temple to Saturn Augustus by the priest Publius Octavius Fortunatus.

EDCS-25401733.translation: Pontilia Festa, dutiful, lived 55 years; she is placed here. May her bones rest well.
EDCS-25401733.summary: This is a tomb inscription for Pontilia Festa, who lived 55 years.

EDCS-25401735.text_edition: \n Pro salute Imperatoris Caesaris Marci Aureli Severi Antonini Pii Felicis Augusti Parthici maximi Germanici maximi Britannici maximi pontificis maximi tribunicia potestate imperatoris III consulis IIII patris patriae proconsulis et Iuliae Domnae Augustae Piae Felicis matris Augusti et castrorum et senatus et patriae totiusque domus divinae Sentius Felix Repostus ob honorem fili sui Luci Senti Felicis Repostiani flamonii perpetui sive XI primatus et magisterii non administrati sua pecunia fecit\n
EDCS-25401735.translation: For the health of Imperator Caesar Marcus Aurelius Severus Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus Parthicus Maximus, Germanicus Maximus, Britannicus Maximus, chief priest, with tribunician power for the third time, consul for the fourth time, father of the country, proconsul, and of Iulia Domna Augusta Pia Felix, mother of the emperor, of the camps, of the senate, and of the whole country, and of the entire divine household. Sentius Felix Repostus made this at his own expense for the honor of his son Lucius Sentius Felix Repostianus, perpetual priest, and holder of the XI primatus and magistracy, which he did not administer.
EDCS-25401735.summary: Sentius Felix Repostus dedicated this to ensure the health of Emperor Caracalla and Empress Julia Domna, commemorating his son Lucius Sentius Felix Repostianus's honorary priesthood, likely dating to the early 3rd century CE.

EDCS-25401736.translation: The city of Furnos, by decree of its decurions and with public funds, erected this monument to the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus, son of Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus Arabicus Adiabenicus Parthicus Maximus, grandson of the deified Marcus Aurelius Pius Germanicus Sarmaticus, great-grandson of the deified Antoninus Pius, great-great-grandson of the deified Hadrian, great-great-great-grandson of the deified Trajan Parthicus and the deified Nerva.
EDCS-25401736.summary: This inscription records the erection of a public monument by the city of Furnos to Emperor Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus, likely during his reign (170s-180 AD).

EDCS-25401737.translation: The entire populace, by decree of the decurions and with public funds, erected a statue to Lucius Octavius Felicianus Octavianus, decurion of the colony of Iulia Aurelia Antoniniana Karthago, flamen of the deified Pius, master of the Cerealian rites in the year 276 (of the province), professor of the aedileship, patron, and twice curator of the municipality of Aureli Antoniniani Furnitani Minores, because of his outstanding justice and benevolence; on the occasion of its dedication, he himself gave theatrical games and a banquet to the people, and a site for a gymnasium was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-25401737.summary: This inscription records the erection of a statue and the granting of a gymnasium site to Lucius Octavius Felicianus Octavianus, a prominent local official in Furnos, by the populace, and his subsequent gifts of games and a banquet.

EDCS-25401738.translation: The entire populace, by decree of the decurions and with public funds, granted a site to Quintus Paccius Victor Candidianus, who had been honored with public equestrian status, master of the Ceres rites in the year 264 (of the province), flamen of the deified Severus, and curator of the public affairs of his municipality of Furnitani Minores, because of his incomparable affection for all his fellow citizens.
EDCS-25401738.summary: This inscription records the granting of a site to Quintus Paccius Victor Candidianus, a local official in Furnos, by the populace in recognition of his affection for the citizens.

EDCS-25401739.translation: A site was granted to Cassia Victoria, daughter of Caius, by Sentia Rogatiana, her daughter, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-25401739.summary: This inscription records the granting of a burial plot by a daughter to her mother, Cassia Victoria, by decree of the decurions.

EDCS-25401740.summary: This inscription is a short, sentimental phrase, possibly a dedication or a personal remembrance.

EDCS-25401742.translation: Flavius Vitalis, perpetual flamen, twice curator of the state, lived.
EDCS-25401742.summary: This inscription commemorates Flavius Vitalis, who held the positions of perpetual flamen and twice curator of the state.

EDCS-25401743.translation: Cottinus, the faithful physician-in-chief, departed in peace on the seventh day before the Ides of January.
EDCS-25401743.summary: This is an epitaph for Cottinus, a physician-in-chief, who died on January 7th.

EDCS-25401744.summary: This is a brief epitaph for Blossus, emphasizing his virtues of innocence and faithfulness.

EDCS-25401745.translation: Karthago, faithful, lived in peace for one year, 2 months, and 15 days.
EDCS-25401745.summary: This inscription records the lifespan of a loyal individual named Karthago.

EDCS-25401746.translation: Victor, innocent, lived in peace for eight years, three months, and twenty-one days.
EDCS-25401746.summary: This inscription records the lifespan of an innocent individual named Victor.

EDCS-25401747.summary: This inscription records the peaceful death of a loyal individual named Victor.

EDCS-25401749.translation: Blossius Honoratus Ingenuus, actor, completed [this monument].
EDCS-25401749.summary: This inscription records the completion of a monument by Blossius Honoratus Ingenuus, an actor.

EDCS-25401750.translation: Rutunda, faithful, died in peace on the 13th day before the Kalends of November.
EDCS-25401750.summary: This inscription records the death of a loyal individual named Rutunda on a specific date.

EDCS-25401752.translation: To the deified Aurelian Augustus, from the townspeople of the municipium of Sicilibba.
EDCS-25401752.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the deified emperor Aurelian by the citizens of Sicilibba.

EDCS-25401753.translation: To Flavius Valerius Constantinus, most noble Caesar, consul for the second time, from the municipium of Sicilibbenses.
EDCS-25401753.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Caesar Flavius Valerius Constantinus by the citizens of Sicilibbenses.

EDCS-25401754.translation: To Quintus Commius Armiger Crescentius, most distinguished man, curule aedile, official from the acts of the senate, quaestor, member of the second turma of the Arn equites, one of the ten men for judging disputes, and incomparable patron, from the townspeople of the Sicilibbenses.
EDCS-25401754.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Quintus Commius Armiger Crescentius, a prominent official, by the citizens of Sicilibbenses.

EDCS-25401759.summary: This inscription records the peaceful repose of Gellius Eulutus.

EDCS-25401760.translation: For Aurelius Antoninus, son of Augustus, of both orders.
EDCS-25401760.summary: A brief dedication to Aurelius Antoninus, son of Augustus, likely referring to the Emperor Caracalla and indicating his connection to both senatorial and equestrian classes.

EDCS-25401764.translation: [...rumo], an outstanding man, our proconsul of the province of Africa.
EDCS-25401764.summary: This inscription likely honors a proconsul of Africa named Rumonus or similar.

EDCS-25402333.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Concordia lived for [---] years.
EDCS-25402333.summary: A funerary dedication to the Divine Spirits for Concordia, stating her lifespan.

EDCS-25402334.translation: To Saturn. Lucius Furius Seleucus, freedman of Lucius, saw [this vision].
EDCS-25402334.summary: A dedication to the god Saturn, possibly related to a divine vision experienced by Lucius Furius Seleucus.

EDCS-25402335.translation: Sacred to Saturn Augustus. D. Secundus willingly paid his vow.
EDCS-25402335.summary: A votive inscription to Saturn Augustus, where D. Secundus fulfilled a promise.

EDCS-25402336.translation: To Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus Armeniacus, Pontifex Maximus, holding tribunician power for the 19th time, Imperator for the 3rd time, Consul for the 3rd time, by decree of the town council, at public expense.
EDCS-25402336.summary: An official inscription honoring Emperor Marcus Aurelius Antoninus, dating to his 19th tribunician year and 3rd consulship, funded by the state.

EDCS-25402337.translation: For the most blessed age of Our Invictus Lords, our Emperors Constantinus the Great, Victor, Forever Augustus, and Constantinus the Younger, and Constantius, most glorious Caesars, a temple or curia, and also a sexagonal building, and a curia which had collapsed from its foundations, during the proconsulship of Marcus Ceionius Iulianus, most distinguished man, and of his legate Gezilius Largus Maternianus, most distinguished man, patrons of our colony, by the plan and with the assistance of Lucius Modius Valention, curator of our republic, with [---] overseeing.
EDCS-25402337.summary: A lengthy inscription detailing public works, including the construction and restoration of buildings, commissioned during the proconsulship of Marcus Ceionius Iulianus and overseen by Lucius Modius Valention, honoring the emperors of the time, likely late 4th century CE.

EDCS-25402338.translation: Maria Extricata, high priestess, dutiful, lived for 103 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-25402338.summary: A funerary epitaph for Maria Extricata, a high priestess, recording her long life and burial.

EDCS-25402340.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Kalventius lived for [---] years.
EDCS-25402340.summary: A funerary dedication to the Divine Spirits for Kalventius, stating his lifespan.

EDCS-25402341.translation: Felix Icius lived for 20 years; may your bones rest well, may the earth be light upon you.
EDCS-25402341.summary: A funerary epitaph for Felix Icius, wishing peace for his remains and a light burial.

EDCS-25402342.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Ingenus lived for six years and two hours.
EDCS-25402342.summary: A funerary dedication to the Divine Spirits for Ingenus, detailing his very short lifespan.

EDCS-25402344.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Fudina, daughter of Vacurtus, [dedicated this to] Varsis.
EDCS-25402344.summary: A dedication to the Divine Spirits, possibly a funerary offering from Fudina to Varsis.

EDCS-25402351.translation: To Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Commodus Antoninus Augustus, conqueror of Sarmatia, greatest of the Germans, Lurio Lucullus, procurator, and on behalf of others, as a sacred offering prescribed by the discipline and example.
EDCS-25402351.summary: This inscription records a sacred offering related to Emperor Commodus, likely set up by a procurator.

EDCS-25402354.translation: To Mars the Protector, for the health of the Emperors Severus and Antoninus, and of Geta Caesar, prince of youth, and of Julia Domna Augusta, mother of the camps, Marcus Rossius Vitulus, procurator ducenarius (of the second rank) for the public works of the province of Africa.
EDCS-25402354.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Mars for the health of the imperial family, set up by a high-ranking procurator in Roman Africa, likely during the Severan period.

EDCS-25402356.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Iulius Icisinus lived for 33 years, pious, in peace.
EDCS-25402356.summary: This is a tomb inscription for Iulius Icisinus, recording his age and virtuous character.

EDCS-25402358.translation: With tribunician power for the 10th time, consul. From Maximilla... gifts.
EDCS-25402358.summary: This fragmentary inscription mentions a consul and tribunician power, likely recording some official act or donation.

EDCS-25402359.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Seranus lived for 75 years.
EDCS-25402359.summary: This is a tomb inscription for Seranus, recording his age.

EDCS-25402361.translation: Sacred to Silvanus Augustus. For the health of Lucius Petronius Pompeius Chresimus, in fulfillment of a vow, Crescens gave this gift from his own funds.
EDCS-25402361.summary: This is a votive inscription to the god Silvanus, dedicated by Crescens for the well-being of Lucius Petronius Pompeius Chresimus.

EDCS-25402363.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Lucius Octavius Baric, pious, (lived) twenty years.
EDCS-25402363.summary: This is a tomb inscription for Lucius Octavius Baric, recording his age and piety.

EDCS-25501626.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Selecta Venusta, dutiful, lived 72 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-25501626.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Selecta Venusta, recording her age and burial place.

EDCS-25501627.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Selectus Gududus.
EDCS-25501627.summary: This is a funerary epitaph, likely for Selectus Gududus, dedicated to the departed spirits.

EDCS-25501630.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Gaius Sallustius Caprentius, dutiful, lived 85 years and 7 months; he is buried here.
EDCS-25501630.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Gaius Sallustius Caprentius, recording his age and burial place.

EDCS-25501631.translation: Sacred to Jupiter Best and Greatest, Juno Regina, and Augusta Minerva. Lucius Memmius Pecuarius Marcellinus, with his own funds and in the name of his son Lucius Memmius Marcellus Pecuarianus, a decurion of the colony of Iulia Karthago and designated flamen of the deified Nerva, built and dedicated the temple of the Capitol, which he had promised to his homeland, the Numiulitan people and community, for 20,000 sesterces, and for the honor of the priesthood of his wife Iunia Saturnina, he contributed 4,000 sesterces from the treasury of both orders; he completed it with his own funds, embellished with marble and statues and every amenity. For this dedication, he gave gifts to the decurions of both orders and a feast and gymnasium to the people. Furthermore, due to the high price of grain, he very generously provided grain to the people at a much lower price than was current at that time. He also continuously provided theatrical performances and gymnasia.
EDCS-25501631.summary: This is a monumental dedication inscription by Lucius Memmius Pecuarius Marcellinus, detailing his construction and embellishment of a temple of the Capitol, along with numerous public benefactions in the colony of Iulia Karthago, likely in the late 2nd or early 3rd century CE.

EDCS-25501633.translation: To the Parthian Victor, Pontifex Maximus, with tribunician power for the 21st time, Imperator for the 5th time. By public money and decree of the decurions.
EDCS-25501633.summary: This is a dedication inscription for a public work in the colony of Numiulites, funded by the state and approved by the local council, likely honoring an emperor.

EDCS-25501634.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely referring to a public work or honor approved by the local council.

EDCS-25501638.translation: He made an arch with his own money. Imperator IIII S Augustus.
EDCS-25501638.summary: This is a dedication inscription for an arch, funded by an individual and possibly related to an imperial celebration or visit.

EDCS-25501640.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Of Quintus Avilius Ro[---].
EDCS-25501640.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary epitaph dedicated to the departed spirits.

EDCS-25501641.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Cesia Mamonia, dutiful, lived about 75 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-25501641.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Cesia Mamonia, recording her approximate age and burial place.

EDCS-25501642.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Flavius.
EDCS-25501642.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary epitaph dedicated to the departed spirits.

EDCS-25501643.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Gududus, son of Ali, piously lived 12 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-25501643.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Gududus, son of Ali, who died at the age of 12.

EDCS-25501644.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Iabenia Victoria piously lived 100 years.
EDCS-25501644.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Iabenia Victoria, who lived to be 100 years old.

EDCS-25501645.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. IVNI M AI piously lived 3 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-25501645.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of IVNI M AI, who died at the age of 3.

EDCS-25501646.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Maius Sudemis lived 75 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-25501646.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Maius Sudemis, who died at the age of 75.

EDCS-25501648.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Pomponius Primus piously lived 61 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-25501648.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Pomponius Primus, who died at the age of 61.

EDCS-25501649.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Marcus Siccius Victor piously lived 45 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-25501649.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Marcus Siccius Victor, who died at the age of 45.

EDCS-25501650.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Vitruvia Quieta piously lived 91 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-25501650.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Vitruvia Quieta, who died at the age of 91.

EDCS-25501651.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Volumnia Secunda piously lived 21 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-25501651.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Volumnia Secunda, who died at the age of 21.

EDCS-25501654.translation: He is buried here; she lived 90 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-25501654.summary: This fragmentary funerary inscription records the burial and age of an unknown individual.

EDCS-25501658.translation: To F. Tettius, for his service as *duovir* and *aedile*, of exceptional memory, Marcus Tettius Gallicus Clodianus, Roman knight, perpetual priest, son of them both after service as *duovir* and *aedile*.
EDCS-25501658.summary: This inscription honors F. Tettius for his public offices and commemorates his son, Marcus Tettius Gallicus Clodianus, a Roman knight and perpetual priest, possibly a dedication from the son to the father.

EDCS-25501659.translation: Of the Divine Severus Pius Pertinax.
EDCS-25501659.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the emperor Severus, likely part of a larger monument, dating to his reign.

EDCS-25501661.translation: While our Lords Honorius and Theodosius, perpetual Augusti, were in power, and while Quintus Sentius Fabricius Julianus, a most distinguished man, was serving as proconsul for the second time and judging with sacred authority, Marcus Aurelius Restitutus, a former senator and curator of the republic, along with his distinguished council, placed statues and decorated the fishpond.
EDCS-25501661.summary: This inscription records the dedication of statues and the decoration of a fishpond by Marcus Aurelius Restitutus during the joint reign of Honorius and Theodosius, under the proconsulate of Julianus.

EDCS-25501662.translation: Marcus Staberius Saturninus willingly fulfilled his vow to Mercury Augustus.
EDCS-25501662.summary: This is a votive inscription by Marcus Staberius Saturninus dedicating something to Mercury Augustus.

EDCS-25501663.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Marcus Rumicilius Cato, pious, lived 75 years, 10 months, 15 days, 11 hours. Calcidia Prima made this for her good husband in memory, for a place for herself and her family.
EDCS-25501663.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Marcus Rumicilius Cato, set up by his wife Calcidia Prima, recording his age and the space for their family plot.

EDCS-25501664.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Publius Sallustius Guddem lived 96 years, six months.
EDCS-25501664.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Publius Sallustius Guddem, recording his age.

EDCS-25501665.translation: To Tiberius Caesar, son of Augustus, Augustus, high priest, consul for the fifth time, imperator for the eighth time, holding tribunician power for the thirty-fourth time, Gaius Septumius Saturninus, son of Gaius, a priest, made four columns at his own expense, under the supervision of Lucius Lurius Rufus, son of Quintus.
EDCS-25501665.summary: This is a dedication for four columns made at the expense of Gaius Septumius Saturninus, a priest, to Emperor Tiberius, likely dating to the early imperial period.

EDCS-25501667.translation: To Longeius, son of Quintus Longeius Festus, admitted to the public equestrian order, prefect of the cohort of Roman citizens equipped with shields, from Alexandria. Sextia, daughter of Quintus Peducaeus Speus, his mother and perpetual priestess of the Carthaginians, made this for her pious, excellent, most holy, most worthy son.
EDCS-25501667.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by a mother for her son, Longeius, who held military and civic offices, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-25501670.translation: The Republic of the municipium of Suessa, devoted to the divine power and majesty of the Emperor Caesar Flavius Claudius Julianus Maximus Pius Felix Invictus Augustus, high priest, holder of tribunician power, father of the fatherland, proconsul, dedicated this with public money by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-25501670.summary: This inscription records a dedication by the municipality of Suessa to Emperor Julian the Apostate, funded by public money.

EDCS-25501671.translation: To Gaius Julius Meander, father-in-law of Lucius Popilius Primus Africanus, the Roman citizens of Suessa gave this gift in recognition of his merit.
EDCS-25501671.summary: This inscription records a gift given by the citizens of Suessa to Gaius Julius Meander, their father-in-law, for his merits.

EDCS-25501672.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Quintus Magibius Saturninus, pious, lived 62 years, 10 months. He is buried here.
EDCS-25501672.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Quintus Magibius Saturninus, recording his age and burial location.

EDCS-25501675.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Fabius.
EDCS-25501675.summary: A funerary dedication by Fabius to the Manes, likely from an imperial period tomb.

EDCS-25501676.translation: Modia Quintina, daughter of Caius, dutiful, lived 32 years. Her husband placed her here, devoted to his most distinguished wife.
EDCS-25501676.summary: A funerary epitaph for Modia Quintina, recording her name, parentage, devotion, age at death, and placement by her husband, likely from the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-25501680.translation: By the authority of Emperor Vespasian Caesar Augustus, father of the country, the boundaries of the new and old province were delimited by the royal ditch which was there, under the consulship of Rutilius Gallicus.
EDCS-25501680.summary: A boundary stone from the reign of Vespasian (69-79 CE), marking the provincial limits under the consulship of Rutilius Gallicus.

EDCS-25501682.summary: A dedication to the god Saturn, possibly with imperial associations ('Augustus'), likely from a public or private shrine.

EDCS-25501683.translation: To Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Augustus.
EDCS-25501683.summary: A dedication honoring the emperor Septimius Severus, likely from a public building or monument, dating to his reign (193-211 CE).

EDCS-25501684.translation: To our Lords Honorius and Theodosius, the baths and the splendor of the city, from money of the fourth part (of income), with the innate generosity of [?] they dedicated this, which administered the public walls of the city of...? without any contribution from the order of citizens, while Quintus Sentius Fabricius Julianus was (governor/official) III.
EDCS-25501684.summary: A dedication for the construction or renovation of baths and city walls, commissioned by Quintus Sentius Fabricius Julianus, honoring Emperors Honorius and Theodosius, likely from the early 5th century CE.

EDCS-25501686.translation: Lucius Aquilius Calma, a dutiful centurion, lived 70 years.
EDCS-25501686.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lucius Aquilius Calma, recording his name, rank, devotion, and age at death, likely from the Roman army.

EDCS-25501687.translation: Restored by those above. And the flamen perpetuus Rosario made all the porticoes with fabricis... with...
EDCS-25501687.summary: A restoration inscription by an unknown 'those above', and a dedication for the construction of porticoes by Rosario, a perpetual priest, likely from a Roman city's public works.

EDCS-25501691.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Caius Aurelius Rogatianus Noggumianus, dutiful, lived 35 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-25501691.summary: A funerary dedication by Caius Aurelius Rogatianus Noggumianus to the Manes, recording his name, devotion, age at death, and burial place, likely from an imperial period tomb.

EDCS-25501692.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Datus, son of Lenti Cestoris, dutiful, lived 105 years. He is buried here. To you, bones.
EDCS-25501692.summary: A funerary epitaph for Datus, son of Lenti Cestoris, recording his name, devotion, exceptional age at death, and burial place, likely from an imperial period tomb.

EDCS-25501693.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Felix, son of Primus, pious, aged 45, lies here. May his bones rest well; may the earth be light upon you.
EDCS-25501693.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Felix, son of Primus, aged 45, with a common Latin funerary formula.

EDCS-25501694.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Fortunata, pious, lived 5 years.
EDCS-25501694.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Fortunata, aged 5, with a common Latin funerary formula.

EDCS-25501695.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Fortunata, daughter of Quintus Cerrellius, pious, lived 16 years, lies here.
EDCS-25501695.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Fortunata, daughter of Quintus Cerrellius, aged 16, with a common Latin funerary formula.

EDCS-25501697.summary: An epitaph dedicating a monument to a father named Iulianus.

EDCS-25501698.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Marcus Iulius Lucpusan lived 26 years and 7 months, lies here.
EDCS-25501698.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Marcus Iulius Lucpusan, aged 26 years and 7 months, with a common Latin funerary formula.

EDCS-25501699.summary: An incomplete funerary epitaph recording the name Iulia Venusta and her pious character, with an age placeholder.

EDCS-25501700.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Marcius.
EDCS-25501700.summary: A fragmentary funerary epitaph recording the name Marcius with the standard dedication to the Divine Spirits.

EDCS-25501703.translation: Gaius Ubicus Filapioius, pious, lived 14 years, lies here. May his bones rest well; may the earth be light upon you.
EDCS-25501703.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Gaius Ubicus Filapioius, aged 14, with a common Latin funerary formula.

EDCS-25501705.summary: A very fragmentary inscription likely recording a dedication to a wife.

EDCS-25501706.summary: A funerary epitaph recording an unnamed pious individual aged 61, with a common Latin funerary formula.

EDCS-25501712.translation: Bonosa, faithful, lived in peace for 4 years and 2 months.
EDCS-25501712.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Bonosa, a Christian woman, noting her lifespan.

EDCS-25501713.translation: To our Emperor Caesar Augustus, Attia Quieta (dedicates this).
EDCS-25501713.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Emperor Augustus by Attia Quieta.

EDCS-25501714.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo pro salute Imperatoris Caesaris Augusti Luci Severi et Marci An<t=I>onini [et] G[etae] Caesaris Augusti et Iuliae Domnae Augustae Lurius Seius veteranus legionis II adiutricis piae <f=I>idelis votum solvit no et BS consulibus Tauro et verre \n
EDCS-25501714.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, for the safety of the Emperor Caesar Augustus Lucius Severus and Marcus Antoninus Caesar Augustus and Geta Caesar Augustus and Julia Domna Augusta, Lurius Seius, a veteran of the Second Legion Adjutant, pious and faithful, fulfilled his vow, with Taurus and Verre as consuls, and [consuls] Tauro and Verre.
EDCS-25501714.summary: This is a votive inscription by a veteran to Jupiter for the welfare of the imperial family, dating to the consulship of Taurus and Verre, likely in the early 3rd century AD.

EDCS-25501715.translation: To be honored with the highest honors of the nobles of the Caesars and of the entire divine house, the curatores Caecilius Feliciano and Perdūcerunt, with the public granary, carried out and dedicated it on their own land.
EDCS-25501715.summary: This inscription details the construction and dedication of a public granary, overseen by Caecilius Feliciano, likely during the imperial period.

EDCS-25501717.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcus Datilus.
EDCS-25501717.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicating the tomb to the departed spirits on behalf of Marcus Datilus.

EDCS-25501720.summary: This is a funerary inscription, possibly identifying Aelia Cairionis by a cognomen or ethnic origin.

EDCS-25501722.translation: Sacred to Saturn Augustus. Gaius Aurelius.
EDCS-25501722.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the god Saturn Augustus by Gaius Aurelius.

EDCS-25501723.translation: Sacred to Saturn Augustus. Publius Valerius Clitus paid his vow willingly.
EDCS-25501723.summary: This inscription records Publius Valerius Clitus fulfilling a vow to the god Saturn Augustus.

EDCS-25501731.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Aemilia Venusta, dutiful, lived 80 years, is buried here. May your bones rest well. May the earth be light upon you.
EDCS-25501731.summary: This is a detailed funerary inscription for Aemilia Venusta, noting her age, burial, and offering blessings for her rest.

EDCS-25501732.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcus An[---]
EDCS-25501732.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription dedicated to the departed spirits, mentioning Marcus An[---].

EDCS-25501733.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Marcus Antonius Rufus Honorati filius Tromentina Veiis Arnensis Thignicae genius veritatis pius vixit annis hic situs est ossa tibi bene quiescant terra tibi levis sit \xce\x9f\xe1\xbc\xb5\xce\xb7 \xcf\x80\xce\xb5\xcf\x81 \xcf\x86\xe1\xbd\xbb\xce\xbb\xce\xbb\xcf\x89\xce\xbd \xce\xb3\xce\xb5\xce\xbd\xce\xb5\xe1\xbd\xb5, \xcf\x84\xce\xbf\xe1\xbd\xb7\xce\xb7 \xce\xb4\xe1\xbd\xb2 \xce\xba\xce\xb1\xe1\xbd\xb6 \xe1\xbc\x80\xce\xbd\xce\xb4\xcf\x81\xe1\xbf\xb6\xce\xbd\n
EDCS-25501733.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Marcus Antonius Rufus, son of Honoratus, of the Tromentina tribe, of Veiis Arnensis Thignicae, the spirit of truth, pious, lived X years. He lies here. May your bones rest well, may the earth be light upon you. May the divine power protect you, and the gods favor you.
EDCS-25501733.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Marcus Antonius Rufus, recording his lifespan and expressing wishes for his peaceful repose, also containing Greek blessings for the deceased.

EDCS-25501734.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Ecurius Speratus lived [---] years, is buried here.
EDCS-25501734.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Ecurius Speratus, noting his burial and a partially preserved lifespan.

EDCS-25501735.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Quintus Gavius Geminius, dutiful, lived 35 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-25501735.summary: A funerary epitaph for Quintus Gavius Geminius, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25501736.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Lucretia Bruttia Praesentillia, dutiful, lived 34 years. She is buried here. May your bones rest well; may the earth lie lightly upon you.
EDCS-25501736.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lucretia Bruttia Praesentillia, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25501737.summary: A dedication to Procula, wife of Cerialis, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25501738.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Pullus.
EDCS-25501738.summary: A funerary epitaph for Pullus, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25501739.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Pullaenia Laeta lived [for] years. May your bones rest well.
EDCS-25501739.summary: A funerary epitaph for Pullaenia Laeta, with an incomplete age, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25501740.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Titus Volussius Quintilianus, dutiful, lived 18 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-25501740.summary: A funerary epitaph for Titus Volussius Quintilianus, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25501742.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Inianus lived to be 20 years old, whom the destructive disaster...
EDCS-25501742.summary: A funerary epitaph for Inianus, whose death was attributed to a 'destructive disaster', dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25501746.translation: ISIIL sna lived in peace, faithful, 70 years. Departed on the 12th day before the Kalends of May.
EDCS-25501746.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan and death date (April 20th) of ISIIL sna, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25501748.translation: Sacred to Mercury Augustus. Quintus A N fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-25501748.summary: A votive inscription dedicated to Mercury Augustus by Quintus A N, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25501749.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Luria Augenda, dutiful, lived 23 years. May she rest well; may the earth lie lightly upon you.
EDCS-25501749.summary: A funerary epitaph for Luria Augenda, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25501751.translation: Sacred to the Augustan gods, for the welfare of Imperator Caesar Marcus Aurelius Severus Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus, father of the fatherland, and to Julia Domna Pia Felix Augusta, mother of our camp and senate, the citizen body of Sustritana erected this from a collected fund.
EDCS-25501751.summary: This inscription records a dedication by the citizens of Sustritana to the Augustan gods for the welfare of Emperor Caracalla and his mother Julia Domna, likely dating to their joint reign.

EDCS-25501752.translation: Sacred to Jupiter Best and Greatest, Juno Regina, and the Augustan Fortune, for the welfare of Imperator Caesar Marcus Antonius Gordianus Pius Felix Augustus, chief priest, invested with tribunician power, consul, father of the fatherland, the people of Sustritana rebuilt from the foundations an temple ruined by age and enlarged a cistern, and they dedicated it on the birthday of our lord Augustus, and for both these joyous occasions, they feasted.
