EDCS-25501752.summary: This inscription records the rebuilding and dedication of a temple and cistern by the people of Sustritana to Jupiter, Juno, and Fortune, for the welfare of Emperor Gordian III, likely dating to his reign.

EDCS-25501753.translation: Sacred to Saturn Augustus, Zabo Nargrani, priest.
EDCS-25501753.summary: This is a dedication to Saturn Augustus by a priest named Zabo Nargrani, likely from the Roman province of Africa.

EDCS-25501755.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Aelia Saturnina, dutiful, lived for 75 years. She is laid here. May your bones rest well. May the earth be light upon you.
EDCS-25501755.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Aelia Saturnina, providing her age at death and customary wishes for her repose.

EDCS-25501756.translation: MALLETI, dutiful, lived for 90 years. He is laid here. May your bones rest well. May the earth be light upon you.
EDCS-25501756.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a person named Malleti, providing his age at death and customary wishes for his repose.

EDCS-25501757.translation: Dutiful, lived for 10 months and 21 days. He is laid here. May his bones rest well.
EDCS-25501757.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for an infant or young child, providing their lifespan and customary wishes for their repose.

EDCS-25501759.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Germinius Germinianus, dutiful, lived for 31 years, 11 months, and 20 days.
EDCS-25501759.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Germinius Germinianus, providing his age at death.

EDCS-25501763.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Bullatia daughter of Caius, Anthia, dutiful, lived for 40 years, 9 months, and 17 days. Caius Calvisius Honoratianus made this for his most virtuous wife. She is laid here. May your bones rest well. May the earth be light upon you.
EDCS-25501763.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Bullatia Anthia, set up by her husband Caius Calvisius Honoratianus, providing her age at death and customary wishes for her repose.

EDCS-25501764.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Caius Calvisius Honoratus, dutiful, lived for 41 years, 3 months, and 21 days. He is laid here. May your bones rest well. May the earth be light upon you.
EDCS-25501764.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Caius Calvisius Honoratus, providing his age at death and customary wishes for his repose.

EDCS-25501765.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Caecilius Victor, [son of] AMISIAIIC, dutiful, lived for 45 years. He is laid here. May his bones rest well. May the earth be light upon you.
EDCS-25501765.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Caecilius Victor, providing his age at death and customary wishes for his repose.

EDCS-25501766.translation: Here lies. She lived 55 years. May her bones rest well. May the earth be light upon you.
EDCS-25501766.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for an individual, likely a woman, indicating her lifespan and a wish for a peaceful afterlife.

EDCS-25501767.translation: Here lies Donus Attius, pious. He lived 100 years. May his bones rest well.
EDCS-25501767.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Donus Attius, noting his advanced age and expressing a wish for his soul's repose.

EDCS-25501768.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Hanna Honobia, pious, lived 45 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-25501768.summary: This funerary inscription records the death and burial of Hanna Honobia, stating her age.

EDCS-25501769.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Mundicius Faustus, pious, lived 81 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-25501769.summary: This funerary inscription records the death and burial of Mundicius Faustus, stating his age.

EDCS-25501770.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Urria Victorina, pious, lived 18 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-25501770.summary: This funerary inscription records the death and burial of Urria Victorina, stating her young age.

EDCS-25501771.translation: Sacred to Saturnus Augustus. Felix Canius Baliatus willingly paid his vow.
EDCS-25501771.summary: This inscription records a votive offering made by Felix Canius Baliatus to the god Saturnus Augustus.

EDCS-25501772.translation: Sacred to Saturnus Augustus. Martialis, son of Silvanus Bannonis, willingly paid his vow for his priesthood.
EDCS-25501772.summary: This inscription records a votive offering made by Martialis to Saturnus Augustus in fulfillment of a vow related to his priestly office.

EDCS-25501773.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Trajan Hadrian Augustus, father of the fatherland. Philoxenus, son of [---], built and dedicated an arch from its foundations for his own promotion and for the banquet of his son Philoxenus, with additional funds.
EDCS-25501773.summary: This inscription records the dedication of an arch by Philoxenus to Emperor Hadrian, commemorating his own promotion and a banquet for his son, likely dating to Hadrian's reign (117-138 AD).

EDCS-25501774.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Gaius Granius Kalendio, perpetual priest, pious, lived 88 years. May his bones rest well. May the earth be light upon you.
EDCS-25501774.summary: This funerary inscription records the death and burial of Gaius Granius Kalendio, a perpetual priest, noting his age and offering wishes for his afterlife.

EDCS-25501775.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Gaius Aecudius Augentius lived 53 years. May your bones rest well. May the earth be light upon you.
EDCS-25501775.summary: This funerary inscription records the death and burial of Gaius Aecudius Augentius, stating his age and offering wishes for his afterlife.

EDCS-25501776.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Gaius Aecudius Augentius the Younger, son of Gaius Aecudius Augentius, lived here and is buried here.
EDCS-25501776.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Gaius Aecudius Augentius the Younger, stating his name, parentage, and that he is buried here.

EDCS-25501777.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Bullatius Fortunatus, son of Faustinus, pious, lived 80 years and is buried here.
EDCS-25501777.summary: This funerary epitaph records the life and burial of Bullatius Fortunatus, son of Faustinus, who lived for 80 years.

EDCS-25501778.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Faustina, daughter of Gemellus Berecius, pious, lived 93 years and is buried here.
EDCS-25501778.summary: This funerary epitaph records the life and burial of Faustina, daughter of Gemellus Berecius, who lived for 93 years.

EDCS-25501779.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Numitorius V.
EDCS-25501779.summary: This is a very short funerary inscription for someone named Numitorius V.

EDCS-25501780.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Lucius Passenius Ingenus Scapela, pious, lived 45 years and is buried here.
EDCS-25501780.summary: This funerary epitaph records the life and burial of Lucius Passenius Ingenus Scapela, who lived for 45 years.

EDCS-25501781.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Tertulla, daughter of Septimius Gestaris, lived 35 years. Her husband, the former Nius Calendius, in order to reward her services to him and in remembrance of her, set up this altar for her.
EDCS-25501781.summary: This funerary inscription records that Nius Calendius set up an altar for his wife Tertulla, daughter of Septimius Gestaris, who lived 35 years, to honor her services.

EDCS-25501782.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. VSI VOI set up this altar for her husband to reward his services and to perpetuate his memory.
EDCS-25501782.summary: This funerary inscription records that VSI VOI set up an altar for her husband to honor his services and memory.

EDCS-25501783.translation: For perpetual memory of his most sweet mother, P.O. pacified.
EDCS-25501783.summary: This inscription records someone pacifying an altar for the perpetual memory of their mother.

EDCS-25501785.text_edition: \n Ex auctoritate Imperatoris Vespasiani Caesaris Augusti patris patriae fines provinciae sic novae et veteres derecti qua Fossa regia fuit per Rutilium Gallicum consulem pontificem et Sentium Caecilianum praetorem legatos Augusti pro praetore\n
EDCS-25501785.translation: By the authority of Emperor Vespasian Caesar Augustus, father of the country, the boundaries of the new and old provinces were rectified where the Royal Ditch was, through Rutilius Gallicus, consul and pontifex, and Sentius Caecilianus, praetor, legates of Augustus with proconsular authority.
EDCS-25501785.summary: This inscription records the rectification of provincial boundaries under Emperor Vespasian, carried out by imperial legates Rutilius Gallicus and Sentius Caecilianus.

EDCS-25501786.translation: Licinius Felicio lived 70 years. Licinius Felix for his father.
EDCS-25501786.summary: This epitaph records the death of Licinius Felicio at age 70, dedicated by his son, Licinius Felix.

EDCS-25501787.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Octavius Sronius, pious, lived 8 years. May your bones rest well, may the earth be light upon you.
EDCS-25501787.summary: This funerary epitaph records the death of the young Octavius Sronius at age 8, with wishes for his peaceful rest.

EDCS-25501788.translation: To Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Augustus, greatest conqueror of Parthia.
EDCS-25501788.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the emperor Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Augustus, likely from the title 'Parthicus Maximus' indicating a military victory around 166 AD.

EDCS-25501789.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Octavius Zabullus.
EDCS-25501789.summary: This is a funerary dedication to the 'Spirits of the Departed' (Dis Manibus) by Octavius Zabullus.

EDCS-25501790.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Aulus Marius Lampadarius, dutiful, lived 32 years, is buried here. Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Octavia Zabulla, dutiful, lived 55 years, is buried here.
EDCS-25501790.summary: This inscription is a double funerary dedication for Aulus Marius Lampadarius and Octavia Zabulla, recording their ages at death and burial.

EDCS-25501792.translation: Ucittinus lived 45 years, is buried here. Ianuaria lived 81 years, is buried here.
EDCS-25501792.summary: This inscription records the ages at death and burial for Ucittinus and Ianuaria.

EDCS-25501793.summary: This inscription records the age at death for Felix and begins a dedication for Gaius, though it is incomplete.

EDCS-25501794.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Maria Fortunata. Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Publius Patinius Felix.
EDCS-25501794.summary: This inscription is a double funerary dedication to the 'Spirits of the Departed' for Maria Fortunata and Publius Patinius Felix.

EDCS-25501796.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Publius Patinius Optatus, dutiful, lived 32 years and 1 day, is buried here.
EDCS-25501796.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Publius Patinius Optatus, recording his age and the day of his death.

EDCS-25501797.summary: This inscription records the age at death of an individual whose name is lost, likely a funerary dedication.

EDCS-25501798.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Felix Annobalis, dutiful, lived 55 years.
EDCS-25501798.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Felix Annobalis, recording his age at death.

EDCS-25501799.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Cornelia Sabuli filia, lived 76 years, is buried here.
EDCS-25501799.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Cornelia, daughter of Sabulus, recording her age at death and burial.

EDCS-25501800.translation: To the Divine Manes. Gaius Marius Masculus, son of Vor, lived 46 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-25501800.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Gaius Marius Masculus, recording his age and burial place.

EDCS-25501801.translation: To the Divine Manes. [Name and filiation], he lived 28 years.
EDCS-25501801.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary epitaph recording the age of the deceased.

EDCS-25501802.translation: To the Divine Manes. Lucius Pappus Solutor, pious, lived 36 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-25501802.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Pappus Solutor, recording his age and burial place.

EDCS-25501803.translation: To the Divine Manes. Lud, son of RD.
EDCS-25501803.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary epitaph likely recording the name and filiation of the deceased.

EDCS-25501804.translation: Lived 62 years; lived 25 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-25501804.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary epitaph recording burial information and possibly two different ages for the deceased.

EDCS-25600067.translation: To the Divine Manes. For Gabinia Matrona, companion, who died, harsh fate and fortune claimed her while she lived for 36 years not as she deserved; she passed away suddenly. Here lies the conscious aether. May she rest in peace.
EDCS-25600067.summary: This funerary epitaph laments the premature death of Gabinia Matrona after 36 years of life, attributing it to cruel fate.

EDCS-25600068.translation: To the Divine Manes. Marcus Sillius Gnomus lived 101 years.
EDCS-25600068.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcus Sillius Gnomus, recording his remarkable age.

EDCS-25600069.translation: To the memory of Doratus and Agutuais.
EDCS-25600069.summary: This is a funerary dedication commemorating Doratus and Agutuais.

EDCS-25600070.translation: To the Divine Manes. Musculosus lived 95 years.
EDCS-25600070.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Musculosus, recording his age.

EDCS-25600071.translation: To Queen Victoria, to the divinity of Hadrian. Ulpius Namphamo, who ordered the temple to be made, is himself the priest; who for 123 years did not drink wine. He had a daughter Heziva, who at six years old was taken away by her mistress. To Victoria, to Hercules Augustus, sacred.
EDCS-25600071.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a temple by Ulpius Namphamo to Hadrian and Victoria, mentioning his long life without wine and a daughter.

EDCS-25600072.translation: To Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus, son of the deified Marcus Aurelius Pius, conqueror of the Germans and the Sarmatians, brother of the deified Commodus, grandson of the deified Antoninus Pius, great-grandson of the deified Hadrian, great-great-grandson of the deified Trajan the Parthian, great-great-great-grandson of the deified Nerva, pontifex maximus, with tribunician power for the 6th time, imperator for the 11th time, consul for the 2nd time, father of the fatherland, proconsul, expander of the empire, Marcus Passenius Crescens, son of Placidi, for the honor of his magistracy, made this with 2,400,000 sesterces and more, adding 1,000,000 sesterces from his own funds, and he himself dedicated it.
EDCS-25600072.summary: This inscription records a public work funded and dedicated by Marcus Passenius Crescens in honor of his magistracy, dedicated to Emperor Septimius Severus.

EDCS-25600073.translation: To the departed spirits. Victoria Calamensis made this. She lived 65 years. Here.
EDCS-25600073.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the name of the deceased, Victoria Calamensis, and her age.

EDCS-25600074.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. VENVS K dedicated this.
EDCS-25600074.summary: This is a dedication to the departed spirits, with the dedicator named VENVS K.

EDCS-25600077.translation: Placed according to the will of Corneli Ziomedis. He lived 43 years, 3 months, and 12 days. Cornelius Fructosus made this for his brother in memory.
EDCS-25600077.summary: This is a funerary epitaph commemorating Cornelius Fructosus' brother, Corneli Ziomedis, mentioning his age and the circumstances of the monument's placement.

EDCS-25600080.summary: This is a short dedication to the god Saturn Augustus, with the dedicator identified as Felix.

EDCS-25600081.summary: This inscription is likely a funerary epitaph or dedication mentioning Marcus Iunius Rufinus, with the rest of the text lost.

EDCS-25600096.translation: To Apollo Augustus of Theveste, son of Caesar Augustus.
EDCS-25600096.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Apollo Augustus of Theveste, likely indicating a connection to the imperial family.

EDCS-25600097.summary: This is a dedication to Diana of Theveste, with a partial reference to an emperor or imperial cult.

EDCS-25600098.translation: Sacred to Fortuna Augusta. Caius Iulius Sexa willingly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-25600098.summary: This inscription records Caius Iulius Sexa fulfilling a vow to Fortuna Augusta.

EDCS-25600099.translation: Publius Vettius Saturninus, veteran, willingly fulfilled his vow to Jupiter Optimus Maximus Saturn.
EDCS-25600099.summary: This inscription records a veteran, Publius Vettius Saturninus, fulfilling a vow to Jupiter Optimus Maximus Saturn.

EDCS-25600100.translation: Sacred to Jupiter Optimus Maximus. Lucius Vindicius Saturninus.
EDCS-25600100.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Lucius Vindicius Saturninus.

EDCS-25600101.translation: Sacred to Minerva Augusta. Theseus, a freedman clerk, dedicated this at his own expense for the safety of our Emperors, Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus and Lucius Aurelius Verus Augustus.
EDCS-25600101.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Minerva Augusta by the freedman clerk Theseus for the safety of Emperors Marcus Aurelius Antoninus and Lucius Aurelius Verus, likely in the mid-2nd century CE.

EDCS-25600102.translation: Sacred to Neptune Augustus for the fortune of the age.
EDCS-25600102.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Neptune Augustus, likely for the prosperity of the era.

EDCS-25600103.translation: Sacred to Ops Augusta. Aulus Pompeius Dativus, by order of the most holy divine powers through the priests, made this at his own expense.
EDCS-25600103.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Ops Augusta by Aulus Pompeius Dativus, commissioned by religious authorities.

EDCS-25600104.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Virtus Augusta by Evasius.

EDCS-25600105.translation: Lucius Caecilius Saturninus Pulex, priest, willingly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-25600105.summary: This inscription records a priest, Lucius Caecilius Saturninus Pulex, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-25600106.translation: Sacred to Augustus, for the safety of Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Commodus Antoninus Augustus and Crispina Augusta. From Theveste, the most splendid city. In honor of the decurionate, Salvianus, father, disbursed the legal amount for the work. He also provided double that amount to the treasury, 20,000 sesterces, and the customary gifts to the decurions and the people; he also put on theatrical games. Furthermore, he added to this work double the customary gift for marble and gilded coffered ceilings and a retiring room from his quinquennial magistracy of the colony of Theveste. In the colony of Carthage, he provided a banquet and gymnasium for the people for the curiae and the Augustales, and erected this at his own expense.
EDCS-25600106.summary: This extensive inscription details the dedications and public benefactions of Salvianus, likely a prominent citizen of Theveste during the reign of Commodus and Crispina, including games, a gymnasium, and construction works.

EDCS-25600107.translation: Quintus Tedius Victor willingly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-25600107.summary: This inscription records Quintus Tedius Victor fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-25600108.translation: From the workshop of Augurius the craftsman.
EDCS-25600108.summary: This inscription indicates the origin of an object or work from the workshop of a craftsman named Augurius.

EDCS-25600111.translation: Valerius [erected] the porticoes from the very foundations at his own expense for the eternal Augusti, for the happy [future] and [the prosperity of] Paulinus.
EDCS-25600111.summary: This inscription records Valerius dedicating porticoes at his own expense to the perpetual emperors, likely during a period of imperial celebration or to honor Paulinus.

EDCS-25600114.translation: To Marcus Aemilius Clodianus, outstanding man, procurator of our Emperors for the imperial patrimony in the Leptiminan region and also for private property in the Tripolitanian region, for his outstanding integrity, the people of Sabratha publicly [dedicated this].
EDCS-25600114.summary: This is a public dedication by the people of Sabratha to Marcus Aemilius Clodianus, a procurator, for his integrity.

EDCS-25600116.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Gaius Bruttius Exoratus, a veteran of the Third Augustan Legion, lived 90 years. Helvia, his wife, made this. He lies here.
EDCS-25600116.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Gaius Bruttius Exoratus, a veteran of the Third Augustan Legion, erected by his wife.

EDCS-25600117.translation: Lucius Caelius Legatimus, son of Lucius, of the Quirina tribe, a soldier in the Third Augustan Legion, in the century of Fundanius Severus, lived 40 years, served 17 years. He lies here. Iulia Rustica, his wife, placed this.
EDCS-25600117.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Lucius Caelius Legatimus, a soldier in the Third Augustan Legion, erected by his wife.

EDCS-25600118.translation: Tiberius Claudius Manduccus, a soldier of the Third Augustan Legion, lived [X] years.
EDCS-25600118.summary: This is a tombstone fragment for Tiberius Claudius Manduccus, a soldier of the Third Augustan Legion, recording his lifespan.

EDCS-25600119.translation: Publius Durmius Firmus, a soldier of the Third Augustan Legion, lived 22 years, served 4 years. Publius Durmius Firmus, veteran, father, erected this monument for his son.
EDCS-25600119.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Publius Durmius Firmus, a soldier of the Third Augustan Legion, erected by his veteran father who also bore the same name.

EDCS-25600154.translation: Dedicated to the departed spirits. Marcus Abullius Arabus lived for 103 years.
EDCS-25600154.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Marcus Abullius Arabus, who lived to be 103.

EDCS-25600155.translation: Aulus Iunius Pulicio lived for 25 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-25600155.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the life and burial of Aulus Iunius Pulicio.

EDCS-25600156.translation: Dedicated to the departed spirits. Caius Clodius Felix lived for 60 years.
EDCS-25600156.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Caius Clodius Felix, who lived to be 60.

EDCS-25600157.translation: Dedicated to the departed spirits. Iulia Urbana lived for 30 years.
EDCS-25600157.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Iulia Urbana, who lived to be 30.

EDCS-25600469.translation: Dedicated to the departed spirits. Caebicia Victoria, dutiful, lived for 86 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-25600469.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the life and burial of Caebicia Victoria.

EDCS-25600470.translation: Dedicated to the departed spirits. Caecilia Tertia, dutiful, lived for 15 years, 6 months, and 6 days.
EDCS-25600470.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Caecilia Tertia, detailing her age at death.

EDCS-25600471.translation: Dedicated to the departed spirits. Ciceronia Rustica lived for 75 years.
EDCS-25600471.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Ciceronia Rustica, who lived to be 75.

EDCS-25600472.translation: Dedicated to the departed spirits. Tiberius Claudius Abascantus, dutiful, lived for 97 years. His son Tiberius Claudius Clemens made this for a deserving man.
EDCS-25600472.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Tiberius Claudius Clemens for his father Tiberius Claudius Abascantus.

EDCS-25600473.translation: Quintus Germanius Felix Saponianus died at the age of 51. [This is the tomb of] Sapo Felix's son, Germanus, with his wife Martida and his son Felix and his mother Fortunata.
EDCS-25600473.summary: This inscription records the death of Quintus Germanius Felix Saponianus and identifies his family members.

EDCS-25600474.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Milimonia Rogata lived 68 years.
EDCS-25600474.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Milimonia Rogata.

EDCS-25600475.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Publius Felix, dutiful, lived 21 years, 2 months, and 5 days.
EDCS-25600475.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Publius Felix.

EDCS-25600476.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Ragonius Mustus, dutiful, lived 8 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-25600476.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the age at death of Ragonius Mustus and his burial.

EDCS-25600478.translation: To the most unconquered and most fortunate Augustus.
EDCS-25600478.summary: This is an honorific inscription likely dedicated to the emperor, possibly Augustus himself, given the date.

EDCS-25600485.summary: This is a dedication by Lurius Primus to deities, likely local gods.

EDCS-25600487.translation: Fabius Caecilius Praetextatus, perpetual priest and curator of the republic, dedicated this to Fortuna Augusta.
EDCS-25600487.summary: This is a dedication to Fortuna Augusta by Fabius Caecilius Praetextatus, who held significant civic and religious offices.

EDCS-25600489.summary: This is an inscription identifying Aemilius Saturninus as a priest.

EDCS-25600490.translation: Aemilius Zabullus, priest, gladly fulfilled his vow to Saturn Augustus.
EDCS-25600490.summary: This is a votive inscription by Aemilius Zabullus, a priest, dedicating a gift to Saturn Augustus.

EDCS-25600491.translation: Caius Annaenus Felix, priest, gladly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-25600491.summary: This is a votive inscription by Caius Annaenus Felix, a priest, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-25600492.translation: Annius Privatus, priest, gladly fulfilled his vow to Saturn Augustus.
EDCS-25600492.summary: This is a votive inscription by Annius Privatus, a priest, dedicating a gift to Saturn Augustus.

EDCS-25600493.translation: Sacred to Augustus Saturn. Antonius Celer, priest, willingly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-25600493.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to Augustus Saturn by the priest Antonius Celer.

EDCS-25600494.translation: Sacred to Augustus Saturn. Caecilius Bariciolus, priest, willingly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-25600494.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to Augustus Saturn by the priest Caecilius Bariciolus.

EDCS-25600495.translation: Sacred to Augustus Saturn. Quintus Caecilius Datus, priest, willingly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-25600495.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to Augustus Saturn by the priest Quintus Caecilius Datus.

EDCS-25600496.translation: Sacred to Augustus Saturn. Caecilius Fortunatus, priest, willingly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-25600496.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to Augustus Saturn by the priest Caecilius Fortunatus.

EDCS-25600497.translation: Sacred to Augustus Saturn. Caecilius Felix, priest, willingly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-25600497.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to Augustus Saturn by the priest Caecilius Felix.

EDCS-25600498.translation: To Augustus Saturn. Aulus Caecilius Felix, priest, willingly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-25600498.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to Augustus Saturn by the priest Aulus Caecilius Felix.

EDCS-25600499.translation: Sacred to Augustus Saturn. Caecilius Felix, son of Saturninus Pantonius, priest, willingly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-25600499.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to Augustus Saturn by Caecilius Felix, son of Saturninus Pantonius, a priest.

EDCS-25600500.translation: Sacred to Augustus Saturn. Caecilius Fortunatus, priest, willingly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-25600500.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to Augustus Saturn by the priest Caecilius Fortunatus.

EDCS-25600501.translation: Sacred to Augustus Saturn. Caecilius Macrinus Ziommoris, priest, of the divine father.
EDCS-25600501.summary: This inscription records an offering to Augustus Saturn by Caecilius Macrinus Ziommoris, priest of the divine father.

EDCS-25600502.translation: Sacred to Augustus Saturn. Caecilius Rogatianus, priest, willingly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-25600502.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to Augustus Saturn by the priest Caecilius Rogatianus.

EDCS-25600503.translation: Sacred to Augustus Saturn. Caecilius Rusticus, son of Ziommoris, priest.
EDCS-25600503.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a sacred object to Augustus Saturn by Caecilius Rusticus, identified as a priest.

EDCS-25600504.translation: Sacred to Augustus Saturn. Lucius Kaledius Privatus, priest of Saturn, paid his vow willingly.
EDCS-25600504.summary: This inscription records the fulfillment of a vow to Augustus Saturn by Lucius Kaledius Privatus, a priest of Saturn.

EDCS-25600506.translation: Calvius Felix, priest, paid his vow willingly.
EDCS-25600506.summary: This inscription records the fulfillment of a vow by Calvius Felix, identified as a priest.

EDCS-25600509.translation: Cestius Rogatus, son, priest, paid his vow willingly.
EDCS-25600509.summary: This inscription records the fulfillment of a vow by Cestius Rogatus, identified as a priest.

EDCS-25600510.translation: Sacred to Augustus Saturn. Cestius Rufus, priest, paid his vow willingly.
EDCS-25600510.summary: This inscription records the fulfillment of a vow to Augustus Saturn by Cestius Rufus, a priest.

EDCS-25600511.translation: Sacred to Augustus Saturn. Clodius Ianuarius, priest, paid his vow willingly.
EDCS-25600511.summary: This inscription records the fulfillment of a vow to Augustus Saturn by Clodius Ianuarius, a priest.

EDCS-25600513.translation: Sacred to Augustus Saturn. Clodius Rogatianus, also known as Irnemius, priest, paid his vow willingly.
EDCS-25600513.summary: This inscription records the fulfillment of a vow to Augustus Saturn by Clodius Rogatianus (also known as Irnemius), a priest.

EDCS-25600514.translation: Sacred to Augustus Saturn. Cornelius Baricio, priest, paid his vow willingly.
EDCS-25600514.summary: This inscription records the fulfillment of a vow to Augustus Saturn by Cornelius Baricio, a priest.

EDCS-25600515.translation: Sacred to Augustus Saturn. Lucius Cornelius Successus, priest, paid his vow willingly.
EDCS-25600515.summary: This inscription records the fulfillment of a vow to Augustus Saturn by Lucius Cornelius Successus, a priest.

EDCS-25600516.translation: Crassicius Fortunatus, priest, paid his vow willingly.
EDCS-25600516.summary: This inscription records the fulfillment of a vow by Crassicius Fortunatus, identified as a priest.

EDCS-25600517.translation: Sacred to Saturn Augustus. Crescens, son of Sulla, priest, gladly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-25600517.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by Crescens, son of Sulla, to Saturn Augustus, likely on a shrine or altar.

EDCS-25600518.translation: Sacred to Saturn Augustus. Datus Cenute, priest, gladly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-25600518.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by Datus Cenute, a priest, to Saturn Augustus.

EDCS-25600519.translation: Lucius Decimius Silvanus, priest, gladly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-25600519.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by Lucius Decimius Silvanus, a priest.

EDCS-25600520.translation: Sacred to Saturn Augustus. Lucius Decimius Suco, priest, gladly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-25600520.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by Lucius Decimius Suco, a priest, to Saturn Augustus.

EDCS-25600521.translation: Sacred to Saturn Augustus. Dexonius Crescens, priest.
EDCS-25600521.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Dexonius Crescens, a priest, to Saturn Augustus.

EDCS-25600522.translation: Sacred to Saturn Augustus. Ernemius Perennis, priest, gladly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-25600522.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by Ernemius Perennis, a priest, to Saturn Augustus.

EDCS-25600523.translation: Sacred to Saturn Augustus. Marcus Fabius Solutor, priest, gladly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-25600523.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by Marcus Fabius Solutor, a priest, to Saturn Augustus.

EDCS-25600664.translation: Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Augustus, Parthicus Maximus, Britannicus Maximus, Germanicus Maximus, with tribunician power for the 20th time, consul for the 4th time, father of the country, restored [this].
EDCS-25600664.summary: This inscription records the restoration activities of Emperor Marcus Aurelius, detailing his imperial titles and powers up to his 20th tribunician power and 4th consulship.

EDCS-25600666.translation: Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Augustus, conqueror of Parthia, conqueror of Britain, conqueror of Germany, holding tribunician power for the 19th time, consul for the 4th time, father of the country, restored [this monument] in the 12th year.
EDCS-25600666.summary: This inscription records the restoration of a monument by Emperor Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Augustus, likely in the late 2nd century AD, noting his titles and tribunician power.

EDCS-25600667.translation: To Emperor Augustus, conqueror of Parthia, holding tribunician power for the 18th time, Caesar for the 14th time.
EDCS-25600667.summary: This inscription is an dedication to Emperor Augustus, possibly marking a restoration or significant event during his reign, noting his tribunician and Caesarian powers.

EDCS-25600669.translation: Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Severus Antoninus Pius Augustus, conqueror of Parthia, conqueror of Britain, conqueror of Germany, holding tribunician power for the 19th time, Imperator for the 3rd time, consul for the 4th time, father of the country, restored [this monument] in the 12th year.
EDCS-25600669.summary: This inscription records the restoration of a monument by Emperor Caracalla (Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Augustus), likely in the early 3rd century AD, detailing his imperial titles and powers.

EDCS-25600670.translation: Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Severus Antoninus Pius Augustus
EDCS-25600670.summary: This inscription is a titulary of Emperor Marcus Aurelius Severus Antoninus Pius Augustus, also known as Caracalla.

EDCS-25600676.translation: Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Augustus, conqueror of Parthia, conqueror of Britain, conqueror of Germany, with tribunician power for the 19th time, consul for the 4th time, father of the fatherland, restored [this].
EDCS-25600676.summary: This inscription records the restoration of something by Emperor Caracalla, listing his extensive titles and achievements up to his 19th year of tribunician power and 4th consulship.

EDCS-25600679.translation: To Galerius Valerius Maximianus the Younger, most noble Caesar.
EDCS-25600679.summary: This is a dedication to Galerius Valerius Maximianus, who held the title of Caesar, likely in the late 3rd or early 4th century AD.

EDCS-25600680.translation: To our lord Flavius Constantinus, the Greatest, Pious, Fortunate.
EDCS-25600680.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Emperor Constantine the Great, addressing him with reverential titles.

EDCS-25600683.translation: Our lords Emperors Caius Vibius Trebonianus Gallus Pius Felix Augustus, chief priest, with tribunician power, consul elect, father of the fatherland, proconsul, and Emperor Caius Vibius Afinius Gallus Veldumnianus Volusianus Pius Felix Augustus, chief priest, with tribunician power, consul elect, father of the fatherland, proconsul, restored [this] for 20 [units of distance].
EDCS-25600683.summary: This inscription records the restoration of a road for a distance of 20 units by Emperors Trebonianus Gallus and Volusianus, indicating a joint rule likely around 251-253 AD.

EDCS-25600684.translation: Emperor Caesar Gaius Julius Verus Maximinus Pius Felix Augustus, supreme conqueror of Germany, Sarmatia, and Dacia, chief priest, with tribunician power for the 3rd time, emperor for the 6th time, and Gaius Julius Verus Maximus, most noble Caesar, prince of youth, supreme conqueror of Germany, Sarmatia, and Dacia, restored the road from Carthage to the borders of the province of Numidia, which had been corrupted and collapsed through long neglect, for 70 [units of distance].
EDCS-25600684.summary: This inscription records the restoration of a road by Emperor Maximinus Thrax and his son Caesar Maximinus, detailing their extensive military titles and the length of the restoration (70 units).

EDCS-25600685.translation: Emperor Caesar, grandson of the deified Nerva, son of the deified Trajan the Parthian, Trajan Hadrianus Augustus, chief priest, with tribunician power for the 7th time, consul for the 3rd time, paved the road from Carthage to Theveste, through the Third Augustan Legion, with Publius Metilius Secundus as governor (legatus Augusti pro praetore), [for a distance of] 85 [units].
EDCS-25600685.summary: This inscription records the paving of the road from Carthage to Theveste by Emperor Hadrian, carried out by Legio III Augusta under the command of Publius Metilius Secundus, for a distance of 85 units, likely in the early 2nd century AD.

EDCS-25600686.translation: Emperor Caesar Marcus Iulius Philippus Invictus Pius Felix Augustus, chief priest, consul elect, father of the fatherland, proconsul, and Marcus Iulius Philippus, most noble Caesar, Augustus, prince of youth, and Marcia Otacilia Severa, mother of Caesar and of the camp and of the senate and of the fatherland.
EDCS-25600686.summary: This inscription lists the imperial titles of Emperor Philip the Arab, his son Caesar Philip, and Empress Otacilia Severa, indicating their co-rule and familial connection.

EDCS-25600687.translation: To our lord Emperor Constantine the Greatest, Fortunate, Pious Augustus, born for the good of the state.
EDCS-25600687.summary: This is a dedication to Emperor Constantine the Great, praising him with elevated titles that emphasize his beneficial rule.

EDCS-25600688.translation: Emperor Caesar Caius Messius Quintus Traianus Decius Invictus Pius Felix Augustus, supreme conqueror of Parthia, with tribunician power, consul for the 2nd time, father of the fatherland, proconsul, and Quintus Herennius Etruscus Messius Decius Caesar, and Gaius Valens Hostilianus Messius Quintus.
EDCS-25600688.summary: This inscription lists the imperial titles of Emperor Decius, his son Caesar Quintus Herennius Etruscus, and his other son Hostilian, indicating their association with the imperial power, likely around 251 AD.

EDCS-25600713.translation: To the Emperor Nerva Caesar Augustus, consul for the third time, father of the fatherland. 4 miles.
EDCS-25600713.summary: This is a milestone dedicating a 4-mile stretch of road to Emperor Nerva, likely from his third consulship.

EDCS-25600714.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Lucius Domitius Aurelianus, the Pious, Fortunate, Augustus, chief priest, greatest in German affairs, with tribunician power for the third time, consul for the second time, proconsul, father of the fatherland. 14 miles.
EDCS-25600714.summary: This is a milestone dedicating a 14-mile stretch of road to Emperor Aurelian, likely from his third tribunate and second consulship.

EDCS-25600716.translation: To the Emperor Caesar, son of the deified Septimius Severus Pius Arabicus Adiabenicus, greatest in German affairs, grandson of the deified Antoninus Pius Germanicus Sarmaticus, great-grandson of the deified Antoninus Pius, great-great-grandson of the deified Trajan Parthicus and the deified Nerva, Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus, greatest in Parthian affairs.
EDCS-25600716.summary: This is a lengthy titulature inscription for Emperor Caracalla, tracing his lineage back to Nerva and Trajan.

EDCS-25600717.translation: Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Severus Antoninus Pius Augustus, greatest in Parthian, British, and German affairs, chief priest, with tribunician power for the 19th time, emperor for the third time, consul for the fourth time, father of the fatherland.
EDCS-25600717.summary: This is an imperial titulature inscription for Emperor Caracalla, likely from his 19th year of tribunician power and fourth consulship.

EDCS-25600718.translation: Emperor Caesar Gaius Julius Verus Maximinus Pius Felix Augustus, greatest in German, Sarmatian, and Dacian affairs, chief priest, with tribunician power for the third time, emperor for the fifth time, and Gaius Julius Verus Maximus, most noble Caesar, prince of youth, greatest in German and Sarmatian affairs. They restored bridges collapsed from age and a road lost through long neglect, and through their tireless foresight made it passable for travelers. From mile 37.
EDCS-25600718.summary: This inscription records the restoration of collapsed bridges and a neglected road by Emperors Maximinus Thrax and his son Maximus Caesar, marking mile 37.

EDCS-25600719.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Marcus Julius Philippus, the Pious, Fortunate, Augustus, greatest in Parthian affairs, with tribunician power, emperor, consul, father of the fatherland, proconsul, and Marcus Julius Philippus, most noble Caesar. 47 miles from Tacapas.
EDCS-25600719.summary: This milestone dedicates a 47-mile stretch of road from Tacapas to Emperors Philip I and his son Philip II Caesar.

EDCS-25600720.text_edition: \n Imperator Caesar Augusti filius Augustus tribunicia potestate XVI Asprenas consul proconsul VII vir epulonum viam ex castris hibernis Tacapes muniendam curavit legio III Augusta CI\n
EDCS-25600720.translation: Emperor Caesar Augustus, son of Augustus, with tribunician power for the 16th time, consul Asprenas for the 7th time, member of the college of seven epulones, ensured that the road from the winter camp to Tacapes be constructed, Legio III Augusta.
EDCS-25600720.summary: This inscription records Emperor Augustus's order, given through Consul Asprenas, for the construction of a road from the winter camp to Tacapes, carried out by Legio III Augusta.

EDCS-25600727.translation: By the Licinian measure, after death, the pagus Thuggensis is hateful.
EDCS-25600727.summary: This is a short, obscure inscription expressing animosity towards a pagus after death, possibly related to taxation or inheritance.

EDCS-25600728.summary: This is a dedication to an individual named Pacatus, identified as 'the third Arnensis'.

EDCS-25600730.translation: To Pomponia Ingenua, wife of Quintus Pacuvius Honoratus Rufinianus. (With all respect).
EDCS-25600730.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Pomponia Ingenua, wife of Quintus Pacuvius Honoratus Rufinianus.

EDCS-25600731.text_edition: \n Sexto Pullaeno Sexti filio Arnensi Floro Caeciliano praefecto iure dicundo sacerdoti Cererum anni CLXX IIviro quinquennali flamini perpetuo coloniae Iuliae Karthaginis pagus et civitas Thuggensis patrono decreto decurionum pecunia publica curatoribus Lucio Gallio Optato Sallustio Dato\n
EDCS-25600731.translation: To Sextus Pullaenus Florus Caecilianus, son of Sextus, of the Arnian tribe, who served as prefect of justice, priest of Ceres for the 170th year, quinquennial duovir, perpetual priest of the colony of Carthage; the pagus and civitas of Thugga, as patron, by decree of the decurions, at public expense, with Lucius Gallius Optatus and Sallustius Dato as curators.
EDCS-25600731.summary: This inscription records a public monument erected by the pagus and civitas of Thugga in honor of Sextus Pullaenus Florus Caecilianus, a prominent official in the colony of Carthage, likely in the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-25600733.translation: Sopatr, Papirius Sopatr, to Honoratus, Roman knight, former aedile, twice, because of his manifold and proven affection for the fatherland and citizens, and [in the time of] his aedileship, the ordo [honored him].
EDCS-25600733.summary: This inscription honors Papirius Sopatr, a Roman knight and former aedile, for his devotion to the city and its citizens.

EDCS-25600734.translation: To Titisenius Papirius Felicissimus Cornelius, perpetual aedile and flamen, on account of the magnificence of the games and his many generosities, by which he earnestly served the state and homeland, the most splendid colony of Thugga, by the people's vote and the decree of the decurions, with public money.
EDCS-25600734.summary: This is a public dedication by the colony of Thugga to Titisenius Papirius Felicissimus, honoring his generosity and service.

EDCS-25600735.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Gaius Eudius Libanus, a veteran.

EDCS-25600736.translation: To Quintus Vettius Papirius Salvius Julius Rogatianus, for grain.
EDCS-25600736.summary: This inscription records a payment or allocation of grain to Quintus Vettius Papirius Salvius Julius Rogatianus.

EDCS-25600738.translation: To the perpetual priest, a citizen and exemplary man of honorable memory, for his exceptional love for the citizens and his fatherland, both orders rewarded the merits of a good citizen and patron, whom with the authority of their decree they had honored with an equestrian statue. The republic of the municipality of Septimius Aurelius Thuggensis erected (this statue) for eternal remembrance of mutual affection.
EDCS-25600738.summary: This inscription records the erection of an equestrian statue by the municipality of Thugga to honor a former perpetual priest and patron for his love of the citizens and fatherland, likely in the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-25600741.translation: To the priest of Aesculapius, on account of his exceptional generosity, the pagus and civitas of Aurelia Thugga, by decree of the decurions, with public money.
EDCS-25600741.summary: This is a public dedication by the pagus and civitas of Aurelia Thugga to their priest of Aesculapius, recognizing his generosity.

EDCS-25600742.translation: When she had asked, the mother, content with the monument to her son, decreed by the decurions, to Helvius [---].
EDCS-25600742.summary: This fragmentary inscription seems to record a monument set up by a mother for her son, with the approval of the decurions.

EDCS-25600743.translation: To Julia Maxima, perpetual priestess, on account of the outstanding distinction of her sons.
EDCS-25600743.summary: This is a dedication to Julia Maxima, a perpetual priestess, recognizing the achievements of her sons.

EDCS-25600744.translation: To the patron of the pagus and civitas of Aurelia Thugga, the first of all, for his exceptional devotion and harmony towards the pagus and civitas, [---].
EDCS-25600744.summary: This inscription honors a patron of the pagus and civitas of Aurelia Thugga for his devotion and harmony.

EDCS-25600747.translation: He always benefited the state; the state of the municipium of Septimius Aurelius Liberi of Thugga placed [this].
EDCS-25600747.summary: This is a public monument erected by the municipium of Thugga to honor someone who consistently benefited the state.

EDCS-25600748.translation: For the works of the bathhouse, the state of the municipium of Septimius Aurelius Liberi of Thugga.
EDCS-25600748.summary: This inscription likely records the funding or construction of a bathhouse by the municipium of Thugga.

EDCS-25600750.translation: To Quintus Caecilius Restitutianus, son of Quintus Caecilius Honoratianus, an outstanding man, the state of the municipium of Thugga placed [this] by decree of the decurions, with public money.
EDCS-25600750.summary: This is a public dedication by the municipium of Thugga to Quintus Caecilius Restitutianus, honoring him as an outstanding man.

EDCS-25600768.translation: Septentrio, Aquilo, Euroaquilo, Volturnus, Eurus, Leuconotus, Auster, Libonotus, Africus, Faonius, Argestes, Circius.
EDCS-25600768.summary: This inscription lists the names of various winds, possibly as a dedication or a catalog of winds known to the author.

EDCS-25600771.translation: Eros: through you, Amandus Frunitus (received everything).
EDCS-25600771.summary: This is a short dedication or votive text where Amandus Frunitus attributes his success or reception of favors to Eros (possibly a god or personification).

EDCS-25600772.summary: This is a very brief inscription, possibly a playful or poetic statement associated with a geographical location named 'Bocca Derisoris' (Mouth of the Derisor).

EDCS-25600776.translation: Monitor of the barrier, be grim/harsh.
EDCS-25600776.summary: This inscription seems to be a command or a warning directed at a 'monitor' of a barrier, perhaps related to a defensive structure or a boundary.

EDCS-25600852.summary: This is an incomplete funerary inscription recording the name of Arius and the duration of his life.

EDCS-25600853.translation: The officials (curiales) of the entire municipality of Cincari, who were called as provocati, erected this in memory of Tiberius Claudius Iulianus, contributing from their own funds from a donation of his mother, on the date of the founding (of the municipality); the site was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-25600853.summary: This funerary monument was erected by the municipal officials of Cincari in memory of Tiberius Claudius Iulianus, funded by his mother and themselves, with the site granted by the town council.

EDCS-25600857.translation: To Gaius Egnatius Felix, son of Gaius, of the Papiria tribe, the most innocent aedile, his friends, on account of his merit, by whose dedication Egnatius, in addition to the gymnasium and the offerings that aediles are accustomed to provide, increased the sacred celebration of Liberalia, and at his own entire expense provided it for all citizens, and furthermore presented theatrical games and gave a feast to the people; the site was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-25600857.summary: This is a dedication by friends to an aedile, Gaius Egnatius Felix, praising his generosity in funding public works and festivals, with the site granted by the town council.

EDCS-25600858.translation: having performed all the honors in his homeland, defenders of public causes of his municipality of Vallitani, who by investigation...
EDCS-25600858.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription honoring an individual who held various public offices in the municipality of Vallitani, possibly a legal defender.

EDCS-25600859.translation: of the perpetual flaminate, duumvir, patron of his municipality of Vallitani, to repay the merits of both of them, the town council made (this) by public decree.
EDCS-25600859.summary: This inscription states that the town council of Vallitani honored individuals (likely two, given 'both') who held prestigious offices such as perpetual flamen, duumvir, and patron, by public decree to reward their merits.

EDCS-25600862.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Lucius Geminius Seranus, pious, lived 35 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-25600862.summary: This is a standard funerary inscription dedicating a tomb to Lucius Geminius Seranus, stating his name, piety, age, and burial location.

EDCS-25600863.summary: A funerary inscription recording the lifespan of an individual, dated by its style to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25600864.translation: Sacred to Emperor Marcus Aurelius Commodus Antoninus Augustus Sarmaticus Germanicus, Pontifex Maximus, in his seventh tribunician power, Imperator for the fourth time, Consul for the third time, Father of the Fatherland, son of the deified Marcus Antoninus Pius Germanicus Sarmaticus, grandson of the deified Pius, great-grandson of the deified Hadrian, great-great-grandson of the deified Trajan, great-great-great-grandson of the deified Nerva. Quintus Abonius Secundus, son of Lucius, erected this statue, costing 4,000 sesterces, with additional legally approved funds, because of the XI primatus honor, which his order spontaneously decreed to him, and he gave sportulas to the decurions and a banquet to the people for its dedication; the site was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-25600864.summary: A public dedication of a statue to Emperor Commodus by Quintus Abonius Secundus, celebrating his imperial titles and a civic honor, including expenses for the dedication ceremony, dated to Commodus' reign (AD 177-192).

EDCS-25600871.translation: For the safety of the Emperors Caesars Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus Arabicus.
EDCS-25600871.summary: An inscription dedicating something for the well-being of Emperor Septimius Severus, dated to his reign (AD 193-211).

EDCS-25600872.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Pulia Dativa, dutiful, lived 12 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-25600872.summary: A funerary inscription for Pulia Dativa, recording her age at death, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25600873.translation: Her grandfather Secundus erected this monument for Oroscius Rogatus Victorinus, son of Victor.
EDCS-25600873.summary: A funerary monument erected by a grandfather for his grandson, an example of family memorialization in the Roman period.

EDCS-25600874.summary: A fragmentary inscription possibly related to a person named Serarius Anicvius, the context and date are unclear.

EDCS-25600875.summary: A dedication, likely funerary or votive, to Calpennia Victoria, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25600876.translation: Popilius Primus and Faustinus made this at their own expense to Hercules the Preserver and the Genius of the city.
EDCS-25600876.summary: A dedication to Hercules and the city's Genius by Popilius Primus and Faustinus, likely a public or civic benefaction during the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25600877.translation: Popilius Primus and Faustinus made this at their own expense to Venus the Victorious.
EDCS-25600877.summary: A votive dedication to Venus Victrix by Popilius Primus and Faustinus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25600882.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Gaius Cidonius lived 83 years.
EDCS-25600882.summary: A funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Gaius Cidonius, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25600883.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Caecilius Felix, dutiful, lived 91 years.
EDCS-25600883.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan of Caecilius Felix, who lived 91 years.

EDCS-25600884.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Cerelia Quieta lived 70 years.
EDCS-25600884.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan of Cerelia Quieta, who lived 70 years.

EDCS-25600885.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Cutilius Fortunatus lived 3 years.
EDCS-25600885.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan of Cutilius Fortunatus, who lived 3 years.

EDCS-25600886.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan of Faustinus, who lived 57 years.

EDCS-25600887.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Ferennia Felicitas, dutiful, lived 79 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-25600887.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan of Ferennia Felicitas, who lived 79 years, and indicates her burial place.

EDCS-25600888.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Flavonia Urbana, dutiful, lived 72 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-25600888.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan of Flavonia Urbana, who lived 72 years, and indicates her burial place.

EDCS-25600889.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Grania Victoria, daughter of Balienis, lived 43 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-25600889.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan of Grania Victoria, daughter of Balienis, who lived 43 years, and indicates her burial place.

EDCS-25600890.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan of Iulia Saturnina, who lived 75 years.

EDCS-25600891.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Publius Iunius, son of Publius, of the Arnensis tribe, Felix, dutiful, lived 62 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-25600891.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan of Publius Iunius, son of Publius, who lived 62 years, and indicates his burial place.

EDCS-25600892.translation: Titus Mallamsus Primus, dutiful, lived 1 year; he is buried here.
EDCS-25600892.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan of Titus Mallamsus Primus, who lived 1 year, and indicates his burial place.

EDCS-25600893.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Lucius Manilius Licinianus lived 20 years, 2 months, and 12 days. He is buried here.
EDCS-25600893.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan and burial of Lucius Manilius Licinianus.

EDCS-25600894.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Pompius Maximus lived.
EDCS-25600894.summary: A fragmentary funerary epitaph recording the name of Pompius Maximus, indicating he lived.

EDCS-25600895.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Caius Popilius Maximus lived 20 years.
EDCS-25600895.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Caius Popilius Maximus.

EDCS-25600896.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Decimus Popilius Maximus the dutiful lived 45 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-25600896.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan and burial of Decimus Popilius Maximus.

EDCS-25600897.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Decimus Popilius Maximus Calli the dutiful lived 102 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-25600897.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan and burial of Decimus Popilius Maximus Calli.

EDCS-25600898.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Popilius Victor, son of Maximi Galli, lived 93 years.
EDCS-25600898.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Popilius Victor, son of Maximi Galli.

EDCS-25600899.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Postumuleia Faustina lived 47 years.
EDCS-25600899.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Postumuleia Faustina.

EDCS-25600901.translation: Secunda, daughter of Gallus, lived 20 years. May the earth lie lightly upon you, may your bones rest well.
EDCS-25600901.summary: A funerary epitaph for Secunda, daughter of Gallus, wishing her peaceful rest.

EDCS-25600902.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Valeria Quinta lived 80 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-25600902.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan and burial of Valeria Quinta.

EDCS-25600903.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Venuleius Vindemialis lived...
EDCS-25600903.summary: A fragmentary funerary epitaph recording the name Venuleius Vindemialis and the beginning of his lifespan.

EDCS-25600905.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Mamelia Quarta lived for 63 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-25600905.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan and burial of Mamelia Quarta.

EDCS-25600906.translation: Zafrem, son of Rogatus Vindicus Nonnus, lived for 29 years.
EDCS-25600906.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Zafrem.

EDCS-25600908.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Inocus, son of Caius, a Concessus from Rutilius Primosus, lived for 2 years and 3 days.
EDCS-25600908.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Inocus, son of Caius.

EDCS-25600910.translation: To Ceionia Plautia, daughter of Lucius Aelius Caesar, at the expense of the public treasury, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-25600910.summary: A dedication honoring Ceionia Plautia, daughter of Lucius Aelius Caesar, funded by public money.

EDCS-25600912.translation: In the year of the consulship of Stloga and Severus, under the supervision of Agatha, freedwoman, of the workshop of Certus, in the establishment of our lord Emperor Antoninus Augustus Pius.
EDCS-25600912.summary: A record of work done by a workshop under the supervision of Agatha, during the consulship of Stloga and Severus and the reign of Emperor Antoninus Pius.

EDCS-25600913.translation: In the year of the consulship of Stloga and Severus, under the supervision of Agatha, freedwoman, of the workshop of Certus, in the establishment of our lord Emperor Antoninus Augustus Pius.
EDCS-25600913.summary: A record of work done by a workshop under the supervision of Agatha, during the consulship of Stloga and Severus and the reign of Emperor Antoninus Pius.

EDCS-25600914.translation: In the year of the consulship of Stloga and Severus, under the supervision of Agatha, freedwoman, of the workshop of Certus, in the establishment of our lord Emperor Antoninus Augustus Pius.
EDCS-25600914.summary: A record of work done by a workshop under the supervision of Agatha, during the consulship of Stloga and Severus and the reign of Emperor Antoninus Pius.

EDCS-25600915.translation: In the year of the consulship of Stloga and Severus, under the supervision of Agatha, freedwoman, of the workshop of Certus, in the establishment of our lord Emperor Antoninus Augustus.
EDCS-25600915.summary: A record of work done by a workshop under the supervision of Agatha, during the consulship of Stloga and Severus and the reign of Emperor Antoninus Augustus.

EDCS-25600916.translation: In the year of the consulship of Stloga and Severus, under the supervision of Agatha, freedwoman, of the workshop of Certus, in the establishment of our lord Emperor Antoninus Augustus Pius.
EDCS-25600916.summary: A record of work done by a workshop under the supervision of Agatha, during the consulship of Stloga and Severus and the reign of Emperor Antoninus Pius.

EDCS-25600917.translation: In the year of the consulship of Stloga and Severus, under the supervision of Agatha, freedwoman, of the workshop of Al, number LXIV, in the establishment of our lord Emperor Antoninus Augustus Pius.
EDCS-25600917.summary: A record of work done by workshop Al (number LXIV) under the supervision of Agatha, during the consulship of Stloga and Severus and the reign of Emperor Antoninus Pius.

EDCS-25600918.translation: Under the consulship of Orfitus and Priscus, in the 606th year of Emperor Antoninus Augustus Pius' reign, the Royal workshop completed this.
EDCS-25600918.summary: This inscription records the completion of work by the Royal workshop during the consulship of Orfitus and Priscus, dated by the reign of Antoninus Pius.

EDCS-25600919.translation: Under Emperor Antoninus Augustus, our lord, 343 [units of the imperial mint?]; officina of Regia, with Gallicanus and Vetus as consuls.
EDCS-25600919.summary: This inscription records the production of an item under Emperor Antoninus Augustus and consuls Gallicanus and Vetus, likely related to imperial workshops in the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-25600920.translation: Under Emperor Antoninus Augustus Pius, our lord, 5xx [units?]; officina of Agrippa, with Gallicanus and Vetus as consuls.
EDCS-25600920.summary: This inscription records the production of an item under Emperor Antoninus Pius and consuls Gallicanus and Vetus, likely related to imperial workshops in the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-25600921.translation: Under Emperor Antoninus Augustus Pius, our lord, 517 [units?]; officina of Agrippa, with Gallicanus and Vetus as consuls.
EDCS-25600921.summary: This inscription records the production of an item under Emperor Antoninus Pius and consuls Gallicanus and Vetus, likely related to imperial workshops in the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-25600923.translation: The Royal workshop, Condianus and Maximus, completed this in the 192nd year of Emperor Antoninus Augustus Pius, our lord.
EDCS-25600923.summary: This inscription records the completion of work by the Royal workshop under Condianus and Maximus, dated by the reign of Antoninus Pius.

EDCS-25600924.translation: Under Emperor Antoninus Augustus Pius, our lord, [number missing] units; officina of Iunius; with Barbarus and Regulus as consuls.
EDCS-25600924.summary: This inscription records the production of an item under Emperor Antoninus Pius and consuls Barbarus and Regulus, likely related to imperial workshops in the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-25600925.translation: The workshop of Aurelius completed this in the 60th year of Emperor Antoninus Augustus Pius, during the third consulship of Verus Caesar and the second of Commodus.
EDCS-25600925.summary: This inscription records the completion of work by the Aurelius workshop, dated by the reign of Antoninus Pius and the consulships of Verus Caesar and Commodus.

EDCS-25600926.translation: Aprilis completed a new cut at mile 130, location 12, of Telluris.
EDCS-25600926.summary: This inscription records the completion of a new cut by Aprilis at a specific location and distance, likely related to infrastructure or land division.

EDCS-25600927.summary: This brief inscription records that Antoninus Augustus constructed a cistern.

EDCS-25600928.translation: The Augustan new workshop completed this in the 18th year of the consulship of Emperor Lucius Aurelius Verus (III) and Quadratus.
EDCS-25600928.summary: This inscription records the completion of work by the Augustan new workshop during the consulship of Lucius Aurelius Verus and Quadratus.

EDCS-25600929.translation: 305 [units?]; officina of Genius Montis; under Emperor Commodus Augustus (for the second time) and Victorinus (for the second time) as consuls; a boundary marker of Maximus, the procurator.
EDCS-25600929.summary: This inscription records a boundary marker related to an imperial officina and a procurator, dated to the consulship of Commodus and Victorinus, likely in the late 2nd century CE.

EDCS-25600930.translation: 53 [units?]; new officina Aureliana; under Anullinus (for the second time) and Frontonus as consuls; a boundary marker of Athenodorus, the procurator.
EDCS-25600930.summary: This inscription records a boundary marker related to a new imperial officina, dated to the consulship of Anullinus and Frontonus, likely in the late 2nd or early 3rd century CE.

EDCS-25600932.summary: This inscription records the completion of 720 units by Corni, likely a quantity of goods or construction elements.

EDCS-25600934.summary: This inscription records the construction of cut A by the inhabitants of Puteoli.

EDCS-25600935.summary: This inscription indicates a quantity of 720 units associated with Corinthi Caesaris.

EDCS-25600936.summary: This inscription indicates a quantity of 221 units associated with Corinthi Caesaris.

EDCS-25600937.translation: A total of 721 in Corinth, of Caesar's.
EDCS-25600937.summary: This inscription appears to be a count of items or units, possibly related to a census or inventory, associated with Caesar in Corinth.

EDCS-25600952.translation: Workshop discovered by Diotimus, an agent in public affairs.
EDCS-25600952.summary: This inscription records the discovery of a workshop by Diotimus, who held an official position as an agent in public affairs.

EDCS-25600953.translation: Sacred to the shades of the underworld. Agrius Zopatus, a pious veteran, lived 70 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-25600953.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Agrius Zopatus, a pious veteran who lived to 70 years old, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-25600954.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Gaius Fabuleius Victor, a veteran of the III Augusta legion, pious, lived 76 years, is buried here.
EDCS-25600954.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Gaius Fabuleius Victor, a pious veteran of the III Augusta legion, who lived to be 76.

EDCS-25600955.text_edition: \n Lucius Flaminius Decimifilius Arnensis miles legionis III Augustae centuria Iuli Longi dilecto lectus ab Marco Silano militavit annis XIX in praesidio ut esset in salto Philomulsiano ab hostem sic in pugna occissus sic vixit pie annis XL hic situs est\n
EDCS-25600955.translation: Lucius Flaminius, son of Decimus, of the Arnian tribe, a soldier of the III Augusta legion, in the first century of Longus Iulius, was chosen by Marcus Silanus. He served for 19 years on guard duty in the Philomulsian pass against the enemy. He was killed in battle. He lived piously for 40 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-25600955.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Flaminius, a soldier of the III Augusta legion, who served for 19 years and died in battle at the age of 40, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-25600956.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Aemilia Fructa lived about 30 years. May her bones rest well here. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Gaius Julius Modianus, veteran of the II Adjutrix legion, pious, lived about 67 years. He rests here.
EDCS-25600956.summary: This inscription records the burial of two individuals, Aemilia Fructa and Gaius Julius Modianus, a veteran of the II Adjutrix legion, likely from the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-25600958.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Sapia Paulina, pious, lived 61 years, 5 months, and 10 days. Publius Papirius Saturninus Lupus, son of Publius, a veteran of the III Augusta legion.
EDCS-25600958.summary: This tombstone inscription commemorates Sapia Paulina and identifies her husband, Publius Papirius Saturninus Lupus, a veteran of the III Augusta legion.

EDCS-25600959.translation: Lucius Silicius Optatus lived 50 years; intercepted on his journey. The Simithu veterans, while delaying, made this for him from their own means.
EDCS-25600959.summary: This epitaph records the death of Lucius Silicius Optatus, who died while traveling, and was commemorated by the Simithu veterans, likely dating to the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-25600960.translation: Publius Cloventius Hospes, son of Publius, of the Quirina tribe, a pious decurion, lived 70 years, is buried here.
EDCS-25600960.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Publius Cloventius Hospes, a pious decurion from the Quirina tribe, who lived to be 70.

EDCS-25600961.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Aulius Felix, public priest of Saturn, pious, lived... years.
EDCS-25600961.summary: This incomplete tombstone inscription records the life of Aulius Felix, a pious public priest of Saturn.

EDCS-25600962.translation: To Gaius Otidius Iovinus, son of Publius, of the Quirina tribe, prefect of craftsmen and priest of the province of Africa, aged 39, who was the first from his colony to hold this honor. Although the council decreed a statue for him at public expense, he was content with the honor and erected it at his own expense, with Quintus Otidius Praenestinus, son of Publius, of the Quirina tribe, his brother, as curator, who was prefect of craftsmen.
EDCS-25600962.summary: This honorific inscription records a decree for Gaius Otidius Iovinus, a prefect of craftsmen and priest of Africa from his colony, who funded his own statue; it also mentions his brother, Quintus Otidius Praenestinus.

EDCS-25600965.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Aemilianus lived more or less... years.
EDCS-25600965.summary: This incomplete tombstone inscription records the life span of Aemilianus.

EDCS-25600966.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Aemilia Iro, pious, lived 105 years, is buried here.
EDCS-25600966.summary: This tombstone inscription commemorates Aemilia Iro, a pious woman who lived to be 105 years old.

EDCS-25600967.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Arellia Colomba, pious, lived 21 years.
EDCS-25600967.summary: This tombstone inscription records the life of Arellia Colomba, who lived to be 21 years old.

EDCS-25600968.translation: "To the spirits of the departed. Arellia Fortunata, dutiful, lived 30 years. Titinia Festula, dutiful, lived 9 years."
EDCS-25600968.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the ages at death of Arellia Fortunata and Titinia Festula.

EDCS-25600969.translation: Lucius Atinius Primus, pious, lived 68 years. He rests here.
EDCS-25600969.summary: This is an epitaph for Lucius Atinius Primus, recording his age at death and burial, likely from the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-25600970.translation: Aviania Muntana, daughter of Lucius, lived 50 years.
EDCS-25600970.summary: This is an epitaph for Aviania Muntana, daughter of Lucius, recording her age at death, likely from the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-25600971.translation: "To the spirits of the departed. Baebius Torinatus, dutiful, lived 97 years. Nia Victorina lived 65 years. Baebius Felix, dutiful, lived 26 years."
EDCS-25600971.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the ages at death of Baebius Torinatus, Nia Victorina, and Baebius Felix.

EDCS-25600972.translation: Publius Cluventius Felix lived 106 years. He rests here.
EDCS-25600972.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Publius Cluventius Felix, noting his exceptional age, likely from the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-25600973.translation: "To the spirits of the departed. Quintus Cornelius Honoratus, dutiful, lived 52 years and 5 months. He is buried here. May your bones rest well; may the earth lie lightly upon you."
EDCS-25600973.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Quintus Cornelius Honoratus, stating his age at death and including wishes for his repose.

EDCS-25600974.translation: Gaius Cornelius Primus, son of Gaius, of the Quirina tribe, pious, lived about 60 years.
EDCS-25600974.summary: This epitaph records the life of Gaius Cornelius Primus, son of Gaius, a member of the Quirina tribe, noting his age, likely from the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-25600975.translation: Sextus Cornelius Reperitanus, pious, lived 50 years.
EDCS-25600975.summary: This epitaph records the life of Sextus Cornelius Reperitanus, noting his age, likely from the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-25600976.translation: "To the spirits of the departed. Quintus Cornelius Zabo, dutiful, lived 5 years. He is buried here. Light earth."
EDCS-25600976.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Quintus Cornelius Zabo, recording his age at death and wishes for his burial.

EDCS-25600977.translation: Marcus Cossutius Adiutor, pious, lived 75 years. He rests here.
EDCS-25600977.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Marcus Cossutius Adiutor, noting his age, likely from the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-25600978.translation: Gaius Cossutius Primus, son of Gaius, pious, lived 9 years. He rests here.
EDCS-25600978.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Gaius Cossutius Primus, son of Gaius, noting his young age at death, likely from the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-25600980.translation: Quintus Domitius, son of Cnaeus, of the Quirina tribe. Hospita lived 9 years. Domitia, daughter of Cnaeus, dutiful, lived 5 years. Lucius Domitius, son of Cnaeus, of the Quirina tribe, Reburrus, died while his parents were alive, lived 27 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-25600980.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Quintus Domitius Hospita, Domitia Festa, and Lucius Domitius Reburrus, recording their ages at death and burial details.

EDCS-25600981.translation: Gnaeus Domitius Optatus, son of Gnaeus, of the Quirina tribe, pious, was snatched from his parents by his talent. He lived 18 years. He rests here.
EDCS-25600981.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Gnaeus Domitius Optatus, son of Gnaeus, a young man noted for his talent, who died at 18, likely from the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-25600982.translation: Daughter of Lucius, Flavia lived 60 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-25600982.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Flavia, daughter of Lucius, recording her age at death and burial.

EDCS-25600983.translation: "To the spirits of the departed. Gemellina, dutiful, lived 2 years. Her father made this. She is buried here."
EDCS-25600983.summary: This funerary epitaph records the short life of Gemellina and states that her father erected the monument.

EDCS-25600984.translation: "To the spirits of the departed. Quintus Granius Namphamo made this for himself, his wife, and his daughter. Dutiful. His daughter Rogatina Rosaria, dutiful, lived 77 years and 5 months. Grania Quintula, dutiful, lived 25 years."
EDCS-25600984.summary: This is a family funerary epitaph set up by Quintus Granius Namphamo for himself and his female relatives, recording their ages at death.

EDCS-25600986.translation: "To the spirits of the departed. Quintus Hostilius Primus, son of Quintus, dutiful, lived 73 years. May your bones rest well; may the earth lie lightly upon you. He is buried here."
EDCS-25600986.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Quintus Hostilius Primus, stating his age at death and including wishes for his repose.

EDCS-25600987.translation: "To the spirits of the departed. Veturia Secunda, dutiful, lived 50 years. Caius Iulius Primus, dutiful, lived 60 years."
EDCS-25600987.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the ages at death of Veturia Secunda and Caius Iulius Primus.

EDCS-25600988.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Julia Victoria, dutiful, lived 105 years, is buried here. Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Iulia Spesina, dutiful, lived 25 years, is buried here. Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Iulia Namphame, dutiful, lived 50 years, is buried here.
EDCS-25600988.summary: This inscription records the burial of three women: Iulia Victoria, Iulia Spesina, and Iulia Namphame, likely from a family tomb.

EDCS-25600989.summary: This is a tombstone recording the lifespan of Iulia Parthenis.

EDCS-25600990.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Mamillia Paililla, dutiful, lived 21 years. May the earth be light for you.
EDCS-25600990.summary: This is a tombstone recording the death of Mamillia Paililla, with a common epitaph wishing for light earth.

EDCS-25600991.translation: Lucius Manlius Rogatus, son of Lucius, of the Quirina tribe, dutiful, lived 55 years; he rests here.
EDCS-25600991.summary: This is a tombstone for Lucius Manlius Rogatus, recording his name, parentage, tribal affiliation, lifespan, and burial place.

EDCS-25600992.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Lucius Munatius Restitutus, dutiful, lived 70 years, is buried here.
EDCS-25600992.summary: This tombstone records the burial and lifespan of Lucius Munatius Restitutus.

EDCS-25600993.translation: Munatia Quarta, dutiful, lived 65 years; she rests here.
EDCS-25600993.summary: This is a tombstone for Munatia Quarta, recording her name, epithet, lifespan, and burial place.

EDCS-25600994.translation: Mustia Faustina, daughter of Marcus, dutiful, lived 15 years.
EDCS-25600994.summary: This is a tombstone fragment for Mustia Faustina, recording her name, parentage, epithet, lifespan, and burial place (incomplete).

EDCS-25600995.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Marcus Orbius Ianuarius lived 110 years. Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Porcia Anthusa lived 100 years.
EDCS-25600995.summary: This inscription records the lifespans of two individuals, Marcus Orbius Ianuarius and Porcia Anthusa, likely as part of a tomb inscription.

EDCS-25600996.translation: Papiria Quinta, daughter of Lucius, dutiful, lived...
EDCS-25600996.summary: This is a tombstone fragment for Papiria Quinta, recording her name, parentage, epithet, and the beginning of her lifespan.

EDCS-25600997.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Publius Petronius Piscator, dutiful, lived 75 years.
EDCS-25600997.summary: This tombstone records the lifespan of Publius Petronius Piscator.

EDCS-25600998.translation: Plotia Lapa, daughter of Gaius, lived 70 years; she rests here.
EDCS-25600998.summary: This is a tombstone for Plotia Lapa, recording her name, parentage, lifespan, and burial place.

EDCS-25600999.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Quintus Pontidius Fortunatus, son, dutiful, lived 57 years. Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Caius Pontidius Nuptialis lived 45 years.
EDCS-25600999.summary: This inscription records the lifespans of two individuals, Quintus Pontidius Fortunatus and Caius Pontidius Nuptialis, likely brothers from the same family tomb.

EDCS-25601000.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Popidia Tertia, dutiful, lived 85 years, is buried here.
EDCS-25601000.summary: This tombstone records the burial and lifespan of Popidia Tertia.
