EDCS-25601001.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Valeria Fortunata, dutiful, lived 35 years, is buried here. Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Marcus Popilius Vitalis, dutiful, lived 92 years, is buried here.
EDCS-25601001.summary: This inscription records the burial and lifespans of two individuals, Valeria Fortunata and Marcus Popilius Vitalis, likely from a family tomb.

EDCS-25601002.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Caius Postumius Maximus, dutiful, lived 93 years.
EDCS-25601002.summary: This tombstone records the lifespan of Caius Postumius Maximus.

EDCS-25601003.translation: Histonia Probata, daughter of Publius, dutiful, lived 77 years; she rests here.
EDCS-25601003.summary: This is a tombstone for Histonia Probata, recording her name, parentage, epithet, lifespan, and burial place.

EDCS-25601005.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Rabiria Zabulia, dutiful, lived 22 years; she rests here.
EDCS-25601005.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the death of Rabiria Zabulia, who lived 22 years.

EDCS-25601006.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Romania Prima, dutiful, lived 21 years.
EDCS-25601006.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the death of Romania Prima, who lived 21 years.

EDCS-25601007.translation: To Rubria Honorata, dutiful, Titus Flavius Postimus [erected this] for his most cherished wife, who lived 36 years.
EDCS-25601007.summary: This is a tombstone dedicated by Titus Flavius Postimus to his wife Rubria Honorata, recording her name, epithet, lifespan, and relationship to the dedicant.

EDCS-25601008.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Caius Sallustius Cai filius Quirina Fortunatianus Costobius eo quod inter Costobocos nutritus sit \n
EDCS-25601008.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Gaius Sallustius Fortunatianus Costobius, son of Gaius, of the Quirina tribe, because he was raised among the Costoboci.
EDCS-25601008.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the underworld deities (Dis Manibus) by Gaius Sallustius Fortunatianus Costobius, explaining his ethnic origin and tribal affiliation.

EDCS-25601009.translation: [...]na Severa, dutiful, lived 80 years; she rests here.
EDCS-25601009.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the death of Severa, who lived 80 years.

EDCS-25601010.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Gaius Sempronius Namphamo, dutiful, lived [...] years.
EDCS-25601010.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the death of Gaius Sempronius Namphamo, whose age at death is incomplete.

EDCS-25601012.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Sextus Veturius Nummus, dutiful, lived 81 years. Lucretia Prima, dutiful, lived 75 years; he rests here.
EDCS-25601012.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the deaths of Sextus Veturius Nummus and Lucretia Prima, who lived 81 and 75 years respectively.

EDCS-25601013.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Mueturius Primus, son of Marcus, of the Quirina tribe, dutiful, lived [...] years; he rests here. Sacred to the Divine Shades. Aurelia Zabulla, daughter of Sextus, dutiful, lived [...] years; she rests here. Primus and Honoratus Veturii made (this) for (their) excellent parents.
EDCS-25601013.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for multiple individuals, likely parents, made by their sons Primus and Honoratus Veturii.

EDCS-25601014.translation: Vipsania Quinta, dutiful, lived 32 years; she rests here.
EDCS-25601014.summary: This is a tombstone for Vipsania Quinta, recording her name, epithet, lifespan, and burial place.

EDCS-25601019.translation: Sacred to the unconquered Hercules for the well-being of the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Severus Alexander Augustus and Julia Mamaea Augusta. Gemellinus Recavus (dedicated this).
EDCS-25601019.summary: This is a religious dedication to Hercules by Gemellinus Recavus for the health of Emperor Severus Alexander and his mother Julia Mamaea, likely during their reign (222-235 AD).

EDCS-25601021.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Gaius Messius Felix, in memory and for eternity, erected this monument for myself and for my wife, Julia Silicia, in my lands. I set up these inscriptions, being 59 years old. He lived 59 years. Dedicated on the 11th day before the Kalends of December, in the consulship of Messala and Sabinus. Julia Silicia, dutiful, lived 72 years.
EDCS-25601021.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Gaius Messius Felix and his wife Julia Silicia, erected by Felix himself and dated to the consulship of Messala and Sabinus (likely 214 AD).

EDCS-25601023.translation: Sacred to the August Concordia. Titus Pomponius Montanus, son of Titus, of the Fabia tribe, aedile, twice duumvir, designated quinquennalis.
EDCS-25601023.summary: This is a religious dedication to Concordia Augusta by Titus Pomponius Montanus, who held several civic offices in his colony, likely in the 1st or 2nd century AD.

EDCS-25601024.translation: Sacred to the August Genius of the colony. Domitius Valens Sulpicianus, son of Titus, of the Arnensi tribe, [...]
EDCS-25601024.summary: This is a religious dedication to the Genius of the colony by Domitius Valens Sulpicianus, a local official, likely in the 2nd or 3rd century AD.

EDCS-25601025.translation: Quintus Aradius Rufinus, consul, fulfilled his vow to Sol.
EDCS-25601025.summary: This inscription records the fulfillment of a vow to the god Sol by Quintus Aradius Rufinus during his consulship.

EDCS-25601027.translation: Sacred to Mercury Sobrius, Genius Sesas, and the Pantheon, Augustus. For the safety of the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Severus Antoninus Augustus Pius Felix, and Julia Domna Augusta, mother of the Emperor, of the camp, of the Senate, and of the whole fatherland, and of their divine family, Lucilia Cale, priestess of the colony of Thuburnica, built this temple from the ground and gladly fulfilled her vow.
EDCS-25601027.summary: This is a dedication of a temple built from the ground up by Lucilia Cale, a priestess of the colony of Thuburnica, to various deities for the safety of the imperial family, likely in the early 3rd century CE.

EDCS-25601028.translation: Titus Granius Frugi made an altar to Priapus at his own expense for his inheritance.
EDCS-25601028.summary: This inscription records Titus Granius Frugi dedicating an altar to Priapus at his own expense, likely a private dedication with a personal connection to his inheritance.

EDCS-25601029.translation: The aedile, quinquennial official, duovir, and twice priest of the sacred rites, fulfilled his vow willingly.
EDCS-25601029.summary: This inscription records a local magistrate and priest fulfilling a vow, likely from the Roman Republic or early Empire, with specific titles indicating a high level of local office.

EDCS-25601030.translation: By decree of the decurions, at public expense, for the Emperor Caesar Lucius Aurelius Verus Augustus, pontifex maximus, holder of tribunician power for the 3rd time, consul for the 2nd time, proconsul, son of the deified Antoninus, grandson of the deified Hadrian, great-grandson of the deified Trajan Parthicus, great-great-grandson of the deified Nerva.
EDCS-25601030.summary: This inscription details a public dedication made by the town council for Emperor Lucius Aurelius Verus, listing his extensive imperial titles and ancestry, dating to his consulship and tribunician power.

EDCS-25601031.translation: By decree of the decurions, at public expense, for the deified Marcus Aurelius Commodus Antoninus, son of the deified Marcus Aurelius Antoninus, brother of the Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus Arabicus Adiabenicus Parthicus Maximus, father of the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus, and of Publius Septimius Geta Caesar.
EDCS-25601031.summary: This is a public dedication by the town council for the deified Commodus, brother of Septimius Severus and father of Caracalla, likely erected after Commodus's deification.

EDCS-25601032.translation: Quintus Octavius Celsus, father, made and dedicated this at his own expense by decree of the decurions, for Gaius Octavius Honoratus, son of Quintus, of the Cornelian tribe, centurion, admitted from the equestrian order by the deified Pius into the II Augusta legion, centurion of the VII Claudia Pia Fidelis legion, centurion of the XVI Flavia Firma legion, centurion of the X Gemina Pia Fidelis legion, senior principalis.
EDCS-25601032.summary: This inscription records a father's dedication of a monument for his son, a distinguished career soldier who rose through multiple legions, funded by the town council and the father's own money, likely in the Antonine period.

EDCS-25601033.translation: Quintus Octavius, son of Quintus, of the Quirina tribe, a pious veteran, lived 48 years.
EDCS-25601033.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Quintus Octavius, a veteran, recording his name, father's name, tribal affiliation, a pious disposition, and his age at death.

EDCS-25601035.translation: The council, considering that it should decree the erection of a statue at public expense for Quintus Octavius Primo, son of Quintus, of the Cornelian tribe, who had held all honors in his colony, because of his exceptional service to the state and affection for the citizens, his son Caius Octavius Honoratus made it at his own expense. The place was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-25601035.summary: This inscription records the erection of a statue honoring Quintus Octavius Primo for his public service, commissioned by his son Caius Octavius Honoratus and approved by the town council, likely in the late 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-25601036.translation: Marcus Calpurnius Severus, aedile and duovir, lived 65 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-25601036.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Marcus Calpurnius Severus, a local magistrate who served as aedile and duovir, stating his age at death and burial location.

EDCS-25601037.translation: Gaius Memmius Valens, son of Quintus, of the Arnensis tribe, aedile, twice quinquennial magistrate, aged 38.
EDCS-25601037.summary: This inscription records the career and age of a Roman magistrate named Gaius Memmius Valens.

EDCS-25601038.translation: Quintus Aemilius Pudens, son of Marcus, of the Aemilia tribe, lived for 11 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-25601038.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Quintus Aemilius Pudens, recording his age at death.

EDCS-25601039.translation: Caecilia Namphame, devout, lived for 49 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-25601039.summary: This funerary inscription records the name, piety, age, and burial of Caecilia Namphame.

EDCS-25601040.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Fabia Mi, devout, lived for 66 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-25601040.summary: This funerary inscription records the name, piety, age, and burial of Fabia Mi.

EDCS-25601041.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Lucius Flavius Prosper lived for 33 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-25601041.summary: This funerary inscription records the name, age, and burial of Lucius Flavius Prosper.

EDCS-25601042.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Marcus Granius Felix Aelianus, an incomparable friend, lived for 47 years.
EDCS-25601042.summary: This funerary inscription records the name, a description, and age of Marcus Granius Felix Aelianus.

EDCS-25601043.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Iulia Faustilla, daughter of Marcus, of the Faustilla tribe, devout, lived for 45 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-25601043.summary: This funerary inscription records the name, parentage, piety, age, and burial of Iulia Faustilla.

EDCS-25601044.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Gaius Domitius Festus lived for 10 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-25601044.summary: This funerary inscription records the name, age, and burial of Gaius Domitius Festus.

EDCS-25601045.translation: Licinia Fortunata, devout, lived for 20 years.
EDCS-25601045.summary: This funerary inscription records the name, piety, and age of Licinia Fortunata.

EDCS-25601046.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Quintus Longeius Victor, devout, is buried here. He lived for 30 years.
EDCS-25601046.summary: This funerary inscription records the name, piety, burial, and age of Quintus Longeius Victor.

EDCS-25601047.translation: Gaius Lucilius Rusticus, son of Gaius, of the Pollia tribe, dutiful, lived 22 years.
EDCS-25601047.summary: This inscription is a funerary epitaph for Gaius Lucilius Rusticus, recording his name, tribal affiliation, and age at death, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25601048.translation: Peregrinus, son of Arnensis, son of a veteran, dutiful, lived 75 years, is buried here.
EDCS-25601048.summary: This inscription is a funerary epitaph for Peregrinus, noting his father's name, his status as a veteran's son, and his age, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25601049.translation: Dedicated to the departed spirits. Safidia Sabina, dutiful, lived 105 years, is buried here.
EDCS-25601049.summary: This inscription is a funerary epitaph for Safidia Sabina, dedicated to the Manes, recording her name and exceptional age, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25601050.translation: Dedicated to the departed spirits. Sallustius Primus lived 46 years.
EDCS-25601050.summary: This inscription is a funerary epitaph for Sallustius Primus, dedicated to the Manes, recording his name and age, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25601051.translation: Dedicated to the departed spirits. Sallustia Tertulla, dutiful, lived 87 years, is buried here.
EDCS-25601051.summary: This inscription is a funerary epitaph for Sallustia Tertulla, dedicated to the Manes, recording her name and age, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25601056.translation: To the prefect of the praetorian fleet at Misenum, an outstanding man, patron, by decree of the decurions, with public funds, under the administration of Gaius Iulius Optatus.
EDCS-25601056.summary: This inscription records a public dedication or memorial honorific statue to a naval prefect, noting his distinguished service and the officials involved in its erection, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25601057.translation: Dedicated to the departed spirits. Sextus Pompeius Marianus, aedile twice, lived 30 years, is buried here.
EDCS-25601057.summary: This inscription is a funerary epitaph for Sextus Pompeius Marianus, noting his civic offices and age, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25601058.translation: To Publius Sextilius Felix, son of Publius, of the Arnensis tribe, perpetual Augustan flamen, priest of the province of Africa, Publius Ausenius Inclitus Tubero Sextilianus [dedicates this] to his most excellent grandfather for his merits.
EDCS-25601058.summary: This inscription is a dedication by a grandson to his grandfather, a prominent local priest and official in Roman Africa, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25601059.translation: Publius Atius Aliquando, dutiful, lived 2 years and 5 months.
EDCS-25601059.summary: This inscription is a funerary epitaph for Publius Atius Aliquando, recording his name and very young age, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25601060.translation: Dedicated to the departed spirits. Titus Attius Gavillus, son of Titus, dutiful, lived 2 years, is buried here.
EDCS-25601060.summary: This inscription is a funerary epitaph for Titus Attius Gavillus, a young child, dedicated to the Manes, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25601061.translation: Dedicated to the Divine Spirits. Augustalis Primi lived 70 years.
EDCS-25601061.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the Divine Spirits, recording the lifespan of Augustalis Primi.

EDCS-25601063.translation: Dedicated to the Divine Spirits. Quintus Iulius Baliaho, dutiful, lived.
EDCS-25601063.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the Divine Spirits, recording that Quintus Iulius Baliaho lived, but without specifying his age or death date.

EDCS-25601064.translation: Dedicated to the Divine Spirits. Iulia Victoria, dutiful and good, lived 55 years and is buried here. Dedicated to the Divine Spirits. Caius Marius Scintilla, dutiful and a good father, lived 60 years and is buried here.
EDCS-25601064.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the Divine Spirits, recording the lifespans and burials of both Iulia Victoria and Caius Marius Scintilla.

EDCS-25601065.translation: Mutunchlieris, dutiful, lived 90 years and is buried here for his devotion.
EDCS-25601065.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan and burial of Mutunchlieris, emphasizing his devotion.

EDCS-25601066.translation: Marcus Pompeius Faustinus, dutiful, lived 97 years and is buried here.
EDCS-25601066.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan and burial of Marcus Pompeius Faustinus.

EDCS-25601067.translation: Lucius Ventilius Cofo lived 80 years. May your bones rest well.
EDCS-25601067.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Lucius Ventilius Cofo and includes a common funerary wish.

EDCS-25601068.translation: Vicinia Secundina lived 80 years and is buried here.
EDCS-25601068.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan and burial of Vicinia Secundina.

EDCS-25601072.translation: Sallustius Silvanus, dutiful, lived. Sentia Rogata, dutiful, lived.
EDCS-25601072.summary: This inscription seems to be a funerary monument that records the lifespans of Sallustius Silvanus and Sentia Rogata, though their ages are not specified.

EDCS-25601073.translation: Dedicated to the Divine Spirits. Passinia Iucunda, dutiful, lived. Marcus Sulpicius Processianus, dutiful, lived 54 years and is buried here.
EDCS-25601073.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the Divine Spirits, recording the lifespan of Marcus Sulpicius Processianus and mentioning Passinia Iucunda.

EDCS-25601074.translation: Dedicated to the Divine Spirits. Arria Regilla, dutiful mother, lived 2 years. Dedicated to the Divine Spirits. Marcus Iulius Primus, dutiful, lived 25 years. The parents made this for their dearest son, buried here.
EDCS-25601074.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the Divine Spirits by parents for their son Marcus Iulius Primus, also mentioning Arria Regilla and recording the son's age at death.

EDCS-25601075.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Secunda, a dutiful daughter of Secundus, lived 80 years; she lies here.
EDCS-25601075.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death and burial of Secunda, who lived to be 80 years old.

EDCS-25601077.translation: Felicis, son of Usus, and his wife M. and the temple.
EDCS-25601077.summary: A dedication to a temple, possibly by a man named Felicis and his wife.

EDCS-25601082.translation: Oribasius Nabigius and Draconitius, prefect of the city, IO VO VDIS P RISIVIIIO A V IICA, concerning the building of the statue with their own money, Titius Ticius P II PER IICIN RSIIO, and by a judgment of the most ample proconsular authority, they caused the statue to be placed.
EDCS-25601082.summary: A dedication of a statue placed by Oribasius Nabigius and Draconitius, prefect of the city, who funded the project and arranged for its placement through official channels.

EDCS-25601084.summary: A brief inscription indicating an action was taken by Marullius Primus under some form of command.

EDCS-25601085.translation: Callistus, a dutiful man, lived 80 years, 6 months, and 8 days.
EDCS-25601085.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Callistus, who lived 80 years, 6 months, and 8 days.

EDCS-25601086.translation: To Libius, a dutiful man, well-deserving, with his own money.
EDCS-25601086.summary: A dedication to a deserving individual named Libius, funded by himself.

EDCS-25601170.translation: Usus and his most cherished wife.
EDCS-25601170.summary: An incomplete dedication mentioning Usus and his wife, likely part of a larger inscription.

EDCS-25601173.translation: Sacred to Caelestis Augustus. Modius Rusticus, son of M., himself, concerning a statue which was to be erected with public money, under the supervision of Marcus N.
EDCS-25601173.summary: A dedication to Caelestis Augustus, initiated by Modius Rusticus and overseen by Marcus N., concerning a statue funded by public money.

EDCS-25601174.translation: Sacred to Ceres Augusta. Marcus Licinius Tyrannus, freedman of Marcus, and Licinia Prisca, freedwoman of Marcus, having undertaken a vow for the safety of their patron Marcus Licinius Rufus, erected a cella with porticoes and stone columns.
EDCS-25601174.summary: A votive dedication to Ceres Augusta by two freedpersons, Marcus Licinius Tyrannus and Licinia Prisca, for the health of their patron, Marcus Licinius Rufus, who financed the construction of a shrine and colonnades.

EDCS-25601175.translation: Sacred to Ceres Pralaria Augusta. Publius Marcius Quadratus, son of Quintus, of the Arnensis tribe.
EDCS-25601175.summary: A dedication to Ceres Pralaria Augusta by Publius Marcius Quadratus, son of Quintus, identifying his tribal affiliation.

EDCS-25601179.text_edition: \n Fortunae Augustae Veneri Concordiae Augustae sacrum pro salute Imperatoris Caesaris Traiani Hadriani Augusti patris patriae Quintus Maedius Severus patronus pagi et civitatis nomine suo templum quod promiserat ampliata pecunia a fundamentis exstruxit\n
EDCS-25601179.translation: Quintus Maedius Severus, patron of the district and of the citizenry, in his own name, consecrated this temple, which he had promised, enlarged with money, to Fortuna Augusta and Venus Concordia Augusta, for the safety of the Emperor Caesar Trajan Hadrianus Augustus, father of the fatherland, from its foundations.
EDCS-25601179.summary: This is a dedication by Quintus Maedius Severus for the construction of a temple to Fortuna Augusta and Venus Concordia Augusta, intended to ensure the safety of Emperor Hadrian, and records his patron status and the funding of the project.

EDCS-25601180.translation: For the safety of the Emperors Caesar Gaius Aurelius Valerius Diocletianus Pius Felix Invictus Augustus and Marcus Aurelius Valerius Maximianus Pius Felix Invictus Augustus and Flavius Valerius Constantius and Galerius Valerius Maximianus, most noble Caesars. Clarissimus vir ('most illustrious man') adorned the temple of the Genius of the homeland to make it more beautiful, with [---] and other decoration; to which Papirius Balbius Honoratus also contributed 61 [denarii? sesterces?], after giving also sportulae ('bounties/tips') to his fellow decurions, and the heirs of Sergius Firmus Iunianus, because of the greatest [sum of money], dedicated the same thing for the Republic, under the supervision of Octavius Stratonianus, clarissimus vir, curator of the Republic.
EDCS-25601180.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a temple of the Genius of the homeland, adorned and funded by various prominent citizens, including Papirius Balbius Honoratus and the heirs of Sergius Firmus Iunianus, for the welfare of the imperial family and the state, during the curatorship of Octavius Stratonianus.

EDCS-25601182.translation: Sacred to the Genius of the second Aurelian region. Quintus Memmius Felix Caecilianus willingly and deservedly paid his vow.
EDCS-25601182.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to the Genius of a specific city region by Quintus Memmius Felix Caecilianus, likely during the late Roman Empire.

EDCS-25601183.translation: By order of the Divine Augusta (the Empress), Lucius Magnius Felix Remmianus, priest, adorned the image of Queen Juno with her exedra.
EDCS-25601183.summary: This inscription records the work of Lucius Magnius Felix Remmianus, a priest, who, by divine command, embellished a statue of Juno Regina with an exedra, possibly during the 3rd century CE.

EDCS-25601185.summary: A short dedication to the god Liber Pater Augustus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25601187.translation: Sacred to Mercury Augustus, in a place given by the citizenry. He adorned the cella of Mercury with a statue of Mercury.
EDCS-25601187.summary: This inscription records the adornment of a shrine to Mercury Augustus with a statue, funded by the community, likely during the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25601189.translation: Sacred to Mercury Augustus. Lucius Ballenius Secundulus with his family willingly paid his vow with a glad heart.
EDCS-25601189.summary: A votive inscription dedicated to Mercury Augustus by Lucius Ballenius Secundulus and his family, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25601190.translation: Sacred to Mercury Augustus. Lucius Iolius [son of...] paid with his own money.
EDCS-25601190.summary: A dedication to Mercury Augustus funded by Lucius Iolius, likely during the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25601193.summary: A short dedication to the god Mercury Silvio.

EDCS-25601194.translation: Sacred to Mercury and Equity Augusti. Publius Selicius [paid].
EDCS-25601194.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Mercury and Equity Augusti by Publius Selicius, possibly from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25601195.summary: A brief votive inscription to Mercury Augustus by someone named PIO, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25601196.translation: Sacred to Mercury Augustus. Gaius Pluticius Delicianus paid his vow at Mendaciorum.
EDCS-25601196.summary: This inscription records Gaius Pluticius Delicianus fulfilling a vow to Mercury Augustus at a location called Mendaciorum, likely during the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25601198.translation: To Neptune Augustus, sacred. Gaius Helvius Suavis and his wife Cassia Faustina fulfilled their vow. Helvius said, 'I undertook these gifts of the god by vow and established the household gods in my father's house. My wife Faustina placed these same things with me.' To the lord of the waves and father of the Nereids.
EDCS-25601198.summary: A dedication to Neptune by Gaius Helvius Suavis and his wife Cassia Faustina, recording their fulfillment of a vow.

EDCS-25601199.translation: Sacred to Pluto. Aterius fulfilled his vow deservedly.
EDCS-25601199.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled to the god Pluto by Aterius.

EDCS-25601200.translation: Sacred to Pluto, genius of the place.
EDCS-25601200.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Pluto and the local genius of the place.

EDCS-25601203.translation: Sacred to the August Sun God, by the state of the colony of Thugga.
EDCS-25601203.summary: This inscription records a dedication to the Sun God made by the colonial state of Thugga.

EDCS-25601204.translation: For the health of the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Commodus Antoninus, Lucius Octavius Victor Roscianus, on behalf of himself and his wife Venustina, gilded and a temple...
EDCS-25601204.summary: This inscription records a dedication and gilded work on a temple, made for the health of Emperor Commodus by Lucius Octavius Victor Roscianus and his wife.

EDCS-25601207.translation: Titus Iulius Ennius willingly fulfilled his vow deservedly.
EDCS-25601207.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled willingly and deservedly by Titus Iulius Ennius.

EDCS-25601209.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by Quintus Pomp.

EDCS-25601210.translation: Lucius Terentius Luxurius fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-25601210.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by Lucius Terentius Luxurius.

EDCS-25601217.translation: Publius Sabidius Exoratus, with his family, fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-25601217.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by Publius Sabidius Exoratus and his family.

EDCS-25601220.summary: This inscription records a dedication to the August Mercury.

EDCS-25601221.text_edition: \n Divo Augusto sacrum et Tiberio Claudio Caesari Augusto Germanico pontifici maximo tribunicia potestate VIII imperatori XVI consuli IV patri patriae censori Caius Artorius Bassus pontifex aedilis IIvir curator Lucus<t=I>ae patronus pagi dedicavit Iulius Venustus Thinobae filius honoribus peractis flamen divi Augusti et Gabinia Felicula uxor et Faustus filius eius huic senatus et plebs ob merita patris omnium portarum sententiis ornamenta sufetis gratis decrevit suo et Fausti Thinobae patris honoribus peractis flaminis divi Augusti et Firmi qui sic civitas ornamenta sufetis ob merita sua decrevit et Saturi sufetis II qui a civitate et plebe suffragio creatus est et Institoris honoribus peractis flamen sic divi Augusti fratrum suorum nomine sua pecunia fecerunt curatore Iulio Firmo filio \n
EDCS-25601221.translation: Sacred to the deified Augustus and to Tiberius Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus, chief priest, with tribunician power for the 8th time, imperator for the 16th time, consul for the 4th time, father of the fatherland, censor. Gaius Artorius Bassus, priest, aedile twice, duumvir, curator of Lucusta, patron of the district, dedicated it. Julius Venustus, son of Thinobas, after completing his honors as priest of the deified Augustus, and his wife Gabinia Felicula, and his son Faustus, to whom the senate and people decreed ornaments and fasces as a gift for his father's merits with unanimous votes, honored his father Thinobas and himself, as priest of the deified Augustus. And Firmius, who by virtue of his citizenship received ornaments and fasces from the state and people by vote, and Saturus, who was created a fasces-bearer by the state and people by suffrage, and Institor, after completing his honors as priest of the deified Augustus, his brothers, in their name, made it with their own money, with Julius Firmo, his son, as curator.
EDCS-25601221.summary: A dedication of a monument by Gaius Artorius Bassus and Julius Venustus, honoring the emperor Tiberius Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus and the deified Augustus, with extensive details about the honors bestowed on various individuals.

EDCS-25601222.text_edition: \n Imperatori Tiberio Caesari Augusto sacrum curatore Lucio Vergilio Publi filio RufoG dato Viriae Publi filiae Rusticae aviae Marci Licini Rufi flaminis perpetui Augusti coloniae Concordiae Iuliae Karthaginis Marcus Licinius Marci libertus Tyrannus patronus pagi igne consumptas restituit aedem et statuas corruptas exornavit opus intestinum Priscillo filio\n
EDCS-25601222.translation: Sacred to the emperor Tiberius Caesar Augustus. With Lucius Vergilius Rufus, son of Publius, as curator, and given to Viria Rustica, daughter of Publius, grandmother of Marcus Licinius Rufus, perpetual priest of Augustus of the colony of Colonia Concordia Iulia Karthago. Marcus Licinius Tyrannus, freedman of Marcus, son of Marcus, patron of the district, rebuilt the temple, consumed by fire, and adorned the damaged statues, with Priscillus, his son, handling the internal work.
EDCS-25601222.summary: A dedication by Marcus Licinius Tyrannus, a freedman and patron of the district in Karthago, who rebuilt a temple and adorned statues dedicated to Emperor Tiberius Caesar Augustus.

EDCS-25601225.summary: This inscription likely records the deification of Emperor Hadrian, known as Pius.

EDCS-25601227.inscription_type: tituli honorarii, tituli operum, tituli sacri
EDCS-25601227.text_edition: \n Pro salute Imperatoris Titi Aeli Hadriani Antonini Augusti Pii liberorumque eius Quintus Gabinius Marci filius Quirina Felix Faustianus cum Dato et Processa filiis suis porticus fori columnis et contignatione et lacunaribus omnique cultu parietum sua pecunia ornatas pago patriae dedit\n
EDCS-25601227.translation: For the health of Emperor Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Augustus Pius, and his children. Quintus Gabinius Felix Faustianus, son of Marcus of the Quirina tribe, with his sons Dato and Processa, dedicated the portico of the forum, adorned with columns, beams, coffers, and all wall decorations, with his own money, to his fatherland district.
EDCS-25601227.summary: A dedication by Quintus Gabinius Felix Faustianus and his sons, funding the decoration of the forum portico for the health of Emperor Antoninus Pius and his family.

EDCS-25601228.translation: To the deified Antoninus Pius, father of the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus Armeniacus and Emperor Caesar Lucius Aurelius Verus Augustus Armeniacus, the district and city of Thugga, by decree of the decurions, with public money.
EDCS-25601228.summary: A dedication to the deified Emperor Antoninus Pius by the district and city of Thugga.

EDCS-25601231.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus, conqueror of Armenia, conqueror of Parthia, greatest, son of the deified Pius, grandson of the deified Hadrian, great-grandson of the deified Trajan the Parthian, great-great-grandson of the deified Nerva, chief priest, imperator for the fifth time, consul for the third time, with tribunician power for the twenty-second year, father of the country. The pagus of Thugga, increased by their divine favor, by the right to appoint legates, by decree of the decurions, and with public funds.
EDCS-25601231.summary: This inscription records a benefaction by the pagus of Thugga to Emperor Marcus Aurelius Antoninus (reigned 161-180 AD), likely concerning the town's administrative and financial status.

EDCS-25601232.translation: To the deified Verus, brother of the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus, conqueror of Armenia, conqueror of Parthia, greatest, Germanicus, chief priest, with tribunician power for the twenty-seventh year, imperator for the sixth time, consul for the third time, father of the country, proconsul. Nanneia Instania Fida, for the honor of the priesthood, dedicated two colossal statues, which Gaius Terentius Iulianus, the proconsul, had promised for 30,000 sesterces.
EDCS-25601232.summary: This inscription records the dedication of two colossal statues by Nanneia Instania Fida in honor of her priesthood, which were promised by Gaius Terentius Iulianus, likely during the reign of Marcus Aurelius and Lucius Verus (mid-2nd century AD).

EDCS-25601235.translation: To Faustina Augusta, daughter of Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus Armeniacus, and deified Antoninus Pius, the district and city of Thugga, by decree of the decurions, with public money.
EDCS-25601235.summary: A dedication to Empress Faustina, daughter of Marcus Aurelius, by the district and city of Thugga.

EDCS-25601240.translation: While Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus was consul for the second time.
EDCS-25601240.summary: This inscription is a consular dating formula, mentioning Marcus Aurelius Antoninus as consul for the second time, likely from the early part of his reign (around 145 AD).

EDCS-25601241.translation: To Publius Septimius Geta Caesar, Augustus.
EDCS-25601241.summary: This is a dedication to Publius Septimius Geta, who held the title of Caesar and Augustus, likely dating to the period of his co-rule with his father Septimius Severus and brother Caracalla (early 3rd century AD).

EDCS-25601243.translation: To Iulia Domna Augusta, mother of the emperors and of the camps.
EDCS-25601243.summary: This inscription honors Iulia Domna, wife of Septimius Severus and mother of Caracalla and Geta, holding the titles 'Augusta' and 'mother of the emperors and of the camps' (early 3rd century AD).

EDCS-25601244.summary: This is a simple dedication to Iulia Augusta, likely referring to Iulia Domna or another imperial woman of significant status (early 3rd century AD).

EDCS-25601248.translation: And to Iulia Mamaea Augusta, mother of the emperor, and of the camps, and of the senate, and of the fatherland.
EDCS-25601248.summary: This inscription honors Iulia Mamaea, mother of Severus Alexander, bestowing upon her multiple honorific titles, including 'mother of the emperor, and of the camps, and of the senate, and of the fatherland' (reign of Severus Alexander, 222-235 AD).

EDCS-25601251.translation: To our most brave and most pious lord Probus Augustus, that the whole world may flourish in his age. The colony of Thugga, most devoted to his divine will, dedicated [this] under the care of Julius Italicus, a most distinguished man, most devoted to his majesty.
EDCS-25601251.summary: This inscription is a dedication from the colony of Thugga to Emperor Probus (reigned 276-282 AD), expressing loyalty and prosperity under his rule, overseen by Julius Italicus.

EDCS-25601253.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Valerius Maximianus Invictus Augustus, chief priest, with tribunician power for the 3rd time, consul for the 2nd time, father of the fatherland, proconsul. The state of the colony of Thugga, by decree of the decurions, with public money.
EDCS-25601253.summary: A dedication to Emperor Maximian by the state of the colony of Thugga.

EDCS-25601256.text_edition: \n Fortissimo ac nobilissimo Caesari virtute etiam ac pietate praecipuo Flavio Valerio Constantio tribunicia potestate III consuli I patri patriae proconsuli res publica coloniae Thuggensis anno proconsulatus Postumi Titiani clarissimi viri curante Egnatio Tucciano clarissimo viro numini eius maiestatique dicatissimo\n
EDCS-25601256.translation: To the most valiant and noble Caesar, outstanding also in virtue and piety, Flavius Valerius Constantius, with tribunician power for the 3rd time, consul for the 1st time, father of the fatherland, proconsul. The state of the colony of Thugga, in the year of the proconsulship of Postumius Titianus, a most distinguished man, with Egnatius Tuccianus, a most distinguished man, most devoted to his divine majesty.
EDCS-25601256.summary: A dedication to Caesar Flavius Valerius Constantius by the state of the colony of Thugga, during the proconsulship of Postumius Titianus.

EDCS-25601258.translation: For the health of our lords, Gratian, Valentinian, and Theodosius Augustuses. Napotius Felix Antonianus, by whom the games, which the citizens owed him and he had omitted due to neglect and poverty, were presented in a better and more ornate manner, as he was in the office of duovir, for the appearance of the place and the citizens.
EDCS-25601258.summary: This inscription is a dedication for the health of Emperors Gratian, Valentinian, and Theodosius, detailing the sponsorship of public games by Napotius Felix Antonianus during his duovirate, likely in the late 4th century AD.

EDCS-25601265.translation: To the Emperors Caesar and [---] consul, the most distinguished man OE Privatianus ROCCA.
EDCS-25601265.summary: This is a fragmented inscription likely honoring emperors and a local official named Privatianus, dating from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-25601268.summary: This inscription fragment names Quintus Fortunatus, likely a donor or official mentioned in a larger text.

EDCS-25601269.translation: To Appia Alexandria, a most distinguished lady, and Pompeia Appia Cinthia Agathoclia.
EDCS-25601269.summary: A dedication to two women, Appia Alexandria and Pompeia Appia Cinthia Agathoclia.

EDCS-25601270.translation: To Marcus Paccius Silvanus Coredius Gallus Lucius Pullaienus Gargilius Antiquus, consul, for the pagus Thuggensis, as patron, by decree of the decurions, with public money, the curator Lucius Gabinius Clemens, son of Lucius, having served.
EDCS-25601270.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Marcus Paccius Silvanus Coredius Gallus Lucius Pullaienus Gargilius Antiquus, serving as consul and patron of the pagus Thuggensis, with public funds, under the curatorship of Lucius Gabinius Clemens.

EDCS-25601271.text_edition: \n Passieno Rufo tribuno militum legionis XII fulminatae et Passieno Rufi filio Thuggenses pro amicitia quae eis cum patre est libentes dederunt\n
EDCS-25601271.translation: Passienus Rufus, a military tribune of the Twelfth Legion Fulminata, and his son Passienus, have gladly given this to the people of Thugga, in consideration of the friendship they have with the father.
EDCS-25601271.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by the people of Thugga to Passienus Rufus and his son, likely a former official associated with the region, possibly dating to the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-25601272.translation: To Titisenius Papirius Dato Pompeianus, Roman knight, decurion of the most distinguished municipality of Thugga and of the most distinguished colonies of Utica and Uthina, Julius Op us [erected this].
EDCS-25601272.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Titisenius Papirius Dato Pompeianus, a Roman knight and decurion of Thugga and the colonies of Utica and Uthina, erected by Julius Op us.

EDCS-25601273.text_edition: \n Honorati Aulo Vitellio Papiria Felici Honorato equiti Romano fisci advocato at sic vehicula per Flaminiam fisci advocato Transpadum et partem Norici fisci advocato at sic fusa per Numidiam fisci advocato at sic patrimonium Karthaginiense praeposito agenti per Campaniam Calabriam Lucaniam Picenum annonam curanti militibus Augusti nostri sacerdoti Lanuvino pro libertate publica volumtaria sic et gratuita legatione functo ob merita et obsequia eius in patriam et in cives amorem res publica colonia Licinia Thugga decreto decurionum pecunia publica\n
EDCS-25601273.translation: The Republic of the colonia Licinia Thugga, by decree of the decurions and at public expense, has erected this monument to Honoratus, fiscal advocate for Aulus Vitellius Papirius Felix Fortunatus, an equestrian of Rome; fiscal advocate for the Imperial Treasury in the Flaminian region, Transpadana, and part of Noricum; fiscal advocate for the Imperial Treasury's grain supply; fiscal advocate for the Imperial Treasury in Numidia; administrator of the Carthaginian patrimony and agent for Campania, Calabria, Lucania, and Picenum; curator of the grain supply for our Emperor's soldiers; and priest of Lanuvium, who served voluntarily and freely as an ambassador for public liberty, in recognition of his merits and obedience, and his love for his homeland and citizens.
EDCS-25601273.summary: This inscription is a public dedication by the colony of Thugga to Honoratus, a prominent fiscal advocate and former priest, acknowledging his service and love for his homeland, likely dating to the 3rd century CE.

EDCS-25601274.translation: and ginulae, most distinguished women, and ani, most distinguished men, by decree of the decurions, with public money, they made [this] 35.
EDCS-25601274.summary: This inscription records the construction of a monument by distinguished men and women, authorized by the decurions and funded by public money, possibly dating to the later Roman Empire given the numerical notation.

EDCS-25601278.translation: To Asicius Adiutor, a statue decreed by public authority, Marcus Vibius Felix Marcianus and his wife Asicia Victoria [erected this] to the best [man].
EDCS-25601278.summary: This inscription records the public erection of a statue to Asicius Adiutor by Marcus Vibius Felix Marcianus and his wife Asicia Victoria.

EDCS-25601281.text_edition: \n Res publica municipii Septimi Aureli Liberi Thuggae cancellos aereos quos Asicia Victoria flaminica perpetua H Imperatoris ad ornamentum rostrorum ex pollucto HS XXviginti milibus nummum fieri voluit additis a se quattuor cancellis ampliata pecunia dedit\n
EDCS-25601281.translation: The Republic of the municipium of Septimius Aurelius Liber of Thugga has given this, having expanded it with additional funds, of the bronze railings which Asicia Victoria, perpetual flaminica of the Emperor, wished to be made from the privy purse for 20,000 sesterces, to adorn the Rostra, adding four additional railings at her own expense.
EDCS-25601281.summary: This inscription records the completion and expansion of bronze railings for the Rostra in Thugga, funded by Asicia Victoria and supplemented by the local municipality, likely dating to the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-25601283.translation: To Quintus Calpurnius Papirius Rogatianus, patron of the pagus and of the citizen body of Thuggenses, prefect of the craftsmen, honored with the public equestrian rank by the Emperors Marcus Antoninus and Lucius Verus Augusti Armeniaci Parthici Maximi, a statue decreed by public authority, for his merits, his father Marcus Calpurnius Victor, content with the honor, placed [it] at his own expense by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-25601283.summary: This inscription records the erection of a statue to Quintus Calpurnius Papirius Rogatianus, patron of Thuggenses and prefect of craftsmen, honored by Emperors Marcus Aurelius and Lucius Verus, by his father Marcus Calpurnius Victor, following a decree of the decurions.

EDCS-25601285.translation: To Felix LI ino, an excellent youth, to whom the pagus and the citizen body and his mother Grusia, by decree of the decurions, with public money, after death.
EDCS-25601285.summary: This inscription records a posthumous dedication to an excellent youth named Felix LI ino, by the pagus, the citizen body, and his mother Grusia, funded by public money and decreed by the decurions.

EDCS-25601286.translation: NIO S of Marcus Gabinius Clemens Clodianus, patron and defender of the public cause, the decurions of both orders.
EDCS-25601286.summary: This inscription fragment names Marcus Gabinius Clemens Clodianus as patron and defender, with the decurions of both orders indicating their involvement, likely in a public dedication.

EDCS-25601288.translation: The perpetual flamen made this monument.
EDCS-25601288.summary: This inscription records that a perpetual flamen erected this monument.

EDCS-25601289.text_edition: \n Lucio Instanio Papiria Commodo Asicio Adiutori splendidissimae coloniae Thuggae duumviralicio aedilicio libentissime adque abstinentissime ad sacras aures sine onere rei publicae\n
EDCS-25601289.translation: To Lucius Instanius Papirius Commodus Asicius Adiutor, most willingly and with the greatest integrity, without burdening the Republic, for his duumviral and aedilician office, to the sacred ears.
EDCS-25601289.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Lucius Instanius Papirius Commodus Asicius Adiutor, honoring his public offices (duumvir and aedile) in the colonia Thugga, likely dating to the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-25601290.translation: The grandsons and heirs of Caius Julius Martialis Catapala, perpetual flamen, completed and dedicated the ancestral work.
EDCS-25601290.summary: This inscription records that the grandsons and heirs of Caius Julius Martialis Catapala, a perpetual flamen, completed and dedicated a family monument.

EDCS-25601291.translation: Caius Iulius Honoratus Catapalianus Aelianus, son of Marcius Iulius Rogatianus Catapalianus, had begun to build with his private land as perpetual priest with the highest honorary sum, and they (his heirs) completed it with their own money and dedicated it with every adornment.
EDCS-25601291.summary: This inscription records the completion and dedication of a building, likely a public one, started by a perpetual priest, with the work finished by his heirs.

EDCS-25601293.translation: For Caius Marcius Clemens, son of Quintus, of the Arnensis tribe, priest of the deified Vespasian of the colony of Iulia Karthago, who was enrolled in fifteen decuries by the Emperor Antoninus Augustus Pius, due to the generosity of his brother Lucius Marcius Simplex and for the honor of his memory, the pagus and civitas of Thuggenses, by decree of the decurions and with public money, with Caius Modius Rusticus, Lucius Numissius Honoratus, and Iulius Macro Sallustius Iulianus, son of Quintus, as curators.
EDCS-25601293.summary: This inscription is a dedication by the pagus and civitas of Thuggenses to Caius Marcius Clemens, a priest and recipient of honors, likely erected after his death due to his brother's generosity.

EDCS-25601294.translation: For Quintus Marcius Maximus, of the Quirina tribe, son of Lucius Marcius Simplex, due to his son's generosity and for his own merits, the pagus and civitas of Thuggensis, after his death, by decree of the decurions and with public money, with Caius Modius Rusticus, Lucius Numissius Honoratus, and Iulius Macro Sallustius Iulianus, son of Quintus, as curators.
EDCS-25601294.summary: This inscription is a posthumous dedication by the pagus and civitas of Thuggensis to Quintus Marcius Maximus, honoring his own merits and his son's generosity.

EDCS-25601295.translation: Publius Marcius Quadratus, son of Quintus, of the Arnensis tribe, priest of the deified Augustus, pontifex of the colony of Iulia Karthago, who was enrolled in fifteen decuries by the Emperor Antoninus Augustus Pius, for the honor of his perpetual priesthood for his homeland, built a theater from the ground up with his own money, along with basilicas, a portico, xysti, and a stage with scenery and all ornaments; he also dedicated it with theatrical performances, distributions, a banquet, and a gymnasium.
EDCS-25601295.summary: This inscription records Publius Marcius Quadratus, a priest and pontifex, building and dedicating a theater complex in the colony of Iulia Karthago with his own funds.

EDCS-25601421.translation: Rogatilla, restored, 23 years in the Lord's peace.
EDCS-25601421.summary: This is a Christian funerary inscription recording the name and age of Rogatilla.

EDCS-25601456.translation: Sossius Philocratus made this by order.
EDCS-25601456.summary: This is a brief inscription stating that Sossius Philocratus commissioned the object.

EDCS-25601480.translation: To Lucius Attius Exoratus, father of Attius Cornelius, for his singular love for the fatherland and his simple life, the entire senatorial order of Uchitanorum Maiorum gave (this) by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-25601480.summary: This inscription is a public honor bestowed by the decurions of Uchitanorum Maiorum upon Lucius Attius Exoratus for his patriotism and virtuous life.

EDCS-25601481.translation: The state of the colony of Uchitanorum Maiorum, by decree of the decurions and with public money, (erected this) to Caius Mammius Vettius Aemilianus, son of the most excellent man Caius Mammius Vettius Castus, his most loving alumnus and patron.
EDCS-25601481.summary: This inscription is a public dedication by the colony of Uchitanorum Maiorum to Caius Mammius Vettius Aemilianus, honoring him as a beloved patron and alumnus.

EDCS-25601484.translation: Lucius Cornelius Quietus, his son and perpetual priest, made (this) with his own money for his most excellent father, Lucius Cornelius Quietus, a man of honorable memory, who in his will left ten million sesterces to the state of the colony Mariana Augusta Alexandriana Uchitanorum Maiorum through a fideicommissum, from the interest of which, annually on his birthday, distributions should be given to the decurions and games to the people, and he dedicated it after obtaining permission for the location from the order.
EDCS-25601484.summary: This inscription records a son's monument to his father, who left a significant endowment for public distributions and games in the colony of Mariana Augusta Alexandriana Uchitanorum Maiorum.

EDCS-25601500.summary: This is a Christian funerary inscription simply stating the name of Porphyrius.

EDCS-25601501.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Sextus Octavius Felix, pious, lived 40 years; he is buried here.

EDCS-25601521.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan and burial of Morasia Victoria, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-25601522.translation: The estates of the Pullaini, sons of Titinius Pupianus and Petronianus Decimus, most distinguished youths, sons of Celsinus Pupianus, an excellent man, and of Roia Titinia Florentiorum.
EDCS-25601522.summary: A boundary or ownership inscription that names the sons of prominent individuals and their respective estates, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25601523.translation: For the health and safety of the Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus, and the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus, and Lucius Septimius Severus Geta Caesar, and Julia Domna Augusta, mother of the camps, Patroclus, freedman of the Augusti and procurator, established an altar to the deified Hadrian and inscribed the law written below. An example of the law of Hadrian, set up on the altar: Statement of the procurators: Since our Caesar, with tireless care, by which he vigilantly watches over the welfare of mankind, orders all parts of the fields, suitable for olives or vines or grain, to be cultivated, therefore, by his provident permission, power is given to all to occupy even those parts that are in the located centuriae of the Blandian and Udensian pastures, and in those parts that are joined to the Thysdritan from the Lamian and Domitian pastures and are not worked by the tenants. And the right is granted to him who occupies them to possess, enjoy, and leave them to his heir, which right is also comprehended in the Hadrianic law concerning uncultivated lands and those that have been left uncultivated for ten continuous years. And from the Blandian and Udensian pasture, he who occupies those lands will give one third of the produce, which is usually given from those neglected by the tenants. From these regions which are joined to the Thysdritan from the Lamian and Domitian pasture, he will give the same amount. For olives which anyone has planted either in pits or grafted onto wild stock, no part of the harvested fruits will be demanded for the next ten years, nor for seven years for fruits, nor will any other fruits ever be subject to division than those which are sold by the possessors. The parts of the produce which anyone will owe will be paid to the one in whose tenancy he occupied the land within the next five years; after that time, to the account.
EDCS-25601523.summary: An inscription establishing an altar to Hadrian and detailing a land cultivation law issued by the Severan emperors, likely dating to the early 3rd century CE, concerning the cultivation of public lands and benefits for those who bring them into use.

EDCS-25601528.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Quintus Lenasenus Sipo Severianus, most faithful physician, lived 75 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-25601528.summary: A funerary epitaph for Quintus Lenasenus Sipo Severianus, a physician, recording his lifespan and burial, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-25601530.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the life of Honus Pius.

EDCS-25601532.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Gaius Julius Felix of the East lived piously for 70 years, he is buried here.
EDCS-25601532.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the death and age of Gaius Julius Felix, likely from the Eastern part of the Roman Empire.

EDCS-25601533.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Quintus Julius Victor lived piously.
EDCS-25601533.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the pious life of Quintus Julius Victor.

EDCS-25601534.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the deified Empress Octavia.

EDCS-25601535.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Quintus Sallustius Victor lived piously for [some number of] years.
EDCS-25601535.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the pious life of Quintus Sallustius Victor.

EDCS-25601536.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Valeria Feleria lived for 55 years, she is buried here.
EDCS-25601536.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the death and age of Valeria Feleria.

EDCS-25601538.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Buccuncia Pia lived for 16 years, she is buried here.
EDCS-25601538.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the death and age of Buccuncia Pia.

EDCS-25601539.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Caecilia Accepta, daughter of Quintus, lived piously for 105 years, she is buried here.
EDCS-25601539.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the death and age of Caecilia Accepta, daughter of Quintus.

EDCS-25601540.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Luria Ianuaria lived piously for 60 years, she is buried here. Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Gaius Hordionius Honoratus lived piously for 70 years, he is buried here.
EDCS-25601540.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the deaths and ages of two individuals, Luria Ianuaria and Gaius Hordionius Honoratus.

EDCS-25601541.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Quintus Nonius Nampamo lived piously for 45 years, he is buried here. Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Pontia Rustica lived piously for 67 years, she is buried here.
EDCS-25601541.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the deaths and ages of two individuals, Quintus Nonius Nampamo and Pontia Rustica.

EDCS-25601542.translation: Dianus Pius lived 70 years and 4 months; he is buried here. Saturnina Pia lived 41 years and 3 months and 13 days; she is buried here.
EDCS-25601542.summary: This inscription records the burial of Dianus Pius and Saturnina Pia, noting their lifespans.

EDCS-25601544.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Octavia Dionisia Pia lived 90 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-25601544.summary: This inscription records the burial of Octavia Dionisia Pia, noting her age.

EDCS-25601545.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Caius Sallustius, son of Felicis, Pius, lived 41 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-25601545.summary: This inscription records the burial of Caius Sallustius, noting his age and parentage.

EDCS-25601546.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Servilia Matica Pia lived 70 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-25601546.summary: This inscription records the burial of Servilia Matica Pia, noting her age.

EDCS-25601547.summary: This is a dedication to the goddess Augusta.

EDCS-25601548.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Ianuarius, son of Fortunati Barniccalonis, Pius, lived 102 years.
EDCS-25601548.summary: This inscription records the lifespan of Ianuarius, son of Fortunati Barniccalonis.

EDCS-25601549.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Iulia Fortunata Calediana Pia lived 33 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-25601549.summary: This inscription records the burial of Iulia Fortunata Calediana Pia, noting her age.

EDCS-25601552.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Quintus Modius Felix Pius lived 85 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-25601552.summary: This inscription records the burial of Quintus Modius Felix Pius, noting his age.

EDCS-25601553.translation: Dedication from LVSIII IVVS DIC, priest and designated aedile, from Atica, mother of the Colony of Concordia Iulia Karthago.
EDCS-25601553.summary: This is a dedication by Atica, mother of the colony of Carthage, who held religious and civic offices.

EDCS-25601748.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Iulius Rusticus lived 30 years.
EDCS-25601748.summary: This inscription records the lifespan of Iulius Rusticus.

EDCS-25601749.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Julia Secunda, daughter of Arator, pious, lived 58 years. May your bones rest well here. She is buried here.
EDCS-25601749.summary: A funerary epitaph for Julia Secunda, likely dating to the imperial period, recording her name, parentage, piety, and age at death.

EDCS-25601750.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Munatia Nafaminna, daughter of Quintus, lived 50 years.
EDCS-25601750.summary: A funerary epitaph for Munatia Nafaminna, likely dating to the imperial period, recording her name, parentage, piety, and age at death.

EDCS-25601751.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Ponpilius Secundus, pious, lived 76 years.
EDCS-25601751.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lucius Ponpilius Secundus, likely dating to the imperial period, recording his name, piety, and age at death.

EDCS-25601752.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Pomponia Primosa, pious, lived 31 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-25601752.summary: A funerary epitaph for Pomponia Primosa, likely dating to the imperial period, recording her name, piety, age at death, and burial location.

EDCS-25601757.translation: To Marcus Attius Cornelius, most eminent prefect of the Praetorian Guard, a distinguished man, citizen, and patron, for his incomparable love of the fatherland and fellow citizens, the state of the colony Mariana Augusta Alexandriana of the Uchitani Majores, by decree of the decurions, with public funds.
EDCS-25601757.summary: A public dedication by the colony of Mariana Augusta Alexandriana to Marcus Attius Cornelius, a high-ranking official, honoring his love for the fatherland and citizens, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-25601765.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus A manus, pious, lived 33 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-25601765.summary: A funerary epitaph for Quintus A manus, likely dating to the imperial period, recording his name, piety, age at death, and burial location.

EDCS-25601766.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Aabim Amplia S lived [---] years. She is buried here.
EDCS-25601766.summary: A fragmented funerary epitaph for Aabim Amplia S, likely dating to the imperial period, recording her name and burial location, with the age at death missing.

EDCS-25601767.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Edinia Nampamina, pious, lived 55 years. She is buried here.

EDCS-25601768.translation: Atiutor, pious, lived 75 years. He is buried here.
