EDCS-25700292.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Secundus, son of Bal, lived 52 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-25700292.summary: A funerary inscription recording the death of Secundus, son of Bal, who lived 52 years.

EDCS-25700293.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Marcus Aurelius Victor lived 93 years and 5 days.
EDCS-25700293.summary: A funerary inscription recording the death of Marcus Aurelius Victor, who lived 93 years and 5 days.

EDCS-25700294.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Novellus, son of Crescens, pious, returned the honors to his city.
EDCS-25700294.summary: A funerary inscription for Novellus, son of Crescens, who was pious and returned honors to his city.

EDCS-25700295.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Caius Pomponius Victor, perpetual priest and pious priest of Caelestis.
EDCS-25700295.summary: A funerary inscription honoring Caius Pomponius Victor, a perpetual priest and priest of Caelestis.

EDCS-25700296.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. C. Lucana lived 61 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-25700296.summary: A funerary inscription recording the death of C. Lucana, who lived 61 years.

EDCS-25700297.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Ceto, son of Zabonis.
EDCS-25700297.summary: A funerary inscription for Ceto, son of Zabonis.

EDCS-25700298.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Cornelius Gallus, pious, lived 65 years and 5 months; he is buried here.
EDCS-25700298.summary: A funerary inscription recording the death of Cornelius Gallus, who lived 65 years and 5 months.

EDCS-25700299.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Crescentia, daughter of Marcianus, pious, lived 25 years; she is buried here under the care of [---].
EDCS-25700299.summary: A funerary inscription recording the death of Crescentia, daughter of Marcianus, who lived 25 years.

EDCS-25700300.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Demetria Ancilla lived 80 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-25700300.summary: A funerary inscription recording the death of Demetria Ancilla, who lived 80 years.

EDCS-25700301.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Gaganius, son of Clementis Galli, pious, lived 43 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-25700301.summary: A funerary inscription recording the death of Gaganius, son of Clementis Gallus, who lived 43 years.

EDCS-25700302.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Helvia Rogata lived 81 years. She is buried here. Galicus her son-in-law and daughter took care of the burial.
EDCS-25700302.summary: A funerary epitaph for Helvia Rogata, who lived 81 years, erected by her son-in-law and daughter.

EDCS-25700303.translation: Lived 3 years and 1 day. Ianuarius the pious lived 71 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-25700303.summary: A funerary epitaph for Ianuarius, who lived 71 years and 1 day (likely a father and son or two individuals with the same name).

EDCS-25700304.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Ianuarius Bagrem the pious lived 60 years.
EDCS-25700304.summary: A funerary epitaph for Ianuarius Bagrem, who lived 60 years.

EDCS-25700305.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. [He/She] lived 101 years. He is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Iunius Adiutor lived 61 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-25700305.summary: A funerary epitaph for two individuals, one who lived 101 years and Lucius Iunius Adiutor who lived 61 years.

EDCS-25700306.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Ollius Mi, son of Titius, lived 53 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-25700306.summary: A funerary epitaph for Ollius Mi, son of Titius, who lived 53 years.

EDCS-25700307.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Marinia the pious lived 56 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-25700307.summary: A funerary epitaph for Marinia, who lived 56 years.

EDCS-25700308.translation: Lived 40 years. He is buried here under the care of his wife. Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus Memmius the pious lived 60 years. He is buried here under the care of his son Solutor. Lived 73 years. He is buried here under the care of his son Caius Memmius Quintasius. Sacred to the departed spirits. Dulcis, daughter of Victor, the pious lived 80 years. She is buried here under the care of her son Solutor.
EDCS-25700308.summary: A complex funerary inscription recording at least four individuals (Quintus Memmius, a wife, Dulcis, and potentially two others), with ages and caretakers mentioned.

EDCS-25700309.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. [He/She] Masgabes the pious lived 41 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-25700309.summary: A funerary epitaph for Masgabes, who lived 41 years.

EDCS-25700310.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Namgede, daughter of Baliatonis, the pious lived 51 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-25700310.summary: A funerary epitaph for Namgede, daughter of Baliatonis, who lived 51 years.

EDCS-25700311.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Ninus, son of Saturus, lived 45 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-25700311.summary: A funerary epitaph for Ninus, son of Saturus, who lived 45 years.

EDCS-25700312.translation: Numerius, son of Marci Novelli, lived 56 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-25700312.summary: A funerary inscription recording the lifespan and burial of Numerius, son of Marci Novelli.

EDCS-25700313.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Petronius Tittos, dutiful, lived 23 years; he is buried here. Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Lucius Petronius, dutiful, lived 56 years; with the care of the city.
EDCS-25700313.summary: A funerary inscription for Petronius Tittos and Lucius Petronius, noting their lifespans and mentioning care from the city.

EDCS-25700314.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Pistu, daughter of Biricbalis, dutiful, lived 51 years; she is buried here. Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Acutus Crescens, dutiful, lived 65 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-25700314.summary: A funerary inscription for Pistu, daughter of Biricbalis, and Acutus Crescens, recording their ages at death.

EDCS-25700315.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Rogata, daughter of Publi, dutiful, lived 67 years; she is buried here, with her husband caring for her.
EDCS-25700315.summary: A funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Rogata, daughter of Publi, with her husband mentioned as the caregiver.

EDCS-25700316.translation: Rufus Martialis, son of Sadunis, dutiful, lived 16 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-25700316.summary: A funerary inscription recording the short life and burial of Rufus Martialis, son of Sadunis.

EDCS-25700317.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. S Berectina, dutiful, lived 10 years; she is buried here, with her father and mother caring for her. Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Chelidon, daughter of Masclonis, dutiful, lived 35 years; cared for.
EDCS-25700317.summary: A funerary inscription for S Berectina and Chelidon, daughter of Masclonis, detailing their ages and the caretakers.

EDCS-25700318.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Sattun, son of Zabonis, dutiful, lived 53 years; he is buried here. May the earth be light for you, may your bones be well.
EDCS-25700318.summary: A funerary inscription for Sattun, son of Zabonis, recording his age and including a common epitaph wishing peace.

EDCS-25700319.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Saturus, son of Hagiris Laudonis, dutiful, lived 25 years; with his brothers caring for him.
EDCS-25700319.summary: A funerary inscription for Saturus, son of Hagiris Laudonis, noting his age and that he was cared for by his brothers.

EDCS-25700320.translation: Sempronia, daughter of Victoris, lived 75 years; her daughter Saturnina arranged for her burial here.
EDCS-25700320.summary: A funerary inscription stating the lifespan of Sempronia, daughter of Victoris, and that her daughter Saturnina arranged her burial.

EDCS-25700321.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Victoria, daughter of Matrones, lived 85 years; cared for by her heir Guddemi; she is buried here.
EDCS-25700321.summary: A funerary inscription for Victoria, daughter of Matrones, recording her age and indicating her heir, Guddemi, arranged her burial.

EDCS-25700322.translation: Tvn has completed her functions, she lived for 35 years, cared for by her husband; here she is laid. MIII has completed his functions, cared for by his children; he lived for 61 years; here he is laid.
EDCS-25700322.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of two individuals, Tvn and MIII, with their ages and caretakers.

EDCS-25700323.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Aulus Vidius, [son of] N...
EDCS-25700323.summary: This is a fragmentary dedication to the Manes, likely for Aulus Vidius.

EDCS-25700325.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Sissoi, daughter of Primi, pious, lived for 75 years; here she is laid. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Namphamus, son of Diilo, pious, lived for 35 years; here he is laid.
EDCS-25700325.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of two individuals, Sissoi and Namphamus, detailing their ages and piety.

EDCS-25700326.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Berecbal, pious, lived for 31 years, for her deserving father.
EDCS-25700326.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Berecbal, who lived for 31 years, dedicated by her father.

EDCS-25700327.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Publius Iulianus, pious, lived for 55 years.
EDCS-25700327.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Publius Iulianus, who lived for 55 years.

EDCS-25700328.translation: Lucius M Liberalis lived for 71 years.
EDCS-25700328.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Lucius M Liberalis, who lived for 71 years.

EDCS-25700329.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Rogatus lived for 27 years.
EDCS-25700329.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Rogatus, who lived for 27 years.

EDCS-25700330.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Quintus Sempronius, who lived for 45 years.

EDCS-25700331.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Lucius Murrius Fronto, veteran of the II Adiutrix legion, DONALARIS, pious, lived for 75 years; here he is laid.
EDCS-25700331.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Lucius Murrius Fronto, a veteran of the II Adiutrix legion, who lived for 75 years.

EDCS-25700333.summary: This inscription appears to be a fragmentary dedication or naming of Ninus Caesar, possibly with a numerical or military context.

EDCS-25700335.translation: Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus, greatest conqueror of Parthia, of Britain, and of Germany, holding the tribunician power for the 19th time, consul for the 4th time, father of the fatherland, restored [this].
EDCS-25700335.summary: This inscription records the restoration of something by Emperor Marcus Aurelius Antoninus, likely in the late 2nd or early 3rd century CE.

EDCS-25700336.translation: To the most unconquered Emperors Caesar Flavius Valerius Constantius and Galerius Valerius Maximianus, devotedly, 47 [years].
EDCS-25700336.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Emperors Constantius and Maximianus, likely dating to the Tetrarchy period (late 3rd/early 4th century CE).

EDCS-25700337.translation: To Emperor Caesar Gaius Flavius Valerius Constantinus Pius Felix Invictus Augustus, chief priest, holding the tribunician power for the 19th time, consul for the 6th time, father of the fatherland, proconsul.
EDCS-25700337.summary: This inscription honors Emperor Constantine the Great, likely during his reign in the early 4th century CE.

EDCS-25700338.translation: To our Lord Caesar Flavius Valerius Constan[tinus].
EDCS-25700338.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription honoring Emperor Constantine, likely from the early 4th century CE.

EDCS-25700339.translation: Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus, greatest conqueror of Parthia, of Britain, and of Germany, holding the tribunician power for the 19th time, consul for the 4th time, father of the fatherland, restored [this], 41 [years].
EDCS-25700339.summary: This inscription records the restoration of something by Emperor Marcus Aurelius Antoninus, likely in the late 2nd or early 3rd century CE, with a measurement of 41 units.

EDCS-25700341.translation: To Emperor Caesar Gaius Flavius Valerius Constantinus Maximus Pius Felix Invictus Augustus, born for the good of the state, chief priest, greatest conqueror of Germany and Sarmatia, holding the tribunician power for the 9th time, consul for the 3rd time, consul designate for the 4th time.
EDCS-25700341.summary: This inscription honors Emperor Constantine the Great, likely in the late 310s or early 320s CE, highlighting his military successes and multiple consulships.

EDCS-25700343.translation: Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus, greatest conqueror of Parthia and of Britain, holding the tribunician power for the 19th time, consul for the 4th time, father of the fatherland, restored [this], 58 [units].
EDCS-25700343.summary: This inscription records the restoration of something by Emperor Marcus Aurelius Antoninus, likely in the late 2nd or early 3rd century CE, with a measurement of 58 units.

EDCS-25700344.translation: Emperor Caesar, grandson of the deified Nerva, son of the deified Trajan, Trajan Hadrian Augustus, chief priest, holding the tribunician power for the 7th time, consul for the 3rd time, paved the road from Carthage to Theveste, through the Legio III Augusta, under Publius Metilius Secundus, governor with the rank of imperial legate, 62 [units].
EDCS-25700344.summary: This inscription records Emperor Hadrian's paving of a road by Legio III Augusta under the governor Publius Metilius Secundus, dated to his 7th tribunician power and 3rd consulship (around 125-128 CE).

EDCS-25700345.translation: Under Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Probus Pius Felix Augustus.
EDCS-25700345.summary: This inscription is a dedication or record made during the reign of Emperor Marcus Aurelius Probus, likely in the late 3rd century CE.

EDCS-25700346.translation: Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Constantinus, [for] 6 years, VIVICOR, Augustus, chief priest, holding tribunician power, consul, proconsul, father of the fatherland, 69 [units].
EDCS-25700346.summary: This inscription honors Emperor Constantine the Great, likely from the early 4th century CE, mentioning his consulships and years of power.

EDCS-25700347.translation: Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Augustus, greatest Parthian, greatest German, with tribunician power for the 19th time, consul for the 4th time, father of the country, restored [this] 71.
EDCS-25700347.summary: This inscription records the restoration of a monument (indicated by 'restituit') by Emperor Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Augustus, likely dating to his reign based on his titles and tribunician power count.

EDCS-25700348.translation: To Emperor Caesar Valerius Diocletianus, pious, fortunate Augustus 71.
EDCS-25700348.summary: This is a dedication to Emperor Valerius Diocletianus, likely part of a monument, dating to his reign.

EDCS-25700349.translation: To the most powerful Emperor and pacifier of the world, Marcus Claudius Tacitus, pious, fortunate Augustus.
EDCS-25700349.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Emperor Tacitus, celebrating him as a pacifier of the world, likely from the period of his reign.

EDCS-25700352.translation: The Emperors Caesar Gaius Julius Verus Maximinus Pius Felix Augustus, Germanicus Maximus, Sarmaticus Maximus, Dacicus Maximus, Pontifex Maximus, holding tribunician power for the 3rd time, Imperator for the 5th time, and Gaius Julius Verus Maximus, most noble Caesar, Princeps of the Youth, Germanicus Maximus, Sarmaticus Maximus, Dacicus Maximus, paved the road from Carthage [...].
EDCS-25700352.summary: This inscription records the paving of a road from Carthage by Emperors Maximinus Thrax and his son Caesar Maximus, with the completion date indicated by their titles and imperial powers, likely around 236-238 CE.

EDCS-25700353.translation: To the perpetual Emperor Caesar Lucius Domitius Aurelianus, pious, fortunate Augustus.
EDCS-25700353.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Emperor Aurelian, praising his perpetual and fortunate reign.

EDCS-25700354.translation: Emperor Caesar Marcus Philippus, Invictus, Pius, Felix Augustus, chief priest, with tribunician power, consul designate, father of the country, proconsul, and Marcus Iulius Philippus, most noble Caesar Augustus, princeps.
EDCS-25700354.summary: This inscription records the titles of Emperor Philippus and his son, Caesar Philippus, highlighting their imperial powers and roles.

EDCS-25700356.translation: Emperor Caesar Marcus Antonius Gordianus, grandson of the deified Marcus Antonius Gordianus, son of the sister of the deified Marcus Antonius Gordianus, to the pious, fortunate, most victorious Augustus.
EDCS-25700356.summary: This inscription lists the full titulature of Emperor Gordian III, emphasizing his lineage and divine connections.

EDCS-25700357.translation: Emperor Caesar, descendant of the deified Nerva, son of the deified Trajan Parthicus.
EDCS-25700357.summary: This inscription identifies an emperor by his divine ancestry, linking himself to the deified Nerva and Trajan.

EDCS-25700358.translation: Trajan Hadrian Augustus, Pontifex Maximus, holding tribunician power for the 7th time, Consul for the 3rd time, paved the road from Carthage to Theveste, with the 85th mile marker, through Legio III Augusta, under Publius Metilius Secundus, legate of the Emperor pro praetore.
EDCS-25700358.summary: This inscription records the construction of the road from Carthage to Theveste by Emperor Hadrian, completed under the governorship of Publius Metilius Secundus by Legio III Augusta, likely around 123 CE.

EDCS-25700361.translation: To our Lord Constantine, most pious, most noble Caesar 87.
EDCS-25700361.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Constantine as Caesar, likely part of a larger monument, dating to his period as Caesar.

EDCS-25700362.translation: To Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Probus, pious, fortunate Augustus, chief priest, with tribunician power for the 3rd time.
EDCS-25700362.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Emperor Probus, listing his imperial titles and tribunician power.

EDCS-25700365.translation: To our most peaceful Emperor Lucius Domitius Aurelianus, unconquered, pious, fortunate Augustus 93.
EDCS-25700365.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Emperor Aurelian, emphasizing his peaceful and victorious reign.

EDCS-25700366.translation: To the most peaceful Emperor Caesar Marcus Claudius Tacitus Pius Felix Augustus, 123.
EDCS-25700366.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Emperor Tacitus, likely on a public monument given the numerical designation.

EDCS-25700367.translation: To our lord Dominus IV, the Germanicus Sarmaticus Augustus, Flavius Valerius Constantinus, 116.
EDCS-25700367.summary: This inscription honors Emperor Constantine I, possibly on a monument indicating his victories or titles.

EDCS-25700370.translation: Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus, Parthicus Maximus, Britannicus Maximus, Germanicus Maximus, with tribunician power for the 19th time, consul for the 4th time, father of the fatherland, restored (this), 116.
EDCS-25700370.summary: This inscription records the restoration activities of Emperor Caracalla, highlighting his numerous titles and powers.

EDCS-25700373.translation: Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Augustus, Parthicus Maximus, Britannicus Maximus, Germanicus Maximus, with tribunician power for the 19th time, consul for the 4th time, father of the fatherland, restored (this), 151.
EDCS-25700373.summary: This inscription records the restoration activities of Emperor Caracalla, emphasizing his titles and powers, likely on a restored structure.

EDCS-25700377.summary: This is a brief dedication to an emperor referred to as Caesar Augustus, possibly indicating an imperial cult or a general imperial dedication.

EDCS-25700384.translation: To our lord Julianus, forever Augustus, Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Augustus, Parthicus Maximus, Britannicus Maximus, Germanicus Maximus, with tribunician power for the 18th time, consul for the 4th time, father of the fatherland, restored (this), 185.
EDCS-25700384.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Emperor Julian, recording his restoration achievements and extensive imperial titles.

EDCS-25700385.summary: This is a fragmented inscription referring to Emperor Marcus Aurelius, possibly part of a titulature or a list of honors.

EDCS-25700388.translation: Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Augustus, Parthicus Maximus, Britannicus Maximus, Germanicus Maximus, with tribunician power for the 18th time, consul for the 4th time, father of the fatherland, restored (this), 187.
EDCS-25700388.summary: This inscription records the restoration activities of Emperor Caracalla, highlighting his numerous titles and powers.

EDCS-25700389.text_edition: \n Imperator Caesar divi Traiani Parthici filius divi Nervae nepos Traianus Hadrianus Augustus pontifex maximus tribunicia potestate VII consul III viam a Carthagine Thevestem milia passuum CXCIcentum nonaginta unum miliaDCCXXXXseptingentos quadraginta stravit Publio Metilio Secundo legato Augusti pro praetore consule designato per legionem III Augustam\n
EDCS-25700389.translation: Emperor Caesar, son of the deified Trajan Parthicus, grandson of the deified Nerva, Trajan Hadrian Augustus, Pontifex Maximus, holding tribunician power for the 7th time, Consul for the 3rd time, paved the road from Carthage to Theveste, 191 miles and 740 paces, through Legio III Augusta, under Publius Metilius Secundus, legate of the Emperor pro praetore, consul-designate.
EDCS-25700389.summary: This inscription details Emperor Hadrian's paving of the road from Carthage to Theveste, specifying the length, and attributing its construction to Legio III Augusta under Publius Metilius Secundus, dating to around 117-119 CE.

EDCS-25700390.translation: Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus, Parthicus Maximus, Britannicus Maximus, Germanicus Maximus, with tribunician power for the 19th time, consul for the 4th time, father of the fatherland, restored (this), 49.
EDCS-25700390.summary: This inscription records the restoration activities of Emperor Caracalla, emphasizing his titles and powers, possibly on a restored monument.

EDCS-25700391.text_edition: \n Imperatore Caesare Vespasiano Augusto pontifice maximo tribunicia potestate VII imperatore XVII consule VII qui primusitionem flumin aperuit Imperatore Tito Vespasiano Augusti filio imperatore XI pontifice tribunicia potestate V consule V Caesare Augusti filio Domitiano consule IIII pontifice Quinto Egnatio Cato legato Augusti pro praetore legio III Augusta\n
EDCS-25700391.translation: During the reign of Emperor Caesar Vespasian Augustus, Pontifex Maximus, holding tribunician power for the 7th time, Imperator for the 17th time, Consul for the 7th time, who first opened the course of the river, and Emperor Titus Vespasian Augustus, son of Augustus, Imperator for the 11th time, Pontifex, holding tribunician power for the 5th time, Consul for the 5th time, and Caesar Augustus' son Domitian, Consul for the 4th time, Pontifex, under Quintus Egnatius Catus, legate of the Emperor pro praetore, with Legio III Augusta.
EDCS-25700391.summary: This inscription records public works, including the opening of a river course, carried out under Emperors Vespasian and Titus, and Caesar Domitian, with the involvement of Legio III Augusta and legate Quintus Egnatius Catus, likely during the 70s CE.

EDCS-25700392.translation: Emperor Caesar, son of the divine Nerva, Nerva Trajan Optimus Augustus Germanicus Dacicus, chief priest, with tribunician power for the 16th time, emperor for the 6th time, consul for the 6th time, father of the fatherland, built a new bridge from its foundations with the work of his soldiers and at his own expense for the province of Africa.
EDCS-25700392.summary: This inscription records Emperor Trajan's construction of a new bridge in the province of Africa, detailing his many honors and the resources used.

EDCS-25800046.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Aurelius Carus, the Unconquered, Pious, Fortunate, Augustus, and to Marcus Aurelius Carinus and Marcus Aurelius Numerian, most noble Caesars.
EDCS-25800046.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the emperors Carus, Carinus, and Numerian.

EDCS-25800047.translation: To the most noble Caesars, Flavius Valerius Constantius and Galerius Valerius Maximian, Augusti, the state of the municipality of Thibilis.
EDCS-25800047.summary: This inscription is a dedication by the municipality of Thibilis to the Caesars Constantius and Maximian.

EDCS-25800090.translation: The people of Sicca to the deified Augustus, the founder.
EDCS-25800090.summary: This inscription is a dedication by the people of Sicca to the deified Augustus.

EDCS-25800094.translation: To the most eminent proconsul Lucius Flavius Julianus, in his second consulship.
EDCS-25800094.summary: This inscription honors Lucius Flavius Julianus for his second consulship.

EDCS-25800095.translation: To Julius Aquilinus, son of Caius, of the voting tribe Quirina, equo publico, admitted into the V decuriae, prefect.
EDCS-25800095.summary: This inscription honors Julius Aquilinus, detailing his public career and equestrian status.

EDCS-25800096.translation: The order of citizens of Sicca to Nepotianus, an outstanding man, procurator of sixty years, from the acts, a procurator of one hundred years, of the first bench, a citizen and fellow decurion, by decree of the decurions, at public expense.
EDCS-25800096.summary: This inscription honors Nepotianus, a distinguished official of the city of Sicca, detailing his long service and honors.

EDCS-25800104.translation: Gaius Julius Optatus, freedman of Venus, lived 40 years.
EDCS-25800104.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Gaius Julius Optatus, recording his name, patron, and age at death.

EDCS-25800105.translation: Marisath, daughter of Nicer, the Tectoris, lived 80 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-25800105.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marisath, daughter of Nicer, recording her name, father, and age at death.

EDCS-25800106.translation: Adiutor, son of Aeneas, lived 31 years.
EDCS-25800106.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Adiutor, son of Aeneas, recording his name, father, and age at death.

EDCS-25800107.translation: Marcus Aemilius Adiutor lived 51 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-25800107.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcus Aemilius Adiutor, recording his name and age at death.

EDCS-25800108.translation: Aemilius Martialis lived 30 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-25800108.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Aemilius Martialis.

EDCS-25800109.translation: Marcus Aemilius Saturninus, son of Marcus, lived 60 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-25800109.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Marcus Aemilius Saturninus.

EDCS-25800110.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Lucius Aemilius Valentinus.

EDCS-25800111.translation: Quintus Aemilius Victor lived 35 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-25800111.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Quintus Aemilius Victor.

EDCS-25800112.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Alfius Felix Flavianus, who lived 82 years and preserved his substance, acquired through excessive frugality, unimpaired until the day of his death, is buried here; having established this at the boundary of life, he distributed it to his children, considering their harmony, and satisfied his mind while still able, he provided for his freedmen, whom he had, with granted freedom. He equaled his daughter-in-law in affection, bestowed on both gold and silver, and assigned his own clothing with both hands, so that he might recommend himself as pleasing and dutiful to his deserving relatives; and he did much more, and never weakened in his life, lived 82 years, was called Felix, and lived happily with his family.
EDCS-25800112.summary: A complex funerary epitaph detailing the life and posthumous arrangements of Alfius Felix Flavianus, who lived 82 years and ensured his wealth was distributed to his family and freedmen.

EDCS-25800113.translation: Alfia Callipoda lived 70 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-25800113.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Alfia Callipoda.

EDCS-25800114.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Sextus Annius Felix lived 71 years; he is buried here.

EDCS-25900053.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the name Cornutius, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25900054.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Matia Saturnina lived 71 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-25900054.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Matia Saturnina, who lived 71 years and is buried here, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25900055.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Sallustius.
EDCS-25900055.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the name Sallustius, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25900056.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a "most dutiful sister" who lived 42 years, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25900059.translation: Pavia Pia lived 100 years and [some] months. She is buried here.
EDCS-25900059.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Pavia Pia, who lived 100 years and some months and is buried here, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25900060.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Vitalis.
EDCS-25900060.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the name Vitalis, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25900063.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Gaius Seius Donatus, dutiful, lived 67 years. He is buried here. 'I was not, I was, I am not; what is it to me?'
EDCS-25900063.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Gaius Seius Donatus, who lived 67 years, and includes a philosophical reflection on life and death.

EDCS-25900064.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulia Zaba, great priestess, lived 78 years.
EDCS-25900064.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Iulia Zaba, a 'great priestess,' who lived 78 years.

EDCS-25900065.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Sextus Palnius Valerianus lived 70 years and 3 months and 18 days. He is buried here.
EDCS-25900065.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Sextus Palnius Valerianus, recording his lifespan and burial.

EDCS-25900066.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the gods Sol, Jupiter, and Luna, possibly mentioning a person named Fortunata.

EDCS-25900067.translation: Berecbal, daughter of Faustus, dutiful, lived 25 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-25900067.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Berecbal, daughter of Faustus, who lived 25 years.

EDCS-25900068.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulia Rogata Celsina lived 81 years. She is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Cuminius Privatus lived 6 years. He is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Udio lived 7 years. He is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Baric NI S lived [---] years. He is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Cuminius Erogatianus lived 80 years. He is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulia Sabina lived 63 years. She is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Cuminius Rogatianus lived 31 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-25900068.summary: This is a complex funerary inscription recording the deaths and burials of multiple individuals from the Cuminius family and others, with varying lifespans.

EDCS-25900069.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Sittius Lucius lived 47 years. Sittia Gududia, Sittius Iulianus, Sittius Venerius, Sittia Fortunata, Sittius Possessor. He is buried here.
EDCS-25900069.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Sittius Lucius, who lived 47 years, and also lists other family members, indicating a family burial plot.

EDCS-25900070.translation: [I]lia Maiorica, dutiful, lived 85 years. She is buried here. Flavius Cududus, dutiful, lived 60 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-25900070.summary: This inscription contains two separate funerary epitaphs for Ilia Maiorica and Flavius Cududus, both recording their lifespans and burial.

EDCS-25900071.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Publius Crepius Papiria Rusticianus lived 20 years.
EDCS-25900071.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Publius Crepius Papiria Rusticianus, who lived 20 years.

EDCS-25900072.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Faustulus, dutiful, lived 2 years. He is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Caesia Casta lived 21 years.
EDCS-25900072.summary: This inscription contains two separate funerary epitaphs, one for a child named Faustulus who lived 2 years, and another for Caesia Casta who lived 21 years.

EDCS-25900073.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcus Marcius Felix lived 70 years and is buried here.
EDCS-25900073.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Marcus Marcius Felix, who lived to be 70 years old.

EDCS-25900075.translation: To Decimus Valerius, son of Decimus, of the Arnensian tribe; [dedicated to] Jupiter Optimus Maximus.
EDCS-25900075.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus for Decimus Valerius, son of Decimus.

EDCS-25900076.translation: Gallus IG NO TERBERI made this sacred offering to Gallus Augustus and fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-25900076.summary: This inscription records a votive offering made by Gallus to Gallus Augustus.

EDCS-25900077.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulius Felix lived 75 years.
EDCS-25900077.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Iulius Felix, who lived to be 75 years old.

EDCS-25900078.summary: This is a dedication to Emperor Augustus.

EDCS-25900079.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Cilius Gududio lived 71 years.
EDCS-25900079.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Cilius Gududio, who lived to be 71 years old.

EDCS-25900081.translation: Sacred to Neptune Augustus for the health of our Emperors and the entire divine house.
EDCS-25900081.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Neptune Augustus for the well-being of the imperial family.

EDCS-25900082.translation: [Child's name?] FI S PVLE, sweet one, lived 2 years and is buried here.
EDCS-25900082.summary: This is a funerary dedication for a child named [restored] who lived for 2 years.

EDCS-25900084.translation: Merulus lived in peace for 102 years, buried on the 10th day of February in the seventh indiction.
EDCS-25900084.summary: This funerary inscription records the long life and burial date of Merulus.

EDCS-25900085.translation: To Vinicus, according to my ability, as vowed. These are the things that I could do. Farewell.
EDCS-25900085.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by an unnamed individual to Vinicus.

EDCS-25900086.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Publius AIIIVS, dutiful, lived.
EDCS-25900086.summary: This is a funerary dedication to the Divine Shades by Publius AIIIVS.

EDCS-25900087.translation: To Honoratus, for his most holy mother.
EDCS-25900087.summary: This is a dedication to a mother by Honoratus.

EDCS-25900088.translation: Sacred to the August gods Jupiter, Saturn, Silvanus, Caelestis, Pluto, Minerva, and Venus. The district of Veneriensis, its patron Lucius Antonius Brittannus, its curators Publius Octavius Marcellus, Saturninus' priest Sextus Octavius Felix, Quintus Clodius Optatus, Quintus Vibius Saturninus, offered from among those listed below a ram, a lamb, a goat, two kids, and a hen. Caecilius Secundus [dedicated this].
EDCS-25900088.summary: This is a dedication to several deities by the pagus Veneriensis and its officials, with offerings listed, likely for a public cult.

EDCS-25900091.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Laronia Tertulla, dutiful, lived 50 years, is buried here. Sacred to the Divine Shades. Lucius Bennius Saturninus, dutiful, lived 60 years, is buried here.
EDCS-25900091.summary: This is a double funerary dedication to the Divine Shades for Laronia Tertulla and Lucius Bennius Saturninus.

EDCS-25900092.translation: Gaius Annius Hilario, son of Gaius Annius, lived 20 years, is buried here.
EDCS-25900092.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Gaius Annius Hilario.

EDCS-25900093.translation: Here Fortunata remains in eternal peace, and lived 70 years in god.
EDCS-25900093.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Fortunata, indicating a Christian context.

EDCS-25900094.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Ab On, dutiful, lived 1 year, is buried here.
EDCS-25900094.summary: This is a funerary dedication to the Divine Shades for Ab On, who died in infancy.

EDCS-25900095.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Fintera.

EDCS-25900096.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Mania.

EDCS-25900097.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Salvinus.

EDCS-25900098.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, Quintus Antonius Clemens Antullianus, prefect in his second term as quaestor, twice a duovir, perpetual priest, erected the bronze eagle with its base, which Antonius Clemens, his father, had promised because of the honor of his son Caius Antonius Clemens Antullianus becoming perpetual priest, from a doubled honorary sum, and he set it up with additional funds by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-25900098.summary: This is a dedication to Jupiter, set up by Quintus Antonius Clemens Antullianus, likely in the early 3rd century CE, commemorating his father's promise and his own priesthood.

EDCS-25900101.text_edition: \n Caius Iulius Quinti filius Felix Aurunculeianus aedilis ob honorem aedilitatis signum Marsyae quod ex HS IICCCCduobus milibus quadringentis nummum cum legitima summa taxaverat adiecta amplius pecunia posuit et dedicavit decreto decurionum idemque primus ludos dedit\n
EDCS-25900101.translation: Gaius Julius Felix Aurunculeianus, son of Quintus, as aedile, for the honor of his aedileship, has placed and dedicated the statue of Marsyas, which he had valued at 2400 sesterces with the legal sum, adding more money from his own funds, and he himself was the first to present games.
EDCS-25900101.summary: This inscription records Gaius Julius Felix Aurunculeianus, as an aedile, dedicating a statue of Marsyas and presenting games at his own expense, likely in the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-25900106.translation: Marcus Valerius Quadratus, son of Marcus, of the Quirina tribe, served as the decemvir for judging lawsuits, tribune of the soldiers of the III Augusta legion, and quaestor designate, and erected this to Emperor Caesar Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Pius, son of the deified Hadrian, grandson of the deified Trajan Parthicus, great-grandson of the deified Nerva, consul for the second time, censor, father of the fatherland, the best of princes, because of his singular indulgence towards him.
EDCS-25900106.summary: This is a dedication to Emperor Antoninus Pius, erected by Marcus Valerius Quadratus, likely during the reign of Antoninus Pius (138-161 CE), honoring the emperor for his favor.

EDCS-25900107.translation: To the deified Empress Aurelia Galeria Lucilla, wife of Emperor Caesar Lucius Aurelius Verus Augustus, Armenian, Parthian the Great, the Physician.
EDCS-25900107.summary: This is a dedication to the deified Empress Lucilla, wife of Lucius Verus, likely from the late 2nd century CE.

EDCS-25900109.translation: To Julia Augusta, wife of Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus, Arabicus, Adiabenicus, pontifex maximus, holding tribunician power for the seventh time, emperor for the eighth time, consul for the second time, father of the fatherland, mother of the most sacred prince Marcus Aurelius Antoninus, daughter of the deified Marcus Antoninus Pius Germanicus Sarmaticus, brother of the deified Commodus, grandson of the deified Antoninus Pius, great-grandson of the deified Hadrian, great-great-grandson of the deified Trajan Parthicus, great-great-great-grandson of the deified Nerva.
EDCS-25900109.summary: This is a dedication to Julia Domna, wife of Septimius Severus, likely from the period of Severus' reign (193-211 CE), detailing her extensive imperial lineage.

EDCS-25900110.translation: To Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Caesar, designated emperor, prince of youth.
EDCS-25900110.summary: This is an honorific inscription for Marcus Aurelius Antoninus (later Emperor Marcus Aurelius), likely from his time as Caesar and co-emperor with Antoninus Pius, before 161 CE.

EDCS-25900113.translation: To Quintus Servilius Pudens, most distinguished man.
EDCS-25900113.summary: This is an honorific inscription for Quintus Servilius Pudens, a prominent individual, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-25900115.translation: Attidius Aster dedicated for 50,000 sesterces or more to the Vallo of the area.
EDCS-25900115.summary: This inscription records a dedication of a sum of money by Attidius Aster for a specific area, possibly related to a boundary or fortification, dated to the Imperial period.

EDCS-25900122.translation: Priest, lived 32 years and 3 months. Sextia Eucarpia, his mother, made this for her deserving son. He is buried here.
EDCS-25900122.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for a priest who died young, erected by his mother, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-25900123.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Antistes Laetilius Victor, who died in his youthful age, with diligent hands, placed these four fingers, a dutiful boy, lived [X] years. He is buried here.
EDCS-25900123.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Laetilius Victor, who died young, with a dedication from himself or for himself, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-25900124.summary: This is a very brief inscription, possibly the name or description of a boat or a ferry service, from an unknown date.

EDCS-25900128.summary: This is likely a metrical inscription or a name association for a ship, possibly related to the horse-transporting vessel of Icarus Ferox and a person named Cupido.

EDCS-25900129.summary: This inscription identifies a ship named Portisculus, functioning as a sailing vessel.

EDCS-25900133.summary: This fragmentary inscription appears to record a command related to a patron.

EDCS-25900135.summary: This inscription names a measure, likely for grain, as Musculus, a bushel.

EDCS-25900137.translation: Others that a swift boat be of use, another LEN A...
EDCS-25900137.summary: This inscription discusses the utility of a swift boat, with some words possibly referring to a specific type or brand.

EDCS-25900140.translation: Vegeia Advena, how gently the wave carries Vegeia

EDCS-25900141.summary: This inscription seems to name a vessel or cargo 'Placida' (calm/gentle), perhaps referring to a burden associated with someone or something named LAIA.

EDCS-25900144.summary: This inscription records a military action where a legion transported something across a river or stream.

EDCS-25900149.summary: This inscription seems to refer to a person named Apaiona, possibly of the Liburnian people.

EDCS-25900150.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Marcus Aemilius Trofimus lived 95 years; he is buried here.

EDCS-25900151.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Arsima the pious lived 35 years; he is buried here.

EDCS-25900154.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Calliope the pious lived 34 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-25900154.summary: This epitaph records the death of Calliope the pious, who lived 34 years and is buried here.

EDCS-25900155.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Fabia Dativa lived 25 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-25900155.summary: This funerary inscription marks the burial place of Fabia Dativa, who lived for 25 years.

EDCS-25900156.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Fortunatus lived...
EDCS-25900156.summary: This incomplete funerary inscription begins by dedicating the site to the spirits of the departed and mentions the name Fortunatus.

EDCS-25900157.translation: Quintus Helvius Corona the pious lived 24 years.
EDCS-25900157.summary: This epitaph records the life of Quintus Helvius Corona, who died at the age of 24.

EDCS-25900158.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Gaius Julius Victor, dutiful, lived for 34 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-25900158.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the death of Gaius Julius Victor, who lived for 34 years.

EDCS-25900159.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Iulia Catula, dutiful.
EDCS-25900159.summary: This is a tombstone inscription dedicating the place to the spirits of the departed for Iulia Catula.

EDCS-25900160.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Qiariovohn Maximus Aiodimius Y.
EDCS-25900160.summary: This is a tombstone inscription dedicating the place to the spirits of the departed for Qiariovohn Maximus Aiodimius Y.

EDCS-25900161.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Munatius Romanus lived for 3 years, 10 months, and 3 days; he is buried here.
EDCS-25900161.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the death of Munatius Romanus, who lived for 3 years, 10 months, and 3 days.

EDCS-25900162.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Ponponius Crementius lived for 14 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-25900162.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the death of Ponponius Crementius, who lived for 14 years.

EDCS-25900163.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Gaius Rurius Victoricus lived for 27 years more or less. To the spirits of the departed. Helvia Victoria lived for 80 years; she is buried here.

EDCS-25900164.translation: Secundinus, dutiful, lived for 91 years; he is buried here.

EDCS-25900165.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Sempronius Fortunatus, dutiful, lived for 71 years; he is buried here.

EDCS-25900166.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Quintus Silvius Felix, son of Silvius, dutiful, lived for 13 years and 5 months; he is buried here.

EDCS-25900167.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Publius Valerius Surus, dutiful, lived for 65 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-25900167.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the death of Publius Valerius Surus, who lived for 65 years.

EDCS-25900168.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Venustus, dutiful, lived 54 years; he is buried here.

EDCS-25900172.translation: Navimni, son of P. Murinus, lived 90 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-25900172.summary: A tombstone recording the death and burial of Navimni, who lived 90 years.

EDCS-25900174.translation: Clotsianus, sweet one, lived 70 years, 2 months, and 11 days in peace.

EDCS-25900175.translation: Florida, faithful one, may she rest.

EDCS-25900176.summary: A fragment of an inscription likely recording the name of a deceased person who rested in peace.

EDCS-25900177.translation: to the supreme pontiff, father of the fatherland, through the urging of Macrinus Sossianus, a most distinguished man, the legate.

EDCS-25900179.translation: Donatus, curator of the public affairs of Citium, erected this aqueduct, raising devoted spirits and stimulating them towards the dominion of our lords, after the completion of many works.

EDCS-25900180.translation: [...]ris, son of Barihis, lived 35 years; he is here buried.

EDCS-25900182.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Aelius Barihcottae, dutiful, lived 59 years; he is buried here.

EDCS-25900183.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Clodius Ninus, father, lived 70 years. He is buried here.

EDCS-25900184.translation: Felix lived 75 years. Sacred to the Divine Spirits.

EDCS-25900186.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Cecud lived 62 years.

EDCS-25900187.summary: A funerary epitaph for two individuals, Cladia Miccin (aged 1 year) and Cladius Silvanus (aged 61 years).

EDCS-25900188.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Luccassius lived 57 years.

EDCS-25900189.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Iulia Satura lived [X] years.

EDCS-25900192.summary: A dedication to the divine personification of Victory Augusta.

EDCS-25900194.translation: Of Germanicus Sarmaticus, father of the fatherland and of the whole divine house, [in the year] of the consul Iono Felix.

EDCS-25900198.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Coelia Secura, pious, lived 60 years. She is buried here. [Dedicated by] Felix Victorinus Silvanus to his most beloved mother. EDCS-25900199.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Duda lived 84 years. In peace.

EDCS-25900200.translation: Faustus, son of Stiabus, lived 100 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-25900200.summary: This is a tomb inscription for Faustus, recording his name, parentage, and age at death.

EDCS-25900201.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Iulius Privatus lived 15 years. He is buried here. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Iulia Donata lived 12 years. She is buried here.

EDCS-25900202.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Iulia Fortunata, the dutiful, lived 40 years. She set this up for her wife and children.

EDCS-25900203.translation: Macrina lived 36 years. She is buried here.

EDCS-25900204.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Marcella, daughter of Publius Marcia, lived 60 years. May your bones rest well. She is buried here.

EDCS-25900205.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Papinia Ciaventilla lived 33 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-25900205.summary: This tomb inscription records the lifespan and burial of Papinia Ciaventilla.

EDCS-25900206.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Lucius Tonnelius Fortis, son of Marcu, the dutiful, lived 3 years. He is buried here.

EDCS-25900207.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Marcus Tonnetius Restitutus, the dutiful, lived 11 years. He is buried here.

EDCS-25900228.translation: Geilamir, king of the Vandals and Alans.

EDCS-25900229.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Abbod Nim Pag, the dutiful, lived [---] years. She is buried here.

EDCS-25900233.text_edition: \n At deas Caelestes argenteas fabricandas II ex HS milibus nummum quae Aburnius Avillius Felix testamento suo ab heredibus suis praestari voluit rei publicae dederunt templum deae Caelestis Augustae, ex pollicitatione Gabini Rufi patris ob honorem flamonii perpetui itemque Iuliae Gallitae matris ex HS LX milibus nummum coeptum est inlatis quoque rei publicae Thuggensium ante diem dedicationis HS XXX milibus nummum die dedicationis rei publicae numeratis ex testamento Avilliae filiae Venustae ex quorum reditu sportulae et ludi praestentur Quintus Gabinius Rufus Felix Beatianus multiplicata a se pecunia ob honorem parentum suorum HS milibus nummum ad ornamentum patriae suae sua liberalitate constitutis perfecit excoluit et cum statuis ceterisque solo privato dedicavit ludis editis datis sportulis et epulo et gymnasio\n
EDCS-25900233.translation: To the goddesses, silver statues of whom are to be made for 10,000 sesterces, which Aburnius Avillius Felix wished to be provided by his heirs in his will, the Republic gave. The temple of the goddess Caelestis Augusta was begun from the promise of Gabinius Rufus Felix Beatianus, father, for the honor of his perpetual priesthood, and similarly from that of Julia Gallita, mother, for 60,000 sesterces. Furthermore, 30,000 sesterces were paid to the Republic of Thugga before the dedication day, from the will of Avillia Venusta, daughter. From the income of these, distributions and games are to be provided. Quintus Gabinius Rufus Felix Beatianus, having multiplied the money for the honor of his parents, established, perfected, and adorned it with statues and other items on private land, dedicating it with games presented, distributions given, a feast, and a gymnasium.
EDCS-25900233.summary: This complex inscription details a series of dedications and constructions in Thugga, involving multiple generations of the Gabinius and Avillius families, related to religious honors and public amenities, likely spanning the late 2nd to 3rd century CE.

EDCS-26001061.translation: Sacred to the Genius of Tibar, the republic of the people of Tibar dedicated this gift.
EDCS-26001061.summary: This inscription records a gift from the republic of Tibar to the Genius of Tibar, likely a public dedication.

EDCS-26001065.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Quintus Iulius Aerondo, son of Lucius, dutiful, lived 21 years, is buried here.
EDCS-26001065.summary: This is a tomb inscription for Quintus Iulius Aerondo, recording his name, parentage, filial piety, age at death, and burial.

EDCS-26001066.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Nonia Octavia, dutiful, lived 75 years, is buried here.
EDCS-26001066.summary: This is a tomb inscription for Nonia Octavia, recording her name, filial piety, age at death, and burial.

EDCS-26001067.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Octavia Honorata, dutiful, lived 75 years, is buried here. May your bones rest well, may the earth be light upon you.
EDCS-26001067.summary: This is a tomb inscription for Octavia Honorata, including standard funerary blessings and recording her age at death.

EDCS-26001068.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Perp Veri, dutiful, lived 9 years, is buried here.
EDCS-26001068.summary: This is a tomb inscription for Perp Veri, recording his name, filial piety, age at death, and burial.

EDCS-26001069.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Caius Propertius Optatus, dutiful, lived 25 years, is buried here.
EDCS-26001069.summary: This is a tomb inscription for Caius Propertius Optatus, recording his name, filial piety, age at death, and burial.

EDCS-26001070.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Lucius Silicius Arnensi Honoratus, dutiful, lived 65 years, and Manlia Fortunata, wife of Claudius, dutiful, lived 51 years, are buried here. May your bones rest well, may the earth be light upon you. Tiberius Claudius Honoratus.
EDCS-26001070.summary: This is a joint tomb inscription for Lucius Silicius Honoratus and Manlia Fortunata, recording their ages at death, burial, and a funerary blessing, possibly erected by Tiberius Claudius Honoratus.

EDCS-26001071.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Publius Percennius Rogatus, son of Quintus Arnensi, dutiful, lived 51 years, 10 years after the dedication of the altar.
EDCS-26001071.summary: This inscription records the lifespan of Publius Percennius Rogatus, noting his age at death and a specific event related to an altar's dedication.

EDCS-26001074.translation: Sacred to the Augustan Empress. Gaius Pacuvius Felix, son of Gaius, made and dedicated this at his own expense, in his own name and that of his wife Tullia Primula.
EDCS-26001074.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a sacred monument to the divine Augusta (likely a member of the imperial family) by Gaius Pacuvius Felix for himself and his wife, dating possibly to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-26001076.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Lucius Domitius Aurelianus, Pius, Felix, Augustus, pontiff, holder of tribunician power, father of the country, proconsul. The republic of the colony Mariana Augusta Alexandriana of the Uchitani Majores, devoted to his divine majesty and authority, by decree of the decurions, at public expense.
EDCS-26001076.summary: This is a public dedication to Emperor Aurelian by the colony of Mariana Augusta Alexandriana of the Uchitani Majores, detailing his titles and the means of funding.

EDCS-26001077.translation: To the Lord of the Triumph of Liberty and our Rescuer through his invincible labors, for the welfare of private citizens and the public, the state of the devoted colony of Uchitanorum Maiorum dedicates this eternally to Lucius Flavius Valerius Constantinus, perpetual Augustus, to his divine majesty.
EDCS-26001077.summary: This inscription is a formal dedication by the colony of Uchitanorum Maiorum to Emperor Constantine, praising him as a deliverer and worshipping his divine authority, likely dating to the 4th century CE.

EDCS-26001078.translation: To our lords, Flavius Valens, victorious and triumphant, always Augustus. The republic of the colony of the Uchitani Majores, devoted.
EDCS-26001078.summary: This inscription is a dedication from the republic of the Uchitani Majores to the emperors Valentinian and Valens, expressing their devotion.

EDCS-26001079.translation: Sextus Pullaienus Florus Caecilianus made this at his own expense and gave it as a gift to the Greater Uchitani, with our Lords Valentinian and Theodosius, the greatest emperors, being well, with Furius Victorinus, perpetual flamen, supported by ancestral honor, being superior in this liberality.
EDCS-26001079.summary: This inscription records a public work funded by Sextus Pullaienus Florus Caecilianus and dedicated to the community of the Greater Uchitani, dating to the reign of Valentinian and Theodosius.

EDCS-26001081.translation: By decree of the town council, the Republic of the colony of Mariana Augusta Alexandriana of the Greater Uchitani, out of public funds, [dedicated this] to Lucius Marcius Honoratus Fabianus, of equestrian rank, a man of honorable memory, a citizen and patron.
EDCS-26001081.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by the town council of the colony of Mariana Augusta Alexandriana of the Greater Uchitani to Lucius Marcius Honoratus Fabianus, a distinguished citizen and patron.

EDCS-26001084.summary: This is a simple funerary inscription identifying the deceased as Antonius Rogatus.

EDCS-26001088.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Aedilius Felix, dutiful, lived for six years, is buried here.

EDCS-26001089.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Sextus Manlius Fortunatus pius vixit annos LXXI hic situs est\n
EDCS-26001089.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Dead. Sextus Manlius Fortunatus, dutiful, lived for 71 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-26001089.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the name, piety, age, and burial place of Sextus Manlius Fortunatus, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-26001090.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Quintus Numisius, son of Caius, of the Arnensian tribe, Copo Helvacianus, dutiful, lived for 14 years, is buried here.

EDCS-26001091.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Arius Poponius, dutiful, lived for 73 years, is buried here.

EDCS-26001092.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Geminia, daughter of Lucius, Carcelina, lived for 36 years, is buried here.
EDCS-26001092.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the death and burial of Geminia Carcelina at the age of 36.

EDCS-26001093.translation: To Hercules Augustus, the Genius of the fatherland. Lucius Valerius Maximus, son of Valerius Faustinus, in honor of his son Faustinus, having promised a sum of money for the adornment of the work which he had undertaken in his honor, erected a statue of Hercules at his own expense and dedicated it. Likewise, Publius Valerius, at his own expense, fulfilled his promise for the honor of Lucius Valerius Faustinus, his son.
EDCS-26001093.summary: This is a dedication of a statue of Hercules erected by Lucius Valerius Maximus and Publius Valerius in honor of Lucius Valerius Faustinus, likely an official or significant family member.

EDCS-26001095.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Antonia Saturnina lived 13 years; she is buried here.

EDCS-26001096.translation: Dabar, son of Ortinis, lived 75 years; he is buried here.

EDCS-26001099.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Iunia Victoria, daughter of Quintus, also known as Libosa, lived 27 years; she is buried here. May your bones rest well.

EDCS-26001101.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcus Oppius.
EDCS-26001101.summary: This is a tomb inscription for Marcus Oppius.

EDCS-26001102.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Publius Oppius lived 15 years; he is buried here.

EDCS-26001104.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Sutoria Lucilla, dutiful, lived 71 years. She is buried here.

EDCS-26001105.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Sutoria Saturnina, dutiful, lived 13 years. She is buried here.

EDCS-26001106.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Gaius Valerius, son of Lucius, of the Arnensian tribe, lived 112 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-26001106.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Gaius Valerius, who lived to be 112 years old.

EDCS-26100002.translation: To our lord Marcus Flavius Valerius Constantius, most noble Caesar, the state of the municipality of Aunobaritanum is devoted to his divine majesty.
EDCS-26100002.summary: This is a dedication from the municipality of Aunobaritanum to the Caesar Marcus Flavius Valerius Constantius.

EDCS-26100003.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Octavia Prima, dutiful, lived 75 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-26100003.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Octavia Prima, who lived to be 75 years old.

EDCS-26100004.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Titus Raecius Severus, dutiful, lived 90 years. Behold, how many temples of the gods you frequented; now your glorious piety is evident, Severus. You lived your life, filling it with goodness. Healthy in limbs, with eyes and body sound, now you tread the Elysian fields and the green grass, scattered with flowers, you lie on the meadows. Nor less do you enjoy the groves, as long as your fame endures. Therefore, farewell, laden with much good piety. Your grandson Victor has dedicated these verses to you, holy one, and has offered these gifts, which I have sent to your tomb and consecrated. He is buried here. The Dutiful.
EDCS-26100004.summary: This is an elaborate funerary epitaph for Titus Raecius Severus, who lived 90 years, detailing his piety and a posthumous dedication from his grandson.

EDCS-26100005.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Lucius Instanius, son of Lucius, of the Arnensian tribe, Fortunatus Fidelianus, dutiful, lived 93 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-26100005.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Instanius Fortunatus Fidelianus, who lived to be 93 years old.

EDCS-26100008.translation: To the dutiful wife of Felix, granddaughter of the emperor Divus Antoninus Pius, daughter of Marcus Aurelius Caesar, by decree of the decurions, at public expense.
EDCS-26100008.summary: This monument was erected by public expense, by decree of the decurions, in honor of the wife of Felix, granddaughter of Antoninus Pius and daughter of Marcus Aurelius Caesar.

EDCS-26100013.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Gnaeus Cornelius Datus, decurion, priest of Ceres, treasurer, aedile, prefect with judicial authority in place of a duovir, a good man, dutiful, lived 52 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-26100013.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Gnaeus Cornelius Datus, who held numerous civic and religious offices and lived to be 52 years old.

EDCS-26100014.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Quintus Cossutius Fortunatianus, son of Lucius, public priest, dutiful, lived 70 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-26100014.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Quintus Cossutius Fortunatianus, a public priest, who lived to be 70 years old.

EDCS-26100015.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Lucius Fabius, son of Lucius, Cornelia Felix, decurion of the municipium of Mustitani, pious, lived 20 years, 4 months, 1 day. Is buried here.
EDCS-26100015.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Lucius Fabius Felix, a decurion, who died at the age of 20 years, 4 months, and 1 day.

EDCS-26100016.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Iulia Spica, daughter of Marcius, most chaste and pious, lived 87 years. Is buried here. To the spirits of the departed. Lucius Fabius Fortunatus, son of Lucius, Cornelia, decurion of the municipium of Mustitani, flamen, aedile, quaestor, pious, lived 30 years. Is buried here.
EDCS-26100016.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for two individuals, Iulia Spica and Lucius Fabius Fortunatus, who held various civic and religious offices.

EDCS-26100017.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Quintus Iulius Tertius Urbanus, father of all fasces and perpetual flamen, patron of the Cerealium, pious, lived 88 years. Is buried here.
EDCS-26100017.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Quintus Iulius Tertius Urbanus, who held significant religious and civic roles.

EDCS-26100018.summary: This is a very brief inscription identifying Iustinus as a priest of the Cerealium.

EDCS-26100019.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Marcus Marius Felix Obellianus, duumvir quinquennalis designated, pious, lived 59 years. Is buried here.
EDCS-26100019.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Marcus Marius Felix Obellianus, who was designated as a quinquennial duumvir.

EDCS-26100020.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Cornelia Bonifatia Callosina, daughter of Lucius, pious, lived 85 years. Is buried here. To the spirits of the departed. Sextus Sempronius Saturninus, decurion, flamen, aedile, pious, lived 95 years. Is buried here. To the spirits of the departed. Sempronia Ia lia, pious, lived 1 year, 1 month. Is buried here.
EDCS-26100020.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for three individuals: Cornelia Bonifatia Callosina, Sextus Sempronius Saturninus (a decurion, flamen, and aedile), and Sempronia Ia lia.

EDCS-26100021.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Caelia Bonosa Mazica, midwife, wife, most chaste and modest, lived 42 years, 3 months. Is buried here. To the spirits of the departed. Publius Flavius, son of Publius, Cornelia Felix, pious, lived 75 years, 6 months. Is buried here.
EDCS-26100021.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for two individuals, Caelia Bonosa Mazica, a midwife, and Publius Flavius Felix.

EDCS-26100022.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Victor verna, steward, pious, lived 46 years. Is buried here.
EDCS-26100022.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Victor verna, a steward, who died at the age of 46.

EDCS-26100023.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Iulia Castula Arraniana, pious, lived 72 years. Is buried here. To the spirits of the departed. Lucius Aninius Potitianus, son of Marcius, Cornelia Felix, pious, lived 91 years. Is buried here.
EDCS-26100023.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for two individuals, Iulia Castula Arraniana and Lucius Aninius Potitianus.

EDCS-26100024.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Aninia Secunda Quieta, pious, lived 31 years. To the spirits of the departed. Lucius M. Barcio, pious, lived 90 years. Is buried here.
EDCS-26100024.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for two individuals, Aninia Secunda Quieta and Lucius M. Barcio.

EDCS-26100025.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Gaius Avianius Victoricus, a most ingenious man, who surpassed others in skill and talent, lived piously for 38 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-26100025.summary: A funerary epitaph for Gaius Avianius Victoricus, a man praised for his ingenuity and skill, who died at age 38.

EDCS-26100026.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Quintus Caecilius Hyacinius lived piously for 70 years; he is buried here. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Quintus Caecilius Cocceius lived piously for 45 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-26100026.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the deaths and burial places of two individuals, Quintus Caecilius Hyacinius and Quintus Caecilius Cocceius.

EDCS-26100027.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Gaius CaeIsanius Nampamo lived piously for 96 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-26100027.summary: A funerary epitaph for Gaius CaeIsanius Nampamo, who died at age 96.

EDCS-26100028.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the spirits of the departed. Gaius Caivenius Saturninus lived piously for 91 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-26100028.summary: A funerary epitaph for Gaius Caivenius Saturninus, who died at age 91.

EDCS-26100029.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Lucius Cominius Vincentius lived piously for 43 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-26100029.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lucius Cominius Vincentius, who died at age 43.

EDCS-26100030.summary: A fragmentary inscription that appears to be the beginning of a name, possibly Publius Cornelius.

EDCS-26100031.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Gaius Cornelius Privatianus lived piously for 35 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-26100031.summary: A funerary epitaph for Gaius Cornelius Privatianus, who died at age 35.

EDCS-26100032.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Quintus Cossutius Homullus lived piously for 20 years; he is buried here. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Pompeia Africana lived piously for 71 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-26100032.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the deaths and burial places of Quintus Cossutius Homullus (age 20) and Pompeia Africana (age 71).

EDCS-26100033.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Firma lived piously for 20 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-26100033.summary: A funerary epitaph for Firma, who died at age 20.

EDCS-26100034.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Fuxida lived piously for 7 years. Flavius, the priest, [dedicated] a table to his well-deserving wife.

EDCS-26100035.translation: Thyce the pious lived 32 years; she rests here.
EDCS-26100035.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Thyce, recording her name, piety, age at death, and burial.

EDCS-26100036.translation: Aulus Iulius Bonifatius the pious lived 45 years; he rests here.
EDCS-26100036.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Aulus Iulius Bonifatius, recording his name, piety, age at death, and burial.

EDCS-26100037.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Iulia Ampliata the pious lived 88 years; she rests here. Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Lucius Iulius Felix the pious lived...
EDCS-26100037.summary: This funerary inscription records the death and burial of Iulia Ampliata and begins recording the details for Lucius Iulius Felix, who died at an unspecified age.

EDCS-26100038.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Caius Iulius Restutus Tustlianus, a man endowed with all praise and innocence, the pious, lived 40 years, 6 months; he rests here.
EDCS-26100038.summary: This funerary epitaph records the death and burial of Caius Iulius Restutus Tustlianus, highlighting his virtues and his age at death.

EDCS-26100039.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Caecilia Victoria, daughter of Caius, the pious, lived 52 years; she rests here. Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Lucius Iunius Rogatianus the pious lived 71 years.
EDCS-26100039.summary: This funerary inscription records the death and burial of Caecilia Victoria and begins recording the details for Lucius Iunius Rogatianus, who died at an unspecified age.

EDCS-26100040.translation: Lucius Iulius Victor the pious lived 22 years.
EDCS-26100040.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Iulius Victor, recording his name, piety, and age at death.

EDCS-26100041.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Lucillia Felicula the pious lived 71 years; she rests here.
EDCS-26100041.summary: This funerary epitaph records the death and burial of Lucillia Felicula, noting her piety and age at death.

EDCS-26100042.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Marcia Hilara the pious lived 77 years.
EDCS-26100042.summary: This funerary epitaph records the death of Marcia Hilara, noting her piety and age.

EDCS-26100043.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Sextilia Secundina the pious lived 69 years; she rests here. Marcus Memmius Romanus the pious lived 87 years; he rests here.
EDCS-26100043.summary: This funerary inscription records the death and burial of Sextilia Secundina and Marcus Memmius Romanus, noting their piety and ages at death.

EDCS-26100044.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Terentia Processa the pious lived 55 years; she rests here. Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Marcus Metilius Cornelia Crecinus, son of Marcus, the pious, lived 54 years, 8 months; he rests here.
EDCS-26100044.summary: This funerary inscription records the death and burial of Terentia Processa and Marcus Metilius Cornelia Crecinus, noting their piety and ages at death.

EDCS-26100045.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Marcus Metilius Crecinus, dutiful, lived 41 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-26100045.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcus Metilius Crecinus, recording his age at death and burial location.

EDCS-26100046.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Muttihunbal, son of Pastor, dutiful, lived 70 years.
EDCS-26100046.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Muttihunbal, son of Pastor, recording his age at death.

EDCS-26200196.translation: Licinia Seveara, daughter of Licinius Paternus, a splendid and praiseworthy man, who died today. When asked what, and by whom, it would be pleasing to do in her memory and for the consolation of her father, Lucius Calpurnius Maximus Albinus voted, 'It is decreed as written below: Since the moderation of life and the greatest and most practical testimony of character of Licinius Paternus, a man among our leading citizens, shine forth not only in fostering the resources of our state but also in the exceptional and outstanding generosity of his parents and ancestors, both in building and embellishing our city walls and in supporting and maintaining our citizens, and because of this, although our consolations to him may be small in the face of his immense grief, nevertheless, in order to alleviate and restrain the impulses of his sorrow and to honor the memory of this young girl who was snatched away by a sad misfortune, it is fitting that a most beautiful statue be erected at public expense for the same Licinia Seveara in the most frequented public place, so that it may perpetually attest to the affection of our order towards Paternus.'
EDCS-26200196.summary: A decree by the decurions to erect a statue of Licinia Seveara at public expense to honor her and console her grieving father, Licinius Paternus, praising Paternus's civic contributions and character.

EDCS-26200197.translation: To Valerius Romanus, a man of the highest distinction, curator of the state of the most splendid colony of Siccenses, and [to] Venus, for his remarkable goodness and integrity, because he restored the statue of the goddess which had long before been damaged by robbers and removed due to the damaged state of the temple. They set up a statue of Venus to perpetuate his memory through all ages, [erected by] his loyal client out of affection.
EDCS-26200197.summary: An inscription dedicated to Valerius Romanus, curator of the colony of Siccenses, and to Venus, praising Romanus for restoring a statue of Venus that had been damaged by robbers and erected by his client.

EDCS-26200244.translation: Antonia Bellosa lived 11 years; she is placed here.
EDCS-26200244.summary: A funerary epitaph for the young Antonia Bellosa, recording her age at death.

EDCS-26200245.translation: Antonia Iulla the dutiful lived 72 years; she is placed here.
EDCS-26200245.summary: A funerary epitaph for Antonia Iulla, recording her age at death.

EDCS-26200246.translation: Appia Maxima lived 77 years; she is placed here.

EDCS-26200247.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Apileia.
EDCS-26200247.summary: A funerary dedication to the departed spirits, with the name Apileia, likely part of a tomb inscription.

EDCS-26200248.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Apuleia Liciniana, daughter of Lucius, from Ammaedara, dutiful, lived 35 years, 6 months, and 16 days; she is placed here. This is her house.
EDCS-26200248.summary: A funerary epitaph for Apuleia Liciniana from Ammaedara, detailing her lifespan and indicating it is her tomb.

EDCS-26200249.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Attia Venusta, daughter of Quintus, lived 25 years; she is placed here.

EDCS-26200251.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Lucius Aufidius Victor lived 91 years; he is placed here.

EDCS-26200252.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Caius Avianus Agricola the dutiful lived 15 years.

EDCS-26200253.summary: A funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Avilia Secura.

EDCS-26200255.translation: Quintus Aurelius Optatus lived 28 years; he is buried here. Aurelius Fortunatus lived 25 years; brothers.

EDCS-26200259.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Baricca, son of Rogatus, slave of Venus, pious, lived 25 years.

EDCS-26200269.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Antonia Rogata, a dutiful woman, lived 67 years; she is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Gaius Caninius Fuscus, a dutiful man, lived 71 years; he is buried here.
