EDCS-26300050.summary: This is a dedication by the citizens of Tipasa to Quintus Geminius Severinus, honoring him for his love of the state, and identifies his father and tribal affiliation.

EDCS-26300052.translation: To Lucius Saedius Octavius Felix, a veteran, quinquennalis, and husband of Octavia Africana, from his father.
EDCS-26300052.summary: This inscription is a dedication by a father to his son, Lucius Saedius Octavius Felix, noting his veteran status and his role as a quinquennalis and husband.

EDCS-26300053.translation: On these estates of Marcus Hortensius Gaudentis and his sons, Gaudentiis. Restitutus. Province 239.
EDCS-26300053.summary: This inscription seems to record property ownership or a transaction related to the estates of Marcus Hortensius Gaudentis and his sons, with a reference to a province or date, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-26300055.translation: To the good spirits, from Marcus Hortensius Volocas and his sons.
EDCS-26300055.summary: This inscription is a dedication to 'good spirits' (Bonis) by Marcus Hortensius Volocas and his sons, likely a private dedication for well-being.

EDCS-26300064.translation: Lucius Cos, son of Lucius, placed [this].
EDCS-26300064.summary: This is a simple dedication by Lucius Cos, son of Lucius, indicating he erected this monument or object.

EDCS-26300066.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: Publius Claud Secundus.
EDCS-26300066.summary: This is a funerary dedication to the deceased Secundus, identified as Publius Claud.

EDCS-26300067.summary: This inscription is too fragmentary to provide any meaningful information.

EDCS-26300068.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: Statia Secunda made this for her most devoted sister Statia Datae. She lived 25 years and [some months].
EDCS-26300068.summary: This funerary monument records the death of Statia Datae, who lived 25 years, and was erected by her sister Statia Secunda.

EDCS-26300069.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: Turpilia Servanda lived 24 years.
EDCS-26300069.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Turpilia Servanda, who lived 24 years.

EDCS-26300070.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Gaius Julius Saturninus, identified as a dearest father, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-26300303.translation: Of Iuventus, who was also called Efractor.
EDCS-26300303.summary: This inscription likely records the name and possibly an agnomen or nickname of an individual.

EDCS-26300307.translation: To his most devoted father: Caesia Quartina [dedicated this to] Gaius Caesius Fronto, perpetual priest.

EDCS-26400643.translation: Sicea, the maker of a work, from the house of...

EDCS-26400644.translation: Ianus, a most perfect man, governor of the province...
EDCS-26400644.summary: This inscription records the name and high provincial office of a man named Ianus.

EDCS-26400646.translation: Me Mode Cu, with her husband...
EDCS-26400646.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription, likely a dedication or epitaph mentioning two individuals, 'Me Mode Cu' and her husband.

EDCS-26400650.translation: To Lucius Egnatuleius Sabinus, son of Publius, of the Galeria tribe, pontiff of the Palatual College, procurator of the Emperor for the Revenue Office of Gallia, procurator of the Emperor for the strategos of the Thebaid, procurator of the Emperor for the collection of taxes in Macedonia, prefect of the Cinithian people, tribune of the IV Scythica Legion, [flamen of the] Emperor of the colony of Thysdritis. Egnatuleia Sabina, daughter of Publius. Lucius Egnatuleius Sabinus [son of...]
EDCS-26400650.summary: This is a complex funerary inscription honouring Lucius Egnatuleius Sabinus and his family members, listing his extensive imperial administrative and military career across various provinces, likely dating to the late 2nd or early 3rd century CE.

EDCS-26400651.translation: To Gaius Julius Laetitus, enrolled in the squadrons of Roman knights by the Emperors Caesar Antoninus and Verus Augusti, as a four-man commissioner for Sabine districts, enrolled in the number of the Laurentes Lavinates priests, [as] patron.
EDCS-26400651.summary: This inscription honors Gaius Julius Laetitus, detailing his military and civic appointments under Emperors Antoninus and Verus.

EDCS-26400653.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Aurelius Maximianus lived 51 years, 8 months, 22 days. His dearest wife made [this] for her most rare husband.
EDCS-26400653.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Aurelius Maximianus and indicating it was erected by his wife.

EDCS-26400654.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. To Iulius Vitalianus. His dearest brother and sister made [this] for Virentius.
EDCS-26400654.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated to Iulius Vitalianus by his loving siblings.

EDCS-26400655.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Terentia Celetina lived 5 years and 5 months and some days. Tecusa made [this].
EDCS-26400655.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a young girl named Terentia Celetina, likely erected by Tecusa.

EDCS-26400656.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Hermas lived 11 years.
EDCS-26400656.summary: This is a brief funerary inscription recording the short life of Hermas.

EDCS-26400657.translation: ...tina lies here. She lived 39 years. Her parents made [this] for their daughter.
EDCS-26400657.summary: This funerary epitaph records the life of a woman named ...tina, erected by her parents.

EDCS-26400659.translation: Seqda in the peace of Christ. As in the peace of Christ.
EDCS-26400659.summary: This inscription, using Christian terminology, likely marks a burial place or commemorates individuals within a Christian community.

EDCS-26400663.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Flavius Apollonis Sacap, aged 90 years. Pious.
EDCS-26400663.summary: A funerary inscription for Flavius Apollonis Sacap, who lived to be 90 years old.

EDCS-26400664.translation: To the most illustrious man, the proconsul.
EDCS-26400664.summary: An inscription honoring a proconsul, likely part of a larger monument.

EDCS-26400665.translation: Here are preserved the memories of the saints Pantaleon, Julian, and their companions.
EDCS-26400665.summary: An inscription indicating the burial place or memorial of saints and their companions.

EDCS-26400666.translation: Astius Mustelus, perpetual Christian priest, lived 72 years and rested on the 8th day before the Ides of December in the 4th year of the reign of our lord King Childeric.
EDCS-26400666.summary: A funerary inscription for Astius Mustelus, a Christian priest, dating to the reign of King Childeric.

EDCS-26400667.translation: Dinamius Valeri, placed in peace, rested on the day before the Nones of December, lived 19 years.
EDCS-26400667.summary: A funerary inscription for Dinamius Valeri, who died at the age of 19.

EDCS-26400668.translation: Secundinus lived 6 years, was laid to rest on the 15th day before the Kalends of February in the 7th indiction.
EDCS-26400668.summary: A funerary inscription for Secundinus, who died at the age of 6, dated by an indiction.

EDCS-26400669.translation: Gaius Sulpicius Lupercus lived 49 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-26400669.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the age at death of Gaius Sulpicius Lupercus.

EDCS-26400670.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Sulpicia Rogata lived 30 years, here she lies.
EDCS-26400670.summary: A funerary inscription for Sulpicia Rogata, who died at the age of 30.

EDCS-26400671.translation: Marcus Aurelius Pius Felix lived 22 years.
EDCS-26400671.summary: A funerary inscription for Marcus Aurelius Pius Felix, who died at the age of 22.

EDCS-26400672.translation: Of Aulus Coronicius, son of Caius Coronicius.
EDCS-26400672.summary: A fragmented inscription that appears to be a dedication to Aulus Coronicius.

EDCS-26400673.translation: To Bultia Hortensia Surdinia Antonia Postuma, perpetual priestess of the entire curia and of the tailors and subaediani, a place was granted by decree of the decurions because of her constant and frequent liberality towards all her fellow citizens.
EDCS-26400673.summary: A decree by local officials granting a burial plot to Bultia Hortensia Surdinia Antonia Postuma in recognition of her generosity.

EDCS-26400675.translation: To the son of the divine Augustus, Adventus, son of Gnaeus, of the Arnian tribe.
EDCS-26400675.summary: This is an epitaph for Adventus, son of Gnaeus, who identifies himself with the Arnian tribe and dedicates the monument to the son of the divine Augustus, likely an imperial figure.

EDCS-26400676.translation: To Florentius, blessed and happy Augustus.
EDCS-26400676.summary: This is a dedication to an emperor, likely Antoninus Pius or Marcus Aurelius, referred to as Florentius, blessed and happy Augustus.

EDCS-26400677.translation: Smaragdus, exarch of Italy, gave this statue of his majesty as a gift to our lord Phocas, the best, most merciful, and most fortunate emperor.
EDCS-26400677.summary: This inscription records that Smaragdus, the exarch of Italy, dedicated a statue to Emperor Phocas in the 6th or 7th century CE.

EDCS-26500001.translation: Son of Aurelius Antoninus, who lived for...
EDCS-26500001.summary: This is a fragmented epitaph for the son of Aurelius Antoninus, recording his lifespan.

EDCS-26500003.summary: This is a fragmented inscription, likely an epitaph, mentioning an auspicious year and the lifespan of an individual.

EDCS-26500004.summary: This is a dedication or epitaph for Laelius, characterized as most innocent.

EDCS-26500009.translation: Here, where the city walls are praised with such clear roofs, and you see the holy altars shining, it is not necessary for the elders, but the glory of so great a deed. The name of Alexander, the ruler, triumphs through the ages, whose honored labors fame displays, the former generations rejoiced to place them in a most beautiful dwelling, whom the rest of the day deceived, thinking they could be seen. Now they shine with light, supported by a beautiful altar, and rejoice that their assembly flourishes, which a clever and honorable guardian has fulfilled, and the Christian age, surrounded by the desire to visit, comes and rejoices to touch the holy thresholds with happy feet, singing all sacred things, extending their hands in devotion.
EDCS-26500009.summary: This is a lengthy funerary or commemorative inscription praising Alexander, a ruler, and celebrating the construction and adornment of a Christian church, likely from the late antique period.

EDCS-26500026.translation: In the name of Christ, Sindivult rests in peace, who lived for eleven years.
EDCS-26500026.summary: This is a Christian epitaph for Sindivult, who died at the age of eleven, and is recorded as resting in peace.

EDCS-26500027.translation: In memory of Stephen, he departed in peace on the third day before the Kalends of May.
EDCS-26500027.summary: This is a Christian epitaph recording the death of Stephen on a specific date, who departed in peace.

EDCS-26500028.translation: In memory of Stephania, received in peace.
EDCS-26500028.summary: This is a Christian epitaph commemorating Stephania, who has been received in peace.

EDCS-26500038.translation: To the spirits of the departed; Africanus, of the tribe Voltinia, lived 31 years; [dedicated by] A. Taisa, most devoted.
EDCS-26500038.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Africanus, dating to the Roman Imperial period, recording his name, tribal affiliation, age at death, and a dedicant.

EDCS-26500663.translation: Caius Fidiculanius Abdacus, freedman of Caius, died. Caius Fidiculanius Rufus, son of Caius, of the Arnensian tribe, lived. Fidiculania Hippolithe, freedwoman of Caius, lived. Hippolithe gave this fatal seat for the common good, for herself and for her partner and co-freedman, out of devotion.
EDCS-26500663.summary: This funerary epitaph likely dates to the Roman Imperial period and records the deaths of Caius Fidiculanius Abdacus and Caius Fidiculanius Rufus, and the dedication of a burial plot by Fidiculania Hippolithe for herself and her partner.

EDCS-26500668.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, possibly funerary, from the Roman Imperial period, containing personal names.

EDCS-26500671.translation: Fastiditus sleeps in peace; he lived 4 years, 1 month, and 3 hours.
EDCS-26500671.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Fastiditus, likely from the Roman Imperial period, recording his age at death in years, months, and hours.

EDCS-26500672.summary: This is a brief funerary epitaph, likely from the Roman Imperial period, for a person named Felicitas.

EDCS-26500677.summary: This is a funerary epitaph, likely from the Roman Imperial period, recording a person's faithfulness and their age at death as 100 years.

EDCS-26500679.translation: May you live in God; may you always rejoice.
EDCS-26500679.summary: This is a short inscription, likely Christian from the Roman Imperial period, expressing a wish for eternal life and joy.

EDCS-26500680.summary: This is a short inscription, possibly funerary, from the Roman Imperial period, containing a personal name and an epithet.

EDCS-26500681.translation: [---] of Quintus, son of Idianus, for judging for 4 months. He is buried here.
EDCS-26500681.summary: This is a funerary epitaph, likely from the Roman Imperial period, recording the duration of service (possibly legal) for Quintus, son of Idianus, and stating he is buried there.

EDCS-26500682.translation: Sacred to Mercury Augustus. Caius Antisitius Honoratus, because of the honor.
EDCS-26500682.summary: This is a dedication inscription, likely from the Roman Imperial period, dedicated to Mercury Augustus by Caius Antisitius Honoratus, possibly related to holding an office or honor.

EDCS-26500685.translation: Sacred to the Victory of Augustus, Lucius Rutilius Festianus, son of Festus, made this at his own expense for the health of Emperor Caesar Trajan Optimus Augustus.
EDCS-26500685.summary: This is a dedication made by Lucius Rutilius Festianus for the health of Emperor Trajan.

EDCS-26500686.translation: For the health of Emperor Caesar Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Augustus Pius, Caius Iulius Ianuarius and Caius Iulius Apulus [erected] four Charystian columns, 50 feet high.
EDCS-26500686.summary: This inscription records the erection of four Charystian columns for the health of Emperor Antoninus Pius.

EDCS-26500687.translation: To Marcus Aurelius Caesar, son of Emperor Caesar Lucius Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Augustus Pius.
EDCS-26500687.summary: This is an honorary inscription dedicated to Marcus Aurelius Caesar.

EDCS-26500688.translation: May your bones rest well, Tertulla. May the earth lie lightly upon you.
EDCS-26500688.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Tertulla, wishing her peace in the afterlife.

EDCS-26500691.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the departed. Sallustia Nampamii lived piously for 2 years and 15 days.
EDCS-26500691.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Sallustia Nampamii, detailing her lifespan.

EDCS-26500692.translation: Sacred to the Greek Ceres, by order. Marcus Lartidius A[m]bugaeus, first priest, dedicated this altar with steps on his own property.
EDCS-26500692.summary: This is a dedication of an altar to Ceres Graeca by the priest Marcus Lartidius Ambugaeus.

EDCS-26500696.text_edition: \n Tiberius Caesar divi Augusti filius Augustus pontifex maximus tribunicia potestate XXXI consul III Caius Vibius Marsus pro consul III dedicavit\n
EDCS-26500696.translation: Tiberius Caesar Augustus, son of the deified Augustus, chief priest, holding tribunician power for the 31st time, consul for the 3rd time, Gaius Vibius Marsus, proconsul for the 3rd time, dedicated this.
EDCS-26500696.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a monument by Gaius Vibius Marsus, proconsul, under the authority of Tiberius Caesar.

EDCS-26500699.summary: This inscription records the making and dedication of a monument by an unnamed individual.

EDCS-26500700.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the departed. Caius Iulius Hilarus, pious, lived for one year, 8 months, and 27 days. Datosus, the steward, and Paccia Iustina, his parents, made this for their dearest son. He is buried here.
EDCS-26500700.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Caius Iulius Hilarus, set up by his parents.

EDCS-26500702.summary: This is a funerary inscription stating the lifespan of an individual named Alisius.

EDCS-26500703.translation: Caecilia Zaba, high priestess, lived 85 years.
EDCS-26500703.summary: This is an epitaph for Caecilia Zaba, a high priestess, recording her age at death.

EDCS-26500704.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Imperiosus Iunior, a devoted slave of the Pescennii, lived for 3 years, 4 months, and 8 days. Imperiosus, his father, [erected this] for his dearest son.
EDCS-26500704.summary: A funerary epitaph for a young slave boy, erected by his father.

EDCS-26500706.translation: Gargilio Venator, son of Titus, of the Quirina tribe, chief centurion promoted in rank, appointed by the deified Hadrian, when he was prefect.
EDCS-26500706.summary: A fragmentary inscription recording the military career and promotion of Gargilio Venator.

EDCS-26500707.translation: Caius Domitius Pudens, son of Caius, of the Quirina tribe, and Caius Domitius Concessus, son of Caius, of the Quirina tribe, erected [this] for Valeria Concessa, daughter of Lucius, their most excellent mother, who had deserved well of her sons, and also as priestess of Ceres, by decree of the town council, in her own place and at her own expense.
EDCS-26500707.summary: A funerary monument dedicated by two sons to their mother, who also served as a public priestess of Ceres.

EDCS-26500708.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Publius Fabius Victor, devoted, lived for 25 years, 6 months, and 15 days. He is buried here.
EDCS-26500708.summary: A funerary epitaph for Publius Fabius Victor, who died at the age of 25.

EDCS-26500710.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Quintus Memmius Martinus, devoted, lived for 56 years.
EDCS-26500710.summary: A funerary epitaph for Quintus Memmius Martinus, who died at the age of 56.

EDCS-26500711.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Marcus Munatius Decimus Optatianus.
EDCS-26500711.summary: A funerary epitaph for Marcus Munatius Decimus Optatianus.

EDCS-26500712.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Quintus Strabonius Honoratianus, devoted, is buried here.
EDCS-26500712.summary: A funerary epitaph for Quintus Strabonius Honoratianus.

EDCS-26500713.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Lucius Vibius Vibianus, devoted, lived for 24 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-26500713.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lucius Vibius Vibianus, who died at the age of 24.

EDCS-26500714.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Datius, devoted, lived for 60 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-26500714.summary: A funerary epitaph for Datius, who died at the age of 60.

EDCS-26500715.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Lucius Licinius Maximus Spanius lived for 3 months and 12 days. He is buried here.
EDCS-26500715.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lucius Licinius Maximus Spanius, who died as an infant.

EDCS-26500716.translation: To the Augustan gods and to the sacred place, Primus, freedman of Augustus, procurator of Numidian marbles, dedicated this altar.
EDCS-26500716.summary: This inscription records the dedication of an altar to the Augustan gods and a sacred place by Primus, a procurator of Numidian marbles.

EDCS-26500718.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Pompeia Prima, devoted and a woman of good character, lived 25 years.
EDCS-26500718.summary: This funerary inscription records the life of Pompeia Prima, who died at the age of 25.

EDCS-26500719.translation: To Marcus Aurelius Verus Caesar, consul for the 2nd time, son of the Emperor Caesar Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Augustus Pius, by decree of the decurions, at public expense.
EDCS-26500719.summary: This is a dedication to Marcus Aurelius Verus Caesar, son of Antoninus Pius, funded by public money and decreed by local officials.

EDCS-26500720.translation: To the deified Publius Helvius Pertinax Augustus Pius, father of the fatherland, by decree of the decurions, at public expense.
EDCS-26500720.summary: This is a dedication to the deified Emperor Pertinax, funded by public money and decreed by local officials.

EDCS-26500721.summary: This is a very brief dedication or memorial to Antonius Namphamo.

EDCS-26500722.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Hostilia Asclepias, devoted, lived 35 years. Marcus Hostilius Reginus, son of Quintus, of the Quirina tribe, made this for his freedwoman and most excellent wife, and for himself. May the earth rest lightly upon you.
EDCS-26500722.summary: This funerary inscription records the life of Hostilia Asclepias, who died at age 35, and was made by her husband Marcus Hostilius Reginus.

EDCS-26500723.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Lucius Murdius Felix, devoted, lived 28 years.
EDCS-26500723.summary: This funerary inscription records the life of Lucius Murdius Felix, who died at the age of 28.

EDCS-26500724.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Lucius Octavius Honoratianus, devoted, lived ninety years and forty-three days. He is buried here.
EDCS-26500724.summary: This funerary inscription records the life of Lucius Octavius Honoratianus, who died at the age of 90 years and 43 days.

EDCS-26500725.translation: Caius Umbirius Honoratus, devoted, lived 34 years, 5 months, and 24 days. He is buried here.
EDCS-26500725.summary: This funerary inscription records the life of Caius Umbirius Honoratus, who died at the age of 34 years, 5 months, and 24 days.

EDCS-26500726.translation: Quintus Aradius Rufinus, consul, to Luna, a vow.
EDCS-26500726.summary: This inscription records a vow made to the goddess Luna by Quintus Aradius Rufinus, who held the consulship.

EDCS-26500727.translation: By decree of the decurions, at public expense, to Publius Septimius Geta, son of the Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus Arabicus Adiabenicus Parthicus Maximus, consul three times, brother of the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus Pius Felix Parthicus, consul three times.
EDCS-26500727.summary: This inscription records a public monument erected by decree of the local council in honor of Publius Septimius Geta, brother of Emperor Caracalla.

EDCS-26500729.translation: Quintus Annaeus Balbus Faventinus, son of Quintus, of the Pollia tribe, aged 53, a soldier of the V Legion, twice decorated, formerly the chief magistrate of Thuburnica, is buried here. He lived honorably, and hail to you, by the decision of Quintus Annaeus Scapula.
EDCS-26500729.summary: This funerary inscription records the life and career of Quintus Annaeus Balbus Faventinus, a decorated soldier and former magistrate, who died at age 53.

EDCS-26500730.translation: He himself made this with his own money, Quintus Cocceius Gemellus Fuscinanus, priest, aedile, quaestor, and quinquennial duovir.
EDCS-26500730.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by Quintus Cocceius Gemellus Fuscinanus, who held several municipal offices, likely for a public building.

EDCS-26500732.translation: Servilla Florida, daughter of Sextus, aged 25, is buried here.
EDCS-26500732.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Servilla Florida, recording her name, parentage, and age at death.

EDCS-26500733.translation: The Furnitanian order dedicated this to our most Clement Prince and Lord of the whole world, Augustus our Lord Valentinian, during the proconsulship of Iulius Festus, a man of the highest distinction, along with Antonius Dracontius, a man of the highest distinction, acting in place of the praetorian prefects.
EDCS-26500733.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by the Furnitanian order to Emperor Valentinian, mentioning high-ranking officials Iulius Festus and Antonius Dracontius.

EDCS-26500736.translation: His heirs, Maretis son of Felix.
EDCS-26500736.summary: This is a fragmentary dedication or ownership marker, possibly for a tomb, naming Maretis and indicating it passed to his heirs.

EDCS-26500737.summary: This is a simple funerary epitaph or ownership marker for Cornelia Stercoria.

EDCS-26500882.text_edition: \n Caius Marius Cai filius aedilis signum Aequitatis sacrum de sua pequnia sic ex decreto decurionum faciundum curavit\n
EDCS-26500882.translation: Gaius Marius, son of Caius, as aedile, commissioned this sacred statue of Equity to be made from his own funds, in accordance with the decree of the decurions.
EDCS-26500882.summary: This inscription records the commissioning of a statue of Equity by Gaius Marius, an aedile, using his own money as per a local decree.

EDCS-26500886.summary: This incomplete inscription likely records the name of Sextius, son of Aurelius Antoninus, possibly related to a dedication or funerary monument.

EDCS-26500906.text_edition: \n D equo publico ab Imperatore Caesare Hadriano Augusto flamen perpetuus ob liberalitatem HS CCCLmilium Syllae posuit decreto decurionum pecunia publica\n
EDCS-26500906.translation: He erected this from public funds, by decree of the decurions, with 350,000 sesterces from the Emperor Caesar Hadrianus Augustus, perpetual priest, for his generosity with public horses.
EDCS-26500906.summary: This inscription records a public monument erected with imperial funds and a decree of local officials to honor a perpetual priest for his generosity with public horses.

EDCS-26500910.translation: From Uthina, by decree of the decurions, with public money.
EDCS-26500910.summary: This inscription indicates a monument or work was funded by the public treasury and approved by the local council (decurions) of Uthina.

EDCS-26500918.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely part of a larger dedication, specifying the recipient as the 'perpetual flamen' (a high priestly office).

EDCS-26500926.translation: To Publius Valerius Honoratus, son of Publius, the aedile.
EDCS-26500926.summary: This inscription records a dedication made to Publius Valerius Honoratus, son of Publius, who served as an aedile.

EDCS-26500931.summary: This is a dedication to Emperor Marcus Baebius, likely part of a larger inscription.

EDCS-26500932.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription, possibly a funerary marker or dedication, containing the name Quintus Bis and an abbreviation.

EDCS-26500940.translation: From the workshop of Marcus of Utina.
EDCS-26500940.summary: This is a maker's mark from the workshop of Marcus of Utina.

EDCS-26500945.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes, three times.
EDCS-26500945.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the Manes, possibly with a repetition or emphasis indicated by 'ter tus'.

EDCS-26500946.translation: Pius lived 80 years, he is buried here.
EDCS-26500946.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the name Pius, his age at death, and his burial location.

EDCS-26500951.translation: The ninth place of the curia belongs to Valeria.
EDCS-26500951.summary: This inscription likely marks a seating arrangement or division within a curia (council meeting place) assigned to Valeria.

EDCS-26500952.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a marble statue to or by a person named Eutechnus.

EDCS-26500953.translation: From the public treasury of Annius Clodius.
EDCS-26500953.summary: This inscription likely indicates the source of funds from the public treasury of Annius Clodius for a monument.

EDCS-26500956.summary: This inscription records the ownership or dedication by Quintus Granius Marcianinus.

EDCS-26500957.summary: This inscription records the ownership or dedication by Quintus Granius Pelagius.

EDCS-26500960.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, possibly from a tombstone or dedication, wishing good fortune to an individual.

EDCS-26500972.translation: and of a most honorable man
EDCS-26500972.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription, likely part of a longer text praising an honorable man.

EDCS-26500979.translation: and of a most honorable man
EDCS-26500979.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription, likely part of a longer text praising an honorable man.

EDCS-26500980.translation: Secundus, son of Faustus, set this up by the favor of Bacchus.
EDCS-26500980.summary: This is a dedication by Secundus, son of Faustus, likely for a religious or votive offering, indicating favor from the god Bacchus.

EDCS-26500982.summary: This fragment likely refers to two individuals named Octavius, possibly indicating a familial or collegial relationship.

EDCS-26500983.translation: and the duovirate, thus the Memmii
EDCS-26500983.summary: This fragment seems to mention the office of duovir and refers to individuals named Memmius, possibly related to local governance.

EDCS-26500985.translation: of Marcus CucuIIus, a most honorable man
EDCS-26500985.summary: This fragment praises Marcus CucuIIus as a most honorable man, likely part of a dedication or epitaph.

EDCS-26500986.text_edition: \n Luci M L Dogasi honestissimi viri\n
EDCS-26500986.translation: of Lucius Marius Dogasus, a most honorable man
EDCS-26500986.summary: This fragment praises Lucius Marius Dogasus as a most honorable man, likely part of a dedication or epitaph.

EDCS-26501005.translation: To Licinius Fluminis, son of Lucius.
EDCS-26501005.summary: This is a dedication to Licinius Fluminis, son of Lucius.

EDCS-26501022.translation: To Iunia, daughter of Gaius, in the ninth region.
EDCS-26501022.summary: This inscription likely records a division or allocation of space or property within a city or region to Iunia, daughter of Gaius.

EDCS-26501028.translation: [---] nineteen [---] the second of the Ides of January [---].
EDCS-26501028.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription that appears to record a date, possibly relating to a festival or event.

EDCS-26501029.translation: Vendianus, son of Gaius Caecilius, honorable father of the order, was consul.
EDCS-26501029.summary: This inscription honors Vendianus, son of Gaius Caecilius, a prominent figure possibly holding a senatorial rank, indicating his consulship.

EDCS-26501030.translation: Marcus Petronius Vitalis, an ordinary *clarissimus vir*, [paid for something].
EDCS-26501030.summary: This inscription appears to record the name and honorific title of an individual, likely a dedication or commemoration.

EDCS-26501034.translation: Marsinus Campester gave two performances and gifts.
EDCS-26501034.summary: This inscription records a performance or games given by Marsinus Campester.

EDCS-26800195.summary: This is a simple maker's mark, indicating that Terentius was responsible for the creation of the object.

EDCS-26800212.translation: Doliar ware from the estates of Lucius Aurelius Caesar, the work of Marcus Valerius Iulianus.
EDCS-26800212.summary: This inscription identifies the origin of pottery as from the estates of Lucius Aurelius Caesar and attributes its manufacture to Marcus Valerius Iulianus.

EDCS-26800218.translation: Lucius Bruttidius Augustalis made this doliar ware from the potteries of our Caesar, when Propinquus and Ambibulus were consuls.
EDCS-26800218.summary: This inscription records the production of pottery by Lucius Bruttidius Augustalis from imperial workshops during the consulship of Propinquus and Ambibulus.

EDCS-26800220.translation: Lucius Bruttidius Augustalis made this tilework from the kilns of our Caesar, when Propinquus and Ambibulus were consuls.
EDCS-26800220.summary: This inscription records a tilemaker, Lucius Bruttidius Augustalis, and the production of tilework from imperial kilns during the consulship of Propinquus and Ambibulus.

EDCS-26800221.translation: Lucius Bruttidius Augustalis made this doliar ware from the potteries of our Caesar, when Propinquus and Ambibulus were consuls.
EDCS-26800221.summary: This inscription records the production of pottery by Lucius Bruttidius Augustalis from imperial workshops during the consulship of Propinquus and Ambibulus.

EDCS-26800224.translation: Doliar ware from the potteries of our Caesar, Caius [---] Calpurnius Piso?
EDCS-26800224.summary: This inscription indicates the origin of pottery from imperial workshops, naming the emperor possibly as Caesar and a consular figure.

EDCS-26800225.translation: Tilework from the kilns of Asinia Quadratilla, made by Gaius Nannius Fortunatus for Lucius Quadratus, when he was consul.

EDCS-26800227.summary: This inscription records ceramic products from the workshops of Asinia Quadrata, made by Unnus Fortunatus, and dated by the consulship of Lucius Quadratus.

EDCS-26800229.translation: Doliar ware from the estates of Domitia Lucilla, from the workshop of Quintus Flavius Aprilis, when Lucius Statius Quadratus and Gaius Cuspius Rufus were consuls.

EDCS-26801057.inscription_type: tituli honorarii, tituli operum, tituli sacri
EDCS-26801057.translation: For the health of Emperor Caesar Publius Licinius Gallienus Pius Felix Augustus Germanicus, pontifex maximus, holder of tribunician power for the 13th time, acclaimed imperator for the 12th time, consul for the 6th time, father of the country, proconsul, and of Cornelia Salonina Augusta; the curator of the res publica provided the portico of the forum, as planned, with 50,000 sesterces, which is also called a sportula, from the generosity of the most holy Emperor, [giving] benevolence, favor, and liberality. Papiria Felix Iulianus, an equestrian of Rome, perpetual priest, holder of the duumviral office, from his perpetual priesthood, gave the sportulae and the banquet for the decurions, adding to the public treasury 50,000 sesterces and on the day of dedication [provided] a banquet and staged theatrical games for the entire populace.
EDCS-26801057.summary: This extensive inscription records a significant public dedication including a portico, a cash donation (sportula), a banquet, games, and offerings, made by Papiria Felix Iulianus in honor of Emperor Gallienus and Empress Cornelia Salonina, likely dating to the period of Gallienus' reign.

EDCS-26900128.translation: I adjure you, whatever spirit you are, death-dweller, unburied, by the seven consorts of the chthonic king, [strange words], that you bind the horses of the green faction, whose names I entrust to you: Dareios, Agile, Koupeidinos, Pouyones, Pretiōson, Prounikos, Dardanos, Eiinachos, Phloridos, Pardos, Seruatos, Fouldigos, Ouidktores, Prouphikios. Bind their race, their strength, their spirit; take away their victory; impede their feet; cripple their sinews, dislocate their limbs, so that tomorrow they may not be able on the hippodrome to run or walk or win, nor go out through the gates of the stables, nor advance on the track, nor round the turning posts, but may they fall with their charioteers, Prōtos and Phileikes and Narkissos. For I adjure you, deity, by the holy names [strange words], bind the horses of the green faction, whose names I have entrusted to you: Dareios, Agile, Koupeidinos, Pouyones, Pretiōson, Prounikos, Dardanos, Eiinachos, Phloridos, Pardos, Seruatos, Fouldigos, Ouidktores, Prouphikios. Bind for them their race, feet, victory, impulse, spirit, speed; cripple their sinews, dislocate their limbs, so that tomorrow they may not be able on the hippodrome to run or walk or win, nor go out through the gates of the stables, nor advance on the track, nor the spatium, nor round the turning posts, but may they fall with their charioteers, Prōtos and Phileikes and Narkissos. Bind for them their hands; take away their victory, their dismount, and their sight, so that they may not be able to see their opponents while driving, but rather seize them from their chariots and throw them to the ground, so that they may fall in every place on the hippodrome with their own horses, with damage to their bodies and fracture of their legs. Now, now, now! Quickly, quickly, quickly! Bind!
EDCS-26900128.summary: A curse tablet (defixio) written in Greek, likely from the Roman period, intended to magically impede the horses and charioteers of the 'green' faction in chariot races, and ensure victory for the 'red' or another rival faction, by invoking chthonic deities and listing the names of the horses and charioteers. This is a complex magical text from the ancient world, likely from the Roman Empire, using Greek language.

EDCS-26900519.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the burial of Fabius Pacatus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-26900520.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Fabia Rogata lived 35 years; here she lies.
EDCS-26900520.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan and burial of Fabia Rogata, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-26900521.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Iulia Sabina lived 59 years. Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Flavius V lived 61 years in Carthage.
EDCS-26900521.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespans of Iulia Sabina and Flavius V, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-26900522.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Matronula. Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Geminius.
EDCS-26900522.summary: This is a funerary inscription, possibly a paired burial or a dedication to the Spirits of the Departed for Matronula and Geminius, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-26900523.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Publius Herculanus, son of Publius, of the Quirina tribe, Rogatus, lived 35 years.
EDCS-26900523.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Publius Herculanus Rogatus, identified by his father and tribal affiliation, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-26900524.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Iulius Baliatus, pious, lived 40 years.
EDCS-26900524.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of the pious Iulius Baliatus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-26900525.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Iulius Baliha lived about 75 years.
EDCS-26900525.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the approximate lifespan of Iulius Baliha, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-26900526.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Publius Iulius M ius lived.
EDCS-26900526.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Publius Iulius M ius, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-26900527.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Iulius Rogatianus lived 94 years. Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Iulia Quintana lived 60 years.
EDCS-26900527.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespans of Iulius Rogatianus and Iulia Quintana, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-26900528.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Gaius Julius Victor lived 70 years.
EDCS-26900528.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Gaius Julius Victor, who lived 70 years.

EDCS-26900529.translation: Iulia Marcella, daughter of Marcus, lived 11 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-26900529.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Iulia Marcella, daughter of Marcus, who died at age 11.

EDCS-26900530.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Logunius Rogatianus of good memory lived 25 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-26900530.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Logunius Rogatianus, who died at age 25.

EDCS-26900531.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Vibius Esricatus lived 57 years. Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Alfia Getula lived 81 years.
EDCS-26900531.summary: This funerary inscription records the deaths of Vibius Esricatus (57 years) and Alfia Getula (81 years).

EDCS-26900532.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Donatus, son of Marcus, who died at age 52.

EDCS-26900533.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Donata, the pious, with her age missing.

EDCS-26900538.translation: Antonis of the Guri, pious, lived 80 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-26900538.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Antonis of the Guri, who died at age 80.

EDCS-26900539.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Anneus Secundinus the pious lived 73 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-26900539.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Anneus Secundinus, the pious, who died at age 73.

EDCS-26900540.translation: Privatus, his freedman, erected this in honor of Marcus Caecilius Faustus, most pious, most religious, and best patron, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-26900540.summary: This is a public inscription honoring Marcus Caecilius Faustus by his freedman, Privatus, following a decree by local officials.

EDCS-26900541.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Crispia Maxima lived 5 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-26900541.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Crispia Maxima, who died at age 5.

EDCS-26900542.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Inia Fabia Prima, a slave, lived [some number of] years; she is buried here.
EDCS-26900542.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a slave named Inia Fabia Prima, indicating her name, status, and burial place.

EDCS-26900543.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Postumius Elico lived 35 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-26900543.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Postumius Elico, indicating his name, age at death, and burial place.

EDCS-26900544.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Optatus the actor lived 33 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-26900544.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Optatus, an actor, indicating his profession, age at death, and burial place.

EDCS-26900545.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Calpurnia Va lived 81 years; she is buried here. Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Vibius Optatus lived 20 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-26900545.summary: This funerary inscription contains two separate epitaphs for Calpurnia Va (aged 81) and Vibius Optatus (aged 20), both indicating their burial places.

EDCS-26900547.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Iulius Donatus, a soldier of the First Urban Cohort, pious, lived 36 years; he is buried here. Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Sextus Iulius Rufinus, son of [---], a soldier of the III Augusta Legion, pious, lived 20 years; he is buried here. Secunda, mother, his heir, with her own money, for herself and...
EDCS-26900547.summary: This inscription contains two funerary epitaphs for soldiers, Iulius Donatus (36) and Sextus Iulius Rufinus (20), and begins a dedication by Secunda, likely as a burial plot owner or memorializer.

EDCS-26900548.translation: Lucius Caninius Fortunatus, son of Caius, pious, lived 86 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-26900548.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Caninius Fortunatus, indicating his name, patronymic, age at death, and burial place.

EDCS-26900549.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. For Donata, daughter of Claudius Ianuarius, [she] lived 21 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-26900549.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Donata, daughter of Claudius Ianuarius, indicating her name, parentage, age at death, and burial place.

EDCS-26900550.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Expletus lived 25 years.
EDCS-26900550.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Expletus, indicating his name and age at death, though the burial location is not specified.

EDCS-26900551.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Geminia Victoria lived 75 years; she is buried here. Gaius Julius Marcellus lived 95 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-26900551.summary: This funerary inscription contains two separate epitaphs for Geminia Victoria (aged 75) and Gaius Julius Marcellus (aged 95), both indicating their burial places.

EDCS-26900552.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Micilia Novella, pious, lived 50 years. Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Iulius Nico, pious.
EDCS-26900552.summary: This inscription contains two funerary epitaphs: one for Micilia Novella, indicating her name, piety, and age at death (50), and another for Iulius Nico, noting his name and piety.

EDCS-26900553.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Omidia Saturnina lived 85 years, she is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Licinius Publius lived 95 years, he is buried here.
EDCS-26900553.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication for two individuals, Omidia Saturnina and Licinius Publius, indicating their ages at death and burial.

EDCS-26900554.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Licinius Saturninus, dutiful, lived 85 years.
EDCS-26900554.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication for Licinius Saturninus, noting his age at death and describing him as dutiful.

EDCS-26900556.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Mreonia lived 33 years, she is buried here.
EDCS-26900556.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication for Mreonia, stating her age at death and burial.

EDCS-26900557.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Novi m lived [---] years. Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcus N NCEI us [---].
EDCS-26900557.summary: This inscription is a fragmentary funerary dedication with incomplete names and ages, likely for two individuals.

EDCS-26900558.translation: PIPOP LA P is buried here.
EDCS-26900558.summary: This is a very brief funerary inscription recording that someone named PIPOP LA P is buried here.

EDCS-26900559.translation: Lucius Plotius Successus lived 95 years, he is buried here.
EDCS-26900559.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication for Lucius Plotius Successus, stating his age at death and burial.

EDCS-26900560.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Pompeius Marcianus lived 13 years.
EDCS-26900560.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication for Pompeius Marcianus, noting his young age at death.

EDCS-26900561.summary: This is a very short inscription that appears to be an epitaph for Quintus Pomponius.

EDCS-26900563.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. etia Vctoria, dutiful, lived 17 years, she is buried here. Vibius Martialis, dutiful, lived 73 years, he is buried here.
EDCS-26900563.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication for two individuals, etia Vctoria and Vibius Martialis, detailing their ages at death and burial.

EDCS-26900565.translation: Euticianus, innocent, lived in peace for thirty days.
EDCS-26900565.summary: This inscription records the brief life of Euticianus, stating he lived for thirty days in peace.

EDCS-26900566.summary: This inscription records a military loss of 443 soldiers from Chellenses Numidae, likely from a battle or disaster.

EDCS-26900568.translation: The same person, IB, made and dedicated this statue with steps to Minerva Augusta.
EDCS-26900568.summary: This is a dedication of a statue and steps to Minerva Augusta by a person identified only by the initials IB.

EDCS-26900572.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the dead. Caesella Pulcella, dutiful, lived for 41 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-26900572.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Caesella Pulcella, recording her age at death and burial.

EDCS-26900573.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the dead. Furia Victoria, dutiful, lived for 57 years; she is buried here. CD AM V AT RMV, dutiful, lived for 65 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-26900573.summary: This inscription is a funerary epitaph recording the lives and burials of two individuals, Furia Victoria and CD AM V AT RMV.

EDCS-26900574.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the dead. Iulius Honoratus lived for 111 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-26900574.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Iulius Honoratus, remarkably recording his age at death and burial.

EDCS-26900575.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the dead. Iulia Felicia, dutiful, lived for [---] years.
EDCS-26900575.summary: This is an incomplete funerary epitaph for Iulia Felicia, recording her name and piety, but missing her age at death.

EDCS-26900576.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the dead. Iulia Rogata lived for 80 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-26900576.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Iulia Rogata, recording her age at death and burial.

EDCS-26900577.translation: VA M S lived for 45 years.
EDCS-26900577.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription, possibly recording the age of an individual whose name is largely lost.

EDCS-26900578.translation: He is buried here at 25 years of age.
EDCS-26900578.summary: This is a very fragmentary funerary inscription indicating the age at death and burial of an individual.

EDCS-26900580.translation: ONIE P I, Caius Caelius Rogatus, having been warned by the appearance of another, made this with his own money and dedicated it.
EDCS-26900580.summary: This inscription records Caius Caelius Rogatus dedicating a monument funded by himself, prompted by a supernatural vision or omen.

EDCS-26900581.translation: The pagan community of the colony of Julia Veneria Chirtensis Nova, located at Aubuzza, rebuilt the pagan sanctuary from the ground up with their own money.
EDCS-26900581.summary: This inscription records the rebuilding of a pagan sanctuary by the pagan community of Aubuzza in the colony of Julia Veneria Chirtensis Nova.

EDCS-26900582.translation: To the Genius of the Emperor Caesar Antoninus Hadrianus Augustus, Lucius Annaeus Hermes, priest and tribune of the Larenses tribe, of the AI IA century of Eron, built and dedicated at his own expense from the ground up the pagan sanctuary, portico, caldarium, and cohort with all their furnishings, with Severus Silvanus Vindicus acting as curator and perpetual priest.
EDCS-26900582.summary: This inscription records the construction and dedication of a pagan sanctuary complex by Lucius Annaeus Hermes, a priest and tribune, possibly during the reign of Antoninus Pius or Marcus Aurelius.

EDCS-26900583.translation: Marcus Seius Salvus made this to Jupiter Optimus Maximus Capitolinus.
EDCS-26900583.summary: This is a dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus Capitolinus made by Marcus Seius Salvus.

EDCS-26900587.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus Aquilius Renatus, son of Quintus, of the Quirina tribe, lived for 40 years.
EDCS-26900587.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the death of Quintus Aquilius Renatus at the age of 40.

EDCS-26900588.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Blessia Flacchilla, daughter of Caius, of the Quirina tribe, has paid the debt of nature. This inscription was set up by her loving husband, Caelius Victor, for his most loving wife. She lived 41 years. She rests here.
EDCS-26900588.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Blessia Flacchilla, who died at age 41, set up by her husband Caelius Victor.

EDCS-26900589.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Caecilia Donata, daughter of Ilaris, of the Quirina tribe, [wife] of Marcus Caecilius Liberalis, lived 83 years.
EDCS-26900589.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Caecilia Donata, who died at the age of 83.

EDCS-26900591.translation: Caius Clodius Felix, son of Caius, lived 75 years. He rests here.
EDCS-26900591.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Caius Clodius Felix, who died at the age of 75.

EDCS-26900592.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Cornelius Rufus lived 54 years. He rests here.
EDCS-26900592.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Cornelius Rufus, who died at the age of 54.

EDCS-26900593.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Fabia Rogata lived 35 years. She rests here.
EDCS-26900593.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Fabia Rogata, who died at the age of 35.

EDCS-26900594.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Helvia Fortunata lived 55 years. She rests here.
EDCS-26900594.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Helvia Fortunata, who died at the age of 55.

EDCS-26900595.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Iulius Honoratianus lived 48 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-26900595.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Iulius Honoratianus, who died at the age of 48.

EDCS-26900596.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Marcus Iulius Honoratus lived 105 years.
EDCS-26900596.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Marcus Iulius Honoratus, who lived to be 105 years old.

EDCS-26900597.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Lucius Iulius Honoratus, son of Lucius, of the Quirina tribe, the Younger, lived 40 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-26900597.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Lucius Iulius Honoratus Iunior, who died at the age of 40.

EDCS-26900598.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Marcus Iulius Niptheus lived 25 years.
EDCS-26900598.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Marcus Iulius Niptheus, who died at the age of 25.

EDCS-26900599.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Caius Iulius Primus lived 52 years.
EDCS-26900599.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Caius Iulius Primus, who died at the age of 52.

EDCS-26900600.translation: Iulia Marcella, daughter of Marcus, lived 41 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-26900600.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Iulia Marcella, who died at the age of 41.

EDCS-26900601.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Licinia Saturnina lived 50 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-26900601.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Licinia Saturnina, who died at the age of 50.

EDCS-26900602.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Licinia Saturnina lived 63 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-26900602.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Licinia Saturnina, who died at the age of 63.

EDCS-26900603.translation: Lucceia Donata, the pious, lived 50 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-26900603.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Lucceia Donata, who died at the age of 50.

EDCS-26900604.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Papinia Fortunata, the pious, lived 24 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-26900604.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Papinia Fortunata, who died at the age of 24.

EDCS-26900605.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Pomponius, son of Quintus, of the Quirina tribe, lived 75 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-26900605.summary: A funerary inscription recording the death of Pomponius, including his name, father's name, tribal affiliation, and age at death.

EDCS-26900606.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Gaius Sertorius Saturninus, of the Quirina tribe, from Maguntia, lived 121 years.
EDCS-26900606.summary: A funerary inscription recording the death of Gaius Sertorius Saturninus, including his name, tribal affiliation, place of origin, and extreme age at death.

EDCS-26900607.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Gaius Sextilius Rufus lived 53 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-26900607.summary: A funerary inscription recording the death of Gaius Sextilius Rufus, including his name, age at death, and burial.

EDCS-26900608.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Gaius Vettius Messor lived 14 years. Quintus Lucius Vettius Secundus lived 53 years. Quintus...
EDCS-26900608.summary: A funerary inscription recording the deaths of Gaius Vettius Messor and Quintus Lucius Vettius Secundus, including their ages at death and partial names.

EDCS-26900610.translation: [...], tribune of the Fortensian soldiers, Benenatus, Abundius Victor, Roman martyr, deacon Petros, Felis, Rogatus TTO, tribune, Felis Cinnamus, Felix Gregorius, Felis Rogatus, Donatus martyr, our Libertinus, Feliculus, Cresconius, Paterni, Rogatus, Controsarus, Filargyri, Abundantius, Donatinus, Mariclus, Bitor, Mauri, Fuzon, Kadizon, Donatus, Bonifatius, Natalicus, Bictrianus, Natalicus, Tinus, Gauziosus, Romanus, Inulus, these names in our homily, individual parts...
EDCS-26900610.summary: A list of names, possibly martyrs or church officials, with titles such as tribune, martyr, and deacon, and including place names and tribal affiliations, possibly from an inscription related to a religious text or commemoration.

EDCS-26900611.translation: Caecilia Fortunata, dutiful, lived 40 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-26900611.summary: A funerary inscription recording the death of Caecilia Fortunata, including her name, epithet, age at death, and burial.

EDCS-26900612.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Petreia Bonifatia, dutiful, lived 65 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-26900612.summary: A funerary inscription recording the death of Petreia Bonifatia, including her name, epithet, age at death, and burial.

EDCS-26900613.translation: To our lords, the Emperors Valentinian, Valens, and Gratian, and to Sextius Rusticus, most excellent proconsul of the province of Africa, and to the most excellent legate of Numidia, the baths, which were restored, were supported by the devotion of the entire council, by the work and diligence and expenses of the curator of public affairs.
EDCS-26900613.summary: A dedication for the restoration of baths, mentioning emperors Valentinian, Valens, and Gratian, the proconsul of Africa Sextius Rusticus, the legate of Numidia, and the curator rei publicae, likely from the late 4th century.

EDCS-26900614.translation: Fortunata lived 16 years, 3 months. She is buried here. Gellia Satura [dedicated this] to her son Victor [who lived] IIII [years].
EDCS-26900614.summary: A funerary inscription for Fortunata, including her age at death, and a separate dedication by Gellia Satura for her son Victor, indicating his short life.

EDCS-26900615.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Durvia Salsula, daughter of Quintus, dutiful, lived 55 years. She is buried here. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Gaius Iulius Rufus Achilla, dutiful, lived 98 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-26900615.summary: A double funerary inscription recording the deaths of Durvia Salsula and Gaius Iulius Rufus Achilla, including their names, parentage (for Durvia), epithets, ages at death, and burial.

EDCS-26900616.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Iulia Extricata, dutiful, lived 65 years; she is buried here. Lucius Ostilius Honoratus, a hatter, dutiful, lived 73 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-26900616.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the burials and ages of Iulia Extricata and Lucius Ostilius Honoratus.

EDCS-26900617.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Rufinia Nigra lived 1 year; she is buried here.
EDCS-26900617.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the burial and age of Rufinia Nigra.

EDCS-26900618.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Sextus Terentius, son of Quintus, and Cornelia Felix Iulianus, dutiful, lived 30 years, 2 months, and 20 days; he is buried here.
EDCS-26900618.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the burial and age of Sextus Terentius and Cornelia Felix Iulianus.

EDCS-26900619.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Marcus Valerius, son of Marcus, and Cornelia Felix Gallio, aedile and quinquennial official, priest of the god Ditis, in the first place, good, honest, incomparable, dutiful, lived 65 years; he is buried here. Auspici
EDCS-26900619.summary: A funerary epitaph for Marcus Valerius, son of Marcus, noting his various civic and religious offices, and his age at death.

EDCS-26900620.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Onomasta Redducta, dutiful, lived 90 years; she is buried here. Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Lucius Ostilius Redductulus, dutiful, lived 30 years; he is buried here. Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Lucius Ostilius Katullus, dutiful, lived [age missing]; he is buried here.
EDCS-26900620.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the burials and ages of Onomasta Redducta, Lucius Ostilius Redductulus, and Lucius Ostilius Katullus.

EDCS-26900621.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Caius Marcius, son of Caius, and Cornelia Kastus Vitellianus, dutiful, lived 13 years, 7 months; he is buried here.
EDCS-26900621.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the burial and age of Caius Marcius and Cornelia Kastus Vitellianus.

EDCS-26900622.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Quintus Papius Fortunatus, dutiful, lived 85 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-26900622.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the burial and age of Quintus Papius Fortunatus.

EDCS-26900623.translation: To my dearest and most loving daughter, who did not deserve this, but when nature's debt had to be paid so suddenly, her father Successus made this for his most longed-for, dutiful daughter, who lived 8 years and 7 months; she is buried here.
EDCS-26900623.summary: A funerary epitaph from a father, Successus, for his young daughter, noting her age at death.

EDCS-26900624.translation: Sacred to Caelestis Augusta. For the safety of the Emperor Caesar Caius Maximius Pius Felix Augustus, pontifex maximus, with tribunician power, father of the fatherland, and for all his divine household, the colonists of the estate of Turris Rutunda, lords of our Augustus, rebuilt the fallen temple of Augustus with their own money, adorned with columns, and dedicated it under the magistracy of Lucius Cornelius, under the priesthood of Annius Cornelianus.
EDCS-26900624.summary: A dedication by colonists of the Turris Rutunda estate for the safety of Emperor Maximinus Thrax, rebuilding a temple.

EDCS-26900626.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Quintus Pompeius Gallio, dutiful, lived 72 years; he is buried here. Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Aplonia Rogata, dutiful, lived 40 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-26900626.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the burials and ages of Quintus Pompeius Gallio and Aplonia Rogata.

EDCS-26900627.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the August Deities.

EDCS-26900628.translation: Sacred to the August Victories, for the safety of the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Severus Alexander Pius Felix Augustus, pontifex maximus, holder of tribunician power.
EDCS-26900628.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the August Victories, made for the safety of Emperor Severus Alexander, likely during his reign (222-235 AD).

EDCS-26900629.translation: For the safety of the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Commodus Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus Germanicus Sarmaticus Britannicus, pontifex maximus, holder of tribunician power for the 13th time, imperator for the 8th time, consul for the 5th time, father of the fatherland. Caius Orfius Luciscus, son of Lucius, of the Cornelia tribe, prefect for dispensing justice for the second time, twice duovir, quinquennial, public priest of the goddess Caelestis and Aesculapius, completed and dedicated the arch which he had promised in his own name and that of Caius Orfius, out of special devotion to the most sacred divinity and for perpetual love of the fatherland, with an additional statue; he also erected a statue in the Forum of Marsyas. Because of its dedication, they presented theatrical games and a banquet to the curiae and the Cerealic cults.
EDCS-26900629.summary: This inscription records the dedication of an arch and statues by Caius Orfius Luciscus, a prominent local official, in honor of Emperor Commodus, likely during the late 2nd century AD.

EDCS-26900631.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Fundania L. lived for [---] years. Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Iulius Pontius, son of Lucius, of the Cornelia tribe, pious.
EDCS-26900631.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the departed spirits, recording the life of Fundania L. and Lucius Iulius Pontius, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-26900632.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Germanus ICAPID. Aelius Germanus erected this altar for his dearest wife, aged 23 years. [He] lived piously for 40 years, he is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. PVI geIrmanus Manlius for his most holy, pious daughter, lived [---]. She is buried here.
EDCS-26900632.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the departed spirits, recording the deaths and ages of two individuals, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-26900633.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Caecilius Blandianus, son of Lucius, of the Cornelia tribe, pious, lived for 20 years and 10 months, he is buried here.
EDCS-26900633.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the departed spirits, recording the death and age of Lucius Caecilius Blandianus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-26900659.text_edition: \n Iunoni Liviae Augusti sacrum Lucio Passieno Rufo imperatore Africam obtinente Cnaeus Cornelius Cnaei filius Cornelia Rufus et Maria Cai filia Galla Cnaei conservati vota libentes merito solvont sic\n
EDCS-26900659.translation: To Juno. Cnaeus Cornelius Rufus, son of Cnaeus, of the Cornelia tribe, and Maria Galla, daughter of Caius, together with Cnaeus, give thanks for their deliverance and willingly fulfill their vows, with Lucius Passienus Rufus as governor of Africa.
EDCS-26900659.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Juno, recording the fulfillment of vows by Cnaeus Cornelius Rufus and Maria Galla during the governorship of Lucius Passienus Rufus in Africa, likely dating to the late Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-26900662.translation: Flavia Saturnina, daughter of Titus, dutiful, lived 80 years, is buried here.
EDCS-26900662.summary: A tombstone recording the death of Flavia Saturnina, who lived 80 years.

EDCS-26900663.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Primus was my name while life remained; robbed of the light of heaven, I now rest below, secure, with no further danger of life. My mind was pure and my will maintained. Primus.
EDCS-26900663.summary: A funerary inscription, likely on a tombstone, of a person named Primus who reflects on his life and death.

EDCS-26900664.translation: Luillimmas Tinus lived 75 years, is buried here.

EDCS-26900668.translation: and for the dedication, they gave gifts to the town councillors and a feast to the members of the council.
