EDCS-27600019.translation: For Antoninus Pius Augustus, for the health of the entire household, [---] I am all.
EDCS-27600019.summary: This inscription is a dedication for the health of an entire household, likely made during the reign of Antoninus Pius.

EDCS-27600020.summary: This is a personal name, likely referring to the emperor Marcus Aurelius Antoninus.

EDCS-27600021.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Domitia Prima lived for 12 years, more or less.
EDCS-27600021.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Domitia Prima, who died at approximately 12 years old.

EDCS-27600022.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Caius Iulius Arpastus lived for 70 years.
EDCS-27600022.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Caius Iulius Arpastus, who died at 70 years old.

EDCS-27600023.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Agonia, son of Magni, lived for 18 years.
EDCS-27600023.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Agonia, son of Magni, who died at 18 years old.

EDCS-27600024.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Egnatia Lais lived for 20 years.
EDCS-27600024.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Egnatia Lais, who died at 20 years old.

EDCS-27600028.translation: To our Lords Diocletian, Maximian, the Pious, Fortunate, Senior Augusti, and to the eternal Maxentius, Victorious, and to Flavius Valerius Constantinus, most noble Caesar.
EDCS-27600028.summary: This inscription records acclamations to several Roman emperors, including Diocletian, Maximian, Maxentius, and Constantine, likely from the Tetrarchic period or early 4th century.

EDCS-27600030.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Gaius Valerius Diocletian, Pious, Fortunate, Unconquered Augustus, high priest, holder of tribunician power, consul, father of the fatherland, proconsul, and to the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Valerius Maximian, Pious, Fortunate, Unconquered Augustus, high priest, holder of tribunician power, consul, father of the fatherland, proconsul, publicly from Tacapa, six Roman miles.
EDCS-27600030.summary: This inscription is a dedication to emperors Diocletian and Maximian, possibly marking the construction of a road or milestone indicating distance from Tacapa, likely during their co-reign in the late 3rd or early 4th century.

EDCS-27600038.translation: To our lord and emperor Constantine the Great, Invictus, Pious, Happy Augustus, founder of the public good. To our lord Magnus Decentius Caesar. (Dated) 8.
EDCS-27600038.summary: This is a dedicatory inscription honoring Emperor Constantine the Great and Caesar Magnus Decentius, likely a milestone or boundary marker from the 4th century AD.

EDCS-27600040.translation: To the Emperor Flavius Valentinianus, Pious, Fortunate, Always Augustus, for the ninth time.
EDCS-27600040.summary: This inscription likely refers to Emperor Valentinian III, possibly related to an honorific or consular dating from the 5th century.

EDCS-27600042.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Gaius Messius Decius Traianus, Pious, Fortunate, Unconquered Augustus, high priest, holder of tribunician power, father of the fatherland, proconsul, for the eleventh time.
EDCS-27600042.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Emperor Decius, possibly marking a public work or honor, with dating from his consulship in the mid-3rd century.

EDCS-27600044.translation: To our Lord Constantinus, father of the fatherland, Victor, born for the good of the state.
EDCS-27600044.summary: This inscription honors Emperor Constantine I, praising his rule and dedication to the Roman state, likely from the early 4th century.

EDCS-27600045.translation: To our lord Constantine the Great, Victor, Ever Augustus, founder of the public good. (Dated) 10.
EDCS-27600045.summary: This is a dedicatory inscription honoring Emperor Constantine the Great, likely a milestone or boundary marker from the early 4th century AD.

EDCS-27600046.translation: To the deified Constantinus, the Great Victor, always Augustus, born for the good of the state.
EDCS-27600046.summary: This inscription honors the deified Emperor Constantine I, celebrating his victory and his beneficial rule, likely from the mid-4th century after his death and deification.

EDCS-27600047.translation: To our most esteemed father of the fatherland, the unconquered Augustus, Constantius.
EDCS-27600047.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Emperor Constantius as "father of the fatherland" and "invictus", likely from the 4th century CE.

EDCS-27600049.translation: To our lord Valens, the pious, fortunate Augustus.
EDCS-27600049.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Emperor Valens, referring to him as "lord", "pious", and "fortunate", likely from the 4th century CE.

EDCS-27600050.translation: To Flavius Constantius, most noble and most fortunate Caesar, founder of the public good. (Dated illegible).
EDCS-27600050.summary: This is a dedicatory inscription honoring Caesar Flavius Constantius, likely dating to the period of the Tetrarchy or early 4th century AD.

EDCS-27600051.translation: To the most fortunate Caesar, born for the good of the republic.
EDCS-27600051.summary: This is an honorific inscription for a Caesar, praising him as "most fortunate" and beneficial to the state, likely from the 3rd or 4th century CE.

EDCS-27600061.translation: Emperor Caesar Probus, the pontifex maximus, father of the fatherland, twice proconsul, the great Adiabenian.
EDCS-27600061.summary: This inscription lists the titles of Emperor Probus, including his victory titles and provincial governance, dating to his reign (276-282 CE).

EDCS-27600062.translation: Emperor Caesar Marcus Julius Philippus Pius Felix Augustus, chief priest, with tribunician power, consul, father of the fatherland, and Marcus Julius Philippus, the most noble Caesar, restored [this monument].
EDCS-27600062.summary: This inscription records the restoration of a monument by Emperor Philip the Arab and his son, Caesar Philip, during their joint rule in the mid-3rd century CE.

EDCS-27600064.summary: This is a simple inscription bearing the name and titles of Emperor Marcus Aurelius Antoninus (Caracalla), likely from the early 3rd century CE.

EDCS-27600065.translation: To our lord Flavius Constantinus, the pious, fortunate victor, born for the good of the republic, always Augustus.
EDCS-27600065.summary: This inscription honors Emperor Constantine I as "lord", "pious", "fortunate victor", and "father of the fatherland", likely from the early 4th century CE.

EDCS-27600068.translation: To the father of the fatherland, the proconsul.
EDCS-27600068.summary: This inscription is a dedication to an unnamed individual holding the title "father of the fatherland" and serving as proconsul, dating uncertain but likely imperial period.

EDCS-27600074.translation: To Flavius Constantinus, the pious, fortunate victor, always Augustus, our lord, born for the good of the republic.
EDCS-27600074.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Emperor Constantine I, praising his virtues and role as "lord" and "father of the fatherland", likely from the early 4th century CE.

EDCS-27600075.translation: To our lords Flavius Constantius and Galerius Valerius Maximianus, the most noble Caesars, Augusti.
EDCS-27600075.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Emperors Constantius I and Maximian as "lords" and "Caesars", likely from the late 3rd or early 4th century CE.

EDCS-27600077.translation: To our lord Flavius Claudius Julianus, most noble Caesar.
EDCS-27600077.summary: This inscription honors Flavius Claudius Julianus as Caesar, likely dating to his period of co-rule.

EDCS-27600081.translation: To our lord Flavius Claudius Julianus, pious, happy, always Augustus.
EDCS-27600081.summary: This inscription honors Flavius Claudius Julianus as Augustus, likely dating to his period of sole rule or co-rule with high titles.

EDCS-27600082.translation: To our lord Constantine, greatest, victorious, always Augustus, born for the good of the state.
EDCS-27600082.summary: This inscription praises Constantine as Augustus, emphasizing his victory and role in protecting the state, likely dating to his reign.

EDCS-27600084.translation: For the health and safety of our lords Diocletian and Maximian, Augusti.
EDCS-27600084.summary: This inscription records a prayer for the well-being of the co-emperors Diocletian and Maximian, dating to their joint rule.

EDCS-27600085.translation: To the emperor, our lord Flavius Claudius Julianus, always Augustus.
EDCS-27600085.summary: This inscription dedicates a monument to Flavius Claudius Julianus as Emperor Augustus, likely during his reign.

EDCS-27600086.translation: To our lord Flavius Constantius, most noble and most fortunate Caesar, born for the good of the state.
EDCS-27600086.summary: This inscription honors Flavius Constantius as Caesar, highlighting his noble status and dedication to the state, likely dating to his time as Caesar.

EDCS-27600089.translation: To our lord Flavius Julius Crispus, most noble Caesar.
EDCS-27600089.summary: This inscription honors Flavius Julius Crispus as Caesar, indicating a significant period of his career, likely during the Tetrarchy.

EDCS-27600090.translation: To our lord Flavius Julius Crispus.
EDCS-27600090.summary: This is a brief dedication to Flavius Julius Crispus, likely as Caesar or a distinguished figure.

EDCS-27600091.translation: To our lord Emperor Caesar Flavius Valerius Constantius, Pious, Happy, Invictus Augustus, chief priest, with tribunician power for the 14th time, consul for the 6th time, father of the fatherland, proconsul. (Damaged).
EDCS-27600091.summary: This is a formal inscription detailing the titles and powers of Emperor Constantius I, likely from the late 3rd or early 4th century AD.

EDCS-27600093.translation: To the emperor, Caesar Lucius Domitius Aurelianus, pious, happy, Augustus, chief priest, holder of tribunician power, father of the country, consul, proconsul; twenty-five miles.
EDCS-27600093.summary: This inscription marks a milestone (miliarium) for Emperor Aurelian, detailing his numerous titles and indicating a road distance of 25 miles, dating to his reign.

EDCS-27600094.translation: Of the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Numerianus, pious, happy.
EDCS-27600094.summary: This inscription is a fragmentary dedication or possessive statement related to Emperor Marcus Aurelius Numerianus, dating to his co-rule with Carinus.

EDCS-27600095.translation: Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus, greatest conqueror of Britain, greatest conqueror of Germany, with tribunician power for the 19th time, consul for the 3rd time, restored. (Dated) 19.
EDCS-27600095.summary: This inscription records the titles and accomplishments of Emperor Caracalla, including his victories and dating his tribunician power and consulship, likely from the early 3rd century AD.

EDCS-27600096.translation: To the grandson of the deified Marcus Antoninus, great-grandson of the deified Antoninus Pius, great-great-grandson of the deified Hadrian, great-great-great-grandson of the deified Trajan Parthicus Maximus and the deified Nerva, Pius Felix Augustus, Parthicus Maximus, Britannicus Maximus, Germanicus Maximus, Pontifex Maximus, with tribunician power for the 19th time, Imperator for the 3rd time, Consul for the 4th time, Father of the Fatherland, Proconsul, 33 miles.
EDCS-27600096.summary: This inscription records the construction of a road 33 miles long, dedicated to the emperor Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus in his 19th year of tribunician power.

EDCS-27600099.translation: To Emperor Caesar Flavius Valerius Constantine Pius Felix.
EDCS-27600099.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Emperor Constantine I, likely part of a larger monument.

EDCS-27600100.translation: Emperor Caesar Marcus Opellius Severus Macrinus Pius Felix Augustus, Consul II, and Marcus Opellius Antoninus Diadumenianus Caesar, IIIIX [either 14 or 18?], established a new paved road.
EDCS-27600100.summary: This inscription records the establishment of a new paved road by Emperors Macrinus and Diadumenianus in their second consulship.

EDCS-27600102.translation: To the unconquered and eternal Emperors Diocletian and Maximian Augusti, the colony Septimia Vagensis.
EDCS-27600102.summary: This inscription is a dedication from the colony of Septimia Vagensis to the Emperors Diocletian and Maximian, likely dating to their joint rule.

EDCS-27600104.translation: To M C ORAC VMA, always Augustus, LX.
EDCS-27600104.summary: This fragmentary inscription is a dedication to an emperor referred to as 'always Augustus', with a numerical value of LX (60).

EDCS-27600106.translation: To our lord Valerius Licinianus Licinius the Younger, most noble Caesar, the colony of Vallis Numini, devoted.
EDCS-27600106.summary: This inscription is a dedication from the colony of Vallis Numini to their lord, the Caesar Valerius Licinianus Licinius Iunior.

EDCS-27600114.translation: Emperor Caesar Marcus Antonius Gordianus, grandson of the divine Gordian, son of the sister of the divine Gordian, Pius Felix Augustus, chief priest, with tribunician power, consul, proconsul, father of the fatherland.
EDCS-27600114.summary: This inscription details the full imperial titles and lineage of Emperor Gordian III, likely dating to his reign in the mid-3rd century AD.

EDCS-27600122.translation: Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurellius Antoninus Pius Augustus, Parthicus Maximus, Britannicus Maximus, Germanicus Maximus, with tribunician power for the 19th time, Consul IIII, Father of the Fatherland, restored LXVI [either 66 miles or a building].
EDCS-27600122.summary: This inscription records the restoration of a road or structure covering 66 units (miles or building blocks) by Emperor Caracalla in his 19th year of tribunician power.

EDCS-27600126.translation: To Emperor Constantius Pius Felix Augustus.
EDCS-27600126.summary: This is a dedication to Emperor Constantius I, likely part of a larger monument.

EDCS-27600128.translation: Emperor Caesar Marcus Antonius Gordianus, grandson of the deified Gordian, son of the sister of the deified Gordian, the Unconquered, Pius Felix Augustus, Pontifex Maximus, with tribunician power.
EDCS-27600128.summary: This inscription records the titles and lineage of Emperor Gordian III, emphasizing his divine ancestry and imperial dignities.

EDCS-27600129.translation: To our lord Maxentius, the Unconquered, Pius Felix Augustus.
EDCS-27600129.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the emperor Maxentius, highlighting his epithets of 'Unconquered' and 'Pius Felix'.

EDCS-27600130.translation: Emperor Caesar Hadrian, son of the deified Nerva, grandson of the deified Trajan Parthicus, high priest, with tribunician power for the 7th time, consul for the 3rd time, paved the road from Carthage to Theveste through the Legio III Augusta, with Publius Metilius Secundus as governor (legatus Augusti pro praetore).
EDCS-27600130.summary: This inscription records Emperor Hadrian's paving of a road from Carthage to Theveste, completed by Legio III Augusta under governor Publius Metilius Secundus, likely in the early 2nd century CE.

EDCS-27600137.translation: Emperor Caesar Gordian, grandson of the deified Gordian, son of his sister the deified Gordian, Pious, Fortunate, Augustus, supreme pontiff, with tribunician power for the 3rd time, consul, proconsul, restored this.
EDCS-27600137.summary: This inscription states that Emperor Gordian restored something, indicating his authority and titles, likely dating to his reign in the mid-3rd century CE.

EDCS-27600138.translation: To the August, Marcus Aurelius Carinus, most noble.
EDCS-27600138.summary: This is a dedication to Marcus Aurelius Carinus, a noble figure, likely a military or imperial honor, dating to the late 3rd century CE.

EDCS-27600141.translation: Emperor Caesar Trajan Hadrianus Augustus, grandson of the divine Nerva, son of the divine Trajan Parthicus, chief priest, with tribunician power for the 7th time, consul for the 3rd time, paved the road from Carthage to Theveste by means of the Legio III Augusta, under Publius Metilius Secundus, governor. (Dated) 82.
EDCS-27600141.summary: This inscription records Emperor Hadrian's paving of a road from Carthage to Theveste by Legio III Augusta, under the governorship of P. Metilius Secundus, likely dating to the 2nd century AD and possibly referencing a distance of 82 miles.

EDCS-27600142.translation: To Emperor Caesar Publius Licinius Valerianus, Pious, Fortunate, Augustus, supreme pontiff, with tribunician power, consul for the 2nd time, father of the fatherland, father of our lord Emperor Caesar Pious Licinius Gallienus Pious, Fortunate.
EDCS-27600142.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Emperor Valerian, listing his titles and acknowledging his son Gallienus as emperor, dating to their joint reign in the mid-3rd century CE.

EDCS-27600143.translation: Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Claudius, Pious, Fortunate, Augustus, father of the fatherland, supreme pontiff, with tribunician power, consul.
EDCS-27600143.summary: This inscription lists the titles of Emperor Claudius Gothicus, likely a dedication or record of his achievements during his reign in the late 3rd century CE.

EDCS-27600144.summary: This is a brief dedication to an "Unconquered Augustus," likely an emperor receiving divine honors, with a numerical value possibly indicating a significant milestone or length of reign, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-27600148.text_edition: \n Imperator Caesar divi Nervae nepos divi Traiani Parthici filius Traianus Hadrianus Augustus pontifex maximus tribunicia potestate VII consul III viam a Karthagine Thevestem stravit per legionem III Augustam Publio Metilio Secundo legato Augusti pro praetore\n
EDCS-27600148.translation: Emperor Caesar, grandson of the divine Nerva, son of the divine Trajan Parthicus, Trajan Hadrian Augustus, chief priest, with the tribunician power for the 7th time, consul for the 3rd time, paved the road from Carthage to Theveste, through Legio III Augusta, with Publius Metilius Secundus as his legate with the power of a propraetor.
EDCS-27600148.summary: This inscription records the paving of a road by Emperor Hadrian, undertaken by Legio III Augusta.

EDCS-27600149.translation: Emperor Caesar, Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus, Parthicus Maximus, Britannicus Maximus, Germanicus Maximus, with tribunician power.
EDCS-27600149.summary: This is a titulary inscription of Emperor Marcus Aurelius Antoninus, listing his adopted names and honors, with an incomplete record of his tribunician power.

EDCS-27600150.translation: Emperor Caesar, Gaius Messius Quintus Decius Trajanus Pius Felix Augustus, chief priest, [greatest of the greatest], father of the fatherland, [in his] 85th year.
EDCS-27600150.summary: This is a titulary inscription of Emperor Decius, listing his titles and noting a date related to his reign, likely an era or year count.

EDCS-27600151.translation: Of Emperor Caesar, Gaius Messius Quintus Decius Trajanus Pius Felix Augustus, chief priest, father of the fatherland, with tribunician power, [in his] 86th year.
EDCS-27600151.summary: This is a titulary inscription of Emperor Decius, listing his titles and noting a date related to his reign, likely an era or year count.

EDCS-27600152.translation: To our Perpetual, Pious, Fortunate, Unconquered Emperor Augustus, Lucius Domitius Aurelianus.
EDCS-27600152.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Emperor Aurelian, emphasizing his divine and enduring qualities, dating to his reign in the late 3rd century CE.

EDCS-27600153.translation: To Emperor Caesar Gaius Valerius Diocletianus, Pious, Fortunate, Augustus, consul, with tribunician power.
EDCS-27600153.summary: This is a dedication to Emperor Diocletian, listing his imperial titles, likely dating to the beginning of his reign in the late 3rd century CE.

EDCS-27600156.translation: To our Lords Maximian and Victor, the Pious, Fortunate, Perpetual, Ever-Augustus, the municipality of Agbium, devoted to their divine majesty and authority.
EDCS-27600156.summary: This inscription shows the municipality of Agbium dedicating itself to the emperors Maximian and Victor (likely Maximian and his son Crispus or another co-emperor), dating to the early 4th century CE.

EDCS-27600159.translation: Emperor Caesar Gaius Messius Traianus Decius, Pious, Fortunate, Augustus, supreme pontiff, with tribunician power, father of the fatherland.
EDCS-27600159.summary: This inscription records the titles of Emperor Trajan Decius, likely a dedication or monument from his reign in the mid-3rd century CE.

EDCS-27600160.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Publius Licinius Valerianus, pious, fortunate, Augustus, chief priest, with tribunician power, consul for the second time, father of the fatherland.
EDCS-27600160.summary: This inscription honors Emperor Valerian with his titles, likely on a public monument.

EDCS-27600161.translation: To our strongest Emperor and peacemaker of the city, Marcus Claudius Tacitus, pious, fortunate, Augustus, 89.
EDCS-27600161.summary: This inscription honors Emperor Tacitus, possibly on a public building or monument, dated by the number 89.

EDCS-27600162.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Probus, pious, fortunate, Augustus, chief priest, with tribunician power.
EDCS-27600162.summary: This inscription records titles for Emperor Probus, likely part of a dedication or honorific monument.

EDCS-27600164.translation: To our Lord Theodosius, the Great, pious, fortunate, victorious, forever Augustus, the municipality of Mustis, born for the good of the state.
EDCS-27600164.summary: This inscription is a civic dedication from the municipality of Mustis to Emperor Theodosius I, praising him for the good of the state.

EDCS-27600165.translation: The Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus, Parthicus Maximus, Britannicus Maximus, Germanicus Maximus, for the 19th time consul for the third time, father of the fatherland, restored (this) 90.
EDCS-27600165.summary: This inscription, likely from a building or monument, records Emperor Caracalla's titles and his restoration activities, dated by the number 90.

EDCS-27600167.translation: To our Lords, the forever Augusti Emperors Constantius and Maximianus, 92. And Marcus Iulius Philippus, most noble Caesar, prince of youth, and Marcia Otacilia Severa Augusta, wife of our Augustus, and mother of our Caesar, and of the camps, and of the senate, and of the fatherland, 92.
EDCS-27600167.summary: This complex inscription honors multiple members of the imperial family, likely from a monument erected during the reigns of Constantius and Maximian, dated by the number 92.

EDCS-27600171.translation: To our Lords, the forever Augusti Emperors Constantius and Maximianus, 92.
EDCS-27600171.summary: This is a dedication to Emperors Constantius and Maximian, likely on a public monument, dated by the number 92.

EDCS-27600173.translation: The Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus.
EDCS-27600173.summary: This inscription simply lists the titles of Emperor Caracalla, likely part of a larger text or a simple dedication.

EDCS-27600174.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Gaius Messius Quintus Decius Traianus Pius Felix Augustus, chief priest, with tribunician power.
EDCS-27600174.summary: This inscription records the titles of Emperor Decius, likely on a public monument.

EDCS-27600175.translation: 86. To Marcus Aurelius Valerius Maximianus, pious, fortunate, Augustus, chief priest, with tribunician power, proconsul.
EDCS-27600175.summary: This inscription honors Emperor Maximian with his titles, likely part of a public monument, dated by the number 86.

EDCS-27600176.summary: This is a dedication to the emperor Antoninus, likely dating to the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-27600179.translation: To our most peaceful, most Pious, Fortunate, and unconquered Emperor Domitius Aurelianus
EDCS-27600179.summary: This inscription honors Emperor Aurelian, known for his military successes and administrative reforms, likely dating to his reign (270-275 CE).

EDCS-27600180.translation: To Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Carus, the Unconquered, Pious, and Fortunate Augustus, Pontifex Maximus, Father of the Fatherland, for the second time, and to Marcus Aurelius Carinus, his most noble son, Caesar, and to Marcus Aurelius Numerian, most noble Caesar
EDCS-27600180.summary: This inscription honors the emperors Carus and his sons Carinus and Numerian, likely dating to their joint reign in the late 3rd century CE.

EDCS-27600181.translation: To Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Severus Alexander, the Pious, Fortunate, and Unconquered Augustus, Pontifex Maximus, Father of the Fatherland, holding tribunician power for the second time, Consul, Proconsul
EDCS-27600181.summary: This inscription honors Emperor Severus Alexander, dating to his reign (222-235 CE), likely commemorating a public work or dedication.

EDCS-27600182.translation: To our most valiant Emperor and peacemaker of the city, Marcus Claudius Tacitus, the Pious and Fortunate Augustus
EDCS-27600182.summary: This inscription honors Emperor Tacitus, praising him as a peacemaker, likely dating to his short reign (275-276 CE).

EDCS-27600184.translation: To our Lords, the Emperors Constantius and Maximian, ever Augustuses
EDCS-27600184.summary: This inscription honors the co-emperors Constantius I and Maximian, likely dating to the period of the Tetrarchy (late 3rd to early 4th century CE).

EDCS-27600186.translation: To our Lord Flavius Valerius Constantius
EDCS-27600186.summary: This inscription honors Emperor Constantius I (Constantius Chlorus), likely dating to his reign as Augustus (305-306 CE).

EDCS-27600188.summary: This inscription honors Emperor Constantine I (the Great), likely dating to his reign as Augustus (307-337 CE).

EDCS-27600189.translation: To our most peaceful Emperor Lucius Domitius Aurelianus, the Pious, Fortunate, and Unconquered Augustus
EDCS-27600189.summary: This inscription honors Emperor Aurelian, likely dating to his reign (270-275 CE) and possibly related to military victories.

EDCS-27600190.summary: This inscription honors Emperor Constantius I (Constantius Chlorus), possibly dating to his reign as Caesar or Augustus in the late 3rd or early 4th century CE.

EDCS-27600193.translation: To our lord Flavius Claudius Constantius, most noble Caesar.
EDCS-27600193.summary: This is an honorary inscription dedicated to the Caesar Flavius Claudius Constantius, likely dating to the mid-4th century CE.

EDCS-27600194.translation: To our lords Flavius Valerius Constantinus, unconquered Augusti of the Germans and Sarmatians.
EDCS-27600194.summary: This is an honorary inscription dedicated to the Augusti Flavius Valerius Constantinus, likely dating to the early 4th century CE.

EDCS-27600195.translation: To our perpetual emperor, Lucius Domitius Aurelianus, pious, fortunate, unconquered Augustus.
EDCS-27600195.summary: This is an honorary inscription dedicated to the emperor Lucius Domitius Aurelianus, dating to his reign in the late 3rd century CE.

EDCS-27600196.summary: This is an honorary inscription dedicated to the Caesar Constantius, likely dating to the mid-4th century CE.

EDCS-27600197.translation: To the strongest emperor and pacifier of the world, Marcus Claudius Tacitus, pious, fortunate, unconquered Augustus.
EDCS-27600197.summary: This is an honorary inscription dedicated to the emperor Marcus Claudius Tacitus, dating to his brief reign in 275-276 CE.

EDCS-27600198.translation: To our lords Flavius Valentinianus and Valens, triumphant, perpetual Augusti.
EDCS-27600198.summary: This is an honorary inscription dedicated to the co-emperors Flavius Valentinianus and Valens, likely dating to the mid-to-late 4th century CE.

EDCS-27600202.translation: To the perpetual emperor Lucius Domitius Aurelianus.
EDCS-27600202.summary: This is an honorary inscription dedicated to the emperor Lucius Domitius Aurelianus, dating to his reign in the late 3rd century CE.

EDCS-27600206.translation: To the emperors, Caesars, our lords Gallus and Volusianus.
EDCS-27600206.summary: This is an honorary inscription dedicated to the co-emperors Gallus and Volusianus, dating to their joint reign in 251-253 CE.

EDCS-27600207.translation: To the most unconquered and most pious emperor, Caesar Marcus Claudius Tacitus, pious, fortunate Augustus.
EDCS-27600207.summary: This is an honorary inscription dedicated to the emperor Marcus Claudius Tacitus, dating to his brief reign in 275-276 CE.

EDCS-27600209.translation: Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Augustus, great conqueror of the Parthians, great conqueror of the Britons, great conqueror of the Germans, holding tribunician power for the 19th time, consul for the 4th time, father of the country, restored (this).
EDCS-27600209.summary: This is a dedicatory inscription by Emperor Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Augustus, detailing his titles and achievements, likely dating to 179 CE.

EDCS-27600221.translation: To our lord Flavius Valerius Constantius, divine Galerius Maximianus.
EDCS-27600221.summary: This is a dedication to the emperors Constantius and Maximianus, likely erected in the early 4th century CE.

EDCS-27600222.translation: To our most peaceful lord Lucius Domitius Aurelianus, pious, fortunate Augustus.
EDCS-27600222.summary: This inscription honors the emperor Aurelian, dating to his reign in the late 3rd century CE.

EDCS-27600223.translation: To our perpetual emperor Lucius Domitius Aurelianus, pious, fortunate, unconquered Augustus.
EDCS-27600223.summary: This inscription honors the emperor Aurelian, dating to his reign in the late 3rd century CE.

EDCS-27600224.translation: To our lords Flavius Valerius Constantinus.
EDCS-27600224.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Constantine I, likely from the early 4th century CE.

EDCS-27600225.translation: To our lord Flavius Claudius Julianus, pious, fortunate, always Augustus.
EDCS-27600225.summary: This inscription honors the emperor Julian, dating to his reign in the mid-4th century CE.

EDCS-27600226.translation: To our lord Flavius Claudius Julianus.
EDCS-27600226.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the emperor Julian, dating to the mid-4th century CE.

EDCS-27600227.translation: To the emperor, our fortunate Caesar Augustus.
EDCS-27600227.summary: This is a dedication to an emperor, likely from the late Roman period.

EDCS-27600228.translation: To our emperors, our lords Lucius Domitius Alexander and Flavius Constantinus, Augusti.
EDCS-27600228.summary: This inscription honors co-emperors Alexander Severus and Constantine I, dating to the early 4th century CE.

EDCS-27600229.translation: To our lord Magnus Decentius Caesar, pious, fortunate, always our Augustus.
EDCS-27600229.summary: This inscription honors the Caesar Decentius, brother of Magnentius, dating to the mid-4th century CE.

EDCS-27600230.translation: To Aurelius, the pacifier, holder of tribunician power, father of the fatherland, consul.
EDCS-27600230.summary: This inscription honors an individual named Aurelius, likely a high-ranking official, possibly from the 3rd century CE.

EDCS-27600231.translation: To the holder of tribunician power, father of the fatherland, consul, proconsul, and to Herennia Etruscilla, his Augusta, wife of our Augustus.
EDCS-27600231.summary: This inscription is a dedication to an emperor and his wife, likely from the 3rd century CE.

EDCS-27600232.translation: To the Great and Unconquered Emperor Caesar Valerius Diocletian, Unconquered, Pious, Fortunate Augustus, chief priest, with tribunician power for the 2nd time, consul for the 2nd time, proconsul for the 2nd time; and to Valerius Maximianus, Pious, Fortunate Augustus, with tribunician power for the 2nd time, consul, proconsul.
EDCS-27600232.summary: This inscription honors Emperors Diocletian and Maximian, likely commemorating joint consular or proconsular terms.

EDCS-27600233.translation: To our lords Flavius Valerius Constantius and Galerius Valerius Maximianus, most noble Caesars.
EDCS-27600233.summary: This inscription is a dedication to two Caesars, Constantius I and Galerius, likely from the late 3rd or early 4th century CE.

EDCS-27600237.translation: To our lord Magnentius, pious, happy, ever Augustus, the colony of Thunusuda devoted to his majesty.
EDCS-27600237.summary: This inscription is a dedication from the colony of Thunusuda to the emperor Magnentius, likely from the mid-4th century CE.

EDCS-27600239.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Flavius Claudius Julianus Augustus, the colony of Simitthus devoted. (First dedication?)
EDCS-27600239.summary: This inscription is a dedication from the colony of Simitthus to the emperor Julian, likely from the mid-4th century CE.

EDCS-27600240.translation: To our lord Flavius Delmatius, most noble Caesar. The colony of Simitthus devoted. (First dedication?) To the Emperors and Caesars, the Flavii Valentinianus and Valens, Augusti, the colony of Simitthus devoted. (First dedication?)
EDCS-27600240.summary: This inscription is a dedication from the colony of Simitthus to Caesar Delmatius and to the emperors Valentinian I and Valens, likely from the mid-4th century CE.

EDCS-27600241.translation: To Magnentius, ever Augustus. (Dedication?) IVL N. The colony of Simitthus devoted. (First dedication?)
EDCS-27600241.summary: This inscription is a dedication from the colony of Simitthus to the emperor Magnentius, likely from the mid-4th century CE.

EDCS-27600242.translation: Of the Emperor Caesar Caius Valerius Diocletianus, the Invincible, Augustus, the happy, consul, with tribunician power.
EDCS-27600242.summary: This inscription likely refers to Diocletian and his titles, possibly related to a consulship in the late 3rd century CE.

EDCS-27600245.translation: Hadrianus Augustus, chief priest, with tribunician power for the 13th time, consul for the 3rd time, father of the fatherland, made the road from Simitthu to Thabracam.
EDCS-27600245.summary: This inscription records a public works project by Emperor Hadrian, specifically the construction of a road, dated to his 13th tribunician power and 3rd consulship (around 128-129 CE).

EDCS-27600248.translation: To Flavius Claudius Constantius, most noble Caesar.
EDCS-27600248.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Caesar Constantius II, likely from the first half of the 4th century CE.

EDCS-27600289.translation: To Diocletianus, pious, happy, Augustus. (First dedication?)
EDCS-27600289.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the emperor Diocletian, likely from the late 3rd or early 4th century CE.

EDCS-27600297.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Magnus Magnentius, the Augustus.
EDCS-27600297.summary: This is a dedication to the emperor Magnentius, who reigned from 350-353 AD.

EDCS-27600303.translation: To the most sacred and invincible Emperors, from Valerius Maximinus, [son] of Titus Aelius Valerius Valerius, [and] the sons of Valerius Maximinus, to the Emperors.
EDCS-27600303.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the emperors by Valerius Maximinus and his sons, likely from the early 4th century AD.

EDCS-27800138.translation: To our Lords, Emperors Valentinian and Valens and Valentinian, eternal Augusti, during the proconsulship of Decimus Hesperius, most distinguished and most eminent man, proconsul of the province of Africa, by the legation of Macius Rufinus, most distinguished man, splendid legate of Carthage: the portico of the forum, a part of which had long been in existence, was now restored, embellished, and dedicated to a better state of cultivation by Gabinius Benignus, curator of the republic, with the most devoted order.
EDCS-27800138.summary: This inscription, dating to the period of Emperors Valentinian and Valens (late 4th century CE), records the restoration and dedication of a forum portico in Carthage by Gabinius Benignus, the local curator, during the proconsulship of Decimus Hesperius and the legation of Macius Rufinus.

EDCS-27800149.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari divi Marci Antonini Pii Germanici Sarmatici filio divi Commodi fratri divi Antonini Pii nepoti divi Hadriani pronepoti divi Traiani Parthici abnepoti divi Nervae adnepoti Lucio Septimio Severo Pio Pertinaci Augusto Arabico Adiabenico pontifici maximo tribunicia potestate VI imperatori XI consuli II proconsuli optimo maximoque principi patri Imperatoris Caesaris Marci Aureli Antonini Augusti principis iuventutis et Publi Septimi Getae nobilissimi Caesaris pagus Thibaritanus decreto decurionum pecunia publica\n
EDCS-27800149.translation: To Emperor Caesar, son of the divine Marcus Antoninus Pius Germanicus Sarmaticus, brother of the divine Commodus, grandson of the divine Antoninus Pius, great-grandson of the divine Hadrian, great-great-grandson of the divine Trajan Parthicus, descendant of the divine Nerva, Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus Arabicus Adiabenicus, chief priest, with tribunician power for the 6th time, imperator for the 11th time, consul for the 2nd time, proconsul, the best and greatest prince, father of Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus, prince of youth, and of Publius Septimius Geta, most noble Caesar, by decree of the decurions of the pagus Thibaritanus, at public expense.
EDCS-27800149.summary: This inscription records a dedication by the pagus Thibaritanus to Emperor Septimius Severus and his son Caracalla (as Caesar Geta), commemorating his imperial titles and paternal role.

EDCS-27800399.translation: To the great god Zeus Helios Sarapis and the associated gods, Publius Aurelius Dioscorus dedicated [this].
EDCS-27800399.summary: This inscription is a dedication by Publius Aurelius Dioscorus to Zeus Helios Sarapis and other gods, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE given the syncretic deity.

EDCS-27800403.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari Tito Aelio Hadriano Antonino Augusto Pio pontifici maximo tribunicia potestate XV imperatori II consuli IIII patri patriae Lepcitani publice\n
EDCS-27800403.translation: To Emperor Caesar Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Augustus Pius, chief priest, with tribunician power for the 15th time, imperator for the 2nd time, consul for the 4th time, father of the fatherland, by the people of Lepcis.
EDCS-27800403.summary: This inscription records a public dedication by the people of Lepcis to Emperor Antoninus Pius, listing his significant imperial titles.

EDCS-27800420.translation: Sacred to Neptune Augustus, for the safety of the Emperors Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus, and Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus Pius, and the most noble Caesar Publius Septimius Geta, and Julia Augusta, mother of our Augusti. Victorinus Getulicus Ianuarius, imperial slaves, made this at their own expense on their property, under the care of Ianuarius, their father, formerly one of the administrators.
EDCS-27800420.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Neptune Augustus for the imperial family's safety, made by imperial slaves Victorinus Getulicus Ianuarius and Ianuarius at their own expense, dating to the Severan period (early 3rd century CE).

EDCS-27800421.translation: On the estates of Lucius Memmius Victoricus and his sons, built and dedicated from the ground up, when Fuscus and Dexter were consuls.
EDCS-27800421.summary: This inscription records the construction and dedication of buildings or features on the estates of Lucius Memmius Victoricus and his sons, dating to the consulship of Fuscus and Dexter (likely 150 or 200 CE).

EDCS-27900289.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Azanneus lived 67 years and is buried here.
