EDCS-27900290.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Aurelius Mitun lived 85 years. Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Aurelia Peregrina lived 70 years.
EDCS-27900290.summary: This funerary inscription records the ages at death for Aurelius Mitun and Aurelia Peregrina.

EDCS-27900291.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Aurelius Victor, dutiful son of Stalli.
EDCS-27900291.summary: This funerary inscription honors Aurelius Victor, son of Stalli, and is dedicated to the Spirits of the Departed.

EDCS-27900292.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Berecte, daughter of Rogatus, lived 32 years and is buried here.
EDCS-27900292.summary: This funerary inscription records the age at death of Berecte, daughter of Rogatus, and states that she is buried here.

EDCS-27900293.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Iulius Mellus, son of Florentius, lived 13 years. Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Garvilia Marcella lived 51 years.
EDCS-27900293.summary: This funerary inscription records the ages at death for Iulius Mellus, son of Florentius, and Garvilia Marcella.

EDCS-27900294.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Caius Postumius Cosconius lived 59 years and is buried here.
EDCS-27900294.summary: This funerary inscription records the age at death of Caius Postumius Cosconius and states that he is buried here.

EDCS-27900295.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Lucius Postumius Paemulus, dutiful son of Ianuarius, died in Rome, lived 21 years and is buried here.
EDCS-27900295.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Lucius Postumius Paemulus in Rome, his age at death, and that he is buried here.

EDCS-27900296.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Raphia, daughter of Nini, lived 52 years and is buried here.
EDCS-27900296.summary: This funerary inscription records the age at death of Raphia, daughter of Nini, and states that she is buried here.

EDCS-27900297.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Rogatus, son of Marcius, dutiful, lived 80 years.
EDCS-27900297.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Rogatus, son of Marcius, who lived 80 years.

EDCS-27900298.translation: Secundus, son of Secundus, lived 103 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-27900298.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Secundus, son of Secundus, who lived 103 years.

EDCS-27900299.translation: Monument of GEN, dutiful, lived 36 years.
EDCS-27900299.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for GEN, who lived 36 years.

EDCS-27900300.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Ebuza Marina lived 81 years. Sacred to the Divine Shades. Quintus Marcus Surh lived 51 years.
EDCS-27900300.summary: This inscription records two separate funerary epitaphs for Ebuza Marina and Quintus Marcus Surh.

EDCS-27900301.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Annia, daughter of Lucius, dutiful, lived 37 years. Sabina lived 20 years; they are buried here.
EDCS-27900301.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Annia, daughter of Lucius, and Sabina, who lived 37 and 20 years respectively.

EDCS-27900302.translation: She is buried here. Sacred to the Divine Shades. Annibonia lived 8 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-27900302.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Annibonia, who lived 8 years.

EDCS-27900303.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Atilus Barihhas lived 75 years. Sacred to the Divine Shades. ximus is buried here.
EDCS-27900303.summary: This inscription records two separate funerary epitaphs, one for Atilus Barihhas and one for 'ximus'.

EDCS-27900304.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Annobal Harmatis lived [years]. Sacred to the Divine Shades. Aurelia Saturnina, dutiful, lived 75 years.
EDCS-27900304.summary: This inscription records two separate funerary epitaphs, one for Annobal Harmatis and one for Aurelia Saturnina.

EDCS-27900305.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Iulius Redulus lived 70 years; he is buried here. Sacred to the Divine Shades. Caelia Donata lived [years].
EDCS-27900305.summary: This inscription records two separate funerary epitaphs, one for Iulius Redulus and one for Caelia Donata.

EDCS-27900306.translation: Regilla, daughter of Bassus, dutiful, lived 65 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-27900306.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Regilla, daughter of Bassus, who lived 65 years.

EDCS-27900307.translation: To the departed spirits. Sabullina, devoted wife of Iulius Leporinus, lived for 30 years, 2 months, and 16 days.
EDCS-27900307.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Sabullina, wife of Iulius Leporinus.

EDCS-27900308.summary: A brief funerary epitaph stating the death of Aelpidice.

EDCS-27900309.translation: To the departed spirits. Iunia Berihbal lived for 17 years and is buried here.
EDCS-27900309.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan and burial of Iunia Berihbal.

EDCS-27900310.translation: To the departed spirits. Salvia Colomba, devoted, lived for 55 years. To the departed spirits. Quintus Flavius Ianuarius, devoted, lived for [---]. Flavius Barichan, son of O[---]A[---], devoted, lived for 7 years and is buried here.
EDCS-27900310.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespans of Salvia Colomba and Flavius Barichan, son of O[---]A[---].

EDCS-27900311.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the incomplete lifespan of Valeria Saturnina.

EDCS-27900312.translation: To the departed spirits. Gabinius Mustiolus lived for 26 years. To the departed spirits. Gabinius Clodianus lived for 18 years.
EDCS-27900312.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespans of Gabinius Mustiolus and Gabinius Clodianus.

EDCS-27900313.translation: To the departed spirits. Badius Rogatus... To the departed spirits. Albia Felicia.
EDCS-27900313.summary: A funerary epitaph mentioning Badius Rogatus and Albia Felicia, possibly recording their deaths or dedications.

EDCS-27900314.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Cornelia Marsa.

EDCS-27900315.translation: To the departed spirits. Iulia Sperata, daughter of Titus, lived for 75 years and is buried here. To the departed spirits. Lucius Marcius Calendarus lived for [---].
EDCS-27900315.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan and burial of Iulia Sperata and the incomplete lifespan of Lucius Marcius Calendarus.

EDCS-27900316.translation: To the departed spirits. Modia Romana lived for 91 years and is buried here.
EDCS-27900316.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan and burial of Modia Romana.

EDCS-27900318.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Publius Octavius Rogatus lived 86 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-27900318.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Publius Octavius Rogatus, who lived 86 years.

EDCS-27900319.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Octavia Birich lived 91 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-27900319.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Octavia Birich, who lived 91 years.

EDCS-27900320.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Rufina lived 80 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-27900320.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Rufina, who lived 80 years.

EDCS-27900321.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Volussia Prisca lived 15 years.
EDCS-27900321.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Volussia Prisca, who lived 15 years.

EDCS-27900322.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Firm, from the region of Calenus, [is recorded?].
EDCS-27900322.summary: A fragmentary funerary epitaph, possibly for a woman named Firma from the region of Calenus.

EDCS-27900399.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Fabia Urbica, dutiful, lived 70 years, 3 months, and 11 days; she is buried here.
EDCS-27900399.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Fabia Urbica, who lived 70 years, 3 months, and 11 days.

EDCS-27900400.summary: A very fragmentary inscription, possibly recording names of individuals.

EDCS-27900408.translation: Ocia, placed in peace, the day before the Kalends of June.
EDCS-27900408.summary: An epitaph recording the burial of Ocia on May 31st.

EDCS-27900423.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Lucius Papirius Victor, dutiful, lived 22 years and 7 months. Lucius Papirius Felix, 102.
EDCS-27900423.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the deaths of Lucius Papirius Victor (aged 22 years, 7 months) and Lucius Papirius Felix (aged 102).

EDCS-28000291.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Anconius Felix, pious, lived 29 years, rests here.
EDCS-28000291.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the death of Anconius Felix, who lived 29 years and is buried here.

EDCS-28000292.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Faust[us?].
EDCS-28000292.summary: A fragmentary funerary epitaph, likely for someone named Faustus.

EDCS-28000294.translation: To the everlasting emperors Constantine the Victorious and Triumphant and the most noble Caesars Constantius, Florus and Thigibba [set up?] devoted vows for twenty [years].
EDCS-28000294.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to the emperors Constantine and Constantius by Florus and Thigibba, likely dating to the 4th century CE.

EDCS-28000296.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Caius Iulius Optatus, dutiful, lived 106 years. Iulia Rogata lived 65 years. Mundus, his heir, is buried here.
EDCS-28000296.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the lives and burial of Caius Iulius Optatus, Iulia Rogata, and Mundus, his heir, likely dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-28000297.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Aemilia Rogata lived 75 years.
EDCS-28000297.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the lifespan of Aemilia Rogata, likely dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-28000298.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Marcus Calpurnius Liber lived 120 years.
EDCS-28000298.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the lifespan of Marcus Calpurnius Liber, likely dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-28000299.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the lifespan of M. Rufus, likely dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-28000300.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Iulia Publia lived 65 years. Copoti [and] sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Marcus Munatius Saturninus lived 51 years.
EDCS-28000300.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the lifespans of Iulia Publia and Marcus Munatius Saturninus, likely dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-28000301.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Ireria Saturnina lived 73 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-28000301.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the lifespan and burial of Ireria Saturnina, likely dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-28000302.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Calpurnia Nuscula lived 35 years. She is buried in this place. Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Caius Gallius Felix lived 87 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-28000302.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the lifespans and burials of Calpurnia Nuscula and Caius Gallius Felix, likely dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-28000303.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Anius Tertullus lived 47 years. He is buried here. Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Ania Pudentila lived 17 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-28000303.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the lifespans and burials of Anius Tertullus and Ania Pudentila, likely dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-28100181.summary: This is a brief inscription identifying Sergius as a merchant from Africa, likely dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-28100182.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely a tombstone or a milestone, identifying Sergius as a merchant.

EDCS-28100184.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely a tombstone or a milestone, identifying Todorus as a merchant.

EDCS-28100185.translation: Bishop Fortunius of the sixth region.
EDCS-28100185.summary: This inscription identifies Fortunius as a bishop and assigns him to the sixth region, possibly for administrative or ecclesiastical purposes.

EDCS-28100186.summary: This inscription identifies Victorianus as a bishop.

EDCS-28100191.translation: Our lord Theodosius, Pious, Happy, Augustus, for his 20th vows, [renewed for] many [years], 30 [and] 1.
EDCS-28100191.summary: This inscription records the twentieth anniversary (vicennalia) vows of Emperor Theodosius, likely celebrating his 20th year of rule, around the late 4th or early 5th century AD.

EDCS-28100192.summary: This inscription identifies Benedictus, likely a soldier or official, by his title 'domesticus'.

EDCS-28100254.translation: The gifts of God, Cresconius [made this].
EDCS-28100254.summary: This inscription appears to be a dedication, possibly for a religious building or artwork, crediting its creation to Cresconius as a gift of God.

EDCS-28200092.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Severus Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus, Germanicus, Pontifex Maximus, holding tribunician power, Imperator for the fourth time, Consul for the fourth time, Father of the Fatherland, Proconsul; and to Julia Augusta, mother of the Emperor, mother of the camp, and of the Senate and Fatherland, [honoured on] the 51st and 123rd day.
EDCS-28200092.summary: This is a formal dedication from 213 AD honouring Emperor Caracalla and his mother Julia Domna, likely for a public work or honour.

EDCS-28300490.translation: Emperor Caesar Gaius Julius Verus Maximinus Pius Felix Augustus, Germanicus Maximus, Sarmaticus Maximus, Dacicus Maximus, Pontifex Maximus, holding tribunician power for the 3rd time, Imperator for the 5th time; and Gaius Julius Verus Maximinus, most noble Caesar, Prince of Youth, Germanicus Maximus, Sarmaticus Maximus, Dacicus Maximus, restored the road from Carthage to the borders of the province of Numidia, which through long neglect had been corrupted and fallen into disrepair, on the 111th day.
EDCS-28300490.summary: This inscription from 236-238 AD records the restoration of a major road between Carthage and Numidia by Emperors Maximinus Thrax and his son Maximinus the Younger, highlighting their engineering and administrative efforts.

EDCS-28701407.translation: Whoever shall dedicate anything here, let his name be for a short time; Solomon the most excellent, and of the Tadvonid family, with desire, [let those who follow him] pursue with gold, and may they see the six hundred and twelfth [year?] of his monument.
EDCS-28701407.summary: This highly damaged and obscure inscription is a curious epitaph or warning, potentially from the 5th or 6th century AD, that attempts to curse those who desecrate the monument of Solomon and elevate the legacy of the deceased.

EDCS-30100059.translation: To the great god Sarapis, Publius Servius, the priest, from the society, dedicated a vow and offered two pillars with two lamps.
EDCS-30100059.summary: This is a votive inscription to Jupiter Sarapis by a priest from a society, dedicating pillars and lamps.

EDCS-30100060.text_edition: \n Quintus Titleis Cai filius Sarapi Isidi dedit\n
EDCS-30100060.translation: Quintus Titleis, son of Cai, gave [this] to Isis Sarapis.
EDCS-30100060.summary: This is a votive inscription recording Quintus Titleis dedicating something to the deity Isis Sarapis.

EDCS-30100061.text_edition: \n Claudius Syrapiacus votum solvit Claudius Syrapiacus votum solvit\n
EDCS-30100061.translation: Claudius Syrapiacus fulfilled [his] vow. Claudius Syrapiacus fulfilled [his] vow.
EDCS-30100061.summary: This is a votive inscription where Claudius Syrapiacus states that he fulfilled his vow, likely to a deity associated with Syrapiacus.

EDCS-30100063.translation: To Lord Saturn, in the street of Antistius, having undertaken a vow, Iu[---]n, son of Giaduris, made this statue.
EDCS-30100063.summary: This is a dedicatory inscription to Saturn by an individual named Iunius (restored), identified by his father Giaduris.

EDCS-30100065.text_edition: \n Dignae meritae ac obsequentissimae coniugi Felicitati Gaudentius fecit in pace\n
EDCS-30100065.translation: Gaudentius made [this] for his worthy, deserving, and most obedient wife, Felicitas, in peace.
EDCS-30100065.summary: This is a funerary inscription where Gaudentius dedicated a monument to his wife, Felicitas.

EDCS-30100066.text_edition: \n Dulcissimo compari Iulio Ianuario qui vicsit sic cum suis annis XXXII plus minus in pace requievit\n
EDCS-30100066.translation: Rest in peace, [my] dearest companion, Julius Ianuarius, who lived about 32 years with his own.
EDCS-30100066.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Julius Ianuarius, who lived approximately 32 years and is buried in peace.

EDCS-30100067.translation: Most beloved daughter Natalica lived in peace for 10 years, 8 months, 21 days. Placed on the 8th day before the Ides of October.
EDCS-30100067.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Natalica, recording her age and date of burial.

EDCS-30100068.translation: Rufius Bonifatius lived for 34 years in peace.
EDCS-30100068.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Rufius Bonifatius, recording his age and peaceful life.

EDCS-30100069.translation: Donatianus the husband made this for his most holy wife Aemilia Sabiniana, and Donatianus the father made this for his daughter Aelia Restituta.
EDCS-30100069.summary: This is a funerary inscription commemorating a wife and daughter, erected by the husband/father.

EDCS-30100070.translation: To Minerva Augusta, Quintus Aurelius Florentius and Aurelia Afrodite with their images.
EDCS-30100070.summary: This is a dedication to Minerva Augusta by a couple, Quintus Aurelius Florentius and Aurelia Afrodite, along with their statues.

EDCS-30100071.translation: For Quintus Agrius Rusticinus, an outstanding man, procurator of our Augustus in the province of Carthage, procurator of the private treasury throughout Italy, procurator of the private treasury of the province of Mauretania Caesariensis, also acting as vice-governor and procurator of the imperial poll tax, procurator of the twentieth of inheritances in the province of Narbonensis, procurator of the Laurentine and Ardeatine roads, also acting as vice-procurator of the twentieth of freedom, curator of the Pedana Septimia Valeriana road, and for his sons Quintus Agrius Valerianus Rusticinus, Roman knight, and Agria Aelia Valeriana, the best citizens of the municipality of Aureli Pheraditani Maioris.
EDCS-30100071.summary: This is a complex epitaph honoring Quintus Agrius Rusticinus and his children, detailing his extensive imperial administrative career.

EDCS-30100072.summary: This is a memorial inscription dedicated to Saint Maximinus.

EDCS-30100073.translation: In memory of Paschas the monk, who lived faithfully in peace for 20 years. Departed on the Ides of October.
EDCS-30100073.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Paschas the monk, recording his age and date of death.

EDCS-30100074.translation: Olumpius the priest lived faithfully in peace, more or less 50 years. Departed on the 4th day before the Kalends of February.
EDCS-30100074.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Olumpius the priest, recording his approximate age and date of death.

EDCS-30100076.translation: The most courageous and innocent, faithful, lived in peace for 9 months and 18 days. Departed on the 6th day before the Kalends of August.
EDCS-30100076.summary: This epitaph commemorates an individual who lived faithfully in peace for a specific duration before their death, with the date of departure recorded.

EDCS-30100077.translation: In memory of Alexander, a presbyter of CA IA, who lived in peace and of the body.
EDCS-30100077.summary: This inscription is a memorial for Alexander, a presbyter, noting his life in peace and possibly his physical state.

EDCS-30100078.translation: In memory of Nune, subdeacon, who lived in peace for 27 years, more or less. Departed on the 4th day before the Kalends of September.
EDCS-30100078.summary: This epitaph records the life and death of Nune, a subdeacon, stating his age at death and the date of his departure.

EDCS-30100079.translation: In memory of Iahini, monk, who lived in peace for 85 years, more or less. Departed on the 15th day before the Kalends of March.
EDCS-30100079.summary: This memorial inscription is for Iahini, a monk, indicating his age and the date of his death.

EDCS-30100081.translation: In memory of Amanti, faithful, lived in peace for 80 years, more or less.
EDCS-30100081.summary: This epitaph commemorates Amanti, a faithful individual, stating their lifespan in peace.

EDCS-30100082.translation: Libera, most sweet, ordered this memorial to be made for herself and lived in peace for 81 years and one month and 21 days.
EDCS-30100082.summary: This inscription records that Libera commissioned her own memorial and specifies her lifespan and peaceful existence.

EDCS-30100083.summary: This epitaph simply states that Victoria, who was faithful, lived in peace.

EDCS-30100084.translation: Archidomus made [this] in peace for six months.
EDCS-30100084.summary: This inscription records that Archidomus created something (likely a structure or monument) in peace over a period of six months.

EDCS-30100085.translation: Vincentius made [this] for 3 months and 6 days, who rests in peace in eternity.
EDCS-30100085.summary: This inscription records Vincentius's construction over a period of 3 months and 6 days, with a wish for his eternal peace.

EDCS-30100086.translation: Aselle, you innocently made [this] in peace for 30 days in eternity.
EDCS-30100086.summary: This inscription addresses Aselle, noting their innocent creation of something in peace for 30 days and its eternal nature.

EDCS-30100089.translation: You have done well in peace, innocent one.
EDCS-30100089.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for an innocent individual, possibly commemorating a virtuous life or a good deed.

EDCS-30100091.translation: Asselica, servant of God, lived in peace for 63 years and departed on the 8th day before the Kalends of February.
EDCS-30100091.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan and death date of Asselica, identified as a servant of God.

EDCS-30100092.translation: Ponticana, servant of God, lived in peace for 20 years more or less.
EDCS-30100092.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Ponticana, identified as a servant of God.

EDCS-30100093.translation: Paschasius the innocent lived for two years, he rested in peace.
EDCS-30100093.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Paschasius, who died at the age of two and is described as innocent and at peace.

EDCS-30100094.translation: Superianus lived in peace for three years, he departed on the 10th day before the Kalends of August.
EDCS-30100094.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan and departure date of Superianus.

EDCS-30100095.translation: Memory of Saint Cobuldeus the presbyter, who departed on the seventh Kalends, served in the presbytery for VI [years?].
EDCS-30100095.summary: This inscription commemorates Saint Cobuldeus, a presbyter, noting his death date and period of service.

EDCS-30100096.translation: Leontius the faithful lived for 35 years, he rested in peace on the 3rd day before the Nones.
EDCS-30100096.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan and death date of Leontius, identified as faithful.

EDCS-30100097.translation: lived in peace for two years and departed on the Kalends of January; Bictor lived in peace for 80 years more or less and departed on the 15th day before the Kalends of May.
EDCS-30100097.summary: This inscription contains two funerary notices, recording the lifespans and departure dates of two individuals.

EDCS-30100098.translation: Creschonius lived in peace for 60 years more or less, he departed on the 4th day before the Nones of July.
EDCS-30100098.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan and departure date of Creschonius.

EDCS-30100099.translation: ius the innocent lived in peace, faithful, for 25 months, departed on the 11th day before the Kalends of June; servant of God, in peace, faithful, for [X] years on the day of the Kalends of October.
EDCS-30100099.summary: This inscription combines funerary information for at least two individuals, one named ius and another described as a servant of God, detailing their lifespans and departure dates.

EDCS-30100100.translation: In memory of Tecoress, who lived faithfully in peace for more or less 70 years. Rests after the month of October.
EDCS-30100100.summary: This is a funerary inscription commemorating Tecoress and noting her lifespan and date of death, likely from late antiquity.

EDCS-30100101.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Gaius Gelasius vixit annos LXXII\n
EDCS-30100101.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Gaius Gelasius lived 72 years.
EDCS-30100101.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the death of Gaius Gelasius, who lived 72 years.

EDCS-30100102.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Caerellius Sextilius pius vixit annos XXII Faustinus pater\n
EDCS-30100102.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Caerellius Sextilius, pious, lived 22 years. His father Faustinus [dedicated this].
EDCS-30100102.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by Faustinus for his son, Caerellius Sextilius, who lived 22 years.

EDCS-30100103.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Fausti Acerotis fecit sibi et coniugi suae se vivente annis LXX sibi et coniugi suae annis LX\n
EDCS-30100103.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Faustus Acerotis made this for himself and his wife while he was alive, at age 70, and for himself and his wife, at age 60.
EDCS-30100103.summary: This funerary inscription records Faustus Acerotis dedicating a tomb for himself and his wife, specifying their ages at death.

EDCS-30100104.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Caius Minucius Fla Dis Manibus sacrum Minucia Iulia\n
EDCS-30100104.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Gaius Minucius Fla[...]. Sacred to the Divine Manes. Minucia Iulia.
EDCS-30100104.summary: This fragmented funerary inscription mentions Gaius Minucius and Minucia Iulia.

EDCS-30100105.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Namfamo vixit annos XXXVI \n
EDCS-30100105.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Namfamus lived for 36 years.
EDCS-30100105.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespan of Namfamus.

EDCS-30100106.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Munnia Saturnina vixit annis XXXX Lucius Caelius Praestans filius curavit\n
EDCS-30100106.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Munnia Saturnina lived for 40 years. Her son, Lucius Caelius Praestans, took care of this.
EDCS-30100106.summary: This funerary inscription records Munnia Saturnina's lifespan and states that her son, Lucius Caelius Praestans, arranged her burial.

EDCS-30100107.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Gaius Cannius Aris vixit annis LXXV hic situs est\n
EDCS-30100107.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Gaius Cannius Aris lived for 75 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-30100107.summary: This funerary inscription records Gaius Cannius Aris's lifespan and burial.

EDCS-30100109.summary: This short inscription records the name of the person who carved it, Gaius Allius Maialicus.

EDCS-30100110.text_edition: \n Imperator Caesar Caius Iulius Verus Maximinus Pius Felix Augustus Germanicus maximus Sarmaticus maximus Dacicus maximus pontifex maximus tribunicia potestate III imperator V et Caius Iulius Verus Maximus nobilissimus Caesar princeps iuventutis Germanicus maximus Sarmaticus maximus Dacicus maximus pontes vetustate conlabsos sic et iter longa incuria corruptum restituerunt et pro sua infatigabili providentia pervium commeantibus reddiderunt IIVX\n
EDCS-30100110.translation: Emperor Caesar Gaius Julius Verus Maximinus Pius Felix Augustus Germanicus maximus Sarmaticus maximus Dacicus maximus, pontifex maximus, holding tribunician power for the 3rd time, imperator for the 5th time, and Gaius Julius Verus Maximus, most noble Caesar, prince of youth, Germanicus maximus, Sarmaticus maximus, Dacicus maximus, restored the bridges which had collapsed from age and the road which had been corrupted by long neglect, and, by their tireless foresight, made them passable for travelers.
EDCS-30100110.summary: This inscription records the restoration of collapsed bridges and a neglected road by Emperors Maximinus Thrax and his son Maximus Caesar, likely from the early 3rd century AD.

EDCS-30100111.text_edition: \n Imperator Caesar Publius Licinius Egnatius Gallienus Pius Felix Augustus pontifex maximus tribunicia potestate III consul IIII Domino nostro Flavio Theudossius sic Augusto IIII\n
EDCS-30100111.translation: Emperor Caesar Publius Licinius Egnatius Gallienus Pius Felix Augustus, pontifex maximus, holding tribunician power for the 3rd time, consul for the 4th time, and our Lord Flavius Theodosius, Augustus for the 4th time.
EDCS-30100111.summary: This inscription lists the titles and honors of Emperor Gallienus and Emperor Theodosius II, likely dating from the mid-4th century AD.

EDCS-30100112.translation: Of Quintus Anicius Faustus and Caius Memmius Placidus.
EDCS-30100112.summary: This inscription appears to be a dedication or ownership marker, possibly for a building or monument, belonging to Quintus Anicius Faustus and Caius Memmius Placidus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-30100113.text_edition: \n Caio Iunio Faustino Placido Postumiano clarissimo viro cons(uli) adlecto inter comites Auggustorum nnostrorum sacerdoti Flaviali Titiali legato Auggustorum pro praetore provinciae Mysiae sic inferioris legato Auggustorum pro praetore provinciae Belgicae legato Auggustorum pro praetore provinciae Lusetaniae! legato Auggustorum legionis primae adiutricis piae fidelis iuridico per Aemiliam et Etruriam et Tusciam praetori candidato legato provinciae Africae dioeceseos Karthaginiensis tribuno plebis candidato quaestori provinciae Africae decemviro stlitibus iudicandis patrono perpetuo \n
EDCS-30100113.translation: To Gaius Junius Faustinus Placidas Postumianus, most distinguished man, consul, appointed among the companions of our Augusti, priest of the Flavian and Titian families, legate of the Augusti with praetorian power of the province of Lower Mysia, legate of the Augusti with praetorian power of the province of Belgica, legate of the Augusti with praetorian power of the province of Lusitania, legate of the First Adjutant Legion, pious and faithful, legal officer for Aemilia, Etruria, and Tuscia, praetor-designate, legate of the province of Africa in the diocese of Carthage, tribune of the plebs-designate, quaestor of the province of Africa, decemvir for judging lawsuits, perpetual patron.
EDCS-30100113.summary: This lengthy senatorial career inscription honors Gaius Junius Faustinus Placidas Postumianus, detailing his extensive public service and dignities, likely from the late 2nd or 3rd century AD.

EDCS-30100114.text_edition: \n Baeatissimo saeculo Cuttilulenses Macrini Sossiani legati clarissimi viri\n
EDCS-30100114.translation: To the most blessed age of Cuttilulenses. Macrinus Sossianus, most distinguished legate.
EDCS-30100114.summary: This inscription honors Macrinus Sossianus, identified as a distinguished legate associated with Cuttilulenses, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-30100116.summary: This is a simple funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Caprarius, probably from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-30100117.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Metthun, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-30100118.translation: To the divine shades. Titurnia Nina, priestess, lived 115 years. Rogatus Felix Messor erected this for his mother.
EDCS-30100118.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Titurnia Nina, a priestess who lived to be 115, erected by Rogatus Felix Messor, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-30100119.translation: Sacred to the divine shades. Modia Saturnina, initiated into the mystery rites, lived 35 years, for her parents.
EDCS-30100119.summary: This funerary inscription honors Modia Saturnina, who was initiated into religious rites and lived 35 years, placed by her parents, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-30100120.translation: Sacred to the divine shades. Saturninus the slave is buried here, who lived 26 years and 3 days. Aurelius Fortunatus Prima to his dearest son; Zabullus Primulus Albanus to his brother.
EDCS-30100120.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Saturninus, a slave who lived 26 years and 3 days, with dedications from his father and brother, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-30100121.translation: To the Genius of the most distinguished order of decurions of the municipality of Alexandria Giufitana. Publius Pompeius Geminus, son of Publius, of the Papiria tribe, and Caius Areius Rogatus, son of Publius, of the Papiria tribe, quaestorian aediles, made this through their generosity, and on the occasion of the dedication, they gave a banquet to the decurions. The place was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-30100121.summary: This inscription records a public work and banquet funded by two aediles, Publius Pompeius Geminus and Caius Areius Rogatus, for the decurions of Alexandria Giufitana, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-30100123.summary: This is a dedication to a deity, likely a fertility god, from the Roman period.

EDCS-30100124.text_edition: \n Et tu exuri sartor quod disperabas explicitu est sede in catena\n
EDCS-30100124.translation: And you, tailor, have been made whole, what you despaired of has been completed; the seat is in chains.
EDCS-30100124.summary: This fragmentary inscription, likely from a tomb, records a recovery from illness or despair and mentions a seat in chains, possibly a metaphor.

EDCS-30100125.translation: Licinius Bassus, son of Publius, of the Bassus family, dutiful, lived 43 years, is buried here.
EDCS-30100125.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Licinius Bassus, recording his age and burial, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-30100127.translation: To the memory of the most distinguished man, with money...
EDCS-30100127.summary: This is a fragment of a funerary inscription commemorating a distinguished man, with a lacuna indicating further details about the cost or dedication.

EDCS-30100128.translation: Pius lived 60 years and 9 months; he is buried here.
EDCS-30100128.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the age at death of Pius and stating he is buried at this location.

EDCS-30100129.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Caelius Felix lived 67 years.
EDCS-30100129.summary: This funerary inscription records the age at death of Caelius Felix.

EDCS-30100130.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Caelius Victor, son of Cassius, lived 54 years, 3 months, and 12 days.
EDCS-30100130.summary: This funerary inscription records the age at death of Caelius Victor, son of Cassius.

EDCS-30100131.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Avidius Primus, the physician, lived 70 years and 2 months.
EDCS-30100131.summary: This funerary inscription records the age at death of Avidius Primus, a physician.

EDCS-30100136.text_edition: \n Parthici di Auspici Felicis cultu ornavit e[t ------\n
EDCS-30100136.translation: With the worship of the fortunate Parthian god, he adorned...
EDCS-30100136.summary: This inscription fragment refers to the worship and adornment associated with a deity named the 'fortunate Parthian god', likely part of a dedicatory or honorific text.

EDCS-30100140.translation: Sacred to the goddess Fortuna Augusta. Caius Pleminius, the heir and her husband, had it made from the will of Maria Prisca, daughter of Silvanus, whom he ordered to be made for 4,000 sesterces, and dedicated it; on account of this dedication, he gave a banquet to the decurions; the place was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-30100140.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a monument to Fortuna Augusta, funded by Maria Prisca's will and executed by her husband Caius Pleminius, who also provided a banquet for the town council.

EDCS-30100141.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Marcus Oppius Felix pius vixit annos XXXIII hic situs est\n
EDCS-30100141.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Marcus Oppius Felix, dutiful, lived 33 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-30100141.summary: This is a standard funerary epitaph recording the name, pietas, age at death, and burial place of Marcus Oppius Felix.

EDCS-30100142.text_edition: \n Sexti filius Arnensi Fortunatus pius vixit annos V sit tibi terra levis ossa tibi bene quiescant hic situs est\n
EDCS-30100142.translation: Fortunatus, son of Sextus, of the Arnensian tribe, dutiful, lived 5 years. May the earth lie lightly on you, may your bones rest well. He is buried here.
EDCS-30100142.summary: This is a touching epitaph for a young boy named Fortunatus, recording his parentage, tribe, age, and expressing wishes for his peaceful afterlife.

EDCS-30100143.inscription_type: tituli honorarii, tituli operum, tituli sacri
EDCS-30100143.text_edition: \n Genti Valeriae aeternae ddominorum nnostrorum Imperatoris Caesaris Cai Valeri Diocletiani Pii Felicis Invicti Augusti et Imperatoris Caesaris Marci Aureli Valeri Maximiani Pii Felicis Inuicti Augusti et Flavi Valeri Constanti et Galeri Valeri Maximini fortissimorum felicissimorumque Caesarum templum cum omni cultu plebs municipii Mariani Thibaritani devota numini maiestatique ipsorum et s eorum cumulata participantibus secum civibus suis votivae devotionis magno exemplo incohatum perfecit et perfectum ac dedicatum consecravit [ex auctoritate] [[[Luci Aeli Helvi Dionysi ------\n
EDCS-30100143.translation: To the eternal Genti Valeriae of our Lords, the Emperor Caesar Caius Valerius Diocletianus Pius Felix Invictus Augustus and the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Valerius Maximianus Pius Felix Invictus Augustus and the most brave and fortunate Caesars Flavius Valerius Constantius and Galerius Valerius Maximianus, the people of the municipality of Mariani Thibaritani, devoted to their divine power and majesty, having completed a temple with all worship, and having consecrated it when perfect and dedicated, with the participation of their fellow citizens as a great example of votive devotion, initiated [under the authority] of Lucius Aelius Helvius Dionysius...
EDCS-30100143.summary: This lengthy inscription records the construction and dedication of a temple by the people of Mariani Thibaritani to the Tetrarchic emperors, highlighting their devotion and the grand scale of the project.

EDCS-30100149.text_edition: \n Memoriae Syluuli sacerdotis inter lapsos vixit annos XXV in fide\n
EDCS-30100149.translation: To the memory of Sylvulus, priest, among the fallen, lived 25 years, in faith.
EDCS-30100149.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Sylvulus, a priest, who died at 25 years of age, possibly in battle or during a period of turmoil, and is remembered for his faith.

EDCS-30400027.translation: Restuta, who was also called Rustica, lived in peace more or less 50 years.
EDCS-30400027.summary: This funerary inscription records the name (with an alternative) and approximate age at death of Restuta, also known as Rustica.

EDCS-30400028.translation: Tripolius sleeps in peace. He rested on the Nones of December.
EDCS-30400028.summary: This funerary inscription states that Tripolius died and rested on December 5th.

EDCS-30400029.translation: Paulina sleeps in peace. She lived 27 years and 2 months.
EDCS-30400029.summary: This funerary inscription records the age at death of Paulina.

EDCS-30400042.summary: This is an incomplete inscription, likely the beginning of a funerary or dedication text, mentioning Gaius Oppius Res.

EDCS-30501138.translation: Marius Victorianus completed for the most illustrious Macedone, proconsul of the province of Africa, along with his legates, the olive oil warehouse and the grain warehouse, by decree of the council of all honours, from the workshop of Cupi Floriani, the builder.
EDCS-30501138.summary: This inscription records the completion of two warehouses (for olive oil and grain) by Marius Victorianus in honour of the proconsul Macedone and his legates, built by Cupi Floriani.

EDCS-30501140.text_edition: \n Abienii eximiae integritatis viro ac mire bonitatis exemplo Postumio Rufio Festo amplissimo proconsuli clarissimo viro vice sacr[a iudicanti ------\n
EDCS-30501140.translation: To Postumius Rufus Festus, most eminent proconsul, a most distinguished man, an example of outstanding integrity and admirable goodness, vice sacred[ly] judging...
EDCS-30501140.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription honoring Postumius Rufus Festus, a proconsul, recognizing his integrity and goodness during his judicial duties.

EDCS-30501141.text_edition: \n Marco Tettio Gallico Clodiano equiti Romano flamini perpetuo et Tettiae Pomponiae Cosconianae filiae eorum Iucundus servus actor\n
EDCS-30501141.translation: Iucundus, the steward, [erected this] for Marcus Tettius Gallicus Clodianus, Roman equestrian, perpetual flamen, and for their daughter Tettia Pomponia Cosconiana.
EDCS-30501141.summary: This inscription records the erection of a monument by a steward for Marcus Tettius Gallicus Clodianus, a Roman equestrian and perpetual flamen, and his daughter.

EDCS-30501142.text_edition: \n ae Marci Tetti Gallici Clodiani equitis Romani flaminis perpetui et Marco Tettio Gallicano Clodiano filio eorum Iucundus servus actor\n
EDCS-30501142.translation: Iucundus, the steward, [erected this] for Marcus Tettius Gallicus Clodianus, Roman equestrian, perpetual flamen, and for their son Marcus Tettius Gallicanus Clodianus.
EDCS-30501142.summary: This inscription records the erection of a monument by a steward for Marcus Tettius Gallicus Clodianus, a Roman equestrian and perpetual flamen, and his son.

EDCS-30501145.translation: To Marcus Herculanius Calvus Paconianus, son of Publius, of the Quirina tribe, prefect of the first cohort of cavalry of the Spaniards, tribune of the cavalry of the first cohort of a thousand Batavians, quinquennial duovir, Plotius Felix Caelestis, priest, erected this to his excellent patron.
EDCS-30501145.summary: This inscription is a dedication by Plotius Felix Caelestis to his patron, Marcus Herculanius Calvus Paconianus, who held several military and civic offices, likely dating to the late 1st or early 2nd century CE.

EDCS-30501146.translation: Sacred to Caelestis Augusta. Lucius Sentius Fortis made this vow for the health of our lord.
EDCS-30501146.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to the goddess Caelestis Augusta by Lucius Sentius Fortis for the well-being of the emperor, probably from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-30501164.text_edition: \n Imperator Caesar Caius Aurelius Valerius Diocletianus Pius Felix Invictus Augustus et Imperator Caesar Aurelius Valerius Maximianus Pius Felix Invictus Augustus et Flavius Valerius Constantius et Galerius Valerius Maximianus nobbilissimi Caessares a Tipasa milia passuum IIII\n
EDCS-30501164.translation: Emperor Caesar Gaius Aurelius Valerius Diocletianus Pius Felix Invictus Augustus, and Emperor Caesar Aurelius Valerius Maximianus Pius Felix Invictus Augustus, and Flavius Valerius Constantius and Galerius Valerius Maximianus, most noble Caesars, [set this up] 4 miles from Tipasa.
EDCS-30501164.summary: This is a milestone indicating a distance of 4 miles from Tipasa, set up by the Tetrarchs, including Diocletian, Maximian, Constantius, and Galerius, likely in the late 3rd or early 4th century CE.

EDCS-31600160.translation: From the potteries of Marcian(us), belonging to Caius Satrinius Communis.
EDCS-31600160.summary: This is a ownership or origin mark from a pottery works, indicating it belonged to Caius Satrinius Communis and was associated with 'figlinae Marcianae', likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-31600161.summary: This inscription names Agathobulus and links him to Domitius Tullus, possibly indicating ownership or a patron-client relationship, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-31600162.summary: This inscription names Nicomachus and links him to Domitius Tullus, possibly indicating ownership or a patron-client relationship, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-31800053.translation: From the workshop of the Pullaeni.
EDCS-31800053.summary: This inscription indicates the origin of a product or workshop associated with the family or group name Pullaeni, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-31800055.summary: This inscription names Pullaenus Possessor, likely referring to an individual owner or craftsman associated with a workshop or property, probably from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-31800097.translation: I beseech the Great God, and the Ancestors, and Him who holds the highest authority above the head, and the seven stars, and she who does not sleep by night. Sextillius Dionysius, son of Ourathos, is implored: may he not sleep, nor sit, nor speak, but may he have in his mind Septima Amena, daughter of Ourathos, with my love and my desire. My soul and heart, implored Sextillius Dionysius, son of Ourathos, with my love and my desire. But you, Abar Barbari Eloee Sabaoth Pachnouphy Pythipemi, make Sextillius Dionysius, son of Ourathos, not to sleep in a dream, but in my love and my desire. I implore him whose spirit and heart embraces all members of the body. Sextillius Dionysius, son of Ourathos, if I descend into the abysses of Osiris, and dissolve the flesh and let it be carried by the river, for I am the great leader of the great god Achrammachala.
EDCS-31800097.summary: This is a complex magical or religious text, likely a curse or incantation inscribed for a specific purpose, involving invocations to various deities and a plea concerning Sextillius Dionysius and Septima Amena, dating possibly to the Roman period given the Greek and Latin influences and the mention of Osiris.

EDCS-31800269.translation: Lucius Bruttidius Augustalis made this tiling work from the Emperor's tiles, with Propinquus and Ambibulus as consuls.
EDCS-31800269.summary: This inscription records a tiling work made by Lucius Bruttidius Augustalis using imperial tiles, dating to the consulship of Propinquus and Ambibulus.

EDCS-31800270.translation: Lucius Bruttidius Augustalis made this tiling work from the Emperor's tiles, with Propinquus and Ambibulus as consuls.
EDCS-31800270.summary: This inscription records a tiling work made by Lucius Bruttidius Augustalis using imperial tiles, dating to the consulship of Propinquus and Ambibulus.

EDCS-31800271.summary: This inscription indicates the owner and the type of work, Lucius Bruttidius Augustalis, related to pottery production, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-32300442.translation: He fulfilled his vow with a happy spirit.
EDCS-32300442.summary: This is a short, formulaic inscription recording the fulfillment of a vow, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-32800177.translation: Doliare ware from the Terentian potteries, from the estates of our Domitia Lucilla, from Saturninus.
EDCS-32800177.summary: This inscription records pottery originating from the estates of Domitia Lucilla and Saturninus, produced in the Terentian potteries.

EDCS-32800178.translation: Doliare ware from the estates of Lucilla, from the Terentian potteries of Verus, the work of Lucius Servilius Fortunatus.
EDCS-32800178.summary: This inscription indicates doliare ware from Lucilla's estates, made in the Terentian potteries by Lucius Servilius Fortunatus.

EDCS-33000284.translation: Doliare ware from the estates of our Caesar, from Aprile, from Aquilia Sozomena.
EDCS-33000284.summary: This inscription records doliare ware from Caesar's estates, originating from Aprile and Aquilia Sozomena.

EDCS-33400637.translation: To Marcus Vettius Latro, son of Caius, of the Quirina tribe, flamen of the deified Augustus, priest of Ceres, 137 years old, enrolled in the public equestrian order and in the five decuries, decorated with awards by the Emperor Caesar Nerva Traianus Augustus Germanicus Dacicus for his service in the Dacian War with a pure spear, a mural crown, a silver vexillum, as tribune of soldiers in the legion II Adiutrix Pia Fidelis, prefect of the ala Siliana civium Romanorum torquata armillata, procurator of the grain supply of Ostia and Portus, procurator of the province of Sicily, procurator of the Cottian Alps, procurator of Mauretania Caesariensis; Marcus Vettius Euthychides, his freedman, [erected this] to his most excellent patron, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-33400637.summary: This extensive funerary inscription honors Marcus Vettius Latro, detailing his distinguished career in military, administrative, and religious offices, culminating in his procuratorships of several provinces, and was erected by his freedman Euthychides.

EDCS-33500001.translation: Sacred to Mercurius Augustus. Lucius Iulius Atius Rogatianus, the priest, with his people, willingly fulfilled his vow; the site was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-33500001.summary: This votive inscription records the fulfillment of a vow to Mercurius Augustus by the priest Lucius Iulius Atius Rogatianus, with the site granted by local officials.

EDCS-33500002.translation: Sacred to Mercurius Augustus. Lucius Iunius Proculus Rufinianus fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-33500002.summary: This votive inscription records the fulfillment of a vow to Mercurius Augustus by Lucius Iunius Proculus Rufinianus.

EDCS-33500007.summary: This inscription likely refers to an individual holding the perpetual priesthood of Augustus.

EDCS-33500016.summary: This inscription appears to record the name and title of a former proconsul, Maximus Sextus.

EDCS-33500017.translation: Sudius Felicianus, Publius Octavius Maximus Aelianus, Octavius Sabrinianus.
EDCS-33500017.summary: This is a list of three names: Sudius Felicianus, Publius Octavius Maximus Aelianus, and Octavius Sabrinianus.

EDCS-33500018.translation: Julius Iulianus, son of Saggei, of the Vibus tribe.
EDCS-33500018.summary: This inscription records the name of Julius Iulianus, son of Saggei, and his tribal affiliation.

EDCS-33500019.summary: This is a funerary inscription likely commemorating Aelius Donatus.

EDCS-33500020.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Abdelim, son of Pinaris, dutiful, lived 65 years. Here he lies.
EDCS-33500020.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the death of Abdelim, son of Pinaris, who lived 65 years.

EDCS-33500022.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Lucius Aelius Victor, dutiful, lived 60 years. Here he lies.
EDCS-33500022.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the death of Lucius Aelius Victor, who lived 60 years.

EDCS-33500023.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Lucius Annaeus.
EDCS-33500023.summary: This is a funerary inscription likely commemorating Lucius Annaeus.

EDCS-33500024.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Apronia Rogata, dutiful, lived [---] years.
EDCS-33500024.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the death of Apronia Rogata, whose age is partially illegible.

EDCS-33500025.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Berecbal, daughter of Saturnines Oriclonis, dutiful, lived 4 years.
EDCS-33500025.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the death of Berecbal, daughter of Saturnines Oriclonis, who lived 4 years.

EDCS-33500026.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Berect, daughter of Mutunbalis, dutiful, lived 9 years. Here she lies.
EDCS-33500026.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the death of Berect, daughter of Mutunbalis, who lived 9 years.

EDCS-33500027.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Aulus Caecilius Iulianus, dutiful, lived 30 years. Here he lies.
EDCS-33500027.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the death of Aulus Caecilius Iulianus, who lived 30 years.

EDCS-33500028.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Caecilia, daughter of Aulus, Antulla, dutiful, lived 2 years and 1 month. Here she lies.
EDCS-33500028.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the death of Caecilia Antulla, daughter of Aulus, who lived 2 years and 1 month.

EDCS-33500030.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Caelius Fuscus, lived 7 years and 2 months. Asiaticus, dutiful, here he lies.
EDCS-33500030.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the death of Caelius Fuscus, who lived 7 years and 2 months, possibly with a separate mention of Asiaticus.

EDCS-33500031.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Castatlia the dutiful lived 30 years, is buried here.
EDCS-33500031.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Castatlia at the age of 30.

EDCS-33500032.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Caecilius Celanus lived 13 and a half years.
EDCS-33500032.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Caecilius Celanus at the age of 13 and a half.

EDCS-33500033.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Cornelius Faustus, dutiful son of Asianus, lived 50 years, is buried here.
EDCS-33500033.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Cornelius Faustus at the age of 50.

EDCS-33500034.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Dannea Donata the dutiful lived 16 years and 8 months, is buried here.
EDCS-33500034.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Dannea Donata at the age of 16 years and 8 months.

EDCS-33500035.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Apuleia Rogata the dutiful lived 83 years, is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Gaius Eglogius Saturninus of Iulaitanus, the dutiful, lived 108 years, is buried here.
EDCS-33500035.summary: A funerary epitaph with two individuals, Apuleia Rogata who died at 83 and Gaius Eglogius Saturninus who died at 108.

EDCS-33500037.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus Fabius Ianuarius the dutiful lived 48 years, is buried here.
EDCS-33500037.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Quintus Fabius Ianuarius at the age of 48.

EDCS-33500039.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Euchus Viator lived...
EDCS-33500039.summary: A funerary epitaph that is incomplete, only stating the name and that Euchus Viator lived an unspecified number of years.

EDCS-33500040.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Geminius Iustus the dutiful lived 71 years, is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Lorinia Saturnina the dutiful lived 70 years, is buried here.
EDCS-33500040.summary: A funerary epitaph with two individuals, Geminius Iustus who died at 71 and Lorinia Saturnina who died at 70.

EDCS-33500041.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus Geminius Victor Papiria Octavianus
EDCS-33500041.summary: An inscription likely recording the names of two individuals, Quintus Geminius Victor and Papiria Octavianus, possibly a dedication or funerary notice.

EDCS-33500044.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucatia Castula the dutiful lived 32 years, is buried here.
EDCS-33500044.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Lucatia Castula at the age of 32.

EDCS-33500045.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Maior, daughter of Silvanus, pious, lived 23 years, is buried here.
EDCS-33500045.summary: A tombstone recording the death of Maior, daughter of Silvanus.

EDCS-33500319.inscription_type: tituli honorarii, tituli operum, tituli sacri
EDCS-33500319.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari Marco Aurelio Antonino Augusto divi Veri fratri Armeniaco Parthico Medico Germanico pontifici maximo tribunicia potestate XXVII imperatori VI cons(uli) III patri patriae proconsuli pagus Uchitanorum Maiorum aedem vetustate corruptam ex auctoritate Iuni Sabiniani proconsulis clarissimi viri petente procuratore transtulit et aquam induxit itemque fontem fecit curatore ato magistro pagi\n
EDCS-33500319.translation: The pagus Uchitanorum Maiorum, at the request of the procurator and under the authority of the most distinguished man, the proconsul Iunius Sabinianus, transferred a temple corrupted by age to Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus, brother of the deified Verus, conqueror of Armenia, Parthia, and Media, Germanicus, chief priest, with tribunician power for the 27th time, imperator for the 6th time, consul for the 3rd time, father of his country, proconsul, and brought water to it, and also made a fountain, with Ato as the curator and master of the pagus.
EDCS-33500319.summary: This inscription details the relocation of an old temple and the introduction of a water supply and fountain by the pagus Uchitanorum Maiorum, authorized by proconsul Iunius Sabinianus and dedicated to Emperor Marcus Aurelius Antoninus.

EDCS-33500320.summary: This inscription likely refers to an official title, 'perpetual priest', possibly within a religious or civic context.

EDCS-33500321.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Lucius Aurelius Verus
EDCS-33500321.summary: This inscription records a dedication to the Roman Emperor Lucius Aurelius Verus, likely dating to his reign (161-169 AD).

EDCS-33500451.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari Lucio Septimio Severo Pertinaci Augusto pontifici maximo tribunicia potestate II imperatori IIII consuli II proconsuli patri patriae civitas Limisa decreto decurionum pecunia publica fecit anno Publi Corneli Anullini proconsulis clarissimi viri \n
EDCS-33500451.translation: The city of Limisa, by decree of the decurions and with public funds, made this for Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pertinax Augustus, chief priest, with tribunician power for the 2nd time, imperator for the 4th time, consul for the 2nd time, proconsul, father of his country, in the year of Publius Cornelius Anullinus, most distinguished man, as proconsul.
EDCS-33500451.summary: This inscription records the construction of a monument by the city of Limisa using public funds in honor of Emperor Septimius Severus Pertinax, during the proconsulship of P. Cornelius Anullinus.

EDCS-33500455.text_edition: \n Palladi Lucio Iunio Publi filio Papiria Proculo Feliciano flamini Augusti perpetuo municipii Limisensium cui cum ordo ob eximia eius merita publice statuam de sportulis ponendam censuisset honore muneris oblati contentus sua pecunia posuit locus datus decreto decurionum\n
EDCS-33500455.translation: Palladius Lucius Junius Publius's son Papirius Proculus Felicianus, perpetual flamen of Augustus of the municipality of Limisa, who, when the council had decreed that a statue should be erected to him at public expense in recognition of his exceptional merits, was content with the honor offered and erected it at his own expense, the site having been granted by decree of the council.
EDCS-33500455.summary: This inscription records that Palladius Lucius Junius Publius Proculus Felicianus, a local magistrate and priest in Limisa, erected his own statue, despite the council's decree to fund it, in recognition of his merits.

EDCS-33500458.translation: Caecilius Faustus Baliatho, magistrate, [dedicated this] to Ceres for the safety of the Emperor Caesar.

EDCS-33500461.translation: Sacred to Mercury Augustus. The devotees of the hunt made this at their own expense. Lucius Iulius Atius Rogatianus, public priest; Publius Iunius Proculus Romanianus, Roman knight, perpetual priest; Lucius Iunius Proculus Rufinianus, Roman knight; Publius Iunius Felix Rogatianus, Roman knight; Publius Aelius Herma; Lucius Sutorius Rogatus; Marcus Pescennius Saturnus; Caius Iulius Atius Rogatus; Caius Iulius Atius Masc[---]; Caius Iulius Atius Saturninus; Lucius Da[---]deus Maximus; Sudius Ziquanus; Annaeus Liber; Vinius Victor; Icicius Felix; Rifinius Faustus; Itorius Victor; Iunius Hippolytus; Caecilius Victor; Aemilius Gududio; Apronius Secundianus Fuscus; Catonis Aemilius Tecton; Crispius Castus; Arnesius Secundus; Aebutius Felix; Caecilius Adiutor; Iunius Victorianus; Barnaeus Lesbius; Florius Agentius; Valerius Pescinus. The site was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-33500461.summary: This inscription records the construction of a shrine to Mercury Augustus by hunters, with various officials and prominent citizens listed as donors or participants, and notes the land was granted by the local council, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-34000300.translation: Make her fettered like a pigeon, like a petal, like a dove, whom a lover bore, frenzied with love for me, so that she may not sleep until she comes to me, the delights of girls, Desecus Ballincum of the Lollii, driven from his chariot, so that he may not be able to come before me. And you, whatever daemon you are, I implore you to force her to come to me for the sake of love and my desire.
EDCS-34000300.summary: This is a magical curse text, likely from a defixio, intended to compel a lover's return by binding her and incapacitating a rival.
