EDCS-43400454.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription recording the name of an individual, Marcus Novius, son of Titus.

EDCS-43400455.summary: This is a dedication inscription indicating that Lucius Domitius was the maker or dedicator of a monument or object.

EDCS-43400462.summary: This is a dedication inscription indicating that Lucius Domitius was the maker or dedicator of a monument or object.

EDCS-43400463.summary: This is a funerary or ownership inscription identifying Caius Oppius Restitutus as the deceased or the owner of the property.

EDCS-43400464.summary: This is a dedication inscription indicating that Lucius Domitius was the maker or dedicator of a monument or object.

EDCS-43400478.summary: This is a funerary or ownership inscription identifying Caius Clodius Spurinna as the deceased or the owner of the property.

EDCS-43400504.summary: This is a funerary or ownership inscription identifying Caius Oppius Restitutus as the deceased or the owner of the property.

EDCS-43400506.summary: This is a funerary or ownership inscription identifying Caius Atilius Restitutus as the deceased or the owner of the property.

EDCS-43400508.summary: This is a funerary or ownership inscription identifying Caius Oppius Restitutus as the deceased or the owner of the property.

EDCS-43400510.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the name of Marcus Novius Justus.

EDCS-43400513.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the name of Marcus Novius Justus.

EDCS-43400514.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the name of Marcus Novius Germanus.

EDCS-43400515.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the name of Gaius Oppius Restitutus.

EDCS-43400517.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the name of Lucius Cornelius Victor.

EDCS-43400518.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the name of Marcus Novius Justus.

EDCS-43400522.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the name of Lucius M. Restitutus.

EDCS-43400524.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the name of Marcus Novius Justus.

EDCS-43400525.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the name of Gaius Oppius Restitutus.

EDCS-43400534.translation: Sacred to the shades below. Marcus Corlius Secundus lived 90 years. Marcus CorOPlius Africanus made [this] for his dearest father.
EDCS-43400534.summary: This is a funerary monument where Marcus CorOPlius Africanus dedicated a tomb for his father, Marcus Corlius Secundus, who lived 90 years.

EDCS-43400535.translation: Silvana placed this for her deserving brother.
EDCS-43400535.summary: A funerary epitaph for a deserving brother, dedicated by his sister Silvana.

EDCS-43400536.translation: Of the sons of Decimus Avianius.
EDCS-43400536.summary: A fragment of an inscription, possibly referring to the sons of Decimus Avianius.

EDCS-43400802.translation: Anastasia, sweet one, lived 4 months in peace.
EDCS-43400802.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the short life of Anastasia, who lived for 4 months.

EDCS-43400806.translation: Bonitas, innocent one, lived 1 year, 4 months, and 23 days in peace.
EDCS-43400806.summary: A funerary epitaph detailing the lifespan of Bonitas, who lived for 1 year, 4 months, and 23 days.

EDCS-43400808.summary: A funerary epitaph simply stating the name Abundantia, likely indicating her peaceful rest.

EDCS-43400809.summary: A funerary epitaph simply stating the name Atquisitor, likely indicating his peaceful rest.

EDCS-43400810.summary: A funerary epitaph simply stating the name Covuldeus, likely indicating his peaceful rest.

EDCS-43400811.summary: A funerary epitaph simply stating the name Covuldeus, likely indicating his peaceful rest.

EDCS-43400812.summary: A funerary epitaph simply stating the name Lollianus, likely indicating his peaceful rest.

EDCS-43400813.summary: A funerary epitaph simply stating the name Lollianus, likely indicating his peaceful rest.

EDCS-43400814.summary: This inscription is a simple epitaph for an individual named Munerius.

EDCS-43400815.summary: This inscription is a simple epitaph for an individual named Sterculus.

EDCS-43400816.translation: Susanna, who is also called Lolliana, is at peace.
EDCS-43400816.summary: This inscription is an epitaph for Susanna, who also used the name Lolliana.

EDCS-43400817.translation: Dearest Bonifatia, innocent, is at peace.
EDCS-43400817.summary: This inscription is an epitaph for Bonifatia, described as 'innocent'.

EDCS-43400818.translation: Apriles lived for 70 years in peace.
EDCS-43400818.summary: This epitaph records the lifespan of Apriles, who lived for 70 years.

EDCS-43400819.translation: Calbessanus lived for 20 years in peace and departed on the 6th day before the Kalends of April.
EDCS-43400819.summary: This epitaph records the age of Calbessanus, who died at 20 years old, and his date of death.

EDCS-43400820.translation: Maximilla, innocent, lived in peace for 17 years, 4 months, and 12 days; she was laid to rest on the 10th day before the Kalends of February.
EDCS-43400820.summary: This epitaph records the lifespan and burial date of Maximilla, who died at 17 years, 4 months, and 12 days old.

EDCS-43400821.summary: This inscription invokes peace in God for Seberus.

EDCS-43400822.summary: This is a funerary inscription likely for Flavia Domitilla, dating to the Christian period (indicated by 'in pace').

EDCS-43400823.summary: This inscription is a simple epitaph for an individual named Laurentia.

EDCS-43400824.translation: Vitale lived for seven years and ten months in peace. Zosimus, his father, completed this.
EDCS-43400824.summary: This epitaph records the lifespan of Vitale, who lived for seven years and ten months, and states that his father, Zosimus, erected it.

EDCS-43400825.translation: Victorina lived twenty-eight years in peace.
EDCS-43400825.summary: This epitaph records the lifespan of Victorina.

EDCS-43400826.translation: F. Lucilius, her son, in peace.
EDCS-43400826.summary: This epitaph records the son of the deceased, F. Lucilius.

EDCS-43400830.translation: Verrius Petronius Candidus lived forty-two years, nine months, fifteen days, and five hours in peace.
EDCS-43400830.summary: This epitaph records the lifespan of Verrius Petronius Candidus in considerable detail.

EDCS-43400831.translation: Memory of Alexandria; she lived twenty years with peace. Maximus, her husband, made this.
EDCS-43400831.summary: This epitaph records the lifespan of Alexandria, dedicated by her husband Maximus.

EDCS-43500002.translation: Gennia Victorina made this for her husband with a willing spirit.
EDCS-43500002.summary: This funerary monument was dedicated by Gennia Victorina to her husband.

EDCS-43500003.translation: To the Manes. Iulia Roricata lived sixty years.
EDCS-43500003.summary: This epitaph records the lifespan of Iulia Roricata, dedicated to the Manes.

EDCS-43500004.translation: Sacred to the Manes. Moafus, aged eighty years. His heirs [made this] for an excellent parent.
EDCS-43500004.summary: This epitaph records the age of Moafus and was erected by his heirs.

EDCS-43500008.summary: This inscription is too fragmentary to provide a meaningful summary.

EDCS-43500015.translation: fidelis in peace rianus in peace was laid to rest
EDCS-43500015.summary: This inscription is too fragmentary to provide a meaningful summary.

EDCS-43500024.summary: This epitaph commemorates Fortuna, likely a person or a concept of good fortune.

EDCS-43500030.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Licinia Bona.

EDCS-43500037.summary: This is a funerary inscription possibly for a freedman named Felix or for a man named Germanicus who was fortunate.

EDCS-43500041.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Viutus, son of Hinitius, lived 90 years. His heirs established this.
EDCS-43500041.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Viutus, detailing his age and noting that his heirs established the monument.

EDCS-43500042.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Cossidia Maior, pious daughter of Lucius, lived 50 years, is buried here.
EDCS-43500042.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Cossidia Maior, daughter of Lucius, specifying her age and burial location.

EDCS-43500043.translation: For the safety of the Emperor Marcus Aurelius Severus Antoninus. Egrilius, perpetual priest, [established this].
EDCS-43500043.summary: This is a dedication honoring Emperor Marcus Aurelius Severus Antoninus by Egrilius, a perpetual priest.

EDCS-43500044.translation: The household of Titus Valerius Vnus, [and] Valerianus.
EDCS-43500044.summary: This is an inscription likely marking a property or tomb belonging to Titus Valerius Vnus and Valerianus.

EDCS-43500045.translation: Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus, conqueror of Parthia, conqueror of Britain, conqueror of Germany, holding tribunician power for the 19th time, consul for the 4th time, father of the country, restored [this] in the year 50 [of the Seleucid era? or other system?].
EDCS-43500045.summary: This is a lengthy imperial dedication by Marcus Aurelius Antoninus, recording his titles and achievements, and likely dating to his 19th tribunician power year.

EDCS-43500059.translation: Lucius Cassius Fuscus, soldier of the III Augusta legion, of Quintus Vennius's century, lived 34 years, served 19 years, is buried here.
EDCS-43500059.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Cassius Fuscus, a soldier of the III Augusta legion, detailing his age and military service.

EDCS-43500060.translation: Claudius Secundus, by his will, placed this house [monument] for Iuppilius. He is buried here. [Possibly 'restored' or 'erected'].
EDCS-43500060.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording that Claudius Secundus, according to his will, erected this monument for Iuppilius.

EDCS-43500063.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Iulius Coscivius lived 75 years.
EDCS-43500063.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Iulius Coscivius, stating his age.

EDCS-43500064.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Marcus Julius Philippus Pius Felix Invictus Augustus, pontifex maximus, father of the fatherland, holder of tribunician power, consul, and to Marcus Julius Philippus, most noble Caesar, prince of the youth, and to Marcia Otacilia Severa, Augusta, mother of the Emperor, and of the camp, and of the senate, and of the fatherland, for 52 years.
EDCS-43500064.summary: This is a dedication by the Emperor Philippus and his family, likely from the mid-3rd century CE.

EDCS-43500065.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Augustus, the greatest Parthian, the greatest Briton.
EDCS-43500065.summary: This inscription honors Emperor Caracalla with his titles, likely from the early 3rd century CE.

EDCS-43500066.translation: To our lord Galerius Valerius Maximianus, most noble Caesar, for 50 years.
EDCS-43500066.summary: This is a dedication to Caesar Galerius Maximianus, likely from the late 3rd or early 4th century CE.

EDCS-43600047.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Cessius Vitalis, dutiful, lived for forty-three years.
EDCS-43600047.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Cessius Vitalis, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-43600048.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. The son of Cosvus lived for sixty-one years; he is buried here.
EDCS-43600048.summary: This is a funerary dedication for the son of Cosvus, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-43600049.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulia Obasia lived for ninety years; she is buried here.
EDCS-43600049.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Iulia Obasia, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-43600050.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcus Sulpicius, legate, dutiful, lived for twenty-five years; he is buried here.
EDCS-43600050.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Marcus Sulpicius, a legate, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-43600054.summary: This is a fragment of a funerary inscription recording a very short lifespan, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-43600057.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription likely recording the lifespan of two individuals, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-43600063.summary: This is a dedication to Lucius Septumius Contus, likely funerary or honorary, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-43600066.translation: Emperor Caesar, grandson of the deified Nerva, son of the deified Trajan the Parthian, Trajan Hadrian Augustus, chief priest, in his seventh year of tribunician power, consul for the third time, paved the road from Carthage to Theveste through the Legio III Augusta, with Publius Metilius Secundus as governor.
EDCS-43600066.summary: This is a military road dedication by Emperor Hadrian, built by Legio III Augusta, dating to his early reign (around 100-120 AD).

EDCS-43700629.translation: From the workshop of Herac(l)es Philargurius.
EDCS-43700629.summary: This inscription identifies a workshop owned by Herac(l)es Philargurius, likely for pottery or other craft goods.

EDCS-43700631.summary: This is a dedication or memorial for Gaius Iunius Dracon, possibly setting up an object or honoring him.

EDCS-43700633.translation: From the workshop of Marcus Antonius Saturninus.
EDCS-43700633.summary: This inscription indicates that an object originates from the workshop of Marcus Antonius Saturninus, likely a craftsman or producer.

EDCS-43700636.summary: This inscription identifies the 'Officina Pullaeni', likely a business or workshop known for its products.

EDCS-43700637.translation: Bulla, daughter of Titus Aelius Crassus.
EDCS-43700637.summary: This is a tombstone or memorial inscription for Bulla, the daughter of Titus Aelius Crassus.

EDCS-43700638.translation: Ianuarius, from the workshop of Iulius Lupus, freedman of Augustus.
EDCS-43700638.summary: This inscription identifies Ianuarius as a worker from the workshop of Iulius Lupus, who was a freedman of Augustus.

EDCS-43700647.translation: she lived 14 years, she is buried here; he lived 90 years, he is buried here.
EDCS-43700647.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the ages and burial of two individuals, likely a married couple or family members.

EDCS-43700648.translation: Ticinius Victor lived 70 years; Ticinius [son/brother?] [lived] X years.
EDCS-43700648.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Ticinius Victor and another Ticinius, likely relatives, recording their ages at death.

EDCS-43700649.translation: For the prosperity of the times, Gaius Alanius Sirmaniam, freedman of the people, with his people (?) and co-freedmen (?).
EDCS-43700649.summary: This inscription is a dedication for the prosperity of the times by Gaius Alanius Sirmaniam, likely a freedman or public official.

EDCS-43700653.translation: Secundus, a man worthy of praise.
EDCS-43700653.summary: This is a fragmentary epitaph honoring a man named Secundus, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-43700757.translation: Felix, on the third day before the Kalends of December.
EDCS-43700757.summary: This inscription records a date, the third day before the Kalends of December, possibly for an event or a commemoration, associated with the name Felix.

EDCS-43700758.translation: Iuncina, on the fourteenth day before the Kalends of January.
EDCS-43700758.summary: This inscription records a date, the fourteenth day before the Kalends of January, possibly for an event or a commemoration, associated with the name Iuncina.

EDCS-43700759.translation: Monnika, on the day before the Kalends of January.
EDCS-43700759.summary: This inscription records a date, the day before the Kalends of January, possibly for an event or a commemoration, associated with the name Monnika.

EDCS-43700760.translation: Agape, on the fourth day before the Nones of August.
EDCS-43700760.summary: This inscription records a date, the fourth day before the Nones of August, possibly for an event or a commemoration, associated with the name Agape.

EDCS-44100029.translation: To the Emperor Caesar, son of the deified Septimius Severus Pius, Arabicus Adiabenicus, the greatest victor in Parthia and Britain, grandson of the deified Antoninus Pius Germanicus Sarmaticus, great-grandson of the deified Antoninus Pius, descendant in the fourth generation of the deified Hadrian, descendant in the fifth generation of the deified Trajan Parthicus and the deified Nerva, Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus, greatest victor in Parthia.
EDCS-44100029.summary: This is a formal dedication to Emperor Caracalla, listing his extensive titulature and lineage, typical of imperial inscriptions from the early 3rd century CE.

EDCS-44100030.translation: You Pro Maxucia through LVCTSVN Consti-
EDCS-44100030.summary: This is a fragmented inscription, possibly part of a dedication or an epitaph, with names and unclear context, dating likely to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-44100041.translation: St... lived for thirteen years, three months, and one day.
EDCS-44100041.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the age at death of an individual identified by the fragmented name 'St...' who lived for 13 years, 3 months, and 1 day, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-44100042.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the age at death of a freedman named Cerellianus, who lived for six years, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-44200018.translation: To Vesta Augusta, Clodius Felix, son of Decimus, willingly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-44200018.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Vesta Augusta by Clodius Felix, son of Decimus, indicating a personal offering, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-44200019.translation: Sacred to the divine will of Augustus. The community of Thignica erected this at their own expense by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-44200019.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by the community of Thignica to the divine will of Augustus, funded by public money and authorized by local officials.

EDCS-44200027.summary: This inscription is a fragmentary dedication or ownership marker belonging to Iunius Restitutus Maximus.

EDCS-44200028.translation: Fortunata lived in peace, faithful, for 9 years, on the 7th day before the Kalends of January.
EDCS-44200028.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespan and death date of Fortunata, indicating a Christian context with the phrase 'in pace'.

EDCS-44200032.translation: For Emperor Caesar Marcus Valerius Maximianus Pius Felix Augustus, 146.
EDCS-44200032.summary: This inscription is a dedication or indication of some measure (perhaps a distance or quantity) related to Emperor Caesar Marcus Valerius Maximianus.

EDCS-44200033.translation: For Emperor Caesar Gaius Vibius Trebonianus Gallus Pius Felix Augustus, chief priest, father of the fatherland, with tribunician power, and Emperor Caesar Gaius Vibius Veldumnianus Volusianus Gallus Pius Felix Augustus, chief priest, father of the fatherland, with tribunician power, 140.
EDCS-44200033.summary: This inscription honors Emperors Trebonianus Gallus and Volusianus Gallus, listing their titles and powers, possibly associated with a measure of 140.

EDCS-44200034.translation: For Emperor Caesar Gaius Messius Quintus Decius Pius Felix Augustus.
EDCS-44200034.summary: This is a dedication to Emperor Caesar Gaius Messius Quintus Decius Pius Felix Augustus, likely from the period of his reign.

EDCS-44200035.translation: Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus, greatest conqueror of Parthia, greatest conqueror of Britain, greatest conqueror of Germania, with tribunician power for the 19th year, consul for the 4th time, father of the fatherland, restored 139 [units/miles].
EDCS-44200035.summary: This inscription records public works restored by Emperor Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus, detailing his titles and the extent of his achievements.

EDCS-44200036.translation: For Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Caro Pius Felix Augustus, and for Marcus Aurelius Carinus, most noble Caesar, and for Marcus Aurelius Numerius, most noble Caesar.
EDCS-44200036.summary: This inscription honors Emperors Marcus Aurelius Caro, and Caesars Carinus and Numerian, likely a dedication or official proclamation.

EDCS-44200037.translation: Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus, greatest conqueror of Parthia, greatest conqueror of Britain, greatest conqueror of Germania, with tribunician power for the 19th year, consul for the 4th time, father of the fatherland, restored 143 [units/miles].
EDCS-44200037.summary: This inscription records public works restored by Emperor Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus, detailing his titles and the extent of his achievements, similar to EDCS-44200035.

EDCS-44200038.translation: Of Emperor Caesar Publius Licinius Valerianus Augustus and Emperor Caesar Publius Licinius Gallienus Augustus.
EDCS-44200038.summary: This inscription refers to the authority or joint rule of Emperors Valerian and Gallienus.

EDCS-44200039.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Marcus Valerius Maximianus, Pious, Fortunate, Augustus, 145.
EDCS-44200039.summary: This is a dedication to Emperor Maximian, likely dating to his reign (late 3rd/early 4th century CE), with the numbers possibly indicating a date or a sequential marker.

EDCS-44200041.translation: Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Augustus, conqueror of Parthia, conqueror of Britain, conqueror of Germany, with tribunician power for the 19th time, consul for the 4th time, father of the fatherland, restored this, 147.
EDCS-44200041.summary: This inscription records the restoration of something by Emperor Caracalla, highlighting his numerous titles and achievements, and likely dates to 216 CE.

EDCS-44200043.summary: This is a dedication to the usurper Emperor Magnentius, likely dating to 347 CE.

EDCS-44200044.translation: To the divine genius of the place. The comrades of Magarensium Colocausentus dedicated this: Antonius Absuntius, Pontius Fortunatus, Marcius Victor, Caninius Horatianus, Marcus Aelius Victor, Cominius Felix, Lucius Statius Florus, Pompeius Godeus, Pontius Honoratus, Pontius Clementius, Marcius Donatus, by the good fortune of Pinarius Felix.
EDCS-44200044.summary: This is a dedication to the local spirit by a group of soldiers or comrades, likely from the 1st to 3rd century CE.

EDCS-44200045.translation: To Flavius Valerius Constantius, most noble Caesar.
EDCS-44200045.summary: This is a dedication to Caesar Constantius I, likely dating to his period as Caesar (293-306 CE).

EDCS-44200068.translation: Chadda, son of Nimirmirath, Nytros, and Felimun, son of Thubab.
EDCS-44200068.summary: This inscription appears to be a funerary marker for several individuals, likely of non-Latin origin based on the names, with a possible date range from the Roman to early Byzantine period.

EDCS-44200070.translation: Of Quintus Anicius Faustus, son of Caius, 2000 paces.
EDCS-44200070.summary: This inscription likely marks a boundary or a distance related to Quintus Anicius Faustus, possibly from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-44200072.translation: Sacred to Augusta. Maximus, tribune of the plebs, dedicated this at his own expense.
EDCS-44200072.summary: This is a dedication to a divinity named Augusta by Maximus, a tribune of the plebs, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-44200073.translation: Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Augustus, Parthicus Maximus, Britannicus Maximus, Germanicus Maximus, having his tribunician power for the 20th time, consul for the 4th time, father of the fatherland, restored [the structure] in the 7th year.
EDCS-44200073.summary: This is a dedication by Emperor Marcus Aurelius, listing his titles and achievements, indicating he restored a structure (likely public), dating to his reign (161-180 CE).

EDCS-44200076.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Virilus from Vienna, a soldier of the VII Gemina Felix legion, serving in the century of the first cohort's centurion, served for 13 years, lived for 30 years. His heir, for his excellent merits, had this made at his own expense for his comrade.
EDCS-44200076.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Virilus, a soldier of the VII Gemina Felix legion, dated by his service and life span (likely 2nd-3rd century CE).

EDCS-44200077.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Gaius Sulpicius, son of Aturmus, a soldier of the VII Gemina Felix legion, serving in the century of Flavius Castus, lived for 30 years. He lies here. Gaius Cornelius Maternus, his heir, had this made at his own expense for his excellent comrade.
EDCS-44200077.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Gaius Sulpicius, a soldier of the VII Gemina Felix legion, dated by his life span (likely 2nd-3rd century CE).

EDCS-44200081.translation: To Emperor Antoninus Augustus Pius, father of the fatherland, the citizen community of Numluli, at public expense.
EDCS-44200081.summary: This is a dedication by the community of Numluli to Emperor Antoninus Pius, likely Caracalla, funded by public money, dating to his reign (211-217 CE).

EDCS-44200189.translation: To our lord Flavius Constantius, most flourishing Caesar.
EDCS-44200189.summary: This is a dedication to Caesar Constantius II, likely dating to his period as Caesar or Augustus (mid-4th century CE).

EDCS-44200191.translation: Emperor Caesar, son of the divine Nerva, Trajan Augustus Germanicus.
EDCS-44200191.summary: This is an imperial titulature inscription, likely from a monument dedicated to Emperor Trajan.

EDCS-44200198.translation: Emperor Caesar Marcus Iulius Philippus Pius Felix Augustus Invictus, chief priest, with tribunician power, consul, and Marcus Iulius Philippus, most noble Caesar, prince of youth, and Marcia Otacilia Severa, wife of Augustus, mother of the senate, of the camps, and of the fatherland, restored [this].
EDCS-44200198.summary: This inscription records the restoration of a monument by Emperor Philip the Arab, his son, and his wife, likely during the mid-3rd century AD.

EDCS-44200199.translation: To Emperor Caesar Gaius Messius Quintus Trajanus Decius Pius Felix Augustus, chief priest, father of the fatherland, with tribunician power, consul for the second time, proconsul for the 126th time.
EDCS-44200199.summary: This is a dedication to Emperor Trajan Decius, likely from a public monument, dating to his reign in the mid-3rd century AD.

EDCS-44200201.translation: Here lies Felix, whom the dreadful day snatched away at the very threshold of honor and drowned in a bitter death, nor was it granted to him to touch the joys of life. He [served as] aedile, so that he could equal his father in praise. He lived 28 years, 6 months. Here he lies.
EDCS-44200201.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a young man named Felix, who died at age 28 and had served as an aedile, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-44200202.translation: To our lord Caesar Flavius Valentinianus Maximus Felix Victor and triumphant, always Augustus, born for the good of the republic.
EDCS-44200202.summary: This is a dedication to Emperor Valentinian III, likely from a monument or honorific inscription, dating to the 5th century AD.

EDCS-44200203.translation: To our lord Flavius Constantius, most noble Caesar, 10.
EDCS-44200203.summary: This is a dedication to Caesar Constantius II, the meaning of 'X' is unclear but it likely signifies a rank or count, dating to the 4th century AD.

EDCS-44200346.translation: Emperor Caesar Gaius Julius Verus Maximinus Pius Felix Augustus, Germanicus Maximus, Sarmaticus Maximus, Dacicus Maximus, chief priest, having his tribunician power for the 3rd time, emperor for the 5th time, and Gaius Julius Verus Maximus, most noble Caesar, prince of the youth, Germanicus Maximus, Sarmaticus Maximus, Dacicus Maximus, restored the road from Carthage to the borders of the province of Numidia, which had been corrupted and ruined by long neglect.
EDCS-44200346.summary: This inscription records the restoration of a road between Carthage and Numidia by Emperors Maximinus Thrax and his son Caesar Maximus, dating to their joint rule (c. 236-238 CE).

EDCS-44200347.translation: To Emperor, son of the divine Nerva, Trajan Augustus, chief priest, with tribunician power, consul.
EDCS-44200347.summary: This is an imperial titulature inscription, likely from a monument dedicated to Emperor Trajan, dating to his reign (98-117 AD).

EDCS-44400115.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Munatia Bonosa lived 35 years.
EDCS-44400115.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Munatia Bonosa, likely from her tombstone, dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-44400116.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Gaetula lived 25 years.
EDCS-44400116.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Gaetula, likely from her tombstone, dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-44400117.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Decimus Iunius Ceriolus, aged 32 years.
EDCS-44400117.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Decimus Iunius Ceriolus, likely from his tombstone, dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-44400118.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Lucius Pompeius Proculus lived 55 years.

EDCS-44400351.translation: Emperor Caesar Gaius Julius Verus Maximinus Pius Felix Augustus, Germanicus Maximus, Sarmaticus Maximus, Dacicus Maximus, having tribunician power for the 3rd time, emperor for the 5th time, and Gaius Julius Verus Maximus, most noble Caesar, prince of the youth, Germanicus Maximus, Sarmaticus Maximus, Dacicus Maximus, restored the bridges, fallen into ruin with age, and the road, corrupted by long neglect, and by their tireless foresight made it passable for travelers, [in the 30th year].

EDCS-45300004.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Safidius Felix, dutiful, lived for 30 years. He is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. EDCS-45300005.summary: A funerary inscription recording the lives and burials of Gabinia Olympia and Aulus Assidonius Triumphalis, placed by their respective parents and sons.

EDCS-45300006.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Octavius Saturus lived for 18 years. He is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Abudia Satura lived for 80 years. Octavia Procula lived for 25 years. She is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucia Conmeuta lived for 65 years. Dutiful grandsons placed this. She is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcus Longinius Silvanus lived for 95 years. Dutiful sons placed this for their father. He is buried here.
EDCS-45300006.summary: A funerary inscription recording the lives and burials of Lucius Octavius Saturus, Abudia Satura, Octavia Procula, Lucia Conmeuta, and Marcus Longinius Silvanus, placed by their descendants.

EDCS-45300007.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Secunda, dutiful, lived for 30 years. She is buried here. Her dutiful husband set this up.

EDCS-45300008.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Valeria Nina, also called Saprucina, lived for 40 years. She is laid here. Lucius Sittius Saturninus set this up for his dutiful wife.
EDCS-45300008.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Valeria Nina, set up by her husband Lucius Sittius Saturninus.

EDCS-45300009.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcus Cerficius Gaetulicus lived for [---] years. He is laid here. Cerficius Vindex, his father, set this up for his most dutiful son. Marcus Cerficius Vindicianus lived for 18 years. He is laid here. Cerficius Vindex, his father, set this up for his most dutiful son. Sacred to the departed spirits. Larnia Extricata lived for 73 years. Marcus Cerficius Vindex set this up for his dutiful mother. Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcus Cerficius Saturninus lived for 87 years. Marcus Cerficius Vindex [set this up for his] father.

EDCS-45300010.translation: Lucretius Victorinus lived for 8 years and 5 months. Ianuaria, his mother, set this up for her most beloved son.

EDCS-45300011.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus Modius Fortunatus lived for 40 years. He is laid here. His dutiful sister set this up for her brother.

EDCS-45300012.translation: Caius Remius Aprilis lived for [---] years. Cattula, his religious wife.

EDCS-45300013.translation: Lucius Rodienus Gallus paid his vow willingly.
EDCS-45300013.summary: A dedication recording Lucius Rodienus Gallus fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-45300014.translation: Sacred to Antoniae Rogata. Sacred to Publius Antonius Ianuarius.

EDCS-45300016.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Flavia Victoria Antulliana, dutiful, lived for 37 years, 11 months, and 23 days. Antonius Faustinianus, her husband, and Gessius Victor, her son, made this.
EDCS-45300016.summary: A funerary epitaph for Flavia Victoria Antulliana, set up by her husband and son.

EDCS-45300018.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Titus Flavius Felix Natalianus, dutiful, lived for 75 years and 6 months. Flavia Tyche, his wife, made this. He is laid here.
EDCS-45300018.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Titus Flavius Felix Natalianus, set up by his wife Flavia Tyche.

EDCS-45300061.translation: Saturninus, pious, lived 20 years, is buried here.
EDCS-45300061.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan and burial of Saturninus.

EDCS-45300070.summary: An incomplete inscription fragment that likely refers to a freedman named Primus.

EDCS-45300073.translation: To the divine spirits. Dedicated to Aemilia Saturnina, who lived 71 years.
EDCS-45300073.summary: A funerary dedication to Aemilia Saturnina, who lived 71 years.

EDCS-45300074.summary: A brief inscription naming Nabigius, likely an artist.

EDCS-45300080.translation: Pacontius, may you live in God.
EDCS-45300080.summary: A short inscription, possibly a blessing or epitaph, mentioning Pacontius and a divine reference.

EDCS-45300081.summary: A very short inscription, possibly an epitaph or a wish for good health, mentioning Praetextatia.

EDCS-45300097.translation: to the legate of Augustus at Astura
EDCS-45300097.summary: A fragment of an inscription possibly related to an official or monument concerning a legate of Augustus at Astura.

EDCS-45300098.translation: To the divine spirits. Dedicated to Pontia Quarta, dutiful, who lived 52 years and who rests here until the day of her death. May your bones rest well.
EDCS-45300098.summary: A funerary dedication to Pontia Quarta, who lived 52 years and wished for her remains to rest peacefully.

EDCS-45300099.translation: To the divine spirits. Dedicated to Scantia Paullina, who rests here and lived 27 years. Lucius Nonius Saturninus made this for his most dutiful wife.
EDCS-45300099.summary: A funerary dedication from Lucius Nonius Saturninus to his wife Scantia Paullina, who lived 27 years.

EDCS-45300101.translation: Ocus the dutiful lived 41 years and 13 days.
EDCS-45300101.summary: An epitaph recording the lifespan of Ocus, who lived 41 years and 13 days.

EDCS-45300107.summary: A dedication to Titus Helvius Comitius, possibly for a monument or as a memorial.

EDCS-45300136.translation: To the divine spirits. Dedicated to Marcus Egnatius Agrippa Aelianus the dutiful, who lived 85 years and rests here. His son Sempronius made this.
EDCS-45300136.summary: A funerary dedication from Sempronius to his father Marcus Egnatius Agrippa Aelianus, who lived 85 years.

EDCS-45300137.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Ianuvia lived 40 years. Victor lived 85 years. His daughter Victoria lived 40 years.
EDCS-45300137.summary: A funerary inscription recording the lifespans of Ianuvia, Victor, and Victoria, likely family members.

EDCS-45300138.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulia Saturnina lived 90 years.
EDCS-45300138.summary: A funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Iulia Saturnina.

EDCS-45300139.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucustius lived 29 years and 3 months. Sempronius made this for his dearest son.
EDCS-45300139.summary: A funerary inscription for Lucustius, set up by his father Sempronius.

EDCS-45300140.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Minucius Flavius lived 35 years.
EDCS-45300140.summary: A funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Minucius Flavius.

EDCS-45300141.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Caelius Pinulus, dutiful, lived 8 years, 3 months, 24 days, and 9 hours. He rests here in peace.
EDCS-45300141.summary: A funerary inscription for Caelius Pinulus, detailing his age at death and stating he rests in peace.

EDCS-45300142.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits, in memory of Vesolenna Felicitas, most dutiful and dearest. She lived 45 years. Lucius Calpurnius Papa, her husband, [set this up] for his wife.
EDCS-45300142.summary: A funerary inscription set up by Lucius Calpurnius Papa for his wife Vesolenna Felicitas.

EDCS-45300144.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulia Bonilla lived 65 years. She rests here. Gavius Felix, also called Micissa, dutiful, placed this for his dutiful grandmother. Sacred to the departed spirits. Gavius Lucescus lived 85 years. He rests here. Gavius Felix, also called Micisa, dutiful, placed this for his dutiful grandfather.
EDCS-45300144.summary: A funerary inscription recording the lives of Iulia Bonilla, Gavius Lucescus, and attributing the erection of the monument to Gavius Felix (Micissa/Micisa) for his grandparents.

EDCS-45300173.translation: For the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Caro Pius Felix Augustus, holder of tribunician power, father of the fatherland, proconsul, by decree of the decurions, at public expense.
EDCS-45300173.summary: A dedication to Emperor Carus, likely on a public monument, funded by the local council.

EDCS-45300198.translation: BACV EO CV II VII N SET VCVISTASAI C VSIII consul IAMI O Caesaribuss cos 17,000.
EDCS-45300198.summary: This inscription appears to be highly abbreviated or damaged, possibly recording a quantity related to a consul or Caesar, with a numerical value of 17,000.

EDCS-45300211.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Licinia Marchina lived 36 years. Munatius Felix, son of the father, [set this up].
EDCS-45300211.summary: A funerary inscription for Licinia Marchina, set up by Munatius Felix.

EDCS-45300212.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Licinius Geminus lived 75 years. Licinius Frugi made this.
EDCS-45300212.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the age of the deceased, Lucius Licinius Geminus, and identifying the dedicator as Licinius Frugi.

EDCS-45300213.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Publius Catellius Optimus lived 28 years. Publius Catellius Maximus, a dutiful father, made this.
EDCS-45300213.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the age of the deceased, Publius Catellius Optimus, and identifying the dedicator as his father, Publius Catellius Maximus.

EDCS-45300214.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the age of a child named Pastoricus.

EDCS-45300220.translation: To the son of Quintus, his son, perpetual... (restored text).
EDCS-45300220.summary: A fragmented inscription likely of a funerary or dedicatory nature, mentioning a son of Quintus.

EDCS-45300222.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Tetteia Saturnina.
EDCS-45300222.summary: A funerary epitaph identifying the deceased as Tetteia Saturnina.

EDCS-45300223.summary: A fragmentary inscription likely indicating ownership or dedication by Gaius Clodius Successus.

EDCS-45300225.translation: Gaius Salvius Lucius [---]. Lucius Satur lived 35 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-45300225.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the age of Lucius Satur and stating he is buried in this location.

EDCS-45500016.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. To my most devoted wife, Secunda, daughter of Marcus. Caius Modius Silvanus Ciceronianus [made this]. Prima, for the sake of my lineage, my mother herself, Secunda, beloved by me, then my own Cicero, for whom I had the opportunity to raise two sons, and to have them for myself, I lived fuller years, if the envious Fate had granted me six more months. As I cherished my husband chastely, so he loved me, and that he would be mindful of me, these monuments attest. You who read, know this: I lived thirty-three years, and in my homeland. Here I am planted, here I am laid to rest.
EDCS-45500016.summary: A lengthy funerary epitaph by Caius Modius Silvanus Ciceronianus for his wife Secunda, detailing their family and her life and death at age 33, placed in their homeland.

EDCS-45500021.translation: Celer, renowned for outstanding merit and the praise of his parents, and for the name well-deposited in everyone's heart, celebrated with joyous love through his duties, bearing witness to an exceptional mind with a paternal nature, embracing all things, hastening to come into prayers, took up the example of his father and Celeris' name, sent down through the statue into the ages.
EDCS-45500021.summary: An honorific inscription celebrating Celer for his merits, paternal character, and exemplary life, with his name perpetuated through a statue.

EDCS-45500027.translation: My name was found to be Moribus, [also] Mera, Damula, who is now also called Invidiosa, will go under the earth. This image covers the members of the faithful, whom the eternal Earth embraces in sleep. She rests, laid in the tomb. She lived in peace 9 years, 4 months, 18 days. Buried on the 5th day before the Kalends of May. The sorrows of the always buried parents are renewed.
EDCS-45500027.summary: A funerary epitaph for a girl who lived 9 years, 4 months, and 18 days, specifying her burial date and mentioning her multiple names and the sorrow of her parents.

EDCS-45600001.translation: Vini lived two years in peace. Inodurius lived twelve years in peace. Boneana lived two years in peace.
EDCS-45600001.summary: This epitaph records the lifespans of three individuals, Vini, Inodurius, and Boneana, emphasizing their peaceful existence.

EDCS-45600005.translation: He lived nine years and is buried here.
EDCS-45600005.summary: This brief epitaph records the age at death and burial of an individual whose name is partially lost.

EDCS-45600006.translation: Urbanus, pious, lived fifteen years and is buried here.
EDCS-45600006.summary: This epitaph records the age at death and burial of a pious individual named Urbanus.

EDCS-45600084.summary: This is a posthumous honorific inscription praising a man named Secundus.

EDCS-45600088.summary: This is a posthumous honorific inscription praising a man named Silbanus.

EDCS-45600089.summary: This is a posthumous honorific inscription praising a man named Raginarius.

EDCS-45600090.translation: Of Atanasus, prefect, and of Petrus, proconsul.
EDCS-45600090.summary: This inscription records the names and high offices (prefect and proconsul) of two individuals, Atanasus and Petrus.

EDCS-45600092.summary: This is a posthumous honorific inscription praising a man named Purpurius.

EDCS-45600093.translation: Of Nero, a most distinguished man.
EDCS-45600093.summary: This is a posthumous honorific inscription praising a man named Nero, described as 'most distinguished'.

EDCS-45600119.translation: With tribunician power, designated consul, father of the country, proconsul, and Marcus Julius Philippus, the most noble Caesar Augustus, prince of the youth, and Marcia Otacilia Severa Augusta, mother of Caesar, Augustus, and of the camp, and of the senate, and of the fatherland, 78.
EDCS-45600119.summary: This inscription lists several high-ranking imperial titles and honorifics held by multiple individuals, including emperor, Caesar, and Augusta, likely dating to the mid-3rd century CE based on the names and titles.

EDCS-45600121.translation: Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus, most great conqueror of Parthia, most great conqueror of Britain, most great conqueror of Germany, chief priest, holding tribunician power for the 19th time, hailed as imperator for the 3rd time, consul for the 4th time, father of the country, restored this, 81.
EDCS-45600121.summary: This inscription records the restoration of something by Emperor Marcus Aurelius Antoninus, listing his numerous titles and honours, with a numerical marker 'LXXXI' possibly indicating the location or a measure.

EDCS-45600129.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Quintus Calpurnius Presius Pius lived 40 years. Lucius Calpurnius Presuatius Pius lived 25 years.
EDCS-45600129.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the ages of two individuals, Quintus Calpurnius Presius Pius and Lucius Calpurnius Presuatius Pius.

EDCS-45600154.translation: To the father of the fatherland, and consul, and thrice [consul?], and to the Augusta, mother of the camp.
EDCS-45600154.summary: This inscription honors a high-ranking official, likely a general or emperor, referred to by multiple prestigious titles including 'father of the fatherland' and 'mother of the camp'.

EDCS-45600165.translation: Pottery works from the estates of Lucilla.
EDCS-45600165.summary: This inscription records the origin of pottery, stating it comes from the estates belonging to Lucilla.

EDCS-45800001.translation: [---] Yriraban son of Isicuar, BABAR, EIMSE VLH, 5NI.
EDCS-45800001.summary: This inscription is fragmented and appears to record a personal dedication or epitaph with names and possibly numerical or directional information.

EDCS-45900001.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Victoricus, pious, lived 25 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-45900001.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Victoricus, stating his age and that he is buried here.

EDCS-45900005.translation: Dittea, a matron, lived in Christ.
EDCS-45900005.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a Christian matron named Dittea.

EDCS-45900012.summary: This is a brief invocation wishing protection from the Ausonians, an ancient Italic people.

EDCS-45900016.translation: Publius Caelius Secundus lived 80 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-45900016.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Publius Caelius Secundus, stating his age and that he is buried here.

EDCS-45900018.translation: To our lord, Imperator Caesar Flavius Constantinus Maximus Pius Felix Victor and Triumphant ever Augustus, born for the good of the state, and to Flavius Claudius Constantinus, the most noble Caesars.
EDCS-45900018.summary: This is a dedication to Emperor Constantinus Maximus and Caesar Constantinus, honoring them as rulers beneficial to the state.

EDCS-45900019.summary: This inscription likely indicates a distance, possibly in miles or paces, from a place called Tacapis.

EDCS-45900035.translation: [MIVII?] Mientius, may you [live?] happily with your [---] bono tuus EMENI
EDCS-45900035.summary: This inscription appears to be a dedication or wish for well-being, possibly for a person named Mientius, with some unclear Latin phrases.

EDCS-45900041.translation: Dativa with her grandchildren in peace.
EDCS-45900041.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Dativa and her grandchildren, indicating they are at rest.

EDCS-45900042.summary: This is a name, likely of a freedman given the cognomen Felix, possibly an owner's name or the name of the deceased.

EDCS-45900043.translation: Dedicated to the spirits of the underworld. Saturus lived for 8 days.
EDCS-45900043.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the death of a very young child, Saturus, who lived for only 8 days.

EDCS-45900046.translation: To our lords, the most noble Caesars Flavius Valerius Constantinus.
EDCS-45900046.summary: This is a dedication to the Roman Emperors Constantine I, likely part of a larger inscription on a public monument.

EDCS-45900049.summary: This is a short epitaph for a woman named Anna, indicating her faithful adherence to Christianity.

EDCS-45900050.translation: Bitalis, faithful, lived in peace for 7 years, buried on the 4th day before the Nones of April in the 5th indiction.
EDCS-45900050.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Bitalis, who lived for 7 years and was buried on a specific date within the 5th indiction, suggesting a Christian context.

EDCS-45900054.summary: This is likely an ownership inscription or a dedication naming Tiberius Claudius Apotisedes.

EDCS-45900059.summary: This is an ownership inscription or a dedication, possibly on a tomb or a public work, belonging to Lucius Gellius Quadratus.

EDCS-45900065.summary: This is a brief indication of origin and parentage, possibly for a freedman or a local official in Carthage.

EDCS-45900068.translation: Imperator Caesar Marcus Aurellius Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus, Parthicus Maximus, Britannicus Maximus, Germanicus Maximus, in his 18th year of tribunician power, consul for the 4th time, father of the fatherland.
EDCS-45900068.summary: This is a lengthy imperial titulature of Marcus Aurelius, recording his titles and powers up to his 18th tribunician power and 4th consulship, dating it to around 175 AD.

EDCS-45900070.translation: To our lords, the most noble Caesars Flavius Valerius Constantinus and Galerius Valerius Maximianus.
EDCS-45900070.summary: This is a dedication to the Roman Emperors Constantine I and Maximian, likely part of a public inscription from the period of their co-rule.

EDCS-46100452.translation: This is Augustine's place; Crescens and Marinus made it.
EDCS-46100452.summary: This inscription records the construction of a place by Crescens and Marinus, dedicated to Augustine, likely in the late Roman period.

EDCS-46100461.summary: This inscription is a simple dedication to Quintus Oppius Natalis, possibly a tombstone or memorial.

EDCS-46100463.translation: Bonifatius, faithful, lived in peace for 27 years. Sabuatia, faithful, lived in peace for 40 years. Bolitanus, faithful, lived for 2 years and 2 months. Minnace, faithful, lived for 22 years.
EDCS-46100463.summary: This inscription records the lifespans of four individuals (Bonifatius, Sabuatia, Bolitanus, and Minnace) who are described as 'faithful' and lived 'in peace', likely a Christian burial inscription from the late Roman or early Byzantine period.

EDCS-46100473.summary: This inscription identifies Lucullus as 'the secretary', possibly a funerary or commemorative marker for an official.

EDCS-46100475.summary: This inscription is a dedication or memorial to Theodore, identified as an archbishop, likely from the early Christian period.

EDCS-46100477.summary: This inscription identifies Georgius as 'chief secretary', possibly a funerary or commemorative marker for a high-ranking official.

EDCS-46100481.translation: In this place rested Quintus. He lived as a faithful one in peace.
EDCS-46100481.summary: This inscription marks the burial place of Quintus, describing him as 'faithful' and having lived 'in peace', likely a Christian epitaph.

EDCS-46100482.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcia Caecilia, dutiful, lived for 18 years and months. She is buried here.
EDCS-46100482.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication to Marcia Caecilia, stating her age at death and that she is buried here, likely a pagan Roman epitaph.

EDCS-46100483.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcus Mesallinus Aliquas lived for 30 years and 6 months and 5 days. His most dutiful sisters made this.
EDCS-46100483.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication to Marcus Mesallinus Aliquas, stating his age at death and that it was made by his sisters, likely a pagan Roman epitaph.

EDCS-46100484.translation: Lucius Pontius Iaser lived for 70 years. The day of his burial is the 13th day before the Kalends of April.
EDCS-46100484.summary: This inscription records the lifespan of Lucius Pontius Iaser and the date of his burial, likely a Roman epitaph.

EDCS-46100485.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Severus lived 65 years. Saturninus made (this monument).
EDCS-46100485.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Severus and stating that Saturninus erected the monument.

EDCS-46100490.translation: Lucius Domitius Agatiarius lived 65 years and bequeathed his heirs the place of burial. His heirs, who were born, made this monument for their father.
EDCS-46100490.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespan of Lucius Domitius Agatiarius and states that his heirs erected the monument for him.

EDCS-46100499.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Lucius Domitius Aurelianus, Pious, Fortunate, Augustus, Consul. 39 miles.
EDCS-46100499.summary: This inscription records a measurement of 39 miles dedicated to Emperor Aurelian.

EDCS-46100509.translation: The names of those who built the basilica and its appurtenances at their own expense: Lucius Castricius Messor, priest; Publius Apuleius Felix; Tiberius Claudius Victor Felix; Titus Flavius Karus; Sextus Iulius Felix; Caius Antonius Felix; Lucius Geminius Felix; Titus Flavius Potitus; Tiberius Iulius Annianus; Helvius Primus; Helvius Maximus; Caius Iulius Sabinus; Caius Licceius Felix; Lucius Licceius Lucinus; Marcus Cornelius Primus; Caius Licceius Grontha; Caius Marcius Pudens; Caius Modius Madauritanus; Lucius Antonius Datus; Titus Flavius Honorinus; Decimus Marcus Lucceius Extricatus; Caius Iulius Namphamo; Caius Geminius Datus; Lucius Egnatius Saturninus; Marcus Vitruvius Derisor; Quintus Munius Musicus; Caius Iulius Baliathon; Caius Marius Marchianus; Quintus Munius Datus; Caius Iulius Paulus; Caius Minucius Datus; Caius Iulius Felix; Caius Iulius Felix Narcissus.
EDCS-46100509.summary: This inscription lists the names of individuals who collectively funded the construction of a basilica and its associated structures.

EDCS-46200053.summary: This is a fragment of a funerary inscription recording the name Bier and a portion of their lifespan.

EDCS-46200057.summary: This is a tombstone or funerary marker identifying Equitia Cesia Florin.

EDCS-46200060.translation: From the workshop of Lucius Plotius Clemens.
EDCS-46200060.summary: This inscription indicates that the object it is on was made in the workshop of Lucius Plotius Clemens.

EDCS-46200064.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Fortun lived 11 years.
EDCS-46200064.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Fortun.

EDCS-46200071.translation: Lived 29 years, 10 months, and 24 days. Marcus Aemilius Aquilinus Setinianus (dedicated this) to his most loving brother. He is buried here.
EDCS-46200071.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespan of a deceased individual and states that it was erected by his brother.

EDCS-46200072.translation: Of the Emperor Caesar, son of the divine Septimius Severus Pius Arabicus Adiabenicus Parthicus Maximus Britannicus Maximus, grandson of the divine Antoninus Pius Germanicus Sarmaticus, great-grandson of the divine Antoninus Pius, [great-great-grandson] of the divine Hadrian...
EDCS-46200072.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription detailing the imperial lineage, likely part of a dedication or honorific title for an emperor.

EDCS-46200073.translation: Emperor Caesar Marcus Antonius Gordianus, grandson of the deified Antoninus Gordianus, son of the sister of the deified Antoninus Gordianus, Pious, Happy, Augustus, most brave, most fortunate, chief priest, with tribunician power, father of the country, consul, proconsul for the 78th time.
EDCS-46200073.summary: This is a dedication by Emperor Gordian III, listing his titles and honors, likely from the 3rd century CE.

EDCS-46200090.translation: From the potteries of Quintus A. M., under the consuls Servianus (for the 3rd time) and Varus.
EDCS-46200090.summary: This is a potter's mark indicating the origin of ceramics, dated to the consulship of Servianus and Varus.

EDCS-46200109.translation: To Minerva Augusta, of the people of Thusdria.
EDCS-46200109.summary: This is a dedication to the goddess Minerva Augusta by the community of Thusdria.

EDCS-46200112.summary: This inscription likely marks ownership or a dedication by Gaius Cassius Salinus.

EDCS-46200113.summary: This inscription identifies Iulianus and notes his former position as prefect.

EDCS-46200114.translation: Of Favor, daughter of Gnaeus Domitius.
EDCS-46200114.summary: This inscription identifies Favor, possibly a dedication or memorial, and her father Gnaeus Domitius.

EDCS-46200115.translation: The place of Victorinus; he lived 50 years, 5 days.
EDCS-46200115.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Victorinus, recording his name, lifespan, and burial location.

EDCS-46300013.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Sintropa Secunda lived sixty-five years.
EDCS-46300013.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Sintropa Secunda, dedicated to the spirits of the dead and recording her age.

EDCS-46300019.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Ammahanius Privatus lived eighty-two years; he is buried here.
EDCS-46300019.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Ammahanius Privatus, dedicated to the spirits of the dead and recording his age and burial.

EDCS-46300020.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Gaius Annius Mellitus, pious, lived 75 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-46300020.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Gaius Annius Mellitus, dedicated to the spirits of the dead and recording his age and burial.

EDCS-46300021.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Atiolena Felicitas, dutiful, lived 75 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-46300021.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Atiolena Felicitas after living 75 years.

EDCS-46300022.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Gaius Clodius Lucilianus, dutiful, lived more or less 93 years.
EDCS-46300022.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Gaius Clodius Lucilianus after living approximately 93 years.

EDCS-46300023.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Lucius Flavius Romanianus, dutiful, lived 18 years, 6 months, and 18 days; he is buried here. May your bones rest well.
EDCS-46300023.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lucius Flavius Romanianus, who died at the age of 18 years, 6 months, and 18 days.

EDCS-46300024.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Fortunata.
EDCS-46300024.summary: A very brief funerary epitaph for Fortunata.

EDCS-46300025.translation: Clodius Hospitalis, dutiful, lived 95 years; he is buried here. May the earth be light upon you.
EDCS-46300025.summary: A funerary epitaph for Clodius Hospitalis, who lived 95 years.

EDCS-46300026.translation: Lucius Sedius Firmus, dutiful, lived 85 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-46300026.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lucius Sedius Firmus, who lived 85 years.

EDCS-46300041.translation: A happy, fortunate new year to you, Cellia For.
EDCS-46300041.summary: A New Year's greeting or dedication, possibly to a person named Cellia For.

EDCS-46300047.summary: A dedication or inscription naming Carterius Philtatius, possibly a tombstone or a gift.

EDCS-46300069.translation: Innocentius, faithful, lived in peace for 2 years, on the Ides of August, in the tenth indiction.
EDCS-46300069.summary: A funerary epitaph for Innocentius, who lived for 2 years and died on the Ides of August during the tenth indiction.

EDCS-46300077.translation: and decay, and with his own generosity, expenses, and costs, dedicated the games.
EDCS-46300077.summary: This fragment likely records the dedication of games by an official from his own resources.

EDCS-46300082.translation: Caecilia Rogati, daughter, lived 17 years; she is placed here.
EDCS-46300082.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Caecilia Rogati, recording her age at death.

EDCS-46300083.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Publius Flavius Securus, devoted, lived 9 years; he is placed here.
EDCS-46300083.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Publius Flavius Securus, recording his age at death and dedicating the monument to the underworld deities.

EDCS-46300084.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Iulia Restuta lived 80 years.
EDCS-46300084.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Iulia Restuta, recording her age at death and dedicating the monument to the underworld deities.

EDCS-46300085.translation: Matutina, slave woman, lived 30 years; placed here.
EDCS-46300085.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Matutina, a slave, recording her age at death.

EDCS-46300086.translation: Habetdeus the faithful lived 4 months and 14 days; placed on the third day before the Nones of July in the third year.
EDCS-46300086.summary: This inscription records the lifespan of Habetdeus and provides a precise date of placement, likely marking a burial in the third year of an unspecified reign or era.

EDCS-46300087.translation: Iulia Fedosa the faithful lived 70 years in peace; she is placed here.
EDCS-46300087.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Iulia Fedosa, recording her age at death and noting her peaceful life.

EDCS-46300089.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Licinia Saturnina lived 35 years.
EDCS-46300089.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Licinia Saturnina, recording her age at death and dedicating the monument to the underworld deities.

EDCS-46300090.translation: The tomb of Lucius Amnius Quintus.
EDCS-46300090.summary: This inscription marks the tomb of Lucius Amnius Quintus.

EDCS-46300091.summary: This is a simple funerary inscription, likely a name on a tombstone, for Aurelius Crescens.

EDCS-46300092.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Optatus for his most beloved wife Iustae, who lived 1 year, 7 months, and 9 days; she is placed here.
EDCS-46300092.summary: This tombstone inscription records the short life of Iustae, beloved wife of Optatus, and is dedicated to the underworld deities.

EDCS-46300094.translation: To our Lord Flavius Valerius Constantinus, a German, noble by birth, for the good of the Republic.
EDCS-46300094.summary: This inscription honors Emperor Constantine I, likely dating to his reign (306-337 AD).

EDCS-46300095.translation: To our Lord Flavius Claudius Julianus, ever Augustus.
EDCS-46300095.summary: This inscription honors Emperor Julian the Apostate, likely dating to his reign (361-363 AD).

EDCS-46300103.translation: Dermensius Dativus, with his family, has paid his vow.
EDCS-46300103.summary: This is a votive inscription from an individual named Dativus, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-46400965.translation: For the safety of our Emperor Caesar Trajanus, princeps of the whole world, and of his divine household, the best, Germanicus, Parthicus, given by Licinius Maximus and Felix Victor Augustus, freedmen procurators, according to the example of the Mancian law. Those who will live within the estate of the Villa Magnae Varianae, that is Mappalia Siga, are permitted to cultivate the lands that are surplus, according to the Mancian law, in such a way that whoever cultivates them shall have the use of the produce that grows in that place for himself, but shall provide to the owners or their contractors or overseers their shares according to the law. On this condition, that the farmers shall render to the contractors or overseers of that estate the full amounts of produce from each crop that they should bring to the threshing floor and process, according to their own judgment. And if the contractors or overseers of that estate announce that they will give the farmer's share, the farmers shall be bound by contract, by which they must provide the farmer's share of the produce and vines to the contractors or overseers of that estate, as is customary. Those who have or will have farms in the Villa Magnae or Mappalia Siga estate must provide to the owners or their contractors or overseers their share of the produce and vines according to their judgment, namely one-third of the wheat from the threshing floor, one-third of the barley from the threshing floor, one-third of the beans from the threshing floor, one-third of the wine from the vat, one-third of the pressed oil, one sextarius of honey from each hive. The law written above this was made by Lurius Victor, son of Odilo, master, and Flavius Geminius, defender. Felice Annobalis Birzilis will have five hives. At the time of the honey harvest, he must give to the owners or contractors or overseers of that estate, those who farm for a share, if anyone moves hives, swarms, honey vessels from the Villa Magnae or Mappaliae Siga estate to an area of eight iugera, so that fraud against the owners or contractors or overseers does not occur, the hives, swarms, honey vessels, and honey that are in that estate will belong to the contractors or overseers of that estate. Figs and trees outside the orchard, which is within the villa itself, shall not exceed the number of iugera that the farmer, according to his judgment, must give to the contractor or overseer of the fruits collected. Old fig groves and olive groves planted before this law must provide their fruits to the contractor or overseer according to custom. If any fig grove is made later, its fruits may be enjoyed by the one who planted it at his own discretion for five continuous fig harvests. After the fifth harvest, the same law as written above must be provided to the contractors or overseers of that estate. It is permitted to plant and cultivate vines in place of old ones, on the condition that for the next five grape harvests, the one who planted them may enjoy the fruits of those vines at his own discretion. Likewise, after the fifth harvest, they must provide one-third of the fruits of those vines to the contractors or overseers of that estate, according to the Mancian law. It is permitted to plant and cultivate an olive grove in a place that one has cleared from uncultivated land, on the condition that for the next ten olive harvests, the one who planted it may enjoy the fruits of that olive grove at his own discretion. After the olive harvests, they must provide one-third of the pressed oil to the contractors or overseers of that estate. Those who graft wild olive trees must provide one-third after five years. The fruits of those lands in the Villa Magnae Varianae or Mappaliae Siga which are or will be outside those areas that have villages, must be given to the contractors or overseers. Guards must collect for each head of cattle grazed within the Villa Magnae or Mappaliae Siga estate, four asses to the contractors or overseers of the owners of that estate. If anyone cuts, picks, transports, burns, or otherwise removes fruits, whether standing, hanging, ripe, or unripe, from the Villa Magnae or Mappaliae Siga estate, the farmer shall owe compensation to the contractors or overseers of that estate for the loss. If those who have planted in the Villa Magnae or Mappaliae Siga estate have legitimate children born in lawful marriage, they may bequeath them by will. Superficies that have been or will be granted under the Mancian law or by trust shall be preserved. The right of trust under the Mancian law shall be observed. Whoever has cultivated a superficies from uncultivated land and has built a building thereon, or whoever cultivated it and later ceased to cultivate it, at the time when that superficies ceased to be cultivated, the right of cultivation shall be preserved for them for two full years from the day on which they ceased to cultivate. After two years, the contractors or overseers of that estate shall be deemed to own that superficies which was cultivated in the preceding year and has ceased to be cultivated. The contractor or overseer of that estate must announce the cultivated superficies. The announcement is marked by a seal. Likewise, in the following year, the contractor or overseer of that estate must order it to be cultivated without complaint, after two years. No contractor or overseer shall compel any tenant farmer living within the Villa Magnae or Mappaliae Siga estate to provide to the owners or contractors or overseers annually, for each person, two days of labor for plowing, two days of labor for harvesting, and two days of labor for weeding of any kind. The tenant farmers of that estate must provide, within the year, for their own names, to the contractors for individual guard duties, and for the stipendiaries who live in the Villa Magnae or Mappaliae Siga estate, to the contractors, overseers, guards, and servants, one-quarter of each.
EDCS-46400965.summary: This is a detailed agricultural lease agreement (lex fundi) for the Villa Magnae Varianae and Mappalia Siga estates, outlining the rights and obligations of landowners, contractors, overseers, and tenant farmers regarding cultivation, produce sharing, and labor duties, issued under the authority of Emperor Trajan and regulated by Mancian law.

EDCS-46601036.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Cariaia the pious lived for 55 years.
EDCS-46601036.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the name and lifespan of a deceased woman, Cariaia, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-46601044.translation: Severus lived in Cos [during the reign of] Tada.
EDCS-46601044.summary: This is a very brief inscription recording the name Severus and his presence in Cos, possibly referencing a specific period or official, likely Roman Imperial.

EDCS-46601045.summary: This is a simple funerary inscription stating the name and age of the deceased, Lucilla, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-46601046.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Sentia Ianuaria lived for 74 years. Most excellent Postumia Inuia.
