EDCS-46601048.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Postumia Saturnina lived for [unknown years]. Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Imerius lived for 81 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-46601048.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lives of two individuals, Postumia Saturnina and Imerius, with the latter's age and burial location specified, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-46601050.translation: To our Lord Galerius Valerius Maximianus, most noble Caesar.
EDCS-46601050.summary: This is an honorific inscription dedicated to Caesar Galerius Valerius Maximianus, likely from the late Roman Empire.

EDCS-46601051.translation: To our lord Magnus Magnentius, pious, fortunate, ever-Augustus.
EDCS-46601051.summary: This is a dedication to the emperor Magnentius.

EDCS-46601054.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Julius Hermas, pious, lived 5 years and 6 months; his father took care of him.
EDCS-46601054.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Julius Hermas, set up by his father.

EDCS-46601055.translation: Euticia, sweet one, lived 30 years in peace; she died on the fourth day before the Kalends of June.
EDCS-46601055.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Euticia, dating to May 29th.

EDCS-46601058.translation: To our lords Flavius Valentinianus and Valens, ever-Augusti.
EDCS-46601058.summary: This is a dedication to the emperors Valentinian I and Valens.

EDCS-46700145.translation: Bernacla lived two years in peace.
EDCS-46700145.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Bernacla.

EDCS-46700148.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Aurelius Kandidus.

EDCS-46700149.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Dativa.

EDCS-46700151.translation: Aelius Victorianus lived 11 years and 2 months in peace.
EDCS-46700151.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Aelius Victorianus.

EDCS-46700152.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Fortunata.

EDCS-46700158.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Ispesina.

EDCS-46700159.translation: Ciisonia, faithful, lived in peace for 28 years.
EDCS-46700159.summary: A funerary inscription for Ciisonia, who died at the age of 28.

EDCS-46700162.summary: A very brief funerary inscription for Maxentia.

EDCS-46700163.translation: Sacred to the goddess Sancta Genitrix Masclianis, Conservator, at the oracle of her divinity's command, Lucius Aurelius Ianuarius, freedman of the Augusti and procurator of Masclianis, restored and dedicated the temple, which had collapsed from age, from its foundations at his own expense.
EDCS-46700163.summary: A dedication by Lucius Aurelius Ianuarius of a restored temple to the goddess Sancta Genitrix Masclianis, prompted by an oracle.

EDCS-46700164.translation: Artorius Selaci, conductor, this Mercurian villa and
EDCS-46700164.summary: An incomplete inscription that seems to record the actions of Artorius Selaci concerning a villa named Mercurian.

EDCS-46700165.translation: Measure of the estate of Publius Ramius Badius and Augustus, 1060 iugera; boundary stone placed at 30 [paces?].
EDCS-46700165.summary: A boundary stone marking the extent of an estate belonging to Publius Ramius Badius and Augustus, with a measure of 1060 iugera.

EDCS-46700166.translation: To Marcus Voltinius Certo, son of Lucius, of the Horatia tribe.
EDCS-46700166.summary: A dedication to Marcus Voltinius Certo, son of Lucius, likely a funerary or honorary inscription.

EDCS-46800005.translation: Freedman of Sextus Caecilius Salvius, lived 77 years. Felicitas, his wife, lived 53 years.
EDCS-46800005.summary: A funerary inscription for a freedman of Sextus Caecilius Salvius and his wife Felicitas.

EDCS-46800006.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Albia Aurelia Fortunata, dutiful, lived 24 years and [some] months. Marcus Bucius Victor dedicated this to his dearest wife.
EDCS-46800006.summary: A funerary inscription dedicated by Marcus Bucius Victor to his wife Albia Aurelia Fortunata, who died at age 24.

EDCS-46800007.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Lolliac Reducta, dutiful, lived 80 years and 5 months. Placed here.
EDCS-46800007.summary: A funerary inscription for Lolliac Reducta, who died at the age of 80 years and 5 months.

EDCS-46800118.translation: Restitutus, in peace, lived [age, missing] years; departed on the day before the Kalends of January.
EDCS-46800118.summary: A funerary inscription for Restitutus, who died on December 31st.

EDCS-46800119.translation: Honoratus lived in peace for 3 years, departed on the day before the Ides of April.
EDCS-46800119.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan and death date of Honoratus, likely a child.

EDCS-46800120.translation: Sweet Daltia lived in peace for 30 years, departed on the 15th day before the Kalends of January.
EDCS-46800120.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan and death date of Daltia.

EDCS-46800121.translation: Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Severus Alexander Pius Felix Augustus, chief priest, with tribunician power for the 4th time, [ordered this] through Publius Flavius Clemens, his procurator, 3 miles from Aras.
EDCS-46800121.summary: This is a milestone inscription indicating a distance from Aras, commissioned by Emperor Severus Alexander and overseen by his procurator.

EDCS-46800122.translation: and Gaius Julius Maximus, most noble Caesar, prince of youth, [ordered] the Augustan milestones to be placed through Claudius Pyrrhus, from Aras.
EDCS-46800122.summary: This is a milestone inscription indicating the placement of Augustan milestones, commissioned by Gaius Julius Maximus.

EDCS-46800124.translation: 4 miles from Aras for the blessed Augustus.
EDCS-46800124.summary: This is a milestone inscription indicating a distance from Aras, dedicated to Augustus.

EDCS-46800126.translation: Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Severus Alexander Pius Felix Augustus, chief priest, father of the fatherland, with tribunician power, consul, proconsul, ordered this milestone to be made through Publius Flavius Clemens, his procurator, 7 miles from Aras.
EDCS-46800126.summary: This is a milestone inscription detailing a distance from Aras, commissioned by Emperor Severus Alexander and overseen by his procurator.

EDCS-46800142.translation: lived 53 years, is buried here for 13 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-46800142.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording a person's lifespan and indicating their burial place, possibly with a revision to the burial duration.

EDCS-46800143.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of a person.

EDCS-46800144.summary: This is a funerary inscription commemorating a wife, recording her lifespan.

EDCS-46800145.translation: Monument of FYLSRRI, lived 64 years, and of IULICIA, lived 15 years.
EDCS-46800145.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespans of two individuals, FYLSRRI and IULICIA, for whom a monument was erected.

EDCS-46800146.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Marcia S, number 80. Sacred to the Divine Manes. QV T C.
EDCS-46800146.summary: This is a funerary dedication to the Divine Manes, with some unclear abbreviations at the end.

EDCS-46800147.translation: Marius Rogatus made this for himself and his wife during his lifetime. He also requested it. He lived 75 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-46800147.summary: This is a self-funded funerary epitaph for Marius Rogatus and his wife, dating from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-46800149.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Iulia Tutiana lived 34 years and 4 months. Quintianus for his dearest wife.
EDCS-46800149.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by Quintianus to his wife, Iulia Tutiana, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-46800188.summary: This is a simple funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of a child named Bellator.

EDCS-46800189.translation: Maninius Rogatianus. Caninius Felix dedicated this. Maninius Rogatus, father.
EDCS-46800189.summary: This funerary inscription records the dedication made by Maninius Rogatus, father of Maninius Rogatianus, possibly Caninius Felix.

EDCS-46800190.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Caius Memius Marci Maxutius lived 51 years. Caius Memius Donatus lived 67 years.
EDCS-46800190.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to the Divine Manes and records the lifespans of two individuals, Caius Memius Marci Maxutius and Caius Memius Donatus.

EDCS-46800191.translation: Cilius Vonifatius lived 70 years, more or less, in peace.
EDCS-46800191.summary: This epitaph records the lifespan of Cilius Vonifatius, who lived 'in pace' (in peace), a common phrase on Christian funerary monuments.

EDCS-46800193.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. O OCEA PAPAN is buried here.
EDCS-46800193.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to the Divine Manes and marks the burial place of O OCEA PAPAN.

EDCS-46800194.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. L Hilarus lived 1 year and 12 days. He is buried here.
EDCS-46800194.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to the Divine Manes and records the short life of L. Hilarus, who lived for 1 year and 12 days.

EDCS-46800195.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Nonia D lived 50 years. Felix for her, well deserving.
EDCS-46800195.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated by Felix to Nonia D, who lived 50 years, honoring her as 'well deserving'.

EDCS-46800196.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. LIA QUARTA lived 109 years. Caius Tadius made this for his dearest wife.
EDCS-46800196.summary: A funerary dedication by Caius Tadius for his wife, Lia Quarta, who lived 109 years.

EDCS-46800198.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. IULIA SATURNINA lived 70 years. Her devoted husband made this monument.
EDCS-46800198.summary: A funerary monument created by a devoted husband for his wife, Iulia Saturnina, who lived 70 years.

EDCS-46800199.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. FIEROXAANISI made this for his son who lived 5 years.
EDCS-46800199.summary: A funerary dedication for a son who died at the age of 5.

EDCS-46800207.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. ANTONIO NICASTRIS was the wife of Caius Tadius Saturninus.
EDCS-46800207.summary: A funerary dedication for Antonio Nicastris, wife of Caius Tadius Saturninus.

EDCS-46800209.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. POMPEIA SPES, pious, lived 82 years, lies here. Lucius Scribonius, son of Marcus, Quirina Barbarus, pious, lived 62 years, lies here. Scribonius Felix Caecilianus Faustus made this for his parents.
EDCS-46800209.summary: A joint funerary monument for Pompeia Spes and Lucius Scribonius Barbarus, made by their son Scribonius Felix Caecilianus Faustus.

EDCS-46800218.translation: IULIA, daughter of Marcus, pious, lived 48 years, [sacred] to the departed spirits. Her husband Dia Manibus Marcus Bennius Saturninus, pious, lived 97 years, lies here.
EDCS-46800218.summary: A funerary monument for Iulia, wife of Marcus Bennius Saturninus, who lived 48 years, and for Marcus Bennius Saturninus himself, who lived 97 years.

EDCS-46800223.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. MEMMIA BASSILLIA lived 6 years, 5 months, and 13 days. Rufus, her most beloved father, made this. She lies here.
EDCS-46800223.summary: A funerary dedication by Rufus for his daughter Memmia Bassillia, who died at the age of 6 years, 5 months, and 13 days.

EDCS-46800225.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. CAIUS LUCRONIUS MUSTUS, pious, lived 43 years, lies here.
EDCS-46800225.summary: A funerary dedication for Caius Lucronius Mustus, who lived 43 years.

EDCS-46800226.translation: To our lord Constantinus, the greatest, Augustus, the good, born for the state.
EDCS-46800226.summary: An honorific inscription likely dedicated to Emperor Constantine I, praising his role in the state.

EDCS-46900002.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. HONORATUS, pious, lived [number] years.
EDCS-46900002.summary: A partial funerary dedication for Honoratus, who was pious and lived an unspecified number of years.

EDCS-46900004.translation: To the Divine Manes. Modius Honoratus lived 5 years.
EDCS-46900004.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a child named Modius Honoratus, indicating his lifespan.

EDCS-46900006.translation: To the Divine Manes. Tiberius Claudius Extricatus lived 77 years.
EDCS-46900006.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Tiberius Claudius Extricatus, indicating his lifespan.

EDCS-46900007.translation: To the Divine Manes. La Qua, pious, lived 20 years, is buried here. Aelius Ianuarius, pious, lived 80 years, is buried here.
EDCS-46900007.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lives and burials of two individuals, La Qua and Aelius Ianuarius.

EDCS-46900009.summary: This is a dedication to the emperor Vespasian.

EDCS-46900010.translation: To the Divine Manes. Secunda Felicis, daughter of Carpi Zaebulis, pious, lived 12 years, is buried here.
EDCS-46900010.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a young girl named Secunda Felicis, indicating her lifespan and burial.

EDCS-46900015.translation: Vibius, son of Saturninus, pious, lived 35 years.
EDCS-46900015.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Vibius, son of Saturninus, indicating his lifespan.

EDCS-46900016.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for an individual named Gid, indicating her lifespan.

EDCS-46900017.summary: This inscription appears to be a simple name inscription, possibly for Marcus Octavius.

EDCS-46900018.translation: Idius Hospitalis, veteran, lived 65 years. To the Divine Manes.
EDCS-46900018.summary: This funerary epitaph is for Idius Hospitalis, a veteran, indicating his lifespan.

EDCS-46900019.translation: Caius Sessius Merops, pious, lived 90 years, is buried here.
EDCS-46900019.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Caius Sessius Merops, indicating his lifespan and burial.

EDCS-46900020.translation: Victoria the pious lived for 5 years; she lies here.
EDCS-46900020.summary: This inscription records the burial of a young girl named Victoria.

EDCS-46900021.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcus Cornelius Celsinus lived for 21 years; he lies here.
EDCS-46900021.summary: This inscription records the burial of Marcus Cornelius Celsinus, who died at the age of 21.

EDCS-46900022.translation: Quintilius Privatus lived for 25 years; he lies here.
EDCS-46900022.summary: This inscription records the burial of Quintilius Privatus, who died at the age of 25.

EDCS-46900278.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcus Livius Optatus lived for 75 years.
EDCS-46900278.summary: This inscription records the burial of Marcus Livius Optatus, who died at the age of 75.

EDCS-46900279.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Caius Cornelius Honoratus the pious lived for 67 years.
EDCS-46900279.summary: This inscription records the burial of Caius Cornelius Honoratus, who died at the age of 67.

EDCS-46900281.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Caius Cornelius Festus the pious lived for [some number of] years.
EDCS-46900281.summary: This inscription records the burial of Caius Cornelius Festus, with the age at death missing.

EDCS-46900296.translation: Narcissus, Pallas the younger. The swift destruction of hares.
EDCS-46900296.summary: This inscription is a witty epitaph for a person or animal named Narcissus, likening them to Pallas and the swiftness of hares.

EDCS-46900299.translation: Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Lucius Cossonius Eggius Marullus, Cossonius Scipio Orfitus Naragsara.
EDCS-46900299.summary: This inscription lists several high-status Roman names, likely related to a person's full nomenclature or a familial inscription.

EDCS-46900306.summary: This inscription records a sacred offering made by a priest.

EDCS-46900323.translation: Emperor Caesar Caius Messius Quintus Traianus Decius Pius Felix Augustus, chief priest, greatest conqueror of the Germans, with tribunician power for the 4th time, consul for the 3rd time, father of the fatherland, proconsul, and Quintus Herennius Etruscus Messius Decius, most noble Caesar, and Caius Valentius Hostilianus Messius Quintus, most noble Caesar, and Herennia Etruscilla Augusta, wife of our Augustus, restored the milestones.
EDCS-46900323.summary: This inscription records the restoration of milestones by Emperor Trajan Decius, his son Herennius Etruscus, his other son Hostilian, and his wife Herennia Etruscilla, likely during the mid-3rd century CE.

EDCS-46900324.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Publius Aelius Optatus, dutiful, lived [his years]. He is buried here.
EDCS-46900324.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Publius Aelius Optatus, recording his name and his burial.

EDCS-46900325.translation: Aelius Ianuarianus lived 25 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-46900325.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Aelius Ianuarianus, recording his name and age at death.

EDCS-46900326.translation: Aurelius Honoratus lived in peace [his years] and was made [---].
EDCS-46900326.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Aurelius Honoratus, mentioning his life in peace and a completion of some kind.

EDCS-46900328.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Licinia Saturnina Tuscinilla lived 7 years.
EDCS-46900328.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Licinia Saturnina Tuscinilla, recording her name and age at death.

EDCS-46900329.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Sentia Maxima lived 95 years.
EDCS-46900329.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Sentia Maxima, recording her name and age at death.

EDCS-46900331.translation: Geminius the faithful lived in peace more or less 22 years.
EDCS-46900331.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Geminius, recording his name, faithfulness, life in peace, and approximate age at death.

EDCS-46900332.translation: Fasilia lived in peace more or less 50 years.
EDCS-46900332.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Fasilia, recording her name, life in peace, and approximate age at death.

EDCS-46900333.translation: Eupalius, who belonged to God, lived in peace more or less 35 years and 5 months and 12 days.
EDCS-46900333.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Eupalius, recording his name, his belonging to God, life in peace, and approximate lifespan with months and days.

EDCS-46900334.translation: Pascasius lived in peace more or less 65 years.
EDCS-46900334.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Pascasius, recording his name, life in peace, and approximate age at death.

EDCS-46900335.translation: Herennia Martia, daughter of Boncus, dutiful, lived 34 years.
EDCS-46900335.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Herennia Martia, daughter of Boncus, recording her name, filial piety, and age at death.

EDCS-47100002.translation: Munatia Cicot, daughter of Marcus, lived 75 years.
EDCS-47100002.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Munatia Cicot, recording her name and age at death.

EDCS-47100003.translation: Iulia Rufina, daughter of Quintus, dutiful, lived 11 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-47100003.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Iulia Rufina, recording her name, parentage, piety, age, and burial.

EDCS-47100004.translation: Dedicated to the departed spirits. Homulla Saturnina, dutiful, lived 11 years; she is buried here. Dedicated to the departed spirits. Fabius Oratus lived 2 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-47100004.summary: This is a combined funerary epitaph for Homulla Saturnina and Fabius Oratus, recording their names, piety (for Homulla), ages, and burial.

EDCS-47100005.translation: Lucius Iulius Pudens lived 40 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-47100005.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Iulius Pudens, recording his name, age, and burial.

EDCS-47100006.translation: Dedicated to the departed spirits. Aemilia Dudate, freedwoman, dutiful, lived 61 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-47100006.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Aemilia Dudate, a freedwoman, recording her name, piety, age, and burial.

EDCS-47100007.translation: Lucius Pelcius Fidelis, son of Quintus, of the Quirina tribe, dutiful, lived 45 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-47100007.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Pelcius Fidelis, recording his name, parentage, tribal affiliation, piety, age, and burial.

EDCS-47100008.translation: Dedicated to the departed spirits. Iulia Secura lived 30 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-47100008.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Iulia Secura, recording her name, age, and burial.

EDCS-47100009.translation: Dedicated to the departed spirits. Iulia Arisut, dutiful, lived 55 years. Iulius Farus Cinnus lived 75 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-47100009.summary: This is a combined funerary epitaph for Iulia Arisut and Iulius Farus Cinnus, recording their names, piety (for Iulia), ages, and burial.

EDCS-47100010.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Caius Marius Olius, recording his name and age at death.

EDCS-47100011.translation: Iulia Rosa, daughter of Caius, dutiful, lived 13 years.
EDCS-47100011.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Iulia Rosa, recording her name, parentage, piety, and age at death.

EDCS-47100012.translation: Quintus Antonius Phethunis, son of Phethunis, lived 61 years.
EDCS-47100012.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Quintus Antonius Phethunis.

EDCS-47100013.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Lucius Cornelius Dubitatus lived.
EDCS-47100013.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the Divine Spirits, recording the name of Lucius Cornelius Dubitatus.

EDCS-47100014.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Caecilia Cati, pious, lived 55 years, is buried here. Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Caius Iulius Rufilianus, son of Caius, of the Quirina tribe, pious, lived 57 years, is buried here.
EDCS-47100014.summary: This is a double funerary inscription recording the lifespans and burial of Caecilia Cati and Caius Iulius Rufilianus.

EDCS-47100015.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Caius Iulius Rufulianus, son of Caius, pious, lived 25 years, is buried here.
EDCS-47100015.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan and burial of Caius Iulius Rufulianus.

EDCS-47100016.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Domitia Quarta lived 30 years.
EDCS-47100016.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Domitia Quarta.

EDCS-47100041.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Matrona, wife of Bailthon, lived years.
EDCS-47100041.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the name of Matrona, wife of Bailthon, but the lifespan is incomplete.

EDCS-47100043.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Marcus Flavius Cogitans lived approximately.
EDCS-47100043.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the name of Marcus Flavius Cogitans, with an incomplete lifespan.

EDCS-47100049.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Artoria Namsete lived years.
EDCS-47100049.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the name of Artoria Namsete, but the lifespan is incomplete.

EDCS-47100050.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Aphtonus Saturninus.

EDCS-47100056.translation: Lucius Iulius Romanus, son of Caius, lived 3 years, is buried here.
EDCS-47100056.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan and burial of Lucius Iulius Romanus.

EDCS-47100057.translation: Iulia Venusta lived 45 years; she lies here.
EDCS-47100057.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Iulia Venusta, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-47100058.summary: This is a simple funerary epitaph for Vincentius, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-47100060.translation: Marcus Helvius Barnaeus lived 55 years; he lies here.
EDCS-47100060.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcus Helvius Barnaeus, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-47200096.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Caius Iulius Fortunatus the younger lived 23 years.
EDCS-47200096.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated to the departed spirits, for Caius Iulius Fortunatus the younger, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-47200097.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Caius Maculipus nus lived 25 years; he lies here.
EDCS-47200097.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated to the departed spirits, for Caius Maculipus nus, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-47200098.translation: Caius Iulius Candus, son of Caius, of the Quirina tribe, dutiful, lived.
EDCS-47200098.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Caius Iulius Candus, a dutiful Roman citizen, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-47200099.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Modianus the dutiful lived 20 years.
EDCS-47200099.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated to the departed spirits, for Modianus, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-47200100.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Marcus Minthonius Victoricus lived 67 years.
EDCS-47200100.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated to the departed spirits, for Marcus Minthonius Victoricus, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-47200101.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Fulcinius Mesor lived 90 years.
EDCS-47200101.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated to the departed spirits, for Fulcinius Mesor, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-47200103.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Faustus lies here, of immense glory and renown through ancestors and lineage.
EDCS-47200103.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated to the departed spirits, praising the deceased Faustus for his lineage and renown, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-47200104.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Asissonia lived 91 years.
EDCS-47200104.summary: A funerary inscription recording the death of Asissonia after 91 years of life.

EDCS-47200106.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Electus the faithful lived here.
EDCS-47200106.summary: A funerary inscription recording the life of Electus, a faithful person.

EDCS-47200108.translation: Maximilianus the dutiful lived 46 years. M. Calpurnius lived 22 years.
EDCS-47200108.summary: A funerary inscription recording the deaths of Maximilianus and M. Calpurnius.

EDCS-47200109.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Fulvia Proculeia lived 65 years and 4 months.
EDCS-47200109.summary: A funerary inscription recording the death of Fulvia Proculeia after 65 years and 4 months of life.

EDCS-47200398.translation: Ovillia Iunia the dutiful lived 42 years and 5 days. Pelag...
EDCS-47200398.summary: A funerary inscription recording the death of Ovillia Iunia after 42 years and 5 days.

EDCS-47200399.translation: Selicius Apollinaris, son of Caius, the dutiful, lived 32 years. Lucius Selicius Restutus placed this for his patron. Farewell.
EDCS-47200399.summary: A funerary inscription set up by Lucius Selicius Restutus for his patron, Selicius Apollinaris, who died at 32 years of age.

EDCS-47200403.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Publius Iannius Felix lived 87 years.
EDCS-47200403.summary: A funerary inscription recording the death of Publius Iannius Felix after 87 years of life.

EDCS-47200404.translation: Marcus Aurelius Aris lived 65 years. He made this for himself while alive.

EDCS-47400181.translation: ... to his dearest wife was placed. She is buried here.
EDCS-47400181.summary: A funerary inscription dedicating a monument to a wife, indicating she is buried there.

EDCS-47400183.translation: ... was placed by a dutiful father.
EDCS-47400183.summary: A funerary inscription indicating a monument was placed by a dutiful father.

EDCS-47400189.summary: This inscription is a fragmentary funerary dedication mentioning Lucius Ota Must.

EDCS-47400192.translation: Clodia Victoria lived 26 years. She is buried here. Marcus Mess [---]
EDCS-47400192.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the life and death of Clodia Victoria, with a partial mention of Marcus Mess.

EDCS-47400193.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Dead. Nius Liberalis Natianus lived 17 years and 3 months. [He died of] a Greek sickness. His father Orius Ma mus placed [this here].
EDCS-47400193.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Nius Liberalis Natianus, who died at age 17 years and 3 months from a Greek illness, and was set up by his father.

EDCS-47400197.translation: Quintus Accius, son of Quintus, of the Titi tribe, from Lata, with his friends Ianti and Lucius Claudius Ga [---]
EDCS-47400197.summary: This inscription appears to be a dedication or a record of association involving Quintus Accius and his friends.

EDCS-47400198.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Dead. Lucius Aemilius Emeritus lived 40 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-47400198.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the life and death of Lucius Aemilius Emeritus, who lived to be 40 years old.

EDCS-47400199.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Dead. Marcus Aemilius Martialis lived 26 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-47400199.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the life and death of Marcus Aemilius Martialis, who lived to be 26 years old.

EDCS-47400200.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Dead. Sextus Aemilius Numerianus lived 20 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-47400200.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the life and death of Sextus Aemilius Numerianus, who lived to be 20 years old.

EDCS-47400201.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Dead. Quintus Apuleius Felix lived [---]
EDCS-47400201.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription for Quintus Apuleius Felix, indicating he lived for some duration.

EDCS-47400202.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Dead. Clodia Hedone, daughter of Publius, pious, lived 28 years. She is buried here. Lucius Pompeius Pudens [dedicated this] to his most excellent wife.
EDCS-47400202.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Clodia Hedone, dedicated by her husband Lucius Pompeius Pudens, stating she lived 28 years.

EDCS-47400203.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Dead. Cornelia Prima lived 70 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-47400203.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the life and death of Cornelia Prima, who lived to be 70 years old.

EDCS-47400204.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Publius Geminius Martialis, son of Publius, of the Quirina tribe, lived 27 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-47400204.summary: This is a tomb inscription recording the death and burial of Publius Geminius Martialis, who lived 27 years.

EDCS-47400205.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Publius Labienus Firmus lived 80 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-47400205.summary: This tomb inscription records the death of Publius Labienus Firmus, who lived 80 years.

EDCS-47400206.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Caelius Ursus set this up for his devoted wife, Valeria Fortunata, who lived 32 years.
EDCS-47400206.summary: This tomb inscription records that Caelius Ursus set up a monument for his wife Valeria Fortunata, who died at the age of 32.

EDCS-47400207.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Victor lived 35 years; his devoted mother Titia Ianuaria set this up for him; he is buried here.
EDCS-47400207.summary: This tomb inscription records the death of Victor, who lived 35 years, and was commemorated by his mother.

EDCS-47400208.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Flavia Sperata lived 39 years, 11 months, and 5 days; she is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Vedius Nortianus lived 38 years, 7 months, and 15 days; he is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Flavius Eutichus lived 32 years, 5 months; he is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Flavia Olympia lived 59 years, 8 months, and 23 days; she is buried here. Aurelius Exsuperans, freedman of the emperor, for his parents.
EDCS-47400208.summary: This is a complex tomb inscription recording the deaths of multiple individuals, including Flavia Sperata, Vedius Nortianus, Flavius Eutichus, and Flavia Olympia, with Aurelius Exsuperans dedicating it to his parents.

EDCS-47400209.translation: The Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Augustus, Parthicus Maximus, Britannicus Maximus, holder of tribunician power for the 20th time, consul for the 4th time, father of his country, restored (this).
EDCS-47400209.summary: This inscription records a restoration carried out by Emperor Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Augustus, likely during his reign (161-180 AD).

EDCS-47400210.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Vindicia Victorina lived 70 years, 3 months, 12 days. Her dutiful father erected this. Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulia Maxima lived 30 years, 7 months. Julius Maximus erected this for his dutiful daughter. She rests here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Aemilius Tertullus lived 7 years, [3] months. He rests here. His father erected this. Sacred to the departed spirits. Aemilius Saturninus lived 3 years, 2 months. He rests here. His father erected this.
EDCS-47400210.summary: This is a collection of four funerary inscriptions (epitaphs) dedicated to the departed spirits, recording the names, ages at death, and familial relationships of the deceased.

EDCS-47400211.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Aemilia Victoria lived.
EDCS-47400211.summary: This is a fragment of a tomb inscription that begins by dedicating the monument to the departed spirits and names Aemilia Victoria.

EDCS-47400212.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Aetrius Victoricus lived 90 years; he is buried here. His wife Donata set this up.
EDCS-47400212.summary: This tomb inscription records the death of Aetrius Victoricus, who lived 90 years, and was commemorated by his wife Donata.

EDCS-47400213.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Apiae Q lived 90 years; her devoted sons set this up; she is buried here.
EDCS-47400213.summary: This tomb inscription records that the devoted sons set up a monument for Apiae Q, who lived 90 years.

EDCS-47400214.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Arrius Compius lived 66 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-47400214.summary: This tomb inscription records the death of Arrius Compius, who lived 66 years.

EDCS-47400216.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Bacchis lived 35 years. Victor, her husband, placed this. She is buried here.
EDCS-47400216.summary: A funerary epitaph for Bacchis, placed by her husband Victor, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-47400217.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Lucius Caecilius Crescens, son of Lucius Caelius Fortunatus, of the Quirina tribe, lived 25 years. A devoted father placed this for his son. He is buried here. Sacred to the Divine Shades. Titus Caelius Vitalis lived 25 years. He is buried here. A devoted father placed this for his son.
EDCS-47400217.summary: A funerary epitaph commemorating Titus Caelius Vitalis and Lucius Caecilius Crescens, with a father setting up monuments for his sons, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-47400219.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Perelius Impetratus lived 45 years. Sacred to the Divine Shades. Clodia Catella lived 29 years.
EDCS-47400219.summary: A funerary epitaph for Perelius Impetratus and Clodia Catella, each with their age at death, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-47400221.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Sextus Duronius Fortunatus lived 10 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-47400221.summary: A funerary epitaph for Sextus Duronius Fortunatus, recording his age at death, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-47400222.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Of Quintus Egnatius, son of Caius, of the Quirina tribe, Maximini, lived 62 years, 7 months, 23 days. Vinnia Rutila placed this for her most beloved husband. He is buried here.
EDCS-47400222.summary: A funerary epitaph for Maximini, husband of Vinnia Rutila, detailing his age and burial, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-47400223.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Fabia Corrur lived 70 years. Victor placed this for his devoted mother. Sacred to the Divine Shades. Geminius Venustutus lived 3 years. He is buried here. Victor placed this for his devoted son. Sacred to the Divine Shades. Varia Satura lived 25 years. She is buried here. Victor placed this for his dearest, devoted wife. Sacred to the Divine Shades. Geminius Victor lived 80 years. He is buried here. Victor placed this for his devoted father.
EDCS-47400223.summary: A complex funerary monument where Victor set up epitaphs for his mother, son, wife, and father, all from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-47400224.translation: [...] lived 10 years, 5 months. He is buried here. Archimimus. Devoted parents placed this.
EDCS-47400224.summary: A funerary epitaph for Archimimus, erected by his parents, recording his age at death, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-47400225.translation: Felix lived 80 years. He is buried in this place. Valerius lived 58 years. He is buried in this place. Priva made this.
EDCS-47400225.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by Priva, recording the burial and ages of Felix and Valerius, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-47400226.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. [I]sii Forunatus
EDCS-47400226.summary: An incomplete funerary epitaph fragment, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-47400227.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Fortunatus lived 65 years. His sons placed this for their devoted father.
EDCS-47400227.summary: A funerary epitaph for Fortunatus, erected by his sons, recording his age at death, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-47400228.translation: Optata Venusta, having lived 35 years, was placed here. A devoted father set this up; she is buried here.
EDCS-47400228.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Optata Venusta, recording her age and that she was set up by her devoted father.

EDCS-47400229.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Granius Pelagius Aurelianus, who lived 29 years and 20 days, is buried here. A devoted brother set this up.
EDCS-47400229.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Granius Pelagius Aurelianus, recording his age and that he was set up by his devoted brother.

EDCS-47400230.translation: IVSLALISI lived 30 years and is buried here. Caius Iulius Grillus set this up as a devoted son.
EDCS-47400230.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for IVSLALISI, recording his age and that he was set up by his devoted son, Caius Iulius Grillus.

EDCS-47400231.translation: Having lived 35 years, Labenius Nundinarius set this up.
EDCS-47400231.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording that Labenius Nundinarius set up the monument after living 35 years.

EDCS-47400232.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcus Marius Petronianus, who lived 60 years, is buried here. Cassius Cuminus set this up.
EDCS-47400232.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcus Marius Petronianus, recording his age and that he was set up by Cassius Cuminus.

EDCS-47400233.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Pusa, who lived 23 years, is buried here. Primitivus set this up for his most devoted wife. Sacred to the departed spirits. Primitivus Pius, who lived 35 years, is buried here. Atticus set this up for his devoted son.
EDCS-47400233.summary: This inscription contains two separate funerary epitaphs: one for Pusa, set up by her husband Primitivus, and another for Primitivus Pius, set up by his son Atticus.

EDCS-47400234.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Tziula Pia, who lived 19 years, is buried here. Parthenius set this up for his most beloved wife.
EDCS-47400234.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Tziula Pia, recording her age and that she was set up by her beloved husband Parthenius.

EDCS-47400235.translation: Varro set this up for his devoted father; he is buried here.
EDCS-47400235.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording that Varro set up the monument for his devoted father, who is buried here.

EDCS-47400238.translation: Capriola Magnifica rested in peace; she lived 42 years and was buried on the first day of the Kalends of January, in the 13th indiction.
EDCS-47400238.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Capriola Magnifica, recording her age, date of burial, and a specified indiction, likely from the late Roman period.

EDCS-47400239.translation: Ioannes, also called Zuasti Magnificus, rested in peace; he lived 25 years and was buried on the tenth day before the Kalends of November, in the 9th indiction.
EDCS-47400239.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Ioannes (Zuasti Magnificus), recording his age, date of burial, and a specified indiction, likely from the late Roman period.

EDCS-47400240.translation: May the Lord turn to my assistance, O Lord, make haste to help me. John the subdeacon rested in peace. He lived 60 years. Buried on the fourth day before the Kalends of November, in the eighth indiction.
EDCS-47400240.summary: This is a Christian epitaph recording the death and burial of John the subdeacon, including his age and burial date.

EDCS-47400241.translation: Redentus the lector rested in peace. He lived 13 years, 5 months, and 14 days. Buried on the Ides of July, in the fifteenth indiction.
EDCS-47400241.summary: This is a Christian epitaph recording the death and burial of Redentus the lector, detailing his age and burial date.

EDCS-47400242.translation: My redeemer, my God, lives, and in the last days I shall rise again. I shall encompass my skin anew, and in my flesh I shall see my Lord. Secundus, most blessed bishop, rested in peace. He lived 70 years. Buried on the day of the indiction.
EDCS-47400242.summary: This is a Christian epitaph for Secundus, a bishop, stating his age and likely burial date, and including a profession of faith.

EDCS-47400243.translation: Silanus the deacon rested in peace. He lived 81 years and 8 months. Buried on the sixth day before the Kalends of November, in the sixth indiction.
EDCS-47400243.summary: This is a Christian epitaph recording the death and burial of Silanus the deacon, including his age and burial date.

EDCS-47400253.translation: April and September: 1st hour and 11, 24 feet; 2nd hour and 10, 14 feet; 3rd hour and 9, 10 feet; 4th hour and 8, 5 feet; 6th hour alone, 4 feet. May and August: 1st hour and 11, 23 feet; 2nd hour and 10, 13 feet; 3rd hour and 9, 9 feet; 4th hour and 8, 6 feet; 5th hour and 7, 4 feet; 6th hour alone, 3 feet. June and July: 1st hour and 11, 22 feet; 2nd hour and 10, 12 feet; 3rd hour and 9, 8 feet; 4th hour and 8, 5 feet; 5th hour and 7, 3 feet; 6th hour alone, 2 feet. By order of our lord father Iaquintus the bishop, I made this in Carthage in the quarter of the citadel near Placidiana's property.
EDCS-47400253.summary: This inscription records measurements of sunlight at different hours for various pairs of months, likely for architectural or astronomical purposes, commissioned by Bishop Iaquintus in Carthage.

EDCS-47400281.summary: This is a simple epitaph recording the name and age of Caius P. Vilonius.

EDCS-47400282.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Annia Secunda lived piously for 35 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-47400282.summary: This is a Roman funerary inscription for Annia Secunda, stating her pious life of 35 years and her burial place.

EDCS-47400285.translation: To our lord Lucius Domitius Alexander Pius.
EDCS-47400285.summary: This is a dedication to the emperor Lucius Domitius Alexander.

EDCS-47400286.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Nerva Trajanus Augustus Germanicus Dacicus, son of the divine Nerva, pontifex maximus, with tribunician power for the 13th time, imperator for the 6th time, consul for the 5th time, father of the country, [of the distance in] paces.
EDCS-47400286.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription honoring Emperor Trajan, listing his titles and achievements, likely part of a public monument.

EDCS-47400287.translation: To Emperor Caesar Publius Licinius Valerianus Pius Felix Augustus, pontifex maximus, with tribunician power for the 3rd time, consul for the 2nd time, father of the country, proconsul, and to Emperor Caesar Publius Licinius Gallienus Pius Felix Augustus, consul, father of the country, proconsul, by decree of the state of the Hipponiensian Region with the decree of the decurions.
EDCS-47400287.summary: This inscription records a decree by the city of Hipponium Regium honoring both Emperor Valerian and his son Gallienus, reflecting imperial authority and local governance.

EDCS-47400288.translation: To Emperor Caesar Gaius Vibius Trebonianus Gallus Pius Felix Augustus, chief priest, holding tribunician power, father of the country, consul. To Emperor Caesar Gaius Vibius Afinius Gallus Veldumnianus Volusianus Pius Felix Augustus, chief priest, holding tribunician power, father of the country.
EDCS-47400288.summary: This inscription records dedications to two Roman Emperors, Trebonianus Gallus and his co-emperor Volusianus, listing their official titles and honours.

EDCS-47400289.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Callinicus lived piously for 30 years and 3 months. Vibia Ianuaria made this for her deserving husband. May the earth lie lightly upon you.
EDCS-47400289.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Callinicus, set up by his wife Vibia Ianuaria, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-47400314.translation: From the estates of Flavius Aper. A tile work by Euphemius.
EDCS-47400314.summary: This is a mark on pottery or tilework, indicating ownership or origin from the estates of Flavius Aper and production by Euphemius.

EDCS-47400342.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Matusivia Saturnina lived piously for 20 years. Quintus Oriclonius Fortunatus lived piously for 85 years.
EDCS-47400342.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lives of Matusivia Saturnina and Quintus Oriclonius Fortunatus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-47400344.translation: Bizacenus the faithful lived in peace for two years.
EDCS-47400344.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Bizacenus, recording his faithful life of two years, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-47400345.translation: Publius Cornelius Victor lived piously for 80 years. Maria Hospita lived piously for 70 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-47400345.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Publius Cornelius Victor and Maria Hospita, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-47400346.summary: This is a fragmented inscription that mentions 'victor Constantine', likely referring to an emperor.

EDCS-47400347.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Enialion lived piously for 80 years.
EDCS-47400347.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Enialion, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-47400348.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Ulre, who is also called Nolu, lived for 60 years.
EDCS-47400348.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Ulre (also known as Nolu), likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-47400349.translation: VEAE L I VL TSE of the mother and the one who grows RER in FSMVT, unhappy.
EDCS-47400349.summary: This is a fragmented and difficult funerary inscription, possibly related to a mother and child, with unclear context and date.

EDCS-47400350.translation: Laurinus lived in peace for one year and four months.
EDCS-47400350.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Laurinus, recording his life of one year and four months, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-47400351.translation: In peace, Ebraxia lived for 6 years and 1 day.
EDCS-47400351.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Ebraxia, recording her life of 6 years and 1 day, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-47400352.translation: Secundiana lived in peace for 13 years, [some months and] days.
EDCS-47400352.summary: This epitaph records the lifespan of Secundiana, likely a young woman or girl given the mention of months and days.

EDCS-47400353.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Lollia Secunda, who lived 91 years, is buried here. Fabius Reburrus had this made for his mother.
EDCS-47400353.summary: This funerary epitaph was commissioned by Fabius Reburrus for his mother, Lollia Secunda, who lived to be 91.

EDCS-47400354.translation: Matsitsanus the loyal one [lived] 16 months in peace.
EDCS-47400354.summary: This epitaph marks the resting place of Matsitsanus, who died at 16 months of age.

EDCS-47400356.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Primitivus the pious lived 30 years, is buried here.
EDCS-47400356.summary: This funerary epitaph records the death of Primitivus, who was 30 years old.

EDCS-47400357.translation: Statia Restituta the pious lived 23 years, is buried here.
EDCS-47400357.summary: This epitaph records the death of Statia Restituta, who died at the age of 23.

EDCS-47400358.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Nainis the pious lived 8 years, is buried here.
EDCS-47400358.summary: This funerary epitaph records the death of Nainis, who died at the age of 8.

EDCS-47400365.translation: Donatianus the husband made [this] for his most virtuous wife Aemilia Subitana, and Renatus the father made [this] for his daughter Aelia Restituta.
EDCS-47400365.summary: This monument was dedicated by a husband to his wife and by a father to his daughter.

EDCS-47400366.summary: This epitaph records the lifespan of Bonifatius, who died at 31 years of age.

EDCS-47400368.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Sextia Tryphosa, freedwoman of Quinti, the pious, lived [some years], is buried here.
EDCS-47400368.summary: This funerary epitaph records the death of Sextia Tryphosa, a freedwoman, whose exact age is lost.

EDCS-47400370.translation: For the health and safety of our lord, the greatest and bravest Emperor Caesar Gaius Messius Quintus Traianus Decius, consul...
EDCS-47400370.summary: This fragmentary inscription is a dedication for the well-being of Emperor Trajan Decius, likely from the mid-3rd century CE.

EDCS-47400373.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Julius Galianus, a cavalryman of the First Wing of the Ituraeans, lived 45 years and served 23 years. Caius Beliabo, his heir, and Marcus Intaeius, his second heir, [set this up] for the armies of Lower Pannonia.
EDCS-47400373.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Julius Galianus, a cavalryman who served in Pannonia Inferior, set up by his heirs.

EDCS-47400375.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Atilius Pinna lived 75 years, 6 months, and 15 days; he is buried here.
EDCS-47400375.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan and burial of Atilius Pinna.

EDCS-47500643.translation: Sacred to Augustus. The most important men of the Mactaritan community, Oaelxa [did this] for me. Their names are listed below: Baliathon, son of Iopomp; Onnus, son of Bassus; Rogatus, son of Quadratus; Saris Baliathonis Novellus; Iuratha, son of Rimus; Rusticus, son of Quinti; Felix Sabini Rogatus; Caius Satur Patricius; Baliathonis Fidus; Laeti Barigbal Selcheni; Salius Hospitis; Aufulenius Ilec, son of Baracho; Ianuarius Bassi Faustus; Baliathonis Victor; Severi; [son] of Arsacis Baliatho; Flori Sedatus; [son] of Muggunis Barigbal; Rogatus Sapphir; [son] of Orassu.
EDCS-47500643.summary: This inscription, sacred to Augustus, lists prominent members of the Mactaritan community who contributed to a monument, likely erected during the Augustan period.

EDCS-47500645.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Marcus Egnatius Datus made this tomb for himself and his brother in his own plot. Iulia Sagitta, his wife, lived [an unspecified number of] years; she is buried here.
EDCS-47500645.summary: A funerary epitaph for Marcus Egnatius Datus and his wife Iulia Sagitta, who is buried in a plot he prepared.

EDCS-47500647.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Marcus Stade.
EDCS-47500647.summary: A very brief funerary epitaph for Marcus Stade.

EDCS-47500649.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Honoratus lived [an unspecified number of] years.
EDCS-47500649.summary: A funerary epitaph for Honoratus, recording his lifespan, though the exact number of years is missing.

EDCS-47600066.summary: A short inscription, possibly a motto or dedication related to chaplains.

EDCS-47600069.summary: A fragmentary inscription, likely a name and possibly initials or a title.

EDCS-47600070.summary: A very fragmentary inscription, beginning with the name Lucius Pill.

EDCS-47600552.translation: [...] 60 years. Caius A TR RVI pius [...].
EDCS-47600552.summary: A fragmentary inscription that appears to record an age of 60 years and the name Caius A TR RVI pius.

EDCS-48200099.translation: To Sextus Palpellius Faustus, son of Publius, of the Quirina tribe, *flamen* of the deified Augustus, *duovir* twice, *duovir quinquennalis* of the colony of Julia Karthago, quaestor, elected from the splendid order of the Carthaginians and by the people.
EDCS-48200099.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Sextus Palpellius Faustus, detailing his numerous civic and religious offices in Carthage, likely dating to the early Imperial period.

EDCS-48200100.translation: To Geminius Optio Mucianus, *flamen* of Aesculapius, whose ancestors [were honoured].
EDCS-48200100.summary: This is a dedication to Geminius Optio Mucianus, *flamen* of Aesculapius, likely from the Imperial period, mentioning his ancestors' honours.

EDCS-48200121.translation: Pastor, son of Imilcon, lived 40 years.
EDCS-48200121.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the name, parentage, and age at death of Pastor, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-48200122.translation: Marcus Julius Saturninus, dutiful, lived [XX] years.
EDCS-48200122.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the name, epithet, and age at death of Marcus Julius Saturninus, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-48200123.translation: Dedicated to the departed spirits. Licinia Victorilla, dutiful, lived 36 years. Quintus Licinius Efficax, dutiful, lived 79 years. Here they are buried.
EDCS-48200123.summary: This is a joint funerary inscription for Licinia Victorilla and Quintus Licinius Efficax, recording their names, epithets, ages at death, and burial, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-48300002.translation: In the consulship of Orfitus and Priscinius, according to the accounts of Callistus, from the group of 61, Certus, from the group of 50, [and] from the group of 50.
EDCS-48300002.summary: This inscription appears to record financial or administrative accounts from a specific period, possibly related to distribution or resource management, during the consulship of Orfitus and Priscinius.

EDCS-48300003.summary: This is a very brief inscription possibly indicating ownership or dedication related to Abascantus and someone associated with Caesar, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-48500128.translation: Unconquered divine powers. Junius Amicus, a sesquiplicarius (soldier paid one-and-a-half times the normal rate), who was also a librarius (clerk/scribe), restored part of the former bathhouse with the entire contingent of soldiers.
EDCS-48500128.summary: This inscription records the restoration of a bathhouse by Junius Amicus, a soldier of sesquiplicarius rank and a clerk, with the assistance of his military unit.

EDCS-48500135.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely the name of an individual, Sextus Marchius Felix, possibly on a tombstone or dedication, from the Roman period.

EDCS-48500136.translation: Gaius Cossinius Seranus, dutiful, lived 71 years. Here he is buried.
EDCS-48500136.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the name, epithet, age at death, and burial of Gaius Cossinius Seranus, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-48500137.translation: Gaius Creperius Saturninus, dutiful, lived 30 years. Here he is buried.
EDCS-48500137.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the name, epithet, age at death, and burial of Gaius Creperius Saturninus, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-48500138.translation: Sextus Pomponius Felix lived 25 years; he is buried here.
