EDCS-51900488.translation: To the Divine Shades. Quintus Gargilius Primus Bacetianus, priest, [dedicated this to] Quintus Gargilius Fortunatus Otanius Fla.
EDCS-51900488.summary: This funerary inscription is a dedication by Quintus Gargilius Primus Bacetianus to Quintus Gargilius Fortunatus, likely a relative or associate.

EDCS-51900490.translation: Marcus Aufidius Rufinus, son of Marcus, of the voting tribe Quirina, pious, lived for 3 years, is buried here.
EDCS-51900490.summary: This is a child's epitaph for Marcus Aufidius Rufinus, who died at the age of three, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-51900491.translation: To the Divine Shades. Orbia, daughter of Quintus, a chaste, pure, and pious woman, lived for 50 years. May your bones rest well; may the earth lie lightly upon you.
EDCS-51900491.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Orbia, recording her age at death and including a common epitaph wishing peace for the deceased.

EDCS-51900492.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Publius Anicius Baric lived 115 years and returned nature's debt.
EDCS-51900492.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Publius Anicius Baric, who lived to an exceptional age, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-51900493.translation: Quintus Gesinnius Secundus, pious, lived for 75 years.
EDCS-51900493.summary: This is a simple funerary epitaph recording the name and age of the deceased, Quintus Gesinnius Secundus.

EDCS-51900494.translation: To the Divine Shades. Fabia Fructosa lived for 20 years.
EDCS-51900494.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Fabia Fructosa, stating her age at death.

EDCS-51900495.translation: To the Divine Shades. Cornelius Festus, pious, lived for 55 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-51900495.summary: This funerary inscription records the death and burial of Cornelius Festus, specifying his age.

EDCS-51900496.translation: Lucius Gargilius Paetus, son of Lucius, of the Arnensis tribe, pious, lived 70 years, is buried here.
EDCS-51900496.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lucius Gargilius Paetus, providing his name, parentage, tribal affiliation, age at death, and stating he is buried here, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-51900497.translation: To the Divine Shades. Caius Iulius Rogatus, son of Anculeius Rogatus, pious, lived for 7 years.
EDCS-51900497.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of a young boy, Caius Iulius Rogatus, stating his age and parentage.

EDCS-51900498.translation: To the Divine Shades. Solutrica, pious, lived for 33 years. She is buried here. Aurelius Primus [dedicated this] to his wife.
EDCS-51900498.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated by Aurelius Primus to his wife, Solutrica, recording her age and burial.

EDCS-51900499.translation: To the Divine Shades. Fortuna lived for 71 years. Quintus Silvani lived for 55 years. May your bones rest well.
EDCS-51900499.summary: This inscription appears to record the ages of two individuals, Fortuna and Quintus Silvani, under the invocation to the Divine Shades.

EDCS-51900500.translation: Tettia Prima, daughter of Lucius, pious, lived 23 years, is buried here. May your bones rest well.
EDCS-51900500.summary: A funerary epitaph for Tettia Prima, including her name, parentage, piety, age at death, burial location, and a wish for her peaceful rest, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-51900505.translation: To the Divine Shades. Plotia Ana lived for 28 years and 39 days and 3 hours.
EDCS-51900505.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Plotia Ana, detailing her age at death with precise durations.

EDCS-51900506.translation: The names of those who contributed to the statues of Quintus Geminus Faustus and his sons: Vibius Pudens, perpetual flamen, priest of the deified Severus, 200 denarii; moreover, for transportation, 25 denarii from interest.
EDCS-51900506.summary: This inscription records contributions made by several individuals, including Vibius Pudens, for the erection of statues dedicated to Quintus Geminus Faustus and his sons, likely dating to the Severan period.

EDCS-51900507.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulia Ricula, also known as Sfolata, lived 63 years, 6 months. She is buried here.
EDCS-51900507.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Iulia Ricula, indicating her lifespan and burial place.

EDCS-51900508.translation: Marcus Vettius Lupus, son of Titus, fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-51900508.summary: This is a dedication recording Marcus Vettius Lupus fulfilling a vow, likely to a deity.

EDCS-51900509.translation: Quintus Vettius Daius, son of Lucius, fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-51900509.summary: This is a dedication recording Quintus Vettius Daius fulfilling a vow, likely to a deity.

EDCS-51900528.translation: Cobuldeus, the deacon, rests here in peace; he lived 50 years and was buried on the day of the Ides of April in the fourth indiction.
EDCS-51900528.summary: This is a Christian epitaph for Cobuldeus, a deacon, noting his lifespan and burial date.

EDCS-51900529.translation: Latentia the faithful lived in peace for 53 years, 6 months; she was buried on the day of the third Ides of April in the second indiction.
EDCS-51900529.summary: This is a Christian epitaph for Latentia, noting her lifespan and burial date.

EDCS-52302289.translation: Privatianus may fall, may be turned; Salutaris may fall, may be turned; Superstianus the reddish, who is also Naucellius, may fall, may be turned; Castor; Superstites the reddish, slave of Regulus, may fall, may be turned; Aelius, may be turned; Romanus, may be turned; Repentinus, may be turned; Argutus; Croceus; may they fall; may they be broken; may they be disordered; may they turn badly; those stirring up the Venetian and reddish ones, may they be turned and not....
EDCS-52302289.summary: This inscription appears to be a magical text, possibly a curse or a protective spell, listing names and actions intended to incapacitate adversaries, likely related to chariot racing factions in the 3rd century AD.

EDCS-52302290.translation: Privatianus may fall, may be turned; Salutaris may fall, may be turned; Superstianus the reddish, who is also Naucellius, may fall, may be turned; Superstites the reddish, slave of Regulus, may fall, may be turned; Aelius, may fall, may be turned; Castor, may fall, may be turned; Argutus; Croceus; may they fall; Tyrius; Lupercus; may they fall; Italus; may fall; may fall Centaurus; Crisaspis; bind and fasten the horses and the drivers of the Venetian and reddish ones, may they fall, may they be turned and not hold the reins nor be able to drive nor to hold the horses.
EDCS-52302290.summary: This inscription is a magical text, likely a curse aimed at hindering or immobilizing the horses and drivers of rival chariot racing factions, the Veneti and Russi.

EDCS-52302291.translation: may fall Alumnus, may fall Adamatus, may fall Danubius, Ideus, may they fall; Virgineus, Bracatus, may they fall; Epafus, Victor, may they fall; Lydeus, may fall; Elegans, may fall; Pancratius, Oclopecta, Verbosus, Crinitus, may they fall; may they be turned; Securua, Mantineua, Praevalens, may they fall; Lydeus, Latro, Vagulus, may they fall; Helve, may fall; Lydeus, Hellenicus, Inhumanus, may they fall; Multivolus, may they fall; Delusor, may fall; Improbus, Vagarfita, may they fall; the young men, Capria, Mirandus, may they fall; Caesareus, Divites, Garulus, Ganimedes, Cursor, Agricola, may they fall; Privatianus, may fall, may be turned; Salutaris, may fall, may be turned; Superstianus the reddish, who is also Naucellius, may fall, may be turned; Superstites the reddish, slave of Regulus, may fall, may be turned; Romanus, may fall, may be turned; Repentinus, may fall, may be turned; Aelius, may fall, may be turned; Castor, may fall, may be turned; may the Venetian and reddish ones not be able to run, nor obey the reins, nor may their feet be separated, nor may they see their opponents, nor may they win.
EDCS-52302291.summary: This inscription is a magical curse, likely related to chariot racing, intended to incapacitate numerous individuals and prevent the Veneti and Russi factions from competing effectively, possibly from the 3rd century AD.

EDCS-52302292.translation: Superstitianus, who is also Naucellius, may fall, may be broken; Zitries, may fall, may be broken; Romanus Niofitianus, may fall, may be broken; Lydeus, Superstites, may they fall, may they be broken; Repentinus, Europetes, may they fall, may they be broken; may they be turned; Verbosus, may fall; Mantineus, Praevalens, may they fall; Vagarfita, may fall; Paratus, Elegantus, Puerina, may they fall; Iperesius, Diamantes, may fall; Secundinus, slave, may fall, may he fall, may he be broken, may he be disordered; Cassidatus, may fall; Vagulus, Oceanus, may they fall; Iscintilla, may fall; Carlus, may they fall; Gentiles, may fall; Equi, may fall; Bracchiatus, may fall; Germanus, Amandus, Celestinus; bind and fasten and weigh down the horses of the Venetian and reddish ones, and may they not take the reins, may they fall, may they be broken, those stirring up the Venetian and reddish ones, and may they not win, may they be turned.
EDCS-52302292.summary: This inscription is a magical curse, likely aimed at harming or incapacitating individuals and horses associated with the Venetian and Russi factions in chariot races, possibly from the 3rd century AD.

EDCS-52302293.translation: Naucellius, Superstianus, Helius, Privatianus, Zenor, Castor, D... Arator, may they fall; Macedo, Atquaesitor, may they fall; Hellenicus, Virgineus, may they fall; Comatus, Indus, may they fall; Farius, Amatus, may they fall; Ideus, Centaurus, may they fall; may they fall, may they be broken, may they be disordered, may they turn badly, may they not be able to win the palm, nor may they obey the reins, may they fall.
EDCS-52302293.summary: This inscription is a magical curse, likely concerning chariot racing, intended to cause the downfall and defeat of named individuals and potentially their factions, possibly from the 3rd century AD.

EDCS-52302294.translation: Naucellius Superstianus Helius Privatianus Zenor Castor Roseus Exuperator, may they fall! Macedo Atquesitor, may they fall! Hellenicus Comatus Indus, may they fall! Pran, may they fall! Amatus Farius, may they fall! Ideus Centaurus, may they fall! May they fall, may they break, may they be shattered, may they turn badly, may they not be able to win the palm, may they not fall and obey the reins!
EDCS-52302294.summary: This is a curse inscription, likely related to a foot race or competition, listing numerous names and invoking a curse against them to ensure they do not win or perform well.

EDCS-52302295.translation: Privatianus, may he fall and turn over! Salutaris, may he fall and turn over! Aelius Superstianus, reddish, also known as Naucellius, may he fall and turn over! Castor Superstites, reddish, slave of Regulus, may he fall and turn over! Castor Repentinus, may he fall and turn over! Aelius Argutus Croceus, may they fall! Tyrius Italus, may they fall! Lupercus, may he fall! Candor Farus, may they fall! Alumnus, may he fall! Adamatus, may he fall! Centaurus Crisaspis Tigrides, may they fall! Epafus, may he fall! Ideus Danubius, may they fall! Virgineus Bracatus, may they fall! Lydius Victor, may they fall! Pancratius Oclopecta Verbosus Crinitus, may they fall! Latro Vagilus, may they fall! Tagus Hellenicus, may they fall! Inhumanus, may he fall! Delusor, may he fall! Multivolus, may he fall! Improbus Vagarfita, may they fall! Cesareus Divites Garulus, may they fall! Agricola, may he fall! Iuvenes Capria Mirandus, may they fall! Ganimedes Superstianus Superstites russei servus Reguli, may he fall and turn over! Romanus, may he fall! Repentinus, may he fall and turn over! Aelius, may he fall! Aelius, may he fall! May they fall and turn over! Lydeus Gravate and bind the horses, the veneti and russei, so that they may not be able to run, nor obey the reins, nor move themselves, but may they fall, be broken, be shattered, turn badly, the veneti and russei may turn over, may they hold the reins, and may they not be able to drive, neither in front of them nor their adversaries, nor may they win, may they fall, be broken!
EDCS-52302295.summary: This inscription, a curse formula, likely refers to horses and their riders, invoked to prevent them from competing effectively in a race or contest, potentially for betting or a similar purpose.

EDCS-52302296.translation: Privatianus, may he fall and turn over! Salutaris, may he fall and turn over! Superstianus, reddish, also known as Naucellius, may he fall and turn over! Superstites, reddish, slave of Regulus, may he fall and turn over! Aelius, may he fall! Castor, may he fall! Repentinus, may he fall! Croceus, may he fall! Italus, may he fall! Tyrius, may he fall! Lupercus, may he fall! Farus, may he fall! Candor, may he fall! Crisaspis Tigrides, may they fall! Alumnus, may he fall! Ideus Centaurus, may they fall! Lydeus, may he fall! Virgineus Bracatus, may they fall! Adamatus, may he fall! Lyceus Epafus, may they fall! Victor, may he fall! ElegansE, may he fall! Lydeus, may he fall! Pancratius Oclopecta Verbosus Crinitus, may they fall! Lydeus, may he fall! Securus Mantineus PrevalensE, may they fall! Hilarus, may he fall! Latro Vagulus, may they fall! Lydeus, may he fall! Hellenicus, may he fall! Danuvius, may he fall! Inhumanus, may he fall! Derisor, may he fall! Improbus Vagarfita, may they fall! Iuvenes Capria Mirandus, may they fall! Caesareus Divites Garulus, may they fall! Ganimedes, may he fall! Cursor Agricola, may they fall! Vagarfita, may he fall! Privatianus, may he fall and turn over! Salutaris, may he fall and turn over! Superstianus, reddish, also known as Naucellius, may he fall and turn over! Superstites, reddish, slave of Regulus, may he fall and turn over! Aelius, may he turn over! Romanus, may he fall and turn over! Castor, may he turn over! Repentinus, may he fall! Bind and tie down the horses, the veneti and russei, so that they may not be able to run, nor obey the reins, nor move themselves, but may they fall, be broken, be disjoined, turn badly, and the veneti and russei, may they turn over, and may they not hold the reins, nor may they see in front of them, nor their adversaries, but may they turn over, be broken, may they not be able to win the palm!
EDCS-52302296.summary: This curse inscription, likely for a competition, lists many names and horses (implied by 'veneti et russei') and invokes a hex to ensure their failure and disablement.

EDCS-52302297.translation: Privatianus, Naucellius, Superstianus, reddish, Repentinus, Superstites, reddish, slave of Regulus, Aelius, Castor, ElegansE, Glaucus, Argutus, veneti, Destroiugus, Glauci, may they fall! ElegansE, may he fall! Ideus Centaurus, may they fall! Bracatus, Virgineus, may they fall! Novicius, Securus Mantineus, PrevalensE, Ilarinus, may they fall! Danuvius, Pancratius, Oclopecta, Verbosus, Crinitus, may they fall! Auricomus, ElegansE, Cesareus, Improbus, Vagarfita, may they fall! Paratus, Delusor, may they fall! Latro Vagulus, may they fall! Hellenus, Divites, Garulus, may they fall! Adamatus, may he fall! Danuvius, may he fall! Acceptor, may he fall! Germanicus, veneti, may he fall! ElegansE, may he fall! Eolus, Decor, Oceanus, EminensE, Tagus, may they fall! Eburnus, Epafus, may they fall! Agricola, may he fall! Mirandus, veneti, Multivolus, Capria, Inhumanus, may they fall! VoluptasE, Capriolus, Viator, Securus, Augurius, AudaxE, Pardus, Tigrides, Percussor, Aliator, may they fall! Massinissa, may he fall, may he be broken! Privatianus, may he fall and turn over! Naucellius, may he fall and turn over! Superstites, reddish, slave of Regulus, may he fall and turn over! Aelius, Castor, may they fall, may they turn over! Aelius, may he fall and turn over! Lidus, Repentinus, may they fall and turn over! Naucellius, may he turn over! Privatianus, Superstites, reddish, slave of Regulus, Castor, and Aelius, and Repentinus, and Castor, and Privatianus, and Naucellius, may they not be able to drive, nor hold the horses, nor may they hold the reins, they may not be able! Bind and tie down and burden the horses, the veneti and russei, so that they may not be able to run, nor obey the reins, nor move their feet, but may they fall, be broken, be disjoined, may they not be able to win the palm!
EDCS-52302297.summary: This lengthy curse inscription, possibly associated with chariot racing or a similar equestrian event, lists numerous names and invokes divine or magical means to incapacitate horses and drivers, ensuring their failure.

EDCS-52302298.translation: Privatianus, Helius, Pompeius, Privatianus, Helius, Pompeius, Repentinus, FelixE, Surdus, Superstites, reddish, Regius, Centaurus, Bracatus, Virgineus, Celestinus, Paratus, Glaucus, Eolus, Igneus, Decor, Oceanus, Garulus, Eburnus, Verbosus, Germanicus, EminensE, Tagus, VoluptasE, Capriolus, Viator, Securus, Magurius, AudaxE, Arbustus, Cesareus, Capria, Placidus, Medus, Linceus, Pardus, Tigrides, FelixE, Percussor, Aliator, Decoratus, ElegansE, Corentus, Paratus, Vagarfita, Derisor, PrevalensE, Aureus, Eucles, Massinissa, Latro Egiptus, I ask you, may they fall! Privatianus, Helius, Pompeius, Repentinus, FelixE, Surdus, Superstites, reddish, Regius, Centaurus, Bracatus, Virgineus, Celestinus, Paratus, Glaucus, Eolus, Igneus, Decor, Oceanus, Garulus, Eburnus, Verbosus, Germanicus, EminensE, Tagus, VoluptasE, Capriolus, Viator, Securus, Magurius, AudaxE, Arbustus, Cesareus, Capria, Placidus, Medus, Linceus, Pardus, Tigrides, FelixE, Percussor, Aliator, Decoratus, ElegansE, Corentus, Massunissa, Vagarfita, Paratus, Derisor, PrevalensE, Aureus, Eucles, Latro Aegyptus, I ask you, may they fall, may they turn badly! I ask you, bind the horses, MINESREN, so that they may not be able to move themselves, but may they fall, may they turn badly, and those who are driving, may they turn over, and may they not hold the reins, nor may they see in front of them, nor their adversaries, nor may they win, may they turn badly!
EDCS-52302298.summary: This inscription is a curse invoking misfortune upon a long list of individuals and possibly horses, likely related to a competitive event where the speaker wished for the downfall of their opponents.

EDCS-52302299.translation: Proteus, FelixE, Pompeius, Castrensis, Cesareus, Romanus, Amandus, Acceptor, Luxurius, LOTI, V Africus, nus, Diamantes, Victoricus, sces, may they fall! May they fall! Let them be shattered, let them be broken, let them turn badly, let them turn over, and may they not be able to run! May they fall, may they fall, may they fall, may they fall! Let them be shattered! May they fall! O R.
EDCS-52302299.summary: This is a curse formula, likely inscribed to ensure the failure or disablement of rivals in a race or contest, listing several names and invoking hexes.

EDCS-52800516.translation: a faithful one lived for X years, buried on the fourth day before the Nones of June.
EDCS-52800516.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan and burial date of an individual identified as 'a faithful one'.

EDCS-52900005.translation: To the most fortunate prince of the youth, from the most splendid colony of Hipponensium Regiorum, in the year of the proconsul Lucius Cossonius Eggius Marullus, a most distinguished man, as legate, and to his son.
EDCS-52900005.summary: This is a dedication from the colony of Hipponensium Regiorum to the prince of the youth (likely a princeps iuventutis, a title held by a successor to the throne), dating it to the proconsulship of Lucius Cossonius Eggius Marullus.

EDCS-53100077.summary: This is a title or epithet identifying a female individual as a priestess of the goddess Ceres.

EDCS-53100078.summary: This is a title or epithet identifying a female individual as a priestess of the goddess Ceres.

EDCS-53100081.translation: Sacred to the memory of Sentenia Charis, most pious wife, most holy. Germanicus Aponius dedicated this to Faunus, to Ceres, and to the gods of the place who made the inhabitants... [---]
EDCS-53100081.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication by Germanicus Aponius to his wife Sentenia Charis and to several deities, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-53100085.translation: Lucius Felicius Caeso gave this offering to the god Mercury.
EDCS-53100085.summary: This is a votive offering to Mercury by Lucius Felicius Caeso, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-53100086.translation: Sacred to Mercury Augustus. Aulus Pullaenus Saturus gladly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-53100086.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by Aulus Pullaenus Saturus to Mercury Augustus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-53100089.translation: Sacred to Saturn Augustus. Marcus Iulius Victor, first priest, gladly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-53100089.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by Marcus Iulius Victor, a priest, to Saturn Augustus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-53100090.translation: Sacred to Saturn Augustus. Caius Rusticelius Ingenuus, who is also Pro M...
EDCS-53100090.summary: This inscription is dedicated to Saturn Augustus by Caius Rusticelius Ingenuus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-53100094.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the god Saturn Augustus, with illegible text following, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-53100097.translation: ... Caius Tiberius Saturnus, the unconquered god.
EDCS-53100097.summary: This inscription refers to Caius Tiberius Saturnus as an unconquered god, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-53100098.translation: Sacred to Saturn Balcaranensis. Lucius Antestius Celsus fulfilled his vow upon seeing...
EDCS-53100098.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by Lucius Antestius Celsus to Saturn Balcaranensis, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-53100099.translation: ... to the most distinguished man, the consul, proconsul, Salio Palatino of the Atellani.
EDCS-53100099.summary: This inscription is a dedication or honorific text addressed to a high-ranking official, possibly related to the Salii Palatini and the Atellani, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-53100101.summary: This is a simple inscription identifying Marcus Luccius Vitalis as a priest, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-53100104.translation: Tus fulfilled his vow to Frumentus according to the will.
EDCS-53100104.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the fulfillment of a vow by Tus, potentially concerning the deceased Frumentus.

EDCS-53100105.translation: Tus the priest willingly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-53100105.summary: This is a dedication recording a priest named Tus who willingly fulfilled a vow.

EDCS-53100107.translation: O Votary, you willingly fulfilled your vow.
EDCS-53100107.summary: This is a dedication recording an unknown individual who willingly fulfilled a vow.

EDCS-53100109.translation: Rivsi willingly fulfilled his vow to Vncius.
EDCS-53100109.summary: This is a dedication recording Rivsi who willingly fulfilled a vow to Vncius.

EDCS-53100114.translation: Numisius Felix made this at his own expense.
EDCS-53100114.summary: This is a building or dedication inscription stating that Numisius Felix funded its construction.

EDCS-53100115.translation: Bassus, son of Lucius, of the Arnensi tribe.
EDCS-53100115.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely recording the name and tribal affiliation of Bassus.

EDCS-53100116.translation: Orasti, I do not wish to see the end.
EDCS-53100116.summary: This is a personal inscription expressing a wish not to witness a conclusion.

EDCS-53100122.translation: Parthicus Maximus, of the deified Antoninus.
EDCS-53100122.summary: This inscription likely refers to Lucius Verus, who was granted the cognomen Parthicus Maximus and was associated with the deified Antoninus Pius.

EDCS-53200230.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription identifying an individual named Gaius Salius from the Pinaria gens.

EDCS-53200236.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely recording the name Publius Sa[---] and mentioning honor.

EDCS-53200237.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that appears to list personal names.

EDCS-53200239.translation: Felix and Ethus, Tor Ethus, Felix
EDCS-53200239.summary: This inscription seems to record names, possibly related to a funerary context.

EDCS-53200241.translation: of the marble, tribune of the cohort
EDCS-53200241.summary: This inscription mentions a tribune of a cohort and marble, possibly related to a military building or dedication.

EDCS-53200243.translation: To Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus, conqueror of Parthia, greatest.
EDCS-53200243.summary: This is a formal titulary inscription for Emperor Marcus Aurelius, likely from a public monument.

EDCS-53200244.translation: To Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Probus Pius Felix Augustus, holding tribunician power, consul for the first time.
EDCS-53200244.summary: This is a formal titulary inscription for Emperor Probus, likely from a public monument.

EDCS-53200248.translation: Salvius Maecenas, advocate of the imperial treasury, dutiful, lived [X?] years, 2 months.
EDCS-53200248.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Salvius Maecenas, an advocate, noting his lifespan and profession.

EDCS-53200249.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcus Baebius Repentinus, son of Marcus, of the Galeria tribe, dutiful, lived 50 years. His father, mother, and coheirs made this.
EDCS-53200249.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Marcus Baebius Repentinus, detailing his age, tribe, and familial dedication.

EDCS-53200250.translation: Gaius Flavius Magnil and his coheirs, of the city, [born?] lived.
EDCS-53200250.summary: This inscription seems to record the names of Gaius Flavius Magnil and his coheirs, possibly related to property or burial.

EDCS-53200251.translation: of the urban cohort, century of Vesinus, lived 25 years, for his most dutiful son.
EDCS-53200251.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a soldier of the urban cohort, noting his age and dedication to his son.

EDCS-53200255.translation: standard-bearer, by the praise of the cohort, discharge.
EDCS-53200255.summary: This inscription appears to commemorate a standard-bearer upon his honorable discharge from a cohort.

EDCS-53200256.summary: This inscription records the disposition of property by Marcus Valerius Bono.

EDCS-53200259.translation: To [?], Ge[?]-ssius Apro, son of [?], aged 4004 [?].
EDCS-53200259.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely recording funerary details and the name of Ge-ssius Apro.

EDCS-53200260.translation: He lived 50 years, served 20 years, he is buried here.
EDCS-53200260.summary: This inscription records the lifespan and military service of an unnamed individual.

EDCS-53200265.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Caius Hostorius Athenio, the chorister.
EDCS-53200265.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Caius Hostorius Athenio, a musician.

EDCS-53400806.translation: Marinus and Doryphorus send greetings to their Primigenius. Here is an example of a letter written to us by Tutilius Pudens, an outstanding man, so that you may know, and may you propose what follows in the most frequented places. Verridius Bassus and Ianuarius send greetings to their Martialis. If any fields are lying fallow and are untilled, or are wild or marshy, and are in that district, if they are willing to cultivate those fields by the Mancian law, do not prevent them. We ask that you, as procurators, through your foresight, which you provide in Caesar's name, wish to consult both us and his utility and to give us those fields which are in the marshes and in the wild areas to be established with olive groves and vineyards by the Mancian law, under the condition of the Neroian estate. Our neighbors, when we were drawing up this petition of ours, with the Neronian estate, the increase of the inhabitants, order that we should have the fundus described above. By the sermo of the procurators of the Emperor Caesar Hadrian Augustus, because our Caesar, through his tireless care, by which he constantly watches over human utilities, orders that all parts of the fields which are suitable for olives or vineyards or grains should be cultivated; therefore, by the permission of his foresight, the power is given to all to occupy even those parts which are in the located centuriations of the Blandian and Udens estates in those parts which are given by the tenants, but those who occupy neglected places by the tenants, which are usually given, will give the third part of the produce from those regions which are joined to the Tuzritano estate from the Lamiano and Domitian estates, they will give the same amount from the olives which anyone plants in pits or inserts three olive trees, of the captured produce.
EDCS-53400806.summary: This is a lengthy inscription detailing land management and cultivation rights under Roman law, specifically mentioning the Mancian and Neronian laws, and involving procurators acting on behalf of Emperor Hadrian.

EDCS-53500002.translation: The faith of the mind, always kept for your husband, has brought your joys of life to heaven. You remain an example for chaste women to imitate on earth. Praise has this merit, your fame preserves your modesty, surpassing the law of death as it endures into eternity. Thus do morals live, thus does time never fail. All your kin grieved for you, all chaste women grieved for you. Whoever marveled at your innocent life in time, does not die; bodies are released from fate. You conquered the narrow years of life's time. Caelestina.
EDCS-53500002.summary: A poetic epitaph celebrating the virtue and piety of a woman named Caelestina, whose exemplary life is seen as having transcended death, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-53500003.translation: To the gods of the underworld. Publius Caledius Rufus has paid to the Fates thrice-five years, twice single ones, and has completed them; with a not humble talent, by which I was pleasing to my masters, I spoke, I wrote, I painted. I dedicated my mind to learning, for when I was sixteen years old, I was pleasing with Greek letters in common sayings, I pleased greatly. I rest in a peaceful place, I return to nature, therefore, nothing excessive, nothing unjustly desired. May we rest, may the circumstances of life become gentler, when you have placed me [in this condition]. Alas, I lived. In perpetuity, by the wound of my death.
EDCS-53500003.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Publius Caledius Rufus, detailing his age at death (16 years), his talents in arts and learning, and his peaceful rest in the afterlife.

EDCS-53500004.translation: Hunter, exceedingly pleasing with your skill with wild beasts, agile, pleasing, most brave, audacious, who as a boy to youth, before you reached the years, you were completing all things with mature effort, who, although you pleased the people of your own region with praise, you surpassed others so that they could not win with you, and your rewards of form were so admirable, that after death they fear and praise you, companions. Alas, now snatched away so suddenly by the bile of death, this tomb captures you, which not the fortresses of Carthage could have borne in an amphitheater triumph, but nothing do you lose to the Manes with this bitter funeral. The long-lasting fame of your beauty will live after you, and Carthage will always speak your name.
EDCS-53500004.summary: This is a laudatory epitaph for a hunter, likely a gladiator or performer, celebrating his bravery, skill, and popularity, and lamenting his untimely death.

EDCS-53500006.translation: To the gods of the underworld. Whoever travels the road, look upon Marcus, memorable by name, and not so much by the fates and injustice of death. He lived for sixty-four years and four months, and the same number of days, with light. His wife IAATI V siae, although she mourns his death, Marcus IVIM SISIAIVIIAM, prudent, while her husband was alive, I OS IA.
EDCS-53500006.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Marcus, who lived for 64 years, 4 months, and 4 days, and is remembered by his wife.

EDCS-53500007.translation: Statues, honors, great Karthago has the shadow after death; thus the beautiful limbs imitate the cold marbles, the faces. I, a disciple, imitating you from the first, I earned this glory from you, by being placed first. When the crowd roared, I imbued strength and brave deeds, prostrating my body naked in the waves. Nor can I recount my complaint to you, Phoebus, nor you, goddess, how many youths death snatched away, how many threads my too harsh sisters, the Fates, spun. For grim fates dictate that glory is handed over to death, and they quickly snatch away the praises of the world. Happy, alas, too happy, if I were seeking a beautiful death through wounds in that very gift. The earth, the mother, embracing me in her bosom, covers this empty body here, and the stone with an inscription for the ages. He lived 26 years, 5 months, 10 days.
EDCS-53500007.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a young man who died at the age of 26, lamenting his short life and the unfairness of fate, and comparing his physical beauty to cold marble statues.

EDCS-53500008.translation: A grieving brother fulfilled the funeral rites; he erected this tomb with inscriptions and marked his fate. Gaius Julius Victor, who lived 46 years, made this for his brother.
EDCS-53500008.summary: This is a funerary epitaph erected by Gaius Julius Victor for his brother, dating from antiquity.

EDCS-53500009.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Quintus Pomponius Fortunatus, son of Quintus, of the Quirina tribe, aedile, praised for his singular innocence and modesty, approved integrity, recognized frugality and loyalty, and great, unheard-of gravity, a sober, just youth of holy and equitable character, unchanging, skilled in law, who in his early age corresponded to the frugality of his elders and was found to be their equal, lived 22 years and 2 months. Placed here, under the care of his brothers Proculus and Festa.
EDCS-53500009.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Quintus Pomponius Fortunatus, an aedile who died young, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-53701592.translation: The lion of the tribe of Judah has conquered, the root of David.
EDCS-53701592.summary: This is a short inscription, likely religious or symbolic, invoking biblical imagery.

EDCS-53701593.translation: The lion of the tribe of Judah has conquered, the root of David. Envious envy, you have no power against the pure and clean soul. Michael, Raphael, Uriel, Gabriel, victory!
EDCS-53701593.summary: This is a religious inscription invoking divine protection and victory, likely from the late antique or early medieval period.

EDCS-53701594.translation: Ask and it will be given to you; seek and you will find. The house of Christ is open, awaiting the prayers of the people, priests, and bishops for the sins of the people.
EDCS-53701594.summary: This is a religious inscription, likely from a church or devotional site, related to prayer and seeking divine favor.

EDCS-53900002.translation: The spirit of Felicianus in peace.
EDCS-53900002.summary: This is a simple epitaph, likely from a Christian burial, indicating the deceased's name and peaceful rest.

EDCS-53900003.translation: Germana the innocent rested in peace; she lived 5 years and 6 months, interred on the 10th day before the Kalends of April.
EDCS-53900003.summary: This is a Christian epitaph for a young child named Germana, providing her age and date of burial.

EDCS-53900004.translation: The spirit of Emeritus lies in peace; he lived three years and ten months.
EDCS-53900004.summary: This is a Christian epitaph for a child named Emeritus, indicating his age at death.

EDCS-53900005.summary: This is a Christian epitaph for a woman named Iulia, stating her age at death.

EDCS-53900006.translation: Quintiliana lived 37 years and 10 months in peace. Her betrothed Bonifatius and her son made this.
EDCS-53900006.summary: This is a Christian epitaph for Quintiliana, made by her betrothed and son, providing her age at death.

EDCS-53900007.translation: Libius Securus lived for 34 years and 9 months, during which he had nothing; he died in peace.
EDCS-53900007.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan and peaceful death of Libius Securus.

EDCS-53900008.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Covuldeus, in peace.
EDCS-53900008.summary: A brief funerary dedication to the departed spirit of Covuldeus.

EDCS-53900009.translation: Gudutza lived for 70 years. Ax, her son, made this.
EDCS-53900009.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Gudutza and made by her son, Ax.

EDCS-53900010.translation: Maxima lived for 72 years, in peace. Cuminus, her son, placed this.
EDCS-53900010.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Maxima and placed by her son, Cuminus.

EDCS-53900011.translation: In memory of Victoriana, faithful, lived for 43 years.
EDCS-53900011.summary: A funerary inscription commemorating Victoriana, noting her faithfulness and lifespan.

EDCS-53900012.translation: Lampas lived for two years and seven days, in peace. Her parents placed this for their son.

EDCS-53900014.summary: A funerary epitaph stating that Caprassa died innocently and in peace.

EDCS-54601027.translation: Clodianus Gaianus lived for 63 years. He is buried here. May your bones rest well. May the earth lie lightly upon you.

EDCS-54601243.translation: Acasanila, most faithful, lived in peace for 24 years. She was laid to rest on the Kalends of May, in the sixth indiction.

EDCS-54800004.translation: Sacred to Augustus Saturn. Felix Lanius Baliato fulfilled his vow willingly with a good spirit.

EDCS-55701631.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Magnius Victorinus lived 21 years, 2 months, and 10 days.

EDCS-55701632.translation: Sacred to the Queen of the Earth, at public expense, for the cella and porticus, with the care of Marcus Postimius Donatus.

EDCS-55701638.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Calpurnia Novella, dedicating the tomb to the Manes and recording her age at death.

EDCS-55701639.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Quinta Comnia Furia lived 87 years.

EDCS-55701642.translation: Caius Domitius Celsus lived 40 years, is buried here.

EDCS-55701643.translation: Publius Iulius Clemens, son of Caius, lived 50 years, is buried here.

EDCS-55701644.translation: Iulia Africana, daughter of Caius, lived 30 years, is buried here.
EDCS-55701644.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Iulia Africana, recording her name, parentage, and age at death.

EDCS-55701645.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcus Lucceius Castus lived 85 years, is buried here.
EDCS-55701645.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcus Lucceius Castus, dedicating the tomb to the Manes and recording his age at death.

EDCS-55701646.translation: Publius Maius Primus lived 75 years, is buried here.

EDCS-55701647.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Quintus Manlius Felix lived for 20 years. He is buried here.

EDCS-55701648.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Pompeia Siddena lived for 70 years. Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Munatius Rogatus lived for 60 years.
EDCS-55701648.summary: This funerary inscription records the lives and deaths of two individuals, Pompeia Siddena and Munatius Rogatus.

EDCS-55701649.translation: Aquilius Anina made this monument. He lived for seventy years, or this monument.
EDCS-55701649.summary: This funerary inscription records that Aquilius Anina erected this monument and states his lifespan.

EDCS-55701650.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Quinta Arisis, recording her lifespan.

EDCS-55701651.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Caius Sulpicius Felix lived for 50 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-55701651.summary: This funerary epitaph for Caius Sulpicius Felix records his lifespan and burial.

EDCS-55701652.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Quintus Sulpicius Martialis lived for 50 years.
EDCS-55701652.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespan of Quintus Sulpicius Martialis.

EDCS-55701653.translation: Titia Smasaris lived for 30 years. Titia Maia [died?].
EDCS-55701653.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespan of Titia Smasaris and likely indicates the death of Titia Maia.

EDCS-55701654.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. [Nia] Pia lived for 40 years.

EDCS-55701655.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Melior, recording his exceptional lifespan.

EDCS-55701656.summary: This inscription appears to be a short wish or dedication related to a burial or monument.

EDCS-55701657.translation: Judas Isaac, son of God, donated this; he made it at his own expense.
EDCS-55701657.summary: This inscription records a votive offering donated by Judas Isaac, likely of Jewish background, who funded its construction himself.

EDCS-55701658.translation: Sacred, dedicated by decree of the decurions with public funds by Marcus Valerius, while Gnaeus Pinarius Caecilius Simplex was proconsul and legate pro praetore.
EDCS-55701658.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a public work funded by public money and authorized by local officials, during the proconsulship of Gnaeus Pinarius Caecilius Simplex.

EDCS-55701659.translation: This altar is sacred to Neptune Augustus. Heracla, freedman of Lucius Aelius Tironis, centurion of the III Augusta Legion, willingly fulfilled his vow for the safety and return of his master.
EDCS-55701659.summary: This inscription records a votive offering dedicated to Neptune Augustus by a freedman for the well-being of his centurion master.

EDCS-56500212.translation: To Gaius Marius Fidus, son of Sextus, of the Quirina tribe, quaestor, prefect of justice, duovir, perpetual flamen, the people of Emerita set up this equestrian monument from the money he contributed for his games, as he promised annual, perpetual, and festive donations for his merits and generosity; and on his behalf, his equestrian sons erected the equestrian monument and the pedestrian one for himself, according to his will.
EDCS-56500212.summary: A dedication by the people of Emerita for Gaius Marius Fidus, honoring him for his public service and generosity with games, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-56500213.translation: Sacred to Pluto Augustus. Baric Honorati, the sufetes, made and dedicated this portico with columns.
EDCS-56500213.summary: This inscription records the construction and dedication of a portico with columns by the sufetes Baric Honorati, dedicated to Pluto Augustus.

EDCS-56500316.summary: This inscription is highly enigmatic and likely a personal or poetic text, possibly found on a mosaic or artwork, reflecting on beauty and perception.

EDCS-57200135.translation: Quintus Cornelius Iustinianus, pious, lived with Aemilianus, her husband.
EDCS-57200135.summary: This inscription is a funerary text commemorating Quintus Cornelius Iustinianus, who lived with his husband Aemilianus.

EDCS-57200207.translation: To Emperor Caesar Gaius Messius Quintus Decius Traianus.
EDCS-57200207.summary: This is a titulary inscription for Emperor Decius, likely part of a public monument from his reign.

EDCS-57300077.translation: Valerius Fis, son of Marsilius, (dedicated this).
EDCS-57300077.summary: This is a dedication by Valerius Fis, son of Marsilius, potentially for a religious or public monument.

EDCS-57300079.translation: Valerius Luciscus erected (this) for his wife.
EDCS-57300079.summary: This is a funerary epitaph erected by Valerius Luciscus for his wife.

EDCS-57300080.summary: This is a dedication or mention of Publius Domitius, possibly on a monument or boundary marker.

EDCS-57300081.translation: To Juno Caelestis from Audius, son of Caesus.
EDCS-57300081.summary: This is a religious dedication to the goddess Juno Caelestis by Audius, son of Caesus.

EDCS-57500043.summary: This is a brief inscription likely recording a victory in a race, possibly chariot racing, with the winner named Asinus.

EDCS-57500044.translation: To the most pious consul Valerianus Constantinus.
EDCS-57500044.summary: This is a dedication to Valerianus Constantinus, likely honored for his consular service.

EDCS-58200010.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Lucius Flavius Rogatianus the younger lived 16 years, 10 months, 23 days. Lucius Rogatianus for his most obedient son. Though snatched too soon by cruel fate after sweet Muses, after the groves and springs, the rivers of Virgil, this place holds me, surrounded by a dark grove. I do not grieve that I was quickly carried off to the shades below, but that my camp and flourishing military studies, having become a deserter by the deadly law of fate. Let my final supreme sin and this be after my death. I do not cast these eternal things to the resounding Muse.
EDCS-58200010.summary: A poignant epitaph for a young man named Lucius Flavius Rogatianus, who died at 16, lamenting his unfulfilled potential and interrupted studies, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-58200015.translation: To our lord Flavius Claudius Julianus, the unconquered, most noble prince Augustus, the state of the colony of Uchitani Maiorum, devoted to his divine power and majesty.
EDCS-58200015.summary: This is a dedication from the city of Uchitani Maiorum to Emperor Julian, praising his virtues and acknowledging his authority, likely from the mid-4th century CE.

EDCS-58200016.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Fulvius Fortunatianus, pious, lived 65 years, is buried here.
EDCS-58200016.summary: A funerary epitaph for Fulvius Fortunatianus, stating his name, piety, age at death, and burial location, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-58200017.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Lucius Pomponius Vitalis, pious, lived 83 years, is buried here.

EDCS-58200020.translation: To the departed spirits. Servius Agilio lived piously for 85 years.

EDCS-58200024.translation: To the departed spirits. Quintus Caecilius Vitalis lived 75 years and 2 months; he lies buried here. His sons, Caecilius Vitalianus Barbarus and Rusticulus, made this for their most excellent father, most learned in all literature and most skilled in both Greek and Latin languages, a propagator of this lineage, a good man.
EDCS-58200024.summary: A funerary monument erected by sons for their father, Quintus Caecilius Vitalis, praising his literary skills and family legacy.

EDCS-58200115.translation: To our lords Flavius Claudius Julianus, ever victorious Augustus, and to our lords Valentinian, Valens, and Gratian, ever Augustuses.
EDCS-58200115.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the emperors Julian, Valentinian, Valens, and Gratian, likely from the late 4th century.

EDCS-58200217.translation: Arnensis lived 30 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-58200217.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a man named Arnensis who died at the age of 30.

EDCS-58200219.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Cemalos who died at the age of 44.

EDCS-58200223.translation: Iunia Maiorica, dutiful, lived 47 years; she is buried here.

EDCS-59600004.text_edition: \n Neroni Claudio divi Claudi filio Germanici nepoti Tiberi Caesaris pronepoti divi Augusti abnepoti Caesari Augusto Germanico pontifici maximo tribunicia potestate VIII imperatori consuli IIII patri patriae Servius Cornelius Servi filius Lemonia Orfitus quaestor divi Claudi praetor urbanus consul pontifex sodalis Augustalis proconsul patronus dedicavit Publio Silio Celere legato columnas et super columnia et super ostia in tribus Ithymbal Arinis filius Sabinus Tapapius flamen divi Augusti sufetu faciendas curavit idemque curator pecuniae publicae eas porticus\n
EDCS-59600004.translation: Servius Cornelius Orfitus, quaestor of the deified Claudius, urban praetor, consul, pontiff, sodalis Augustalis, proconsul, patron, dedicated this for Nero Claudius, son of the deified Claudius, grandson of Germanicus, great-grandson of Tiberius Caesar, great-great-grandson of the deified Augustus Caesar Germanicus, chief pontiff, holding tribunician power for the 8th time, emperor, consul for the 4th time, father of the fatherland. Publius Silio Celer, legate, supervised the construction of the columns, the structures above the columns, and the doorways in the three Ithymbal Arinis. His son Sabinus Tapapius, flamen of the deified Augustus and sufes, saw to their construction and was also supervisor of public funds for these porticoes.
EDCS-59600004.summary: A dedication of porticoes, columns, and doorways by Servius Cornelius Orfitus to Emperor Nero Claudius, with details of Roman official careers and the supervision of construction by Publius Silio Celer and Sabinus Tapapius.

EDCS-59600007.translation: To the Divine Augustuses, for the health of the Emperor Caesar Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Augustus Pius and his children, the city of the Thacensians made this with their own money, with Felix, son of Aelius, as suffete.
EDCS-59600007.summary: This is a public dedication by the city of Thacensium to the deified emperors Antoninus Pius and his family, likely dating to the 2nd century AD.

EDCS-59600074.translation: To the departed spirits. Titus Claudius Donatus, soldier of Legion III Augusta Pia Vindex, lived 52 years.
EDCS-59600074.summary: A funerary epitaph for Titus Claudius Donatus, a soldier of Legion III Augusta Pia Vindex, who died at age 52.

EDCS-59600075.translation: ...legate; soldier of Legion III Augusta Pia Vindex, lived 31 years.
EDCS-59600075.summary: A fragmented funerary epitaph recording the service and lifespan of a soldier, identified as a legate, from Legion III Augusta Pia Vindex.

EDCS-59600076.translation: The soldiers of the Severiana vexillation of Legion III Augusta Pia Vindex, devoted to your divine majesty and power, [erected this] for Julia Mamaea, mother of our Emperor Marcus Aurelius Severus Alexander Pius Felix Augustus, under the supervision of Aelius Crescentinus, first-rank centurion.
EDCS-59600076.summary: A dedication by soldiers of Legion III Augusta Pia Vindex to Julia Mamaea, mother of Emperor Alexander Severus, overseen by Aelius Crescentinus.

EDCS-59600077.translation: To our lords Theodosius, Arcadius, and Honorius, ever triumphant Augustuses, because of the splendor of the Alexandrian Baths.
EDCS-59600077.summary: This inscription is a dedication related to the Alexandrian Baths and honors the emperors Theodosius, Arcadius, and Honorius, likely from the late 4th or early 5th century.

EDCS-59600079.translation: Titus Aelius Iucundus gladly paid his vow.
EDCS-59600079.summary: This is a votive inscription recording Titus Aelius Iucundus fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-59600080.translation: To Geminius Optumus Mucianus, [flamen] of Aesculapius, whose ancestors [honors]...
EDCS-59600080.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription honoring Geminius Optumus Mucianus, who held the priesthood of Aesculapius, possibly a dedication or a monument to his family.

EDCS-59600081.translation: To the god Aesculapius Repentinus, Caius Cornelius Afranius Felix set this up.
EDCS-59600081.summary: This is a dedication to the god Aesculapius Repentinus made by Caius Cornelius Afranius Felix.

EDCS-59600091.translation: Filtered lamps, Asene being the contractor.
EDCS-59600091.summary: This inscription records a contract for filtered lamps, likely from a commercial or public context.

EDCS-59700180.translation: To the Divine Shades. Cornelia Cliopu made this for her daughter Julia Victorina, who lived 11 years and 9 days, [a] dutiful daughter.
EDCS-59700180.summary: A funerary epitaph for a young girl named Julia Victorina, set up by her mother.

EDCS-59700181.translation: Victor Pescennius, curator for many years, lived 55 years. His wife made this to the Divine Shades.
EDCS-59700181.summary: A funerary epitaph for Victor Pescennius, set up by his wife.

EDCS-59800006.translation: He restored and dedicated the aqueducts, which were submerged in dark and unsightly gloom and did not enjoy any happy sight, to the splendid municipality of MET, through the benefit of foresight, which was distributed for private use, and to the baths, which he ordered to be made for the citizens, freed from those burdens, during the proconsulship of Aemilius Paternus, a most distinguished and illustrious man, and of Erius Fannius Geminianus, a most distinguished man, legate of Caius Vibius Candidus, perpetual flamines, and the duumvirs, at public expense.
EDCS-59800006.summary: This inscription records the restoration and dedication of aqueducts and baths to a municipality, likely during the late Roman period given the names of officials.

EDCS-59800041.translation: The colony of Thugga, devoted to the victories of our Caesars.
EDCS-59800041.summary: A dedication from the colony of Thugga expressing loyalty to the Roman emperors and their victories.

EDCS-59800042.translation: Secundio, actor for Quintus Servilius Candidus, lived 66 years, 5 months, and 12 and a half days.
EDCS-59800042.summary: A funerary epitaph for Secundio, an actor for Quintus Servilius Candidus, recording his lifespan.

EDCS-59800048.translation: Titus Iulius Crisontianus, soldier of the III Augusti LII.
EDCS-59800048.summary: A fragmented inscription for Titus Iulius Crisontianus, a soldier of Legion III Augusta.

EDCS-59800074.summary: A very fragmented epitaph recording the lifespan of an individual.

EDCS-59800083.translation: For the good memory of Magora, [she] lived [....] years.
EDCS-59800083.summary: A fragmented funerary epitaph for Magora, recording her name and an incomplete lifespan.

EDCS-59800084.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Benedicta Sabina, likely a tombstone label.

EDCS-59800085.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Benedicta Roga, likely a tombstone label.

EDCS-59800086.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Benedicta Pro[---], likely a tombstone label.

EDCS-59800088.summary: This inscription likely refers to a memorial for Aurelia.

EDCS-59800093.summary: This fragmentary inscription mentions a subdeacon.

EDCS-59800095.summary: This fragmentary inscription seems to record something related to Proiecta.

EDCS-59800096.summary: This inscription records a memorial dedicated to Kasianus.

EDCS-59800097.translation: Aurellia Cornelia Hammonilla lived for 25 years in peace
EDCS-59800097.summary: This funerary inscription records the life span of Aurellia Cornelia Hammonilla.

EDCS-59800102.translation: To Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus and Lucius Aurelius Verus Augustus Armeniacus [---] / [---] in accordance with his will [---] ordered to be made [---] / [---] Publius Ampelius, a most distinguished and eminent proconsul
EDCS-59800102.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Emperors Marcus Aurelius Antoninus and Lucius Aurelius Verus, mentioning a commission by a proconsul, likely from the late 2nd century AD.

EDCS-59800105.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Marcus Ulpius Fortunatus, freedman and procurator of Augustus, pious, lived 42 years, is buried here. Coelia Thallusa, daughter of Aulus, his most devoted wife, made this.
EDCS-59800105.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to Marcus Ulpius Fortunatus by his wife Coelia Thallusa, and dates to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-59800106.translation: The municipality of Iulius Aurelius Mustitanus, devoted to our lord Flavius Valentinianus Maximus Pius Felix Victorious Ever Augustus, and to his divine majesty and authority.
EDCS-59800106.summary: A dedication from the municipality of Mustis to the emperor Valentinian III, likely from the 5th century CE.

EDCS-59800108.translation: To the divine virtue and perpetual clemency of the greatest emperor, founder of eternal peace, restorer of public safety and common liberty, our lord Flavius Valerius Constantinus, most powerful emperor, the municipality of Iulium Aurelium Mustitanum, devoted to his divinity and majesty.
EDCS-59800108.summary: This is a civic dedication by the municipality of Mustitanum to Emperor Constantine, praising his virtues and role as a ruler, likely from the 4th century CE.

EDCS-59800109.translation: To Iulia Domna Augusta, mother of the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Severus Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus, and of the camps, the senate, and the fatherland, wife of the divine Severus Pius, father of our lord the Emperor Antoninus Augustus, Parthicus Maximus, Britannicus Maximus, Pontifex Maximus, Pater Patriae, the council of Mustitanum, by decree of the decurions, at public expense, has dedicated this monument to Fortuna Redux and to Fertility.
EDCS-59800109.summary: This is a dedication by the council of Mustitanum to Empress Iulia Domna, mother and wife of emperors, honoring her maternal and marital roles, likely from the early 3rd century CE.

EDCS-59900011.translation: Aemilia Marciana, daughter of Quintus, a most distinguished woman, [dedicated] Hygias of silver, with books and...
EDCS-59900011.summary: An incomplete dedication of a silver statue of Hygias, possibly a cult image or votive offering, by a distinguished woman named Aemilia Marciana.

EDCS-59900134.translation: from the Alps to Setimpnus, son of Augustus.
EDCS-59900134.summary: An incomplete inscription possibly related to a boundary or a route marker, mentioning a location and a person associated with the imperial family.

EDCS-59900138.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pertinax Augustus Pius Arabicus Adiabenicus, father of the fatherland, pontifex maximus, holding tribunician power for the Vth time, imperator for the VIIth time, consul for the II time, proconsul, son of the divine Marcus Antoninus Pius Germanicus Sarmaticus, the Best and Greatest, and a most brave prince.
EDCS-59900138.summary: A lengthy imperial dedication honoring Emperor Septimius Severus, listing his titles and victories, likely erected by a public body.

EDCS-59900139.translation: To Augusta, mother of the emperor, of the camps, of the senate, and of the fatherland, the people of Hippon Regius, by decree of the decurions and with public funds.
EDCS-59900139.summary: This inscription records a public dedication to Augusta by the community of Hippon Regius.

EDCS-59900142.translation: To our lord Flavius Valentius, victorious and triumphal, ever Augustus, restorer of the land, sea, and public liberty, the state of the colony of Hippon Regius, by decree of the decurions and with public funds.
EDCS-59900142.summary: This inscription records a public dedication to the emperor Valentius by the community of Hippon Regius.

EDCS-59900144.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription, likely an honorific dedication to Marcus Titinius, possibly related to the Augustales.

EDCS-59900161.translation: [Name fragment] from [name fragment], a descendant in the fourth generation, added this work above his father's building.
EDCS-59900161.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary or commemorative inscription recording a descendant's addition to a building, likely a tomb, with an uncertain date.

EDCS-59900172.translation: In the name of his parents, that is, of his father and of Avillia Gabinia Venusta his mother, from a vow, a temple to the goddess Caelestis, which was begun for the honor of the perpetual priesthood and the quinquennial magistracy of the state of Thugga, at a cost of 60,000 sesterces, with 30,000 sesterces having been contributed for the crafting of silver statues of the goddesses, which Aburnius Avillius Felix wished to be provided by his heirs in his will, and also from the estate, according to his will, from whose income the gifts and games were to be provided, Quintus Gabinius Rufus Felix Beatianus, having increased the funds, completed and embellished it, and dedicated it, along with other statues, to the community from his own generosity on the day of dedication, having paid out the gifts and the banquet and the gymnasium.
EDCS-59900172.summary: This inscription details the completion and dedication of a temple and associated amenities to the goddess Caelestis, funded by a combination of parental vows, a private inheritance, and significant personal expenditure by Quintus Gabinius Rufus Felix Beatianus, likely in relation to his magistracies in Thugga.

EDCS-60200052.translation: Epiphanius the faithful lived for years
EDCS-60200052.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Epiphanius, with the age missing.

EDCS-60200057.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus, prince of the youth, consul, son of the Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus Arabicus Adiabenicus Parthicus Maximus, most strong, most fortunate, by decree of the decurions and with public funds.
EDCS-60200057.summary: This inscription records a public dedication to the emperor Caracalla by the community, likely in his early reign.

EDCS-60200075.translation: Musa, tell me the causes, with what light impaired
EDCS-60200075.summary: This is a hexameter verse, likely the beginning of a poem or an invocation to the Muse, possibly found on a tomb or related to a literary person.

EDCS-60500067.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Clodius Speratus lived sixteen years and [some] months.
EDCS-60500067.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the death of Clodius Speratus at the age of sixteen.

EDCS-60500068.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Caius Satirius Quietanus lived 25 years.
EDCS-60500068.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the death of Caius Satirius Quietanus at the age of 25.

EDCS-60500069.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. To Laelius Macro, son. Lived 5 months, 9 days.
EDCS-60500069.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the death of Laelius Macro at the age of 5 months and 9 days.

EDCS-60500077.summary: This inscription appears to record a personal vow fulfilled by Ius Athoius.

EDCS-60500078.translation: Ius Oetius had this set up and cared for it.
EDCS-60500078.summary: This inscription records a building or monument that was erected and maintained by Ius Oetius.

EDCS-60500082.translation: [Name fragment], son of [name fragment], lived for thirty years. He is buried here.
EDCS-60500082.summary: This is a simple funerary epitaph recording the name, parentage, age at death, and burial of an individual, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-60500083.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Primigenius, slave of Flavius Av[--], lived for twenty-five years.
EDCS-60500083.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a slave named Primigenius, indicating his owner and age at death, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-60500087.translation: From the workshop of Felix of Salernus.
EDCS-60500087.summary: This inscription indicates the origin of a manufactured object, originating from the workshop of Felix of Salernus.

EDCS-60500094.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Caecilia Ly...dia, devout, lived for 13 years and 3 months; she is buried here.
EDCS-60500094.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Caecilia Ly...dia, who died at the age of 13 years and 3 months.

EDCS-60500106.translation: Antonia Faustilla, devout, lived for 80 years; the care was managed by the Vaberi. Caius Vaberius Proculus, devout, lived for 85 years; the care was managed by his grandsons, the Vaberi. He is buried here.
EDCS-60500106.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Antonia Faustilla and Caius Vaberius Proculus, with their grandsons, the Vaberi, acting as caretakers.

EDCS-60500107.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. For Aulus, son of Lucius, devout, lived for 70 years. Lespica, devout, his wife, lived for 50 years. The care was managed by Rogatus, their son, and Ti asa, his wife.
EDCS-60500107.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Aulus and his wife Lespica, with their son Rogatus and his wife Ti asa managing the care.

EDCS-60500108.translation: Sorica lived in peace for 40 years, more or less. Euticius lived in peace for 50 years, more or less. On the Ides of May.
EDCS-60500108.summary: This inscription records the lifespan of Sorica and Euticius, who both lived for approximately 40 and 50 years respectively, with a date noted as the Ides of May.

EDCS-60500113.translation: Renata lived for one year, two months, and 18 days. She passed away on the Kalends of November.
EDCS-60500113.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan of Renata, who died at the age of 1 year, 2 months, and 18 days, with her death occurring on the Kalends of November.

EDCS-60500117.translation: Nemodella lived for 25 years, more or less. She rested on the 15th day before the Kalends of December.
EDCS-60500117.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan of Nemodella, who died at approximately 25 years of age, with her date of rest noted as the 15th day before the Kalends of December.

EDCS-60500118.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Aemilia Vernacula lived for 1 year and 7 months.
EDCS-60500118.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan of Aemilia Vernacula, who died at the age of 1 year and 7 months.

EDCS-60500119.translation: To the Divine Manes. Marcus C. Aemilianus lived 9 years, number 6.
EDCS-60500119.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a child named Marcus C. Aemilianus, recording his age at death.

EDCS-60500120.translation: To Calpurnia Theoclia, also known as Tatia Tharissa, lived as many years as she could, to one deserving.
EDCS-60500120.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Calpurnia Theoclia, also known as Tatia Tharissa, with an affectionate sentiment towards her.

EDCS-60500121.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Hateria Tertulla, also known as Robia, lived 43 years.
EDCS-60500121.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Hateria Tertulla, also known as Robia, recording her age at death.

EDCS-60500122.translation: To the Divine Manes. Lucius Hortensius Protus lived 80 years.
EDCS-60500122.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Hortensius Protus, recording his age at death.

EDCS-60500123.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Marcus Iulius Hilarus lived 4 years.
EDCS-60500123.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a child named Marcus Iulius Hilarus, recording his age at death.

EDCS-60500124.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Marcus Iulius Suriacus lived 8 years.
EDCS-60500124.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a child named Marcus Iulius Suriacus, recording his age at death.

EDCS-60500125.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Iulia Felicissima lived 62 years, 4 months, and 1 day.
EDCS-60500125.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Iulia Felicissima, recording her precise age at death.

EDCS-60500126.translation: To the Divine Manes. For Pompeia Secunda.
EDCS-60500126.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Pompeia Secunda.

EDCS-60500127.translation: To the Divine Manes. Gnaeus Pontius Saturninus lived 37 years.
EDCS-60500127.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Gnaeus Pontius Saturninus, recording his age at death.

EDCS-60500128.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary epitaph for an individual named Saturninus, recording his age at death.

EDCS-60500129.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Lucius Sergius Ingenuus lived 30 years.
EDCS-60500129.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Sergius Ingenuus, recording his lifespan.

EDCS-60500130.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Aulus Sergius Successus lived 30 years.
EDCS-60500130.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Aulus Sergius Successus, recording his lifespan.

EDCS-60500131.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Lucius Valerius Paulinus lies here, having lived 33 years.
EDCS-60500131.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Valerius Paulinus, recording his burial and lifespan.

EDCS-60500132.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Varius Oceanus lived 25 years.
EDCS-60500132.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Varius Oceanus, recording his lifespan.

EDCS-60500133.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Quintus Venidius Agricola lived 21 years.
EDCS-60500133.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Quintus Venidius Agricola, recording his lifespan.

EDCS-60500134.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcus Venidius Florus, recording his lifespan.

EDCS-60500135.summary: This inscription likely indicates ownership or a dedication related to Lucius Venidius Rusticus, possibly on a tomb or monument.

EDCS-60500136.summary: This inscription is likely a dedication or memorial to Venidia Gratia.

EDCS-60500137.summary: This inscription likely indicates ownership or a dedication related to Lucius Venidius Maximus, possibly on a tomb or monument.

EDCS-60500138.translation: To Quintus Venidius Agricola, son of Rusticus.
EDCS-60500138.summary: This inscription is a dedication or memorial to Quintus Venidius Agricola, son of Rusticus.

EDCS-60500146.translation: The Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Augustus, conqueror of Parthia, conqueror of Britain, conqueror of Germany, holding tribunician power for the 19th time, consul for the 4th time, father of his country, restored this.
EDCS-60500146.summary: This is an imperial rescript from the reign of Marcus Aurelius, likely dating to his later years, indicating the restoration of a building or monument.

EDCS-60500148.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Marcus Aufidius Felix Lucanus lived for 48 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-60500148.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcus Aufidius Felix Lucanus, likely from the Roman Imperial period, recording his name, age at death, and burial.

EDCS-60500149.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Caius Aufidius Verus, son of Marci, dutiful, lived for 62 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-60500149.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Caius Aufidius Verus, likely from the Roman Imperial period, recording his name, father's name, age at death, and burial.

EDCS-60500150.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Quintus Gallus Feneratoris, dutiful, lived for 45 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-60500150.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Quintus Gallus Feneratoris, likely from the Roman Imperial period, recording his name, age at death, and burial.

EDCS-60500153.translation: Martialis the priest lived for 31 years and rested in peace.
EDCS-60500153.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Martialis, a priest, likely from the late Roman or early Christian period, recording his age at death and peaceful rest.

EDCS-61300095.translation: [Fragmentary legal petition and imperial response concerning land rights and labor obligations, possibly related to a dispute over the saltus Burunitanus between landowners and a conductor (manager/tenant) and concerning abuses of power by officials.]
EDCS-61300095.summary: This is a very fragmentary text containing a legal petition and imperial responses, likely from the Roman Imperial period, concerning property rights, labor duties, and alleged abuses by officials in the province of Africa Proconsularis.

EDCS-61800282.translation: Tarsas Capito, son of Dinni, a Bessian tribesman, a cavalryman (eques) and standard-bearer (vexillarius) of the Pannonian ala, of the Peregrini troop, born in the citizenship of Dinorasci, lived for 30 years, served for 9 years; he is buried here. Cimanus, a cavalryman of the Pannonian ala, of the Gemelli troop, his son's guardian, set this up.
EDCS-61800282.summary: This is a funerary monument for Tarsas Capito, a soldier in a Pannonian cavalry unit, dating to the Roman Imperial period, recording his tribal origin, military service, age, and burial, with a dedication by his guardian.

EDCS-61800284.translation: Sentia Vitalis [epitaph text includes a mention of an omnipotent god, her age, and a plea to her husband to live well while he can].
EDCS-61800284.summary: This is a fragmentary epitaph for Sentia Vitalis, mentioning her age and religious beliefs, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-61800285.translation: I, Lolliana, was placed here, snatched away in a few years, whose character and life were contrary, upright, pitiable, who did not live to be twenty-five years old.
EDCS-61800285.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lolliana, a young woman, likely from the Roman Imperial period, lamenting her premature death at age 25 and praising her character.

EDCS-61800286.translation: If it pleases you, learn here whose Manes rests: Auruseus, distinguished among citizens and friends, who surpassed his ancestors in merit. He lived faithfully in peace for 49 years and departed on the Kalends of January.
EDCS-61800286.summary: This is a funerary epitaph, likely from the Roman Imperial period, for Auruseus, praising his character and recording his age at death and date of passing.

EDCS-61900145.summary: This is a short funerary epitaph for Eolius, likely from the early Christian period, indicating peaceful repose after death.

EDCS-61900146.translation: Pelagia sleeps in peace, the 3rd day before the Ides of November.
EDCS-61900146.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Pelagia, likely from the early Christian period, indicating peaceful repose after death and the date of her passing.

EDCS-61900147.summary: This is a short epitaph recording the repose of Vincitius.

EDCS-61900148.summary: This epitaph records the peaceful and innocent repose of Pascassus.

EDCS-61900149.translation: Fortucius rests in peace on the sixth day before the Nones of June.
EDCS-61900149.summary: This epitaph records the repose of Fortucius and gives a specific date of death.

EDCS-61900152.summary: This epitaph records Agapia, described as innocent in Christ.

EDCS-61900153.translation: Aelia Theodora lived one year, two months, and twenty days in peace.
EDCS-61900153.summary: This epitaph records the lifespan of Aelia Theodora, who died at the age of one year, two months, and twenty days.

EDCS-61900154.translation: Florentia lived eight months and eleven days, dying on the twelfth day before the Kalends of December.
EDCS-61900154.summary: This epitaph records the lifespan of Florentia, who died at the age of eight months and eleven days, and provides her date of death.

EDCS-63202240.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Numerius, son of Cl...
EDCS-63202240.summary: This is a fragment of a dedication to the departed spirits, beginning with the name Numerius.

EDCS-63202241.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. DVIC E TADEVS, who for your piety and to afford solace to the living while I myself am still alive and the spirit rules these limbs, always honored me with gifts. Licinia Al built this for herself.
EDCS-63202241.summary: This is a complex funerary inscription dedicated to the departed spirits by Licinia Al for herself and her husband (implied by DVIC E TADEVS), emphasizing piety and remembrance.

EDCS-63202242.translation: To the departed spirits. IME IV V
EDCS-63202242.summary: This is a fragmented inscription dedicated to the departed spirits.

EDCS-63300069.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Publius, son of I S V, made this for himself while alive.
EDCS-63300069.summary: This funerary inscription records that Publius, son of I S V, erected this monument for himself during his lifetime.

EDCS-63300078.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the god Mithras, likely by Secundinus.

EDCS-63600337.translation: Gududia and Sallustius, faithful, in peace.
EDCS-63600337.summary: This inscription records the names Gududia and Sallustius, described as faithful and at peace, likely from a funerary context.

EDCS-63600338.summary: This inscription records the name Felix, described as faithful and at peace, likely from a funerary context.

EDCS-63600339.summary: This inscription records the name Florentius, described as faithful and at peace, likely from a funerary context.

EDCS-63600340.translation: Ianuaria, faithful, innocent in God, entered.
EDCS-63600340.summary: This inscription records Ianuaria, described as faithful and innocent in God, likely from a funerary context.

EDCS-63600341.summary: This inscription records Ospitiana, described as faithful, with a truncated statement about her lifespan, likely from a funerary context.

EDCS-63600365.summary: This inscription records the name Iovinus, described as sweet and in peace, likely from a funerary context.

EDCS-63700015.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Ianuariana, faithful, departed on the 6th day before the Ides of February, in the 16th year of the indiction, the 6th year. The Lord, in his goodness, has deigned to call her from this transitory world to his kingdoms, where is her eternal seat and everlasting rest. Amen. She lived more or less 12 years, on the 6th day before the Ides of February.
EDCS-63700015.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the death of Ianuariana, including her age, burial date, and a religious statement about her passage to the afterlife, dated by indiction year.

EDCS-64100002.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Mevia Scula lived 52 years, is buried here. Sacred to the Divine Shades. Mevia Iunia lived 16 years, is buried here. Sacred to the Divine Shades. Marcus Mevius Urbanus lived 18 years, is buried here. Sacred to the Divine Shades. Marcus Mevius Restitutus lived 35 years, is buried here. His brothers erected this for their pious brother.
EDCS-64100002.summary: This funerary inscription records the deaths and ages of four individuals (Mevia Scula, Mevia Iunia, Marcus Mevius Urbanus, and Marcus Mevius Restitutus), with the last one being honored by his brothers.

EDCS-64100003.summary: This inscription records the names Titinia Laeta and Sterculina, likely a dedication from one to the other.

EDCS-64100004.translation: Of Tiberius Julius Iustus, son of Iulius Anthus and Marianus.
EDCS-64100004.summary: This is a funerary inscription mentioning the father of Tiberius Julius Iustus, likely recording his parentage.

EDCS-64100006.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Meurius Aemilius lived 30 years, here he lies buried. Castulus, pious, placed [this]. Sacred to the departed spirits. Castulus lived 10 years.
EDCS-64100006.summary: A tombstone commemorating two individuals, Meurius Aemilius and Castulus, noting their ages at death and a dedicant.

EDCS-64100007.summary: A very short inscription, likely a tombstone or dedication, simply naming Licinia Antonila.

EDCS-64100009.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Velius Victor, son of Lucius, lived [several] years, here he lies buried. Lucius Mussius [dedicated this].
EDCS-64100009.summary: A tombstone for Lucius Velius Victor, indicating his lifespan and a funerary dedication by Lucius Mussius.

EDCS-64100010.translation: Sacred to the August Deities. For the health of the Emperors Caesar Augustus Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Parthicus Arabicus Adiabenicus and Marcus Aurelius Antoninus and Caesar Augustus Publius Septimius Geta and of their entire divine house, Octavia Marc and her son Octavius Iucundus, priests, made [this] from their own land with their own money, as a gift of nature, [worth] 100,000 sesterces, and the area for the temple attendants from their revenues, from where we have consecrated the measure of the curia.
EDCS-64100010.summary: A dedication to the imperial family and deities for their health, made by priests Octavia Marc and Octavius Iucundus, likely for a temple or religious building.
