EDCS-64100011.translation: To Lucius Sallustius Donatus, son of Lucius, of the Arnensian tribe, aedile, duumvir, perpetual flamen, a place was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-64100011.summary: An honorary inscription granting burial space to Lucius Sallustius Donatus, a local magistrate, by the town council.

EDCS-64100035.summary: A very short inscription, likely a tombstone or dedication, simply naming Antonius Optimus.

EDCS-64100038.translation: Victorinus the presbyter in peace. Nianus the presbyter in peace lived years [on the] Kalends.
EDCS-64100038.summary: An epitaph for two presbyters, Victorinus and Nianus, indicating their religious office and their peaceful passing, with a partial date.

EDCS-64100039.translation: Rinasius the deacon rested in peace on the 11th day before the Kalends of June, lived 62 years, 4 months, 3 days, enjoying justice in the dark depths. NEOE IVI.
EDCS-64100039.summary: An epitaph for Rinasius, a deacon, recording his death date and lifespan, and describing his spiritual state.

EDCS-64100041.translation: Marcianus the faithful lived 50 years, departed on the 7th day before the Ides of September.
EDCS-64100041.summary: An epitaph for Marcianus, noting his lifespan and the date of his death.

EDCS-64100042.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Adata, recording her faithful passing.

EDCS-64100043.translation: Constantinus departed in peace on the third day before the Kalends of December, having lived 40 years.
EDCS-64100043.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Constantinus, recording his death date and age.

EDCS-64100044.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Galliga, recording her passing.

EDCS-64100046.translation: Sabinianus, faithful, lived well in peace.
EDCS-64100046.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Sabinianus, highlighting his faithful and good life.

EDCS-64100047.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Amatia, recording her faithful passing.

EDCS-64100048.translation: Asinarius, faithful, lived 60 years, laid to rest on the fourth day before the Kalends of December.
EDCS-64100048.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Asinarius, recording his age and burial date.

EDCS-64100049.translation: Nigrina, faithful, lived well in God in peace.
EDCS-64100049.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Nigrina, emphasizing her faithful life in faith.

EDCS-64100050.translation: Gaudiosus, faithful, lived 3 years and 8 months in peace.
EDCS-64100050.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Gaudiosus, recording his young age at death.

EDCS-64100051.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Surgentius, recording his faithful passing.

EDCS-64100052.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Victorianus, describing him as innocent.

EDCS-64100054.translation: Marcus, faithful, lived in peace for 60 years and 3 months.
EDCS-64100054.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Marcus.

EDCS-64100056.translation: Monninis, faithful, lived in peace and departed in the Lord on the Nones of December.
EDCS-64100056.summary: This is a funerary inscription noting the death of Monninis on a specific date.

EDCS-64100057.translation: Pascasius, subdeacon, lived in peace and was buried on the fourth day before the Kalends of November.
EDCS-64100057.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Pascasius, a subdeacon, stating his burial date.

EDCS-64100058.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Crescentia, noting her virtues and peaceful repose.

EDCS-64100059.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Bonifatia, noting her virtues and peaceful repose.

EDCS-64100060.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Sifila, indicating her faithful status and peaceful rest.

EDCS-64100061.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Vitalis, indicating his faithful status and peaceful rest.

EDCS-64100062.translation: Iulius, innocent, faithful, lived in peace for 15 years.
EDCS-64100062.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan and virtues of Iulius.

EDCS-64100063.translation: Naborina lived for one year and two months.
EDCS-64100063.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the short lifespan of Naborina.

EDCS-64100065.translation: Celido, faithful, lived in peace for 34 years.
EDCS-64100065.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Celido.

EDCS-64100066.translation: Felicitas the faithful lived in peace for 20 years and departed 8 days before the Kalends of January.
EDCS-64100066.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Felicitas, recording her age at death and date of passing.

EDCS-64100067.translation: Adeodata lived for 30 years and departed 14 days before the Kalends of March. Mauricella lived for 7 years and departed 5 days before the Ides of September.
EDCS-64100067.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Adeodata and Mauricella, recording their ages at death and dates of passing.

EDCS-64100068.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Parastatica, indicating her faithful status and peaceful repose.

EDCS-64100069.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Geminus, indicating his faithful status and peaceful repose.

EDCS-64100070.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Bonifatius, indicating his faithful status and peaceful repose.

EDCS-64100072.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Maioricus, noting his clerical rank and peaceful repose.

EDCS-64100073.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Ceciliana, indicating her peaceful repose.

EDCS-64100074.translation: Helvia Dativa the faithful lived in peace for 73 years and 10 months.
EDCS-64100074.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Helvia Dativa, recording her age at death and faithful status.

EDCS-64100075.translation: Gemnula the faithful in peace. Teudulus the faithful in peace.
EDCS-64100075.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Gemnula and Teudulus, indicating their faithful status and peaceful repose.

EDCS-64100076.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Pascassa, indicating her faithful status and peaceful repose.

EDCS-64100077.translation: Secunda, faithful, lived in peace for 60 years.
EDCS-64100077.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a woman named Secunda, who lived to be 60 years old.

EDCS-64100079.translation: Mustacius, faithful, lived in peace for 70 years.
EDCS-64100079.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a man named Mustacius, who lived to be 70 years old.

EDCS-64100080.summary: This is a brief funerary epitaph for a woman named Victorina, indicating her faithful presence in peace.

EDCS-64100081.summary: This is a brief funerary epitaph for a woman named Maxima, indicating her faithful presence in peace.

EDCS-64100082.translation: Dativa and Victoria, faithful, in peace.
EDCS-64100082.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for two women, Dativa and Victoria, indicating their faithful presence in peace.

EDCS-64100083.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a man named Revocatus, who lived an innocent life in peace.

EDCS-64100084.translation: Catta, innocent, faithful, departed in peace on the 6th day before the Ides of September.
EDCS-64100084.summary: This funerary epitaph records the death of Catta, described as innocent and faithful, on September 8th.

EDCS-64100085.summary: This funerary epitaph records the death of Honorina, described as innocent and faithful, at the age of 3.

EDCS-64100087.translation: Trigetia, faithful, lived in peace for 45 years.
EDCS-64100087.summary: This funerary epitaph records that Trigetia, who was faithful, lived in peace for 45 years.

EDCS-64100088.translation: Ulpius Neophytus, faithful, lived in peace for 73 years.
EDCS-64100088.summary: This funerary epitaph records that Ulpius Neophytus, who was faithful, lived in peace for 73 years.

EDCS-64100089.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Ingennus, who is described as faithful and

EDCS-64100090.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Rebecia, who is described as innocent.

EDCS-64100091.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Fatalis, who is described as innocent and at peace.

EDCS-64100092.translation: Datibus, faithful, lived in peace for seventy-five years.
EDCS-64100092.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Datibus, who lived 75 years and is described as faithful and at peace.

EDCS-64100093.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Restitutus, who is described as being at peace.

EDCS-64100094.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Natalis, who is described as innocent and at peace.

EDCS-64100097.translation: Faus, faithful, lived in peace for 43 years; departed on the 14th day before the Kalends of November.
EDCS-64100097.summary: This funerary inscription records that Faus lived 43 years and died on October 19th, described as faithful and at peace.

EDCS-64100098.translation: Sissinus, faithful, lived in peace for 56 years; departed on the 2nd day before the Kalends of November.
EDCS-64100098.summary: This funerary inscription records that Sissinus lived 56 years and died on October 31st, described as faithful and at peace.

EDCS-64100100.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Ianuarius, who is described as faithful and at peace.

EDCS-64100101.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Restuta, who is described as faithful and at peace.

EDCS-64100102.translation: Ickus lived well in peace for seventy years.
EDCS-64100102.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Ickus.

EDCS-64100103.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the faithfulness of Quodvultdeus.

EDCS-64800298.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Mussius Ingenuus lived for [number] years.
EDCS-64800298.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary epitaph for Mussius Ingenuus, indicating his age at death, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-64800299.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Marcus Fadius Claros lived for 35 years, 3 months, and 25 days.
EDCS-64800299.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcus Fadius Claros, providing his age at death, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-65000109.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Iudas Icositanus monumentum vivus fecit\n
EDCS-65000109.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Iudas Icositanus made this monument for himself while alive.
EDCS-65000109.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Iudas Icositanus, who commissioned his own monument (a 'living tomb'), likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-65000121.summary: This inscription records the name Lucius Gravius Romanus, likely a funerary dedication or a name panel.

EDCS-65400059.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus Porcius Verus lived 47 years. Fulvius Primus placed this for his father. He is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Porcius Martialis lived 22 years. Quintus Porcius Verus placed this for his brother. He is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Fulvia Tertiola lived 4 years. Quintus Porcius Verus, her father, placed this. She is buried here.
EDCS-65400059.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Quintus Porcius Verus, his brother Porcius Martialis, and his daughter Fulvia Tertiola, with dedications from family members, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-65400092.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Aelia Flora lived for 28 years; her brothers and husband set this up for her because of her good morals and discipline; she lies here.
EDCS-65400092.summary: This funerary epitaph honors Aelia Flora, recording her age and the people who set it up for her.

EDCS-65400093.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Publius Aelius Rogatianus lived for 4 years; he lies here. Aelius Rogatus set this up for his pious son.
EDCS-65400093.summary: This funerary epitaph honors Publius Aelius Rogatianus, recording his age and that his father set it up.

EDCS-65400094.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Caelia Nina lived for 90 years; she lies here. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Sextus Servenius Gemellus lived for 78 years; he lies here. His son set this up for his father.
EDCS-65400094.summary: This funerary epitaph records the ages of Caelia Nina and Sextus Servenius Gemellus, and notes that the latter's son set up the monument.

EDCS-65400095.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Quintus Caelius Victor lived for 40 years, 6 months, 20 days, and 10 hours; he lies here. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Caelia Donatula lived for 8 years, 30 days, and 9 hours; she lies here. A pious father set this up. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Volussia Fortunata, also called Tuttula, lived for 21 years, 4 months, 16 days, and 6 hours; she lies here. Her pious husband set this up for his wife.
EDCS-65400095.summary: This funerary epitaph records the ages and lifespans of Quintus Caelius Victor, Caelia Donatula, and Volussia Fortunata, with family members setting up the monuments.

EDCS-65400096.translation: Clodia Libera lived for 21 years; she lies here. Clodius Libosus set this up for his most sweet daughter, and Aemilius Vitalis for his most excellent wife.
EDCS-65400096.summary: This funerary epitaph records the age of Clodia Libera and names her father and her sister's husband as the dedicator.

EDCS-65400097.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Decimia Silvana lived for 65 years; she lies here. Her pious husband set this up. Antiochia, aged 22, was laid to rest here in peace on the day before the Kalends of June.
EDCS-65400097.summary: This funerary epitaph records the age of Decimia Silvana and notes her husband as the dedicator, and also records the burial and age of Antiochia.

EDCS-65400098.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Marcus Hortensius Celer lived for [---] years; he lies here.
EDCS-65400098.summary: This fragmentary funerary epitaph records the name Marcus Hortensius Celer and his burial place.

EDCS-65400099.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Quinta Iulia Quiria lived for 8 months. Quintus Iulius Tittor set this up for his pious daughter. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Flavia Maxima lived for [---] years; she lies here. Quintus Iulius Tittor set this up for his pious mother. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Quintus Iulius Victor lived for 73 years; he lies here. Quintus Iulius Tittor set this up for his pious father.
EDCS-65400099.summary: This funerary inscription records the ages and burials of Quinta Iulia Quiria, Flavia Maxima, and Quintus Iulius Victor, all with monuments dedicated by Quintus Iulius Tittor.

EDCS-65400100.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Gaius Iulius Ferronius lived 83 years, is buried here. Iulius Secundus placed this for his dutiful father. Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Iulia Rogatina lived 90 years, is buried here. Iulius Secundus placed this for his dutiful mother.
EDCS-65400100.summary: This is a funerary epitaph commemorating two parents, Gaius Iulius Ferronius and Iulia Rogatina, with their son Iulius Secundus as the dedicator.

EDCS-65400101.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Titinia Laeta Sterculina lived 62 years, is buried here. Iulius Gaetulicus placed this for his dutiful wife. Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Iulius Gaetulicus lived 88 years, is buried here. Iulius Pallans placed this for his dutiful father. Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Rusticelia Octavianilla lived 28 years and 8 days, is buried here. Iulius Pallans placed this for his dutiful wife. Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Iulius Gaetulicus lived 36 years, is buried here. Iulius Pallans lived 36 years, is buried here. Iulius Pallans placed this for his sons. Gaius Iulius Pallans lived 80 years, is buried here.
EDCS-65400101.summary: This complex epitaph records the burials of multiple individuals, including Iulius Gaetulicus, his wife Titinia Laeta Sterculina, his son Iulius Pallans, and Iulius Pallans' wife Rusticelia Octavianilla, with various family members acting as dedicators.

EDCS-65400102.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Mevius Ingenuus lived 51 years, is buried here. Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Numisia Fortunata lived 70 years, is buried here. Mevii Ingenuus and Secundus placed this for their dutiful mother. Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Gaius Mevius lived 65 years, is buried here. His sons placed this for their dutiful father.
EDCS-65400102.summary: This funerary inscription commemorates Mevius Ingenuus, Numisia Fortunata, and Gaius Mevius, with dedications from their children.

EDCS-65400103.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Iunonia lived 6 months. Felicio, her grandfather, placed this. Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Iulius Mantius lived 28 years. Felicio, his father, placed this.
EDCS-65400103.summary: This epitaph records the short lives of a child named Iunonia and a young man named Iulius Mantius, both commemorated by their respective grandfathers/fathers named Felicio.

EDCS-65400104.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Iulius Secundus, son of Lucius, of the tribe Quirina, lived 68 years, is buried here.
EDCS-65400104.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Iulius Secundus, son of Lucius, indicating his age at death and burial location.

EDCS-65400105.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Lauta the dutiful lived 7 years and 6 months. Saturus, her dutiful father, placed this for his daughter. She is buried here.
EDCS-65400105.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a young girl named Lauta, dedicated by her dutiful father Saturus.

EDCS-65400106.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Mevia Urbana lived 20 years, is buried here. Mevi placed this for his sister. Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Mevia Secundula lived 21 years, is buried here. Mevi placed this for his sister.
EDCS-65400106.summary: This epitaph records the deaths of two sisters, Mevia Urbana and Mevia Secundula, both commemorated by a relative named Mevi.

EDCS-65400107.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Modia Rufinula the dutiful lived 31 years, is buried here. Camurenius Sapidus placed this for his dearest wife.
EDCS-65400107.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Modia Rufinula, dedicated by her husband Camurenius Sapidus.

EDCS-65400108.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Gaius Munatius Privatus lived 23 years, is buried here. Gaius Munatius Primulus placed this for his most dutiful brother.
EDCS-65400108.summary: This funerary epitaph commemorates Gaius Munatius Privatus, dedicated by his brother Gaius Munatius Primulus.

EDCS-65400109.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Novatilla the dutiful lived 55 years and 10 months. Marcus Iulius Victoricus placed this for his excellent wife. She is buried here. Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Marcus Iulius Victoricus lived 70 years, is buried here.
EDCS-65400109.summary: This funerary inscription records the deaths of Novatilla and her husband Marcus Iulius Victoricus, with mutual dedications.

EDCS-65400110.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Lucius Pompeius Victor, son of Lucius, of the Quirina tribe, lived 31 years and is buried here. Pompeius Mercurialis dedicated this to his most devoted mother and brother. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Iulia Casta, devoted, lived 35 years and is buried here.
EDCS-65400110.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the ages and burial places of Lucius Pompeius Victor and Iulia Casta, with the latter being dedicated by Pompeius Mercurialis.

EDCS-65400111.translation: Lucius Postumius Felix Pompeianus lived 3 months and 21 days.
EDCS-65400111.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the very short lifespan of Lucius Postumius Felix Pompeianus.

EDCS-65400112.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Sextus Postumius Fortunatus lived 40 years and is buried here. Camurina Clara made this for her most loving son.
EDCS-65400112.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Sextus Postumius Fortunatus, dedicated by his mother Camurina Clara.

EDCS-65400113.translation: The freedmen of Tarcellius, Publius and Gnaeus, made this for their father, who lived 17 years, 7 months, and 23 days and is buried here.
EDCS-65400113.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Tarcellius by his freedmen, stating his age and burial.

EDCS-65400115.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Tupidius Ciriminnus lived 5 years and is buried here. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Tupidius Nundinarius lived 9 years and is buried here. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Tupidius Castinus, a pious child, lived 10 years and is buried here. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Antonia Rutum lived [age missing]. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Tupidius Ianuarius made this for his sons.
EDCS-65400115.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the burials and ages of several members of the Tupidius family, including children, and also Antonia Rutum, likely related.

EDCS-65400116.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Victoricus lived 1 year and 8 months; his mother placed this; he is buried here.
EDCS-65400116.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the short lifespan of Victoricus, dedicated by his mother.

EDCS-65400117.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Aelia Faustina lived 35 years and is buried here. Publius Agrius Vitalis dedicated this to his devoted wife.
EDCS-65400117.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Aelia Faustina, dedicated by her husband Publius Agrius Vitalis.

EDCS-65400118.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Caius Avidius Victoricus lived 33 years; his devoted father placed this; he is buried here.
EDCS-65400118.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Caius Avidius Victoricus, dedicated by his father.

EDCS-65500007.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription, possibly part of a longer text, mentioning a date and a state of peace.

EDCS-65500012.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription indicating the burial of a person whose name is incomplete but includes 'fidelis'.

EDCS-65500014.summary: A short epitaph for an individual named P. Annius, stating they are at rest in peace.

EDCS-65500015.translation: Faithful, six days before the Kalends.
EDCS-65500015.summary: A fragment of an inscription, likely funerary, giving a date relative to the Roman calendar.

EDCS-65500016.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Calpurnia Optata placed this monument for herself. She lived one hundred years. She is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Rubia Galosa lived two years and four months. She is buried here.
EDCS-65500016.summary: A funerary inscription recording the deaths of two women, Calpurnia Optata and Rubia Galosa, detailing their ages and indicating they placed the monument for themselves or were buried there.

EDCS-65500017.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Tiberius Haterius Zoticus lived seventeen years. He is buried here. Tiberia Hateria Laudica placed [this] for her pious husband.
EDCS-65500017.summary: A funerary inscription for Tiberius Haterius Zoticus, who died at 17, with the monument erected by his wife Tiberia Hateria Laudica.

EDCS-65500018.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Honoratus lived seventeen years, a dutiful father.
EDCS-65500018.summary: A funerary inscription for Honoratus, who died at 17, noting his piety and role as a father.

EDCS-65500019.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus Otacilius Quintillus lived eighty years. He is buried here.
EDCS-65500019.summary: A funerary inscription for Quintus Otacilius Quintillus, who died at 80 years of age.

EDCS-65500020.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. M. Calidia Sorica lived 2 years, 10 months, and 13 days. Her father placed [this] for his sweetest, dearest daughter.
EDCS-65500020.summary: A funerary inscription for M. Calidia Sorica, detailing her young age at death and the monument erected by her father.

EDCS-65500021.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Cossinia Lucifera Quirina, daughter of Oli, lived sixty years. She is buried here. Licinia Antonila placed [this] for her pious mother, her daughter.
EDCS-65500021.summary: A funerary inscription for Cossinia Lucifera Quirina, who died at 60, with the monument erected by her daughter Licinia Antonila.

EDCS-65500022.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Helvia Ilica, daughter of Quintus, lived forty-five years. She is buried here. Caecilius Vitalis placed [this] for his dearest wife.
EDCS-65500022.summary: A funerary inscription for Helvia Ilica, who died at 45, with the monument erected by her husband Caecilius Vitalis.

EDCS-65500023.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Evillia Erotis lived fifty-five years. She is buried here. Eucharistus placed [this] for his pious wife.
EDCS-65500023.summary: A funerary inscription for Evillia Erotis, who died at 55, with the monument erected by her husband Eucharistus.

EDCS-65500024.translation: To the Divine Shades. Marcus Iulius Eperephanus lived 63 years, here he lies. Ovilia Saturna placed [this] for her pious husband.
EDCS-65500024.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Marcus Iulius Eperephanus and its dedication by his wife Ovilia Saturna.

EDCS-65500025.translation: To the Divine Shades. Umidius Saturus lived 67 years, here he lies. To the Divine Shades. Dubitata lived 3 years. Umidius Saturus and Iulia Donata placed [this] for their dearest daughter. To the Divine Shades. Umidia Saputula lived 32 years, her pious husband placed [this] for her, here she lies.
EDCS-65500025.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the deaths of Umidius Saturus, his daughter Dubitata, and his wife Umidia Saputula, with dedications by the surviving family members.

EDCS-65500026.translation: To the Divine Shades. Felicitas lived 1 year, 5 months, and 10 days, here she lies. Her pious uncle Caecilius Florentius placed [this]. She lived 33 years, here she lies, a most frugal, most chaste, most obedient woman to her husband. Caecilius Florentius placed [this] for his most rare, pious sister. For 40 years I lived, a friend to all, simple, good, generous, as much as I could according to my frugality. Now I have withdrawn to this tomb, as I made life. As much as I could. Here he lies. Caecilius Florentius placed [this] for his pious brother-in-law.
EDCS-65500026.summary: A complex funerary epitaph for Felicitas, her brother Caecilius Florentius, and another Caecilius Florentius, likely the brother-in-law of the deceased, with self-written epitaphs for the latter two and a poem for the sister.

EDCS-65500027.translation: To the Divine Shades. Marcus Caecilius Pa lived 23 years, here he lies. Caecilius Praetorianus placed [this] for his pious brother.
EDCS-65500027.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Marcus Caecilius Pa and its dedication by his brother Caecilius Praetorianus.

EDCS-65500028.translation: To the Divine Shades. Fabia Fortunata lived 40 years, here she lies. Caesius Liberalis [placed this] for his dearest wife. To the Divine Shades. Caesius Liberalis lived 47 years, here he lies. Caesius Liberalis, the father, had to make this tomb for his pious son.
EDCS-65500028.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the deaths of Fabia Fortunata and Caesius Liberalis, with dedications by each other and by the father for his son.

EDCS-65500029.translation: To the Divine Shades. Aemilius Saturus lived 50 years, here he lies. Aemilia, his daughter, placed [this].
EDCS-65500029.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Aemilius Saturus and its dedication by his daughter Aemilia.

EDCS-65500030.translation: To the Divine Shades. Aonia Hyola lived 73 years, here she lies. Valerius Luciscus placed [this] for his pious wife.
EDCS-65500030.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Aonia Hyola and its dedication by her husband Valerius Luciscus.

EDCS-65500031.translation: To the Divine Shades. Publius Domitius Rogatus from Thmuis, piously, here he lies. He lived 60 years.
EDCS-65500031.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Publius Domitius Rogatus, a man from Thmuis, including his age.

EDCS-65500032.translation: To the Divine Shades. Fullonia Quartula lived [X] years, here she lies. She placed [this] for herself. To the Divine Shades. Bolana the pious lived [X] years, here she lies. Fullonia placed [this] for her pious mother.
EDCS-65500032.summary: A funerary epitaph for Fullonia Quartula, who dedicated it to herself, and for her mother Bolana, dedicated by Fullonia.

EDCS-65500033.translation: To the Divine Shades. Pactimea Urbana lived 15 years, she made [this] with her mother. M. [Husband].
EDCS-65500033.summary: A funerary epitaph for Pactimea Urbana, who lived 15 years, dedicated by herself and her mother, with a partial dedication by her husband.

EDCS-65500034.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Sossia Matrona lived 100 years and is buried here. Marcus Aurelius Tertius placed this for his mother. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Aurelius Tertius lived 60 years and is buried here. Marcus Aurelius Tertius placed this for his father.
EDCS-65500034.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Sossia Matrona and Aurelius Tertius, with dedications by their son Marcus Aurelius Tertius.

EDCS-65500036.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Antonia Saturnina lived 42 years and is buried here. Her brothers placed this. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Casidius Iunior lived 48 years.
EDCS-65500036.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Antonia Saturnina, dedicated by her brothers, and mentions Casidius Iunior.

EDCS-65500037.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Crescens lived 70 years. Baebia Ianuaria, devoted, placed this and she is buried here.
EDCS-65500037.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Crescens, dedicated by Baebia Ianuaria.

EDCS-65500038.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Caecilia Rusticilla lived 11 years and 9 months and is buried here. Caecilius Vitalianus Barbarus and Rusticulus made this.
EDCS-65500038.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Caecilia Rusticilla, made by Caecilius Vitalianus Barbarus and Rusticulus.

EDCS-65500039.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Camidenius Lucretianus lived 2 years, 2 months, and 8 days and is buried here.
EDCS-65500039.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Camidenius Lucretianus.

EDCS-65600082.translation: Aemilia Eufrosyna placed this cupola for her freedman Aemilius Dainus. He lived 35 years. Sacred to the departed spirits.
EDCS-65600082.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of the freedman Aemilius Dainus at age 35, dedicated by his patroness Aemilia Eufrosyna.

EDCS-65600083.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Agria Sabina, a chaste matron, lived 30 years. She is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Asidonius Repentinus lived [3] years. He is buried here.
EDCS-65600083.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Agria Sabina, a married woman, and Asidonius Repentinus, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-65600084.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Clodia Venusta lived 80 years. Her most dutiful sons placed this.
EDCS-65600084.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Clodia Venusta, who lived 80 years, and was commemorated by her sons.

EDCS-65600085.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Caius Cornelius Perpetuus Vipianus, son of Caius, of the Quirina tribe, lived 6 years. He is buried here. Caius Cornelius Primus placed this for his dearest son.
EDCS-65600085.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of a young boy, Caius Cornelius Perpetuus Vipianus, who died at age 6, dedicated by his father Caius Cornelius Primus.

EDCS-65600086.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Titus Lartius Vegetus lived 80 years. He is buried here. A dutiful son placed this. Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulia Quintulla lived 60 years. She is buried here. A dutiful son placed this. Sacred to the departed spirits. Titus Lartius Pudens lived 42 years. He is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Edinia Regilla lived [3] years.
EDCS-65600086.summary: This funerary inscription records the burials of Titus Lartius Vegetus, Iulia Quintulla, Titus Lartius Pudens, and Edinia Regilla, with dedications likely from their children.

EDCS-65600087.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Caius Marius Tertulus Luciolus lived fifty years. To him, who with [3] Aquilus Luciolus wished, the sons of Marius placed this for their dearest father. He is buried here.
EDCS-65600087.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Caius Marius Tertulus Luciolus, who died at age 50, dedicated by his sons.

EDCS-65600088.translation: Numonia Candida, a woman without equal, lived 38 years. She is buried here. Her parents, whom death cruelly struck, placed this so that the memory of her name might endure through reading.
EDCS-65600088.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Numonia Candida, who lived 38 years, and was memorialized by her parents who had also passed away.

EDCS-65600090.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Tilia Concordia lived 17 years and 30 days. T. N. P., her dutiful father, placed this. Sacred to the departed spirits. Tilius [3]nus [3] lived [3] years [3] M [3].
EDCS-65600090.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Tilia Concordia, who died at age 17, dedicated by her father, and a second fragmented burial record.

EDCS-65600091.translation: To the gods, the shades. Ulpia Cata, a woman of honorable memory, lived 28 years. She lies here. Ulpius Colonus made this for his most devoted wife.
EDCS-65600091.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Ulpia Cata, set up by her husband Ulpius Colonus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-65600093.translation: To the gods, the shades. Flavius [---], lived [3] years. He lies here. Primitivus placed this for his most beloved son. // To the gods, the shades. Flavius Felix, aged 20, lived 16 years, [6] months, [6] days. He made this for his devoted son. // To the gods, the shades. Flavius Primitivus, lived 36 years, 3 months. He lies here. The Flavii placed this for their father.
EDCS-65600093.summary: This inscription appears to be a composite text with at least three funerary notices for members of the Flavius family, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-65600094.translation: To the gods, the shades. Iulia Fortunata [---]
EDCS-65600094.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary epitaph for Iulia Fortunata, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-65600095.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Caius Atilius Felix lived 65 years and is buried here. Atilius Ianuarianus placed this for his father.
EDCS-65600095.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Caius Atilius Felix, dedicated by his son Atilius Ianuarianus.

EDCS-65600096.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Laelia Secunda lived 50 years.
EDCS-65600096.summary: This epitaph records the lifespan of Laelia Secunda.

EDCS-65600097.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Flavia Ianuaria lived 33 years and 6 months and is buried here. Modius Martialis lived 2 years and 2 months. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Pompeia Fortunata lived 25 years and 10 months and is buried here.
EDCS-65600097.summary: This epitaph records the burials of Flavia Ianuaria and Pompeia Fortunata, with Modius Martialis also mentioned.

EDCS-65600098.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Quintus Cutilius Felix placed this for his dearest wife, Pompeia Victoria, who died in childbirth. She lived 40 years and is buried here.
EDCS-65600098.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Pompeia Victoria, dedicated by her husband Quintus Cutilius Felix.

EDCS-65600099.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Aemilius Donatus lived 30 years and died not undeservedly before his time. His devoted mother placed this for her dearest son.
EDCS-65600099.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Aemilius Donatus, dedicated by his mother.

EDCS-65600100.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Alfia Donata lived 21 years. Marcus Alfius placed [this]. Here lies.
EDCS-65600100.summary: A funerary epitaph for Alfia Donata, set up by her father Marcus Alfius, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-65600102.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Publius Iulius Marcellinus (of the Quirina tribe) lived 91 years. His son placed [this] for his father.
EDCS-65600102.summary: A funerary epitaph for Publius Iulius Marcellinus, dedicated by his son, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-65600103.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Octavius Labo lived 25 years. His devoted father placed [this]. Here he lies.
EDCS-65600103.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lucius Octavius Labo, erected by his devoted father, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-65600104.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Victor Finus, who lived [---] years. His sons wanted this tomb, so that you may not be able to appropriate his burial.
EDCS-65600104.summary: A funerary epitaph for Victor Finus, erected by his sons, emphasizing the preservation of his burial plot, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-65600105.translation: Cornelius Venustus lived 40 years, sacred to the departed spirits. Magnia Cutina lived 73 years, sacred to the departed spirits. Gaius Cornelius Venustus lived 45 years, sacred to the departed spirits. X
EDCS-65600105.summary: A complex funerary inscription listing the lives and deaths of Cornelius Venustus, Magnia Cutina, and Gaius Cornelius Venustus, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-65600106.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Caius Iulius Rogatus lived 60 years. Here he lies. Iulia Libera placed [this] for her devoted husband.
EDCS-65600106.summary: A funerary epitaph for Caius Iulius Rogatus, erected by his devoted wife Iulia Libera, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-65600108.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. For Gaius Orbius Bassus, son of Aulus, of the Quirina tribe. Orbius Bassianus and Bassus placed [this] for their dearest father. Here he lies.
EDCS-65600108.summary: A funerary epitaph for Gaius Orbius Bassus, dedicated by his sons Orbius Bassianus and Bassus, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-65600109.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus Caecilius Vitalis lived 78 years. Here he lies. Quintus Caecilius Vitalis [his son] made [this] for his most excellent father and instructor of this entire region and descendant, a good man.
EDCS-65600109.summary: A funerary epitaph for Quintus Caecilius Vitalis, erected by his son who also praises him as an instructor of the region, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-65600111.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Mivius Martialialis, son of Publius, of the Quirina tribe, lived 80 years. Here he lies. Lucius Mivius Lucustarius placed [this] for his most excellent and rare father.
EDCS-65600111.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lucius Mivius Martialialis, erected by his son Lucius Mivius Lucustarius, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-65600112.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Publius Aelius Principius lived 13 years. His parents Allius and Hilaritas [placed this] for their son.
EDCS-65600112.summary: A funerary epitaph for Publius Aelius Principius, who died at the age of 13, set up by his parents Allius and Hilaritas, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-65600113.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Crepereius Bacnilusus, who lived 8 years, 5 months, and 20 days, is buried here.
EDCS-65600113.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a child named Crepereius Bacnilusus, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-65600114.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulius Ianuarius lived 6 years; his father placed this for his son. He is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Octavia Quintulla lived 90 years; her husband placed this for his most exceptional wife. She is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulius Marcellinus lived 101 years, 4 months, and 22 days. He is buried here.
EDCS-65600114.summary: This inscription records the burials of three individuals: Iulius Ianuarius (a child), Octavia Quintulla, and Iulius Marcellinus, likely from a single family plot.

EDCS-65600115.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Nonia Placida lived about 5 years; she is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Iucundia Rogata lived 35 years; her husband Nonius Saturninus made this.
EDCS-65600115.summary: This inscription commemorates two women, Nonia Placida and Iucundia Rogata, with the latter's husband identified as the dedicator.

EDCS-65600117.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Eternal sleep. Rubria Secunda lived 27 years; she is buried here. Not having deserved this fate, Coranius Felix, her husband, placed this for his most beloved and pious wife.
EDCS-65600117.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated by Coranius Felix to his wife Rubria Secunda, lamenting her untimely death.

EDCS-65600118.translation: Verna Maior is buried here. He who for a long time covered this land, previously a forest, P P [possibly 'proprietarius' or similar, referring to ownership].
EDCS-65600118.summary: This inscription marks the burial place of Verna Maior and notes his ownership or development of the land.

EDCS-65600119.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Ionia Cinasia lived 1 year; she is buried here. Onius Liberalis made this for his pious daughter.
EDCS-65600119.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated by Onius Liberalis to his young daughter, Ionia Cinasia.

EDCS-65600121.translation: To the gods, the shades, sacred. Gaius Julius Agilis, son of Gaius, of the Quirina tribe, [---]
EDCS-65600121.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary epitaph for Gaius Julius Agilis, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-65600131.translation: [---]nius, a veteran of the III Augusta legion, served 20 years, lived [---] years. [---]
EDCS-65600131.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary epitaph for a veteran of the III Augusta legion, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-65600133.translation: To the gods, the shades, sacred. Quintus Aemilius Saturninus, lived 20-29 years. He lies here.
EDCS-65600133.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Quintus Aemilius Saturninus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-65600134.translation: [To the gods, the shades], sacred. Appia Galla, lived 90 years. Her devoted children placed this. She lies here.
EDCS-65600134.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Appia Galla, set up by her children, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-65600135.translation: To the gods, the shades, sacred. Asclepiades lived [3] years. Asidonia Felicitas placed this for her devoted [---]rono. He lies here.
EDCS-65600135.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary epitaph for Asclepiades, set up by Asidonia Felicitas, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-65600136.translation: To the gods, the shades. Of Quintus Avii Quirina [---] lived 12 years. She lies here.
EDCS-65600136.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary epitaph for a female, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-65600137.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary epitaph for Aurelia Matita, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-65600138.translation: Dius Felix lived 6 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-65600138.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the life span and burial of Dius Felix.

EDCS-65600139.translation: Rogata lived 80 years. Her sons, Corneli Martialis and Apronianus, placed this for their pious mother. She is buried here.
EDCS-65600139.summary: This inscription records the burial of Rogata and is dedicated by her sons, Corneli Martialis and Apronianus.

EDCS-65600140.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Cossutia, daughter of Publius, Veneria, pious, lived 30 years; she is buried here. Lucius Sergius Sterceius placed this for his pious wife.
EDCS-65600140.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated by Lucius Sergius Sterceius to his pious wife, Cossutia Veneria.

EDCS-65600141.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Fabius [---] [---] erected [this monument]. He is buried here.
EDCS-65600141.summary: A fragmentary funerary inscription dedicated to the departed, mentioning Fabius and a monument erected by an unknown person.

EDCS-65600142.translation: Gavinnia Dorchas lived 16 years; her devoted sons erected this.
EDCS-65600142.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the life span of Gavinnia Dorchas, erected by her sons.

EDCS-65600143.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Geminia Spes lived 6 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-65600143.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the life span and burial of Geminia Spes.

EDCS-65600145.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Iulius Subitanus, a boy of good disposition, lived 12 years; Iulius Generosus erected this for his foster-son; he is buried here.
EDCS-65600145.summary: A funerary inscription recording the death of the young Iulius Subitanus, for whom Iulius Generosus erected the monument.

EDCS-65600146.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Iulia Concordia lived 17 years and 30 days; her son erected this out of devotion.
EDCS-65600146.summary: A funerary epitaph for Iulia Concordia, recording her age at death and erected by her son.

EDCS-65600147.translation: Martialis lived 3 years and 3 months; his pious father placed this for his most beloved son. He is buried here.
EDCS-65600147.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated by a grieving father to his young son, Martialis.

EDCS-65600148.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Aulus Numonius Rogatus lived 75 years; he is buried here; his sons erected this for their devoted father.
EDCS-65600148.summary: A funerary epitaph for Aulus Numonius Rogatus, recording his age at death and erected by his sons.

EDCS-65600149.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Publius Valerius Liberalis lived 30 years; he is buried here; his father erected this for his son.
EDCS-65600149.summary: A funerary epitaph for Publius Valerius Liberalis, recording his age at death and erected by his father.

EDCS-65600150.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Varius Restutus lived [---] years; he is buried here.
EDCS-65600150.summary: A fragmentary funerary epitaph for Varius Restutus, recording his burial.

EDCS-65600151.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Marcus Virtus Masi lived 29 years.
EDCS-65600151.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the age at death of Marcus Virtus Masi.

EDCS-65600152.translation: Primitivus placed this for his wife.
EDCS-65600152.summary: This is a brief funerary inscription indicating Primitivus dedicated a monument to his wife.

EDCS-65600153.translation: To the Divine Spirits, for Rusina Cisca, the best.
EDCS-65600153.summary: This is a dedication to the Divine Spirits for Rusina Cisca, likely a funerary monument.

EDCS-65600158.translation: To the departed spirits. Gaius Vinnius Trophimus, freedman of Gaius, lived 91 years. He rests here. Gaius Vinnius Servilius placed this for his devoted father.
EDCS-65600158.summary: This is a tombstone commemorating Gaius Vinnius Trophimus, who lived to be 91, and was set up by his son, Gaius Vinnius Servilius.

EDCS-65600160.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Frontia, pious, lived 30 years. Her sons erected this.
EDCS-65600160.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Frontia, erected by her sons.

EDCS-65600161.translation: To the departed spirits. Sallustina(?) lived 16 years. She rests here. Grata placed this for her sister.
EDCS-65600161.summary: This is a tombstone for Sallustina(?), who died at age 16, and was set up by her sister, Grata.

EDCS-65600162.translation: To the departed spirits. Aventius Protagoras lived 60 years. Asidonia Buntesia made this for a good man. He rests here.
EDCS-65600162.summary: This tombstone records the death of Aventius Protagoras at age 60 and was made by Asidonia Buntesia for him.

EDCS-65600163.translation: To the departed spirits. Adventus lived 70 years. His sons placed this for their devoted father. He rests here.
EDCS-65600163.summary: This tombstone commemorates Adventus, who lived to be 70, and was set up by his sons.

EDCS-65600164.translation: To the departed spirits. Quintus Aelius(?).
EDCS-65600164.summary: This is a fragment of a tombstone with the name Quintus Aelius(?).

EDCS-65600165.translation: To the departed spirits. Lucius Aelius Catullinus lived 50 years. He rests here.
EDCS-65600165.summary: This tombstone commemorates Lucius Aelius Catullinus, who lived to be 50 and rests here.

EDCS-65600166.translation: To the departed spirits. Arrius Avicius, son of Lucius, lived 27 years, as fate permitted. To the departed spirits. Aelius Comenialis lived [3] years.
EDCS-65600166.summary: This tombstone fragment records the death of Arrius Avicius at age 27 and also mentions Aelius Comenialis.

EDCS-65600167.translation: To the departed spirits. Carvilia Antonilla lived 87 years. Her sons placed this for their most rare mother. She rests here. To the departed spirits. Quintus Aelius Saturninus lived 90 years. His sons placed this for their most rare father. He rests here.
EDCS-65600167.summary: This tombstone records two burials: Carvilia Antonilla, who lived to 87 and was commemorated by her sons, and Quintus Aelius Saturninus, who lived to 90 and was also commemorated by his sons.

EDCS-65600168.translation: To the departed spirits. Aelia Ianuaria lived 28 years. Caninius Felix placed this for his devoted wife.
EDCS-65600168.summary: This tombstone records the death of Aelia Ianuaria at age 28 and was erected by her husband, Caninius Felix.

EDCS-65600171.translation: To the departed spirits. Aemilia Rogatina, devout, lived [3] years. She rests here. Aemilius Capito placed this for his daughter with his own money.
EDCS-65600171.summary: This tombstone commemorates Aemilia Rogatina, who died at age [3], and was set up by her father, Aemilius Capito.

EDCS-65600172.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Aeternius lived for 27 years and 6 months.
EDCS-65600172.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Aeternius, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-65600173.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Allia Rogatina lived for 27 years. Here lies Lucius Geminius Orfitianus.
EDCS-65600173.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan of Allia Rogatina and mentions Lucius Geminius Orfitianus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-65600174.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Marcus Antonius Baricio lived for 50 years. Here he lies. His dutiful sons placed this.
EDCS-65600174.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan of Marcus Antonius Baricio and states it was erected by his sons, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-65600175.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Marcus Antonius Fortunatus lived for [3] years. His son placed this. Here he lies.
EDCS-65600175.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan of Marcus Antonius Fortunatus and notes it was placed by his son, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-65600176.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Antonia Marciana lived for 20 years. Here she lies. Marianus placed this for his devoted wife.
EDCS-65600176.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan of Antonia Marciana and states it was erected by her husband, Marianus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-65600177.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Apria Maiga lived for 35 years. Though poor, she was a matron. Statilius Paternianus, her devoted husband, placed this. Here she lies.
EDCS-65600177.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan of Apria Maiga, describing her as a matron, and notes it was erected by her devoted husband, Statilius Paternianus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-65600178.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Nina Isperata lived for 65 years. His dutiful son placed this. Here she lies. // Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Apuleius Secundinus lived for 70 years. His dutiful son placed this for his father. [Here he lies].
EDCS-65600178.summary: This monument contains two funerary epitaphs, one for Nina Isperata and another for Apuleius Secundinus, likely erected by sons, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-65600180.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Arruntia Maior lived for 105 years. Her dutiful sons placed this for their mother. Here she lies.
EDCS-65600180.summary: This funerary epitaph records the very long lifespan of Arruntia Maior and states it was erected by her sons, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-65600181.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Asidonia Asiane lived for 45 years. Here she lies. Asidonius Facilis and Athena and A[---]danus made this for their dearest mother.
EDCS-65600181.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan of Asidonia Asiane and notes it was erected by her children, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-65600182.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Redducta Victoria lived for 35 years and 5 months. Asidonius Calvus placed this for his sister. Here she lies.
EDCS-65600182.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan of Redducta Victoria and states it was erected by her brother, Asidonius Calvus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-65600183.translation: To the departed spirits. Attia Marciana lived 50 years; here she lies. Modius Victoricus placed this for his most beloved wife.
EDCS-65600183.summary: This is a tombstone for Attia Marciana, set up by her husband Modius Victoricus, dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-65600184.translation: To the departed spirits. Augustica(?) lived for [3] years and [3] months; her dutiful children placed this.
EDCS-65600184.summary: This is a tombstone for Augustica (?), set up by her dutiful children, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-65600185.translation: To the departed spirits. Aurelia Victorina(?) the dutiful...
EDCS-65600185.summary: This is a fragmentary tombstone for Aurelia Victorina (?), likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-65600186.translation: Publius Baebidius Victor, son of Publius, of the tribe Quirina, dutiful, lived 35 years; here he lies. Quintus Geminius Secundus placed this for his best friend.
EDCS-65600186.summary: This is a tombstone for Publius Baebidius Victor, set up by his friend Quintus Geminius Secundus, dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-65600188.translation: To the departed spirits. Baebinia Donatula lived 57 years; her dutiful children placed this for their mother; here she lies.
EDCS-65600188.summary: This is a tombstone for Baebinia Donatula, set up by her dutiful children, dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-65600190.translation: To the departed spirits. Bucosus lived 21 years; here he lies. [---] placed this for his dutiful son.
EDCS-65600190.summary: This is a tombstone for Bucosus, set up by his father, dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-65600191.translation: To the departed spirits. Bolanius Liberalis lived 46 years...
EDCS-65600191.summary: This is a fragmentary tombstone for Bolanius Liberalis, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-65600192.translation: To the departed spirits. Caecilia Secundula, also known as Monnula, lived 17 years and 7 months; her dutiful mother placed this. To the departed spirits. Quintus Caecilius Secundianus lived 52 years. Gavia Septimina, his dutiful wife, placed this; here he lies.
EDCS-65600192.summary: This is a double tombstone recording the deaths of Caecilia Secundula (erected by her mother) and Quintus Caecilius Secundianus (erected by his wife), likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-65600193.summary: This is a fragmentary tombstone for a member of the Caecilius family, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-65600194.translation: To the departed spirits. Caecilia Donata lived [---]13 years...
EDCS-65600194.summary: This is a fragmentary tombstone for Caecilia Donata, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-65600195.translation: To the Divine Shades. Caecilia Iulla, pious, lived 18 years, 6 months, and 3 days. Caecilius Amandus, father, erected this for his pious daughter. She lies here.
EDCS-65600195.summary: A funerary epitaph for Caecilia Iulla, set up by her father, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-65600196.translation: To the Divine Shades. [Caecilia] Tertia lived 14 years. [Quintus] Caecilius Firmianus erected [this for his daughter]. She lies here. To the Divine Shades. Sacred. Caecilia Privata lived 27 years. She lies here. Quintus Caecilius Firmianus erected [this] for his pious wife.
EDCS-65600196.summary: A funerary inscription recording the deaths of two women, Caecilia Tertia and Caecilia Privata, both of whom were set up by a Quintus Caecilius Firmianus, likely a father and husband respectively, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-65600197.translation: To the Divine Shades. Sacred. Lucius Caelius Germanus lived 26 years. He lies here. Lucius Caelius [son's name?] erected this for his pious brother.
EDCS-65600197.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lucius Caelius Germanus, erected by his brother, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-65600198.translation: To the Divine Shades. Sacred. Titus Caelius Martialis lived 51 years. He lies here.
EDCS-65600198.summary: A funerary epitaph for Titus Caelius Martialis, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-65600199.translation: To the Divine Shades. Sacred. Caelia Euporia lived 38 years. She lies here. Caelius Praetor(?), erected this for his excellent wife.
EDCS-65600199.summary: A funerary epitaph for Caelia Euporia, erected by her husband, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-65600200.translation: [Name] lived 51 years, [duration] months. Caelia Tertulla, his wife, erected this for her deserving and pious husband.
EDCS-65600200.summary: A funerary epitaph for an unnamed man, erected by his wife Caelia Tertulla, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-65600201.translation: [Name] erected this for his father Caelis. He lies here.
EDCS-65600201.summary: A funerary epitaph for a father named Caelis, erected by his son, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-65600203.translation: To the Divine Shades. Sacred. Calventius Commodus lived 81 years.
EDCS-65600203.summary: A funerary epitaph for Calventius Commodus, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-65600205.translation: To the Divine Shades. Gaius Camurenus Saturninus, son of Gaius, of the Quirina tribe, lived 54 years. He lies here. [His son] Camurenus Saturninus erected this for his pious father.
EDCS-65600205.summary: A funerary epitaph for Gaius Camurenus Saturninus, erected by his son, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-65600207.translation: To the Divine Shades. Sacred. Titus Carmeius Nundinarius lived 11 years. He lies here. And Carmeia Augurina lived 9 years. She lies here. Carmeius Augurinus, father, erected this for his most pious children. To the Divine Shades. Sacred. Volussia Servilia lived 55 years. She lies here. Canneius Augurinus erected this for his dearest, most pious wife. To the Divine Shades. Sacred. Titus Carmeius Felix lived 87 years. He lies here. Carmeia Festa lived 75 years. She lies here. Carmeius Augurinus erected this for his most pious father and mother.
EDCS-65600207.summary: A complex funerary inscription recording the deaths and burials of multiple family members, including Titus Carmeius Nundinarius, Carmeia Augurina, Volussia Servilia, Titus Carmeius Felix, and Carmeia Festa, with epitaphs set up by Carmeius Augurinus, likely a father and husband, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-65600209.translation: Cata, daughter of Lucius, lived 10 years. She lies here.
EDCS-65600209.summary: A tombstone recording the death of a girl named Cata, who died at the age of ten.

EDCS-65600210.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Claudius Colonicus lived 75 years. He lies here. Domitia, his wife, erected this.
EDCS-65600210.summary: A funerary epitaph for Claudius Colonicus, who lived to 75, erected by his wife Domitia.

EDCS-65600211.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Titia Sallusa Candi[d]iana lived 23 years and 10 months. For my most dutiful daughter, she lies here. Gaius Titius Agrius Maximus, her father, erected this. Sacred to the departed spirits. Claudia Candida lived 59 years and 6 months. For my incomparable wife, an example of chastity, most lauded of matrons, she lies here. [Gaius Titius] Agrius Maximus, her husband, erected this.
EDCS-65600211.summary: This inscription is a double epitaph, commemorating both a daughter, Titia Sallusa Candi[d]iana, and her mother, Claudia Candida, both erected by the father and husband, Gaius Titius Agrius Maximus.

EDCS-65600212.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Claudia Tryphena lived 75 years. She lies here.
EDCS-65600212.summary: A funerary epitaph for Claudia Tryphena, who lived to 75.

EDCS-65600213.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Claudia [---] lived 44 years. She lies here. Clod[ius ---]anus for his wife, pious, modest, to whom faith, integrity, and freedom never failed; who lost her, lost [it?].
EDCS-65600213.summary: A funerary epitaph for a woman named Claudia, whose husband Clodius expresses his grief over her death and her virtues.

EDCS-65600214.translation: Estenia Paulina placed [this] for her husband. Sacred to the departed spirits. Clodius Crescentianus lived 63 years, more or less.
EDCS-65600214.summary: This monument records the death of Clodius Crescentianus, who lived approximately 63 years, and was set up by his wife Estenia Paulina.

EDCS-65600215.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Clodius Tracalus lived 19 years, 7 days, and 7 hours. For his excellent son, he lies here.
EDCS-65600215.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lucius Clodius Tracalus, who died at 19 years, 7 days, and 7 hours, erected by his father.

EDCS-65600216.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. For Cornelius Antinianus, dearest infant. Sacred to the departed spirits. Ulpia Sever[a] lived 33 years. She lies here.
EDCS-65600216.summary: This inscription is a double epitaph, one for a child named Cornelius Antinianus and another for Ulpia Severa, who died at 33.

EDCS-65600217.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Cornelius Felix lived 49 years. He lies here. Porcia Laeta [erected this?] for her excellent husband.
EDCS-65600217.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lucius Cornelius Felix, who lived to 49, likely erected by his wife Porcia Laeta.

EDCS-65600218.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Cornelia Dubitata lived 54 years and 3 months. She lies here. Caecilius Amandus erected this for his most pious wife.
EDCS-65600218.summary: A funerary epitaph for Cornelia Dubitata, who died at 54 years and 3 months, erected by her husband Caecilius Amandus.

EDCS-65600219.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Cornelia Extricata lived 22 years. Larnia Sal... her daughter placed [this]. She lies here.
EDCS-65600219.summary: A funerary epitaph for Cornelia Extricata, who lived 22 years, set up by her daughter, dated to the Imperial period.

EDCS-65600220.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Cornelia Felicitas lived 36 years, 10 months, and 17 days. Lucius Sittius Maritus placed [this] for his dearest wife. She lies here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius, her son, lived 30 days. His devoted father placed [this]. He lies here.
EDCS-65600220.summary: A double funerary epitaph recording the deaths of Cornelia Felicitas and her infant son Lucius, both set up by Lucius Sittius Maritus, dated to the Imperial period.

EDCS-65600221.translation: Marcus Decumus Capito lived 48 years. Manlia Victoria placed [this] for her husband.
EDCS-65600221.summary: A funerary epitaph for Marcus Decumus Capito, who lived 48 years, erected by his wife Manlia Victoria, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-65600222.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Deuterius lived 6 years, 7 months, and 19 days. He lies here. Iulius ..., Nice, and Cirus made [this] for their dearest foster-son.
EDCS-65600222.summary: A funerary epitaph for Deuterius, a child who lived 6 years, set up by his foster parents or guardians, dated to the Imperial period.

EDCS-65600223.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Publius Domitius lived 35 years. He lies here. Pursaccus placed [this] for his dearest brother.
EDCS-65600223.summary: A funerary epitaph for Publius Domitius, who lived 35 years, erected by his brother Pursaccus, dated to the Imperial period.

EDCS-65600224.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Aeternia Feculina lived 92 years. Cornelius Felix made [this] for her out of devotion. Sacred to the departed spirits. Domitius Felix lived 65 years. He lies here. Iulius Nundinarius, his son, placed [this] for his father.
EDCS-65600224.summary: A double funerary epitaph recording Aeternia Feculina and Domitius Felix, with Cornelius Felix and Iulius Nundinarius as dedicants, dated to the Imperial period.

EDCS-65600225.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Eventius lived 5 years. His devoted father placed [this]. He lies here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Eventius lived 2 years. His devoted father made [this].
EDCS-65600225.summary: A double funerary epitaph for a child named Eventius, who died twice according to the text, with his devoted father as the dedicant, dated to the Imperial period.

EDCS-65600226.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus Fabius Pirforus lived 81 years. He lies here. His sons placed [this] for their father.
EDCS-65600226.summary: A funerary epitaph for Quintus Fabius Pirforus, who lived 81 years, erected by his sons, dated to the Imperial period.

EDCS-65600227.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Fabia Secundula lived 50 years. Iunius Fabianus, her devoted son, placed [this].
EDCS-65600227.summary: A funerary epitaph for Fabia Secundula, who lived 50 years, erected by her devoted son, dated to the Imperial period.

EDCS-65600228.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Gaius Fa[...]/hospes(?) lived 6 years. He lies here.
EDCS-65600228.summary: A funerary epitaph for Gaius Fa[...]/hospes(?), a child who lived 6 years, dated to the Imperial period.

EDCS-65600229.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Flaminius Castulus lived 40 years. To the Spirits of the Departed. Geminia Maxima lived... years. To the Spirits of the Departed. Flaminia Estricatula lived 1 year and 7 days. Vibia Urbana(?)...
EDCS-65600229.summary: This fragmentary inscription appears to contain three separate funerary notices for individuals named Flaminius Castulus, Geminia Maxima, and Flaminia Estricatula, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-65600230.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. [A name missing] Flamon lived 6 years, 3 months, and 6 days. [His parents] lovingly set this up.
EDCS-65600230.summary: This funerary inscription, likely from the Roman Imperial period, records the death of a child named Flamon at the age of 6 years and 12 days, set up by his parents.

EDCS-65600231.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Flavius Conventalis lived 36 years and is laid to rest here. To the Spirits of the Departed. Magni(a) Voluptas lived 28 years and is laid to rest here. To the Spirits of the Departed. Flavia Victoria lived 7 years, 3 months, and is laid to rest here. To the Spirits of the Departed. Flavius Secundus lived 13 years, 3 months, and is laid to rest here; his uncles set this up.
EDCS-65600231.summary: This inscription contains four separate funerary notices for Flavius Conventalis, Magni(a) Voluptas, Flavia Victoria, and Flavius Secundus, all from the Roman Imperial period, with two of the deceased having their monuments erected by relatives.

EDCS-65600232.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Titus Flavius Fronto lived 2 years and is laid to rest here. Quintus Flavius Felix, the father, set this up.
EDCS-65600232.summary: This is a funerary inscription from the Roman Imperial period recording the death of Titus Flavius Fronto at the age of 2, with his father Quintus Flavius Felix as the dedicator.

EDCS-65600233.translation: Flavius Valerius Falacrius lived 33 years and 2 months and is buried here.
EDCS-65600233.summary: This is a funerary inscription from the Roman Imperial period recording the life and burial of Flavius Valerius Falacrius.

EDCS-65600234.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Flavius Romanus lived 29 years. Fidus in friendship always without [illegible] blood and [illegible] mother [illegible] ... Junius ... [illegible] ... Here he rests. His brother...
EDCS-65600234.summary: This damaged funerary inscription from the Roman Imperial period commemorates Flavius Romanus, who died at 29, and mentions his brother and mother.

EDCS-65600235.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Lucius Flavius Saturninus lived 11 years and 7 months and is laid to rest here. Liberalis made [this] for his good son(?).
EDCS-65600235.summary: This funerary inscription from the Roman Imperial period records the death of Lucius Flavius Saturninus at age 11 years and 7 months, with a dedication likely from his son.

EDCS-65600236.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Lucius Flavius Urbanianus the younger lived 1 year and 7 months. Flavius Urbanianus the father set [this] up for his son; here he rests.
EDCS-65600236.summary: This funerary inscription from the Roman Imperial period records the death of Lucius Flavius Urbanianus the younger at 1 year and 7 months, with his father Flavius Urbanianus as the dedicator.

EDCS-65600238.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Fortitosa Peculiaris, daughter, lived 12 years; her dearest mother, two sisters, and four brothers set up the tomb out of piety; here she rests.
EDCS-65600238.summary: This funerary inscription from the Roman Imperial period records the death of Fortitosa Peculiaris at age 12, with the monument erected by her mother and siblings.

EDCS-65600239.summary: This fragmentary inscription simply records the name Fortunatus.

EDCS-65600240.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Frumentia, daughter of Frumentius, lived 9 years and 1 month; here she rests.
EDCS-65600240.summary: This funerary inscription from the Roman Imperial period records the death of Frumentia at age 9 years and 1 month, likely set up by her family.

EDCS-65600242.translation: To the gods of the underworld. Galla lived for 35 years, 6 months, and 10 days. She rests here. Liberalis placed this for his devoted wife.
EDCS-65600242.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the life span of Galla and erected by her husband, Liberalis.

EDCS-65600243.translation: Gargilia Spes, daughter of Caius, also called Daia Flavia, lived for 2 years. She rests here. Rumi­cilia Faustina took care of the burial.
EDCS-65600243.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for the infant Gargilia Spes, with care of the burial managed by Rumi­cilia Faustina.

EDCS-65600244.translation: To the gods of the underworld. Lucius Geminius... lived for 74 years. Quintus Geminius Martialis made this for his father. He rests here.
EDCS-65600244.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Geminius, erected by his son Quintus Geminius Martialis.

EDCS-65600245.translation: Felix Geminius, son of Lucius, from the Arni region, born at Carthage.
EDCS-65600245.summary: This is a dedication or epitaph for Felix Geminius, identifying his parentage and origin.

EDCS-65600246.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Caius Geminius Liberalis lived 60 years. Geminius Catlus, his son, erected this to his most pious father.
EDCS-65600246.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Caius Geminius Liberalis, erected by his son.

EDCS-65600247.translation: To the gods of the underworld. Geminia Secundula lived for 32 years. She rests here. Papius Servilianus placed this for his devoted wife.
EDCS-65600247.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Geminia Secundula, erected by her husband Papius Servilianus.

EDCS-65600248.translation: ... Nabor lived for 21 years, 4 months, and 26 days. He rests here... lived for 60... Geminius(?) N... dearest(?).
EDCS-65600248.summary: This fragmented funerary epitaph records the lifespan of Nabor and possibly part of another inscription for a Geminius.

EDCS-65600249.translation: To the gods of the underworld. Gentia Tertullica lived for 19 years. She rests here. Gentius Victorius placed this for his devoted daughter.
EDCS-65600249.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Gentia Tertullica, erected by her father Gentius Victorius.

EDCS-65600250.translation: To the gods of the underworld. Golaia lived for 10 years... She rests here. Her mother placed this.
EDCS-65600250.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Golaia, erected by her mother.

EDCS-65600251.translation: To the gods of the underworld. Quintus Helvius Iovinus...
EDCS-65600251.summary: This is the beginning of a funerary epitaph for Quintus Helvius Iovinus.

EDCS-65600253.translation: To the gods of the underworld. Herennius Victorianus, their foster child, lived for 10 years. He rests here. // To the gods of the underworld. Titus Herennius Victor lived for 47 years, 10 months, and 12 days. He rests here. Considia Victoria placed this for her devoted husband.
EDCS-65600253.summary: This inscription records two funerary epitaphs: one for Herennius Victorianus, likely a foster child, and another for Titus Herennius Victor, erected by his wife Considia Victoria.

EDCS-65600255.translation: To the gods of the underworld. Hail, Hon­o­ra­tus! Why did you live so briefly after fate had decreed...?
EDCS-65600255.summary: This is a funerary epitaph, likely addressed to Hon­o­ra­tus, questioning his short life.

EDCS-65600256.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Agria Fortunata lived 116 years; her grandchildren and son-in-law, recognizing her merits, set this up; she lies here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Gaius Hortensius Dativus lived 40 years and 4 months; his devoted mother set this up. Sacred to the departed spirits. Gaius Hortensius Barigbal lived 67 years; his devoted son and wife set this up.
EDCS-65600256.summary: This is a funerary monument with three separate inscriptions commemorating Agria Fortunata, Gaius Hortensius Dativus, and Gaius Hortensius Barigbal, detailing their ages and who erected the memorials.

EDCS-65600257.translation: [?]lius, sacred to the departed spirits. Kalvaria lived 87 years and 5 hours for her parents. Hor() Silvana, his wife, lived 72 years and 2 hours.
EDCS-65600257.summary: This funerary inscription records the ages of Kalvaria and his wife Hor() Silvana, with Kalvaria's memorial erected for his parents.

EDCS-65600258.translation: Gaius Julius Donatus lived 90 years. Julius Donatus set this up for his devoted father. He lies here.
EDCS-65600258.summary: This is a funerary inscription where Gaius Julius Donatus' son, also named Julius Donatus, erected a memorial for his father who lived 90 years.

EDCS-65600259.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Gaius Julius Fortunatus lived [---] years.
EDCS-65600259.summary: This is a fragment of a funerary inscription for Gaius Julius Fortunatus, stating his name and that he lived for an unspecified number of years.

EDCS-65600260.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Julius Hilarius [---].
EDCS-65600260.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription for Julius Hilarius.

EDCS-65600261.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Gaius Julius Saturninus lived 25 years and six months. His mother set this up.
EDCS-65600261.summary: This funerary inscription records that Gaius Julius Saturninus lived 25 years and six months, and his mother erected the monument.

EDCS-65600262.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Gaius Julius Silvinus lived 40 years. He lies here. Popilia Floria set this up for her devoted husband.
EDCS-65600262.summary: This funerary inscription states that Gaius Julius Silvinus lived 40 years and was commemorated by his wife, Popilia Floria.

EDCS-65600263.translation: This is the eternal home. Julius Trifolium made for himself during his lifetime, who lived as many years as he could, not as many as he wanted. He lies here. This is the eternal home. Julia Victoria made for herself during her lifetime, who lived as many years as she could, not as many as she wanted. She lies here.
EDCS-65600263.summary: This inscription consists of two parallel texts for Julius Trifolium and Julia Victoria, describing the eternal homes they built for themselves and reflecting philosophically on the duration of their lives.

EDCS-65600264.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus Julius Tutocosus lived [---]17 years. He set this up for himself during his lifetime.
EDCS-65600264.summary: This funerary inscription records that Quintus Julius Tutocosus lived 17 years and set up the monument for himself during his lifetime.

EDCS-65600265.translation: He lies here. Gaius Julius Felix set this up for his devoted son. He lived 8 years. Gaius Julius Felix, the father, set this up for his devoted daughter.
EDCS-65600265.summary: This funerary monument contains two parts: one dedicated by Gaius Julius Felix to his son who lived 8 years, and another dedicated by the same father to his daughter.

EDCS-65600267.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Iulia Primitiva lived 70 years. She lies buried here. Antonia Rogata placed this for her most dutiful mother.
EDCS-65600267.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Iulia Primitiva, with a dedication by her daughter Antonia Rogata, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-65600268.translation: Iulia Rogata, daughter of Marcus, lived [about] 34 years. She lies buried here.
EDCS-65600268.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Iulia Rogata, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-65600270.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Quintus Junius Ingenuus lived 40 years. He lies buried here. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Iunia Sisso[..] lived 5 years. She lies buried here. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Quintus Junius Mauricius lived 2 years. He lies buried here. Viria Romana placed this for her husband and sons.
EDCS-65600270.summary: A complex funerary monument recording the deaths of at least three individuals, with a separate dedication by Viria Romana for her family, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-65600271.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Lucius Labienus Saturus lived 35 years. He lies buried here. Iulia Pupa placed this for her husband out of devotion.
EDCS-65600271.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Lucius Labienus Saturus, with a dedication by his wife Iulia Pupa, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-65600272.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Laelius Maximus lived 26 years and 48 days. He lies buried here. His mother placed this for her most dutiful and dearest son.
EDCS-65600272.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Laelius Maximus, with a dedication by his mother, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-65600275.translation: son of Caius Lucilius Faustus, slave, lived for...
