EDCS-65600275.summary: This fragmentary inscription records the name and lineage of an individual who was a slave.

EDCS-65600276.translation: [..] lived [about] 30 years. She lies buried here. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Gaius Lucretius Severus lived 45 years. He lies buried here.
EDCS-65600276.summary: A fragmented funerary epitaph, with the legible portion recording the death of Gaius Lucretius Severus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-65600277.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Antonia Fortunata lived 60 years. She lies buried here. Her husband [dedicated this] for his wife. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Quintus Maevius Heros lived 45 years and 2 months. He lies buried here. Maevius Speratus placed this for his son. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Maevia Secunda lived 33 years. She lies buried here. Her dutiful father placed this for his dutiful daughter. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Lucius Maevius Aeros lived 114 years. He lies buried here. Lucius Maevius Speratus placed this for his father.
EDCS-65600277.summary: A complex funerary monument recording the deaths of at least four individuals, with dedications by family members, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-65600278.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Lucius Mevius Martialis Nepos, son of Lucius, of the Quirina tribe, lived 50 years and 7 months. He lies buried here. Cocceia Fortunata placed this for her dutiful son.
EDCS-65600278.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Lucius Mevius Martialis Nepos, with a dedication by his mother Cocceia Fortunata, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-65600279.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Mevius Rusticus lived [about] 11 months. He lies buried here. Mevius Victor placed this for his dutiful son.
EDCS-65600279.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Mevius Rusticus, with a dedication by his father Mevius Victor, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-65600280.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Mevia Paula, daughter of Publius, lived 60 years. She lies buried here.
EDCS-65600280.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Mevia Paula, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-65600281.translation: "To the departed spirits. Mevia Rufina, daughter of Caius, lived 68 years and is buried here. Cornelia Marcella, her daughter, placed this for her pious mother."
EDCS-65600281.summary: A funerary epitaph for Mevia Rufina, who lived 68 years, set up by her daughter Cornelia Marcella, likely dating to the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-65600282.translation: "To the departed spirits. Mevia Veneria lived 35 years. Rutillus placed this for his devoted daughter. She is buried here. // To the departed spirits. Mevia Novella lived 71 years. Rutillus placed this for his devoted wife. She is buried here."
EDCS-65600282.summary: A double funerary epitaph recording Mevia Veneria, who lived 35 years and was placed by Rutillus, and Mevia Novella, who lived 71 years and was also placed by Rutillus, likely dating to the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-65600283.translation: "Abaci I. To the departed spirits. Caius Magnius Felix Ianuarius lived 3 months and is buried here. Lampadarius and Aquilina placed this for their son."
EDCS-65600283.summary: A funerary epitaph for Caius Magnius Felix Ianuarius, who lived 3 months, set up by his parents Lampadarius and Aquilina, likely dating to the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-65600284.translation: "To the departed spirits. Lucius Magnius Saturninus lived 12 years and 2 months and is here. Magnius, his father, placed this for his devoted son."
EDCS-65600284.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lucius Magnius Saturninus, who lived 12 years and 2 months, set up by his father Magnius, likely dating to the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-65600285.translation: "To the departed spirits. Magnia Quinta, a holy woman, lived 25 years and [3] days and is buried here. // To the departed spirits. Lucius Magnius Murena lived 103 years, 2 months, and 4 days and is buried here. Quintus Magnius Rufinus Fortunatus placed this for his most excellent father."
EDCS-65600285.summary: A double funerary epitaph recording Magnia Quinta, who lived 25 years, and Lucius Magnius Murena, who lived 103 years, the latter set up by his son Quintus Magnius Rufinus Fortunatus, likely dating to the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-65600286.translation: "To the departed spirits. Magnia Successa lived 81 years. Her devoted sons placed this."
EDCS-65600286.summary: A funerary epitaph for Magnia Successa, who lived 81 years, set up by her devoted sons, likely dating to the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-65600287.translation: "To the departed spirits. M[...ilia] Optata, pious, lived 66 years. Aemilius Capito placed this [for her]. She is buried here."
EDCS-65600287.summary: A funerary epitaph for M[...ilia] Optata, who lived 66 years, set up by Aemilius Capito, likely dating to the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-65600288.translation: "To the departed spirits. Publius Marcius Sillanus lived 30 years."
EDCS-65600288.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Publius Marcius Sillanus, who lived 30 years, likely dating to the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-65600289.translation: "To the departed spirits. Publius Mar[cius Ian]uarius."
EDCS-65600289.summary: A fragmentary funerary epitaph for Publius Mar[cius Ian]uarius, likely dating to the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-65600290.translation: "To the departed spirits. Maria Faustina lived 75 years and is buried here. Cornia Faustina placed this for her pious grandmother."
EDCS-65600290.summary: A funerary epitaph for Maria Faustina, who lived 75 years, set up by her granddaughter Cornia Faustina, likely dating to the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-65600291.translation: To the Infernal Gods. Silvanus (son of) Mart(a), his good wife, daughter of Marcus. Lived X years, V months. Matu[...]
EDCS-65600291.summary: This epitaph, dedicated to the Infernal Gods, records the death of Marta, wife of Silvanus, and specifies her lifespan.

EDCS-65600292.translation: Sacred to the Infernal Gods. Merula lived XXXVI years; she lies here. Marcus Flavius Secundus placed this for his devout wife.
EDCS-65600292.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to the Infernal Gods and records the death of Merula, with her husband Marcus Flavius Secundus erecting the monument.

EDCS-65600293.translation: Victorius Felix lived LXV years and IIII months. Lucius Minucius Fortis lived LXXV years.
EDCS-65600293.summary: This inscription records the lives of two individuals, Victorius Felix and Lucius Minucius Fortis, likely on a shared funerary monument.

EDCS-65600294.translation: Sacred to the Infernal Gods. Munatia lived XLV years; she lies here. Valerianus placed this.
EDCS-65600294.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to the Infernal Gods and records the life and burial of Munatia, with Valerianus identified as the erector.

EDCS-65600295.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Nerutia, daughter of Publius, pious, lived 75 years. Baebius Novellus, her son-in-law, and Nerutia Eupolis, erected this to their most pious mother.
EDCS-65600295.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Nerutia Pia, erected by her son-in-law and daughter.

EDCS-65600297.translation: [...] he lies here. Marcus Nonius, son, placed this for his devoted father.
EDCS-65600297.summary: This funerary inscription records Marcus Nonius placing a monument for his devoted father.

EDCS-65600298.translation: Sacred to the Infernal Gods. Quintus Octavius Antonianus lived XXIII years; he lies here. Octavius made this for his devoted father.
EDCS-65600298.summary: This funerary inscription honors Quintus Octavius Antonianus, who lived XXIII years, and was made by his father, also named Octavius.

EDCS-65600299.translation: Sacred to the Infernal Gods. Quintus Octavius Magnus lived II years; his devout mother placed this. Sacred to the Infernal Gods. Quintus Octavius Magnus lived XXXVI years; his devout wife placed this. He lies here.
EDCS-65600299.summary: This inscription appears to be a funerary monument with two separate dedications for individuals named Quintus Octavius Magnus, one by his mother and another by his wife.

EDCS-65600301.translation: To the Infernal Gods. Publius Ofillius Processus lived [...] years
EDCS-65600301.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to the Infernal Gods and records the name and lifespan of Publius Ofillius Processus.

EDCS-65600302.translation: To the Infernal Gods. For Aulus Orbi Saturnini, son of Lucius, of the Quirina tribe. [---] Orbiani. lived [...] years
EDCS-65600302.summary: This funerary inscription, dedicated to the Infernal Gods, names Aulus Orbi Saturnini and possibly Orbiani, noting their tribal affiliation and lifespan.

EDCS-65600303.translation: To the Infernal Gods. For Orbia Paulina, his most virtuous wife, daughter of Marcus Ulpius Alexander, who lived XX years, X months. She lies here.
EDCS-65600303.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to the Infernal Gods for Orbia Paulina, wife of Marcus Ulpius Alexander, noting her age and burial.

EDCS-65600304.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Otacilia Quartilla lived eighteen years; she rests here.
EDCS-65600304.summary: A tombstone recording the death of Otacilia Quartilla at age 18, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-65600305.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Asinia Surisca, dutiful, lived thirty-five years; she rests here. Papirius Bassus. Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Quintus Papirius Bassus lived forty years; he rests here. Parents and Fortunata placed (this).
EDCS-65600305.summary: A funerary monument commemorating Asinia Surisca (died aged 35) and Quintus Papirius Bassus (died aged 40), erected by their parents and Fortunata, likely Roman Imperial.

EDCS-65600306.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Maria Faustina lived ninety years; she rests here. Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Quintus Papirius Victor lived eighty years; he rests here. His sons placed (this) for their dutiful father.
EDCS-65600306.summary: A funerary monument for Maria Faustina (died aged 90) and Quintus Papirius Victor (died aged 80), erected by the latter's sons, likely Roman Imperial.

EDCS-65600308.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Percennius Marcianus lived [age illegible]; he rests here. [Illegible text] placed (this) for his son.
EDCS-65600308.summary: A partially preserved tombstone recording Percennius Marcianus, with a dedication by his son, likely Roman Imperial.

EDCS-65600309.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Gaius Petilius Restutus lived fifty years. His wife placed (this) for [her dutiful husband?].
EDCS-65600309.summary: A funerary inscription for Gaius Petilius Restutus, who lived 50 years, with a partial dedication by his wife, likely Roman Imperial.

EDCS-65600310.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Petronia Honorata lived fifty years; she rests here. Her dutiful sons placed (this) for their pious mother. Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Gaius Petronius Antigonus lived sixty years; he rests here. His sons for their most dutiful father, outstanding in his devotion to his children. May your bones rest well. May the earth lie lightly upon you.
EDCS-65600310.summary: A double tombstone commemorating Petronia Honorata (died aged 50) and Gaius Petronius Antigonus (died aged 60), erected by their sons, likely Roman Imperial.

EDCS-65600313.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. [Illegible name] Phonicus lived thirty-five years. Hellen() his daughter.
EDCS-65600313.summary: A fragmented tombstone recording the death of Phonicus at age 35, with a dedication by his daughter Hellen(), likely Roman Imperial.

EDCS-65600314.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Septimia Ingenua lived seventy-six years; she rests here. Gaius Pompeius Faustus placed (this) for his most dutiful mother. Gaius Pompeius Simplicus, a man of rare innocence, lived forty-two years; he rests here. Septimia Ingenua his wife and Pompeius Faustus his son placed (this) for their parent because of his outstanding kindness.
EDCS-65600314.summary: A complex funerary monument for Septimia Ingenua (died aged 76) and her son Gaius Pompeius Simplicus (died aged 42), erected by the surviving son and wife, likely Roman Imperial.

EDCS-65600315.translation: [Illegible text] he rests here. Pompeia Draca lived twenty-five years; she rests here.
EDCS-65600315.summary: A partial tombstone recording the death of Pompeia Draca at age 25, likely Roman Imperial.

EDCS-65600316.translation: Pompeia Rogata, dutiful, lived seventy years; she rests here.
EDCS-65600316.summary: A tombstone recording the death of Pompeia Rogata at age 70, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-65600317.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Pompeia lived for 13 years and 4 months; she rests here. Fructosa placed this for her daughter.
EDCS-65600317.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Pompeia, who died at age 13 years and 4 months, set up by her daughter Fructosa, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-65600318.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Caius Pomponius Victor lived 27 years and 2 months. Caius Pomponius Capriolus erected this to his dearest son. Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Caius Pomponius Capriolus lived 70 years. Aeterna Cefona, his wife, erected this to her husband. Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Caius Pomponius Pusinnus lived 22 years and 4 months. Caius Pomponius Capriolus erected this to his dearest son.
EDCS-65600318.summary: This is a complex funerary monument that records the deaths and dedications for three individuals: Caius Pomponius Victor, Caius Pomponius Capriolus, and Caius Pomponius Pusinnus, with Capriolus appearing as both a deceased and a dedicator.

EDCS-65600320.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Postumius Festus lived for 70 years; he rests here. His sons made this tomb for their dearest father.
EDCS-65600320.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Postumius Festus, who died at age 70, and records that his sons erected the tomb, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-65600321.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Postumia Buntesia lived for 60 years; she rests here. Her dearest daughter placed this.
EDCS-65600321.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Postumia Buntesia, who died at age 60, set up by her daughter, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-65600322.translation: Lived for 90 years; she rests here. Postumia Laeta placed this for her pious mother-in-law.
EDCS-65600322.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for an unnamed woman who lived to 90, set up by her mother-in-law Postumia Laeta, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-65600323.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Prescenius Sorex lived for 68 years; his most beloved son placed this. He rests here. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Prescenius Fortunatus lived for 65 years; he placed this for himself while alive. He rests here.
EDCS-65600323.summary: This is a double funerary epitaph recording two individuals named Prescenius: Sorex, for whom his son erected a monument, and Fortunatus, who set up his own tomb while alive; both likely date to the Imperial period.

EDCS-65600324.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Aurelia Dativa lived for 81 years; she rests here. Racilius Neptunalis placed this for his pious mother. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Quintus Racilius Tibullus lived for 93 years; he rests here. Racilius Neptunalis placed this for his pious father.
EDCS-65600324.summary: This is a double funerary epitaph recording Aurelia Dativa, set up by her son Racilius Neptunalis, and Quintus Racilius Tibullus, also set up by his son Racilius Neptunalis, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-65600325.translation: To the departed spirits. A monument for Roscia Victoria, placed. She lived for 60 years; she rests here.
EDCS-65600325.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Roscia Victoria, who lived to 60, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-65600327.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Securus lived for 11 years. His parents [placed this] for their son. He rests here.
EDCS-65600327.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary epitaph for Securus, who died at age 11, set up by his parents, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-65600328.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Sempronius Dubitatus lived for 100 years.
EDCS-65600328.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary epitaph for Sempronius Dubitatus, who lived to 100 years, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-65600330.translation: Lived for 51 years; his wife and his pious sons made [this]. They rest here. And for Septimius, a son, [he] lived for 11 years.
EDCS-65600330.summary: This is a double funerary epitaph recording a man who lived 51 years and his son Septimius who lived 11 years, both erected by the wife and sons, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-65600331.translation: To the departed spirits. Marcus Servilius Pacatus lived many years; he is buried here. Fruentius placed this for his devoted father.
EDCS-65600331.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Marcus Servilius Pacatus, with the monument dedicated by his son Fruentius, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-65600332.translation: To the departed spirits. Sittius Aectus, his grandson, lived 8 years, 2 months, 21 days. To the departed spirits. Sittia Aecta lived 75 years.
EDCS-65600332.summary: This epitaph commemorates two individuals, Sittius Aectus (a child) and Sittia Aecta (an adult), likely related and buried together, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-65600333.translation: To the departed spirits. Sittia Gemellina lived 5 years. To the departed spirits. Valeria Victorilla lived 27 years. Marcus Sittius [---]nalis placed this for his wife [---].
EDCS-65600333.summary: This funerary inscription records the deaths of Sittia Gemellina and Valeria Victorilla, with the latter’s monument erected by her husband Marcus Sittius [---]nalis, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-65600334.translation: To the departed spirits. Spesina lived 25 years, 5 months. Sambucius placed this for his most beloved wife.
EDCS-65600334.summary: This funerary monument records the life of Spesina and was dedicated by her husband Sambucius, likely dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-65600335.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that likely begins with a personal name and parentage.

EDCS-65600336.translation: To the departed spirits. Stenia Severa lived 40 years; she is buried here. Allius Fortunatus placed this for his devoted wife.
EDCS-65600336.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Stenia Severa, with the monument erected by her husband Allius Fortunatus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-65600337.translation: To the departed spirits. Tadius Epicte tus lived 46 years; he is buried here. Lucius Tadius Epagatus placed this for his devoted brother.
EDCS-65600337.summary: This funerary monument commemorates Tadius Epicte tus and was erected by his brother Lucius Tadius Epagatus, likely dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-65600338.translation: To the departed spirits. Terentius Augustalis lived 30 years. His devoted mother placed this; he is buried here.
EDCS-65600338.summary: This funerary inscription records the life of Terentius Augustalis, with the monument erected by his mother, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-65600339.translation: Tillia Primulla, daughter of Nymphodotus, lived 50 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-65600339.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Tillia Primulla, daughter of Nymphodotus, likely dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-65600340.translation: To the departed spirits. Titinius Victor lived 70 years. Titinius Victoricus placed this for his devoted father; he is buried here. To the departed spirits. Sallustia Quirilla lived 60 years. Titinius Victoricus placed this for his devoted mother; she is buried here. To the departed spirits. Aemilia Maxima lived 50 years. Iulia Felicitas placed this for her devoted mother; she is buried here. To the departed spirits. Aemilia Castula lived 6 years. Iulia Felicitas placed this for her devoted sister; she is buried here. To the departed spirits. Titinius Victoricus lived 5 years, 10 months. His devoted father placed this; he is buried here. To the departed spirits. Titinius Donatus lived two years. His father placed this for his son; he is buried here.
EDCS-65600340.summary: This is a multi-part funerary monument recording the lives and burials of at least five individuals from the Titinius and Aemilia families, likely dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-65600341.translation: To the departed spirits. Caius Trebbins Felix lived 31 years; he is buried here. Aemilia Amata, his devoted wife, [placed this] for her husband.
EDCS-65600341.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Caius Trebbins Felix, with the monument erected by his wife Aemilia Amata, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-65600342.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Marcus Tullius Aquilinus lived for 15 years. He lies here.
EDCS-65600342.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Marcus Tullius Aquilinus at the age of 15, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-65600343.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Turrania Veneria Augustia lived for one year and 3 months. She lies here. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Turranius Sucessus lived for 7 months. Turranius Nasir lived for 14 years. P. T. A. VIII. He lies here. Turranius Saturnius and Valeria Donata, parents, set [this up].
EDCS-65600343.summary: A complex funerary monument recording the deaths of Turrania Veneria Augustia (1 year, 3 months), Turranius Sucessus (7 months), and Turranius Nasir (14 years), with parents Turranius Saturnius and Valeria Donata setting up the monument, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-65600344.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Publius Valerius Felix lies here. He lived for 18 years. Publius Valerius Fortunatus, his father, set this up for his dutiful son. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Iulia Secundula lies here. She lived for 30 years. Publius Valerius Fortunatus set this up for his most dutiful wife. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Publius Valerius Fortunatus, son of Publius, of the Quirina tribe, lived for 87 years. He lies here. His sons set this up for their dutiful father.
EDCS-65600344.summary: A family funerary monument commemorating three individuals: Publius Valerius Felix (18), his wife Iulia Secundula (30), and the patriarch Publius Valerius Fortunatus (87), likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-65600345.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Valerius Restutus lived for 32 years. He lies here. For a good friend.
EDCS-65600345.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Valerius Restutus at the age of 32, set up by a friend, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-65600346.translation: Lucius Valerius Vitalis, son of Lucius, lies here. Lucius Valerius, his father (?), made [this].
EDCS-65600346.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lucius Valerius Vitalis, with his father Lucius mentioned as the maker, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-65600347.translation: Here lies Valeria. Her son erected [this].
EDCS-65600347.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Valeria, erected by her son.

EDCS-65600348.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Varius Delphicus lived for 48 years. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Pompeia Calla lived for 94 years. A son set this up for his parents. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Varia Prisca lived for 65 years. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Septiminius Aprilis lived for 53 years.
EDCS-65600348.summary: A funerary monument recording the deaths of four individuals: Varius Delphicus (48), Pompeia Calla (94), Varia Prisca (65), and Septiminius Aprilis (53), with a son dedicating the monument to his parents, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-65600349.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Publius Vereius Sebosus lived for 60 years. Vereius Felix set this up for his son. He lies here.
EDCS-65600349.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Publius Vereius Sebosus at the age of 60, set up by his son Vereius Felix, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-65600350.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Victorina lived for 7 years and 7 months. She lies here. Dutiful parents made [this] for their daughter. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. [Name illegible] lived for 4 years, 5 months, and 15 days. She lies here. Dutiful parents made [this] for their daughter.
EDCS-65600350.summary: A funerary monument for two young girls, Victorina (7 years, 7 months) and another unnamed child (4 years, 5 months, 15 days), both with epitaphs set up by their devoted parents, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-65600351.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Saturus lived for 35 years and 10 months. He lies here. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Vinnius Felix lived for 7 years, 8 months, and 20 days. He lies here. His mother set [this] up for her son.
EDCS-65600351.summary: A funerary monument for two individuals: Saturus (35 years, 10 months) and Vinnius Felix (7 years, 8 months, 20 days), with the latter's epitaph set up by his mother, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-65600352.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Gaius Surus Vinius Honoratus lived for 33 years, 11 months, and 6 days. Helvia Fortunata set [this] up for her dearest husband. He lies here.
EDCS-65600352.summary: A funerary epitaph for Gaius Surus Vinius Honoratus, who lived 33 years, 11 months, and 6 days, dedicated by his wife Helvia Fortunata, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-65600353.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Vinnia Bocchis lived for sixteen years; she lies here. Vinnia Urbana, her most dutiful mother, placed this for her most dutiful daughter.
EDCS-65600353.summary: A funerary epitaph for Vinnia Bocchis, who died at sixteen, set up by her mother, Vinnia Urbana.

EDCS-65600354.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Volussena Salsula lived for eighty-five years; she lies here.
EDCS-65600354.summary: A funerary epitaph for Volussena Salsula, who died at eighty-five.

EDCS-65600357.translation: She lies here. [Son]inus and Maximianus placed this for their pious mother.
EDCS-65600357.summary: A funerary epitaph where sons named Maximianus and possibly Soninus placed a monument for their mother.

EDCS-65600358.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Nilus.

EDCS-65600360.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Usar N is placed here. A son placed this for his father.
EDCS-65600360.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by a son for his deceased father.

EDCS-65600361.translation: Ius and Istania made this for their grandson.
EDCS-65600361.summary: This inscription records that Ius and Istania commissioned a monument for their grandson.

EDCS-65600362.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Sextus.
EDCS-65600362.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Sextus.

EDCS-65600364.translation: Lived [X] years. Placed here. A wife placed this for her devoted husband.
EDCS-65600364.summary: This is a funerary inscription by a wife for her husband.

EDCS-65600367.translation: Lived [X] years. Placed here. For his dearest daughter.
EDCS-65600367.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to a daughter.

EDCS-65600368.summary: This inscription records that sons set up a monument.

EDCS-65700924.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Lucius Nonius Fortunatus lived for 47 years. Volusena Eufrosina placed this for her devoted husband. He is placed here.
EDCS-65700924.summary: This is a funerary inscription by a wife, Volusena Eufrosina, for her husband Lucius Nonius Fortunatus, who lived to be 47.

EDCS-66800027.summary: This inscription lists three personal names, possibly indicating ownership or recipients of an unspecified dedication.

EDCS-67200414.translation: Of Marcellus, a most distinguished man.
EDCS-67200414.summary: This inscription refers to a man named Marcellus, described as 'most distinguished'.

EDCS-67200621.translation: I, Doulketes, donor and Aesonian horseman by birth, have dedicated these things. May the god know that he keeps himself favourable to someone who has made a vow, so that you too may learn the name, starting from the line of mortals, the king...
EDCS-67200621.summary: This is a dedication by Doulketes, an Aesonian horseman, likely on a monument commemorating his status and piety, possibly from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-67200622.translation: Serenus dedicated this bronze statue to Doulkitis, Leptis repaying the Muses, the singer's servant.
EDCS-67200622.summary: This is a dedication of a bronze statue by Leptis to Doulkitis, likely a poet or singer, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-67200772.translation: Antonius Germanus, a veteran, dedicated this with columns.
EDCS-67200772.summary: This is a dedication by Antonius Germanus, a veteran, to accompany a structure with columns, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-67500032.translation: Sacred to the Genius of the place. Lucius gladly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-67500032.summary: This is a votive inscription to the Genius Loci by Lucius, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-67500033.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. In memory of Gratia Beata, daughter of Iassubius, who lived for 9 years, most dutiful. C and F made this for her.
EDCS-67500033.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Gratia Beata, daughter of Iassubius, who died at age 9, dedicated by C and F, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-67500034.translation: Aursorpius O. Gatirimus made this for his most dutiful wife and for himself.
EDCS-67500034.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Ausorpius O. Gatirimus for his wife and himself, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-67500039.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Aris Rogati, son of Arinis, pious, lived for 85 years, is buried here.
EDCS-67500039.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Aris Rogati, son of Arinis, who died at age 85, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-67500041.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Titus Flavius Secundinus lived for 40 years. Licinius felicitas capo made this.
EDCS-67500041.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Titus Flavius Secundinus, who died at age 40, dedicated by Licinius, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-67500043.translation: To Lucius Pullaienus, son of Lucius, of the Arnensis tribe, elected decurion of the colony of Concordia Iulia Karthago, annual flamen, patron of the pagus Uchitanorum Maiorum, for his merit.
EDCS-67500043.summary: This is a dedication honoring Lucius Pullaienus, a decurion and flamen, and patron of the pagus Uchitanorum Maiorum, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-67500044.translation: To Florentius Lucius Pullaienus Petronianus Decimus, most distinguished man, consular, from a noble family, always the most benevolent citizen and patron, the council of the colony Mariana Augusta Alexandriana Uchitanorum Maiorum.
EDCS-67500044.summary: This is a dedication by the council of the colony Mariana Augusta Alexandriana Uchitanorum Maiorum to Florentius Lucius Pullaienus Petronianus Decimus, a prominent consular figure, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-67500047.translation: Clarentius lived faithfully in peace for 2 years and 1 month.
EDCS-67500047.summary: A funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Clarentius.

EDCS-67500048.translation: Victorianus lived in peace for 18 years; Cattosa lived in peace for 7 years.
EDCS-67500048.summary: A funerary inscription recording the lifespans of Victorianus and Cattosa.

EDCS-67500049.translation: On the 18th day before the Kalends of September, the body of Crescenti, a holy presbyter, who had lived worthily in the secular world, is established to be buried in this place in peace.
EDCS-67500049.summary: A funerary inscription dating to late August, recording the burial of the holy presbyter Crescenti.

EDCS-67500050.translation: The Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus, conqueror of the Parthians, conqueror of the Britons, conqueror of the Germans, holding tribunician power for the 19th time, consul for the 4th time, father of the country, restored [this].
EDCS-67500050.summary: An imperial rescript or dedication by Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus, dating to his 19th tribunician power year.

EDCS-67500052.translation: The Emperor Caesar Marcus Iulius Philippus Pius Felix Augustus Invictus, chief priest, holding tribunician power for the 2nd time, consul, father of the country, proconsul, and Marcus Iulius Philippus, most noble Caesar, prince of youth, and Marcia Otacilia Severa, wife of the Augustus.
EDCS-67500052.summary: A dedication or titulature listing the imperial family including Philip I, his son, and his wife Marcia Otacilia Severa.

EDCS-67500053.translation: To our most brave Emperor and peacemaker of the city, Marcus Claudius Tacitus, Pious, Fortunate, Augustus, for the 109th [year of the reckoning?].
EDCS-67500053.summary: A dedication to Emperor Tacitus, possibly dating to the 109th year of a local reckoning or imperial era.

EDCS-67500054.translation: To the great and unconquered Emperor Caesar Gaius Valerius Diocletian Pius Felix Augustus, holding tribunician power for the 2nd time, consul for the 2nd time, proconsul, chief priest, and to Marcus Valerius Maximian, most noble Caesar.
EDCS-67500054.summary: A dedication to Emperors Diocletian and Maximian, likely from the early part of their reign.

EDCS-67500056.translation: Sacred to Neptune Augustus. On the Ides of April, Lucius Munatius Victor, the magistrate of the pagus, made [this] at the decree of the decurions with public money. The pagus paid its vow willingly. Iunius Alcide paid its vow.
EDCS-67500056.summary: A dedication to Neptune Augustus, funded by the pagus and carried out by its magistrate Lucius Munatius Victor, dated to April 13th.

EDCS-68000009.translation: Among the leading citizens of Carthage of Cezeius Eusebius the younger, a most distinguished man; among the leading citizens of the mother city Carthage of Caecilius, a most distinguished man; of Restitutus, a most distinguished man; of Valerianus, a most distinguished man; of Gabinianus and Theodorus, most distinguished men; of Gabinianus Firmus, a most distinguished man; of Pompeius Innocens the younger, a most distinguished boy; of Octavianus, a most distinguished man; of Pu(blius) Iatius; among the leading citizens of the mother city Carthage of Servius Flavius, duovir; and among the most devoted leading citizens of mother Carthage of Sextus Ratio Augusta, who holds office in the treasury of the province of Africa.
EDCS-68000009.summary: A list of distinguished citizens and officials in Carthage, including administrative roles related to the provincial treasury, likely from the late Roman period.

EDCS-68300013.summary: A very brief funerary inscription recording the name and parentage of Diore.

EDCS-68300014.summary: A funerary inscription for Diore, son of Lucernus.

EDCS-68300016.translation: Sanion Anneianus, also known as Lucernarius (lamp-maker).
EDCS-68300016.summary: A funerary epitaph or designation for Sanion Anneianus, identified by his occupation as a lamp-maker.

EDCS-68300020.summary: A funerary inscription for Seberion, a lamp maker.

EDCS-68300036.translation: Herennius Bassus arranged for ten pairs of gifts to be made.
EDCS-68300036.summary: This inscription records Herennius Bassus commissioning ten pairs of gifts.

EDCS-68300159.translation: Furcilia Optata Tiberiana, most illustrious woman, patron and alumna of the colony.
EDCS-68300159.summary: An honorific inscription for Furcilia Optata Tiberiana, a prominent woman in the colony.

EDCS-68900010.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Livia Libaria lived 35 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-68900010.summary: A funerary inscription for Livia Libaria, who died at age 35.

EDCS-69000081.translation: Lucius lies here, and also his pious wife Iulia, who lived with him in equal age and love. For they delighted the citizens with their harmonious life. This couple, having ended their lives with Iulia's death, for she was the first and most dutiful, Lucius himself follows. May the remaining ashes of these two rest with flowers, and may the earth lightly cover their bones.
EDCS-69000081.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lucius and his wife Iulia, celebrating their harmonious and loving marriage and their shared death.

EDCS-69100235.translation: Petre, vicarius of the Caesarian agricultural service of the Nigrensian territory, you produced for me from the Puteos estate the wells of the agricultural service for the soldier Artteaxu and for A, and made for you from the recovery one only in the month of April, in the fifteenth indiction.
EDCS-69100235.summary: This inscription records a complex transaction or arrangement related to agricultural services and possibly payments in kind, involving Petre and the estate of Puteos, dated to April of the fifteenth indiction.

EDCS-69100236.translation: Comita, vicarius of the Caesarian agricultural service of the Nigrensian territory, you produced for me from the eighth indiction.
EDCS-69100236.summary: This inscription mentions Comita, a vicarius of agricultural services for the Nigrensian territory, in relation to the eighth indiction.

EDCS-69100243.translation: Nimmirre, for two days when we bought one fourth of Carthage for our lord King Childeric, 200 (units) of...; also for Porcellus my son, seventy-five bellows.
EDCS-69100243.summary: This inscription records a purchase of goods and potentially a portion of land related to 'Carthage' and King Childeric, as well as seventy-five bellows for someone named Porcellus.

EDCS-69200156.translation: Erenius B arranged for ten pairs of gifts to be made.
EDCS-69200156.summary: This inscription records Erenius B commissioning ten pairs of gifts.

EDCS-69200158.translation: For the safety of the Emperor Caesar Marcus Antonius Gordianus Pius Felix Augustus, father of the country, consul, and of Sabinia Tranquillina Augusta, our Emperor's wife, and of the entire divine household, the citizens of the municipality of Aelius Hadrianus Thamubaiensis dedicated the Gordian baths by decree of the decurions on the sixteenth day before the Kalends of January, with Arrianus and Papus as consuls.
EDCS-69200158.summary: An official dedication by the citizens of Aelius Hadrianus Thamubaiensis of the Gordian baths in honor of Emperor Gordian III and Empress Tranquillina, dated to 19 December 217 CE (error in original text date/consuls may exist).

EDCS-69200159.translation: To good memory. Donatus, vicarius (subordinate official), lived forty years.
EDCS-69200159.summary: A funerary epitaph for Donatus, a vicarius, who died at forty years of age.

EDCS-69200160.translation: Surula, a slave (?), lived for one year and six months. Sacred to the departed spirits.
EDCS-69200160.summary: A funerary epitaph for a slave named Surula, who died at one year and six months old.

EDCS-69200161.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Fortis lived for eighty-seven years.
EDCS-69200161.summary: A funerary epitaph for Fortis, who died at eighty-seven years of age.

EDCS-69200162.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus Aurelius Saturninus lived [...]
EDCS-69200162.summary: A funerary epitaph for Quintus Aurelius Saturninus, with the duration of his life missing.

EDCS-69200163.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Fortunata lived 5 years and 12 days.
EDCS-69200163.summary: A funerary inscription for Fortunata, who died at the age of 5 years and 12 days.

EDCS-69200164.translation: Missus lived for 21 years, 7 months, and 6 days.
EDCS-69200164.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Missus.

EDCS-69200166.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Faus[t]us Roga[t]us lived eighty-one years. His bones are here.
EDCS-69200166.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death and burial of Faustus Rogatus, who lived eighty-one years, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-69200167.translation: Marcus Decrius Quadratus, son of Lucius, of the Voltinia tribe, pious, lived for 30 years. Decria Abornice arranged for his burial.
EDCS-69200167.summary: This funerary inscription records the life and burial arrangements for Marcus Decrius Quadratus, with his mother Decria Abornice as the dedicator.

EDCS-69200485.translation: To Gnaeus Blaesius Atticus, son of Gnaeus, of the Galeria tribe, a veteran. He served twenty-two years and lived sixty-five years. He is buried here. Attius Sedatus, Publius Masurius Evictus, and Titus Masurius Optatus, the heirs, saw to its construction.
EDCS-69200485.summary: A funerary monument dedicated to Gnaeus Blaesius Atticus, a veteran who served for twenty-two years and lived to sixty-five, erected by his heirs, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-69200486.translation: Hirtilia Sabina, freedwoman, and Lelia lived fifty-two years. She is buried here. Quintus Euhodius Marcellus, a soldier of the III Augusta legion, centuria of Publius Iustus Hospes, and Ienticosus [---] placed this.
EDCS-69200486.summary: A funerary epitaph for Hirtilia Sabina and Lelia, erected by soldiers of the III Augusta legion, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-69200487.translation: Lucius Valerius Pastor, son of Lucius, of the Quirina tribe, a veteran. He lived one hundred and eleven years. He is buried here. His son, Lucius Valerius Callistus, placed this.
EDCS-69200487.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lucius Valerius Pastor, a veteran who lived to an extraordinary age of 111, erected by his son, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-69200488.translation: [---]nius. Proculus, a soldier [of the III Augusta legion?], served in the XXII legion Alexandria for six years and in the III Augusta [---] lived forty-five years. [---] killed. He is buried [here].
EDCS-69200488.summary: A fragmented funerary epitaph for a soldier who served in at least two legions, the XXII Alexandria and the III Augusta, and died violently at the age of forty-five, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-69200489.translation: [---], an evocatus of Augustus. He lived fifty years and served eighteen years. His heir made this at his own expense.
EDCS-69200489.summary: A funerary epitaph for an evocatus (a veteran recalled to service) of Augustus, who lived fifty years and served eighteen, with the monument erected by his heir, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-69200493.translation: [---] of the III Augusta legion. He made [this?]. He is buried here.
EDCS-69200493.summary: A very fragmentary funerary epitaph, possibly recording a soldier of the III Augusta legion, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-69200495.summary: A very brief funerary inscription recording the life of Victoria.

EDCS-69200496.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Sacred to the Divine Shades of Quintus Memmius, Sacred to the Divine Shades of Decimus Memmius.
EDCS-69200496.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the Divine Shades (Dis Manibus) for Quintus Memmius and Decimus Memmius.

EDCS-69200497.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Caius Rossius Crecens lived for 31 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-69200497.summary: This funerary inscription is a dedication to the Divine Shades for Caius Rossius Crecens, indicating he is buried at this location.

EDCS-69200498.translation: Caius S. Felix, pious, lived for [unknown number] years; he is buried here.
EDCS-69200498.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Caius S. Felix, noting his piety and indicating he is interred at this site.

EDCS-69200499.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Saturninus, son of Cabdollo, piously lived eighty-five years. He is buried here.
EDCS-69200499.summary: A funerary epitaph for Saturninus, son of Cabdollo, who lived eighty-five years, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-69200500.translation: ... from Faustina. Publius Perellius Saturninus, pious, lived for 101 years.
EDCS-69200500.summary: This inscription seems to be a funerary text originating from Faustina, recording the long life of Publius Perellius Saturninus.

EDCS-69200501.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Quintus Talvonius Felix.
EDCS-69200501.summary: This is a funerary dedication to the Divine Shades for Quintus Talvonius Felix.

EDCS-69200502.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Iulia Quinti[l]a, pious, lived for [unknown number] years; she is buried on her own land.
EDCS-69200502.summary: This funerary inscription is a dedication to the Divine Shades for Iulia Quintila, noting she is buried on her own property.

EDCS-69200503.translation: Sacred to Jupiter the August. For the health of the Emperor Caesar Traian[us Hadrianus?].
EDCS-69200503.summary: A dedication to Jupiter for the health of Emperor Trajanus Hadrianus (or a similar emperor), likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-69200505.translation: Titus Statilius Taurus, consul for the second time.
EDCS-69200505.summary: A dedication or record of the consulship of Titus Statilius Taurus, likely from the Roman Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-69200506.translation: Felix sianus, pious, lived for 70 years and 3 months. Sacred to the Divine Shades. Hordonia Saturnina, pious, lived for 12 years, 2 months, and 13 days; she is buried here.
EDCS-69200506.summary: This funerary inscription records the lives and burials of two individuals, Felix sianus and Hordonia Saturnina, with dedications to the Divine Shades.

EDCS-69200507.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Oppius Saturninus, son of Publius, a dutiful man, lived 16 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-69200507.summary: A funerary inscription recording the life and burial of Oppius Saturninus, who died at the age of 16.

EDCS-69200508.translation: Maxima lived 50 years; Siricina lived 31 years.
EDCS-69200508.summary: A funerary inscription recording the lifespans of two individuals, Maxima and Siricina.

EDCS-69200509.summary: A funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Secundus Fortunatus.

EDCS-69200510.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Secundula, daughter of Publius, a dutiful woman, lived 7 months and 15 days; she is buried here.
EDCS-69200510.summary: A funerary inscription recording the life and burial of Secundula, who died at 7 months and 15 days old.

EDCS-69200511.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Licinia Attica, daughter of Marcus, a dutiful woman, lived 52 years; she is buried here. We did not make your tomb long ago, venerable mother; the artisans' work caused delays.
EDCS-69200511.summary: A funerary inscription for Licinia Attica, who died at 52, with a dedication from her children regarding the construction of her tomb.

EDCS-69200512.translation: Noble Caesar Augustus, prince of youth, and Marcia Octacilia Severa Augusta, mother of Caesar, mother of the camps, of the senate, and of the fatherland.
EDCS-69200512.summary: This inscription honors Emperor Philip the Arab, his wife Marcia Otacilia Severa, and their son Philip II, likely dating to the mid-3rd century CE.

EDCS-69200513.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Caecilius Dativus lived 10 years.
EDCS-69200513.summary: A funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Caecilius Dativus, who died at the age of 10.

EDCS-69200514.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Iulius Litus lived 9 years.
EDCS-69200514.summary: A funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Iulius Litus, who died at the age of 9.

EDCS-69200515.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Marcus Pontius Victor, a dutiful man, lived 75 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-69200515.summary: A funerary inscription recording the life and burial of Marcus Pontius Victor, who died at the age of 75.

EDCS-69200516.translation: Mucia Redemta, daughter of Lucius, of the Via tribe, pious, lived for 14 years, was buried here.
EDCS-69200516.summary: This is a tombstone for a young girl named Mucia Redemta, who died at the age of 14, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-69200517.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Donata, faithful, in peace, lived more or less 93 years.
EDCS-69200517.summary: A funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Donata, who lived approximately 93 years.

EDCS-69200518.translation: To Marcus Aurelius Probus, the Invincible, Pious, Happy, Augustus.
EDCS-69200518.summary: This is a dedication to Emperor Probus, likely a part of a larger honorary inscription, dating to his reign in the late 3rd century CE.

EDCS-69200520.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Marcus Antonius Gordianus, grandson of the deified Marcus Antonius Gordianus, nephew of the deified Antonius Gordianus, most brave, most happy, chief priest, with tribunician power, consul, father of the fatherland, proconsul.
EDCS-69200520.summary: This inscription records the full titulature of Emperor Gordian III, detailing his honors and powers during his reign in the mid-3rd century CE.

EDCS-69200521.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Iulia Rogata, daughter of Rogatus, a dutiful woman, lived 81 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-69200521.summary: A funerary inscription recording the life and burial of Iulia Rogata, who died at the age of 81.

EDCS-69200522.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Paralius Simplicius lived 45 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-69200522.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Paralius Simplicius at the age of 45.

EDCS-69200523.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Prima, wife of Arestus Marionis, lived 85 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-69200523.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Prima at the age of 85.

EDCS-69200524.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Aedilius Namphamo the pious lived 53 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-69200524.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Aedilius Namphamo at the age of 53.

EDCS-69200525.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Aedilius Primus, son of Namphamo, the pious lived 30 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-69200525.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Aedilius Primus, son of Namphamo, at the age of 30.

EDCS-69200526.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Aedilius Primasius lived 27 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-69200526.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Aedilius Primasius at the age of 27.

EDCS-69200527.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Lucanus, son of Mustinus Successus, the pious lived 41 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-69200527.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Lucanus at the age of 41.

EDCS-69200528.translation: Gaius Passienius Septimus built this mausoleum for myself, my wife, and my descendants, and I dedicated it.
EDCS-69200528.summary: This inscription records the construction and dedication of a mausoleum by Gaius Passienius Septimus for his family.

EDCS-69200529.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Suggi Victoria lived...
EDCS-69200529.summary: This incomplete funerary inscription records the name Suggi Victoria and her lifespan, which is cut off.

EDCS-69200530.translation: Sacred to Jupiter Best and Greatest, Augustus, for the health of Passienius, [my] uncle, and his children.
EDCS-69200530.summary: This dedication to Jupiter is made for the health of Passienius and his children.

EDCS-69200531.translation: Valentius lived in peace for almost 80 years.
EDCS-69200531.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a man named Valentius, recording his peaceful life and approximate age at death, likely from the later Roman Empire.

EDCS-69200532.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Kaninius Maius the pious lived 75 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-69200532.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Kaninius Maius at the age of 75.

EDCS-69200533.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Quintus Apronius Maxutius lived 82 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-69200533.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Quintus Apronius Maxutius, recording his age and burial place.

EDCS-69200534.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Cepia Margarita lived 71 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-69200534.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Cepia Margarita, recording her age and burial place.

EDCS-69200535.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Iulia lived 32 years.
EDCS-69200535.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Iulia, recording her age.

EDCS-69200536.translation: Marcus Aninius Honoratus, son of Marcus, dutiful, lived 4 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-69200536.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcus Aninius Honoratus, recording his age and burial place.

EDCS-69200537.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Spilius Napamo lived 2 years.
EDCS-69200537.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Spilius Napamo, recording his age.

EDCS-69200538.translation: To our lord Publius Licinius Valerianus Maximus Pius Felix Victor, 85.
EDCS-69200538.summary: This inscription appears to be a dedication or honorific text related to Emperor Valerian, possibly recording his age at death or a period of reign.

EDCS-69200539.translation: To Perpetuus, Emperor Lucius Domitius Aurelianus, Invincible, Pious, Happy, our Augustus.
EDCS-69200539.summary: This is a dedication to Emperor Aurelian, acknowledging his titles and divine favor, likely from the late 3rd century CE.

EDCS-69200540.translation: To our lord Flavius Claudius Constantinus, most noble Caesar.
EDCS-69200540.summary: This inscription honors the Caesar Flavius Claudius Constantinus, likely Constantine I before his elevation to Augustus, dating to the early 4th century CE.

EDCS-69200541.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Marcus Fictorius Salinator, dutiful, lived 2 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-69200541.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcus Fictorius Salinator, recording his age and burial place.

EDCS-69200542.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Spesina lived [some number of] years [and some number of] months.
EDCS-69200542.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Spesina, recording an incomplete age.

EDCS-69200543.translation: [... of the] age of 41 years, who lived 41 years.
EDCS-69200543.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription that records the age of an individual as 41 years.

EDCS-69200544.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Quintus Caecilius Victor Quadratianus, dutiful, lived 14 years; may your bones rest well.
EDCS-69200544.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Quintus Caecilius Victor Quadratianus, recording his age and a wish for his afterlife.

EDCS-69200545.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Geminia Victoria, dutiful, lived 32 years.
EDCS-69200545.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Geminia Victoria, who died at the age of 32.

EDCS-69200546.translation: Augustalis lived 3 years. His father made this for his son. He lies here.
EDCS-69200546.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Augustalis, who died at the age of 3, with his father as the dedicator.

EDCS-69200548.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Namapamina lived 33 years.
EDCS-69200548.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Namapamina, who died at the age of 33.

EDCS-69200549.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Mustaca, dutiful, lived 31 years. She lies here.
EDCS-69200549.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Mustaca, who died at the age of 31.

EDCS-69200550.translation: Pompeia Secundula, pious, lived for 26 years, is placed here. // Nonia Bonosa, daughter of Faustus, pious, lived for 28 years, is placed here. // Areia Secunda, daughter of Laetus, pious, lived for 55 years, is placed here.
EDCS-69200550.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lives and ages of three women: Pompeia Secundula, Nonia Bonosa, and Areia Secunda, likely from the 3rd century CE.

EDCS-69200551.summary: This is a brief funerary epitaph, possibly for a Christian, indicating the deceased was honored and at peace, likely from the later Roman Empire.

EDCS-69200552.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Manneia Maia, dutiful, lived 71 years. She lies here.
EDCS-69200552.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Manneia Maia, who died at the age of 71.

EDCS-69200553.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Victoria Corinthiana, dutiful, consecrated, lived 32 years. She lies here.
EDCS-69200553.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Victoria Corinthiana, who died at the age of 32.

EDCS-69200554.translation: To the Emperor, Caesar, the Happy, Dutiful, Victorious Augustus, father of the fatherland, consul for the first time.
EDCS-69200554.summary: This is a dedication to Emperor O. O. Felix Pius Victor Augustus, likely from the period of his first consulship.

EDCS-69200555.translation: To Gaius Flavius Galerius Constantius and Gaius Galerius Valerius Maximianus, most noble Caesars.
EDCS-69200555.summary: This inscription dedicates honors to Galerius and Maximian, likely as Caesars in the late 3rd or early 4th century CE.

EDCS-69200556.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Pia lived 161 years and 3 hours. Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Pius lived 6 years and 3 hours. Maiulus lies buried here.
EDCS-69200556.summary: This tombstone inscription records the deaths of Pia (living an impossibly long time) and Pius, who died at age 6, with Maiulus as the buried individual.

EDCS-69200557.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Luria Fr[...]
EDCS-69200557.summary: This is a fragmentary tombstone inscription dedicated to the spirits of the departed, beginning with the name Luria.

EDCS-69200558.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription honoring a perpetual priestess, likely named Luria (continuing from the previous fragment) and described as very dutiful.

EDCS-69200560.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Ernimia Caecilia Venusina, dutiful, lived 23 years.
EDCS-69200560.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Ernimia Caecilia Venusina, recording her piety and age at death.

EDCS-69200561.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Iulia Secundi Pastoris, daughter of Burche, dutiful, lived 71 years, is buried here.
EDCS-69200561.summary: This funerary epitaph records the death and burial of Iulia Secundi Pastoris, noting her piety and age.

EDCS-69200562.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Macrinus lived 60 years.
EDCS-69200562.summary: This is a brief funerary epitaph for Macrinus, stating his age at death.

EDCS-69200563.translation: unharmed, judge, I mourned, wretched, mine, wife of Aevius.
EDCS-69200563.summary: This fragmented inscription seems to be a personal dedication or lament, possibly related to a wife of Aevius.

EDCS-69200567.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Julia Regula, also known as Stolata, lived 63 years and 6 months; she is buried here.
EDCS-69200567.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the name, aliases, lifespan, and burial place of Julia Regula, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-69900025.translation: Soldier of the III Augusta legion, of the cohort, served for [---] years.
EDCS-69900025.summary: This is a military inscription recording the service of a soldier from the III Augusta legion.

EDCS-69900029.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Antonia Africana lived 55 years, is buried here.
EDCS-69900029.summary: This funerary epitaph records the death and burial of Antonia Africana, stating her age.

EDCS-69900030.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Avius Maximus lived 1 year and 9 months. His father placed this.

EDCS-69900031.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Caius Caecilius Saturninus lived 13 years and 2 months, is buried here. Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Iulia Martia lived 57 years, is buried here. Caecilius Saturninus (placed this) for his most beloved parent.

EDCS-69900032.translation: Caecilia Fortunata, daughter of Caecilius Impetratus, lived 70 years, is buried here. Agria Processa placed this for her dutiful mother.
EDCS-69900032.summary: This funerary epitaph records the death and burial of Caecilia Fortunata, placed by her daughter Agria Processa.

EDCS-69900033.translation: Caecilia Quarta, pious daughter of Quintus, lived 80 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-69900033.summary: A funerary epitaph for Caecilia Quarta, recording her age and burial, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-69900034.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Caesia Hygia is buried here. Nonius Donatus, her husband, placed this for his pious wife.
EDCS-69900034.summary: A funerary epitaph dedicated to the departed spirits, with Nonius Donatus setting up the monument for his wife Caesia Hygia.

EDCS-69900035.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Calloniae Aphrodisiae, pious, lived 54 years. Marcus Turius Marcianus, her son, made this for his mother out of piety; she is buried here.
EDCS-69900035.summary: A funerary epitaph dedicated to the departed spirits, set up by Marcus Turius Marcianus for his pious mother, Calloniae Aphrodisiae, recording her age.

EDCS-69900036.translation: Camurinius Sapidus lived 9 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-69900036.summary: A funerary epitaph for Camurinius Sapidus, recording his age and burial, likely that of a child.

EDCS-69900037.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Cassia Pudentilla, pious, lived 15 years; she is buried here. Onius Asclepiades placed this.
EDCS-69900037.summary: A funerary epitaph dedicated to the departed spirits, with Onius Asclepiades setting up the monument for Cassia Pudentilla, recording her age.

EDCS-69900038.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Coddius lived [a] years for his dearest wife; she is buried here.
EDCS-69900038.summary: A funerary epitaph dedicated to the departed spirits, with an unknown dedicator setting up the monument for his dearest wife.

EDCS-69900039.translation: Corfidia Tertulla lived 85 years; she is buried here. Felix placed this for his most holy and pious mother.
EDCS-69900039.summary: A funerary epitaph for Corfidia Tertulla, recording her age and burial, set up by her son Felix.

EDCS-69900040.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Cornelia Matutina lived 61 years.
EDCS-69900040.summary: A funerary epitaph dedicated to the departed spirits, recording the age of Cornelia Matutina.

EDCS-69900041.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Cur Baslia lived 90 years; she is buried here. Cur Cududa placed this for his pious mother.
EDCS-69900041.summary: A funerary epitaph dedicated to the departed spirits, with Cur Cududa setting up the monument for his pious mother Cur Baslia, recording her age.

EDCS-69900043.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Flavia Tertulla lived 30 years; she is buried here. M II placed this. Sacred to the departed spirits. Postumius lived [?] years; he is buried here. Marcus Ser-
EDCS-69900043.summary: A fragmented funerary inscription, possibly recording two individuals, Flavia Tertulla and Postumius, with partial information about their lives and burials.

EDCS-69900044.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Fructuosa, pious, most chaste, lived 37 years, 9 months, 22 days. Bocchus placed this for his wife, most excellent, most faithful preserver. She lies here. Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Bocchus lived 77 years. He lies here.
EDCS-69900044.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the deaths and ages of a wife named Fructuosa and her husband Bocchus, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-69900045.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Ianuaria lived 91 years. She lies here. Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Marcus Mevius Urbanus lived 18 years. He lies here. Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Lucius Mevius Restitutus lived 35 years. He lies here. His pious brothers placed this.

EDCS-69900046.translation: and Iulianus to his dearest sister
EDCS-69900046.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely funerary or dedicatory, mentioning Iulianus and his sister, probably dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-69900048.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the life span of Caius Iulius Quintulus, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-69900049.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Caius Iulius Severus lived 13 years. He lies here. His pious father Iulius D placed this.
EDCS-69900049.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the death of Caius Iulius Severus and its placement by his father, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-69900051.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription recording the name Quintus Iulius Soemas and the beginning of his lifespan, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-69900052.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the life span of Iulia Victorina, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-69900053.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Lucilia Aemilia Tertulla, pious, lived 75 years. She lies here. Lucius Plaetorius Successor placed this for his most pious wife.
EDCS-69900053.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the death of Lucilia Aemilia Tertulla and its placement by her husband Lucius Plaetorius Successor, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-69900054.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Lucrio, pious, lived 22 years, 8 months. His mother placed this. He lies here.
EDCS-69900054.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the death and age of Lucrio, placed by his mother, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-69900055.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Mucro. Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Vot
EDCS-69900055.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription mentioning two names, Mucro and Vot, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-69900056.translation: Munatius lived 3 years. He is buried here. Munatius Vitalis placed [this] for his son.
EDCS-69900056.summary: A funerary epitaph for a child named Munatius, set up by his father, Munatius Vitalis.

EDCS-69900058.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Optata lived V years.
EDCS-69900058.summary: A funerary epitaph, likely for Optata, dedicated to the departed spirits.

EDCS-69900059.translation: Publius Ovidius Aemilianus placed [this] for his incomparable wife. She lived [X] years. She is buried here.
EDCS-69900059.summary: A funerary epitaph by Publius Ovidius Aemilianus for his wife, stating her burial and lifespan.

EDCS-69900060.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Papirius Lucilianus placed [this] for his good son, Papirius Victorinus. He lived 14 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-69900060.summary: A funerary epitaph for Papirius Victorinus, who died at 14, set up by his father, Papirius Lucilianus.

EDCS-69900061.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Plotia Casta lived 25 years and [X] months. She is buried here.
EDCS-69900061.summary: A funerary epitaph for Plotia Casta, recording her age at death and burial.

EDCS-69900062.translation: Marcus Pompeius Fortunatus lived 4 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-69900062.summary: A funerary epitaph for Marcus Pompeius Fortunatus, who died at the age of 4.

EDCS-69900063.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Postumia Iul[a] lived 30 years. Martialis, her husband, placed [this] for his wife. She is buried here.
EDCS-69900063.summary: A funerary epitaph for Postumia Iula, set up by her husband Martialis, recording her age at death.

EDCS-69900064.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Secunda lived 5 years and 6 months. Her devoted father placed [this].
EDCS-69900064.summary: A funerary epitaph for Secunda, who died at 5 years and 6 months, set up by her father.

EDCS-69900065.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Steia Donatula, also called Urupila, lived 50 years. Titus Lartius Quintulus placed [this] for his most devoted wife. She is buried here.
EDCS-69900065.summary: A funerary epitaph for Steia Donatula, also known as Urupila, set up by her husband Titus Lartius Quintulus.

EDCS-69900066.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Caius Tuccius lived 4 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-69900066.summary: A funerary epitaph for Caius Tuccius, who died at the age of 4.

EDCS-69900067.translation: Gaius Valerius Bucco is laid here. Valeria Orestina placed this for her brother.
EDCS-69900067.summary: A funerary epitaph by Valeria Orestina for her brother Gaius Valerius Bucco.

EDCS-69900068.translation: Gaius Valerius Valerianus is laid here. Valerius Bucco placed this for his son.
EDCS-69900068.summary: A funerary epitaph by Valerius Bucco for his son Gaius Valerius Valerianus.

EDCS-69900069.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus Varius Perpetuus, son of Quintus Varius Ter, of the tribe Ve [---].
EDCS-69900069.summary: A funerary dedication to the departed spirits by Quintus Varius Perpetuus for his father.

EDCS-69900071.translation: Gaius, son of [---], of the tribe Quirina, lived for 65 years. [---] for his father.
EDCS-69900071.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the age of Gaius, son of [---], and likely a dedication to his father.

EDCS-69900072.translation: She is laid here. His sons made this for a most rare mother. He is laid here. His sons made this for a most rare father.
EDCS-69900072.summary: A funerary epitaph with identical phrases for a mother and a father, erected by their sons.

EDCS-69900073.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Ianuaria lived for 8 years, 4 months, and 14 days.
EDCS-69900073.summary: A funerary epitaph for Ianuaria, recording her short lifespan.

EDCS-69900075.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Hilarus lived [---] and Caelianus [---].
EDCS-69900075.summary: A funerary dedication to the departed spirits, mentioning Hilarus and Caelianus.

EDCS-69900076.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Ianuaria lived for 25 years.
