EDCS-69900077.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Iupia lived for 23 years. Iulius Donatus placed this for his dutiful wife.
EDCS-69900077.summary: A funerary epitaph by Iulius Donatus for his wife Iupia, noting her piety and age.

EDCS-69900078.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Gaius Iulius Victor lived for [---] years. His mother placed this for her dearest son.
EDCS-69900078.summary: A funerary epitaph by a mother for her son Gaius Iulius Victor, recording his age at death.

EDCS-69900079.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Iulia Fructosa lived 25 years. Her pious mother placed this; she is buried here.
EDCS-69900079.summary: This funerary epitaph records the burial of Iulia Fructosa, placed by her mother, and likely dates to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-69900080.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Natalis lived 9 years; the pious Narcissus is buried here.
EDCS-69900080.summary: This funerary epitaph records the burial of Natalis, who died at age 9, and was likely placed by Narcissus.

EDCS-69900081.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Pompeia Successa lived 70 years; she placed this for herself and is buried here.
EDCS-69900081.summary: This funerary epitaph records the burial of Pompeia Successa, who lived to 70 and provided for her own burial.

EDCS-69900083.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Volusenus Pannychus lived 70 years; he is buried here. Volusena Euhodia and Hateria Pannychis placed this.
EDCS-69900083.summary: This funerary epitaph records the burial of Volusenus Pannychus, who lived to 70, and was commemorated by Volusena Euhodia and Hateria Pannychis.

EDCS-69900085.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Apertia Prima lived 80 years; she is buried here. Petronius Primus placed this for his dearest, pious mother.
EDCS-69900085.summary: This funerary epitaph records the burial of Apertia Prima, who lived to 80, and was commemorated by her son Petronius Primus.

EDCS-69900086.translation: Lucius Caecilius Praesumptus Metrodorus lived 24 years, 1 month, and [missing number] days; he is buried here.
EDCS-69900086.summary: This funerary epitaph records the burial of Lucius Caecilius Praesumptus Metrodorus, who died at age 24 years, 1 month, and an indeterminate number of days.

EDCS-69900087.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Marcus Iulius Donatus lived 5 years, 10 months, and 5 days; he is buried here.
EDCS-69900087.summary: This funerary epitaph records the burial of Marcus Iulius Donatus, who died at the age of 5 years, 10 months, and 5 days.

EDCS-69900088.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Marcus Iulius [and] Iulia.
EDCS-69900088.summary: This fragmentary inscription, dedicated to the Divine Shades, possibly records the names Marcus Iulius and Iulia, but its purpose is unclear.

EDCS-69900089.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Maxima lived 36 years. Mitinus placed this for his dearest wife.
EDCS-69900089.summary: This funerary epitaph records the burial of Maxima, who died at 36, and was commemorated by her husband Mitinus.

EDCS-69900090.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Helvia Gallita, daughter of Lucius, a Getulian woman, lived 55 years. Tiberius Caecilius Vitalis placed this for his dearest wife.
EDCS-69900090.summary: This funerary epitaph records the burial of Helvia Gallita, daughter of Lucius and of Getulian origin, who lived to 55, and was commemorated by her husband Tiberius Caecilius Vitalis.

EDCS-69900091.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Gaius Pompeius Avitus lived 49 years. Sacred to the departed spirits. Publius Aelius Crecens lived 27 years, is buried here, on the Kalends of [---]. Sacred to the departed spirits. Postumia Irene lived 88 years, is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Gaius Pompeius Palormus lived 57 years and 6 months. Aelia Colonica placed this for her husband, is buried here.
EDCS-69900091.summary: This inscription records the burial details and lifespans of four individuals, with Aelia Colonica dedicating a part for her husband.

EDCS-69900092.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Eusebia, wife of Erotis, lived 55 years, is buried here. Eucharisius placed this for his devoted wife.
EDCS-69900092.summary: This inscription records the burial of Eusebia, for whom her husband Eucharisius dedicated a monument.

EDCS-69900093.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Aemilia Maxima lived 50 years. Antonius Felix placed this for his devoted wife, is buried here.
EDCS-69900093.summary: This inscription records the burial of Aemilia Maxima, for whom her husband Antonius Felix dedicated a monument.

EDCS-69900094.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Apuleius Secundinus lived 31 years. His devoted brothers placed this.
EDCS-69900094.summary: This inscription records the burial of Apuleius Secundinus, for whom his brothers dedicated a monument.

EDCS-69900095.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Baebia Dubitata lived 15 years, is buried here.
EDCS-69900095.summary: This inscription records the burial of Baebia Dubitata.

EDCS-69900096.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Caecilius Ianuarius lived 79 years, is buried here. His wife, sons, and grandsons placed this.
EDCS-69900096.summary: This inscription records the burial of Lucius Caecilius Ianuarius, for whom his family placed a monument.

EDCS-69900097.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Gaius Camidenius Gemellus lived 61 years. His devoted sons placed this for their father, is buried here.
EDCS-69900097.summary: This inscription records the burial of Gaius Camidenius Gemellus, for whom his sons dedicated a monument.

EDCS-69900098.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Gaius Clodius Ianuarius lived 40 years, is buried here. Vitricius and his wife placed this for their devoted son. Sacred to the departed spirits. Aelia Secunda lived 85 years. Her devoted husband placed this, is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Gaius Tettius Quetulus lived 95 years. His devoted grandson placed this.
EDCS-69900098.summary: This inscription records the burial details and lifespans of three individuals, with family members dedicating monuments.

EDCS-69900099.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Cornelia Honorata lived 45 years and 3 months, is buried here. Marcus Salvidenius Martialis placed this for his most rare wife. Sacred to the departed spirits. Salvidenius Martialis lived 75 years and 3 months, is buried here. Placed for themselves.
EDCS-69900099.summary: This inscription records the burial of Cornelia Honorata, for whom her husband Marcus Salvidenius Martialis dedicated a monument, and also Salvidenius Martialis himself.

EDCS-69900101.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Fannia Silvana lived 90 years, is buried here. Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Caecius Celerinus lived 80 years, is buried here.
EDCS-69900101.summary: This inscription records the burial details and lifespans of two individuals.

EDCS-69900102.translation: To the Spirits of the Dead, sacred. Helvius Calus erected this for his pious father, Italicus, who lived 70 years; he is buried here. Italicus lived here. He is buried here.
EDCS-69900102.summary: This funerary inscription records the death and burial of Helvius Calus's father, Italicus, who lived 70 years, and was erected by his son.

EDCS-69900103.translation: To the Spirits of the Dead, sacred. Maevia Isi.
EDCS-69900103.summary: This is a very brief funerary inscription dedicated to Maevia Isi.

EDCS-69900104.translation: To the Spirits of the Dead, sacred. Secunda lived 5 years. Her son erected this for his dearest mother. Pompeia Restuta lived 8 years; she is buried here. Pompeius Grillus lived 13 years; he is buried here. His pious mother erected this.
EDCS-69900104.summary: This inscription records the burial of Secunda (5 years old), Pompeia Restuta (8 years old), and Pompeius Grillus (13 years old), with erected by a son and a mother.

EDCS-69900105.translation: To the Spirits of the Dead, sacred. Porcellas lived 17 years, 9 months, and 6 days. Senti Porcellus and Kalchedonia erected this for their son.
EDCS-69900105.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Porcellas, who lived 17 years, 9 months, and 6 days, and was erected by his parents Senti Porcellus and Kalchedonia.

EDCS-69900106.translation: To the Spirits of the Dead, sacred. Quintus Porcius Verus, 47 years old, and Fulvius Primus for his father. He is buried here. To the Spirits of the Dead, sacred. Porcius Martialis, 22 years old. Quintus Porcius Verus erected this for his brother. He is buried here. To the Spirits of the Dead, sacred. Fulvia Tertiola, 4 years old. Quintus Porcius Verus, her father, erected this. She is buried here.
EDCS-69900106.summary: This funerary inscription records the deaths and burials of Quintus Porcius Verus (47), Porcius Martialis (22), and Fulvia Tertiola (4), with relationships indicated as father, brother, and son/daughter.

EDCS-69900107.translation: To the Spirits of the Dead, sacred. Postumius Fortunatus lived 42 years; he is buried here. To the Spirits of the Dead, sacred. Caius Postumius Venustus lived 40 years. Aelina, his wife, made this for her dearest husband.
EDCS-69900107.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Postumius Fortunatus (42 years old) and Caius Postumius Venustus (40 years old), with the latter's wife Aelina as the dedicator.

EDCS-69900108.translation: To the Spirits of the Dead, sacred. Recta Tertulla, pious, lived 135 years; she is buried here. Itimininus, pious, erected this.
EDCS-69900108.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Recta Tertulla, who lived 135 years, and was erected by Itimininus.

EDCS-69900109.translation: To the Spirits of the Dead, sacred. Titsena Maxima lived 30 years; she is buried here. Licinius erected this for his pious wife. To the Spirits of the Dead, sacred. Licinia Victorina lived 18 years; she is buried here. Her pious father erected this.
EDCS-69900109.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Titsena Maxima (30 years old) and Licinia Victorina (18 years old), with dedications from a husband and a father.

EDCS-69900110.translation: To the Spirits of the Dead, sacred. Valeria Dubitata lived 5 years and 20 days. Her father erected this for his daughter. To the Spirits of the Dead, sacred. Vel I Luci, son Victor, lived here. He is buried here.
EDCS-69900110.summary: This funerary inscription records the deaths and burials of Valeria Dubitata (5 years old) and Victor, with dedications from a father and an unspecified individual.

EDCS-69900111.translation: To the Spirits of the Dead, sacred. Publius Vibius Peregrinus lived one year and 10 months. To the Spirits of the Dead, sacred. Peregrius lived 13 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-69900111.summary: This funerary inscription records the deaths and burials of Publius Vibius Peregrinus (1 year, 10 months) and Peregrius (13 years).

EDCS-69900114.summary: This is a very brief funerary inscription, likely a dedication by parents to their child, Parvotus.

EDCS-69900115.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Titus Flavius Hylas lived 16 years, 5 months. His brother Flavi Hylas and Bona placed [this] for their dearest brother.
EDCS-69900115.summary: This tombstone records the death of Titus Flavius Hylas at age 16 and was set up by his siblings.

EDCS-69900116.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Tilius Impetratus lived 35 years; placed [this] for his dearest father. Here he lies. Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Tilia Stercula lived 4 years; her devoted father placed [this] for his dearest daughter. Here she lies.
EDCS-69900116.summary: This inscription records the deaths of a father and daughter, Tilius Impetratus and Tilia Stercula, with the father setting up the monument for his daughter and a son setting one up for his father.

EDCS-69900118.translation: Assidonius Hermes was dear to his friends, lived 45 years, not worthy, died quickly, because fate thus decreed. His parents placed [this] for their devoted son. Here he lies.
EDCS-69900118.summary: This tombstone commemorates Assidonius Hermes, who died young and is mourned by his parents.

EDCS-69900119.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Caelia Acceptula lived 3 years; here she lies. Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Publius Caelius Victor, formerly praetor, lived 75 years; here he lies. His devoted son placed [this].
EDCS-69900119.summary: This inscription records the deaths of two individuals, Caelia Acceptula (a child) and Publius Caelius Victor (a former praetor), with the latter's monument erected by his son.

EDCS-69900120.translation: Caius Carvilius Mustulus lived 80 years. His devoted father Honoratus placed [this].
EDCS-69900120.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Caius Carvilius Mustulus at age 80 and was set up by his devoted father, Honoratus.

EDCS-69900121.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Claanius Donatus lived [X] years. Claanius Venustus lived 12 years. Claanius Secundulus lived 18 years; here they lie. Claania Flavia Tita placed [this].
EDCS-69900121.summary: This tombstone records the deaths of three individuals named Claanius, with the monument erected by Claania Flavia Tita.

EDCS-69900122.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Donatus lived 41 years, two months, and 11 days; his devoted brothers placed [this] for him. Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Bibia Quieta lived 80 years; here she lies. Her son placed [this] for his dearest mother.
EDCS-69900122.summary: This inscription records the deaths of Donatus (erected by his brothers) and Bibia Quieta (erected by her son).

EDCS-69900123.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Lucius Cranius Mus lived 3 years; his devoted wife placed [this]. Here he lies.
EDCS-69900123.summary: This tombstone records the death of Lucius Cranius Mus at age 3 and was erected by his devoted wife.

EDCS-69900124.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Lucilia Revocata, also called Coronata, lived [X] years. [She] placed [this].

EDCS-69900125.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Julius Nundinarius, dutiful, lived 65 years; he is buried here. His son placed [this].
EDCS-69900125.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Julius Nundinarius and erected by his son, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-69900127.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Antonia Peculiaris, dearest mother, lived 47 years. Her dutiful sons erected this; she is buried here.
EDCS-69900127.summary: A funerary epitaph for Antonia Peculiaris, set up by her sons, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-69900128.translation: [...] lived 65 years; she is buried here.

EDCS-69900129.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Gaius C. Gaius H. lived 83 years.
EDCS-69900129.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Gaius C. Gaius H., likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-69900130.translation: [...]nius Marchellus lived 83 years. His heir, his son, made this.

EDCS-69900134.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Cesonius Victor lived 61 years.
EDCS-69900134.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of Lucius Cesonius Victor, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-69900135.translation: Cluvia Sabina, most chaste, lived 40 years.
EDCS-69900135.summary: A funerary epitaph for Cluvia Sabina, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-69900136.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Gaius Aemilius Saturninus lived 69 years and 6 months. His sons erected this for a good father.
EDCS-69900136.summary: A funerary epitaph for Gaius Aemilius Saturninus, erected by his sons, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-69900137.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Fabia Silvana lived 80 years and 11 days.
EDCS-69900137.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Fabia Silvana.

EDCS-69900138.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Iulius M C lived 50 years, seven months, and 4 days.
EDCS-69900138.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Iulius M C.

EDCS-69900139.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Iunius P made [this] for Emeritus, who lived 41 years.
EDCS-69900139.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Iunius P for his son Emeritas.

EDCS-69900140.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Claudius Licinus lived 95 years and 6 months. Claudia Fortunata, his most devoted wife, made [this].
EDCS-69900140.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Claudia Fortunata for her husband Claudius Licinus.

EDCS-69900151.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Caius Clodius Successus.

EDCS-69900152.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Iuventius Secundus.

EDCS-69900155.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Munatius Adiectus.

EDCS-69900156.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Munatius Adiectus.

EDCS-69900158.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Munatius Adiectus.

EDCS-69900160.summary: This is a funerary epitaph likely for Marcus Novius Justus.

EDCS-69900161.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely indicating ownership or a dedication by Gaius Oppius Restitutus.

EDCS-69900162.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely indicating ownership or a dedication by Gaius Oppius Restitutus.

EDCS-69900163.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely indicating ownership or a dedication by Gaius Oppius Restitutus.

EDCS-69900164.summary: A fragmentary inscription likely recording ownership, possibly of a grave or object, belonging to Caius Fadius Secundus, Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-69900167.summary: This inscription records the origin of an item or work from the workshop of Turnio.

EDCS-69900169.translation: To the goddess Minerva, Gaius Servilius Maurinus, perpetual priest, fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-69900169.summary: This is a dedication to the goddess Minerva by Gaius Servilius Maurinus, a perpetual priest, who fulfilled a vow.

EDCS-70000012.translation: Sacred to the Dis Manes. Caecilia Tulla lived 47 years.
EDCS-70000012.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the death of Caecilia Tulla at the age of 47.

EDCS-70000013.translation: Sacred to the Dis Manes. Maxima, daughter of Maximi Kapito, lived 85 years.
EDCS-70000013.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the death of Maxima, daughter of Maximi Kapito, at the age of 85.

EDCS-70000015.translation: Sacred to the Dis Manes. Venerius Rogatus lived 35 years.
EDCS-70000015.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the death of Venerius Rogatus at the age of 35.

EDCS-70000016.translation: Sacred to the Dis Manes. Aelius Rogatus lived 35 years. Here lies Aelius Attius, who lived 27 years. Here lies.
EDCS-70000016.summary: This is a double funerary inscription recording the deaths of Aelius Rogatus and Aelius Attius.

EDCS-70000017.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that likely records the name of Plinius Rufinus, possibly as a dedication or owner.

EDCS-70000018.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Satrius Optatus lived 40 years, here he lies buried.
EDCS-70000018.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the death of Satrius Optatus.

EDCS-70000019.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Iulius Tertullus lived 13 years, here he lies.
EDCS-70000019.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the death of Iulius Tertullus.

EDCS-70000067.translation: Restitutus the faithful, buried on the 7th day before the Kalends of February in the 16th year of the 6th indiction. Good memory, Restitutus, the lord has deigned to call him from this transitory age to his kingdoms, where there is an eternal seat and eternal rest. Amen. He lived more or less 14 years, buried on the 7th day before the Kalends of February.
EDCS-70000067.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Restitutus, a faithful servant, indicating his burial date and approximate age.

EDCS-70000068.translation: Budala the faithful lived in peace more or less 15 years, buried on the 9th day before the Kalends in the 91st year of the 6th indiction.
EDCS-70000068.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Budala, a faithful servant, indicating her burial date and approximate age.

EDCS-70000069.translation: Florentius the faithful lived in peace more or less 2 years and 3 months, buried on the 1st day of the Ides of February in the 16th year of the 6th indiction.
EDCS-70000069.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Florentius, a faithful servant, indicating his burial date and approximate age.

EDCS-70000070.translation: Good memory, Fortunata, the lord has deigned to call her from this transitory age to his kingdoms, where there is an eternal seat and eternal rest. Amen. She lived in peace more or less
EDCS-70000070.summary: This is a fragmented funerary epitaph for Fortunata, mentioning her faithful life and heavenly calling.

EDCS-70000071.translation: Restitutus the faithful lived in peace 16 years and 74 days, buried on the 3rd day before the Kalends of April in the 36th year of the tenth indiction.
EDCS-70000071.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Restitutus, a faithful servant, indicating his burial date and precise age.

EDCS-70000072.translation: Matrona the faithful lived in peace more or less 35 years, buried on the 9th day before the Kalends of February in the 19th year of the 9th indiction.
EDCS-70000072.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Matrona, a faithful servant, indicating her burial date and approximate age.

EDCS-70000073.translation: Secundianus the faithful lived in peace 19 years and 138 days, buried on the 15th day before the Kalends of June in the 37th year of the 11th indiction.
EDCS-70000073.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Secundianus, a faithful servant, indicating his burial date and precise age.

EDCS-70000074.translation: Petrus the most eminent lived in peace 65 years, buried on the 15th day before the Kalends of July in the 10th indiction.
EDCS-70000074.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Petrus, indicating his age and burial date.

EDCS-70000087.translation: From the workshop of Lucius Iulius Romanus.
EDCS-70000087.summary: This inscription indicates the origin of a product from the workshop of Lucius Iulius Romanus.

EDCS-70000088.translation: From the workshop of Quintus Minucius Cremialis.
EDCS-70000088.summary: This inscription indicates the origin of a product from the workshop of Quintus Minucius Cremialis.

EDCS-70000089.translation: From the workshop of the Iulii.
EDCS-70000089.summary: This inscription indicates the origin of a product from the workshop of the Iulii family.

EDCS-70000091.translation: From the workshop of the freedmen.
EDCS-70000091.summary: This inscription indicates the origin of a product from the workshop of freedmen.

EDCS-70000095.translation: Matrona, a widow, lived in faith and rested in peace on the ninth day before the Kalends of February.
EDCS-70000095.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan and peaceful repose of a widow named Matrona.

EDCS-70000105.summary: This inscription likely records two individuals, Felicianus and Victoria, possibly as a dedication or a funerary notice.

EDCS-70000108.translation: To the unconquered, ever-August, most noble Caesar, by decree of the town councillors, at public expense.
EDCS-70000108.summary: This inscription records a public dedication to an emperor or Caesar, funded by the town council.

EDCS-70000110.translation: To the splendid order [in honor of] Nino, son of Lucius Turranius, of the Vicani Felicioris.
EDCS-70000110.summary: This inscription is a dedication by the local council to Nino, son of Lucius Turranius, associated with the Vicani Felicioris.

EDCS-70000122.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Aurelia Romana lived 61 years, 11 months, 21 days, 3 hours.
EDCS-70000122.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Aurelia Romana, detailing her age at death.

EDCS-70100184.translation: Gaius Pomponius Felicius, priest, made a sacred offering to Saturnus Augustus and willingly paid his vow.
EDCS-70100184.summary: This inscription records a religious act by Gaius Pomponius Felicius, a priest, who made an offering and fulfilled a vow to Saturnus Augustus.

EDCS-70200487.translation: Iulius, son of Publius, dutiful and pious, lived for 1 year, 10 months, and 6 days.
EDCS-70200487.summary: This is a tombstone commemorating Iulius, son of Publius, who died at a young age.

EDCS-70200497.translation: To Emperor Caesar Gaius Aurelius Valerius Diocletian, the Unconquered Augustus, Pious, Fortunate, chief priest, with tribunician power for the 6th time, consul for the 3rd time, father of the country, proconsul; and to Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Valerius Maximianus Herculius, the Unconquered [Augustus], [consul]...
EDCS-70200497.summary: A dedication honoring the emperors Diocletian and Maximian, detailing their titles and offices, likely from the late 3rd or early 4th century CE.

EDCS-70200503.translation: To our lords Emperors [Gaius] Valerius Diocletian and [Marcus Aurelius Valerius] Maximian and [Maximian]...
EDCS-70200503.summary: A dedication to the emperors Diocletian and Maximian, likely part of a larger inscription honoring their joint rule, late 3rd or early 4th century CE.

EDCS-70200504.translation: [...] to Aurelius Valerius Constantius and Galerius Valerius Maximianus, most noble Caesars.
EDCS-70200504.summary: A dedication to the Caesars Constantius and Maximian, likely a continuation of imperial dedications, dating to the Tetrarchic period (late 3rd/early 4th century CE).

EDCS-70200529.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Euvarcius lived for 38 years and 17 days. His wife made this for her dearest husband.
EDCS-70200529.summary: This tombstone records the death of Euvarcius, erected by his wife.

EDCS-70200530.translation: Publius Aelius Uranius Fortunatus lived for 12 years, 2 months, and 25 days. His parents made this.
EDCS-70200530.summary: This tombstone records the death of Publius Aelius Uranius Fortunatus, erected by his parents.

EDCS-70200531.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Volussia Amantia lived for 4 years, 4 months, and 5 days.
EDCS-70200531.summary: This tombstone records the death of Volussia Amantia, likely a child.

EDCS-70200532.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. For Lucius Septimius Agrippa, the sweetest infant, who lived for 11 years, 5 months, and 12 days. Lucius Septimius Agrippa, a centurion, his father, made this.
EDCS-70200532.summary: This tombstone records the death of Lucius Septimius Agrippa, an infant, erected by his centurion father.

EDCS-70200533.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. For Grania Vitalina, who lived for 3 years, 5 months, and 13 days. Her parents made this.
EDCS-70200533.summary: This tombstone records the death of Grania Vitalina, erected by her parents.

EDCS-70300005.summary: This inscription records that sons made a monument, though the dedicatee and location are lost.

EDCS-70300011.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Silvana, also known as Tsura, lived for 22 years.
EDCS-70300011.summary: This tombstone records the death of Silvana, who also went by the name Tsura.

EDCS-70300013.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Mustitonius Romanus.

EDCS-70300015.summary: This funerary inscription records the name Iniminius Pistius with the phrase 'in peace'.

EDCS-70300019.summary: This is a simple funerary epitaph for Issballa.

EDCS-70300021.summary: This is a funerary epitaph stating that Emerita rests here.

EDCS-70300022.summary: This is a Christian funerary epitaph for Cassica.

EDCS-70300025.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Felicitas.

EDCS-70300026.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Domitia, possibly repeated for emphasis.

EDCS-70300030.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Simplicius.

EDCS-70300035.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Iustine.

EDCS-70300036.translation: Ori, also called Memori, rests in peace, Memori
EDCS-70300036.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Ori, who is also identified as Memori.

EDCS-70300038.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Aprilis.

EDCS-70300042.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Lucius Maevius Valerianus, also called Moflontius, is buried here; he lived 35 years and 3 months.
EDCS-70300042.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the name, alias, and lifespan of Lucius Maevius Valerianus, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-70400036.summary: This inscription seems to record a greeting or dedication involving Invicta Apeona and Canna.

EDCS-70700100.translation: My dear brother, whom [3] knows, send [3] with him what [3] have, [send] ten denarii. I ask that they be directed to me because I hope [3] will pay [3] from the exotic [3] and I order [3] to trade [3] for me from the oil [3] and ask [3]...
EDCS-70700100.summary: A personal letter requesting money and business instructions, written on a wax tablet or similar medium, Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-70700104.translation: He has, by Sanius, six miles.
EDCS-70700104.summary: This inscription may relate to a boundary or measurement, possibly related to land owned by Sanius.

EDCS-70700120.translation: Days of the gymnasia from the will of Cornelius Egrilianus: January 1st, January 3rd, January 17th, January 23rd, January 27th, January 31st, February 7th, March 3rd, March 7th, March 9th, March 11th, March 13th, March 14th, March 16th, March 17th, March 19th, April 7th, April 8th, April 11th, April 15th, April 17th, April 18th, May 1st, May 5th, May 6th, May 9th, June 1st, June 2nd, June 11th, July 14th, August 1st, August 30th, September 11th, September 12th, September 13th, September 14th, October 10th, October 11th, October 13th, October 17th, October 18th, October 21st, October 21st, October 21st, October 21st, October 21st, October 21st.
EDCS-70700120.summary: This inscription lists a complex schedule of dates, likely related to the operation of public gymnasia as stipulated in a will.

EDCS-71100054.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. He is buried here, born from noble blood, Burpurius, superior in piety to all. He had recently completed sixty years of life, but now he obtains eternal rest in a peaceful dwelling, pleasing to the gods above, thus to the gods below. He is buried here.
EDCS-71100054.summary: A funerary epitaph for Burpurius, praising his noble birth and piety, and noting his death at sixty years of age, Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-71200007.summary: A short epitaph identifying Marcellina and mentioning her resting in peace, likely from a Christian context, Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-71200402.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Optatilia Fadilla, the pious, lived 11 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-71200402.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the name, epithet, lifespan, and burial place of Optatilia Fadilla, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-71200403.translation: Under the administration of the most invincible princes Flavius Polybius, a most distinguished man, there was grace and indeed splendor.
EDCS-71200403.summary: This inscription praises the administration of Flavius Polybius, likely during the reign of certain emperors.

EDCS-71200604.inscription_type: tituli honorarii, tituli operum, tituli sacri
EDCS-71200604.translation: For the safety of Emperor Caesar Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Augustus Pius and his children, Julia Paula Laenatiana, for the honor of her perpetual priesthood, [built] the temple of Minerva on private land and for its dedication gave gifts to the district and the community and the decurions, and to the whole people a gymnasium and a feast, overseen by the curators Asicius Adiutor and Marcus Terentius [---].
EDCS-71200604.summary: This inscription records a woman, Julia Paula Laenatiana, building a temple to Minerva and providing gifts and entertainment for the community and its officials, likely dating to the reign of Antoninus Pius.

EDCS-71200605.inscription_type: tituli honorarii, tituli operum, tituli sacri
EDCS-71200605.translation: For the safety of Emperor Caesar Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Augustus Pius and his children, Iulia Paula Laenati[ana], for the honor of her perpetual priesthood, [built] the temple of Minerva on private land and for its dedication gave gifts to the district and the community and the decurions, and to the whole people a gymnasium and a feast, overseen by the curators Asicio Adiuto[re] and Marcus Terentio Gell[io...].
EDCS-71200605.summary: This is a partially reconstructed version of the previous inscription, recording the same dedication by Julia Paula Laenatiana of a temple to Minerva and community gifts, likely during the reign of Antoninus Pius.

EDCS-71300300.text_edition: \n [[]] no Casto tribuno militum legionis III Augustae cives b VI Lepcitani[3]\n
EDCS-71300300.translation: [...] to Castus, tribune of the soldiers of the III Augusta legion, the citizens of Lepcis B[e]n[eficiarii...].
EDCS-71300300.summary: This fragmentary inscription records a dedication to a military tribune, Castus, by citizens identified as Lepcitani, likely from Lepcis Magna.

EDCS-71300302.translation: Sacred to the departed gods. Aelia Victoria lived for 40 years, cared for by her father Aelius Fortunatus.
EDCS-71300302.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the death of Aelia Victoria at the age of 40, with her father Aelius Fortunatus listed as the one who set up the monument.

EDCS-71300303.translation: Sacred to the departed gods. Aulus Cassius Sentius lived for 50 years.
EDCS-71300303.summary: This fragmentary tombstone inscription records the death of Aulus Cassius Sentius at the age of 50.

EDCS-71300306.translation: Sacred to the departed gods. Valgia Ingenua, most faithful, lived for 60 years.
EDCS-71300306.summary: This tombstone inscription records the death of Valgia Ingenua at the age of 60, with an epithet emphasizing her faithfulness.

EDCS-71300307.translation: Sacred to the departed gods. Apollonius, son of Vindicis, lived for 28 years.
EDCS-71300307.summary: This tombstone inscription records the death of Apollonius, son of Vindicis, at the age of 28.

EDCS-71300308.translation: Sacred to the departed gods. Donata lived for 22 years. May your bones rest well.
EDCS-71300308.summary: This tombstone inscription records the death of Donata at the age of 22 and includes a common Latin funerary wish.

EDCS-71300309.translation: Sacred to the departed gods. Fortunata lived for 2 years.
EDCS-71300309.summary: This tombstone inscription records the death of Fortunata at the age of 2.

EDCS-71300310.translation: Sacred to the departed gods, to the memory of Gaia Scuptis, who lived for 2[...].
EDCS-71300310.summary: This fragmentary tombstone inscription records the death of Gaia Scuptis, with the age at death partially lost.

EDCS-71300311.translation: Dedicated to the Spirits of the Departed. Iovinus lived 10 months and 7 days.
EDCS-71300311.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the short life of Iovinus, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-71300312.translation: Dedicated to the Spirits of the Departed. Pious Saturninus lived 47 years; his son Nabor [erected this].
EDCS-71300312.summary: A funerary epitaph for Saturninus, set up by his son Nabor, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-71300315.translation: Dedicated to the Spirits of the Departed. Aelia Gemella lived 60 years.
EDCS-71300315.summary: A funerary epitaph for Aelia Gemella, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-71300316.translation: Dedicated to the Spirits of the Departed. Cilia Fanent lived 20 years.
EDCS-71300316.summary: A funerary epitaph for Cilia Fanent, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-71300317.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Fuscha Audnia lived 80 years, a most dutiful and most sweet [person].
EDCS-71300317.summary: A funerary epitaph for Fuscha Audnia, describing her character, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-71300318.translation: Gaius Sempronius Auricinus lived 45 years; this [monument] his good son made for his parents.
EDCS-71300318.summary: A funerary epitaph for Gaius Sempronius Auricinus, erected by his son for his parents, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-71300319.translation: Quintus Menius Saturninus lived 85 years and 1 day.
EDCS-71300319.summary: A funerary epitaph for Quintus Menius Saturninus, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-71300320.translation: Dedicated to the Spirits of the Departed. Iulius Italicus lived 22 years, and his daughter Maia lived 1 month.
EDCS-71300320.summary: A funerary epitaph for Iulius Italicus and his daughter Maia, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-71300324.translation: On a good and fortunate day, Fausta established a boundary.
EDCS-71300324.summary: This is a boundary stone inscription, likely marking property, set up by Fausta.

EDCS-71300325.translation: On a good, prosperous, and fortunate day, Callus, son of Figulus, fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-71300325.summary: This is a votive inscription recording the fulfillment of a vow by Callus.

EDCS-71300353.summary: This is a fragmented inscription likely identifying a person and their origin.

EDCS-71800458.summary: This is a short Christian inscription or prayer.

EDCS-72000079.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari divi Septimi Severi Pii Arabici Adiabenici Parthici Maximi Britanici Maximi filius divi Marci Antonini Pii Germanici Sarmatici nepos divi Antonini Pii pronepos divi Hadriani abnepos divi Traiani Parthici et divi Nervae abnepos Marco Aurelio Antonino Pio Felici Augusto Parthico maximo Britanico maximo Germanico maximo pontifici maximo tribuniciae potestatis XVIIII imperatori III consuli IIII patri patriae proconsuli miliarius II\n
EDCS-72000079.translation: To Imperator Caesar, son of the divine Septimius Severus Pius Arabicus Adiabenicus Parthicus Maximus Britannicus Maximus, grandson of the divine Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Germanicus Sarmaticus, great-grandson of the divine Antoninus Pius, great-great-grandson of the divine Hadrian, great-great-great-grandson of the divine Trajan Parthicus and the divine Nerva, Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus, supreme Parthicus, Britannicus, Germanicus, chief priest, holding tribunician power for the 19th time, imperator for the 3rd time, consul for the 4th time, father of the fatherland, proconsul, builder of the 2nd milestone.
EDCS-72000079.summary: An imperial titulature inscription for Marcus Aurelius Antoninus (Caracalla), listing his titles and lineage, likely from the early 3rd century CE.

EDCS-72000082.translation: Dacicus Maximus restored bridges collapsed by age and a road corrupted by long neglect, and with his tireless foresight made it passable for travelers again for 9 miles.
EDCS-72000082.summary: This inscription commemorates the restoration of bridges and a road by Dacicus Maximus, likely a governor or official.

EDCS-72000084.text_edition: \n pontifex maximus tribuniciae potestatis consul pater patriae miliarium XXXVIIII\n
EDCS-72000084.translation: Chief priest, holding tribunician power, consul, father of the fatherland, builder of the 39th milestone.
EDCS-72000084.summary: An abbreviated imperial titulature or a dedication related to a milestone, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-72000085.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari divi Septimi Severi Pii Arabici Adiabenici Parthici maximi Britanici maximi filio et divi Nervae adnepoti Marco Aurelio Antonino Pio Felici Augusto Parthico maximo Britannico maximo Germanico maximo tribunicia potestate XVIIII imperatori III consuli IIII patri patriae proconsuli miliarium numero LXXXIIII\n
EDCS-72000085.translation: To Emperor Caesar, son of the deified Septimius Severus Pius Arabicus Adiabenicus Parthicus Maximus Britannicus Maximus, and great-great-grandson of the deified Nerva, Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus, Parthicus Maximus, Britannicus Maximus, Germanicus Maximus, with tribunician power for the 19th time, consul for the 3rd time, emperor for the 4th time, father of the country, proconsul, milemarker 84.
EDCS-72000085.summary: This is a milestone inscription from the reign of Caracalla, indicating a distance of 84 miles.

EDCS-72000088.text_edition: \n Imperator Caesar Marcus Antonius Gordianus Pius Felix Augustus miliarium numero L\n
EDCS-72000088.translation: To Emperor Caesar Marcus Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus, milemarker 50.
EDCS-72000088.summary: This is a milestone inscription from the reign of Gordian III, indicating a distance of 50 miles.

EDCS-72000091.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari divi Septimi Severi Pii Arabici Adiabenici \n
EDCS-72000091.translation: To Emperor Caesar, son of the deified Septimius Severus Pius Arabicus Adiabenicus.
EDCS-72000091.summary: This fragment likely belongs to a longer dedication, possibly a milestone or honorific monument, from the Severan period.

EDCS-72000093.translation: To the Emperor Caesar, son of the deified Septimius Severus Pius Arabicus Adiabenicus Parthicus Maximus Britannicus Maximus, grandson of the deified Antoninus Pius Germanicus Sarmaticus, great-grandson of the deified Antoninus Pius, great-great-grandson of the deified Hadrian, great-great-great-grandson of the deified Traianus Parthicus and the deified Nerva, Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus Parthicus Maximus Britannicus Maximus Germanicus Maximus, Pontifex Maximus, holding tribunician power for the 19th time, consul for the 3rd time, father of the country, proconsul, for a milestone.
EDCS-72000093.summary: This is a lengthy dedication for a milestone (miliarium) to Emperor Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus, detailing his extensive lineage and titles.

EDCS-72000094.summary: This is a fragment of a milestone inscription, likely recording a distance and referencing a proconsul.

EDCS-72000095.translation: To Emperor Caesar, son of the deified Septimius Severus.
EDCS-72000095.summary: This is a fragment of a dedication from the Severan period, likely a milestone or honorary inscription.

EDCS-72000098.translation: To the Emperor Caesar, son of the deified Septimius Severus Pius Arabicus Adiabenicus Parthicus Maximus Britannicus Maximus, grandson of the deified Antoninus Pius Germanicus Sarmaticus, great-grandson of the deified Antoninus Pius, great-great-grandson of the deified Hadrian, great-great-great-grandson of the deified Traianus Parthicus and the deified Nerva, Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus Parthicus Maximus.
EDCS-72000098.summary: This is a fragmentary dedication for a monument or milestone to Emperor Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus, listing his imperial lineage.

EDCS-72000099.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari divi Septimi Severi Pii Arabici Adiabenici Parthici maximi Brittanici maximi filio divi Antonini Pii Germanici Sarmatici nepoti divi Antonini Pii pronepoti divi Hadriani abnepoti divi Traiani Parthici et divi Nervae adnepoti Marco Aurelio Antonino Pio Felici Augusto Parthico maximo Brittanico maximo Germanico maximo pontifici maximo tribuniciae potestatis XIX imperatori III consuli IIII patri patriae proconsuli XXXII\n
EDCS-72000099.translation: To Emperor Caesar, son of the deified Septimius Severus Pius Arabicus Adiabenicus Parthicus Maximus Britannicus Maximus, grandson of the deified Antoninus Pius Germanicus Sarmaticus, great-grandson of the deified Antoninus Pius, great-great-grandson of the deified Hadrian, great-great-great-grandson of the deified Trajan Parthicus and great-great-grandson of the deified Nerva, Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus, Parthicus Maximus, Britannicus Maximus, Germanicus Maximus, chief priest, with tribunician power for the 19th time, emperor for the 3rd time, consul for the 4th time, father of the country, proconsul, milemarker 32.
EDCS-72000099.summary: This is a milestone inscription from the reign of Caracalla, indicating a distance of 32 miles and detailing his extensive titulature.

EDCS-72000101.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari divi Septimi Severi Pii Arabici Adiabenici Parthici maximi Brittanici maximi filio divi Antonini Pii Germanici Sarmatici nepoti divi Antonini Pii pronepoti divi Hadriani abnepoti divi Traiani Parthici et divi Nervae adnepoti M(arco) Aurelio Antonino Pio Felici Augusto Parthico maximo Brittanico maximo Germanico maximo pontifici maximo tribuniciae potestatis XIX imperatori III consuli IIII patri patriae proconsuli miliarium CXLIII\n
EDCS-72000101.translation: To Emperor Caesar, son of the deified Septimius Severus Pius Arabicus Adiabenicus Parthicus Maximus Britannicus Maximus, grandson of the deified Antoninus Pius Germanicus Sarmaticus, great-grandson of the deified Antoninus Pius, great-great-grandson of the deified Hadrian, great-great-great-grandson of the deified Trajan Parthicus and great-great-grandson of the deified Nerva, Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus, Parthicus Maximus, Britannicus Maximus, Germanicus Maximus, chief priest, with tribunician power for the 19th time, emperor for the 3rd time, consul for the 4th time, father of the country, proconsul, milemarker 143.
EDCS-72000101.summary: This is a milestone inscription from the reign of Caracalla, indicating a distance of 143 miles and detailing his extensive titulature.

EDCS-72000103.text_edition: \n Pio Felici Augusto Parthico maximo Brittanico maximo Germanico maximo pontifici maximo tribuniciae potestatis XIX imperatori consuli IIII patri patriae proconsuli numero XLVIIII\n
EDCS-72000103.translation: To the Pius Felix Augustus, Parthicus Maximus, Britannicus Maximus, Germanicus Maximus, chief priest, with tribunician power for the 19th time, emperor for the 4th time, consul, father of the country, proconsul, number 49.
EDCS-72000103.summary: This is a milestone inscription likely from the reign of Caracalla, indicating a distance of 49 miles and listing his honors.

EDCS-72400115.translation: To Marcus Aelius Aurelius Verus Caesar, son of the deified Augustus Pius, with tribunician power, consul for the 2nd time, at public expense by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-72400115.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Marcus Aurelius (as Caesar), sponsored by local town councillors, likely for a public work or monument.

EDCS-72500070.translation: Cornelia Fortuna, daughter of Spurius, priestess of the Augusta, pious, lived 45 years, lies here. May your bones rest well. May the earth lie lightly upon you.
EDCS-72500070.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Cornelia Fortunata, a priestess, recording her name, parentage, religious role, lifespan, and offering a common epitaph.

EDCS-72600340.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription for Marcus Novius, son of Titus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-72700002.translation: To our saviors, the Augusti and Caesar, Egnatuleius Crescens, a most distinguished man and governor of Numidia.
EDCS-72700002.summary: This inscription honors the emperors and is dedicated by Egnatuleius Crescens, governor of Numidia, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-72700005.translation: Emperor Caesar Gaius Julius Verus Maximinus Pius Felix Augustus, conqueror of the Germans, the Sarmatians, and the Dacians, pontifex maximus, holding tribunician power for the third time, acclaimed imperator for the seventh time. [Gaius] Julius Verus Maxi[minus...
EDCS-72700005.summary: This is a fragment of an imperial titulature inscription for Maximinus Thrax and his son, likely dating to his co-reign and the period of his third tribunician power.

EDCS-72700006.translation: ...holding tribunician power for the third time, acclaimed imperator for the fifth time, and Gaius Julius Verus Maximinus, most noble Caesar, prince of the youth, conqueror of the Germans, the Sarmatians, and the Dacians, restored the road from Carthage up to the borders of the province of Numidia, which had been corrupted and dilapidated through long neglect.
EDCS-72700006.summary: This inscription records the restoration of a road between Carthage and Numidia, undertaken by Maximinus Thrax and his son Maximinus Caesar, likely from the early 3rd century CE.

EDCS-72700007.translation: Emperor Caesar Marcus Antonius Gordianus, grandson of the deified Gordian...
EDCS-72700007.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription mentioning Emperor Gordian III, likely from the mid-3rd century CE.

EDCS-72700008.translation: To our lord, the Emperor Constantius Pius Felix Augustus.
EDCS-72700008.summary: This is a dedication to Emperor Constantius II, likely from the 4th century CE.

EDCS-72700009.translation: To our Lords Flavius Valentinianus and Valens, victorious, ever August Emperors, the municipality of Thignica.
EDCS-72700009.summary: This inscription is a dedication by the municipality of Thignica to the emperors Valentinian and Valens, likely from the 4th century CE.

EDCS-72700010.translation: To Caesar Marcus Aurelius Probus, pontifex maximus, holding tribunician power, consul for the fourth time, father of the fatherland.
EDCS-72700010.summary: This inscription honors Emperor Probus, likely dating to his fourth consulship and reign in the late 3rd century CE.

EDCS-72700017.summary: This is a tombstone recording the death of a person named Victor, who died at the age of 95.

EDCS-72700019.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Iulia Honorata, a dutiful daughter of Lucius, lived for 30 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-72700019.summary: This inscription is a tombstone for Iulia Honorata, recording her name, parentage, age at death (30), and burial.

EDCS-72700022.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Stinula, dutiful, lived for 16 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-72700022.summary: This is a tombstone for Stinula, recording her name, piety, age at death (16), and burial.

EDCS-72700024.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. [---]AV.
EDCS-72700024.summary: This is a fragmentary tombstone inscription, likely beginning with a dedication to the spirits of the departed and possibly a name.

EDCS-72700030.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Ani.
EDCS-72700030.summary: This is a fragmentary tombstone inscription, beginning with a dedication to the spirits of the departed and possibly a name.

EDCS-72700033.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Hilaria, dutiful, lived for [X] years.
EDCS-72700033.summary: This is a fragmentary tombstone inscription for Hilaria, recording her name and that she lived for an unspecified number of years.

EDCS-72700035.translation: In [---], a dutiful person, lived for 90 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-72700035.summary: This is a fragmentary tombstone recording that a dutiful individual, whose name is partially lost, lived for 90 years and is buried there.

EDCS-72700036.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Corus lived for 89 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-72700036.summary: This tombstone records the burial of Corus, who lived for 89 years.

EDCS-72700037.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Arius.
EDCS-72700037.summary: This is a fragmentary tombstone inscription, beginning with a dedication to the spirits of the departed and the name Arius.

EDCS-72700040.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Paiedius Placidus, pious, lived 20 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-72700040.summary: A funerary epitaph for Paiedius Placidus, who died at age 20.

EDCS-72700041.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Nomia Ina, pious, lived 35 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-72700041.summary: A funerary epitaph for Nomia Ina, who died at age 35.

EDCS-72700042.translation: Salius Primigenius, pious, lived 30 years. He is buried here. May your bones rest well; may the earth be light upon you.
EDCS-72700042.summary: A funerary epitaph for Salius Primigenius, who died at age 30, expressing wishes for his afterlife.

EDCS-72700045.translation: C. Maca, chaste and most modest, lamented her miserable life. His wife, Caes... twenty and
EDCS-72700045.summary: A fragmented funerary inscription possibly for C. Maca, lamenting her life.

EDCS-72700046.translation: Emperor Caesar, grandson of the deified Nerva, son of the deified Trajan Parthicus, Trajan Hadrianus Augustus, pontifex maximus, holding tribunician power for the seventh time, consul for the third time...
EDCS-72700046.summary: This is a fragment of an imperial titulature inscription for Emperor Hadrian, likely dating to his seventh tribunician power and third consulship, in the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-72700048.translation: The Emperor Caesar, consul for the third time. 86 [years?].
EDCS-72700048.summary: A fragmentary inscription mentioning an emperor and his third consulship, possibly with an age or date.

EDCS-72700053.translation: To Herennia Etruscilla, Augusta, mother of the camp, of the senate, and of the fatherland. 84 [years?].
EDCS-72700053.summary: An honorific inscription for Herennia Etruscilla, likely a notable imperial figure, possibly indicating her age.

EDCS-72700072.translation: To Lucius Sempronius Ianurius, an outstanding man, procurator of our Emperor, of the eighty-second rank, in charge of the patrimony.
EDCS-72700072.summary: A dedication to Lucius Sempronius Ianurius, honoring his career as an imperial procurator.

EDCS-72700081.translation: To Faustina Augusta, daughter of Emperor Caesar Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Augustus Pius, father of the fatherland...
EDCS-72700081.summary: This inscription honors Empress Faustina I, wife of Antoninus Pius, likely from the mid-2nd century CE.

EDCS-72700083.translation: Legio III Augusta demarcated with Gaius Vibius Marso, proconsul, for the third time: 70 quinarii in the front rank, 30 decumani, 350 beyond the dividing line.
EDCS-72700083.summary: This inscription records a financial demarcation by Legio III Augusta and proconsul Gaius Vibius Marso, likely from the 2nd century CE in Roman Africa.

EDCS-72700084.summary: A funerary epitaph for Donatianus, a deacon, who died at age 83.

EDCS-72700085.translation: Pompeianus the faithful lived in peace for 8 years, laid to rest on the Ides of May in the 9th indiction.
EDCS-72700085.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the age and burial date of Pompeianus.

EDCS-72700086.translation: Pompeianus the faithful lived for 1 year and 6 months in peace, rested on the 11th day before the Ides of December in the 2nd indiction.
EDCS-72700086.summary: This funerary inscription records the age and burial date of Pompeianus.

EDCS-72700087.translation: Pompeianus the faithful lived in peace for 45 years, [was buried?] the day before the Nones of May in the [?] indiction.
EDCS-72700087.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription recording the age and burial date of Pompeianus.

EDCS-72700088.translation: Marcianus, faithful, lived in peace for 26 years. He was laid to rest on the 9th day before the Kalends of November, under the fourth consulship.
EDCS-72700088.summary: A funerary epitaph for Marcianus, a faithful individual, who died at age 26, with a specific burial date and consular mention.

EDCS-72700090.translation: Doste, faithful in Christ, lived in peace for 1 year, 7 months, and Mas [?] for 20 years, 3 months. Year 5 of the indiction 11.
EDCS-72700090.summary: A funerary epitaph for Doste, a faithful Christian, with a complex dating of her life and death including a specific indiction year.

EDCS-72700091.translation: Mustelus, faithful in Christ, lived in peace for 27 years; he was buried on the Ides of May, in the indicated indiction.
EDCS-72700091.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Mustelus, a Christian who lived 27 years and was buried on a specific date.

EDCS-72700092.translation: Rogatianus, faithful, lived in peace for ninety years; he was buried in February, in the indicated indiction.
EDCS-72700092.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Rogatianus, who lived for 90 years and was buried in February.

EDCS-72700093.translation: Soracius, faithful, lived in peace for 26 years.
EDCS-72700093.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Soracius, a faithful person who lived for 26 years.

EDCS-72700094.translation: Alexsanter, a soldier, lived in peace for 40 years.
EDCS-72700094.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Alexsanter, a soldier who lived for 40 years.

EDCS-72700097.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Aurelius Restutus lived for 35 years.
EDCS-72700097.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the age of Lucius Aurelius Restutus.

EDCS-72700098.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcus Iunius Rogatianus lived for 3 years, is buried here.
EDCS-72700098.summary: This funerary inscription records the age and burial place of Marcus Iunius Rogatianus.

EDCS-72700099.translation: [Sacred to the departed spirits] Avielius Maximus lived for 18 years, is buried here.
EDCS-72700099.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription recording the age and burial place of Avielius Maximus.

EDCS-72700100.translation: Sextus Marius Pudens, son of Titus, lived for 21 years, is buried here.
EDCS-72700100.summary: This funerary inscription records the age and burial place of Sextus Marius Pudens.

EDCS-72700101.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Donatus, son of Siddinis, lived for 10 years, is buried here, interred.
EDCS-72700101.summary: This funerary inscription records the age and burial place of Donatus.

EDCS-72700102.translation: Hotmilcot Arinis [daughter?] of Labio lived for 71 years, is buried here.
EDCS-72700102.summary: This funerary inscription records the age and burial place of Hotmilcot Arinis.

EDCS-72700103.translation: Munda son of Aechanes lived for 75 years, is buried here.
EDCS-72700103.summary: This funerary inscription records the age and burial place of Munda.

EDCS-72700104.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Sattaras, son of Alauchus, lived 61 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-72700104.summary: A funerary inscription recording the name, parentage, age, and burial of Sattaras.

EDCS-72700105.translation: Amot, daughter of the dutiful Rusticus, daughter of Asmunis Macas, lived 26 years.
EDCS-72700105.summary: A funerary inscription recording the name, parentage, and age of Amot.

EDCS-72700106.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Coloapis, son of Fronto, the dutiful, lived 83 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-72700106.summary: A funerary inscription recording the name, parentage, age, and burial of Coloapis.

EDCS-72700107.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Tulius Rogatus lived 68 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-72700107.summary: A funerary inscription recording the name, age, and burial of Tulius Rogatus.

EDCS-72700108.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Valeria Lathinia lived 51 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-72700108.summary: A funerary inscription recording the name, age, and burial of Valeria Lathinia.

EDCS-72700109.translation: Publius Aufidius Saturninus, a veteran, saw to the construction of two columns at his own expense.
EDCS-72700109.summary: A dedication recording the commissioning of two columns by Publius Aufidius Saturninus, a veteran, at his own expense.

EDCS-72700110.translation: To the departed spirits. Nonius Lucius lived for 75 years.
EDCS-72700110.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the departed spirits, recording the lifespan of Nonius Lucius as 75 years.

EDCS-72700111.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Nonia Aurelia lived 82 years.
EDCS-72700111.summary: A funerary inscription recording the name and age of Nonia Aurelia.

EDCS-72700112.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Modia Victoria, the dutiful, lived 31 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-72700112.summary: A funerary inscription recording the name, epithet, age, and burial of Modia Victoria.

EDCS-72700113.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Baricbal Prima Serruma, the dutiful, lived 40 years.
EDCS-72700113.summary: A funerary inscription recording the names, epithet, and age of Baricbal Prima Serruma, with a lacuna at the end.

EDCS-72700114.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Moggui, son of Catton, lived for 85 years; he rests here.
EDCS-72700114.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the departed spirits, recording that Moggui Cattonis lived 85 years and rests here.

EDCS-72700116.translation: By decree of the decurions, at public expense, for Domitia Aurelia Faustina, daughter of Aurelius Caesar.
EDCS-72700116.summary: A public dedication honoring Domitia Aurelia Faustina, daughter of Aurelius Caesar, funded by public money by order of the town council.

EDCS-72800127.translation: Salius Pius Primigenius lived for 30 years; he rests here. May your bones rest well; may the earth rest lightly upon you.
EDCS-72800127.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Salius Pius Primigenius, who lived 30 years and is buried here, with wishes for a peaceful afterlife.

EDCS-73400410.summary: This inscription records a personal note about a person named Firma who lived.

EDCS-73400453.translation: To the departed spirits. Lucius Nonius Victor lived for 2 years and 1 month. Lucius Nonius Victor and Domitia Saturnina set this up for their sweetest son; he rests here.
EDCS-73400453.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Lucius Nonius Victor and Domitia Saturnina for their son, Lucius Nonius Victor, who died at the age of 2 years and 1 month.

EDCS-73400454.translation: Sacred to Victory Augusta. Marcus Junius Crescens, son of Africanus, a municipal official holding the quinquennial office, fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-73400454.summary: This is a dedication to Victory Augusta by Marcus Junius Crescens, likely a magistrate, who fulfilled a vow.

EDCS-73400455.translation: Sacred to Mars Augustus. Marcus Junius Crescens, son of Africanus, a magistrate holding the quinquennial office, fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-73400455.summary: This is a dedication to Mars Augustus by Marcus Junius Crescens, likely a magistrate, who fulfilled a vow.

EDCS-73400456.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Quintus Geminius Celsus, a soldier of the III Augusta legion, lived for 45 years, with 18 years of service. His tent-mates erected this.
EDCS-73400456.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Quintus Geminius Celsus, a soldier who served 18 years and lived 45 years, erected by his contubernales (tent-mates).

EDCS-73400458.translation: To Aemilius Himilis, son of Himilis, flamen Augusti.
EDCS-73400458.summary: This is a dedication, possibly funerary or honorary, for Aemilius Himilis, who held the position of flamen Augusti.

EDCS-73400459.translation: Marcus Junius Crescens, son of Afri, for Nemesis Augusta, as quinquennial duovir and munerarius, fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-73400459.summary: This inscription records a religious vow fulfilled by Marcus Junius Crescens, a local magistrate, to the goddess Nemesis Augusta, likely in the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-73400460.translation: Marcus Junius Crescens, son of Afri, for Nemesis Augusta, as quinquennial duovir and munerarius, fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-73400460.summary: This inscription records a religious vow fulfilled by Marcus Junius Crescens, a local magistrate, to the goddess Nemesis Augusta, likely in the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-73900281.translation: Dedicated to the departed spirits. Felix, son of Macrinus and Menotis, lived piously for 73 years. Likewise Maior, daughter of Extricatus, lived piously for 68 years.
EDCS-73900281.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Felix and Maior, recording their pious lives and ages.

EDCS-73900282.translation: Dedicated to the departed spirits. Aulus Egnatius Mulinus lived piously for 45 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-73900282.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Aulus Egnatius Mulinus, recording his pious life and age.

EDCS-73900284.translation: From the workshop of Modius Julianus.
EDCS-73900284.summary: This inscription indicates a place of origin or ownership, likely related to a workshop or business.

EDCS-73900285.translation: To Jupiter Augustus sacred. To the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Commodus Antoninus Augustus Germanicus Sarmaticus Maximus, holding tribunician power for the 7th time, consul for the 3rd time, father of the country, son of the divine Marcus Antoninus Pius Germanicus Sarmaticus, grandson of the divine Antoninus Pius, great-grandson of the divine Hadrian, great-great-grandson of the divine Trajan Parthicus, great-great-great-grandson of the divine Nerva. [Gaetulicus] promised and contributed 2,000 sesterces and an additional 4,000 sesterces from the office of [decurion?] for the construction of the temple with a marble statue, marble columns, and all its furnishings, and the steps of the platform, and beyond that, for two [columns?], he promised and contributed, and on the day of dedication and the celebrations, he gave gifts to the decurions for the dedication, a gymnasium, and games to the entire populace.
EDCS-73900285.summary: This complex inscription records a large dedication by Gaetulicus to Jupiter Augustus and likely commemorates an imperial visit or significant public works, including a temple, gymnasium, and games, under Commodus.

EDCS-73900287.translation: Greatest Pontiff, with tribunician power, Emperor, Consul, Proconsul, 71.
EDCS-73900287.summary: This fragmentary inscription lists imperial titles and a number, likely referring to a high-ranking official or emperor, possibly dating to the late Roman period.

EDCS-73900431.translation: To the most peaceful Emperor, our Augustus, Lucius Domitius Aurelianus Invictus Pius Felix. 94.
EDCS-73900431.summary: This is an acclamation or dedication to Emperor Aurelian, likely dating to his reign.

EDCS-74000013.translation: For the Emperors Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus and Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus and [Publius] Septimius [Geta] Caesar Augustus and Julia Augusta, mother of the camp. A cistern.
EDCS-74000013.summary: This inscription records the construction of a cistern under the joint rule of Septimius Severus, Caracalla, Geta, and Julia Domna.

EDCS-74000023.summary: This inscription appears to be in a language other than Latin or is heavily abbreviated/corrupted, and its meaning is unclear.

EDCS-74100051.translation: Zimarcus lived in peace for 65 years and 9 months, buried.
EDCS-74100051.summary: This epitaph records the lifespan of Zimarcus, who lived for 65 years and 9 months and was buried, likely from the early Christian period.

EDCS-74100259.translation: Sacred to Mars Augustus. For the safety of the Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pertinax Augustus Adiabenicus, [---]. [---]. The curia of Mars, they built and dedicated a shrine from the ground up and a statue with their own money, a place having been given [---].
EDCS-74100259.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a shrine and a statue to Mars Augustus and for the emperor's safety, funded by the curia Martis, likely dating to the reign of Septimius Severus.

EDCS-74100266.translation: Vicentius the faithful lived for 70 years. Restitutus the faithful lived for 80 years. Vicentius rested on the Kalends of June. Restitutus rested on the 13th day before the Kalends of May.
EDCS-74100266.summary: This epitaph commemorates two individuals, Vicentius and Restitutus, providing their lifespans and dates of rest, characteristic of early Christian burial inscriptions.

EDCS-74100267.summary: This brief epitaph mentions Upaetoria and her daughters, indicating they are at peace, likely from the early Christian period.

EDCS-74100268.summary: This short epitaph states Ioulianus is in peace, a common formula for early Christian burials.

EDCS-74100269.summary: This epitaph describes Dardanius as innocent and in peace, a typical early Christian inscription.

EDCS-74100270.summary: This inscription identifies Flavius Vitalis as a bishop, likely from the late Roman or early Byzantine period.

EDCS-74200160.translation: Faunus; Oricimuicus; Leontius; Spina; [---]ecta; Pinnatus; Auspicator; Eventus.
EDCS-74200160.summary: This inscription is a list of names, possibly belonging to a group or individuals commemorated on a monument, with no further context provided.

EDCS-74300095.translation: After the consulship of our lords Valentinian and Valens Augusti, on the third day before the Nones of June. I, Pomponius Maximus, son of Rogatus, of the estate of Goretianus, being of sound mind and sound memory, have made this testament, and I have had it written by Iulius Secundus, who is also Secundianus, whose trustworthiness I have experienced. I dictated it on triple tablets in ink, and since I could not find the prepared codex at present, I offered it for signing after it was read to me. My sons Pomponius Soricus Letorianus and Rogatianus, and Maximus, my dearest sons, are to be heirs of all my possessions in equal portions from the farms Pasinianus, Goretianus, Guruli Iuliani, Bosonis, also called Musunis, and other places within the boundaries of the estates, except for those things which I have specifically given to Letorianus and Rogatianus, my sons and heirs, in equal portions. They are to be my heirs, that is, my son and heir Letorianus shall have a fourth part of all my possessions, and also the fields in the estate Pasinianus which are called Liconis, with their boundaries, access roads, slopes, and hills, which came to me from the inheritance of Rogatus, my late father, and any personal property which he has acquired or will acquire. My son and heir Rogatianus shall have a fourth part of all my possessions, and also the fields in the estate Pasinianus which are called Lierapix, with their boundaries, access roads, slopes, and hills, and personal property.
EDCS-74300095.summary: This is a detailed testament inscribed on stone, likely in the late 4th century CE, by Pomponius Maximus, outlining the inheritance and property distribution among his sons, with specific provisions for land and personal property.

EDCS-74300264.translation: Sacred to Pluto Augustus, the Genius of the people of Aunobarissa. Marcus Numisius Martialis, their patron, with his own funds, rebuilt the temple walls damaged by an earthquake, and equipped it with a statue of the god and all other decorations, spending 10,000 sesterces from the foundations, and he also purchased the area in front of the temple, with Marcus Numisius Martialis, their patron, as curator.
EDCS-74300264.summary: This inscription records the rebuilding and dedication of a temple to Pluto and the Genius of the people of Aunobarissa, funded by Marcus Numisius Martialis, who also purchased the forecourt.

EDCS-74300426.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Caelia Pia lived 55 years.
EDCS-74300426.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the name and lifespan of Caelia Pia.

EDCS-74300427.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Messe.
EDCS-74300427.summary: This is a very brief funerary inscription, likely recording the name of the deceased, Messe.

EDCS-74400135.translation: Sacred to Augustus. Publius Nonius Victor, as priest and prefect with the right to judge, and twice as chief magistrate, for his period as chief magistrate, added 1,000 sesterces from his own funds to the honorific sum required for construction, and he himself dedicated it.
EDCS-74400135.summary: This inscription records the honors and public works undertaken by Publius Nonius Victor during his magistracies, funded partly by himself.

EDCS-74700031.translation: By the authority of Quintus Junius Rusticus, prefect of the city, a man of consular rank. (Weight) ten pounds.
EDCS-74700031.summary: This inscription records a decree or authorization made by Quintus Junius Rusticus, prefect of the city, and a weight of ten pounds, likely related to official business or a levy.

EDCS-74700522.translation: To the Emperor Caesar, son of the deified Septimius Severus Pius Arabicus Adiabenicus Parthicus Maximus Britannicus Maximus, grandson of the deified Marcus Antoninus Pius Germanicus(?), great-grandson of the deified Antoninus Pius, great-great-grandson of the deified Hadrian, great-great-great-grandson of the deified Trajan and deified Nerva, [son's son] Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Augustus Parthicus Maximus Britannicus Maximus [Germanicus].
EDCS-74700522.summary: This is a lengthy imperial titulature inscribed on a monument, glorifying Marcus Aurelius Antoninus (likely Caracalla) by listing his divine ancestors and his own titles, dating to his reign.

EDCS-74700526.translation: Philip [with tribunician power, consul designate for the third time, father of the country, proconsul] and Marcus Julius Philippus nobilissimus Caesar Augustus, prince of the youth, and Marcia Otacilia Severa Augusta, mother of the Emperor Caesar Augustus, and of the camp, and of the senate, and of the country. Seventy-eight.
EDCS-74700526.summary: This inscription lists the titles and honors of the emperors Philip I and his son Philip II, along with Empress Otacilia Severa, possibly on a public monument or milestone, dating to their co-reign.

EDCS-75100001.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Egnatia Donata, pious, lived 12 years, is buried here.
EDCS-75100001.summary: This funerary inscription records the name, age, and burial of Egnatia Donata.

EDCS-75200007.translation: To our lord Flavius Claudius Constantinus the most noble Caesar, to our lord Constantius the most noble Caesar, to our lord Magnus Decentius the most noble Caesar, Emperor, to our lord Flavius Theodosius Augustus.
EDCS-75200007.summary: This inscription is a dedication or acknowledgment of several contemporary emperors and caesars, likely from the mid-4th century CE.

EDCS-75200008.translation: To our lord Flavius Valerius Constantinus.
EDCS-75200008.summary: This is a dedication to Emperor Constantine the Great, likely from the early 4th century CE.

EDCS-75200097.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the name and age of the deceased, Bernus.

EDCS-75200099.summary: This is likely a tombstone inscription recording the name and age of the deceased, Flabia.

EDCS-75200103.summary: This inscription appears to be a tombstone marking the burial of Auo Anibon, possibly indicating their well-being or a dedicatory offering.

EDCS-75200105.translation: Selhan lived 61 years; Flabia lived 75 years.
EDCS-75200105.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the names and ages of two individuals, Selhan and Flabia.

EDCS-75200107.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the name and age of the deceased, Ariston.

EDCS-75200108.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of an individual.

EDCS-75200110.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Balerianus.

EDCS-75200111.translation: To Mercury, the healer, [dedicated by] VI.
EDCS-75200111.summary: This is a dedication to the god Mercury as a healer, with the dedicator identified by the numeral VI.

EDCS-75200115.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Galeria.

EDCS-75200116.translation: Luna lived [X] years. Leptana lived [X] years.
EDCS-75200116.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespans of two individuals, Luna and Leptana.

EDCS-75200117.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Demetrius.

EDCS-75200119.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Domitius.

EDCS-75200120.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Nearca.

EDCS-75200122.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Rogata.

EDCS-75200123.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Iambart.

EDCS-75200124.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Iambart.

EDCS-75200128.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespans of two individuals, Arisus and another person whose name is lost.

EDCS-75200129.summary: This epitaph records the exceptionally long lifespan of an individual named Therus.

EDCS-75200130.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the name and lifespan of Teius.

EDCS-75200131.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication, although partially damaged and unclear, it records a child named Mamar who lived 3 years.

EDCS-75200132.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespan of a young girl named Peregrinia.

EDCS-75200133.translation: Saturna died before the third month.
EDCS-75200133.summary: This epitaph records the death of Saturna, indicating she died before the third month of a year.

EDCS-75200134.summary: This epitaph records the age of an individual identified as 'grandfather' at the time of their death.

EDCS-75200135.summary: A tombstone recording the lifespan of Guda, who died at the age of 10.

EDCS-75200138.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespan of an individual named Mercuras.

EDCS-75200139.summary: This epitaph records the partial lifespan of an individual named Irus, with the exact age lost.

EDCS-75200143.summary: This epitaph commemorates Agag, describing him as an innocent boy.

EDCS-75200144.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan of an individual whose name is lost.

EDCS-75200145.summary: This epitaph records the age of an individual identified as 'grandfather Amonis' at the time of their death.

EDCS-75200146.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the age of the deceased, Kallios, at death.

EDCS-75200148.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Avolim.

EDCS-75300322.translation: To our lords Emperors Flavius Valerius Constantinus and Galerius Valerius Maximianus, most pious, fortunate, unconquered Augusti, when they were consuls for the fifth time.
EDCS-75300322.summary: A dedication to Emperors Constantinus and Maximianus, dating to a period when they both held the consulship for the fifth time.

EDCS-75300323.translation: Of Valerius Pudentis Marsilliani, a man of clarissimal rank.
EDCS-75300323.summary: A fragmentary inscription likely recording the name and status of Valerius Pudentis Marsilliani.

EDCS-75300325.translation: Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Severus Antoninus Pius Augustus, greatest victor in Parthia, greatest victor in Britain, greatest victor in Germany, holder of tribunician power for the 18th time, consul for the 3rd time, father of the fatherland, restored.
EDCS-75300325.summary: An imperial inscription detailing the titles and achievements of Emperor Caracalla, indicating he restored something, likely a building or monument.

EDCS-75300331.translation: To our Emperors Caesars Gaius Aurelius Valerius Diocletianus Pius Invictus Augustus, four times, and Marcus Aurelius.
EDCS-75300331.summary: A dedication to Emperors Diocletian and Maximian (whose name is only partially preserved), referring to their multiple consulships.

EDCS-75300332.translation: Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Augustus, greatest victor in Parthia, greatest victor in Britain, greatest victor in Germany, holder of tribunician power for the 19th time, consul for the 4th time, father of the fatherland, established.
EDCS-75300332.summary: An imperial inscription detailing the titles and achievements of Emperor Caracalla, indicating he established something, likely a building or monument.

EDCS-75300335.translation: To our most pious, fortunate, unconquered Augustus Flavius Valerius Constantinus, born for the good of the state.
EDCS-75300335.summary: A dedication to Emperor Constantine, praising him as beneficial to the state.

EDCS-75300336.translation: To our lords Emperors Gaius Valerius Diocletianus Pius Felicis Invictissimis Augusti, when they were consuls.
