EDCS-75300336.summary: A dedication to Emperors Diocletian and Maximian, noting their consulship.

EDCS-75300337.translation: To our lord Licinius Licinianus Pius Felicis Augustus.
EDCS-75300337.summary: A dedication to Emperor Licinius, praising his piety and good fortune.

EDCS-75300338.translation: To Flavius Valerius Crispinus, most noble Caesar.
EDCS-75300338.summary: This inscription is a dedication, likely on a monument, to Flavius Valerius Crispinus, who held the title of Caesar and is described as most noble, probably dating to the 4th century CE.

EDCS-75300339.translation: To our lord Flavius Julius Constantius, most noble and most flourishing Caesar, born for the good of the state.
EDCS-75300339.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Emperor Constantius I, referring to him as 'Caesar' and praising his birth for the benefit of the public, likely from the late 3rd or early 4th century CE.

EDCS-75300341.translation: Crementius and his associates to the god Neptune, built a temple at their own expense, with Tertius as master, urging them on.
EDCS-75300341.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a temple to Neptune, built at private expense by Crementius and his associates, under the supervision of Tertius as magister, probably from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-75300342.translation: Emperor Caesar Marcus Antonius Gordianus, grandson of the deified Marcus Antonius Gordianus, son of the sister of the deified Marcus Antonius Gordianus, Pious, Fortunate, Augustus, Most Holy, Most Fortunate.
EDCS-75300342.summary: A titulary inscription for Emperor Gordianus III, likely from the 3rd century AD, listing his imperial titles and lineage.

EDCS-75300345.translation: Kalendio lived 85 years in peace. He rested on the 7th day before the Kalends of May.
EDCS-75300345.summary: A tombstone recording the lifespan and date of death (April 25th) of Kalendio in the 3rd-4th century AD.

EDCS-75300346.translation: Florentia the faithful rested in peace on the 7th day before the Ides of May.
EDCS-75300346.summary: A tombstone recording the death date (May 9th) of Florentia, a faithful Christian, from the 3rd-4th century AD.

EDCS-75300347.translation: Paulina lived 70 years in peace. She died the day before the Ides of October.
EDCS-75300347.summary: A tombstone recording the lifespan and date of death (October 14th) of Paulina, a Christian, from the 3rd-4th century AD.

EDCS-75300348.translation: From the gifts of God, Crescens the presbyter made this.
EDCS-75300348.summary: A dedication inscription by Crescens, a presbyter (priest), likely related to a church or religious building, possibly from the Late Roman or early Byzantine period.

EDCS-75300350.translation: Emperor Caesar Marcus Antonius Gordianus, grandson of the deified Gordian, son of the deified Gordian's sister, Pius Felix Augustus, pontifex maximus.
EDCS-75300350.summary: This inscription is a titulature of Emperor Gordian III, listing his imperial titles and ancestry, dating to his reign in the mid-3rd century CE.

EDCS-75300352.summary: A fragmentary inscription with the names Tiberius Claudius, possibly the beginning of a longer dedication or epitaph.

EDCS-75300353.translation: To Aulus Gabinius Dato, son of Aulus, of the Arnensis tribe, flamen of the deified Titus, enrolled in the five decuries by Emperor Caesar Trajan Hadrian Augustus, patron of the village and of the city, the village and city of Thugga, placed (this monument) with their own money, with [---] supervising and dedicating.
EDCS-75300353.summary: This inscription records the erection of a monument by the people of Thugga in honor of Aulus Gabinius Dato, who held significant civic and religious positions, including flamen and a position granted by Emperor Hadrian, dating to the Hadrianic period (mid-2nd century CE).

EDCS-75300354.translation: [...] of Abentius, a man of consular rank, judging with vice sacra, so that he might render greater favor to the portico of the village and the temples.
EDCS-75300354.summary: A fragmentary inscription recording a decision made by a high-ranking official (vice sacra iudicantis) regarding public works, likely from the imperial period.

EDCS-75300355.translation: May all things be fortunate for you.
EDCS-75300355.summary: A short, positive inscription, possibly a personal greeting or wish, suitable for various contexts.

EDCS-75300356.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Chrysanthus, freedman of the emperor, chief steward, made this for his well-deserving friend Titus Flavius Venustus, freedman of Emperor Domitian Augustus, who lived eighty years without torture.
EDCS-75300356.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Titus Flavius Venustus, a freedman of Emperor Domitian, who lived to 80, with the monument erected by his friend Chrysanthus, also an imperial freedman and steward, likely from the late 1st or early 2nd century CE.

EDCS-75300359.translation: Emperor Caesar Gaius Vibius Trebonianus Gallus, Pius Felix Augustus, pontifex maximus, holding tribunician power for the second time, father of the country, consul designate for the second time, proconsul; and Emperor Caesar Gaius Vibius Afinius Gallus Veldumnianus Volusianus.
EDCS-75300359.summary: This inscription is a fragment of an imperial titulature, listing the titles of Emperors Trebonianus Gallus and Volusianus, dating to their joint reign in the mid-3rd century CE.

EDCS-75300361.translation: To our lord Flavius Valerius Constantinus Pius Felix Victor, always Augustus, pontifex maximus, holding tribunician power for the 15th time, consul for the 6th time, acclaimed emperor for the 14th time, father of the country, proconsul. The council of the municipality of Zicchilium placed (this) through its liberality, with Marcus Lutatius Luzanus, son of Marcus, curator of public affairs, overseeing and dedicating.
EDCS-75300361.summary: This inscription is a dedication by the municipality of Zicchilium to Emperor Constantine I, listing his extensive titles and powers, dating to his later reign, around 324-325 CE.

EDCS-75300365.translation: Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Augustus Parthicus maximus, Britannicus maximus, Germanicus maximus, with tribunician power for the 19th time, consul for the 4th time, father of the fatherland, restored this in the year 250.
EDCS-75300365.summary: An imperial rescript inscription by Emperor Gallienus (dated by tribunician power and consulships) recording the restoration of something in the year 250 AD.

EDCS-75300370.translation: To our lord and emperor, Flavius Valerius Constantinus Augustus, the greatest German, the eternal Augustus, born for the good of the Republic.
EDCS-75300370.summary: This is an honorific inscription dedicated to Emperor Constantine I, dating to his reign in the early 4th century CE.

EDCS-75300373.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription, likely honorific, mentioning an emperor named Flavius, possibly Constantine I or another emperor with that name.

EDCS-75300374.translation: To our lord Flavius Valerius Severus, most noble Caesar.
EDCS-75300374.summary: This is an honorific inscription for the Caesar Flavius Valerius Severus, likely dating to the early 4th century CE when he served as Caesar.

EDCS-75300375.translation: Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Probus Pius Felix Augustus, chief priest, with tribunician power, father of the country, twice consul, proconsul, restored this in the 172nd year.
EDCS-75300375.summary: This inscription records a restoration by Emperor Probus, dating to his reign (276-282 CE) and mentioning a local era ('172nd year').

EDCS-75300376.translation: To our lords Valentinian, Valens, and Gratian, always Augusti.
EDCS-75300376.summary: This is an honorific inscription dedicated to the co-emperors Valentinian I, Valens, and Gratian, dating to their joint reign between 367 and 375 CE.

EDCS-75300382.translation: Prosperity in peace. Victory in peace.
EDCS-75300382.summary: This is a short, possibly votive or celebratory, inscription expressing wishes for success and victory.

EDCS-75300383.translation: Petrus, the procurator of the agrarian lands of the Nigrensian Casarum, you have yielded me the Puteos agrarian land; for the soldier Serbus, I have made this for you from the collection, only in the month of April, in the fifteenth indiction.
EDCS-75300383.summary: This inscription records a transaction concerning land management and potentially tax collection by an official named Petrus, dating to the 15th indiction (likely in the 4th-6th centuries CE).

EDCS-75300384.translation: Comitas, the procurator of the agrarian lands of the Nigrensian Casarum, you have yielded me the eighth agrarian land of the indiction.
EDCS-75300384.summary: This inscription records a transaction concerning land management by an official named Comitas, referring to the 8th indiction (likely in the 4th-6th centuries CE).

EDCS-75400168.translation: To the prince of youth, Flavius Valerius Constantius, most noble Caesar. The colony Aelia Hadriana Augusta of the Bullenses Regii, devoted to his divine majesty and his greatness.
EDCS-75400168.summary: This inscription is a dedication by the colony of Aelia Hadriana Augusta to Flavius Valerius Constantius, honoring him as 'prince of youth' and 'most noble Caesar', likely from the 4th century CE.

EDCS-75500083.translation: Marcus Aelius Marcellus, veteran of the III Augusta legion, served for 25 years, lived for 70 years. He lies here.
EDCS-75500083.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Marcus Aelius Marcellus, a veteran of a Roman legion, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-75500084.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. To Marcus Etoxus, dearest brother, he lived 23 years, 2 months, 18 days, 11 hours. He lies here.
EDCS-75500084.summary: This is a tombstone inscription dedicated to Marcus Etoxus by a relative, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-75600168.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the name and peaceful repose of Indulgentius.

EDCS-75600169.translation: Preiecta lived in peace, she rested for VI Nones of July, in the third indiction.
EDCS-75600169.summary: This funerary epitaph records the name, lifespan, date of repose, and indiction for Preiecta.

EDCS-75600179.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the name and faithful repose of Tius.

EDCS-75600252.translation: Indulgentius lived for 42 years, he rested in peace on the fifth day of February.
EDCS-75600252.summary: This funerary epitaph records the name, lifespan, and date of repose for Indulgentius.

EDCS-75600253.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Florillus lived for 98 years. May the earth lie lightly upon you.
EDCS-75600253.summary: This funerary epitaph is dedicated to the departed spirits and records the name and lifespan of Florillus.

EDCS-75600254.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Antonia Prima lived for 115 years. Sacred to the departed spirits. Artema the Third lived for 75 years.
EDCS-75600254.summary: This funerary epitaph is dedicated to the departed spirits and records the names and lifespans of Antonia Prima and Artema the Third.

EDCS-75700090.translation: Iulia Gududia, pious, sober, faithful, lived for 63 years, she lies here.
EDCS-75700090.summary: This funerary epitaph records the name, virtues, lifespan, and burial location of Iulia Gududia.

EDCS-75700194.translation: Titia, daughter of Namphama, pious, lived 60 years. Here she lies. May your bones rest well, may the earth lie light upon you.
EDCS-75700194.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Titia, daughter of Namphama, who lived to 60 years, including common Latin funerary formulae, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-75700196.summary: This inscription likely records the names of Gaius Cornelius Fuscus and Aemilia, possibly as part of a dedication or funerary monument.

EDCS-75700197.translation: Gaius Cesennius Secundus, dutiful, lived 75 years.
EDCS-75700197.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the name, piety, and age at death of Gaius Cesennius Secundus.

EDCS-75700198.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription identifying someone as the son of Decimus.

EDCS-75700199.translation: Gaius Rasinius Faustus, veteran, dutiful, lived 50 [plus] years. Here he lies.
EDCS-75700199.summary: This funerary inscription commemorates the veteran Gaius Rasinius Faustus, noting his piety and age at death.

EDCS-75700200.translation: [---] Manlius, son of Lucius, of the Quirina tribe, Receptus, aedile, duovir, perpetual flamen(?), lived [---] years.
EDCS-75700200.summary: This incomplete inscription records the career of Manlius Receptus, who held various municipal magistracies and priesthoods.

EDCS-75700201.translation: Cornelia Fausta, daughter of Sextus, dutiful(?), lived 26 years.
EDCS-75700201.summary: This funerary epitaph records the name, parentage, and age at death of Cornelia Fausta.

EDCS-75700202.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription beginning with the name Titus Veturius, possibly part of a larger text.

EDCS-75700203.summary: This is a fragment of a funerary inscription for Capito, son of Cossutius, noting his lifespan.

EDCS-75700205.translation: May your bones rest well. Iulia Rosa, daughter of Caius, dutiful, lived 100 years. Here she lies. May the earth lie lightly upon you.
EDCS-75700205.summary: This epitaph is for Iulia Rosa, who lived to 100 years of age, and includes common funerary formulae.

EDCS-75700206.translation: Sextus Pompeius, son of Sextus, of the Quirina tribe, R[---], lived 75 years. Here he lies.
EDCS-75700206.summary: This funerary inscription records the name, tribal affiliation, lifespan, and burial place of Sextus Pompeius.

EDCS-75700207.translation: Gargilia Zara, dutiful, lived 35 years. Here she lies.
EDCS-75700207.summary: This funerary inscription records the name, piety, age at death, and burial of Gargilia Zara.

EDCS-75700208.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Gaius Pontius Umbrianus, son of [---], a veteran, served for [3] years. He lived for [3] years. He is buried here.
EDCS-75700208.summary: A tombstone for Gaius Pontius Umbrianus, a veteran, indicating his military service and lifespan.

EDCS-75900077.text_edition: \n Imperatore Caesare Marco Aurelio Antonino Augusto pontifice maximo tribunicia potestate XVI consule III et Imperatore Caesare Lucio Aurelio Vero Augusto tribunicia potestate II consule II aedem Apollinis pecunia publica facta Quinto Voconio Saxa Fido proconsule Marcus Ummidius Annianus Quadratianus legatus fecit idemque dedicavit\n
EDCS-75900077.translation: Under Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus, pontifex maximus, in his sixteenth year of tribunician power, and consul for the third time, and Emperor Caesar Lucius Aurelius Verus Augustus, in his second year of tribunician power, and consul for the second time, Marcus Ummidius Annianus Quadratianus, legate, built the temple of Apollo with public funds and dedicated it, while Quintus Voconius Saxa Fidus was proconsul.
EDCS-75900077.summary: A dedication for the construction and dedication of the temple of Apollo, commissioned by Marcus Ummidius Annianus Quadratianus under the joint consulship of Marcus Aurelius and Lucius Verus, during the proconsulship of Quintus Voconius Saxa Fidus.

EDCS-75900483.summary: This inscription appears to be a dedication or commendation of someone named Clarus, possibly in an official capacity, by a council.

EDCS-75900484.summary: This funerary epitaph records the name, faithfulness, and lifespan of Spendeus.

EDCS-75900485.translation: Quadratianus lived in peace for 60 years; he departed on the 6th day before the Kalends of October.
EDCS-75900485.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan and death date of Quadratianus.

EDCS-76100169.translation: Aurelius Chrestinus and Caelia Dativa made this for their daughter Caelia Chrestina, on account of her innocence.
EDCS-76100169.summary: A funerary monument set up by Aurelius Chrestinus and Caelia Dativa for their daughter Caelia Chrestina.

EDCS-76100170.translation: Istidius lived for 15 years, 7 months, and 15 days.
EDCS-76100170.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Istidius.

EDCS-76100171.translation: Urbanus set this up for his most beloved wife, Varia Victoria, for remembrance, on account of their cohabitation for 45 years.
EDCS-76100171.summary: A memorial for Varia Victoria, erected by her husband Urbanus after 45 years of marriage.

EDCS-76100173.summary: A simple epitaph for Vincentia, indicating her peaceful repose.

EDCS-76100176.summary: This is a funerary epitaph simply stating the name Benatia, implying peaceful repose.

EDCS-76100177.summary: This is a funerary epitaph simply stating the name Innocentia, implying peaceful repose.

EDCS-76100178.translation: Severina lived for 7 years, 5 months, and 20 days.
EDCS-76100178.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Severina.

EDCS-76100179.translation: Exitiosa lived for 5 years and 2 months.
EDCS-76100179.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Exitiosa.

EDCS-76100180.translation: Aurelius Iustianus lived for 2 years, 1 month, and 13 days.
EDCS-76100180.summary: An epitaph recording the short lifespan of Aurelius Iustianus.

EDCS-76300055.translation: Marcus Caecilius Honoratus set this up for his dearest brother, [---] Caecilius [---] Secundus, son of [---] Secundus, [---] honored with public office, [---] prefect of the first cohort of Thracians, Roman citizens, perpetual flamen. The place was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-76300055.summary: A funerary monument for Secundus, a former prefect and flamen, erected by his brother Marcus Caecilius Honoratus and approved by the local council.

EDCS-76300056.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Laberia Lena was placed here for remembrance; she lived for 55 years.
EDCS-76300056.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated to the memory of Laberia Lena, recording her age at death.

EDCS-76300057.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Gaius Ceius, son of Marcus, of the Arnensian tribe.
EDCS-76300057.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicating the burial to the Spirits of the Departed and identifying the deceased, Gaius Ceius.

EDCS-76300058.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. C. Nampamo lived for 45 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-76300058.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated to the Spirits of the Departed, identifying C. Nampamo and recording his age at death.

EDCS-76600228.translation: clarissimus vir, proconsul of the province of Africa.
EDCS-76600228.summary: This fragmentary inscription refers to a clarissimus vir (a man of senatorial rank) who served as proconsul of Africa.

EDCS-77300052.translation: Nerva, decurion, elected to the curia, [in the] vicus [of] Basibus, in[th...]
EDCS-77300052.summary: This inscription seems to record the membership of Nerva as a decurion and his election to the curia in the vicus of Basibus, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-77400004.translation: Publius Annius Fuscus Masurius, son of Lucius Annius Constans, lived for 15 years.
EDCS-77400004.summary: An epitaph recording the lifespan of Publius Annius Fuscus Masurius.

EDCS-77400005.translation: Gaius Selius Felix made this for himself and his family.
EDCS-77400005.summary: A funerary monument commissioned by Gaius Selius Felix for himself and his household.

EDCS-77400006.summary: A fragmentary inscription likely related to Publius Faustinus Rufus.

EDCS-77400007.summary: This is a simple funerary inscription identifying Flavia Annia Maximosa, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-77400008.summary: This inscription records the name of Flavia Aponia Saloninula, likely a tombstone or an epitaph.

EDCS-77400010.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely referring to Publius Laetorius Triones, possibly a dedication or funerary marker from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-77400011.summary: This inscription, mentioning Constantine and the concept of 'peace,' is likely a funerary text from the Late Roman or Early Christian period.

EDCS-77400013.translation: To Maxima, in peace and serenity, your soul
EDCS-77400013.summary: This is a funerary inscription wishing peace and serenity to the soul of Maxima, likely dating to the Late Roman or Early Christian period.

EDCS-77400014.translation: Scribonia lived five years more or less, in peace
EDCS-77400014.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespan of Scribonia as approximately five years, mentioning her passing 'in peace,' likely from the Late Roman or Early Christian period.

EDCS-77400017.translation: Sabbat(i)olus, who is also Iubentinus, placed in peace.
EDCS-77400017.summary: This inscription records the burial of Sabbat(i)olus, also known as Iubentinus, with the deceased being placed in peace.

EDCS-77400052.summary: This inscription lists angelic or divine names, likely from a funerary or religious context, possibly dating to the Late Roman or Early Christian period, reflecting syncretic beliefs.

EDCS-77700143.translation: Lucius Marius Paulinus fulfilled his vow
EDCS-77700143.summary: This inscription records Lucius Marius Paulinus fulfilling a votive offering, typical of Roman religious practice, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-77700144.translation: Publius Saturninius Guddul, son of Publius, fulfilled his vow
EDCS-77700144.summary: This inscription records Publius Saturninius Guddul, son of Publius, fulfilling a votive offering, typical of Roman religious practice, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-77700145.translation: Marcus Vettius Lupus, son of Titus, fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-77700145.summary: This inscription records Marcus Vettius Lupus, son of Titus, fulfilling a vow, likely on a religious monument.

EDCS-77700146.translation: Quintus Vettius Datus, son of Titus, fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-77700146.summary: This inscription records Quintus Vettius Datus, son of Titus, fulfilling a vow, likely on a religious monument.

EDCS-77700153.translation: Publius Popillius Neo, son of Publius, freedman, a merchant, is buried here.
EDCS-77700153.summary: This inscription records the burial of Publius Popillius Neo, a freedman and merchant.

EDCS-77700154.translation: Sacred to Saturn Augustus. The gift was given and they dedicated it: Marcus Valerius Longinus Marcianus and Valeria Proculina, children, and placed it
EDCS-77700154.summary: This inscription records a dedication of a sacred gift to Saturn Augustus by Marcus Valerius Longinus Marcianus and Valeria Proculina, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-77700201.translation: To Flavius Caecilius Primus, their custodian, manager, and procurator, a most excellent man, the founder of all the new estates, who served in the Glebonian estate for 40 years, and afterward, after this inscription was written, administered it again for some years. Let those who have lived hear and those who will live learn to love their patrons thus, to give faith and affection, praise, and to imitate such a witness. Here Primus, and elsewhere, he built a new estate from its foundations with all his possessions, and in other estates, many of his possessions were lacking, he built [---] and according to our accounts and through the course of years, down to the smallest statue and the bath of Satus VINCO.
EDCS-77700201.summary: This is a funerary and commendatory inscription for Flavius Caecilius Primus, detailing his long service as an administrator and his founding of new estates.

EDCS-78300369.translation: Aquilia Blaesilla, a most distinguished woman, his sister, erected this to Marcus Aquilius, son of Caius Haterianus, by the will of Aquilius Postumius, his father.
EDCS-78300369.summary: This funerary monument was erected by a sister for her brother, Marcus Aquilius Haterianus, following the wishes of their father.

EDCS-78300370.translation: To Aquilia Blaesilla, daughter of Caius, [---] most excellent.
EDCS-78300370.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Aquilia Blaesilla.

EDCS-78300372.translation: Bonifatius, a penis in indivisible life.
EDCS-78300372.summary: A short, crude inscription mentioning a person named Bonifatius.

EDCS-78300373.translation: Victor, son of Nabor, willingly fulfilled his vow with his own expense.
EDCS-78300373.summary: This inscription records Victor, son of Nabor, willingly and at his own expense fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-78300374.translation: To the Divine Shades. Alphinius’ wife, Gadda, made this. She lived 64 years.
EDCS-78300374.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Gadda, wife of Alphinius, who lived 64 years.

EDCS-78300375.translation: Publius Pullus lived 75 years, 10 months, and 27 days. He gained profit. He lived well.
EDCS-78300375.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Publius Pullus, detailing his lifespan and a concluding remark on his life.

EDCS-78300376.translation: Dedicated to the Spirits of the Dead. [Name]adius lived 25 years.
EDCS-78300376.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of a person named [3]adius, who lived 25 years.

EDCS-78300379.translation: Dedicated to the Spirits of the Dead. For his dearest wife Fabricia Donatilla, [Name] Veturius Speratus erected this statue for her merits; she lived 27 years.
EDCS-78300379.summary: This funerary inscription records Veturius Speratus erecting a statue for his wife Fabricia Donatilla, honoring her merits, and states she lived 27 years.

EDCS-78300380.translation: Sacred to Sobrius Augustus Mercury, for the well-being of Hadrian Augustus. Ianuarius, son of Merula, fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-78300380.summary: This inscription records Ianuarius Merulae fulfilling a vow to Mercury Sobrius Augustus for the health of Emperor Hadrian.

EDCS-78300381.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Vilania Rogata, dutifully.
EDCS-78300381.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Vilania Rogata.

EDCS-78300382.translation: Titus Paetius Protoctetus built a bath with his own land and money, and after holding a feast for the people, he dedicated it, and by his generosity, he donated it to the community of Galita.
EDCS-78300382.summary: This is a dedication inscription for a public bath built and donated by Titus Paetius Protoctetus to the community of Galita.

EDCS-78300383.translation: Sacred to Neptune and the August Nymphs. The community of Thabor, with its suffetes Secundus, son of Zdruba, and Verus, son of Marcellus, fulfilled their vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-78300383.summary: This inscription records the community of Thabor, through its officials Secundus Zdrubalis and Verus Marcelli, fulfilling a vow to Neptune and the Nymphs.

EDCS-78300385.translation: Names of those who contributed to the statues of Quintus Geminius Faustus and his sons. Vibius Pudens, perpetual flamen, priest of the divine Severus, 200 denarii, moreover for the transport of one base, 25 denarii.
EDCS-78300385.summary: This inscription records contributions made by Vibius Pudens for the erection of statues and their bases in honor of Quintus Geminius Faustus and his sons.

EDCS-78300387.translation: To the Emperor Caesar, Flavius Constantinus Maximus Pius Felix Invictus Augustus.
EDCS-78300387.summary: This is a dedication to Emperor Constantine the Great.

EDCS-78300391.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely honoring Emperor Severus, possibly marking a monument or a dedication.

EDCS-78300392.translation: To the most pious, fortunate Emperor Maxim(us) Augustus, from the devoted colony Julia Augusta Numidica Simitthus. Twice devoted.
EDCS-78300392.summary: This inscription records the devotion of the colony of Simitthus to Emperor Maxim(us) Augustus, possibly indicating a repeated pledge of loyalty.

EDCS-78300394.translation: Lucius Gavius Felix and Valeria Isara, for the honor of the perpetual flamonic office, had this built at their own expense, for the Roman district.
EDCS-78300394.summary: This inscription records a private benefaction by Lucius Gavius Felix and Valeria Isara, who funded the construction of something related to the perpetual flamonic office in the Roman district.

EDCS-78300395.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Corfidia Tertia lived 110 years. Here she lies. Felicius and Fortunatus placed this for their devoted mother.
EDCS-78300395.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Corfidia Tertia, who lived to be 110, erected by her sons Felicius and Fortunatus.

EDCS-78300396.translation: Quintus Cornelius Felix, son of Quintus, of the Quirina tribe, lived 70 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-78300396.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Quintus Cornelius Felix, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-78400198.translation: O Me Lampo, Phacarpotion who is also Nilus.
EDCS-78400198.summary: This is a Greek inscription, likely funerary or dedicatory, mentioning a person named Phacarpotion, also known as Nilus.

EDCS-79200019.translation: Patricius, do not doubt that I am present with you in concord, which carries out undertakings, which preserves the minds of the curia; you have made me pleased, I shall willingly place my steps.
EDCS-79200019.summary: This is a poetic inscription, possibly related to politics or personal sentiment, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-79200022.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Vibulena Privata, pious, lived 20 years; she is buried here. May your bones rest well; may the earth be light upon you. Sacred to the Divine Shades.
EDCS-79200022.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Vibulena Privata, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-79200023.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Caius Domitius Iulianus lived 8 years; he is buried here. May your bones rest well.
EDCS-79200023.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Caius Domitius Iulianus, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-79200139.translation: Sacred to Saturn Augustus. Beru esivius, priest, willingly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-79200139.summary: This is a dedication to Saturn Augustus, made by the priest Beru esivius, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-79200140.translation: Sacred to Saturn Augustus. Gaius Petronius, priest.
EDCS-79200140.summary: This is a dedication to Saturn Augustus, made by the priest Gaius Petronius, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-79200141.translation: Sacred to Saturn. Marcus nius Bassus, priest.
EDCS-79200141.summary: This is a dedication to Saturn, made by the priest Marcus nius Bassus, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-79200142.translation: Sacred to Saturn. Publius Petronius Proculus vowed willingly.
EDCS-79200142.summary: This is a dedication to Saturn, made by Publius Petronius Proculus, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-79200145.translation: To Saturn Cryptensis Purpuratus, the first priests A...
EDCS-79200145.summary: This is a dedication to Saturn Cryptensis Purpuratus by priests, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-79200146.translation: Octavia, pious daughter of Sextus, lived 35 years; she is buried here.
EDCS-79200146.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Octavia, recording her name, parentage, piety, age at death, and burial.

EDCS-79200147.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Julius Biosus, pious son of Rogatus, lived 103 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-79200147.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Julius Biosus, recording his name, parentage, piety, age at death, and burial.

EDCS-79200148.translation: Publius Aulius Mustinus, pious son of Publius, of the Arnensis tribe, lived 5 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-79200148.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Publius Aulius Mustinus, recording his name, parentage, tribal affiliation, piety, age at death, and burial.

EDCS-79300035.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Sissinas the pious lived 21 years. His heir placed this for his friend.
EDCS-79300035.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Sissinas, who died at age 21, with the monument erected by his heir for his friend.

EDCS-79300080.translation: To Saturn of Crypta, Purpuratus, first priest, and to Salustius Felix, first in the temple, I (dedicated this) PEROVO (statue/offering) to my temple.
EDCS-79300080.summary: This inscription records a dedication to the god Saturn and his priest Salustius Felix, possibly by a temple official named PEROVO.

EDCS-79600002.translation: To Marcus Vibius Gemellus Marcianus, son of Lucius, of the Arnensian tribe, patron of the district and the city, for his exceptional generosity by which he adorned our homeland with most excellent temples, the city of Thugga, by decree of the decurions, erected this at public expense, with the curatorship of Mucius Felix, the senior sufete, and Julius Macro, son of Felicis.
EDCS-79600002.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a monument by the city of Thugga to Marcus Vibius Gemellus Marcianus, a patron honored for his generosity in building temples, with officials named.

EDCS-79600003.translation: 3000 sesterces to the curators Marcus Vibius Rogatus, son of Marcus, and Marcus Morasius.
EDCS-79600003.summary: This inscription records a financial transaction, possibly a donation or payment, involving 3000 sesterces to two curators.

EDCS-79600050.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Rutilius Primitivus, a shipping agent for the navigators of Suff..., his friends made this. To Pomponia Crescentia, his most beloved wife. Publius Turpilius Victor, husband, and Turpilia Victoria, daughter, made this.
EDCS-79600050.summary: This inscription is a double funerary monument, first honoring Rutilius Primitivus, an agent for shipping interests, and then his wife Pomponia Crescentia, with both epitaphs erected by surviving family members.

EDCS-79600051.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Aemilia Bonifatia, a most beloved and incomparable woman, lived 22 years, 2 months, and 15 days. Severianus, her husband, made this for the deserving woman.
EDCS-79600051.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Aemilia Bonifatia, who died at a young age, erected by her husband Severianus.

EDCS-79600052.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Lucius Licinius lived 20 years. Faustus, his father, [placed this] for his son.
EDCS-79600052.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary epitaph for Lucius Licinius, who died at age 20, erected by his father Faustus.

EDCS-79600053.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Unda of Augusta, lived 8 months.
EDCS-79600053.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Unda of Augusta, recording her name and age at death in months.

EDCS-79600055.summary: This is a fragmented inscription likely related to a marriage or a dedication to a wife, mentioning a duration of 60 years.

EDCS-79600058.summary: This is a very brief inscription indicating that Marcus vius was the maker of something.

EDCS-79600059.translation: To the god Fruit-Bearer. Marcus Pomponius Montanus dedicated this offering.
EDCS-79600059.summary: This is a dedication of a votive offering to the god Frugifer by Marcus Pomponius Montanus.

EDCS-79600060.translation: To Lucius Caelio Saturninus, son of Caius Caelio, Flamen of Augustus, and former duovir, by the curiales of the college of Liber Pater, as patron, for his merits, they made (this) with their own money.
EDCS-79600060.summary: This is a dedication by a college to a patron, likely commemorating his service to the community and religious office, dating possibly to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-79600062.translation: Marcus Antonius Perm, flamen, willingly fulfilled (his) vow.
EDCS-79600062.summary: This inscription records a religious vow fulfilled by Marcus Antonius Perm, who held the office of flamen.

EDCS-79600063.translation: Lucius Furnius us willingly fulfilled (his) vow to Saturn.
EDCS-79600063.summary: This inscription records a religious vow fulfilled by Lucius Furnius us to the god Saturn.

EDCS-79600064.translation: To the departed spirits. Lucius Appius Donatus, son of Donatus, called Nigrinianus, lived for 54 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-79600064.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the name, patronymic, filiation, cognomen, and age of a deceased individual, likely from the 2nd to 3rd century CE.

EDCS-79600066.translation: To the departed spirits. Ennius Op[tatus?] lived.
EDCS-79600066.summary: A funerary inscription commemorating the life of Ennius Op[tatus?].

EDCS-79600067.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Epaenis lived, a pious Cas[s---?]
EDCS-79600067.summary: A funerary inscription for Epaenis, recording her pious life.

EDCS-79600068.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that likely records the name and origin of an individual, with the date being uncertain but potentially Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-79600069.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcus Julius Celerio lived for 27 years, 11 months, and 16 days.
EDCS-79600069.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the name and lifespan of a deceased individual, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-79600071.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the name and lifespan of a deceased individual, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-79600072.translation: Natesius the pious lived 96 years and... months.
EDCS-79600072.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the name, epithet, and lifespan of a deceased individual, with an unusually long lifespan noted, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-79600075.translation: He lived 62 years. He lies here. Sitius Secundus, his son.
EDCS-79600075.summary: A tombstone for Sitius Secundus, son of the deceased, who lived 62 years.

EDCS-79600098.translation: To Mercury, the holy ancestral god. Quintius, freedman of August[us?], assistant of the record office for the overseas accounts, dedicated an altar with his statue.
EDCS-79600098.summary: A dedication to the god Mercury by Quintius, an administrative official, likely from the imperial period.

EDCS-79600221.translation: Constantia lived in peace for 55 years and died on the 7th of the Ides of August. Gaudiosa lived in peace for 22 years and died on the 3rd of the Ides of May. [---]
EDCS-79600221.summary: A Christian funerary inscription recording the lives and death dates of Constantia and Gaudiosa.

EDCS-79600222.translation: Felix the presbyter lived for 98 years.
EDCS-79600222.summary: A funerary inscription for Felix, a presbyter (priest), likely from a Christian context.

EDCS-79600223.translation: Maxutius the presbyter lived in peace for 90 years. He rested on the 11th day before the Kalends of September.
EDCS-79600223.summary: A Christian funerary inscription for Maxutius, a presbyter, noting his lifespan and date of repose.

EDCS-79600224.translation: Florentius the presbyter, accepted by God, lived in peace for 75 years. He rested on the 11th day before the Kalends of May.
EDCS-79600224.summary: A Christian funerary inscription for Florentius, a presbyter, mentioning his acceptance by God and date of repose.

EDCS-79600225.translation: Victor lived in peace for 92 years. He rested on the 10th of the Ides of December.
EDCS-79600225.summary: A Christian funerary inscription recording the life and repose date of Victor.

EDCS-79600226.translation: Passibus the lector lived in peace for 14 years. He rested on the 11th day before the Kalends of October.
EDCS-79600226.summary: A Christian funerary inscription for Passibus, a lector, noting his young age and date of repose.

EDCS-79600227.translation: Generosus the presbyter lived 40 years in peace and rested on the 15th day before the Kalends of September.
EDCS-79600227.summary: This inscription records the death of Generosus, a presbyter, who lived 40 years and died on August 18th.

EDCS-79600228.translation: Concordius lived 3 years in peace and was accepted on the 7th day before the Ides of December.
EDCS-79600228.summary: This inscription records the death of Concordius, who lived 3 years and died on December 6th.

EDCS-79600229.translation: Felix lived 12 years in peace and rested on the Ides of July.
EDCS-79600229.summary: This inscription records the death of Felix, who lived 12 years and died on July 15th.

EDCS-79600230.translation: Lucida the faithful lived 60 years in peace and rested on the 11th day before the Ides of March.
EDCS-79600230.summary: This inscription records the death of Lucida, who lived 60 years and died on March 2nd.

EDCS-79600231.translation: Quintus the faithful lived 65 years in peace and rested on the 6th day before the Kalends of March.
EDCS-79600231.summary: This inscription records the death of Quintus, who lived 65 years and died on February 23rd.

EDCS-79600232.translation: Florentina lived 60 years in peace and rested on the 11th day before the Ides of January.
EDCS-79600232.summary: This inscription records the death of Florentina, who lived 60 years and died on January 2nd.

EDCS-79600233.summary: This incomplete inscription records Lucius, who was faithful in peace.

EDCS-79600234.translation: Felix lived 6 years in peace and died on the 3rd day before the Kalends of August.
EDCS-79600234.summary: This inscription records the death of Felix, who lived 6 years and died on July 30th.

EDCS-79600235.translation: Felix the faithful lived 78 years and 5 months in peace.
EDCS-79600235.summary: This inscription records Felix, who lived 78 years and 5 months and was faithful in peace.

EDCS-79600236.translation: Matziceus the faithful lived 42 years in peace and rested on the 15th day before the Kalends of June.
EDCS-79600236.summary: This inscription records the death of Matziceus, who lived 42 years and died on May 18th.

EDCS-79600237.translation: Aurus lived in peace for 85 years and rested on the 3rd day before the Kalends of December.
EDCS-79600237.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan and date of rest for Aurus.

EDCS-79600238.translation: Victor the faithful lived in peace for 70 years and rested on the Ides of August.
EDCS-79600238.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan and date of rest for Victor.

EDCS-79600239.translation: Lauricia the faithful lived for 24 years and rested on the 6th day before the Kalends of October.
EDCS-79600239.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan and date of rest for Lauricia.

EDCS-79600240.translation: Bonifatius lived in peace for 35 years and died on the Nones of August.
EDCS-79600240.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan and date of death for Bonifatius.

EDCS-79600241.translation: Bonifatius the innocent lived 11 years in peace and died on the 6th day before the Ides of December.
EDCS-79600241.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan and date of death for Bonifatius Innox.

EDCS-79600242.translation: Maxus the faithful lived in peace for 11 years and rested on the Ides of December.
EDCS-79600242.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan and date of rest for Maxus.

EDCS-79600243.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Octavianus, identified as a deacon.

EDCS-79600244.summary: This is a very brief funerary inscription for Grecus.

EDCS-79600245.translation: Grecus the faithful lived for 27 years in peace and rested on the 18th day before the Kalends of October.
EDCS-79600245.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan and date of rest for Grecus.

EDCS-79600246.translation: Rusticus the faithful gave back on the 16th day before the Kalends of May.
EDCS-79600246.summary: This funerary inscription records the date of death for Rusticus, with 'gave back' implying he returned his soul to God.

EDCS-79600247.summary: This epitaph records the deacon Isportella, who died in peace.

EDCS-79600248.translation: Naucelius lived for 40 years in peace and rested on the 9th day before the Ides of August.
EDCS-79600248.summary: This epitaph records the lifespan and death date of Naucelius, who died in peace.

EDCS-79600249.translation: Naucelius lived for 45 years in peace and rested on the day before the Ides of November.
EDCS-79600249.summary: This epitaph records the lifespan and death date of Naucelius, who died in peace.

EDCS-79600250.translation: Victoricus lived for 75 years in peace and rested on the 13th day before the Kalends of May.
EDCS-79600250.summary: This epitaph records the lifespan and death date of Victoricus, who died in peace.

EDCS-80000233.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that likely records the name of an individual, possibly a tombstone or a dedication, with the date being uncertain but potentially Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-80100126.summary: This is a name inscription for Gaius Atilius Vestalis, likely for a tomb.

EDCS-80100163.summary: This inscription records that the Honoratianii family made a monument or object.

EDCS-80100164.summary: This inscription records that the Honoratianii family made a monument or object.

EDCS-80100165.summary: This inscription records that the Honoratianii family made a monument or object.

EDCS-80100166.summary: This inscription records that the Victorinianii family made a monument or object.

EDCS-80300094.translation: Marcus Planius, son of Lucius, of Russinus.
EDCS-80300094.summary: This is a funerary or ownership inscription identifying Marcus Planius, son of Lucius, of Russinus.

EDCS-80300095.translation: Of Marcus Planius Russinus, son of Lucius.
EDCS-80300095.summary: This inscription is a simple filiation and gentilician name, likely part of a larger inscription or a funerary marker.

EDCS-80300096.translation: Of Marcus Planius Russinus, son of Lucius.
EDCS-80300096.summary: This inscription is a simple filiation and gentilician name, likely part of a larger inscription or a funerary marker.

EDCS-80300097.translation: Of Marcus Planius Russinus, son of Lucius.
EDCS-80300097.summary: This inscription is a simple filiation and gentilician name, likely part of a larger inscription or a funerary marker.

EDCS-80300113.translation: To the outstanding man Fulvius Paterno, the outstanding man who led the First Adjutant Legion and three hundred sesterces.
EDCS-80300113.summary: This inscription honors Fulvius Paterno for his service to the First Adjutant Legion and includes a monetary amount, possibly a dedication or a record of payment.

EDCS-80600003.translation: To Lucius Octavius Fortunatus, son of Lucius, of the Papiria tribe, priest of the Augusti, twice chief magistrate, for his loyalty in public affairs and his diligent work on the temple and the entire curia.
EDCS-80600003.summary: This is a dedication to Lucius Octavius Fortunatus, a local official, recognizing his loyalty and contributions to public works, likely from the late 1st or early 2nd century CE.

EDCS-80600005.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Clodia Tertia. [---]
EDCS-80600005.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Clodia Tertia, indicating it is a dedication to the Divine Spirits, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-80600006.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Marcus Summesius Ianuarius lived for 17 years.
EDCS-80600006.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Marcus Summesius Ianuarius, who died at the age of 17, dedicated to the Divine Spirits.

EDCS-80600007.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. For Marcus Otacilius Rogatianus the Younger, who lived for 20 years.
EDCS-80600007.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Marcus Otacilius Rogatianus the Younger, who died at the age of 20, dedicated to the Divine Spirits.

EDCS-80600008.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Mamonicus Marcius Otacilius Rogatianus.
EDCS-80600008.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the Divine Spirits for Mamonicus Marcius Otacilius Rogatianus.

EDCS-80600009.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Julius Optatus lived for 75 years. He lies here.
EDCS-80600009.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Julius Optatus, who died at the age of 75, dedicated to the Divine Spirits, indicating his burial place.

EDCS-80600011.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Villia Victoria, dutiful, lived 71 years. She is buried here.
EDCS-80600011.summary: A tombstone inscription for Villia Victoria, who lived 71 years.

EDCS-80600012.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Felicitas, dutiful, lived 23 years.
EDCS-80600012.summary: A tombstone inscription for Felicitas, who lived 23 years.

EDCS-80600013.translation: Rogata the packer gladly paid her vow to Saturn.
EDCS-80600013.summary: A votive inscription by Rogata, a packer, to the god Saturn.

EDCS-80600015.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Saturninus.

EDCS-80600016.summary: A tombstone inscription for Luria Quintula, who lived 5 months.

EDCS-80600018.translation: To the Health of the Augusti, Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus Arabicus Adiabenicus Parthicus Maximus, father of the fatherland, and Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus, and...
EDCS-80600018.summary: This is a fragmentary dedication to the health of Emperors Septimius Severus and Marcus Aurelius Antoninus, dating to their joint rule, likely early 3rd century CE.

EDCS-80600019.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Lucius Iunius Datus lived 82 years and [his wife?] lived 65 years.
EDCS-80600019.summary: A tombstone inscription for Lucius Iunius Datus and his wife.

EDCS-80600020.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Gaia Apronia Ianuaria, dutiful, lived just over 1 year.
EDCS-80600020.summary: A tombstone inscription for Gaia Apronia Ianuaria, who lived just over 1 year.

EDCS-80600021.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Exorata, dutiful, lived 38 years. May the earth lie lightly upon you.
EDCS-80600021.summary: A tombstone inscription for Exorata, who lived 38 years.

EDCS-80600022.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Restituta, dutiful, lived 45 years, 9 months, and 4 days. May the earth lie lightly upon you.
EDCS-80600022.summary: A tombstone inscription for Restituta, who lived 45 years, 9 months, and 4 days.

EDCS-80600025.translation: To Lucius Pullaenius, son of Marcius, of the tribe Quirina, shipmaster, prefect of the First Cohort of Ituraeans.
EDCS-80600025.summary: A dedication to Lucius Pullaenius, a shipmaster and prefect of an auxiliary cohort.

EDCS-81000079.translation: The monument of Cai Valerius Romanus, who is Amasvalath, which his sons Fronto and Acavas, the craftsman Masof, made.
EDCS-81000079.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a monument by sons for their father, Cai Valerius Romanus.

EDCS-81000122.summary: This inscription is a simple name, likely marking a tomb or ownership.

EDCS-81000123.summary: This inscription is a genitive name, likely related to ownership or a funerary context.

EDCS-81000124.summary: This inscription is a genitive name, likely related to ownership or a funerary context.

EDCS-81100017.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that likely records the name of an individual, possibly a tombstone or a dedication, with the date being uncertain but potentially Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-81100018.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that likely records the name of an individual, possibly indicating ownership or a dedication, with the date being uncertain but potentially Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-81100041.summary: This is a very brief inscription, likely the name of the person commemorated or the maker of the object, possibly from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-81100042.summary: This inscription consists of a personal name, Lucius Munatius Phile, likely identifying an individual, possibly from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-81200038.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Aurelia [---]a, pious, lived [---] years. Julius Primus made this for his well-deserving friend.
EDCS-81200038.summary: This funerary inscription records the dedication of a tomb by Julius Primus for his friend Aurelia.

EDCS-81200039.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Marcus Minucius Fidelis lived 70 years, 5 months. Nothing was, nothing is mine. Nothing pains me.
EDCS-81200039.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the death of Marcus Minucius Fidelis, who lived 70 years and 5 months, with a philosophical reflection on mortality.

EDCS-81300088.inscription_type: tituli honorarii, tituli sacri, tituli sepulcrales

EDCS-81300090.translation: Tiberius Larcius Carialis, Quintus Clodius Crescens, [son]nianus, Quintus +AR[---]
EDCS-81300090.summary: This inscription appears to list multiple Roman names, possibly indicating a group of individuals or a dedication, with incomplete information.

EDCS-81300091.translation: Gaius Vibius Animosus [---] of the Marcii Rusonianii [---]
EDCS-81300091.summary: This inscription mentions Gaius Vibius Animosus and the Marcii Rusonianii family, suggesting a connection between them, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-81300092.translation: Of Heraclius // of Serenos // Of Barea [---]NT
EDCS-81300092.summary: This inscription includes Greek names and potentially Latin affiliation, possibly relating to ownership or dedication of a monument.

EDCS-81300101.summary: This inscription lists three personal names, possibly indicating a dedication or a group of individuals, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-81300102.summary: This inscription presents variations of the name Macar, possibly indicating different individuals or grammatical uses, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-81300104.summary: This inscription repeats the Greek name Marrion, possibly for emphasis or as an owner's mark, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-81300107.translation: To Nemesis Augusta. Marcus Junius Crescens, son of Afri, imperial priest, curator of the public service, augur, twice chief magistrate, bearing the cost from his own funds, fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-81300107.summary: This is a dedication to Nemesis Augusta by Marcus Junius Crescens, who held several important civic and religious offices, recording his fulfillment of a vow, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-81300110.translation: To Nemesis Augusta, Marcus Junius Crescens, son of Africanus, twice-chiliarch and quinquennial official, a munerarius, fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-81300110.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Nemesis by Marcus Junius Crescens, who held several local magistracies, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-81300113.summary: This inscription appears to be a fragmented dedication or funerary text, possibly naming individuals and a group.

EDCS-81300116.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Cenonis, son of Cerialis, probably from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-81300117.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Marcus Aurelius, freedman of Augustus, Aphrodisius, to his dearest wife, Pompeia Zois.
EDCS-81300117.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated by Marcus Aurelius Aphrodisius to his beloved wife Pompeia Zois, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-81300118.translation: Publius Saturnini Guddul, son of Publius, made their vow.
EDCS-81300118.summary: This is a votive inscription recording a vow made by Publius Saturnini Guddul, son of Publius, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-81300119.summary: This inscription is a name, possibly identifying an individual or a freedwoman.

EDCS-81300120.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Hadrian Augustus, son of the deified Trajan the Parthian, grandson of the deified Nerva, Pontifex Maximus, VII times holding tribunician power, III times consul, Father of the Fatherland; Gaius Junius Maximus, son of Publius, of the Quirina tribe, perpetual priest, built the temple to Hadrian Augustus for the honor of the perpetual priesthood, valued at 21,000 sesterces, with multiplied money, from his own foundations, along with his sons Gaius Junius Severus and Publius Junius Maximus, son of Gaius, and he himself dedicated it.
EDCS-81300120.summary: This is a monumental dedication by Gaius Junius Maximus, a priest, for the construction and dedication of a temple to Emperor Hadrian, detailing the cost and his sons, dating to Hadrian's reign (117-138 AD).

EDCS-81300121.translation: To our lord Flavius Valentinianus, pious, happy, victorious, and triumphant, always Augustus.
EDCS-81300121.summary: This inscription is a formal dedication to the emperor Valentinian III, likely from the 5th century CE.

EDCS-81300122.translation: [For X]alissa, a most distinguished man, [for his] exceptional defense and distinguished leadership, for the common good, because through his exemplary services by which he diligently and with singular devotion considered the fatherland and all citizens, publicly and privately, the distinguished order of Arados, responding with his merits and repaid services with greater than expected duties, with its own devotion, has erected a statue to his name and honor for eternal memory, felicitously.
EDCS-81300122.summary: This is an honorific inscription by the city of Arados to an esteemed individual named Xalissa for his public and private services, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-81300123.translation: Ten pounds. By authority of Quintus Junius Rusticus, prefect of the city, a most distinguished man. Ten pounds.
EDCS-81300123.summary: This inscription records a quantity of ten pounds, authorized by Quintus Junius Rusticus, the prefect of the city, likely a record of goods or payments, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-81300131.translation: devoted to his divinity and majesty.
EDCS-81300131.summary: This inscription is a fragment expressing devotion to a divine ruler, likely an emperor.

EDCS-81300132.translation: L. L. lived 97 years, he is buried here. He lived 99 years, she is buried here.
EDCS-81300132.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespans and burial of two individuals, likely a couple.

EDCS-81300134.summary: This is a short inscription, likely a name or a dedication, possibly funerary, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-81400095.translation: Quintus Titurnius Saturninus willingly fulfilled his vow according to the order.
EDCS-81400095.summary: This is an ex-voto inscription recording the fulfillment of a vow by Quintus Titurnius Saturninus.

EDCS-81400096.translation: Sacred to Saturn Augustus. Publius Postumius Victor, the priest, willingly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-81400096.summary: This is an ex-voto inscription dedicated to Saturn Augustus by the priest Publius Postumius Victor.

EDCS-81400097.translation: Sacred to Saturn Augustus. Caius Attius Rufus fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-81400097.summary: This is an ex-voto inscription dedicated to Saturn Augustus by Caius Attius Rufus.

EDCS-81700014.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Iunius Saturninus lived 100 years.
EDCS-81700014.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Iunius Saturninus, dedicated to the underworld deities.

EDCS-81700355.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Quintus Julius Zabullus lived piously for 66 years. He is buried here.
EDCS-81700355.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Quintus Julius Zabullus, who lived 66 years, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-81700356.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Secundula Fulvia lived piously for 75 years.
EDCS-81700356.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Secundula Fulvia, who lived 75 years, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-82000013.translation: In memory in Christ of Marcus Avises Marsalis, he rests.
EDCS-82000013.summary: This is an early Christian funerary inscription commemorating Marcus Avises Marsalis.

EDCS-82000014.summary: This is a short epitaph for Agentus Sentanus, possibly of Christian origin given the phrase 'in pace'.

EDCS-82000021.summary: This is a brief funerary inscription marking the memorial of Antistia.

EDCS-82000124.translation: C. Ahalcuiluisu, son of Adonibal, from Aamr, servant of Mysm.
EDCS-82000124.summary: This inscription appears to be of Punic or Neo-Punic origin, possibly recording a dedication or a genealogy.

EDCS-82000130.translation: Of Flabius Vasira, son of Artimst.
EDCS-82000130.summary: This is a funerary inscription commemorating Flabius Vasira, likely from the Roman province of Arabia.

EDCS-82000132.translation: Of Kaysnis, son of... Beatino, son of... Ekyc, son of... Duc.
EDCS-82000132.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription recording a patronymic line of descent.

EDCS-82000134.summary: This is a heavily damaged inscription, possibly funerary or dedicatory, with names and partial words remaining.

EDCS-82000135.summary: This inscription, possibly of Punic or related origin, records a name and patronymic, with damage to the text.

EDCS-82000137.translation: Ioses Theodorus, the tax collector, from the estate of Vinius.
EDCS-82000137.summary: This inscription identifies Ioses Theodorus as a tax collector possibly connected to the property of Vinius.

EDCS-82000231.summary: This inscription is too fragmentary to provide a translation or summary.

EDCS-82100017.translation: Serenus set up this bronze statue of a Muse, a singer, in return for the favor of Leptis.
EDCS-82100017.summary: This is a funerary epigram in Greek, likely for a statue dedicated by or to someone named Serenus, possibly in Leptis, and refers to a Muse.

EDCS-82200009.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Pompeius Nabor, who lived 29 years and 7 months. Sacred to the Divine Manes. Pompeius Barea, who lived 27 years and 10 days. Pompeius [...]pus, his parent, for his children.
EDCS-82200009.summary: This is a double funerary inscription honoring Pompeius Nabor and Pompeius Barea, with a parent dedicating the monument to their children.

EDCS-82200012.translation: Doulkos, donor and equestrian of the Ausonians by birth. A god knows the rest of his affairs. In order that you too may understand, keep it before your eyes, beginning from the top of the page.
EDCS-82200012.summary: This is a Greek epigram encouraging the reader to pay attention to the inscription's contents, attributed to someone named Doulkos.

EDCS-82200013.translation: To Zeus Helios Megas Sarapis and the associated gods, Aurelius Dioscorus, along with Aurelius Dioscorus his father, and Aurelia Theodora his sister, and Cansuleia Claudiana his wife, and his children Aurelius Dioscorus and Aurelia Eutychia, and his sister's children Aurelius Potamon and Aurelia Theodora, and Aurelius Potamon their father, I dedicated this in thanksgiving to the most manifest god for great illness.
EDCS-82200013.summary: This is a Greek votive inscription dedicated to Sarapis and associated gods by Aurelius Dioscorus and his family, thanking the god for recovery from a serious illness.

EDCS-82200014.translation: Aurelius Dioscorus, along with Aurelius Dioscorus his father, and Aurelia Theodora his sister, and Canuleia Claudiana his wife, and his children Aurelius Dioscorus and Aurelia Eutychia, and his sister's children Aurelius Potamon and Aurelia Theodora, and Aurelius Potamon their father, dedicated [this statue/offering] to the most renowned Dioscurus [i.e., the gods] and to Zeus Hypsistos for good fortune.
EDCS-82200014.summary: This Greek inscription is a votive dedication to Zeus Hypsistos and possibly the Dioscuri, made by Aurelius Dioscorus and his extensive family.

EDCS-82200016.translation: Aniketos, having made a vow, dedicated [this] to Zeus Helios Megas Sarapis and the associated gods. Marcus Aurelius Petronius, also called Demetrius.
EDCS-82200016.summary: This is a Greek votive inscription dedicating an offering to Sarapis and associated gods, made by Marcus Aurelius Petronius, also known as Demetrius.

EDCS-82200017.translation: Aurelius Origenes, also called Athenodoros, and his daughter, and his wife Gellia Asca, dedicated [this] to Zeus Helios Megas Sarapis and the associated gods.
EDCS-82200017.summary: This is a Greek votive inscription dedicated to Sarapis and associated gods by Aurelius Origenes (Athenodoros), his daughter, and his wife Gellia Asca.

EDCS-82200018.translation: Aurelius Origenes, also called Athenodoros, along with his daughter [dedicated this] to Zeus Helios Megas Sarapis and the associated gods.
EDCS-82200018.summary: This is a Greek votive inscription dedicated to Sarapis and associated gods by Aurelius Origenes (Athenodoros) and his daughter.

EDCS-82200019.translation: Lucius Aurelius Hierax dedicated [this] to Zeus Helios Megas Sarapis and the associated gods.
EDCS-82200019.summary: This is a Greek votive inscription dedicating an offering to Sarapis and associated gods by Lucius Aurelius Hierax.

EDCS-82200021.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Gaius Valerius Diocletian Pius Felix Augustus, for the fourth time. To the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Valerius Maximian Pius Felix Augustus, for the third time. consuls(?). To the unconquered lords... 54 miles.
EDCS-82200021.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription honoring the emperors Diocletian and Maximian, possibly related to a milestone or an imperial dedication, dating to their consulships.

EDCS-82200022.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Flavius Venustus, who lived 70 years. His sons [dedicated this] to the deserving [father].
EDCS-82200022.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Flavius Venustus, set up by his sons.

EDCS-82200023.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Cornelia Quintula, who lived 22 years. Her husband made [this].
EDCS-82200023.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Cornelia Quintula, set up by her husband.

EDCS-82200025.translation: Julius Flavus, healthy, 66 years old. This is the grave of Mia, 33 years old.
EDCS-82200025.summary: This is a simple epitaph recording the ages of two individuals, Julius Flavus and Mia, likely a family or related individuals.

EDCS-82200026.translation: Marcius Metasan, son of Fidelis, and Flavia Hanochulam, and Seic[---] and Fidel[is], grandsons, erected this tablet for the eternal rest of Flavia. And [---] VII [---] and [---]VIS [---] VI[---] and [---] BUNOM MRAYSYNAU[---]YSFELUMBUL AYBYDBANNOM.
EDCS-82200026.summary: This inscription records the erection of a tablet by Marcius Metasan and other relatives for the memory of Flavia, with the latter part of the text being largely illegible but potentially containing a dedication or personal names.

EDCS-82200031.translation: In this sign, Granius Bibas with his sons and grandsons.
EDCS-82200031.summary: This is a funerary inscription marking a grave or tomb belonging to Granius Bibas and his family.

EDCS-82200032.translation: Muthunibal lived 78 years. She lies here. Caius Julius Probus made this for his mother with his own money.
EDCS-82200032.summary: This is a Latin funerary epitaph commemorating Muthunibal, erected by her son Caius Julius Probus.

EDCS-82200033.translation: Enensu, beloved in heart, dear to his own, whom the dark day took away, lived in peace for more or less 25 years, departed from this world on a November day, first indiction, the tenth.
EDCS-82200033.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Enensu, who lived about 25 years and died in November, dated to the first indiction.

EDCS-82200038.translation: On a day of the month of July, Vnsaiivnt, may the Lord grant you eternal rest and may perpetual light grieve for you.
EDCS-82200038.summary: This inscription is a funerary epitaph, likely for someone named Vnsaiivnt, mentioning a July date and wishing eternal rest and perpetual light.

EDCS-82200039.translation: L. Departed from this world on a day of the month of December, second indiction. Amen. May the Lord grant you eternal rest.
EDCS-82200039.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the departure of 'L.' in December, dated to the second indiction.

EDCS-82200040.translation: IIII. May the Lord grant you eternal rest and may perpetual light grieve for you. Amen.
EDCS-82200040.summary: A brief funerary epitaph wishing eternal rest and perpetual light, possibly referencing a numbered individual or day.

EDCS-82200041.translation: II. Departed from this world in the month of July, seventh indiction. Deus Sabaoth.
EDCS-82200041.summary: This inscription notes a departure in July, dated to the seventh indiction, with a reference to Deus Sabaoth.

EDCS-82200042.translation: II. Month of June, fourteenth indiction. May the Lord grant you eternal rest.
EDCS-82200042.summary: A funerary inscription recording a death in June, dated to the fourteenth indiction, with a prayer for eternal rest.

EDCS-82200043.translation: Iot, whom the dark day took away, lived in peace for more or less [X] years, departed from this world on a day of the month, second, may the Lord grant you eternal rest and may perpetual light grieve for you. Holy immortal, have mercy on me. II. Beloved in his own, whom the dark day RVS MO S SA
EDCS-82200043.summary: This fragmented funerary inscription records a person named Iot who lived about [X] years, died in early February, and includes pleas for mercy and eternal rest.

EDCS-82200044.translation: Lived for more or less 10 years, departed from this world on the 21st day of the month of February, sixth indiction. In peace. Amen.
EDCS-82200044.summary: This is a funerary inscription for an individual who lived approximately 10 years and died on February 21st, dated to the sixth indiction.

EDCS-82200045.translation: II Iys. Departed from this world on a day of the month of January, second indiction. Amen. V.
EDCS-82200045.summary: A funerary inscription noting a departure in January, dated to the second indiction, likely for someone abbreviated as 'Iys' or 'V'.

EDCS-82200046.translation: In this tomb lies the body of Petrus of good memory, who was beloved in his own, lived in peace for more or less 36 years, departed from this world under the second indiction, the thirteenth.
EDCS-82200046.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Petrus, who lived about 36 years and died under the thirteenth indiction.

EDCS-82200053.translation: In this tomb lies the body of Xpiamas, of good memory, who was dear and beloved to her family; she lived in peace for more or less 25 years and departed from this world on the 10th day of August, may she have eternal rest.
EDCS-82200053.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Xpiamas, who died at approximately 25 years old and was loved by her family.

EDCS-82200057.translation: In this tomb lies the body of Esidorus, of good memory, who was beloved by his family and bright in spirit, who suffered from fevers for 22 days and departed from this world on the __ day of the month __.
EDCS-82200057.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Esidorus, who died after suffering from fevers, with his age or date of death partially lost.

EDCS-82200059.translation: In this tomb lies Bonifatius, who was dear and beloved to his family, whom a dark day took away; he lived in peace for more or less 28 years and departed from this world on the 23rd day of May in the 8th indiction, may the Lord grant you eternal rest.
EDCS-82200059.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Bonifatius, who died at approximately 28 years old, with a prayer for his eternal rest.

EDCS-82200065.translation: In this tomb lies the body of Silvestris, of good memory, who lived in peace for more or less 30 years and departed from this world on the 5th day of March in the first indiction.
EDCS-82200065.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Silvestris, who died at approximately 30 years old and lived a peaceful life.

EDCS-82200068.translation: arius departed from this world, may the Lord God.
EDCS-82200068.summary: A very fragmented inscription that seems to record someone's departure from this world and invokes God.

EDCS-82200070.translation: In this tomb lies the body of Iras, of good memory, who lived in peace for more or less 17 years and departed from this world on the 14th day of September, may Christ who will call you to Abraham's bosom receive you, may holy angels lead you.
EDCS-82200070.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Iras, who died at approximately 17 years old, with prayers for her reception into the afterlife.

EDCS-82200076.translation: In this tomb lies the body of Iuia, of good memory, who lived for more or less __ years and departed from this world on the __ day of December.
EDCS-82200076.summary: A funerary inscription for Iuia, with the exact age or date of death partially lost.

EDCS-82200079.translation: Lived in peace for __ years, departed from this world on the __ day of August in the 5th indiction, may Saint Fortis have eternal rest.
EDCS-82200079.summary: An inscription that mentions living in peace and departing from this world, possibly related to Saint Fortis.

EDCS-82200080.translation: Departed from this world at more or less 32 years of age on the 15th day of August in the 8th indiction, Saint Fortis.
EDCS-82200080.summary: This inscription records the death of someone, possibly Saint Fortis, at approximately 32 years old on August 15th.

EDCS-82200082.translation: Departed from this world on the __ day of September in the 15th indiction, Saint Fortis.
EDCS-82200082.summary: An inscription recording a departure from this world in September, possibly related to Saint Fortis, with the day and indiction partially lost.

EDCS-82200083.translation: May the name of God protect you, Holy Spirit, holy God, holy and strong.
EDCS-82200083.summary: A short prayer for divine protection, likely inscribed on a personal object or a small devotional marker.

EDCS-82200085.translation: In this tomb is laid the body of Faustina of good memory, who was dear to her family and beloved in heart, whom a cruel day took away without cause. Lingering, she lived more or less 19 years. She departed from this world on the 28th day of the month of August, indiction 3. May the Lord give her eternal rest. Say Amen, all, Amen, because she was beloved.
EDCS-82200085.summary: A funerary inscription for Faustina, detailing her age at death and the date of her passing, likely from the 4th-6th century due to the mention of indiction.

EDCS-82200086.translation: Dear to her family, she lived more or less 19 years. She departed from this world on the 5th day of the month of March, indiction 9. In this tomb lies the body of KI tibi IMPLGLEI.
EDCS-82200086.summary: A funerary inscription that records the lifespan and death date of an individual, with a cryptic mention of 'KI tibi IMPLGLEI', possibly a prayer or an invocation, dating to the 4th-6th century.

EDCS-82200089.translation: Holy immortal, have mercy on me.
EDCS-82200089.summary: A brief Christian prayer for mercy, likely inscribed as a personal devotion or charm.

EDCS-82200092.translation: In the year six thousand four hundred and eighty-nine, in this tomb lies the body of Maria of good memory, wife of Karinus. She lived in this world more or less 55 years. May she have eternal rest and possess eternal life. O all you who pass by the way and see this, if my sorrow is like your sorrow, how great is your love? Pray for me on the day of judgment, that I may be saved. Amen, Amen. Holy, holy, holy is the Lord God of Sabaoth, Lord God of Sabaoth.
EDCS-82200092.summary: A funerary inscription for Maria, wife of Karinus, dating to the year 6489 (likely a dating system based on Creation, placing it in the 10th century AD), requesting prayers for salvation and invoking the seraphic hymn.

EDCS-82200094.translation: In the name of Christ, in this tomb lies the body of Petrus the most illustrious judge of good memory. He lived in this world sixty years more or less. In the year 6000, indiction 15, on the first day of the month of March, he departed from this world. May he have eternal rest and possess eternal life with all the saints and the elect. Amen, Amen, Amen. In you, Lord, will I hope, I shall not be confounded forever.
EDCS-82200094.summary: A funerary inscription for Petrus, a distinguished judge, detailing his age at death and the date of his passing (year 6000, indiction 15, March 1st), likely from the 6th century AD, and including a biblical quote.

EDCS-82200095.translation: In this tomb lies the body of Fokion of good memory, by the mercy of God. More or less 50 years, he departed from this world on the twentieth day of the month of December, indiction 8. May the Lord give you eternal rest and perpetual light. Let your dry bones mourn. You will rise again and live and see the majesty of the Lord Sabaoth. The Lord God Christ.
EDCS-82200095.summary: A funerary inscription for Fokion, giving his approximate age and the date of his death (December 20th, indiction 8), likely from the 4th-6th century, containing a promise of resurrection and invoking God and Christ.

EDCS-82200098.translation: In this tomb lies the body of Solomonine of good memory. Eternal life... The Lord has taken my soul.
EDCS-82200098.summary: A fragmentary funerary inscription for Solomonine, expressing a desire for eternal life and acknowledging divine reception of the soul.

EDCS-82200099.translation: In this tomb lies the body of [Rus] of good memory. He lived approximately 30 years. He departed from this world in the year 6000, 477, on the 15th day in the month of August. O all you who pass by the ways, look and see: is my sorrow like your sorrow? Pray for me, that you may have God as helper on the day of judgment. Amen.
EDCS-82200099.summary: A funerary inscription for an individual named Rus, dating to the year 6477 (likely a dating system based on Creation, placing it in the 10th century AD), requesting prayers and comparing the deceased's sorrow to that of the passersby.

EDCS-82200100.translation: In this tomb lies the body of Cora G of good memory. She lived in this world 27 years. She departed from this world in the year 6000, 477, indiction 2, in the month of February. May eternal rest be lamented for you.
EDCS-82200100.summary: A funerary inscription for Cora G, stating her age at death and the date of her passing (year 6477, indiction 2, February), likely from the 10th century AD.

EDCS-82200101.translation: In this tomb lies the body of Andreas of good memory. He lived for more or less 45 years and departed this world in the 60,554th year, in the fourth indiction, on the 12th day of December, before the birth of our Lord Jesus Christ. O all you who pass by the way, see and look if your sorrow is like my sorrow. Pray for me that God may be your helper, as the apostle James said. Pray for Christ mutually that you may be saved. Amen. Holy, immortal.
EDCS-82200101.summary: This epitaph commemorates Andreas, who died in December before the birth of Christ, and includes a plea for prayers and biblical references, likely dating from the late antique or early medieval period.

EDCS-82200102.translation: In the name of Christ, in this tomb lies the body of Speratus Petrus, son of good memory. He lived in this world for more or less 40 years and migrated from this world in the 60,512th year, in the second indiction, in the month of November. May he have eternal rest and possess eternal life. Amen, amen, amen. What is my sorrow! Pray for me, as the apostle James said. Pray for Christ mutually that you may be saved. May he have eternal rest and guard eternal life with all the saints and the elect. Amen.
EDCS-82200102.summary: This epitaph records the death of Speratus Petrus, son, who lived approximately 40 years and died in November of the 60,512th year (likely a Christian era dating), requesting eternal rest and prayers.

EDCS-82200103.translation: In this tomb lies the body of abbot Laurentius, most sweet monk, of good memory. He lived in peace for more or less 63 years and departed from this world on the third day before the Kalends of December, in the 13th indiction.
EDCS-82200103.summary: This epitaph commemorates abbot Laurentius, a monk of good memory, who lived about 63 years and died before the Kalends of December in the 13th indiction.

EDCS-82200104.translation: In this tomb lies the body of abbot Petrus, monk, of good memory. He lived in peace for more or less 75 years and departed from this world on the 21st day of the 10th indiction. May the Lord grant you eternal rest and perpetual light. May indulgence mourn for you. Holy, holy, holy, Lord God of Sabaoth. Holy, Holy.
EDCS-82200104.summary: This epitaph records the death of abbot Petrus, a monk of good memory, who lived about 75 years and died on the 21st day of the 10th indiction, with a prayer for eternal rest.

EDCS-82200106.translation: Of good memory, AUS Victorinus lived 75 years more or less and fell asleep in peace on the twelfth day of the month of March.
EDCS-82200106.summary: This epitaph is for Victorinus, of good memory, who lived about 75 years and died on March 12th.

EDCS-82200107.translation: A funerary inscription in an unknown language.
EDCS-82200107.summary: This is a badly damaged funerary inscription, possibly in a non-Latin language, with unclear meaning.

EDCS-82200110.translation: My mother, beloved Pudens, your labor [is repaid?]. The sum of 1700 denarii paid for burial. [---]
EDCS-82200110.summary: This inscription appears to be a funerary text, possibly a ledger or payment record for a burial, mentioning a sum of 1700 denarii and a person named Pudens, with unclear context due to damage.

EDCS-82200111.translation: An inscription in an unknown language with some legible names and titles.
EDCS-82200111.summary: This is a fragmented inscription, likely funerary, with some Latinized names and titles like 'procurator', indicating an administrative role.

EDCS-82200112.translation: A funerary inscription in an unknown language.
EDCS-82200112.summary: This is a damaged funerary inscription in an unknown language, with numbers possibly indicating age or quantity.

EDCS-82200113.translation: And his wife and Uarnychsen and M METU and Masinthan, the heirs, built this memorial, as is visited. The memorial of YTHNYCHISOUE NIFSE was made and Melior [paid?] 30 [units?] of the thousand folles.
EDCS-82200113.summary: This inscription records that the heirs of Uarnychsen, M METU, and Masinthan, along with his wife, built a memorial for YTHNYCHISOUE NIFSE, with a mention of a payment of 30 folles from a thousand.

EDCS-82200115.summary: This is a short Greek funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of a person named Faustus.

EDCS-82800061.translation: Julia Quieta, daughter of Quintus, priestess, lived 91 years. Quintus Julius Ampliatus, veteran, lived 85 years. Quintus Julius Respectus, son of Quintus, lived 17 years.
EDCS-82800061.summary: This is a complex funerary inscription recording the lifespans of at least three individuals, two of whom are from the Iulius family.

EDCS-82800063.translation: Valeria Nica placed this at her own expense while alive on these lands.
EDCS-82800063.summary: This is a dedication by Valeria Nica, who funded the erection of something on her property during her lifetime.

EDCS-82800064.translation: Sacred to the shades of the departed. Aelius Nepotianus, Roman equestrian, lived 39 years, 5 months, and 10 days. His brother Aelius Clementianus managed the burial. May your bones rest well.
EDCS-82800064.summary: This is a Roman funerary inscription for Aelius Nepotianus, specifying his age and the person responsible for his burial, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-82800065.translation: Sacred to the shades of the departed. Iulia Rogatina.
EDCS-82800065.summary: This is a simple Roman funerary inscription dedicated to Iulia Rogatina.
